This is essential', '\t\t * because the default keyring may be the session keyring, and', '\t\t * joining a keyring only requires Search permission.', '\t\t *', '\t\t * However, this check is skipped for the "requestor keyring" so', '\t\t * that /sbin/request-key can itself use request_key() to add', "\t\t * keys to the original requestor's destination keyring.", '\t\t */', '\t\tif (dest_keyring && do_perm_check) {', '\t\t\tret = key_permission(make_key_ref(dest_keyring, 1),', '\t\t\t\t\t     KEY_NEED_WRITE);', '\t\t\tif (ret) {', '\t\t\t\tkey_put(dest_keyring);', '\t\t\t\treturn ret;', '\t\t\t}', '\t\t}', '\treturn 0;']}
description: The KEYS subsystem in the Linux kernel before 4.14.6 omitted an access-control check when adding a key to the current task's "default request-key keyring" via the request_key() system call, allowing a local user to use a sequence of crafted system calls to add keys to a keyring with only Search permission (not Write permission) to that keyring, related to construct_get_dest_keyring() in security/keys/request_key.c.

code_evidence: When no destination keyring is supplied, the switch selects a default keyring based on cred->jit_keyring; the KEY_REQKEY_DEFL_SESSION_KEYRING branch obtains the session keyring via key_get without any permission check.
The requestor-keyring branch returns a key_get'd dest_keyring and breaks, but no Write permission is ever validated against the selected keyring before use.
The function stores the selected keyring into *_dest_keyring and returns void, so callers link the requested key into it with no authorization decision.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs a resource-modifying action (linking a key into a keyring) without any authorization check on the destination keyring, directly matching CWE-862 Missing Authorization. This is distinct from an incorrect check: the check is entirely absent at this resolution point.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: construct_get_dest_keyring() resolves a default destination keyring (e.g., session keyring via KEY_REQKEY_DEFL_SESSION_KEYRING) and hands it to request_key() linking without verifying KEY_NEED_WRITE. Trigger: a local user with only Search permission joins/selects a keyring as the default and invokes request_key(), causing a key to be linked. Consequence: unauthorized key insertion into a keyring the caller may not write to, violating access control.

commit_msg:
bpf/verifier: fix bounds calculation on BPF_RSH

Incorrect signed bounds were being computed.
If the old upper signed bound was positive and the old lower signed bound was
negative, this could cause the new upper signed bound to be too low,
leading to security issues.

Fixes: b03c9f9fdc37 ("bpf/verifier: track signed and unsigned min/max values")
Reported-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Edward Cree <ecree@solarflare.com>
Acked-by: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@kernel.org>
[jannh@google.com: changed description to reflect bug impact]
Signed-off-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t/* BPF_RSH is an unsigned shift, so make the appropriate casts */', '\t\tif (dst_reg->smin_value < 0) {', '\t\t\tif (umin_val) {', '\t\t\t\t/* Sign bit will be cleared */', '\t\t\t\tdst_reg->smin_value = 0;', '\t\t\t} else {', '\t\t\t\t/* Lost sign bit information */', '\t\t\t\tdst_reg->smin_value = S64_MIN;', '\t\t\t\tdst_reg->smax_value = S64_MAX;', '\t\t\t}', '\t\t} else {', '\t\t\tdst_reg->smin_value =', '\t\t\t\t(u64)(dst_reg->smin_value) >> umax_val;', '\t\t}'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t/* BPF_RSH is an unsigned shift.  If the value in dst_reg might', '\t\t * be negative, then either:', '\t\t * 1) src_reg might be zero, so the sign bit of the result is', '\t\t *    unknown, so we lose our signed bounds', "\t\t * 2) it's known negative, thus the unsigned bounds capture the", '\t\t *    signed bounds', '\t\t * 3) the signed bounds cross zero, so they tell us nothing', '\t\t *    about the result', '\t\t * If the value in dst_reg is known nonnegative, then again the', '\t\t * unsigned bounts capture the signed bounds.', '\t\t * Thus, in all cases it suffices to blow away our signed bounds', '\t\t * and rely on inferring new ones from the unsigned bounds and', '\t\t * var_off of the result.', '\t\t */', '\t\tdst_reg->smin_value = S64_MIN;', '\t\tdst_reg->smax_value = S64_MAX;']}
description: kernel/bpf/verifier.c in the Linux kernel through 4.14.8 allows local users to cause a denial of service (memory corruption) or possibly have unspecified other impact by leveraging incorrect BPF_RSH signed bounds calculations.

code_evidence: In the BPF_RSH case, when dst_reg->smin_value < 0 and umin_val is nonzero, the code sets smin_value = 0 claiming the sign bit is cleared; otherwise it widens to S64_MIN/S64_MAX. When smin_value >= 0 it computes smin_value = (u64)(smin_value) >> umax_val. These signed-bound updates ignore the possibility that src_reg may be zero or that signed bounds cross zero, so the computed signed bounds can be too low.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The incorrect verifier bounds directly permit out-of-bounds memory operations by BPF programs, matching CWE-119's out-of-buffer read/write scope. The underlying defect is a bounds-calculation flaw, but the supported consequence is improper operations within a memory buffer.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: incorrect signed min/max bound computation on BPF_RSH lets the verifier infer a range narrower than the true possible values. Trigger: a BPF program shifts a value whose signed bounds are negative or cross zero with an unconstrained/zero shift amount. Supported consequence: the verifier accepts out-of-range register values, enabling subsequent memory accesses outside the intended buffer (memory corruption/DoS).

commit_msg:
It turns out that currently we rely only on sysfs attribute
permissions:

  $ ll /sys/bus/rbd/{add*,remove*}
  --w------- 1 root root 4096 Sep  3 20:37 /sys/bus/rbd/add
  --w------- 1 root root 4096 Sep  3 20:37 /sys/bus/rbd/add_single_major
  --w------- 1 root root 4096 Sep  3 20:37 /sys/bus/rbd/remove
  --w------- 1 root root 4096 Sep  3 20:38 /sys/bus/rbd/remove_single_major

This means that images can be mapped and unmapped (i.e. block devices
can be created and deleted) by a UID 0 process even after it drops all
privileges or by any process with CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE in its user namespace
as long as UID 0 is mapped into that user namespace.

Be consistent with other virtual block devices (loop, nbd, dm, md, etc)
and require CAP_SYS_ADMIN in the initial user namespace for mapping and
unmapping, and also for dumping the configuration string and refreshing
the image header.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Ilya Dryomov <idryomov@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\tif (!capable(CAP_SYS_ADMIN))', '\t\treturn -EPERM;']}
description: The rbd block device driver in drivers/block/rbd.c in the Linux kernel through 5.8.9 used incomplete permission checking for access to rbd devices, which could be leveraged by local attackers to map or unmap rbd block devices, aka CID-f44d04e696fe.

code_evidence: The function proceeds directly from local variable declarations to try_module_get() and then rbd_add_parse_args(), rbd_get_client(), rbd_dev_create() and device_add_disk(), with no capability or privilege check anywhere in the body.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-863 fits because the function performs an action gated by an authorization decision that is not correctly enforced in code; the missing CAP_SYS_ADMIN check lets an actor lacking the required privilege perform the operation. This is an authorization-check flaw rather than a memory-safety issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: do_rbd_add performs the privileged mapping operation (device creation via rbd_dev_device_setup/device_add_disk) relying only on sysfs attribute permissions, without verifying CAP_SYS_ADMIN. Trigger: a process with UID 0 mapped into a user namespace, or one holding CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE, writes to the sysfs add attribute. Consequence: mapping of rbd block devices is authorized incorrectly, bypassing the intended privilege boundary.

commit_msg:
mwifiex: Fix three heap overflow at parsing element in cfg80211_ap_settings

mwifiex_update_vs_ie(),mwifiex_set_uap_rates() and
mwifiex_set_wmm_params() call memcpy() without checking
the destination size.Since the source is given from
user-space, this may trigger a heap buffer overflow.

Fix them by putting the length check before performing memcpy().

This fix addresses CVE-2019-14814,CVE-2019-14815,CVE-2019-14816.

Signed-off-by: Wen Huang <huangwenabc@gmail.com>
Acked-by: Ganapathi Bhat <gbhat@marvell.comg>
Signed-off-by: Kalle Valo <kvalo@codeaurora.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (*(wmm_ie + 1) > sizeof(struct mwifiex_types_wmm_info))', '\t\t\treturn;']}
description: There is heap-based buffer overflow in kernel, all versions up to, excluding 5.3, in the marvell wifi chip driver in Linux kernel, that allows local users to cause a denial of service(system crash) or possibly execute arbitrary code.

code_evidence: cfg80211_find_vendor_ie locates a WMM vendor IE inside the user-supplied params->beacon.tail buffer (length tail_len). When found, wmm_ie points into that attacker-controlled IE and memcpy copies *(wmm_ie + 1) bytes from wmm_ie + sizeof(struct ieee_types_header) into bss_cfg->wmm_info with no bound check against the destination size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked memcpy writes beyond a heap-allocated destination (bss_cfg->wmm_info), which is the defining pattern of CWE-122 Heap-based Buffer Overflow. It is not merely a stack overflow or out-of-bounds read, since the overflowed buffer is heap-allocated and is written past its end.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The IE length byte *(wmm_ie + 1) is taken from user-space beacon tail data and used directly as the memcpy length into the fixed-size bss_cfg->wmm_info heap object. A crafted IE with an oversized length byte causes a heap buffer overflow, corrupting adjacent heap memory and potentially leading to crash or code execution.

Return error when there are more mmco params than allocated size

The patch adds a local i_temp and returns ERROR_DBP_MANAGER_T when it is negative.

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the error return of ih264d_read_mmco_commands (triggered by crafted MMCO data exceeding the allocated command array) is assigned to the unsigned u4_bitoffset without validation. buf_out_len is also u_int16_t; buf_out_len += len (line 25) wraps for large len, after strncpy at line 24 already copied len bytes.

buf_out_len += len;

commit_msg:
KVM: use after free in kvm_ioctl_create_device()

We should move the ops->destroy(dev) after the list_del(&dev->vm_node)
so that we don't use "dev" after freeing it.

Fixes: a28ebea2adc4 ("KVM: Protect device ops->create and list_add with kvm->lock")
Signed-off-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Reviewed-by: David Hildenbrand <david@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Radim Krčmář <rkrcmar@redhat.com>

description: Use-after-free vulnerability in the kvm_ioctl_create_device function in virt/kvm/kvm_main.c in the Linux kernel before 4.8.13 allows host OS users to cause a denial of service (host OS crash) or possibly gain privileges via crafted ioctl calls on the /dev/kvm device.

code_evidence: On failure of anon_inode_getfd (line 31), the error path calls ops->destroy(dev) at line 33 before taking kvm->lock and removing dev from kvm->devices via list_del at line 35. The destroy callback may free dev, so the subsequent list_del(&dev->vm_node) dereferences freed memory. The patch moves destroy after list_del to fix this ordering.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-264 covers weaknesses in permission/privilege and security-feature management; the error-path use-after-free in KVM device creation undermines the kernel's access-control boundary, enabling host users via /dev/kvm to crash or possibly gain privileges, matching the target category.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: use-after-free ordering in the error path—ops->destroy(dev) can release dev before list_del(&dev->vm_node) uses it. Trigger: anon_inode_getfd returns a negative value (e.g., fd exhaustion). Consequence: host kernel dereferences freed memory, causing a crash or potentially privilege escalation.

commit_msg:
We're holding the request reference, but we need to go one higher
to ensure that the ctx remains valid after the request has finished.
If the ring is closed with pending task_work inflight, and the
given io_kiocb finishes sync during issue, then we need a reference
to the ring itself around the task_work execution cycle.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # v5.7+
Reported-by: syzbot+9b260fc33297966f5a8e@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Signed-off-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tstruct io_ring_ctx *ctx = req->ctx;', '\tpercpu_ref_put(&ctx->refs);']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel before 5.8.2. fs/io_uring.c has a use-after-free related to io_async_task_func and ctx reference holding, aka CID-6d816e088c35.

code_evidence: The function derives req from the task_work callback, then passes req to io_poll_task_handler; when a next request exists it submits nxt via __io_req_task_submit. The function never takes or releases the io_ring_ctx reference that keeps req->ctx alive across this task_work execution, so the callback can run while the ring is being torn down.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe operation is continued use of req and its ctx after the ring can be freed, which is the defining pattern of CWE-416. The missing ctx reference is the cause; subsequent handler/submit access is the use-after-free effect, not a separate weakness class.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: task_work execution is not protected by a ctx reference, so the ring context associated with req can be freed before or during io_poll_task_handler/__io_req_task_submit. Trigger: ring closed with pending task_work in flight while the io_kiocb completes synchronously during issue. Consequence: use-after-free access to ctx/req state, leading to memory corruption or crash.

description: TensorFlow is an open source platform for machine learning. If `Save` or `SaveSlices` is run over tensors of an unsupported `dtype`, it results in a `CHECK` fail that can be used to trigger a denial of service attack. We have patched the issue in GitHub commit 5dd7b86b84a864b834c6fa3d7f9f51c87efa99d4. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.10.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.9.1, TensorFlow 2.8.1, and TensorFlow 2.7.2, as these are also affected and still in supported range. There are no known workarounds for this issue.

code_evidence: The original code computes size_bound using MaxBytesPerElement(DataTypeToEnum<T>::value) without validating that the dtype is supported; for unsupported dtypes this path can hit a CHECK-fail inside MaxBytesPerElement rather than returning an error.
The DCHECK_GE and DCHECK_LE assertions on ss->ByteSize() are reachable debug assertions, but the primary reachable-failure path is the dtype-dependent size computation preceding Fill.

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the serialization path invokes MaxBytesPerElement on an unsupported dtype without a guard, so an attacker-supplied tensor dtype reaches an internal CHECK/assert. Trigger: running Save/SaveSlices over an unsupported dtype. Consequence: process abort, i.e., denial of service, rather than a returned InvalidArgument.

commit_msg: Add missing NULL check in ble-l2cap.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    LOG_WARN("process_l2cap_credit: invalid len: %d\\n", len);'], 'added_lines': ['  if(channel == NULL) {', '    LOG_WARN("input_l2cap_credit: no channel found for sender address\\n");', '    return;', '  }', '', '    LOG_WARN("input_l2cap_credit: invalid len: %d\\n", len);']}
description: Contiki-NG is an open-source, cross-platform operating system for Next-Generation IoT devices. Versions prior to 4.9 contain a NULL Pointer Dereference in BLE L2CAP module. The Contiki-NG operating system for IoT devices contains a Bluetooth Low Energy stack. An attacker can inject a packet in this stack, which causes the implementation to dereference a NULL pointer and triggers undefined behavior. More specifically, while processing the L2CAP protocol, the implementation maps an incoming channel ID to its metadata structure. In this structure, state information regarding credits is managed through calls to the function input_l2cap_credit in the module os/net/mac/ble/ble-l2cap.c. Unfortunately, the input_l2cap_credit function does not check that the metadata corresponding to the user-supplied channel ID actually exists, which can lead to the channel variable being set to NULL before a pointer dereferencing operation is performed. The vulnerability has been patched in the "develop" branch of Contiki-NG, and will be included in release 4.9. Users can apply the patch in Contiki-NG pull request #2253 as a workaround until the new package is released.

code_evidence: Line 7 stores the result of get_channel_for_addr(...) in channel without checking it. Line 15 unconditionally dereferences channel->channel_peer.credits using attacker-influenced data, so a NULL return crashes.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits because a pointer expected to be valid is dereferenced while NULL, matching the missing check at line 7 before the dereference at line 15.

evidence_lines.code:
l2cap_channel_t *channel = get_channel_for_addr(packetbuf_addr(PACKETBUF_ADDR_SENDER));
channel->channel_peer.credits += credits;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the return value of get_channel_for_addr for the sender address is used without a NULL check. Trigger: an injected L2CAP credit packet whose sender address has no matching channel makes channel NULL, and the credits update dereferences it, causing a NULL pointer dereference and crash (DoS).

description: SphinxSearch in Sphinx Technologies Sphinx through 3.1.1 allows directory traversal (in conjunction with CVE-2019-14511) because the mysql client can be used for CALL SNIPPETS and load_file operations on a full pathname (e.g., a file in the /etc directory). NOTE: this is unrelated to CMUSphinx.

code_evidence: In files mode, the caller-supplied tOptions.m_sSource is concatenated onto g_sSnippetsFilePrefix with SetSprintf at line 18 and the resulting path is opened with SPH_O_READ at line 19. No canonicalization or traversal check exists in this function; the diff adds TestEscaping after the concatenation, confirming the original code trusted the joined path.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-22 fits because external input is used to construct a pathname meant to stay under a restricted prefix, yet special elements can escape that directory. This is path traversal via the file-open path, not merely a generic input-validation issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the path is built by naive prefix+input concatenation and opened without neutralizing '..' or absolute components. Trigger: a snippets request in files mode with a source such as '/etc/passwd' or '../../../etc/passwd'. Consequence: the opened file is read into the snippet buffer, disclosing files outside the intended snippets scope.

commit_msg:
Reject fonts with invalid ranges in cmap

A corrupt or malicious font may have a negative size in its cmap
range, which in turn could lead to memory corruption. This patch
detects the case and rejects the font, and also includes an assertion
in the sparse bit set implementation if we missed any such case.

External issue:
https://code.google.com/p/android/issues/detail?id=192618

Bug: 26413177
Change-Id: Icc0c80e4ef389abba0964495b89aa0fae3e9f4b2
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['        if (end < start) {', '            // invalid group range: size must be positive', '            return false;', '        }']}
description: The Minikin library in Android 5.0.x before 5.0.2, 5.1.x before 5.1.1, and 6.x before 2016-04-01 does not properly consider negative size values in font data, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory corruption and reboot loop) via a crafted font, aka internal bug 26413177.

code_evidence: The loop reads attacker-controlled start (line 16) and end (line 17) character codes from the font cmap group without checking that end >= start. addRange(coverage, start, end + 1) (line 18) then computes a size from end + 1; when end is less than start, the resulting range is invalid and can produce a negative/huge size in the sparse bit set.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function accepts structured font input and fails to validate a required property of the data (that each group's end is not less than its start) before using it. That is improper input validation (CWE-20); the negative-size memory corruption is the downstream consequence rather than the root cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the cmap group range fields are parsed but the relationship end >= start is never validated before being passed to addRange. A crafted font with end < start triggers an invalid range whose derived size is negative, leading to memory corruption. Consequence is denial of service (crash/reboot loop); the cause is missing validation of the range consistency, not the memory corruption itself.

commit_msg:
CVE-2017-13036/OSPFv3: Add a bounds check before fetching data

This fixes a buffer over-read discovered by Bhargava Shastry,
SecT/TU Berlin.

Add a test using the capture file supplied by the reporter(s), modified
so the capture file won't be rejected as an invalid capture.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\tND_TCHECK_32BITS(&hellop->hello_options);']}
description: The OSPFv3 parser in tcpdump before 4.9.2 has a buffer over-read in print-ospf6.c:ospf6_decode_v3().

code_evidence: hellop is derived from op + OSPF6HDR_LEN without verifying that the hello6 body (including hello_options) lies within the captured packet; lines 14-16 then read EXTRACT_32BITS(&hellop->hello_options) before any bounds check.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Reading hello_options without first confirming the field is within the captured buffer is a direct out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). The fix adds ND_TCHECK_32BITS before the read, confirming the missing constraint; this is distinct from an out-of-bounds write.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the HELLO branch dereferences the hello6 options field with no length validation against dataend. Trigger: a truncated OSPFv3 HELLO packet whose captured data ends before hello_options. Consequence: an out-of-bounds read of up to 4 bytes past the packet buffer, potentially exposing memory or crashing tcpdump.

commit_msg:
Fix `tf.raw_ops.SparseCross` failing CHECK.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 368701671
Change-Id: Id805729dd9ba0bda36e4bb309408129b55fb649d
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    OP_REQUIRES_OK(context, context->GetAttr("internal_type", &internal_type_));']}
description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. The API of `tf.raw_ops.SparseCross` allows combinations which would result in a `CHECK`-failure and denial of service. This is because the implementation(https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/3d782b7d47b1bf2ed32bd4a246d6d6cadc4c903d/tensorflow/core/kernels/sparse_cross_op.cc#L114-L116) is tricked to consider a tensor of type `tstring` which in fact contains integral elements. Fixing the type confusion by preventing mixing `DT_STRING` and `DT_INT64` types solves this issue. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.5.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.4.2, TensorFlow 2.3.3, TensorFlow 2.2.3 and TensorFlow 2.1.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: The constructor reads scalar attributes num_buckets and hash_key and stores hash_key_ as uint64; it never retrieves the 'internal_type' attribute that the kernel uses to interpret element data. Without this attribute, the kernel cannot validate that the string inputs are genuinely DT_STRING rather than DT_INT64 values reinterpreted as tstring.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-843 fits because the same element memory is accessed as a tstring while it actually holds integral values, a direct type confusion. The missing internal_type retrieval removes the constraint needed to prevent this incompatible-type access.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the op construction omits the internal_type attribute, so the implementation cannot distinguish DT_STRING from DT_INT64 inputs and treats integral elements as tstring. Trigger: SparseCross is invoked with mixed DT_STRING/DT_INT64 combinations; the resulting tstring interpretation reaches a CHECK failure, causing denial of service.

commit_msg:
The driver for XillyUSB devices maintains a kref reference count on each
xillyusb_dev structure, which represents a physical device. This reference
count reaches zero when the device has been disconnected and there are no
open file descriptors that are related to the device. When this occurs,
kref_put() calls cleanup_dev(), which clears up the device's data,
including the structure itself.

However, when xillyusb_open() is called, this reference count becomes
tricky: This function needs to obtain the xillyusb_dev structure that
relates to the inode's major and minor (as there can be several such).
xillybus_find_inode() (which is defined in xillybus_class.c) is called
for this purpose. xillybus_find_inode() holds a mutex that is global in
xillybus_class.c to protect the list of devices, and releases this
mutex before returning. As a result, nothing protects the xillyusb_dev's
reference counter from being decremented to zero before xillyusb_open()
increments it on its own behalf. Hence the structure can be freed
due to a rare race condition.

To solve this, a mutex is added. It is locked by xillyusb_open() before
the call to xillybus_find_inode() and is released only after the kref
counter has been incremented on behalf of the newly opened inode. This
protects the kref reference counters of all xillyusb_dev structs from
being decremented by xillyusb_disconnect() during this time segment, as
the call to kref_put() in this function is done with the same lock held.

There is no need to hold the lock on other calls to kref_put(), because
if xillybus_find_inode() finds a struct, xillyusb_disconnect() has not
made the call to remove it, and hence not made its call to kref_put(),
which takes place afterwards. Hence preventing xillyusb_disconnect's
call to kref_put() is enough to ensure that the reference doesn't reach
zero before it's incremented by xillyusb_open().

It would have been more natural to increment the reference count in
xillybus_find_inode() of course, however this function is also called by
Xillybus' driver for PCIe / OF, which registers a completely different
structure. Therefore, xillybus_find_inode() treats these structures as
void pointers, and accordingly can't make any changes.

Reported-by: Hyunwoo Kim <imv4bel@gmail.com>
Suggested-by: Alan Stern <stern@rowland.harvard.edu>
Signed-off-by: Eli Billauer <eli.billauer@gmail.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20221030094209.65916-1-eli.billauer@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (rc)', '', '\tkref_get(&xdev->kref);'], 'added_lines': ['\tmutex_lock(&kref_mutex);', '', '\tif (rc) {', '\t\tmutex_unlock(&kref_mutex);', '\t}', '', '\tkref_get(&xdev->kref);', '\tmutex_unlock(&kref_mutex);', '\tkref_put(&xdev->kref, cleanup_dev);']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel through 6.0.9. drivers/char/xillybus/xillyusb.c has a race condition and use-after-free during physical removal of a USB device.

code_evidence: xillybus_find_inode() returns xdev after releasing its internal global mutex, so nothing keeps xdev alive between the lookup and the later kref_get().
The reference is only taken at line 37, after chan->lock is acquired and several checks pass; until then xdev is used (lines 12, 16, 23) without an owning reference.
The unmutex_fail path exits without dropping a reference, consistent with the reference not yet being held.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect is improper synchronization: the shared xdev lifetime is not exclusively held across the lookup-to-kref_get sequence, so a concurrent disconnect can decrement the count to zero. This is a race condition (CWE-362); the use-after-free is the consequence rather than the root weakness.

evidence_lines.code:
kref_get(&xdev->kref);
if (filp->f_mode & FMODE_READ)

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: xillyusb_open() resolves the device via xillybus_find_inode(), which releases the list mutex before returning; xillyusb_disconnect() can then reach kref_put()/cleanup_dev() and free xdev before xillyusb_open() calls kref_get(). The window between lookup and reference acquisition allows use of freed xdev (channels, dev pointer), causing a use-after-free race.

commit_msg: Fixed bug #77831 - Heap-buffer-overflow in exif_iif_add_value in EXIF
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\texif_iif_add_tag(ImageInfo, SECTION_APP12, "Company", TAG_NONE, TAG_FMT_STRING, l1, buffer+2);', '\t\t\texif_iif_add_tag(ImageInfo, SECTION_APP12, "Info", TAG_NONE, TAG_FMT_STRING, l2, buffer+2+l1+1);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\texif_iif_add_tag(ImageInfo, SECTION_APP12, "Company", TAG_NONE, TAG_FMT_STRING, l1, buffer+2, l1);', '\t\t\texif_iif_add_tag(ImageInfo, SECTION_APP12, "Info", TAG_NONE, TAG_FMT_STRING, l2, buffer+2+l1+1, l2);']}
description: When processing certain files, PHP EXIF extension in versions 7.1.x below 7.1.28, 7.2.x below 7.2.17 and 7.3.x below 7.3.4 can be caused to read past allocated buffer in exif_iif_add_value function. This may lead to information disclosure or crash.

code_evidence: l1 is computed as the bounded length of the string at buffer+2 using php_strnlen over length-2, then passed to exif_iif_add_tag with the raw pointer buffer+2 but no explicit validated copy length.
l2 is bounded by length-2-l1-1 and passed to exif_iif_add_tag with buffer+2+l1+1, again relying on the callee to respect the computed length when reading the string data.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is a read beyond the intended buffer during tag processing, matching CWE-125 Out-of-bounds Read rather than a write-side overflow.

evidence_lines.code:
if ((l1 = php_strnlen(buffer+2, length-2)) > 0) {
exif_iif_add_tag(ImageInfo, SECTION_APP12, "Company", TAG_NONE, TAG_FMT_STRING, l1, buffer+2);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the tag-adding helper is given a length derived from php_strnlen but the call site does not convey a bounded copy extent, so downstream handling can read past the allocated APP12 buffer. Trigger: crafted EXIF APP12 data where the string region reaches or exceeds buffer bounds. Consequence: out-of-bounds read leading to information disclosure or crash.

commit_msg:
Fix double-free in gdImageWebPtr()

The issue is that gdImageWebpCtx() (which is called by gdImageWebpPtr() and
the other WebP output functions to do the real work) does not return whether
it succeeded or failed, so this is not checked in gdImageWebpPtr() and the
function wrongly assumes everything is okay, which is not, in this case,
because there is a size limitation for WebP, namely that the width and
height must by less than 16383.

We can't change the signature of gdImageWebpCtx() for API compatibility
reasons, so we introduce the static helper _gdImageWebpCtx() which returns
success respective failure, so gdImageWebpPtr() and gdImageWebpPtrEx() can
check the return value. We leave it solely to libwebp for now to report
warnings regarding the failing write.

This issue had been reported by Ibrahim El-Sayed to security@libgd.org.

CVE-2016-6912

description: Double free vulnerability in the gdImageWebPtr function in the GD Graphics Library (aka libgd) before 2.2.4 allows remote attackers to have unspecified impact via large width and height values.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The shown function only frees argb once and out once; no double free is visible in this function, and the described failure path depends on gdImageWebpPtr behavior not present here.

commit_msg:
adb: switch the socket list mutex to a recursive_mutex.

sockets.cpp was branching on whether a socket close function was
local_socket_close in order to avoid a potential deadlock if the socket
list lock was held while closing a peer socket.

Bug: http://b/28347842
Change-Id: I5e56f17fa54275284787f0f1dc150d1960256ab3
(cherry picked from commit 9b587dec6d0a57c8fe1083c1c543fbeb163d65fa)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    adb_mutex_lock(&socket_list_lock);', '        local_socket_next_id = 1;', '', '    adb_mutex_unlock(&socket_list_lock);'], 'added_lines': ['    std::lock_guard<std::recursive_mutex> lock(local_socket_list_lock);', '        fatal("local socket id overflow");']}
description: The Java Debug Wire Protocol (JDWP) implementation in adb/sockets.cpp in Android 4.x before 4.4.4, 5.0.x before 5.0.2, 5.1.x before 5.1.1, and 6.x before 2016-09-01 mishandles socket close operations, which allows attackers to gain privileges via a crafted application, aka internal bug 28347842.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function only manages the local socket ID counter and list insertion under a mutex; it contains no permission, privilege, or access-control decision, so it does not directly support CWE-264.

commit_msg:
Fix OOB write in grappler.

Discovered via internal fuzzing.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 482097391
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    if (attr.first >= inputs.size()) {', '      return errors::InvalidArgument("Invalid attribute index, got ",', '                                     attr.first, " but expected less than ",', '                                     inputs.size());', '    }']}
description: TensorFlow is an open source platform for machine learning. The function MakeGrapplerFunctionItem takes arguments that determine the sizes of inputs and outputs. If the inputs given are greater than or equal to the sizes of the outputs, an out-of-bounds memory read or a crash is triggered. We have patched the issue in GitHub commit a65411a1d69edfb16b25907ffb8f73556ce36bb7. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.11.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.8.4, 2.9.3, and 2.10.1.

code_evidence: arg_attr is sized to inputs.size() and default-initialized to nullptr. The loop over func.arg_attr() writes arg_attr.at(attr.first) using attr.first directly from the FunctionDef without checking it against inputs.size(). If a malformed FunctionDef supplies an attribute index >= inputs.size(), .at() is out of range.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the unchecked index causes a read past the end of the intended arg_attr buffer. The patch adds an explicit attr.first >= inputs.size() guard, confirming the missing constraint; this is an out-of-bounds read rather than a write.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: missing bounds validation on the attribute index attr.first before indexing the inputs-sized vector. Trigger: a FunctionDef whose arg_attr index is >= inputs.size(). Consequence: arg_attr.at() performs an out-of-range access, yielding an out-of-bounds read (or abort/crash), matching the reported fuzzing finding.

commit_msg:
x86/paravirt: Fix spectre-v2 mitigations for paravirt guests

Nadav reported that on guests we're failing to rewrite the indirect
calls to CALLEE_SAVE paravirt functions. In particular the
pv_queued_spin_unlock() call is left unpatched and that is all over the
place. This obviously wrecks Spectre-v2 mitigation (for paravirt
guests) which relies on not actually having indirect calls around.

The reason is an incorrect clobber test in paravirt_patch_call(); this
function rewrites an indirect call with a direct call to the _SAME_
function, there is no possible way the clobbers can be different
because of this.

Therefore remove this clobber check. Also put WARNs on the other patch
failure case (not enough room for the instruction) which I've not seen
trigger in my (limited) testing.

commit_msg:
avcodec/idctdsp: Transmit studio_profile to init instead of using AVCodecContext profile

These 2 fields are not always the same, it is simpler to always use the same field
for detecting studio profile

Fixes: null pointer dereference
Fixes: ffmpeg_crash_3.avi

Found-by: Thuan Pham <thuanpv@comp.nus.edu.sg>, Marcel Böhme, Andrew Santosa and Alexandru RazvanCaciulescu with AFLSmart
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>

description: libavcodec in FFmpeg 4.0 may trigger a NULL pointer dereference if the studio profile is incorrectly detected while converting a crafted AVI file to MPEG4, leading to a denial of service, related to idctdsp.c and mpegvideo.c.

code_evidence: When bits_per_raw_sample is 9 or 10, line 21 selects the studio-profile IDCT path by checking avctx->codec_id and avctx->profile. In that branch only c->idct_put is assigned (line 22); c->idct_add and c->idct are left unassigned, unlike the else branch at lines 24-26.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function leaves IDCT function pointers unset under a mis-detected profile, and their later invocation dereferences NULL. This matches CWE-476 (NULL Pointer Dereference) as the direct cause of the crash.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the studio-profile detection can disagree with the actual stream, so the 10-bit studio branch is taken and only idct_put is set while idct_add/idct remain unset. commit_msg: Don't overflow stack buffer in msg_parse_fetch
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      while (*s && *s != \'\\"\')', '      while (isdigit((unsigned char) *s))'], 'added_lines': ['      while (*s && (*s != \'\\"\') && (ptmp != (tmp + sizeof(tmp) - 1)))', '      while (isdigit((unsigned char) *s) && (ptmp != (tmp + sizeof(tmp) - 1)))']}
description: An issue was discovered in Mutt before 1.10.1 and NeoMutt before 2018-07-16. imap/message.c has a stack-based buffer overflow for a FETCH response with a long INTERNALDATE field.

code_evidence: A fixed-size stack buffer tmp[SHORT_STRING] is declared at line 3. In the INTERNALDATE branch, ptmp is set to tmp (line 34), then the loop at lines 35-36 copies every character from the network-supplied FETCH response until a quote is found, with no bound on ptmp, and line 40 writes a terminator. A long INTERNALDATE value overflows tmp.
The RFC822.SIZE branch similarly sets ptmp = tmp (line 47) and the loop at lines 48-49 copies an unbounded run of digits, followed by *ptmp = '\0' at line 50, again overflowing tmp.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes attacker-controlled bytes beyond the bounds of the intended stack buffer tmp, which matches CWE-787 (out-of-bounds write). It is not merely a read overrun or truncation; the unchecked pointer increment causes the write itself to exceed the buffer.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the copy loops advance ptmp without checking it against tmp + sizeof(tmp), so the input length controls how far the write proceeds. Trigger: an IMAP FETCH response containing a long INTERNALDATE field (or long digit run for RFC822.SIZE). Consequence: writes past the end of the stack buffer, corrupting adjacent stack memory and potentially enabling code execution or a crash.

commit_msg: Fix #241, potential double free
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['                if (!output_buffer->noalloc)', '                {', '                    output_buffer->hooks.deallocate(output_buffer->buffer);', '                }'], 'added_lines': []}
description: Dave Gamble cJSON version 1.7.2 and earlier contains a CWE-415: Double Free vulnerability in cJSON library that can result in Possible crash or RCE. This attack appear to be exploitable via Attacker must be able to force victim to print JSON data, depending on how cJSON library is used this could be either local or over a network. This vulnerability appears to have been fixed in 1.7.3.

code_evidence: On the cJSON_Raw path, when item->valuestring is NULL, the function calls output_buffer->hooks.deallocate(output_buffer->buffer) at line 43 and then returns false at line 45 without clearing output_buffer->buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The explicit deallocate call on a shared buffer followed by an error return matches CWE-415's double-free pattern because the buffer pointer is not reset, permitting a second free. This is distinct from a simple memory leak, which would omit the free rather than repeat it.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: an error path frees the shared output buffer while leaving the pointer intact, so a later error or cleanup path can deallocate the same address again. Trigger: printing a Raw item whose valuestring is NULL while allocation is enabled. Supported consequence: double free of the output buffer, leading to memory corruption, crash, or potential code execution.

commit_msg:
Fix a padding oracle in PKCS7_dataDecode and CMS_decrypt_set1_pkey

An attack is simple, if the first CMS_recipientInfo is valid but the
second CMS_recipientInfo is chosen ciphertext. If the second
recipientInfo decodes to PKCS #1 v1.5 form plaintext, the correct
encryption key will be replaced by garbage, and the message cannot be
decoded, but if the RSA decryption fails, the correct encryption key is
used and the recipient will not notice the attack.

As a work around for this potential attack the length of the decrypted
key must be equal to the cipher default key length, in case the
certifiate is not given and all recipientInfo are tried out.

The old behaviour can be re-enabled in the CMS code by setting the
CMS_DEBUG_DECRYPT flag.

Reviewed-by: Matt Caswell <matt@openssl.org>
(Merged from https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/9777)

(cherry picked from commit 5840ed0cd1e6487d247efbc1a04136a41d7b3a37)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    if (!cert)', '        cms->d.envelopedData->encryptedContentInfo->havenocert = 1;', '    else', '        cms->d.envelopedData->encryptedContentInfo->havenocert = 0;']}
description: In situations where an attacker receives automated notification of the success or failure of a decryption attempt an attacker, after sending a very large number of messages to be decrypted, can recover a CMS/PKCS7 transported encryption key or decrypt any RSA encrypted message that was encrypted with the public RSA key, using a Bleichenbacher padding oracle attack. Applications are not affected if they use a certificate together with the private RSA key to the CMS_decrypt or PKCS7_decrypt functions to select the correct recipient info to decrypt. Fixed in OpenSSL 1.1.1d (Affected 1.1.1-1.1.1c). Fixed in OpenSSL 1.1.0l (Affected 1.1.0-1.1.0k). Fixed in OpenSSL 1.0.2t (Affected 1.0.2-1.0.2s).

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function only sets debug/havenocert flags and dispatches to CMS_decrypt_set1_pkey and cms_copy_content; it contains no cryptographic algorithm selection or use, so it does not directly support CWE-327.

Correct Tiles rows and cols check

Bug: 36231493
Bug: 34064500
Change-Id: Ib17b2c68360685c5a2c019e1497612a130f9f76a
(cherry picked from commit 07ef4e7138e0e13d61039530358343a19308b188)

description: A remote code execution vulnerability in libhevc in Mediaserver could enable an attacker using a specially crafted file to cause memory corruption during media file and data processing. This issue is rated as Critical due to the possibility of remote code execution within the context of the Mediaserver process.Product: Android. Versions: 5.0.2, 5.1.1, 6.0, 6.0.1, 7.0, 7.1.1, 7.1.2. code_evidence: Parser reads attacker-controlled num_tile_columns_minus1/num_tile_rows_minus1 via UEV_PARSE, stores value+1 in i1_num_tile_columns/i1_num_tile_rows, then validates them only against ps_sps->i2_pic_wd_in_ctb and i2_pic_ht_in_ctb. commit_msg:
Check for return size in enc_untrusted_read

Check return size does not exceed requested. The returned result and
content still cannot be trusted, but it's expected behavior when not
using a secure file system.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 333827386
Change-Id: I0bdec0aec9356ea333dc8c647eba5d2772875f29
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  return static_cast<ssize_t>(EnsureInitializedAndDispatchSyscall('], 'added_lines': ['  ssize_t ret = static_cast<ssize_t>(EnsureInitializedAndDispatchSyscall(', '  if (ret != -1 && ret > count) {', '    ::asylo::primitives::TrustedPrimitives::BestEffortAbort(', '        "enc_untrusted_read: read result exceeds requested");', '  }', '  return ret;']}
description: An arbitrary memory read vulnerability in Asylo versions up to 0.6.0 allows an untrusted attacker to make a call to enc_untrusted_read whose return size was not validated against the requrested size. The parameter size is unchecked allowing the attacker to read memory locations outside of the intended buffer size including memory addresses within the secure enclave. We recommend upgrading past commit b1d120a2c7d7446d2cc58d517e20a1b184b82200

code_evidence: The function forwards caller-controlled count directly to the read syscall and returns its result without ever comparing the returned byte count to count, so a syscall reporting more bytes than requested is accepted as-is and the caller may consume buf beyond the intended buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the unchecked read length causes data to be read past the end of the intended buffer. It is not an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) since the flaw is an over-reported read length consumed by callers, not a write beyond bounds.

evidence_lines.code:
return static_cast<ssize_t>(EnsureInitializedAndDispatchSyscall(
asylo::system_call::kSYS_read, fd, buf, count));

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the return value of EnsureInitializedAndDispatchSyscall (kSYS_read) is not validated against the requested count. Trigger: the underlying read returns a size larger than count. Consequence: callers trusting the returned length treat buf as holding more bytes than were requested, reading past the intended buffer and potentially exposing enclave memory (confidentiality impact).

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tshift = ctts->version ? ctts_shift : ctts->entries[0].decodingOffset;'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (ctts->version) {', '\t\tshift = ctts_shift;', '\t} else {', '\t\tshift = ctts->nb_entries ? ctts->entries[0].decodingOffset : 0;', '\t}']}

The loop then subtracts shift from each entry's decodingOffset; when nb_entries is 0, shift is read from the empty entries array before this loop.

commit_msg:
acpi: Disable APEI error injection if securelevel is set

ACPI provides an error injection mechanism, EINJ, for debugging and testing
the ACPI Platform Error Interface (APEI) and other RAS features. If
supported by the firmware, ACPI specification 5.0 and later provide for a
way to specify a physical memory address to which to inject the error.

Injecting errors through EINJ can produce errors which to the platform are
indistinguishable from real hardware errors. This can have undesirable
side-effects, such as causing the platform to mark hardware as needing
replacement.

While it does not provide a method to load unauthenticated privileged code,
the effect of these errors may persist across reboots and affect trust in
the underlying hardware, so disable error injection through EINJ if
securelevel is set.

Signed-off-by: Linn Crosetto <linn@hpe.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\tif (get_securelevel() > 0)', '\t\treturn -EPERM;']}
description: The einj_error_inject function in drivers/acpi/apei/einj.c in the Linux kernel allows local users to simulate hardware errors and consequently cause a denial of service by leveraging failure to disable APEI error injection through EINJ when securelevel is set.

code_evidence: einj_error_inject validates flags/type/address but has no securelevel check before reaching inject, so an unprivileged caller can pass type, flags, param1-param4 into __einj_error_inject.
The inject label unconditionally locks einj_mutex and calls __einj_error_inject(type, flags, param1, param2, param3, param4), forwarding attacker-controlled parameters to the firmware EINJ interface.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-74 fits because unneutralized attacker-influenced values (type, flags, addresses) are passed into a downstream EINJ interface that interprets them as error-injection commands. This is command/parameter injection into a privileged backend rather than a memory-safety flaw.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function accepts externally supplied injection parameters and forwards them to the EINJ firmware backend without a securelevel guard. Triggering it lets a local user simulate hardware errors, producing platform-level faults that may cause denial of service and persist across reboots.

commit_msg:
RSA key generation: ensure BN_mod_inverse and BN_mod_exp_mont both get called with BN_FLG_CONSTTIME flag set.

CVE-2018-0737

Reviewed-by: Rich Salz <rsalz@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Matt Caswell <matt@openssl.org>
(cherry picked from commit 6939eab03a6e23d2bd2c3f5e34fe1d48e542e787)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    BN_set_flags(rsa->p, BN_FLG_CONSTTIME);', '    BN_set_flags(rsa->q, BN_FLG_CONSTTIME);']}
description: The OpenSSL RSA Key generation algorithm has been shown to be vulnerable to a cache timing side channel attack. An attacker with sufficient access to mount cache timing attacks during the RSA key generation process could recover the private key. Fixed in OpenSSL 1.1.0i-dev (Affected 1.1.0-1.1.0h). Fixed in OpenSSL 1.0.2p-dev (Affected 1.0.2b-1.0.2o).

code_evidence: Line 45 sets BN_FLG_CONSTTIME only on the temporary r2, not on rsa->p or rsa->q.
Line 52 calls BN_mod_inverse(r1, r2, rsa->e, ctx), where r2 = p-1; the modulus rsa->e and the secret-derived value lack const-time flagging on the prime.
Lines 75-77 repeat the same non-constant-time inversion with rsa->q-1.
Lines 90-94 swap p and q by comparison, but the primes still carry no const-time flag before later secret-dependent operations.
Line 108 computes the private exponent via BN_mod_inverse(rsa->d, rsa->e, pr0, ctx); pr0 is flagged, but the secret operands rsa->p/rsa->q were never flagged.
Line 124 computes iqmp with BN_mod_inverse using p, which is flagged via BN_with_flags, but the underlying secret prime generation path remained unprotected.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-327 covers use of a broken or risky cryptographic algorithm/implementation; here RSA key generation is implemented with a non-constant-time modular-inverse path, making the cryptographic operation unsafe in a side-channel context. This is the targeted risky-crypto weakness rather than a generic memory flaw.

evidence_lines.code: BN_set_flags(r2, BN_FLG_CONSTTIME);
if (BN_mod_inverse(r1, r2, rsa->e, ctx) != NULL) {

if (BN_mod_inverse(r1, r2, rsa->e, ctx) != NULL) {
}

if (BN_cmp(rsa->p, rsa->q) < 0) {
}
if (!BN_mod_inverse(rsa->d, rsa->e, pr0, ctx))
if (!BN_mod_inverse(rsa->iqmp, rsa->q, p, ctx))

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The key-generation path performs modular inversion and related big-number operations on secret primes while the primes are not marked BN_FLG_CONSTTIME, so their ladder/division execution depends on secret values. An attacker able to mount a cache-timing side channel during RSA key generation can correlate timing with the secret primes and recover the private key.

commit_msg:
ipv4: Don't do expensive useless work during inetdev destroy.

When an inetdev is destroyed, every address assigned to the interface
is removed.  And in this scenerio we do two pointless things which can
be very expensive if the number of assigned interfaces is large:

1) Address promotion.  We are deleting all addresses, so there is no
   point in doing this.

2) A full nf conntrack table purge for every address.  We only need to
   do this once, as is already caught by the existing
   masq_dev_notifier so masq_inet_event() can skip this.

Reported-by: Solar Designer <solar@openwall.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
Tested-by: Cyrill Gorcunov <gorcunov@openvz.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\tif (in_dev->dead)', '\t\tgoto no_promotions;', 'no_promotions:']}
description: The IPv4 implementation in the Linux kernel before 4.5.2 mishandles destruction of device objects, which allows guest OS users to cause a denial of service (host OS networking outage) by arranging for a large number of IP addresses.

code_evidence: The function walks every entry in in_dev->ifa_list (lines 35-89) and then performs route-deletion work, calling fib_magic multiple times (lines 90-97), without any early exit when the device is being destroyed.
The patch adds an in_dev->dead check after the subnet computation to skip promotion logic, but this function still traverses the full address list and issues route deletions for each call.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is improper resource management: unbounded, repeated expensive work during device destruction consumes host CPU and degrades availability, matching the Resource Management Errors category.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: fib_del_ifaddr performs full address-list iteration and route-deletion work for each address even when the inetdev is being torn down, where all addresses are removed anyway. Trigger: a guest creates many IP addresses on an interface and then destroys it, causing each removal to invoke this expensive path. Supported consequence: excessive CPU work in the host kernel, producing a networking denial of service.

commit_msg:
Individual lengths inside received server data can overflow
the previously reserved memory.

It is therefore important to validate every single length
field to not overflow the previously agreed sum of all invidual
length fields.

v2: consume remaining bytes in the reply buffer on error.

Signed-off-by: Tobias Stoeckmann <tobias@stoeckmann.org>
Reviewed-by: Matthieu Herrb@laas.fr
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tif (screen->ndepths > rep.numDepths) {', '\t    Xfree (xri);', '\t    Xfree (xData);', '\t    _XEatDataWords (dpy, rep.length);', '\t    UnlockDisplay (dpy);', '\t    SyncHandle ();', '\t    return 0;', '\t}', '\trep.numDepths -= screen->ndepths;', '\t    if (depth->nvisuals > rep.numVisuals) {', '\t\tXfree (xri);', '\t\tXfree (xData);', '\t\t_XEatDataWords (dpy, rep.length);', '\t\tUnlockDisplay (dpy);', '\t\tSyncHandle ();', '\t\treturn 0;', '\t    }', '\t    rep.numVisuals -= depth->nvisuals;']}
description: Multiple buffer overflows in the (1) XvQueryAdaptors and (2) XvQueryEncodings functions in X.org libXrender before 0.9.10 allow remote X servers to trigger out-of-bounds write operations via vectors involving length fields.

code_evidence: The per-screen depth count xScreen->nDepth is copied into screen->ndepths and drives the loop bound at line 134; the allocated depth array was sized from rep.numDepths, but the nested count is never checked against the remaining entries.
Similarly, depth->nvisuals comes from xDepth->nPictVisuals and bounds the inner loop at 140, while xVisual advances through the xData buffer without any check against rep.numVisuals.
After the nested loops, depth and xDepth pointers advance past consumed entries; oversized nested counts let these pointers walk beyond the allocated xri and xData regions.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The root cause is missing validation of received length metadata before it is used to bound processing, which is improper input validation (CWE-20). The out-of-bounds write is the consequence; the weakness is the unchecked input that drives the loop bounds.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The server-supplied nested length fields (nDepth, nPictVisuals) are trusted without being validated against the aggregate counts used to size the allocations. A malicious X server can set these lengths larger than rep.numDepths/rep.numVisuals, causing the loops to write past the end of the XRenderDepth/XRenderVisual arrays and read past xData, yielding out-of-bounds writes and reads.

patch 8.2.4040: keeping track of allocated lines is too complicated

Inside the loop, get_function_line(eap, line_to_free, 0, GETLINE_CONCAT_CONT) fetches the next line; the returned theline is then used via skipwhite(theline) and p = skipwhite(theline), so p points into memory whose lifetime is governed by line_to_free handling.

char_u**line_to_free)
{

commit_msg:

Currently, the backend of VirtFS doesn't have a cleanup
function. This will lead resource leak issues if the backed
driver allocates resources. This patch addresses this issue.

Signed-off-by: Li Qiang <liq3ea@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Greg Kurz <groug@kaod.org>
Signed-off-by: Greg Kurz <groug@kaod.org>

description: Memory leak in hw/9pfs/9p.c in QEMU (aka Quick Emulator) allows local privileged guest OS users to cause a denial of service (host memory consumption and possibly QEMU process crash) by leveraging a missing cleanup operation in FileOperations.

code_evidence: v9fs_device_unrealize_common frees only s->tag and s->ctx.fs_root; it never invokes the backend's cleanup hook (s->ops->cleanup) before discarding the context. The patch adds that guarded call, showing the pre-patch function omitted release of resources owned by the backend driver.

commit_msg:
The functions that were used in the emulation of fxrstor, fxsave, sgdt and
sidt were originally meant for task switching, and as such they did not
check privilege levels.  This is very bad when the same functions are used
in the emulation of unprivileged instructions.  This is CVE-2018-10853.

The obvious fix is to add a new argument to ops->read_std and ops->write_std,
which decides whether the access is a "system" access or should use the
processor's CPL.

Fixes: 129a72a0d3c8 ("KVM: x86: Introduce segmented_write_std", 2017-01-12)
Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t     struct x86_exception *exception)', '\treturn kvm_read_guest_virt_helper(addr, val, bytes, vcpu, 0, exception);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t     struct x86_exception *exception, bool system)', '\tu32 access = 0;', '', '\tif (!system && kvm_x86_ops->get_cpl(vcpu) == 3)', '\t\taccess |= PFERR_USER_MASK;', '', '\treturn kvm_read_guest_virt_helper(addr, val, bytes, vcpu, access, exception);']}
description: A flaw was found in the way Linux kernel KVM hypervisor before 4.18 emulated instructions such as sgdt/sidt/fxsave/fxrstor. It did not check current privilege(CPL) level while emulating unprivileged instructions. An unprivileged guest user/process could use this flaw to potentially escalate privileges inside guest.

code_evidence: emulator_read_std performs a guest virtual read by calling kvm_read_guest_virt_helper with a hardcoded access flag of 0, so no CPL-based user-access check is applied to the emulated read.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function fails to check privileges for an emulated access, creating an unintended sphere of control for an unprivileged guest actor, which matches CWE-269 Improper Privilege Management. The defect is the absent privilege check, not merely the escalation impact.

evidence_lines.code:
struct kvm_vcpu *vcpu = emul_to_vcpu(ctxt);
return kvm_read_guest_virt_helper(addr, val, bytes, vcpu, 0, exception);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The emulation helper does not derive access permissions from the current privilege level; it always passes 0 as the access mask. When invoked to emulate unprivileged instructions such as sgdt/sidt, an unprivileged guest process's read is performed without the user-mode access constraint, allowing it to access data that should be restricted. Root cause is the missing CPL check; the supported consequence is privilege escalation within the guest.

commit_msg:
libsepol/cil: Check for statements not allowed in optional blocks

While there are some checks for invalid statements in an optional
block when resolving the AST, there are no checks when building the
AST.

OSS-Fuzz found the following policy which caused a null dereference
in cil_tree_get_next_path().
  (blockinherit b3)
  (sid SID)
  (sidorder(SID))
  (optional o
    (ibpkeycon :(1 0)s)
    (block b3
      (filecon""block())
      (filecon""block())))

The problem is that the blockinherit copies block b3 before
the optional block is disabled. When the optional is disabled,
block b3 is deleted along with everything else in the optional.
Later, when filecon statements with the same path are found an
error message is produced and in trying to find out where the block
was copied from, the reference to the deleted block is used. The
error handling code assumes (rightly) that if something was copied
from a block then that block should still exist.

It is clear that in-statements, blocks, and macros cannot be in an
optional, because that allows nodes to be copied from the optional
block to somewhere outside even though the optional could be disabled
later. When optionals are disabled the AST is reset and the
resolution is restarted at the point of resolving macro calls, so
anything resolved before macro calls will never be re-resolved.
This includes tunableifs, in-statements, blockinherits,
blockabstracts, and macro definitions. Tunable declarations also
cannot be in an optional block because they are needed to resolve
tunableifs. It should be fine to allow blockinherit statements in
an optional, because that is copying nodes from outside the optional
to the optional and if the optional is later disabled, everything
will be deleted anyway.

Check and quit with an error if a tunable declaration, in-statement,
block, blockabstract, or macro definition is found within an
optional when either building or resolving the AST.

Signed-off-by: James Carter <jwcart2@gmail.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tif (ast->flavor == CIL_OPTIONAL) {', '\t\targs->optional = ast;', '\t}', '']}
description: The CIL compiler in SELinux 3.2 has a heap-based buffer over-read in ebitmap_match_any (called indirectly from cil_check_neverallow). This occurs because there is sometimes a lack of checks for invalid statements in an optional block.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function only records AST flavor pointers into args and contains no buffer access, indexing, or read operation; the out-of-bounds read occurs in ebitmap_match_any, which is not present here.

commit_msg:
evtchn: avoid NULL derefs

Commit fbbd5009e6 ("evtchn: refactor low-level event channel port ops")
added a de-reference of the struct evtchn pointer for a port without
first making sure the bucket pointer is non-NULL. This de-reference is
actually entirely unnecessary, as all relevant callers (beyond the
problematic do_poll()) already hold the port number in their hands, and
the actual leaf functions need nothing else.

For FIFO event channels there's a second problem in that the ordering
of reads and updates to ->num_evtchns and ->event_array[] was so far
undefined (the read side isn't always holding the domain's event lock).
Add respective barriers.

This is XSA-221.

Reported-by: Ankur Arora <ankur.a.arora@oracle.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    /*', "     * Callers aren't required to hold d->event_lock, so we need to synchronize", '     * with add_page_to_event_array().', '     */', '    smp_rmb();', '']}
description: Xen through 4.8.x does not validate the port numbers of polled event channel ports, which allows guest OS users to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference and host OS crash) or possibly obtain sensitive information, aka XSA-221.

code_evidence: The function validates the port number against d->evtchn_fifo->num_evtchns and returns NULL if out of range, but does not check whether d->evtchn_fifo itself is NULL before dereferencing it at line 5.
Line 9 dereferences d->evtchn_fifo->event_array[p] and returns a pointer derived from it; if event_array[p] is NULL, the returned event_word_t pointer is invalid for callers.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits because the function dereferences pointers (d->evtchn_fifo, event_array[p]) that may be NULL, directly enabling a crash. This is a NULL dereference rather than an out-of-bounds issue, since the port range check is present but the pointer validity check is missing.

evidence_lines.code:
if ( unlikely(port >= d->evtchn_fifo->num_evtchns) )
return NULL;
return d->evtchn_fifo->event_array[p] + w;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function dereferences d->evtchn_fifo and event_array[p] without validating that the bucket/event-array entry is non-NULL. Trigger: a caller passes a port for a domain whose FIFO event-channel bucket is uninitialized or not yet populated. Consequence: NULL pointer dereference, causing a host OS crash (DoS), as described in XSA-221.

commit_msg:
Before this patch, function read_rindex_entry would set a rgrp
glock's gl_object pointer to itself before inserting the rgrp into
the rgrp rbtree. The problem is: if another process was also reading
the rgrp in, and had already inserted its newly created rgrp, then
the second call to read_rindex_entry would overwrite that value,
then return a bad return code to the caller. Later, other functions
would reference the now-freed rgrp memory by way of gl_object.
In some cases, that could result in gfs2_rgrp_brelse being called
twice for the same rgrp: once for the failed attempt and once for
the "real" rgrp release. Eventually the kernel would panic.
There are also a number of other things that could go wrong when
a kernel module is accessing freed storage. For example, this could
result in rgrp corruption because the fake rgrp would point to a
fake bitmap in memory too, causing gfs2_inplace_reserve to search
some random memory for free blocks, and find some, since we were
never setting rgd->rd_bits to NULL before freeing it.

This patch fixes the problem by not setting gl_object until we
have successfully inserted the rgrp into the rbtree. Also, it sets
rd_bits to NULL as it frees them, which will ensure any accidental
access to the wrong rgrp will result in a kernel panic rather than
file system corruption, which is preferred.

Signed-off-by: Bob Peterson <rpeterso@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\trgd->rd_bits = NULL;']}
description: An issue was discovered in fs/gfs2/rgrp.c in the Linux kernel before 4.8. A use-after-free is caused by the functions gfs2_clear_rgrpd and read_rindex_entry.

code_evidence: The function frees the rgrp's bitmap buffer with kfree(rgd->rd_bits) at line 18 and then frees the rgrp structure itself via kmem_cache_free at line 20, but rd_bits is never cleared, leaving a stale pointer in freed memory. Any later reference to that rgrp or its rd_bits field accesses freed storage.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the code leaves a dangling reference to memory it has already released, and later use of that pointer is the direct weakness. This is a use-after-free rather than a simple double free, since the concern is continued referencing of freed storage.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The root cause is that gfs2_clear_rgrpd frees rd_bits and the rgrp object without nulling rd_bits, so a stale pointer to freed bitmap memory survives. When a concurrent or subsequent path (e.g. gfs2_inplace_reserve) dereferences the freed rgrp's rd_bits, it reads or searches freed memory, enabling use-after-free leading to corruption or crash.

commit_msg: Fixed possible foveon buffer overrun (Secunia SA750000)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  ushort huff[512], vpred[2][2], hpred[2];'], 'added_lines': ['  ushort huff[1024], vpred[2][2], hpred[2];']}

Line 6 passes this buffer to foveon_huff(huff), which populates the Huffman table; the diff enlarges it to huff[1024], indicating the pre-patch table write exceeds 512 entries.

The root cause is the undersized buffer rather than a separate integer-overflow primitive in this function.

foveon_huff (huff);
diff = ljpeg_diff(huff);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The Huffman table buffer is sized at 512 entries but foveon_huff() writes a larger table into it, overflowing the stack buffer. The overflow occurs when loading a crafted Foveon image whose CAMF data drives the table construction; the enlarged 1024-entry buffer in the patch confirms the out-of-bounds write. This corrupts adjacent stack data (vpred/hpred) and can lead to memory corruption or code execution.

commit_msg:
Limit the number of HTTP requests processed from a connection in I/O cycle

Signed-off-by: Yan Avlasov <yavlasov@google.com>

Signed-off-by: Ryan Northey <ryan@synca.io>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  if (max_requests_during_dispatch_ != UINT32_MAX) {', '    deferred_request_processing_callback_ =', '        dispatcher_->createSchedulableCallback([this]() -> void { onDeferredRequestProcessing(); });', '  }']}
description: The HTTP/2 protocol allows a denial of service (server resource consumption) because request cancellation can reset many streams quickly, as exploited in the wild in August through October 2023.

code_evidence: The function binds dispatcher_ from the accepted connection and increments downstream connection gauges (downstream_cx_total_/active_) for every connection, with no cap or rejection path in this callback.

It installs per-connection timers for idle timeout and max connection duration, but these are optional and only bounded by configuration; when unset, no timer is created and the connection persists without a time-based limit.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-400 fits because the function tracks and maintains a limited resource (connections) without enforcing any bound or throttling on how many are allocated, which is the 'lack of throttling for allocated resources' pattern. It is not CWE-401 (missing release) since the concern is uncontrolled allocation, not leaked references.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: connection initialization performs unconditional accounting and optional-only timers, so the number of concurrently accepted connections is never throttled here. Trigger: a peer opens many connections (or keeps them open past request completion); each invocation of this function consumes a connection slot and stream-info/filter-state resources. Consequence: server-side resource consumption grows with connection count, supporting denial of service. The commit's request-limiting callback is added elsewhere and is not present in this function, so it does not mitigate this path.

[DevTools] Do not use "settings" query param.

Implemented the same functionality on embedder side.
Also, sanitizing "settings" query param for remote frontends.

Review-Url: https://codereview.chromium.org/2177983004

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['                                    bool can_dock,', '                                    const std::string& settings) {', '  if (settings.size())', '    url_string += "&settings=" + settings;'], 'added_lines': ['                                    bool can_dock) {']}
description: Cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the Developer Tools (aka DevTools) subsystem in Google Chrome before 53.0.2785.89 on Windows and OS X and before 53.0.2785.92 on Linux allows remote attackers to inject arbitrary web script or HTML via the settings parameter in a chrome-devtools-frontend.appspot.com URL's query string.

code_evidence: When the caller-supplied settings string is non-empty, it is concatenated verbatim into the DevTools URL query string as '&settings=' + settings, with no URL-encoding or validation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This is improper neutralization of user-controllable input during web page generation, matching CWE-79; the unencoded settings concatenation is the entry point for XSS rather than mere open-redirect or parameter tampering.

evidence_lines.code:
if (settings.size())
url_string += "&settings=" + settings;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The settings parameter is attacker-influenced and is appended unencoded to a URL that is later loaded as a web page by DevTools. A crafted value containing markup or script allows injection into the generated page, resulting in script execution in the DevTools context.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  /*', '     Verify that file size large enough to contain a JNG datastream.', '  */', '  if (GetBlobSize(image) < 147)', '    ThrowReaderException(CorruptImageError,"InsufficientImageDataInFile");', '']}
description: In ImageMagick before 6.9.9-0 and 7.x before 7.0.6-1, a crafted PNG file could trigger a crash because there was an insufficient check for short files.

code_evidence: Reads only 8 bytes for the JNG magic and validates the header via count/memcmp, but performs no check that the remaining blob is large enough for a JNG datastream.
After the header check, the code proceeds directly to allocate MngInfo and call ReadOneJNGImage without any size precondition; a short file passes the header test and enters the deeper parser.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function omits a check for an unusual condition — a file shorter than the minimum JNG datastream — and proceeds on the assumption it cannot happen. This is improper checking of an exceptional condition (CWE-754), distinct from a generic out-of-bounds read since the defect is the missing length precondition.

evidence_lines.code:
mng_info=(MngInfo *) AcquireMagickMemory(sizeof(*mng_info));
image=ReadOneJNGImage(mng_info,image_info,exception);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the reader assumes a valid 8-byte signature implies a complete JNG datastream, so it never verifies the blob length before parsing. Trigger: a crafted/truncated PNG/JNG file that supplies the correct magic bytes but too few remaining bytes. Consequence: the downstream parser reads past the available data, causing a crash (DoS).
