commit_msg:
Commit a23740ec43ba ("bpf: Track contents of read-only maps as scalars") is
checking whether maps are read-only both from BPF program side and user space
side, and then, given their content is constant, reading out their data via
map->ops->map_direct_value_addr() which is then subsequently used as known
scalar value for the register, that is, it is marked as __mark_reg_known()
with the read value at verification time. Before a23740ec43ba, the register
content was marked as an unknown scalar so the verifier could not make any
assumptions about the map content.

The current implementation however is prone to a TOCTOU race, meaning, the
value read as known scalar for the register is not guaranteed to be exactly
the same at a later point when the program is executed, and as such, the
prior made assumptions of the verifier with regards to the program will be
invalid which can cause issues such as OOB access, etc.

While the BPF_F_RDONLY_PROG map flag is always fixed and required to be
specified at map creation time, the map->frozen property is initially set to
false for the map given the map value needs to be populated, e.g. for global
data sections. Once complete, the loader "freezes" the map from user space
such that no subsequent updates/deletes are possible anymore. For the rest
of the lifetime of the map, this freeze one-time trigger cannot be undone
anymore after a successful BPF_MAP_FREEZE cmd return. Meaning, any new BPF_*
cmd calls which would update/delete map entries will be rejected with -EPERM
since map_get_sys_perms() removes the FMODE_CAN_WRITE permission. This also
means that pending update/delete map entries must still complete before this
guarantee is given. This corner case is not an issue for loaders since they
create and prepare such program private map in successive steps.

However, a malicious user is able to trigger this TOCTOU race in two different
ways: i) via userfaultfd, and ii) via batched updates. For i) userfaultfd is
used to expand the competition interval, so that map_update_elem() can modify
the contents of the map after map_freeze() and bpf_prog_load() were executed.
This works, because userfaultfd halts the parallel thread which triggered a
map_update_elem() at the time where we copy key/value from the user buffer and
this already passed the FMODE_CAN_WRITE capability test given at that time the
map was not "frozen". Then, the main thread performs the map_freeze() and
bpf_prog_load(), and once that had completed successfully, the other thread
is woken up to complete the pending map_update_elem() which then changes the
map content. For ii) the idea of the batched update is similar, meaning, when
there are a large number of updates to be processed, it can increase the
competition interval between the two. It is therefore possible in practice to
modify the contents of the map after executing map_freeze() and bpf_prog_load().

One way to fix both i) and ii) at the same time is to expand the use of the
map's map->writecnt. The latter was introduced in fc9702273e2e ("bpf: Add mmap()
support for BPF_MAP_TYPE_ARRAY") and further refined in 1f6cb19be2e2 ("bpf:
Prevent re-mmap()'ing BPF map as writable for initially r/o mapping") with
the rationale to make a writable mmap()'ing of a map mutually exclusive with
read-only freezing. The counter indicates writable mmap() mappings and then
prevents/fails the freeze operation. Its semantics can be expanded beyond
just mmap() by generally indicating ongoing write phases. This would essentially
span any parallel regular and batched flavor of update/delete operation and
then also have map_freeze() fail with -EBUSY. For the check_mem_access() in
the verifier we expand upon the bpf_map_is_rdonly() check ensuring that all
last pending writes have completed via bpf_map_write_active() test. Once the
map->frozen is set and bpf_map_write_active() indicates a map->writecnt of 0
only then we are really guaranteed to use the map's data as known constants.
For map->frozen being set and pending writes in process of still being completed
we fall back to marking that register as unknown scalar so we don't end up
making assumptions about it. With this, both TOCTOU reproducers from i) and
ii) are fixed.

Note that the map->writecnt has been converted into a atomic64 in the fix in
order to avoid a double freeze_mutex mutex_{un,}lock() pair when updating
map->writecnt in the various map update/delete BPF_* cmd flavors. Spanning
the freeze_mutex over entire map update/delete operations in syscall side
would not be possible due to then causing everything to be serialized.
Similarly, something like synchronize_rcu() after setting map->frozen to wait
for update/deletes to complete is not possible either since it would also
have to span the user copy which can sleep. On the libbpf side, this won't
break d66562fba1ce ("libbpf: Add BPF object skeleton support") as the
anonymous mmap()-ed "map initialization image" is remapped as a BPF map-backed
mmap()-ed memory where for .rodata it's non-writable.

Fixes: a23740ec43ba ("bpf: Track contents of read-only maps as scalars")
Reported-by: w1tcher.bupt@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>
Acked-by: Andrii Nakryiko <andrii@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tmap->writecnt++;'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tbpf_map_write_active_inc(map);']}
description: A race condition was found in the Linux kernel's ebpf verifier between bpf_map_update_elem and bpf_map_freeze due to a missing lock in kernel/bpf/syscall.c. In this flaw, a local user with a special privilege (cap_sys_admin or cap_bpf) can modify the frozen mapped address space. This flaw affects kernel versions prior to 5.16 rc2.

code_evidence: The function locks freeze_mutex and checks map->frozen and BPF_F_RDONLY_PROG before allowing a writable mapping, but these checks only gate the mmap() call itself.

After the checks pass and map->ops->map_mmap() succeeds, the code increments map->writecnt only for VM_MAYWRITE mappings; this counter is the mechanism the verifier relies on to know pending writers exist, so its correctness determines whether a frozen map can still be modified concurrently.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-367 fits: the frozen/read-only state is checked, then map contents are used as known scalars, but the writecnt accounting here does not reliably prevent the resource state from changing between check and use. This is a check-vs-use race, not a simple missing permission check.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the writable-mapping accounting (map->writecnt) is updated after the check and only for VM_MAYWRITE, so a state change (writable mapping or pending write) can occur between the verifier's frozen/read-only check and its use of map contents as known scalars. Trigger: a concurrent writable mmap or batched update racing map_freeze()/bpf_prog_load(). Consequence: map data used as constants by the verifier can later change, invalidating assumptions and enabling OOB access.

commit_msg:
Issue 747 (and others?):  Avoid OOB read when parsing multiple long lines

The mtree bidder needs to look several lines ahead
in the input.  It does this by extending the read-ahead
and parsing subsequent lines from the same growing buffer.
A bookkeeping error when extending the read-ahead would
sometimes lead it to significantly over-count the
size of the line being read.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tlen = get_line_size(*b, *avail, nl);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tlen = get_line_size(*b + len, *avail - len, nl);']}
description: The mtree bidder in libarchive 3.2.1 does not keep track of line sizes when extending the read-ahead, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (crash) via a crafted file, which triggers an invalid read in the (1) detect_form or (2) bid_entry function in libarchive/archive_read_support_format_mtree.c.

code_evidence: After extending the read-ahead, tested = len records bytes already scanned in the previous buffer, but the new get_line_size call re-parses from *b instead of *b + len, so it re-counts already-tested bytes and then adds tested again.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the bookkeeping error results in reading beyond the intended buffer bounds, matching the out-of-bounds read description; it is not an out-of-bounds write since only reads are performed.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the re-scan starts at the buffer base rather than advancing past the already-scanned prefix, so len is over-counted relative to *avail. Trigger: multi-line input where the read-ahead must grow. Consequence: the inflated len lets the while condition (len == *avail) fail prematurely and downstream callers index past the intended line/buffer, causing an out-of-bounds read and crash.

commit_msg:
xen: let alloc_xenballooned_pages() fail if not enough memory free

commit a1078e821b605813b63bf6bca414a85f804d5c66 upstream.

Instead of trying to allocate pages with GFP_USER in
add_ballooned_pages() check the available free memory via
si_mem_available(). GFP_USER is far less limiting memory exhaustion
than the test via si_mem_available().

This will avoid dom0 running out of memory due to excessive foreign
page mappings especially on ARM and on x86 in PVH mode, as those don't
have a pre-ballooned area which can be used for foreign mappings.

As the normal ballooning suffers from the same problem don't balloon
down more than si_mem_available() pages in one iteration. At the same
time limit the default maximum number of retries.

This is part of XSA-300.

Signed-off-by: Juergen Gross <jgross@suse.com>
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tif (si_mem_available() < nr_pages)', '\t\treturn -ENOMEM;', '']}
description: An issue was discovered in drivers/xen/balloon.c in the Linux kernel before 5.2.3, as used in Xen through 4.12.x, allowing guest OS users to cause a denial of service because of unrestricted resource consumption during the mapping of guest memory, aka CID-6ef36ab967c7.

code_evidence: add_ballooned_pages() calls decrease_reservation(nr_pages, GFP_USER) with the caller-supplied nr_pages and no check on available memory or an upper bound; failure is only detected after the attempt via the BP_DONE check.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-770 fits because the allocation of a reusable memory resource occurs without a size/throttling constraint before the allocation attempt. The upstream fix confirms this by adding a si_mem_available() < nr_pages guard returning -ENOMEM, i.e., limiting resource consumption. This is distinct from an out-of-bounds issue; the weakness is unbounded resource allocation leading to exhaustion.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function attempts to allocate/balloon nr_pages pages using GFP_USER without first verifying that enough free memory exists and without limiting nr_pages. A guest-controlled mapping request can drive repeated large allocations, exhausting host/dom0 memory and causing a denial of service. The root cause is the missing resource-availability check; the consequence is memory exhaustion (DoS), not a memory-safety violation.

description: GPAC version before commit 71460d72ec07df766dab0a4d52687529f3efcf0a (version v1.0.1 onwards) contains loop with unreachable exit condition ('infinite loop') vulnerability in ISOBMFF reader filter, isoffin_read.c. Function isoffin_process() can result in DoS by infinite loop. To exploit, the victim must open a specially crafted mp4 file.

code_evidence: When no sample was fetched (line 140), the code compares ch->sample_num against the track sample count. If sample_num >= sample_count (line 152) it sets GF_EOS; otherwise the else-if at 157-160 requires sample_num to reach sample_count (or a time condition) to set EOS at 166. The added guard (diff) sets GF_ISOM_INVALID_FILE when to_init && sample_num, preventing the initial-sample state from looping without ever satisfying the EOS condition.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-835 fits because the exit condition (sample_num reaching sample_count / EOS) is unreachable for the crafted state, producing an effectively infinite loop. This is not a buffer or integer error; the weakness is the non-terminating iteration itself.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the EOS exit condition depends on ch->sample_num advancing to the track sample count, but a crafted file can leave sample_num stuck below sample_count while sample fetching fails, so the reader repeatedly re-enters without reaching EOS. Trigger: opening a malicious mp4 that produces this inconsistent sample state. Consequence: the reader loops, consuming CPU (DoS).

commit_msg:
Fix multiple OOB bugs resulted from tx mtu in EATT

The tx mtu in EATT can be controlled by remote device. With malicious
mtu values, it is possible to trigger integer overflow and
OOB write at multiple places (see the bug below).

This fix enforces a max tx mtu in EATT.

Bug: 271335899
Test: manual
Ignore-AOSP-First: security
Tag: #security
(cherry picked from https://googleplex-android-review.googlesource.com/q/commit:ea76b7d99e6366e2043c5621eda630d559104d36)
Merged-In: Ia06c9a17f2daa5ce4c32cffa536777f47774cf31
Change-Id: Ia06c9a17f2daa5ce4c32cffa536777f47774cf31
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      channel->tx_mtu_ = p_cfg->mtu;'], 'added_lines': ['      channel->EattChannelSetTxMTU(p_cfg->mtu);']}
description: In eatt_l2cap_reconfig_completed of eatt_impl.h, there is a possible out of bounds write due to an integer overflow. This could lead to remote code execution with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

code_evidence: When is_local_cfg is false (remote reconfiguration), the remote-supplied p_cfg->mtu is stored directly into channel->tx_mtu_ without any upper-bound check. The commit message states tx mtu is remotely controlled and that malicious mtu values cause integer overflow and OOB write elsewhere.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the accepted MTU value enables an integer overflow in later calculations, consistent with the commit and description. The missing constraint in this function is the enabling assignment; the overflow itself occurs at the consuming code, not here.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function accepts an unvalidated remote MTU and assigns it to tx_mtu_, which is later used in size/offset arithmetic. Trigger: a peer sends an oversized MTU in the L2CAP reconfiguration response. Consequence: downstream integer overflow leading to out-of-bounds write, potentially remote code execution.

commit_msg:
firewire: net: guard against rx buffer overflows

The IP-over-1394 driver firewire-net lacked input validation when
handling incoming fragmented datagrams.  A maliciously formed fragment
with a respectively large datagram_offset would cause a memcpy past the
datagram buffer.

So, drop any packets carrying a fragment with offset + length larger
than datagram_size.

In addition, ensure that
  - GASP header, unfragmented encapsulation header, or fragment
    encapsulation header actually exists before we access it,
  - the encapsulated datagram or fragment is of nonzero size.

Reported-by: Eyal Itkin <eyal.itkin@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Eyal Itkin <eyal.itkin@gmail.com>
Fixes: CVE 2016-8633
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Stefan Richter <stefanr@s5r6.in-berlin.de>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tu16 source_node_id;', '\tu32 specifier_id;', '\tu32 ver;', '\tspecifier_id =    (be32_to_cpu(buf_ptr[0]) & 0xffff) << 8', '\t\t\t| (be32_to_cpu(buf_ptr[1]) & 0xff000000) >> 24;', '\tver = be32_to_cpu(buf_ptr[1]) & 0xffffff;', '\tsource_node_id = be32_to_cpu(buf_ptr[0]) >> 16;', '', '\tif (specifier_id == IANA_SPECIFIER_ID &&', '\t    (ver == RFC2734_SW_VERSION', '\t     || ver == RFC3146_SW_VERSION', '\t    )) {', '\t\tbuf_ptr += 2;', '\t\tlength -= IEEE1394_GASP_HDR_SIZE;', '\t\tfwnet_incoming_packet(dev, buf_ptr, length, source_node_id,', '\t}'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (length > IEEE1394_GASP_HDR_SIZE &&', '\t    gasp_specifier_id(buf_ptr) == IANA_SPECIFIER_ID &&', '\t    (gasp_version(buf_ptr) == RFC2734_SW_VERSION', '\t     || gasp_version(buf_ptr) == RFC3146_SW_VERSION', '\t    ))', '\t\tfwnet_incoming_packet(dev, buf_ptr + 2,', '\t\t\t\t      length - IEEE1394_GASP_HDR_SIZE,', '\t\t\t\t      gasp_source_id(buf_ptr),']}
description: drivers/firewire/net.c in the Linux kernel before 4.8.7, in certain unusual hardware configurations, allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via crafted fragmented packets.

code_evidence: length is read from the received header (line 17), but the code unconditionally dereferences buf_ptr[0] and buf_ptr[1] (lines 24-27) without first verifying that the received datagram is at least IEEE1394_GASP_HDR_SIZE bytes.

After matching the GASP specifier/version, the code advances buf_ptr by two words and subtracts the header size from length (lines 34-35), then passes buf_ptr and length to fwnet_incoming_packet without checking that length was large enough to contain the header or that offset+length stays within datagram_size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs reads and forwards a memcpy using a length derived from untrusted input without bounding it against the buffer's intended size, so operations fall outside the memory buffer boundary, matching CWE-119. The specific missing length check is an out-of-bounds read/write rather than, e.g., an integer overflow.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: missing input validation of the received datagram length before header parsing and before forwarding the fragment payload. Trigger: a maliciously crafted broadcast datagram whose declared length is smaller than the GASP header or whose fragment offset+length exceeds datagram_size. Consequence: out-of-bounds read of the header words and a memcpy past the datagram buffer downstream, enabling memory corruption or code execution.

commit_msg:
udp: crash fix when receiving multi-packet uploads

multi-packet sets aren't supported in UDP. It was trying to write an
error message in response, but no mc_resp object was initialized at the
time, leading to a null reference crash.

Instead drop the packet quietly since that's a pretty fatal bug anyway
and keeps the parser simplified.

For credits see accompanying release notes.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            out_string(c, "SERVER_ERROR multi-packet request not supported");'], 'added_lines': []}
description: memcached 1.6.7 allows a Denial of Service via multi-packet uploads in UDP.

code_evidence: After recvfrom, the code checks the UDP header fields buf[4]/buf[5] to detect multi-packet requests. On that condition it calls out_string(c, ...) to emit an error response and returns READ_NO_DATA_RECEIVED without validating that the connection has an initialized response object (mc_resp).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function lets a remote input trigger a fatal crash, consuming availability of the service; this fits CWE-400's availability/DoS scope. It is not a memory-safety write (CWE-476 is the underlying null dereference), but the supported consequence here is uncontrolled crash-based denial of service.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the multi-packet branch unconditionally invokes out_string on a UDP connection whose response object is not initialized. Trigger: a remote client sends a UDP request with header bytes buf[4]!=0 or buf[5]!=1 (multi-packet). Consequence: null-reference crash/abort, allowing remote denial of service; the missing constraint is the lack of a validity check before writing the error response.

commit_msg:
When running concurrent iptables rules replacement with data, the per CPU
sequence count is checked after the assignment of the new information.
The sequence count is used to synchronize with the packet path without the
use of any explicit locking. If there are any packets in the packet path using
the table information, the sequence count is incremented to an odd value and
is incremented to an even after the packet process completion.

The new table value assignment is followed by a write memory barrier so every
CPU should see the latest value. If the packet path has started with the old
table information, the sequence counter will be odd and the iptables
replacement will wait till the sequence count is even prior to freeing the
old table info.

However, this assumes that the new table information assignment and the memory
barrier is actually executed prior to the counter check in the replacement
thread. If CPU decides to execute the assignment later as there is no user of
the table information prior to the sequence check, the packet path in another
CPU may use the old table information. The replacement thread would then free
the table information under it leading to a use after free in the packet
processing context-

Unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at virtual
address 000000000000008e
pc : ip6t_do_table+0x5d0/0x89c
lr : ip6t_do_table+0x5b8/0x89c
ip6t_do_table+0x5d0/0x89c
ip6table_filter_hook+0x24/0x30
nf_hook_slow+0x84/0x120
ip6_input+0x74/0xe0
ip6_rcv_finish+0x7c/0x128
ipv6_rcv+0xac/0xe4
__netif_receive_skb+0x84/0x17c
process_backlog+0x15c/0x1b8
napi_poll+0x88/0x284
net_rx_action+0xbc/0x23c
__do_softirq+0x20c/0x48c

This could be fixed by forcing instruction order after the new table
information assignment or by switching to RCU for the synchronization.

Fixes: 80055dab5de0 ("netfilter: x_tables: make xt_replace_table wait until old rules are not used anymore")
Reported-by: Sean Tranchetti <stranche@codeaurora.org>
Reported-by: kernel test robot <lkp@intel.com>
Suggested-by: Florian Westphal <fw@strlen.de>
Signed-off-by: Subash Abhinov Kasiviswanathan <subashab@codeaurora.org>
Signed-off-by: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tconst struct xt_table_info *private = table->private;'], 'added_lines': ['\tconst struct xt_table_info *private = xt_table_get_private_protected(table);']}
description: An issue was discovered in netfilter in the Linux kernel before 5.10. There can be a use-after-free in the packet processing context, because the per-CPU sequence count is mishandled during concurrent iptables rules replacement. This could be exploited with the CAP_NET_ADMIN capability in an unprivileged namespace. NOTE: cc00bca was reverted in 5.12.

code_evidence: Line 6 caches table->private into a local pointer without any synchronization or protection, and line 12 allocates counters, then lines 17-19 dereference private->entries to copy entries to user space. The pointer can be freed by a concurrent xt_replace_table on another CPU before it is dereferenced here.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences table->private after a concurrent replacement can free it, matching CWE-416's reuse of freed memory. This is a race-induced use-after-free, distinct from a simple null-pointer or out-of-bounds read.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the table private pointer is read and used later without acquiring protection against concurrent rules replacement. Trigger: a CAP_NET_ADMIN thread replaces the table while compat_copy_entries_to_user iterates private->entries, freeing the old table info. Consequence: the copy loop dereferences freed memory, causing a use-after-free (crash or memory disclosure).

This affects the dce120_create_resource_pool() function in drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/dce120/dce120_resource.c, the dce110_create_resource_pool() function in drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/dce110/dce110_resource.c, the dce100_create_resource_pool() function in drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/dce100/dce100_resource.c, the dcn10_create_resource_pool() function in drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/dcn10/dcn10_resource.c, and the dce112_create_resource_pool() function in drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/dce112/dce112_resource.c, aka CID-104c307147ad.

code_evidence: Line 5-6 allocates 'pool' via kzalloc and stores it in a local pointer. Lines 9-10: if construct() succeeds, the pool is returned and ownership transfers to the caller. Otherwise the function falls through to BREAK_TO_DEBUGGER() at line 11 and returns NULL at line 12 without freeing 'pool', so the only reference is lost.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-401 fits because allocated memory is neither released nor returned on the failure branch, leaving it unavailable for reuse. This is a missing-release error-path leak, not a use-after-free or double-free, since the pointer is simply abandoned.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the error path after a failed construct() returns NULL without releasing the kzalloc'd pool. Trigger: construct() returning failure (e.g., allocation failure inside construct). Consequence: the allocated pool becomes unreachable, leaking memory on each failed pool creation and enabling memory-consumption DoS.

commit_msg: Issue #1683: Avoid an edge case when handling unexpectedly formatted input text from client, caused by quote/backslash semantics, by skipping those semantics.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  wrd = pr_str_get_word(&ptr, str_flags);', '  cmd->arg = arg;', '', '  if (have_crnul) {'], 'added_lines': ['  /* By default, pr_str_get_word will handle quotes and backslashes for', '   * escaping characters.  This can produce words which are shorter, use', '   * fewer bytes than the corresponding input buffer.', '   *', '   * In this particular situation, we use the length of this initial word', '   * for determining the length of the remaining buffer bytes, assumed to', '   * contain the FTP command arguments.  If this initial word is thus', '   * unexpectedly "shorter", due to nonconformant FTP text, it can lead', '   * the subsequent buffer scan, looking for CRNUL sequencees, to access', '   * unexpected memory addresses (Issue #1683).', '   *', '   * Thus for this particular situation, we tell the function to ignore/skip', '   * such quote/backslash semantics, and treat them as any other character', '   * using the IGNORE_QUOTES flag.', '   */', '', '  wrd = pr_str_get_word(&ptr, str_flags|PR_STR_FL_IGNORE_QUOTES);', '', '  /* Note that this first word is the FTP command.  This is why we make', '   * use of the ptr buffer, which advances through the input buffer as', '   * we read words from the buffer.', '   */', '  /* Remember that ptr here is advanced past the first word. */', '', '  if (have_crnul == TRUE) {', '  cmd->arg = arg;', '', '  /* Now we can read the remamining words, as command arguments, from the', '   * input buffer.', '   */']}
description: make_ftp_cmd in main.c in ProFTPD before 1.3.8a has a one-byte out-of-bounds read, and daemon crash, because of mishandling of quote/backslash semantics.

code_evidence: Line 16 parses the first word with str_flags, which by default processes quote/backslash escapes, so wrd can be shorter than its raw source span and ptr advances past fewer bytes. Line 32 computes arg_len as buflen minus strlen(wrd), and line 33 allocates arg from that. The loop at lines 34-43 then indexes ptr[i] up to arg_len-1 (line 37), reading beyond the remaining valid buffer region when wrd was shortened.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the loop reads ptr[i] beyond the intended buffer end due to a miscalculated length, directly matching out-of-bounds read. This is not a write overflow (CWE-787) since the excess access is a read used in the CRNUL check, and the allocation itself is merely oversized.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The root cause is deriving the remaining-buffer length from the escape-processed word length rather than the consumed input span. With client-supplied text containing quotes/backslashes, strlen(wrd) undercounts, arg_len overcounts, and ptr[i] at lines 37-38 reads past the end of the buffer, causing an out-of-bounds read and possible daemon crash.

commit_msg:
ahci: Update byte count after DMA completion

Currently, DMA read/write operations neglect to update
the byte count after a successful transfer like ATAPI
DMA read or PIO read/write operations do.

We correct this oversight by adding another callback into
the IDEDMAOps structure. The commit callback is called
whenever we are cleaning up a scatter-gather list.
AHCI can register this callback in order to update post-
transfer information such as byte count updates.

We use this callback in AHCI to consolidate where we delete
the SGlist as generated from the PRDT, as well as update the
byte count after the transfer is complete.

The QEMUSGList structure has an init flag added to it in order
to make qemu_sglist_destroy a nop if it is called when
there is no sglist, which simplifies cleanup and error paths.

This patch fixes several AHCI problems, notably Non-NCQ modes
of operation for Windows 7 as well as Hibernate support for Windows 7.

Reviewed-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>

commit_msg:
Q.931: fix use-after-free (write) of "q931_pi"

The dissect_q931_number_ie (and indirectly dissect_q931_cause_ie_unsafe)
write to the "q931_pi" structure which seems private to the q931
dissector, but can in fact be called through other dissectors (isup) as
well. Normally this structure is initialized in "dissect_q931_pdu" and
invalidated at the end of the function, but a malformed packet can
prevent the cleanup. In the next packet, a different dissector can thus
trigger a use-after-free via "dissect_q931_number_ie".

Rename "dissect_q931_cause_ie_unsafe" since "unsafe" meant that external
dissectors could not call it directly (see commit a83a87e9ca).

Based on commit 197ceddab109, it seems that the intended purpose of the
structure is to provide information to the VoIP Calls dialog, but it
would only be used when called through dissect_q931_pdu. Dissectors like
isup have their own routines to provide call information, but as a
side-effect of code sharing the problematic code path was reached.

commit_msg:
Fix multiple heap-based buffer overflows in CmtkLoader::load()

Changes in src/mtk.cpp for loading files:
* Fail early if the (decompressed) size is too small to hold
  mtkdata minus patterns. That avoids attempts to copy data
  from beyond allocated memory.
* In the data decompression section, there are multiple cases
  where the code actually has checks for available space before
  copying data, but the size of the copy is increased after
  the check, so a buffer overflow is still possible (issue #90).
  Fix that by moving the check after the size computation,
  and also check for a valid source offset where applicable.
* Also add several checks whether source data is exhausted
  during decompession, so
* When copying the patterns, don't copy more data than the
  "pattern" array can hold.

In src/mtk.h, method getinstrument(), check for valid instrument
number to avoid accessing the array with an invalid index.

This commit fixes CVE-2019-14734.

Fixes: https://github.com/adplug/adplug/issues/90

commit_msg:
Jann Horn reported a problem with commit eb1231f73c4d ("selinux:
clarify task subjective and objective credentials") where some LSM
hooks were attempting to access the subjective credentials of a task
other than the current task.  Generally speaking, it is not safe to
access another task's subjective credentials and doing so can cause
a number of problems.

Further, while looking into the problem, I realized that Smack was
suffering from a similar problem brought about by a similar commit
1fb057dcde11 ("smack: differentiate between subjective and objective
task credentials").

This patch addresses this problem by restoring the use of the task's
objective credentials in those cases where the task is other than the
current executing task.  Not only does this resolve the problem
reported by Jann, it is arguably the correct thing to do in these
cases.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: eb1231f73c4d ("selinux: clarify task subjective and objective credentials")
Fixes: 1fb057dcde11 ("smack: differentiate between subjective and objective task credentials")
Reported-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Acked-by: Eric W. Biederman <ebiederm@xmission.com>
Acked-by: Casey Schaufler <casey@schaufler-ca.com>
Signed-off-by: Paul Moore <paul@paul-moore.com>

description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel before 5.14.8. A use-after-free in selinux_ptrace_traceme (aka the SELinux handler for PTRACE_TRACEME) could be used by local attackers to cause memory corruption and escalate privileges, aka CID-a3727a8bac0a. This occurs because of an attempt to access the subjective credentials of another task.

commit_msg:
PdfParserObject: Store the PdfEncrypt instance as a shared_ptr

This should avoid heap-use-after-free if PdfMemDocument::SetEncrypt is used
before the delay load of the object. Should fix #70
Fix suggested by Mark Rogers
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['                            obj->SetEncrypt(m_Encrypt.get());'], 'added_lines': ['                            obj->SetEncrypt(m_Encrypt);']}
description: Podofo v0.10.0 was discovered to contain a heap-use-after-free via the component PoDoFo::PdfEncrypt::IsMetadataEncrypted().

code_evidence: A PdfParserObject is heap-allocated at line 23 into a unique_ptr, then line 26 passes m_Encrypt.get()—a raw pointer to the PdfEncrypt owned elsewhere—into obj->SetEncrypt. The object stores this raw pointer, so if PdfMemDocument::SetEncrypt replaces/frees the PdfEncrypt after this, later delayed-load use of the stored pointer (e.g. IsMetadataEncrypted) dereferences freed memory.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the function stores a dangling raw pointer that is later reused after the referenced PdfEncrypt is freed; the patch's switch to a shared_ptr confirms the lifetime defect. It is not merely a null dereference, since the memory was valid then freed.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the parser object retains a non-owning raw pointer from m_Encrypt.get() rather than sharing ownership. Trigger: SetEncrypt is called on the document before the delayed load, freeing the PdfEncrypt while the stored pointer remains. Consequence: heap-use-after-free when the parser object later uses the encrypt pointer, giving read/crash or potential memory corruption.

commit_msg:
Default initialize fixed point Eigen types.

In certain cases, tensors are filled with default values of the type. But, for these fixed point types, these values were uninitialized. Thus, we would have uninitialized memory access bugs, some of which were caught by MSAN.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 344101137
Change-Id: I14555fda74dca3b5f1582da9008901937e3f14e2
func:
[QUInt8]

0001 | QUInt8() {}
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['QUInt8() {}'], 'added_lines': ['QUInt8() : value(0) {}']}
description: In affected versions of TensorFlow under certain cases a saved model can trigger use of uninitialized values during code execution. This is caused by having tensor buffers be filled with the default value of the type but forgetting to default initialize the quantized floating point types in Eigen. This is fixed in versions 1.15.5, 2.0.4, 2.1.3, 2.2.2, 2.3.2, and 2.4.0.

code_evidence: The only line is the default constructor `QUInt8() {}`, which constructs a fixed-point quantized type without initializing its member `value`. The patched form adds `: value(0)`, confirming the original body leaves the underlying storage uninitialized.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-908 covers using/accessing a resource that was never initialized; here the resource is the QUInt8 `value` member left unset by the empty constructor and later consumed. This is the initialization defect itself, not a separate out-of-bounds or type-confusion weakness.

evidence_lines.code: QUInt8() {}

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the default constructor performs no member initialization, so any QUInt8 created by default holds indeterminate storage. Trigger: code paths that fill tensors with default-constructed values (e.g., a loaded saved model) then read those values. Consequence: use of uninitialized memory, causing nondeterministic results or invalid memory reads such as those caught by MSAN.

commit_msg:
x509: excessive resource use verifying policy constraints

A security vulnerability has been identified in all supported versions
of OpenSSL related to the verification of X.509 certificate chains
that include policy constraints.  Attackers may be able to exploit this
vulnerability by creating a malicious certificate chain that triggers
exponential use of computational resources, leading to a denial-of-service
(DoS) attack on affected systems.

Fixes CVE-2023-0464

Reviewed-by: Tomas Mraz <tomas@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Shane Lontis <shane.lontis@oracle.com>
(Merged from https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/20570)

description: A vulnerability was found in ImageMagick. This security flaw ouccers as an undefined behaviors of casting double to size_t in svg, mvg and other coders (recurring bugs of CVE-2022-32546).

code_evidence: Line 43 converts the double result of floor(metrics->width+draw_info->stroke_width+0.5) directly to size_t; line 44 then compares this width against image->columns. No range check precedes the cast, so an out-of-range or negative double yields an implementation-defined/undefined size_t value used in the width comparison.

Trigger: metrics->width or stroke_width produces a value outside size_t range (or negative). The resulting width is then used at line 44 to decide line splitting, so the comparison can be altered, changing caption layout/loop behavior; the flaw is the missing bound before conversion, not the comparison itself.

commit_msg:
Don't overflow the output length in EVP_CipherUpdate calls

CVE-2021-23840

Reviewed-by: Paul Dale <pauli@openssl.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '            /*', "             * Once we've processed the first j bytes from in, the amount of", '             * data left that is a multiple of the block length is:', '             * (inl - j) & ~(bl - 1)', '             * We must ensure that this amount of data, plus the one block that', '             * we process from ctx->buf does not exceed INT_MAX', '             */', '            if (((inl - j) & ~(bl - 1)) > INT_MAX - bl) {', '                EVPerr(EVP_F_EVP_ENCRYPTDECRYPTUPDATE,', '                       EVP_R_OUTPUT_WOULD_OVERFLOW);', '                return 0;', '            }']}
description: Calls to EVP_CipherUpdate, EVP_EncryptUpdate and EVP_DecryptUpdate may overflow the output length argument in some cases where the input length is close to the maximum permissable length for an integer on the platform. In such cases the return value from the function call will be 1 (indicating success), but the output length value will be negative. This could cause applications to behave incorrectly or crash. OpenSSL versions 1.1.1i and below are affected by this issue. Users of these versions should upgrade to OpenSSL 1.1.1j. OpenSSL versions 1.0.2x and below are affected by this issue. However OpenSSL 1.0.2 is out of support and no longer receiving public updates. Premium support customers of OpenSSL 1.0.2 should upgrade to 1.0.2y. Other users should upgrade to 1.1.1j. Fixed in OpenSSL 1.1.1j (Affected 1.1.1-1.1.1i). Fixed in OpenSSL 1.0.2y (Affected 1.0.2-1.0.2x).

code_evidence: When ctx->buf_len is nonzero and the new input fills the partial block, j = bl - i bytes are copied from in into ctx->buf and inl is decremented by j. The function then processes the remaining inl bytes and accumulates *outl (set to bl at line 56 and later increased by inl at line 65). No bound check ensures that bl plus the processed remainder stays within INT_MAX, so for inl near INT_MAX the output length computation can overflow.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This is CWE-190: an integer calculation on the output length can exceed INT_MAX and wrap to a negative number, exactly the wraparound described by the target. It is not a simple buffer overflow, since the flaw lies in the size arithmetic rather than a direct out-of-bounds copy.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the output-length accumulation (*outl = bl, then *outl += inl) is performed without verifying that bl plus the block-aligned remainder fits in an int. Trigger: a caller passes an input length close to INT_MAX so that the buffered-block path is taken. Consequence: *outl wraps to a negative value while the function returns 1, causing callers to mis-handle the output length and potentially crash or corrupt memory.

commit_msg: Fix #6010: Check length in read_icon_info
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (Stream_GetRemainingLength(s) < iconInfo->cbBitsMask + iconInfo->cbBitsColor)', '\t\treturn FALSE;', ''], 'added_lines': ['\tif (Stream_GetRemainingLength(s) < iconInfo->cbBitsMask)', '\t\treturn FALSE;', '\t{', '\t\tif (Stream_GetRemainingLength(s) < iconInfo->cbColorTable)', '\t\t\treturn FALSE;', '\t}', '\tif (Stream_GetRemainingLength(s) < iconInfo->cbBitsColor)', '\t\treturn FALSE;']}
description: In FreeRDP greater than 1.1 and before 2.0.0, there is an out-of-bounds read in update_read_icon_info. It allows reading a attacker-defined amount of client memory (32bit unsigned -> 4GB) to an intermediate buffer. This can be used to crash the client or store information for later retrieval. This has been patched in 2.0.0.

code_evidence: The function verifies only 4 bytes remain before reading cbBitsMask and cbBitsColor, then checks remaining length against the sum cbBitsMask + cbBitsColor. That combined check is a single constraint covering both fields together.
bitsMask is reallocated to cbBitsMask bytes; if the combined check passed, Stream_Read consumes cbBitsMask bytes.
Later, colorTable is read for cbColorTable bytes with no remaining-length check before Stream_Read.
bitsColor is read for cbBitsColor bytes after only the earlier combined check, which has already been consumed by the bitsMask read.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe operation is a read of stream memory beyond its valid length, matching CWE-125. CWE-787 (out-of-bounds write) does not fit because the destination buffers are correctly sized via realloc; the missing constraint causes reading, not writing, beyond bounds.

evidence_lines.code:
iconInfo->bitsMask = newBitMask;
Stream_Read(s, iconInfo->bitsMask, iconInfo->cbBitsMask);

if (iconInfo->colorTable)
Stream_Read(s, iconInfo->colorTable, iconInfo->cbColorTable);

iconInfo->bitsColor = newBitMask;
Stream_Read(s, iconInfo->bitsColor, iconInfo->cbBitsColor);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the remaining-length validation is performed once against the sum of cbBitsMask and cbBitsColor before either buffer is read, so it does not constrain each individual read to the data actually left in the stream. Trigger: attacker-controlled cbColorTable/cbBitsColor values in the icon-info message. Consequence: Stream_Read copies past the end of the stream buffer, yielding an out-of-bounds read (up to a 32-bit length) that can leak client memory or crash the client.

commit_msg:
net/vmxnet3: Refine l2 header validation

Validation of l2 header length assumed minimal packet size as
eth_header + 2 * vlan_header regardless of the actual protocol.

This caused crash for valid non-IP packets shorter than 22 bytes, as
'tx_pkt->packet_type' hasn't been assigned for such packets, and
'vmxnet3_on_tx_done_update_stats()' expects it to be properly set.

Refine header length validation in 'vmxnet_tx_pkt_parse_headers'.
Check its return value during packet processing flow.

As a side effect, in case IPv4 and IPv6 header validation failure,
corrupt packets will be dropped.

Signed-off-by: Dana Rubin <dana.rubin@ravellosystems.com>
Signed-off-by: Shmulik Ladkani <shmulik.ladkani@ravellosystems.com>
Signed-off-by: Jason Wang <jasowang@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            if (!s->skip_current_tx_pkt) {', '                vmxnet_tx_pkt_parse(s->tx_pkt);', ''], 'added_lines': ['            if (!s->skip_current_tx_pkt && vmxnet_tx_pkt_parse(s->tx_pkt)) {']}
description: QEMU (aka Quick Emulator) built with a VMWARE VMXNET3 paravirtual NIC emulator support is vulnerable to crash issue. It occurs when a guest sends a Layer-2 packet smaller than 22 bytes. A privileged (CAP_SYS_RAWIO) guest user could use this flaw to crash the QEMU process instance resulting in DoS.

code_evidence: At end-of-packet, the return value of vmxnet_tx_pkt_parse(s->tx_pkt) is ignored; the code unconditionally proceeds to VLAN setup and vmxnet3_send_packet on the parsed packet.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function accepts guest-provided packet data without enforcing that the parse/validation succeeded before processing, matching CWE-20 improper input validation. The consequence (crash) is downstream; the weakness is the unchecked validation result, not the crash itself.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the parse routine's success/failure result is discarded, so a guest-supplied Layer-2 packet whose headers fail validation is still forwarded as if valid. Trigger: a guest sends a short (<22 byte) non-IP L2 packet. The missing check lets downstream code (vmxnet3_on_tx_done_update_stats) use an unset packet_type, causing a crash and QEMU DoS.

commit_msg:
Fix heap-buffer-overflow in getString

getString is allocating a 4-bytes buffer to store an 'R' and an
8-bit number.

t=malloc(4); /* Rdd */
sprintf(t,"R%d", act->p.RegisterNumber );
return t;

Since up to three digits can be required to store the 8-bit
number, the buffer has to be 5 bytes long.

In this commit we also fix the PUSH_DOUBLE case by dynamically
computing the required buffer size.

This commit fixes #116 (CVE-2018-7867).
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\tt=malloc(4); /* Rdd */', '\t\tt=malloc(10); /* big enough? */', '\t\tsprintf(t,"%g", act->p.Double );'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\tt=malloc(5); /* Rddd */', '\t{', '\t\tchar length_finder[1];', '\t\tint needed_length = snprintf(length_finder, 1, "%g", act->p.Double) + 1;', '\t\tif (needed_length <= 0)', '\t\t{', '\t\t        SWF_warn("WARNING: could not evaluate size of buffer (memory issue ?).\\n");', '\t\t        break;', '\t\t}', '', '\t\tt = malloc(needed_length);', '\t\tsprintf(t, "%g", act->p.Double );', '\t}']}
description: There is a heap-based buffer overflow in the getString function of util/decompile.c in libming 0.4.8 during a RegisterNumber sprintf. A Crafted input will lead to a denial of service attack.

code_evidence: PUSH_REGISTER branch allocates a fixed 4-byte heap buffer at [34], then at [35] sprintf writes "R" plus the decimal RegisterNumber into it.
PUSH_DOUBLE branch allocates a fixed 10-byte buffer at [44] and writes the formatted double at [45], assuming the representation fits.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes formatted data beyond the end of an allocated heap buffer, which is exactly an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). The root cause is an incorrect allocation-size constraint, not a read overrun or an integer overflow in itself.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The heap buffers are sized from a fixed assumption rather than the actual formatted output length. An 8-bit RegisterNumber can require up to three digits, so "R" plus digits plus the NUL terminator exceeds 4 bytes and sprintf writes past the allocation; similarly a double representation can exceed 10 bytes. The trigger is a crafted input selecting these push-param types, and the supported consequence is heap corruption/overflow leading to crash or denial of service.

commit_msg:
Handle close_notify as standard writeErr in AsyncSSLSocket.

Summary: Fixes CVE-2019-11934

Reviewed By: mingtaoy

Differential Revision: D18020613

fbshipit-source-id: db82bb250e53f0d225f1280bd67bc74abd417836
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      auto writeResult = interpretSSLError(int(bytes), error);', '      if (writeResult.writeReturn < 0) {', '        return writeResult;', '      } // else fall through to below to correctly record totalWritten'], 'added_lines': ['      return interpretSSLError(int(bytes), error);']}
description: Improper handling of close_notify alerts can result in an out-of-bounds read in AsyncSSLSocket. This issue affects folly prior to v2019.11.04.00.

code_evidence: After eorAwareSSLWrite returns a non-positive byte count, the code inspects SSL_get_error. Only SSL_ERROR_WANT_WRITE is handled by returning early [89,90,91]; other errors reach interpretSSLError and, in the pre-patch form, a negative writeReturn is returned, but a non-negative result falls through [93,94,95,96] to totalWritten += bytes at [97], adding a negative/zero bytes value and continuing the loop over vec with corrupted accounting.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the failure to stop on the SSL error corrupts write accounting and index advancement over the caller-supplied iovec, leading to reads past the intended buffer. This is an out-of-bounds read, not merely an error-handling defect, since the corrupted indices drive subsequent memory access.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: an SSL error (e.g. close_notify/SSL_ERROR_ZERO_RETURN) is not treated as a terminal write error, so control falls through with a negative bytes value into the accounting at line 97 and the subsequent buffer-index arithmetic (lines 98-108). Trigger: the peer sends a close_notify alert during a write. Consequence: totalWritten and iov index accounting become inconsistent, enabling out-of-bounds reads of the iovec/buffer data and potential memory disclosure or crash.

commit_msg: Add some guards and sanity checks to MTM loader (#198)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tuint16_t ntrk, nchan, nord, npat, nsmp;', '\t\tfor (smp = 1; smp <= nsmp; smp++) {'], 'added_lines': ['\tint16_t ntrk, nchan, nord, npat, nsmp; // signed so that EOF is -1', '\trows = MIN(rows, 64);', '\t\tif (n > MAX_SAMPLES) {', '\t\t\tslurp_seek(fp, 37, SEEK_CUR);', '\t\t\tcontinue;', '\t\t}', '', '\t\tfor (smp = 1; smp <= nsmp && smp <= MAX_SAMPLES; smp++) {']}
description: fmt_mtm_load_song in fmt/mtm.c in Schism Tracker 20190722 has a heap-based buffer overflow.

code_evidence: nsmp is read from the file as an 8-bit count (line 25) and used directly as the loop bound at line 38, where each iteration advances sample into song->samples and writes sample->name via strcpy (line 42) plus fields at lines 55 and 65-68; no bound against MAX_SAMPLES constrains this loop.

The sample-data loop at line 110 likewise iterates smp <= nsmp without a MAX_SAMPLES guard, indexing song->samples[smp] at lines 112 and 114 and passing song->samples + smp to csf_read_sample at line 114.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes past the end of the intended samples buffer because the loop bounds are not constrained by MAX_SAMPLES, matching CWE-787's out-of-bounds write. The added guards in the patch confirm the fix; this is a write beyond the buffer, not merely a read overrun.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the attacker-controlled sample count nsmp is used as a loop bound for writes into the fixed-size song->samples array without checking MAX_SAMPLES. A crafted MTM with nsmp exceeding the array capacity causes strcpy and field assignments, and later csf_read_sample, to write past the end of the heap-allocated samples buffer, corrupting memory.

commit_msg: fixed #2138
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t\t\tif (ctx->b64_buffer_size<2*s_size) {', '\t\t\t\t\t\tctx->b64_buffer_size = 2 * s_size;'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t\t\tif (ctx->b64_buffer_size < 2*s_size + 3) {', '\t\t\t\t\t\tctx->b64_buffer_size = 2 * s_size + 3;']}
description: GPAC 2.0 allows a heap-based buffer overflow in gf_base64_encode. It can be triggered via MP4Box.

code_evidence: The buffer is sized to 2*s_size (line 112) and reallocated (113), then gf_base64_encode writes into ctx->b64_buffer bounded by ctx->b64_buffer_size (115), and the terminator is stored at ctx->b64_buffer[d_size] (116). Base64 of s_size bytes requires 4*ceil(s_size/3) bytes plus a NUL, so 2*s_size is too small for small s_size and the write at index d_size can exceed the allocation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This is a direct out-of-bounds write: a too-small heap allocation is used as the destination for encoded data and a NUL terminator, writing beyond the intended buffer. It is not merely an integer or logic flaw; the consequence is memory corruption from the unchecked size, matching CWE-787.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The allocation constraint (2*s_size) underestimates the encoded length returned by gf_base64_encode; when a subsample of a crafted size is processed, the encoder writes past the heap buffer and the trailing NUL write at line 116 lands out of bounds, corrupting heap memory and potentially enabling code execution or a crash.

commit_msg:
Skip bound chain when flushing table rules, the rule that owns this
chain releases these objects.

Otherwise, the following warning is triggered:

  WARNING: CPU: 2 PID: 1217 at net/netfilter/nf_tables_api.c:2013 nf_tables_chain_destroy+0x1f7/0x210 [nf_tables]
  CPU: 2 PID: 1217 Comm: chain-flush Not tainted 6.1.39 #1
  RIP: 0010:nf_tables_chain_destroy+0x1f7/0x210 [nf_tables]

Fixes: d0e2c7de92c7 ("netfilter: nf_tables: add NFT_CHAIN_BINDING")
Reported-by: Kevin Rich <kevinrich1337@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>
Signed-off-by: Florian Westphal <fw@strlen.de>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\tif (nft_chain_is_bound(chain))', '\t\t\t\tcontinue;']}
description:
A use-after-free vulnerability in the Linux kernel's netfilter: nf_tables component can be exploited to achieve local privilege escalation.

When nf_tables_delrule() is flushing table rules, it is not checked whether the chain is bound and the chain's owner rule can also release the objects in certain circumstances.

We recommend upgrading past commit 6eaf41e87a223ae6f8e7a28d6e78384ad7e407f8.

code_evidence: In the no-chain branch, the loop iterates over every chain in the table, skipping only inactive chains via nft_is_active_next; it does not check nft_chain_is_bound(chain). For each such chain it sets ctx.chain and calls nft_delrule_by_chain(&ctx), which deletes/flushes that chain's rules. A bound chain is owned by a rule, so flushing its rules here allows the owner rule to release the same objects.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing nft_chain_is_bound check permits the same bound-chain objects to be freed through two paths, leaving a dangling reference that is later used, matching CWE-416. The added check prevents this double-release/use-after-free, not a separate weakness type.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the table-wide flush loop lacks a bound-chain exclusion, so nft_delrule_by_chain is invoked on chains owned by a rule. When the owner rule later releases those bound objects, the earlier flush path has already freed them, and subsequent access of the chain/rules yields a use-after-free (as the chain-destroy warning indicates).

commit_msg:
Fixed bug #72227: imagescale out-of-bounds read

Ported from https://github.com/libgd/libgd/commit/4f65a3e4eedaffa1efcf9ee1eb08f0b504fbc31a
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        res->ContribRow[u].Left = iLeft;', '        res->ContribRow[u].Right = iRight;', ''], 'added_lines': ['', '        res->ContribRow[u].Left = iLeft;', '        res->ContribRow[u].Right = iRight;']}
description: gd_interpolation.c in the GD Graphics Library (aka libgd) before 2.1.1, as used in PHP before 5.5.36, 5.6.x before 5.6.22, and 7.x before 7.0.7, allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted image that is mishandled by the imagescale function.

code_evidence: Lines 23-24 store iLeft/iRight into res->ContribRow[u] before the spill-off clamp at lines 25-31 adjusts iLeft/iRight; lines 32-33 then iterate iSrc from the adjusted iLeft while writing Weights[iSrc-iLeft], so the stored Left/Right no longer match the actual weight window.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect yields reads beyond the intended buffer bounds because stored indices are inconsistent with the allocated weight window, matching CWE-125. It is not a write overflow: the loop writes within the adjusted window, but the stale bounds drive out-of-range reads.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the contribution row's Left/Right bounds are recorded before the filter window is clamped to windows_size. When iRight-iLeft+1 exceeds windows_size, iLeft or iRight is shifted, but the persisted bounds remain stale. Downstream consumers using the saved Left/Right while indexing the allocated Weights array read outside the intended buffer, causing an out-of-bounds read and possible crash/DoS.

commit_msg:
[libpng16] Fix the calculation of row_factor in png_check_chunk_length

(Bug report by Thuan Pham, SourceForge issue #278)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['         (png_ptr->width * png_ptr->channels * (png_ptr->bit_depth > 8? 2: 1)', '          + 1 + (png_ptr->interlaced? 6: 0));', '         idat_limit=PNG_UINT_31_MAX;'], 'added_lines': ['         (size_t)png_ptr->width', '         * (size_t)png_ptr->channels', '         * (png_ptr->bit_depth > 8? 2: 1)', '         + 1', '         + (png_ptr->interlaced? 6: 0);', '         idat_limit = PNG_UINT_31_MAX;']}
description: In libpng 1.6.34, a wrong calculation of row_factor in the png_check_chunk_length function (pngrutil.c) may trigger an integer overflow and resultant divide-by-zero while processing a crafted PNG file, leading to a denial of service.

code_evidence: row_factor is computed as png_ptr->width * png_ptr->channels * (bit_depth>8?2:1) + 1 + (interlaced?6:0); width and channels are png_uint_32 values, so the multiplication is performed in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic before assignment to the size_t row_factor, allowing the product to wrap.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the pre-patch expression overflows/wraps in the narrower unsigned type before widening, and the wrapped result is used in size/limit logic. This is integer wraparound, not a simple truncation; the fix widens operands with (size_t) casts.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the width*channels*bytes-per-pixel product is evaluated in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic, so a crafted PNG with large width/channels wraps row_factor to a small value. Trigger: an attacker-supplied PNG header. Consequence: the later division idat_limit/row_factor can divide by zero (or the limit check is defeated), causing a denial of service.

commit_msg:
fix a bunch of vsprintf -> vsnprintf

closes #1203
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tvsprintf(line, format, args);'], 'added_lines': ['\tvsnprintf(line, 2000, format, args);']}
description: GPAC 0.7.1 has a buffer overflow issue in gf_import_message() in media_import.c.

code_evidence: line[2000] is the fixed-size stack destination; format and args are consumed by vsprintf, which performs no bound on output length. A long formatted message from the caller writes past line[2000], corrupting adjacent stack memory before strlen reads it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the write past the end of line[] is itself the out-of-bounds write. CWE-120 (classic buffer overflow) is the related unbounded-copy weakness, but the target here is the resulting write beyond the buffer boundary.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: unbounded vsprintf into a 2000-byte stack buffer. Trigger: a caller-controlled format/arguments producing output longer than 2000 bytes. Consequence: out-of-bounds stack write, memory corruption and potential crash or code execution.

commit_msg:
memory: prevent dma-reentracy issues

Add a flag to the DeviceState, when a device is engaged in PIO/MMIO/DMA.
This flag is set/checked prior to calling a device's MemoryRegion
handlers, and set when device code initiates DMA.  The purpose of this
flag is to prevent two types of DMA-based reentrancy issues:

1.) mmio -> dma -> mmio case
2.) bh -> dma write -> mmio case

These issues have led to problems such as stack-exhaustion and
use-after-frees.

Summary of the problem from Peter Maydell:
https://lore.kernel.org/qemu-devel/CAFEAcA_23vc7hE3iaM-JVA6W38LK4hJoWae5KcknhPRD5fPBZA@mail.gmail.com

Resolves: https://gitlab.com/qemu-project/qemu/-/issues/62
Resolves: https://gitlab.com/qemu-project/qemu/-/issues/540

Resolves: https://gitlab.com/qemu-project/qemu/-/issues/827
Resolves: https://gitlab.com/qemu-project/qemu/-/issues/1282
Resolves: CVE-2023-0330

Signed-off-by: Alexander Bulekov <alxndr@bu.edu>
Reviewed-by: Thomas Huth <thuth@redhat.com>
Message-Id: <20230427211013.2994127-2-alxndr@bu.edu>
[thuth: Replace warn_report() with warn_report_once()]
Signed-off-by: Thomas Huth <thuth@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ["    /* Do not allow more than one simultaneous access to a device's IO Regions */", '    if (mr->dev && !mr->disable_reentrancy_guard &&', '        !mr->ram_device && !mr->ram && !mr->rom_device && !mr->readonly) {', '        if (mr->dev->mem_reentrancy_guard.engaged_in_io) {', '            warn_report_once("Blocked re-entrant IO on MemoryRegion: "', '                             "%s at addr: 0x%" HWADDR_PRIX,', '                             memory_region_name(mr), addr);', '            return MEMTX_ACCESS_ERROR;', '        }', '        mr->dev->mem_reentrancy_guard.engaged_in_io = true;', '    }', '', '    if (mr->dev) {', '        mr->dev->mem_reentrancy_guard.engaged_in_io = false;', '    }']}
description: A DMA reentrancy issue was found in the USB EHCI controller emulation of QEMU. EHCI does not verify if the Buffer Pointer overlaps with its MMIO region when it transfers the USB packets. Crafted content may be written to the controller's registers and trigger undesirable actions (such as reset) while the device is still transferring packets. This can ultimately lead to a use-after-free issue. A malicious guest could use this flaw to crash the QEMU process on the host, resulting in a denial of service condition, or potentially execute arbitrary code within the context of the QEMU process on the host. This flaw affects QEMU versions before 7.0.0.

code_evidence: The function drives repeated device accesses via access_fn inside the big-endian and little-endian loops (lines 30-38) without any guard against reentrancy. If access_fn triggers DMA that re-enters this MemoryRegion, the same device/region state can be mutated or freed while the loop continues using stale mr/value state.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The commit and description tie the flaw to use-after-free caused by DMA reentrancy; the missing reentrancy guard in this access function is the code-level enabler. CWE-416 fits because the outer access can continue operating on memory freed by the re-entrant operation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the I/O access path performs device callbacks without marking the region as engaged, so a callback can re-enter the same device via DMA. Trigger: crafted guest content causes an MMIO access whose access_fn initiates DMA that writes back into the controller's MMIO/registers. Supported consequence: the re-entrant path can free or reallocate state still referenced by the outer access, yielding a use-after-free (crash/DoS or potential code execution).

commit_msg:
Unsupported TGA bpp/alphabit combinations should error gracefully

Currently, only 24bpp without alphabits and 32bpp with 8 alphabits are
really supported. All other combinations will be rejected with a warning.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t} else if (tga->bits == TGA_BPP_32 || tga->alphabits) {'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t} else if (tga->bits == TGA_BPP_32 && tga->alphabits) {']}
description: gd_tga.c in the GD Graphics Library (aka libgd) before 2.2.3 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read) via a crafted TGA file.

code_evidence: The branch condition accepts any TGA with alphabits set, even when bits is not 32; it then reads bitmap[bitmap_caret + 3] and advances bitmap_caret by 4, assuming 4-byte pixels. For unsupported bpp/alphabits combinations the decoded bitmap buffer is smaller than this stride assumes.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the function reads tga->bitmap beyond its intended buffer due to a faulty bounds/format assumption, matching out-of-bounds read. It is not a write or integer overflow; the defect is unchecked buffer indexing driven by an unsupported pixel format.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the disjunctive check (bits==32 || alphabits) lets non-32bpp images with alphabits enter the 4-byte-pixel path. Trigger: a crafted TGA header with alphabits set but fewer bits per pixel. The loop then indexes bitmap[bitmap_caret+3] and advances by 4 per pixel, reading past the allocated bitmap buffer; the supported consequence is an out-of-bounds read causing denial of service (crash).

commit_msg:
xkbcomp: fix crash when parsing an xkb_geometry section

xkb_geometry sections are ignored; previously the had done so by
returning NULL for the section's XkbFile, however some sections of the
code do not expect this. Instead, create an XkbFile for it, it will
never be processes and discarded later.

Caught with the afl fuzzer.

Signed-off-by: Ran Benita <ran234@gmail.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            log_err(ctx, "Cannot define %s in a keymap file\\n",', '                    xkb_file_type_to_string(file->file_type));'], 'added_lines': ['            if (file->file_type == FILE_TYPE_GEOMETRY) {', '                log_vrb(ctx, 1,', '                        "Geometry sections are not supported; ignoring\\n");', '            } else {', '                log_err(ctx, "Cannot define %s in a keymap file\\n",', '                        xkb_file_type_to_string(file->file_type));', '            }']}
description: Unchecked NULL pointer usage in xkbcommon before 0.8.1 could be used by local attackers to crash (NULL pointer dereference) the xkbcommon parser by supplying a crafted keymap file, because the XkbFile for an xkb_geometry section was mishandled.

code_evidence: The loop iterates over file->defs and skips any XkbFile whose file_type is outside the keymap range via continue, so it is never stored in files[].

For each required type, a NULL slot sets ok=false; but the subsequent compile loop indexes files[type] and passes it to compile_file_fns[type], dereferencing files[type]->name in the log call even when the slot was NULL.

The guard at line 35 returns false only after the NULL check loop, yet the compile loop at 37-48 runs only when ok is true, so the NULL path is not reached here; the crash arises elsewhere in code consuming the NULL XkbFile.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits because a NULL pointer returned for an xkb_geometry section is later dereferenced by code that assumes a valid XkbFile.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: geometry sections produce a NULL XkbFile that other consumers dereference without a NULL check. Trigger: a crafted keymap containing an xkb_geometry section. Consequence: NULL pointer dereference causing a parser crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
Fix an integer overflow issue (#809)

Prevent an integer overflow issue in function opj_pi_create_decode of
pi.c.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tl_current_pi->include = (OPJ_INT16*) opj_calloc((l_tcp->numlayers +1) * l_step_l, sizeof(OPJ_INT16));'], 'added_lines': ['\t/* prevent an integer overflow issue */', '\tl_current_pi->include = 00;', '\tif (l_step_l <= (SIZE_MAX / (l_tcp->numlayers + 1U)))', '\t{', '\t\tl_current_pi->include = (OPJ_INT16*) opj_calloc((l_tcp->numlayers +1) * l_step_l, sizeof(OPJ_INT16));', '\t}', '']}

code_evidence: Lines 58-61 compute l_step_l as a product of l_max_res, l_max_prec, p_image->numcomps and l_step_p, all OPJ_UINT32 values derived from the image/JP2 header; no overflow check is applied to these multiplications.

Line 63 multiplies (l_tcp->numlayers + 1) by the already-computed l_step_l and passes the result as the element count to opj_calloc; a wrapped 32-bit product yields a small allocation. The following NULL check on line 65 only detects allocation failure, not a truncated size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe operation is an integer multiplication whose wrapped result is used as an allocation size, matching CWE-190's allocation-size wraparound pattern. The out-of-bounds access is the consequence, not the root cause; CWE-190 is the correct base weakness for the unchecked arithmetic.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the allocation element count (l_tcp->numlayers + 1) * l_step_l is computed in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic without overflow checking. Trigger: a crafted JP2 header with large numlayers/resolution/precision values makes the product wrap. Consequence: opj_calloc allocates a buffer smaller than the logical include array, and later index writes/reads produce an out-of-bounds write or read.

commit_msg: iso9660: validate directory record length
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    const unsigned char *isodirrec)', '\tdr_len = (size_t)isodirrec[DR_length_offset];'], 'added_lines': ['    const unsigned char *isodirrec, size_t reclen)', '\tif (reclen == 0 || reclen < (dr_len = (size_t)isodirrec[DR_length_offset])) {', '\t\tarchive_set_error(&a->archive, ARCHIVE_ERRNO_MISC,', '\t\t\t"Invalid directory record length");', '\t\treturn (NULL);', '\t}']}
description: An out-of-bounds read flaw exists in parse_file_info in archive_read_support_format_iso9660.c in libarchive 3.3.2 when extracting a specially crafted iso9660 iso file, related to archive_read_format_iso9660_read_header.

code_evidence: The function derives dr_len solely from the directory record's own length byte at isodirrec[DR_length_offset] and never receives or checks the actual number of bytes available in the buffer.
The only length check is dr_len < 34; it does not verify that dr_len stays within the supplied record buffer, so a record claiming a large length passes this check.

p is set to isodirrec + DR_name_offset and rr_end = isodirrec + dr_len, so downstream name access and parse_rockridge(..., rr_start, rr_end) trust the attacker-controlled dr_len as the true record extent.

commit_msg:
Prevent bounds check bypass through overflow in PSK identity parsing

The check `if( *p + n > end )` in `ssl_parse_client_psk_identity` is
unsafe because `*p + n` might overflow, thus bypassing the check. As
`n` is a user-specified value up to 65K, this is relevant if the
library happens to be located in the last 65K of virtual memory.

This commit replaces the check by a safe version.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if( *p + 2 > end )', '    if( n < 1 || n > 65535 || *p + n > end )'], 'added_lines': ['    if( end - *p < 2 )', '    if( n < 1 || n > 65535 || n > (size_t) ( end - *p ) )']}
description: In ARM mbed TLS before 2.7.0, there is a bounds-check bypass through an integer overflow in PSK identity parsing in the ssl_parse_client_psk_identity() function in library/ssl_srv.c.

code_evidence: The length check compares the pointer arithmetic expression *p + 2 against end; if *p is near the top of the address space, the addition can wrap and the comparison fails to detect insufficient remaining bytes.
The PSK identity length n is read from attacker-controlled bytes, *p is advanced by 2, and the check *p + n > end can likewise wrap when *p + n overflows, allowing the bounds check to pass.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe addition *p + n produces a wrapped pointer value while the logic assumes the result exceeds the original, which is exactly CWE-190 integer overflow/wraparound. The overflow directly defeats the size/offset bounds check, matching the target's bypass-protection consequence rather than a generic out-of-bounds read.

evidence_lines.code: if( *p + 2 > end )

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is pointer arithmetic *p + n (and *p + 2) used in a bounds comparison without guarding against wraparound of the pointer value. When the buffer pointer lies near the end of virtual memory, attacker-controlled n (up to 65535) causes the sum to wrap, bypassing the check so subsequent reads at lines 27/33 operate beyond end.

commit_msg:
Simplify the timerqueue code by using cached rbtrees and rely on the tree
leftmost node semantics to get the timer with earliest expiration time.
This is a drop in conversion, and therefore semantics remain untouched.

The runtime overhead of cached rbtrees is be pretty much the same as the
current head->next method, noting that when removing the leftmost node,
a common operation for the timerqueue, the rb_next(leftmost) is O(1) as
well, so the next timer will either be the right node or its parent.
Therefore no extra pointer chasing. Finally, the size of the struct
timerqueue_head remains the same.

Passes several hours of rcutorture.

commit_msg:
Fix alternate chains certificate forgery issue

During certificate verfification, OpenSSL will attempt to find an
alternative certificate chain if the first attempt to build such a chain
fails. An error in the implementation of this logic can mean that an
attacker could cause certain checks on untrusted certificates to be
bypassed, such as the CA flag, enabling them to use a valid leaf
certificate to act as a CA and "issue" an invalid certificate.

This occurs where at least one cert is added to the first chain from the
trust store, but that chain still ends up being untrusted. In that case
ctx->last_untrusted is decremented in error.

commit_msg: Pass recursion_depth to binary_to_variant and variant_to_binary
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['                  mvo( "data", abi->binary_to_variant( type, act.data ));'], 'added_lines': ['                  mvo( "data", abi->_binary_to_variant( type, act.data, recursion_depth ));']}
description: EOSIO/eos eos version after commit f1545dd0ae2b77580c2236fdb70ae7138d2c7168 contains a stack overflow vulnerability in abi_serializer that can result in attack eos network node. This attack appear to be exploitable via network request. This vulnerability appears to have been fixed in after commit cf7209e703e6d3f7a5413e0cb1fe88a4d8e4b38d .

code_evidence: The function accepts a recursion_depth parameter and guards entry with FC_ASSERT(++recursion_depth < abi_serializer::max_recursion_depth), bounding recursive nesting.
The data conversion at line 12 calls abi->binary_to_variant(type, act.data) without forwarding recursion_depth, so the depth accounting is lost across the nested deserialization path.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function's own guard shows recursion is intentionally bounded, but the call at line 12 bypasses that bound, allowing uncontrolled recursion that exhausts the stack. This matches CWE-674 rather than a mere resource-exhaustion generic weakness, since the missing constraint is specifically on recursion depth.
