static void add(mutable_variant_object &out, const char* name, const action& act, Resolver resolver, size_t recursion_depth) {
FC_ASSERT( ++recursion_depth < abi_serializer::max_recursion_depth, "recursive definition, max_recursion_depth" );

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the depth guard is enforced in add(), but the recursive abi deserialization is invoked through binary_to_variant without passing the tracked recursion_depth, so nested type definitions can recurse without the counter advancing. Trigger: a network-supplied action whose ABI type is recursively defined. Consequence: unbounded stack growth leading to stack overflow and node DoS.

commit_msg:
tss2_rc: ensure layer number is in bounds

The layer handler array was defined as 255, the max number of uint8,
which is the size of the layer field, however valid values are 0-255
allowing for 256 possibilities and thus the array was off by one and
needed to be sized to 256 entries. Update the size and add tests.

Note: previous implementations incorrectly dropped bits on unknown error
output, ie TSS2_RC of 0xFFFFFF should yeild a string of 255:0xFFFFFF,
but earlier implementations returned 255:0xFFFF, dropping the middle
bits, this patch fixes that.

Fixes: CVE-2023-22745

Signed-off-by: William Roberts <william.c.roberts@intel.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    handler = !handler ? unknown_layer_handler : handler;', '', '    UINT16 err_bits = tpm2_error_get(rc);', '    const char *e = err_bits ? handler(err_bits) : "success";', '    if (e) {', '    } else {', '        catbuf(buf, "0x%X", err_bits);'], 'added_lines': ['    if (handler) {', '        UINT16 err_bits = tpm2_error_get(rc);', '        const char *e = err_bits ? handler(err_bits) : "success";', '        if (e) {', '            catbuf(buf, "%s", e);', '        } else {', '            catbuf(buf, "0x%X", err_bits);', '        }', '    } else {', '        /*', "         * we don't want to drop any bits if we don't know what to do with it", '         * so drop the layer byte since we we already have that.', '         */', '        const char *e = unknown_layer_handler(rc >> 8);', '        assert(e);']}
description: tpm2-tss is an open source software implementation of the Trusted Computing Group (TCG) Trusted Platform Module (TPM) 2 Software Stack (TSS2). In affected versions `Tss2_RC_SetHandler` and `Tss2_RC_Decode` both index into `layer_handler` with an 8 bit layer number, but the array only has `TPM2_ERROR_TSS2_RC_LAYER_COUNT` entries, so trying to add a handler for higher-numbered layers or decode a response code with such a layer number reads/writes past the end of the buffer. This Buffer overrun, could result in arbitrary code execution. An example attack would be a MiTM bus attack that returns 0xFFFFFFFF for the RC. Given the common use case of TPM modules an attacker must have local access to the target machine with local system privileges which allows access to the TPM system. Usually TPM access requires administrative privilege.

code_evidence: The 8-bit layer number is extracted from the response code and used directly to index the layer_handler array; the array size and any bound on layer are not visible in this function, so the read of layer_handler[layer] can go out of bounds when layer is 255.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-120 covers buffer copies lacking input-size checks; here the analogous missing bound check on the layer index produces an out-of-bounds table access used to select a handler, matching the buffer-overrun described.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: an unvalidated 8-bit layer value indexes a fixed handler/name table without a size check. Trigger: a crafted RC (e.g., 0xFFFFFFFF) whose layer byte exceeds the table bounds. Consequence: out-of-bounds read of handler and name pointers, leading to invalid pointer dereference and potential memory corruption or code execution.

commit_msg:
scsi: bfa: release allocated memory in case of error

In bfad_im_get_stats if bfa_port_get_stats fails, allocated memory needs to
be released.

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20190910234417.22151-1-navid.emamdoost@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Navid Emamdoost <navid.emamdoost@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Martin K. Petersen <martin.petersen@oracle.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (rc != BFA_STATUS_OK)'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (rc != BFA_STATUS_OK) {', '\t\tkfree(fcstats);', '\t}']}
description: A memory leak in the bfad_im_get_stats() function in drivers/scsi/bfa/bfad_attr.c in the Linux kernel through 5.3.11 allows attackers to cause a denial of service (memory consumption) by triggering bfa_port_get_stats() failures, aka CID-0e62395da2bd.

code_evidence: fcstats is allocated with kzalloc and its only reference is the local pointer; on failure it must be freed before returning.
The error branch returns NULL without releasing fcstats, so the allocation is leaked on every bfa_port_get_stats failure.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-401 fits because the function fails to release memory after its effective lifetime on an error condition. This is a missing free, not a use-after-free or double free, which would require later access or duplicate release.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the error path after bfa_port_get_stats returns a non-OK status exits without freeing the kzalloc'd fcstats. Trigger: bfa_port_get_stats failure. Consequence: the allocation becomes unreachable, causing memory consumption and potential denial of service.

commit_msg:
CVE-2017-12897/ISO CLNS: Use ND_TTEST() for the bounds checks in isoclns_print().

This fixes a buffer over-read discovered by Kamil Frankowicz.

Don't pass the remaining caplen - that's too hard to get right, and we
were getting it wrong in at least one case; just use ND_TTEST().

Add a test using the capture file supplied by the reporter(s).
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['                    isoclns_print(ndo, p + 1, length - 1, ndo->ndo_snapend - p - 1);', '                    isoclns_print(ndo, p, length, ndo->ndo_snapend - p);'], 'added_lines': ['                    isoclns_print(ndo, p + 1, length - 1);', '                    isoclns_print(ndo, p, length);']}
description: The ISO CLNS parser in tcpdump before 4.9.2 has a buffer over-read in print-isoclns.c:isoclns_print().

code_evidence: For ETHERTYPE_ISO, length is checked to be at least 2 and ND_TCHECK_16BITS(p) validates two bytes at p. The function then passes a separate caplen argument (ndo->ndo_snapend - p - 1 or ndo->ndo_snapend - p) to isoclns_print, which is the value the patch removes; the callee uses this caplen for its own bounds checks, so an incorrect remaining-length value lets it read past the captured buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function supplies a miscalculated remaining-caplen that defeats the callee's bounds checks, directly enabling reads past the end of the intended buffer, which is CWE-125. It is not merely a truncation/DoS issue; the supported consequence is out-of-bounds memory read.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the caller computes the remaining captured length itself and passes it to isoclns_print, and this computation is wrong in at least one branch. Trigger: a crafted ISO CLNS/CHDLC packet where the derived caplen exceeds the actual bytes available. Consequence: isoclns_print's bounds checks pass incorrectly and it reads beyond the captured buffer (buffer over-read).

commit_msg: Update help.c
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['   /* CVE-2020-12649 */']}
description: Gurbalib through 2020-04-30 allows lib/cmds/player/help.c directory traversal for reading administrative paths.

code_evidence: The only traversal defense is splitting arg on "/" and rejecting when more than one element exists (szof > 1); this blocks slashes but not the literal ".." component, since ".." contains no separator.

arg is then passed to normalize_path with restricted bases "/doc/help/" and "/doc/help/wiz/", and the resulting path is opened via show_help, so an arg such as ".." can resolve outside the intended help directory.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-22 fits because external input builds a pathname intended to stay under /doc/help/ but the filter fails to neutralize the ".." special element, letting the path escape the restricted directory. The weakness is path traversal rather than a mere input-validation gap, since the consequence is reading files outside the intended parent directory.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the input filter rejects only multi-segment paths rather than neutralizing ".." components, so a single ".." element passes. Trigger: a user supplies a help topic of ".." (or an equivalent non-slash traversal token). Consequence: normalize_path resolves the path above the restricted help directory, and show_help reads the resulting file, enabling read access to paths outside /doc/help/.

commit_msg:
ALSA: timer: Harden slave timer list handling

A slave timer instance might be still accessible in a racy way while
operating the master instance as it lacks of locking.  Since the
master operation is mostly protected with timer->lock, we should cope
with it while changing the slave instance, too.  Also, some linked
lists (active_list and ack_list) of slave instances aren't unlinked
immediately at stopping or closing, and this may lead to unexpected
accesses.

This patch tries to address these issues.  It adds spin lock of
timer->lock (either from master or slave, which is equivalent) in a
few places.  For avoiding a deadlock, we ensure that the global
slave_active_lock is always locked at first before each timer lock.

Also, ack and active_list of slave instances are properly unlinked at
snd_timer_stop() and snd_timer_close().

Last but not least, remove the superfluous call of _snd_timer_stop()
at removing slave links.  This is a noop, and calling it may confuse
readers wrt locking.  Further cleanup will follow in a later patch.

Actually we've got reports of use-after-free by syzkaller fuzzer, and
this hopefully fixes these issues.

Reported-by: Dmitry Vyukov <dvyukov@google.com>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Takashi Iwai <tiwai@suse.de>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (timeri->master)'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (timeri->master && timeri->timer) {', '\t\tspin_lock(&timeri->timer->lock);', '\t\tspin_unlock(&timeri->timer->lock);', '\t}']}
description: sound/core/timer.c in the Linux kernel before 4.4.1 employs a locking approach that does not consider slave timer instances, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (race condition, use-after-free, and system crash) via a crafted ioctl call.

code_evidence: The function holds slave_active_lock, sets SNDRV_TIMER_IFLG_RUNNING, then dereferences timeri->master and adds timeri->active_list to master->slave_active_head without taking timeri->timer->lock. The master instance's slave_active_head and the slave's timer state are shared with concurrent master operations, so this list insertion is not exclusive against them.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The code performs a shared-resource update (list_add_tail into master->slave_active_head) without the synchronization that concurrent master operations require, which is exactly a concurrent-execution race with improper synchronization. It is not merely a missing check but an atomicity/exclusivity violation on shared list state.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the slave start path mutates master-owned linked-list state while only slave_active_lock is held, omitting the timer lock used on the master side. Trigger: a local ioctl starting a slave timer races with master operations or close/stop paths. Supported consequence: unsynchronized list access can yield use-after-free, crash, or other memory corruption (DoS).

commit_msg:
[tflite] Ensure `ResolveAxis` properly handles negative inputs.

In Python, a list `l` of length `n` allows indexing with negative indices, `l[i]`. The only constraint is that `n + i` becomes positive. Code in `ResolveAxis` assumes the constraints and only checks it using a `DCHECK`. But the macro is a no-op in non-debug builds and that can result in reading from negative offsets (buffer underflows).

PiperOrigin-RevId: 332530683
Change-Id: I464e073fee618054ae3719a3679739007bb3f3bc
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    if (current < 0 || current >= num_dims) {', '      return false;', '    }']}
description: In tensorflow-lite before versions 1.15.4, 2.0.3, 2.1.2, 2.2.1 and 2.3.1, to mimic Python's indexing with negative values, TFLite uses `ResolveAxis` to convert negative values to positive indices. However, the only check that the converted index is now valid is only present in debug builds. If the `DCHECK` does not trigger, then code execution moves ahead with a negative index. This, in turn, results in accessing data out of bounds which results in segfaults and/or data corruption. The issue is patched in commit 2d88f470dea2671b430884260f3626b1fe99830a, and is released in TensorFlow versions 1.15.4, 2.0.3, 2.1.2, 2.2.1, or 2.3.1.

code_evidence: Line 8 converts a negative axis by adding num_dims, but line 9 only enforces the resulting range with TFLITE_DCHECK, a no-op in non-debug builds.
The unchecked 'current' is then used as a write index: line 18 stores it into out_axis[*out_num_axis] and line 19 increments the count, with no runtime bound check.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked index is used as a destination offset in out_axis[*out_num_axis], so the operation writes outside the intended buffer, matching CWE-787. It is a write, not merely an out-of-bounds read, which would map to CWE-125.

evidence_lines.code:
int current = axis[idx] < 0 ? (axis[idx] + num_dims) : axis[idx];
TFLITE_DCHECK(current >= 0 && current < num_dims);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the validity of the converted index is guarded only by a debug-only assertion. When axis[idx] is negative enough that axis[idx] + num_dims stays negative (or otherwise out of range), non-debug builds proceed with that index; it is written to out_axis at line 18, producing an out-of-bounds write relative to the intended axis buffer.

commit_msg:
In saa7134_initdev, it will call saa7134_hwinit1. There are three
function invoking here: saa7134_video_init1, saa7134_ts_init1
and saa7134_vbi_init1.

All of them will init a timer with same function. Take
saa7134_video_init1 as an example. It'll bound &dev->video_q.timeout
with saa7134_buffer_timeout.

In buffer_activate, the timer funtcion is started.

If we remove the module or device which will call saa7134_finidev
to make cleanup, there may be a unfinished work. The
possible sequence is as follows, which will cause a
typical UAF bug.

Fix it by canceling the timer works accordingly before cleanup in
saa7134_finidev.

CPU0                  CPU1

                    |saa7134_buffer_timeout
saa7134_finidev     |
  kfree(dev);       |
                    |
                    | saa7134_buffer_next
                    | //use dev

Fixes: 1e7126b4a86a ("media: saa7134: Convert timers to use timer_setup()")
Signed-off-by: Zheng Wang <zyytlz.wz@163.com>
Signed-off-by: Hans Verkuil <hverkuil-cisco@xs4all.nl>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tdel_timer_sync(&dev->ts_q.timeout);']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel before 6.3.2. A use-after-free was found in saa7134_finidev in drivers/media/pci/saa7134/saa7134-core.c.

code_evidence: saa7134_ts_fini() releases the page table via saa7134_pgtable_free() and returns without synchronizing against the TS queue timer. The diff adds del_timer_sync(&dev->ts_q.timeout), showing the timer callback (saa7134_buffer_timeout -> saa7134_buffer_next) can still run concurrently and access dev->ts_q while teardown frees its resources.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function lacks exclusive synchronization between teardown and an asynchronous timer that shares dev->ts_q, which is the concurrent shared-resource access without proper synchronization described by CWE-362. The UAF is the resulting impact, not the primary weakness; CWE-362 fits as the race enabling it.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: teardown of the TS queue proceeds without canceling/synchronizing the queue timer. Trigger: a timer fires on another CPU while saa7134_ts_fini frees the queue's page table and the device is later freed. Consequence: concurrent access to freed state, a use-after-free/race leading to memory corruption or crash.

commit_msg: fix #111
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['                                                                max_file_size * 2 + 128 * 1024 * 1024));'], 'added_lines': ['                                                                ((size_t)max_file_size) * 2 + 128 * 1024 * 1024));']}
description: read_ujpg in jpgcoder.cc in Dropbox Lepton 1.2.1 allows attackers to cause a denial-of-service (application runtime crash because of an integer overflow) via a crafted file.

code_evidence: Line 14 bounds compressed_header_size and max_file_size to 128*1024*1024, but in the ujgversion!=1 branch line 54 computes max_file_size * 2 + 128*1024*1024 as the decompression output limit.

max_file_size is a 32-bit value (assigned from LEtoUint32 at line 166); the multiplication and addition at line 54 occur in that narrow type before being passed as the BrotliDecompress size bound, so the arithmetic can wrap.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the size calculation can wrap in its integer type and the wrapped value feeds a resource/size bound. It is not merely a memory-safety issue (e.g., CWE-787); the defect is the unchecked arithmetic producing an attacker-influenced size.

evidence_lines.code:
Sirikata::BrotliCodec::Decompress(compressed_header_buffer.data(),
compressed_header_buffer.size(),
JpegAllocator<uint8_t>(),
max_file_size * 2 + 128 * 1024 * 1024));

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the decompression size limit max_file_size * 2 + 128*1024*1024 is evaluated in 32-bit arithmetic without widening. Trigger: a crafted file that sets max_file_size near the 128 MB cap makes the product wrap to a small or negative value used as the Brotli output bound. Supported consequence: incorrect size limit, leading to a crash/DoS during header decompression; the fix casts to size_t before multiplying.

commit_msg:
patch 8.1.1365: source command doesn't check for the sandbox

Problem:    Source command doesn't check for the sandbox. (Armin Razmjou)
Solution:   Check for the sandbox when sourcing a file.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '    // Disallow sourcing a file in the sandbox, the commands would be executed', '    // later, possibly outside of the sandbox.', '    if (check_secure())', '\treturn;', '']}
description: getchar.c in Vim before 8.1.1365 and Neovim before 0.3.6 allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary OS commands via the :source! command in a modeline, as demonstrated by execute in Vim, and assert_fails or nvim_input in Neovim.

code_evidence: openscript() opens a script file and, when directly is set, enters a loop calling normal_cmd() to execute the sourced commands. The only guard before opening is the nesting check and the ignore_script check; there is no sandbox/secure check before mch_fopen() and before the command-execution loop.

joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function is the execution path that turns externally supplied script contents into executed commands without a trust/sandbox constraint, matching CWE-78's improper neutralization of special elements used in an OS command. The defect is a missing authorization check on a command-execution path, not mere file disclosure.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: sourcing a file is permitted without consulting check_secure(), so a modeline-driven :source! can reach openscript() and execute file contents. Trigger: a crafted modeline causes the source command to run in a sandbox/secure context. Consequence: attacker-chosen Ex commands (e.g., :execute) run as OS commands, escaping the sandbox.

commit_msg:
commit bcf85fcedfdd17911982a3e3564fcfec7b01eebd upstream.

romfs has a superblock field that limits the size of the filesystem; data
beyond that limit is never accessed.

romfs_dev_read() fetches a caller-supplied number of bytes from the
backing device.  It returns 0 on success or an error code on failure;
therefore, its API can't represent short reads, it's all-or-nothing.

However, when romfs_dev_read() detects that the requested operation would
cross the filesystem size limit, it currently silently truncates the
requested number of bytes.  This e.g.  means that when the content of a
file with size 0x1000 starts one byte before the filesystem size limit,
->readpage() will only fill a single byte of the supplied page while
leaving the rest uninitialized, leaking that uninitialized memory to
userspace.

Fix it by returning an error code instead of truncating the read when the
requested read operation would go beyond the end of the filesystem.

Fixes: da4458bda237 ("NOMMU: Make it possible for RomFS to use MTD devices directly")
Signed-off-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>
Reviewed-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
Cc: David Howells <dhowells@redhat.com>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Link: http://lkml.kernel.org/r/20200818013202.2246365-1-jannh@google.com
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (pos >= limit)', '\tif (buflen > limit - pos)', '\t\tbuflen = limit - pos;'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (pos >= limit || buflen > limit - pos)']}
description: An issue was discovered in romfs_dev_read in fs/romfs/storage.c in the Linux kernel before 5.8.4. Uninitialized memory leaks to userspace, aka CID-bcf85fcedfdd.

code_evidence: romfs_maxsize(sb) establishes the filesystem limit. When the requested read crosses that limit, lines 8-9 silently reduce buflen to limit - pos, so the caller's buffer is only partially filled and the remaining bytes are never written by this function.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function returns success while leaving part of the destination buffer uninitialized; the caller subsequently uses that uninitialized resource, matching CWE-908. This is distinct from an out-of-bounds read: no data beyond the limit is accessed, but unwritten memory is used.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: romfs_dev_read() truncates an over-limit request instead of failing, returning success after filling only part of the caller's buffer. Trigger: a read whose range extends past the filesystem size limit, e.g. a file of size 0x1000 starting one byte before the limit. The caller treats the buffer as fully populated, so uninitialized page memory is exposed to userspace.

commit_msg:
x86/32on64: don't allow recursive page tables from L3

L3 entries are special in PAE mode, and hence can't reasonably be used
for setting up recursive (and hence linear) page table mappings. Since
abuse is possible when the guest in fact gets run on 4-level page
tables, this needs to be excluded explicitly.

This is XSA-185 / CVE-2016-7092.

Reported-by: Jérémie Boutoille <jboutoille@ext.quarkslab.com>
Reported-by: "栾尚聪(好风)" <shangcong.lsc@alibaba-inc.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Reviewed-by: Andrew Cooper <andrew.cooper3@citrix.com>
diff_func:
--- func_before
+++ func_after
@@ -15,7 +15,9 @@
 
     rc = get_page_and_type_from_pagenr(
         l3e_get_pfn(l3e), PGT_l2_page_table, d, partial, 1);
-    if ( unlikely(rc == -EINVAL) && get_l3_linear_pagetable(l3e, pfn, d) )
+    if ( unlikely(rc == -EINVAL) &&
+         !is_pv_32bit_domain(d) &&
+         get_l3_linear_pagetable(l3e, pfn, d) )
         rc = 0;
 
     return rc;
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if ( unlikely(rc == -EINVAL) && get_l3_linear_pagetable(l3e, pfn, d) )'], 'added_lines': ['    if ( unlikely(rc == -EINVAL) &&', '         !is_pv_32bit_domain(d) &&', '         get_l3_linear_pagetable(l3e, pfn, d) )']}
description: The get_page_from_l3e function in arch/x86/mm.c in Xen allows local 32-bit PV guest OS administrators to gain host OS privileges via vectors related to L3 recursive pagetables.

code_evidence: get_page_and_type_from_pagenr is called for the L3 entry's PFN requesting PGT_l2_page_table; on -EINVAL the code falls through to the get_l3_linear_pagetable check and clears rc to 0, accepting the mapping.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The flaw is a missing privilege/domain restriction in page-table permission handling, permitting an unprivileged guest administrator to bypass access controls and gain host privileges. CWE-264 (permissions/privileges management) fits this access-control weakness; the missing is_pv_32bit_domain guard is the specific constraint.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the -EINVAL path unconditionally allows a linear/recursive L3 pagetable via get_l3_linear_pagetable without checking whether the domain is a 32-bit PV guest. Trigger: a 32-bit PV guest administrator supplies an L3 entry that fails normal typing but passes the linear-pagetable test. Consequence: recursive page-table mappings are accepted, letting the guest escalate to host privileges.

commit_msg:
x86/mm: Set old_guest_table when destroying vcpu pagetables

Changeset 6c4efc1eba ("x86/mm: Don't drop a type ref unless you held a
ref to begin with"), part of XSA-299, changed the calling discipline
of put_page_type() such that if put_page_type() returned -ERESTART
(indicating a partially de-validated page), subsequent calls to
put_page_type() must be called with PTF_partial_set.  If called on a
partially de-validated page but without PTF_partial_set, Xen will
BUG(), because to do otherwise would risk opening up the kind of
privilege escalation bug described in XSA-299.

One place this was missed was in vcpu_destroy_pagetables().
put_page_and_type_preemptible() is called, but on -ERESTART, the
entire operation is simply restarted, causing put_page_type() to be
called on a partially de-validated page without PTF_partial_set.  The
result was that if such an operation were interrupted, Xen would hit a
BUG().

Fix this by having vcpu_destroy_pagetables() consistently pass off
interrupted de-validations to put_old_page_type():
- Unconditionally clear references to the page, even if
  put_page_and_type failed
- Set old_guest_table and old_guest_table_partial appropriately

While here, do some refactoring:

 - Move clearing of arch.cr3 to the top of the function

description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.12.x allowing x86 PV guest OS users to gain host OS privileges by leveraging race conditions in pagetable promotion and demotion operations, because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2019-18421. XSA-299 addressed several critical issues in restartable PV type change operations. Despite extensive testing and auditing, some corner cases were missed. A malicious PV guest administrator may be able to escalate their privilege to that of the host. All security-supported versions of Xen are vulnerable. Only x86 systems are affected. Arm systems are not affected. Only x86 PV guests can leverage the vulnerability. x86 HVM and PVH guests cannot leverage the vulnerability. Note that these attacks require very precise timing, which may be difficult to exploit in practice.

code_evidence: put_old_guest_table(v) is called first to resume/complete a previously interrupted type change; if it returns nonzero the function bails out, so any in-flight partial state must already be persisted for this restart path.

The top-level page is dereferenced via put_page_and_type_preemptible(page); this call can return -EINTR mid-operation, leaving the page partially de-validated and the reference state inconsistent with the rest of the function.

On rc from the preemptible put, l4e_write/guest_table/guest_table_user clearing are gated by !rc; when the put was interrupted, the page's type reference has already been dropped but the pagetable entry and guest_table_user reference are not cleared, so a restart re-enters with a stale reference.
The return converts -EINTR to -ERESTART but does not record which page was partially de-validated (old_guest_table/old_guest_table_partial), so the restart path cannot resume with PTF_partial_set.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect is an improper synchronization of a shared pagetable reference across an interruptible, restartable code sequence: the put and the state clearing are not atomic, and the interrupted window leaves shared reference state inconsistent, matching CWE-362. It is not merely a logic/missing-check bug because the failure depends on a concurrent/preempting restart against the same page state.

evidence_lines.code: return rc != -EINTR ? rc : -ERESTART;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function drops a pagetable type reference via a preemptible operation that can be interrupted, yet only clears the associated pagetable entries and guest_table_user reference when rc==0, and it returns -ERESTART without storing the partially de-validated page. Trigger: a vCPU destroy interrupted between the put and the clearing. Consequence: the restart re-runs the put without PTF_partial_set on an already partially de-validated page, violating the type-ref discipline and risking BUG()/privilege escalation described in XSA-299.

commit_msg:
l2tp: fix racy SOCK_ZAPPED flag check in l2tp_ip{,6}_bind()

Lock socket before checking the SOCK_ZAPPED flag in l2tp_ip6_bind().
Without lock, a concurrent call could modify the socket flags between
the sock_flag(sk, SOCK_ZAPPED) test and the lock_sock() call. This way,
a socket could be inserted twice in l2tp_ip6_bind_table. Releasing it
would then leave a stale pointer there, generating use-after-free
errors when walking through the list or modifying adjacent entries.

description: Race condition in the L2TPv3 IP Encapsulation feature in the Linux kernel before 4.8.14 allows local users to gain privileges or cause a denial of service (use-after-free) by making multiple bind system calls without properly ascertaining whether a socket has the SOCK_ZAPPED status, related to net/l2tp/l2tp_ip.c and net/l2tp/l2tp_ip6.c.

code_evidence: The SOCK_ZAPPED check at lines 8-9 runs without holding the socket lock; the socket is only locked later at line 20, so a concurrent bind can change the flag between the check and lock_sock().
Lines 15-19 perform the bind-table lookup under read_lock_bh, then release it before lock_sock() at line 20, leaving a window where another sequence can insert the same socket.
Lines 34-39 add sk to l2tp_ip_bind_table and clear SOCK_ZAPPED without re-validating the flag, so a second bind can re-insert an already-bound socket, leaving a stale node after close.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function allows concurrent execution against shared socket state and the bind table without exclusive access, exactly the improper synchronization described by CWE-362. The use-after-free is a downstream consequence of the race, not the primary weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the SOCK_ZAPPED state is tested and the bind-table insertion performed without holding the socket lock across both operations. Trigger: concurrent bind() calls on the same L2TP/IPv4 socket pass the unlocked flag check and both insert the socket into l2tp_ip_bind_table. Consequence: the list holds a duplicate/stale pointer, and socket release leaves a dangling entry, yielding a use-after-free when the table is later traversed or modified.

commit_msg:
patch 9.0.2106: [security]: Use-after-free in win_close()

Problem:  [security]: Use-after-free in win_close()
Solution: Check window is valid, before accessing it

If the current window structure is no longer valid (because a previous
autocommand has already freed this window), fail and return before
attempting to set win->w_closing variable.

Add a test to trigger ASAN in CI

Signed-off-by: Christian Brabandt <cb@256bit.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t    if (!win_valid(win))', '\t\treturn FAIL;']}
description: Vim is an open source command line text editor. When closing a window, vim may try to access already freed window structure. Exploitation beyond crashing the application has not been shown to be viable. This issue has been addressed in commit `25aabc2b` which has been included in release version 9.0.2106. Users are advised to upgrade. There are no known workarounds for this vulnerability.

code_evidence: When the alternate window's buffer differs from curbuf, the code sets win->w_closing = TRUE, then calls apply_autocmds(EVENT_BUFLEAVE, ...). Autocommands can execute arbitrary commands, including those that free the window structure. The subsequent if (!win_valid(win)) return FAIL; guard exists after the autocmd; the patch adds a win_valid(win) check before win->w_closing = TRUE so a window already freed by a prior autocommand is not dereferenced.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Accessing win->w_closing on a window structure that may have been freed by an autocommand is a direct reuse of freed memory, matching CWE-416. The added win_valid check prevents the access; this is not merely a null-pointer issue but a lifetime/validity violation of the freed win object.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: win->w_closing is written without confirming the window pointer is still valid after earlier autocommand processing could have freed it. Trigger: a BUFLEAVE/autocmd sequence frees the window, then win_close proceeds to access win->w_closing. Consequence: use-after-free read/write on freed memory, potentially leading to crash or memory corruption.

commit_msg:
Bug 697015: Avoid object references vanishing during repair.

A PDF repair can be triggered 'just in time', when we encounter
a problem in the file. The idea is that this can happen without
the enclosing code being aware of it.

Thus the enclosing code may be holding 'borrowed' references
(such as those returned by pdf_dict_get()) at the time when the
repair is triggered. We are therefore at pains to ensure that
the repair does not replace any objects that exist already, so
that the calling code will not have these references unexpectedly
invalidated.

The sole exception to this is when we replace the 'Length' fields
in stream dictionaries with the actual lengths. Bug 697015 shows
exactly this situation causing a reference to become invalid.

The solution implemented here is to add an 'orphan list' to the
document, where we put these (hopefully few, small) objects. These
orphans are kept around until the document is closed.

commit_msg:
Fix heap buffer overflow in UnsortedSegmentSum.

When Index=int32, data_size and num_segments were truncated from int64 to int32. This truncation can produce negative numbers, which causes UnsortedSegmentFunctor to access out of bounds memory.

Also:
- Switches some indexing calculations to int64 to avoid signed integer overflow when either the input or output tensors have more than 2**31 - 1 elements.
- Fixes a range check error in the GPU kernel. The segment ID was checked against an upper bound measured in elements, not segments.
PiperOrigin-RevId: 256451663
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['__global__ void UnsortedSegmentCustomKernel(const Index input_outer_dim_size,', '                                            const Index inner_dim_size,', '                                            const Index output_outer_dim_size,', '  const Index input_total_size = input_outer_dim_size * inner_dim_size;', '  const Index output_total_size = output_outer_dim_size * inner_dim_size;', '  for (int input_index : GpuGridRangeX(input_total_size)) {', '    const Index input_segment_index = input_index / inner_dim_size;', '    const Index segment_offset = input_index % inner_dim_size;', '    if (output_segment_index < 0 || output_segment_index >= output_total_size) {', '    const Index output_index ='], 'added_lines': ['__global__ void UnsortedSegmentCustomKernel(const int64 input_outer_dim_size,', '                                            const int64 inner_dim_size,', '                                            const int64 output_outer_dim_size,', '  const int64 input_total_size = input_outer_dim_size * inner_dim_size;', '  for (int64 input_index : GpuGridRangeX(input_total_size)) {', '    const int64 input_segment_index = input_index / inner_dim_size;', '    const int64 segment_offset = input_index % inner_dim_size;', '    if (output_segment_index < 0 ||', '        output_segment_index >= output_outer_dim_size) {', '    const int64 output_index =']}
description: In TensorFlow before 1.15, a heap buffer overflow in UnsortedSegmentSum can be produced when the Index template argument is int32. In this case data_size and num_segments fields are truncated from int64 to int32 and can produce negative numbers, resulting in accessing out of bounds heap memory. This is unlikely to be exploitable and was detected and fixed internally in TensorFlow 1.15 and 2.0.

code_evidence: input_total_size and output_total_size are computed in the Index type; when Index is int32, the products input_outer_dim_size*inner_dim_size and output_outer_dim_size*inner_dim_size can overflow/truncate to negative values.

The loop bound uses the possibly-negative input_total_size, and the guard compares output_segment_index against output_total_size (an element count) rather than the segment count, so the check can pass for an invalid segment id.
output_index is then computed in Index and used as output + output_index in the reduction, dereferencing memory at an out-of-range offset.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is an incorrect conversion/narrowing between numeric types (Index/int32 vs int64 sizes), producing unexpected values used in bounds checks and pointer arithmetic. The out-of-bounds access is a downstream consequence of this numeric conversion error, matching CWE-681 rather than an arithmetic or bounds-checking weakness alone.

evidence_lines.code:
const Index input_total_size = input_outer_dim_size * inner_dim_size;
const Index output_total_size = output_outer_dim_size * inner_dim_size;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: size products and the segment-id bound are computed in a narrow/incorrect numeric type, so int32 Index values truncate or overflow to negative or oversized numbers. Trigger: large input/output dimensions or a segment id exceeding the segment count. Consequence: the bounds check fails to reject the id, and output_index indexes outside the output heap buffer.

commit_msg:
Prevent heap OOB read in TFLite's `gather.cc`.

Passing negative indices is illegal but there was a missing check so that resulted in OOB accesses.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 387231300
Change-Id: I3111b54b2f232638d795be17efc46abe4ede6bf8
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '  bool indices_has_only_positive_elements = true;', '  const size_t num_indices = positions->bytes / sizeof(PositionT);', '  for (size_t i = 0; i < num_indices; i++) {', '    if (indexes[i] < 0) {', '      indices_has_only_positive_elements = false;', '      break;', '    }', '  }', '  TF_LITE_ENSURE(context, indices_has_only_positive_elements);', '']}
description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. In affected versions TFLite's [`GatherNd` implementation](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/149562d49faa709ea80df1d99fc41d005b81082a/tensorflow/lite/kernels/gather_nd.cc#L124) does not support negative indices but there are no checks for this situation. Hence, an attacker can read arbitrary data from the heap by carefully crafting a model with negative values in `indices`. Similar issue exists in [`Gather` implementation](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/149562d49faa709ea80df1d99fc41d005b81082a/tensorflow/lite/kernels/gather.cc). We have patched the issue in GitHub commits bb6a0383ed553c286f87ca88c207f6774d5c4a8f and eb921122119a6b6e470ee98b89e65d721663179d. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.6.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.5.1, TensorFlow 2.4.3, and TensorFlow 2.3.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: indexes is read from the positions tensor via GetTensorData; the loop iterates over num_indexes elements and loads pos = indexes[i] without any check that pos is non-negative. The only bound enforced is pos < num_strings, which does not constrain the lower bound, so a negative PositionT value passes the check and is passed to GetString(input, pos).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads memory at an index derived from attacker-controlled tensor data without validating that the index is within [0, num_strings). A negative index causes a read before the beginning of the intended buffer, matching CWE-125. This is not merely a logic error because the unsupported index directly produces an out-of-bounds memory read.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the missing lower-bound check on the gather index allows negative values to reach GetString. Trigger: a crafted model supplies negative entries in the positions tensor. Consequence: the index is used to locate a string entry before the start of the intended buffer, yielding an out-of-bounds read (heap data disclosure or crash).

commit_msg:
tracing: Have error path in predicate_parse() free its allocated memory

In predicate_parse, there is an error path that is not going to
out_free instead it returns directly which leads to a memory leak.

Link: http://lkml.kernel.org/r/20190920225800.3870-1-navid.emamdoost@gmail.com

Signed-off-by: Navid Emamdoost <navid.emamdoost@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Steven Rostedt (VMware) <rostedt@goodmis.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\tif (top - op_stack > nr_parens)', '\t\t\t\treturn ERR_PTR(-EINVAL);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\tif (top - op_stack > nr_parens) {', '\t\t\t\tret = -EINVAL;', '\t\t\t\tgoto out_free;', '\t\t\t}']}
description: A memory leak in the predicate_parse() function in kernel/trace/trace_events_filter.c in the Linux kernel through 5.3.11 allows attackers to cause a denial of service (memory consumption), aka CID-96c5c6e6a5b6.

code_evidence: Lines 18-29 allocate op_stack, prog_stack and inverts; on later allocation failure the code jumps to out_free, which frees all three buffers.
The '(' case at lines 39-42 returns ERR_PTR(-EINVAL) directly when top - op_stack > nr_parens, bypassing the out_free cleanup label.
out_free at lines 142-150 is the sole path that releases op_stack, inverts and prog_stack (and its pred entries); the direct return never reaches it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-401 fits because memory allocated at lines 18-26 is not released on the early-return error path; this is a missing release of memory after its effective lifetime, distinct from a use-after-free since the memory is merely leaked, not dereferenced.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the parenthesis-depth error branch returns without going through out_free, so the previously allocated op_stack, prog_stack and inverts buffers are left unreleased. Trigger: input with more '(' nesting than nr_parens reaches line 40-41. Consequence: each such malformed filter leaks kernel memory, enabling resource-consumption denial of service.

commit_msg:
x86/PV: check GDT/LDT limits during emulation

Accesses beyond the LDT limit originating from emulation would trigger
the ASSERT() in pv_map_ldt_shadow_page(). On production builds such
accesses would cause an attempt to promote the touched page (offset from
the present LDT base address) to a segment descriptor one. If this
happens to succeed, guest user mode would be able to elevate its
privileges to that of the guest kernel. This is particularly easy when
there's no LDT at all, in which case the LDT base stored internally to
Xen is simply zero.

Also adjust the ASSERT() that was triggering: It was off by one to
begin with, and for production builds we also better use
ASSERT_UNREACHABLE() instead with suitable recovery code afterwards.

This is XSA-298.

Reported-by: Andrew Cooper <andrew.cooper3@citrix.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Reviewed-by: Andrew Cooper <andrew.cooper3@citrix.com>

-         ((gate_sel >= FIRST_RESERVED_GDT_BYTE) && !(gate_sel & 4)) ||

+          * We're interested in call gates only, which occupy a single

+                        : v->arch.pv.gdt_ents)) ||

description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.12.x allowing 32-bit PV guest OS users to gain guest OS privileges by installing and using descriptors. There is missing descriptor table limit checking in x86 PV emulation. When emulating certain PV guest operations, descriptor table accesses are performed by the emulating code. Such accesses should respect the guest specified limits, unless otherwise guaranteed to fail in such a case. Without this, emulation of 32-bit guest user mode calls through call gates would allow guest user mode to install and then use descriptors of their choice, as long as the guest kernel did not itself install an LDT. (Most OSes don't install any LDT by default). 32-bit PV guest user mode can elevate its privileges to that of the guest kernel. Xen versions from at least 3.2 onwards are affected. Only 32-bit PV guest user mode can leverage this vulnerability. HVM, PVH, as well as 64-bit PV guests cannot leverage this vulnerability. Arm systems are unaffected.

code_evidence: The guard only rejects gate_sel < 4 and selectors at/above FIRST_RESERVED_GDT_BYTE (when not LDT), then reads the descriptor via __get_user. It does not compare gate_sel against the guest's GDT/LDT entry counts (gdt_ents/ldt_ents), so an out-of-limit selector still yields a descriptor.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing limit check lets an unprivileged actor obtain and exercise descriptor privileges outside its intended sphere, i.e. improper privilege management. CWE-269 fits the privilege-assignment root cause rather than only the escalation impact.

evidence_lines.code:
if ( (gate_sel < 4) ||
((gate_sel >= FIRST_RESERVED_GDT_BYTE) && !(gate_sel & 4)) ||
__get_user(desc, pdesc) )
return 0;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: read_gate_descriptor lacks a descriptor-table limit check against the guest-specified GDT/LDT size. Trigger: 32-bit PV user mode supplies a call-gate selector beyond the table (or with no LDT installed, base zero). The emulator then reads/uses an out-of-bounds descriptor, letting user mode install and use descriptors of its choice, elevating to guest-kernel privilege.

commit_msg:
(uid_t) -1 is still used as placeholder to mean "unset". This is OK, since
there should be no users with such number, see
https://systemd.io/UIDS-GIDS#special-linux-uids.

(uid_t) -1 is used as the default value in class initialization.

When a user or group above INT32_MAX is created, the numeric uid or
gid wraps around to negative when the value is assigned to gint, and
polkit gets confused. Let's accept such gids, except for -1.

A nicer fix would be to change the underlying type to e.g. uint32 to
not have negative values. But this cannot be done without breaking the
API, so likely new functions will have to be added (a
polkit_unix_user_new variant that takes a unsigned, and the same for
_group_new, _set_uid, _get_uid, _set_gid, _get_gid, etc.). This will
require a bigger patch.

Fixes https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/polkit/polkit/issues/74.

commit_msg:
ahci: Update byte count after DMA completion

Currently, DMA read/write operations neglect to update
the byte count after a successful transfer like ATAPI
DMA read or PIO read/write operations do.

We correct this oversight by adding another callback into
the IDEDMAOps structure. The commit callback is called
whenever we are cleaning up a scatter-gather list.
AHCI can register this callback in order to update post-
transfer information such as byte count updates.

We use this callback in AHCI to consolidate where we delete
the SGlist as generated from the PRDT, as well as update the
byte count after the transfer is complete.

The QEMUSGList structure has an init flag added to it in order
to make qemu_sglist_destroy a nop if it is called when
there is no sglist, which simplifies cleanup and error paths.

This patch fixes several AHCI problems, notably Non-NCQ modes
of operation for Windows 7 as well as Hibernate support for Windows 7.

Signed-off-by: John Snow <jsnow@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>
Tested-by: Michael S. Tsirkin <mst@redhat.com>
Message-id: 1412204151-18117-3-git-send-email-jsnow@redhat.com
Signed-off-by: Stefan Hajnoczi <stefanha@redhat.com>

description: The ahci_commit_buf function in ide/ahci.c in QEMU allows attackers to cause a denial of service (NULL dereference) when the command header 'ad->cur_cmd' is null.

code_evidence: When n > 0 the function calls dma_buf_commit(s) and then advances sector_num, nsector and io_buffer; the diff replaces this with an assert on s->io_buffer_size and a size-passing commit, so the commit path depends on transfer state being consistent.

The range-check branch calls dma_buf_commit(s) followed by ide_dma_error(s); the diff removes this commit, so the cleanup path is reworked and the commit callback must tolerate a partially initialized or absent command state.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is a NULL pointer dereference: the commit path assumes the command header is non-NULL and dereferences it without a guard. This matches CWE-476 rather than a bounds or use-after-free issue, because no memory range is violated and no freed object is reused; the dereferenced pointer is simply NULL.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: In the patched design dma_buf_commit invokes a DMA commit callback that dereferences the command header via the device state. If the commit callback runs when the command header (ad->cur_cmd) has not been set or has been cleared, the callback dereferences a NULL pointer; the trigger is a DMA completion or error cleanup path reaching commit without a valid current command. The supported consequence is a host crash (DoS).

code_evidence: Line 17 gates the UTF-8 decoding path on string.length != 0, but the branch at 18-21 computes end from string.size and derives s via njs_string_offset(string.start, end, slice.start), so the guard does not distinguish byte-sized (ASCII) strings from multi-byte UTF-8 strings.
Line 31 instead handles the non-UTF-8 case with memcpy from string.start + slice.start using slice.length, which is only safe when the earlier branch correctly classified the string.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The root cause is an incorrect numeric comparison used to classify string representation, i.e. improper calculation/interpretation of length versus size, which falls under the Numeric Errors category (CWE-189). Contrast with a pure buffer overflow (CWE-119): here the misclassified length/size relationship drives the bad offset computation.

evidence_lines.code:
} else {
memcpy(p, string.start + slice.start, slice.length);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The condition at line 17 conflates 'non-empty' with 'UTF-8 encoded'. An ASCII string with non-zero length is routed into the UTF-8 decode branch, where slice.start/slice.length offsets (potentially derived from negative arguments) are applied to byte-oriented string.start/string.size, producing an out-of-bounds offset and the reported segmentation fault.

commit_msg:
io_get_file_fixed will access io_uring's context. Lock it if it is
invoked unlocked (eg via io-wq) to avoid a race condition with fixed
files getting unregistered.

No single upstream patch exists for this issue, it was fixed as part
of the file assignment changes that went into the 5.18 cycle.

Signed-off-by: Jheng, Bing-Jhong Billy <billy@starlabs.sg>
Signed-off-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t\t       struct io_kiocb *req, int fd, bool fixed)', '\t\treturn io_file_get_fixed(ctx, req, fd);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t\t       struct io_kiocb *req, int fd, bool fixed,', '\t\t\t\t       unsigned int issue_flags)', '\t\treturn io_file_get_fixed(ctx, req, fd, issue_flags);']}
description:
A use-after-free vulnerability in the Linux Kernel io_uring system can be exploited to achieve local privilege escalation.

The io_file_get_fixed function lacks the presence of ctx->uring_lock which can lead to a Use-After-Free vulnerability due a race condition with fixed files getting unregistered.

We recommend upgrading past commit da24142b1ef9fd5d36b76e36bab328a5b27523e8.

code_evidence: io_file_get dispatches to io_file_get_fixed(ctx, req, fd) when fixed is true, without passing any lock/issue context; the fixed path is taken based solely on the caller-supplied fixed flag and fd.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the unsynchronized fixed lookup can obtain and use a file pointer after its registration was freed. This is a race-induced use-after-free, not merely a missing-lock or null-dereference issue; the consequence is reuse of freed memory.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the fixed-file lookup is invoked without ctx->uring_lock synchronization, so it can race with fixed-file unregistration. Trigger: a request reaches the fixed branch (fixed true) via an unlocked invocation such as io-wq. Consequence: the file reference may be resolved from a table entry being freed, yielding a use-after-free of the file object.

commit_msg:
Custom buttons should only handle accelerators when focused.

BUG=541415

Review URL: https://codereview.chromium.org/1437523005

Cr-Commit-Position: refs/heads/master@{#360130}

However, only top level', '  // widgets can be active, so for child widgets check if they are focused', '  // instead.', '  if ((IsChildWidget() && !FocusInChildWidget()) ||', '      (!IsChildWidget() && !GetWidget()->IsActive())) {', '    return false;', '  }']}
description: The CustomButton::AcceleratorPressed function in ui/views/controls/button/custom_button.cc in Google Chrome before 48.0.2564.82 allows remote attackers to spoof URLs via vectors involving an unfocused custom button.

code_evidence: The function unconditionally calls SetState(STATE_NORMAL) and NotifyClick(synthetic_event) whenever AcceleratorPressed fires, without verifying that the button's widget is active or focused. The patch adds a guard returning false for unfocused child widgets or inactive top-level widgets; the pre-patch code lacks this check.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-254 (7PK - Security Features) covers missing security-feature enforcement such as access/activation gating. The missing active/focus check is exactly such a missing security feature; the direct member CWE-284 (improper access control) is the concrete mapping, but the target category fits as the umbrella.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: no focus/activation constraint before dispatching a synthetic click. Trigger: an accelerator delivered while the custom button is in an unfocused widget. Consequence: the unfocused button fires its click handler, enabling UI spoofing behavior (e.g., URL-bar spoofing) since the action executes without user intent on that control.

commit_msg:

By sending short SONMP packets, an attacker can make the decoder crash
by reading too much data on the heap. SONMP packets are fixed in size,
just ensure we get the enough bytes to contain a SONMP packet.

CVE-2021-43612

commit_msg:
make the dump directories owned by root by default

It was discovered that the abrt event scripts create a user-readable
copy of a sosreport file in abrt problem directories, and include
excerpts of /var/log/messages selected by the user-controlled process
name, leading to an information disclosure.

This issue was discovered by Florian Weimer of Red Hat Product Security.

Related: #1212868

Signed-off-by: Jakub Filak <jfilak@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    struct dump_dir *dd = create_dump_dir_from_problem_data(pd, g_settings_dump_location);'], 'added_lines': ['    struct dump_dir *dd = NULL;', '', '    if (g_settings_privatereports)', '        dd = create_dump_dir_from_problem_data_ext(pd, g_settings_dump_location, 0);', '    else', '        dd = create_dump_dir_from_problem_data(pd, g_settings_dump_location);']}
description: The event scripts in Automatic Bug Reporting Tool (ABRT) uses world-readable permission on a copy of sosreport file in problem directories, which allows local users to obtain sensitive information from /var/log/messages via unspecified vectors.

code_evidence: The function calls load_abrt_conf() and then unconditionally invokes create_dump_dir_from_problem_data(pd, g_settings_dump_location).

The resulting dump directory handle dd is used to copy its directory name and close it; the directory and any files copied into it retain whatever permissions that creation path assigns, with no private-mode constraint applied here.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-200 fits because the function manages storage of sensitive problem data that is made accessible to actors not authorized to read it, an information-exposure weakness in handling sensitive resources. CWE-732 (incorrect permissions) is the underlying mechanism, but the target here is the resultant exposure of sensitive information.

evidence_lines.code:
load_abrt_conf();
struct dump_dir *dd = create_dump_dir_from_problem_data(pd, g_settings_dump_location);

problem_id = xstrdup(dd->dd_dirname);
dd_close(dd);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the problem-data directory is created through a path that does not enforce private permissions, so files copied into it (such as a sosreport copy) remain readable by other local users. Trigger: a local user causes a problem to be saved; the consequence is disclosure of sensitive contents (including user-selected /var/log/messages excerpts) to unauthorized actors.

commit_msg:
dm: Reset virtio device before release

With virtio polling mode enabled, a timer is running in the virtio
backend service. And the timer will also be triggered if its frondend
driver didn't do the device reset in shutdown. A freed virtio device
will be accessed in the polling timer handler.

Do the virtio reset() callback specifically to clear the polling timer
before the free.

Tracked-On: #6147
Signed-off-by: Shuo A Liu <shuo.a.liu@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Yonghua Huang <yonghua.huang@intel.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\t\tvirtio_input_reset(vi);']}
description: The polling timer handler in ACRN before 2.5 has a use-after-free for a freed virtio device, related to devicemodel/hw/pci/virtio/*.c.

code_evidence: Teardown destroys the mutex, frees event_queue, closes fd, frees evdev and serial, then frees the virtio_input object vi and sets the local pointer to NULL. The patch adds virtio_input_reset(vi) before free(vi); the pre-patch version frees the device without stopping the polling timer that still references it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function frees the virtio device without first clearing the timer that later dereferences it, so memory is referenced after free, matching CWE-416. This is distinct from a simple double free, since the defect is post-free reuse by the timer handler.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the device object is freed while the virtio polling timer remains active and retains a reference to it. Trigger: after teardown frees vi, the polling timer handler fires and accesses the freed virtio_input memory. Supported consequence: use-after-free, allowing invalid reads/writes and potential crash or memory corruption.

commit_msg:
write_wakeup can happen in parallel with close/hangup where tty->disc_data
is set to NULL and the netdevice is freed thus also freeing
disc_data. write_wakeup accesses disc_data so we must prevent close from
freeing the netdev while write_wakeup has a non-NULL view of
tty->disc_data.

We also need to make sure that accesses to disc_data are atomic. Which can
all be done with RCU.

This problem was found by Syzkaller on SLCAN, but the same issue is
reproducible with the SLIP line discipline using an LTP test based on the
Syzkaller reproducer.

A fix which didn't use RCU was posted by Hillf Danton.

Fixes: 661f7fda21b1 ("slip: Fix deadlock in write_wakeup")
Fixes: a8e83b17536a ("slcan: Port write_wakeup deadlock fix from slip")
Reported-by: syzbot+017e491ae13c0068598a@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Signed-off-by: Richard Palethorpe <rpalethorpe@suse.com>
Cc: Wolfgang Grandegger <wg@grandegger.com>
Cc: Marc Kleine-Budde <mkl@pengutronix.de>
Cc: "David S. Miller" <davem@davemloft.net>
Cc: Tyler Hall <tylerwhall@gmail.com>
Cc: linux-can@vger.kernel.org
Cc: netdev@vger.kernel.org
Cc: linux-kernel@vger.kernel.org
Cc: syzkaller@googlegroups.com
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\ttty->disc_data = NULL;'], 'added_lines': ['\trcu_assign_pointer(tty->disc_data, NULL);', '\tsynchronize_rcu();']}
description: In the Linux kernel before 5.4.16, a race condition in tty->disc_data handling in the slip and slcan line discipline could lead to a use-after-free, aka CID-0ace17d56824. This affects drivers/net/slip/slip.c and drivers/net/can/slcan.c.

code_evidence: Line 3 reads tty->disc_data into sl before any synchronization. Lines 7-9 clear disc_data and sl->tty under sl->lock, but line 10 flush_work then line 15 unregister_netdev run outside that lock, freeing the netdev and the disc_data object while a concurrent write_wakeup may still hold a non-NULL view of tty->disc_data.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-362 fits: the shared tty->disc_data is accessed concurrently without exclusive synchronization, so an interfering sequence (write_wakeup) retains access after close releases the resource, violating atomicity/exclusivity and enabling the UAF.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: slip_close clears tty->disc_data and frees the netdev without waiting for concurrent write_wakeup readers that already captured disc_data. Trigger: write_wakeup runs in parallel with close/hangup. Consequence: use-after-free of the freed disc_data/netdev, causing crash or memory corruption.

commit_msg:
Revised handling of TIFFTAG_INKNAMES and related TIFFTAG_NUMBEROFINKS value

In order to solve the buffer overflow issues related to TIFFTAG_INKNAMES and related TIFFTAG_NUMBEROFINKS value, a revised handling of those tags within LibTiff is proposed:

Behaviour for writing:
    `NumberOfInks`  MUST fit to the number of inks in the `InkNames` string.
    `NumberOfInks` is automatically set when `InkNames` is set.
    If `NumberOfInks` is different to the number of inks within `InkNames` string, that will be corrected and a warning is issued.
    If `NumberOfInks` is not equal to samplesperpixel only a warning will be issued.

Behaviour for reading:
    When reading `InkNames` from a TIFF file, the `NumberOfInks` will be set automatically to the number of inks in `InkNames` string.
    If `NumberOfInks` is different to the number of inks within `InkNames` string, that will be corrected and a warning is issued.
    If  `NumberOfInks` is not equal to samplesperpixel only a warning will be issued.

This allows the safe use of the NumberOfInks value to read out the InkNames without buffer overflow

This MR will close the following issues:  #149, #150, #152, #168 (to be checked), #250, #269, #398 and #456.

It also fixes the old bug at http://bugzilla.maptools.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2599, for which the limitation of `NumberOfInks = SPP` was introduced, which is in my opinion not necessary and does not solve the general issue.

description: A vulnerability was found in the libtiff library. This flaw causes a heap buffer overflow issue via the TIFFTAG_INKNAMES and TIFFTAG_NUMBEROFINKS values.

code_evidence: In the TIFFTAG_INKNAMES case, the caller-supplied count v is read from varargs and passed to checkInkNamesString(tif, v, s), which returns a validated length. Only when v > 0 is the string copied via _TIFFsetNString(&td->td_inknames, s, v) and td_inknameslen set to v. The stored NumberOfInks value is never reconciled with the actual ink count here, so the count that later drives reads of td_inknames can diverge from the actual string length.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the unsynchronized count leads to writing data beyond the intended ink-names buffer during readout. This is a direct out-of-bounds write rather than a mere read overrun (CWE-125) or integer truncation alone.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the InkNames handling stores a length derived from the caller-supplied count without tying td_numberofinks to the number of inks actually present in the string. Trigger: a TIFF file or caller sets TIFFTAG_INKNAMES with a count inconsistent with the ink-name content. Consequence: downstream use of NumberOfInks to read out InkNames writes past the allocated buffer, producing a heap buffer overflow.

commit_msg:
Fix a null pointer exception caused by branching on uninitialized data.

This is due to not checking that the params for the quantization exists. If there is no quantization, we should not access the `.params` field.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 385168337
Change-Id: I28661e4f12ba1c92cfeae23d22a3fb2df2a2c6a4
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  TF_LITE_ENSURE(context,', '                 cell_state->quantization.type != kTfLiteNoQuantization);', '  TF_LITE_ENSURE(context,', '                 output_tensor->quantization.type != kTfLiteNoQuantization);', '      TF_LITE_ENSURE(context,', '                     intermediate->quantization.type != kTfLiteNoQuantization);', '  TF_LITE_ENSURE(context, hidden->quantization.type != kTfLiteNoQuantization);']}
description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. In affected versions all TFLite operations that use quantization can be made to use unitialized values. [For example](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/460e000de3a83278fb00b61a16d161b1964f15f4/tensorflow/lite/kernels/depthwise_conv.cc#L198-L200). The issue stems from the fact that `quantization.params` is only valid if `quantization.type` is different that `kTfLiteNoQuantization`. However, these checks are missing in large parts of the code. We have patched the issue in GitHub commits 537bc7c723439b9194a358f64d871dd326c18887, 4a91f2069f7145aab6ba2d8cfe41be8a110c18a5 and 8933b8a21280696ab119b63263babdb54c298538. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.6.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.5.1, TensorFlow 2.4.3, and TensorFlow 2.3.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: At lines 15-18, cell_state_params and proj_params are derived by casting cell_state->quantization.params and output_tensor->quantization.params without verifying that quantization.type != kTfLiteNoQuantization; when no quantization is configured, params is uninitialized and later dereferenced (e.g., cell_state_params->scale->data[0]).
At lines 99-102, intermediate->quantization.params is cast and params->scale/zero_point are read with no type check in the use_layer_norm branch.
At lines 110-113, hidden->quantization.params is cast and hidden_params->scale/zero_point are read without checking quantization.type.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-908 fits because the function reads a resource (quantization.params) that was never initialized, and the missing type guard directly permits that use. This is distinct from a general NULL-pointer dereference; the field is uninitialized rather than explicitly null.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the code accesses the quantization.params field without confirming quantization.type is not kTfLiteNoQuantization, so params may be uninitialized. Trigger: a model whose tensors carry no quantization parameters. Consequence: dereferencing the uninitialized params pointer yields invalid reads, potentially a crash or incorrect values.

Consequence: out-of-bounds read of memory after the input, potentially crashing the process (DoS) and reading adjacent memory.

description: TensorFlow is an open source platform for machine learning. If `RaggedBincount` is given an empty input tensor `splits`, it results in a segfault that can be used to trigger a denial of service attack. We have patched the issue in GitHub commit 7a4591fd4f065f4fa903593bc39b2f79530a74b8. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.10.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.9.1, TensorFlow 2.8.1, and TensorFlow 2.7.2, as these are also affected and still in supported range. There are no known workarounds for this issue.

code_evidence: The function derives num_rows = splits.size() - 1 from the untrusted splits input, then immediately dereferences splits(0) and splits(num_rows) without first checking that splits is non-empty.
In the accumulation loop, batch_idx is advanced by while (idx >= splits(batch_idx)) with no bound against num_rows, so indexing depends on the same splits data.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The crash stems from missing validation of a required input property (non-empty splits) before the data is used to derive indices, matching CWE-20's improper input validation with an availability impact. It is not a transformation/filtering flaw; the input itself is used unsafely because its size constraint was never checked.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the splits tensor's size is not validated before num_rows is computed and splits(0)/splits(num_rows) are accessed. Trigger: an empty splits tensor makes num_rows negative and the subsequent flat-tensor indexing out of bounds, producing a segfault. Supported consequence is a crash (denial of service) rather than memory disclosure.

description: cups-filters contains backends, filters, and other software required to get the cups printing service working on operating systems other than macos. If you use the Backend Error Handler (beh) to create an accessible network printer, this security vulnerability can cause remote code execution. `beh.c` contains the line `retval = system(cmdline) >> 8;` which calls the `system` command with the operand `cmdline`. `cmdline` contains multiple user controlled, unsanitized values. As a result an attacker with network access to the hosted print server can exploit this vulnerability to inject system commands which are executed in the context of the running server. This issue has been addressed in commit `8f2740357` and is expected to be bundled in the next release. Users are advised to upgrade when possible and to restrict access to network printers in the meantime.

code_evidence: Lines 4-8 copy the externally supplied URI into scheme and truncate it at the first ':', producing an attacker-influenced backend name. Lines 18-22 interpolate that scheme plus argv[1..5] and filename into cmdline using single-quote wrapping only. Line 30 passes the assembled string to system(), which invokes a shell.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-78 fits because the function builds an OS command from externally influenced input and sends it to system() without proper neutralization of special elements. This is command injection, not merely argument injection, since the shell interprets the injected separators and runs extra commands.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: user-controlled values (URI scheme, argv arguments, filename) are concatenated into a shell command string without neutralizing shell metacharacters; the single quotes are insufficient because a value containing a quote can escape them. Trigger: a forged job title/argument or URI containing quote and command separators. Consequence: the shell executes attacker-supplied commands in the context of the CUPS backend process, enabling remote code execution.

commit_msg:
x86/pv: Flush TLB in response to paging structure changes

With MMU_UPDATE, a PV guest can make changes to higher level pagetables.  This
is safe from Xen's point of view (as the update only affects guest mappings),
and the guest is required to flush (if necessary) after making updates.

However, Xen's use of linear pagetables (UPDATE_VA_MAPPING, GNTTABOP_map,
writeable pagetables, etc.) is an implementation detail outside of the
API/ABI.

Changes in the paging structure require invalidations in the linear pagetable
range for subsequent accesses into the linear pagetables to access non-stale
mappings.  Xen must provide suitable flushing to prevent intermixed guest
actions from accidentally accessing/modifying the wrong pagetable.

For all L2 and higher modifications, flush the TLB.  PV guests cannot create
L2 or higher entries with the Global bit set, so no mappings established in
the linear range can be global.  (This could in principle be an order 39 flush
starting at LINEAR_PT_VIRT_START, but no such mechanism exists in practice.)

Express the necessary flushes as a set of booleans which accumulate across the
operation.  Comment the flushing logic extensively.

This is XSA-286.

Signed-off-by: Andrew Cooper <andrew.cooper3@citrix.com>
Reviewed-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>

description: Nextcloud also ships a CLI utility called nextcloudcmd which is sometimes used for automated scripting and headless servers. Versions of nextcloudcmd prior to 3.6.1 would incorrectly trust invalid TLS certificates, which may enable a Man-in-the-middle attack that exposes sensitive data or credentials to a network attacker. This affects the CLI only. It does not affect the standard GUI desktop Nextcloud clients, and it does not affect the Nextcloud server.

(void)account;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the SSL error handler unconditionally accepts every certificate presented in an error, with no approval or trust check. Trigger: any TLS handshake producing a QSslError, including an attacker's self-signed or mismatched certificate during a man-in-the-middle attempt. Consequence: the client proceeds with a connection to an unverified peer, exposing credentials and data to a network attacker.

description: In libming 0.4.8, there is an integer overflow (caused by an out-of-range left shift) in the readUInt32 function (util/read.c). Remote attackers could leverage this vulnerability to cause a denial-of-service via a crafted swf file.

code_evidence: readUInt8(f) returns an int (signed 32-bit); each byte is left-shifted by 8, 16, and 24 and OR-ed into an unsigned long result. The shift at line 7 applies to a signed int operand before promotion, so the int value is shifted by 24 within a 32-bit signed representation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function computes a value via a shift that can overflow the operand's integer representation, matching CWE-190 integer overflow/wraparound. It is not merely a truncation issue; the arithmetic itself can wrap and yield an incorrect result.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the left shift of the signed int returned by readUInt8 by 24 at line 7 is evaluated in int type, so for byte values >= 0x80 the sign bit is set and the shift overflows/wraps, producing a negative or out-of-range value. Trigger: a crafted swf file supplies such a byte in the fourth position. Supported consequence: the computed 32-bit value is wrong, leading to malformed parsed values and denial-of-service (CVE-2018-5251); the patch casts to unsigned long before shifting.

commit_msg:
There is a current use after free possible on a gatt server if a client
disconnects while a WriteValue call is being processed with dbus.

This patch includes the addition of a pending disconnect callback to handle
cleanup better if a disconnect occurs during a write, an acquire write
or read operation using bt_att_register_disconnect with the cb.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\tsend_write(device, attrib, chrc->proxy, queue,', '\t\t\t\t\tbt_att_get_link_type(att), true, true);', '\t\tif (acquire_write(chrc, device, attrib, id, value, len,', '\t\t\t\t\t\tbt_att_get_link_type(att)))', '\tif (send_write(device, attrib, chrc->proxy, queue, id, value, len,', '\t\t\toffset, bt_att_get_link_type(att), false, false))'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\tsend_write(att, attrib, chrc->proxy, queue,', '\t\t\t\t\ttrue, true);', '\t\tif (acquire_write(chrc, att, attrib, id, value, len))', '\tif (send_write(att, attrib, chrc->proxy, queue, id, value, len,', '\t\t\toffset, false, false))']}
description: An issue was discovered in gatt-database.c in BlueZ 5.61. A use-after-free can occur when a client disconnects during D-Bus processing of a WriteValue call.

code_evidence: The callback resolves device via att_get_device(att) and bails if it is absent, but the bt_att pointer is not retained for later lifetime tracking.
The D-Bus path calls acquire_write(chrc, device, attrib, id, value, len, bt_att_get_link_type(att)) and returns; no disconnect callback is registered to cancel the pending operation.

The fallback calls send_write(device, attrib, chrc->proxy, queue, id, value, len, offset, bt_att_get_link_type(att), false, false) and returns, again leaving the async D-Bus write outstanding without disconnect handling.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the root cause is a lifetime mismatch: async write processing continues to reference freed ATT/device memory after client disconnect. This is not merely a missing error check; the referenced memory can be released before use.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: chrc_write_cb starts asynchronous D-Bus operations (acquire_write/send_write) that outlive the callback, but it never registers a disconnect handler to cancel them. If the client disconnects while the WriteValue D-Bus processing is pending, the ATT/device context can be torn down while the async operation still holds references, leading to a use-after-free when that operation later completes.
