commit_msg:
As part of CVE-2013-4288, the D-Bus clients were allowed (and
encouraged) to submit the UID of the subject of authorization checks
to avoid races against UID changes (notably using executables
set-UID to root).

However, that also allowed any client to submit an arbitrary UID, and
that could be used to bypass "can only ask about / affect the same UID"
checks in CheckAuthorization / RegisterAuthenticationAgent /
UnregisterAuthenticationAgent.  This allowed an attacker:

- With CheckAuthorization, to cause the registered authentication
  agent in victim's session to pop up a dialog, or to determine whether
  the victim currently has a temporary authorization to perform an
  operation.

  (In principle, the attacker can also determine whether JavaScript
  rules allow the victim process to perform an operation; however,
  usually rules base their decisions on information determined from
  the supplied UID, so the attacker usually won't learn anything new.)

- With RegisterAuthenticationAgent, to prevent the victim's
  authentication agent to work (for a specific victim process),
  or to learn about which operations requiring authorization
  the victim is attempting.

To fix this, expose internal _polkit_unix_process_get_owner() /
obsolete polkit_unix_process_get_owner() as a private
polkit_unix_process_get_racy_uid__() (being more explicit about the
dangers on relying on it), and use it in
polkit_backend_session_monitor_get_user_for_subject() to return
a boolean indicating whether the subject UID may be caller-chosen.

Then, in the permission checks that require the subject to be
equal to the caller, fail on caller-chosen UIDs (and continue
through the pre-existing code paths which allow root, or root-designated
server processes, to ask about arbitrary subjects.)

Signed-off-by: Miloslav Trmač <mitr@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  /* every subject has a user */', '                                                                         subject,'], 'added_lines': ['  /* every subject has a user; this is supplied by the client, so we rely', '   * on the caller to validate its acceptability. */', '                                                                         subject, NULL,']}
description: A flaw was found in polkit before version 0.116. The implementation of the polkit_backend_interactive_authority_check_authorization function in polkitd allows to test for authentication and trigger authentication of unrelated processes owned by other users. This may result in a local DoS and information disclosure.

code_evidence: The function derives user_of_subject from the caller-supplied subject via polkit_backend_session_monitor_get_user_for_subject without any check that subject belongs to caller.

The derived user_of_subject is passed directly into polkit_backend_interactive_authority_check_authorization_sync together with caller and subject, so the authorization decision uses the client-chosen subject identity.
Temporary authorization lookup uses the same unchecked subject, allowing queries about another user's retained authorization.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs authorization-dependent work on a subject without verifying the caller is entitled to ask about that subject, i.e., a missing authorization check on the subject/caller relationship. This fits CWE-862 rather than mere spoofing, since no ownership constraint is enforced before acting.

evidence_lines.code:
implicit_authorization = polkit_backend_interactive_authority_check_authorization_sync (interactive_authority,
caller,
subject,
user_of_subject,
session_is_local,
session_is_active,
action_id,
details,
implicit_authorization);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: check_authorization_sync trusts the client-supplied subject and resolves its UID without validating that it matches the caller. Trigger: a local client submits a subject for another user. Consequence: the authorization agent is invoked for, and temporary authorization state is disclosed about, unrelated users' processes, enabling information disclosure and local DoS.

commit_msg:
Prevent division by 0 in LSH projection.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 387225857
Change-Id: Iaeb572a763618c64f503e0026f6dd9fd769bf50c
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  TF_LITE_ENSURE(context, SizeOfDimension(input, 0) >= 1);']}
description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. In affected versions an attacker can craft a TFLite model that would trigger a division by zero error in LSH [implementation](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/149562d49faa709ea80df1d99fc41d005b81082a/tensorflow/lite/kernels/lsh_projection.cc#L118). We have patched the issue in GitHub commit 0575b640091680cfb70f4dd93e70658de43b94f9. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.6.0. We will also cherrypick thiscommit on TensorFlow 2.5.1, TensorFlow 2.4.3, and TensorFlow 2.3.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: Input tensor is fetched and only checked for rank (NumDimensions >= 1); its first dimension SizeOfDimension(input, 0) is never constrained to be nonzero.
When weights are supplied, SizeOfDimension(weight, 0) is required to equal SizeOfDimension(input, 0), propagating the unconstrained zero-sized dimension into downstream shape/logic computations.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The patch adds TF_LITE_ENSURE(SizeOfDimension(input, 0) >= 1), confirming the prior absence of a zero-size guard on a dimension used in division. This directly matches CWE-369, where an unvalidated zero value reaches a divisor; it is not merely a bounds/validation issue (CWE-20) because the supported consequence is specifically division by zero.

evidence_lines.code:
TF_LITE_ENSURE_OK(context, GetInputSafe(context, node, 1, &input));
TF_LITE_ENSURE(context, NumDimensions(input) >= 1);

TF_LITE_ENSURE_EQ(context, SizeOfDimension(weight, 0),
SizeOfDimension(input, 0));

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The Resize path accepts an input whose leading dimension is zero, since only rank is validated. A crafted TFLite model can supply such a zero-sized dimension, which later participates as a divisor in the LSH projection computation, causing a divide-by-zero crash (DoS). The root cause is the missing nonzero-size constraint; the consequence is an availability failure.

commit_msg:
x86/vvmx: Disallow the use of VT-x instructions when nested virt is disabled

c/s ac6a4500b "vvmx: set vmxon_region_pa of vcpu out of VMX operation to an
invalid address" was a real bugfix as described, but has a very subtle bug
which results in all VT-x instructions being usable by a guest.

The toolstack constructs a guest by issuing:

  XEN_DOMCTL_createdomain
  XEN_DOMCTL_max_vcpus

and optionally later, HVMOP_set_param to enable nested virt.

As a result, the call to nvmx_vcpu_initialise() in hvm_vcpu_initialise()
(which is what makes the above patch look correct during review) is actually
dead code.  In practice, nvmx_vcpu_initialise() first gets called when nested
virt is enabled, which is typically never.

As a result, the zeroed memory of struct vcpu causes nvmx_vcpu_in_vmx() to
return true before nested virt is enabled for the guest.

Fixing the order of initialisation is a work in progress for other reasons,
but not viable for security backports.

A compounding factor is that the vmexit handlers for all instructions, other
than VMXON, pass 0 into vmx_inst_check_privilege()'s vmxop_check parameter,
which skips the CR4.VMXE check.  (This is one of many reasons why nested virt
isn't a supported feature yet.)

However, the overall result is that when nested virt is not enabled by the
toolstack (i.e. the default configuration for all production guests), the VT-x
instructions (other than VMXON) are actually usable, and Xen very quickly
falls over the fact that the nvmx structure is uninitialised.

In order to fail safe in the supported case, re-implement all the VT-x
instruction handling using a single function with a common prologue, covering
all the checks which should cause #UD or #GP faults.  This deliberately
doesn't use any state from the nvmx structure, in case there are other lurking
issues.

This is XSA-278

Reported-by: Sergey Dyasli <sergey.dyasli@citrix.com>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Cooper <andrew.cooper3@citrix.com>
Reviewed-by: Sergey Dyasli <sergey.dyasli@citrix.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['int nvmx_handle_vmxon(struct cpu_user_regs *regs)'], 'added_lines': ['static int nvmx_handle_vmxon(struct cpu_user_regs *regs)']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen 4.9.x through 4.11.x, on Intel x86 platforms, allowing x86 HVM and PVH guests to cause a host OS denial of service (NULL pointer dereference) or possibly have unspecified other impact because nested VT-x is not properly restricted.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function only adds 'static' to nvmx_handle_vmxon; it contains no NULL dereference, and the described flaw (uninitialized nvmx state making nvmx_vcpu_in_vmx return true) is not a NULL pointer dereference in this function.

commit_msg:
Fix copy length calculation in sdp_copy_raw_data

Test: compilation
Bug: 110216176
Change-Id: Ic4a19c9f0fe8cd592bc6c25dcec7b1da49ff7459
(cherry picked from commit 23aa15743397b345f3d948289fe90efa2a2e2b3e)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['      cpy_len -= 1;', '      uint8_t* old_p = p;', '      if ((int)cpy_len < (p - old_p)) {', '        SDP_TRACE_WARNING("%s: no bytes left for data", __func__);', '        return;', '      }', '      cpy_len -= (p - old_p);']}
description: In sdp_copy_raw_data of sdp_discovery.cc, there is a possible out of bounds write due to an incorrect bounds check. This could lead to remote code execution over bluetooth with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation. Product: Android Versions: Android-7.0 Android-7.1.1 Android-7.1.2 Android-8.0 Android-8.1 Android-9.0 Android ID: A-110216176

code_evidence: Line 16 derives cpy_len from remaining raw buffer space; line 18 points p at rsp_list. When offset is set (line 19), lines 20-21 advance p past the type/length header via sdpu_get_len_from_type, but cpy_len is not reduced by the header bytes consumed. Line 23 clamps cpy_len only against list_len, and line 26's rem_len check compares against SDP_MAX_LIST_BYTE_COUNT minus the header offset, not against the destination raw buffer. Line 36 then memcpy's cpy_len bytes into raw_data[raw_used], and line 37 advances raw_used.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs a bounded-by-intent copy into raw_data, but the incorrect length computation lets memcpy write beyond the destination buffer, which is precisely an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). It is not merely an out-of-bounds read or integer issue because the supported consequence is memory modification past the buffer end.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the copy length is not decremented by the header bytes consumed by sdpu_get_len_from_type, so cpy_len can exceed the bytes actually remaining in the destination raw buffer. Trigger: an SDP response with offset set and a length field that keeps cpy_len within list_len but beyond raw_size - raw_used. Consequence: memcpy at line 36 writes past the end of raw_data, corrupting adjacent memory and potentially enabling code execution, matching the reported remote OOB write.

commit_msg:
rgw:  make init env methods return an error

Since web frontends may signal an error when requests are malformed or so, let
us double check this and raise errors early. The current user of this is
civetweb frontend; which can potentially return null from `parse_http_headers`
when a HTTP header without a ":" is supplied at which point headers.value is
null which can lead to undefined behaviour later in RGW.

Fixes: http://tracker.ceph.com/issues/23039
Signed-off-by: Abhishek Lekshmanan <abhishek@suse.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['void RGWCivetWeb::init_env(CephContext *cct)', '    return;'], 'added_lines': ['int RGWCivetWeb::init_env(CephContext *cct)', '    // request info is NULL; we have no info about the connection', '    return -EINVAL;', '', '    if (header->name == nullptr || header->value==nullptr) {', '      lderr(cct) << "client supplied malformatted headers" << dendl;', '      return -EINVAL;', '    }', '', '  return 0;']}
description: In Ceph before 12.2.3 and 13.x through 13.0.1, the rgw_civetweb.cc RGWCivetWeb::init_env function in radosgw doesn't handle malformed HTTP headers properly, allowing for denial of service.

code_evidence: The loop reads header->name into a boost::string_ref and header->value without verifying either is non-NULL. name.size() then sizes a VLA at line 25 and value is passed to env.set at line 35; a malformed header lacking ':' yields NULL name/value, so string_ref construction and later operations dereference NULL.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits because the function dereferences header->name/header->value pointers that may be NULL for malformed input, with no NULL check before use. This is a direct NULL pointer dereference, distinct from mere improper input validation, since the concrete flaw is the unchecked NULL dereference.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: init_env assumes every civetweb mg_header has non-NULL name and value. Trigger: a client sends a malformed HTTP header without a colon, producing a NULL header->value (and possibly name). The unchecked string_ref construction, name.size() VLA sizing, and env.set call then dereference the NULL pointer, causing a crash/denial of service.

commit_msg:
nfc: fix NULL ptr dereference in llcp_sock_getname() after failed connect

It's possible to trigger NULL pointer dereference by local unprivileged
user, when calling getsockname() after failed bind() (e.g. the bind
fails because LLCP_SAP_MAX used as SAP):

  BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000000
  CPU: 1 PID: 426 Comm: llcp_sock_getna Not tainted 5.13.0-rc2-next-20210521+ #9
  Hardware name: QEMU Standard PC (i440FX + PIIX, 1996), BIOS 1.14.0-1 04/01/2014
  Call Trace:
   llcp_sock_getname+0xb1/0xe0
   __sys_getpeername+0x95/0xc0
   ? lockdep_hardirqs_on_prepare+0xd5/0x180
   ? syscall_enter_from_user_mode+0x1c/0x40
   __x64_sys_getpeername+0x11/0x20
   do_syscall_64+0x36/0x70
   entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x44/0xae

This can be reproduced with Syzkaller C repro (bind followed by
getpeername):
https://syzkaller.appspot.com/x/repro.c?x=14def446e00000

Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Fixes: d646960f7986 ("NFC: Initial LLCP support")
Reported-by: syzbot+80fb126e7f7d8b1a5914@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Reported-by: butt3rflyh4ck <butterflyhuangxx@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Krzysztof Kozlowski <krzysztof.kozlowski@canonical.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20210531072138.5219-1-krzysztof.kozlowski@canonical.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\tllcp_sock->dev = NULL;', '\t\tllcp_sock->dev = NULL;']}
description: net/nfc/llcp_sock.c in the Linux kernel before 5.12.10 allows local unprivileged users to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference and BUG) by making a getsockname call after a certain type of failure of a bind call.

code_evidence: llcp_sock->dev is assigned from the device at line 33, but on the service_name allocation failure path only llcp_sock->local is cleared (line 44) before jumping to put_dev; llcp_sock->dev remains set, so this path does not itself null the dev pointer.

On the LLCP_SAP_MAX failure path, llcp_sock->local and service_name are cleared (lines 51-53) but llcp_sock->dev is left set; the failed bind returns with the socket still LLCP_CLOSED while dev/local fields are inconsistent, enabling a later getname path to dereference a stale/NULL state.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The supported consequence is dereferencing a pointer expected valid but NULL after a failed bind, matching CWE-476. The defect is missing state cleanup enabling the NULL dereference, not a memory leak or race.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: failed bind error paths clear llcp_sock->local but do not consistently reset llcp_sock->dev, leaving socket state inconsistent after bind fails. Trigger: an unprivileged local user calls bind with LLCP_SAP_MAX (or triggers allocation failure), then calls getsockname/getpeername. Consequence: NULL pointer dereference in the getname path, causing a kernel BUG/DoS.

commit_msg:
In function con_insert_unipair(), when allocation for p2 and p1[n]
fails, ENOMEM is returned, but previously allocated p1 is not freed,
remains as leaking memory. Thus we should free p1 as well when this
allocation fails.

Signed-off-by: Gen Zhang <blackgod016574@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Kees Cook <keescook@chromium.org>
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tif (!p2) return -ENOMEM;'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (!p2) {', '\t\t\tkfree(p1);', '\t\t\tp->uni_pgdir[n] = NULL;', '\t\t\treturn -ENOMEM;', '\t\t}']}
description: An issue was discovered in con_insert_unipair in drivers/tty/vt/consolemap.c in the Linux kernel through 5.1.5. There is a memory leak in a certain case of an ENOMEM outcome of kmalloc. NOTE: This id is disputed as not being an issue

code_evidence: Line 8 allocates p1 via kmalloc_array and stores it in p->uni_pgdir[n]; lines 11-12 initialize its entries. Line 16 then allocates p2 = p1[n] and stores it in p1[n]. If that second kmalloc_array fails, line 17 returns -ENOMEM without freeing or clearing the previously allocated p1, so the p1 block remains referenced only through p->uni_pgdir[n] but the error path abandons it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-401 fits because the function fails to release allocated memory (p1) on an error path; the allocation is not freed after its effective lifetime ends, which is a missing-release memory leak rather than an out-of-bounds or use-after-free defect.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the error path after the p2 allocation failure returns -ENOMEM without releasing the p1 array allocated earlier in the same call. Trigger: a second kmalloc_array failure after p1 was successfully allocated. Consequence: the p1 allocation is leaked and the p->uni_pgdir[n] slot retains the stale pointer, consuming memory on repeated failures (resource exhaustion).

commit_msg:
Use document referrer policy when preloading

Previously, preload requests used the referrer policy from meta tags
encountered during scanning, but not from headers delivered with the
page. This CL uses the document's current referrer policy when the
preload scan starts.

BUG=605451

Review-Url: https://codereview.chromium.org/1913983002
Cr-Commit-Position: refs/heads/master@{#390264}
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    referrerPolicy = ReferrerPolicyDefault;'], 'added_lines': ['    referrerPolicy = document->getReferrerPolicy();']}
description: WebKit/Source/core/html/parser/HTMLPreloadScanner.cpp in Blink, as used in Google Chrome before 52.0.2743.82, does not consider referrer-policy information inside an HTML document during a preload request, which allows remote attackers to bypass the Content Security Policy (CSP) protection mechanism via a crafted web site, as demonstrated by a "Content-Security-Policy: referrer origin-when-cross-origin" header that overrides a "<META name='referrer' content='no-referrer'>" element.

code_evidence: The constructor hardcodes referrerPolicy to ReferrerPolicyDefault instead of deriving it from the document's actual referrer policy, so the preload scanner ignores the policy delivered via headers or meta tags.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The code fails to use the correct referrer-policy value (metadata) supplied with the document, effectively ignoring that input and applying an unsafe default; this is improper handling of input metadata rather than transformation or encoding, matching CWE-20.

evidence_lines.code: referrerPolicy = ReferrerPolicyDefault;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the cached document parameters discard the document's referrer policy and substitute a default. When a preload scan starts, the scanner uses this wrong policy, so a header-supplied policy (e.g. origin-when-cross-origin) is not honored and the meta no-referrer directive is bypassed. Consequence: referrer information leaks despite the page's stated policy, weakening CSP referrer protection.

commit_msg:
fbcon_get_font() is reading out-of-bounds. A malicious user may resize
`vc->vc_font.height` to a large value, causing fbcon_get_font() to
read out of `fontdata`.

fbcon_get_font() handles both built-in and user-provided fonts.
Fortunately, recently we have added FONT_EXTRA_WORDS support for built-in
fonts, so fix it by adding range checks using FNTSIZE().

This patch depends on patch "fbdev, newport_con: Move FONT_EXTRA_WORDS
macros into linux/font.h", and patch "Fonts: Support FONT_EXTRA_WORDS
macros for built-in fonts".

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Reported-and-tested-by: syzbot+29d4ed7f3bdedf2aa2fd@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Link: https://syzkaller.appspot.com/bug?id=08b8be45afea11888776f897895aef9ad1c3ecfd
Signed-off-by: Peilin Ye <yepeilin.cs@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Daniel Vetter <daniel.vetter@ffwll.ch>
Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/b34544687a1a09d6de630659eb7a773f4953238b.1600953813.git.yepeilin.cs@gmail.com
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (font->charcount * j > FNTSIZE(fontdata))', '\t\t\treturn -EINVAL;', '', '\t\tif (font->charcount * j > FNTSIZE(fontdata))', '\t\t\treturn -EINVAL;', '', '\t\tif (font->charcount * (vc->vc_font.height * sizeof(u32)) > FNTSIZE(fontdata))', '\t\t\treturn -EINVAL;', '', '\t\tif (font->charcount * j > FNTSIZE(fontdata))', '\t\t\treturn -EINVAL;', '']}
description: A buffer over-read (at the framebuffer layer) in the fbcon code in the Linux kernel before 5.8.15 could be used by local attackers to read kernel memory, aka CID-6735b4632def.

code_evidence: Width<=8 branch: j is vc_font.height and each iteration memcpy reads j bytes from fontdata, advancing fontdata by j across font->charcount iterations with no bound against the fontdata allocation size.
Width<=16 branch: same pattern with j = height*2, reading 2*height bytes per character from fontdata without validating charcount*j against the buffer size.
Width<=24 branch: inner loop reads fontdata[0..2] and advances by sizeof(u32) per row, for height rows per character, again with no range check.
Else branch: j = height*4 and memcpy reads j bytes per character, advancing fontdata by j for charcount iterations without bounds validation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads beyond the intended fontdata buffer, matching CWE-125 (out-of-bounds read). The missing FNTSIZE() range check is the cause; the read past the buffer is the weakness, not a write overflow (CWE-787).
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: vc_font.height (and derived j) is attacker-controllable and the loops copy charcount*height bytes from fontdata without checking against the actual font allocation size. Trigger: a malicious user sets vc_font.height large; the memcpy/direct reads in every width branch then walk past fontdata's end. Consequence: kernel out-of-bounds read copied into font->data, leaking kernel memory.

commit_msg:
debuggerd: verify that traced threads belong to the right process.

Fix two races in debuggerd's PTRACE_ATTACH logic:
  1. The target thread in a crash dump request could exit between the
     /proc/<pid>/task/<tid> check and the PTRACE_ATTACH.
  2. Sibling threads could exit between listing /proc/<pid>/task and the
     PTRACE_ATTACH.

Bug: http://b/29555636
Change-Id: I4dfe1ea30e2c211d2389321bd66e3684dd757591
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  char task_path[64];', '  snprintf(task_path, sizeof(task_path), "/proc/%d/task", pid);', '    if (ptrace(PTRACE_ATTACH, tid, 0, 0) < 0) {'], 'added_lines': ['  char task_path[PATH_MAX];', '  if (snprintf(task_path, PATH_MAX, "/proc/%d/task", pid) >= PATH_MAX) {', '    ALOGE("debuggerd: task path overflow (pid = %d)\\n", pid);', '    abort();', '  }', '    if (!ptrace_attach_thread(pid, tid)) {']}
description: debuggerd/debuggerd.cpp in Debuggerd in Android 5.0.x before 5.0.2, 5.1.x before 5.1.1, 6.x before 2016-09-01, and 7.0 before 2016-09-01 mishandles the interaction between PTRACE_ATTACH operations and thread exits, which allows attackers to gain privileges via a crafted application, aka internal bug 29555636.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function only lists /proc/<pid>/task entries and calls PTRACE_ATTACH on each tid; it contains no permission, privilege, or access-control check, and the described race (thread exiting between listing and attach) is not a CWE-264 permissions/privileges weakness.

commit_msg:
Merge pull request from GHSA-q9cp-8wcq-7pfr

description: PJSIP is a free and open source multimedia communication library written in C. A buffer overflow vulnerability in versions 2.13 and prior affects applications that use PJSIP DNS resolver. It doesn't affect PJSIP users who do not utilise PJSIP DNS resolver. This vulnerability is related to CVE-2022-24793. The difference is that this issue is in parsing the query record `parse_query()`, while the issue in CVE-2022-24793 is in `parse_rr()`. A patch is available as commit `d1c5e4d` in the `master` branch. A workaround is to disable DNS resolution in PJSIP config (by setting `nameserver_count` to zero) or use an external resolver implementation instead.

code_evidence: For type A, pj_memcpy copies 4 bytes from p into rr->rdata.a.ip_addr and advances p by 4 without checking p+4 against max.
For type AAAA, pj_memcpy copies 16 bytes into rr->rdata.aaaa.ip_addr and advances p by 16 without a bounds check.
For type SRV, three successive pj_memcpy calls copy 2 bytes each (priority, weight, port) and advance p by 6, with no check that 6 bytes remain before max.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function copies fixed-length input into record fields via pj_memcpy without verifying that the input buffer has enough bytes remaining, matching CWE-120's buffer copy without size checking. The added p+4, p+16 and p+6 guards confirm the missing constraint; this is a copy/bounds issue rather than a mere out-of-bounds read.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The prior length check at line 40 only ensures p + rr->rdlength <= max, but the fixed-size copies for A, AAAA and SRV records assume the remaining packet bytes suffice. A crafted DNS response with a small rdlength but a matching record type causes pj_memcpy to read past the packet buffer, resulting in a heap buffer over-read/overflow.

commit_msg:
Bug 689699: Avoid buffer overrun.

When cleaning a pdf file, various lists (of pdf_xref_len length) are
defined early on.

If we trigger a repair during the clean, this can cause pdf_xref_len
to increase causing an overrun.

Fix this by watching for changes in the length, and checking accesses
to the list for validity.

This also appears to fix bugs 698700-698703.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tint num, other;'], 'added_lines': ['\tint num, other, max_num;', '\t\t\tmax_num = fz_maxi(num, other);', '\t\t\tif (max_num >= opts->list_len)', '\t\t\t\texpand_lists(ctx, opts, max_num);']}
description: pdf/pdf-write.c in Artifex MuPDF before 1.12.0 mishandles certain length changes when a repair operation occurs during a clean operation, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (buffer overflow and application crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted PDF document.

code_evidence: Line 11 indexes opts->use_list[num] and opts->use_list[other] using num and other, whose bounds derive from xref_len captured at line 4 rather than the current list length.
Lines 62-65 write opts->renumber_map[num], opts->renumber_map[other], opts->rev_renumber_map[newnum] and opts->use_list[fz_maxi(num, other)] without validating these indices against opts->list_len.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs array reads and writes at indices that can exceed the buffer's intended boundary, matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds memory operation. The missing length check against opts->list_len is the direct cause; this is an out-of-bounds write rather than merely a NULL dereference or logic error.

evidence_lines.code: if (num == other || !opts->use_list[num] || !opts->use_list[other])

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the loops are bounded by the stale xref_len, but if a repair during cleaning grows the document, num/other can reach indices beyond the allocated renumber/use lists. Trigger: a crafted PDF that forces a repair while removeduplicateobjs runs, then duplicate objects with high indices cause out-of-bounds indexing; the consequence is a buffer overrun and crash.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\tiPinCount = iACLen - 1;\t\t'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\tiPinCount = iACLen > 0 ? iACLen - 1 : 0;']}
description: An issue was discovered in OpenSC through 0.19.0 and 0.20.x through 0.20.0-rc3. libopensc/card-setcos.c has an incorrect read operation during parsing of a SETCOS file attribute.

code_evidence: Line 24 derives iACLen from the low nibble of buf[iOffset]; the guard at 25 only checks iACLen > len, so iACLen can be 0 while len > 1.

In the else branch, line 88 computes iPinCount = iACLen - 1, which underflows when iACLen is 0. Line 107 decrements again if bit 0x20 is set, and the iPinCount > 0 test at 109 can then still be satisfied by the wrapped large value. Line 112 reads buf[iOffset + 2] and line 115 reads buf[iOffset + 1] without a re-check that these indices are within the remaining len; offset/len are advanced at 122-123 across iterations.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads bytes at computed offsets past the remaining buffer without validating that the index is within len, which is a read past the end of the intended buffer, matching CWE-125. The underflow is the trigger, not an arithmetic weakness per se; the observable weakness is the out-of-bounds read.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: When a parsed attribute has iACLen == 0 and the 0x20 flag set, iPinCount underflows (0-1, then -1) and the >0 branch is entered, causing reads of buf[iOffset+1] and buf[iOffset+2] even though the remaining length may not cover them. The root cause is the missing lower-bound/length constraint on iACLen and on the derived indices; the supported consequence is an out-of-bounds read of the attribute buffer, potentially leaking or crashing.

description: Buffer overflow in libxml2 allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code by leveraging an incorrect limit for port values when handling redirects.

code_evidence: When ctxt->port != 80, the header buffer size is increased by only 12 bytes (proxy) or 6 bytes (non-proxy).
The undersized header buffer is allocated with xmlMallocAtomic(blen).
The proxy branch formats the request line with the port number, writing into the allocated buffer.
The non-proxy branch formats the Host header with ctxt->hostname and ctxt->port.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-119 fits because the function performs writes into a heap buffer whose intended boundary is exceeded due to an incorrect size calculation for the port value. This is a direct out-of-bounds write on a memory buffer, matching the class description.

evidence_lines.code: bp = (char*)xmlMallocAtomic(blen);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the size estimate for the request/header buffer reserves a fixed 6 or 12 bytes for a port number, assuming a short port value. Trigger: a URL with a port number exceeding this reserved width (e.g., a large port, especially with proxy formatting) causes snprintf to write more bytes than blen accounts for. Supported consequence: memory outside the allocated buffer is written, leading to heap overflow and possible code execution or crash.

description: An issue was discovered in LibVNCServer before 0.9.13. libvncserver/rfbregion.c has a NULL pointer dereference.

code_evidence: sraSpanRemove dereferences span->_prev and span->_next without any NULL check; the function's parameter span is used unconditionally as the base of two chained pointer dereferences.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The code dereferences a pointer expected to be valid but potentially NULL, which is exactly CWE-476. The fix guards with if(span), confirming the missing NULL check rather than a different memory-safety issue.

evidence_lines.code:
span->_prev->_next = span->_next;
span->_next->_prev = span->_prev;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function assumes span is non-NULL and immediately reads span->_prev and span->_next. Trigger: a caller passes a NULL span (e.g., a span already detached from a region list). Consequence: NULL pointer dereference causing a crash/DoS, matching the commit's added null check.

description: Moonlight-common-c contains the core GameStream client code shared between Moonlight clients. Moonlight-common-c is vulnerable to buffer overflow starting in commit f57bd745b4cbed577ea654fad4701bea4d38b44c. A malicious game streaming server could exploit a buffer overflow vulnerability to crash a moonlight client. Achieving RCE is possible but unlikely, due to stack canaries in use by modern compiler toolchains. The published binaries for official clients Qt, Android, iOS/tvOS, and Embedded are built with stack canaries, but some unofficial clients may not use stack canaries. This vulnerability takes place after the pairing process, so it requires the client to be tricked into pairing to a malicious host. It is not possible to perform using a man-in-the-middle due to public key pinning that takes place during the pairing process. The bug was addressed in commit b2497a3918a6d79808d9fd0c04734786e70d5954.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function only formats a fixed-format SDP tail with sprintf and a constant version-dependent port; it performs no input-to-output buffer copy with attacker-controlled length, so it does not demonstrate the unchecked buffer copy required by CWE-120.

Count using ints instead of guint16s.

Make sure dissect_packetcable_ccc_option and

description: In Wireshark 2.2.0 to 2.2.3 and 2.0.0 to 2.0.9, the DHCPv6 dissector could go into a large loop, triggered by packet injection or a malformed capture file. This was addressed in epan/dissectors/packet-dhcpv6.c by changing a data type to avoid an integer overflow.

code_evidence: tlv_len, opt_len and sub_value are declared guint16 while off/sub_off are int; tlv_len is read from the packet via tvb_get_ntohs into this 16-bit type.
The outer loop condition off - voff < len uses the int off, which is advanced by opt_len + 4; opt_len carries the packet-controlled tlv_len.
In CL_OPTION_TLV5, tlv5_counter is incremented by tlv5_cap_len (a guint8 from the packet) and the loop runs while tlv5_counter < tlv_len, so counter accumulation can wrap.
In CL_OPTION_DOCS_CMTS_CAP, field_len accumulates tagLen + 2 in a loop bounded by field_len < opt_len, with tagLen taken from the packet.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The root cause is accumulation of packet-controlled values into finite-width integers that can wrap, matching CWE-190 (integer overflow/wraparound). The commit message itself states the fix changes data types to avoid integer overflow; the consequence here is a large loop/DoS rather than memory corruption, but the underlying weakness is the wraparound arithmetic.

evidence_lines.code:
guint16 type,
tlv_len, 
opt_len, 
sub_value;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Packet-controlled length fields (tlv_len, tagLen, tlv5_cap_len) are accumulated into counters/offsets whose types can wrap. When a counter wraps to a small or negative value, the loop condition remains true, so the dissector keeps iterating over the same region, consuming CPU until the capture is abandoned.

commit_msg:
There is a current use after free possible on a gatt server if a client
disconnects while a WriteValue call is being processed with dbus.

This patch includes the addition of a pending disconnect callback to handle
cleanup better if a disconnect occurs during a write, an acquire write
or read operation using bt_att_register_disconnect with the cb.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t\t\tstruct btd_device *device,', '\t\t\t\t\tconst uint8_t *value, size_t len,', '\t\t\t\t\tuint8_t link_type)', '\top = pending_write_new(device, chrc->pending_writes, attrib, id, value,', '\t\t\t\tlen, 0, link_type, false, false);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t\t\tstruct bt_att *att,', '\t\t\t\t\tconst uint8_t *value, size_t len)', '\top = pending_write_new(att, chrc->pending_writes, attrib, id, value,', '\t\t\t\tlen, 0, false, false);']}
description: An issue was discovered in gatt-database.c in BlueZ 5.61. A use-after-free can occur when a client disconnects during D-Bus processing of a WriteValue call.

code_evidence: acquire_write allocates a pending_op via pending_write_new bound to the caller-supplied device and stores it in chrc->pending_writes; the op holds pointers (device/attrib/value) that may be owned by the connection.

The op is then passed as user_data to g_dbus_proxy_method_call (AcquireWrite); if the D-Bus call is initiated, the function returns op and relies on later callbacks (acquire_write_reply/setup) to free it, but no disconnect callback is registered here to cancel/free the op when the client disconnects during processing.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function creates and hands off a heap object whose lifetime outlives the connection that owns its referenced data, with no disconnect cleanup registered; later callback use of that object after the connection teardown frees it is a use-after-free (CWE-416). This is not merely a missing NULL check; the defect is object lifetime vs. asynchronous D-Bus processing.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the pending_op created for an in-flight AcquireWrite D-Bus call has no lifetime tie to the ATT connection; if the client disconnects while the D-Bus method is being processed, the underlying device/ATT objects can be freed while op (and its stored pointers) remain referenced by the pending D-Bus callback. Trigger: a client disconnect concurrent with a WriteValue/AcquireWrite D-Bus operation. Consequence: the reply/setup callback later dereferences freed memory (use-after-free), enabling crash or memory corruption.

commit_msg:
In commit ee13cb249fab ("powerpc/64s: Add support for software count
cache flush"), I added support for software to flush the count
cache (indirect branch cache) on context switch if firmware told us
that was the required mitigation for Spectre v2.

As part of that code we also added a software flush of the link
stack (return address stack), which protects against Spectre-RSB
between user processes.

That is all correct for CPUs that activate that mitigation, which is
currently Power9 Nimbus DD2.3.

What I got wrong is that on older CPUs, where firmware has disabled
the count cache, we also need to flush the link stack on context
switch.

To fix it we create a new feature bit which is not set by firmware,
which tells us we need to flush the link stack. We set that when
firmware tells us that either of the existing Spectre v2 mitigations
are enabled.

Then we adjust the patching code so that if we see that feature bit we
enable the link stack flush. If we're also told to flush the count
cache in software then we fall through and do that also.

On the older CPUs we don't need to do do the software count cache
flush, firmware has disabled it, so in that case we patch in an early
return after the link stack flush.

The naming of some of the functions is awkward after this patch,
because they're called "count cache" but they also do link stack. But
we'll fix that up in a later commit to ease backporting.

This is the fix for CVE-2019-18660.

Reported-by: Anthony Steinhauser <asteinhauser@google.com>
Fixes: ee13cb249fab ("powerpc/64s: Add support for software count cache flush")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # v4.4+
Signed-off-by: Michael Ellerman <mpe@ellerman.id.au>

description: The Linux kernel before 5.4.1 on powerpc allows Information Exposure because the Spectre-RSB mitigation is not in place for all applicable CPUs, aka CID-39e72bf96f58. This is related to arch/powerpc/kernel/entry_64.S and arch/powerpc/kernel/security.c.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function only formats Spectre-v2 mitigation status text into a seq_buf for a sysfs attribute; it performs no sensitive-information handling and the missing link-stack-flush reporting is a mitigation-gap description issue, not an information exposure in this code.

commit_msg:
Fix issue #1616

This is a more comprehensive fix than #1617, it adds new functions to the API for getting/setting uint32 and uint64 settings.  Using these functions is preferable over calling `yr_(get|set)_configuration` directly.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        yr_get_configuration(YR_CONFIG_MAX_MATCH_DATA, &max_match_data));'], 'added_lines': ['        yr_get_configuration_uint32(YR_CONFIG_MAX_MATCH_DATA, &max_match_data));']}
description: A Buffer Overflow vulnerablity exists in VirusTotal YARA git commit: 605b2edf07ed8eb9a2c61ba22eb2e7c362f47ba7 via yr_set_configuration in yara/libyara/libyara.c, which could cause a Denial of Service.

code_evidence: max_match_data is read via yr_get_configuration into a uint32_t; new_match->data_length is set to yr_min(match_length, (int32_t) max_match_data), then a buffer of that length is allocated and match_data is memcpy'd into it with new_match->data_length bytes.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-120 fits because a buffer copy (memcpy at line 80) occurs without an independent check that the copy length is within the destination allocation; the size used for allocation (line 74) and copy (line 80) is derived from configuration rather than validated against the source. This is a classic buffer-copy sizing flaw, not an out-of-bounds read.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The destination allocation size derives from the YR_CONFIG_MAX_MATCH_DATA setting interpreted as int32_t, while the copy length comes from match_length (int32_t) via yr_min. If the configuration value is set inconsistently with the actual match length or exceeds the source buffer semantics, the copied length and allocated length can diverge, so memcpy at line 80 writes past the allocated notebook buffer. Trigger is a crafted configuration plus a match whose length exceeds the allocated data_length; consequence is heap corruption/DoS.

description: In FreeRDP before 2.1.0, there is an out-of-bound read in irp functions (parallel_process_irp_create, serial_process_irp_create, drive_process_irp_write, printer_process_irp_write, rdpei_recv_pdu, serial_process_irp_write). This has been fixed in 2.1.0.

code_evidence: Line 15 reads attacker-controlled PathLength from the IRP stream; line 16 checks only Stream_GetRemainingLength(irp->input) < PathLength and line 18 then seeks PathLength bytes. The pre-patch check does not account for the stream's own consumption/position semantics, so the subsequent Stream_Seek can advance past the buffer end.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads attacker-controlled length data and seeks based on it without a safe-bounds operation, matching CWE-125 out-of-bounds read. The fix replaces the check-and-seek with Stream_SafeSeek, confirming the unsafe read; this is not merely an integer overflow (CWE-190) but a direct reads-past-end issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the length guard compares remaining length against PathLength but the seek is performed unconditionally after a non-safe check, allowing the stream position to move beyond the intended buffer. Trigger: a crafted IRP with a PathLength exceeding the actual remaining data. Consequence: subsequent stream reads operate out-of-bounds (CWE-125).

This function is implemented using case-insensitive pattern matching,
unlike filesystem::ends_with(). I missed this when writing my original
fix, so the vulnerability still applied to .pbl files on a
case-insensitive filesystem (e.g. NTFS and FAT* on Windows) by using
different case to bypass the check.

description: The (1) filesystem::get_wml_location function in filesystem.cpp and (2) is_legal_file function in filesystem_boost.cpp in Battle for Wesnoth before 1.12.4 and 1.13.x before 1.13.1, when a case-insensitive filesystem is used, allow remote attackers to obtain sensitive information via vectors related to inclusion of .pbl files from WML.  NOTE: this vulnerability exists because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2015-5069.

code_evidence: The guard rejects filenames ending in ".pbl" using ends_with(filename, ".pbl"), a case-sensitive suffix comparison. description: DexLoader function get_stringidx_fromdex() in Redex prior to commit 3b44c64 can load an out of bound address when loading the string index table, potentially allowing remote code execution during processing of a 3rd party Android APK file.

code_evidence: Lines 24-28 only check that the header's file_size equals the actual dexsize; they do not validate the section-table quantities (string_ids_size, class_defs_size, offsets) against the file size.

description: A vulnerability was found in GPAC 2.3-DEV-rev35-gbbca86917-master. It has been declared as critical. Affected by this vulnerability is an unknown functionality of the file filters/load_text.c. The manipulation leads to buffer overflow. Local access is required to approach this attack. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue. The identifier VDB-223297 was assigned to this vulnerability.

code_evidence: szLineConv is a fixed 2048-byte stack buffer; the loop iterates over len bytes of the input line and, for each high-bit byte, may write one or two bytes into szLineConv without any bounds check on j before the fix.
After the loop, szLineConv[j]=0 and strcpy(szLine, szLineConv) copy the accumulated content; if j exceeded 2047 the terminator write and strcpy already wrote past szLineConv.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-120 fits: input-derived data is copied into a fixed-size destination without checking the output size, producing an out-of-bounds write. This is a classic buffer copy overflow, not merely an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) nor a size-calculation error (CWE-131).

evidence_lines.code:
szLineConv[j] = 0;
strcpy(szLine, szLineConv);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the conversion loop increments j for every encoded byte copied into the fixed-size szLineConv but never compares j against the buffer size. Trigger: a text input line (read via gf_fgets into szLine) long enough that its UTF-8 conversion exceeds 2048 bytes. Consequence: stack buffer overflow when writing szLineConv[j] and the subsequent strcpy, corrupting adjacent stack memory and potentially enabling code execution or crash.

commit_msg:
tun: call dev_get_valid_name() before register_netdevice()

register_netdevice() could fail early when we have an invalid
dev name, in which case ->ndo_uninit() is not called. For tun
device, this is a problem because a timer etc. are already
initialized and it expects ->ndo_uninit() to clean them up.

We could move these initializations into a ->ndo_init() so
that register_netdevice() knows better, however this is still
complicated due to the logic in tun_detach().

Therefore, I choose to just call dev_get_valid_name() before
register_netdevice(), which is quicker and much easier to audit.
And for this specific case, it is already enough.

commit_msg:
Ensure that EXFLAG_INVALID_POLICY is checked even in leaf certs

Even though we check the leaf cert to confirm it is valid, we
later ignored the invalid flag and did not notice that the leaf
cert was bad.

Fixes: CVE-2023-0465
Reviewed-by: Hugo Landau <hlandau@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Tomas Mraz <tomas@openssl.org>
(Merged from https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/20586)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        int i;', '        for (i = 1; i < sk_X509_num(ctx->chain); i++) {'], 'added_lines': ['        int i, cbcalled = 0;', '        for (i = 0; i < sk_X509_num(ctx->chain); i++) {', '            if ((x->ex_flags & EXFLAG_INVALID_POLICY) != 0)', '                cbcalled = 1;', '        if (!cbcalled) {', '            /* Should not be able to get here */', '            ERR_raise(ERR_LIB_X509, ERR_R_INTERNAL_ERROR);', '            return 0;', '        }', '        /* The callback ignored the error so we return success */']}
description:
Applications that use a non-default option when verifying certificates may be
vulnerable to an attack from a malicious CA to circumvent certain checks.

Invalid certificate policies in leaf certificates are silently ignored by
OpenSSL and other certificate policy checks are skipped for that certificate.
A malicious CA could use this to deliberately assert invalid certificate policies
in order to circumvent policy checking on the certificate altogether.

Policy processing is disabled by default but can be enabled by passing
the `-policy' argument to the command line utilities or by calling the
`X509_VERIFY_PARAM_set1_policies()' function.

code_evidence: In the X509_PCY_TREE_INVALID branch, the loop starts at i = 1, so the leaf certificate at chain index 0 is never examined for EXFLAG_INVALID_POLICY; only CB_FAIL_IF on non-leaf certs can report X509_V_ERR_INVALID_POLICY_EXTENSION. The function then unconditionally returns 1 (success), so an invalid leaf policy is silently ignored and the verification callback is never invoked for it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function fails to properly validate a certificate's policy extension, accepting an invalid leaf certificate as verified, which is improper certificate validation (CWE-295). It is not merely a logic bug: the missing check on the leaf directly defeats certificate validation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the invalid-policy scan skips the leaf certificate (loop begins at index 1) and then reports success. Trigger: a malicious CA issues a leaf with an invalid certificate policy while policy processing is enabled. Consequence: the invalid policy is not reported, policy checks are skipped for that certificate, and verification succeeds, bypassing the intended policy enforcement.

commit_msg:
HID: cp2112: fix sleep-while-atomic

A recent commit fixing DMA-buffers on stack added a shared transfer
buffer protected by a spinlock. This is broken as the USB HID request
callbacks can sleep. Fix this up by replacing the spinlock with a mutex.

Fixes: 1ffb3c40ffb5 ("HID: cp2112: make transfer buffers DMA capable")
Cc: stable <stable@vger.kernel.org>	# 4.9
Signed-off-by: Johan Hovold <johan@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Benjamin Tissoires <benjamin.tissoires@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Jiri Kosina <jkosina@suse.cz>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tunsigned long flags;', '\tspin_lock_irqsave(&dev->lock, flags);', '\tspin_unlock_irqrestore(&dev->lock, flags);'], 'added_lines': ['\tmutex_lock(&dev->lock);', '\tmutex_unlock(&dev->lock);']}
description: drivers/hid/hid-cp2112.c in the Linux kernel 4.9.x before 4.9.9 uses a spinlock without considering that sleeping is possible in a USB HID request callback, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (deadlock) via unspecified vectors.

code_evidence: The function acquires dev->lock with spin_lock_irqsave, disabling interrupts and holding a spinlock across the subsequent operation.
While holding that spinlock it calls hid_hw_raw_request, a USB HID request callback that may sleep.
The lock is only released at the exit label via spin_unlock_irqrestore, so the sleeping call executes with the spinlock held and interrupts disabled.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-404 covers improper resource release where a held lock is not made available for reuse because the acquisition/release discipline is violated by sleeping inside the critical section. The lock remains held during the blocking request, so other users cannot obtain or reuse it.

evidence_lines.code:
unsigned long flags;
spin_lock_irqsave(&dev->lock, flags);
spin_unlock_irqrestore(&dev->lock, flags);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The root cause is holding a spinlock, which forbids sleeping, across a call path (hid_hw_raw_request) that can block. Triggering this path lets the sleeping request occur under the spinlock, and since the same lock is not released until the request returns, the lock cannot be freed for reuse, producing a deadlock/DoS.

commit_msg:
guest_physmap_remove_page() needs its return value checked

Callers, namely such subsequently freeing the page, must not blindly
assume success - the function may namely fail when needing to shatter a
super page, but there not being memory available for the then needed
intermediate page table.

As it happens, guest_remove_page() callers now also all check the
return value.

Furthermore a missed put_gfn() on an error path in gnttab_transfer() is
also being taken care of.

This is part of XSA-222.

Reported-by: Julien Grall <julien.grall@arm.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Signed-off-by: Julien Grall <julien.grall@arm.com>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Cooper <andrew.cooper3@citrix.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    guest_physmap_remove_page(d, _gfn(iorp->gmfn),', '                              _mfn(page_to_mfn(iorp->page)), 0);'], 'added_lines': ['    if ( guest_physmap_remove_page(d, _gfn(iorp->gmfn),', '                                   _mfn(page_to_mfn(iorp->page)), 0) )', '        domain_crash(d);']}
description: Xen through 4.8.x does not validate memory allocations during certain P2M operations, which allows guest OS users to obtain privileged host OS access, aka XSA-222.

code_evidence: hvm_remove_ioreq_gmfn() calls guest_physmap_remove_page() but discards its return value, then unconditionally executes clear_page(iorp->va). The function never checks whether the P2M removal actually succeeded before treating the ioreq page as released.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-20 fits because the code omits validation of the operation result that signals an unsafe state; the missing check on the returned status is the root cause, and the consequence is that failure is not handled. This is improper validation of a required condition rather than a separate memory-corruption primitive.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: guest_physmap_remove_page() can fail when shattering a super page if no memory is available for the intermediate page table. Because the return value is ignored, the failure is not validated and the caller proceeds to clear_page() on a page whose P2M mapping may still be present, allowing stale/incorrect memory handling to go unnoticed instead of aborting the domain.

commit_msg:
[CVE-2017-0152] MSFT: 10592731 : Issue with Function name capturing in param scope

In a function expression with name, where the name is captured in one
of the param scope functions, if there is a function or var declaration
with the same name as the function expression name we were marking the
function expression name as shadowed. In non-eval case this causes
issue because the name symbol won't get added to the body. This change is to
fix it in such a way if the name is captured in the param scope then we
split the param and body scope such that the name symbol is added to the
param scope not body scope.

commit_msg:
Fix tf.raw_ops.EmptyTensorList vulnerability with invalid `element_shape`.

Check that given `element_shape` is valid.
Add graph/eager unit tests. Graph mode was already ok but eager mode was not.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 461906461
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  } else if (t.shape().dims() != 1) {', '    return errors::InvalidArgument("Shape must be at most rank 1 but is rank ",', '                                   t.shape().dims());']}
description: TensorFlow is an open source platform for machine learning. If `EmptyTensorList` receives an input `element_shape` with more than one dimension, it gives a `CHECK` fail that can be used to trigger a denial of service attack. We have patched the issue in GitHub commit c8ba76d48567aed347508e0552a257641931024d. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.10.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.9.1, TensorFlow 2.8.1, and TensorFlow 2.7.2, as these are also affected and still in supported range. There are no known workarounds for this issue.

code_evidence: TensorShapeFromTensor first branches on a scalar (rank-0) tensor via t.shape() == TensorShape({}). Inside that branch it only accepts the scalar value -1, otherwise returning InvalidArgument. The function then, for non-scalar tensors, dispatches to PartialTensorShape::MakePartialShape based solely on dtype (DT_INT32 at lines 12-14, DT_INT64 at lines 15-17), passing t.vec<int32>().data()/t.vec<int64_t>().data() together with t.NumElements(). There is no rank check on the non-scalar path before calling the vector accessor and MakePartialShape, so a rank>1 element_shape tensor reaches MakePartialShape.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is a reachable assertion triggered by attacker-controlled element_shape input, matching CWE-617: an assert/CHECK reachable via an unvalidated input leads to process exit (availability DoS). It is not merely an input-validation weakness (CWE-20) because the supported consequence is the assertion-driven crash.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function validates only the scalar case and never constrains the rank of a non-scalar element_shape tensor before invoking the vector accessor and PartialTensorShape::MakePartialShape. Trigger: an attacker supplies an element_shape with more than one dimension (rank>1) to EmptyTensorList in eager mode. Supported consequence: the downstream shape construction hits a CHECK/assert failure, aborting the process and causing a denial of service rather than returning a recoverable InvalidArgument status.

modify the skb as such (another error from prior). Now that we have the
number of fragments required, we can safely allocate exactly that amount

Fixes: c09440f7dcb3 ("macsec: introduce IEEE 802.1AE driver")

description: Heap-based buffer overflow in drivers/net/macsec.c in the MACsec module in the Linux kernel through 4.10.12 allows attackers to cause a denial of service or possibly have unspecified other impact by leveraging the use of a MAX_SKB_FRAGS+1 size in conjunction with the NETIF_F_FRAGLIST feature, leading to an error in the skb_to_sgvec function.

code_evidence: Line 13 sizes the scatterlist region using the fixed constant (MAX_SKB_FRAGS + 1) rather than the actual number of fragments needed for the skb. Line 14 allocates that fixed-size block, and lines 17-18 carve out *sg and *iv pointers into the same kmalloc buffer. If the required fragment count exceeds MAX_SKB_FRAGS+1, the scatterlist region is undersized.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-119 fits because the allocation size does not bound the subsequent scatterlist writes, so operations run outside the intended buffer boundary. A more specific child (e.g., CWE-122 heap-based buffer overflow) would be narrower, but the target CWE-119 correctly captures the out-of-bounds memory operation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the buffer for scatterlist entries is sized by a compile-time constant (MAX_SKB_FRAGS+1) instead of the runtime fragment count. Trigger: an skb needing more fragments (e.g., NETIF_F_FRAGLIST) is passed to skb_to_sgvec, which writes past the allocated scatterlist region. Consequence: out-of-bounds write into the shared kmalloc allocation, causing heap corruption/overflow and possible DoS or further impact.

Consequence: heap-based out-of-bounds write, memory corruption, and potential crash or code execution.

commit_msg:
KVM: x86: avoid calling x86 emulator without a decoded instruction

Whenever x86_decode_emulated_instruction() detects a breakpoint, it
returns the value that kvm_vcpu_check_breakpoint() writes into its
pass-by-reference second argument.  Unfortunately this is completely
bogus because the expected outcome of x86_decode_emulated_instruction
is an EMULATION_* value.

Then, if kvm_vcpu_check_breakpoint() does "*r = 0" (corresponding to
a KVM_EXIT_DEBUG userspace exit), it is misunderstood as EMULATION_OK
and x86_emulate_instruction() is called without having decoded the
instruction.  This causes various havoc from running with a stale
emulation context.

The fix is to move the call to kvm_vcpu_check_breakpoint() where it was
before commit 4aa2691dcbd3 ("KVM: x86: Factor out x86 instruction
emulation with decoding") introduced x86_decode_emulated_instruction().
The other caller of the function does not need breakpoint checks,
because it is invoked as part of a vmexit and the processor has already
checked those before executing the instruction that #GP'd.

This fixes CVE-2022-1852.

Reported-by: Qiuhao Li <qiuhao@sysec.org>
Reported-by: Gaoning Pan <pgn@zju.edu.cn>
Reported-by: Yongkang Jia <kangel@zju.edu.cn>
Fixes: 4aa2691dcbd3 ("KVM: x86: Factor out x86 instruction emulation with decoding")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Sean Christopherson <seanjc@google.com>
Message-Id: <20220311032801.3467418-2-seanjc@google.com>
[Rewrote commit message according to Qiuhao's report, since a patch
 already existed to fix the bug. - Paolo]
Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>

description: A NULL pointer dereference flaw was found in the Linux kernel’s KVM module, which can lead to a denial of service in the x86_emulate_insn in arch/x86/kvm/emulate.c. This flaw occurs while executing an illegal instruction in guest in the Intel CPU.

Trigger: a guest executes an instruction that hits a code breakpoint. Consequence: emulation proceeds with a stale context, leading to a NULL pointer dereference in x86_emulate_insn and guest-triggered host denial of service.

commit_msg:
Preserve GSS context on init/accept failure

After gss_init_sec_context() or gss_accept_sec_context() has created a
context, don't delete the mechglue context on failures from subsequent
calls, even if the mechanism deletes the mech-specific context (which
is allowed by RFC 2744 but not preferred).  Check for union contexts
with no mechanism context in each GSS function which accepts a
gss_ctx_id_t.

CVE-2017-11462:

RFC 2744 permits a GSS-API implementation to delete an existing
security context on a second or subsequent call to
gss_init_sec_context() or gss_accept_sec_context() if the call results
in an error.  This API behavior has been found to be dangerous,
leading to the possibility of memory errors in some callers.  For
safety, GSS-API implementations should instead preserve existing
security contexts on error until the caller deletes them.

All versions of MIT krb5 prior to this change may delete acceptor
contexts on error.  Versions 1.13.4 through 1.13.7, 1.14.1 through
1.14.5, and 1.15 through 1.15.1 may also delete initiator contexts on
error.

description: RADOS Gateway in Ceph 12.1.0 through 12.2.1 allows remote authenticated users to cause a denial of service (assertion failure and application exit) by leveraging "full" (not necessarily admin) privileges to post an invalid profile to the admin API, related to rgw/rgw_iam_policy.cc, rgw/rgw_basic_types.h, and rgw/rgw_iam_types.h.

Fix oobread in macho core symbolication ##crash

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tfor (i = 0; i < hdr->n_segments && cursor < end; i++) {'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tfor (i = 0; i < hdr->n_segments && cursor + sizeof (RCoreSymCacheElementSegment) < end; i++) {']}
description: Heap-based Buffer Overflow in GitHub repository radareorg/radare2 prior to 5.6.4.

code_evidence: The segment loop is bounded by `cursor < end` before reading, but each iteration dereferences `cursor` and reads 8 bytes at line 67, then advances by 8 at line 68; the loop condition only guarantees cursor points inside the buffer, not that 8 bytes remain.

`result->segments` is allocated for `hdr->n_segments` entries at line 59, and the loop at line 65 iterates up to `hdr->n_segments`, so the loop bound itself is consistent with the allocation; the out-of-bounds access is the buffer read past `end`.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The patch fixes an out-of-bounds memory access caused by a missing size check. However, the target is CWE-787 (out-of-bounds write), while the actual flaw is a read past the buffer end (an out-of-bounds read), so the function does not directly support an out-of-bounds write.

if (hdr->n_segments > 0) {
result->segments = R_NEWS0 (RCoreSymCacheElementSegment, hdr->n_segments);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the loop guard `cursor < end` fails to ensure a full 8-byte read fits before `r_read_le64(cursor)`. Trigger: a crafted CoreSymbolication header whose segment data places `cursor` within 8 bytes of `end`. commit_msg:
Fix heap OOB in `tf.raw_ops.RaggedGather`

PiperOrigin-RevId: 388355464
Change-Id: If14d96231d1cd7aad7c4d1c22c1bab1576b75717
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    DCHECK_GT(params_nested_splits_in.size(), 0);  // Enforced by REGISTER_OP.'], 'added_lines': ['', '    OP_REQUIRES(', '        context, params_nested_splits_in.size() > 0,', '        errors::InvalidArgument("params_nested_splits must be non empty"));', '', '    OP_REQUIRES(context, params_nested_splits_in[0].dims() > 0,', '                errors::InvalidArgument("Split tensors must not be scalars"));']}
description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. In affected versions if the arguments to `tf.raw_ops.RaggedGather` don't determine a valid ragged tensor code can trigger a read from outside of bounds of heap allocated buffers. The [implementation](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/8d72537c6abf5a44103b57b9c2e22c14f5f49698/tensorflow/core/kernels/ragged_gather_op.cc#L70) directly reads the first dimension of a tensor shape before checking that said tensor has rank of at least 1 (i.e., it is not a scalar). Furthermore, the implementation does not check that the list given by `params_nested_splits` is not an empty list of tensors. We have patched the issue in GitHub commit a2b743f6017d7b97af1fe49087ae15f0ac634373. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.6.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.5.1, TensorFlow 2.4.3, and TensorFlow 2.3.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: The input list params_nested_splits is fetched without verifying it is non-empty; the prior guard is only a DCHECK, which is compiled out in release builds.

Line 9 immediately indexes params_nested_splits_in[0] and calls dim_size(0) without confirming the split tensor has rank at least 1, so a scalar split or empty list leads to an out-of-bounds read of tensor shape data.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Reading dimension metadata of an empty list element or a scalar tensor accesses memory outside the intended buffer, matching CWE-125's out-of-bounds read. It is not merely an invalid-argument validation gap, since the unchecked index and dim_size access directly read out-of-bounds memory.

evidence_lines.code: DCHECK_GT(params_nested_splits_in.size(), 0);      SPLITS_TYPE num_params = params_nested_splits_in[0].dim_size(0) - 1;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the code dereferences params_nested_splits_in[0] and reads dim_size(0) guarded only by a DCHECK that is absent in release builds, and it never validates that the split tensor is non-scalar. Trigger: crafted RaggedGather arguments with an empty params_nested_splits list or a rank-0 split tensor. Consequence: an out-of-bounds heap read when the first dimension of the shape is accessed.

commit_msg:
patch 8.2.3923: Vim9: double free with split argument list in nested function

Problem:    Vim9: double free if a nested function has a line break in the
            argument list.
Solution:   Set cmdlinep when freeing the previous line.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t    if (*eap->cmdlinep == *line_to_free)', '\t\t*eap->cmdlinep = theline;']}
description: vim is vulnerable to Use After Free

code_evidence: The inner while loop obtains a continuation line via eap->getline() into theline, then at line 38 calls vim_free(*line_to_free) before line 39 assigns *line_to_free = theline. The pointer *eap->cmdlinep is not updated when the freed buffer is the same object it references; it continues to point at freed memory that is now reused by theline.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the code frees a buffer while a still-live pointer (*eap->cmdlinep) references it, and subsequent operations use that stale pointer. The patch's added reassignment confirms the dangling-reference pattern rather than a mere memory leak or out-of-bounds access.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: freeing *line_to_free without reconciling *eap->cmdlinep leaves a dangling pointer when both alias the same buffer. Trigger: a nested function whose argument list contains a line break, so getline() returns a new line and the previous line is freed. Consequence: later use of *eap->cmdlinep dereferences freed memory, enabling double free, crash, or memory corruption.

commit_msg:
i40e: prevent memory leak in i40e_setup_macvlans

In i40e_setup_macvlans if i40e_setup_channel fails the allocated memory
for ch should be released.

Signed-off-by: Navid Emamdoost <navid.emamdoost@gmail.com>
Tested-by: Andrew Bowers <andrewx.bowers@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Jeff Kirsher <jeffrey.t.kirsher@intel.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\tkfree(ch);']}
description: A memory leak in the i40e_setup_macvlans() function in drivers/net/ethernet/intel/i40e/i40e_main.c in the Linux kernel through 5.3.11 allows attackers to cause a denial of service (memory consumption) by triggering i40e_setup_channel() failures, aka CID-27d461333459.

code_evidence: Line 54 allocates ch via kzalloc; on failure the code jumps to err_free without a leak since nothing was allocated.
Line 61 calls i40e_setup_channel; when it returns false, line 62 sets ret and line 63 jumps to err_free, leaving the ch allocated at line 54 unreferenced.
The err_free label at lines 71-74 only frees the channel list via i40e_free_macvlan_channels; the just-allocated ch was never added to vsi->macvlan_list, so it is not released.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function allocates memory and fails to release it on an error path, matching CWE-401 (missing release of memory after effective lifetime). It is not a use-after-free or double-free, since the pointer is simply abandoned without being freed or dereferenced.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the error path after a failed i40e_setup_channel does not free the freshly kzalloc'd ch, which has not yet been linked into vsi->macvlan_list. Trigger: i40e_setup_channel returns false. Consequence: each failed setup iteration leaks a channel object, enabling memory-consumption DoS.

commit_msg:
There are multiple similar bugs implicitly introduced by the
commit c0cfa2d8a788fcf4 ("vsock: add multi-transports support") and
commit 6a2c0962105ae8ce ("vsock: prevent transport modules unloading").

The bug pattern:
 [1] vsock_sock.transport pointer is copied to a local variable,
 [2] lock_sock() is called,
 [3] the local variable is used.
VSOCK multi-transport support introduced the race condition:
vsock_sock.transport value may change between [1] and [2].

Let's copy vsock_sock.transport pointer to local variables after
the lock_sock() call.

Fixes: c0cfa2d8a788fcf4 ("vsock: add multi-transports support")
Signed-off-by: Alexander Popov <alex.popov@linux.com>
Reviewed-by: Stefano Garzarella <sgarzare@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Jorgen Hansen <jhansen@vmware.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20210201084719.2257066-1-alex.popov@linux.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tconst struct vsock_transport *transport = vsk->transport;'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tconst struct vsock_transport *transport;', '', '', '\t\ttransport = vsk->transport;']}
description: A local privilege escalation was discovered in the Linux kernel before 5.10.13. Multiple race conditions in the AF_VSOCK implementation are caused by wrong locking in net/vmw_vsock/af_vsock.c. The race conditions were implicitly introduced in the commits that added VSOCK multi-transport support.

code_evidence: The SOCK_STREAM branch reads vsk->transport into the local 'transport' at line 30, then acquires the socket lock at line 31. The local pointer is subsequently dereferenced via transport->stream_is_active/notify_poll_in (lines 35-39) and transport->notify_poll_out (lines 51-54), then the lock is released at line 68. Thus the shared transport pointer is sampled before the lock that is supposed to protect it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-667 fits because the lock is acquired but the shared resource (vsk->transport) is not properly protected: it is read before locking and used inside the critical section, violating the locking discipline. This is improper locking, not merely a missing NULL check.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: vsk->transport is copied outside the lock_sock() critical section, so a concurrent transport change (multi-transport support) can occur between the copy and the lock. Trigger: another thread swaps the vsock transport while vsock_poll runs. The stale local pointer is then used under the lock, calling through a transport that may be detached/unloaded, causing a race with potential use-after-free and local privilege escalation.

description: In FreeRDP before 2.1.0, there is an out-of-bound read in irp functions (parallel_process_irp_create, serial_process_irp_create, drive_process_irp_write, printer_process_irp_write, rdpei_recv_pdu, serial_process_irp_write). This has been fixed in 2.1.0.

commit_msg:
datasets: don't allow absolute or paths with directory traversal

For dataset filenames coming from rules, do not allow filenames that
are absolute or contain a directory traversal with "..". This prevents
datasets from escaping the define data-directory which may allow a bad
rule to overwrite any file that Suricata has permission to write to.

Add a new configuration option,
"datasets.rules.allow-absolute-filenames" to allow absolute filenames
in dataset rules. This will be a way to revert back to the pre 6.0.13
behavior where save/state rules could use any filename.

Ticket: #6118
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if (PathIsAbsolute(save)) {', '        return 0;'], 'added_lines': ['    int allow_absolute = 0;', '    (void)ConfGetBool("datasets.rules.allow-absolute-filenames", &allow_absolute);', '    if (allow_absolute) {', '        SCLogNotice("Allowing absolute filename for dataset rule: %s", save);', '    } else {', '        if (PathIsAbsolute(save)) {', '            SCLogError(SC_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT, "Absolute paths not allowed: %s", save);', '            return -1;', '        }', '', '        if (SCPathContainsTraversal(save)) {', '            SCLogError(SC_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT, "Directory traversals not allowed: %s", save);', '            return -1;', '        }']}
description: In Suricata before 6.0.13 (when there is an adversary who controls an external source of rules), a dataset filename, that comes from a rule, may trigger absolute or relative directory traversal, and lead to write access to a local filesystem. This is addressed in 6.0.13 by requiring allow-absolute-filenames and allow-write (in the datasets rules configuration section) if an installation requires traversal/writing in this situation.

code_evidence: SetupSavePath takes the rule-supplied 'save' filename and, when it is not absolute, builds a path by concatenating the configured data directory with 'save' via snprintf("%s/%s", dir, save) and copies it back into 'save'. The only pre-fix guard is PathIsAbsolute(save); there is no check for '..' traversal sequences before the joined path is written into the caller's buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-22 covers constructing a pathname under a restricted parent without neutralizing special elements such as '..' or absolute paths. Here the missing traversal check on rule-controlled input matches that pattern; the fix adds SCPathContainsTraversal and configurable absolute-path rejection. This is path traversal rather than mere path canonicalization because the input is external and the escape is the security-relevant effect.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the filename from an externally supplied rule is joined under the data directory without neutralizing '..' components, so the restriction to the parent directory is not enforced. Trigger: a rule provides a save filename containing '../' sequences. Consequence: the resulting path can resolve outside the intended data directory, allowing file write to attacker-chosen locations writable by Suricata.

commit_msg:
Bug 697015: Avoid object references vanishing during repair.

A PDF repair can be triggered 'just in time', when we encounter
a problem in the file. The idea is that this can happen without
the enclosing code being aware of it.

Thus the enclosing code may be holding 'borrowed' references
(such as those returned by pdf_dict_get()) at the time when the
repair is triggered. We are therefore at pains to ensure that
the repair does not replace any objects that exist already, so
that the calling code will not have these references unexpectedly
invalidated.

The sole exception to this is when we replace the 'Length' fields
in stream dictionaries with the actual lengths. Bug 697015 shows
exactly this situation causing a reference to become invalid.

The solution implemented here is to add an 'orphan list' to the
document, where we put these (hopefully few, small) objects. These
orphans are kept around until the document is closed.

description: An arbitrary memory read vulnerability in Asylo versions up to 0.6.0 allows an untrusted attacker to make a call to enc_untrusted_recvmsg using an attacker controlled result parameter. The parameter size is unchecked allowing the attacker to read memory locations outside of the intended buffer size including memory addresses within the secure enclave. description: In Wireshark 3.2.0 to 3.2.7, the GQUIC dissector could crash. This was addressed in epan/dissectors/packet-gquic.c by correcting the implementation of offset advancement.

code_evidence: tag_offset_start and total_tag_len are computed with unsigned 32-bit arithmetic from attacker-influenced tag_number and per-tag lengths. tag_len = offset_end - tag_offset can be negative when offset_end < tag_offset, yet tag_len is gint32 and added to unsigned total_tag_len (line 20), so the sum wraps. The function then returns offset + total_tag_len (line 105), which can wrap to a value <= offset.
