commit_msg:
Since 3e135cd499bf ("netfilter: nft_dynset: dynamic stateful expression
instantiation"), it is possible to attach stateful expressions to set
elements.

cd5125d8f518 ("netfilter: nf_tables: split set destruction in deactivate
and destroy phase") introduces conditional destruction on the object to
accomodate transaction semantics.

nft_expr_init() calls expr->ops->init() first, then check for
NFT_STATEFUL_EXPR, this stills allows to initialize a non-stateful
lookup expressions which points to a set, which might lead to UAF since
the set is not properly detached from the set->binding for this case.
Anyway, this combination is non-sense from nf_tables perspective.

This patch fixes this problem by checking for NFT_STATEFUL_EXPR before
expr->ops->init() is called.

The reporter provides a KASAN splat and a poc reproducer (similar to
those autogenerated by syzbot to report use-after-free errors). It is
unknown to me if they are using syzbot or if they use similar automated
tool to locate the bug that they are reporting.

For the record, this is the KASAN splat.

[   85.431824] ==================================================================
[   85.432901] BUG: KASAN: use-after-free in nf_tables_bind_set+0x81b/0xa20
[   85.433825] Write of size 8 at addr ffff8880286f0e98 by task poc/776
[   85.434756]
[   85.434999] CPU: 1 PID: 776 Comm: poc Tainted: G        W         5.18.0+ #2
[   85.436023] Hardware name: QEMU Standard PC (i440FX + PIIX, 1996), BIOS 1.14.0-2 04/01/2014

Fixes: 0b2d8a7b638b ("netfilter: nf_tables: add helper functions for expression handling")
Reported-and-tested-by: Aaron Adams <edg-e@nccgroup.com>
Signed-off-by: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tgoto err1;', '\t\tgoto err2;', '\t\tgoto err3;', 'err3:', 'err2:', 'err1:'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tgoto err_expr_parse;', '', '\terr = -EOPNOTSUPP;', '\tif (!(expr_info.ops->type->flags & NFT_EXPR_STATEFUL))', '\t\tgoto err_expr_stateful;', '\t\tgoto err_expr_stateful;', '\t\tgoto err_expr_new;', 'err_expr_new:', 'err_expr_stateful:', 'err_expr_parse:']}
description: net/netfilter/nf_tables_api.c in the Linux kernel through 5.18.1 allows a local user (able to create user/net namespaces) to escalate privileges to root because an incorrect NFT_STATEFUL_EXPR check leads to a use-after-free.

code_evidence: nf_tables_expr_parse parses the expression and populates expr_info; on failure it jumps to err1, skipping owner/ops cleanup.
After parse succeeds, the code allocates the expression via kzalloc using expr_info.ops->size without first verifying the expression type is stateful.
nf_tables_newexpr initializes the expression (calling ops->init) only after allocation; the stateful check is absent before this init path.
On error paths err3/err2, the code frees expr and releases ops, but the expression's init may already have bound a set for a non-stateful lookup expression.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function permits initialization of a lookup expression that leaves a set bound, leading to the set being freed while still referenced. This is exactly CWE-416: memory is reused after free, and subsequent operations on the stale set pointer are invalid. It is not merely a missing input check; the direct consequence is a dangling reference to freed set memory.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: nft_expr_init does not require NFT_EXPR_STATEFUL before allocating and initializing the expression via nf_tables_newexpr. Trigger: a local user creates a set element referencing a non-stateful lookup expression pointing to a set; ops->init runs and binds the set, but the set is not properly detached during destruction. Consequence: the set memory is freed while still referenced, producing a use-after-free (KASAN splat in nf_tables_bind_set), enabling memory corruption and privilege escalation.

commit_msg: Signed-off-by: Al Viro <viro@zeniv.linux.org.uk>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tstruct list_head *p, *q = &cursor->d_u.d_child;', '\t\tstruct dentry *next = list_entry(p, struct dentry, d_u.d_child);'], 'added_lines': ['\tstruct list_head *p, *q = &cursor->d_child;', '\t\tstruct dentry *next = list_entry(p, struct dentry, d_child);']}
description: The d_walk function in fs/dcache.c in the Linux kernel through 3.17.2 does not properly maintain the semantics of rename_lock, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (deadlock and system hang) via a crafted application.

code_evidence: Line 5 initializes the cursor list node q from cursor->d_u.d_child, while line 12 treats list entries as embedded at d_u.d_child; the rename_lock/d_lock-protected list operations at lines 10 and 25 (list_move) and the iteration at line 11 manipulate dentry list links.

Lines 8-9, 18-19, 23-24, 26, 29-30 show the dentry->d_lock held across the subdirectory list walk, with list_move(q, p) at line 25 under d_lock, so the list linkage and lock ordering are tied to the lock semantics.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The supported consequence is a denial of service via deadlock/hang from improper lock/resource handling, which fits CWE-400's availability impact of DoS. The code-level resource is the lock-held list traversal, not an allocation issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function walks and relocates dentry subdirectory list nodes under dentry->d_lock while relying on the list linkage/lock discipline. If the rename_lock semantics are not properly maintained by the surrounding d_walk logic, the readdir loop can contend on the dentry lock in a way that deadlocks, causing a system hang.

commit_msg:
AES: move look-up tables to .data section and unshare between processes

* cipher/rijndael-internal.h (ATTR_ALIGNED_64): New.
* cipher/rijndael-tables.h (encT): Move to 'enc_tables' structure.
(enc_tables): New structure for encryption table with counters before
and after.
(encT): New macro.
(dec_tables): Add counters before and after encryption table; Move
from .rodata to .data section.
(do_encrypt): Change 'encT' to 'enc_tables.T'.
(do_decrypt): Change '&dec_tables' to 'dec_tables.T'.
* cipher/cipher-gcm.c (prefetch_table): Make inline; Handle input
with length not multiple of 256.
(prefetch_enc, prefetch_dec): Modify pre- and post-table counters
to unshare look-up table pages between processes.
--

GnuPG-bug-id: 4541
Signed-off-by: Jussi Kivilinna <jussi.kivilinna@iki.fi>

commit_msg:
Jann Horn points out that our TLB flushing was subtly wrong for the
mremap() case.  What makes mremap() special is that we don't follow the
usual "add page to list of pages to be freed, then flush tlb, and then
free pages".  No, mremap() obviously just _moves_ the page from one page
table location to another.

That matters, because mremap() thus doesn't directly control the
lifetime of the moved page with a freelist: instead, the lifetime of the
page is controlled by the page table locking, that serializes access to
the entry.

As a result, we need to flush the TLB not just before releasing the lock
for the source location (to avoid any concurrent accesses to the entry),
but also before we release the destination page table lock (to avoid the
TLB being flushed after somebody else has already done something to that
page).

This also makes the whole "need_flush" logic unnecessary, since we now
always end up flushing the TLB for every valid entry.

Reported-and-tested-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Acked-by: Will Deacon <will.deacon@arm.com>
Tested-by: Ingo Molnar <mingo@kernel.org>
Acked-by: Peter Zijlstra (Intel) <peterz@infradead.org>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tbool need_flush = false;', '\t\t\t\t\t\t    old_end, old_pmd, new_pmd,', '\t\t\t\t\t\t    &need_flush);', '\t\t\t  new_pmd, new_addr, need_rmap_locks, &need_flush);', '\tif (need_flush)', '\t\tflush_tlb_range(vma, old_end-len, old_addr);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t\t\t\t    old_end, old_pmd, new_pmd);', '\t\t\t  new_pmd, new_addr, need_rmap_locks);']}
description: Since Linux kernel version 3.2, the mremap() syscall performs TLB flushes after dropping pagetable locks. If a syscall such as ftruncate() removes entries from the pagetables of a task that is in the middle of mremap(), a stale TLB entry can remain for a short time that permits access to a physical page after it has been released back to the page allocator and reused. This is fixed in the following kernel versions: 4.9.135, 4.14.78, 4.18.16, 4.19.

code_evidence: Line 8 declares need_flush, a deferred flag controlling whether a TLB flush occurs.
Lines 33-35 pass &need_flush into move_huge_pmd, which sets it when moving a huge PMD, but no flush is performed at that point.
Lines 50-51 pass &need_flush into move_ptes, which sets it when moving page-table entries, again deferring the flush.
Lines 53-54 perform the only flush_tlb_range, after the loop, keyed on need_flush, and after the destination page-table locks taken inside move_ptes are released.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-459 fits because the function fails to clean up (flush) the stale TLB mapping before releasing the lock protecting the moved entry, so temporary translation state is not removed before the resource is reused. This is a cleanup-ordering defect, not a plain missing-flush: the flush exists but occurs too late.

evidence_lines.code: bool need_flush = false;

move_ptes(vma, old_pmd, old_addr, old_addr + extent, new_vma,
new_pmd, new_addr, need_rmap_locks, &need_flush);

if (need_flush)
flush_tlb_range(vma, old_end-len, old_addr);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The root cause is that stale TLB entries for moved pages are only invalidated after the destination page-table lock is dropped; the flush is deferred until after move_ptes/move_huge_pmd release the lock. A concurrent operation such as ftruncate can then reuse the freed physical page while a stale TLB mapping still permits access, allowing read/write of the reused page.

commit_msg:
Fix segfault/heap buffer overflow in `{Experimental,}DatasetToTFRecord` where dataset is numeric.

Code assumes only strings inputs and then interprets numbers as valid `tstring`s. Then, when trying to compute the CRC of the record this results in heap buffer overflow.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 387675909
Change-Id: I7396b9b8afc1ac744112af7c0b1cd7bb41e0f556
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    components.reserve(finalized_dataset->output_dtypes().size());'], 'added_lines': ['    const int num_output_dtypes = finalized_dataset->output_dtypes().size();', '    if (num_output_dtypes != 1) {', '      return errors::InvalidArgument(', '          "ToTFRecordOp currently only support datasets of 1 single column, ",', '          "but got ", num_output_dtypes);', '    }', '    const DataType dt = finalized_dataset->output_dtypes()[0];', '    if (dt != DT_STRING) {', '      return errors::InvalidArgument(', '          "ToTFRecordOp currently only supports DT_STRING dataypes, but got ",', '          DataTypeString(dt));', '    }', '    components.reserve(num_output_dtypes);']}
description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. In affected versions the implementation for `tf.raw_ops.ExperimentalDatasetToTFRecord` and `tf.raw_ops.DatasetToTFRecord` can trigger heap buffer overflow and segmentation fault. The [implementation](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/f24faa153ad31a4b51578f8181d3aaab77a1ddeb/tensorflow/core/kernels/data/experimental/to_tf_record_op.cc#L93-L102) assumes that all records in the dataset are of string type. However, there is no check for that, and the example given above uses numeric types. We have patched the issue in GitHub commit e0b6e58c328059829c3eb968136f17aa72b6c876. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.6.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.5.1, TensorFlow 2.4.3, and TensorFlow 2.3.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: The loop fetches the next record into `components` and, when not done, calls `components[0].scalar<tstring>()()` and passes the result to `writer->WriteRecord`. There is no check that the dataset's output dtype is DT_STRING; `components[0]` may hold a numeric scalar (e.g., int64), and interpreting its buffer as a `tstring` yields a bogus length/pointer that `WriteRecord` then reads/writes out of bounds.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the unchecked type assumption leads to writing/reading memory beyond the intended buffer during record serialization. It is an out-of-bounds memory operation, not merely a type-confusion logic error.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the record retrieval path assumes every element is a string tensor without verifying `output_dtypes()`. Trigger: a dataset emitting numeric elements. The numeric buffer is reinterpreted as a `tstring`, so its length field is arbitrary; the CRC/write in `WriteRecord` reads past the allocated buffer, producing a heap buffer overflow and possible segfault.

description:
There is a logic error in io_uring's implementation which can be used to trigger a use-after-free vulnerability leading to privilege escalation.

In the io_prep_async_work function the assumption that the last io_grab_identity call cannot return false is not true, and in this case the function will use the init_cred or the previous linked requests identity to do operations instead of using the current identity. commit_msg:
magic.c: check for failure of RAND_[pseudo_]bytes

When magic() is implemented via libcrypto's RAND_bytes or
RAND_pseudo_bytes we should check for a failure and abort to
ensure we don't use a predictable session_id.

This prevents (further) weakening* of the TACACS+ protocol
"encryption" since session_id is an input to the algorithm.

*by modern standards TACACS+ is deemed "obfuscated" - RFC 8907.

+++ func_after
@@ -1,6 +1,12 @@

                         const char **argv) {
+
+/* Task ID has no need to be cryptographically strong so we don't
+ * check for failures of the RAND functions. If they fail then we are
+ * as well sending the accounting request regardless of whether any value
+ * was written to task_id.
+ */
 #if defined(HAVE_OPENSSL_RAND_H) && defined(HAVE_LIBCRYPTO)
 # if defined(HAVE_RAND_BYTES)
 	RAND_bytes((unsigned char *) &task_id, sizeof(task_id));

description: libtac in pam_tacplus through 1.5.1 lacks a check for a failure of RAND_bytes()/RAND_pseudo_bytes(). This could lead to use of a non-random/predictable session_id.

code_evidence: The session_id task_id is populated from RAND_bytes/RAND_pseudo_bytes (lines 6,8) without any check of their return value; the comment states failures are not checked. If those calls fail, task_id retains whatever value it had (or is left partially/entirely unwritten), so a non-random value flows into _pam_account as the TACACS+ session_id.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function supplies a security-relevant value (session_id) from an RNG whose failure is unchecked, yielding insufficiently random values, matching CWE-330. It is not merely CWE-252 because the missing check directly produces a predictable session_id used downstream.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the RAND_* return status is discarded, so a failed RNG call does not abort. Trigger: libcrypto RAND_bytes/RAND_pseudo_bytes returns failure. Consequence: a predictable or stale task_id is used as the session_id sent in the accounting request, weakening the TACACS+ obfuscation that depends on that value.

commit_msg:
sock_init_data() assumes that the `struct socket` passed in input is
contained in a `struct socket_alloc` allocated with sock_alloc().
However, tap_open() passes a `struct socket` embedded in a `struct
tap_queue` allocated with sk_alloc().
This causes a type confusion when issuing a container_of() with
SOCK_INODE() in sock_init_data() which results in assigning a wrong
sk_uid to the `struct sock` in input.
On default configuration, the type confused field overlaps with
padding bytes between `int vnet_hdr_sz` and `struct tap_dev __rcu
*tap` in `struct tap_queue`, which makes the uid of all tap sockets 0,
i.e., the root one.
Fix the assignment by using sock_init_data_uid().

Fixes: 86741ec25462 ("net: core: Add a UID field to struct sock.")
Signed-off-by: Pietro Borrello <borrello@diag.uniroma1.it>
Reviewed-by: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tsock_init_data(&q->sock, &q->sk);'], 'added_lines': ['\tsock_init_data_uid(&q->sock, &q->sk, inode->i_uid);']}
description: A flaw was found in the Linux Kernel. The tun/tap sockets have their socket UID hardcoded to 0 due to a type confusion in their initialization function. While it will be often correct, as tuntap devices require CAP_NET_ADMIN, it may not always be the case, e.g., a non-root user only having that capability. This would make tun/tap sockets being incorrectly treated in filtering/routing decisions, possibly bypassing network filters.

code_evidence: Line 12-13 allocates `q` as a `struct tap_queue` via `sk_alloc`, so the embedded `q->sock` is not part of a `struct socket_alloc`. Line 25 then calls `sock_init_data(&q->sock, &q->sk)`, which internally derives the containing `socket_alloc` via `container_of`/`SOCK_INODE` on this embedded socket.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The same memory object is allocated/initialized as `tap_queue` but accessed through a `socket_alloc`-based type interpretation, matching CWE-843. This is type confusion rather than a plain logic bug because the layout mismatch is what yields the wrong UID.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: `sock_init_data` assumes its `struct socket` argument belongs to a `socket_alloc` and computes the inode/uid from that assumed layout; here the socket is embedded in a `tap_queue` from `sk_alloc`. Trigger: opening a tap device reaches line 25. Consequence: the wrong field is read as `sk_uid`, hardcoding the socket UID (0/root), causing incorrect filtering/routing decisions.

commit_msg:
By validating length fields from server responses, out of boundary
accesses and endless loops can be mitigated.

Signed-off-by: Tobias Stoeckmann <tobias@stoeckmann.org>
Reviewed-by: Matthieu Herrb <matthieu@herrb.eu>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['SizeClassInfo(xAnyClassPtr *any, int num_classes)'], 'added_lines': ['SizeClassInfo(xAnyClassPtr *any, size_t len, int num_classes)', '                    if (len < sizeof(v))', '                        return 0;', '        if ((*any)->length > len)', '            return 0;']}
description: Multiple integer overflows in X.org libXi before 1.7.7 allow remote X servers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds memory access or infinite loop) via vectors involving length fields.

code_evidence: The size accumulator is computed as sizeof(XValuatorInfo) + (v->num_axes * sizeof(XAxisInfo)), where v->num_axes is an attacker-controlled length field from the server response. The multiplication and addition are performed without validating num_axes against a bound, so the computed value can wrap around before being passed to pad_to_xid and added to size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the defect is an unchecked arithmetic calculation on a length field that can produce an integer wraparound. The patch's added len bound checks address the related length-field validation, but the core arithmetic overflow in the size computation is the integer overflow weakness.

evidence_lines.code:
size += pad_to_xid(sizeof(XValuatorInfo) +
(v->num_axes * sizeof(XAxisInfo)));

commit_msg:
ath9k_htc: release allocated buffer if timed out

In htc_config_pipe_credits, htc_setup_complete, and htc_connect_service
if time out happens, the allocated buffer needs to be released.
Otherwise there will be memory leak.

Signed-off-by: Navid Emamdoost <navid.emamdoost@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Kalle Valo <kvalo@codeaurora.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\tkfree_skb(skb);']}
description: Memory leaks in drivers/net/wireless/ath/ath9k/htc_hst.c in the Linux kernel through 5.3.11 allow attackers to cause a denial of service (memory consumption) by triggering wait_for_completion_timeout() failures. This affects the htc_config_pipe_credits() function, the htc_setup_complete() function, and the htc_connect_service() function, aka CID-853acf7caf10.

code_evidence: Line 7 allocates skb via alloc_skb; line 18 passes it to htc_issue_send; lines 21-24 detect the wait_for_completion_timeout failure and return -ETIMEDOUT without freeing skb, while the err path at line 28 does free it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-401 fits because memory is allocated and then becomes unreachable on an exceptional return path without release. This is a missing-release leak, distinct from a use-after-free (CWE-416) where freed memory is reused.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The skb allocated at line 7 is not released on the timeout path (lines 22-24), so each timed-out htc_config_pipe_credits call leaks the buffer. Repeated timeouts exhaust kernel memory, supporting a denial-of-service consequence; the cause is the missing kfree_skb, not the timeout itself.

commit_msg:
unix: correctly track in-flight fds in sending process user_struct

The commit referenced in the Fixes tag incorrectly accounted the number
of in-flight fds over a unix domain socket to the original opener
of the file-descriptor. This allows another process to arbitrary
deplete the original file-openers resource limit for the maximum of
open files. Instead the sending processes and its struct cred should
be credited.

To do so, we add a reference counted struct user_struct pointer to the
scm_fp_list and use it to account for the number of inflight unix fds.

Fixes: 712f4aad406bb1 ("unix: properly account for FDs passed over unix sockets")
Reported-by: David Herrmann <dh.herrmann@gmail.com>
Cc: David Herrmann <dh.herrmann@gmail.com>
Cc: Willy Tarreau <w@1wt.eu>
Cc: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Suggested-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Hannes Frederic Sowa <hannes@stressinduktion.org>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\tfpl->user = NULL;', '', '\tif (!fpl->user)', '\t\tfpl->user = get_uid(current_user());', '']}
description: The Linux kernel before 4.5 allows local users to bypass file-descriptor limits and cause a denial of service (memory consumption) by leveraging incorrect tracking of descriptor ownership and sending each descriptor over a UNIX socket before closing it. NOTE: this vulnerability exists because of an incorrect fix for CVE-2013-4312.

code_evidence: When no list exists, a new scm_fp_list is allocated and count/max are initialized, but no owner/user accounting is recorded for the descriptors it will hold.
Each accepted fd is pinned with fget_raw and stored in fpl->fp with fpl->count incremented; these in-flight file references are not charged to the sending process's user_struct.
The function returns num after copying descriptors, so the in-flight references persist beyond the call without ownership accounting.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-399 covers improper management of system resources; the missing owner accounting lets in-flight fds escape the sender's limit, directly supporting resource exhaustion. This is an accounting/ownership defect rather than a mere memory-safety bug.

evidence_lines.code: return num;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: scm_fp_copy stores file references from fget_raw without attributing them to the sending process's resource owner. Trigger: a local sender repeatedly passes descriptors over a UNIX socket and closes them. Consequence: the descriptors remain in flight and are not counted against the sender, so file-descriptor/resource limits can be bypassed, enabling resource exhaustion and denial of service.

commit_msg:
The code now checks for consistency of the MCU sizes across
hierarchical levels, and fails in case they are different.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['      if (m_pLargestScale) {', '        class Frame *frame = m_pLargestScale->FrameOf();', '        while(frame) {', '          if (frame->ComponentOf(i)->SubXOf() != sx || frame->ComponentOf(i)->SubYOf() != sy)', '            JPG_THROW(MALFORMED_STREAM,"HierarchicalBitmapRequester::PrepareForDecoding",', '                      "component subsampling is inconsistent across hierarchical levels");', '          frame = frame->NextOf();', '        }', '      }', '']}
description: libjpeg 1.63 has a heap-based buffer over-read in HierarchicalBitmapRequester::FetchRegion in hierarchicalbitmaprequester.cpp because the MCU size can be different between allocation and use.

code_evidence: The loop iterates over each component, reading its subsampling factors sx and sy from m_pFrame->ComponentOf(i), then uses these values to create an upsampler sized with m_ulPixelWidth/m_ulPixelHeight and mark m_bSubsampling.

The subsampling factors read here come from the current frame's component, but the allocated MCU/upsampler buffers are sized from these per-component values; if another hierarchical level declares different SubXOf/SubYOf for the same component index, the allocation and later use disagree.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The described consequence is reading data beyond an intended buffer, matching CWE-125. The inconsistency is the enabling condition, but the supported weakness is the out-of-bounds read rather than a pure input-validation flaw.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function derives upsampler/MCU geometry from one frame's component subsampling without verifying consistency against other hierarchical frames. Trigger: a malformed hierarchical JPEG where SubXOf/SubYOf differ between allocation and use levels. This allows later region fetches to read past the allocated MCU buffer, producing an out-of-bounds read.

commit_msg: Fix crash when mapping a big memory and calling uc_close
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if (QLIST_EMPTY(&uc->ram_list.blocks)) {'], 'added_lines': ['    if (QLIST_EMPTY_RCU(&uc->ram_list.blocks)) {']}
description: Unicorn Engine v2.0.0-rc7 and below was discovered to contain a NULL pointer dereference via qemu_ram_free.

code_evidence: The function checks QLIST_EMPTY(&uc->ram_list.blocks) without RCU read-side protection, then returns 0 when the list appears empty. Under concurrent teardown (uc_close freeing RAM blocks via qemu_ram_free), this non-RCU emptiness test can observe a transient/inconsistent list state rather than the RCU-protected view.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The patch replaces QLIST_EMPTY with QLIST_EMPTY_RCU, indicating the defect enables a NULL/stale pointer dereference during concurrent RAM block freeing, matching CWE-476. It is not merely a race condition label because the demonstrable impact is dereferencing an invalid block pointer.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the list emptiness/iteration is performed with the non-RCU QLIST_EMPTY macro despite the list being concurrently modified and freed under RCU. Trigger: mapping a large memory then calling uc_close causes RAM blocks to be freed while find_ram_offset traverses the list, so a stale or NULL block pointer is dereferenced. Supported consequence: NULL pointer dereference leading to a crash (availability DoS).

commit_msg: Fix 697401: Error when dropping extra arguments to lightweight functions.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tjs_pop(J, F->numparams - n);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tjs_pop(J, n - F->numparams);']}
description: Heap-based buffer overflow in the js_stackoverflow function in jsrun.c in Artifex Software, Inc. MuJS allows attackers to have unspecified impact by leveraging an error when dropping extra arguments to lightweight functions.

code_evidence: When the argument count n exceeds F->numparams, the code calls js_pop with F->numparams - n. Because n > F->numparams, this subtraction is negative, so js_pop receives a negative pop count instead of the intended positive number of extra arguments to discard.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The incorrect negative pop count drives stack-pointer manipulation beyond the intended buffer boundary, matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds memory operation. The defect is an out-of-bounds stack adjustment, not merely an integer sign error; the reversed subtraction is the cause, and the out-of-bounds access is the supported consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the operand order of the subtraction is reversed, producing a negative count. Trigger: calling a lightweight function with more arguments than its formal parameters. Consequence: js_pop operates on a negative stack offset, moving the stack pointer outside the intended buffer region and enabling the reported heap-based buffer overflow.

commit_msg:
Correctly load/initialize classes when using ConstantPool

- do not load classes in the "ifLoaded" calls
- never intitialize classes in the natives
- do not update the constant pool when querying from the natives

Fixes: #12016

[ci skip]

Signed-off-by: Graham Chapman <graham_chapman@ca.ibm.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\tif (ramCPEntry != NULL) {'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\tif ((NULL != ramCPEntry) && J9_ARE_NO_BITS_SET(resolveFlags, J9_RESOLVE_FLAG_NO_CP_UPDATE)) {']}
description: In Eclipse Openj9 to version 0.25.0, usage of the jdk.internal.reflect.ConstantPool API causes the JVM in some cases to pre-resolve certain constant pool entries. This allows a user to call static methods or access static members without running the class initialization method, and may allow a user to observe uninitialized values.

code_evidence: The guard at line 143 previously wrote resolved field data into ramCPEntry whenever the entry was non-NULL. The patch adds J9_ARE_NO_BITS_SET(resolveFlags, J9_RESOLVE_FLAG_NO_CP_UPDATE) so callers that must not update the constant pool skip this block. Inside, lines 162-168 set J9FieldFlagResolved, valueOffset and flags on the RAM constant pool entry.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-909 fits: the RAM constant pool entry, a resource expected to be initialized only through proper resolution/class-init flow, was populated and flagged resolved prematurely, bypassing initialization. This is a missing initialization constraint on the resource's lifecycle, not merely a visibility or access-control flaw.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: When a no-CP-update resolve (e.g., reflective ConstantPool access) was requested, the function still marked the RAM field ref resolved and stored offset/flags, pre-resolving the entry. Callers relying on resolution semantics could then access the field/static member without triggering class initialization, observing uninitialized values. The fix prevents the premature state write that made the entry appear initialized.

commit_msg:
tty: Fix unsafe ldisc reference via ioctl(TIOCGETD)

ioctl(TIOCGETD) retrieves the line discipline id directly from the
ldisc because the line discipline id (c_line) in termios is untrustworthy;
userspace may have set termios via ioctl(TCSETS*) without actually
changing the line discipline via ioctl(TIOCSETD).

However, directly accessing the current ldisc via tty->ldisc is
unsafe; the ldisc ptr dereferenced may be stale if the line discipline
is changing via ioctl(TIOCSETD) or hangup.

Wait for the line discipline reference (just like read() or write())
to retrieve the "current" line discipline id.

Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Peter Hurley <peter@hurleysoftware.com>
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

description: Race condition in the tty_ioctl function in drivers/tty/tty_io.c in the Linux kernel through 4.4.1 allows local users to obtain sensitive information from kernel memory or cause a denial of service (use-after-free and system crash) by making a TIOCGETD ioctl call during processing of a TIOCSETD ioctl call.

commit_msg:
Fixed recursive async function calls.

Previously, PromiseCapability record was stored (function->context)
directly in function object during a function invocation.  This is
not correct, because PromiseCapability record should be linked to
current execution context.  As a result, function->context is
overwritten with consecutive recursive calls which results in
use-after-free.

This closes #451 issue on Github.

description: ext/spl/spl_array.c in PHP before 5.6.26 and 7.x before 7.0.11 proceeds with SplArray unserialization without validating a return value and data type, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service or possibly have unspecified other impact via crafted serialized data.

commit_msg:
fs: limit filesystem stacking depth

Add a simple read-only counter to super_block that indicates how deep this
is in the stack of filesystems.  Previously ecryptfs was the only stackable
filesystem and it explicitly disallowed multiple layers of itself.

Overlayfs, however, can be stacked recursively and also may be stacked
on top of ecryptfs or vice versa.

To limit the kernel stack usage we must limit the depth of the
filesystem stack.  Initially the limit is set to 2.

Signed-off-by: Miklos Szeredi <mszeredi@suse.cz>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\tsb->s_stack_depth = max(upperpath.mnt->mnt_sb->s_stack_depth,', '\t\t\t\tlowerpath.mnt->mnt_sb->s_stack_depth) + 1;', '', '\terr = -EINVAL;', '\tif (sb->s_stack_depth > FILESYSTEM_MAX_STACK_DEPTH) {', '\t\tpr_err("overlayfs: maximum fs stacking depth exceeded\\n");', '\t\tgoto out_put_workpath;', '\t}']}
description: The eCryptfs subsystem in the Linux kernel before 3.18 allows local users to gain privileges via a large filesystem stack that includes an overlayfs layer, related to fs/ecryptfs/main.c and fs/overlayfs/super.c.

code_evidence: After vfs_statfs on lowerpath, ufs->lower_namelen is set and upper/lower private mounts are cloned without any check on the super_block stack depth of the underlying filesystems (upperpath.mnt->mnt_sb and lowerpath.mnt->mnt_sb). The added diff computes sb->s_stack_depth from those mount superblocks and rejects depths above FILESYSTEM_MAX_STACK_DEPTH, showing the pre-patch function permitted arbitrarily deep stacking.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-264 covers weaknesses in management of permissions/privileges and other security features used for access control; here the missing stacking-depth limit is a security-policy enforcement gap that lets a local user bypass intended filesystem layering restrictions and gain privileges. It is not merely a memory-safety defect, since the unsafe condition is an unenforced resource/privilege boundary.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: ovl_fill_super accepts lower/upper mounts without constraining how many filesystem layers already sit beneath them, so a user can recursively stack overlayfs (possibly atop ecryptfs). Trigger: mounting with deeply nested lowerdir/upperdir paths. Supported consequence: unbounded kernel stack consumption during nested filesystem operations, which the commit describes as enabling local privilege escalation; the depth counter and EINVAL check are the missing constraint.

commit_msg:
x86/vpt: fix race when migrating timers between vCPUs

The current vPT code will migrate the emulated timers between vCPUs
(change the pt->vcpu field) while just holding the destination lock,
either from create_periodic_time or pt_adjust_global_vcpu_target if
the global target is adjusted. Changing the periodic_timer vCPU field
in this way creates a race where a third party could grab the lock in
the unlocked region of pt_adjust_global_vcpu_target (or before
create_periodic_time performs the vcpu change) and then release the
lock from a different vCPU, creating a locking imbalance.

Introduce a per-domain rwlock in order to protect periodic_time
migration between vCPU lists. Taking the lock in read mode prevents
any timer from being migrated to a different vCPU, while taking it in
write mode allows performing migration of timers across vCPUs. The
per-vcpu locks are still used to protect all the other fields from the
periodic_timer struct.

Note that such migration shouldn't happen frequently, and hence
there's no performance drop as a result of such locking.

This is XSA-336.

Reported-by: Igor Druzhinin <igor.druzhinin@citrix.com>
Tested-by: Igor Druzhinin <igor.druzhinin@citrix.com>
Signed-off-by: Roger Pau Monné <roger.pau@citrix.com>
Reviewed-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    spin_lock(&v->arch.hvm.tm_lock);', '        spin_unlock(&v->arch.hvm.tm_lock);', '    spin_unlock(&v->arch.hvm.tm_lock);', '                spin_lock(&v->arch.hvm.tm_lock);', '                spin_unlock(&v->arch.hvm.tm_lock);'], 'added_lines': ['    pt_vcpu_lock(v);', '        pt_vcpu_unlock(v);', '    pt_vcpu_unlock(v);', '                pt_vcpu_lock(v);', '                pt_vcpu_unlock(v);']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.14.x. There is a race condition when migrating timers between x86 HVM vCPUs. When migrating timers of x86 HVM guests between its vCPUs, the locking model used allows for a second vCPU of the same guest (also operating on the timers) to release a lock that it didn't acquire. The most likely effect of the issue is a hang or crash of the hypervisor, i.e., a Denial of Service (DoS). All versions of Xen are affected. Only x86 systems are vulnerable. Arm systems are not vulnerable. Only x86 HVM guests can leverage the vulnerability. x86 PV and PVH cannot leverage the vulnerability. Only guests with more than one vCPU can exploit the vulnerability.

code_evidence: pt_update_irq acquires the per-vCPU timer lock v->arch.hvm.tm_lock at entry, releases it at line 39, then re-acquires it at line 67 and releases it at 76 while still operating on the shared tm_list and earliest_pt. The timer list is walked and earliest_pt is located and dereferenced under the lock, but the vCPU association of timers can be changed concurrently by pt_adjust_global_vcpu_target or create_periodic_time under only the destination vCPU lock.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The code sequence requires exclusive access to the shared timer list and earliest_pt, but the per-vCPU lock does not prevent concurrent migration modifying that resource, matching CWE-362's non-exclusive concurrent access. It is a synchronization race, not merely a missing lock, since locking exists but is scoped incorrectly.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The lock is per-vCPU while the timer list is shared across vCPUs during migration; a timer can be moved between lists in the unlocked region, so a second vCPU may later release a lock it did not acquire, causing locking imbalance. Trigger is concurrent timer migration during pt_update_irq; consequence is hypervisor hang or crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
WireGuard: fix null pointer crash

It was assumed that the WireGuard dissector is always called on the
first pass before the second pass. That might not be the case when the
heuristics dissector sets a conversation dissector later in the stream.
Be prepared to handle this case. Do not simply abort, the previous
packets may be valid data messages.

This issue affects Apache OpenOffice up to and including version 4.1.10

code_evidence: nLen derives from m_aRealFieldLengths[i] and is used to compute pData = m_pBuffer + nByteOffset; the TIMESTAMP branch copies fixed 8 bytes (two memcpy of 4) regardless of nLen.
The INTEGER branch takes nLen as the copy length into pData via memcpy(&nValue,nLen), so an oversized nLen writes past the field's buffer slot.
The DOUBLE branch copies 8 bytes of d into pData using nLen, again without validating nLen against the destination size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs buffer copies (memcpy into pData) without checking that the input length nLen is within the destination buffer size, matching CWE-120's buffer-copy-without-size-check pattern. It is not merely an out-of-bounds read; the write past the buffer end is the core weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Field length nLen comes from document metadata (m_aRealFieldLengths) and is trusted. In the TIMESTAMP/INTEGER/DOUBLE cases, memcpy writes into pData located in m_pBuffer without confirming nLen fits the allocated slot, so a crafted DBF field length causes a heap/stack buffer overflow that can overwrite adjacent memory and potentially redirect execution.

commit_msg:
mlx4_en: Fix out of bounds array access

When searching for a free entry in either mlx4_register_vlan() or
mlx4_register_mac(), and there is no free entry, the loop terminates without
updating the local variable free thus causing out of array bounds access. Fix
this by adding a proper check outside the loop.

Signed-off-by: Eli Cohen <eli@mellanox.co.il>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\tif (free < 0) {', '\t\terr = -ENOMEM;', '\t\tgoto out;', '\t}', '']}
description: In the Linux kernel before 2.6.37, an out of bounds array access happened in drivers/net/mlx4/port.c. When searching for a free entry in either mlx4_register_vlan() or mlx4_register_mac(), and there is no free entry, the loop terminates without updating the local variable free thus causing out of array bounds access.

code_evidence: free is initialized to -1 and only set inside the loop when an unused refs slot is found; the loop bound is MLX4_MAX_MAC_NUM - 1.
If no free slot exists and no matching MAC is found, free remains -1, yet the code proceeds to index table->refs[free] and table->entries[free].
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs reads/writes on table->refs and table->entries using an unvalidated index (free = -1), an out-of-bounds memory buffer operation matching CWE-119. This is an indexing/bounds defect rather than a simple null dereference or type confusion.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the search loop can terminate without assigning free, leaving it at the sentinel -1. Trigger: a table with no free entry and no matching MAC reaches the indexing after the total/max check. Consequence: array accesses at index -1 write outside the intended mac_table array bounds.

commit_msg:
Fixes CVE-2023-3138: X servers could return values from XQueryExtension
that would cause Xlib to write entries out-of-bounds of the arrays to
store them, though this would only overwrite other parts of the Display
struct, not outside the bounds allocated for that structure.

Reported-by: Gregory James DUCK <gjduck@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Alan Coopersmith <alan.coopersmith@oracle.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tif (event_number < 0 ||', '\t    event_number > LastExtensionEvent) {', '\t    fprintf(stderr, "Xlib: ignoring invalid extension event %d\\n",', '\t\t    event_number);', '\t    return (WireToEventType)_XUnknownWireEvent;', '\t}']}
description: A vulnerability was found in libX11. The security flaw occurs because the functions in src/InitExt.c in libX11 do not check that the values provided for the Request, Event, or Error IDs are within the bounds of the arrays that those functions write to, using those IDs as array indexes. They trust that they were called with values provided by an Xserver adhering to the bounds specified in the X11 protocol, as all X servers provided by X.Org do. As the protocol only specifies a single byte for these values, an out-of-bounds value provided by a malicious server (or a malicious proxy-in-the-middle) can only overwrite other portions of the Display structure and not write outside the bounds of the Display structure itself, possibly causing the client to crash with this memory corruption.

code_evidence: event_number is used directly as an index into dpy->event_vec for both reading (line 9) and writing (line 10) without any bounds check; the patched version adds a check for event_number < 0 or > LastExtensionEvent before these accesses.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked index at line 10 performs an out-of-bounds write into event_vec, matching CWE-787 (write past the intended buffer). The read at line 9 is a related out-of-bounds read, but the write is the supported consequence here.

evidence_lines.code:
oldproc = dpy->event_vec[event_number];
dpy->event_vec[event_number] = proc;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function trusts event_number supplied by an X server and indexes the fixed-size event_vec array with it for both read and write. Trigger: a malicious server or proxy returns an out-of-range extension event ID. Consequence: the write at line 10 corrupts other fields of the Display structure, potentially crashing the client.

commit_msg: Fix libarchive/archive_read_support_format_mtree.c:1388:11: error: array subscript is above array bounds
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\tnumbers[argc++] = (unsigned long)mtree_atol(&p);', '\t\t\tif (argc > MAX_PACK_ARGS) {'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\tif (argc >= MAX_PACK_ARGS) {', '\t\t\tnumbers[argc++] = (unsigned long)mtree_atol(&p);']}
description: Stack-based buffer overflow in the parse_device function in archive_read_support_format_mtree.c in libarchive before 3.2.1 allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via a crafted mtree file.

code_evidence: numbers is a fixed stack array of MAX_PACK_ARGS (3) unsigned longs (line 5). argc starts at 0 (line 19) and the loop over la_strsep results (line 20) writes numbers[argc++] before any bound check (line 26). The guard on line 27 tests argc > MAX_PACK_ARGS after the increment, so when argc reaches 4 the write to numbers[3] has already occurred past the array end.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes past the intended boundary of the numbers buffer, which matches CWE-119's improper restriction of operations within a memory buffer. The off-by-one ordering of check versus write is the specific defect; the out-of-bounds stack write is the buffer-boundary violation described by CWE-119.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the bounds check is placed after the array write and uses a strict > comparison, so the fourth parsed number is stored at numbers[3], one element beyond the 3-element stack buffer. Trigger: a crafted mtree file supplying four or more comma-separated numbers to a known pack format. Supported consequence: out-of-bounds stack write, corrupting adjacent stack data potentially leading to code execution or crash.

commit_msg:
Fix a possible security issue
- Require manually set flag to run scripts from absolute pathname
- Mostly applies to scripts given on the command line
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tabsPath = fileName;'], 'added_lines': ['\tconst bool okToRunScriptFromAbsolutePath=StelApp::getInstance().getSettings()->value("scripts/flag_script_allow_absolute_path", false).toBool();', '\t{', '\t\t// Absolute paths may bear a security risk. We need a flag to allow them!', '\t\tif (okToRunScriptFromAbsolutePath)', '\t\t\tabsPath = fileName;', '\t\telse', '\t\t{', '\t\t\tqWarning() << "SCRIPTING CONFIGURATION ISSUE: You are trying to run a script from absolute pathname.";', '\t\t\tqWarning() << "  To enable this, edit config.ini and set [scripts]/flag_script_allow_absolute_path=true";', '\t\t\treturn false;', '\t\t}', '\t}']}
description: In Stellarium through 1.2, attackers can write to files that are typically unintended, such as ones with absolute pathnames or .. directory traversal.

code_evidence: When the caller-supplied fileName is absolute, the function assigns it directly to absPath without confinement to the scripts directory; only non-absolute names are routed through StelFileMgr::findFile("scripts/" + fileName). The resulting absPath is then opened and preprocessed.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-22 covers constructing a pathname from external input without neutralizing elements that escape the restricted parent directory, explicitly including absolute pathnames. Here the absolute-path branch bypasses the scripts/ prefix entirely, so the target CWE fits; CWE-36 would be the absolute-path child, but the parent is acceptable.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: caller-controlled path input is accepted verbatim as an absolute path with no restriction to the intended scripts directory. Trigger: invoking prepareScript with an absolute pathname (or a traversal name resolved by the file manager). Consequence: the function opens and preprocesses an arbitrary file outside the scripts directory, supporting read/execution of unintended scripts.

commit_msg: Fix OOB Access on PcxDecode.c
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if (strcmp(im->mode, "1") == 0 && state->xsize > state->bytes * 8) {', '        state->errcode = IMAGING_CODEC_OVERRUN;', '        return -1;', '    } else if (strcmp(im->mode, "P") == 0 && state->xsize > state->bytes) {'], 'added_lines': ['    if ((state->xsize * state->bits + 7) / 8 > state->bytes) {']}
description: In libImaging/PcxDecode.c in Pillow before 7.1.0, an out-of-bounds read can occur when reading PCX files where state->shuffle is instructed to read beyond state->buffer.

code_evidence: The bounds check only covers modes "1" and "P"; other modes skip the state->bytes validation entirely before decoding.
The RLE copy loop guards against state->x >= state->bytes, but that bound derives from the insufficient upfront check.
After a row is filled, memmove and state->shuffle read state->buffer using xsize/stride values that may exceed the bytes actually validated, so shuffle can read past the buffer end.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect is a missing/conditional length constraint that permits reading past the intended buffer boundary in state->buffer, matching CWE-125. It is an over-read, not a write (CWE-787) or integer issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the pre-decode validation restricts the xsize-vs-bytes comparison to modes "1" and "P", leaving other modes unvalidated. Trigger: a crafted PCX file whose declared width makes xsize exceed the populated buffer length. Consequence: state->shuffle reads beyond state->buffer, an out-of-bounds read.

commit_msg:
avformat/movenc: Check that frame_types other than EAC3_FRAME_TYPE_INDEPENDENT have a supported substream id

Fixes: out of array access
Fixes: ffmpeg_bof_1.avi

Found-by: Thuan Pham, Marcel Böhme, Andrew Santosa and Alexandru Razvan Caciulescu with AFLSmart
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['            }', '        } else {', '            if (hdr->substreamid != 0) {', '                avpriv_request_sample(mov->fc, "Multiple non EAC3 independent substreams");', '                ret = AVERROR_PATCHWELCOME;', '                goto end;']}
description: In FFmpeg 4.0.1, improper handling of frame types (other than EAC3_FRAME_TYPE_INDEPENDENT) that have multiple independent substreams in the handle_eac3 function in libavformat/movenc.c may trigger an out-of-array access while converting a crafted AVI file to MPEG4, leading to a denial of service or possibly unspecified other impact.

code_evidence: The frame_type branch only bounds-checks and rejects substreamid for EAC3_FRAME_TYPE_INDEPENDENT frames (lines 24-32); for all other frame types control falls through to lines 39-43.

Lines 39-43 index info->substream[hdr->substreamid] and write fscod/bsid/bsmod/acmod/lfeon using the header-derived substreamid, which was never validated against the size of the substream array for non-independent frame types.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-129 fits because an untrusted header field (substreamid) is used directly as an array index without validation on the non-independent path. The added else branch rejects substreamid != 0, confirming the missing index constraint; this is improper index validation rather than a general integer overflow.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the substreamid bounds check is confined to the EAC3_FRAME_TYPE_INDEPENDENT path, so a crafted packet with a non-independent frame type and a large substreamid reaches info->substream[hdr->substreamid]. Trigger: parsing an attacker-supplied EAC3 header in a crafted AVI during MPEG4 conversion. Consequence: out-of-array write/access, corrupting memory or crashing (DoS).

commit_msg:
When fw_change() is called on an existing filter, the whole
tcf_result struct is always copied into the new instance of the filter.

This causes a problem when updating a filter bound to a class,
as tcf_unbind_filter() is always called on the old instance in the
success path, decreasing filter_cnt of the still referenced class
and allowing it to be deleted, leading to a use-after-free.

Fix this by no longer copying the tcf_result struct from the old filter.

Fixes: e35a8ee5993b ("net: sched: fw use RCU")
Reported-by: valis <sec@valis.email>
Reported-by: Bing-Jhong Billy Jheng <billy@starlabs.sg>
Signed-off-by: valis <sec@valis.email>
Signed-off-by: Jamal Hadi Salim <jhs@mojatatu.com>
Reviewed-by: Victor Nogueira <victor@mojatatu.com>
Reviewed-by: Pedro Tammela <pctammela@mojatatu.com>
Reviewed-by: M A Ramdhan <ramdhan@starlabs.sg>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20230729123202.72406-3-jhs@mojatatu.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tfnew->res = f->res;'], 'added_lines': []}
description:
A use-after-free vulnerability in the Linux kernel's net/sched: cls_fw component can be exploited to achieve local privilege escalation.

When fw_change() is called on an existing filter, the whole tcf_result struct is always copied into the new instance of the filter. This causes a problem when updating a filter bound to a class, as tcf_unbind_filter() is always called on the old instance in the success path, decreasing filter_cnt of the still referenced class and allowing it to be deleted, leading to a use-after-free.

We recommend upgrading past commit 76e42ae831991c828cffa8c37736ebfb831ad5ec.

code_evidence: Line 26 copies the old filter's tcf_result (f->res) into fnew, preserving its bound class reference. After fw_set_parms and replacement, line 48 calls tcf_unbind_filter(tp, &f->res) on the old instance, decrementing the referenced class's filter_cnt, then lines 49-50 schedule the old filter for deletion; fnew->res still points at the class but no longer holds the count.
The new filter is installed and returned via *arg (lines 35,51) while the class reference it carries was already released for the old instance.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The flaw leaves a stale reference to freed memory (the deleted class) reachable through fnew->res, matching CWE-416's reuse of freed memory. It is not merely a reference-count leak; the unbalanced unbind enables premature free and subsequent invalid access.

evidence_lines.code:
err = fw_set_parms(net, tp, fnew, tb, tca, base, flags, extack);
*arg = fnew;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: copying f->res into fnew while the success path unconditionally unbinds the old filter's result, so the class's filter_cnt is decremented despite fnew still referencing it. Trigger: updating an existing fw filter bound to a class. Consequence: the class can be deleted while fnew->res still points to it, yielding a use-after-free (CWE-416).

commit_msg:
x86: limit linear page table use to a single level

That's the only way that they're meant to be used. Without such a
restriction arbitrarily long chains of same-level page tables can be
built, tearing down of which may then cause arbitrarily deep recursion,
causing a stack overflow. To facilitate this restriction, a counter is
being introduced to track both the number of same-level entries in a
page table as well as the number of uses of a page table in another
same-level one (counting into positive and negative direction
respectively, utilizing the fact that both counts can't be non-zero at
the same time).

Note that the added accounting introduces a restriction on the number
of times a page can be used in other same-level page tables - more than
32k of such uses are no longer possible.

Note also that some put_page_and_type[_preemptible]() calls are
replaced with open-coded equivalents.  This seemed preferrable to
adding "parent_table" to the matrix of functions.

Note further that cross-domain same-level page table references are no
longer permitted (they probably never should have been).

This is XSA-240.

Reported-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Signed-off-by: George Dunlap <george.dunlap@citrix.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['            current->arch.old_guest_ptpg = NULL;']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.9.x allowing x86 PV guest OS users to cause a denial of service (unbounded recursion, stack consumption, and hypervisor crash) or possibly gain privileges via crafted page-table stacking.

code_evidence: On -ERESTART the function saves partial progress (page->nr_validated_ptes, page->partial_pte) and on hard failure records current->arch.old_guest_table = page when i is nonzero. The patch adds clearing current->arch.old_guest_ptpg = NULL alongside that assignment, but the function itself only stores the page reference for later teardown and does not bound how many same-level page tables can be chained or how deeply teardown may recurse.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-400 fits because the weakness is uncontrolled consumption of a limited resource (hypervisor stack) via unbounded page-table chains, leading to DoS. It is not CWE-674 here because the function lacks the depth-tracking constraint rather than performing the recursive call itself.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is failure to constrain same-level page-table stacking: alloc_l3_table accepts and records references to guest page tables without limiting chain length. A PV guest can build arbitrarily long same-level chains, and teardown recurses through them, exhausting the hypervisor stack and crashing it. The function supports the resource-accounting/teardown side but does not itself enforce the depth limit.

commit_msg: Fix #14334 - Double-free in ms command
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\tfree (cwd);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\tR_FREE (cwd);']}
description: In radare2 through 3.5.1, cmd_mount in libr/core/cmd_mount.c has a double free for the ms command.

code_evidence: After r_fs_shell_prompt returns, cwd is freed with free(cwd) at line 257; the completion state is then restored via r_pvector_clear and memcpy at 258-259. The patch replaces this free with R_FREE(cwd), which nulls the pointer after freeing, indicating cwd may be freed again on a later path or through the restored completion context.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The commit explicitly fixes a double free of cwd in the 'ms' path, matching CWE-415. R_FREE both frees and nulls the pointer, preventing a second free; this is distinct from a use-after-free, where freed memory would be dereferenced.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: cwd is released with plain free() and the pointer is not reset, so any subsequent release of the same cwd (e.g., via the restored line-completion state or a repeated 'ms' invocation) frees an already-freed address. Trigger: executing the 'ms' shell-prompt path. Consequence: heap corruption that can lead to memory modification or code execution.

commit_msg: Fix #18666 - uaf in python bin parser
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tpyc_object *ret;', '', '\tret = R_NEW0 (pyc_object);'], 'added_lines': ['\tpyc_object *ret = R_NEW0 (pyc_object);']}
description: In radare2 through 5.3.0 there is a double free vulnerability in the pyc parse via a crafted file which can lead to DoS.

code_evidence: Line 8 allocates ret->data via strdup. Lines 9-11 free ret with R_FREE when strdup fails, but the function does not return NULL there; line 12 returns the freed ret pointer to the caller.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-415 fits because the freed ret pointer escapes to the caller, which may free it again, causing a double free. This is more specific than a generic use-after-free (CWE-416): the returned pointer enables a second free() on the same address.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: on strdup failure, ret is freed at line 10 but control falls through to line 12, returning a dangling pointer. The caller then uses or frees this already-released pyc_object, triggering a use-after-free and potentially a double free. The trigger is the allocation failure of ret->data in get_none_object.

commit_msg:
block: blk_init_allocated_queue() set q->fq as NULL in the fail case

We find the memory use-after-free issue in __blk_drain_queue()
on the kernel 4.14. After read the latest kernel 4.18-rc6 we
think it has the same problem.

Memory is allocated for q->fq in the blk_init_allocated_queue().
If the elevator init function called with error return, it will
run into the fail case to free the q->fq.

Then the __blk_drain_queue() uses the same memory after the free
of the q->fq, it will lead to the unpredictable event.

The patch is to set q->fq as NULL in the fail case of
blk_init_allocated_queue().

Fixes: commit 7c94e1c157a2 ("block: introduce blk_flush_queue to drive flush machinery")
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Ming Lei <ming.lei@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Bart Van Assche <bart.vanassche@wdc.com>
Signed-off-by: xiao jin <jin.xiao@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tq->fq = NULL;']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel before 4.18.7. In block/blk-core.c, there is an __blk_drain_queue() use-after-free because a certain error case is mishandled.

code_evidence: In the error path, out_exit_flush_rq may call q->exit_rq_fn(q, q->fq->flush_rq), then out_free_flush_queue calls blk_free_flush_queue(q->fq). After this free, q->fq is not cleared before returning -ENOMEM, leaving a dangling pointer in the request_queue. A caller or later cleanup path that reuses q->fq (e.g., __blk_drain_queue) then references freed memory.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the function frees q->fq and returns with the pointer still stored, so subsequent references through q->fq reuse freed memory. This is not merely a double free or NULL dereference; the dangling pointer enables use-after-free.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the fail path frees the flush queue via blk_free_flush_queue(q->fq) but leaves q->fq pointing at the released object. Trigger: elevator_init or blk_init_rl fails, taking the error path; the queue persists and q->fq is later dereferenced. Supported consequence: use-after-free of the flush queue, enabling memory corruption or crash.

commit_msg: Ensure image extent does not exceed maximum
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  status=SetImageExtent(image,image->columns,image->rows,exception);', '  if (status == MagickFalse)', '    return(DestroyImageList(image));'], 'added_lines': ['              status=SetImageExtent(image,image->columns,image->rows,exception);', '              if (status == MagickFalse)', '                break;', '              status=SetImageExtent(image,image->columns,image->rows,exception);', '              if (status == MagickFalse)', '                break;']}
description: The WPG parser in ImageMagick before 6.9.4-4 and 7.x before 7.0.1-5, when a memory limit is set, allows remote attackers to have unspecified impact via vectors related to the SetImageExtent return-value check, which trigger (1) a heap-based buffer overflow in the SetPixelIndex function or an invalid write operation in the (2) ScaleCharToQuantum or (3) SetPixelIndex functions.

code_evidence: Bitmap header width/height/depth are read from the file and assigned to image->columns, image->rows and bpp before jumping to UnpackRaster; the raster is unpacked/inserted before any extent allocation is validated.
Same pattern for record 0x14: attacker-controlled width/height/depth set image->columns/rows and bpp, then UnpackRaster runs.
UnpackRaster computes image->colors=one<<bpp and allocates a colormap, but does not verify that the pixel extent matches the declared raster size.
For WPG2 record 0x0E, image->columns/rows come from Bitmap2Header1 and the colormap is sized from bpp without a prior SetImageExtent check.
ldblk is computed from bpp*image->columns, BImgBuff is allocated to that size, and InsertRow/UnpackWPG2Raster write rows into the image using the declared extent.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-119 fits because the missing extent check lets subsequent pixel writes exceed the intended image buffer boundary. The fix moves SetImageExtent before raster unpacking and breaks on failure, directly constraining the buffer to the declared extent; this is a bounds violation, not merely a resource-limit denial.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the parser trusts file-supplied width/height/depth and unpacks/inserts raster data before confirming that SetImageExtent succeeded for those dimensions. Trigger: a crafted WPG bitmap record whose declared extent exceeds the memory limit or otherwise fails extent allocation. Consequence: InsertRow/UnpackWPGRaster/SetPixelIndex and ScaleCharToQuantum then operate on a pixel buffer not sized to the declared raster, causing out-of-bounds writes (heap buffer overflow) rather than a clean failure.

commit_msg:
Fix - memory leak when deleting client from client list

Signed-off-by: Rob White <rob@blue-wave.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tfree(client->token);', '\tfree(client->hid);', '\tfree(client->custom);', '\tfree(client->client_type);', '\tfree(client->cid);', '', '\tif (strcmp(client->cpi_query, "") == 0) {', '\t\tfree(client->cpi_query);', '\t}', '']}
description: An issue was discovered in the captive portal in OpenNDS before version 10.1.3. It has multiple memory leaks due to not freeing up allocated memory. This may lead to a Denial-of-Service condition due to the consumption of all available memory.

code_evidence: The function allocates msg and cidinfo, frees those two buffers at lines 12-13, then frees only the client structure itself at line 16; the pointed-to members of client (such as cid, token, hid, custom, client_type, cpi_query) are never released. Each call to _client_list_free_node therefore drops the last reference to those member allocations.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-401 fits because allocated memory owned by client outlives its last pointer without being released. This is a missing-free lifetime defect, not a double free or use-after-free, since the freed struct is not dereferenced afterward.

evidence_lines.code: free(client);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the node teardown frees the container struct but not the heap-allocated strings it owns. Trigger: any client node removal that reaches line 16, which is the normal path. Consequence: leaked member buffers accumulate on repeated removals, consuming memory and supporting a DoS under sustained client churn.

commit_msg: Fix bug #72241: get_icu_value_internal out-of-bounds read
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tint \tlen =0; ', '\t\tmod_loc_name = loc_name ; ', '\t\t\tif( singletonPos!=-1){ ', "\t\t\t\tif( (*(mod_loc_name+singletonPos)=='x') || (*(mod_loc_name+singletonPos)=='X') ){\t\t", '\t'], 'added_lines': ['\tint \tlen =0;', '\t\tmod_loc_name = loc_name ;', '\t\t\tif( singletonPos!=-1){', "\t\t\t\tif( (*(mod_loc_name+singletonPos)=='x') || (*(mod_loc_name+singletonPos)=='X') ){", '']}
description: The get_icu_value_internal function in ext/intl/locale/locale_methods.c in PHP before 5.5.36, 5.6.x before 5.6.22, and 7.x before 7.0.7 does not ensure the presence of a '\0' character, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted locale_get_primary_language call.

code_evidence: loc_name is accepted and its length computed into len after assigning mod_loc_name; no check that the string is NUL-terminated before later length-based reads.
When singletonPos + 2 == len, the code takes the empty branch and breaks without reading beyond; the estrndup path uses len-(singletonPos+2), which is bounded by the earlier strlen.
The else branch checks singletonPos+1 >= len and breaks before advancing, so the pointer advance is guarded by the computed length.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs length-driven reads over an input string whose termination is not guaranteed, matching CWE-125 out-of-bounds read. It is not a write overflow (CWE-787) because the unsafe access is a read during strlen/character comparison, not a store beyond bounds.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is reliance on strlen/len of the caller-supplied loc_name without ensuring a terminating NUL exists; if the input buffer lacks '\0', strlen and the subsequent pointer arithmetic can read past the buffer. Trigger is a crafted locale name passed to locale_get_primary_language, producing an out-of-bounds read and possible crash/DoS.

commit_msg:
x86/pv: Rewrite guest %cr4 handling from scratch

The PV cr4 logic is almost impossible to follow, and leaks bits into guest
context which definitely shouldn't be visible (in particular, VMXE).

The biggest problem however, and source of the complexity, is that it derives
new real and guest cr4 values from the current value in hardware - this is
context dependent and an inappropriate source of information.

Rewrite the cr4 logic to be invariant of the current value in hardware.

First of all, modify write_ptbase() to always use mmu_cr4_features for IDLE
and HVM contexts.  mmu_cr4_features *is* the correct value to use, and makes
the ASSERT() obviously redundant.

For PV guests, curr->arch.pv.ctrlreg[4] remains the guests view of cr4, but
all logic gets reworked in terms of this and mmu_cr4_features only.

Two masks are introduced; bits which the guest has control over, and bits
which are forwarded from Xen's settings.  One guest-visible change here is
that Xen's VMXE setting is no longer visible at all.

pv_make_cr4() follows fairly closely from pv_guest_cr4_to_real_cr4(), but
deliberately starts with mmu_cr4_features, and only alters the minimal subset
of bits.

The boot-time {compat_,}pv_cr4_mask variables are removed, as they are a
remnant of the pre-CPUID policy days.  pv_fixup_guest_cr4() gains a related
derivation from the policy.

Another guest visible change here is that a 32bit PV guest can now flip
FSGSBASE in its view of CR4.  While the {RD,WR}{FS,GS}BASE instructions are
unusable outside of a 64bit code segment, the ability to modify FSGSBASE
matches real hardware behaviour, and avoids the need for any 32bit/64bit
differences in the logic.

Overall, this patch shouldn't have a practical change in guest behaviour.
VMXE will disappear from view, and an inquisitive 32bit kernel can now see
FSGSBASE changing, but this new logic is otherwise bug-compatible with before.

This is part of XSA-293.

Signed-off-by: Andrew Cooper <andrew.cooper3@citrix.com>
Reviewed-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['              ? pv_guest_cr4_to_real_cr4(v)', '              : ((read_cr4() & ~(X86_CR4_PCIDE | X86_CR4_TSD)) | X86_CR4_PGE);', '', '    ASSERT(is_pv_vcpu(v) || read_cr4() == mmu_cr4_features);'], 'added_lines': ['              ? pv_make_cr4(v) : mmu_cr4_features;']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.11.x allowing x86 PV guest OS users to cause a denial of service or gain privileges because a guest can manipulate its virtualised %cr4 in a way that is incompatible with Linux (and possibly other guest kernels).

code_evidence: new_cr4 is computed from the guest's current virtualized CR4 via pv_guest_cr4_to_real_cr4(v) for PV vCPUs, and from read_cr4() for non-PV contexts. The guest-controlled CR4 value flows directly into switch_cr3_cr4() at lines 14/20 without any masking or filtering of bits the guest must not influence.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is improper validation of the guest-supplied CR4 value: the function accepts and forwards unvalidated guest input rather than constraining it to an allowed set, matching CWE-20. It is not merely a transformation bug; the missing validation of which CR4 bits the guest may set is the core defect.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function derives the real CR4 from guest-supplied CR4 (and current hardware CR4) without restricting which bits the guest controls. Trigger: a PV guest sets CR4 bits such as VMXE that are incompatible with guest kernels. Consequence: the guest can manipulate virtualized %cr4, leading to DoS or privilege gain, and leaks Xen bits into guest context.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['          SetPSDPixel(image,channels,type,packet_size,(((unsigned char) pixel)', '            & (0x01 << (7-bit))) != 0 ? 0 : QuantumRange,q++,indexes,x++);'], 'added_lines': ['          SetPSDPixel(image,channels,type,packet_size,', '            (((unsigned char) ((ssize_t) pixel)) & (0x01 << (7-bit))) != 0 ? 0 :', '            QuantumRange,q++,indexes,x++);']}
description: A vulnerability was found in ImageMagick, causing an outside the range of representable values of type 'unsigned char' at coders/psd.c, when crafted or untrusted input is processed. This leads to a negative impact to application availability or other problems related to undefined behavior.

code_evidence: At line 57, the value 'pixel' is cast to '(unsigned char)' before the bit test. 'pixel' is a Quantum (unsigned short) whose value may exceed 0xFF; the cast truncates it. The fix adds an intermediate cast to '(ssize_t)' before the '(unsigned char)' cast, indicating the truncation of an out-of-range value was the defect. The bit test at line 58 then uses the truncated byte to choose 0 or QuantumRange, so a wrong bit value is produced for large pixel values when image->depth <= 1.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 covers calculations producing values outside the representable range of a type. The '(unsigned char)' cast of an out-of-range Quantum is exactly such a narrowing conversion, and the patch's added '(ssize_t)' cast confirms the out-of-range conversion was the defect. The bit-mask logic then acts on the wrapped value, matching the wraparound consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the code converts the Quantum 'pixel' to 'unsigned char' without ensuring the value fits, so a value outside the representable range of 'unsigned char' is truncated. Trigger: a crafted PSD with image depth <= 1 and pixel values that exceed 0xFF. Consequence: the truncated byte selects an incorrect output value in SetPSDPixel, producing wrong pixel data and undefined-behavior-related problems affecting application availability.

commit_msg:
Properly handle the case where `SpecializeType()` returns an error `Status`.

If the error case in `SpecializeType()` is reached, then we would get a crash when trying to access the value of an errorenous `StatusOr` object

PiperOrigin-RevId: 408380069
Change-Id: If3c3fc876dcf9384d5ec7a4985adc68c23ea7318
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  DCHECK(ret.status().ok()) << "while instantiating types: " << ret.status();'], 'added_lines': ['  if (!ret.status().ok()) {', '    construction_status_ = ret.status();', '    return;', '  }']}
description: Tensorflow is an Open Source Machine Learning Framework. Under certain scenarios, TensorFlow can fail to specialize a type during shape inference. This case is covered by the `DCHECK` function however, `DCHECK` is a no-op in production builds and an assertion failure in debug builds. In the first case execution proceeds to the `ValueOrDie` line. This results in an assertion failure as `ret` contains an error `Status`, not a value. In the second case we also get a crash due to the assertion failure. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.8.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.7.1, and TensorFlow 2.6.3, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: SpecializeType() returns a StatusOr; line 5 only checks its status with DCHECK, which is compiled out in production builds. Line 6 then unconditionally calls ValueOrDie() on the same object, so when the status is an error the call asserts/crashes instead of propagating the error.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reaches an assertion (DCHECK/ValueOrDie) that an attacker-influenced failure can trigger, causing a crash rather than graceful error handling—exactly CWE-617. This is an availability impact from a reachable assertion, not memory corruption or an input-validation weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the error Status from SpecializeType() is guarded only by a debug-only DCHECK rather than a real branch. Trigger: shape/type specialization fails for crafted input. Consequence: ValueOrDie() reaches its internal assertion, aborting the process (DoS) in both debug and production builds.

description: addressbook/backends/ldap/e-book-backend-ldap.c in Evolution-Data-Server in GNOME Evolution through 3.29.2 might allow attackers to trigger a Buffer Overflow via a long query that is processed by the strcat function. NOTE: the software maintainer disputes this because "the code had computed the required string length first, and then allocated a large-enough buffer on the heap.

code_evidence: query_length is computed by summing, for every prop_info entry, 1 + strlen(ldap_attr) + strlen(match_str), then big_query = g_malloc0(query_length + 1).

The allocation is sized for all entries, but the strcat loop only appends for entries passing the prop_type/bl/priv filters; the sizing loop applies no such filters, so the allocation is over-, not under-, provisioned. The appended bytes always fit within the computed length, so no out-of-bounds write is demonstrated.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-119 requires an operation outside the buffer's intended bounds; the function's allocation is derived from the same string lengths used for the concatenations and is not shown to be exceeded. The maintainer's dispute is consistent with the code, so buffer-overflow evidence is insufficient.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause would be a size mismatch between the computed buffer length and the bytes actually written by strcat. Here the sizing loop unconditionally includes every prop_info entry while the write loop is filtered, making the allocated buffer larger than needed; match_str is built from the escaped query string and its length is counted. The trigger (long query value) only increases both the allocation and the writes consistently, so no write past the buffer boundary is supported.

@@ -173,7 +173,7 @@

-                if (TYPE(CHILD(n, i)) == COMMA)
