evidence_lines.code: QLIST_SAFE_REMOVE(block, next);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the removal macro dereferences the block's linkage fields without a NULL check on the relevant next pointer. Trigger: calling qemu_ram_free with a block whose list linkage is NULL or stale. Consequence: NULL pointer dereference causing a crash (availability impact).

commit_msg:
Fix gatt_end_operation buffer overflow

Added boundary check for gatt_end_operation to prevent writing out of
boundary.

Since response of the GATT server is handled in
gatt_client_handle_server_rsp() and gatt_process_read_rsp(), the maximum
lenth that can be passed into the handlers is bounded by
GATT_MAX_MTU_SIZE, which is set to 517, which is greater than
GATT_MAX_ATTR_LEN which is set to 512. The fact that there is no spec
that gaurentees MTU response to be less than or equal to 512 bytes can
cause a buffer overflow when performing memcpy without length check.

Bug: 261068592
Test: No test since not affecting behavior
Tag: #security
Ignore-AOSP-First: security
(cherry picked from https://googleplex-android-review.googlesource.com/q/commit:7236e4492470e30c129d01d521a7d218494725b4)
Merged-In: I49e2797cd9300ee4cd69f2c7fa5f0073db78b873
Change-Id: I49e2797cd9300ee4cd69f2c7fa5f0073db78b873
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '      if (cb_data.att_value.len > GATT_MAX_ATTR_LEN) {', '        LOG(WARNING) << __func__', '                     << StringPrintf(" Large cb_data.att_value, size=%d",', '                                     cb_data.att_value.len);', '        cb_data.att_value.len = GATT_MAX_ATTR_LEN;', '      }']}
description: In gatt_end_operation of gatt_utils.cc, there is a possible out of bounds write due to a missing bounds check. This could lead to remote code execution with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

code_evidence: Line 18 copies the attacker-influenced peer response length p_clcb->counter into cb_data.att_value.len without any upper bound. Lines 19-20 then memcpy that length into the fixed-size tGATT_VALUE.value buffer. Because GATT_MAX_MTU_SIZE (517) can exceed GATT_MAX_ATTR_LEN (512), counter may exceed the destination capacity, so the copy writes past the end of att_value.value.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs a memcpy with a length derived from network input into a fixed-size destination without checking capacity, directly producing a write beyond the buffer, which matches CWE-787. It is not merely an out-of-bounds read, since the overflow is on the write destination.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: missing length validation before copying peer-controlled response data into a fixed-size buffer. Trigger: a GATT server response whose length exceeds the attribute buffer size. Consequence: out-of-bounds write into adjacent stack memory, corrupting data and potentially enabling code execution or crash.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tmd = firstDayOfMonth[InLeapYear(y)][(int)m];'], 'added_lines': ['\tint im;', '\tim = (int)m;', '\tif (im < 0 || im >= 12)', '\t\treturn NAN;', '', '\tmd = firstDayOfMonth[InLeapYear(y)][im];']}
description: An issue was discovered in Artifex Software, Inc. MuJS before 8f62ea10a0af68e56d5c00720523ebcba13c2e6a. The MakeDay function in jsdate.c does not validate the month, leading to an integer overflow when parsing a specially crafted JS file.

code_evidence: MakeDay adjusts the year with floor(m/12) and then reduces the month via pmod(m,12), producing a floating-point value in [0,12). Line 11 casts this double to int and indexes firstDayOfMonth[InLeapYear(y)][(int)m] with no bounds check on the resulting index.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe conversion and unchecked index arithmetic in the month calculation allow an out-of-range integer value to be used as an array offset, consistent with integer overflow/wraparound leading to memory access beyond the valid range. The missing range check on the converted month is the core defect.

The root cause is the unchecked conversion/index computation, not the later addition of yd, md and date.

commit_msg:

In the client, read the reply headers from a coroutine, switching the
read side between the "read header" coroutine and the I/O coroutine that
reads the body of the reply.

In the server, if the server can read more requests it will create a new
"read request" coroutine as soon as a request has been read.  Otherwise,
the new coroutine is created in nbd_request_put.

commit_msg:
Fixed OOB read in update_read_cache_bitmap_v3_order

CVE-2020-11096 thanks @antonio-morales for finding this.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tcache_bitmap_v3->bpp = CBR23_BPP[bitsPerPixelId];'], 'added_lines': ['\tBOOL rc;', '\tcache_bitmap_v3->bpp = get_cbr2_bpp(bitsPerPixelId, &rc);', '\tif (!rc)', '\t\tgoto fail;']}
description: In FreeRDP before version 2.1.2, there is a global OOB read in update_read_cache_bitmap_v3_order. As a workaround, one can disable bitmap cache with -bitmap-cache (default). This is fixed in version 2.1.2.

code_evidence: bitsPerPixelId is extracted from the attacker-controlled flags field via (flags & 0x00000078) >> 3, yielding a value in 0..15. It is then used directly as an index into CBR23_BPP without any bounds check, so an index beyond the array's valid range reads past the end of the global CBR23_BPP table.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads memory beyond the bounds of the CBR23_BPP buffer due to a missing index check, which is exactly CWE-125 (Out-of-bounds Read). It is not a write-based weakness, since the out-of-range access only reads the table; the later realloc/Stream_Read path is bounded by separate checks.

cache_bitmap_v3->bpp = CBR23_BPP[bitsPerPixelId];

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: an unvalidated bitfield from the wire-derived flags value indexes the fixed CBR23_BPP array with no range constraint. Trigger: a crafted bitmap-cache order supplying a bitsPerPixelId larger than the array bound causes an out-of-bounds read of global memory; the resulting bpp value may then propagate into later processing. Supported consequence is a global out-of-bounds read (memory disclosure or crash).

commit_msg:
Default initialize fixed point Eigen types.

In certain cases, tensors are filled with default values of the type. But, for these fixed point types, these values were uninitialized. Thus, we would have uninitialized memory access bugs, some of which were caught by MSAN.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 344101137
Change-Id: I14555fda74dca3b5f1582da9008901937e3f14e2
func:
[QUInt16]

0001 | QUInt16() {}
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['QUInt16() {}'], 'added_lines': ['QUInt16() : value(0) {}']}
description: In affected versions of TensorFlow under certain cases a saved model can trigger use of uninitialized values during code execution. This is caused by having tensor buffers be filled with the default value of the type but forgetting to default initialize the quantized floating point types in Eigen. This is fixed in versions 1.15.5, 2.0.4, 2.1.3, 2.2.2, 2.3.2, and 2.4.0.

code_evidence: The QUInt16 default constructor body is empty and does not initialize the member 'value', leaving the fixed-point quantized type with an indeterminate value whenever it is default-constructed (e.g., tensor buffers filled with default values).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-908 covers use/access of a resource that was not initialized; here the QUInt16 value remains uninitialized after construction and is later consumed, matching the base weakness directly.

evidence_lines.code: QUInt16() {}

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the default constructor performs no initialization of the underlying storage. Trigger: code default-constructs QUInt16, such as filling tensor buffers with the type's default value. Consequence: downstream reads use uninitialized memory, producing undefined behavior and uninitialized-value access (caught by MSAN).

commit_msg:
nfc: replace improper check device_is_registered() in netlink related functions

The device_is_registered() in nfc core is used to check whether
nfc device is registered in netlink related functions such as
nfc_fw_download(), nfc_dev_up() and so on. Although device_is_registered()
is protected by device_lock, there is still a race condition between
device_del() and device_is_registered(). The root cause is that
kobject_del() in device_del() is not protected by device_lock.

   (cleanup task)         |     (netlink task)
                          |
nfc_unregister_device     | nfc_fw_download
 device_del               |  device_lock
  ...                     |   if (!device_is_registered)//(1)
  kobject_del//(2)        |   ...
 ...                      |  device_unlock

The device_is_registered() returns the value of state_in_sysfs and
the state_in_sysfs is set to zero in kobject_del(). If we pass check in
position (1), then set zero in position (2). As a result, the check
in position (1) is useless.

This patch uses bool variable instead of device_is_registered() to judge
whether the nfc device is registered, which is well synchronized.

Fixes: 3e256b8f8dfa ("NFC: add nfc subsystem core")
Signed-off-by: Duoming Zhou <duoming@zju.edu.cn>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (!device_is_registered(&dev->dev)) {'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (dev->shutting_down) {']}
description: A use-after-free flaw was found in the Linux kernel's NFC core functionality due to a race condition between kobject creation and delete. This vulnerability allows a local attacker with CAP_NET_ADMIN privilege to leak kernel information.

code_evidence: The function acquires device_lock and then checks device_is_registered() to decide whether the device is still usable before proceeding [5,6,7,8,9].
After the check passes, it uses the device state and calls dev->ops->fw_download() [19,20,21], relying on the earlier registration check remaining valid.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This is a classic TOCTOU pattern: the function checks the resource state (device registration) before use, but the state can change between check and use due to a race. The target CWE-367 directly captures this check-then-use race rather than a mere missing lock.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The registration check in device_is_registered() is only protected by device_lock, but device_del()/kobject_del() can clear state_in_sysfs without that lock. A concurrent nfc_unregister_device can therefore invalidate the check after it passes, so the subsequent fw_download use operates on a device being torn down, supporting use-after-free/info leak.

read_ret = http_buf_read(h, buf, size);

Trigger: a malicious HTTP server returns a crafted chunk header. This leads to an out-of-bounds memory operation via the derived read size, enabling heap corruption or crash.

commit_msg:
io_get_file_fixed will access io_uring's context. Lock it if it is
invoked unlocked (eg via io-wq) to avoid a race condition with fixed

No single upstream patch exists for this issue, it was fixed as part

description:
A use-after-free vulnerability in the Linux Kernel io_uring system can be exploited to achieve local privilege escalation.

The io_file_get_fixed function lacks the presence of ctx->uring_lock which can lead to a Use-After-Free vulnerability due a race condition with fixed files getting unregistered.

We recommend upgrading past commit da24142b1ef9fd5d36b76e36bab328a5b27523e8.

code_evidence: io_file_get is called with only req->ctx, req, sp->splice_fd_in and the fixed-fd flag; the current issue_flags (which indicate whether the call is made from io-wq without ctx->uring_lock) are not passed, so the fixed-file lookup proceeds without the lock.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing lock allows a freed file object to be obtained and subsequently dereferenced by do_splice, matching CWE-416. This is a race-based lifetime/locking defect rather than an out-of-bounds access; the unsynchronized reference is the cause and the use-after-free is the consequence.

evidence_lines.code:
in = io_file_get(req->ctx, req, sp->splice_fd_in,
(sp->flags & SPLICE_F_FD_IN_FIXED));

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the fixed-file lookup in io_file_get is performed without ctx->uring_lock when io_splice runs from io-wq. Trigger: a concurrent fixed-file unregistration races with this unlocked lookup. Consequence: the returned file reference can refer to already-freed memory, and do_splice later uses it, supporting a use-after-free.

description: Multiple buffer overflows in mediaserver in Android 4.x before 4.4.4, 5.0.x before 5.0.2, 5.1.x before 5.1.1, and 6.x before 2016-07-01 allow attackers to gain privileges via a crafted application that provides an AudioEffect reply, as demonstrated by obtaining Signature or SignatureOrSystem access, aka internal bug 28173666.

code_evidence: The EFFECT_CMD_GET_PARAM branch validates pCmdData, cmdSize, pReplyData and *replySize, then at line 50 performs memcpy(pReplyData, pCmdData, sizeof(effect_param_t) + p->psize). The copy length is derived from p->psize read out of the caller-supplied pCmdData, but the pre-patch guard only checks *replySize >= sizeof(effect_param_t); it never bounds p->psize against the destination buffer size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-119 fits because the function writes to a memory buffer using a length that can exceed the destination's intended boundary; the added psize > *replySize - sizeof(effect_param_t) check confirms the missing bound. It is a direct out-of-bounds write rather than merely an integer issue.

commit_msg:
The SNDRV_RAWMIDI_IOCTL_PARAMS ioctl may resize the buffers and the
current code is racy.  For example, the sequencer client may write to
buffer while it being resized.

As a simple workaround, let's switch to the resized buffer inside the
stream runtime lock.

Reported-by: syzbot+52f83f0ea8df16932f7f@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Takashi Iwai <tiwai@suse.de>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tchar *newbuf;', '\t\tnewbuf = krealloc(runtime->buffer, params->buffer_size,', '\t\t\t\t  GFP_KERNEL);'], 'added_lines': ['\tchar *newbuf, *oldbuf;', '\t\tnewbuf = kmalloc(params->buffer_size, GFP_KERNEL);', '\t\tspin_lock_irq(&runtime->lock);', '\t\toldbuf = runtime->buffer;', '\t\truntime->appl_ptr = runtime->hw_ptr = 0;', '\t\tspin_unlock_irq(&runtime->lock);', '\t\tkfree(oldbuf);']}
description: It was found that the raw midi kernel driver does not protect against concurrent access which leads to a double realloc (double free) in snd_rawmidi_input_params() and snd_rawmidi_output_status() which are part of snd_rawmidi_ioctl() handler in rawmidi.c file. A malicious local attacker could possibly use this for privilege escalation.

code_evidence: The function reads runtime->buffer_size and runtime->buffer without holding runtime->lock. On resize, krealloc(runtime->buffer, ...) at [16,17] may free the old buffer and return a new one; the pointer is then published to runtime->buffer at [20] with no synchronization. A concurrent sequencer writer or the ioctl path can still dereference the prior runtime->buffer value, or realloc can run twice on the same pointer, producing a double free/use-after-free.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe reuse of runtime->buffer after krealloc frees the old allocation is exactly CWE-416: a stale pointer references freed memory that may be reallocated. This is not merely an unsynchronized race; the race is the trigger enabling the use-after-free.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: buffer reallocation and pointer replacement are performed without the stream runtime lock, so the old allocation can be freed while another context still uses it. Trigger: concurrent snd_rawmidi_output_params / write access on the same substream. Supported consequence: use-after-free (and double free) of the runtime buffer, leading to memory corruption or crash.

to the nested_funcs array that I made when I wrongly thought looping
might occur in scan_unit_for_symbols.

	pname param.  Return status.  Make name const.  Don't abort,
	return an error.  Formatting.  Exit if current info_ptr matches

	nested_funcs an array of structs for extensibility.  Formatting.

description: find_abstract_instance_name in dwarf2.c in the Binary File Descriptor (BFD) library (aka libbfd), as distributed in GNU Binutils 2.29, allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (infinite recursion and application crash) via a crafted ELF file.

code_evidence: On DW_AT_specification, the function unconditionally recurses into find_abstract_instance_name with the referenced DIE's attribute, with no check that the target differs from the current DIE or a previously visited DIE, and the recursion's return value is simply assigned to name.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The recursive call at [85] has an exit condition that a self-referential DW_AT_specification makes unreachable, producing non-terminating recursion and a crash. This matches CWE-835's unreachable-exit-condition infinite loop; the fix confirms it by comparing info_ptr to orig_info_ptr and returning an error.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: A crafted DWARF DIE whose DW_AT_specification references itself (or forms a cycle) drives unbounded recursive calls; each call re-reads the same DIE and recurses again, so the recursion never terminates and exhausts the stack, crashing the application (availability DoS). Root cause is the missing self/cycle guard on the recursive edge; trigger is attacker-controlled DW_AT_specification data in an ELF file.

commit_msg: imgcodecs: add overflow checks
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    uchar* old = m_current;', '    CV_Assert(m_current >= old);  // overflow check']}
description: In OpenCV 3.3.1, an assertion failure happens in cv::RBaseStream::setPos in modules/imgcodecs/src/bitstrm.cpp because of an incorrect integer cast.

code_evidence: CV_Assert(bytes >= 0) only validates the sign of bytes, then m_current += bytes advances the pointer by an attacker-influenced count without any bound or overflow check against the buffer end.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function contains a reachable CV_Assert that attacker-influenced input can trip, with availability impact (crash/exit), matching CWE-617; the patch adds a second assert rather than a real bound check, so the reachable-assertion weakness remains. This is not CWE-190 (integer overflow) because no integer arithmetic overflow occurs here—only unchecked pointer advancement and an assertion.

evidence_lines.code:
CV_Assert(bytes >= 0);
m_current += bytes;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: skip() accepts a non-negative byte count and blindly advances m_current with no upper-bound check. Trigger: a crafted input drives a large bytes value, moving m_current past the buffer. The pointer advance itself is unchecked, so subsequent reads or pointer arithmetic can violate buffer bounds; the assertion failure described in the report is the observable crash. The cause is the missing bound check, not the assertion itself.

description: PJSIP is a free and open source multimedia communication library written in C language implementing standard based protocols such as SIP, SDP, RTP, STUN, TURN, and ICE. This issue is similar to GHSA-9pfh-r8x4-w26w. Possible buffer overread when parsing a certain STUN message. The vulnerability affects applications that uses STUN including PJNATH and PJSUA-LIB. The patch is available as commit in the master branch.

code_evidence: Line 9 reads the attribute header via GETATTRHDR, establishing attr->hdr.length from attacker-controlled STUN input. Line 10 then immediately calls GETVAL32H(buf, 4), reading four bytes at offset 4 before the length is validated on line 11.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked offset read touches memory beyond the supplied STUN buffer before validating its size, matching CWE-122's out-of-bounds heap buffer access. It is an overread rather than the write-oriented CWE-787, but the missing length constraint before access is the same heap-buffer class.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the 32-bit value is read from the packet before confirming that the attribute length is 4, so the read is not bounded by the declared attribute size. Trigger: a malformed STUN attribute whose actual buffer is shorter than the four bytes consumed at offset 4. Consequence: an out-of-bounds read past the received buffer, which can crash or leak adjacent heap memory; the patch moves the read after the length check.

commit_msg: fixed #2138
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (outSize < (inSize * 2)+1) return 0;', '\tout[(inSize * 2)] = 0;', ''], 'added_lines': ['\tif (outSize < (inSize * 2)) return 0;']}
description: GPAC 2.0 allows a heap-based buffer overflow in gf_base64_encode. It can be triggered via MP4Box.

code_evidence: Line 7 only requires outSize >= inSize*2+1, then the loop at lines 8-11 writes out[2*i] and out[2*i+1] for each i, and line 12 writes the NUL terminator out[inSize*2]. The caller-supplied outSize is checked but the writes at indices up to inSize*2 are performed unconditionally relative to that bound.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the function writes to out[inSize*2] and out[2*i+1] beyond the intended buffer bound when outSize is insufficient; the fix in the diff removes the terminator write and tightens the guard, confirming an out-of-bounds write.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the size guard uses inSize*2+1 but the loop writes two bytes per input byte plus the terminator without re-checking against outSize. When a caller passes a buffer of exactly inSize*2+1 bytes the writes fit, but any caller passing outSize between inSize*2 and inSize*2+1 is rejected; the actual overflow arises when inSize*2 overflows or when callers rely on the returned size while outSize equals exactly inSize*2+1 — the terminator write at index inSize*2 is the last legal byte only if outSize == inSize*2+1. Trigger: crafted MP4Box input producing large inSize. Consequence: heap-based buffer overflow (memory corruption, possible code execution).

commit_msg:
Do not attempt to unwind the WITH stack in the Parse object following an error. This fixes a separate case to [de6e6d68].

FossilOrigin-Name: d29edef93451cc67a5d69c1cce1b1832d9ca8fff1f600afdd51338b74d077b92
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  if( db->mallocFailed || sqliteProcessJoin(pParse, p) ){'], 'added_lines': ['  if( pParse->nErr || db->mallocFailed || sqliteProcessJoin(pParse, p) ){']}
description: selectExpander in select.c in SQLite 3.30.1 proceeds with WITH stack unwinding even after a parsing error.

code_evidence: Line 24 pushes the WITH stack via sqlite3WithPush before walking the FROM items; at line 81 the abort condition checks only db->mallocFailed and sqliteProcessJoin, not pParse->nErr, so a parse error raised earlier (e.g., in withExpand or table lookup) still lets the walker return WRC_Abort without the guard that the patch adds.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The patch adds pParse->nErr to the abort test, showing the function mishandled the exceptional parsing-error condition. CWE-755 fits because the weakness is improper handling of an exceptional condition (parse error) rather than a memory-safety flaw.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the error path aborts the walk but fails to detect that pParse->nErr is already set, so the WITH stack pushed at line 24 is left in an inconsistent state relative to the parse error. Trigger: a malformed SELECT with a WITH clause that raises a parse error before this check. Consequence: subsequent parsing proceeds with a stale WITH stack, causing incorrect handling of the exceptional parse-error condition.

description: Crash in the Sysdig Event dissector in Wireshark 3.6.0 and 3.4.0 to 3.4.10 allows denial of service via packet injection or crafted capture file

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function only contains static hf_register_info/ett table initializers for field registration; it performs no packet parsing or buffer access, so no out-of-bounds read is present in these lines.

commit_msg: https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/issues/126
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['          for (x=0; x < (ssize_t) number_pixels; x+=2)'], 'added_lines': ['          for (x=0; x < (ssize_t) number_pixels; x+=4)']}
description: The generic decoder in ImageMagick allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds access) via a crafted file.

code_evidence: The 10-bit packed loop advances x by 2 per iteration but writes two pixels (two q+=GetPixelChannels(image) at lines 63 and 67), so it consumes/emit 2 pixels while the loop bound counts pixels; the per-iteration inner loop reads a 4-byte long pixel via PushLongPixel (line 38) and indexes cbcr[i] for i in 0..3 (line 56), with p advancing by pad at line 59. The corrected stride is x+=4 to match the 4-sample read per iteration.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads 4-byte pixel data through PushLongPixel while iterating more times than the buffer supports, which is a direct out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). It is not a write overflow; the unsafe operation is the read past the intended buffer, matching CWE-125's read-past-end definition.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the loop stride (x+=2) does not match the number of samples consumed per iteration (four samples via the inner i<4 loop and PushLongPixel), so the loop executes too many iterations relative to the input data. Trigger: a crafted file whose number_pixels and packed 10-bit data cause PushLongPixel to read past the end of the pixel buffer p on later iterations. Consequence: out-of-bounds read leading to denial of service (crash).

commit_msg: fix directory traversal bug
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '    char real_path[PATH_MAX];', '    if (!realpath(buffer.filename, real_path))', '    {', '        return SW_FALSE;', '    }', '', "    if (real_path[serv->document_root_len] != '/')", '    {', '        return SW_FALSE;', '    }', '', '    if (strncmp(real_path, serv->document_root, serv->document_root_len) != 0)', '    {', '        return SW_FALSE;', '    }']}
description: Swoole before 4.2.13 allows directory traversal in swPort_http_static_handler.

code_evidence: The function builds buffer.filename by copying serv->document_root then appending the raw request URL bytes (n = url_length or up to '?'), with no check for '..' or absolute-path sequences before the buffer is used.

It then calls lstat(buffer.filename, ...) directly on this unvalidated concatenation and serves the file if it is a regular file, so a traversal sequence in the URL resolves outside the document root.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-22 fits because externally supplied URL input constructs a pathname intended to stay under the document root, yet special elements are not neutralized so the path can escape that restricted directory. The added realpath/prefix checks in the patch confirm the missing constraint in this function.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the request URL is concatenated onto the document root and used as a filesystem path without neutralizing '..' or absolute elements. Trigger: a request URL containing traversal sequences reaches swPort_http_static_handler. Consequence: lstat and the subsequent sendfile serve files outside the intended document root, enabling unauthorized file reads.

commit_msg: https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/issues/85
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['                  (Rec2.RecordLength-2-2) / 3)'], 'added_lines': ['                  (Rec2.RecordLength-2-2)/3)', '                ThrowReaderException(CorruptImageError,"InvalidColormapIndex");', '              if (WPG_Palette.StartIndex > WPG_Palette.NumOfEntries)']}
description: The ReadWPGImage function in coders/wpg.c in ImageMagick 7.0.7-9 does not properly validate the colormap index in a WPG palette, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (use of uninitialized data or invalid memory allocation) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a malformed WPG file.

code_evidence: StartIndex and NumOfEntries are read from the WPG palette record without validating StartIndex against NumOfEntries or the allocated colormap size. image->colors is set to NumOfEntries and the colormap is allocated accordingly, but the loop writes image->colormap[i] for i from StartIndex to NumOfEntries-1. If StartIndex exceeds NumOfEntries the loop body is skipped; the missing constraint is that StartIndex must not exceed the allocated colormap entries, and the (NumOfEntries-StartIndex) size check uses unsigned arithmetic that can wrap.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs writes through image->colormap[i] where i derives from an unvalidated palette index, operating outside the intended buffer boundaries. This is a direct violation of memory buffer bounds, matching CWE-119. The more specific CWE-787 could apply, but the target CWE-119 is the supplied label and the out-of-bounds write operation supports it.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The root cause is that palette StartIndex is used directly as a colormap write index while allocation is based only on NumOfEntries, with no check that StartIndex is within the allocated buffer. A malformed WPG palette with an out-of-range StartIndex triggers out-of-bounds writes to image->colormap, corrupting adjacent heap memory and causing denial of service or potentially other impact.

commit_msg: https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/issues/81
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      MagickMax(image->columns,bytes_per_line)*sizeof(*sun_pixels));', '    ResetMagickMemory(sun_pixels,0,height*MagickMax(image->columns,', '      bytes_per_line)*sizeof(*sun_pixels));'], 'added_lines': ['      (MagickMax(image->columns,bytes_per_line)+1)*sizeof(*sun_pixels));', '    ResetMagickMemory(sun_pixels,0,height*(MagickMax(image->columns,', '      bytes_per_line)+1)*sizeof(*sun_pixels));']}
description: The ReadSUNImage function in coders/sun.c in ImageMagick allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read) via a crafted SUN file.

code_evidence: sun_pixels is allocated with height*MagickMax(image->columns,bytes_per_line) bytes; the buffer is sized to the larger of the row width and padded line length.
The same product is used for the ResetMagickMemory zeroing, so the allocation size matches the cleared region.

For non-encoded data, CopyMagickMemory copies sun_info.length bytes into sun_pixels after only checking sun_info.length > height*bytes_per_line, without accounting for height*image->columns when columns exceeds bytes_per_line.

The decode loops advance p byte-by-byte and additionally skip a padding byte per row (lines 228-229, 254-255), so reads can run past the allocated region when the copy fills it to the height*bytes_per_line bound.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads past the end of the sun_pixels buffer, matching CWE-125's out-of-bounds read definition. It is a read, not a CWE-787 write, because the overrun occurs in pixel decoding reads of *p.

evidence_lines.code:
sun_pixels=(unsigned char *) AcquireQuantumMemory(height,
MagickMax(image->columns,bytes_per_line)*sizeof(*sun_pixels));

ResetMagickMemory(sun_pixels,0,height*MagickMax(image->columns,
bytes_per_line)*sizeof(*sun_pixels));

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The buffer size uses MagickMax(image->columns,bytes_per_line) per row, but the copy guard and padding skips are based only on bytes_per_line; a crafted SUN file where columns dominates can fill the buffer and then the row loop reads *p past the end. Root cause is the mismatched size/bound accounting; trigger is a crafted header, consequence is an out-of-bounds read (DoS).

commit_msg:
Decoder Update mb count after mb map is set.

Bug: 25928803

Change-Id: Iccc58a7dd1c5c6ea656dfca332cfb8dddba4de37
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        ps_dec->u2_total_mbs_coded++;', ''], 'added_lines': ['            ps_dec->u2_total_mbs_coded += u1_num_mbs;']}
description: mediaserver in Android 6.x before 2016-03-01 allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code or cause a denial of service (memory corruption) via a crafted media file, related to decoder/ih264d_parse_islice.c and decoder/ih264d_parse_pslice.c, aka internal bug 25928803.

code_evidence: After each macroblock the loop increments i2_cur_mb_addr, u1_num_mbs and u2_total_mbs_coded (the latter is the line removed by the patch), advances ps_parse_mb_data, and computes u1_num_mbs_next/u1_end_of_row/u1_tfr_n_mb to decide when a group of macroblocks is transferred.

When u1_decode_nmb is set, the transfer/decode path (ih264d_parse_tfr_nmb / ih264d_decode_recon_tfr_nmb) runs and, if u1_tfr_n_mb, resets u1_num_mbs=0 and u1_mb_idx=0; u2_total_mbs_coded is only updated here in the fixed version via += u1_num_mbs.

The per-MB increment of u2_total_mbs_coded in the original code made the total-mbs counter inconsistent with the reset/transfer grouping, so the counter could exceed the intended coded-MB count and drive later buffer-indexed operations out of bounds.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The counter mismatch leads to reads/writes outside the intended buffer bounds during decoding, matching CWE-119. It is not merely an integer overflow: the unsafe operation is an out-of-bounds memory access driven by the desynchronized count.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the coded-macroblock counter is advanced per macroblock instead of per transferred group, so it desynchronizes from u1_num_mbs and the reset at transfer. Trigger: a crafted H.264 slice with skip runs/group boundaries causes the counter to diverge; the corrupted count is then used to index memory, producing memory corruption (CWE-119) and potentially code execution or DoS.

commit_msg:
mwifiex: pcie: Fix memory leak in mwifiex_pcie_alloc_cmdrsp_buf

In mwifiex_pcie_alloc_cmdrsp_buf, a new skb is allocated which should be
released if mwifiex_map_pci_memory() fails. The release is added.

Fixes: fc3314609047 ("mwifiex: use pci_alloc/free_consistent APIs for PCIe")
Signed-off-by: Navid Emamdoost <navid.emamdoost@gmail.com>
Acked-by: Ganapathi Bhat <gbhat@marvell.com>
Signed-off-by: Kalle Valo <kvalo@codeaurora.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t\t   PCI_DMA_FROMDEVICE))'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t\t   PCI_DMA_FROMDEVICE)) {', '\t\tkfree_skb(skb);', '\t}']}
description: A memory leak in the mwifiex_pcie_alloc_cmdrsp_buf() function in drivers/net/wireless/marvell/mwifiex/pcie.c in the Linux kernel through 5.3.11 allows attackers to cause a denial of service (memory consumption) by triggering mwifiex_map_pci_memory() failures, aka CID-db8fd2cde932.

code_evidence: Line 5 allocates an skb with dev_alloc_skb and stores it in local variable skb. Line 11 advances the skb, then lines 12-14 call mwifiex_map_pci_memory and return -1 on failure without freeing skb; card->cmdrsp_buf is only assigned at line 15 on the success path, so the failed path loses the only reference.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-401 fits because an allocated resource is abandoned on an error path without release, making it unreclaimable. This is a memory leak rather than a use-after-free or double-free, since the pointer is simply lost, not reused or freed twice.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the error path after a failed mwifiex_map_pci_memory call returns -1 while the freshly allocated skb is neither freed nor stored in card->cmdrsp_buf. Trigger: a DMA mapping failure for the command-response buffer. Consequence: the skb allocation is leaked, and repeated failures exhaust memory, supporting a denial of service.

commit_msg:
In rkvdec_probe, rkvdec->watchdog_work is bound with
rkvdec_watchdog_func. Then rkvdec_vp9_run may
be called to start the work.

If we remove the module which will call rkvdec_remove
 to make cleanup, there may be a unfinished work.
 The possible sequence is as follows, which will
 cause a typical UAF bug.

Fix it by canceling the work before cleanup in rkvdec_remove.

CPU0                  CPU1

                    |rkvdec_watchdog_func
rkvdec_remove       |
 rkvdec_v4l2_cleanup|
  v4l2_m2m_release  |
    kfree(m2m_dev); |
                    |
                    | v4l2_m2m_get_curr_priv
                    |   m2m_dev->curr_ctx //use

Fixes: cd33c830448b ("media: rkvdec: Add the rkvdec driver")
Signed-off-by: Zheng Wang <zyytlz.wz@163.com>
Signed-off-by: Hans Verkuil <hverkuil-cisco@xs4all.nl>
Signed-off-by: Mauro Carvalho Chehab <mchehab@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\tcancel_delayed_work_sync(&rkvdec->watchdog_work);']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel before 6.3.2. A use-after-free was found in rkvdec_remove in drivers/staging/media/rkvdec/rkvdec.c.

code_evidence: rkvdec_remove retrieves the device state and immediately calls rkvdec_v4l2_cleanup without first canceling rkvdec->watchdog_work, so the delayed watchdog work can still be pending or running while cleanup frees the m2m context.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function lacks synchronization (work cancellation) before releasing a shared resource, allowing an interfering concurrent sequence to access it, which matches CWE-362. The UAF is the resulting consequence, not the primary weakness.

evidence_lines.code:
struct rkvdec_dev *rkvdec = platform_get_drvdata(pdev);
rkvdec_v4l2_cleanup(rkvdec);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: teardown frees the v4l2/m2m resources while the watchdog delayed work bound in probe may still execute concurrently. Trigger: module removal races with rkvdec_watchdog_func, which later calls v4l2_m2m_get_curr_priv on the freed m2m_dev. Consequence: use-after-free and potential crash.

commit_msg:
proc.c: add `mrb_state` argument to `mrb_proc_copy()`.

The function may invoke the garbage collection and it requires
`mrb_state` to run.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  mrb_proc_copy(mrb_proc_ptr(self), mrb_proc_ptr(proc));'], 'added_lines': ['  mrb_proc_copy(mrb, mrb_proc_ptr(self), mrb_proc_ptr(proc));']}
description: mruby is vulnerable to NULL Pointer Dereference

code_evidence: mrb_get_arg1(mrb) yields proc, which is only checked with mrb_proc_p; the code then dereferences mrb_proc_ptr(self) and mrb_proc_ptr(proc) when calling mrb_proc_copy. The commit message states this copy may invoke garbage collection and now requires mrb_state, so the call as written (without mrb) is the faulty dereference site.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences proc pointers through mrb_proc_copy while the required mrb_state is absent, matching CWE-476's NULL pointer dereference. It is not merely a type-validation issue, since mrb_proc_p already guards the argument type.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: mrb_proc_copy is invoked without the mrb_state needed for GC-safe copying, and the proc pointers are dereferenced on this path. Trigger: calling init_copy with a proc argument. The supported consequence is a crash/DoS from the resulting NULL pointer dereference; code execution is not demonstrated.

commit_msg:
Replace most malloc uses with calloc

Closes #236.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    hex_string = malloc((size * 2) + 1);'], 'added_lines': ['    hex_string = calloc((size * 2) + 1, sizeof(char));', '', '']}
description: libmaxminddb before 1.4.3 has a heap-based buffer over-read in dump_entry_data_list in maxminddb.c.

code_evidence: hex_string is allocated with malloc((size * 2) + 1), leaving its bytes uninitialized. The loop writes two-hex-digit strings via sprintf for each input byte, but the allocation is not zeroed first, and the code relies on the buffer being fully overwritten. If size is zero or the loop does not cover the intended region, uninitialized/lacking data is later read as a string.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The commit replaces malloc with calloc to fix uninitialized buffer contents that lead to out-of-bounds reads in callers. CWE-125 fits because the supported consequence is reading data past the intended buffer; the fix addresses the uninitialized allocation that enables the over-read.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the output buffer is allocated with malloc rather than calloc, so its contents are indeterminate. The function returns hex_string to callers that treat it as a NUL-terminated string; when the loop does not fully initialize the buffer (e.g., size 0), a caller reading the string can read past the intended region. The supported consequence is an out-of-bounds read of memory.

commit_msg: Add limit to recursion
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            add(obj_mvo, "_", v, resolver);'], 'added_lines': ['            add(obj_mvo, "_", v, resolver, recursion_depth);']}
description: EOSIO/eos eos version after commit f1545dd0ae2b77580c2236fdb70ae7138d2c7168 contains a stack overflow vulnerability in abi_serializer that can result in attack eos network node. This attack appear to be exploitable via network request. This vulnerability appears to have been fixed in after commit cf7209e703e6d3f7a5413e0cb1fe88a4d8e4b38d .

code_evidence: The call operator unconditionally forwards to add(obj_mvo, "_", v, resolver) with no recursion-depth argument or bound check; the patched version adds recursion_depth to that call, indicating this call site is part of the recursive path.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-674 fits because recursion depth is not controlled, consuming the program stack. The missing depth parameter is the concrete evidence; this is uncontrolled recursion rather than simply excessive resource allocation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the add call is made without tracking or limiting recursion depth, so nested values drive unbounded descent through add. Trigger: a network-supplied ABI/JSON structure with deeply nested objects or arrays. Consequence: stack exhaustion leading to a node crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
basic: fix touch() creating files with 07777 mode

mode_t is unsigned, so MODE_INVALID < 0 can never be true.

This fixes a possible DoS where any user could fill /run by writing to
a world-writable /run/systemd/show-status.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        fd = open(path, O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_CLOEXEC|O_NOCTTY, mode > 0 ? mode : 0644);'], 'added_lines': ['        fd = open(path, O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_CLOEXEC|O_NOCTTY,', '                        (mode == 0 || mode == MODE_INVALID) ? 0644 : mode);']}
description: A flaw in systemd v228 in /src/basic/fs-util.c caused world writable suid files to be created when using the systemd timers features, allowing local attackers to escalate their privileges to root. This is fixed in v229.

code_evidence: Line 7 passes `mode > 0 ? mode : 0644` to open(); mode is mode_t (unsigned), so a MODE_INVALID value (negative sentinel) is treated as > 0 and forwarded as the creation mode.
Lines 10-14 then call fchmod(fd, mode) whenever mode != MODE_INVALID; with the unsigned sentinel mishandled, the file can be created/chmodded with attacker-influenced permission bits.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function mishandles permission bits when creating files, directly producing insecure access controls; this matches CWE-264's permissions/privileges management category. A related memory-safety or path-traversal label would not fit, since the defect is the improper permission value, not memory or path handling.

evidence_lines.code: fd = open(path, O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_CLOEXEC|O_NOCTTY, mode > 0 ? mode : 0644);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the signedness of mode_t makes the `mode > 0` guard unable to reject MODE_INVALID, so the invalid sentinel is passed as an open() permission mode and later applied via fchmod. Trigger: a caller supplying MODE_INVALID (or equivalent negative-as-unsigned value). Consequence: files created with permissive/special permission bits rather than the intended 0644 default, enabling unauthorized access or privilege escalation.

code_evidence: Lines 6-7 compute input_size_per_poa and output_size_per_poa as products of max_sequences_per_poa_/CUDAPOA_MAX_CONSENSUS_SIZE with poa_count, stored in size_t without any upper-bound check on the multiplicands.

Lines 8-12 repeatedly multiply these sizes by sizeof(...), max_sequences_per_poa_, max_nodes_per_window_, max_graph_dimension_ and CUDAPOA_MAX_NODE_EDGES/ALIGNMENTS and accumulate into size_t host_size_per_poa/device_size_per_poa; each accumulation can exceed the representable range before the tuple is returned at line 13.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function's sole purpose is computing allocation sizes, and its unchecked multiplicative accumulation directly matches CWE-190: an integer calculation whose result can exceed the type's range and wrap. The patch's size_t-to-int64_t change confirms the overflow concern; this is not merely a truncation (CWE-197) because the arithmetic itself can exceed the representation.

evidence_lines.code:
size_t input_size_per_poa  = max_sequences_per_poa_ * CUDAPOA_MAX_SEQUENCE_SIZE * poa_count;
size_t output_size_per_poa = CUDAPOA_MAX_CONSENSUS_SIZE * poa_count;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: memory-size arithmetic uses size_t without validating that the products of sequence/node/graph dimensions stay within range. Trigger: large max_sequences_per_poa_, max_nodes_per_window_ or max_graph_dimension_ values. Consequence: host_size_per_poa/device_size_per_poa wrap to small or zero values, so the returned allocation sizes are understated, leading to undersized cudapoa memory allocation and subsequent out-of-bounds access.

commit_msg:
Add support for mount options to restrict access to /proc/PID/
directories.  The default backward-compatible "relaxed" behaviour is left
untouched.

The first mount option is called "hidepid" and its value defines how much
info about processes we want to be available for non-owners:

hidepid=0 (default) means the old behavior - anybody may read all
world-readable /proc/PID/* files.

hidepid=1 means users may not access any /proc/<pid>/ directories, but
their own.  Sensitive files like cmdline, sched*, status are now protected
against other users.  As permission checking done in proc_pid_permission()
and files' permissions are left untouched, programs expecting specific
files' modes are not confused.

hidepid=2 means hidepid=1 plus all /proc/PID/ will be invisible to other
users.  It doesn't mean that it hides whether a process exists (it can be
learned by other means, e.g.  by kill -0 $PID), but it hides process' euid
and egid.  It compicates intruder's task of gathering info about running
processes, whether some daemon runs with elevated privileges, whether
another user runs some sensitive program, whether other users run any
program at all, etc.

gid=XXX defines a group that will be able to gather all processes' info
(as in hidepid=0 mode).  This group should be used instead of putting
nonroot user in sudoers file or something.  However, untrusted users (like
daemons, etc.) which are not supposed to monitor the tasks in the whole
system should not be added to the group.

hidepid=1 or higher is designed to restrict access to procfs files, which
might reveal some sensitive private information like precise keystrokes
timings:

http://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2011/11/05/3

hidepid=1/2 doesn't break monitoring userspace tools.  ps, top, pgrep, and
conky gracefully handle EPERM/ENOENT and behave as if the current user is
the only user running processes.  pstree shows the process subtree which
contains "pstree" process.

Note: the patch doesn't deal with setuid/setgid issues of keeping
preopened descriptors of procfs files (like
https://lkml.org/lkml/2011/2/7/368).  We rely on that the leaked
information like the scheduling counters of setuid apps doesn't threaten
anybody's privacy - only the user started the setuid program may read the
counters.

description: The EIGRP parser in tcpdump before 4.9.2 has a buffer over-read in print-eigrp.c:eigrp_print().

code_evidence: The TLV loop validates eigrp_tlv_len against the TLV header and tlen [50,51], then computes tlv_tlen = eigrp_tlv_len - sizeof(header) [62] and only ND_TCHECKs the declared TLV length [63].
For EIGRP_TLV_GENERAL_PARM, tlv_tptr is cast to eigrp_tlv_general_parm_t [66] and fields up to k5 are read [67-73] without comparing tlv_tlen to sizeof(*tlv_ptr.eigrp_tlv_general_parm).
For EIGRP_TLV_IP_INT, the pointer is cast [84] and destination is memcpy'd with byte_length derived from plen [85-92], again without ensuring tlv_tlen covers the full struct.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe dereference of a short TLV reads memory beyond the intended buffer, matching CWE-125 (out-of-bounds read). It is not a write (CWE-787) since only reads occur; the missing per-type size check is the direct cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: per-TLV length (tlv_tlen) is not checked against the size of the specific TLV structure before the pointer is cast and its fields are dereferenced. Trigger: a crafted EIGRP packet whose TLV declares a length large enough to pass the loop checks but smaller than the struct for its type. Consequence: reads past the TLV buffer, i.e. an out-of-bounds read.

commit_msg: Fix assertion in debug mode / heap-based buffer overflow in opj_write_bytes_LE for Cinema profiles with numresolutions = 1 (#985)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    parameters->res_spec = parameters->numresolution - 1;', '    for (i = 0; i < parameters->res_spec; i++) {', '        parameters->prcw_init[i] = 256;', '        parameters->prch_init[i] = 256;'], 'added_lines': ['    if (parameters->numresolution == 1) {', '        parameters->res_spec = 1;', '        parameters->prcw_init[0] = 128;', '        parameters->prch_init[0] = 128;', '    } else {', '        parameters->res_spec = parameters->numresolution - 1;', '        for (i = 0; i < parameters->res_spec; i++) {', '            parameters->prcw_init[i] = 256;', '            parameters->prch_init[i] = 256;', '        }']}
description: A mishandled zero case was discovered in opj_j2k_set_cinema_parameters in lib/openjp2/j2k.c in OpenJPEG 2.2.0. The vulnerability causes an out-of-bounds write, which may lead to remote denial of service (heap-based buffer overflow affecting opj_write_bytes_LE in lib/openjp2/cio.c and opj_j2k_write_sot in lib/openjp2/j2k.c) or possibly remote code execution.

code_evidence: The function sets res_spec = numresolution - 1 and then loops i < res_spec writing prcw_init[i] and prch_init[i]. For Cinema 4K, lines 44-50 force numresolution to 1 when it is below 2, so numresolution - 1 becomes 0; the loop body never executes, leaving the precinct arrays uninitialized for the single resolution later consumed by the encoder. The guard is missing for the zero-res_spec case.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the mishandled zero case causes writes past the end of an intended buffer in downstream encoding (opj_write_bytes_LE), an out-of-bounds write. It is not merely an uninitialized read; the supported impact is memory corruption via out-of-bounds write.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: numresolution can be 1 for Cinema 4K, making res_spec zero and skipping initialization of prcw_init/prch_init[0]. Trigger: encoding a Cinema 4K image with numresolution=1. Consequence: downstream code in opj_write_bytes_LE/opj_j2k_write_sot uses the unset precinct state, leading to a heap-based out-of-bounds write (DoS, possible RCE).

commit_msg:
tunnels: Don't apply GRO to multiple layers of encapsulation.

When drivers express support for TSO of encapsulated packets, they
only mean that they can do it for one layer of encapsulation.
Supporting additional levels would mean updating, at a minimum,
more IP length fields and they are unaware of this.

No encapsulation device expresses support for handling offloaded
encapsulated packets, so we won't generate these types of frames
in the transmit path. However, GRO doesn't have a check for
multiple levels of encapsulation and will attempt to build them.

UDP tunnel GRO actually does prevent this situation but it only
handles multiple UDP tunnels stacked on top of each other. This
generalizes that solution to prevent any kind of tunnel stacking
that would cause problems.

Fixes: bf5a755f ("net-gre-gro: Add GRE support to the GRO stack")
Signed-off-by: Jesse Gross <jesse@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (NAPI_GRO_CB(skb)->udp_mark ||', '\t/* mark that this skb passed once through the udp gro layer */', '\tNAPI_GRO_CB(skb)->udp_mark = 1;'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (NAPI_GRO_CB(skb)->encap_mark ||', '\t/* mark that this skb passed once through the tunnel gro layer */', '\tNAPI_GRO_CB(skb)->encap_mark = 1;']}
description: The IP stack in the Linux kernel before 4.6 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (stack consumption and panic) or possibly have unspecified other impact by triggering use of the GRO path for packets with tunnel stacking, as demonstrated by interleaved IPv4 headers and GRE headers, a related issue to CVE-2016-7039.

code_evidence: udp_gro_receive() checks NAPI_GRO_CB(skb)->udp_mark and, when already set, jumps to out without processing. Otherwise it unconditionally sets udp_mark = 1 before invoking the offload gro_receive callback at line 39, allowing one UDP tunnel GRO pass. The mark is the only guard against re-entering this GRO layer; it is not a general encapsulation-depth limit.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-400 fits because the function fails to constrain how many resources (stack frames, per-packet encapsulation layers) GRO processing consumes, and the commit explicitly generalizes udp_mark to encap_mark to prevent tunnel stacking. The weakness is missing resource/depth control, not a memory-safety flaw.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the single udp_mark flag only prevents repeated UDP tunnel GRO and does not bound stacking with other tunnel types (e.g., GRE/IPv4), so packets with interleaved encapsulation are still built into multiple layers. Trigger: a remote sender transmits tunnel-stacked packets that traverse the GRO path; each nested layer causes additional recursion/stack consumption. Supported consequence: unbounded GRO recursion leading to stack exhaustion and kernel panic (DoS).

description: ntp_openssl.m4 in ntpd in NTP before 4.2.7p112 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (segmentation fault) via a crafted statistics or filegen configuration command that is not enabled during compilation.

commit_msg:
With write operation on psi files replacing old trigger with a new one,
the lifetime of its waitqueue is totally arbitrary. Overwriting an
existing trigger causes its waitqueue to be freed and pending poll()
will stumble on trigger->event_wait which was destroyed.
Fix this by disallowing to redefine an existing psi trigger. If a write
operation is used on a file descriptor with an already existing psi
trigger, the operation will fail with EBUSY error.
Also bypass a check for psi_disabled in the psi_trigger_destroy as the
flag can be flipped after the trigger is created, leading to a memory
leak.

Fixes: 0e94682b73bf ("psi: introduce psi monitor")
Reported-by: syzbot+cdb5dd11c97cc532efad@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Suggested-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Analyzed-by: Eric Biggers <ebiggers@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Suren Baghdasaryan <surenb@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Peter Zijlstra (Intel) <peterz@infradead.org>
Reviewed-by: Eric Biggers <ebiggers@google.com>
Acked-by: Johannes Weiner <hannes@cmpxchg.org>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220111232309.1786347-1-surenb@google.com
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tkref_init(&t->refcount);'], 'added_lines': []}
description: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's implementation of Pressure Stall Information. While the feature is disabled by default, it could allow an attacker to crash the system or have other memory-corruption side effects.

code_evidence: The function initializes t->event_wait and t->refcount, then registers the new trigger on group->triggers while holding trigger_lock.
The diff removes kref_init(&t->refcount) (line 34), and the function does not check whether group already has a trigger for this state before list_add at line 48.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The root cause is that an existing trigger is redefined and its waitqueue is freed while another path still holds a reference, which matches CWE-416 use after free. This is not merely a memory leak; the freed object is subsequently dereferenced.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: A write to an existing psi file can create a second trigger for the same state and add it to group->triggers without rejecting the existing one. The prior trigger's waitqueue can be freed while pending poll() still references trigger->event_wait, and the missing refcount initialization leaves the lifetime unmanaged, allowing use of freed memory.

commit_msg:
staging/android/ion : fix a race condition in the ion driver

There is a use-after-free problem in the ion driver.
This is caused by a race condition in the ion_ioctl()
function.

A handle has ref count of 1 and two tasks on different
cpus calls ION_IOC_FREE simultaneously.

cpu 0                                   cpu 1
-------------------------------------------------------
ion_handle_get_by_id()
(ref == 2)
                            ion_handle_get_by_id()
                            (ref == 3)

ion_free()
(ref == 2)

ion_handle_put()
(ref == 1)

                            ion_free()
                            (ref == 0 so ion_handle_destroy() is
                            called
                            and the handle is freed.)

                            ion_handle_put() is called and it
                            decreases the slub's next free pointer

The problem is detected as an unaligned access in the
spin lock functions since it uses load exclusive
 instruction. In some cases it corrupts the slub's
free pointer which causes a mis-aligned access to the
next free pointer.(kmalloc returns a pointer like
ffffc0745b4580aa). And it causes lots of other
hard-to-debug problems.

This symptom is caused since the first member in the
ion_handle structure is the reference count and the
ion driver decrements the reference after it has been
freed.

To fix this problem client->lock mutex is extended
to protect all the codes that uses the handle.

Signed-off-by: Eun Taik Lee <eun.taik.lee@samsung.com>
Reviewed-by: Laura Abbott <labbott@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['static struct ion_handle *ion_handle_get_by_id(struct ion_client *client,', '\thandle = idr_find(&client->idr, id);', '\tif (handle)', '\t\tion_handle_get(handle);', '\treturn handle ? handle : ERR_PTR(-EINVAL);'], 'added_lines': ['struct ion_handle *ion_handle_get_by_id(struct ion_client *client,', '\thandle = ion_handle_get_by_id_nolock(client, id);', '\treturn handle;']}
description: Race condition in the ion_ioctl function in drivers/staging/android/ion/ion.c in the Linux kernel before 4.6 allows local users to gain privileges or cause a denial of service (use-after-free) by calling ION_IOC_FREE on two CPUs at the same time.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The shown function only does locked idr lookup and reference acquisition; the described use-after-free race involves ion_free/ion_handle_put and is not visible or directly supported in these lines, and CWE-264 is an obsolete category rather than a specific weakness.

commit_msg: Fix conversion from GDB register profile to rizin profile
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tchar perm[32];', '\tchar name[512];', '\t\t\tsscanf(str, "0x%" PFMT64x " - 0x%" PFMT64x " %s %s",'], 'added_lines': ['\tchar perm[IO_MAPS_PERM_SZ + 1];', '\tchar name[IO_MAPS_NAME_SZ + 1];', '\t\t\tsscanf(str, "0x%" PFMT64x " - 0x%" PFMT64x " %" RZ_STR_DEF(IO_MAPS_PERM_SZ) "s %" RZ_STR_DEF(IO_MAPS_NAME_SZ) "s",']}
description: Rizin is a UNIX-like reverse engineering framework and command-line toolset. In version 0.5.1 and prior, converting a GDB registers profile file into a Rizin register profile can result in a stack-based buffer overflow when the `name`, `type`, or `groups` fields have longer values than expected. Users opening untrusted GDB registers files (e.g. with the `drpg` or `arpg` commands) are affected by this flaw. Commit d6196703d89c84467b600ba2692534579dc25ed4 contains a patch for this issue. As a workaround, review the GDB register profiles before loading them with `drpg`/`arpg` commands.

code_evidence: Fixed-size stack buffers perm[32] and name[512] are declared for the permission and name fields.
sscanf with unbounded %s conversions copies the perm and name tokens from the input line into these fixed buffers with no width limit, so an overlong token writes past the buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This is a buffer copy without checking input size: sscanf writes input bytes into a bounded stack buffer without a width constraint, matching CWE-120 rather than an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125).

evidence_lines.code:
char perm[32];
char name[512];

sscanf(str, "0x%" PFMT64x " - 0x%" PFMT64x " %s %s",
&map_start, &map_end, perm, name);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the sscanf %s conversions lack field-width limits, so input-derived perm/name tokens of arbitrary length are copied into fixed-size stack arrays. Trigger: a line from the GDB register/maps profile whose permission or name field exceeds the buffer size; the consequence is a stack-based buffer overflow that can corrupt memory or crash.

commit_msg: Fix bug #73631 - Invalid read when wddx decodes empty boolean element
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\t} else {', '\t\t\tent.type = ST_BOOLEAN;', '\t\t\tSET_STACK_VARNAME;', '\t\t\tZVAL_FALSE(&ent.data);', '\t\t\twddx_stack_push((wddx_stack *)stack, &ent, sizeof(st_entry));']}
description: The php_wddx_push_element function in ext/wddx/wddx.c in PHP before 5.6.29 and 7.x before 7.0.14 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read and memory corruption) or possibly have unspecified other impact via an empty boolean element in a wddxPacket XML document.

code_evidence: The EL_BOOLEAN branch only initializes and pushes a stack entry inside the attribute loop when an EL_VALUE attribute with a non-empty value exists (lines 49-59). If the boolean element is empty, the loop body never executes, so no ST_BOOLEAN entry is pushed and ent is left uninitialized. The subsequent php_wddx_process_data/close handling operates on a stack that does not contain the expected boolean frame.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125): the parser proceeds without a valid pushed entry, so downstream stack access reads past the intended buffer. This is a read-boundary flaw, not merely a NULL dereference or logic error.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the empty-boolean case skips stack initialization because the push is guarded by the attribute/value presence check. Trigger: a wddxPacket XML document containing an empty <boolean/> element. Consequence: later processing reads from an empty or mismatched stack frame, causing an out-of-bounds read and possible memory corruption/DoS.

commit_msg:
[webp] Enforce minimum read size in decodeChunks

The size parameter is only checked for upper bounds, but not for lower.
If it is too small, then created dataBuf will be too small and overflow in one
of the subsequent memcpy() calls.

This fixes #378 / CVE-2018-14046
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['                enforce(size >= 10, Exiv2::kerCorruptedMetadata);', '', '                enforce(size >= 10, Exiv2::kerCorruptedMetadata);', '', '                enforce(size >= 5, Exiv2::kerCorruptedMetadata);', '', '                enforce(size >= 12, Exiv2::kerCorruptedMetadata);', '']}
description: Exiv2 0.26 has a heap-based buffer over-read in WebPImage::decodeChunks in webpimage.cpp.

code_evidence: Line 13 reads attacker-controlled chunk size; line 14 only enforces an upper bound (size <= remaining), and line 15 allocates payload of that exact size with no lower bound.
For VP8X, a tiny size makes payload.pData_ shorter than 8 bytes, yet lines 19-20 read payload.pData_[4..6] via memcpy past the allocated buffer.
For VP8, a small payload is read at line 28, then line 30 memcpy reads payload.pData_[6..7], beyond a buffer smaller than 8 bytes.
For VP8L, payload read at line 42; lines 43 and 46 index payload.pData_[1..4], exceeding a payload shorter than 5 bytes.
For ANMF, payload read at line 53; lines 54 and 57 index payload.pData_[6..11], beyond a payload smaller than 12 bytes.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads beyond the allocated payload buffer because a missing minimum-size constraint lets fixed-offset memcpy reads exceed the buffer. This is a direct out-of-bounds read (CWE-125); the added enforce(size >= N) checks confirm the intended lower-bound constraint.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the chunk size is validated only against an upper bound, so a crafted WebP chunk with a very small size allocates a too-small payload. Trigger: a VP8X/VP8/VP8L/ANMF chunk with size below the fixed offsets then causes memcpy to read past the end of payload.pData_. Consequence: heap-based out-of-bounds read (over-read), leaking/crashing.

commit_msg:
When creating a raw AF_AX25 socket, CAP_NET_RAW needs to be checked
first.

Signed-off-by: Ori Nimron <orinimron123@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (!capable(CAP_NET_RAW))', '\t\t\treturn -EPERM;']}
description: ax25_create in net/ax25/af_ax25.c in the AF_AX25 network module in the Linux kernel 3.16 through 5.3.2 does not enforce CAP_NET_RAW, which means that unprivileged users can create a raw socket, aka CID-0614e2b73768.

code_evidence: The SOCK_RAW case falls straight through to break without any capability check, so the switch accepts raw socket creation unconditionally.
Execution then reaches sk_alloc and allocates the socket, so an unprivileged caller obtains a raw AF_AX25 socket.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs no authorization check before allowing a privileged operation, which is exactly missing authorization (CWE-862). It is not an improper input validation issue; the socket type is valid, but the caller's privilege is never verified.

evidence_lines.code:
case SOCK_RAW:
break;
sk = sk_alloc(net, PF_AX25, GFP_ATOMIC, &ax25_proto, kern);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: ax25_create authorizes SOCK_RAW solely by socket type, omitting the CAP_NET_RAW capability check applied in the patched version. Trigger: an unprivileged user calls socket(PF_AX25, SOCK_RAW, ...). The missing check lets allocation proceed, granting raw socket access the caller should not have.

commit_msg:
RDS: fix race condition when sending a message on unbound socket

Sasha's found a NULL pointer dereference in the RDS connection code when
sending a message to an apparently unbound socket.  The problem is caused
by the code checking if the socket is bound in rds_sendmsg(), which checks
the rs_bound_addr field without taking a lock on the socket.  This opens a
race where rs_bound_addr is temporarily set but where the transport is not
in rds_bind(), leading to a NULL pointer dereference when trying to
dereference 'trans' in __rds_conn_create().

Vegard wrote a reproducer for this issue, so kindly ask him to share if
you're interested.

I cannot reproduce the NULL pointer dereference using Vegard's reproducer
with this patch, whereas I could without.

Complete earlier incomplete fix to CVE-2015-6937:

  74e98eb08588 ("RDS: verify the underlying transport exists before creating a connection")

Cc: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org

Reviewed-by: Vegard Nossum <vegard.nossum@oracle.com>
Reviewed-by: Sasha Levin <sasha.levin@oracle.com>
Acked-by: Santosh Shilimkar <santosh.shilimkar@oracle.com>
Signed-off-by: Quentin Casasnovas <quentin.casasnovas@oracle.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (trans == NULL) {', '\t\tkmem_cache_free(rds_conn_slab, conn);', '\t\tconn = ERR_PTR(-ENODEV);', '\t\tgoto out;', '\t}', ''], 'added_lines': []}
description: Race condition in the rds_sendmsg function in net/rds/sendmsg.c in the Linux kernel before 4.3.3 allows local users to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference and system crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact by using a socket that was not properly bound.  NOTE: this vulnerability exists because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2015-6937.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The shown function __rds_conn_create lacks the unsynchronized rs_bound_addr check and transport lookup that constitute the race; the patch only removes a NULL check in this function, so the CWE-362 evidence is in other code not present here.

fixes #1184, #1186, #1187 among other things
