commit_msg:
prevent overflow in hufUncompress if nBits is large

Signed-off-by: Peter Hillman <peterh@wetafx.co.nz>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if ( ptr + (nBits+7 )/8 > compressed+nCompressed)'], 'added_lines': ['    uint64_t nBytes = (static_cast<uint64_t>(nBits)+7) / 8 ;', '', '    if ( ptr + nBytes > compressed+nCompressed)']}
description: A flaw was found in OpenEXR's hufUncompress functionality in OpenEXR/IlmImf/ImfHuf.cpp. This flaw allows an attacker who can submit a crafted file that is processed by OpenEXR, to trigger an integer overflow. The highest threat from this vulnerability is to system availability.

code_evidence: nBits is read from the untrusted compressed buffer as a 32-bit int at line 15 and is not range-checked before use. At line 19 the bound check computes (nBits+7)/8 in signed 32-bit arithmetic; a large nBits (near INT_MAX) makes nBits+7 overflow to a negative value, so the computed byte count is small or negative and the ptr + ... > compressed+nCompressed test can pass, bypassing notEnoughData().
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the defect is precisely an integer overflow/wraparound in a size calculation that is then used as a bound check, matching the Base-level weakness. It is not merely an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125); the overflow is the enabling root cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the required-byte count for nBits is computed with signed 32-bit addition (nBits+7) on an attacker-controlled value, so it can wrap. Trigger: a crafted file whose header sets nBits to a very large value. Consequence: the insufficient-data guard is defeated, allowing subsequent decoding to read past the compressed buffer, affecting availability (and potentially memory integrity).

commit_msg:
Bug 701118: Handle appending large display list nodes.

The size of the begin layer node depends on the size of the layer
name. That name may be a string from the page's property resources,
and is only bounded by memory when parsed by lex_string(). So the
append_list_node() logic cannot simply double the size of the
display list and hope that the node fits, since the node may be
of arbitrary size.

Now append_list_node() would repeatedly double the size of the
display list until the node fits, or malloc() runs out of memory.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (list->len + size > list->max)'], 'added_lines': ['\twhile (list->len + size > list->max)']}
description: Artifex MuPDF 1.15.0 has a heap-based buffer overflow in fz_append_display_node located at fitz/list-device.c, allowing remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via a crafted PDF file. This occurs with a large BDC property name that overflows the allocated size of a display list node.

code_evidence: The node size is accumulated from private_data_len and path_size; for a large BDC property name, private_data_len can be arbitrarily large, making size exceed MAX_NODE_SIZE and the current list->max.
The capacity check uses a single if: it doubles list->max once, reallocates, but does not re-check whether list->len + size still exceeds the new max.

node.size=size and the assert(size < (1<<9)) are only a debug assertion; node_ptr=&list->list[list->len] then *node_ptr=node writes past the reallocated buffer when size is larger than the grown capacity.
The subsequent memcpy(out_private, private_data, private_data_len) writes into node_ptr[private_off] within the undersized allocation, extending the overflow by the attacker-controlled length.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes a display node and its private data past the end of the reallocated list buffer, which is the out-of-bounds write described by CWE-787. The insufficient size check is the root cause, but the supported weakness is the resulting buffer overflow write rather than a mere integer issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: capacity growth is bounded to one doubling instead of looping until the node fits, so a node larger than the new allocation is accepted. Trigger: a crafted PDF with a very large BDC property name passed as private_data. Consequence: out-of-bounds heap writes via *node_ptr and the private-data memcpy, enabling memory corruption and potential code execution.

commit_msg: Validate the calculated address pointer based on the source routing header.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      uint8_t *addr_ptr = ((uint8_t *)rh_header) + RPL_RH_LEN + RPL_SRH_LEN + (i * (16 - cmpri));'], 'added_lines': ['      ptrdiff_t rh_offset = (uint8_t *)rh_header - uip_buf;', '      size_t addr_offset = RPL_RH_LEN + RPL_SRH_LEN + (i * (16 - cmpri));', '', '      if(rh_offset + addr_offset + 16 - cmpr > UIP_BUFSIZE) {', '        LOG_ERR("Invalid SRH address pointer\\n");', '        return 0;', '      }', '', '      uint8_t *addr_ptr = ((uint8_t *)rh_header) + addr_offset;']}
description: Contiki-NG is an open-source, cross-platform operating system for internet of things devices. The RPL-Classic and RPL-Lite implementations in the Contiki-NG operating system versions prior to 4.6 do not validate the address pointer in the RPL source routing header This makes it possible for an attacker to cause out-of-bounds writes with packets injected into the network stack. Specifically, the problem lies in the rpl_ext_header_srh_update function in the two rpl-ext-header.c modules for RPL-Classic and RPL-Lite respectively. The addr_ptr variable is calculated using an unvalidated CMPR field value from the source routing header. An out-of-bounds write can be triggered on line 151 in os/net/routing/rpl-lite/rpl-ext-header.c and line 261 in os/net/routing/rpl-classic/rpl-ext-header.c, which contain the following memcpy call with addr_ptr as destination. The problem has been patched in Contiki-NG 4.6. Users can apply a patch out-of-band as a workaround.

code_evidence: Line 31 computes index i from path_len and segments_left; line 32 derives addr_ptr from rh_header plus RPL_RH_LEN + RPL_SRH_LEN + (i * (16 - cmpri)) without any bounds check against the packet buffer.
Line 35 copies 16 - cmpr bytes to the IPv6 destination and line 36 copies 16 - cmpr bytes into addr_ptr, so the unvalidated offset becomes a memcpy destination.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because line 36 performs a memcpy into addr_ptr whose destination is not validated against buffer bounds, writing beyond the intended buffer. This is a write-side overflow, distinct from out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) at the same pointer.

evidence_lines.code:
memcpy(((uint8_t *)&UIP_IP_BUF->destipaddr) + cmpr, addr_ptr, 16 - cmpr);
memcpy(addr_ptr, ((uint8_t *)&current_dest_addr) + cmpr, 16 - cmpr);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The CMPR/path_len-derived offset is used directly to form addr_ptr with no verification that addr_ptr plus 16 - cmpr stays within uip_buf. An attacker-supplied source routing header with crafted Cmpri/segments_left makes i large, so the memcpy at line 36 writes past the packet buffer. The root cause is the missing bounds constraint on the calculated pointer; the consequence is an out-of-bounds write corrupting adjacent memory.

commit_msg: closes bpo-34656: Avoid relying on signed overflow in _pickle memos. (GH-9261)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    size_t mask = (size_t)self->mt_mask;'], 'added_lines': ['    size_t mask = self->mt_mask;']}
description: Modules/_pickle.c in Python before 3.7.1 has an integer overflow via a large LONG_BINPUT value that is mishandled during a "resize to twice the size" attempt. This issue might cause memory exhaustion, but is only relevant if the pickle format is used for serializing tens or hundreds of gigabytes of data. This issue is fixed in: v3.4.10, v3.4.10rc1; v3.5.10, v3.5.10rc1, v3.5.7, v3.5.7rc1, v3.5.8, v3.5.8rc1, v3.5.8rc2, v3.5.9; v3.6.10, v3.6.10rc1, v3.6.11, v3.6.11rc1, v3.6.12, v3.6.7, v3.6.7rc1, v3.6.7rc2, v3.6.8, v3.6.8rc1, v3.6.9, v3.6.9rc1; v3.7.1, v3.7.1rc1, v3.7.1rc2, v3.7.2, v3.7.2rc1, v3.7.3, v3.7.3rc1, v3.7.4, v3.7.4rc1, v3.7.4rc2, v3.7.5, v3.7.5rc1, v3.7.6, v3.7.6rc1, v3.7.7, v3.7.7rc1, v3.7.8, v3.7.8rc1, v3.7.9.

code_evidence: Line 6 casts self->mt_mask to size_t unconditionally, and line 9 derives hash from key; line 10 computes i = hash & mask, then line 11 indexes table[i] without any bound check on i relative to the table size.
The probe loop at lines 14-16 recomputes i = (i << 2) + i + perturb + 1 and indexes table[i & mask]; this arithmetic on size_t can wrap, and the mask value is assumed to keep the index in range.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the index computation relies on size_t arithmetic whose result is assumed to remain larger/in-range; wraparound breaks the bounds invariant. It is not merely a missing bounds check (CWE-125) because the flaw is the unchecked integer computation feeding the index.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the memo-table index is produced by arithmetic on size_t (the perturb sequence and mask) with the implicit assumption that the computed index stays within the table and that mask reflects the table size. Trigger: a large LONG_BINPUT value drives table growth and mask updates; the cast/arithmetic can wrap so the assumed invariant (index < table size) fails. Supported consequence: out-of-bounds table access and memory corruption or exhaustion during unpickling.

commit_msg:
net: fix missing server-side num_players validation (CVE-2020-14983)

The server in Chocolate Doom 3.0.0 and Crispy Doom 5.8.0 doesn't
validate the user-controlled num_players value, leading to a buffer
overflow. A malicious user can overwrite the server's stack.

Fixes CVE-2020-14983, found by Michał Dardas from LogicalTrust.

Fixes: #1293.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    for (i = 0; i < settings->num_players; ++i)'], 'added_lines': ['    for (i = 0; i < settings->num_players && i < NET_MAXPLAYERS; ++i)']}
description: The server in Chocolate Doom 3.0.0 and Crispy Doom 5.8.0 doesn't validate the user-controlled num_players value, leading to a buffer overflow. A malicious user can overwrite the server's stack.

code_evidence: Line 20 reads the attacker-controlled settings->num_players from the packet with no range check. Line 26 loops i from 0 to that unbounded value, and each iteration at lines 28-29 writes into settings->player_classes[i], an array of fixed size NET_MAXPLAYERS.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The loop copies packet-derived data into a fixed-size output array without checking that the count is below the buffer size, which is a classic buffer copy overflow (CWE-120). It is not merely a size-calculation error, since the bound is simply absent.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: num_players is decoded from the network packet without validating it against NET_MAXPLAYERS. Trigger: a malicious client sends num_players larger than the array size, so the loop writes past the end of player_classes, overwriting adjacent stack memory. Consequence: server stack corruption, potentially leading to crash or code execution.

description: The IEEE 802.11 dissector in Wireshark 1.12.x before 1.12.11 and 2.0.x before 2.0.3 does not properly restrict element lists, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (deep recursion and application crash) via a crafted packet, related to epan/dissectors/packet-capwap.c and epan/dissectors/packet-ieee80211.c.

code_evidence: The loop trusts the wire-provided subelement length: tmp_sublen is read from tvb at offset+1 and then used directly to advance both tag_len and offset without checking it against the remaining tag_len or the actual buffer length. add_tagged_field is invoked with no restriction on which element IDs may be recursively dissected, so a crafted subelement can re-enter the dissector.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function fails to validate packet-supplied length and element-type metadata before using it, matching CWE-20's improper input validation. The recursion/DoS is the consequence; the weakness is the missing validation of the subelement length and ID.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the length byte and element identity from the packet are consumed without validation against remaining length or an allowed-ID set. Trigger: a crafted Channel Switch Wrapper element with a nested subelement that recurses into itself. Consequence: unbounded recursion and a crash (DoS); the unchecked subtraction can also drive offset/tag_len out of range.

Prevent null pointer deref due to bad form id

Origin: https://anonscm.debian.org/cgit/collab-maint/w3m.git/commit/?id=9db438094e5f0d84842bcbd248f282594ccb3c89

description: An issue was discovered in the Tatsuya Kinoshita w3m fork before 0.5.3-33. w3m allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (segmentation fault and crash) via a crafted HTML page.

The guard at line 372 checks only form_id bounds and that the forms array itself is non-NULL, then line 374 dereferences forms[form_id] into form without verifying that this individual element is non-NULL. A crafted form id can index a slot holding a NULL pointer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads forms[form_id] and uses it as an object without a NULL check, matching CWE-476 (dereference of a pointer expected to be valid but NULL). This is a missing NULL check, not an out-of-bounds array access, since bounds are already enforced.

commit_msg: Added a check whether all components in a scan are actually present.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  //', '  // Check whether all components are there.', '  for(UBYTE i = 0;i < m_ucCount && i < 4;i++) {', '    if (ComponentOf(i) == NULL) {', '      JPG_THROW(MALFORMED_STREAM,"Scan::CreateParser",', '                "found a component ID in a scan that does not exist");', '    }', '  }']}
description: In libjpeg 1.63, there is a NULL pointer dereference in Component::SubXOf in component.hpp.

code_evidence: CreateParser reads the frame's scan type and asserts that no parser exists yet, then dispatches on that type to construct a scan parser; there is no validation that the scan's component IDs actually exist in the frame.

The JPEG_LS single-component path only checks m_ucCount, not whether ComponentOf(i) resolves to a real component; with a malformed stream carrying a component ID absent from the frame, the constructed parser later resolves that ID via Component::SubXOf and dereferences a NULL component.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is a NULL pointer dereference: a missing existence check lets a NULL component pointer reach a dereference. It is not an out-of-bounds access, since the pointer is NULL rather than pointing outside an array.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function builds a scan parser from attacker-controlled scan metadata without verifying that each referenced component ID maps to an existing frame component. Trigger: a malformed codestream whose scan references a nonexistent component ID. Consequence: downstream Component::SubXOf dereferences the NULL component, crashing the decoder (DoS).

commit_msg:
Prevent integer overflow in copyString

The copyString function is only used for encoding string supplied by
the library user.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  int charsRequired = 0;'], 'added_lines': ['  size_t charsRequired = 0;']}
description: In Expat (aka libexpat) before 2.4.5, there is an integer overflow in copyString.

code_evidence: charsRequired is declared as a signed int and incremented in the while loop until the terminating NUL, then incremented once more. That value is multiplied by sizeof(XML_Char) in the malloc_fcn argument on line 9 and again in the memcpy length on line 12. Because the counter and the multiplication are done in int arithmetic, a very long input string can make charsRequired*sizeof(XML_Char) exceed INT_MAX and wrap to a small or negative value.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the size calculation used for allocation and copying wraps when the length exceeds the int representation, and the logic assumes the result remains larger than the original length. This is integer overflow rather than a mere off-by-one, since the defect is the numeric wraparound in the size computation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the string length and allocation/copy size are computed with a signed int instead of size_t, so the multiplication can overflow. Trigger: a library-user-supplied string long enough that charsRequired*sizeof(XML_Char) exceeds the int range. Consequence: an undersized allocation followed by a memcpy of the wrapped length, causing heap memory corruption and possible crash or code execution.

commit_msg:
Bug#24388746: PRIVILEGE ESCALATION AND RACE CONDITION USING CREATE TABLE

During REPAIR TABLE of a MyISAM table, a temporary data file (.TMD)
is created. When repair finishes, this file is renamed to the original
.MYD file. The problem was that during this rename, we copied the
stats from the old file to the new file with chmod/chown. If a user
managed to replace the temporary file before chmod/chown was executed,
it was possible to get an arbitrary file with the privileges of the
mysql user.

This patch fixes the problem by not copying stats from the old
file to the new file. This is not needed as the new file was
created with the correct stats. This fix only changes server
behavior - external utilities such as myisamchk still does
chmod/chown.

No test case provided since the problem involves synchronization
with file system operations.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\tconst char * name, int rep_quick)', '\t\t\t    (param->testflag & T_BACKUP_DATA ?', '\t\t\t     MYF(MY_REDEL_MAKE_BACKUP): MYF(0))) ||'], 'added_lines': ['                       const char * name, int rep_quick, my_bool no_copy_stat)', '      myf flags= 0;', '      if (param->testflag & T_BACKUP_DATA)', '        flags |= MY_REDEL_MAKE_BACKUP;', '      if (no_copy_stat)', '        flags |= MY_REDEL_NO_COPY_STAT;', '\t\t\t    flags) ||']}
description: Race condition in Oracle MySQL before 5.5.52, 5.6.x before 5.6.33, 5.7.x before 5.7.15, and 8.x before 8.0.1; MariaDB before 5.5.52, 10.0.x before 10.0.28, and 10.1.x before 10.1.18; Percona Server before 5.5.51-38.2, 5.6.x before 5.6.32-78-1, and 5.7.x before 5.7.14-8; and Percona XtraDB Cluster before 5.5.41-37.0, 5.6.x before 5.6.32-25.17, and 5.7.x before 5.7.14-26.17 allows local users with certain permissions to gain privileges by leveraging use of my_copystat by REPAIR TABLE to repair a MyISAM table.

code_evidence: After a successful repair, the temporary data file is closed and then change_to_newfile() renames it to the real data file; the pre-patch call passed only MY_REDEL_MAKE_BACKUP or 0, so the rename helper also copied stats (chmod/chown) onto the target. The new flags variable and no_copy_stat parameter (lines 319-326) show the stat copy is the risky part being removed; the rename and the stat copy are separate file-system steps on the same path.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The check-then-act sequence over a shared file-system path has a timing window allowing an interfering process to swap the resource, matching CWE-362's non-atomic shared-resource access. The privilege gain is the consequence; the weakness itself is the unsynchronized rename/statch operation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the rename of the .TMD temp file onto the .MYD data file is not atomic with the subsequent chmod/chown of the target path. Between the rename and the stat copy, an attacker with write access to the directory can replace the target with a symlink or another file, so chmod/chown is applied to attacker-chosen file using the mysql user's privileges.

commit_msg:
Use correct origin when prompting for proxy authentication.

Since M49, Chrome has been prompting for proxy authentication
credentials using the target origin instead of the origin of the proxy
server. Even if the proxy origin was displayed correctly, a mischievous
network operator could still spoof the proxy server origin. To mitigate
these problems, this CL:

* Fixes the origin used in the proxy authentication login prompt to use
  the origin of the proxy server.

* Indicate if the proxy server connection is insecure.

* Always throw up an interstitial and clear the omnibox when showing a
  proxy auth prompt.

* Use the correct origin when saving proxy authentication credentials.

description: The ReadPSDImage function in MagickCore/locale.c in ImageMagick allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read) via a crafted PSD file.

code_evidence: The function allocates 'blocks' with AcquireQuantumMemory((size_t) length, sizeof(*blocks)) at [145,146]. It then reads 'length' bytes into that buffer at [149]. The check at [150,151] only verifies the read count equals 'length' and that LocaleNCompare compares 4 bytes against "8BIM"; it does not verify length >= 4 before the 4-byte comparison. If a crafted PSD supplies a resource-block length of 1-3, blocks holds fewer than 4 bytes but LocaleNCompare still reads 4 bytes from it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the code reads 4 bytes from a buffer sized by an attacker-controlled length that may be less than 4, i.e., reading past the end of the intended buffer. The fix adds (length < 4) to prevent the short-buffer comparison; this is an out-of-bounds read, not an out-of-bounds write.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: missing lower-bound check on 'length' before a fixed 4-byte comparison of the buffer read with that length. Trigger: a crafted PSD whose image-resource-block length is 1 to 3, causing ReadBlob to fill fewer than 4 bytes. Consequence: LocaleNCompare reads past the allocated buffer, an out-of-bounds read that can crash the process (DoS) or disclose adjacent memory.

description: The AP4_AtomSampleTable::GetSample function in Core/Ap4AtomSampleTable.cpp in Bento4 mp42ts before 1.5.0-616 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference and application crash) via a crafted mp4 file.

code_evidence: Line 96 allocates a sample table for each track and stores it in cursors[index].m_Locator.m_SampleTable; if GetSampleCount() returns nonzero the code calls GetSample(0,...) (lines 99-100), otherwise it sets m_EndReached (lines 101-103).
In the selection loop, the guard at lines 110-111 checks only m_EndReached before calling cursors[i].m_Locator.m_Sample.GetOffset(); the patched condition adds a check that m_SampleTable is non-NULL.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing NULL check on a pointer that is subsequently dereferenced matches CWE-476 (NULL Pointer Dereference). The supported consequence is a crash; this is a null-check omission rather than an out-of-bounds or type-confusion issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The root cause is that a track cursor can be used in the min-offset loop without its m_SampleTable being validated. A malformed MP4 that yields a NULL or unusable sample table for a track leaves the corresponding cursor eligible, and the loop dereferences m_Sample.GetOffset(), causing a NULL pointer dereference and crash (DoS).

description: A Segmentation fault casued by heap use after free vulnerability exists in Gpac through 1.0.1 via the mpgviddmx_process function in reframe_mpgvid.c when using mp4box, which causes a denial of service.

code_evidence: In the GF_EOS branch, the code reallocs ctx->hdr_store and then copies from data+vosh_start into ctx->hdr_store+hdr_store_size. When the input packet data pointer (data) aliases ctx->hdr_store (set at lines 69-70 after accumulating into the store, or lines 77-78 with resume_from), the realloc may free the old buffer, so the subsequent memcpy reads from the freed/relocated pointer data. The patch adds a data == ctx->hdr_store check and memmove in that case, confirming the aliasing path is the defect.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Reading from data after gf_realloc invalidated the aliased buffer is reuse of freed memory, fitting CWE-416. It is not merely an out-of-bounds copy because the freed pointer is dereferenced after reallocation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the copy source (data) can alias the destination store buffer, and gf_realloc may free/move that buffer before the memcpy reads it. Trigger: an EOS during header parsing after data was set to ctx->hdr_store. Consequence: heap use-after-free read, causing a crash/denial of service as described.

commit_msg:
When huang uses sched_switch tracepoint, the tracepoint
does only one thing in the mounted ebpf program, which
deletes the fixed elements in sockhash ([0])

It seems that elements in sockhash are rarely actively
deleted by users or ebpf program. Therefore, we do not
pay much attention to their deletion. Compared with hash
maps, sockhash only provides spin_lock_bh protection.
This causes it to appear to have self-locking behavior
in the interrupt context.

  [0]:https://lore.kernel.org/all/CABcoxUayum5oOqFMMqAeWuS8+EzojquSOSyDA3J_2omY=2EeAg@mail.gmail.com/

Reported-by: Hsin-Wei Hung <hsinweih@uci.edu>
Fixes: 604326b41a6f ("bpf, sockmap: convert to generic sk_msg interface")
Signed-off-by: Xin Liu <liuxin350@huawei.com>
Acked-by: John Fastabend <john.fastabend@gmail.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20230406122622.109978-1-liuxin350@huawei.com
Signed-off-by: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\traw_spin_lock_bh(&bucket->lock);', '\traw_spin_unlock_bh(&bucket->lock);'], 'added_lines': ['\tunsigned long flags;', '\traw_spin_lock_irqsave(&bucket->lock, flags);', '\traw_spin_unlock_irqrestore(&bucket->lock, flags);']}
description: A deadlock flaw was found in the Linux kernel’s BPF subsystem. This flaw allows a local user to potentially crash the system.

code_evidence: The bucket lock is acquired with raw_spin_lock_bh (bottom-half disabling) at line 10 and released with raw_spin_unlock_bh at line 18, while the protected critical section at lines 11-17 performs lookup, hlist_del_rcu, sock_map_unref and sock_hash_free_elem on the bucket.
The lock choice only disables softirqs, not hard IRQs, so the same bucket lock can be re-entered from hard-interrupt context.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Improper locking: the function uses an insufficient lock acquisition/release discipline for the shared bucket resource. The fix replaces the bh variants with irqsave/irqrestore, confirming the lock variant was the defect, which fits CWE-667 rather than a data-corruption weakness.

evidence_lines.code:
raw_spin_lock_bh(&bucket->lock);
raw_spin_unlock_bh(&bucket->lock);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The bucket's raw spinlock is taken with a bottom-half-only variant, so a hard IRQ that reaches the same locking path can attempt to acquire an already-held bucket lock on the same CPU, causing self-deadlock. The trigger is concurrent deletion via the sockhash tracepoint/ebpf program racing with interrupt-context access to the same bucket; the supported consequence is a system hang/crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
MIPS/readelf: Simplify GOT[1] data availability check

Unavailable data is handled gracefully in MIPS GOT processing done by
`print_mips_got_entry', so all that is needed in special GOT[1] handling
is to verify whether data can be retrieved for the purpose of the GNU
marker check done with `byte_get'.  Remove the extra error reporting
code then, introduced with commit 75ec1fdbb797 ("Fix runtime seg-fault
in readelf when parsing a corrupt MIPS binary.") in the course of
addressing PR binutils/21344, and defer the error case to regular local
GOT entry processing.

	binutils/
	* readelf.c (process_mips_specific): Remove error reporting from
	GOT[1] processing.

Otherwise this is an ordinary local entry.', '\t PR 21344: Check for the entry being fully available before', '\t fetching it.  */', '      if (data', '\t  && data + ent - pltgot + addr_size <= data_end', '\t  && (byte_get (data + ent - pltgot, addr_size)', '\t      >> (addr_size * 8 - 1)) != 0)', '\t{', '\t  ent = print_mips_got_entry (data, pltgot, ent, data_end);', '\t  printf (_(" Module pointer (GNU extension)\\n"));', '\t  if (ent == (bfd_vma) -1)', '\t    goto got_print_fail;']}
description: GNU Binutils 2.28 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (heap-based buffer over-read and application crash) via a crafted ELF file, related to MIPS GOT mishandling in the process_mips_specific function in readelf.c.

code_evidence: The GOT[1] handling reads byte_get(data + ent - pltgot, addr_size) after only checking data + ent - pltgot > data_end - addr_size. This guard is insufficient: when the entry is exactly at the boundary, the subtraction can underflow, and the check does not reliably ensure addr_size bytes remain, so byte_get can read past data_end.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the defect is a read beyond the fetched GOT buffer due to a missing/ineffective bounds check. It is not CWE-787 (out-of-bounds write) since byte_get only reads data; the crash follows from the read, not a write.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the availability guard for the GOT[1] entry uses a flawed boundary comparison that can underflow and does not guarantee addr_size readable bytes. Trigger: a crafted MIPS ELF with pltgot/local_gotno/ent values placing GOT[1] near the end of the fetched GOT data. Consequence: byte_get performs an out-of-bounds read past the buffer, causing a crash or disclosure.

Fixed bug #72227: imagescale out-of-bounds read

Ported from https://github.com/libgd/libgd/commit/4f65a3e4eedaffa1efcf9ee1eb08f0b504fbc31a

description: gd_interpolation.c in the GD Graphics Library (aka libgd) before 2.1.1, as used in PHP before 5.5.36, 5.6.x before 5.6.22, and 7.x before 7.0.7, allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted image that is mishandled by the imagescale function.

code_evidence: The alpha-blending path iterates y from bbox.y to end_y and x from 0 to end_x, computes src_pt via gdAffineApplyToPointF, then passes src_offset_x + src_pt.x and src_offset_y + src_pt.y to getPixelInterpolated without checking they lie within src bounds.
The non-blending path performs the same interpolation with the same unvalidated src_offset_x/src_pt.x and src_offset_y/src_pt.y coordinates before writing to dst_p.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function directly indexes source pixels using unvalidated computed coordinates, so data is read past the intended buffer boundary, matching CWE-125. It is an out-of-bounds read rather than a write because the unchecked access is the source pixel fetch.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: getPixelInterpolated is called with source coordinates derived from the affine-transformed bounding box without clamping to the source image dimensions. Trigger: a crafted image/affine region causes src_pt to fall outside src. Consequence: getPixelInterpolated reads outside the source pixel buffer, giving an out-of-bounds read (DoS or information disclosure).

commit_msg:
Fix readSInt16, readUInt16 and readSInt32 methods

* Rewrite readSInt16, readUInt16 and readSInt32.

    Avoid calling all read{U,S}Int8(f) in one line, order of
    evaluation is not guaranteed in the C standard (undefined
    behavior).

* Change return type of readUInt16 from int to unsigned int.

* Rewrite readUInt32.

    Use |= operator instead of adding four separate integers. Less
    memory usage, better readable.

commit_msg:
An privileged attacker can cause a crash by mounting a crafted ext4
image which triggers a out-of-bounds read in the function
ext4_valid_block_bitmap() in fs/ext4/balloc.c.

This issue has been assigned CVE-2018-1093.

BugLink: https://bugzilla.kernel.org/show_bug.cgi?id=199181
BugLink: https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1560782
Reported-by: Wen Xu <wen.xu@gatech.edu>
Signed-off-by: Theodore Ts'o <tytso@mit.edu>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tstruct ext4_sb_info *sbi = EXT4_SB(sb);', '\tif ((bitmap_blk <= le32_to_cpu(sbi->s_es->s_first_data_block)) ||', '\t    (bitmap_blk >= ext4_blocks_count(sbi->s_es))) {', '\t\text4_error(sb, "Invalid block bitmap block %llu in "', '\t\t\t   "block_group %u", bitmap_blk, block_group);', '\t\treturn ERR_PTR(-EFSCORRUPTED);', '\t}']}
description: The ext4_valid_block_bitmap function in fs/ext4/balloc.c in the Linux kernel through 4.15.15 allows attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read and system crash) via a crafted ext4 image because balloc.c and ialloc.c do not validate bitmap block numbers.

code_evidence: Line 11 obtains bitmap_blk directly from the on-disk group descriptor via ext4_block_bitmap() and line 12 passes it to sb_getblk() without checking it against the filesystem's valid block range; a crafted image can supply an out-of-range block number.

Lines 54-56 call ext4_validate_block_bitmap() on the resulting buffer; with an unvalidated bitmap block number, this verification path reads bitmap contents at a location past the intended buffer, producing the out-of-bounds read.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function permits a read at an out-of-range block derived from untrusted on-disk metadata, matching CWE-125 (Out-of-bounds Read). This is distinct from a write overflow because the unsafe access is a read used to verify the bitmap, not a buffer write.

evidence_lines.code:
bitmap_blk = ext4_block_bitmap(sb, desc);
bh = sb_getblk(sb, bitmap_blk);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the block bitmap block number read from the group descriptor is used without validating it against s_first_data_block and the total block count. Trigger: a privileged attacker mounts a crafted ext4 image whose descriptor names an invalid bitmap block. Consequence: the verification path reads past the intended buffer, causing an out-of-bounds read and a system crash (DoS).

description: ImageMagick 7.0.7-28 has a memory leak vulnerability in WritePCXImage in coders/pcx.c.

code_evidence: page_table is allocated via AcquireQuantumMemory at [48,49] and only freed on later error paths (e.g., [139,140]) or the normal path at [294,300].
pcx_colormap is allocated at [114,115]; on its allocation failure the original code throws at [117] without releasing the already-allocated page_table.
The pixel_info allocation failure block at [135-142] shows the correct pattern: it relinquishes pcx_colormap and page_table before throwing, confirming the leak on the earlier failure path.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function allocates page_table and fails to release it on the colormap-allocation error path, matching CWE-772's missing release of a resource after its effective lifetime. This is a memory leak rather than a use-after-free (CWE-416) or double-free (CWE-415), since the buffer is simply never freed.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: when AcquireQuantumMemory for pcx_colormap fails at [116,117], the function throws without releasing page_table, which was allocated earlier at [48,49]. Trigger: memory pressure causing the colormap allocation to fail while page_table is non-NULL (DCX or multi-image path). Consequence: the page_table buffer leaks, supporting resource-consumption/denial of service.

commit_msg:
dnxhdenc: fix mb_rc size

Fixes out of array access with RC_VARIANCE set to 0

Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michaelni@gmx.at>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    FF_ALLOCZ_OR_GOTO(ctx->m.avctx, ctx->mb_rc, 8160*ctx->m.avctx->qmax*sizeof(RCEntry), fail);'], 'added_lines': ['    FF_ALLOCZ_OR_GOTO(ctx->m.avctx, ctx->mb_rc, 8160*(ctx->m.avctx->qmax + 1)*sizeof(RCEntry), fail);']}
description: A vulnerability was found in FFmpeg 2.0. It has been classified as problematic. Affected is the function dnxhd_init_rc of the file libavcodec/dnxhdenc.c. The manipulation leads to memory corruption. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue.

code_evidence: The mb_rc buffer is allocated as 8160*qmax*sizeof(RCEntry); the qscale/qmax-derived index range used later can reach qmax+1 entries, so the allocation undercounts by one qmax block.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function directly sizes a heap buffer that is subsequently written past its end, matching CWE-787 out-of-bounds write. The defect is an incorrect allocation bound rather than a read overrun, so CWE-787 fits better than CWE-125.

evidence_lines.code: FF_ALLOCZ_OR_GOTO(ctx->m.avctx, ctx->mb_rc, 8160*ctx->m.avctx->qmax*sizeof(RCEntry), fail);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is an undersized allocation for ctx->mb_rc: the size uses qmax instead of qmax+1, while downstream RC_VARIANCE encoding indexes entries across the full qscale range. Trigger is encoding with RC_VARIANCE and qscale reaching the maximum; the write lands past the allocated RCEntry array, causing memory corruption/out-of-array access.

The same uri pointer is later dereferenced by uriDebugString(uri) at line 20 after mLastURI assignment, so the function retains and reuses a pointer whose lifetime it does not control.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The freed backing buffer is accessed through a stale pointer, an out-of-bounds read/write of a memory buffer that matches CWE-119's improper restriction of operations within buffer bounds. The fix copies uri into mLastURI first and nulls uri, confirming the dangling-pointer use.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is retaining the raw uri pointer in mLastURI while continuing to use it in the same call. When reconnect() invokes connect() with uri == mLastURI.c_str(), the assignment at line 17 overwrites the backing string and invalidates the pointer, so the later uriDebugString(uri) at line 20 reads freed memory, enabling memory corruption.

commit_msg:
DO NOT MERGE omx: check buffer port before using

Bug: 28816827
Change-Id: I3d5bad4a1ef96dec544b05bb31cc6f7109aae0a5
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    OMX_BUFFERHEADERTYPE *header = findBufferHeader(buffer);'], 'added_lines': ['    OMX_BUFFERHEADERTYPE *header = findBufferHeader(buffer, kPortIndexInput);', '    if (header == NULL) {', '        return BAD_VALUE;', '    }']}
description: omx/OMXNodeInstance.cpp in libstagefright in mediaserver in Android 4.x before 4.4.4, 5.0.x before 5.0.2, 5.1.x before 5.1.1, and 6.x before 2016-08-01 does not validate the buffer port, which allows attackers to gain privileges via a crafted application, aka internal bug 28816827.

code_evidence: findBufferHeader(buffer) returns a header without validating which port the buffer belongs to; the result is immediately dereferenced at header->pAppPrivate with no NULL or ownership check.

The metadata branch reads backup->base() and codec->base() as VideoNativeMetadata/VideoGrallocMetadata and writes codecMeta.pHandle; these accesses assume the buffer is a valid input-port metadata buffer.
The else branch does bounds-check rangeOffset/rangeLength against header->nAllocLen, showing the code expects a valid header, but only after the unvalidated dereference at line 8.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked header lookup leads to reads/writes through header and metadata pointers that are not bounded to the intended buffer, matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds memory operations. The missing port validation is the root cause; the resultant out-of-bounds access is the memory-buffer weakness described by CWE-119.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the buffer id is resolved to a header without confirming it belongs to kPortIndexInput, so an attacker-supplied buffer id can yield a header of the wrong port or an invalid/NULL header. Trigger: calling emptyBuffer with a crafted buffer id. Consequence: the unchecked header->pAppPrivate dereference and subsequent metadata reads/writes operate outside the intended buffer, enabling memory corruption and privilege escalation.

description: The ParseDsdiffHeaderConfig function of the cli/dsdiff.c file of WavPack 5.1.0 allows a remote attacker to cause a denial-of-service (heap-based buffer over-read) or possibly overwrite the heap via a maliciously crafted DSDIFF file.

code_evidence: The PROP chunk size ckDataSize is used directly as the malloc size and DoReadFile length with no lower-bound check; if the chunk is smaller than 4 bytes, prop_chunk holds fewer than 4 bytes but the following strncmp(prop_chunk, "SND ", 4) at line 73 still reads 4 bytes.
When the chunk is not "SND ", the debug path at lines 150-152 reads prop_chunk[0..3] from the same undersized allocation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads fixed 4-byte sequences from a buffer whose size is set by an unchecked, attacker-controlled chunk length, so the read can exceed the allocated buffer's end. This is a direct out-of-bounds read (CWE-125); the heap overwrite mentioned in the advisory is a separate possible consequence, not the weakness evidenced here.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the attacker-controlled DSDIFF PROP chunk size (ckDataSize) is not constrained to at least 4 before allocating and reading the chunk. Trigger: a malicious .DFF file with a PROP chunk smaller than 4 bytes. Consequence: strncmp and the debug logging read past the end of the heap allocation, producing a heap-based out-of-bounds read (crash/DoS and potentially memory disclosure).

description: An issue was discovered in gpac before 1.0.1. The abst_box_read function in box_code_adobe.c has a heap-based buffer over-read.

code_evidence: ptr->size is checked only once before the first string loop; the allocated tmp_str has size ptr->size-8, yet each loop reads up to ptr->size-8 bytes with gf_bs_read_u8. The entry loops at lines 36-38 and 51-53 and the drm/meta loops at 64-66 reuse the same tmp_strsize derived from ptr->size without any per-read size decrement, so the bitstream is read past the box boundary and beyond the allocated buffer's remaining data.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads data past the intended buffer boundary because the size constraint is not enforced per read, which is exactly an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125), not a write.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the loop bounds are computed from the box size but the underlying bitstream is not checked against remaining box bytes during repeated gf_bs_read_u8 calls. Trigger: a crafted abst box whose declared size does not cover all the string/count fields. Consequence: heap-based out-of-bounds read of the input buffer, potentially leaking memory or crashing.

commit_msg:
Fix 697448: Limit the maximum program size to something reasonable.

A regular expression with lots of nested repetition can lead to
integer overflow when calculating the size of the program.

Check max program size when counting the number of instructions required
for a loop, so we can bail before integer overflow can happen.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tint i;', '\tg.prog->start = g.prog->end = alloc(ctx, NULL, (count(node) + 6) * sizeof (Reinst));', '\tdumpnode(node);', "\tputchar('\\n');"], 'added_lines': ['\tint i, n;', '#ifdef TEST', '\tdumpnode(node);', "\tputchar('\\n');", '#endif', '', '\tn = 6 + count(&g, node);', '\tif (n < 0 || n > MAXPROG)', '\t\tdie(&g, "program too large");', '', '\tg.prog->start = g.prog->end = alloc(ctx, NULL, n * sizeof (Reinst));']}
description: An integer overflow vulnerability was observed in the regemit function in regexp.c in Artifex Software, Inc. MuJS before fa3d30fd18c348bb4b1f3858fb860f4fcd4b2045. The attack requires a regular expression with nested repetition. A successful exploitation of this issue can lead to code execution or a denial of service (buffer overflow) condition.

code_evidence: Line 7 declares only `int i`; there is no bounded local for the instruction count. Line 35 computes `(count(node) + 6) * sizeof (Reinst)` directly inside `alloc` with no overflow check before the multiplication and size conversion.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The root cause is an unchecked integer arithmetic on an attacker-influenced count used as an allocation size, matching CWE-190. The fix in the patch (compute `n = 6 + count`, reject `n < 0 || n > MAXPROG` before multiplying) confirms the overflow-on-size weakness rather than a separate out-of-bounds issue.

evidence_lines.code:
int i;
g.prog->start = g.prog->end = alloc(ctx, NULL, (count(node) + 6) * sizeof (Reinst));

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The instruction count returned by `count(node)` for a regex with nested repetition can be large; adding 6 and multiplying by `sizeof(Reinst)` in a signed int context can overflow/wrap, yielding a small or negative allocation size. The subsequent `emit`/`compile` calls then write instructions into an undersized buffer, giving heap corruption or crash.

commit_msg:
Jan Kara's analysis of the syzbot report (edited):

  The reproducer opens a directory on FUSE filesystem, it then attaches
  dnotify mark to the open directory.  After that a fuse_do_getattr() call
  finds that attributes returned by the server are inconsistent, and calls
  make_bad_inode() which, among other things does:

          inode->i_mode = S_IFREG;

  This then confuses dnotify which doesn't tear down its structures
  properly and eventually crashes.

Avoid calling make_bad_inode() on a live inode: switch to a private flag on
the fuse inode.  Also add the test to ops which the bad_inode_ops would
have caught.

This bug goes back to the initial merge of fuse in 2.6.14...

Reported-by: syzbot+f427adf9324b92652ccc@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Signed-off-by: Miklos Szeredi <mszeredi@redhat.com>
Tested-by: Jan Kara <jack@suse.cz>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tmake_bad_inode(inode);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tfuse_make_bad(inode);']}
description: An issue was discovered in the FUSE filesystem implementation in the Linux kernel before 5.10.6, aka CID-5d069dbe8aaf. fuse_do_getattr() calls make_bad_inode() in inappropriate situations, causing a system crash. NOTE: the original fix for this vulnerability was incomplete, and its incompleteness is tracked as CVE-2021-28950.

code_evidence: When the inode type changes, the code calls make_bad_inode(inode) on a live inode, then iput(inode) and retries via goto retry. make_bad_inode mutates the inode state (including i_mode) but does not tear down the dnotify/mark structures previously attached to the open inode.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-459 (Incomplete Cleanup) fits because the code fails to properly remove supporting dnotify mark resources before invalidating and releasing the inode. The defect is the missing teardown of associated structures, not merely a type confusion.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: make_bad_inode() is invoked on a live inode that still has dnotify marks associated with it, leaving those supporting structures attached while the inode is mutated and released. Trigger: a FUSE server returns attributes whose type differs from the cached inode, reaching line 30. Consequence: dnotify state is not properly cleaned up, leading to use-after-free/crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
evutil_parse_sockaddr_port(): fix buffer overflow

@asn-the-goblin-slayer:
  "Length between '[' and ']' is cast to signed 32 bit integer on line 1815. Is
   the length is more than 2<<31 (INT_MAX), len will hold a negative value.
   Consequently, it will pass the check at line 1816. Segfault happens at line
   1819.

   Generate a resolv.conf with generate-resolv.conf, then compile and run
   poc.c. See entry-functions.txt for functions in tor that might be
   vulnerable.

   Please credit 'Guido Vranken' for this discovery through the Tor bug bounty
   program."

Reproducer for gdb (https://gist.github.com/azat/be2b0d5e9417ba0dfe2c):
  start
  p (1ULL<<31)+1ULL
  # $1 = 2147483649
  p malloc(sizeof(struct sockaddr))
  # $2 = (void *) 0x646010
  p malloc(sizeof(int))
  # $3 = (void *) 0x646030
  p malloc($1)
  # $4 = (void *) 0x7fff76a2a010
  p memset($4, 1, $1)
  # $5 = 1990369296
  p (char *)$4
  # $6 = 0x7fff76a2a010 '\001' <repeats 200 times>...
  set $6[0]='['
  set $6[$1]=']'
  p evutil_parse_sockaddr_port($4, $2, $3)
  # $7 = -1

Before:
  $ gdb bin/http-connect < gdb
  (gdb) $1 = 2147483649
  (gdb) (gdb) $2 = (void *) 0x646010
  (gdb) (gdb) $3 = (void *) 0x646030
  (gdb) (gdb) $4 = (void *) 0x7fff76a2a010
  (gdb) (gdb) $5 = 1990369296
  (gdb) (gdb) $6 = 0x7fff76a2a010 '\001' <repeats 200 times>...
  (gdb) (gdb) (gdb) (gdb)
  Program received signal SIGSEGV, Segmentation fault.
  __memcpy_sse2_unaligned () at memcpy-sse2-unaligned.S:36

After:
  $ gdb bin/http-connect < gdb
  (gdb) $1 = 2147483649
  (gdb) (gdb) $2 = (void *) 0x646010
  (gdb) (gdb) $3 = (void *) 0x646030
  (gdb) (gdb) $4 = (void *) 0x7fff76a2a010
  (gdb) (gdb) $5 = 1990369296
  (gdb) (gdb) $6 = 0x7fff76a2a010 '\001' <repeats 200 times>...
  (gdb) (gdb) (gdb) (gdb) $7 = -1
  (gdb) (gdb) quit

Fixes: #318
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tint len;', '\t\tlen = (int) ( cp-(ip_as_string + 1) );', '\t\tif (len > (int)sizeof(buf)-1) {'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tsize_t len;', '\t\tlen = ( cp-(ip_as_string + 1) );', '\t\tif (len > sizeof(buf)-1) {']}
description: Stack-based buffer overflow in the evutil_parse_sockaddr_port function in evutil.c in libevent before 2.1.6-beta allows attackers to cause a denial of service (segmentation fault) via vectors involving a long string in brackets in the ip_as_string argument.

code_evidence: len is declared as signed int [10] and assigned the cast result of cp-(ip_as_string+1) [14], where cp points to the closing ']' found by strchr [11]. The bound check [15] compares len against sizeof(buf)-1, but a bracket span exceeding INT_MAX wraps to a negative len, which passes the check. memcpy [18] then copies a huge size_t (negative len converted) into char buf[128], and buf[len] [19] writes out of bounds.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the flawed length check permits memcpy and buf[len] to write beyond the stack buffer buf. This is an out-of-bounds write; the signed truncation is the enabling root cause rather than a mere integer issue with no memory effect.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the bracket length is truncated into a signed int before the size check, so oversized lengths become negative and bypass the guard. Trigger: an ip_as_string whose '[' ... ']' span exceeds INT_MAX. Consequence: memcpy and the buf[len] terminator write far past the 128-byte stack buffer, causing memory corruption and a crash.

description: Botan 2.5.0 through 2.6.0 before 2.7.0 allows a memory-cache side-channel attack on ECDSA signatures, aka the Return Of the Hidden Number Problem or ROHNP, related to dsa/dsa.cpp, ec_group/ec_group.cpp, and ecdsa/ecdsa.cpp. To discover an ECDSA key, the attacker needs access to either the local machine or a different virtual machine on the same physical host.

code_evidence: Constructor receives DSA private key data (m_x from dsa.get_x()) and stores it in the signature operation object; no randomization or blinding parameter is accepted.
The body only optionally derives the RFC6979 hash; it performs no blinding of the secret scalar or signature computation, leaving the private-key-dependent operation exposed to observation.

DSA_Signature_Operation(const DSA_PrivateKey& dsa, const std::string& emsa) :
PK_Ops::Signature_with_EMSA(emsa),
m_group(dsa.get_group()),
m_x(dsa.get_x()),
m_mod_q(dsa.group_q())

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the DSA signature operation computes with the secret key without any blinding, so timing/cache-observable operations depend directly on secret values. Trigger: an attacker with local or co-resident VM access observes the operation. Consequence: the private key can be recovered via the ROHNP side channel, exposing sensitive key material.

commit_msg:
If the device node of dvb_ca_en50221 is open() and the
device is disconnected, a UAF may occur when calling
close() on the device node.

The root cause is that wake_up() and wait_event() for
dvbdev->wait_queue are not implemented.

So implement wait_event() function in dvb_ca_en50221_release()
and add 'remove_mutex' which prevents race condition
for 'ca->exit'.

[mchehab: fix a checkpatch warning]

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/linux-media/20221121063308.GA33821@ubuntu
Signed-off-by: Hyunwoo Kim <v4bel@theori.io>
Signed-off-by: Mauro Carvalho Chehab <mchehab@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\tmutex_lock(&ca->remove_mutex);', '\tif (dvbdev->users == 1 && ca->exit == 1) {', '\t\tmutex_unlock(&ca->remove_mutex);', '\t\twake_up(&dvbdev->wait_queue);', '\t} else {', '\t\tmutex_unlock(&ca->remove_mutex);', '\t}', '']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel through 6.0.10. In drivers/media/dvb-core/dvb_ca_en50221.c, a use-after-free can occur is there is a disconnect after an open, because of the lack of a wait_event.

code_evidence: The release path clears ca->open, calls dvb_ca_en50221_thread_update_delay(ca), then dvb_generic_release, module_put and dvb_ca_private_put(ca), and returns err without any synchronization on ca->remove_mutex or wake_up on dvbdev->wait_queue.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the freed ca object (freed via dvb_ca_private_put) can be referenced afterward by the concurrent removal path; the missing wait_event/mutex is the cause, not a separate weakness class.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: release does not wait for the CA thread/removal path to finish and does not hold remove_mutex or signal wait_queue, so dvb_ca_private_put(ca) can free ca while the disconnect/removal path still uses it. Trigger: open the device node, disconnect the device, then close(); the missing wait_event/wake_up and mutex allows a race. Supported consequence: use-after-free of ca, with possible crash or memory corruption.

commit_msg:
Consult the 'unconditional IO exiting' and 'use IO bitmaps' VM-execution
controls when checking instruction interception. If the 'use IO bitmaps'
VM-execution control is 1, check the instruction access against the IO
bitmaps to determine if the instruction causes a VM-exit.

Signed-off-by: Oliver Upton <oupton@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tunsigned int port;'], 'added_lines': ['\tunsigned short port;']}
description: A flaw was discovered in the way that the KVM hypervisor handled instruction emulation for an L2 guest when nested virtualisation is enabled. Under some circumstances, an L2 guest may trick the L0 guest into accessing sensitive L1 resources that should be inaccessible to the L2 guest.

code_evidence: The declared port variable is unsigned int (line 5), while the I/O port extracted from EXIT_QUALIFICATION is a 16-bit value (line 10, shift by 16).
The extracted port and computed size are passed to nested_vmx_check_io_bitmaps (line 12) to decide whether the L2 I/O instruction is intercepted.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The supported consequence is that an unauthorized L2 guest gains access to sensitive L1 resources, i.e., exposure of sensitive information to an actor not authorized for it, matching CWE-200. The bitmap-check logic is the mechanism enabling the exposure; the weakness is the resultant confidentiality loss rather than a distinct memory-safety class.

evidence_lines.code: unsigned int port;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the port width/truncation handling combined with the I/O bitmap check allows an L2 guest's I/O instruction to be evaluated as non-intercepted under certain conditions. Trigger: an L2 guest issues an I/O instruction while nested virtualization is enabled and the use-IO-bitmaps control is set. Consequence: the L2 guest can cause the L0 hypervisor to access L1 resources that should be inaccessible, exposing sensitive L1 information.

commit_msg:
Jan Kara's analysis of the syzbot report (edited):

  The reproducer opens a directory on FUSE filesystem, it then attaches
  dnotify mark to the open directory.  After that a fuse_do_getattr() call
  finds that attributes returned by the server are inconsistent, and calls
  make_bad_inode() which, among other things does:

          inode->i_mode = S_IFREG;

  This then confuses dnotify which doesn't tear down its structures
  properly and eventually crashes.

Avoid calling make_bad_inode() on a live inode: switch to a private flag on
the fuse inode.  Also add the test to ops which the bad_inode_ops would
have caught.

This bug goes back to the initial merge of fuse in 2.6.14...

Reported-by: syzbot+f427adf9324b92652ccc@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Signed-off-by: Miklos Szeredi <mszeredi@redhat.com>
Tested-by: Jan Kara <jack@suse.cz>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>

NOTE: the original fix for this vulnerability was incomplete, and its incompleteness is tracked as CVE-2021-28950.

commit_msg:
h264bsdActivateParamSets: Prevent multiplication overflow.

Report MEMORY_ALLOCATION_ERROR if pStorage->picSizeInMbs would
exceed UINT32_MAX bytes.

Bug: 28532266
Change-Id: Ia6f11efb18818afcdb5fa2a38a14f2a2d8c8447a
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        pStorage->picSizeInMbs =', '            pStorage->activeSps->picWidthInMbs *', '            pStorage->activeSps->picHeightInMbs;'], 'added_lines': ['', '        /* report error before multiplication to prevent integer overflow */', '        if (pStorage->activeSps->picWidthInMbs == 0)', '        {', '            pStorage->picSizeInMbs = 0;', '        }', '        else if (pStorage->activeSps->picHeightInMbs >', '                 UINT32_MAX / pStorage->activeSps->picWidthInMbs)', '        {', '            return(MEMORY_ALLOCATION_ERROR);', '        }', '        else', '        {', '            pStorage->picSizeInMbs =', '                pStorage->activeSps->picWidthInMbs *', '                pStorage->activeSps->picHeightInMbs;', '        }']}
description: Integer overflow in codecs/on2/h264dec/source/h264bsd_storage.c in libstagefright in mediaserver in Android 4.x before 4.4.4, 5.0.x before 5.0.2, 5.1.x before 5.1.1, and 6.x before 2016-07-01 allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code or cause a denial of service (memory corruption) via a crafted media file, aka internal bug 28532266.

code_evidence: At lines 22-24 picSizeInMbs is computed as the unchecked product of attacker-influenced picWidthInMbs and picHeightInMbs from the active SPS; no overflow check guards this multiplication.
At lines 34-35 this possibly-wrapped picSizeInMbs is used as the element count for ALLOCATE of pStorage->mb and pStorage->sliceGroupMap, so a wrapped small value yields undersized buffers.
At lines 38-39 memset uses the same picSizeInMbs count; downstream decoding of macroblocks then indexes mbStorage_t/sliceGroupMap entries beyond the allocated regions.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The overflow leads to allocations smaller than the intended macroblock storage, and subsequent operations access memory outside those buffers, matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds read/write on a memory buffer. The integer overflow is the cause; the out-of-bounds memory operation is the supported consequence.

evidence_lines.code:
ALLOCATE(pStorage->mb, pStorage->picSizeInMbs, mbStorage_t);
ALLOCATE(pStorage->sliceGroupMap, pStorage->picSizeInMbs, u32);

H264SwDecMemset(pStorage->mb, 0,
pStorage->picSizeInMbs * sizeof(mbStorage_t));

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the width*height product is computed without an overflow guard, so crafted SPS dimensions wrap picSizeInMbs to a small value. Trigger: activating such parameter sets causes undersized allocations (lines 34-35) followed by macroblock processing that writes/reads past the buffer, giving memory corruption exploitable for code execution or DoS.

commit_msg:
If the device node of dvb_frontend is open() and the device is
disconnected, many kinds of UAFs may occur when calling close()
on the device node.

The root cause of this is that wake_up() for dvbdev->wait_queue
is implemented in the dvb_frontend_release() function, but
wait_event() is not implemented in the dvb_frontend_stop() function.

So, implement wait_event() function in dvb_frontend_stop() and
add 'remove_mutex' which prevents race condition for 'fe->exit'.

[mchehab: fix a couple of checkpatch warnings and some mistakes at the error handling logic]

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/linux-media/20221117045925.14297-2-imv4bel@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Hyunwoo Kim <imv4bel@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Mauro Carvalho Chehab <mchehab@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (!fepriv->thread)'], 'added_lines': ['\tmutex_lock(&fe->remove_mutex);', '', '\tif (!fepriv->thread) {', '\t\tmutex_unlock(&fe->remove_mutex);', '\t}', '', '\tmutex_unlock(&fe->remove_mutex);', '', '\tif (fepriv->dvbdev->users < -1) {', '\t\twait_event(fepriv->dvbdev->wait_queue,', '\t\t\t   fepriv->dvbdev->users == -1);', '\t}']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel through 6.0.9. drivers/media/dvb-core/dvb_frontend.c has a race condition that can cause a use-after-free when a device is disconnected.

code_evidence: The function reads and updates the shared fe->exit flag and checks fepriv->thread without any synchronization, then calls kthread_stop(fepriv->thread). The before-function has no mutex protecting these shared fields, so a concurrent device-removal path can change fe->exit or tear down the thread while this sequence runs.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The code sequence lacks exclusivity/atomicity over shared state accessed by concurrent code, which is exactly CWE-362. The later wait_event fix confirms a race window; CWE-416 is only a downstream consequence, not the root weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: unsynchronized access to shared fe->exit and fepriv->thread across concurrent stop/release paths. Trigger: dvb_frontend_stop runs concurrently with device disconnection/release. Consequence: the thread may be stopped while another path still uses its state, enabling use-after-free/crash.

commit_msg:
net: vmxnet: initialise local tx descriptor

In Vmxnet3 device emulator while processing transmit(tx) queue,
when it reaches end of packet, it calls vmxnet3_complete_packet.
In that local 'txcq_descr' object is not initialised, which could
leak host memory bytes a guest.

Reported-by: Li Qiang <liqiang6-s@360.cn>
Signed-off-by: Prasad J Pandit <pjp@fedoraproject.org>
Reviewed-by: Dmitry Fleytman <dmitry@daynix.com>
Signed-off-by: Jason Wang <jasowang@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    memset(&txcq_descr, 0, sizeof(txcq_descr));']}
description: The vmxnet3_complete_packet function in hw/net/vmxnet3.c in QEMU (aka Quick Emulator) allows local guest OS administrators to obtain sensitive host memory information by leveraging failure to initialize the txcq_descr object.

code_evidence: The local stack object txcq_descr is declared at line 3 without initialization. Only two fields are assigned (txdIdx at line 6 and gen at line 7), leaving the remaining bytes of the descriptor structure uninitialized. The whole object is then passed by pointer to vmxnet3_ring_write_curr_cell at line 8, which copies it into the completion ring visible to the guest.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-665 fits because the resource (txcq_descr) is not properly initialized before use, leaving it in an unexpected state. The disclosure is the downstream consequence of this improper initialization, not a separate out-of-bounds or logic flaw.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: a stack-allocated descriptor structure is only partially written before being copied out. Trigger: any packet completion path reaching this function writes the partially initialized descriptor into guest-accessible ring memory. Consequence: residual host stack bytes are disclosed to the guest, leaking host memory information.

commit_msg:
[CVE-2022-23308] Use-after-free of ID and IDREF attributes

If a document is parsed with XML_PARSE_DTDVALID and without
XML_PARSE_NOENT, the value of ID attributes has to be normalized after
potentially expanding entities in xmlRemoveID. Otherwise, later calls
to xmlGetID can return a pointer to previously freed memory.

ID attributes which are empty or contain only whitespace after
entity expansion are affected in a similar way. This is fixed by
not storing such attributes in the ID table.

The test to detect streaming mode when validating against a DTD was
broken. In connection with the defects above, this could result in a
use-after-free when using the xmlReader interface with validation.
Fix detection of streaming mode to avoid similar issues. (This changes
the expected result of a test case. But as far as I can tell, using the
XML reader with XIncludes referencing the root document never worked
properly, anyway.)

All of these issues can result in denial of service. Using xmlReader
with validation could result in disclosure of memory via the error
channel, typically stderr. The security impact of xmlGetID returning
a pointer to freed memory depends on the application. The typical use
case of calling xmlGetID on an unmodified document is not affected.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    xmlValidNormalizeString(ID);']}
description: valid.c in libxml2 before 2.9.13 has a use-after-free of ID and IDREF attributes.

code_evidence: Line 11 obtains the ID string via xmlNodeListGetString with entity substitution enabled (flag 1), so the ID may differ from the normalized form stored in the hash table.
Lines 14-19 look up the hash entry using this non-normalized ID; when lookup fails, the entry with the normalized key is never removed, leaving a stale ID entry referencing the attribute's memory.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing normalization causes a stale table entry to reference memory that is subsequently freed, and later retrieval dereferences it, matching CWE-416 (use-after-free). This is distinct from a mere logic error: the retained pointer is later used after free.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function removes an ID from doc->ids by recomputing the key from the attribute value with entity expansion but without normalizing it. If the attribute value contains entity references or whitespace that normalization would change, xmlHashLookup fails to match the stored entry, so the ID table retains a pointer to freed attribute memory; later xmlGetID returns that dangling pointer, causing use-after-free.

commit_msg:
teredo: be stricter on what to consider valid teredo

Invalid Teredo can lead to valid DNS traffic (or other UDP traffic)
being misdetected as Teredo. This leads to false negatives in the
UDP payload inspection.

Make the teredo code only consider a packet teredo if the encapsulated
data was decoded without any 'invalid' events being set.

Bug #2736.

This would technically be valid, but still weird.', '     *  - NH 0 (HOP) and not enough data.', '     *', '     *  If all these conditions are met, the tunnel decoder will be called.', '     *  If the packet gets an invalid event set, it will still be rejected.', '', '        /* ignore hoplimit 0 packets, most likely an artifact of bad detection */', '        if (IPV6_GET_RAW_HLIM(thdr) == 0)', '            return TM_ECODE_FAILED;', '', '        /* if nh is 0 (HOP) with little data we have a bogus packet */', '        if (IPV6_GET_RAW_NH(thdr) == 0 && IPV6_GET_RAW_PLEN(thdr) < 8)', '            return TM_ECODE_FAILED;', '', '                                                  DECODE_TUNNEL_IPV6_TEREDO, pq);']}
description: Open Information Security Foundation Suricata prior to version 4.1.2 is affected by: Denial of Service - DNS detection bypass. The impact is: An attacker can evade a signature detection with a specialy formed network packet. The component is: app-layer-detect-proto.c, decode.c, decode-teredo.c and decode-ipv6.c (https://github.com/OISF/suricata/pull/3590/commits/11f3659f64a4e42e90cb3c09fcef66894205aefe, https://github.com/OISF/suricata/pull/3590/commits/8357ef3f8ffc7d99ef6571350724160de356158b). The attack vector is: An attacker can trigger the vulnerability by sending a specifically crafted network request. The fixed version is: 4.1.2.

code_evidence: After stripping the Teredo header, the code only checks IP version and that the declared IPv6 payload length plus header matches the remaining buffer before tunneling; the embedded IPv6 header fields are otherwise trusted as-is.
The encapsulated packet is handed to the tunnel decoder via PacketTunnelPktSetup with DECODE_TUNNEL_IPV6, so malformed inner IPv6 data is treated as valid Teredo and forwarded for further decoding.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function accepts input as a valid Teredo packet without sufficiently validating the properties of the encapsulated IPv6 header, which is improper input validation (CWE-20). It is not merely a length check bug; the missing validation of derived header properties is the core weakness, enabling misclassification and detection bypass.

evidence_lines.code:
Packet *tp = PacketTunnelPktSetup(tv, dtv, p, start, blen,
DECODE_TUNNEL_IPV6, pq);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the Teredo detector validates only version and total length of the encapsulated IPv6 header, accepting packets whose inner header fields (hop limit, next header) are nonsensical. Trigger: a crafted UDP packet that mimics a Teredo origin indication and carries a malformed IPv6 payload. Consequence: non-Teredo UDP/DNS traffic is misclassified as Teredo, causing the encapsulated payload to be decoded and evading UDP payload signature inspection.

description: In nDPI through 3.2, the OpenVPN dissector is vulnerable to a heap-based buffer over-read in ndpi_search_openvpn in lib/protocols/openvpn.c.

code_evidence: The length gate uses packet->payload_packet_len >= 40, but for TCP payloads the pointer is advanced by 2 (ovpn_payload += 2) without reducing the length bound.
opcode is read at ovpn_payload[0] after that shift, so the effective buffer is 2 bytes shorter than the length check assumes.

alen is read at ovpn_payload[P_PACKET_ID_ARRAY_LEN_OFFSET(hmac_size)], and session_remote is computed as ovpn_payload + offset + 1 + alen*4; the subsequent memcmp and the session_remote[0..7] reads in the debug log use this pointer with no check that offset+8 stays within payload_packet_len.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This is an out-of-bounds read: the code dereferences session_remote and indexes ovpn_payload beyond the allocated payload without a bounds check. It is not a write or buffer overflow, since only reads occur, matching CWE-125.

evidence_lines.code: opcode = ovpn_payload[0] & P_OPCODE_MASK;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The payload length check is not adjusted after the TCP 2-byte shift, and the attacker-controlled alen/hmac_size-derived offset is never validated against the actual payload length. A crafted OpenVPN packet with a large alen makes session_remote point past the payload buffer, so memcmp and the debug log read out-of-bounds heap memory.

commit_msg:
Patch series "Fix several device private page reference counting issues",
v2

This series aims to fix a number of page reference counting issues in
drivers dealing with device private ZONE_DEVICE pages.  These result in
use-after-free type bugs, either from accessing a struct page which no
longer exists because it has been removed or accessing fields within the
struct page which are no longer valid because the page has been freed.

During normal usage it is unlikely these will cause any problems.  However
without these fixes it is possible to crash the kernel from userspace. 
These crashes can be triggered either by unloading the kernel module or
unbinding the device from the driver prior to a userspace task exiting. 
In modules such as Nouveau it is also possible to trigger some of these
issues by explicitly closing the device file-descriptor prior to the task
exiting and then accessing device private memory.

This involves some minor changes to both PowerPC and AMD GPU code. 
Unfortunately I lack hardware to test either of those so any help there
would be appreciated.  The changes mimic what is done in for both Nouveau
and hmm-tests though so I doubt they will cause problems.


This patch (of 8):

When the CPU tries to access a device private page the migrate_to_ram()
callback associated with the pgmap for the page is called.  However no
reference is taken on the faulting page.  Therefore a concurrent migration
of the device private page can free the page and possibly the underlying
pgmap.  This results in a race which can crash the kernel due to the
migrate_to_ram() function pointer becoming invalid.  It also means drivers
can't reliably read the zone_device_data field because the page may have
been freed with memunmap_pages().

Close the race by getting a reference on the page while holding the ptl to
ensure it has not been freed.  Unfortunately the elevated reference count
will cause the migration required to handle the fault to fail.  To avoid
this failure pass the faulting page into the migrate_vma functions so that
if an elevated reference count is found it can be checked to see if it's
expected or not.

description: A vulnerability was found in Linux Kernel. It has been classified as problematic. Affected is an unknown function of the file mm/memory.c of the component Driver Handler. The manipulation leads to use after free. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue. The identifier of this vulnerability is VDB-211020.

code_evidence: Line 10 obtains 'page' from migrate->src[i] via migrate_pfn_to_page() without taking a reference. Line 33 derives mapping from that page, and lines 44-45 pass page_folio(page) into migrate_folio() for the migration, all while no reference pins the page.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function references a page it does not own or pin against concurrent freeing, which is the use-after-free pattern. The patch that adds a fault_page check confirms the missing reference was the root defect; this is not a mere leak because the freed page is subsequently dereferenced.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The source device-private page is used (mapping lookup and migrate_folio) without a reference held on it. A concurrent migration can free the page and its pgmap between fault handling and this use, so migrate_folio dereferences freed memory or an invalid function pointer, causing a kernel crash (use-after-free).
