commit_msg:
Fix tf.raw_ops.AudioSummaryV2 vulnerability with invalid `sample_rate`.

Check that `sample_rate` has the required shape.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 460819553
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['      OP_REQUIRES(c,', '                  sample_rate_tensor.IsAligned() &&', '                      sample_rate_tensor.NumElements() == 1,', '                  errors::InvalidArgument(', '                      "sample_rate must be rank-0 or contain a single value"));']}
description: TensorFlow is an open source platform for machine learning. When `AudioSummaryV2` receives an input `sample_rate` with more than one element, it gives a `CHECK` fails that can be used to trigger a denial of service attack. We have patched the issue in GitHub commit bf6b45244992e2ee543c258e519489659c99fb7f. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.10.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.9.1, TensorFlow 2.8.1, and TensorFlow 2.7.2, as these are also affected and still in supported range. There are no known workarounds for this issue.

code_evidence: The function reads input(2) as sample_rate_tensor and immediately calls scalar<float>() on it without verifying that it contains exactly one element.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked input reaches an assertion-style CHECK inside the scalar accessor, making the assertion attacker-reachable and terminating the process; this matches CWE-617 (Reachable Assertion). A generic input-validation label would describe the missing check but not the assertion-triggered crash consequence.

evidence_lines.code:
const Tensor& sample_rate_tensor = c->input(2);
sample_rate = sample_rate_tensor.scalar<float>()();

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: no shape/element-count check on the user-supplied sample_rate tensor before scalar<float>() is invoked. Trigger: an AudioSummaryV2 call with a sample_rate tensor holding more than one element; the scalar accessor's internal CHECK fails. Consequence: the process aborts, enabling a denial of service.

commit_msg:
CVE-2021-43825

Response filter manager crash

Signed-off-by: Yan Avlasov <yavlasov@google.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  ENVOY_STREAM_LOG(debug, "response data too large watermark exceeded", parent_);']}
description: Envoy is an open source edge and service proxy, designed for cloud-native applications. Sending a locally generated response must stop further processing of request or response data. Envoy tracks the amount of buffered request and response data and aborts the request if the amount of buffered data is over the limit by sending 413 or 500 responses. However when the buffer overflows while response is processed by the filter chain the operation may not be aborted correctly and result in accessing a freed memory block. If this happens Envoy will crash resulting in a denial of service.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function only branches on encoder_filters_streaming_ and calls watermark/local-reply helpers; it contains no memory free, pointer reuse, or other use-after-free operation, and the added line is only a debug log.

description: In Wireshark 2.2.0 to 2.2.1 and 2.0.0 to 2.0.7, the OpenFlow dissector could crash with memory exhaustion, triggered by network traffic or a capture file. This was addressed in epan/dissectors/packet-openflow_v5.c by ensuring that certain length values were sufficiently large.

code_evidence: match_length is read from the packet and immediately used to compute pad_length and set the item length (14-16) before any lower-bound validation; the patched function later rejects match_length < 4, confirming the pre-patch value was unchecked.
The OFPMT_STANDARD branch computes match_length - 4 as the expert-format length and advances offset by match_length-4 (21-23), so a match_length below 4 underflows the guint16 arithmetic.

The OFPMT_OXM branch computes fields_end = offset + match_length - 4 (26); with match_length < 4 this yields a fields_end below offset, so the while loop at 27 is skipped and later pad handling advances from a stale offset.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-399 (Resource Management Errors) fits because the unchecked length arithmetic corrupts the dissector's resource/offset management, enabling crash or memory exhaustion under hostile input; the commit itself frames the fix as avoiding offset rewind. This is not a simple buffer overflow but a failure to bound consumed resources.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: an attacker-controlled OpenFlow match length is used in subtractions and offset arithmetic without a minimum-length check. Trigger: a capture/traffic packet declaring match_length < 4. The underflowed lengths and inconsistent offset advances can drive out-of-range tvb access and dissector looping, leading to crash or memory exhaustion.

description: binutils version 2.32 and earlier contains a Integer Overflow vulnerability in objdump, bfd_get_dynamic_reloc_upper_bound,bfd_canonicalize_dynamic_reloc that can result in Integer overflow trigger heap overflow. Successful exploitation allows execution of arbitrary code.. This attack appear to be exploitable via Local. This vulnerability appears to have been fixed in after commit 3a551c7a1b80fca579461774860574eabfd7f18f.

code_evidence: symcount is a signed long computed from the untrusted section header size hdr->sh_size divided by sizeof_sym; the subsequent (symcount + 1) * sizeof(asymbol *) multiplication is stored in long symtab_size and returned without any overflow check.

This is the size-computation cause, not merely the downstream heap overflow consequence.

The returned size is used by callers to size relocation/symbol buffers, so the undersized allocation enables a heap overflow.

commit_msg:
net: fix a kernel infoleak in x25 module

Stack object "dte_facilities" is allocated in x25_rx_call_request(),
which is supposed to be initialized in x25_negotiate_facilities.
However, 5 fields (8 bytes in total) are not initialized. This
object is then copied to userland via copy_to_user, thus infoleak
occurs.

Signed-off-by: Kangjie Lu <kjlu@gatech.edu>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tmemset(dte, 0, sizeof(*dte));']}
description: The x25_negotiate_facilities function in net/x25/x25_facilities.c in the Linux kernel before 4.5.5 does not properly initialize a certain data structure, which allows attackers to obtain sensitive information from kernel stack memory via an X.25 Call Request.

code_evidence: Line 6 declares the stack struct 'theirs' without initialization; line 8 clears it, but the output parameter 'dte' passed at line 10 is not cleared here. Line 9 copies only 'ours' into 'new', leaving 'dte' contents dependent on x25_parse_facilities (line 10), which the commit states leaves 5 fields (8 bytes) uninitialized.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function fails to initialize a data structure that is subsequently transferred to userland, directly disclosing kernel stack contents to an unauthorized actor. This is an explicit information-exposure mistake, matching CWE-200 rather than a generic memory-safety flaw.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the caller-supplied 'dte' stack object is not zeroed before being partially populated by x25_parse_facilities, so padding/unparsed facility fields retain stale stack bytes. Trigger: an X.25 Call Request whose facilities do not fill all 'dte' fields; the struct is later copied to userland, exposing kernel stack memory (CWE-200).

commit_msg:
commit 386e4fb6962b9f248a80f8870aea0870ca603e89 upstream.

In prior kernels, we did file assignment always at prep time. This meant
that req->task == current. But after deferring that assignment and then
pushing the inflight tracking back in, we've got the inflight tracking
using current when it should in fact now be using req->task.

Fixup that error introduced by adding the inflight tracking back after
file assignments got modifed.

Fixes: 9cae36a094e7 ("io_uring: reinstate the inflight tracking")
Signed-off-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

description: A null pointer dereference issue was discovered in fs/io_uring.c in the Linux kernel before 5.15.62. A local user could use this flaw to crash the system or potentially cause a denial of service.

code_evidence: The guard only checks REQ_F_INFLIGHT; on the first call it sets the flag and then dereferences current->io_uring without checking that current->io_uring is non-NULL. The patch changes this to req->task->io_uring, showing the dereference target was wrong and could be NULL for the calling context.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe operation is a direct dereference of a pointer assumed valid without a NULL check, matching CWE-476's NULL pointer dereference. The fix redirects the dereference to req->task->io_uring, confirming the wrong pointer was used rather than a separate weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function dereferences current->io_uring unconditionally after setting REQ_F_INFLIGHT, with no NULL check. Trigger: a request reaches this path when the calling task's io_uring context is NULL. Consequence: a NULL pointer dereference crashes the kernel, giving local denial of service.

commit_msg:
ext_mbstring: Fix invalid free() in php_mb_parse_encoding

Summary:
A chunk of memory allocated by 'req::calloc_noptrs' was being freed by 'free'. The former internally calls 'calloc' and returns a pointer at an index sizeof(MallocNode) inside the allocated buffer. This led to freeing invalid memory.

CVE-2019-11930

Reviewed By: jjergus

Differential Revision: D18179908

fbshipit-source-id: 0e3fe77628e0b9dee8361e712b8abac59ae5ed22
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      free(*return_list);'], 'added_lines': ['      req::free(*return_list);']}
description: An invalid free in mb_detect_order can cause the application to crash or potentially result in remote code execution. This issue affects HHVM versions prior to 3.30.12, all versions between 4.0.0 and 4.8.5, all versions between 4.9.0 and 4.23.1, as well as 4.24.0, 4.25.0, 4.26.0, 4.27.0, 4.28.0, and 4.28.1.

code_evidence: On failure (ret false), the function cleans up *return_list by calling free(*return_list) at line 17 and then nulls the pointer. The allocation was produced by the parse-encoding helpers, which use req::calloc_noptrs; that allocator returns an interior pointer offset past a MallocNode header, so passing it to plain free releases an invalid pointer.

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the cleanup path deallocates a req-allocated buffer with the mismatched plain free() rather than req::free(), so free() receives a pointer that is not the start of the underlying malloc block. commit_msg:
There are multiple refcounting bugs related to multi-BSSID:
 - In bss_ref_get(), if the BSS has a hidden_beacon_bss, then
   the bss pointer is overwritten before checking for the
   transmitted BSS, which is clearly wrong. Fix this by using
   the bss_from_pub() macro.

 - In cfg80211_bss_update() we copy the transmitted_bss pointer
   from tmp into new, but then if we release new, we'll unref
   it erroneously. We already set the pointer and ref it, but
   need to NULL it since it was copied from the tmp data.

 - In cfg80211_inform_single_bss_data(), if adding to the non-
   transmitted list fails, we unlink the BSS and yet still we
   return it, but this results in returning an entry without
   a reference. We shouldn't return it anyway if it was broken
   enough to not get added there.

This fixes CVE-2022-42720.

Reported-by: Sönke Huster <shuster@seemoo.tu-darmstadt.de>
Tested-by: Sönke Huster <shuster@seemoo.tu-darmstadt.de>
Fixes: a3584f56de1c ("cfg80211: Properly track transmitting and non-transmitting BSS")
Signed-off-by: Johannes Berg <johannes.berg@intel.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ["\t\t/* we'll set this later if it was non-NULL */", '\t\tnew->pub.transmitted_bss = NULL;']}
description: Various refcounting bugs in the multi-BSS handling in the mac80211 stack in the Linux kernel 5.1 through 5.19.x before 5.19.16 could be used by local attackers (able to inject WLAN frames) to trigger use-after-free conditions to potentially execute code.

code_evidence: Line 34 copies the entire tmp structure into new, including tmp->pub.transmitted_bss, so new inherits a transmitted_bss pointer to a peer BSS without taking its own reference. Lines 62-69 only take a reference (bss_ref_get on pbss) and re-set the pointer when tmp->pub.transmitted_bss is non-NULL; when it is NULL the copied pointer is never cleared, and the peer's reference is not held.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the copied transmitted_bss pointer is dereferenced after the referenced BSS has been freed due to mismatched refcounting (missing get or erroneous unref). This is a use-after-free, distinct from a mere memory leak, since the dangling pointer remains reachable and usable.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: memcpy at line 34 duplicates transmitted_bss from tmp, but the refcount is only acquired in the conditional block at lines 62-69. When the conditional is skipped or the new entry is later released via bss_ref_put, the transmitted_bss reference is dropped without a corresponding get, freeing the peer BSS while new still points to it. Trigger: processing multi-BSSID frames where the transmitted/non-transmitted relationship is established. Consequence: use-after-free of the peer BSS structure, enabling read/modify of freed memory or code execution by local attackers injecting WLAN frames.

commit_msg:
DH_check(): Do not try checking q properties if it is obviously invalid

If  |q| >= |p| then the q value is obviously wrong as q
is supposed to be a prime divisor of p-1.

We check if p is overly large so this added test implies that
q is not large either when performing subsequent tests using that
q value.

Otherwise if it is too large these additional checks of the q value
such as the primality test can then trigger DoS by doing overly long
computations.

Fixes CVE-2023-3817

Reviewed-by: Matt Caswell <matt@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Paul Dale <pauli@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Tom Cosgrove <tom.cosgrove@arm.com>
Reviewed-by: Todd Short <todd.short@me.com>
(Merged from https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/21550)

(cherry picked from commit 1c16253f3c3a8d1e25918c3f404aae6a5b0893de)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    int ok = 0, r;'], 'added_lines': ['    int ok = 0, r, q_good = 0;', '        if (BN_ucmp(dh->params.p, dh->params.q) > 0)', '            q_good = 1;', '        else', '            *ret |= DH_CHECK_INVALID_Q_VALUE;', '    }', '', '    if (q_good) {']}
description:
Issue summary: Checking excessively long DH keys or parameters may be very slow.

Impact summary: Applications that use the functions DH_check(), DH_check_ex()
or EVP_PKEY_param_check() to check a DH key or DH parameters may experience long
delays. Where the key or parameters that are being checked have been obtained
from an untrusted source this may lead to a Denial of Service.

The function DH_check() performs various checks on DH parameters. After fixing
CVE-2023-3446 it was discovered that a large q parameter value can also trigger
an overly long computation during some of these checks. A correct q value,
if present, cannot be larger than the modulus p parameter, thus it is
unnecessary to perform these checks if q is larger than p.

An application that calls DH_check() and supplies a key or parameters obtained
from an untrusted source could be vulnerable to a Denial of Service attack.

The function DH_check() is itself called by a number of other OpenSSL functions.
An application calling any of those other functions may similarly be affected.
The other functions affected by this are DH_check_ex() and
EVP_PKEY_param_check().

Also vulnerable are the OpenSSL dhparam and pkeyparam command line applications
when using the "-check" option.

The OpenSSL SSL/TLS implementation is not affected by this issue.

The OpenSSL 3.0 and 3.1 FIPS providers are not affected by this issue.

code_evidence: When dh->params.q is non-NULL, the function runs BN_check_prime(q) and BN_div(p, q) and BN_mod_exp(g, q, p) without first verifying that q is smaller than p; the size of q is attacker-influenced and only p's size is bounded at line 13.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The expensive operations on an unbounded, attacker-supplied q constitute excessive iteration/computation over a value whose size is not sufficiently limited, matching CWE-834's resource-consumption DoS. The missing check that |q| < |p| is the absent constraint enabling prolonged computation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: q is used in expensive primality, modular exponentiation and division computations without a size relation constraint to p. Trigger: an untrusted DH parameter set supplies an oversized q. Consequence: the large-number computations consume excessive CPU time, causing a denial of service (CVE-2023-3817).

commit_msg:
AK: Don't read past the end in BitmapView::count_in_range()

The current code is factored such that reads to the entirety of the last
byte should be dropped. This was relying on the fact that last would be
one past the end in that case. Instead of actually reading that byte
when it's completely out of bounds of the bitmask, just skip reads that
would be invalid. Add more tests to make sure that the behavior is
correct for byte aligned reads of byte aligned bitmaps.

commit_msg: Fix for #4866: Added additional length checks
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\tif (Stream_GetRemainingLength(s) < drdynvc_cblen_to_bytes(cbChId) + drdynvc_cblen_to_bytes(Sp))', '\t\treturn ERROR_INVALID_DATA;', '']}
description: FreeRDP FreeRDP 2.0.0-rc3 released version before commit 205c612820dac644d665b5bb1cdf437dc5ca01e3 contains a Other/Unknown vulnerability in channels/drdynvc/client/drdynvc_main.c, drdynvc_process_capability_request that can result in The RDP server can read the client's memory.. This attack appear to be exploitable via RDPClient must connect the rdp server with echo option. commit_msg:
Jing Xia and Chunyan Zhang reported that on failing to allocate part of the
tracing buffer, memory is freed, but the pointers that point to them are not
initialized back to NULL, and later paths may try to free the freed memory
again. Jing and Chunyan fixed one of the locations that does this, but
missed a spot.

Link: http://lkml.kernel.org/r/20171226071253.8968-1-chunyan.zhang@spreadtrum.com

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: 737223fbca3b1 ("tracing: Consolidate buffer allocation code")
Reported-by: Jing Xia <jing.xia@spreadtrum.com>
Reported-by: Chunyan Zhang <chunyan.zhang@spreadtrum.com>
Signed-off-by: Steven Rostedt (VMware) <rostedt@goodmis.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\tbuf->buffer = NULL;']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel before 4.14.11. A double free may be caused by the function allocate_trace_buffer in the file kernel/trace/trace.c.

code_evidence: After alloc_percpu fails, line 12 frees buf->buffer but the pointer remains set; the function returns -ENOMEM at line 13 without clearing buf->buffer to NULL, leaving a dangling pointer in the caller-visible struct.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-415 fits because the same memory address (buf->buffer) can be passed to ring_buffer_free twice: once at line 12 and again by a later path using the stale pointer. This is a double-free, not merely a use-after-free, since the supported consequence is a second free of the same allocation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: on the alloc_percpu failure path, the ring buffer is freed but buf->buffer is not reset, so it still references freed memory. Trigger: a later error/cleanup path that frees buf->buffer again. Consequence: double free of the same address, enabling memory corruption or potential code execution.

commit_msg:
ocfs2: subsystem.su_mutex is required while accessing the item->ci_parent

The subsystem.su_mutex is required while accessing the item->ci_parent,
otherwise, NULL pointer dereference to the item->ci_parent will be
triggered in the following situation:

add node                     delete node
sys_write
 vfs_write
  configfs_write_file
   o2nm_node_store
    o2nm_node_local_write
                             do_rmdir
                              vfs_rmdir
                               configfs_rmdir
                                mutex_lock(&subsys->su_mutex);
                                unlink_obj
                                 item->ci_group = NULL;
                                 item->ci_parent = NULL;
	 to_o2nm_cluster_from_node
	  node->nd_item.ci_parent->ci_parent
	  BUG since of NULL pointer dereference to nd_item.ci_parent

Moreover, the o2nm_cluster also should be protected by the
subsystem.su_mutex.

description: In fs/ocfs2/cluster/nodemanager.c in the Linux kernel before 4.15, local users can cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference and BUG) because a required mutex is not used.

code_evidence: Line 6 dereferences the result of to_o2nm_cluster_from_node(node) immediately, with no lock protecting node->nd_item.ci_parent and no NULL check.
The cluster pointer derived at line 6 is then used at line 21 (write_lock(&cluster->cl_nodes_lock)) and again at lines 22 and 29 for tree lookup/insertion, propagating the unchecked value.
The failure path at lines 32-33 only handles ret (e.g. -EEXIST/-EBUSY); there is no branch that detects a missing cluster, so a NULL cluster is never rejected.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The target CWE-476 applies because the unchecked NULL cluster pointer is dereferenced in this function, matching a NULL pointer dereference. The missing mutex is the enabling condition, not a separate lock-ordering or race-label issue; the supported consequence is the NULL dereference.

evidence_lines.code: struct o2nm_cluster *cluster = to_o2nm_cluster_from_node(node);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function reads node->nd_item.ci_parent via to_o2nm_cluster_from_node without holding subsystem.su_mutex, so a concurrent configfs_rmdir can set ci_parent to NULL between the read and its use. Trigger: a local user writes an IPv4 address to a node's configfs attribute while the node is being removed. Consequence: the NULL cluster is dereferenced at write_lock(&cluster->cl_nodes_lock), causing a kernel BUG/DoS crash.

commit_msg: rfadts: add size guard on dmx (#2400)

description: Heap-based Buffer Overflow in GitHub repository gpac/gpac prior to 2.3.0-DEV.

code_evidence: At line 216 the code enters the non-seek path and allocates a destination packet of 'size' bytes (line 217), then copies 'size' bytes from 'sync + offset' into it (line 220).
'size' is derived from the attacker-controlled ADTS header frame_size minus hdr_size (lines 201-204); no check ensures sync + offset + size stays within the remaining buffer before the memcpy.
The only size validation at line 171 checks frame_size against remain but is conditional on the frame being smaller than remain, and does not guard the copy at line 220.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe copy from a heap-allocated buffer (ctx->adts_buffer) driven by unvalidated length fields matches CWE-122 heap-based buffer overflow. It is distinguished from a stack overflow because the source buffer is heap-allocated via gf_realloc at line 47.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the memcpy at line 220 copies 'size' bytes from the heap-backed ADTS buffer using an offset/size derived from parsed header fields, without confirming sync + offset + size <= remain. Trigger: a crafted ADTS frame whose frame_size exceeds the actual buffered data. Consequence: out-of-bounds heap read (and inconsistent packet allocation) leading to memory corruption/crash.

commit_msg: misc oom and possible memory leak fix
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    names = malloc(sizeof (struct dirent *) * count);', '', '    closedir(d);', '    if (NULL == d)', ''], 'added_lines': ['\t', '\tclosedir(d);', '\t', '    names = malloc(sizeof (struct dirent *) * count);', '\tif (!names) ', '\t\treturn -1;', '    if (NULL == d) {', '\t\tfree(names);', '    }', '\t\t\t/* FIXME: OOM, silently skip it?*/', '\t\t\tif (!copyentry)', '\t\t\t\tcontinue;', '\t\t\t']}
description: Boa through 0.94.14rc21 allows remote attackers to trigger an out-of-memory (OOM) condition because malloc is mishandled.

code_evidence: Line 16 allocates names as an array of count pointers based on a first directory scan. Line 23 allocates copyentry of current->d_reclen bytes, and line 24 copies current->d_reclen bytes into it. Line 25 then stores copyentry into names[pos] using pos incremented per selected entry, without any bound check against count.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-119 fits because names[pos] can write outside the malloc'd names buffer when pos exceeds count, corrupting adjacent heap memory. The unchecked NULL from malloc is a related memory-safety flaw but not the out-of-bounds operation described by CWE-119.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The buffer names is sized from the first readdir pass (count), but the second pass re-reads the directory and increments pos for each selected entry without verifying pos < count. If the directory changes between passes so the second pass yields more entries than count, names[pos] writes past the allocated pointer array. The unchecked malloc of copyentry also allows a NULL dereference in memcpy, but the out-of-bounds store is the supported buffer issue.

commit_msg:
Fix acl_file being ignore for default listener if with per_listener_settings

Close #1073. Thanks to Jef Driesen.

Bug: https://github.com/eclipse/mosquitto/issues/1073
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\tconfig->listeners[config->listener_count-1].security_options.acl_file = config->default_listener.security_options.acl_file;']}
description: Eclipse Mosquitto 1.5.x before 1.5.5 allows ACL bypass: if the option per_listener_settings was set to true, and the default listener was in use, and the default listener specified an acl_file, then the acl file was being ignored.

code_evidence: The condition at [48,72] triggers creation of a listener entry when default-listener settings are present, but the list of checked fields omits security_options.acl_file; the default listener's ACL file therefore does not by itself cause a listener to be materialized.

When the entry is created, [117,121] copies password_file, psk_file, auth_plugin_configs, auth_plugin_config_count and allow_anonymous from the default listener's security_options, but never copies security_options.acl_file, so the new listener has a NULL acl_file.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing acl_file propagation causes the critical access-control resource (the ACL file) to be effectively absent for the listener, granting unintended actors more access than the administrator assigned — an incorrect permission assignment for a critical resource, matching CWE-732 rather than a mere parsing bug.

evidence_lines.code:
if(config->listener_count == 0
){

config->listeners[config->listener_count-1].security_options.password_file = config->default_listener.security_options.password_file;
config->listeners[config->listener_count-1].security_options.allow_anonymous = config->default_listener.security_options.allow_anonymous;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the default listener's acl_file is neither considered in the listener-creation condition nor propagated to the newly allocated listener's security_options. Trigger: per_listener_settings=true with a default listener that specifies acl_file; the resulting listener lacks the ACL restriction, so access checks fall back to no ACL and clients gain broader access than the administrator configured.

description: mediaserver in Android 6.x before 2016-03-01 allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code or cause a denial of service (memory corruption) via a crafted media file, related to decoder/ih264d_parse_islice.c and decoder/ih264d_parse_pslice.c, aka internal bug 25928803.

Per iteration, ps_cur_mb_info and ps_cur_deblk_mb are indexed by u1_num_mbs into ps_nmb_info / ps_deblk_mbn without a bound against the allocated group size.
i2_cur_mb_addr, u1_num_mbs and u2_total_mbs_coded all increment each iteration, but u1_num_mbs is only reset when u1_tfr_n_mb, so index growth is not tied to the buffer capacity.
The completion check at 305-306 compares u2_total_mbs_coded against frame dimensions only after the loop, so it cannot prevent an out-of-range index during iteration.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs indexed writes into fixed decoder buffers beyond their intended bounds, matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds buffer operation. The missing bound check on u1_num_mbs is the direct cause, distinguishing it from a pure integer-overflow weakness.

ps_cur_deblk_mb = ps_dec->ps_deblk_mbn + u1_num_mbs;

Trigger: a crafted media file whose skip run or total_mbs_coded drives u1_num_mbs past the allocated group, causing out-of-bounds writes to ps_cur_mb_info and ps_cur_deblk_mb, leading to memory corruption and potential code execution.

description: Jsish v3.5.0 was discovered to contain a heap-use-after-free via SortSubCmd in src/jsiArray.c. This vulnerability can lead to a Denial of Service (DoS).

code_evidence: Line 45 listifies the source array, then the loop at 49-54 moves references from obj->arr into nobj->arr and nulls the source slots. The second loop at 56-60 shifts remaining slots down and nulls the old positions. Later, lines 67-71 shift elements right by ilen and null the vacated slots, after which lines 72-77 assign new values into obj->arr.
The patch adds a guard at lines 8-9 (obj->modifying) that is absent from the analyzed function body, so the function lacks reentrancy protection while it mutates obj->arr.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the function continues to reference array slots (obj->arr[i], obj->arr[m]) after those slots may have been freed or reassigned by a reentrant call, which is exactly reuse of freed memory. This is not merely an out-of-bounds issue: the pointers are valid slots whose lifetime is invalidated by reentrancy.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: jsi_ArraySpliceCmd mutates obj->arr in place (nulling and shifting slots, then assigning via Jsi_ValueDup2) without any guard against reentrant modification. Trigger: a value operation (e.g., Jsi_ValueDup2 or listify) that re-enters splice or otherwise frees/reallocates the array storage while obj->arr pointers are still in use. Consequence: stale obj->arr entries are dereferenced or overwritten, producing a heap-use-after-free leading to crash/DoS.

commit_msg:
Integer Overflow in RAND commands can lead to assertion (CVE-2023-25155)

Issue happens when passing a negative long value that greater than
the max positive value that the long can store.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        if (getLongFromObjectOrReply(c,c->argv[2],&l,NULL) != C_OK) return;', '            if (l < LONG_MIN/2 || l > LONG_MAX/2) {'], 'added_lines': ['        if (getRangeLongFromObjectOrReply(c,c->argv[2],-LONG_MAX,LONG_MAX,&l,NULL) != C_OK) return;', '            if (l < -LONG_MAX/2 || l > LONG_MAX/2) {']}
description: Redis is an in-memory database that persists on disk. Authenticated users issuing specially crafted `SRANDMEMBER`, `ZRANDMEMBER`, and `HRANDFIELD` commands can trigger an integer overflow, resulting in a runtime assertion and termination of the Redis server process. This problem affects all Redis versions. Patches were released in Redis version(s) 6.0.18, 6.2.11 and 7.0.9.

code_evidence: Line 7 parses the count argument with getLongFromObjectOrReply, which accepts the full long range including LONG_MIN; no lower bound is enforced here.

Line 13 guards only when withvalues is set, comparing l against LONG_MIN/2 and LONG_MAX/2; the negative count path without 'withvalues' (argc==3) bypasses this range check entirely before calling hrandfieldWithCountCommand at line 18.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is an integer overflow/wraparound in count handling that leads to a runtime assertion; CWE-190 directly covers arithmetic producing out-of-range values. It is distinct from a simple input-validation gap because the exploited consequence stems from the overflowed count arithmetic, not merely the missing bound.

evidence_lines.code: if (getLongFromObjectOrReply(c,c->argv[2],&l,NULL) != C_OK) return;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the count value is accepted as an unbounded long and only range-checked in the withvalues branch, so a negative value near LONG_MIN passes through unchecked. When hrandfieldWithCountCommand negates or manipulates this count, the arithmetic overflows, producing an assertion and terminating the server (availability impact).

commit_msg:
x86/vpt: fix race when migrating timers between vCPUs

The current vPT code will migrate the emulated timers between vCPUs
(change the pt->vcpu field) while just holding the destination lock,
either from create_periodic_time or pt_adjust_global_vcpu_target if
the global target is adjusted. Changing the periodic_timer vCPU field
in this way creates a race where a third party could grab the lock in
the unlocked region of pt_adjust_global_vcpu_target (or before
create_periodic_time performs the vcpu change) and then release the
lock from a different vCPU, creating a locking imbalance.

Introduce a per-domain rwlock in order to protect periodic_time
migration between vCPU lists. Taking the lock in read mode prevents
any timer from being migrated to a different vCPU, while taking it in
write mode allows performing migration of timers across vCPUs. The
per-vcpu locks are still used to protect all the other fields from the
periodic_timer struct.

Note that such migration shouldn't happen frequently, and hence
there's no performance drop as a result of such locking.

This is XSA-336.

Reported-by: Igor Druzhinin <igor.druzhinin@citrix.com>
Tested-by: Igor Druzhinin <igor.druzhinin@citrix.com>
Signed-off-by: Roger Pau Monné <roger.pau@citrix.com>
Reviewed-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    spin_lock(&v->arch.hvm.tm_lock);', '    spin_unlock(&v->arch.hvm.tm_lock);'], 'added_lines': ['    pt_vcpu_lock(v);', '    pt_vcpu_unlock(v);']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.14.x. There is a race condition when migrating timers between x86 HVM vCPUs. When migrating timers of x86 HVM guests between its vCPUs, the locking model used allows for a second vCPU of the same guest (also operating on the timers) to release a lock that it didn't acquire. The most likely effect of the issue is a hang or crash of the hypervisor, i.e., a Denial of Service (DoS). All versions of Xen are affected. Only x86 systems are vulnerable. Arm systems are not vulnerable. Only x86 HVM guests can leverage the vulnerability. x86 PV and PVH cannot leverage the vulnerability. Only guests with more than one vCPU can exploit the vulnerability.

code_evidence: pt_migrate acquires only the per-vCPU timer lock (tm_lock) around iteration over v->arch.hvm.tm_list and calls migrate_timer, which changes each periodic_timer's vcpu/timer target. The commit shows this vCPU lock does not protect cross-vCPU migration; a concurrent pt_adjust_global_vcpu_target or create_periodic_time can alter pt->vcpu and the list membership while the loop runs, and the lock may then be released by a different vCPU.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function iterates a shared timer list and mutates timers under a lock that does not provide exclusive access against concurrent cross-vCPU migration, a timing window violating exclusivity/atomicity, matching CWE-362. It is not merely a missing NULL check or use-after-free; the defect is improper synchronization of a shared resource.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: migration of periodic timers between vCPUs is serialized only by the per-vCPU tm_lock, which does not exclude a concurrent migrator operating on a different vCPU. Trigger: two vCPUs concurrently migrate timers, so the list is modified during iteration and lock ownership becomes mismatched. Supported consequence: locking imbalance leading to hypervisor hang or crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
ALSA: control: code refactoring for ELEM_READ/ELEM_WRITE operations

ALSA control core handles ELEM_READ/ELEM_WRITE requests within lock
acquisition of a counting semaphore. The lock is acquired in helper
functions in the end of call path before calling implementations of each
driver.

ioctl(2) with SNDRV_CTL_ELEM_READ
...
->snd_ctl_ioctl()
  ->snd_ctl_elem_read_user()
    ->snd_ctl_elem_read()
      ->down_read(controls_rwsem)
      ->snd_ctl_find_id()
      ->struct snd_kcontrol.get()
      ->up_read(controls_rwsem)

ioctl(2) with SNDRV_CTL_ELEM_WRITE
...
->snd_ctl_ioctl()
  ->snd_ctl_elem_write_user()
    ->snd_ctl_elem_write()
      ->down_read(controls_rwsem)
      ->snd_ctl_find_id()
      ->struct snd_kcontrol.put()
      ->up_read(controls_rwsem)

This commit moves the lock acquisition to middle of the call graph to
simplify the helper functions. As a result:

ioctl(2) with SNDRV_CTL_ELEM_READ
...
->snd_ctl_ioctl()
  ->snd_ctl_elem_read_user()
    ->down_read(controls_rwsem)
    ->snd_ctl_elem_read()
      ->snd_ctl_find_id()
      ->struct snd_kcontrol.get()
    ->up_read(controls_rwsem)

ioctl(2) with SNDRV_CTL_ELEM_WRITE
...
->snd_ctl_ioctl()
  ->snd_ctl_elem_write_user()
    ->down_read(controls_rwsem)
    ->snd_ctl_elem_write()
      ->snd_ctl_find_id()
      ->struct snd_kcontrol.put()
    ->up_read(controls_rwsem)

Signed-off-by: Takashi Sakamoto <o-takashi@sakamocchi.jp>
Signed-off-by: Takashi Iwai <tiwai@suse.de>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tint result;', '\tdown_read(&card->controls_rwsem);', '\tif (kctl == NULL) {', '\t\tresult = -ENOENT;', '\t} else {', '\t\tindex_offset = snd_ctl_get_ioff(kctl, &control->id);', '\t\tvd = &kctl->vd[index_offset];', '\t\tif ((vd->access & SNDRV_CTL_ELEM_ACCESS_READ) &&', '\t\t    kctl->get != NULL) {', '\t\t\tsnd_ctl_build_ioff(&control->id, kctl, index_offset);', '\t\t\tresult = kctl->get(kctl, control);', '\t\t} else', '\t\t\tresult = -EPERM;', '\t}', '\tup_read(&card->controls_rwsem);', '\treturn result;'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (kctl == NULL)', '\t\treturn -ENOENT;', '', '\tindex_offset = snd_ctl_get_ioff(kctl, &control->id);', '\tvd = &kctl->vd[index_offset];', '\tif (!(vd->access & SNDRV_CTL_ELEM_ACCESS_READ) && kctl->get == NULL)', '\t\treturn -EPERM;', '', '\tsnd_ctl_build_ioff(&control->id, kctl, index_offset);', '\treturn kctl->get(kctl, control);']}
description: A use after free vulnerability exists in the ALSA PCM package in the Linux Kernel. SNDRV_CTL_IOCTL_ELEM_{READ|WRITE}32 is missing locks that can be used in a use-after-free that can result in a priviledge escalation to gain ring0 access from the system user. We recommend upgrading past commit 56b88b50565cd8b946a2d00b0c83927b7ebb055e

code_evidence: snd_ctl_elem_read acquires card->controls_rwsem at line 8, resolves kctl via snd_ctl_find_id at line 9, and dereferences kctl->vd and kctl->get (lines 14-18) before releasing the lock at line 22; the read lock only protects against concurrent writers, not against a control being freed by a concurrent removal path.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The core defect is dereferencing a kcontrol pointer after its backing memory may have been freed, which is exactly CWE-416. A related race-condition label would describe the synchronization flaw, but the supported consequence here is use of freed memory, so CWE-416 fits the target.

If another thread removes and frees that kcontrol concurrently, the pointer returned by snd_ctl_find_id and the vd/kctl->get dereferences operate on freed memory. Trigger: concurrent SNDRV_CTL_IOCTL_ELEM_READ with control removal. Consequence: use-after-free read or callback invocation on freed memory, potentially enabling memory corruption or privilege escalation.

read side between the "read header" coroutine and the I/O coroutine that

commit_msg:
When using the Hash Page Table (HPT) MMU, userspace memory mappings
are managed at two levels. Firstly in the Linux page tables, much like
other architectures, and secondly in the SLB (Segment Lookaside
Buffer) and HPT. It's the SLB and HPT that are actually used by the
hardware to do translations.

As part of the series adding support for 4PB user virtual address
space using the hash MMU, we added support for allocating multiple
"context ids" per process, one for each 512TB chunk of address space.
These are tracked in an array called extended_id in the mm_context_t
of a process that has done a mapping above 512TB.

If such a process forks (ie. clone(2) without CLONE_VM set) it's mm is
copied, including the mm_context_t, and then init_new_context() is
called to reinitialise parts of the mm_context_t as appropriate to
separate the address spaces of the two processes.

The key step in ensuring the two processes have separate address
spaces is to allocate a new context id for the process, this is done
at the beginning of hash__init_new_context(). If we didn't allocate a
new context id then the two processes would share mappings as far as
the SLB and HPT are concerned, even though their Linux page tables
would be separate.

For mappings above 512TB, which use the extended_id array, we
neglected to allocate new context ids on fork, meaning the parent and
child use the same ids and therefore share those mappings even though
they're supposed to be separate. This can lead to the parent seeing
writes done by the child, which is essentially memory corruption.

There is an additional exposure which is that if the child process
exits, all its context ids are freed, including the context ids that
are still in use by the parent for mappings above 512TB. One or more
of those ids can then be reallocated to a third process, that process
can then read/write to the parent's mappings above 512TB. Additionally
if the freed id is used for the third process's primary context id,
then the parent is able to read/write to the third process's mappings
*below* 512TB.

All of these are fundamental failures to enforce separation between
processes. The only mitigating factor is that the bug only occurs if a
process creates mappings above 512TB, and most applications still do
not create such mappings.

Only machines using the hash page table MMU are affected, eg. PowerPC
970 (G5), PA6T, Power5/6/7/8/9. By default Power9 bare metal machines
(powernv) use the Radix MMU and are not affected, unless the machine
has been explicitly booted in HPT mode (using disable_radix on the
kernel command line). KVM guests on Power9 may be affected if the host
or guest is configured to use the HPT MMU. LPARs under PowerVM on
Power9 are affected as they always use the HPT MMU. Kernels built with
PAGE_SIZE=4K are not affected.

The fix is relatively simple, we need to reallocate context ids for
all extended mappings on fork.

Fixes: f384796c40dc ("powerpc/mm: Add support for handling > 512TB address in SLB miss")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # v4.17+
Signed-off-by: Michael Ellerman <mpe@ellerman.id.au>

description: arch/powerpc/mm/mmu_context_book3s64.c in the Linux kernel before 5.1.15 for powerpc has a bug where unrelated processes may be able to read/write to one another's virtual memory under certain conditions via an mmap above 512 TB. Only a subset of powerpc systems are affected.

commit_msg:
gnttab: Avoid potential double-put of maptrack entry

Each grant mapping for a particular domain is tracked by an in-Xen
"maptrack" entry.  This entry is is referenced by a "handle", which is
given to the guest when it calls gnttab_map_grant_ref().

There are two types of mapping a particular handle can refer to:
GNTMAP_host_map and GNTMAP_device_map.  A given
gnttab_unmap_grant_ref() call can remove either only one or both of
these entries.  When a particular handle has no entries left, it must
be freed.

gnttab_unmap_grant_ref() loops through its grant unmap request list
twice.  It first removes entries from any host pagetables and (if
appropraite) iommus; then it does a single domain TLB flush; then it
does the clean-up, including telling the granter that entries are no
longer being used (if appropriate).

At the moment, it's during the first pass that the maptrack flags are
cleared, but the second pass that the maptrack entry is freed.

Unfortunately this allows the following race, which results in a
double-free:

 A: (pass 1) clear host_map
 B: (pass 1) clear device_map
 A: (pass 2) See that maptrack entry has no mappings, free it
 B: (pass 2) See that maptrack entry has no mappings, free it #

Unfortunately, unlike the active entry pinning update, we can't simply
move the maptrack flag changes to the second half, because the
maptrack flags are used to determine if iommu entries need to be
added: a domain's iommu must never have fewer permissions than the
maptrack flags indicate, or a subsequent map_grant_ref() might fail to
add the necessary iommu entries.

Instead, free the maptrack entry in the first pass if there are no
further mappings.

This is part of XSA-218.

Reported-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Signed-off-by: George Dunlap <george.dunlap@citrix.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    bool_t put_handle = 0;', '    act = active_entry_acquire(rgt, op->map->ref);', '    sha = shared_entry_header(rgt, op->map->ref);', '        status = &status_entry(rgt, op->map->ref);', '    if ( (op->map->flags & (GNTMAP_device_map|GNTMAP_host_map)) == 0 )', '        put_handle = 1;', '', '    if ( put_handle )', '    {', '        op->map->flags = 0;', '        put_maptrack_handle(ld->grant_table, op->handle);', '    }'], 'added_lines': ['    act = active_entry_acquire(rgt, op->ref);', '    sha = shared_entry_header(rgt, op->ref);', '        status = &status_entry(rgt, op->ref);']}
description: The grant-table feature in Xen through 4.8.x provides false mapping information in certain cases of concurrent unmap calls, which allows backend attackers to obtain sensitive information or gain privileges, aka XSA-218 bug 1.

code_evidence: The function decides to release the maptrack handle based on op->map->flags being cleared of both GNTMAP_device_map and GNTMAP_host_map, setting put_handle = 1. This check is performed in the first pass while the maptrack flags may already have been cleared by a concurrent unmap call.

After dropping the grant read lock at line 75, the function performs the deferred handle release: it clears op->map->flags and calls put_maptrack_handle(ld->grant_table, op->handle) at line 79. Because the decision and the release are separated, two concurrent unmap operations can both observe no mappings remaining and both invoke put_maptrack_handle on the same handle.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-415 (Double Free) fits because the same maptrack handle is passed to put_maptrack_handle twice due to the race between the flag check and deferred release. This is a direct double-release of a resource, not merely a use-after-free or race in isolation.

evidence_lines.code:
if ( (op->map->flags & (GNTMAP_device_map|GNTMAP_host_map)) == 0 )
put_handle = 1;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the maptrack entry is freed in a second phase after the grant lock is released, while the flags that determine whether it should be freed are cleared in the first phase. Trigger: two concurrent gnttab_unmap_grant_ref calls for the same handle each clear one mapping flag and then both observe no mappings left. Consequence: put_maptrack_handle is invoked twice for the same handle, a double free of the maptrack entry that can corrupt the maptrack table and potentially enable privilege escalation or information disclosure.

commit_msg: Check remaining space in the packetbuf before writing to it in input_l2cap_frame_flow_channel().
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    if(channel->rx_buffer.sdu_length > packetbuf_remaininglen()) {', '      LOG_WARN("l2cap_frame: illegal L2CAP frame sdu_length: %"PRIu16"\\n",', '               channel->rx_buffer.sdu_length);', '      return;', '    }', '']}
description: Contiki-NG is an open-source, cross-platform operating system for Next-Generation IoT devices. Versions prior to and including 4.8 are vulnerable to an out-of-bounds write that can occur in the BLE-L2CAP module. The Bluetooth Low Energy - Logical Link Control and Adaptation Layer Protocol (BLE-L2CAP) module handles fragmentation of packets up the configured MTU size. When fragments are reassembled, they are stored in a packet buffer of a configurable size, but there is no check to verify that the packet buffer is large enough to hold the reassembled packet. In Contiki-NG's default configuration, it is possible that an out-of-bounds write of up to 1152 bytes occurs. The vulnerability has been patched in the "develop" branch of Contiki-NG, and will be included in release 4.9. The problem can be fixed by applying the patch in Contiki-NG pull request #2254 prior to the release of version 4.9.

code_evidence: When the reassembly condition holds (sdu_length > 0 and sdu_length == current_index), line 32 copies sdu_length bytes from the reassembly buffer into packetbuf_dataptr() without checking that the packet buffer can hold sdu_length bytes.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing capacity check before memcpy into packetbuf directly permits writing past the end of the destination buffer, which is exactly CWE-787 (Out-of-bounds Write). It is not merely an out-of-bounds read or integer issue; the write itself exceeds the buffer bounds.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The reassembled SDU length is attacker-influenced and validated only against BLE_L2CAP_NODE_MTU (lines 13, 23), not against the actual packetbuf capacity. When a complete frame is reassembled, memcpy writes sdu_length bytes into packetbuf_dataptr(), overflowing the packet buffer; the consequence is memory corruption / out-of-bounds write of up to ~1152 bytes in default config.

commit_msg:
Problem: Compilation error due to comparison between signed and unsigned expressions

Solution: Cast the signed expression (which is always positive) to unsigned

Signed-off-by: Guido Vranken <guidovranken@gmail.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['                  || msg_size_ > allocator.data () + allocator.size () - read_pos_ )) {'], 'added_lines': ['                  || msg_size_ >', '                  (size_t)(allocator.data () + allocator.size () - read_pos_))) {']}
description: A pointer overflow, with code execution, was discovered in ZeroMQ libzmq (aka 0MQ) 4.2.x and 4.3.x before 4.3.1. A v2_decoder.cpp zmq::v2_decoder_t::size_ready integer overflow allows an authenticated attacker to overwrite an arbitrary amount of bytes beyond the bounds of a buffer, which can be leveraged to run arbitrary code on the target system. The memory layout allows the attacker to inject OS commands into a data structure located immediately after the problematic buffer (i.e., it is not necessary to use a typical buffer-overflow exploitation technique that changes the flow of control).

code_evidence: The zero-copy capacity check computes `allocator.data() + allocator.size() - read_pos_`, a pointer subtraction whose signed result is compared against the unsigned 64-bit `msg_size_` (line 17). If `read_pos_` lies outside the arena, the difference is negative and converts to a huge unsigned value, so the `msg_size_ > ...` test is false and the zero-copy branch is taken, initializing `_in_progress` over `read_pos_` with `msg_size_` bytes (lines 19-24).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The flawed size computation produces a wrapped/underflowed value that defeats the size check, matching CWE-190's integer wraparound used to determine an offset/size in memory handling. It is not merely a signedness mismatch: the wrapped result is what allows the out-of-bounds buffer operation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the remaining-buffer computation is done with pointer arithmetic/signed comparison, so a negative (underflowing) remaining size is reinterpreted as a large unsigned quantity. Trigger: a crafted v2 message whose size and read position make `allocator.data()+allocator.size()-read_pos_` negative. Consequence: the bounds check passes, `_in_progress.init` references an out-of-bounds region of length `msg_size_`, enabling writes beyond the arena buffer.

description: Contiki-NG is an open-source, cross-platform operating system for IoT devices. In affected versions it is possible to cause a buffer overflow when copying an IPv6 address prefix in the RPL-Classic implementation in Contiki-NG. In order to trigger the vulnerability, the Contiki-NG system must have joined an RPL DODAG. After that, an attacker can send a DAO packet with a Target option that contains a prefix length larger than 128 bits. The problem was fixed after the release of Contiki-NG 4.7. commit_msg:
make the dump directories owned by root by default

It was discovered that the abrt event scripts create a user-readable
copy of a sosreport file in abrt problem directories, and include
excerpts of /var/log/messages selected by the user-controlled process
name, leading to an information disclosure.

This issue was discovered by Florian Weimer of Red Hat Product Security.

Related: #1212868

Signed-off-by: Jakub Filak <jfilak@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ["    /* use fsuid instead of uid, so we don't expose any sensitive", '     * information of suided app in /var/tmp/abrt', '    dd = dd_create_skeleton(path, fsuid, DEFAULT_DUMP_DIR_MODE, /*no flags*/0);'], 'added_lines': ['', '    /* If PrivateReports is on, root owns all problem directories */', '    const uid_t dduid = g_settings_privatereports ? 0 : fsuid;', "    /* use dduid (either fsuid or 0) instead of uid, so we don't expose any", '     * sensitive information of suided app in /var/tmp/abrt', '    dd = dd_create_skeleton(path, dduid, DEFAULT_DUMP_DIR_MODE, /*no flags*/0);', "        /* This function uses fsuid only for its value. The function stores fsuid in a file name 'uid'*/"]}
description: The event scripts in Automatic Bug Reporting Tool (ABRT) uses world-readable permission on a copy of sosreport file in problem directories, which allows local users to obtain sensitive information from /var/log/messages via unspecified vectors.

code_evidence: The dump directory ownership is derived from fsuid, which equals the supplied uid unless the process is setuid (fsuid=0) or an unsafe suid policy applies (fsuid=tmp_fsuid).
dd_create_skeleton(path, fsuid, DEFAULT_DUMP_DIR_MODE, 0) creates the problem directory owned by that fsuid, and dd_create_basic_files copies files using the same fsuid.
dd_reset_ownership(dd) and dd_close(dd) finalize the directory; the fix gates this ownership on g_settings_privatereports to force root (dduid=0).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function manages resources (problem directories and copied diagnostic files) that contain sensitive information but makes them accessible to an unauthorized user through ownership/permission choices. This directly matches CWE-200's scope of confidential information exposure; the underlying permission weakness is the mechanism, and the supported consequence is information disclosure.

evidence_lines.code:
dd_reset_ownership(dd);
dd_close(dd);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the crash-dump directory and its contents are created with the crashing user's fsuid, so when PrivateReports is not enforced the problem directory is owned by a non-root user. That user can read the copied diagnostic files, including the sosreport copy and log excerpts, exposing sensitive information to an unauthorized local actor.

description: Heap-based buffer overflow in the Fp_toString function in jsfunction.c in Artifex Software MuJS allows attackers to cause a denial of service (crash) via crafted input.

code_evidence: Lines 10-13 compute n as the sum of the literal length, F->name length, and each parameter name plus 1 separator, but never include the terminating zero byte; line 14 allocates exactly n bytes.
Lines 15-22 then use strcpy/strcat to write the literal, name, '(', comma-separated parameters and ') { ... }' into that n-byte buffer, requiring n+1 bytes.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function allocates a buffer and then writes past its end, which is an out-of-bounds memory-buffer operation matching CWE-119; the underlying off-by-one size error is the root cause producing the boundary violation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the size computation omits the string terminator while the allocation uses that size. Trigger: calling Fp_toString on a callable function builds and copies the full signature string. Consequence: the final strcat writes the terminating zero one byte past the allocated heap buffer, corrupting heap metadata and enabling crash/DoS as described.

commit_msg:
atl2: Disable unimplemented scatter/gather feature

atl2 includes NETIF_F_SG in hw_features even though it has no support
for non-linear skbs.  This bug was originally harmless since the
driver does not claim to implement checksum offload and that used to
be a requirement for SG.

Now that SG and checksum offload are independent features, if you
explicitly enable SG *and* use one of the rare protocols that can use
SG without checkusm offload, this potentially leaks sensitive
information (before you notice that it just isn't working).  Therefore
this obscure bug has been designated CVE-2016-2117.

Reported-by: Justin Yackoski <jyackoski@crypto-nite.com>
Signed-off-by: Ben Hutchings <ben@decadent.org.uk>
Fixes: ec5f06156423 ("net: Kill link between CSUM and SG features.")
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tnetdev->hw_features = NETIF_F_SG | NETIF_F_HW_VLAN_CTAG_RX;'], 'added_lines': ['\tnetdev->hw_features = NETIF_F_HW_VLAN_CTAG_RX;']}
description: The atl2_probe function in drivers/net/ethernet/atheros/atlx/atl2.c in the Linux kernel through 4.5.2 incorrectly enables scatter/gather I/O, which allows remote attackers to obtain sensitive information from kernel memory by reading packet data.

code_evidence: Line 53 advertises NETIF_F_SG in netdev->hw_features, declaring scatter/gather support even though the atl2 driver cannot handle non-linear skbs; line 54 only adds VLAN features to netdev->features, leaving SG exposed as a negotiable capability.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The misadvertised SG capability leads to unintended disclosure of kernel memory contents to a remote party, matching CWE-200's confidentiality impact. The root error is a hardware-feature misadvertisement whose resultant effect is information exposure, as described in the commit and description.

evidence_lines.code:
netdev->hw_features = NETIF_F_SG | NETIF_F_HW_VLAN_CTAG_RX;
netdev->features |= (NETIF_F_HW_VLAN_CTAG_TX | NETIF_F_HW_VLAN_CTAG_RX);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the driver advertises SG offload it does not implement. Trigger: a user explicitly enables SG and a protocol uses SG without checksum offload, causing the device to transmit/receive non-linear skbs incorrectly. Supported consequence: kernel memory beyond the intended packet payload is exposed in packet data, leaking sensitive information to a remote actor.

commit_msg:
Avoid integer overflows in SETRANGE and SORT (CVE-2022-35977) (#11720)

Authenticated users issuing specially crafted SETRANGE and SORT(_RO)
commands can trigger an integer overflow, resulting with Redis attempting
to allocate impossible amounts of memory and abort with an OOM panic.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        totlen = stringObjectLen(o)+sdslen(append->ptr);', '        if (checkStringLength(c,totlen) != C_OK)'], 'added_lines': ['        if (checkStringLength(c,stringObjectLen(o),sdslen(append->ptr)) != C_OK)']}
description: Redis is an in-memory database that persists on disk. Authenticated users issuing specially crafted `SETRANGE` and `SORT(_RO)` commands can trigger an integer overflow, resulting with Redis attempting to allocate impossible amounts of memory and abort with an out-of-memory (OOM) panic. The problem is fixed in Redis versions 7.0.8, 6.2.9 and 6.0.17. Users are advised to upgrade. There are no known workarounds for this vulnerability.

code_evidence: Line 14 computes totlen as stringObjectLen(o) plus sdslen(append->ptr) in a size_t without any pre-add bound check, so the sum can wrap to a small value. Line 15 then passes the already-wrapped totlen to checkStringLength, which validates the wrong (small) length instead of the true combined size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe addition of two attacker-influenced lengths in size_t is exactly an integer overflow/wraparound (CWE-190), and the wrapped result defeats the subsequent size check. Contrast with CWE-400: resource exhaustion here is the consequence of the arithmetic wraparound, not a missing rate/amount limit.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the two lengths are added into size_t before any limit is enforced, so a large existing string plus a large appended value wraps around. Trigger: APPEND on an existing string with crafted sizes. Consequence: the length check passes on the wrapped value, allowing sdscatlen to attempt an impossible allocation, causing OOM panic/DoS.

commit_msg:
lib: limit size of vty buffer to 4096 bytes

This removes the automatic resizing of the vty input buffer and places a
hard size cap of 4096 bytes. It also fixes a potentially unsafe strcpy.

Signed-off-by: Quentin Young <qlyoung@cumulusnetworks.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  vty_ensure (vty, vty->length + 1);'], 'added_lines': ['  if (vty->length + 1 > VTY_BUFSIZ)', '    return;', '']}
description: All versions of Quagga, 0.93 through 1.1.0, are vulnerable to an unbounded memory allocation in the telnet 'vty' CLI, leading to a Denial-of-Service of Quagga daemons, or even the entire host. When Quagga daemons are configured with their telnet CLI enabled, anyone who can connect to the TCP ports can trigger this vulnerability, prior to authentication. Most distributions restrict the Quagga telnet interface to local access only by default. The Quagga telnet interface 'vty' input buffer grows automatically, without bound, so long as a newline is not entered. This allows an attacker to cause the Quagga daemon to allocate unbounded memory by sending very long strings without a newline. Eventually the daemon is terminated by the system, or the system itself runs out of memory. This is fixed in Quagga 1.1.1 and Free Range Routing (FRR) Protocol Suite 2017-01-10.

code_evidence: vty_ensure(vty, vty->length + 1) grows the buffer to hold one more byte without any upper bound; length is then computed from vty->cp and memmove shifts length bytes to vty->buf[vty->cp + 1], writing at index vty->length.
vty->length++ advances the write position on every self-insert, so repeated calls without a newline keep extending the buffer and the shifted region.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes into vty->buf at the moving index vty->length while relying on an unbounded ensure, so operations can exceed the intended buffer boundary, matching CWE-119. The allocation growth is the enabling cause; the out-of-bounds buffer write is the supported weakness, not merely resource consumption.

evidence_lines.code: vty->length++;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the buffer is resized to vty->length + 1 each call with no maximum, and the memmove target index vty->length assumes that capacity. Trigger: an unauthenticated vty client sends a long line without a newline, repeatedly invoking vty_self_insert. Consequence: unbounded allocation and out-of-bounds writes past the intended buffer, causing memory exhaustion/DoS and possible memory corruption.

description: FreeRDP prior to version 2.0.0-rc4 contains several Out-Of-Bounds Reads in the NTLM Authentication module that results in a Denial of Service (segfault).

code_evidence: Line 3 checks only that 8 bytes remain before the reads, and lines 5-7 then consume exactly 8 bytes (two UINT16 plus one UINT32), so this fragment's own reads stay within the checked length. The function stores the attacker-controlled Len, MaxLen, and BufferOffset values from the stream into fields without validating them against the actual remaining buffer size; those unchecked values are returned to callers via the fields structure.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the unchecked attacker-controlled length/offset fields enable reads beyond the intended buffer when consumed by callers, matching out-of-bounds read with DoS impact. It is not merely an integer overflow or improper input validation; the supported consequence is out-of-bounds memory read.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function parses NTLM message fields and accepts arbitrary Len/MaxLen/BufferOffset values without constraining them to the stream's available data. A caller using these unvalidated lengths/offsets to read payload data can then read past the buffer, causing an out-of-bounds read and a crash (DoS). The defect is the missing validation of parsed field values, not the eight-byte header read itself.

description: In Wireshark 2.4.0 to 2.4.4 and 2.2.0 to 2.2.12, epan/dissectors/packet-wccp.c had a large loop that was addressed by ensuring that a calculated length was monotonically increasing.

description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. An attacker can cause a denial of service by exploiting a `CHECK`-failure coming from the implementation of `tf.raw_ops.RFFT`. Eigen code operating on an empty matrix can trigger on an assertion and will cause program termination. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.5.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.4.2, TensorFlow 2.3.3, TensorFlow 2.2.3 and TensorFlow 2.1.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: The loop builds temp_shape from attacker-influenced fft_shape values without checking that any dimension is nonzero, so temp_shape can have zero elements.
The zero-element temp_shape is passed to allocate_temp and then used for full_fft and the Eigen fft operation, where the Eigen assertion on an empty matrix can fire and terminate the process.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function lets attacker-controlled shape input reach an Eigen assertion that terminates the program, matching CWE-617's reachable assertion leading to DoS. It is not a memory-safety bug like CWE-787; the supported impact is a crash from the assertion, not memory corruption.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: a zero-element FFT shape derived from fft_shape is accepted and used to allocate and operate on an empty Eigen tensor. Trigger: a request supplying a zero dimension in the RFFT shape reaches the Eigen fft call. Consequence: a reachable Eigen assertion aborts the process, causing denial of service.

code_evidence: The loop iterates i from 0 to item_count-1 over attacker-controlled item_count read from the packet (line 17). commit_msg:
Commit a23740ec43ba ("bpf: Track contents of read-only maps as scalars") is
checking whether maps are read-only both from BPF program side and user space
side, and then, given their content is constant, reading out their data via
map->ops->map_direct_value_addr() which is then subsequently used as known
scalar value for the register, that is, it is marked as __mark_reg_known()
with the read value at verification time. Before a23740ec43ba, the register
content was marked as an unknown scalar so the verifier could not make any
assumptions about the map content.

The current implementation however is prone to a TOCTOU race, meaning, the
value read as known scalar for the register is not guaranteed to be exactly
the same at a later point when the program is executed, and as such, the
prior made assumptions of the verifier with regards to the program will be
invalid which can cause issues such as OOB access, etc.

While the BPF_F_RDONLY_PROG map flag is always fixed and required to be
specified at map creation time, the map->frozen property is initially set to
false for the map given the map value needs to be populated, e.g. for global
data sections. Once complete, the loader "freezes" the map from user space
such that no subsequent updates/deletes are possible anymore. For the rest
of the lifetime of the map, this freeze one-time trigger cannot be undone
anymore after a successful BPF_MAP_FREEZE cmd return. Meaning, any new BPF_*
cmd calls which would update/delete map entries will be rejected with -EPERM
since map_get_sys_perms() removes the FMODE_CAN_WRITE permission. This also
means that pending update/delete map entries must still complete before this
guarantee is given. This corner case is not an issue for loaders since they
create and prepare such program private map in successive steps.

However, a malicious user is able to trigger this TOCTOU race in two different
ways: i) via userfaultfd, and ii) via batched updates. For i) userfaultfd is
used to expand the competition interval, so that map_update_elem() can modify
the contents of the map after map_freeze() and bpf_prog_load() were executed.
This works, because userfaultfd halts the parallel thread which triggered a
map_update_elem() at the time where we copy key/value from the user buffer and
this already passed the FMODE_CAN_WRITE capability test given at that time the
map was not "frozen". Then, the main thread performs the map_freeze() and
bpf_prog_load(), and once that had completed successfully, the other thread
is woken up to complete the pending map_update_elem() which then changes the
map content. For ii) the idea of the batched update is similar, meaning, when
there are a large number of updates to be processed, it can increase the
competition interval between the two. It is therefore possible in practice to
modify the contents of the map after executing map_freeze() and bpf_prog_load().

One way to fix both i) and ii) at the same time is to expand the use of the
map's map->writecnt. The latter was introduced in fc9702273e2e ("bpf: Add mmap()
support for BPF_MAP_TYPE_ARRAY") and further refined in 1f6cb19be2e2 ("bpf:
Prevent re-mmap()'ing BPF map as writable for initially r/o mapping") with
the rationale to make a writable mmap()'ing of a map mutually exclusive with
read-only freezing. The counter indicates writable mmap() mappings and then
prevents/fails the freeze operation. Its semantics can be expanded beyond
just mmap() by generally indicating ongoing write phases. This would essentially
span any parallel regular and batched flavor of update/delete operation and
then also have map_freeze() fail with -EBUSY. For the check_mem_access() in
the verifier we expand upon the bpf_map_is_rdonly() check ensuring that all
last pending writes have completed via bpf_map_write_active() test. Once the
map->frozen is set and bpf_map_write_active() indicates a map->writecnt of 0
only then we are really guaranteed to use the map's data as known constants.
For map->frozen being set and pending writes in process of still being completed
we fall back to marking that register as unknown scalar so we don't end up
making assumptions about it. With this, both TOCTOU reproducers from i) and
ii) are fixed.

Note that the map->writecnt has been converted into a atomic64 in the fix in
order to avoid a double freeze_mutex mutex_{un,}lock() pair when updating
map->writecnt in the various map update/delete BPF_* cmd flavors. Spanning
the freeze_mutex over entire map update/delete operations in syscall side
would not be possible due to then causing everything to be serialized.
Similarly, something like synchronize_rcu() after setting map->frozen to wait
for update/deletes to complete is not possible either since it would also
have to span the user copy which can sleep. On the libbpf side, this won't
break d66562fba1ce ("libbpf: Add BPF object skeleton support") as the
anonymous mmap()-ed "map initialization image" is remapped as a BPF map-backed
mmap()-ed memory where for .rodata it's non-writable.

Fixes: a23740ec43ba ("bpf: Track contents of read-only maps as scalars")
Reported-by: w1tcher.bupt@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>
Acked-by: Andrii Nakryiko <andrii@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['', '\tif (map->writecnt) {'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (bpf_map_write_active(map)) {']}
description: A race condition was found in the Linux kernel's ebpf verifier between bpf_map_update_elem and bpf_map_freeze due to a missing lock in kernel/bpf/syscall.c. In this flaw, a local user with a special privilege (cap_sys_admin or cap_bpf) can modify the frozen mapped address space. This flaw affects kernel versions prior to 5.16 rc2.

code_evidence: map_freeze() takes map->freeze_mutex and checks map->writecnt (line 18) before setting map->frozen (line 30). In the pre-fix code this is a plain, unsynchronized read of a counter that concurrent map_update_elem/map_delete_elem paths increment/decrement outside freeze_mutex. The check at line 18 therefore does not guarantee that no write is in flight: a write can pass its permission check, then freeze observes writecnt==0, sets frozen, and the pending write completes afterward, mutating the supposedly immutable map.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function checks map state (writecnt) before committing the frozen flag, but the state can change between check and use, exactly the TOCTOU pattern of CWE-367. The fix replaces the raw check with bpf_map_write_active() using atomic64 semantics to close the race.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the freeze decision reads map->writecnt without atomicity or a shared lock with writers, so the 'no active writes' check can be stale. Trigger: concurrent map_update_elem (userfaultfd or batched updates) overlapping map_freeze. Consequence: map contents change after freeze/verifier load, invalidating verifier assumptions and enabling OOB access.

PJSIP versions 2.12 and prior do not parse incoming RTCP feedback RPSI (Reference Picture Selection Indication) packet, but any app that directly uses pjmedia_rtcp_fb_parse_rpsi() will be affected. A patch is available in the `master` branch of the `pjsip/pjproject` GitHub repository. There are currently no known workarounds.

code_evidence: The header is cast as pjmedia_rtcp_common and the minimum length check only covers sizeof(pjmedia_rtcp_common), but length is later read from the header to derive cnt and drive the loop.

cnt is derived from the packet's length field; the (cnt+3)*4 check uses cnt, and *sli_cnt is clamped, but p starts at sizeof(*hdr) and each iteration writes four bytes to sli[i]. The loop bound depends on packet data rather than the caller's sli array capacity.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Writing beyond the bounds of the caller's sli buffer is an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). It differs from an out-of-bounds read because the loop stores parsed fields into sli[i], modifying memory past the intended buffer.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function trusts the RTCP length field to compute cnt and writes cnt entries into the caller-provided sli array, whose capacity is not validated. Trigger: a crafted RTCP FB SLI packet with an inflated length field causes the loop to write past the end of sli, corrupting adjacent memory.

description: A flaw was found in htmldoc in v1.9.12 and before. Null pointer dereference in file_extension(),in file.c may lead to execute arbitrary code and denial of service.

code_evidence: Line 26 guards against a missing '#' with strchr(extension,'#')==NULL and returns early. Line 28 copies extension into the static buf via strlcpy, which truncates to 1023 chars plus NUL. Line 29 then calls strchr(buf,'#') and immediately dereferences the result without checking for NULL. Because truncation can drop the '#' that was present in extension, strchr(buf,'#') can return NULL, and the assignment writes through a NULL pointer.

A related out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) does not apply because strlcpy bounds the copy; the flaw is the unchecked NULL from strchr after truncation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the '#' presence check is performed on extension (line 26) but the dereference is performed on the truncated copy buf (line 29), so truncation can remove the '#'. Trigger: a long URI/filename whose '#' lies beyond the 1023-byte buffer limit. Consequence: NULL pointer dereference, crashing the process (DoS); the description also claims possible code execution, but only the crash is directly supported here.
