diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ["    if (end - s < 4 || s[3] != ' ') return -1;"], 'added_lines': ["    if (end - s < 4 || isspace(s[0]) || s[3] != ' ') return -1;"]}
description: mq_parse_http in mongoose.c in Mongoose 6.15 has a heap-based buffer over-read.

code_evidence: mg_skip returns a pointer s into the response buffer after skipping the protocol token; the guard only checks end - s < 4 and s[3] != ' ', then atoi(s) reads the code digits. The added isspace(s[0]) check confirms the parser must reject a leading space before the status code. When s[0] is a space (e.g. the skip leaves a space before the code), atoi(s) begins reading at that space and scans forward past the 4-byte window toward the buffer end without any bound tied to end.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe operation is a read past the end of the buffer via atoi on an insufficiently validated pointer, matching CWE-125 (Out-of-bounds Read). It is not a write (CWE-787) because only reading occurs; the missing constraint is that the parsed numeric field must be bounded by end before atoi is invoked.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: atoi is applied to s after a length check that only guarantees four bytes remain, not that the numeric field is terminated within the buffer. Trigger: a malformed response where the status-code region begins with a space or non-digit sequence near the buffer end. Consequence: atoi reads past the intended buffer (heap over-read), which the fix prevents by rejecting a leading space before calling atoi.

description: A Denial of Service condition in Motion-Project Motion 3.2 through 4.3.1 allows remote unauthenticated users to cause a webu.c segmentation fault and kill the main process via a crafted HTTP request.

code_evidence: parm_len is computed as en_pos - st_pos + 1 (or strlen when no slash) and checked against WEBUI_LEN_PARM before snprintf into uri_camid.

joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the unsafe length handling in snprintf causes reads past the end of the source/destination buffers during URL parsing, matching out-of-bounds read. It is not merely CWE-120 buffer overflow since the demonstrated consequence is an over-read leading to segmentation fault.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The code derives parm_len from pointer offsets into webui->url and passes it as the size argument to snprintf, which writes parm_len bytes. The size checks compare parm_len to WEBUI_LEN_PARM but do not ensure parm_len fits the destination buffer semantics; a crafted URL with long segments can drive snprintf to read/copy beyond the intended uri_cmd buffers, leading to out-of-bounds memory access and process crash (DoS).

commit_msg: Fix incorrect value reading in JIT.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if (*cc == PT_CLIST && *cc == XCL_PROP)'], 'added_lines': ['    if (*cc == PT_CLIST && cc[-1] == XCL_PROP)']}
description: An out-of-bounds read vulnerability was discovered in the PCRE2 library in the compile_xclass_matchingpath() function of the pcre2_jit_compile.c file. This involves a unicode property matching issue in JIT-compiled regular expressions. The issue occurs because the character was not fully read in case-less matching within JIT.

code_evidence: After asserting the class item is a property, cc is advanced past the XCL_PROP/XCL_NOTPROP marker at line 55.

The condition at line 56 compares *cc (the property type) against both PT_CLIST and XCL_PROP, so the XCL_PROP check can never be true for the same value; the caseless-set branch is therefore effectively dead, and the following block reads PRIV(ucd_caseless_sets) + cc[1] only if it were reached.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The root cause is an incorrect pointer dereference in the property-type test, which yields an out-of-bounds read of Unicode data during JIT compilation, matching CWE-125. It is not an out-of-bounds write and not merely a logic error, since the supported consequence is reading memory beyond the intended buffer.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The property marker was checked against the wrong pointer: *cc holds the property type, while the marker lives at cc[-1]. The fixed code uses cc[-1] == XCL_PROP. With the buggy comparison the caseless-set bounds (min/max) are not computed and the else branch sets max=READ_CHAR_MAX, min=0; the char is not fully constrained for case-less matching, allowing later processing to read past the intended buffer. Trigger: a JIT-compiled regex with a caseless-set property class.

commit_msg:
http_client: Add missing certificate hostname verification

Before this commit it was possible to have osquery accept
a valid certificate with a wrong hostname.
The commit fixes this adding the hostname verification.

Moreover:

- Regenerate test CA, server certificates and keys, so that
  the CA key is available, to be able to sign other test certs.
- Add a regression test for the hostname verification bug.

Co-Authored-By: Alessandro Gario <alessandro.gario@gmail.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['                             client_options_.remote_hostname_->c_str());'], 'added_lines': ['  const auto remote_hostname = *client_options_.remote_hostname_;', '', '  bool verify_hostname = false;', '    verify_hostname = true;', '    verify_hostname = true;', '    verify_hostname = true;', '                             remote_hostname.c_str());', '', '  if (verify_hostname) {', '    ssl_sock_->set_verify_callback(', '        boost::asio::ssl::rfc2818_verification(remote_hostname));', '  }']}
description: Incorrect validation of the TLS SNI hostname in osquery versions after 2.9.0 and before 4.2.0 could allow an attacker to MITM osquery traffic in the absence of a configured root chain of trust.

code_evidence: Verification mode is chosen from options: verify_peer only when always_verify_peer_ is set, otherwise verify_none; no hostname check is registered here.
Loading a server certificate enables peer verification of the chain, but nothing binds the certificate to the expected host.
Adding a verify path likewise only enables chain verification, not identity verification.
The TLS SNI hostname is set on the socket, but no verification callback such as rfc2818_verification is installed, so the peer certificate is never compared against remote_hostname_.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-295 covers failing to validate a certificate's relevant components; here hostname identity is a required component that is left unchecked even when peer verification is enabled. This is distinct from weak chain validation because the trust path may be valid while the name binding is missing.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The root cause is that the handshake validates at most the certificate chain and never checks the certificate's identity against the intended remote hostname; setting SNI merely announces the name. An attacker positioned to intercept traffic can present a certificate that chains to a trusted root for a different name, and the handshake succeeds, enabling MITM.

commit_msg:
bluetooth: eliminate the potential race condition when removing the HCI controller

There is a possible race condition vulnerability between issuing a HCI
command and removing the cont.  Specifically, functions hci_req_sync()
and hci_dev_do_close() can race each other like below:

thread-A in hci_req_sync()      |   thread-B in hci_dev_do_close()
                                |   hci_req_sync_lock(hdev);
test_bit(HCI_UP, &hdev->flags); |
...                             |   test_and_clear_bit(HCI_UP, &hdev->flags)
hci_req_sync_lock(hdev);        |
                                |
In this commit we alter the sequence in function hci_req_sync(). Hence,
the thread-A cannot issue th.

Signed-off-by: Lin Ma <linma@zju.edu.cn>
Cc: Marcel Holtmann <marcel@holtmann.org>
Fixes: 7c6a329e4447 ("[Bluetooth] Fix regression from using default link policy")
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (!test_bit(HCI_UP, &hdev->flags))', '\t\treturn -ENETDOWN;', '', '\tret = __hci_req_sync(hdev, req, opt, timeout, hci_status);'], 'added_lines': ['\t/* check the state after obtaing the lock to protect the HCI_UP', '\t * against any races from hci_dev_do_close when the controller', '\t * gets removed.', '\t */', '\tif (test_bit(HCI_UP, &hdev->flags))', '\t\tret = __hci_req_sync(hdev, req, opt, timeout, hci_status);', '\telse', '\t\tret = -ENETDOWN;']}
description: net/bluetooth/hci_request.c in the Linux kernel through 5.12.2 has a race condition for removal of the HCI controller.

code_evidence: The HCI_UP state check at lines 6-7 occurs before hci_req_sync_lock(hdev) at line 8, while the subsequent __hci_req_sync call at line 9 uses the device after the lock is acquired. This leaves a window where hci_dev_do_close can clear HCI_UP between the test and the lock.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function contains a concurrent code sequence whose exclusive access to shared hdev state is not protected across the check and use, matching CWE-362's race condition between hci_req_sync and hci_dev_do_close. It is not a mere missing return check, since the flaw is the timing window relative to the lock.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the shared hdev->flags state is tested outside the hci_req_sync_lock critical section, so the check and use are not atomic. Trigger: a concurrent hci_dev_do_close clears HCI_UP after the test but before the lock is taken. Consequence: __hci_req_sync proceeds on a controller being removed, causing unsafe concurrent access and potential instability or crash.

commit_msg: Bug 698064: bounds check xps_encode/decode_font_char_imp
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            for (i2 = 0; i2 < segCount2 - 3; i2 += 2)', '                    return 0;', '                glyph = u16(idRangeOffset + i2 + roff + ((code - start) << 1));'], 'added_lines': ['            byte *giddata;', '            if (segCount2 < 3 || segCount2 > 65535 ||', '               idRangeOffset > font->data + font->length)', '               return gs_error_invalidfont;', '', '           for (i2 = 0; i2 < segCount2 - 3; i2 += 2)', '                if ((giddata = (idRangeOffset + i2 + roff + ((code - start) << 1))) >', '                    font->data + font->length) {', '                    return code;', '                }', '                glyph = u16(giddata);']}
description: The xps_decode_font_char_imp function in xps/xpsfont.c in Artifex Ghostscript GhostXPS 9.21 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (heap-based buffer over-read and application crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted document.

code_evidence: segCount2 is read from the font table at line 14 and used to compute endCount/startCount/idDelta/idRangeOffset pointers (15-18) and to bound the loop (20) without validating it against the actual table length.

Inside the loop, roff is read from idRangeOffset+i2 (30); when roff != 0 the lookup address idRangeOffset + i2 + roff + ((code-start)<<1) is dereferenced via u16 at line 36 with no check that it stays within font->data..font->data+font->length.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe operation is a read (u16) at a computed pointer that can exceed font->data + font->length, matching CWE-125 (out-of-bounds read). The patch's added checks confirm the missing constraint; this is a read overrun, not a write, so it fits CWE-125 rather than an out-of-bounds write weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The root cause is missing bounds validation of table offsets derived from attacker-controlled font data. A crafted cmap format-4 table with large segCount2 or roff causes the computed glyph address to point past the buffer, and u16 dereferences it, producing a heap-based out-of-bounds read that can crash the application.

commit_msg:
[folly] Add additional overflow checks to IOBuf - CVE-2021-24036

Summary:
As per title

CVE-2021-24036

Reviewed By: jan

Differential Revision: D27938605

fbshipit-source-id: 7481c54ae6fbb7b67b15b3631d5357c2f7043f9c
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  if (minCapacity > kMaxIOBufSize) {', '    throw_exception<std::bad_alloc>();', '  }', '']}
description: Passing an attacker controlled size when creating an IOBuf could cause integer overflow, leading to an out of bounds write on the heap with the possibility of remote code execution. This issue affects versions of folly prior to v2021.07.22.00. This issue affects HHVM versions prior to 4.80.5, all versions between 4.81.0 and 4.102.1, all versions between 4.103.0 and 4.113.0, and versions 4.114.0, 4.115.0, 4.116.0, 4.117.0, 4.118.0 and 4.118.1.

code_evidence: minCapacity is attacker-influenced and passed to goodExtBufferSize(minCapacity), whose result becomes mallocSize; the return value is used directly as the allocation size in checkedMalloc(mallocSize). The function itself contains no upper-bound check on minCapacity before this size computation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is integer overflow in a size computation that feeds memory allocation, matching CWE-190's note that it is security critical when determining allocation size. It is distinct from a plain allocation failure; the flaw is the wraparound in the size calculation.

evidence_lines.code:
size_t mallocSize = goodExtBufferSize(minCapacity);
auto buf = static_cast<uint8_t*>(checkedMalloc(mallocSize));

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the size arithmetic in goodExtBufferSize can overflow for a very large minCapacity, yielding a small mallocSize. Trigger: caller-supplied large capacity. Supported consequence: an undersized heap allocation relative to the intended capacity, enabling out-of-bounds writes when data is later stored.

commit_msg:
esp: Fix possible buffer overflow in ESP transformation

The maximum message size that can be send is bigger than
the  maximum site that skb_page_frag_refill can allocate.
So it is possible to write beyond the allocated buffer.

Fix this by doing a fallback to COW in that case.

v2:

Avoid get get_order() costs as suggested by Linus Torvalds.

Fixes: cac2661c53f3 ("esp4: Avoid skb_cow_data whenever possible")
Fixes: 03e2a30f6a27 ("esp6: Avoid skb_cow_data whenever possible")
Reported-by: valis <sec@valis.email>
Signed-off-by: Steffen Klassert <steffen.klassert@secunet.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tunsigned int allocsz;', '', '\tallocsz = ALIGN(skb->data_len + tailen, L1_CACHE_BYTES);', '\tif (allocsz > ESP_SKB_FRAG_MAXSIZE)', '\t\tgoto cow;']}
description: A heap buffer overflow flaw was found in IPsec ESP transformation code in net/ipv4/esp4.c and net/ipv6/esp6.c. This flaw allows a local attacker with a normal user privilege to overwrite kernel heap objects and may cause a local privilege escalation threat.

code_evidence: allocsize is computed only from tailen, not from skb->data_len plus tailen, so skb_page_frag_refill reserves a page fragment sized for the trailer alone. tail is then set to page_address(page)+pfrag->offset, and esp_output_fill_trailer writes tailen bytes there; the page descriptor is filled with length tailen and pfrag->offset advances by allocsize. When skb->data_len is large, the actual write range exceeds the refilled fragment and the allocated page.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes trailer bytes beyond the end of the buffer obtained from skb_page_frag_refill, which is a direct out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). The issue is an incorrect allocation-size calculation leading to a write past the intended buffer, not merely a read overflow or use-after-free.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the allocation size omits skb->data_len, while the subsequent trailer fill and page-descriptor length use tailen. Trigger: a large skb->data_len combined with a tailen that skb_page_frag_refill satisfies for allocsize only. Consequence: esp_output_fill_trailer writes past the page-fragment allocation, corrupting adjacent heap memory; the patch's allocsz check and fallback to cow prevent this path.

commit_msg:
Fix segmentation fault when closing an element

Reported in issue #19. The error happened when the node passed to elm_close
wasn't an element as it was supposed to.

In the example files reported with the issue, the node causing the crash
was a comment.

Now, elm_close will exit with an error if the node it receives isn't
an element. Some calls that could potentially call it with something else
check the node type before calling it.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '  if (nodo->tipo != Node_element) {', '    EXIT("Trying to close a non-element node");', '    return;', '  }', '']}
description: html2xhtml v1.3 was discovered to contain an Out-Of-Bounds read in the function static void elm_close(tree_node_t *nodo) at procesador.c. This vulnerability allows attackers to access sensitive files or cause a Denial of Service (DoS) via a crafted html file.

code_evidence: elm_close takes a tree_node_t* nodo and immediately dereferences it via ELM_PTR(nodo).name without verifying nodo->tipo is Node_element; the patch adds that type guard.
It then reads nodo->cont.elemento.hijo and iterates the sibling chain with elm=elm->sig, indexing ELM_ID(elm) into content[num++], all under the assumption the node is a properly formed element.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe operation is reading memory through an element-typed view of a node that may not be an element, past the intended structure boundary, which matches CWE-125 Out-of-bounds Read. It is not merely a null dereference; the missing type constraint causes reads beyond the valid object.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: elm_close assumes its argument is an element and accesses element-specific union fields (cont.elemento, contentspec) without a type check. Trigger: a comment or other non-element node passed to elm_close, as reported in issue #19. Consequence: the mismatched union interpretation yields an out-of-bounds read/memory access leading to crash (DoS) or disclosure.

description: An issue was discovered in cpp-peglib through v0.1.12. A NULL pointer dereference exists in the peg::AstOptimizer::optimize() located in peglib.h. It allows an attacker to cause Denial of Service.

code_evidence: g["Grammar"].parse() stores its result in r; when r.ret is false the function logs and returns nullptr at line 17, so parsing failure is handled. description: IIPImage High Resolution Streaming Image Server prior to commit 882925b295a80ec992063deffc2a3b0d803c3195 is affected by an integer overflow in iipsrv.fcgi through malformed HTTP query parameters.

description: hso_free_net_device in drivers/net/usb/hso.c in the Linux kernel through 5.13.4 calls unregister_netdev without checking for the NETREG_REGISTERED state, leading to a use-after-free and a double free.

code_evidence: When alloc_netdev fails at line 13, control jumps to the shared exit label at line 15 before net is allocated.
After register_netdev fails at line 52, the code also jumps to the same exit label at line 54, even though the device was added and registration was attempted.
The single exit block at lines 59-60 unconditionally calls hso_free_net_device(hso_dev, true), which frees/unregisters regardless of which earlier step failed.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-415 fits because the shared exit path can free the same net_device-related memory twice: once via the unconditional hso_free_net_device call and again through overlapping cleanup of partially initialized state. This is double free rather than merely improper resource release.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: one error label serves every failure path, so cleanup runs without knowing how far initialization progressed. Trigger: a late failure such as register_netdev returning nonzero at line 51 reaches the same exit as earlier allocation failures. The cleanup then frees network resources that were never fully registered or may already be released, producing a double free/use-after-free.

commit_msg:
CVE-2020-1899

VariableUnserializer should only recognize type 'S' in APCSerialization mode

description: The unserialize() function supported a type code, "S", which was meant to be supported only for APC serialization. This type code allowed arbitrary memory addresses to be accessed as if they were static StringData objects. This issue affected HHVM prior to v4.32.3, between versions 4.33.0 and 4.56.0, 4.57.0, 4.58.0, 4.58.1, 4.59.0, 4.60.0, 4.61.0, 4.62.0.

code_evidence: Line 5 accepts type 'S' regardless of serializer mode. Lines 6-8 validate only a fixed 11-byte span, then line 10 reinterprets the next 8 bytes as a StringData* pointer and line 12 dereferences sd->slice(), treating attacker-controlled bytes as a memory address and reading StringData fields from it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The dereference at lines 10-12 reads StringData contents through an unvalidated pointer, operating outside the intended buffer boundary, which matches CWE-119's out-of-bounds memory access. It is not merely a type-confusion or integer issue; the concrete weakness is unbounded memory access.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the 'S' branch is not gated on APCSerialization mode, so any input can encode an arbitrary 8-byte value interpreted as a StringData pointer. Trigger: crafted serialized data beginning with 'S' followed by a fake pointer; the length check passes but the pointer is dereferenced. Consequence: out-of-bounds read of memory at an attacker-chosen address, potentially crashing or leaking process memory.

commit_msg:
JS: Fix copying of strided image data.

Issue reported by Eugene Lim.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      memcpy(_dest, _src, stride);'], 'added_lines': ['      memcpy(_dest, _src, width);']}
description: There is a vulnerability in the strided image data parsing code in the emscripten wrapper for libheif. An attacker could exploit this through a crafted image file to cause a buffer overflow in linear memory during a memcpy call.

code_evidence: The loop advances _dest by width but _src by stride each iteration, then copies stride bytes into _dest. When stride exceeds width, the copy at line 11 writes stride bytes into a region of only width bytes per row, overrunning the destination buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This is a buffer copy whose length (stride) is not constrained to the destination row size (width), so the input size is not verified against the output buffer size, matching CWE-120. It is not merely an out-of-bounds read, since the overflow occurs on the write to _dest.

evidence_lines.code:
for (int y = 0; y < height; y++, _dest += width, _src += stride) {
memcpy(_dest, _src, stride);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The destination row length is width, but memcpy copies stride bytes per row whenever stride != width. A crafted image with stride larger than width triggers an out-of-bounds write past the destination buffer, corrupting adjacent linear memory (CWE-120 consequence: memory modification, potential crash or code execution).

commit_msg: https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/issues/444
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        ThrowReaderException(CorruptImageError,"UnableToReadImageData");'], 'added_lines': ['        {', '          pixels=(unsigned char *) RelinquishMagickMemory(pixels);', '          ThrowReaderException(CorruptImageError,"UnableToReadImageData");', '        }']}
description: In ImageMagick 7.0.5-5, the ReadAAIImage function in aai.c allows attackers to cause a denial of service (memory leak) via a crafted file.

code_evidence: pixels is allocated with AcquireQuantumMemory based on image->columns and is intended to be freed by the RelinquishMagickMemory call at line 89 after the row loop.

When ReadBlob returns fewer bytes than length, the check at line 61 calls ThrowReaderException directly, which unwinds the function without reaching the RelinquishMagickMemory at line 89, leaking the pixels buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function allocates a resource (pixels) and fails to release it on an early-exit path, matching CWE-772's missing release after effective lifetime. This is a resource-lifetime defect, not an out-of-bounds access, because the buffer is valid but never freed on the error path.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the error path for a short read aborts the function before the allocated pixels buffer is released. Trigger: a crafted AAII file whose pixel data is truncated so ReadBlob returns count != length. Consequence: the heap allocation leaks, and repeated processing of such files consumes memory, supporting denial of service.

commit_msg:
Track byteSize of HeaderMap internally.

Introduces a cached byte size updated internally in HeaderMap. The value
is stored as an optional, and is cleared whenever a non-const pointer or
reference to a HeaderEntry is accessed. The cached value can be set with
refreshByteSize() which performs an iteration over the HeaderMap to sum
the size of each key and value in the HeaderMap.

Signed-off-by: Asra Ali <asraa@google.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      appendToHeader((*ref_lookup_response.entry_)->value(), value.getStringView());'], 'added_lines': ['      const uint64_t added_size =', '          appendToHeader((*ref_lookup_response.entry_)->value(), value.getStringView());', '      addSize(added_size);', '    addSize(key.size() + value.size());']}
description: Upon receiving each incoming request header data, Envoy will iterate over existing request headers to verify that the total size of the headers stays below a maximum limit. The implementation in versions 1.10.0 through 1.11.1 for HTTP/1.x traffic and all versions of Envoy for HTTP/2 traffic had O(n^2) performance characteristics. A remote attacker may craft a request that stays below the maximum request header size but consists of many thousands of small headers to consume CPU and result in a denial-of-service attack.

code_evidence: When a static-lookup key already exists, line 9 appends the incoming value via appendToHeader but, in the pre-patch function, performs no size accounting before value.clear() on line 10; the returned appended length is discarded.
For non-static keys, lines 13-14 insert the new key/value pair into headers_ without updating any cached total, so repeated small insertions accumulate unbounded entries.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-400 fits because the product fails to track and restrict the aggregate resource (header bytes/entries) consumed per request, enabling resource-consumption denial of service. The missing addSize accounting, not a memory-safety flaw, is the root cause; the DoS is the consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function mutates the header map (append or insert) without maintaining a bounded total-size counter or rejecting growth. A remote attacker sending thousands of small headers that individually stay under any per-header limit causes each call to add entries while no aggregated limit is enforced, driving O(n^2) rescanning and CPU exhaustion.

commit_msg:
bpf: fix missing error return in check_stack_boundary()

Prevent indirect stack accesses at non-constant addresses, which would
permit reading and corrupting spilled pointers.

Fixes: f1174f77b50c ("bpf/verifier: rework value tracking")
Signed-off-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\treturn -EACCES;']}
description: The check_stack_boundary function in kernel/bpf/verifier.c in the Linux kernel through 4.14.8 allows local users to cause a denial of service (memory corruption) or possibly have unspecified other impact by leveraging mishandling of invalid variable stack read operations.

code_evidence: Lines 17-22 detect a non-constant stack pointer offset (var_off not const), log the invalid variable stack read, but then fall through without returning an error.

Lines 23-28 compute off from regs[regno].off + var_off.value and only reject when the resulting constant offset or access_size is out of range; with a non-constant var_off the check proceeds using the tnum's value.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing return lets a stack access at a non-constant address bypass the offset/access_size boundary validation, so subsequent stack slot operations may target memory outside the intended buffer boundary, matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds memory operation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the non-constant var_off branch lacks a return, so execution continues past the intended rejection and uses var_off.value as if it were the actual offset. Trigger: a BPF program performs an indirect stack access at a non-constant address. Consequence: the verifier's boundary check is bypassed, permitting reads/corruption of spilled pointers outside the intended stack slot bounds.

description: There is a Null Pointer Dereference in function filter_core/filter_pck.c:gf_filter_pck_new_alloc_internal in GPAC 1.0.1. The pid comes from function av1dmx_parse_flush_sample, the ctx.opid maybe NULL. The result is a crash in gf_filter_pck_new_alloc_internal.

code_evidence: ctx->opid is passed directly to gf_filter_pck_new_alloc without any prior NULL check; the function only guards on pck_size at line 7. If opid is NULL, the returned pck may be invalid and is then dereferenced by gf_filter_pck_merge_properties, gf_filter_pck_set_cts, gf_filter_pck_set_sap, and memcpy into output.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences a pointer (ctx->opid) expected to be valid but possibly NULL, matching CWE-476. The fix adds an explicit !ctx->opid guard, confirming the missing NULL check is the defect rather than a different memory-safety issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: av1dmx_parse_flush_sample assumes ctx->opid is non-NULL but never validates it before allocating and using a packet. Trigger: a flush sample where ctx.opid is NULL, as reported from av1dmx_parse_flush_sample. Consequence: NULL-pointer dereference/crash (DoS) in the packet allocation/use path.

commit_msg:
Fix OOB reads of the TGA decompression buffer

It is possible to craft TGA files which will overflow the decompression
buffer, but not the image's bitmap. Therefore we augment the check for the
bitmap's overflow with a check for the buffer's overflow.

This issue had been reported by Ibrahim El-Sayed to security@libgd.org.

CVE-2016-6906
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t\tif ((bitmap_caret + (encoded_pixels * pixel_block_size)) > image_block_size) {', '\t\t\t\tif ((bitmap_caret + (encoded_pixels * pixel_block_size)) > image_block_size) {'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t\tif ((bitmap_caret + (encoded_pixels * pixel_block_size)) > image_block_size', '\t\t\t\t\t\t|| buffer_caret + pixel_block_size > rle_size) {', '\t\t\t\tif ((bitmap_caret + (encoded_pixels * pixel_block_size)) > image_block_size', '\t\t\t\t\t\t|| buffer_caret + (encoded_pixels * pixel_block_size) > rle_size) {']}
description: The read_image_tga function in gd_tga.c in the GD Graphics Library (aka libgd) before 2.2.4 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read) via a crafted TGA file, related to the decompression buffer.

code_evidence: RLE loop indexes decompression_buffer[buffer_caret] at line 67 and line 68 without verifying buffer_caret is within rle_size; the only bounds check at line 70 guards bitmap_caret/image_block_size, not the source buffer.

The raw-pixel branch reads decompression_buffer[buffer_caret] at line 81 and then memcpy from decompression_buffer + buffer_caret for encoded_pixels*pixel_block_size ints at line 88; line 83 checks only bitmap_caret against image_block_size, so buffer_caret can exceed the rle_size bytes actually read.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Reading past the intended decompression_buffer bounds is exactly CWE-125 (out-of-bounds read). It is not CWE-787 because the missing check leads to reads of source data, not writes past the destination buffer.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the decompression loop validates only the destination bitmap size, not the source decompression_buffer length (rle_size). A crafted TGA whose RLE packet length or encoded_pixels count drives buffer_caret past rle_size triggers reads beyond the allocated/initialized buffer, causing an out-of-bounds read and possible crash (DoS).

We will soon need to fetch part of the page state outside of invalid
PTE entries, so provide the input address to the get_page_state()
helper.

Bug: 264070847
Change-Id: I02e0c7538a15cad8e63591bfab67c6de125631fe
Signed-off-by: Quentin Perret <qperret@google.com>
Bug: 279739439
[willdeacon@: Dropped hunks modifying non-existent code]
Signed-off-by: Will Deacon <willdeacon@google.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\treturn d->get_page_state(pte) == d->desired ? 0 : -EPERM;'], 'added_lines': ['\treturn d->get_page_state(pte, addr) == d->desired ? 0 : -EPERM;']}
description: In multiple functions of mem_protect.c, there is a possible way to access hypervisor memory due to a memory access check in the wrong place. This could lead to local escalation of privilege with System execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

commit_msg:
mount runtime seccomp files read-only (#2602)

avoid creating locations in the file system that are both writable and
executable (in this case for processes with euid of the user).

for the same reason also remove user owned libfiles
when it is not needed any more
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\tcreate_empty_dir_as_root(RUN_SECCOMP_DIR, 0755);', '']}
description: In Firejail before 0.9.60, seccomp filters are writable inside the jail, leading to a lack of intended seccomp restrictions for a process that is joined to the jail after a filter has been modified by an attacker.

code_evidence: Seccomp filter files are copied into RUN_SECCOMP_* paths with getuid()/getgid() as owner and mode 0644, placing them in a tmpfs mounted with mode=755. The patch adds create_empty_dir_as_root(RUN_SECCOMP_DIR, 0755) before these copies, but the resulting filter files and directory remain owned by the calling user with user-writable permissions rather than read-only root ownership.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-732 fits because the code assigns permissions on a security-critical resource (seccomp filters) that grant write access to an unintended actor (the jailed user), enabling modification of execution-control configuration. This is incorrect permission assignment, not merely a missing authorization check.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the seccomp filter files are assigned to the unprivileged user (getuid/getgid) with mode 0644, so the user can modify them. Trigger: an attacker running as that user rewrites the filter before another process joins the jail. Consequence: the modified filter is applied, defeating the intended seccomp restrictions.

commit_msg: relay: fix crash when decoding a malformed websocket frame
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    while (index_buffer + 2 <= buffer_length)', '            if (buffer_length < 1 + length_frame_size)', '        if (buffer_length < 1 + length_frame_size + 4 + length_frame)', '', '        /* read masks (4 bytes) */'], 'added_lines': ['    while (index_buffer + 1 < buffer_length)', '        if (index_buffer >= buffer_length)', '            return 0;', '            if (index_buffer + length_frame_size > buffer_length)', '        /* read masks (4 bytes) */', '        if (index_buffer + 4 > buffer_length)', '        if ((length_frame > buffer_length)', '            || (index_buffer + length_frame > buffer_length))', '        {', '            return 0;', '        }']}
description: WeeChat before 3.2.1 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (crash) via a crafted WebSocket frame that trigger an out-of-bounds read in plugins/relay/relay-websocket.c in the Relay plugin.

code_evidence: Loop guard only ensures two header bytes exist before reading opcode and length at buffer[index_buffer+1].
Header is read at [14,17] and index_buffer advanced past it at [18] without checking the remaining buffer length.
Extended-length check at [22] compares against a constant rather than the advanced index_buffer, so the mask read and length_frame can exceed the buffer.
Decode loop at [52,54] reads buffer[index_buffer+i] up to length_frame bytes past the intended frame without any bound check.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads buffer[index_buffer+i] beyond the supplied buffer's end, matching CWE-125 (out-of-bounds read). This is a read-only overrun, not a write overflow, so CWE-125 is the precise fit.

evidence_lines.code: while (index_buffer + 2 <= buffer_length)

for (i = 0; i < length_frame; i++)
decoded[*decoded_length + i] = (int)((unsigned char)buffer[index_buffer + i]) ^ masks[i % 4];

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: frame length and index_buffer are advanced and used without constraining them against buffer_length, so a crafted WebSocket frame declares a length larger than the actual data. Trigger: malformed frame with a large length field. Consequence: the decode loop reads past the buffer end, causing a crash/DoS (out-of-bounds read).

commit_msg:
The server is failing to apply the umask when creating new objects on
filesystems without ACL support.

To reproduce this, you need to use NFSv4.2 and a client and server
recent enough to support umask, and you need to export a filesystem that
lacks ACL support (for example, ext4 with the "noacl" mount option).

Filesystems with ACL support are expected to take care of the umask
themselves (usually by calling posix_acl_create).

For filesystems without ACL support, this is up to the caller of
vfs_create(), vfs_mknod(), or vfs_mkdir().

Reported-by: Elliott Mitchell <ehem+debian@m5p.com>
Reported-by: Salvatore Bonaccorso <carnil@debian.org>
Tested-by: Salvatore Bonaccorso <carnil@debian.org>
Fixes: 47057abde515 ("nfsd: add support for the umask attribute")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: J. Bruce Fields <bfields@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\tif (!IS_POSIXACL(dirp))', '\t\tiap->ia_mode &= ~current_umask();']}
description: In the Linux kernel before 5.7.8, fs/nfsd/vfs.c (in the NFS server) can set incorrect permissions on new filesystem objects when the filesystem lacks ACL support, aka CID-22cf8419f131. This occurs because the current umask is not considered.

code_evidence: Lines 23-25 build iap->ia_mode from the client-supplied ATTR_MODE, defaulting to 0 if absent, then OR in the file type; no umask is applied here.
The resulting ia_mode is passed directly to vfs_create (line 30), vfs_mkdir (line 35), and vfs_mknod (line 63), so the mode reaches object creation unchanged.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Passing an unmasked mode to vfs_create/vfs_mkdir/vfs_mknod assigns permissions wider than intended, matching CWE-732 incorrect permission assignment for a critical resource. It is not a missing authorization check (CWE-285), since the flaw is the permission value assigned, not a failed access decision.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: nfsd_create_locked assigns the client-requested mode to new objects without masking it by the server's current umask. Trigger: an NFS client creates a file/dir/special file on an exported filesystem lacking ACL support, where the filesystem does not apply the umask itself. Consequence: the object receives broader permissions than the umask permits, exposing it to unintended actors.

commit_msg:
RDS: null pointer dereference in rds_atomic_free_op

set rm->atomic.op_active to 0 when rds_pin_pages() fails
or the user supplied address is invalid,
this prevents a NULL pointer usage in rds_atomic_free_op()

Signed-off-by: Mohamed Ghannam <simo.ghannam@gmail.com>
Acked-by: Santosh Shilimkar <santosh.shilimkar@oracle.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\trm->atomic.op_active = 0;']}
description: In the Linux kernel through 4.14.13, the rds_cmsg_atomic function in net/rds/rdma.c mishandles cases where page pinning fails or an invalid address is supplied, leading to an rds_atomic_free_op NULL pointer dereference.

code_evidence: Line 41 sets rm->atomic.op_active = 1 before any validation of the user-supplied address or page pinning; the op_sg allocation failure path (44-47) jumps to err with op_active still set.
An 8-byte alignment check on args->local_addr (48-51) jumps to err, again leaving op_active set.
rds_pin_pages failure (ret != 1) at 52-54 jumps to err, leaving op_active set.

The err label (69-73) only puts the page and frees op_notifier; it does not clear op_active, so the message retains an active atomic op with no pinned page/SG, later dereferenced by rds_atomic_free_op.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The failure leaves state inconsistent such that a later cleanup routine dereferences a pointer it expects valid but which is NULL, matching CWE-476. The fix adds rm->atomic.op_active = 0 in err, confirming the missing reset is the cause rather than a different memory-safety weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: rm->atomic.op_active is set to 1 at line 41 before the alignment and pinning checks, and the err cleanup path never resets it. Trigger: a caller supplies a misaligned or unpinnable local_addr so the function fails after line 41. Consequence: the message is left with op_active set but no valid page/SG, and the later rds_atomic_free_op dereferences the missing mapping, causing a NULL pointer dereference/DoS.

commit_msg:
vgacon: remove software scrollback support

Yunhai Zhang recently fixed a VGA software scrollback bug in commit
ebfdfeeae8c0 ("vgacon: Fix for missing check in scrollback handling"),
but that then made people look more closely at some of this code, and
there were more problems on the vgacon side, but also the fbcon software
scrollback.

We don't really have anybody who maintains this code - probably because
nobody actually _uses_ it any more.  Sure, people still use both VGA and
the framebuffer consoles, but they are no longer the main user
interfaces to the kernel, and haven't been for decades, so these kinds
of extra features end up bitrotting and not really being used.

So rather than try to maintain a likely unused set of code, I'll just
aggressively remove it, and see if anybody even notices.  Maybe there
are people who haven't jumped on the whole GUI badnwagon yet, and think
it's just a fad.  And maybe those people use the scrollback code.

If that turns out to be the case, we can resurrect this again, once
we've found the sucker^Wmaintainer for it who actually uses it.

Reported-by: NopNop Nop <nopitydays@gmail.com>
Tested-by: Willy Tarreau <w@1wt.eu>
Cc: 张云海 <zhangyunhai@nsfocus.com>
Acked-by: Andy Lutomirski <luto@amacapital.net>
Acked-by: Willy Tarreau <w@1wt.eu>
Reviewed-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tc->vc_origin = c->vc_visible_origin;', '\tvgacon_scrollback_cur->save = 0;', '', '\tif (!vga_is_gfx && !vgacon_scrollback_cur->restore) {', '\t\tscr_memcpyw((u16 *) c->vc_origin, (u16 *) c->vc_screenbuf,', '\t\t\t    c->vc_screenbuf_size > vga_vram_size ?', '\t\t\t    vga_vram_size : c->vc_screenbuf_size);', '\t\tvgacon_scrollback_cur->restore = 1;', '\t\tvgacon_scrollback_cur->cur = vgacon_scrollback_cur->cnt;', '\t}'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (c->vc_origin != c->vc_visible_origin)', '\t\tvgacon_scrolldelta(c, 0);']}
description: The vgacon subsystem in the Linux kernel before 5.8.10 mishandles software scrollback. There is a vgacon_scrolldelta out-of-bounds read, aka CID-973c096f6a85.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function vgacon_restore_screen only assigns origins, copies screenbuf data bounded by vga_vram_size, and resets scrollback fields; it performs no out-of-bounds read. The described OOB read is in vgacon_scrolldelta, not this function.

commit_msg:
x86/MSI-X: restrict reading of table/PBA bases from BARs

When assigned to less trusted or un-trusted guests, devices may change
state behind our backs (they may e.g. get reset by means we may not know
about). Therefore we should avoid reading BARs from hardware once a
device is no longer owned by Dom0. Furthermore when we can't read a BAR,
or when we read zero, we shouldn't instead use the caller provided
address unless that caller can be trusted.

Re-arrange the logic in msix_capability_init() such that only Dom0 (and
only if the device isn't DomU-owned yet) or calls through
PHYSDEVOP_prepare_msix will actually result in the reading of the
respective BAR register(s). Additionally do so only as long as in-use
table entries are known (note that invocation of PHYSDEVOP_prepare_msix
counts as a "pseudo" entry). In all other uses the value already
recorded will get used instead.

Clear the recorded values in _pci_cleanup_msix() as well as on the one
affected error path. (Adjust this error path to also avoid blindly
disabling MSI-X when it was enabled on entry to the function.)

While moving around variable declarations (in many cases to reduce their
scopes), also adjust some of their types.

This is part of XSA-337.

Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Reviewed-by: Roger Pau Monné <roger.pau@citrix.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['        msix->table.first = 0;', '        msix->table.last = 0;', '', '        msix->pba.first = 0;', '        msix->pba.last = 0;']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.14.x. The PCI passthrough code improperly uses register data. Code paths in Xen's MSI handling have been identified that act on unsanitized values read back from device hardware registers. While devices strictly compliant with PCI specifications shouldn't be able to affect these registers, experience shows that it's very common for devices to have out-of-spec "backdoor" operations that can affect the result of these reads. A not fully trusted guest may be able to crash Xen, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) for the entire system. Privilege escalation and information leaks cannot be excluded. All versions of Xen supporting PCI passthrough are affected. Only x86 systems are vulnerable. Arm systems are not vulnerable. Only guests with passed through PCI devices may be able to leverage the vulnerability. Only systems passing through devices with out-of-spec ("backdoor") functionality can cause issues. Experience shows that such out-of-spec functionality is common; unless you have reason to believe that your device does not have such functionality, it's better to assume that it does.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function only clears recorded MSI-X table/PBA base fields during cleanup; it performs no privilege assignment, modification, tracking, or check, so it does not directly support CWE-269.

commit_msg: Make eocd checks more consistent between zip and zip64 cases.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if ((flags & ZIP_CHECKCONS) && offset+size != eocd_offset) {'], 'added_lines': ['    if (offset+size > buf_offset + eocd_offset) {', '\t/* cdir spans past EOCD record */', '\tzip_error_set(error, ZIP_ER_INCONS, 0);', '\treturn NULL;', '    }', '    if ((flags & ZIP_CHECKCONS) && offset+size != buf_offset + eocd_offset) {']}
description: The _zip_read_eocd64 function in zip_open.c in libzip before 1.3.0 mishandles EOCD records, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory allocation failure in _zip_cdir_grow in zip_dirent.c) via a crafted ZIP archive.

code_evidence: Lines 97-100 only reject offset when offset > ZIP_INT64_MAX or offset+size wraps around; size itself is never bounded. In the non-checkcons path the only remaining guard is the optional consistency check at lines 101-104, which is skipped unless ZIP_CHECKCONS is set.

Line 105 then calls _zip_cdir_new(nentry, error) with the unbounded nentry value read from the archive at line 76, allocating central-directory storage proportional to attacker-controlled entry count.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-770 fits because the function allocates a resource (central-directory memory) based on an unvalidated attacker-supplied count, with no limit or throttle, yielding memory-consumption DoS. This is resource-allocation without limits rather than an arithmetic flaw alone; the integer checks at lines 97-100 do not limit the allocation size.

evidence_lines.code:
if ((cd=_zip_cdir_new(nentry, error)) == NULL)
return NULL;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the EOCD64 entry count nentry is trusted without an upper bound, and the prior offset/size check does not constrain it. Trigger: a crafted ZIP whose EOCD64 declares an enormous entry count. Consequence: _zip_cdir_new allocates memory proportional to nentry, exhausting memory and causing denial of service (the described allocation failure in _zip_cdir_grow).

commit_msg:
Commit a23740ec43ba ("bpf: Track contents of read-only maps as scalars") is
checking whether maps are read-only both from BPF program side and user space
side, and then, given their content is constant, reading out their data via
map->ops->map_direct_value_addr() which is then subsequently used as known
scalar value for the register, that is, it is marked as __mark_reg_known()
with the read value at verification time. Before a23740ec43ba, the register
content was marked as an unknown scalar so the verifier could not make any
assumptions about the map content.

The current implementation however is prone to a TOCTOU race, meaning, the
value read as known scalar for the register is not guaranteed to be exactly
the same at a later point when the program is executed, and as such, the
prior made assumptions of the verifier with regards to the program will be
invalid which can cause issues such as OOB access, etc.

While the BPF_F_RDONLY_PROG map flag is always fixed and required to be
specified at map creation time, the map->frozen property is initially set to
false for the map given the map value needs to be populated, e.g. for global
data sections. Once complete, the loader "freezes" the map from user space
such that no subsequent updates/deletes are possible anymore. For the rest
of the lifetime of the map, this freeze one-time trigger cannot be undone
anymore after a successful BPF_MAP_FREEZE cmd return. Meaning, any new BPF_*
cmd calls which would update/delete map entries will be rejected with -EPERM
since map_get_sys_perms() removes the FMODE_CAN_WRITE permission. This also
means that pending update/delete map entries must still complete before this
guarantee is given. This corner case is not an issue for loaders since they
create and prepare such program private map in successive steps.

However, a malicious user is able to trigger this TOCTOU race in two different
ways: i) via userfaultfd, and ii) via batched updates. For i) userfaultfd is
used to expand the competition interval, so that map_update_elem() can modify
the contents of the map after map_freeze() and bpf_prog_load() were executed.
This works, because userfaultfd halts the parallel thread which triggered a
map_update_elem() at the time where we copy key/value from the user buffer and
this already passed the FMODE_CAN_WRITE capability test given at that time the
map was not "frozen". Then, the main thread performs the map_freeze() and
bpf_prog_load(), and once that had completed successfully, the other thread
is woken up to complete the pending map_update_elem() which then changes the
map content. For ii) the idea of the batched update is similar, meaning, when
there are a large number of updates to be processed, it can increase the
competition interval between the two. It is therefore possible in practice to
modify the contents of the map after executing map_freeze() and bpf_prog_load().

One way to fix both i) and ii) at the same time is to expand the use of the
map's map->writecnt. The latter was introduced in fc9702273e2e ("bpf: Add mmap()
support for BPF_MAP_TYPE_ARRAY") and further refined in 1f6cb19be2e2 ("bpf:
Prevent re-mmap()'ing BPF map as writable for initially r/o mapping") with
the rationale to make a writable mmap()'ing of a map mutually exclusive with
read-only freezing. The counter indicates writable mmap() mappings and then
prevents/fails the freeze operation. Its semantics can be expanded beyond
just mmap() by generally indicating ongoing write phases. This would essentially
span any parallel regular and batched flavor of update/delete operation and
then also have map_freeze() fail with -EBUSY. For the check_mem_access() in
the verifier we expand upon the bpf_map_is_rdonly() check ensuring that all
last pending writes have completed via bpf_map_write_active() test. Once the
map->frozen is set and bpf_map_write_active() indicates a map->writecnt of 0
only then we are really guaranteed to use the map's data as known constants.
For map->frozen being set and pending writes in process of still being completed
we fall back to marking that register as unknown scalar so we don't end up
making assumptions about it. With this, both TOCTOU reproducers from i) and
ii) are fixed.

Note that the map->writecnt has been converted into a atomic64 in the fix in
order to avoid a double freeze_mutex mutex_{un,}lock() pair when updating
map->writecnt in the various map update/delete BPF_* cmd flavors. Spanning
the freeze_mutex over entire map update/delete operations in syscall side
would not be possible due to then causing everything to be serialized.
Similarly, something like synchronize_rcu() after setting map->frozen to wait
for update/deletes to complete is not possible either since it would also
have to span the user copy which can sleep. On the libbpf side, this won't
break d66562fba1ce ("libbpf: Add BPF object skeleton support") as the
anonymous mmap()-ed "map initialization image" is remapped as a BPF map-backed
mmap()-ed memory where for .rodata it's non-writable.

Fixes: a23740ec43ba ("bpf: Track contents of read-only maps as scalars")
Reported-by: w1tcher.bupt@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>
Acked-by: Andrii Nakryiko <andrii@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (vma->vm_flags & VM_MAYWRITE) {', '\t\tmutex_lock(&map->freeze_mutex);', '\t\tmap->writecnt++;', '\t\tmutex_unlock(&map->freeze_mutex);', '\t}'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (vma->vm_flags & VM_MAYWRITE)', '\t\tbpf_map_write_active_inc(map);']}
description: A race condition was found in the Linux kernel's ebpf verifier between bpf_map_update_elem and bpf_map_freeze due to a missing lock in kernel/bpf/syscall.c. In this flaw, a local user with a special privilege (cap_sys_admin or cap_bpf) can modify the frozen mapped address space. This flaw affects kernel versions prior to 5.16 rc2.

code_evidence: On writable mmap (VM_MAYWRITE), the code increments map->writecnt under freeze_mutex to record an active writable mapping. This counter is the check that later gates whether the verifier may treat read-only map contents as known scalars; here the increment is a separate lock/unlock sequence rather than a shared atomic accounting used by update/freeze paths.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The verifier checks map frozen/read-only state and then uses map contents as constants, but a concurrent write can alter the resource between check and use. This is precisely a TOCTOU race (CWE-367); the root cause is non-atomic writecnt accounting, and the consequence is invalid verifier assumptions.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The writecnt bookkeeping is only protected locally by freeze_mutex, so it does not atomically coordinate with concurrent map_update_elem or map_freeze operations. A pending write can pass the capability check before freeze, then complete after freeze and bpf_prog_load, letting map contents change after the verifier assumed them constant, invalidating its scalar assumptions and enabling out-of-bounds access.

commit_msg:
Patch series "Fix several device private page reference counting issues",
v2

This series aims to fix a number of page reference counting issues in
drivers dealing with device private ZONE_DEVICE pages.  These result in
use-after-free type bugs, either from accessing a struct page which no
longer exists because it has been removed or accessing fields within the
struct page which are no longer valid because the page has been freed.

During normal usage it is unlikely these will cause any problems.  However
without these fixes it is possible to crash the kernel from userspace. 
These crashes can be triggered either by unloading the kernel module or
unbinding the device from the driver prior to a userspace task exiting. 
In modules such as Nouveau it is also possible to trigger some of these
issues by explicitly closing the device file-descriptor prior to the task
exiting and then accessing device private memory.

This involves some minor changes to both PowerPC and AMD GPU code. 
Unfortunately I lack hardware to test either of those so any help there
would be appreciated.  The changes mimic what is done in for both Nouveau
and hmm-tests though so I doubt they will cause problems.


This patch (of 8):

When the CPU tries to access a device private page the migrate_to_ram()
callback associated with the pgmap for the page is called.  However no
reference is taken on the faulting page.  Therefore a concurrent migration
of the device private page can free the page and possibly the underlying
pgmap.  This results in a race which can crash the kernel due to the
migrate_to_ram() function pointer becoming invalid.  It also means drivers
can't reliably read the zone_device_data field because the page may have
been freed with memunmap_pages().

Close the race by getting a reference on the page while holding the ptl to
ensure it has not been freed.  Unfortunately the elevated reference count
will cause the migration required to handle the fault to fail.  To avoid
this failure pass the faulting page into the migrate_vma functions so that
if an elevated reference count is found it can be checked to see if it's
expected or not.

commit_msg:
tracing/syscalls: Ignore numbers outside NR_syscalls' range

ARM has some private syscalls (for example, set_tls(2)) which lie
outside the range of NR_syscalls.  If any of these are called while
syscall tracing is being performed, out-of-bounds array access will
occur in the ftrace and perf sys_{enter,exit} handlers.

 # trace-cmd record -e raw_syscalls:* true && trace-cmd report
 ...
 true-653   [000]   384.675777: sys_enter:            NR 192 (0, 1000, 3, 4000022, ffffffff, 0)
 true-653   [000]   384.675812: sys_exit:             NR 192 = 1995915264
 true-653   [000]   384.675971: sys_enter:            NR 983045 (76f74480, 76f74000, 76f74b28, 76f74480, 76f76f74, 1)
 true-653   [000]   384.675988: sys_exit:             NR 983045 = 0
 ...

 # trace-cmd record -e syscalls:* true
 [   17.289329] Unable to handle kernel paging request at virtual address aaaaaace
 [   17.289590] pgd = 9e71c000
 [   17.289696] [aaaaaace] *pgd=00000000
 [   17.289985] Internal error: Oops: 5 [#1] PREEMPT SMP ARM
 [   17.290169] Modules linked in:
 [   17.290391] CPU: 0 PID: 704 Comm: true Not tainted 3.18.0-rc2+ #21
 [   17.290585] task: 9f4dab00 ti: 9e710000 task.ti: 9e710000
 [   17.290747] PC is at ftrace_syscall_enter+0x48/0x1f8
 [   17.290866] LR is at syscall_trace_enter+0x124/0x184

Fix this by ignoring out-of-NR_syscalls-bounds syscall numbers.

commit_msg:
Prevent dereferencing of null pointers in TFLite's `add.cc`.

Change-Id: I56094233327fbd8439b92e1dbb1262176e00eeb9
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  } else {'], 'added_lines': ['  } else if (input1_data_ptr != nullptr) {']}
description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. In affected versions an attacker can craft a TFLite model that would trigger a null pointer dereference, which would result in a crash and denial of service. The [implementation](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/149562d49faa709ea80df1d99fc41d005b81082a/tensorflow/lite/kernels/internal/optimized/optimized_ops.h#L268-L285) unconditionally dereferences a pointer. We have patched the issue in GitHub commit 15691e456c7dc9bd6be203b09765b063bf4a380c. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.6.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.5.1, TensorFlow 2.4.3, and TensorFlow 2.3.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: Lines 21-24 select input1_data from unswitched_input1_data or unswitched_input2_data based on use_unswitched, and line 26 assigns it to input1_data_ptr without any null check.
The else branch (lines 50-65) is taken when y4 <= 1; the inner loop at lines 55-61 unconditionally dereferences *input1_data_ptr at line 56 via scalar_broadcast_f.
The patch guard `else if (input1_data_ptr != nullptr)` shows input1_data_ptr may be null, yet the original else path (lines 50-65) performs the dereference regardless.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences input1_data_ptr at line 56 while it may be NULL, matching CWE-476's definition of dereferencing a pointer expected to be valid but NULL. The missing nil check, not an out-of-bounds index, is the defect.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: a null input pointer chosen at lines 21-24 flows into input1_data_ptr and is dereferenced at line 56 without validation when the y4<=1 branch executes. Trigger: a crafted TFLite model yields a null input tensor with a broadcast shape where y4<=1. Consequence: null pointer dereference causing a crash (denial of service).

commit_msg:
list-objects: pass full pathname to callbacks

When we find a blob at "a/b/c", we currently pass this to
our show_object_fn callbacks as two components: "a/b/" and
"c". Callbacks which want the full value then call
path_name(), which concatenates the two. But this is an
inefficient interface; the path is a strbuf, and we could
simply append "c" to it temporarily, then roll back the
length, without creating a new copy.

So we could improve this by teaching the callsites of
path_name() this trick (and there are only 3). But we can
also notice that no callback actually cares about the
broken-down representation, and simply pass each callback
the full path "a/b/c" as a string. The callback code becomes
even simpler, then, as we do not have to worry about freeing
an allocated buffer, nor rolling back our modification to
the strbuf.

This is theoretically less efficient, as some callbacks
would not bother to format the final path component. But in
practice this is not measurable. Since we use the same
strbuf over and over, our work to grow it is amortized, and
we really only pay to memcpy a few bytes.

Signed-off-by: Jeff King <peff@peff.net>
Signed-off-by: Junio C Hamano <gitster@pobox.com>

commit_msg:
exif_scan_JPEG_header: Added length check to prevent information leak

Summary:
'exif_process_SOFn' assumes that the JPEG header has at least 6 length. On providing a length < 6, this leads to an out of bounds heap read.

Fixes CVE-2019-11926

Reviewed By: fredemmott

Differential Revision: D16927050

description: Insufficient boundary checks when processing M_SOFx markers from JPEG headers in the GD extension could allow access to out-of-bounds memory via a maliciously constructed invalid JPEG input. This issue affects HHVM versions prior to 3.30.9, all versions between 4.0.0 and 4.8.3, all versions between 4.9.0 and 4.15.2, and versions 4.16.0 to 4.16.3, 4.17.0 to 4.17.2, 4.18.0 to 4.18.1, 4.19.0, 4.20.0 to 4.20.1.

For M_SOF0..M_SOF15, exif_process_SOFn(Data, marker, &sof_info) is called with Data sized from the attacker-controlled itemlen and no minimum-length check before it is dispatched.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dispatches SOFn data to a parser without ensuring the buffer is long enough, directly enabling a read beyond the intended buffer bounds, which is CWE-125. The missing length constraint is the cause; the out-of-bounds read is the consequence.

case M_SOF1:
case M_SOF2:
case M_SOF3:
case M_SOF5:

commit_msg:
Fix integer overflow in string search causing oobread ##crash

* Reported by @greatergoodest via huntrdev
* BountyID: 8a3dc5cb-08b3-4807-82b2-77f08c137a04
* Reproducer bfileovf
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\twhile (needle < to) {', '\t\tif (needle + 4 < to) {', '\t\t\tut32 n1 = r_read_le32 (buf + needle - from);', '\t\trc = r_utf8_decode (buf + needle - from, to - needle, NULL);', '\t\t\tchar *w = (char *)buf + needle + rc - from;', '\t\t\t\trc = r_utf8_decode (buf + needle - from, to - needle, &r);'], 'added_lines': ['\twhile (needle < to && needle < UT64_MAX - 4) {', '\t\tif (needle < to - 4) {', '\t\t\tut32 n1 = r_read_le32 (buf + (needle - from));', '\t\trc = r_utf8_decode (buf + (needle - from), to - needle, NULL);', '\t\t\tchar *w = (char *)buf + (needle + rc - from);', '\t\t\t\trc = r_utf8_decode (buf + (needle - from), to - needle, &r);']}
description: Out-of-bounds Read in GitHub repository radareorg/radare2 prior to 5.7.0.

code_evidence: The scan loop advances `needle` and computes offsets `buf + needle - from` for r_read_le32 and r_utf8_decode; the loop guard `needle < to` does not bound the pointer arithmetic when `needle` approaches the 64-bit maximum, so the offset can wrap and read outside `buf`.

After decoding, `w` is formed as `buf + needle + rc - from` and dereferenced in the wide-detection checks (w[0]..w[4], w[5]..w[8]); these indices assume remaining bytes exist, so a wrapped/oversized needle yields reads past the buffer end.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences buffer offsets derived from unchecked position arithmetic, reading beyond the intended allocation. This is a direct out-of-bounds read (CWE-125); the integer overflow is the enabling cause, not the primary weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: unbounded arithmetic on `needle` (and `needle + rc`) combined with only a `needle < to` guard allows wraparound/overshoot before pointer offsets are applied to `buf`. Trigger: a crafted input range where the scan position grows near the integer limit. Consequence: out-of-bounds reads of heap memory, potentially a crash or memory disclosure.

description: An issue was discovered in USBGuard before 1.1.0. On systems with the usbguard-dbus daemon running, an unprivileged user could make USBGuard allow all USB devices to be connected in the future.

code_evidence: handlePolicyMethodCall dispatches on a caller-supplied method_name and, in the before version, immediately processes listRules by reading parameters and returning rules via listRules(label) with no authorization gate on invocation.
The appendRule branch likewise parses parameters and calls appendRule(rule_spec, parent_id, !temporary), mutating policy state without verifying the caller.
The removeRule branch parses a rule_id and calls removeRule(rule_id), deleting policy state without any authorization check on the D-Bus invocation.

It is not merely a missing-input-validation issue: the defect is the absent access-control decision before acting on the caller's request.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the D-Bus policy method handler performs actions (listing, appending, removing rules) without validating the caller's authorization on the invocation. Trigger: an unprivileged user sends any of these method calls over usbguard-dbus. Supported consequence: unauthorized read of rules and modification of policy, e.g. allowing all future USB devices, bypassing the intended access-control decision.

commit_msg:
[mlir][scf][bufferize] Fix bug in WhileOp analysis verification

Block arguments and yielded values are not equivalent if there are not enough block arguments. This fixes #59442.

Differential Revision: https://reviews.llvm.org/D145575
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      if (!state.areEquivalentBufferizedValues(', '              it.value(), conditionOp->getBlock()->getArgument(it.index())))', '      if (!state.areEquivalentBufferizedValues(', '              it.value(), yieldOp->getBlock()->getArgument(it.index())))'], 'added_lines': ['      Block *block = conditionOp->getBlock();', '      if (it.index() >= block->getNumArguments() ||', '          !state.areEquivalentBufferizedValues(it.value(),', '                                               block->getArgument(it.index())))', '      Block *block = yieldOp->getBlock();', '      if (it.index() >= block->getNumArguments() ||', '          !state.areEquivalentBufferizedValues(it.value(),', '                                               block->getArgument(it.index())))']}
description: llvm-project commit bd456297 was discovered to contain a segmentation fault via the component mlir::Block::getArgument.

code_evidence: Condition-arg loop indexes the condition block's arguments with it.index() without checking it is within getNumArguments().
Yield loop similarly indexes the yield block's arguments with it.index() without a bounds check.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits: the unsafe operation is an unchecked index into a block's argument container, reading past its end. The missing constraint is it.index() < block->getNumArguments(), matching the fix. This is a read OOB, not a write or null dereference.

evidence_lines.code:
if (!state.areEquivalentBufferizedValues(
it.value(), conditionOp->getBlock()->getArgument(it.index())))

if (!state.areEquivalentBufferizedValues(
it.value(), yieldOp->getBlock()->getArgument(it.index())))

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The loops enumerate condition args / yield results and map each to the corresponding block argument via getArgument(it.index()). When the block has fewer arguments than the enumerated values, the index exceeds the argument count and getArgument reads past the end of the argument list, causing an out-of-bounds read that can crash (segfault).

Fixed bugs due to uninitialized data in the JP2 decoder.
Also, added some comments marking I/O stream interfaces that probably

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tcmap->ents = 0;']}
description: The jp2_cdef_destroy function in jp2_cod.c in JasPer before 2.0.13 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference) via a crafted image.

code_evidence: cmap->numchans is derived from box->datalen (line 6) and cmap->ents is assigned the result of jas_alloc2 (line 7). If allocation fails, the function returns -1 at line 8, but cmap->ents has already been overwritten with NULL by the assignment, so the box's cmap state retains a NULL ents pointer. The loop at lines 10-11 then indexes cmap->ents[i] without any NULL check.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is a pointer (cmap->ents) that can be NULL when allocation fails and is subsequently dereferenced, matching CWE-476. It is not a use-after-free or integer overflow; the core defect is the missing NULL check on a pointer that may legitimately be NULL.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the allocation result is stored directly into the persistent cmap->ents field and failure is handled only by returning -1, leaving cmap->ents NULL. A later consumer of the box's cmap data (e.g., destroy or processing code) dereferences cmap->ents without verifying it is non-NULL, triggering a NULL pointer dereference and crash (DoS).

commit_msg:

XACQUIRE prefixed accesses to the 4Mb range of memory starting at 1Gb
are liable to lock up the processor. Disallow use of this memory range.

Unfortunately the available Core Gen7 and Gen8 spec updates are pretty
old, so I can only guess that they're similarly affected when Core Gen6
is and the Xeon counterparts are, too.

This is part of XSA-282.

Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Reviewed-by: Andrew Cooper <andrew.cooper3@citrix.com>

commit_msg:
When opening files for write, ensure they aren't symbolic links

Issue #1048 identified that if, for example, a non privileged user
created a symbolic link from /etc/keepalvied.data to /etc/passwd,
writing to /etc/keepalived.data (which could be invoked via DBus)
would cause /etc/passwd to be overwritten.

This commit stops keepalived writing to pathnames where the ultimate
component is a symbolic link, by setting O_NOFOLLOW whenever opening
a file for writing.

This might break some setups, where, for example, /etc/keepalived.data
was a symbolic link to /home/fred/keepalived.data. If this was the case,
instead create a symbolic link from /home/fred/keepalived.data to
/tmp/keepalived.data, so that the file is still accessible via
/home/fred/keepalived.data.

There doesn't appear to be a way around this backward incompatibility,
since even checking if the pathname is a symbolic link prior to opening
for writing would create a race condition.

Signed-off-by: Quentin Armitage <quentin@armitage.org.uk>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t\tint fd = open(optarg, O_WRONLY | O_APPEND | O_CREAT, S_IRUSR | S_IWUSR | S_IRGRP | S_IROTH);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t\tint fd = open(optarg, O_WRONLY | O_APPEND | O_CREAT | O_NOFOLLOW, S_IRUSR | S_IWUSR | S_IRGRP | S_IROTH);']}
description: keepalived 2.0.8 didn't check for pathnames with symlinks when writing data to a temporary file upon a call to PrintData or PrintStats. This allowed local users to overwrite arbitrary files if fs.protected_symlinks is set to 0, as demonstrated by a symlink from /tmp/keepalived.data or /tmp/keepalived.stats to /etc/passwd.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function opens a config-test log file for write with O_CREAT/O_APPEND; the demonstrated issue is symlink-following allowing arbitrary file overwrite (a file-write/tampering weakness), not exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor as required by CWE-200.

commit_msg:
patch 9.0.0389: crash when 'tagfunc' closes the window

Problem:    Crash when 'tagfunc' closes the window.
Solution:   Bail out when the window was closed.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t    // A tag function may do anything, which may cause various', '\t    // information to become invalid.  At least check for the tagstack', '\t    // to still be the same.', '\t    if (tagstack != curwin->w_tagstack)', '\t    {', '\t\temsg(_(e_window_unexpectedly_close_while_searching_for_tags));', '\t\tFreeWild(new_num_matches, new_matches);', '\t\tbreak;', '\t    }', '']}
description: Use After Free in GitHub repository vim/vim prior to 9.0.0389.

code_evidence: do_tag caches pointers into the current window's tagstack: tagstack = curwin->w_tagstack, with tagstackidx/tagstacklen snapshotted at entry.
find_tags is invoked while a 'tagfunc' may run; a tag function can close the window, invalidating curwin and freeing the tagstack buffer that tagstack still points to.
After find_tags returns, the stale cached tagstack pointer is dereferenced to store cur_match and cur_fnum, and again at line 439-440, writing into freed memory.
The tagstackidx/tagstacklen values also refer to the destroyed structure, so the loop continues using dangling state.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences and writes through a pointer to memory freed by the tagfunc-triggered window close, which is exactly CWE-416 (use after free). This is not merely a null-pointer or bounds issue: the object is freed and then reused through a stale reference.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: do_tag caches curwin->w_tagstack in a local pointer and never revalidates it after calling find_tags, which can invoke a user 'tagfunc' that closes the window and frees the tagstack. Trigger: a tagfunc that closes the window during tag lookup. The subsequent writes through the stale tagstack pointer are a use-after-free, causing memory corruption or a crash; the added check bails out when the tagstack changed.
