commit_msg:
Handle overflow errors in malformed zchunk files

Thanks to Agostino Sarubbo of Gentoo for the heads up!

Signed-off-by: Jonathan Dieter <jdieter@gmail.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['        if((mp->buffer_len > mp->buffer_len + l) ||', '           (l > mp->buffer_len + l)) {', '            zck_log(ZCK_LOG_ERROR, "Integer overflow when extracting multipart data");', '            return 0;', '        }', '']}
description: zchunk before 1.3.2 has multiple integer overflows via malformed zchunk files to lib/comp/comp.c, lib/comp/zstd/zstd.c, lib/dl/multipart.c, or lib/header.c.

code_evidence: Line 9 checks mp->buffer and line 10 computes mp->buffer_len + l as the zrealloc size; both operands are size_t, so a malformed large l or accumulated buffer_len can wrap the sum.
Line 15 copies l bytes to buf + mp->buffer_len and line 16 recomputes mp->buffer_len + l, reusing the same unchecked addition that determined the allocation size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function's allocation and copy length derive from an unchecked size_t addition, exactly the integer wraparound pattern of CWE-190; the resulting undersized buffer then causes an out-of-bounds write. A pure buffer-overflow label would miss the arithmetic root cause, so the target CWE fits.

evidence_lines.code:
if(mp->buffer) {
buf = zrealloc(mp->buffer, mp->buffer_len + l);

memcpy(buf + mp->buffer_len, b, l);
l = mp->buffer_len + l;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the size calculation mp->buffer_len + l is performed without an overflow check before allocation and copy. Trigger: attacker-controlled multipart data yields a large l that wraps the sum to a small value, so zrealloc allocates too little and memcpy writes l bytes past it. Supported consequence: heap memory corruption, with possible crash or code execution.

commit_msg:
DO NOT MERGE | libvpx: Cherry-pick 0f42d1f from upstream

Description from upstream:
vp8: fix decoder crash with invalid leading keyframes

decoding the same invalid keyframe twice would result in a crash as the
second time through the decoder would be assumed to have been
initialized as there was no resolution change. in this case the
resolution was itself invalid (0x6), but vp8_peek_si() was only failing
in the case of 0x0.
invalid-vp80-00-comprehensive-018.ivf.2kf_0x6.ivf tests this case by
duplicating the first keyframe and additionally adds a valid one to
ensure decoding can resume without error.

Bug: 30593765
Change-Id: I0de85f5a5eb5c0a5605230faf20c042b69aea507
(cherry picked from commit fc0466b695dce03e10390101844caa374848d903)
(cherry picked from commit 1114575245cb9d2f108749f916c76549524f5136)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            if (!(si->h | si->w))', '                res = VPX_CODEC_UNSUP_BITSTREAM;'], 'added_lines': ['            if (!(si->h && si->w))', '                res = VPX_CODEC_CORRUPT_FRAME;']}
description: A remote denial of service vulnerability in libvpx in Mediaserver in Android 4.x before 4.4.4, 5.0.x before 5.0.2, 5.1.x before 5.1.1, and 6.x before 2016-11-01 could enable an attacker to use a specially crafted file to cause a device hang or reboot. This issue is rated as High due to the possibility of remote denial of service. Android ID: A-30593765.

code_evidence: The parser derives frame dimensions from attacker-controlled header bytes and stores them in si->w and si->h, then validates them with a bitwise OR: !(si->h | si->w). This rejects only the case where both dimensions are zero; a frame with one dimension zero and the other non-zero, such as the reported 0x6 width with zero height, passes validation and returns VPX_CODEC_OK.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function accepts malformed header-derived dimension values without correctly validating them, which is improper input validation (CWE-20): the derived width/height properties are not checked against the required non-zero constraint. The consequence is a DoS crash, consistent with the availability impact.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the dimension check uses OR instead of AND, so a zero width or zero height is not treated as invalid input. Trigger: a crafted keyframe whose header yields a zero dimension but non-zero other dimension is accepted as a valid stream. Consequence: the decoder proceeds assuming a valid resolution, leading to a crash and remote denial of service.

commit_msg:
When opening files for write, ensure they aren't symbolic links

Issue #1048 identified that if, for example, a non privileged user
created a symbolic link from /etc/keepalvied.data to /etc/passwd,
writing to /etc/keepalived.data (which could be invoked via DBus)
would cause /etc/passwd to be overwritten.

This commit stops keepalived writing to pathnames where the ultimate
component is a symbolic link, by setting O_NOFOLLOW whenever opening
a file for writing.

This might break some setups, where, for example, /etc/keepalived.data
was a symbolic link to /home/fred/keepalived.data. If this was the case,
instead create a symbolic link from /home/fred/keepalived.data to
/tmp/keepalived.data, so that the file is still accessible via
/home/fred/keepalived.data.

There doesn't appear to be a way around this backward incompatibility,
since even checking if the pathname is a symbolic link prior to opening
for writing would create a race condition.

Signed-off-by: Quentin Armitage <quentin@armitage.org.uk>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tfile = fopen ("/tmp/keepalived.json","w");'], 'added_lines': ['\tfile = fopen_safe("/tmp/keepalived.json", "w");']}
description: keepalived 2.0.8 didn't check for pathnames with symlinks when writing data to a temporary file upon a call to PrintData or PrintStats. This allowed local users to overwrite arbitrary files if fs.protected_symlinks is set to 0, as demonstrated by a symlink from /tmp/keepalived.data or /tmp/keepalived.stats to /etc/passwd.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function only writes keepalived state to /tmp/keepalived.json; the demonstrated issue is symlink-following that enables arbitrary file overwrite (CWE-59/732), not exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor, so the target CWE-200 is not directly supported.

Fixes #52

description: There is an Assertion 'v->d.lval != v' failed at src/jsiValue.c in Jsish v3.5.0.

code_evidence: When v1 and v2 have different value types and are not both null/undefined, the function converts each operand with Jsi_ValueToNumberInt(interp, v1, 0) and Jsi_ValueToNumberInt(interp, v2, 0), storing the results in n1 and n2, then computes r = (n2 - n1). The assertion failure in the report is 'v->d.lval != v' inside src/jsiValue.c, which is the conversion path these calls enter for mismatched value types.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function directly drives execution into an assert-bearing conversion routine from an ordinary comparison of two differently typed values, so an attacker-supplied input can reach the assertion and terminate the process. This is a reachable assertion (CWE-617) rather than a memory-safety defect; the crash is the consequence, not the cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the comparison path passes arbitrary, possibly cyclic or self-referential value objects into the number-conversion routine without any prior type guard beyond the vt mismatch check. Trigger: comparing two values of differing types that are not both null/undefined. Supported consequence: the conversion routine reaches the reachable assertion and aborts the interpreter (DoS), matching the reported assertion failure.

!shared memory policy is not protected against parallel removal by other
thread which is normally protected by the mmap_sem.  do_get_mempolicy,

Early premature up_read is a historical artifact from times when

layering in the memory policy layer.").  but when we have the the
current mempolicy ref count model.  The issue was introduced
accordingly.

description: The do_get_mempolicy function in mm/mempolicy.c in the Linux kernel before 4.12.9 allows local users to cause a denial of service (use-after-free) or possibly have unspecified other impact via crafted system calls.

code_evidence: Under MPOL_F_ADDR, mmap_sem is taken read and pol is derived from vma->vm_policy or the vma get_policy callback while the lock is held.
The premature up_read(&current->mm->mmap_sem) plus vma=NULL releases the read lock before pol is consumed, so another thread can concurrently free the shared mempolicy.
The subsequent mpol_store_user_nodemask/get_policy_nodemask accesses read pol->w.user_nodemask after the lock was dropped, dereferencing possibly freed memory.
The out label's mpol_cond_put(pol) also touches the same pol after the lock is gone; the vma check only guards a second up_read, not pol lifetime.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences pol after the lock that protected its lifetime was released, which is exactly reuse of freed memory (CWE-416). It is not merely a race/locking flaw; the supported consequence is reading a freed object.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is dropping mmap_sem while a reference into the vma's shared mempolicy is still live. Trigger: a concurrent mbind/removal frees the policy between the premature up_read and the later nmask handling; the stale pol is then read, yielding a use-after-free and possible DoS or memory disclosure.

description: An issue was discovered in Poppler 0.74.0. There is a heap-based buffer over-read in the function Splash::blitTransparent at splash/Splash.cc.

code_evidence: The loop bounds are the caller-supplied h and w with no clamping against src dimensions; sp is formed from (ySrc + y) * src->rowSize + (xSrc >> 3) and dereferenced in the x loop, so large h/w or xSrc/ySrc near the edge read past src->data.
Mono8 case: sp = &src->data[(ySrc + y) * bitmap->rowSize + xSrc] and *sp++ reads w bytes per row for h rows, again unbounded by src size.
RGB8/BGR8 case reads three bytes per pixel from sp for x < w and y < h without checking that (ySrc + y) and (xSrc + x) remain inside the source bitmap.
The alpha loop writes memset(q, 0x00, w) into bitmap->alpha at (yDest + y) * bitmap->width + xDest, showing w/h are trusted blindly for both source and destination indexing.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe operation is a read of src->data beyond its allocated bounds, matching CWE-125 (out-of-bounds read). It is not a write overflow: the destination p is advanced in lockstep, but the primary defect is reading source memory past the end.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: blitTransparent trusts w and h and the xSrc/ySrc offsets, never verifying that the requested rectangle lies within src's allocated data. Trigger: a caller passing a width/height or source offset that extends beyond the source bitmap. Consequence: the per-pixel reads (*sp, *sp++) walk past the source buffer, producing a heap-based out-of-bounds read.

commit_msg:
Make `IsSimplifiableReshape` return `Status` instead of `bool`.

This is to allow remove `CHECK`-fails in subsequent commits.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 409160987
Change-Id: I3f050218a3832271395c4372a0b8ea05f1c03d80
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      !IsSimplifiableReshape(*node, properties)) {'], 'added_lines': ['      !IsSimplifiableReshape(*node, properties).ok()) {']}
description: Tensorflow is an Open Source Machine Learning Framework. The Grappler optimizer in TensorFlow can be used to cause a denial of service by altering a `SavedModel` such that `IsSimplifiableReshape` would trigger `CHECK` failures. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.8.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.7.1, TensorFlow 2.6.3, and TensorFlow 2.5.3, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: SimplifyReshape guards on use_shape_info and the presence of attr "T", then calls IsSimplifiableReshape(*node, properties) and converts its result to a boolean with the negation operator. In the pre-fix form this call returns bool; the commit message states the function previously contained CHECK-fails, meaning the assertion inside IsSimplifiableReshape is reachable through this call on an attacker-controlled node.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is a reachable assertion: a CHECK failure inside the called helper is triggered by attacker-supplied model data via this call site, causing process exit. The fix changes the helper to return Status and checks .ok(), confirming the assertion was the defect, which matches CWE-617 rather than a generic input-validation issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: this function invokes IsSimplifiableReshape, whose internal CHECK-based validation can fail on malformed SavedModel node attributes, and the caller does not catch or handle such failure. Trigger: a crafted graph reaches SimplifyReshape with a node whose shape/attribute data violates the assertion. Consequence: the CHECK aborts the process, causing denial of service.

commit_msg:
brcmfmac: avoid potential stack overflow in brcmf_cfg80211_start_ap()

User-space can choose to omit NL80211_ATTR_SSID and only provide raw
IE TLV data. When doing so it can provide SSID IE with length exceeding
the allowed size. The driver further processes this IE copying it
into a local variable without checking the length. Hence stack can be
corrupted and used as exploit.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # v4.7
Reported-by: Daxing Guo <freener.gdx@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Hante Meuleman <hante.meuleman@broadcom.com>
Reviewed-by: Pieter-Paul Giesberts <pieter-paul.giesberts@broadcom.com>
Reviewed-by: Franky Lin <franky.lin@broadcom.com>
Signed-off-by: Arend van Spriel <arend.vanspriel@broadcom.com>
Signed-off-by: Kalle Valo <kvalo@codeaurora.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tif (!ssid_ie)'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (!ssid_ie || ssid_ie->len > IEEE80211_MAX_SSID_LEN)']}
description: Stack-based buffer overflow in the brcmf_cfg80211_start_ap function in drivers/net/wireless/broadcom/brcm80211/brcmfmac/cfg80211.c in the Linux kernel before 4.7.5 allows local users to cause a denial of service (system crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a long SSID Information Element in a command to a Netlink socket.

code_evidence: Lines 35-40 handle the branch where user-space omits settings->ssid and instead supplies raw beacon head data; brcmf_parse_tlvs extracts an SSID TLV whose length is attacker-controlled. Line 41 only checks that the TLV exists, then line 43 memcpy copies ssid_ie->len bytes into the fixed-size stack buffer ssid_le.SSID without any bound check, and line 44 records that length.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked memcpy writes past the intended bounds of a stack buffer, an out-of-bounds write within a memory buffer, which is the core of CWE-119. The more specific CWE-121 (stack-based buffer overflow) is a child of CWE-119 and describes the same root cause; CWE-119 is the supplied target and fits the out-of-bounds write operation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the SSID IE length from the raw IE TLV is copied into the fixed-size local ssid_le.SSID buffer with no size validation. Trigger: a Netlink start-AP command omitting NL80211_ATTR_SSID but carrying an SSID IE longer than the buffer. Consequence: stack memory beyond ssid_le.SSID is overwritten, corrupting the stack and potentially enabling code execution or a crash.

commit_msg:
read_boot(): Handle excessive FAT size specifications

The variable used for storing the FAT size (in bytes) was an unsigned
int. Since the size in sectors read from the BPB was not sufficiently
checked, this could end up being zero after multiplying it with the
sector size while some offsets still stayed excessive. Ultimately it
would cause segfaults when accessing FAT entries for which no memory
was allocated.

Make it more robust by changing the types used to store FAT size to
off_t and abort if there is no room for data clusters. Additionally
check that FAT size is not specified as zero.

Fixes #25 and fixes #26.

Reported-by: Hanno Böck
Signed-off-by: Andreas Bombe <aeb@debian.org>

description: The read_boot function in boot.c in dosfstools before 4.0 allows attackers to cause a denial of service (crash) via a crafted filesystem, which triggers a heap-based buffer overflow in the (1) read_fat function or an out-of-bounds heap read in (2) get_fat function.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The shown function dump_boot only formats and prints boot-sector fields; the excessive FAT size handling, allocation, and out-of-bounds FAT access occur in read_boot/read_fat/get_fat, not in this function.

commit_msg:
Fix #350 - memory leak on exit

This fixes CVE-2018-18443, the last thread pool provider set into the
pool was not being correctly cleaned up at shutdown of the thread pool.

Signed-off-by: Kimball Thurston <kdt3rd@gmail.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    delete provider;', '    delete p;']}
description: OpenEXR 2.3.0 has a memory leak in ThreadPool in IlmBase/IlmThread/IlmThreadPool.cpp, as demonstrated by exrmultiview.

code_evidence: Both destructor branches call finish() on the thread pool provider but never free it: the CXX03 path uses provider->finish() at line 4 with no delete, and the atomic path loads the pointer into p and calls p->finish() at line 7 with no delete.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-772 covers failing to release a resource after its effective lifetime ends. Here the provider's lifetime ends when Data is destroyed, yet no delete occurs in either branch, so the allocated resource is abandoned. This is a missing-release weakness rather than a use-after-free, since the pointer is simply not freed.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The provider object is allocated and stored into the ThreadPool::Data, but the destructor only shuts it down (finish) and drops the pointer without releasing the allocation. When the Data is destroyed at thread-pool shutdown, the provider's memory is never freed, causing a memory leak; the leak is triggered by the normal destruction path exercised on exit.

commit_msg:
(for 4.9.3) CVE-2018-14468/FRF.16: Add a missing length check.

The specification says in a well-formed Magic Number information element
the data is exactly 4 bytes long. In mfr_print() check this before trying
to read those 4 bytes.

This fixes a buffer over-read discovered by Bhargava Shastry,
SecT/TU Berlin.

Add a test using the capture file supplied by the reporter(s).
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['                /* FRF.16.1 Section 3.4.3 Magic Number Information Element */', '                if (ie_len != 4) {', '                    ND_PRINT((ndo, "(invalid length)"));', '                    break;', '                }']}
description: The FRF.16 parser in tcpdump before 4.9.3 has a buffer over-read in print-fr.c:mfr_print().

code_evidence: In the MFR_CTRL_IE_MAGIC_NUM case, the code calls EXTRACT_32BITS(tptr), which unconditionally reads 4 bytes from tptr regardless of the information element's declared data length.

Before the switch, ie_len is reduced by the TLV header size (ie_len -= sizeof(struct ie_tlv_header_t)), so ie_len reflects the remaining data length; the magic-number branch does not verify that this remaining length is at least 4 bytes before the 32-bit read.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because EXTRACT_32BITS(tptr) reads 4 bytes when fewer are valid, exceeding the intended buffer bounds. It is an out-of-bounds read, not an out-of-bounds write, since no data is stored past the buffer.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the magic-number branch reads a fixed 4-byte value without checking that the IE data length is 4. Trigger: a crafted FRF.16 control frame with a Magic Number IE whose data length is less than 4 bytes. Consequence: EXTRACT_32BITS reads past the end of the intended element/buffer, an out-of-bounds read.

commit_msg:

description: PJSIP is a free and open source multimedia communication library written in C. In versions of PJSIP prior to 2.13 the PJSIP parser, PJMEDIA RTP decoder, and PJMEDIA SDP parser are affeced by a buffer overflow vulnerability. Users connecting to untrusted clients are at risk. This issue has been patched and is available as commit c4d3498 in the master branch and will be included in releases 2.13 and later. Users are advised to upgrade. There are no known workarounds for this issue.

code_evidence: Line 4 points s at scanner->curptr and line 5 aliases dst to the same buffer; line 8 dereferences *s without first confirming the scanner is not at EOF, so an empty input yields an out-of-bounds read/write decision.

The do-loop writes decoded bytes through dst while s advances; line 15's bound s+3 <= scanner->end is checked only for the '%' branch, and the spec-matching branch (lines 28-34) advances s and memmoves data without any end bound, allowing copies past scanner->end.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-120 fits because the function copies input bytes to a destination without checking the input size against the buffer end, producing a classic buffer copy overflow. The out-of-bounds read aspect overlaps CWE-125, but the dominant unsafe write/copy behavior supports CWE-120.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the unescape loop copies and decodes characters from s into the same buffer using dst without validating that s remains within scanner->end. Trigger: a '%' escape near the buffer end or a spec-matching run reaching EOF makes s advance past end; the subsequent *s reads and pj_memmove/dst writes corrupt adjacent memory, yielding out-of-bounds access and potential code execution.

description: nanosvg library nanosvg after commit c1f6e209c16b18b46aa9f45d7e619acf42c29726 is affected by: Buffer Overflow. The impact is: Memory corruption leading to at least DoS. More severe impact vectors need more investigation. The component is: it's part of a svg processing library. function nsvg__parseColorRGB in src/nanosvg.h / line 1227. The attack vector is: It depends library usage. If input is passed from the network, then network connectivity is enough. Most likely an attack will require opening a specially crafted .svg file.

code_evidence: The function reads three integers and two bracketed tokens from the SVG color string via sscanf at line 5, but the bracket scans write into fixed 32-byte buffers s1 and s2 (line 4) with no width limit. The %[...] conversion has no field-width specifier, so an arbitrarily long run of matching characters (digits, '%', comma, space, tab) is copied into s1/s2, overflowing the 32-byte stack arrays.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The write past the end of the intended 32-byte buffer is exactly an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). This is the write-side consequence of the missing field-width limit; it is not merely an unbounded read, since the overflowed destination is the stack buffer.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: unbounded %[...] sscanf conversions into fixed-size stack buffers. Trigger: a crafted rgb(...) color string containing a long run of matching characters causes sscanf to write past s1 or s2, corrupting adjacent stack memory; the consequence is memory corruption and at least a crash/DoS.

description: The tinygltf library uses the C library function wordexp() to perform file path expansion on untrusted paths that are provided from the input file. This function allows for command injection by using backticks. An attacker could craft an untrusted path input that would result in a path expansion. We recommend upgrading to 2.6.0 or past commit 52ff00a38447f06a17eab1caa2cf0730a119c751

code_evidence: The function builds quoted_path by wrapping the externally supplied filepath in double quotes ([20]) and passes it to wordexp() ([21]) without escaping backticks, $(), or other shell-special elements that survive inside double quotes.
The result of word expansion is read from p.we_wordv[0] ([27]) and returned via s ([15],[33]); the only guard is an empty-path check ([17]) and a non-zero return fallback ([22]-[24]).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-77 fits because externally influenced input is incorporated into a command-language string (wordexp's shell-like expansion) without neutralizing special elements, allowing unauthorized commands to execute. This is command injection through a non-OS-shell expansion API rather than direct system() invocation (CWE-78).

evidence_lines.code:
std::string s;
return s;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: untrusted filepath content (a glTF URI) is handed to wordexp(), which performs shell-like expansion including command substitution. Trigger: a path containing backticks or $(...) reaches ExpandFilePath on non-Windows/non-mobile builds. Consequence: attacker-controlled commands embedded in the path can be executed during expansion, yielding command injection; the returned string is merely the expanded result, not the cause.

commit_msg:
net/llc: avoid BUG_ON() in skb_orphan()

It seems nobody used LLC since linux-3.12.

Fortunately fuzzers like syzkaller still know how to run this code,
otherwise it would be no fun.

Setting skb->sk without skb->destructor leads to all kinds of
bugs, we now prefer to be very strict about it.

Ideally here we would use skb_set_owner() but this helper does not exist yet,
only CAN seems to have a private helper for that.

Fixes: 376c7311bdb6 ("net: add a temporary sanity check in skb_orphan()")
Signed-off-by: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Reported-by: Andrey Konovalov <andreyknvl@google.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

description: The LLC subsystem in the Linux kernel before 4.9.13 does not ensure that a certain destructor exists in required circumstances, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (BUG_ON) or possibly have unspecified other impact via crafted system calls.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function's bug is a missing skb->destructor/ownership invariant when assigning skb->sk (leading to BUG_ON in skb_orphan), not improper validation of input data properties required by CWE-20.

description: wolfcrypt/src/ecc.c in wolfSSL before 3.15.1.patch allows a memory-cache side-channel attack on ECDSA signatures, aka the Return Of the Hidden Number Problem or ROHNP. To discover an ECDSA key, the attacker needs access to either the local machine or a different virtual machine on the same physical host.

code_evidence: The signing loop computes s = (e + x.r)/k using the ephemeral nonce k from wc_ecc_make_key_ex; mp_invmod at [163] and the subsequent modular multiplications at [165,167,171] operate on values derived directly from k.

k is generated by wc_ecc_make_key_ex at [149] with no blinding or randomization between the nonce and its use in the modular arithmetic, so the operations at [163-171] are performed on unblinded secret-dependent values.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The target CWE-200 covers exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor; here the private ECDSA key is the sensitive secret leaked through cache side-channel observation of unblinded nonce arithmetic. The weakness is an information exposure rooted in missing blinding during signing.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the ECDSA signing path uses the raw ephemeral nonce k in scalar/modular operations without blinding. Trigger: an attacker with local or co-resident VM access observes memory-cache behavior during these operations. Supported consequence: the nonce and thus the private key can be recovered, exposing the long-term signing key (ROHNP).

readelf: Update check for invalid word offsets in ARM unwind information.

	PR binutils/21343
	* readelf.c (get_unwind_section_word): Fix snafu checking for
	invalid word offsets in ARM unwind information.
diff_func:
--- func_before
+++ func_after
@@ -72,9 +72,9 @@
     return FALSE;
 
   /* If the offset is invalid then fail.  */
-  if (word_offset > (sec->sh_size - 4)
-      /* PR 18879 */
-      || (sec->sh_size < 5 && word_offset >= sec->sh_size)
+  if (/* PR 21343 *//* PR 18879 */
+      sec->sh_size < 4
+      || word_offset > (sec->sh_size - 4)
       || ((bfd_signed_vma) word_offset) < 0)
     return FALSE;
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  if (word_offset > (sec->sh_size - 4)', '      /* PR 18879 */', '      || (sec->sh_size < 5 && word_offset >= sec->sh_size)'], 'added_lines': ['  if (/* PR 21343 *//* PR 18879 */', '      sec->sh_size < 4', '      || word_offset > (sec->sh_size - 4)']}
description: GNU Binutils 2.28 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (heap-based buffer over-read and application crash) via a crafted ELF file, related to the byte_get_little_endian function in elfcomm.c, the get_unwind_section_word function in readelf.c, and ARM unwind information that contains invalid word offsets.

code_evidence: Guard rejects word_offset only when word_offset > (sec->sh_size - 4) or (sec->sh_size < 5 && word_offset >= sec->sh_size). For a section with sh_size between 1 and 4, sh_size - 4 underflows as unsigned, so the first comparison is not triggered and word_offset in [0, sh_size-1] passes.
word_offset then indexes arm_sec->data and byte_get reads 4 bytes unconditionally, beyond the sh_size-sized buffer when sh_size < 4.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads 4 bytes from arm_sec->data at a word_offset that can exceed the allocated section data for small sh_size, which is an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). It is not a write or integer-overflow-only issue; the supported impact is memory read past the buffer.

evidence_lines.code: word = byte_get (arm_sec->data + word_offset, 4);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is the unchecked unsigned subtraction (sec->sh_size - 4) combined with a size guard that only handles sh_size < 5 via a separate, insufficient condition, allowing a small section size to admit a 4-byte read past the buffer. Trigger: crafted ARM unwind section with sh_size < 4 and a valid word_offset. Consequence: heap-based out-of-bounds read and crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
Fix handling of symbolic link ACLs

On Linux ACLs on symbolic links are not supported.
We must avoid calling acl_set_file() on symbolic links as their
targets are modified instead.

While here, do not try to set default ACLs on non-directories.

Fixes #1565
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\tret = set_acl(a, fd, name, abstract_acl,', '\t\t\tret = set_acl(a, fd, name, abstract_acl,'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\tret = set_acl(a, fd, name, abstract_acl, mode,', '\t\t\tret = set_acl(a, fd, name, abstract_acl, mode,']}
description: An improper link resolution flaw while extracting an archive can lead to changing the access control list (ACL) of the target of the link. An attacker may provide a malicious archive to a victim user, who would trigger this flaw when trying to extract the archive. A local attacker may use this flaw to change the ACL of a file on the system and gain more privileges.

code_evidence: When POSIX1E access ACLs are present, set_acl is invoked with fd, name, and abstract_acl but no mode argument, so the callee cannot distinguish a symbolic link from its target.
The default-ACL branch likewise calls set_acl without mode, allowing ACL application to non-directories or symlink targets rather than the intended entry.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-59 fits because the function accesses a file by name and fails to prevent that name from resolving through a symbolic link to an unintended resource. The missing mode argument is the specific constraint that would block link following.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the ACL-setting calls omit the entry mode, preventing set_acl from refusing symlinks and non-directory default ACLs. Trigger: extracting an archive whose entry is a symbolic link with ACL metadata. Consequence: the ACL of the link's target is modified instead of the link, enabling privilege escalation via altered access control.

commit_msg:
virtio: properly validate address before accessing config

There are several several issues in the current checking:

- The check was based on the minus of unsigned values which can overflow
- It was done after .{set|get}_config() which can lead crash when config_len
  is zero since vdev->config is NULL

Fix this by:

- Validate the address in virtio_pci_config_{read|write}() before
  .{set|get}_config
- Use addition instead minus to do the validation

description: A flaw was found in the way qemu v1.3.0 and later (virtio-rng) validates addresses when guest accesses the config space of a virtio device. If the virtio device has zero/small sized config space, such as virtio-rng, a privileged guest user could use this flaw to access the matching host's qemu address space and thus increase their privileges on the host.

Walk the entire DefaultRoot path, checking for symlinks of any component,
when AllowChrootSymlinks is disabled.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        struct stat st;', '        pr_fs_clear_cache2(path);', '        res = pr_fsio_lstat(path, &st);', '          xerrno = errno;', '          pr_log_pri(PR_LOG_WARNING, "error: unable to check %s: %s", path,', '            strerror(xerrno));', '', '          errno = xerrno;', '          return -1;', '        }', '', '        if (S_ISLNK(st.st_mode)) {', '          pr_log_pri(PR_LOG_WARNING,', '            "error: DefaultRoot %s is a symlink (denied by AllowChrootSymlinks "', '            "config)", path);'], 'added_lines': ['        res = is_symlink_path(p, path, pathlen);', '          if (errno == EPERM) {', '            pr_log_pri(PR_LOG_WARNING, "error: DefaultRoot %s is a symlink "', '              "(denied by AllowChrootSymlinks config)", path);', '          }']}
description: ProFTPD before 1.3.5e and 1.3.6 before 1.3.6rc5 controls whether the home directory of a user could contain a symbolic link through the AllowChrootSymlinks configuration option, but checks only the last path component when enforcing AllowChrootSymlinks. Attackers with local access could bypass the AllowChrootSymlinks control by replacing a path component (other than the last one) with a symbolic link. The threat model includes an attacker who is not granted full filesystem access by a hosting provider, but can reconfigure the home directory of an FTP user.

code_evidence: When allow_symlinks is FALSE, the code builds the DefaultRoot path string and calls pr_fsio_lstat(path,&st) only on that full path, then rejects only if S_ISLNK(st.st_mode) is true for the final component. Intermediate path components are never inspected for symbolic links.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function accesses a file path without properly preventing a link in a path component from resolving to an unintended resource, matching CWE-59 link following. It is not merely a TOCTOU race; the missing per-component check is the direct weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the AllowChrootSymlinks enforcement checks only the last path component via a single lstat. Trigger: a user-controlled DefaultRoot path whose intermediate directory is replaced by a symlink. Consequence: the symlink check passes while the resolved chroot escapes the intended directory, bypassing the protection mechanism.

commit_msg: Prevent HTTP pipelining which Crow doesn't support.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['            message_complete = false;', '            state = CROW_NEW_MESSAGE();']}
description: HTTP applications (servers) based on Crow through 1.0+4 may allow a Use-After-Free and code execution when HTTP pipelining is used. The HTTP parser supports HTTP pipelining, but the asynchronous Connection layer is unaware of HTTP pipelining. Specifically, the Connection layer is unaware that it has begun processing a later request before it has finished processing an earlier request.

code_evidence: clear() resets req, header_field, header_value, header_building_state and qs_point but does not reset message_complete or set state to CROW_NEW_MESSAGE(); the parser's completion/state flags persist across a reset.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing reset of message_complete/state enables processing a later request before the earlier one finishes, leading to access of freed request data — matching CWE-416 (use after free). A mere logic/state desync (CWE-843 or CWE-444) is the trigger, not the supported consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the reset routine clears per-request fields but leaves the message-complete flag and parser state untouched, so after a request completes the parser can treat the next pipelined request as already complete and begin processing it while the earlier request is still in flight. The Connection layer then frees/reuses the earlier request's resources, and later accesses via the stale request/connection state become use-after-free, supporting memory corruption or code execution.

commit_msg:
This patch adds code to check HCI_UART_PROTO_READY flag before
accessing hci_uart->proto. It fixes the race condition in
hci_uart_tty_ioctl() between HCIUARTSETPROTO and HCIUARTGETPROTO.
This issue bug found by Yu Hao and Weiteng Chen:

BUG: general protection fault in hci_uart_tty_ioctl [1]

The information of C reproducer can also reference the link [2]

Reported-by: Yu Hao <yhao016@ucr.edu>
Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/all/CA+UBctC3p49aTgzbVgkSZ2+TQcqq4fPDO7yZitFT5uBPDeCO2g@mail.gmail.com/ [1]
Reported-by: Weiteng Chen <wchen130@ucr.edu>
Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/lkml/CA+UBctDPEvHdkHMwD340=n02rh+jNRJNNQ5LBZNA+Wm4Keh2ow@mail.gmail.com/T/ [2]
Signed-off-by: "Lee, Chun-Yi" <jlee@suse.com>
Signed-off-by: Luiz Augusto von Dentz <luiz.von.dentz@intel.com>
diff_func:
--- func_before
+++ func_after
@@ -21,7 +21,8 @@
 		break;
 
 	case HCIUARTGETPROTO:
-		if (test_bit(HCI_UART_PROTO_SET, &hu->flags))
+		if (test_bit(HCI_UART_PROTO_SET, &hu->flags) &&
+		    test_bit(HCI_UART_PROTO_READY, &hu->flags))
 			err = hu->proto->id;
 		else
 			err = -EUNATCH;
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tif (test_bit(HCI_UART_PROTO_SET, &hu->flags))'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (test_bit(HCI_UART_PROTO_SET, &hu->flags) &&', '\t\t    test_bit(HCI_UART_PROTO_READY, &hu->flags))']}
description: An issue was discovered in drivers/bluetooth/hci_ldisc.c in the Linux kernel 6.2. In hci_uart_tty_ioctl, there is a race condition between HCIUARTSETPROTO and HCIUARTGETPROTO. HCI_UART_PROTO_SET is set before hu->proto is set. A NULL pointer dereference may occur.

code_evidence: HCIUARTSETPROTO uses test_and_set_bit(HCI_UART_PROTO_SET) to claim the flag, then calls hci_uart_set_proto(hu, arg); hu->proto is only assigned inside that call, so the flag is set before hu->proto becomes non-NULL.

HCIUARTGETPROTO only tests HCI_UART_PROTO_SET and then dereferences hu->proto->id; there is no synchronization with the concurrent setter, so the getter can observe the flag set while hu->proto is still NULL.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This is a race condition: the shared hu->flags and hu->proto state is accessed by concurrent ioctl sequences without exclusive access, violating atomicity of the set-then-publish sequence. It is not merely a NULL check omission; the missing constraint is synchronization between the two ioctl handlers.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The setter publishes HCI_UART_PROTO_SET before hu->proto is initialized, and the getter relies on that flag alone as a readiness indicator. A concurrent HCIUARTGETPROTO call between test_and_set_bit and the protocol assignment passes the check and dereferences a NULL hu->proto, producing a crash/DoS.

commit_msg: More fixes for the CVE-2019-14745
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t\t\t\t\tr_cons_printf ("k bin/pe/%s/%d=%s.%s\\n",', '\t\t\t\t\t\t\tr_cons_printf ("k bin/pe/%s/%d=%s\\n",'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t\t\t\t\tr_cons_printf ("\\"k bin/pe/%s/%d=%s.%s\\"\\n",', '\t\t\t\t\t\t\tr_cons_printf ("\\"k bin/pe/%s/%d=%s\\"\\n",']}
description: In radare2 before 3.9.0, a command injection vulnerability exists in bin_symbols() in libr/core/cbin.c. By using a crafted executable file, it's possible to execute arbitrary shell commands with the permissions of the victim. This vulnerability is due to an insufficient fix for CVE-2019-14745 and improper handling of symbol names embedded in executables.

code_evidence: The PE branch copies the attacker-controlled symbol name into module (185), splits it at '.dll_' (186), filters the suffix into symname (188), and then emits a radare2 command with r_cons_printf (192-196). The module and symname values are only passed through __filterShell, which is shown to be an insufficient fix, and are interpolated into a command string without quoting in this before-version. The patch later adds surrounding quotes, confirming the unquoted interpolation is the flaw.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-78 fits because externally influenced symbol names are used to construct part of an OS command that is not properly neutralized, allowing special elements to modify the intended command. This is command injection rather than mere output corruption because the constructed string is consumed as a command.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: symbol-name text from a crafted executable is embedded into a generated 'k bin/pe/...' command without neutralizing command separators. Trigger: a malicious PE symbol name containing shell metacharacters reaches this branch, so the produced command is interpreted by a downstream shell. Consequence: arbitrary command execution with the victim's privileges.

commit_msg:
pagemap: do not leak physical addresses to non-privileged userspace

As pointed by recent post[1] on exploiting DRAM physical imperfection,
/proc/PID/pagemap exposes sensitive information which can be used to do
attacks.

This disallows anybody without CAP_SYS_ADMIN to read the pagemap.

[1] http://googleprojectzero.blogspot.com/2015/03/exploiting-dram-rowhammer-bug-to-gain.html

[ Eventually we might want to do anything more finegrained, but for now
  this is the simple model.   - Linus ]

Signed-off-by: Kirill A. Shutemov <kirill.shutemov@linux.intel.com>
Acked-by: Konstantin Khlebnikov <khlebnikov@openvz.org>
Acked-by: Andy Lutomirski <luto@amacapital.net>
Cc: Pavel Emelyanov <xemul@parallels.com>
Cc: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>
Cc: Mark Seaborn <mseaborn@chromium.org>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
diff_func:
--- func_before
+++ func_after
@@ -1,5 +1,8 @@
 static int pagemap_open(struct inode *inode, struct file *file)
 {
+	/* do not disclose physical addresses: attack vector */
+	if (!capable(CAP_SYS_ADMIN))
+		return -EPERM;
 	pr_warn_once("Bits 55-60 of /proc/PID/pagemap entries are about "
 			"to stop being page-shift some time soon. See the "
 			"linux/Documentation/vm/pagemap.txt for details.\n");
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t/* do not disclose physical addresses: attack vector */', '\tif (!capable(CAP_SYS_ADMIN))', '\t\treturn -EPERM;']}
description: The pagemap_open function in fs/proc/task_mmu.c in the Linux kernel before 3.19.3, as used in Android 6.0.1 before 2016-03-01, allows local users to obtain sensitive physical-address information by reading a pagemap file, aka Android internal bug 25739721.

code_evidence: pagemap_open unconditionally emits a warning and returns 0, granting every opener of /proc/PID/pagemap access to the file with no capability check; the function contains no capable() call or permission gate before returning success.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-200 fits because the function explicitly governs access to a resource containing sensitive physical-address information yet allows unauthorized actors to open it, directly exposing that data. This is a missing authorization constraint on a sensitive-information resource, not merely a downstream confidentiality impact of another flaw.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the open handler returns 0 for any caller without verifying CAP_SYS_ADMIN, so unprivileged users obtain a pagemap file handle. Trigger: a local user opens /proc/PID/pagemap. Consequence: the file's physical-address metadata is exposed to unauthorized actors, enabling information disclosure and aiding attacks such as DRAM row-hammer exploitation.

commit_msg:
Tiffsep and Tiffsep1 - abort on multi-page input wtithout %d OutputFile

Bug #701821 "Segmentation fault at tiff//libtiff/tif_dirinfo.c:513 in TIFFFindField"

The tiffsep and tiffsep1 only set 'code' to an error when an attempt is
made to write a second output file without using %d in the OutputFile
specification.

This causes problems later when attempting to process the files. The
devices should exit without trying to further process the pages under
these conditions and this commit returns immediately on error.

The other devices like this already return immediately on error, it
looks like the code here was copied between  devices without realising
that the tiffsep and tiffsep1 devices didn't exit when the error
condition was set.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['       goto done;']}
description: A null pointer dereference vulnerability in devices/gdevtsep.c of Artifex Software GhostScript v9.50 allows a remote attacker to cause a denial of service via a crafted postscript file. This is fixed in v9.51.

code_evidence: Lines 36-41: when the parsed format is NULL and PageCount > 0, the code sets code to gs_error_ioerror but does not exit, falling through to file handling.
Lines 42-53: if tfdev->comp_file is NULL the composite file is opened; on failure at line 50 the function jumps to done, but the earlier error path did not prevent reaching this logic.
Lines 146-149: later processing unconditionally calls TIFFCheckpointDirectory(tfdev->tiff[comp_num]) and TIFFCheckpointDirectory(tfdev->tiff_comp), assuming those TIFF handles are non-NULL.
Lines 265-267: TIFFWriteDirectory is called on tfdev->tiff[comp_num] without checking the handle, which may be uninitialized/NULL after the earlier error.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences TIFF handle pointers (tfdev->tiff[comp_num], tfdev->tiff_comp) that can be NULL after the error condition is merely recorded, directly matching CWE-476. This is a null-pointer dereference, not merely improper error handling, since the consequence is a crash from dereferencing an invalid pointer.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the multi-page-without-%d error path only sets code and continues instead of returning. The function then proceeds to TIFF operations (TIFFCheckpointDirectory/TIFFWriteDirectory) on tfdev->tiff handles that may be NULL because separation files were never created, causing a NULL pointer dereference and crash (DoS).

commit_msg: Issue #1683: Avoid an edge case when handling unexpectedly formatted input text from client, caused by quote/backslash semantics, by skipping those semantics.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  char quote_mode = 0;', '  if (**cp == \'\\"\') {', '    quote_mode++;', '    (*cp)++;', "    if (**cp == '\\\\' && quote_mode) {", '', '        *dst = *(++(*cp));', '    ++(*cp);'], 'added_lines': ['  int quote_mode = FALSE;', '  if (!(flags & PR_STR_FL_IGNORE_QUOTES)) {', '    if (**cp == \'\\"\') {', '      quote_mode = TRUE;', '      (*cp)++;', '    }', "    if (**cp == '\\\\' &&", '        quote_mode == TRUE) {', '        *dst++ = *(++(*cp));', '        (*cp)++;', '        continue;', '    (*cp)++;']}
description: make_ftp_cmd in main.c in ProFTPD before 1.3.8a has a one-byte out-of-bounds read, and daemon crash, because of mishandling of quote/backslash semantics.

code_evidence: Inside the quoted-string loop, when **cp is a backslash and quote_mode is set, the code checks *((*cp)+1) for a following character. If the backslash is the last byte before the terminating NUL, the check fails and control falls through to line 36, which copies the backslash and advances; the subsequent loop condition then reads **cp at the NUL terminator. The escaped-character branch at line 33 also advances *cp via ++(*cp) but then line 36 re-copies and line 37 advances again, so pointer advancement around the escape handling is inconsistent with the copy.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads memory beyond the intended string buffer, matching CWE-125's out-of-bounds read. It is not CWE-787 because the observable defect is a read (and crash), not a write past the buffer.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the loop condition and escape handling advance/read *cp without a consistent bound check relative to the terminating NUL, so a quote/backslash sequence at the end of client-supplied text can drive a read one byte past the intended buffer. Trigger: an input ending in a backslash inside quote mode. Consequence: one-byte out-of-bounds read and daemon crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
net: mqtt: Improve buffer bounds validation in mqtt_read_message_chunk

Verify more strictly that data read from the transport fits into RX
buffer. Switch to unsigned integers, where possible, to prevent
unnecessary signed/unsigned operations.

Signed-off-by: Robert Lubos <robert.lubos@nordicsemi.no>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tint remaining;', '\tif (remaining <= 0) {', '\t\treturn 0;', '\t}', '\tif (buf->end + remaining > client->rx_buf + client->rx_buf_size) {', '\t\tMQTT_ERR("[CID %p]: Buffer too small to receive the message",'], 'added_lines': ['\tu32_t remaining;', '', '\t/* In case all data requested has already been buffered, return. */', '\tif (length <= (buf->end - buf->cur)) {', '\t\treturn 0;', '\t}', '\tif ((buf->end + remaining > client->rx_buf + client->rx_buf_size) ||', '\t    (buf->end + remaining < client->rx_buf)) {', '\t\tMQTT_ERR("[CID %p]: Read would exceed RX buffer bounds.",']}
description: In the Zephyr Project MQTT code, improper bounds checking can result in memory corruption and possibly remote code execution. NCC-ZEP-031 This issue affects: zephyrproject-rtos zephyr version 2.2.0 and later versions.

code_evidence: `remaining` is a signed `int` computed as `length - (buf->end - buf->cur)`; the guard `if (remaining <= 0)` only rejects non-positive values before the bounds check.
The check `buf->end + remaining > client->rx_buf + client->rx_buf_size` validates only the upper bound, then `mqtt_transport_read` writes `remaining` bytes into `buf->end`.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function copies transport input into the RX buffer without fully verifying that the copy size fits the destination, matching CWE-120's buffer-copy-without-size-check pattern. It is not merely an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) because the unchecked `remaining` controls a write into `buf->end`.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: a signed subtraction and an upper-bound-only check let a large `length` or inconsistent pointer arithmetic produce a `remaining` value that passes the guard while the destination region is not actually sized for it. Trigger: caller supplies a `length`/buffer state where the computed `remaining` overflows or the pointer sum wraps. Consequence: `mqtt_transport_read` writes past the RX buffer, corrupting memory.

commit_msg: fix static file serving security issue; fix url path encoding issue
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  os << prefix << "<file: " << path_.string() << ">" << std::endl;'], 'added_lines': ['  os << prefix << "<file: " << path_.u8string() << ">" << std::endl;']}
description: This affects the package sprinfall/webcc before 0.3.0. It is possible to traverse directories to fetch arbitrary files from the server.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function only formats a file path for diagnostic output; it performs no path resolution or file access and contains no external-input-to-pathname construction, so it does not support CWE-22.

commit_msg:
Fix NULL dereference triggered via dbus (#183)

Instead of crashing, print the following warning message and ignore it
when no current view exists.
dbus should not be called when there is no document open.

** (gobby-0.5:78328): WARNING **: 10:01:05.468: No current view exists.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tg_assert(m_current_view != NULL);'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (!m_current_view) {', '\t\tg_warning("No current view exists.");', '\t\treturn;', '\t}']}
description: Gobby 0.4.11 allows a NULL pointer dereference in the D-Bus handler for certain set_language calls.

code_evidence: Line 3 guards the function with only g_assert(m_current_view != NULL); in release builds assertions are typically compiled out, so execution proceeds into the active_user branch where m_current_view is dereferenced via get_session() (line 6) and get_text_buffer() (lines 10-11) without any runtime NULL check.

When active_user is non-NULL, the session/buffer derived from m_current_view feed the undo/redo/cut enabling calls (lines 12-19); if m_current_view is NULL these member calls dereference a NULL pointer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences m_current_view after relying on an assert rather than a runtime check, matching CWE-476 (NULL Pointer Dereference). This is not merely a missing-value check on a scalar; the concrete unsafe operation is a pointer dereference, so CWE-476 is the precise fit.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the only protection against a missing current view is an assert, which does not enforce the invariant in production builds. Trigger: on_active_user_changed fires with a non-NULL active_user while no document/view is open, so m_current_view is NULL. Consequence: NULL dereference crash (DoS) when get_session/get_text_buffer are invoked on the NULL pointer.

commit_msg:
Made some changes to the I/O stream library for memory streams.
There were a number of potential problems due to the possibility
of integer overflow.
Changed some integral types to the larger types size_t or ssize_t.
For example, the function mem_resize now takes the buffer size parameter
as a size_t.
Added a new function jas_stream_memopen2, which takes a
buffer size specified as a size_t instead of an int.
This can be used in jas_image_cmpt_create to avoid potential
overflow problems.

Added a new function jas_deprecated to warn about reliance on
deprecated library behavior.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tint n;'], 'added_lines': ['\tssize_t n;']}
description: Multiple integer overflows in the (1) jas_realloc function in base/jas_malloc.c and (2) mem_resize function in base/jas_stream.c in JasPer before 1.900.22 allow remote attackers to cause a denial of service via a crafted image, which triggers use after free vulnerabilities.

code_evidence: Line 3 declares n as a signed int, but line 8 computes n = m->len_ - m->pos_ from stream length/position fields; if the subtraction wraps or the value exceeds int range, n is corrupted. Line 9 clamps cnt = JAS_MIN(n, cnt), then line 10 memcpy uses that cnt as the byte count and line 11 advances m->pos_ by it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is an integer overflow/wraparound in a size computation (len_ - pos_) that feeds a memory copy, matching CWE-190. The patch widening n to ssize_t confirms the narrow-type overflow; this is not merely an out-of-bounds read, since the defect originates in the arithmetic.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the length/position difference is stored in a narrow signed int (line 3) and used directly as a copy size. Trigger: crafted stream metadata makes len_ - pos_ produce a wrapped/negative or oversized value that survives JAS_MIN. Consequence: memcpy with an attacker-influenced count reads out of bounds or copies too much, corrupting memory and possibly crashing.

commit_msg:
Avoid infinite loop in dos_load_ext_table(). (Fixes: #914)

If dos_load_ext_table() was called with a zero offset, the loop
would repeat the exact same conditions ad infinitum.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        if (part_size == 0)'], 'added_lines': ['        /* part_start == 0 would cause infinite recursion */', '        if (part_size == 0 || part_start == 0)']}
description: In The Sleuth Kit (TSK) 4.4.2, opening a crafted disk image triggers infinite recursion in dos_load_ext_table() in tsk/vs/dos.c in libtskvs.a, as demonstrated by mmls.

code_evidence: The loop over the four partition entries reads part_start from the on-disk table (line 51) and only skips entries when part_size == 0 (lines 58-59); a zero start with nonzero size is not filtered.

For an extended entry, the recursive call passes sect_ext_base + part_start as the new sector (lines 75-76), and the bound check at line 68 compares the same expression to max_addr but does not prevent a zero-offset recursion.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The recursive call re-enters with the same arguments and no reachable exit, matching CWE-835's unreachable exit condition. It is a recursion-driven infinite loop rather than a fixed-iteration loop, but the availability impact and missing progress constraint are the same.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the recursion guard omits part_start, so a crafted partition entry with start_sec == 0 and nonzero size causes dos_load_ext_table to call itself with an unchanged sector, repeating the identical state. Trigger: opening a malicious disk image. Consequence: unbounded recursion/CPU consumption (DoS), as reported with mmls.

commit_msg:
As the 'pkt_length' and 'offlen' can be malicious from guest,
the vrend_create_shader function has an integer overflow, this
will make the next 'memcpy' oob access. This patch avoid this.

Signed-off-by: Li Qiang <liq3ea@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Dave Airlie <airlied@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '      /*make sure no overflow */', '      if (pkt_length * 4 < pkt_length ||', '          pkt_length * 4 + sel->buf_offset < pkt_length * 4 ||', '          pkt_length * 4 + sel->buf_offset < sel->buf_offset) {', '            ret = EINVAL;', '            goto error;', '          }', '']}
description: Integer overflow in the vrend_create_shader function in vrend_renderer.c in virglrenderer before 0.6.0 allows local guest OS users to cause a denial of service (process crash) via crafted pkt_length and offlen values, which trigger an out-of-bounds access.

code_evidence: At line 54, the bound check computes pkt_length * 4 + sel->buf_offset and compares it to sel->buf_len, but pkt_length is a guest-controlled uint32_t. If pkt_length * 4 wraps (or the addition wraps), the computed value becomes small and the check passes.
Line 60 then uses the same wrapped offset expression as the destination for memcpy and copies pkt_length * 4 bytes, and line 61 advances sel->buf_offset with the wrapped value.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe operation is exactly an integer overflow/wraparound in a size calculation that is then used for a memory copy, matching CWE-190. The missing constraint is an overflow check before the arithmetic; this is the root cause, distinct from the resulting out-of-bounds write.

evidence_lines.code:
memcpy(sel->tmp_buf + sel->buf_offset, shd_text, pkt_length * 4);
sel->buf_offset += pkt_length * 4;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: pkt_length and sel->buf_offset are attacker-controlled 32-bit values, and the size/offset arithmetic at lines 54 and 60 is performed without overflow checks. Trigger: a crafted pkt_length (or continuation offset) makes pkt_length * 4 + sel->buf_offset wrap to a small value, so the length guard at line 54 is bypassed. Consequence: memcpy at line 60 writes out of bounds, leading to a crash/DoS and potentially memory corruption.

commit_msg: Fixes issue #741
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        markObject(&obj1, xRef, countRef, numOffset, oldRefNum, newRefNum);'], 'added_lines': ['        markObject(&obj1, xRef, countRef, numOffset, oldRefNum, newRefNum, alreadyMarkedDicts);']}
description: PDFDoc::markObject in PDFDoc.cc in Poppler 0.74.0 mishandles dict marking, leading to stack consumption in the function Dict::find() located at Dict.cc, which can (for example) be triggered by passing a crafted pdf file to the pdfunite binary.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function only performs recursive object marking and reference bookkeeping; no code writes to a buffer or computes an index/pointer into a buffer, so out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) is not supported by the shown lines.

commit_msg:
x86: extend get_platform_badpages() interface

Use a structure so along with an address (now frame number) an order can
also be specified.

This is part of XSA-282.

description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.11.x on Intel x86 platforms allowing guest OS users to cause a denial of service (host OS hang) because Xen does not work around Intel's mishandling of certain HLE transactions associated with the KACQUIRE instruction prefix.

code_evidence: get_platform_badpages() returns a pointer and count (array_size) that are used directly to iterate and read entries via *badpage without any bounds or validity check on the returned data.
The second loop similarly trusts hypervisor_reserved_pages() output, iterating array_size entries and dereferencing badpage each time.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The root cause is missing validation of externally provided input (the count and array contents from get_platform_badpages/hypervisor_reserved_pages) before it drives iteration, matching CWE-20's improper input validation. It is not a memory-safety defect in the loop itself but the absence of a check on the supplied data.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function consumes platform/hypervisor-supplied bad-page arrays without validating that array_size and the entries are well-formed before iterating and dereferencing them. An inconsistent or oversized returned count causes out-of-bounds reads of the badpage array, leading to the host hang/DoS described.

commit_msg:
If you export a subdirectory of a filesystem, a READDIRPLUS on the root
of that export will return the filehandle of the parent with the ".."
entry.

The filehandle is optional, so let's just not return the filehandle for
".." if we're at the root of an export.

Note that once the client learns one filehandle outside of the export,
they can trivially access the rest of the export using further lookups.

However, it is also not very difficult to guess filehandles outside of
the export.  So exporting a subdirectory of a filesystem should
considered equivalent to providing access to the entire filesystem.  To
avoid confusion, we recommend only exporting entire filesystems.

Reported-by: Youjipeng <wangzhibei1999@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: J. Bruce Fields <bfields@redhat.com>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Chuck Lever <chuck.lever@oracle.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t/* filesystem root - cannot return filehandle for ".." */'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t/*', '\t\t\t * Don\'t return filehandle for ".." if we\'re at', '\t\t\t * the filesystem or export root:', '\t\t\t */', '\t\t\t\tgoto out;', '\t\t\tif (dparent == exp->ex_path.dentry)']}
description: fs/nfsd/nfs3xdr.c in the Linux kernel through 5.10.8, when there is an NFS export of a subdirectory of a filesystem, allows remote attackers to traverse to other parts of the filesystem via READDIRPLUS. NOTE: some parties argue that such a subdirectory export is not intended to prevent this attack; see also the exports(5) no_subtree_check default behavior

code_evidence: For the ".." entry (namlen==2), dparent is the export root; dget_parent(dparent) yields the parent dentry outside the export. The only guard here is dchild == dparent (filesystem root), so at an export root that is not the filesystem root the outside dentry proceeds to fh_compose.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-22 fits because a pathname element ("..") escapes the restricted export directory and is not neutralized, resolving outside the intended parent. This is relative path traversal, not a mere information leak, since the escaped filehandle grants access beyond the export boundary.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the ".." handling only suppresses a filehandle at the filesystem root, not at the export root, so the parent-of-export dentry is encoded. Trigger: a remote READDIRPLUS on the root of a subdirectory export. Consequence: the client obtains a filehandle outside the exported subtree, enabling traversal to other parts of the filesystem.

commit_msg:
Since 3e135cd499bf ("netfilter: nft_dynset: dynamic stateful expression
instantiation"), it is possible to attach stateful expressions to set
elements.

cd5125d8f518 ("netfilter: nf_tables: split set destruction in deactivate
and destroy phase") introduces conditional destruction on the object to
accomodate transaction semantics.

nft_expr_init() calls expr->ops->init() first, then check for
NFT_STATEFUL_EXPR, this stills allows to initialize a non-stateful
lookup expressions which points to a set, which might lead to UAF since
the set is not properly detached from the set->binding for this case.
Anyway, this combination is non-sense from nf_tables perspective.

This patch fixes this problem by checking for NFT_STATEFUL_EXPR before
expr->ops->init() is called.

The reporter provides a KASAN splat and a poc reproducer (similar to
those autogenerated by syzbot to report use-after-free errors). It is
unknown to me if they are using syzbot or if they use similar automated
tool to locate the bug that they are reporting.

For the record, this is the KASAN splat.

[   85.431824] ==================================================================
[   85.432901] BUG: KASAN: use-after-free in nf_tables_bind_set+0x81b/0xa20
[   85.433825] Write of size 8 at addr ffff8880286f0e98 by task poc/776
[   85.434756]
[   85.434999] CPU: 1 PID: 776 Comm: poc Tainted: G        W         5.18.0+ #2
[   85.436023] Hardware name: QEMU Standard PC (i440FX + PIIX, 1996), BIOS 1.14.0-2 04/01/2014

Fixes: 0b2d8a7b638b ("netfilter: nf_tables: add helper functions for expression handling")
Reported-and-tested-by: Aaron Adams <edg-e@nccgroup.com>
Signed-off-by: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (!(expr->ops->type->flags & NFT_EXPR_STATEFUL))', '\t\tgoto err_set_elem_expr;', ''], 'added_lines': []}
description: net/netfilter/nf_tables_api.c in the Linux kernel through 5.18.1 allows a local user (able to create user/net namespaces) to escalate privileges to root because an incorrect NFT_STATEFUL_EXPR check leads to a use-after-free.

code_evidence: nft_expr_init(ctx, attr) is called before any flag validation, so the expression's ops->init() runs and may bind a set to a non-stateful lookup expression.
Only after init does the code check NFT_EXPR_STATEFUL; a non-stateful expression reaching line 11 is rejected and routed to err_set_elem_expr, but the set binding created during init is not detached.
The GC branch at lines 13-19 is also evaluated after init, confirming validation happens post-initialization rather than gating it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The stale set->binding left after the expression is destroyed is dereferenced later, matching CWE-416's reuse of freed memory. It is not merely a missing validation issue; the ordering flaw produces an actual dangling reference and subsequent invalid access.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the stateful-expression constraint is enforced after expr->ops->init() has already run. Trigger: a local user creates a lookup expression pointing to a set; init binds the set, then the flag check rejects the expression and nft_expr_destroy runs without properly detaching the set->binding. The stale binding is later accessed, yielding a use-after-free (KASAN write in nf_tables_bind_set), enabling privilege escalation.

commit_msg:
Snipped from commit 9ca9fb24d5febccea354089c41f96a8ad0d853f8 upstream.

While reworking the poll hashing in the v6.0 kernel, we ended up
grabbing the ctx->uring_lock in poll update/removal. This also fixed
a bug with linked timeouts racing with timeout expiry and poll
removal.

Bring back just the locking fix for that.

Reported-and-tested-by: Querijn Voet <querijnqyn@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

description:
A use-after-free vulnerability in the Linux Kernel io_uring subsystem can be exploited to achieve local privilege escalation.

Racing a io_uring cancel poll request with a linked timeout can cause a UAF in a hrtimer.

We recommend upgrading past commit ef7dfac51d8ed961b742218f526bd589f3900a59 (4716c73b188566865bdd79c3a6709696a224ac04 for 5.10 stable and 0e388fce7aec40992eadee654193cad345d62663 for 5.15 stable).

code_evidence: io_poll_find() locates preq under completion_lock, then io_poll_disarm(preq) removes it and the lock is dropped at line 13; preq is only a borrowed pointer, not a reference held across the unlock.

After the lock is released, preq is dereferenced and mutated (poll.events, user_data) and passed to io_poll_add()/io_req_complete() without any ctx->uring_lock serialization, so the poll entry can be concurrently removed/freed.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the function continues to read and write a poll request object after it has been disarmed and released to concurrent removal, i.e., it references memory that may already be freed. This is a lifetime/serialization defect, not merely a missing NULL check.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: poll update/removal is not serialized by ctx->uring_lock, so the preq located and disarmed under completion_lock can be concurrently cancelled or freed by another path (e.g. linked timeout expiry). Trigger: racing an io_uring cancel-poll request with a linked timeout. Consequence: the later accesses to preq at lines 16-27 use freed memory, yielding a use-after-free.

description: An integer overflow was discovered in pdf_read_new_xref_section in pdf/pdf-xref.c in Artifex MuPDF 1.11.

code_evidence: Only i0<0 and i1<0 are rejected; the sum i0+i1 is not checked for overflow before use.
i0 (fz_off_t) and i1 (int) are passed to pdf_xref_find_subsection, which sizes/allocates the xref table from these values.
The loop bound i < i0 + i1 recomputes the addition; a wrapped sum can make the bound small or negative, and table[i-i0] indexes using the same i0 offset.

for (i = i0; i < i0 + i1; i++)

commit_msg:
tools/xenstore: remove nodes owned by destroyed domain

In case a domain is removed from Xenstore, remove all nodes owned by
it per default.

This tackles the problem that nodes might be created by a domain
outside its home path in Xenstore, leading to Xenstore hogging more
and more memory. Domain quota don't work in this case if the guest is
rebooting in between.

Since XSA-322 ownership of such stale nodes is transferred to dom0,
which is helping against unintended access, but not against OOM of
Xenstore.

As a fallback for weird cases add a Xenstore start parameter for
keeping today's way to handle stale nodes, adding the risk of Xenstore
hitting an OOM situation.

This is part of XSA-419 / CVE-2022-42322.

Fixes: 496306324d8d ("tools/xenstore: revoke access rights for removed domains")
Signed-off-by: Juergen Gross <jgross@suse.com>
Reviewed-by: Julien Grall <jgrall@amazon.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (!conn)', '\tif (conn->transaction) {', '\t\td = (domid == conn->id && conn->domain) ? conn->domain'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (!node->perms.p)', '\tif (conn && conn->transaction) {', '\t\td = (conn && domid == conn->id && conn->domain) ? conn->domain']}
description: Xenstore: Cooperating guests can create arbitrary numbers of nodes T[his CNA information record relates to multiple CVEs; the text explains which aspects/vulnerabilities correspond to which CVE.] Since the fix of XSA-322 any Xenstore node owned by a removed domain will be modified to be owned by Dom0. This will allow two malicious guests working together to create an arbitrary number of Xenstore nodes. This is possible by domain A letting domain B write into domain A's local Xenstore tree. Domain B can then create many nodes and reboot. The nodes created by domain B will now be owned by Dom0. By repeating this process over and over again an arbitrary number of nodes can be created, as Dom0's number of nodes isn't limited by Xenstore quota.

code_evidence: The function early-returns when conn is NULL, so no accounting of the node's owning domain occurs for that call.

domid is derived from node->perms.p[0].id when perms exist, otherwise from conn->id; the domain entry counter d->nbentry is decremented only when a domain struct is found, and a missing domain triggers corrupt() rather than releasing the node's accounting.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is failure to release/track node resources after their effective lifetime, matching CWE-401's missing release causing resource-consumption DoS. It is not merely a quota bypass (CWE-770) because the core defect is unreleased accumulated node allocations, not a missing rate limit.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: node ownership accounting is tied to a live connection/domain lookup, so nodes whose owning domain is gone (or whose perms were transferred, e.g. to Dom0) are not decremented from the owning domain's entry count and are never released. Trigger: guests repeatedly create nodes outside their home path and reboot, transferring ownership; the stale nodes accumulate. Consequence: unbounded Xenstore memory consumption leading to OOM/DoS.

commit_msg:
Avoid integer overflows in SETRANGE and SORT (CVE-2022-35977) (#11720)

Authenticated users issuing specially crafted SETRANGE and SORT(_RO)
commands can trigger an integer overflow, resulting with Redis attempting
to allocate impossible amounts of memory and abort with an OOM panic.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    /* Perform LIMIT start,count sanity checking. */', '    start = (limit_start < 0) ? 0 : limit_start;'], 'added_lines': ['    /* Perform LIMIT start,count sanity checking.', '     * And avoid integer overflow by limiting inputs to object sizes. */', '    start = min(max(limit_start, 0), vectorlen);', '    limit_count = min(max(limit_count, -1), vectorlen);']}
description: Redis is an in-memory database that persists on disk. Authenticated users issuing specially crafted `SETRANGE` and `SORT(_RO)` commands can trigger an integer overflow, resulting with Redis attempting to allocate impossible amounts of memory and abort with an out-of-memory (OOM) panic. The problem is fixed in Redis versions 7.0.8, 6.2.9 and 6.0.17. Users are advised to upgrade. There are no known workarounds for this vulnerability.

code_evidence: limit_start and limit_count are attacker-controlled longs parsed from the LIMIT arguments into the long variables declared at line 5.

The old code only clamped negative start; start+limit_count-1 at line 111 and the end>=vectorlen check at line 116 compute in long, so a large limit_count can overflow end to a negative or tiny value.
vectorlen is then set from end-start+1 at line 121 and used to size the allocation at line 123, so the wrapped range feeds zmalloc.
outputlen at line 246 is derived from end-start+1 and drives reply/store sizing.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because attacker-controlled integers are combined (start+limit_count-1) without bounds, allowing wraparound that corrupts a size used for allocation. The fix clamps limit_start and limit_count to vectorlen, directly preventing the overflow rather than a separate logic error.

evidence_lines.code:
vectorlen = end-start+1;
vector = zmalloc(sizeof(redisSortObject)*vectorlen);
outputlen = getop ? getop*(end-start+1) : end-start+1;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the LIMIT start/count values are not bounded against vectorlen before arithmetic. A crafted large limit_count makes start+limit_count-1 wrap in long, yielding an incorrect end and a bogus vectorlen/range; the wrapped size feeds the zmalloc at line 123 and later outputlen, leading to impossible allocations and OOM/abort.
