commit_msg:
Fix double-free in gdImageWebPtr()

The issue is that gdImageWebpCtx() (which is called by gdImageWebpPtr() and
the other WebP output functions to do the real work) does not return whether
it succeeded or failed, so this is not checked in gdImageWebpPtr() and the
function wrongly assumes everything is okay, which is not, in this case,
because there is a size limitation for WebP, namely that the width and
height must by less than 16383.

We can't change the signature of gdImageWebpCtx() for API compatibility
reasons, so we introduce the static helper _gdImageWebpCtx() which returns
success respective failure, so gdImageWebpPtr() and gdImageWebpPtrEx() can
check the return value. We leave it solely to libwebp for now to report
warnings regarding the failing write.

This issue had been reported by Ibrahim El-Sayed to security@libgd.org.

CVE-2016-6912
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tgdImageWebpCtx(im, out, quality);'], 'added_lines': ['\t_gdImageWebpCtx(im, out, quality);']}
description: Double free vulnerability in the gdImageWebPtr function in the GD Graphics Library (aka libgd) before 2.2.4 allows remote attackers to have unspecified impact via large width and height values.

code_evidence: Line 7 calls gdImageWebpCtx(im, out, quality) but ignores its outcome; line 8 then unconditionally calls out->gd_free(out), freeing the output context regardless of whether the WebP encoding succeeded.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-415 fits because the same context is released via out->gd_free(out) after a failed encoding path that can also free it, i.e., free() is effectively invoked twice on the same memory. This is a double-free rather than a simple use-after-free, since the defect is the second release of the same allocation.

out->gd_free(out);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: When width/height exceed WebP's 16383 limit, the underlying context operation fails and may already release or leave the context in a freed state; because the return value is unchecked, out->gd_free(out) frees it again, causing a double free. The trigger is oversized dimensions passed to the WebP output path; the consequence is memory corruption potentially leading to code execution.

commit_msg:
Fix `tf.raw_ops.GetSessionTensor` and `tf.raw_ops.DeleteSessionTensor` null pointer dereferences.

description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. In eager mode (default in TF 2.0 and later), session operations are invalid. However, users could still call the raw ops associated with them and trigger a null pointer dereference. The implementation(https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/eebb96c2830d48597d055d247c0e9aebaea94cd5/tensorflow/core/kernels/session_ops.cc#L104) dereferences the session state pointer without checking if it is valid. Thus, in eager mode, `ctx->session_state()` is nullptr and the call of the member function is undefined behavior. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.5.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.4.2, TensorFlow 2.3.3, TensorFlow 2.2.3 and TensorFlow 2.1.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: The handle input is read and its scalar string name extracted at line 3, then passed to ctx->session_state()->DeleteTensor(name) at line 4. The return value of ctx->session_state() is dereferenced immediately without any null check, so if the session state pointer is null the member call dereferences a null pointer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits because the code dereferences a pointer expected to be valid without a null check. The missing validity constraint on ctx->session_state() directly enables the null dereference, rather than a separate type or bounds issue.

evidence_lines.code:
const string& name = handle.scalar<tstring>()();
OP_REQUIRES_OK(ctx, ctx->session_state()->DeleteTensor(name));

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the result of ctx->session_state() is used as a pointer receiver without validating it. Trigger: in eager mode the session state is null, so calling this raw op reaches line 4 and invokes DeleteTensor on a null pointer, causing undefined behavior and a crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
lib: check frame_size is >= INT32_MAX

When parsing a frame header, validate that the frame_size is less than
or equal to INT32_MAX. Given frame_max is limited between 0 and
INT32_MAX in amqp_login and friends, this does not change the API.

This prevents a potential buffer overflow when a malicious client sends
a frame_size that is close to UINT32_MAX, in which causes an overflow
when computing state->target_size resulting in a small value there. A
buffer is then allocated with the small amount, then memcopy copies the
frame_size writing to memory beyond the end of the buffer.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      /* frame length is 3 bytes in */', '      state->target_size =', '          amqp_d32(amqp_offset(raw_frame, 3)) + HEADER_SIZE + FOOTER_SIZE;'], 'added_lines': ['      uint32_t frame_size;', '', '      /* frame length is 3 bytes in */', '      frame_size = amqp_d32(amqp_offset(raw_frame, 3));', '      /* To prevent the target_size calculation below from overflowing, check', '       * that the stated frame_size is smaller than a signed 32-bit. Given', '       * the library only allows configuring frame_max as an int32_t, and', '       * frame_size is uint32_t, the math below is safe from overflow. */', '      if (frame_size >= INT32_MAX) {', '        return AMQP_STATUS_BAD_AMQP_DATA;', '      }', '      state->target_size = frame_size + HEADER_SIZE + FOOTER_SIZE;']}
description: An issue was discovered in amqp_handle_input in amqp_connection.c in rabbitmq-c 0.9.0. There is an integer overflow that leads to heap memory corruption in the handling of CONNECTION_STATE_HEADER. A rogue server could return a malicious frame header that leads to a smaller target_size value than needed. This condition is then carried on to a memcpy function that copies too much data into a heap buffer.

code_evidence: The frame length read from the wire via amqp_d32 (line 38) is a uint32_t added to HEADER_SIZE + FOOTER_SIZE and stored in state->target_size without an upper-bound check. The only guard (line 39) compares target_size against frame_max; a value near UINT32_MAX wraps target_size to a small number that passes this check. amqp_pool_alloc_bytes (line 46) then allocates that small buffer, and memcpy (line 51) copies HEADER_SIZE bytes into it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked wrap yields a small target_size, so the allocation at line 46 is smaller than the data later written into it, producing an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). The integer overflow is the root cause, but the supported weakness is the resulting heap buffer over-write, not merely the overflow arithmetic.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the untrusted 32-bit frame length is added to fixed sizes in an unsigned computation without validating it against INT32_MAX, so the sum can wrap to a small value that bypasses the frame_max check. Trigger: a malicious frame header with a length close to UINT32_MAX. Consequence: an undersized heap buffer is allocated and subsequent copies/indexing write beyond its end, corrupting heap memory.

commit_msg:
Fix overflow CHECK issue with `tf.raw_ops.UnsortedSegmentJoin`.

description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. An attacker can cause a denial of service by controlling the values of `num_segments` tensor argument for `UnsortedSegmentJoin`. This is because the implementation(https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/a2a607db15c7cd01d754d37e5448d72a13491bdb/tensorflow/core/kernels/unsorted_segment_join_op.cc#L92-L93) assumes that the `num_segments` tensor is a valid scalar. Since the tensor is empty the `CHECK` involved in `.scalar<T>()()` that checks that the number of elements is exactly 1 will be invalidated and this would result in process termination. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.5.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.4.2, TensorFlow 2.3.3, TensorFlow 2.2.3 and TensorFlow 2.1.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reaches an assertion-like CHECK on attacker-controlled input, causing process termination, which matches CWE-617 (Reachable Assertion). The added `OP_REQUIRES` guard confirms the missing constraint; this is a reachable assertion, not a memory-safety flaw.

evidence_lines.code:
const Tensor& num_segments_tensor = context->input(2);
auto num_segments = num_segments_tensor.scalar<NUM_SEGMENTS_TYPE>()();

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the code dereferences `num_segments` via `.scalar<T>()()` assuming it holds exactly one element, without checking `NumElements()`. Trigger: a caller supplies an empty `num_segments` tensor. The scalar accessor's element-count CHECK fails, terminating the process (DoS) rather than returning an InvalidArgument error.

commit_msg:
Coalesce handshake buffers

Summary:
It is possible that a peer might send us records in a manner such
that there is a 16KB record and only 1 byte of handshake message in
each record. Since we normally just trim the IOBuf, we would end up
holding 16K of data per actual byte of data. To prevent this we allocate a contiguous
buffer to copy over these bytes for handshake messages for now.

This is a partial fix for CVE-2019-11924

Reviewed By: ngoyal

Differential Revision: D16478044

fbshipit-source-id: 464bc68eaefda065d9a327818100427377293fbd
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  TLSMessage msg;'], 'added_lines': ['  TLSMessage msg{};']}
description: A peer could send empty handshake fragments containing only padding which would be kept in memory until a full handshake was received, resulting in memory exhaustion. This issue affects versions v2019.01.28.00 and above of fizz, until v2019.08.05.00.

code_evidence: read() moves the entire remaining decrypted IOBuf into msg.fragment (line 25) after trimming only the trailing zero octets per buffer, so the retained fragment can be far larger than the meaningful handshake bytes it carries.

The do/while loop walks backward across buffer chains, trimming only trailing zeros (line 20) and stopping at the first non-zero octet; it never bounds how much total data accumulates across successive records with tiny payloads.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function allocates and retains buffers per peer-controlled record without any throttle on total size, matching CWE-770's allocation without limits. CWE-400 is broader; here the specific missing constraint on resource allocation is the supported weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: each record retains a whole 16KB buffer in msg.fragment even when only one handshake byte is non-zero, and no size/count limit is enforced on accumulated fragments. Trigger: a peer sends many records each carrying a single handshake byte plus padding. Consequence: memory consumption grows per byte of real payload, enabling memory exhaustion (DoS).

description: FreeRDP is a free implementation of the Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP), released under the Apache license. Versions of FreeRDP on the 3.x release branch before beta3 are subject to a Use-After-Free in processing `RDPGFX_CMDID_RESETGRAPHICS` packets. If `context->maxPlaneSize` is 0, `context->planesBuffer` will be freed. However, without updating `context->planesBuffer`, this leads to a Use-After-Free exploit vector. In most environments this should only result in a crash. This issue has been addressed in version 3.0.0-beta3 and users of the beta 3.x releases are advised to upgrade. There are no known workarounds for this vulnerability.

code_evidence: maxPlaneSize is computed from width/height, then winpr_aligned_recalloc is called on planesBuffer with maxPlaneSize; the result is assigned back only if non-NULL, otherwise the function returns FALSE.
After reallocation, context->planes[0..3] are set to interior pointers into planesBuffer, so these derived pointers depend on the current allocation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function frees/reallocates planesBuffer while retaining references to it via planesBuffer and planes[], and subsequent operations use memory after free, matching CWE-416. This is not merely a NULL dereference because the freed allocation may be reallocated elsewhere while the stale interior pointers remain.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: When maxPlaneSize is 0, winpr_aligned_recalloc frees or returns NULL for planesBuffer; the early return leaves context->planesBuffer and the context->planes[] interior pointers stale. Later RDPGFX_CMDID_RESETGRAPHICS processing reuses those dangling pointers, causing a use-after-free that can crash or be exploited.

commit_msg:
In the copy code of the elements, we do the following calculation
to reach the end of the MBSSID element:

	/* copy the IEs after MBSSID */
	cpy_len = mbssid[1] + 2;

This looks fine, however, cpy_len is a u8, the same as mbssid[1],
so the addition of two can overflow. In this case the subsequent
memcpy() will overflow the allocated buffer, since it copies 256
bytes too much due to the way the allocation and memcpy() sizes
are calculated.

Fix this by using size_t for the cpy_len variable.

This fixes CVE-2022-41674.

Reported-by: Soenke Huster <shuster@seemoo.tu-darmstadt.de>
Tested-by: Soenke Huster <shuster@seemoo.tu-darmstadt.de>
Fixes: 0b8fb8235be8 ("cfg80211: Parsing of Multiple BSSID information in scanning")
Reviewed-by: Kees Cook <keescook@chromium.org>
Signed-off-by: Johannes Berg <johannes.berg@intel.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tu8 cpy_len;'], 'added_lines': ['\tsize_t cpy_len;']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel before 5.19.16. Attackers able to inject WLAN frames could cause a buffer overflow in the ieee80211_bss_info_update function in net/mac80211/scan.c.

code_evidence: cpy_len is declared as u8 [14], so the computation nontrans_ssid->datalen + 2 at [37] and mbssid[1] + 2 at [43] wrap modulo 256 when the element length is 254 or 255. The wrapped value is then used as the copy length in memcpy at [38] and [44].
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs a memcpy using an integer-truncated length, writing beyond the allocated buffer, which directly matches CWE-787 (out-of-bounds write). The integer overflow is the mechanism enabling the write past the buffer end.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the 8-bit cpy_len truncates the length arithmetic, producing a small value instead of the true length. Trigger: an attacker-injected WLAN frame with an MBSSID element whose length byte is near 255. Consequence: the memcpy at [44] reads/writes with an incorrect length, causing the allocation/copy size mismatch and an out-of-bounds write past the new_ie buffer.

commit_msg:
CVE-2020-1898

Don't allow for unlimited nesting in FBUnserialize or fb_compact_unserialize
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['inline typename V::VariantType FBUnserializer<V>::unserializeThing() {', '      return V::fromMap(unserializeMap());', '      return V::fromVector(unserializeVector());', '      return V::fromVector(unserializeList());', '      return V::fromSet(unserializeSet());'], 'added_lines': ['inline typename V::VariantType', 'FBUnserializer<V>::unserializeThing(size_t depth) {', '  if (UNLIKELY(depth > 1024)) {', '    throw UnserializeError("depth > 1024");', '  }', '', '      return V::fromMap(unserializeMap(depth));', '      return V::fromVector(unserializeVector(depth));', '      return V::fromVector(unserializeList(depth));', '      return V::fromSet(unserializeSet(depth));']}
description: The fb_unserialize function did not impose a depth limit for nested deserialization. That meant a maliciously constructed string could cause deserialization to recurse, leading to stack exhaustion. This issue affected HHVM prior to v4.32.3, between versions 4.33.0 and 4.56.0, 4.57.0, 4.58.0, 4.58.1, 4.59.0, 4.60.0, 4.61.0, 4.62.0.

code_evidence: unserializeThing has no depth parameter or bound, so it cannot limit nesting of recursively decoded containers.
The FB_SERIALIZE_STRUCT case delegates to unserializeMap, which can re-enter unserializeThing for nested structs.
The FB_SERIALIZE_VECTOR case delegates to unserializeVector, which can recurse into nested elements.
The FB_SERIALIZE_LIST case delegates to unserializeList, permitting nested list recursion.
The FB_SERIALIZE_SET case delegates to unserializeSet, permitting nested set recursion.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-674 fits because recursion depth is entirely controlled by input nesting and no conditional stops it, directly matching uncontrolled recursion. This is not merely a memory-size issue: the missing depth constraint lets recursion itself consume the stack.

evidence_lines.code: inline typename V::VariantType FBUnserializer<V>::unserializeThing() {

case FB_SERIALIZE_STRUCT:
return V::fromMap(unserializeMap());

case FB_SERIALIZE_VECTOR:
return V::fromVector(unserializeVector());

case FB_SERIALIZE_LIST:
return V::fromVector(unserializeList());

case FB_SERIALIZE_SET:
return V::fromSet(unserializeSet());

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the deserializer recurses through container cases (map, vector, list, set) without any depth accounting or limit. Trigger: an attacker-supplied serialized string with deeply nested containers causes each level to call back into unserializeThing. Consequence: unbounded recursion exhausts the program stack, causing a crash or denial of service.

commit_msg:
md_is_link_label: Fix if the link label contains just backslash escapes.

The function did not remember the label start line index, leading to bad
consequences.

Fixes #39.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['                if(contents_end == 0)'], 'added_lines': ['                if(contents_end == 0) {', '                    *p_beg_line_index = line_index;', '                }']}
description: md4c 0.2.5 has a heap-based buffer overflow in md_merge_lines because md_is_link_label mishandles the case of a link label composed solely of backslash escapes.

code_evidence: When a backslash escape is found, contents_beg and contents_end are set but p_beg_line_index is never assigned, unlike the non-whitespace branch at lines 39-43 which records *p_beg_line_index = line_index.
The escape branch therefore leaves the caller's label start line index uninitialized/stale when the label consists solely of backslash escapes.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing line-index assignment causes the caller to write past the intended buffer during line merging, matching CWE-787 (out-of-bounds write). The defect is an unset index rather than a boundary-check omission, but the supported consequence is a buffer overflow write.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the backslash-escape branch records content bounds without recording the corresponding start line index. Trigger: a link label composed only of backslash escapes. The caller receives an invalid beg_line_index, and downstream line merging (md_merge_lines) uses it to compute buffer positions, producing an out-of-bounds write.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            ok_jpg_decode_restart_if_needed(decoder);', '            success = ok_jpg_scan_to_next_marker(decoder);'], 'added_lines': ['            success = ok_jpg_decode_restart_if_needed(decoder);', '            if (success) {', '                success = ok_jpg_scan_to_next_marker(decoder);', '            }']}
description: David Brackeen ok-file-formats 97f78ca is vulnerable to Buffer Overflow. When the function of the ok-file-formats project is used, a heap-buffer-overflow occurs in function ok_jpg_convert_YCbCr_to_RGB() in "/ok_jpg.c:513" .

The diff confirms the fix assigns the restart result to success and gates the scan on it. If the restart decode fails, the scan proceeds on inconsistent decoder state.

Trigger: a crafted JPEG with restart markers causing that decode to fail. commit_msg:
When running concurrent iptables rules replacement with data, the per CPU
sequence count is checked after the assignment of the new information.
The sequence count is used to synchronize with the packet path without the
use of any explicit locking. If there are any packets in the packet path using
the table information, the sequence count is incremented to an odd value and
is incremented to an even after the packet process completion.

The new table value assignment is followed by a write memory barrier so every
CPU should see the latest value. If the packet path has started with the old
table information, the sequence counter will be odd and the iptables
replacement will wait till the sequence count is even prior to freeing the
old table info.

However, this assumes that the new table information assignment and the memory
barrier is actually executed prior to the counter check in the replacement
thread. If CPU decides to execute the assignment later as there is no user of
the table information prior to the sequence check, the packet path in another
CPU may use the old table information. The replacement thread would then free
the table information under it leading to a use after free in the packet
processing context-

Unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at virtual
address 000000000000008e
pc : ip6t_do_table+0x5d0/0x89c
lr : ip6t_do_table+0x5b8/0x89c
ip6t_do_table+0x5d0/0x89c
ip6table_filter_hook+0x24/0x30
nf_hook_slow+0x84/0x120
ip6_input+0x74/0xe0
ip6_rcv_finish+0x7c/0x128
ipv6_rcv+0xac/0xe4
__netif_receive_skb+0x84/0x17c
process_backlog+0x15c/0x1b8
napi_poll+0x88/0x284
net_rx_action+0xbc/0x23c
__do_softirq+0x20c/0x48c

This could be fixed by forcing instruction order after the new table
information assignment or by switching to RCU for the synchronization.

Fixes: 80055dab5de0 ("netfilter: x_tables: make xt_replace_table wait until old rules are not used anymore")
Reported-by: Sean Tranchetti <stranche@codeaurora.org>
Reported-by: kernel test robot <lkp@intel.com>
Suggested-by: Florian Westphal <fw@strlen.de>
Signed-off-by: Subash Abhinov Kasiviswanathan <subashab@codeaurora.org>
Signed-off-by: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tconst struct xt_table_info *private = t->private;'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tconst struct xt_table_info *private = xt_table_get_private_protected(t);']}
description: An issue was discovered in netfilter in the Linux kernel before 5.10. There can be a use-after-free in the packet processing context, because the per-CPU sequence count is mishandled during concurrent iptables rules replacement. This could be exploited with the CAP_NET_ADMIN capability in an unprivileged namespace. NOTE: cc00bca was reverted in 5.12.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function reads t->private under the table lock and copies fields into a local info struct; it does not free or reuse freed table memory, so the use-after-free in the packet path is not evidenced here.

description: In function lys_node_free() in libyang <= v1.0.225, it asserts that the value of node->module can't be NULL. But in some cases, node->module can be null, which triggers a reachable assertion (CWE-617).

code_evidence: Error path calls lys_node_free(retval, NULL, 0) without passing ctx; retval was allocated at line 18 and may have an unset module when read_yin_common or child parsing fails before module assignment, so the free path can hit lys_node_free's assertion that node->module is non-NULL.

It is not merely a NULL dereference; the abort comes from the assertion guard.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the error handler invokes lys_node_free with a NULL context and a partially initialized node whose module may not be set. Trigger: a malformed YIN grouping reaching an error branch (e.g., read_yin_common, addchild, or a child reader failure). Consequence: reachable assertion in lys_node_free aborts the process, causing denial of service.

commit_msg: antelope,storage-cfs: Fix length of filename array
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  char filename[INDEX_NAME_LENGTH];'], 'added_lines': ['  char filename[INDEX_NAME_LENGTH + 1];']}
description: Contiki-NG is an operating system for Internet of Things devices. An off-by-one error can be triggered in the Antelope database management system in the Contiki-NG operating system in versions 4.8 and prior. The problem exists in the Contiki File System (CFS) backend for the storage of data (file os/storage/antelope/storage-cfs.c). In the functions `storage_get_index` and `storage_put_index`, a buffer for merging two strings is allocated with one byte less than the maximum size of the merged strings, causing subsequent function calls to the cfs_open function to read from memory beyond the buffer size. The vulnerability has been patched in the "develop" branch of Contiki-NG, and is expected to be included in the next release. As a workaround, the problem can be fixed by applying the patch in Contiki-NG pull request #2425.

code_evidence: filename is declared with INDEX_NAME_LENGTH bytes, but merge_strings(filename, index->rel->name, INDEX_NAME_SUFFIX) merges the relation name and suffix, which can require INDEX_NAME_LENGTH + 1 bytes including the NUL terminator. The undersized buffer is then passed to cfs_open.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The declared maximum size is exactly one less than the correct value, matching CWE-193's off-by-one definition. This is a size-calculation error, not a generic buffer overflow from unbounded copying; the fix simply adds one byte to the bound.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the array bound is one byte short of the maximum merged string size. Trigger: a relation name near INDEX_NAME_LENGTH causes merge_strings to write the terminator past the buffer. Consequence: cfs_open reads beyond the buffer, giving an out-of-bounds read and possible crash or memory disclosure.

commit_msg:
sg_write()/bsg_write() is not fit to be called under KERNEL_DS

Both damn things interpret userland pointers embedded into the payload;
worse, they are actually traversing those.  Leaving aside the bad
API design, this is very much _not_ safe to call with KERNEL_DS.
Bail out early if that happens.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Al Viro <viro@zeniv.linux.org.uk>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\tif (unlikely(segment_eq(get_fs(), KERNEL_DS)))', '\t\treturn -EINVAL;']}
description: The sg implementation in the Linux kernel through 4.9 does not properly restrict write operations in situations where the KERNEL_DS option is set, which allows local users to read or write to arbitrary kernel memory locations or cause a denial of service (use-after-free) by leveraging access to a /dev/sg device, related to block/bsg.c and drivers/scsi/sg.c.  NOTE: this vulnerability exists because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2016-9576.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function lacks the KERNEL_DS guard and relies on user-pointer payload interpretation, but no freed memory is referenced or reused; the shown code supports a missing-address-space restriction, not a use-after-free.

commit_msg:
Heap buffer overflow in tokenadd() (fix #105)

This was an off-by one: the NUL terminator byte was not allocated on
resize.  This was triggered by JSON-encoded numbers longer than 256
bytes.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    p->tokenbuf[p->tokenpos] = 0; // FIXME: invalid'], 'added_lines': ['    p->tokenbuf[p->tokenpos] = 0;']}
description: Off-by-one error in the tokenadd function in jv_parse.c in jq allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (crash) via a long JSON-encoded number, which triggers a heap-based buffer overflow.

code_evidence: Line 18 writes a NUL terminator at p->tokenbuf[p->tokenpos], indexing one past the last valid byte when tokenpos equals the buffer capacity; no bounds check or capacity reservation for the terminator is visible in this function.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs a write at a memory location outside the buffer's intended boundary, which is exactly CWE-119's out-of-bounds memory operation. The off-by-one sizing is the underlying root cause, but the observed weakness is the out-of-bounds write within the buffer operation.

evidence_lines.code: p->tokenbuf[p->tokenpos] = 0;     char* end = 0;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the terminator store at index tokenpos assumes space for tokenpos+1 bytes, but the buffer is sized only for tokenpos data bytes. Trigger: a JSON number longer than the token buffer capacity (per commit, >256 bytes) reaches the numeric branch. Supported consequence: a one-byte heap out-of-bounds write, causing a crash/DoS and potentially corrupting adjacent heap data.

commit_msg:
Update utfcpp to v2.3.6

Fixes #2657

Incorporates the following utfcpp patches:

1. Sass addition of `retreat`.
   https://github.com/nemtrif/utfcpp/pull/20

2. Fix for `replace_invalid` throwing on incomplete sequence at the end
   of the input.
   https://github.com/nemtrif/utfcpp/pull/21
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['void retreat (octet_iterator& it, distance_type n, octet_iterator start)', '            utf8::prior(it, start);'], 'added_lines': ['void retreat (octet_iterator& it, distance_type n, octet_iterator end)', '            utf8::prior(it, end);']}
description: In LibSass prior to 3.5.5, the function handle_error in sass_context.cpp allows attackers to cause a denial-of-service resulting from a heap-based buffer over-read via a crafted sass file.

code_evidence: retreat takes a lower-bound iterator (start) and calls utf8::prior(it, start) in a loop, moving it backward n times. The loop does not verify that it can retreat n valid code points from the current position before reaching start, so prior may dereference bytes before the beginning of the buffer when it is called at or near the boundary.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Reading memory before the beginning of the intended buffer is an out-of-bounds read, matching CWE-125. It is not CWE-787 because the operation reads rather than writes, and not CWE-20 because the defect is the missing boundary constraint on the buffer access.

evidence_lines.code:
void retreat (octet_iterator& it, distance_type n, octet_iterator start)
utf8::prior(it, start);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the backward-scanning loop lacks a check that enough valid code points precede it, and utf8::prior's boundary argument is the lower bound rather than a safe stopping point. Trigger: a crafted UTF-8 input positions the iterator near the start and requests a retreat beyond the available bytes, causing prior to read before the buffer. Consequence: out-of-bounds read, potentially a crash or denial of service.

commit_msg: Fix a crash in the TGA loader with malformed input
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\t\tif (output_pos + count * p_pixel_size > output_pos) {', '\t\t\treturn ERR_PARSE_ERROR;', '\t\t}']}
description: An integer overflow issue exists in Godot Engine up to v3.2 that can be triggered when loading specially crafted.TGA image files. The vulnerability exists in ImageLoaderTGA::load_image() function at line: const size_t buffer_size = (tga_header.image_width * tga_header.image_height) * pixel_size; The bug leads to Dynamic stack buffer overflow. Depending on the context of the application, attack vector can be local or remote, and can lead to code execution and/or system crash.

code_evidence: The loop condition only checks output_pos < p_output_size; count is derived from the attacker-controlled byte c at line 13 and can be up to 128.

In the RLE run branch (c & 0x80), count pixels of p_pixel_size bytes are written to p_uncompressed_buffer[output_pos + j] and output_pos advances by p_pixel_size per iteration, with no bound check against p_output_size.
In the raw branch, count is multiplied by p_pixel_size and written byte-by-byte while incrementing output_pos; again no check ensures output_pos + count stays within p_output_size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The multiplication count * p_pixel_size and the output_pos increment can wrap in size_t, so the size/bounds computation no longer reflects the true write extent, matching CWE-190 (integer overflow/wraparound used in a size/offset calculation). The out-of-bounds write is the consequence, not the target weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The decoder trusts the run count from compressed data and advances output_pos without verifying that the decoded run fits within p_output_size. A crafted TGA with long runs near the buffer end causes writes past p_uncompressed_buffer, producing an out-of-bounds/stack buffer overflow; the patch adds output_pos + count * p_pixel_size > output_pos as a wraparound/overflow guard.

description: The daemon in GDM through 3.29.1 does not properly unexport display objects from its D-Bus interface when they are destroyed, which allows a local attacker to trigger a use-after-free via a specially crafted sequence of D-Bus method calls, resulting in a denial of service or potential code execution.

code_evidence: The display-removed signal is registered to marshal a single G_TYPE_STRING argument (lines 23-25), so handlers receive only the display id, not the GdmDisplay object.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the root cause is that the removed signal delivers an id instead of the object, preventing handlers from unexporting the display before it is freed; subsequent D-Bus calls then reference freed memory. This is a use-after-free, not merely a signal-signature mismatch.

evidence_lines.code:
signals [DISPLAY_REMOVED] =
g_signal_new ("display-removed",
G_TYPE_FROM_CLASS (object_class),
G_SIGNAL_RUN_LAST,
G_STRUCT_OFFSET (GdmDisplayStoreClass, display_removed),
NULL,
NULL,
g_cclosure_marshal_VOID__STRING,
G_TYPE_NONE,
1, G_TYPE_STRING);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Because the signal carries only the id, a handler must call gdm_display_store_lookup to obtain the object, but by the time display-removed is emitted the display has already been removed from the store, so the lookup fails and cleanup cannot run. The display object's D-Bus export is therefore left dangling after destruction, and later D-Bus method calls reference the freed object, causing a use-after-free.

commit_msg:
ext4 isn't validating the sizes of xattrs where the value of the xattr
is stored in an external inode.  This is problematic because
->e_value_size is a u32, but ext4_xattr_get() returns an int.  A very
large size is misinterpreted as an error code, which ext4_get_acl()
translates into a bogus ERR_PTR() for which IS_ERR() returns false,
causing a crash.

Fix this by validating that all xattrs are <= INT_MAX bytes.

This issue has been assigned CVE-2018-1095.

https://bugzilla.kernel.org/show_bug.cgi?id=199185
https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1560793

commit_msg:
Merge pull request from GHSA-cv8x-p47p-99wr

* - Avoid SSL socket parent/listener getting destroyed during handshake by increasing parent's reference count.
- Add missing SSL socket close when the newly accepted SSL socket is discarded in SIP TLS transport.

* - Fix silly mistake: accepted active socket created without group lock in SSL socket.
- Replace assertion with normal validation check of SSL socket instance in OpenSSL verification callback (verify_cb()) to avoid crash, e.g: if somehow race condition with SSL socket destroy happens or OpenSSL application data index somehow gets corrupted.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (listener && listener->tls_setting.on_accept_fail_cb) {'], 'added_lines': ['    if (!listener) {', '\t/* Listener already destroyed, e.g: after TCP accept but before SSL', '\t * handshake is completed.', '\t */', '\tif (new_ssock && accept_status == PJ_SUCCESS) {', '\t    /* Close the SSL socket if the accept op is successful */', '\t    PJ_LOG(4,(THIS_FILE,', '\t\t      "Incoming TLS connection from %s (sock=%d) is discarded "', '\t\t      "because listener is already destroyed",', '\t\t      pj_sockaddr_print(src_addr, addr, sizeof(addr), 3),', '\t\t      new_ssock));', '', '\t    pj_ssl_sock_close(new_ssock);', '\t}', '', '\treturn PJ_FALSE;', '    }', '\tif (listener->tls_setting.on_accept_fail_cb) {', '\tpj_ssl_sock_close(new_ssock);', '', '\tpj_ssl_sock_close(new_ssock);', '']}
description: PJSIP is a free and open source multimedia communication library written in C language implementing standard based protocols such as SIP, SDP, RTP, STUN, TURN, and ICE. In PJSIP before version 2.11.1, there are a couple of issues found in the SSL socket. First, a race condition between callback and destroy, due to the accepted socket having no group lock. Second, the SSL socket parent/listener may get destroyed during handshake. Both issues were reported to happen intermittently in heavy load TLS connections. They cause a crash, resulting in a denial of service. These are fixed in version 2.11.1.

code_evidence: The listener pointer is fetched from the shared SSL socket via pj_ssl_sock_get_user_data and then dereferenced in the accept_status branch only after a guarded check (listener && listener->tls_setting.on_accept_fail_cb).
After the assertion on new_ssock, the code dereferences listener->is_registered without a null check, so a listener destroyed concurrently leaves a dangling pointer.

On pj_ssl_sock_get_info failure the newly accepted socket is closed at line 57, but the same close is missing in the is_registered branch and on tls_create failure, leaking/discarding the accepted socket.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function accesses a listener object shared with the destroy path without holding the group lock or otherwise ensuring it stays alive, so a concurrent destroy violates exclusivity and yields a crash. This is CWE-362; the use-after-free is the consequence, not the root cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The accept callback runs concurrently with listener destruction; the parent/listener can be freed between the get_user_data call and the later dereferences of listener (is_registered, tls_setting, factory). The trigger is a TLS accept completing while the listener is torn down under heavy load, causing a use-after-free/crash (DoS). The missing pj_ssl_sock_close in some failure paths is a separate resource issue, not the race itself.

commit_msg:
There are use-after-free bugs caused by tst_timer. The root cause
is that there are no functions to stop tst_timer in idt77252_exit().
One of the possible race conditions is shown below:

    (thread 1)          |        (thread 2)
                        |  idt77252_init_one
                        |    init_card
                        |      fill_tst
                        |        mod_timer(&card->tst_timer, ...)
idt77252_exit           |  (wait a time)
                        |  tst_timer
                        |
                        |    ...
  kfree(card) // FREE   |
                        |    card->soft_tst[e] // USE

The idt77252_dev is deallocated in idt77252_exit() and used in
timer handler.

This patch adds del_timer_sync() in idt77252_exit() in order that
the timer handler could be stopped before the idt77252_dev is
deallocated.

Fixes: 1da177e4c3f4 ("Linux-2.6.12-rc2")
Signed-off-by: Duoming Zhou <duoming@zju.edu.cn>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220805070008.18007-1-duoming@zju.edu.cn
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\tdel_timer_sync(&card->tst_timer);']}
description: A vulnerability, which was classified as critical, has been found in Linux Kernel. Affected by this issue is the function tst_timer of the file drivers/atm/idt77252.c of the component IPsec. The manipulation leads to use after free. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue. VDB-211934 is the identifier assigned to this vulnerability.

code_evidence: The cleanup loop takes each card from idt77252_chain, stops the PHY, deinitializes the card, disables its PCI device, and frees it with kfree(card) at line 14. No synchronization with the card's tst_timer is performed before this teardown, so the timer handler can still run and access the card after it is freed. The added del_timer_sync(&card->tst_timer) line is the missing constraint that would prevent this overlap.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-362 fits because the teardown sequence and the timer callback concurrently access the shared card/timer resource without exclusive synchronization, creating a timing window where the timer interferes after the card is freed. The essential weakness is the missing synchronization, not the memory-safety effect itself.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: idt77252_exit() frees the idt77252_dev without stopping the concurrently scheduled tst_timer, which was armed via mod_timer in fill_tst. Trigger: module exit races with the timer callback, which reads card->soft_tst after kfree(card). Supported consequence: use-after-free of the card structure, leading to memory corruption or a crash.

around them when something in the function scope calls eval. This
patch sets the parent scope of the expressions introduced due to
those defaults to the new block scope.

description: The parser in Google V8, as used in Google Chrome before 53.0.2785.113, mishandles scopes, which allows remote attackers to obtain sensitive information from arbitrary memory locations via crafted JavaScript code.

commit_msg: Fix wrong offset used in split_region
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        if (block->offset <= mr->addr &&'], 'added_lines': ['        // block->offset is the offset within ram_addr_t, not GPA', '        if (block->mr->addr <= mr->addr &&']}
description: An issue was discovered in split_region in uc.c in Unicorn Engine before 2.0.0-rc5. It allows local attackers to escape the sandbox. An attacker must first obtain the ability to execute crafted code in the target sandbox in order to exploit this vulnerability. The specific flaw exists within the virtual memory manager. The issue results from the faulty comparison of GVA and GPA while calling uc_mem_map_ptr to free part of a claimed memory block. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to escape the sandbox and execute arbitrary code on the host machine.

code_evidence: The lookup loop selects a RAMBlock by testing block->offset (a ram_addr_t offset) against mr->addr (a guest physical address), rather than comparing block->mr->addr. The selected block is then used as the backing host pointer (block->host at line 32) and its flags drive prealloc handling.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is a security-relevant comparison that checks the wrong factor (offset vs. GPA), matching CWE-697 Incorrect Comparison. The diff confirms this: the correct field block->mr->addr replaces block->offset. This is not merely an off-by-one or bounds error; the compared entity itself is wrong.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the block-selection comparison uses the wrong field (block->offset instead of block->mr->addr), so an incorrect RAMBlock may satisfy the predicate. Trigger: a mapped region whose GPA does not correspond to the matched block's offset. Consequence: split_region operates on the wrong host backing, and subsequent uc_mem_map_ptr calls remap freed/incorrect memory, enabling sandbox escape.

description: GOST engine is a reference implementation of the Russian GOST crypto algorithms for OpenSSL. TLS clients using GOST engine when ciphersuite `TLS_GOSTR341112_256_WITH_KUZNYECHIK_CTR_OMAC` is agreed and the server uses 512 bit GOST secret keys are vulnerable to buffer overflow. GOST engine version 3.0.1 contains a patch for this issue. Disabling ciphersuite `TLS_GOSTR341112_256_WITH_KUZNYECHIK_CTR_OMAC` is a possible workaround.

code_evidence: The function serializes the GOST_KEY_TRANSPORT via i2d_GOST_KEY_TRANSPORT(gkt, out ? &out : NULL) and writes the returned length directly into *out_len without comparing it to the caller-supplied output buffer capacity. When out is non-NULL, i2d writes the encoded structure into the caller's buffer regardless of its actual size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-120 fits because the function performs a buffer copy (i2d serialization) into out without verifying that the input/serialized size is less than the output buffer size, i.e., no size check before the write. This is a copy without input-size validation, distinct from an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125).

if ((*out_len = i2d_GOST_KEY_TRANSPORT(gkt, out ? &out : NULL)) > 0)
ret = 1;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the caller-provided buffer capacity in *out_len is never checked against the encoded transport blob size before i2d writes into out. Trigger: a TLS client using the GOST ciphersuite with a server using 512-bit GOST keys produces a larger encoded blob that exceeds the allocated output buffer, causing an out-of-bounds write. Consequence: memory corruption, potentially leading to code execution or crash.

commit_msg:
md_analyze_line: Fix mixing list and table parsing.

If table header underline is not nested the same way as the preceding
line (i.e. the wannabe table header line), then it cannot form a table.

Fixes #41.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    /* Check whether we are table continuation. */', '    if(pivot_line->type == MD_LINE_TABLE  &&  md_is_table_row(ctx, off, &off)) {', '        line->type = MD_LINE_TABLE;', '        goto done;', '    }', '', "       (CH(off) == _T('|') || CH(off) == _T('-') || CH(off) == _T(':')))"], 'added_lines': ['    /* Check whether we are table continuation. */', '    if(pivot_line->type == MD_LINE_TABLE  &&  md_is_table_row(ctx, off, &off)  &&', '       n_parents == ctx->n_containers)', '    {', '        line->type = MD_LINE_TABLE;', '        goto done;', '    }', '', "       (CH(off) == _T('|') || CH(off) == _T('-') || CH(off) == _T(':'))  &&", '       n_parents == ctx->n_containers)']}
description: md4c 0.2.6 has a NULL pointer dereference in the function md_process_line in md4c.c, related to ctx->current_block.

code_evidence: At [139-142], table continuation is accepted whenever pivot_line->type == MD_LINE_TABLE and md_is_table_row succeeds, without requiring n_parents == ctx->n_containers. This can classify a line as MD_LINE_TABLE even when container nesting differs from the pivot line.

At [239-251], table underline detection requires ctx->current_block != NULL and n_lines == 1, then calls md_is_table_underline and md_is_table_row before setting MD_LINE_TABLEUNDERLINE. The patch adds n_parents == ctx->n_containers to both the continuation and underline conditions, preventing a table line from being accepted under mismatched container nesting where current_block may not be set.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits because the defect leads to dereferencing a pointer (ctx->current_block) that is expected to be valid but can be NULL after inconsistent table parsing state. The missing nesting constraint is the cause; the NULL dereference is the supported consequence, distinguishing it from a generic input-validation issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the table-continuation and table-underline checks do not verify that the current container nesting matches the pivot line's nesting. Trigger: a line that looks like a table row or underline but appears at a different container depth is misclassified as table/table-underline. This can leave ctx->current_block NULL when later table processing assumes a current block, producing a NULL dereference and crash (availability impact).

commit_msg:
KEYS: Remove key_type::match in favour of overriding default by match_preparse

A previous patch added a ->match_preparse() method to the key type.  This is
allowed to override the function called by the iteration algorithm.
Therefore, we can just set a default that simply checks for an exact match of
the key description with the original criterion data and allow match_preparse
to override it as needed.

The key_type::match op is then redundant and can be removed, as can the
user_match() function.

Signed-off-by: David Howells <dhowells@redhat.com>
Acked-by: Vivek Goyal <vgoyal@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (!index_key.type->match || !index_key.type->instantiate ||'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (!index_key.type->instantiate ||']}
description: The KEYS subsystem in the Linux kernel before 3.18 allows local users to gain privileges or cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference and system crash) via vectors involving a NULL value for a certain match field, related to the keyring_search_iterator function in keyring.c.

code_evidence: Validation only checks instantiate and that description or preparse exists; the removed match check is no longer required, so a key type lacking match passes this guard.
If preparse is set, it is invoked and may populate index_key.description from prep.description; otherwise description must already be non-NULL.
strlen(index_key.description) is called unconditionally on the description, which is assumed non-NULL after the preparse branch.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The root cause is a missing non-NULL guarantee before dereferencing index_key.description via strlen, which matches CWE-476 (dereference of a NULL pointer expected to be valid). The consequence is a crash/DoS, distinct from an out-of-bounds or use-after-free issue.

evidence_lines.code: index_key.desc_len = strlen(index_key.description);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The guard no longer rejects key types whose match callback is absent, and the description-null check is only performed inside the preparse branch. If a key type has preparse but returns without setting prep.description and the caller supplied a NULL description, index_key.description stays NULL through line 49, and strlen at line 50 dereferences it, causing a NULL pointer dereference and system crash.

commit_msg:
Jonathan Looney reported that a malicious peer can force a sender
to fragment its retransmit queue into tiny skbs, inflating memory
usage and/or overflow 32bit counters.

TCP allows an application to queue up to sk_sndbuf bytes,
so we need to give some allowance for non malicious splitting
of retransmit queue.

A new SNMP counter is added to monitor how many times TCP
did not allow to split an skb if the allowance was exceeded.

Note that this counter might increase in the case applications
use SO_SNDBUF socket option to lower sk_sndbuf.

CVE-2019-11478 : tcp_fragment, prevent fragmenting a packet when the
	socket is already using more than half the allowed space

Signed-off-by: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Reported-by: Jonathan Looney <jtl@netflix.com>
Acked-by: Neal Cardwell <ncardwell@google.com>
Acked-by: Yuchung Cheng <ycheng@google.com>
Reviewed-by: Tyler Hicks <tyhicks@canonical.com>
Cc: Bruce Curtis <brucec@netflix.com>
Cc: Jonathan Lemon <jonathan.lemon@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\tif (unlikely((sk->sk_wmem_queued >> 1) > sk->sk_sndbuf)) {', '\t\tNET_INC_STATS(sock_net(sk), LINUX_MIB_TCPWQUEUETOOBIG);', '\t\treturn -ENOMEM;', '\t}']}
description: Jonathan Looney discovered that the TCP retransmission queue implementation in tcp_fragment in the Linux kernel could be fragmented when handling certain TCP Selective Acknowledgment (SACK) sequences. A remote attacker could use this to cause a denial of service. This has been fixed in stable kernel releases 4.4.182, 4.9.182, 4.14.127, 4.19.52, 5.1.11, and is fixed in commit f070ef2ac66716357066b683fb0baf55f8191a2e.

code_evidence: tcp_fragment splits an skb by allocating a new skb via sk_stream_alloc_skb(sk, nsize, gfp, true) and then charges the socket with sk->sk_wmem_queued += buff->truesize and sk_mem_charge(sk, buff->truesize).

The function has no check that the socket's queued send memory is near its sk_sndbuf limit before allocating and charging the fragment buffer; only skb_unclone failure and allocation failure are handled.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-400 fits because the function allocates and accounts a limited resource (socket send memory) without enforcing a consumption limit, allowing remote input to exhaust it. This is a missing throttling constraint, not a buffer overflow or use-after-free.

evidence_lines.code:
if (skb_unclone(skb, gfp))
return -ENOMEM;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: tcp_fragment performs unbounded allocation and memory accounting of fragment skbs without throttling against sk_sndbuf. Trigger: a remote peer drives repeated fragmentation of the retransmit queue (e.g., via crafted SACK sequences), creating many tiny skbs. Consequence: sk_wmem_queued and memory usage grow beyond intended limits, enabling memory exhaustion and 32-bit counter overflow (DoS).

commit_msg:
UDP IPv6 packets auto flowlabels are using a 32bit secret
(static u32 hashrnd in net/core/flow_dissector.c) and
apply jhash() over fields known by the receivers.

Attackers can easily infer the 32bit secret and use this information
to identify a device and/or user, since this 32bit secret is only
set at boot time.

Really, using jhash() to generate cookies sent on the wire
is a serious security concern.

Trying to change the rol32(hash, 16) in ip6_make_flowlabel() would be
a dead end. Trying to periodically change the secret (like in sch_sfq.c)
could change paths taken in the network for long lived flows.

Let's switch to siphash, as we did in commit df453700e8d8
("inet: switch IP ID generator to siphash")

Using a cryptographically strong pseudo random function will solve this
privacy issue and more generally remove other weak points in the stack.

Packet schedulers using skb_get_hash_perturb() benefit from this change.

Fixes: b56774163f99 ("ipv6: Enable auto flow labels by default")

description: The flow_dissector feature in the Linux kernel 4.3 through 5.x before 5.3.10 has a device tracking vulnerability, aka CID-55667441c84f. This occurs because the auto flowlabel of a UDP IPv6 packet relies on a 32-bit hashrnd value as a secret, and because jhash (instead of siphash) is used. The hashrnd value remains the same starting from boot time, and can be inferred by an attacker. This affects net/core/flow_dissector.c and related code.

code_evidence: Line 4 calls __flow_hash_secret_init() but the hash itself is computed at line 9 by passing the global hashrnd value directly to __flow_hash_from_keys(). The secret is a static u32 initialized once at boot, so the flow hash secret is not refreshed and is derived from a small 32-bit value.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-330 fits because a security-relevant value (the flow hash secret) is generated from insufficiently random, fixed 32-bit state and reused indefinitely, enabling inference. This is distinct from a mere hash collision issue; the weakness is the unpredictable-value requirement failing.

evidence_lines.code:
__flow_hash_secret_init();
return __flow_hash_from_keys(&keys, hashrnd);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the symmetric flow hash uses a fixed 32-bit hashrnd secret rather than a cryptographically strong key. Trigger: an attacker observes flow labels/hashes derived from jhash over receiver-known fields and infers the boot-time secret. Consequence: the attacker can correlate/track a device or user across packets because the secret is stable and guessable.

description: An information disclosure vulnerability in lvm/wrapper/Bundle/EffectBundle.cpp in libeffects in Audioserver could enable a local malicious application to access data outside of its permission levels. This issue is rated as Moderate because it could be used to access sensitive data without permission. Product: Android. Versions: 4.4.4, 5.0.2, 5.1.1, 6.0, 6.0.1, 7.0, 7.1. Android ID: A-32436341.

code_evidence: param2 is read from caller-controlled p->data and only checked with param2 >= NUM_EQ_BANDS, so negative values pass the guard and reach equalizer_get_band_level(eq_ctxt, param2).
The same one-sided check at line 74 lets a negative param2 reach equalizer_get_center_frequency(eq_ctxt, param2).
The same one-sided check at line 83 lets a negative param2 reach equalizer_get_band_freq_range(eq_ctxt, param2, ...), so the band index is used without a lower bound.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The commit and description identify this as an information disclosure: caller-controlled negative indexes bypass the band validation and drive reads outside the intended range, returning data to the caller in the value buffer. joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the bounds checks reject only indexes at or above NUM_EQ_BANDS and never reject negative indexes. Trigger: a local caller supplies a negative band index through the effect parameter data. The negative index then reaches the equalizer accessor functions, which read state outside the intended band range and copy that data into the caller-visible value buffer, exposing information beyond the caller's permission level.

description: libmemcached-awesome is an open source C/C++ client library and tools for the memcached server. `libmemcached` could return data for a previously requested key, if that previous request timed out due to a low `POLL_TIMEOUT`. This issue has been addressed in version 1.1.4. Users are advised to upgrade. There are several ways to workaround or lower the probability of this bug affecting a given deployment. 1: use a reasonably high `POLL_TIMEOUT` setting, like the default. 2: use separate libmemcached connections for unrelated data. 3: do not re-use libmemcached connections in an unknown state.

code_evidence: The loop reads no_msg-1 responses from the connection into a reused result buffer. When memcached_read_one_response returns MEMCACHED_TIMEOUT, the break at lines 35-37 exits the loop without consuming the remaining responses. The callback dispatch at 38-47 is still invoked for the timed-out rc, and the function returns is_successful without resetting the connection or draining the outstanding responses.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-200 fits because the early break causes the connection to return data for a previously requested key to a later caller, i.e., sensitive information is exposed to an actor not authorized for that request. This is a state-mixing exposure, not merely a generic confidentiality loss from memory corruption.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: on MEMCACHED_TIMEOUT the purge loop breaks early, leaving unread responses queued on the connection while the buffer is reused. Trigger: a prior request times out under a low POLL_TIMEOUT and the connection is reused. Consequence: a later request can receive data belonging to the earlier key, exposing another request's data to an unauthorized actor.

commit_msg:
IOMMU: default to always quarantining PCI devices

XSA-302 relies on the use of libxl's "assignable-add" feature to prepare
devices to be assigned to untrusted guests.

Unfortunately, this is not considered a strictly required step for
device assignment. The PCI passthrough documentation on the wiki
describes alternate ways of preparing devices for assignment, and
libvirt uses its own ways as well. Hosts where these alternate methods
are used will still leave the system in a vulnerable state after the
device comes back from a guest.

Default to always quarantining PCI devices, but provide a command line
option to revert back to prior behavior (such that people who both
sufficiently trust their guests and want to be able to use devices in
Dom0 again after they had been in use by a guest wouldn't need to
"manually" move such devices back from DomIO to Dom0).

This is XSA-306.

Reported-by: Marek Marczykowski-Górecki <marmarek@invisiblethingslab.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Reviewed-by: Wei Liu <wl@xen.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    target = (pdev->quarantine && pdev->domain != dom_io) ?'], 'added_lines': ['    target = ((pdev->quarantine || iommu_quarantine) &&', '              pdev->domain != dom_io) ?']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.12.x allowing attackers to gain host OS privileges via DMA in a situation where an untrusted domain has access to a physical device (and assignable-add is not used), because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2019-18424. XSA-302 relies on the use of libxl's "assignable-add" feature to prepare devices to be assigned to untrusted guests. Unfortunately, this is not considered a strictly required step for device assignment. The PCI passthrough documentation on the wiki describes alternate ways of preparing devices for assignment, and libvirt uses its own ways as well. Hosts where these "alternate" methods are used will still leave the system in a vulnerable state after the device comes back from a guest. An untrusted domain with access to a physical device can DMA into host memory, leading to privilege escalation. Only systems where guests are given direct access to physical devices capable of DMA (PCI pass-through) are vulnerable. Systems which do not use PCI pass-through are not vulnerable.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function applies a quarantine policy decision to PCI device deassignment; it does not receive or validate external input, so the improper input validation (CWE-20) target is not supported by the code.

commit_msg:
With write operation on psi files replacing old trigger with a new one,
the lifetime of its waitqueue is totally arbitrary. Overwriting an
existing trigger causes its waitqueue to be freed and pending poll()
will stumble on trigger->event_wait which was destroyed.
Fix this by disallowing to redefine an existing psi trigger. If a write
operation is used on a file descriptor with an already existing psi
trigger, the operation will fail with EBUSY error.
Also bypass a check for psi_disabled in the psi_trigger_destroy as the
flag can be flipped after the trigger is created, leading to a memory
leak.

commit_msg: Bug 701292: Fix test for missing/empty string.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (str->utf8 == NULL)'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (str->utf8 == NULL || str->pos == -1)']}
description: Artifex MuPDF before 1.16.0 has a heap-based buffer over-read in fz_chartorune in fitz/string.c because pdf/pdf-op-filter.c does not check for a missing string.

code_evidence: Guard only checks str->utf8 == NULL before entering the loop, so a str->pos of -1 is not excluded.
s = &str->utf8[str->pos] indexes with str->pos; when pos is -1 this points before the buffer, and fz_chartorune(&rune, s) reads from that address.
The else branch sets str->pos = -1 and breaks, leaving a negative position that a later call would use.
strlen(s+n) and memmove(s, s+n, len+1) also operate from the potentially out-of-bounds s pointer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads memory before the start of the utf8 buffer through a negative index, which is an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). This is not a write or a length-integer issue; the direct consequence is reading outside the intended buffer.

evidence_lines.code:
if (str->utf8 == NULL)
return;

char *s = &str->utf8[str->pos];
int n = fz_chartorune(&rune, s);

str->pos = -1;
break;

len = strlen(s+n);
memmove(s, s+n, len+1);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The root cause is that walk_string accepts a str->pos of -1 and computes &str->utf8[str->pos], producing a pointer before the intended buffer. The trigger is a caller invoking walk_string on a string whose pos was previously set to -1; fz_chartorune then reads before the buffer, causing a heap-based out-of-bounds read.

commit_msg:
patch 9.0.1145: invalid memory access with recursive substitute expression

Problem:    Invalid memory access with recursive substitute expression.
Solution:   Check the return value of vim_regsub().
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t    if (sublen <= 0)', '\t    {', '\t\tga_clear(&ga);', '\t\tbreak;', '\t    }']}
description: Out-of-bounds Write in GitHub repository vim/vim prior to 9.0.1145.

code_evidence: vim_regsub() at line 44 returns sublen, which is used unchecked as the size argument for ga_grow() and in the buffer-length arithmetic at lines 45-46.
The second vim_regsub() copies into ga.ga_data at offset ga.ga_len + i with the same sublen, and line 56 advances ga.ga_len by i + sublen - 1.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked return value of vim_regsub() feeds buffer sizing and copy arithmetic, allowing writes beyond the allocated ga buffer, which is CWE-787 (out-of-bounds write). It is a missing-return-value check rather than a pure bounds check, but the supported consequence is a write past the intended buffer.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: When a recursive substitute expression makes vim_regsub() return a non-positive value (e.g. 0), the ga_grow() size computation and the destination offset/len arithmetic become inconsistent. The copy at lines 53-55 then writes through ga.ga_data with an uncontrolled length, and ga.ga_len is adjusted by sublen - 1, corrupting the array state. This yields an out-of-bounds write / invalid memory access.

commit_msg:
nbd: convert to use qio_channel_yield

In the client, read the reply headers from a coroutine, switching the
read side between the "read header" coroutine and the I/O coroutine that

In the server, if the server can read more requests it will create a new

commit_msg:
The rawmidi core allows user to resize the runtime buffer via ioctl,
and this may lead to UAF when performed during concurrent reads or
writes: the read/write functions unlock the runtime lock temporarily
during copying form/to user-space, and that's the race window.

This patch fixes the hole by introducing a reference counter for the
runtime buffer read/write access and returns -EBUSY error when the
resize is performed concurrently against read/write.

Note that the ref count field is a simple integer instead of
refcount_t here, since the all contexts accessing the buffer is
basically protected with a spinlock, hence we need no expensive atomic
ops.  Also, note that this busy check is needed only against read /
write functions, and not in receive/transmit callbacks; the race can
happen only at the spinlock hole mentioned in the above, while the
whole function is protected for receive / transmit callbacks.

Reported-by: butt3rflyh4ck <butterflyhuangxx@gmail.com>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/CAFcO6XMWpUVK_yzzCpp8_XP7+=oUpQvuBeCbMffEDkpe8jWrfg@mail.gmail.com
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/s5heerw3r5z.wl-tiwai@suse.de
Signed-off-by: Takashi Iwai <tiwai@suse.de>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (runtime->buffer_ref) {', '\t\t\tspin_unlock_irq(&runtime->lock);', '\t\t\tkvfree(newbuf);', '\t\t\treturn -EBUSY;', '\t\t}']}
description: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel’s implementation of MIDI, where an attacker with a local account and the permissions to issue ioctl commands to midi devices could trigger a use-after-free issue. A write to this specific memory while freed and before use causes the flow of execution to change and possibly allow for memory corruption or privilege escalation. The highest threat from this vulnerability is to confidentiality, integrity, as well as system availability.

code_evidence: resize_runtime_buffer swaps runtime->buffer under runtime->lock, then calls kvfree(oldbuf) after unlocking. The patch's check on runtime->buffer_ref (added at line 14) is absent from this before-version, so a concurrent read/write that released the lock during copy_to/from_user can still hold and use the old buffer pointer after it is freed at line 20.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function frees runtime->buffer and leaves a window where another context's pointer to that allocation is dereferenced, which is exactly reusing memory after free (CWE-416). The missing buffer_ref busy check is the specific missing constraint; this is not merely a double free or null dereference.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the old buffer is freed at line 20 without ensuring no concurrent reader/writer still references it; read/write paths drop runtime->lock during user-space copies. Trigger: an ioctl resize races with a concurrent read/write. Consequence: use-after-free of the freed buffer, enabling memory corruption or privilege escalation.

The unit allocated for decNumberCompare was accidentally removed by
commit 680baeffeb7983e7570b5e68db07fe47f94db8c7 (PR #2804)

This caused a stack overflow when comparing a nan with a payload of 1000
or more.

This bug was found by OSS-fuzz.
Ref: https://bugs.chromium.org/p/oss-fuzz/issues/detail?id=64771
Fixes GHSA-7hmr-442f-qc8j

It also fixes 1e999999999 > 1e-1147483646   triggering UBSAN errors
Fixes #2968

description: jq is a command-line JSON processor. Version 1.7 is vulnerable to stack-based buffer overflow in builds using decNumber. Version 1.7.1 contains a patch for this issue.

code_evidence: A bare stack-allocated decNumber `res` is declared and passed to decNumberCompare, which writes the comparison result into it. decNumberCompare may require additional decNumberUnit storage for the result's coefficient (e.g., when the operand is a NaN with a large payload); the fixed-size decNumber alone lacks the trailing units array, so the library writes past the object's bounds.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function supplies an undersized destination buffer to a library call that writes a variable-size result, causing writes past the end of the intended buffer, matching CWE-787. It is an out-of-bounds write rather than merely a read or logic error.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the result buffer allocated for decNumberCompare is a plain decNumber without the trailing decNumberUnit array that decNumber operations may write into. Trigger: comparing numbers whose result needs units beyond the inline storage (NaN with payload >=1000). Consequence: out-of-bounds stack write, observed as stack overflow/crash and potential memory corruption.

description: RIOT 2020.04 has a buffer overflow in the base64 decoder. The decoding function base64_decode() uses an output buffer estimation function to compute the required buffer capacity and validate against the provided buffer size. commit_msg:
Prevent heap OOB read in TFLite's `gather.cc`.

Passing negative indices is illegal but there was a missing check so that resulted in OOB accesses.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 387231300
Change-Id: I3111b54b2f232638d795be17efc46abe4ede6bf8
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['TfLiteStatus Gather(const TfLiteGatherParams& params, const TfLiteTensor* input,', '                    const TfLiteTensor* positions, TfLiteTensor* output) {'], 'added_lines': ['TfLiteStatus Gather(TfLiteContext* context, const TfLiteGatherParams& params,', '                    const TfLiteTensor* input, const TfLiteTensor* positions,', '                    TfLiteTensor* output) {', '  const PositionsT* indexes = GetTensorData<PositionsT>(positions);', '  bool indices_has_only_positive_elements = true;', '  const size_t num_indices = positions->bytes / sizeof(PositionsT);', '  for (size_t i = 0; i < num_indices; i++) {', '    if (indexes[i] < 0) {', '      indices_has_only_positive_elements = false;', '      break;', '    }', '  }', '  TF_LITE_ENSURE(context, indices_has_only_positive_elements);', '']}
description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. In affected versions TFLite's [`GatherNd` implementation](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/149562d49faa709ea80df1d99fc41d005b81082a/tensorflow/lite/kernels/gather_nd.cc#L124) does not support negative indices but there are no checks for this situation. Hence, an attacker can read arbitrary data from the heap by carefully crafting a model with negative values in `indices`. Similar issue exists in [`Gather` implementation](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/149562d49faa709ea80df1d99fc41d005b81082a/tensorflow/lite/kernels/gather.cc). We have patched the issue in GitHub commits bb6a0383ed553c286f87ca88c207f6774d5c4a8f and eb921122119a6b6e470ee98b89e65d721663179d. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.6.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.5.1, TensorFlow 2.4.3, and TensorFlow 2.3.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: Gather receives a positions tensor and passes its raw data GetTensorData<PositionsT>(positions) directly to optimized_ops::Gather without validating that indices are non-negative; there is no bounds check on the index values before they are used to index into the input tensor.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked negative indices cause the gather kernel to read outside the input buffer, which is exactly an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). This is not CWE-787 because the operation reads rather than writes memory.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: indices from the positions tensor are forwarded to the gather kernel unchecked. Trigger: a crafted model supplies negative index values in positions. Consequence: the kernel computes an address before the input buffer and reads heap memory out of bounds, leaking data or crashing.

since they are copied to userspace.  The change from strncpy() to

commit_msg:
xen/rwlock: Add missing memory barrier in the unlock path of rwlock

The rwlock unlock paths are using atomic_sub() to release the lock.
However the implementation of atomic_sub() rightfully doesn't contain a
memory barrier. On Arm, this means a processor is allowed to re-order
the memory access with the preceeding access.

In other words, the unlock may be seen by another processor before all
the memory accesses within the "critical" section.

The rwlock paths already contains barrier indirectly, but they are not
very useful without the counterpart in the unlock paths.

The memory barriers are not necessary on x86 because loads/stores are
not re-ordered with lock instructions.

So add arch_lock_release_barrier() in the unlock paths that will only
add memory barrier on Arm.

Take the opportunity to document each lock paths explaining why a
barrier is not necessary.

This is XSA-314.

Signed-off-by: Julien Grall <jgrall@amazon.com>
Acked-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['        /*', '         * atomic_add_return() is a full barrier so no need for an', '         * arch_lock_acquire_barrier().', '         */']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.13.x, allowing guest OS users to cause a denial of service or possibly gain privileges because of missing memory barriers in read-write unlock paths. The read-write unlock paths don't contain a memory barrier. On Arm, this means a processor is allowed to re-order the memory access with the preceding ones. In other words, the unlock may be seen by another processor before all the memory accesses within the "critical" section. As a consequence, it may be possible to have a writer executing a critical section at the same time as readers or another writer. In other words, many of the assumptions (e.g., a variable cannot be modified after a check) in the critical sections are not safe anymore. The read-write locks are used in hypercalls (such as grant-table ones), so a malicious guest could exploit the race. For instance, there is a small window where Xen can leak memory if XENMAPSPACE_grant_table is used concurrently. A malicious guest may be able to leak memory, or cause a hypervisor crash resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS). Information leak and privilege escalation cannot be excluded.

code_evidence: Line 5 reads the shared lock counter, then line 6 checks whether a read lock is permissible based on that snapshot.
Line 8 atomically adds the read bias to the same counter and line 9 re-checks the result; if the re-check fails, line 11 subtracts the bias to undo the acquisition, while success returns at line 10.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This is a timing window in which the shared lock counter can be modified by a concurrent code sequence between the read and the update, violating the exclusivity/atomicity requirement of the lock and matching CWE-362. The missing barrier is the enabling mechanism, but the supported weakness is the resulting race on the shared resource.

evidence_lines.code:
cnts = atomic_read(&lock->cnts);
if ( likely(_can_read_lock(cnts)) )

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The trylock reads and later modifies the shared lock counter in separate operations, so the decision at line 6 is based on a value that another CPU may change before line 8 executes. A concurrent writer can acquire or release the lock between the read and the atomic_add_return, making the re-checked state inconsistent with the initial decision and allowing the reader to proceed while a writer holds the lock.
