At line 263 ReadBlob fills BImgBuff for each row; on a short read the code jumps to ExitLoop, but the buffer may hold partially read or previously uninitialized bytes that are later consumed.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function exposes uninitialized heap memory to the attacker through the produced image, matching CWE-200's exposure of sensitive information. The underlying error is an uninitialized-memory read (CWE-457); CWE-200 is the supported confidentiality impact and target label here.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the heap buffer BImgBuff is allocated without initialization and its contents are consumed by CalcMinMax (line 249) and pixel import before being fully populated. Trigger: a crafted MAT file whose CellType is miDOUBLE/miSINGLE or whose row data is truncated causes uninitialized process-memory bytes to be read and converted into image pixels, which the attacker can then retrieve. Consequence: disclosure of sensitive process memory (CWE-200).

commit_msg:
Quick fix for a vuln in printing empty tensors.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 503308327
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  if (data == nullptr) {', '    return strings::StrCat("");  // we already print type and shape', '  }']}
description: TensorFlow is an open source platform for machine learning. Prior to versions 2.12.0 and 2.11.1, when the parameter `summarize` of `tf.raw_ops.Print` is zero, the new method `SummarizeArray<bool>` will reference to a nullptr, leading to a seg fault. A fix is included in TensorFlow version 2.12 and version 2.11.1.

code_evidence: SummarizeArray<bool> receives the raw pointer data and never validates it before entering the loop. Line 5 iterates i from 0 to num_elts, and line 6 indexes data[i] on every iteration, dereferencing data unconditionally.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits because the code performs a read through a pointer it expects to be valid but does not check against NULL; the missing guard in lines 4-6 is exactly the null dereference. It is not a buffer overflow, since the index bounds are controlled by num_elts and the failure stems from the pointer's null value, not from an out-of-range index.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function assumes data is non-null and indexes it in the copy loop. Trigger: a caller passes a null data pointer (e.g., printing an empty tensor with summarize=0) while num_elts is nonzero, so data[i] dereferences nullptr. Supported consequence: a segmentation fault, a denial of service, since no null check guards the access.

commit_msg:
Fix multiple OOB bugs resulted from tx mtu in EATT

The tx mtu in EATT can be controlled by remote device. With malicious
mtu values, it is possible to trigger integer overflow and
OOB write at multiple places (see the bug below).

This fix enforces a max tx mtu in EATT.

Bug: 271335899
Test: manual
Ignore-AOSP-First: security
Tag: #security
(cherry picked from https://googleplex-android-review.googlesource.com/q/commit:ea76b7d99e6366e2043c5621eda630d559104d36)
Merged-In: Ia06c9a17f2daa5ce4c32cffa536777f47774cf31
Change-Id: Ia06c9a17f2daa5ce4c32cffa536777f47774cf31
func:
[EattChannelSetTxMTU]

0001 | void EattChannelSetTxMTU(uint16_t tx_mtu) { this->tx_mtu_ = tx_mtu; }
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['void EattChannelSetTxMTU(uint16_t tx_mtu) { this->tx_mtu_ = tx_mtu; }'], 'added_lines': ['void EattChannelSetTxMTU(uint16_t tx_mtu) {', '    this->tx_mtu_ = std::min<uint16_t>(tx_mtu, EATT_MAX_TX_MTU);', '  }']}
description: In eatt_l2cap_reconfig_completed of eatt_impl.h, there is a possible out of bounds write due to an integer overflow. This could lead to remote code execution with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

code_evidence: EattChannelSetTxMTU stores the caller-supplied uint16_t tx_mtu directly into tx_mtu_ with no upper-bound check or clamping; the value originates from the remote device's EATT tx MTU.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the unchecked stored MTU is later used in arithmetic that can wrap, yielding undersized buffers/offsets and OOB writes. The defect is the absent bound on a value feeding integer arithmetic, not merely an out-of-range read.

evidence_lines.code: void EattChannelSetTxMTU(uint16_t tx_mtu) { this->tx_mtu_ = tx_mtu; }

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the setter accepts any 16-bit tx MTU, including attacker-chosen large values, without validating against a maximum. Trigger: a remote peer supplies a malicious MTU that is stored and later used in size/offset calculations. Supported consequence: those downstream computations can overflow and produce out-of-bounds writes, as described for eatt_l2cap_reconfig_completed.

commit_msg: HTTP/2: per-iteration stream handling limit.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    h2c->new_streams = 0;']}
description: The HTTP/2 protocol allows a denial of service (server resource consumption) because request cancellation can reset many streams quickly, as exploited in the wild in August through October 2023.

code_evidence: The handler sets h2c->blocked and then enters the receive loop; the per-iteration stream handling limit (new_streams) is reset elsewhere, so this read handler processes all buffered frames in one pass.
The inner loop repeatedly calls h2c->state.handler for each frame until the buffer is consumed, delivering stream-cancellation frames without any per-iteration cap on newly created streams.
The only flood guard compares total_bytes to payload_bytes after all frames in the iteration are processed, so many small stream-reset frames are handled before any limit is enforced.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-400 fits because the function fails to throttle the number of stream resources handled per iteration, allowing attacker-driven resource consumption. This is not CWE-770's missing allocation limits per se, but the concrete lack of per-iteration throttling enabling DoS.

evidence_lines.code: h2c->blocked = 1;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the read handler processes an unbounded number of frame-driven stream operations per read iteration, and the flood check at [77] runs only after the inner loop completes. Trigger: a client sends many request-cancellation/RST_STREAM frames in a single buffer. Consequence: the server rapidly creates and tears down streams, consuming CPU/memory and enabling denial of service.

commit_msg:
decode_r2007: fix for invalid section size

See GH #350. With fuzzing section->data_size might not fit
section_page->uncomp_size.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  LOG_HANDLE ("read_system_page: size_comp: %" PRId64 ", size_uncomp: %" PRId64', '                 ", repeat_count: %" PRId64 "\\n", size_comp, size_uncomp, repeat_count);']}
description: A heap buffer overflow was discovered in copy_bytes in decode_r2007.c in dwgread before 0.12.4 via a crafted dwg file.

code_evidence: Line 21 computes pesize from size_comp and repeat_count, and lines 22/29 derive block_count and page_size. The size checks at lines 30 and 39 bound page_size against dat->size but do not bound size_uncomp against the allocated buffer's usable region consistently. Line 39 allocates size_uncomp + page_size bytes; line 46 sets rsdata to data + size_uncomp; line 47 reads page_size bytes into rsdata. The branch at lines 55-58 either decompresses into data with size_uncomp as output size or memcpy's size_uncomp bytes from pedata into data, where pedata_size = block_count*239 (line 48) may be smaller than size_uncomp.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs a memory copy/decompression into a buffer sized from an inconsistent, attacker-controlled size, writing beyond the end of the intended buffer. This is a direct out-of-bounds write (CWE-787); it is not merely an out-of-bounds read, since the write target is exceeded.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The allocation size depends on an unbounded size_uncomp while the decoded pedata size depends on block_count derived from size_comp and repeat_count. When size_comp >= size_uncomp, the memcpy at line 58 (or decompress output) writes size_uncomp bytes from a pedata buffer that may be smaller, causing an out-of-bounds write past the end of pedata/rsdata and heap corruption.

commit_msg:
Delete obsolete XPointer range-to function.

BUG=623378

Review-Url: https://codereview.chromium.org/2127493002
Cr-Commit-Position: refs/heads/master@{#403859}
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t    /* Note Type or Function */'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t    /* Node Type or Function */', '                    } else if (ctxt->xptr &&', '                               xmlStrEqual(name, BAD_CAST "range-to")) {', '                        lc = 1;']}
description: Use-after-free vulnerability in libxml2 through 2.9.4, as used in Google Chrome before 52.0.2743.82, allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service or possibly have unspecified other impact via vectors related to the XPointer range-to function.

code_evidence: The function scans an identifier into `name` (line 21, referenced here), enters the `name != NULL` branch at line 29, and walks following characters in the while loop at line 31. At line 48, if the next character is '(', the code calls `xmlXPathIsNodeType(name)` at line 49; if that returns false and no other clause matches, it falls to the else at line 55, sets `lc = 0` and breaks, then frees `name` at line 87. The patched condition (ctxt->xptr && xmlStrEqual(name, "range-to")) is absent in the supplied function, so a range-to call is treated as a generic function call (lc=0) and later parsed by xmlXPathCompFilterExpr at line 100.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the flaw allows a freed resource to be reused while compiling the range-to expression, matching the advisory. It is not merely an input-validation error: the parser's incorrect classification leads to later use of already-freed state.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the parser does not special-case the XPointer `range-to` function; it classifies the name as an ordinary function call (lc=0), frees the scanned name, and dispatches to filter-expression parsing. Trigger: an XPointer expression containing `range-to(` reaches this path. The supported consequence is parser-level mishandling that enables the reported use-after-free during compilation of the range-to expression; the free at line 87 alone is not the defect.

commit_msg: Fix some pipelines to be safe if downstream write fails (fuzz issue 28262)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tthis->m->last_char = buf[len - 1];'], 'added_lines': ['\tthis->m->last_char = buf[len - 1];']}
description: QPDF 9.x through 9.1.1 and 10.x through 10.0.4 has a heap-based buffer overflow in Pl_ASCII85Decoder::write (called from Pl_AES_PDF::flush and Pl_AES_PDF::finish) when a certain downstream write fails.

code_evidence: Pl_Count::write conditionally updates m->count, delegates getNext()->write(buf, len), and then reads buf[len - 1] to record last_char. The buffer access at line 8 occurs after the downstream write returns, and len is only checked for being nonzero, not for the actual buffer size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs a buffer access at buf[len - 1] whose safety depends on the buffer remaining valid after the downstream write; ordering the access after a possibly failing write exposes an out-of-bounds memory access. This aligns with CWE-787's out-of-bounds write/memory corruption concern, though the precise overflow arises in the downstream path.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: state (last_char) is recorded after the downstream write rather than before it. If the downstream write fails or alters/frees the buffer, control can still reach buf[len - 1], indexing the buffer after a failed write. The patch moves the read before getNext()->write so last_char is captured from the valid input buffer before downstream processing. Trigger: a failing downstream write following a nonempty buffer; supported consequence is an out-of-bounds read/write-related memory access on stale or invalid buffer data, consistent with the reported buffer overflow scenario.

commit_msg:
Prevent an infinite loop in the DWARF parsing code when encountering a CU structure with a small negative size.

	PR 22219
	* dwarf.c (process_debug_info): Add a check for a negative
	cu_length field.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      int initial_length_size;'], 'added_lines': ['      unsigned int initial_length_size;', '      else if (compunit.cu_length + initial_length_size < initial_length_size)', '\t{', '\t  warn (_("Debug info is corrupted, length of CU at %s is negative (%s)\\n"),', '\t\tdwarf_vmatoa ("x", cu_offset),', '\t\tdwarf_vmatoa ("x", compunit.cu_length));', '\t  num_units = unit;', '\t  break;', '\t}', '']}
description: process_debug_info in dwarf.c in the Binary File Descriptor (BFD) library (aka libbfd), as distributed in GNU Binutils 2.29, allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (infinite loop) via a crafted ELF file that contains a negative size value in a CU structure.

code_evidence: initial_length_size is a signed int assigned 4 or 12; compunit.cu_length is read from the file via SAFE_BYTE_GET_AND_INC as unsigned. The bounds check at 203-204 computes cu_offset + cu_length + initial_length_size > section->size; with a crafted negative/small cu_length the wrapped arithmetic can pass this check, so no break occurs.

start += compunit.cu_length + initial_length_size (214) can then fail to advance or move backward, while the outer loop condition start < end (77) and the inner while (tags < start) (255) depend on start advancing.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function's loop over units relies on start advancing by cu_length; when the corrupted length prevents progress, the exit condition start < end cannot be reached, matching CWE-835 (infinite loop). The patch adds an explicit negative-length rejection, confirming the loop-progress failure rather than a mere out-of-bounds read.

evidence_lines.code:
for (section_begin = start, unit = 0; start < end; unit++)
while (tags < start)

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the length check at 203-204 does not reject a negative cu_length because the signed/unsigned addition wraps, so control reaches the pointer advance at 214. Trigger: a crafted ELF CU with a small negative size value. Consequence: start does not advance past the unit, so the outer parsing loop repeats indefinitely, causing a denial of service (CPU consumption).

commit_msg:
ALSA: control: Fix an out-of-bounds bug in get_ctl_id_hash()

Since the user can control the arguments provided to the kernel by the
ioctl() system call, an out-of-bounds bug occurs when the 'id->name'
provided by the user does not end with '\0'.

The following log can reveal it:

[    10.002313] BUG: KASAN: stack-out-of-bounds in snd_ctl_find_id+0x36c/0x3a0
[    10.002895] Read of size 1 at addr ffff888109f5fe28 by task snd/439
[    10.004934] Call Trace:
[    10.007140]  snd_ctl_find_id+0x36c/0x3a0
[    10.007489]  snd_ctl_ioctl+0x6cf/0x10e0

Fix this by checking the bound of 'id->name' in the loop.

Fixes: c27e1efb61c5 ("ALSA: control: Use xarray for faster lookups")
Signed-off-by: Zheyu Ma <zheyuma97@gmail.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220824081654.3767739-1-zheyuma97@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Takashi Iwai <tiwai@suse.de>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tconst unsigned char *p;', '\tfor (p = id->name; *p; p++)', '\t\th = MULTIPLIER * h + *p;'], 'added_lines': ['\tint i;', '\tfor (i = 0; id->name[i] && i < SNDRV_CTL_ELEM_ID_NAME_MAXLEN; i++)', '\t\th = MULTIPLIER * h + id->name[i];']}
description: An out-of-bounds access issue was found in the Linux kernel sound subsystem. It could occur when the 'id->name' provided by the user did not end with '\0'. A privileged local user could pass a specially crafted name through ioctl() interface and crash the system or potentially escalate their privileges on the system.

code_evidence: `p` is set to `id->name` and the loop condition `*p` dereferences each byte until a NUL terminator is found; there is no bound check against the array size. If the user-supplied name lacks a terminating '\0', the loop keeps reading past the end of `id->name`.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the function reads memory past the end of the intended `id->name` buffer; the missing length constraint causes an out-of-bounds read rather than a write.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the loop termination depends solely on encountering a NUL byte in an externally supplied name. Trigger: an ioctl passes an `snd_ctl_elem_id` whose name is not NUL-terminated within its buffer. Consequence: out-of-bounds reads (observed as a KASAN stack-out-of-bounds in snd_ctl_find_id), crashing the system or exposing adjacent memory.

commit_msg:
Clear network state only when REMOVE_CACHE is set, not unconditionally

Previously, network state like HSTS data was cleared whenever
BrowsingDataRemover::Remove() was called. Some archaeology
(https://codereview.chromium.org/7717023/) reveals that the original
intention was to clear this state when REMOVE_CACHE was set, but due to
a curly brace mishap, we've been clearing it over-aggressively for
years.

When I changed this behavior to remove network state only when
REMOVE_CACHE is set, it revealed that a number of tests are relying on
state being asynchronously cleared. This is no longer the case, as for
example when only REMOVE_DOWNLOADS is set. This CL fixes that by calling
NotifyIfDone() at the end of RemoveImpl(), to catch cases where no state
is being wiped asynchronously. This is a little weird since download
removal does appear to be async -- but it matches the documentation of
BrowsingDataRemover::Observer, which says that the observer fires when
"keywords have been deleted, cache cleared and all other tasks
scheduled".

BUG=603682

Review-Url: https://codereview.chromium.org/1941073002
Cr-Commit-Position: refs/heads/master@{#391248}
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  // Always wipe accumulated network related data (TransportSecurityState and', '  // HttpServerPropertiesManager data).', '  waiting_for_clear_networking_history_ = true;', '  profile_->ClearNetworkingHistorySince(', '      delete_begin_,', '      base::Bind(&BrowsingDataRemover::OnClearedNetworkingHistory,', '                 weak_ptr_factory_.GetWeakPtr()));', ''], 'added_lines': ['', '    // When clearing cache, wipe accumulated network related data', '    // (TransportSecurityState and HttpServerPropertiesManager data).', '    waiting_for_clear_networking_history_ = true;', '    profile_->ClearNetworkingHistorySince(', '        delete_begin_,', '        base::Bind(&BrowsingDataRemover::OnClearedNetworkingHistory,', '                   weak_ptr_factory_.GetWeakPtr()));', '  // Notify in case all actions taken were synchronous.', '  NotifyIfDone();', '']}
description: browser/browsing_data/browsing_data_remover.cc in Google Chrome before 51.0.2704.63 deletes HPKP pins during cache clearing, which makes it easier for remote attackers to spoof web sites via a valid certificate from an arbitrary recognized Certification Authority.

code_evidence: The REMOVE_CACHE branch (lines 352-360) clears the web cache and schedules HTTP cache removal, but does not clear accumulated network security state such as TransportSecurityState (HPKP/HSTS) or HttpServerPropertiesManager data.

Lines 449-455 unconditionally set waiting_for_clear_networking_history_ and call profile_->ClearNetworkingHistorySince() whenever RemoveImpl runs, regardless of whether REMOVE_CACHE is in remove_mask.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function fails to restrict which resources are affected by the requested operation: it deletes protected network-security state without the corresponding REMOVE_CACHE authorization, which is an improper restriction of access to a resource. This is an access-control enforcement error rather than a separate weakness class.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The network-history wipe is gated only by the function being invoked, not by the REMOVE_CACHE flag. A caller requesting removal of unrelated data (e.g., only REMOVE_DOWNLOADS) still triggers ClearNetworkingHistorySince(), deleting HPKP pins and HSTS state that the requested operation did not authorize. The consequence is loss of certificate-pinning protection, allowing an attacker with a certificate from any recognized CA to spoof sites.

commit_msg:
Issues 396, 397: Ignore entries with empty filenames.

Bugs in the rar and cab readers lead to returning entries
with empty filenames.  Make bsdtar resistant to this.

Of course, we should also fix the rar and cab
readers to handle these cases correctly and either
return correctly-populated entries or fail cleanly.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\tconst char *p = archive_entry_pathname(entry);', "\t\tif (p == NULL || p[0] == '\\0') {", '\t\t\tlafe_warnc(0, "Archive entry has empty or unreadable filename ... skipping.");', '\t\t\tbsdtar->return_value = 1;', '\t\t\tcontinue;', '\t\t}']}
description: bsdtar in libarchive before 3.2.0 returns a success code without filling the entry when the header is a "split file in multivolume RAR," which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference and crash) via a crafted rar file.

code_evidence: archive_read_next_header returns an entry that may have a NULL or empty pathname; the code only checks the return status r, not the entry's pathname validity.
In list mode (mode == 't'), archive_entry_pathname(entry) is passed directly to safe_fprintf; if it returned NULL, this would be a NULL dereference.
In extract mode, archive_entry_pathname(entry) is used in yes()/verbose output and edit_pathname without verifying non-NULL.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences a pointer from archive_entry_pathname that may be NULL, matching CWE-476 (NULL Pointer Dereference). This is distinct from a generic unchecked return value: the specific unsafe operation is the pointer dereference on a possibly-NULL pathname.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: A crafted RAR split-file header causes the reader to return success without populating the entry's pathname. The loop proceeds to dereference archive_entry_pathname(entry) (e.g., in safe_fprintf or edit_pathname) without a NULL check, causing a NULL pointer dereference and crash. Root cause is the missing pathname validation after a successful header read; the consequence is a denial-of-service crash.

commit_msg:
exec: Respect as_tranlsate_internal length clamp

address_space_translate_internal will clamp the *plen length argument
based on the size of the memory region being queried. The iommu walker
logic in addresss_space_translate was ignoring this by discarding the
post fn call value of *plen. Fix by just always using *plen as the
length argument throughout the fn, removing the len local variable.

This fixes a bootloader bug when a single elf section spans multiple
QEMU memory regions.

Signed-off-by: Peter Crosthwaite <peter.crosthwaite@xilinx.com>
Message-Id: <1426570554-15940-1-git-send-email-peter.crosthwaite@xilinx.com>
Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    hwaddr len = *plen;', '        len = MIN(len, (addr | iotlb.addr_mask) - addr + 1);', '        len = MIN(page, len);', '    *plen = len;'], 'added_lines': ['        *plen = MIN(*plen, (addr | iotlb.addr_mask) - addr + 1);', '        *plen = MIN(page, *plen);']}
description: QEMU (aka Quick Emulator) built to use 'address_space_translate' to map an address to a MemoryRegionSection is vulnerable to an OOB r/w access issue. It could occur while doing pci_dma_read/write calls. Affects QEMU versions >= 1.6.0 and <= 2.3.1. A privileged user inside guest could use this flaw to crash the guest instance resulting in DoS.

code_evidence: Line 8 snapshots the caller's *plen into local len, but line 12 passes plen (not len) to address_space_translate_internal, which clamps *plen to the region size. Line 20 and line 29 then MIN against the stale len, and line 31 overwrites the clamped *plen with that stale, larger value, discarding the internal clamp.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function returns an oversized length that callers use as a buffer bound for DMA reads/writes, producing writes past the intended memory region — CWE-787. It is a length/bounds-accounting defect rather than an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125), since the consequence is memory modification beyond the region.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the local len is initialized once from *plen and never refreshed after address_space_translate_internal reduces *plen to the actual memory-region size. When an IOMMU translation or an ELF section spans multiple regions, the returned *plen exceeds the mapped section, so a subsequent pci_dma_read/write accesses past the region boundary, causing an out-of-bounds access and guest DoS.

within the allocation, which means the object could potentially extend
beyond the end of the allocation. Avoid this case by just allocating
enough space to catch any accesses beyond the end. Seen with GCC 13:

      |                                            ^~
../include/uapi/linux/byteorder/little_endian.h:37:51: note: in definition of macro '__le16_to_cpu'

In file included from ../drivers/usb/storage/ene_ub6250.c:5:
In function 'kmalloc',
    inlined from 'ms_lib_process_bootblock' at ../drivers/usb/storage/ene_ub6250.c:942:15:
../include/linux/slab.h:580:24: note: at offset [256, 512] into object of size 512 allocated by 'kmalloc_trace'
  580 |                 return kmalloc_trace(

Cc: Alan Stern <stern@rowland.harvard.edu>

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tPageBuffer = kmalloc(MS_BYTES_PER_PAGE, GFP_KERNEL);'], 'added_lines': ['\tPageBuffer = kzalloc(MS_BYTES_PER_PAGE * 2, GFP_KERNEL);']}
description: An issue was discovered in drivers/usb/storage/ene_ub6250.c for the ENE UB6250 reader driver in the Linux kernel before 6.2.5. An object could potentially extend beyond the end of an allocation.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function performs a single fixed-size kmalloc of MS_BYTES_PER_PAGE with no attacker-controlled or unbounded allocation size/count; the defect is an out-of-bounds access due to insufficient allocation relative to a later struct offset, not resource allocation without limits/throttling (CWE-770).

description: PHP before 5.4.42, 5.5.x before 5.5.26, and 5.6.x before 5.6.10 does not ensure that pathnames lack %00 sequences, which might allow remote attackers to read or write to arbitrary files via crafted input to an application that calls (1) a DOMDocument save method or (2) the GD imagepsloadfont function, as demonstrated by a filename\0.html attack that bypasses an intended configuration in which client users may write to only .html files.

commit_msg:
patch 9.0.0104: going beyond allocated memory when evaluating string constant

Problem:    Going beyond allocated memory when evaluating string constant.
Solution:   Properly skip over <Key> form.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t    {', '\t\tint\t\tmodifiers = 0;', '\t\tint\t\tflags = FSK_KEYCODE | FSK_IN_STRING;', '', '', "\t\t// Skip to the '>' to avoid using '{' inside for string", '\t\t// interpolation.', "\t\tif (p[1] != '*')", '\t\t    flags |= FSK_SIMPLIFY;', '\t\tif (find_special_key(&p, &modifiers, flags, NULL) != 0)', '\t\t    --p;  // leave "p" on the ">"', '\t    }']}
description: Heap-based Buffer Overflow in GitHub repository vim/vim prior to 9.0.0102.

code_evidence: The first loop sizes the heap buffer: it walks the string, and for a backslash followed by '<' it only adds 5 to extra; it does not parse/skip the full <Key> form, so a <Key> whose expansion exceeds the reserved 5 bytes is undercounted.

len is computed from p - *arg + extra and alloc(len) is the heap allocation. In the second loop, the '<' case calls trans_special to expand the key; extra is its returned length, end advances by it, and only then is end checked against the buffer end, so the write already happened past the allocation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The buffer is heap-allocated via alloc(len) and is overwritten past its bounds, matching CWE-122 (heap-based buffer overflow). This is a heap allocation defect rather than a generic stack overflow or off-by-one in a fixed array.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the allocation-size pass underestimates the space needed for <Key> sequences because it merely adds 5 rather than measuring the actual expansion. Trigger: a string constant containing a <Key> form whose expansion is longer than 5 bytes. Consequence: trans_special writes beyond the malloc'd buffer before the post-write bounds check, causing a heap-based buffer overflow.

code_evidence: On a short colormap read, the function throws UnexpectedEndOfFile without first releasing the heap buffer sun_colormap allocated at line 116.
The second red/green/blue read failure likewise throws without freeing the same buffer.
The third read failure repeats the same path, leaving the allocation unreleased.

ThrowReaderException(CorruptImageError,"UnexpectedEndOfFile");

if (count != (ssize_t) image->colors)
ThrowReaderException(CorruptImageError,"UnexpectedEndOfFile");

description: cpp-httplib through 0.5.8 does not filter \r\n in parameters passed into the set_redirect and set_header functions, which creates possibilities for CRLF injection and HTTP response splitting in some specific contexts.

Trigger: a caller passing attacker-influenced values containing \r\n. Consequence: the special elements survive into the header output, enabling CRLF injection/HTTP response splitting when a downstream component parses the response.

commit_msg:
bochs: Use unsigned variables for offsets and sizes (CVE-2014-0147)

Gets us rid of integer overflows resulting in negative sizes which
aren't correctly checked.

Signed-off-by: Kevin Wolf <kwolf@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Stefan Hajnoczi <stefanha@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Max Reitz <mreitz@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Stefan Hajnoczi <stefanha@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    int i;'], 'added_lines': ['    uint32_t i;']}
description: Qemu before 1.6.2 block diver for the various disk image formats used by Bochs and for the QCOW version 2 format, are vulnerable to a possible crash caused by signed data types or a logic error while creating QCOW2 snapshots, which leads to incorrectly calling update_refcount() routine.

code_evidence: The loop counter `i` is declared `int` rather than an unsigned type.
`s->catalog_size` is derived from the on-disk `bochs.catalog` field via `le32_to_cpu` and used directly in `s->catalog_size * 4` for both `g_malloc` and `bdrv_pread`.
The same signed `i` is compared against `s->catalog_size` in the loop, so a large catalog size makes the signed comparison/conversion problematic.
`s->data_offset` is computed as `le32_to_cpu(bochs.header) + (s->catalog_size * 4)`, where the multiplication can wrap.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The root cause is an unchecked arithmetic computation (`catalog_size * 4`, plus the offset addition) that can wrap, which is exactly integer overflow/wraparound. The signed `int i` change addresses the same class of signed-vs-unsigned size confusion; this is not a simple bounds-check omission but an arithmetic representation overflow.

evidence_lines.code: int i;

for (i = 0; i < s->catalog_size; i++)
le32_to_cpus(&s->catalog_bitmap[i]);
s->data_offset = le32_to_cpu(bochs.header) + (s->catalog_size * 4);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The on-disk catalog size is attacker-controlled and used in the multiplication `catalog_size * 4` without an overflow check. With a large value the product wraps to a small/negative size, so g_malloc allocates too little and bdrv_pread's size argument no longer matches the intended catalog, while the signed loop counter also mishandles the bound, leading to out-of-bounds access/crash.

commit_msg:
x86/shadow: hold references for the duration of emulated writes

The (misnamed) emulate_gva_to_mfn() function translates a linear address to an
mfn, but releases its page reference before returning the mfn to its caller.

sh_emulate_map_dest() uses the results of one or two translations to construct
a virtual mapping to the underlying frames, completes an emulated
write/cmpxchg, then unmaps the virtual mappings.

The page references need holding until the mappings are unmapped, or the
frames can change ownership before the writes occurs.

This is XSA-219.

Signed-off-by: Andrew Cooper <andrew.cooper3@citrix.com>
Reviewed-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Reviewed-by: Tim Deegan <tim@xen.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['', '    sh_ctxt->mfn[0] = emulate_gva_to_mfn(v, vaddr, sh_ctxt);', '    if ( !mfn_valid(sh_ctxt->mfn[0]) )', '        return ((mfn_x(sh_ctxt->mfn[0]) == BAD_GVA_TO_GFN) ?', '                MAPPING_EXCEPTION :', '                (mfn_x(sh_ctxt->mfn[0]) == READONLY_GFN) ?', '                MAPPING_SILENT_FAIL : MAPPING_UNHANDLEABLE);', '            return ((mfn_x(sh_ctxt->mfn[1]) == BAD_GVA_TO_GFN) ?', '                    MAPPING_EXCEPTION :', '                    (mfn_x(sh_ctxt->mfn[1]) == READONLY_GFN) ?', '                    MAPPING_SILENT_FAIL : MAPPING_UNHANDLEABLE);'], 'added_lines': ['', '    sh_ctxt->mfn[0] = emulate_gva_to_mfn(v, vaddr, sh_ctxt);', '    if ( !mfn_valid(sh_ctxt->mfn[0]) )', '    {', '        switch ( mfn_x(sh_ctxt->mfn[0]) )', '        {', '        case BAD_GVA_TO_GFN: return MAPPING_EXCEPTION;', '        case READONLY_GFN:   return MAPPING_SILENT_FAIL;', '        default:             return MAPPING_UNHANDLEABLE;', '        }', '    }', '        put_page(mfn_to_page(sh_ctxt->mfn[0]));', '        {', '            put_page(mfn_to_page(sh_ctxt->mfn[0]));', '            switch ( mfn_x(sh_ctxt->mfn[1]) )', '            {', '            case BAD_GVA_TO_GFN: return MAPPING_EXCEPTION;', '            case READONLY_GFN:   return MAPPING_SILENT_FAIL;', '            default:             return MAPPING_UNHANDLEABLE;', '            }', '        }', '        {', '            put_page(mfn_to_page(sh_ctxt->mfn[0]));', '            put_page(mfn_to_page(sh_ctxt->mfn[1]));', '        }']}
description: The shadow-paging feature in Xen through 4.8.x mismanages page references and consequently introduces a race condition, which allows guest OS users to obtain Xen privileges, aka XSA-219.

code_evidence: emulate_gva_to_mfn() returns an mfn whose page reference is released before sh_emulate_map_dest() uses the mfn; the returned mfn is stored in sh_ctxt->mfn[0] and only validated with mfn_valid(), with no reference retained across the call.
The second translation for a cross-page write is likewise stored in sh_ctxt->mfn[1] and validated, again without holding a page reference for subsequent use.

vmap(sh_ctxt->mfn, 2) builds a virtual mapping from the mfn values obtained earlier; between translation and this mapping (and the later emulated write) the caller holds no reference, so the frames can be reallocated or changed in ownership.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs a multi-step sequence (translate, then map/write) on a shared resource (the underlying page frame) without exclusive access, leaving a timing window in which another code sequence can change the frame's ownership. That is a concurrent-execution race with improper synchronization, matching CWE-362 rather than a plain use-after-free, since the defect is the missing reference held across the window.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the translation helpers return mfns without keeping the underlying page references alive, so the mfn values held in sh_ctxt->mfn[] are not pinned. Trigger: a concurrent operation frees or reassigns the frame after translation but before vmap and the emulated write complete. Consequence: the emulated write targets a frame no longer owned for that purpose, enabling a race that can corrupt state and escalate guest privileges.

commit_msg:
NetKVM: BZ#1169718: Checking the length only on read

Signed-off-by: Joseph Hindin <yhindin@rehat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    return ParaNdis_CheckSumVerify(&SGBuffer, ulDataLength, 0, flags, caller);'], 'added_lines': ['                                                BOOLEAN verifyLength,', '    return ParaNdis_CheckSumVerify(&SGBuffer, ulDataLength, 0, flags, verifyLength, caller);']}
description: The NetKVM Windows Virtio driver allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (guest crash) via a crafted length value in an IP packet, as demonstrated by a value that does not account for the size of the IP options.

code_evidence: The function copies the caller-supplied ulDataLength straight into SGBuffer.size without checking it against the actual buffer, then forwards the same unchecked length to ParaNdis_CheckSumVerify.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-20 fits because the function accepts a length input and fails to validate that it is consistent with the actual data before using it for memory access sizing; this is improper validation of a size/consistency property, not a transformation or filtering error.

evidence_lines.code:
SGBuffer.size = ulDataLength;
return ParaNdis_CheckSumVerify(&SGBuffer, ulDataLength, 0, flags, caller);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the wrapper trusts the attacker-controlled ulDataLength as both the scatter-gather size and the length passed to checksum verification, with no bound or consistency check against the real packet/IP header and options size. Trigger: a crafted IP packet whose length field does not account for IP options. Consequence: out-of-bounds processing that can crash the guest, i.e. a denial of service.

commit_msg:
Correctly load/initialize classes when using ConstantPool

- do not load classes in the "ifLoaded" calls
- never intitialize classes in the natives
- do not update the constant pool when querying from the natives

Fixes: #12016

[ci skip]

Signed-off-by: Graham Chapman <graham_chapman@ca.ibm.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (NULL != methodType ) {'], 'added_lines': ['\tif ((NULL != methodType) && J9_ARE_NO_BITS_SET(resolveFlags, J9_RESOLVE_FLAG_NO_CP_UPDATE)) {']}
description: In Eclipse Openj9 to version 0.25.0, usage of the jdk.internal.reflect.ConstantPool API causes the JVM in some cases to pre-resolve certain constant pool entries. This allows a user to call static methods or access static members without running the class initialization method, and may allow a user to observe uninitialized values.

code_evidence: Lines 18-20 return the cached ramCPEntry->type immediately if non-NULL, so a stale entry is trusted without resolving or initializing the referenced class.

Lines 82-86 store the resolved methodType into ramCPEntry->type whenever methodType is non-NULL; the fix adds a J9_RESOLVE_FLAG_NO_CP_UPDATE guard so resolution-only calls (e.g., from ConstantPool API) do not populate the constant pool with an uninitialized class reference.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-909 (Missing Initialization of Resource) fits: the constant-pool entry/class is populated and later consumed without the required class-initialization step, yielding reads of uninitialized data. It is not merely a caching bug; the missing initialization constraint (no CP update during query) is the specific weakness fixed.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the native resolver unconditionally wrote a resolved MethodType (and its referenced classes) into the RAM constant pool even when invoked in a query-only mode that must not pre-resolve entries. Trigger: a user calls jdk.internal.reflect.ConstantPool, which invokes resolution with J9_RESOLVE_FLAG_NO_CP_UPDATE; the entry is cached before class initialization runs. Consequence: later access uses the cached, uninitialized class, exposing uninitialized static values or static members before <clinit>.

commit_msg: tentative libsais safety patches
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    memset(state->sais_array, 0, sizeof(s32) * BWT_BOUND(state->block_size));', '    memset(b2, 0, size_src);']}
description: An issue was discovered in libbzip3.a in bzip3 before 1.3.0. A bz3_decode_block out-of-bounds write can occur with a crafted archive because bzip3 does not follow the required procedure for interacting with libsais.

code_evidence: size_src is derived from attacker-controlled lzp_size, rle_size, or orig_size; decode_bytes writes that many bytes into b2 = state->swap_buffer.
Only bwt_idx >= size_src is rejected; size_src itself is not checked against state->block_size or the swap_buffer capacity before libsais_unbwt.
libsais_unbwt writes the BWT output into b1 using state->sais_array and size_src, so an oversized size_src drives an out-of-bounds write.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked size_src is passed to libsais_unbwt, which writes beyond the intended buffer, directly matching CWE-787. This is a write past the buffer end, not merely a read overrun or integer issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: size_src from the crafted header is used as the unbwt output length without being bounded by the block/swap-buffer capacity (the later size_src check at line 76 occurs after libsais_unbwt). Trigger: a crafted archive sets lzp_size/rle_size/orig_size large but within bz3_bound, causing libsais_unbwt to write past the buffer; consequence is memory corruption/out-of-bounds write.

commit_msg:
We must flush the TLB before releasing i_mmap_rwsem to avoid the
potential reuse of an unshared PMDs page.  This is not true in the case
of move_hugetlb_page_tables().  The last reference on the page table can
therefore be dropped before the TLB flush took place.

Prevent it by reordering the operations and flushing the TLB before
releasing i_mmap_rwsem.

Fixes: 550a7d60bd5e ("mm, hugepages: add mremap() support for hugepage backed vma")
Signed-off-by: Nadav Amit <namit@vmware.com>
Reviewed-by: Mike Kravetz <mike.kravetz@oracle.com>
Cc: Mina Almasry <almasrymina@google.com>
Cc: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\ti_mmap_unlock_write(mapping);'], 'added_lines': ['\ti_mmap_unlock_write(mapping);']}
description: A memory leak flaw in the Linux kernel's hugetlbfs memory usage was found in the way the user maps some regions of memory twice using shmget() which are aligned to PUD alignment with the fault of some of the memory pages. A local user could use this flaw to get unauthorized access to some data.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function is a hugepage mremap helper that reorders i_mmap_unlock_write relative to TLB flush; it contains no memory allocation or release logic, so it does not support CWE-401 (missing release of memory).

commit_msg:
Jan Kara's analysis of the syzbot report (edited):

  The reproducer opens a directory on FUSE filesystem, it then attaches
  dnotify mark to the open directory.  After that a fuse_do_getattr() call
  finds that attributes returned by the server are inconsistent, and calls
  make_bad_inode() which, among other things does:

          inode->i_mode = S_IFREG;

  This then confuses dnotify which doesn't tear down its structures
  properly and eventually crashes.

Avoid calling make_bad_inode() on a live inode: switch to a private flag on
the fuse inode.  Also add the test to ops which the bad_inode_ops would
have caught.

This bug goes back to the initial merge of fuse in 2.6.14...

Reported-by: syzbot+f427adf9324b92652ccc@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Signed-off-by: Miklos Szeredi <mszeredi@redhat.com>
Tested-by: Jan Kara <jack@suse.cz>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (is_bad_inode(inode))'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (fuse_is_bad(inode))']}
description: An issue was discovered in the FUSE filesystem implementation in the Linux kernel before 5.10.6, aka CID-5d069dbe8aaf. fuse_do_getattr() calls make_bad_inode() in inappropriate situations, causing a system crash. NOTE: the original fix for this vulnerability was incomplete, and its incompleteness is tracked as CVE-2021-28950.

code_evidence: The function checks is_bad_inode(inode) and returns -EIO, but this guard relies on make_bad_inode() having set the bad-inode state on a live inode; the patch replaces this with fuse_is_bad(inode) to use a private flag instead.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The guard here is part of the incomplete cleanup: the bad-inode state is checked but the supporting dnotify structures tied to the live inode are not properly removed, matching CWE-459 Incomplete Cleanup rather than a pure input-validation weakness.

evidence_lines.code:
if (is_bad_inode(inode))
return -EIO;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the code path relies on make_bad_inode() marking a live FUSE inode, which resets i_mode to S_IFREG and leaves dnotify structures improperly torn down. Trigger: a FUSE server returns inconsistent attributes so fuse_do_getattr() calls make_bad_inode() on the open directory. Consequence: dnotify bookkeeping is not cleaned up, leading to a system crash.

commit_msg:
x509: excessive resource use verifying policy constraints

A security vulnerability has been identified in all supported versions
of OpenSSL related to the verification of X.509 certificate chains
that include policy constraints.  Attackers may be able to exploit this
vulnerability by creating a malicious certificate chain that triggers
exponential use of computational resources, leading to a denial-of-service
(DoS) attack on affected systems.

Fixes CVE-2023-0464

Reviewed-by: Tomas Mraz <tomas@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Shane Lontis <shane.lontis@oracle.com>
(Merged from https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/20570)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['                                    X509_POLICY_DATA *data)', '            if (ossl_policy_level_add_node(curr, data, node, NULL) == NULL)', '        if (ossl_policy_level_add_node(curr, data, last->anyPolicy, NULL) == NULL)'], 'added_lines': ['                                    X509_POLICY_DATA *data,', '                                    X509_POLICY_TREE *tree)', '            if (ossl_policy_level_add_node(curr, data, node, tree, 0) == NULL)', '        if (ossl_policy_level_add_node(curr, data, last->anyPolicy, tree, 0) == NULL)']}
description:
A security vulnerability has been identified in all supported versions

of OpenSSL related to the verification of X.509 certificate chains
that include policy constraints.  Attackers may be able to exploit this
vulnerability by creating a malicious certificate chain that triggers
exponential use of computational resources, leading to a denial-of-service
(DoS) attack on affected systems.

Policy processing is disabled by default but can be enabled by passing
the `-policy' argument to the command line utilities or by calling the
`X509_VERIFY_PARAM_set1_policies()' function.

code_evidence: The loop iterates over every node in the previous policy level and calls ossl_policy_level_add_node(curr, data, node, NULL) for each match, passing NULL as the tree argument so no tree-level state (such as a node count or depth bound) is available to limit work.
Similarly, the anyPolicy fallback adds a node with NULL tree context, again without any bound on node creation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function is part of X.509 policy-constraint validation, but the defect is unbounded resource use during policy processing, not improper validation of certificate authenticity or identity. CWE-295 concerns failing to correctly validate a certificate; here the certificate is processed, merely at excessive cost.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the policy-tree linking routine adds nodes without passing the X509_POLICY_TREE into ossl_policy_level_add_node, so no tree-wide resource accounting constrains the addition. Trigger: a malicious certificate chain with policy constraints causing matching to recurse across levels. Consequence: exponential node creation and computational resource exhaustion (DoS) during policy verification, not a certificate-validation bypass.

commit_msg:
Prevent overflow due to integer conversion to unsigned.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 387738045
Change-Id: Id7e95bc07e02df1c66b72bd09f389608c87bdebe
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    OP_REQUIRES(context, max_size_per_class > 0,', '                errors::InvalidArgument("max_size_per_class must be positive"));']}
description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. In affected versions an attacker can cause denial of service in applications serving models using `tf.raw_ops.NonMaxSuppressionV5` by triggering a division by 0. The [implementation](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/460e000de3a83278fb00b61a16d161b1964f15f4/tensorflow/core/kernels/image/non_max_suppression_op.cc#L170-L271) uses a user controlled argument to resize a `std::vector`. However, as `std::vector::resize` takes the size argument as a `size_t` and `output_size` is an `int`, there is an implicit conversion to unsigned. If the attacker supplies a negative value, this conversion results in a crash. A similar issue occurs in `CombinedNonMaxSuppression`. We have patched the issue in GitHub commit 3a7362750d5c372420aa8f0caf7bf5b5c3d0f52d and commit [b5cdbf12ffcaaffecf98f22a6be5a64bb96e4f58. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.6.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.5.1, TensorFlow 2.4.3, and TensorFlow 2.3.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: Line 12 reads a user-controlled scalar directly into a signed int max_size_per_class with no lower-bound check; only shape is validated at lines 8-11.

The signed value is passed at lines 46-49 into BatchedNonMaxSuppressionOp, where it is used as a size for vector allocation/resize; a negative value converts to a large unsigned size_t, producing a crash or OOM.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is an incorrect conversion between numeric types: a signed int with a negative value is implicitly converted to an unsigned size_t, producing an unexpected large value used in a sensitive allocation context. This matches CWE-681 rather than a pure bounds-check omission, since the conversion itself yields the dangerous value.

evidence_lines.code:
BatchedNonMaxSuppressionOp(context, boxes, scores, num_boxes,
max_size_per_class, max_total_size_per_batch,
score_threshold_val, iou_threshold_val,
pad_per_class_, clip_boxes_);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: max_size_per_class is extracted as a signed int from attacker-controlled input and forwarded without a positivity constraint, so implicit conversion to an unsigned size in the downstream resize yields a huge value. Trigger: supplying a negative max_output_size. Consequence: denial of service via crash/OOM; the added check at line 12 (in the patch) enforces positivity.

commit_msg: Prevent a possible read out of bounds in the processing of IPv6 extension headers.

description: Contiki-NG is an open-source, cross-platform operating system for Next-Generation IoT devices. The 6LoWPAN implementation in Contiki-NG may cast a UDP header structure at a certain offset in a packet buffer. The code does not check whether the packet buffer is large enough to fit a full UDP header structure from the offset where the casting is made. commit_msg:
PR26574, heap buffer overflow in _bfd_elf_slurp_secondary_reloc_section

A horribly fuzzed object with section headers inside the ELF header.
Disallow that, and crazy reloc sizes.

	PR 26574
	* elfcode.h (elf_object_p): Sanity check section header offset.
	* elf.c (_bfd_elf_slurp_secondary_reloc_section): Sanity check
	sh_entsize.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t  && hdr->sh_info == (unsigned) elf_section_data (sec)->this_idx)'], 'added_lines': ['\t  && hdr->sh_info == (unsigned) elf_section_data (sec)->this_idx', '\t  && (hdr->sh_entsize == ebd->s->sizeof_rel', '\t      || hdr->sh_entsize == ebd->s->sizeof_rela))']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Binary File Descriptor (BFD) library (aka libbfd), as distributed in GNU Binutils 2.35.1. A heap-based buffer over-read can occur in bfd_getl_signed_32 in libbfd.c because sh_entsize is not validated in _bfd_elf_slurp_secondary_reloc_section in elf.c.

code_evidence: Lines 19-20 select a secondary reloc section based on sh_type and sh_info, then line 37 takes entsize = hdr->sh_entsize without validating it against the expected sizeof_rel/sizeof_rela. Line 44 computes reloc_count = NUM_SHDR_ENTRIES(hdr) from the unvalidated sh_entsize.

Lines 59-61 read hdr->sh_size bytes into native_relocs, then the loop at 68-71 advances native_reloc by entsize each iteration for reloc_count iterations, and line 75 passes native_reloc to swap_reloca_in.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads reloc records through a pointer advanced by an unvalidated entsize while the buffer length is sh_size, directly producing a read past the buffer end, which matches CWE-125. It is not merely an integer overflow, since the read itself exceeds the allocated region.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: sh_entsize from the section header is trusted to size per-entry reads and to derive reloc_count, but it is never constrained to sizeof_rel/sizeof_rela. A crafted ELF with an oversized or mismatched sh_entsize makes NUM_SHDR_ENTRIES and the native_reloc pointer stride inconsistent with the buffer read at line 60, so swap_reloca_in reads past the allocated/read native_relocs buffer. Trigger: attacker-supplied secondary reloc section header; consequence: heap-based out-of-bounds read.

commit_msg:
codegen.c: fix a bug in `gen_values()`.

- Fix limit handling that fails 15 arguments method calls.
- Fix too early argument packing in arrays.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if (is_splat || n > limit || cursp() >= slimit) { /* flush stack */'], 'added_lines': ['    if (is_splat || cursp() >= slimit) { /* flush stack */', '  else if (n > limit) {', '    pop_n(n);', '    genop_2(s, OP_ARRAY, cursp(), n);', '    return -1;', '  }']}
description: Heap-based Buffer Overflow in Homebrew mruby prior to 3.2.

code_evidence: In the value-emitting loop, the flush/array-packing branch is entered when is_splat or cursp() >= slimit, but the prior n > limit condition (present in diff_func) is absent; n is reset to 0 after packing and incremented per non-splat element, so n can grow past limit before any flush.
After the loop, when !first, the tail emits OP_ARYPUSH with n and returns -1; there is no check that n is within limit before emitting the packed array/push operation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing limit constraint leads to writing an over-large element count into generated array operations, matching a heap buffer overflow (CWE-122). It is not merely an integer issue; the unsafe operation is unbounded packing that can exceed the allocated buffer.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the limit guard no longer forces a flush when the accumulated element count n exceeds limit, and the tail path packs n elements without a bound check. Trigger: a call/array with many arguments (e.g. 15) makes n exceed limit, causing array construction/push with an oversized count. Consequence: the generated bytecode/stack handling can overflow a heap-allocated buffer, corrupting memory.

commit_msg:
[lite] Add some safety checks to avoid out of bound access for sparsity format

PiperOrigin-RevId: 416910386
Change-Id: Ic0b4dc048dc4b5a6309c572b8c4c9f776e4db60a
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      int orig_dim = traversal_order_[original_rank + block_dim];', '      block_size_[block_dim] = dense_size[orig_dim];', '      blocked_shape_[i] = dense_shape_[i] / dense_size[orig_dim];', '      block_dim++;'], 'added_lines': ['      if (original_rank + block_dim < traversal_order_.size()) {', '        int orig_dim = traversal_order_[original_rank + block_dim];', '        block_size_[block_dim] = dense_size[orig_dim];', '        blocked_shape_[i] = dense_shape_[i] / dense_size[orig_dim];', '        block_dim++;', '      }']}
description: Tensorflow is an Open Source Machine Learning Framework. An attacker can craft a TFLite model that would allow limited reads and writes outside of arrays in TFLite. This exploits missing validation in the conversion from sparse tensors to dense tensors. The fix is included in TensorFlow 2.8.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.7.1, TensorFlow 2.6.3, and TensorFlow 2.5.3, as these are also affected and still in supported range. Users are advised to upgrade as soon as possible.

code_evidence: The loop iterates over original_rank and, when block_map_[block_dim] matches i, computes orig_dim = traversal_order_[original_rank + block_dim] and indexes dense_size[orig_dim]. Neither traversal_order_ nor dense_size is validated against attacker-controlled dimensions, so orig_dim can exceed dense_size bounds, causing an out-of-bounds read/write.
dim_metadata_ is sized to 2*format_.size() but indexed with 2*i and 2*i+1, and dense_size[i] is read without confirming i < dense_size.size(); mismatched format/dense_size vectors allow OOB access.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked orig_dim index into dense_size (and the 2*i indexing of dim_metadata_) permits writes/reads outside the intended buffers, which is exactly an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). The missing bounds check is the cause; the out-of-bounds access is the supported consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: sparse-to-dense conversion trusts traversal_order, block_map, format and dense_size vectors from the crafted model without checking index ranges. Trigger: a TFLite model with inconsistent vector sizes or an orig_dim value derived from traversal_order_ that exceeds dense_size. Consequence: out-of-bounds reads and writes past dense_size or dim_metadata_, enabling limited memory corruption or crash.

The UAF is because:

 mount(pid: 921)               | cifsd(pid: 923)
-------------------------------|-------------------------------
                               | cifs_demultiplex_thread
SMB2_negotiate                 |
 cifs_send_recv                |
  compound_send_recv           |
   smb_send_rqst               |
    wait_for_response          |
     wait_event_state      [1] |
                               |  standard_receive3
                               |   cifs_handle_standard
                               |    handle_mid
                               |     mid->resp_buf = buf;  [2]
                               |     dequeue_mid           [3]
     KILL the process      [4] |
    resp_iov[i].iov_base = buf |
 free_rsp_buf              [5] |
                               |   is_network_name_deleted [6]
                               |   callback

1. After send request to server, wait the response until
    mid->mid_state != SUBMITTED;
2. Receive response from server, and set it to mid;
3. Set the mid state to RECEIVED;
4. Kill the process, the mid state already RECEIVED, get 0;
5. Handle and release the negotiate response;
6. UAF.

It can be easily reproduce with add some delay in [3] - [6].

Only sync call has the problem since async call's callback is
executed in cifsd process.

Add an extra state to mark the mid state to READY before wakeup the
waitter, then it can get the resp safely.

Fixes: ec637e3ffb6b ("[CIFS] Avoid extra large buffer allocation (and memcpy) in cifs_readpages")
Reviewed-by: Paulo Alcantara (SUSE) <pc@manguebit.com>
Signed-off-by: Zhang Xiaoxu <zhangxiaoxu5@huawei.com>
Signed-off-by: Steve French <stfrench@microsoft.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tcase MID_RESPONSE_RECEIVED:'], 'added_lines': ['\tcase MID_RESPONSE_READY:']}
description: A use-after-free flaw was found in smb2_is_status_io_timeout() in CIFS in the Linux Kernel. After CIFS transfers response data to a system call, there are still local variable points to the memory region, and if the system call frees it faster than CIFS uses it, CIFS will access a free memory region, leading to a denial of service.

code_evidence: The switch on mid->mid_state treats MID_RESPONSE_RECEIVED as a completed, safe state: it unlocks and returns 0 without releasing the mid.
For any other state, including the default branch, the function falls through to release_mid(mid) at line 31 after unlocking, freeing the mid.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function directly participates in the race that allows the freed mid/response buffer to be referenced afterward, matching CWE-416. It is not merely a double-free or leak; the flaw is use of memory after release.

evidence_lines.code:
spin_unlock(&server->mid_lock);
release_mid(mid);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The mid state is set to RECEIVED by the receive path before the synchronous waiter resumes; cifs_sync_mid_result accepts that state and returns success while the response buffer/mid is still being handled, then the response buffer is freed. The concurrent receive-side callback later dereferences the freed mid/buffer, causing a UAF read (as in the reported smb2_is_network_name_deleted fault). Root cause: the waiter is woken on a state that does not guarantee the response is no longer in use; the missing READY state means release/access ordering is unsynchronized.

commit_msg:
mm: mempolicy: require at least one nodeid for MPOL_PREFERRED

Using an empty (malformed) nodelist that is not caught during mount option
parsing leads to a stack-out-of-bounds access.

The option string that was used was: "mpol=prefer:,".  However,
MPOL_PREFERRED requires a single node number, which is not being provided
here.

Add a check that 'nodes' is not empty after parsing for MPOL_PREFERRED's
nodeid.

Fixes: 095f1fc4ebf3 ("mempolicy: rework shmem mpol parsing and display")
Reported-by: Entropy Moe <3ntr0py1337@gmail.com>
Reported-by: syzbot+b055b1a6b2b958707a21@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Signed-off-by: Randy Dunlap <rdunlap@infradead.org>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>
Tested-by: syzbot+b055b1a6b2b958707a21@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Cc: Lee Schermerhorn <lee.schermerhorn@hp.com>
Link: http://lkml.kernel.org/r/89526377-7eb6-b662-e1d8-4430928abde9@infradead.org
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t * Insist on a nodelist of one node only'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t * Insist on a nodelist of one node only, although later', '\t\t * we use first_node(nodes) to grab a single node, so here', '\t\t * nodelist (or nodes) cannot be empty.', '\t\t\t\tgoto out;', '\t\t\tif (nodes_empty(nodes))']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel through 5.6.2. mpol_parse_str in mm/mempolicy.c has a stack-based out-of-bounds write because an empty nodelist is mishandled during mount option parsing, aka CID-aa9f7d5172fa. NOTE: Someone in the security community disagrees that this is a vulnerability because the issue “is a bug in parsing mount options which can only be specified by a privileged user, so triggering the bug does not grant any powers not already held.”

code_evidence: For MPOL_PREFERRED, when a nodelist is present the loop only verifies that the string consists of digits; it never checks that any digit exists, so an empty nodelist (e.g. "prefer:,") passes.

Later, because nodelist is non-NULL, the code calls first_node(nodes) on the parsed mask. If the nodelist was empty, nodes was parsed from an empty string and can be empty, so first_node reads a node index from an empty nodemask.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the missing non-empty check lets first_node read/write beyond the intended bounds of the stack nodemask. This is a bounds violation on a buffer rather than merely a logic error; the parse-validation gap is the cause, and the out-of-bounds access is the supported weakness.

evidence_lines.code:
else if (nodelist)
new->v.preferred_node = first_node(nodes);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the MPOL_PREFERRED branch accepts an empty nodelist because the digit-scanning loop does not require at least one digit. Trigger: mounting with a malformed option such as "mpol=prefer:,". Consequence: first_node(nodes) operates on an empty nodemask, causing an out-of-bounds access on the stack-allocated nodes mask.

commit_msg:
Fix oobread crash in java parser ##crash

* Reported by @bet4it via @huntrdev
* BountyID: 229a2e0d-9e5c-402f-9a24-57fa2eb1aaa7
* Reproducer: poc4java
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tut8 *attr_buf = NULL;', '\tattr_buf = (ut8 *) calloc (pending + 1, 1);'], 'added_lines': ['\t// XXX this pending is wrong and too expensive', '\tut8 *attr_buf = (ut8 *) calloc (pending + 1, 1);']}
description: Out-of-bounds Read in r_bin_java_constant_value_attr_new function in GitHub repository radareorg/radare2 prior to 5.7.0. The bug causes the program reads data past the end 2f the intented buffer. Typically, this can allow attackers to read sensitive information from other memory locations or cause a crash. More details see [CWE-125: Out-of-bounds read](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/125.html).

code_evidence: Line 3 computes `pending` as `len - offset` in a signed int; nothing guarantees offset <= len, so pending can be negative, and the cast to calloc's size argument can wrap to a huge value or allocate a small buffer.

Line 4 forms `a_buf = offset + buf` without verifying that offset lies within buf's `len` bytes. Line 11 then memcpy's `pending` bytes from `a_buf` into the allocated attr_buf, reading past the source buffer's end when offset+len exceeds the actual buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe memcpy source pointer extends past the intended buffer boundary, exactly matching CWE-125's out-of-bounds read. It is a read (not CWE-787 write) because the overflow occurs on the source operand; the destination allocation is not the corrupted object.

evidence_lines.code:
int pending = len - offset;
const ut8 *a_buf = offset + buf;

attr_buf = (ut8 *) calloc (pending + 1, 1);
memcpy (attr_buf, a_buf, pending); return attr_buf;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function trusts caller-supplied offset/len/sz without validating that offset <= len or that offset+len stays within buf. Trigger: parsing a malformed Java attribute with an out-of-range offset causes memcpy at line 11 to read beyond buf. commit_msg:
librt: fix NULL pointer dereference (bug 28213)

Helper thread frees copied attribute on NOTIFY_REMOVED message
received from the OS kernel.  Unfortunately, it fails to check whether
copied attribute actually exists (data.attr != NULL).  This worked
earlier because free() checks passed pointer before actually
attempting to release corresponding memory.  But
__pthread_attr_destroy assumes pointer is not NULL.

So passing NULL pointer to __pthread_attr_destroy will result in
segmentation fault.  This scenario is possible if
notification->sigev_notify_attributes == NULL (which means default
thread attributes should be used).

Signed-off-by: Nikita Popov <npv1310@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Siddhesh Poyarekar <siddhesh@sourceware.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      else if (data.raw[NOTIFY_COOKIE_LEN - 1] == NOTIFY_REMOVED)'], 'added_lines': ['      else if (data.raw[NOTIFY_COOKIE_LEN - 1] == NOTIFY_REMOVED && data.attr != NULL)']}
description: In librt in the GNU C Library (aka glibc) through 2.34, sysdeps/unix/sysv/linux/mq_notify.c mishandles certain NOTIFY_REMOVED data, leading to a NULL pointer dereference. NOTE: this vulnerability was introduced as a side effect of the CVE-2021-33574 fix.

code_evidence: In the NOTIFY_REMOVED branch, the code calls __pthread_attr_destroy(data.attr) and free(data.attr) without first verifying that data.attr is non-NULL. data.attr is populated from the received netlink message, and the commit notes it may be NULL when notification->sigev_notify_attributes is NULL (default thread attributes).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Passing a possibly-NULL data.attr to __pthread_attr_destroy, which dereferences it without a NULL check, matches CWE-476 (NULL Pointer Dereference). The added data.attr != NULL guard confirms the missing constraint; this is a direct dereference of an unchecked pointer, not merely a logic flaw.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the NOTIFY_REMOVED handler unconditionally passes data.attr to __pthread_attr_destroy, which assumes a non-NULL pointer. Trigger: a notification message with the NOTIFY_REMOVED cookie and NULL attribute. Consequence: NULL pointer dereference and process crash (DoS).

description: In libavformat/nsvdec.c in FFmpeg 2.4 and 3.3.3, a DoS in nsv_parse_NSVf_header() due to lack of an EOF (End of File) check might cause huge CPU consumption. When a crafted NSV file, which claims a large "table_entries_used" field in the header but does not contain sufficient backing data, is provided, the loop over 'table_entries_used' would consume huge CPU resources, since there is no EOF check inside the loop.

Network transport abstraction layer supports packet fragmentation.
While fragmenting a packet, it checks for more fragments from

description: A CiffDirectory::readDirectory integer overflow and out-of-bounds read in Exiv2 through 0.27.1 allows an attacker to cause a denial of service (SIGSEGV) via a crafted CRW image file.

code_evidence: Line 5 computes the directory offset as getULong(pData + size - 4, byteOrder); if size is 0-3, size-4 wraps to a huge uint32_t, causing an out-of-bounds read before any bound check.
Line 6 checks o + 2 > size; the addition o+2 can itself wrap when o is near UINT32_MAX, so the guard may pass and getUShort(pData + o) reads out of bounds.
Inside the loop, line 14 checks o + 10 > size, but o+10 can wrap after repeated o += 10 increments, and the check is per-entry rather than validating count*10 up front.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the guard expressions rely on additions that can overflow and assume the result is larger than the operands; the wraparound defeats the intended size constraint, directly enabling the out-of-bounds read. The related out-of-bounds read is a consequence, not the root cause.

if (o + 2 > size) throw Error(33);

if (o + 10 > size) throw Error(33);

o += 10;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is unchecked unsigned arithmetic on size and offset: size-4, o+2 and o+10 can wrap to small values, defeating the bounds checks, and the count-driven loop advances o without an overflow-safe total-size constraint. destroy() will decrement the refcount on the interface, so that
it needs to be taken so early that it never undercounts.

description: In the Linux kernel before 5.2.10, there is a use-after-free bug that can be caused by a malicious USB device in the drivers/usb/class/cdc-acm.c driver, aka CID-c52873e5a1ef.

code_evidence: In acm_probe, acm->control is assigned control_interface at line 158, but the interface reference is only acquired later at line 284 via usb_get_intf(control_interface). Error paths alloc_fail1 through alloc_fail6 (lines 296-321) call tty_port_put(&acm->port) and free acm without ever releasing a control-interface reference on those paths; the reference acquired at line 284 is not balanced on alloc_fail6. The patch moves usb_get_intf(acm->control) to immediately after acm->control is set so destruct() can undo it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect is an unbalanced reference-count/lifetime ordering issue whose supported consequence is reuse of freed memory (the acm structure and control interface) during probe error cleanup, matching CWE-416 rather than a pure resource leak.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the control interface reference is taken too late relative to the allocation and error-exit sequence, so destruct()/tty_port_put can decrement a reference that was never taken or is taken after the object is already torn down. Trigger: a malicious USB device causing probe to fail after acm is allocated. Consequence: the interface can be released while still referenced, leading to use-after-free of acm/control_interface during teardown.

x86/spec-ctrl: Mitigate Speculative Return Stack Overflow

On native, synthesise the SRSO bits by probing various hardware properties as
given by AMD.

Extend the IBPB-on-entry mitigations to Zen3/4 CPUs.  There is a microcode
prerequisite to make this an effective mitigation.

This is part of XSA-434 / CVE-2023-20569

Signed-off-by: Andrew Cooper <andrew.cooper3@citrix.com>
Reviewed-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Reviewed-by: Roger Pau Monné <roger.pau@citrix.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    srso_calculations(hw_smt_enabled);', '']}
description: A side channel vulnerability on some of the AMD CPUs may allow an attacker to influence the return address prediction. This may result in speculative execution at an attacker-controlled address, potentially leading to information disclosure.

code_evidence: hw_smt_enabled is computed from check_smt_enabled() and has_spec_ctrl from CPU feature bits, feeding later mitigation decisions.
The opt_rsb_pv default and SC_RSB_IDLE capability depend on hw_smt_enabled and CPU vendor/family, so mitigation state varies with hardware configuration.
ibpb_calculations() is invoked at this point; the patch adds srso_calculations(hw_smt_enabled) immediately before it, but the added call is not present in the supplied function body.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-203 fits because the function's behavior and protections vary observably with hardware/configuration state (SMT, CPU family), which is the discrepancy exploited by the side channel. It is not a direct out-of-bounds or injection flaw; the weakness is the observable, configuration-dependent behavior rather than a specific memory corruption.

evidence_lines.code: ibpb_calculations();

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function derives mitigation settings (RSB, IBPB, spec-ctrl flags) from hardware properties such as SMT state and CPU model. On affected AMD CPUs the return-address predictor can be influenced, and because the mitigation configuration differs by hardware/configuration, the resulting speculative-execution behavior is observable. Root cause is configuration-dependent mitigation state; the supported consequence is information disclosure via a side channel, not a direct memory-safety defect in this function.

description: A use-after-free flaw was found in btrfs_search_slot in fs/btrfs/ctree.c in btrfs in the Linux Kernel.This flaw allows an attacker to crash the system and possibly cause a kernel information lea

code_evidence: btrfs_run_qgroups reads fs_info->quota_root under qgroup_lock and then calls update_qgroup_info_item (line 14) and update_qgroup_status_item (line 27), which descend into btrfs_search_slot using the quota root. The function itself does not take qgroup_ioctl_lock; it relies on callers to serialize against quota disable, and the only guard added is a lockdep assertion.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function accesses a quota root object after it may have been freed by a racing quota disable, which is exactly the reuse of freed memory described by CWE-416. The lockdep assertion documents the missing serialization but does not itself prevent the race; the underlying weakness is use-after-free rather than a mere locking defect.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: btrfs_run_qgroups dereferences fs_info->quota_root without holding qgroup_ioctl_lock, so a concurrent quota disable ioctl can free the quota root (btrfs_put_root) while this function is still using it. Trigger: quota assign ioctl running in parallel with quota disable. Consequence: use-after-free read in btrfs_search_slot, causing a kernel crash and possible information leak.

commit_msg:
[gsm] Delay the creation of the GsmXSMPClient until it really exists

We used to create the GsmXSMPClient before the XSMP connection is really
accepted. This can lead to some issues, though. An example is:
https://bugzilla.gnome.org/show_bug.cgi?id=598211#c19. Quoting:

 "What is happening is that a new client (probably metacity in your
 case) is opening an ICE connection in the GSM_MANAGER_PHASE_END_SESSION
 phase, which causes a new GsmXSMPClient to be added to the client
 store. The GSM_MANAGER_PHASE_EXIT phase then begins before the client
 has had a chance to establish a xsmp connection, which means that
 client->priv->conn will not be initialized at the point that xsmp_stop
 is called on the new unregistered client."

The fix is to create the GsmXSMPClient object when there's a real XSMP
connection. This implies moving the timeout that makes sure we don't
have an empty client to the XSMP server.

https://bugzilla.gnome.org/show_bug.cgi?id=598211
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['', '        if (client->priv->protocol_timeout > 0) {', '                g_source_remove (client->priv->protocol_timeout);', '        }'], 'added_lines': []}
description: Bad reference counting in the context of accept_ice_connection() in gsm-xsmp-server.c in old versions of gnome-session up until version 2.29.92 allows a local attacker to establish ICE connections to gnome-session with invalid authentication data (an invalid magic cookie). Each failed authentication attempt will leak a file descriptor in gnome-session. When the maximum number of file descriptors is exhausted in the gnome-session process, it will enter an infinite loop trying to communicate without success, consuming 100% of the CPU. The graphical session associated with the gnome-session process will stop working correctly, because communication with gnome-session is no longer possible.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The shown function only performs disconnect cleanup (source removal, SmsCleanUp, IceCloseConnection); it contains no loop or exit condition, and the patch merely deletes protocol_timeout cleanup, so it does not directly support an infinite-loop weakness.
