Validate arguments of `FractionalMaxPoolGrad`

PiperOrigin-RevId: 372274982
Change-Id: If46b0c442efa4eaef635ce6a476717060420122c
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    OP_REQUIRES(', '        context, tensor_in.dims() == tensor_in_and_out_dims,', '        errors::InvalidArgument("orig_input should be a tensor of rank 4, got ",', '                                tensor_in.DebugString()));', '    OP_REQUIRES(context, tensor_in.NumElements() > 0,', '                errors::InvalidArgument("orig_input must not be empty, got ",', '                                        tensor_in.DebugString()));', '    OP_REQUIRES(context, tensor_out.dims() == tensor_in_and_out_dims,', '                errors::InvalidArgument(', '                    "orig_output should be a tensor of rank 4, got ",', '                    tensor_out.DebugString()));', '    OP_REQUIRES(context, tensor_out.NumElements() > 0,', '                errors::InvalidArgument("orig_output must not be empty, got ",', '                                        tensor_out.DebugString()));']}
description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. The implementation of `tf.raw_ops.FractionalMaxPoolGrad` triggers an undefined behavior if one of the input tensors is empty. The code is also vulnerable to a denial of service attack as a `CHECK` condition becomes false and aborts the process. The implementation(https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/169054888d50ce488dfde9ca55d91d6325efbd5b/tensorflow/core/kernels/fractional_max_pool_op.cc#L215) fails to validate that input and output tensors are not empty and are of the same rank. Each of these unchecked assumptions is responsible for the above issues. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.5.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.4.2, TensorFlow 2.3.3, TensorFlow 2.2.3 and TensorFlow 2.1.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: input_size and output_size are filled by reading dim_size(i) for i in 0..3 from tensor_in and tensor_out with no rank check; a lower-rank tensor yields missing/unread dimensions.
Eigen maps are constructed over tensor_in and tensor_out_dup using those sizes; an empty or mismatched tensor produces an invalid mapping over unpopulated data.
The loop compares tensor_out_dup_mat(j,i) against tensor_out_mat(j,i) only under DCHECK, which is compiled out in release builds, so uninitialized temp contents are not actually validated.
out_arg_max_flat(index) is read and used as an index into input_backprop_flat, guarded by CHECK that aborts rather than returning an error.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-908 fits because the function uses tensor_out_dup and tensor_out_arg_max contents that were never guaranteed initialized, and the only guard is a release-compiled-out DCHECK. The aborting CHECK is a consequence; the unchecked empty-tensor assumption is the underlying uninitialized-resource use.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the kernel assumes rank-4, non-empty inputs and never validates them before deriving sizes and constructing Eigen maps. When an empty or wrong-rank tensor is supplied, tensor_out_dup/tensor_out_arg_max are used without meaningful initialization, and the DCHECK comparison is removed in release builds. Trigger: calling FractionalMaxPoolGrad with an empty input or output tensor. Consequence: reads of uninitialized resource contents and a failing CHECK that aborts the process (DoS).

commit_msg:
Don't change the state of the ETM flags until CCS processing

Changing the ciphersuite during a renegotiation can result in a crash
leading to a DoS attack. ETM has not been implemented in 1.1.0 for DTLS
so this is TLS only.

The problem is caused by changing the flag indicating whether to use ETM
or not immediately on negotiation of ETM, rather than at CCS. Therefore,
during a renegotiation, if the ETM state is changing (usually due to a
change of ciphersuite), then an error/crash will occur.

Due to the fact that there are separate CCS messages for read and write
we actually now need two flags to determine whether to use ETM or not.

CVE-2017-3733

Reviewed-by: Richard Levitte <levitte@openssl.org>

+++ func_after
@@ -66,7 +66,7 @@

         u_len >= 4 * (max_send_fragment = s->max_send_fragment) &&
         s->compress == NULL && s->msg_callback == NULL &&
-        !SSL_USE_ETM(s) && SSL_USE_EXPLICIT_IV(s) &&
+        !SSL_WRITE_ETM(s) && SSL_USE_EXPLICIT_IV(s) &&
         EVP_CIPHER_flags(EVP_CIPHER_CTX_cipher(s->enc_write_ctx)) &
         EVP_CIPH_FLAG_TLS1_1_MULTIBLOCK) {

description: During a renegotiation handshake if the Encrypt-Then-Mac extension is negotiated where it was not in the original handshake (or vice-versa) then this can cause OpenSSL 1.1.0 before 1.1.0e to crash (dependent on ciphersuite). Both clients and servers are affected.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function only switches the ETM gating check from SSL_USE_ETM to SSL_WRITE_ETM; the CVE-2017-3733 root cause (ETM flag state changed before CCS during renegotiation) lies in the handshake/ciphersuite negotiation code, not in input validation within this write path.

commit_msg:
journalctl: verify sealed log epochs are continuous

Currently empty epochs are not sealed. This allows an attacker to truncate
a sealed log and continue it without any problems showing when verifying the
log.

This partially addresses CVE-2023-31438. One way to extend this change to
address CVE-2023-31438 completely, would be to verify that there is exactly
one seal per epoch (and not sealing when the epoch has not ended yet).

the change also adds a journal-file flag: HEADER_COMPATIBLE_SEALED_CONTINUOUS
this flag indicates that a journal file is sealed continuously and decides whether
any missing crypto epochs should trigger a warning or an error.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['#if HAVE_GCRYPT', '        /* Write the final tag */', '        if (JOURNAL_HEADER_SEALED(f->header) && journal_file_writable(f)) {', '                int r;', '', '                r = journal_file_append_tag(f);', '                if (r < 0)', '                        log_error_errno(r, "Failed to append tag when closing journal: %m");', '        }', '#endif'], 'added_lines': ['        journal_file_write_final_tag(f);']}
description: An issue was discovered in systemd 253. An attacker can truncate a sealed log file and then resume log sealing such that checking the integrity shows no error, despite modifications. NOTE: the vendor reportedly sent "a reply denying that any of the finding was a security vulnerability."

code_evidence: journal_file_offline_close appends a final integrity tag via journal_file_append_tag only when JOURNAL_HEADER_SEALED(f->header) is true and the file is writable; a failure is merely logged with log_error_errno and execution continues to close the file.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-354 fits because the function handles creation of the integrity check value for the journal but does not ensure it is present/valid before close, defeating detection of tampered data. This is about missing validation of the integrity value, not a generic cryptographic weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The close path writes a sealing tag but does not verify that epoch seals are continuous or that a tag was successfully produced before finalizing. If sealing is skipped (header not flagged sealed) or append_tag fails, the file is closed without a valid integrity value, so later verification cannot detect truncation or modification of the sealed log.

commit_msg: Check length of memcmp
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t\t\tif (!memcmp(buf + 5, "include", 7)) {', '\t\t\t\t\t} else if (!memcmp(buf + 5, "exec", 4)) {'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t\t\tif ((len > 12) && !memcmp(buf + 5, "include", 7)) {', '\t\t\t\t\t} else if ((len > 9) && !memcmp(buf + 5, "exec", 4)) {']}
description: Out-of-bounds Read in the send_ssi_file function in civetweb.c in CivetWeb through 1.10 allows attackers to cause a Denial of Service or Information Disclosure via a crafted SSI file.

code_evidence: After terminating buf at index len, the code calls memcmp(buf + 5, "include", 7) without first checking that len >= 12, so the comparison can read past the initialized portion of buf.
Similarly, memcmp(buf + 5, "exec", 4) is called without verifying len >= 9, and on a match do_ssi_exec is invoked with buf + 9.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing length check produces an out-of-bounds read whose supported consequence is disclosure of adjacent memory contents through the response path, matching CWE-200's exposure of information to an unauthorized actor. The primary defect is the unchecked read; CWE-125 describes the memory-safety root cause, while CWE-200 captures the resulting confidentiality impact targeted here.

} else if (!memcmp(buf + 5, "exec", 4)) {
do_ssi_exec(conn, buf + 9);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the SSI tag length is not validated before fixed-length memcmp reads at buf+5. commit_msg:
VideoPlayerCodec: Stop dividing by zero

When parsing a file failed so that needed fields, in our case frameSize
are not available a guess work like with m_channels or m_samplerate does
not help. Therefore fail early.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  for (int nPacket=0; nPacket < 10 && (m_channels == 0 || m_format.m_sampleRate == 0); nPacket++)'], 'added_lines': ['  for (int nPacket = 0;', '       nPacket < 10 && (m_channels == 0 || m_format.m_sampleRate == 0 || m_format.m_frameSize == 0);', '       nPacket++)', "    // if we don't know the framesize yet, we will fail when converting", '    if (m_srcFormat.m_frameSize == 0)', '      return false;', '']}
description: A divide by zero issue discovered in Kodi Home Theater Software 19.5 and earlier allows attackers to cause a denial of service via use of crafted mp3 file.

code_evidence: The decode loop only continues while m_channels or m_format.m_sampleRate is zero; it does not require m_format.m_frameSize to be nonzero, so a crafted file can leave m_srcFormat.m_frameSize at 0 after the loop.
Only m_srcFormat.m_sampleRate is defaulted (to 44100) when zero; m_srcFormat.m_frameSize has no such fallback and remains 0.
When NeedConvert(m_srcFormat.m_dataFormat) is true, m_needConvert is set and m_pResampler is created and initialized from m_srcFormat, including the zero frame size, with no guard before Init.
m_format is then overwritten from m_srcFormat and its data format changed to float, so the zero frame size is retained for later resampling/conversion.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The flaw is a missing nonzero check on a size-like field (frameSize) that is used in later conversion arithmetic, matching CWE-369's description of dividing by an unexpected zero value. The fix confirms this by adding the frameSize==0 condition to the loop and returning false before conversion, distinguishing it from an out-of-bounds or integer-overflow weakness.

evidence_lines.code:
if (m_srcFormat.m_sampleRate == 0)
m_srcFormat.m_sampleRate = 44100;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: m_srcFormat.m_frameSize is never validated or defaulted, and the loop that gathers codec fields does not wait for it. A crafted mp3 that fails to populate frameSize leaves it at 0, and the conversion path proceeds to initialize the resampler with that zero frame size. The supported consequence is a divide-by-zero during conversion/resampling, causing denial of service (crash).

commit_msg:
userns: also map extents in the reverse map to kernel IDs

The current logic first clones the extent array and sorts both copies, then
maps the lower IDs of the forward mapping into the lower namespace, but
doesn't map the lower IDs of the reverse mapping.

This means that code in a nested user namespace with >5 extents will see
incorrect IDs. It also breaks some access checks, like
inode_owner_or_capable() and privileged_wrt_inode_uidgid(), so a process
can incorrectly appear to be capable relative to an inode.

To fix it, we have to make sure that the "lower_first" members of extents
in both arrays are translated; and we have to make sure that the reverse
map is sorted *after* the translation (since otherwise the translation can
break the sorting).

This is CVE-2018-18955.

Fixes: 6397fac4915a ("userns: bump idmap limits to 340")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Tested-by: Eric W. Biederman <ebiederm@xmission.com>
Reviewed-by: Eric W. Biederman <ebiederm@xmission.com>
Signed-off-by: Eric W. Biederman <ebiederm@xmission.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tret = sort_idmaps(&new_map);', '\tif (ret < 0)', '\t\tgoto out;', ''], 'added_lines': ['', '\t/*', '\t * If we want to use binary search for lookup, this clones the extent', '\t * array and sorts both copies.', '\t */', '\tret = sort_idmaps(&new_map);', '\tif (ret < 0)', '\t\tgoto out;']}
description: In the Linux kernel 4.15.x through 4.19.x before 4.19.2, map_write() in kernel/user_namespace.c allows privilege escalation because it mishandles nested user namespaces with more than 5 UID or GID ranges. A user who has CAP_SYS_ADMIN in an affected user namespace can bypass access controls on resources outside the namespace, as demonstrated by reading /etc/shadow. This occurs because an ID transformation takes place properly for the namespaced-to-kernel direction but not for the kernel-to-namespaced direction.

code_evidence: sort_idmaps() is called at line 74 before the translation loop; at that point the reverse array is sorted by untranslated lower_first values.
The loop at lines 78-91 rewrites lower_first only in the forward array (or base extent array) via map_id_range_down; the reverse array's lower_first is never translated.
Lines 96-97 install the forward and reverse arrays into the namespace map, so the reverse map retains kernel-side IDs and is no longer correctly sorted relative to translated values.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The flawed ID translation causes authorization checks (capability/ownership comparisons) to evaluate against incorrect IDs, so access-control decisions are made incorrectly. This is an incorrect authorization check rather than just a data-integrity bug, matching CWE-863.

evidence_lines.code:
map->forward = new_map.forward;
map->reverse = new_map.reverse;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the reverse mapping's lower_first members are not translated into the parent/kernel ID space, and sorting occurs before translation so the reverse array is ordered by stale values. Trigger: a nested user namespace with more than 5 extents writes an ID map. Consequence: reverse lookups (kernel ID to namespaced ID) return wrong IDs, breaking access checks such as inode_owner_or_capable() and privileged_wrt_inode_uidgid(), allowing a process to appear capable over resources outside its namespace.

description: HyperKit is a toolkit for embedding hypervisor capabilities in an application. In versions 0.20210107, function `pci_vtsock_proc_tx` in `virtio-sock` can lead to to uninitialized memory use. In this situation, there is a check for the return value to be less or equal to `VTSOCK_MAXSEGS`, but that check is not sufficient because the function can return `-1` if it finds an error it cannot recover from. Moreover, the negative return value will be used by `iovec_pull` in a while condition that can further lead to more corruption because the function is not designed to handle a negative `iov_len`. This issue may lead to a guest crashing the host causing a denial of service and, under certain circumstance, memory corruption. This issue is fixed in commit af5eba2360a7351c08dfd9767d9be863a50ebaba.

code_evidence: vq_getchain returns an int into iovec_len; only an upper-bound assert is applied, so a negative return value (error) is not checked or rejected.
The unchecked negative iovec_len is passed to dprint_chain and to iovec_pull, which is not designed to handle a negative length, and pulled is asserted equal to sizeof(hdr).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The code fails to check an exceptional error return from vq_getchain before using it, which is precisely an improper check for unusual/exceptional conditions. The negative value is then consumed as a length, matching CWE-754 rather than a pure bounds issue.

evidence_lines.code:
iovec_len = vq_getchain(vq, &idx, iov, VTSOCK_MAXSEGS, flags);
assert(iovec_len <= VTSOCK_MAXSEGS);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the return value of vq_getchain is only checked against the maximum segment count, not for the error/sentinel value -1. Trigger: a guest supplies a malformed or failing descriptor chain so vq_getchain returns a negative value. Consequence: the negative length flows into iovec_pull and related helpers, causing uninitialized memory use, host crash (DoS), and possible memory corruption.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tif (nalu_size<2) return GF_NON_COMPLIANT_BITSTREAM;']}
description: gp_rtp_builder_do_hevc in ietf/rtp_pck_mpeg4.c in GPAC 2.0.0 has a heap-based buffer over-read, as demonstrated by MP4Box.

code_evidence: In the aggregation path, nalu[0] and nalu[1] are read to build the payload header and layer/tid fields without any prior length check; nalu_size is only validated elsewhere (the patch adds nalu_size<2).
Same unchecked nalu[1] read for new_LayerId and new_TID comparisons.
nalu[0]/nalu[1] read again when merging layer id.
nalu[1] read for TID comparison.
In the fragmentation path, payload_hdr[0]/[1] are derived from nalu[0] and nalu[1] with no length guard.
shdr also reads nalu[0] unconditionally.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe operation is a read past the end of the nalu buffer, matching CWE-125's out-of-bounds read. It is not an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) because only reads of nalu occur; the missing nalu_size<2 constraint is the cause, the over-read the consequence.

evidence_lines.code:
builder->hevc_payload_hdr[0] = (nalu[0] & 0x81) | (48 << 1);
builder->hevc_payload_hdr[1] = nalu[1];

builder->hevc_payload_hdr[0] = (builder->hevc_payload_hdr[0] & 0xFE) | (nalu[0] & 0x01);
builder->hevc_payload_hdr[1] = (builder->hevc_payload_hdr[1] & 0x07) | (nalu[1] & 0xF8);
new_TID = nalu[1] & 0x07;

payload_hdr[0] = (nalu[0] & 0x81) | (49 << 1);
payload_hdr[1] = nalu[1];
shdr |= (nalu[0] & 0x7E) >> 1;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function dereferences at least the first two bytes of the supplied NAL unit (nalu[0], nalu[1]) without verifying nalu_size >= 2. Trigger: a caller supplies a NAL unit shorter than two bytes. Consequence: an out-of-bounds heap read of nalu[1] (and nalu[0] for size 0), which can crash or leak adjacent memory.

commit_msg:
fru: Fix buffer overflow vulnerabilities

Partial fix for CVE-2020-5208, see
https://github.com/ipmitool/ipmitool/security/advisories/GHSA-g659-9qxw-p7cp

The `read_fru_area_section` function only performs size validation of
requested read size, and falsely assumes that the IPMI message will not
respond with more than the requested amount of data; it uses the
unvalidated response size to copy into `frubuf`. If the response is
larger than the request, this can result in overflowing the buffer.

The same issue affects the `read_fru_area` function.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tuint32_t off = offset, tmp, finish;'], 'added_lines': ['\tuint32_t off = offset;', '\tuint32_t tmp;', '\tuint32_t finish;', '\tuint32_t size_left_in_buffer;', '\t\tmemset(frubuf + fru->size, 0, length - fru->size);', '\t\tlength = finish - offset;', '\tsize_left_in_buffer = length;', '\t\tif(rsp->data_len < 1', '\t\t   || tmp > rsp->data_len - 1', '\t\t   || tmp > size_left_in_buffer)', '\t\t{', '\t\t\tprintf(" Not enough buffer size");', '\t\t\treturn -1;', '\t\t}', '', '\t\tsize_left_in_buffer -= tmp;']}
description: It's been found that multiple functions in ipmitool before 1.8.19 neglect proper checking of the data received from a remote LAN party, which may lead to buffer overflows and potentially to remote code execution on the ipmitool side. This is especially dangerous if ipmitool is run as a privileged user. This problem is fixed in version 1.8.19.

code_evidence: finish = offset + length is clamped to fru->size, but length itself is not reduced to finish - offset, so the buffer capacity implied by length diverges from the actual copy loop bound.
The request size msg_data[3] is derived from finish - off capped by fru->max_read_size, so the request can be smaller than the total length.
tmp is taken from the unvalidated response byte rsp->data[0] and used directly as the memcpy length into frubuf, with no check that tmp fits the remaining buffer; off and frubuf advance by tmp.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs a buffer copy (memcpy) using an input-controlled, unvalidated size, which is exactly CWE-120's 'buffer copy without checking size of input.' The missing constraint is on tmp relative to remaining buffer space, not an out-of-bounds read, so CWE-125 does not apply.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the response-reported length is trusted as the copy size without comparing it against the requested or remaining output buffer size. Trigger: a remote IPMI endpoint returns a response whose data[0] (doubled for access mode) exceeds the requested read size. Consequence: memcpy writes past the end of frubuf, causing a heap/stack buffer overflow that may corrupt memory or enable code execution.

commit_msg:
list-objects: pass full pathname to callbacks

When we find a blob at "a/b/c", we currently pass this to
our show_object_fn callbacks as two components: "a/b/" and
"c". Callbacks which want the full value then call
path_name(), which concatenates the two. But this is an
inefficient interface; the path is a strbuf, and we could
simply append "c" to it temporarily, then roll back the
length, without creating a new copy.

So we could improve this by teaching the callsites of
path_name() this trick (and there are only 3). But we can
also notice that no callback actually cares about the
broken-down representation, and simply pass each callback
the full path "a/b/c" as a string. The callback code becomes
even simpler, then, as we do not have to worry about freeing
an allocated buffer, nor rolling back our modification to
the strbuf.

This is theoretically less efficient, as some callbacks
would not bother to format the final path component. But in
practice this is not measurable. Since we use the same
strbuf over and over, our work to grow it is amortized, and
we really only pay to memcpy a few bytes.

Signed-off-by: Jeff King <peff@peff.net>
Signed-off-by: Junio C Hamano <gitster@pobox.com>

description: In Wireshark 2.4.0 to 2.4.13, 2.6.0 to 2.6.7, and 3.0.0, the SRVLOC dissector could crash. This was addressed in epan/dissectors/packet-srvloc.c by preventing a heap-based buffer under-read.

code_evidence: The endianness branch iterates i from length down to 1, then reads ascii_text[i] at line 13. description: The ReadVIFFImage function in coders/viff.c in ImageMagick 7.0.6-6 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory consumption) via a crafted VIFF file.

code_evidence: The non-bit path computes max_packets from attacker-controlled number_pixels*viff_info.number_data_bands (line 320) using only HeapOverflowSanityCheck (line 318), which guards integer overflow but not the absolute size.
pixels is then allocated with AcquireQuantumMemory(MagickMax(number_pixels,max_packets),bytes_per_pixel) (lines 322-323), sizing the buffer directly from header-derived dimensions.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-770 applies because the reader allocates memory sized by untrusted input without limiting the amount, producing resource-consumption DoS. It is not an overflow issue: HeapOverflowSanityCheck already prevents integer wraparound, leaving the missing size/throttle constraint as the supported weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the VIFF header's rows/columns and number_data_bands drive max_packets and the pixels allocation without any bound relative to the actual blob size. A crafted file declaring large dimensions triggers a very large allocation, causing memory exhaustion (DoS). The added fix rejects headers where bytes_per_pixel*max_packets exceeds GetBlobSize(image).

commit_msg:
pdfwrite - Guard against trying to output an infinite number

Bug #699255 " Buffer overflow on pprintg1 due to mishandle postscript file data to pdf"

The file uses an enormous parameter to xyxhow, causing an overflow in
the calculation of text positioning (value > 1e39).

Since this is basically a nonsense value, and PostScript only supports
real values up to 1e38, this patch follows the same approach as for
a degenerate CTM, and treats it as 0.

Adobe Acrobat Distiller throws a limitcheck error, so we could do that
instead if this approach proves to be a problem.

description: The set_text_distance function in devices/vector/gdevpdts.c in the pdfwrite component in Artifex Ghostscript through 9.22 does not prevent overflows in text-positioning calculation, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (application crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted PDF document.

code_evidence: Line 4 passes attacker-influenced dx/dy directly to gs_distance_transform_inverse without any magnitude check; the overflow occurs inside that calculation. Lines 6-7 only react after the undefined-result code is returned by resetting pdist to zero, and line 8 returns other errors.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The overflow of a numeric computation used for text positioning can lead to memory-buffer boundary violations (the reported buffer overflow), matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds read/write scope. A related numeric-overflow label would describe the arithmetic root cause, but the supported consequence here is improper memory-buffer operations.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: text-positioning inputs greater than 1e38 are fed into gs_distance_transform_inverse, whose internal computation overflows (the fixed version guards with dx>1e38||dy>1e38). Trigger: a crafted PDF/PostScript file supplying an enormous xyxhow parameter. The overflow corrupts the distance/positioning computation, producing a crash (DoS) and potentially out-of-bounds memory effects.

commit_msg: Add bounds check before signature length read
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '        if( p > end - 2 )', '        {', '            MBEDTLS_SSL_DEBUG_MSG( 1, ( "bad server key exchange message" ) );', '            mbedtls_ssl_send_alert_message( ssl, MBEDTLS_SSL_ALERT_LEVEL_FATAL,', '                                            MBEDTLS_SSL_ALERT_MSG_DECODE_ERROR );', '            return( MBEDTLS_ERR_SSL_BAD_HS_SERVER_KEY_EXCHANGE );', '        }']}
description: ARM mbed TLS before 2.1.11, before 2.7.2, and before 2.8.0 has a buffer over-read in ssl_parse_server_key_exchange() that could cause a crash on invalid input.

code_evidence: Lines 63-64 set p to the start of the ServerKeyExchange body and end to the end of the handshake message, both derived from the received record; p may equal end if the body is empty.
Line 183 reads p[0] and p[1] to form sig_len, then line 184 advances p by 2; line 185 only compares end against p+sig_len after the two-byte read has already occurred.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Reading p[0] and p[1] without a preceding remaining-length check is a direct out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). The later end != p + sig_len check is a length-consistency check, not a bounds check, so it does not prevent the over-read; this is distinct from an out-of-bounds write.

evidence_lines.code:
p   = ssl->in_msg + mbedtls_ssl_hs_hdr_len( ssl );
end = ssl->in_msg + ssl->in_hslen;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the two-byte signature-length field is read before verifying that at least two bytes remain between p and end. Trigger: a malformed ServerKeyExchange message whose body ends at or before p+1. Consequence: p[0]/p[1] read past the received handshake buffer, an out-of-bounds read that can crash the process.

description: elfcomm.c in readelf in GNU Binutils 2.29 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (excessive memory allocation) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted ELF file that triggers a "buffer overflow on fuzzed archive header," related to an uninitialized variable, an improper conditional jump, and the get_archive_member_name, process_archive_index_and_symbols, and setup_archive functions.

code_evidence: Line 17 parses arch->arhdr.ar_name+1 with strtoul; if ar_name is not NUL-terminated within its fixed buffer, strtoul reads past the buffer boundary.

Lines 25-33 iterate longnames up to longnames_size and write arch->longnames[j]='\0'; the bound checks at 31-32 clamp j but the loop can advance j to longnames_size, so the terminator write is at the table edge, and k/j derived from the unbounded strtoul feed this indexing.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-119 fits because the function performs reads/writes on buffers (ar_name via strtoul, longnames terminator) without restricting operations to the intended boundary; the missing termination constraint leads to out-of-bounds memory operations.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the archive header name field is used by strtoul without ensuring it is zero-terminated, so a crafted archive header makes the parser read beyond the fixed ar_name buffer; the resulting index then drives longnames iteration/termination. Trigger: a fuzzed archive member header lacking a terminator. Consequence: out-of-bounds memory access, crash or possible memory corruption.

description: Libde265 v1.0.8 was discovered to contain a heap-buffer-overflow vulnerability via mc_chroma<unsigned short> in motion.cc. This vulnerability allows attackers to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) via a crafted video file.

code_evidence: The reference picture refPic is fetched and only checked for existence/PicState at [49]; no check that its dimensions or chroma format match the current SPS before motion compensation.

In the high-bit-depth branch, mc_chroma reads from refPic->get_image_plane(1/2) with refPic->get_chroma_stride() at [70] and [73], using block sizes nPbW/SubWidthC, nPbH/SubHeightC derived from the current SPS.
The 8-bit branch does the same at [78] and [81], again indexing the reference plane using current-SPS-derived SubWidthC/SubHeightC and block sizes.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the missing size/chroma-format constraint allows mc_chroma to write/read past the intended reference buffer boundary, matching out-of-bounds memory access driven by an unchecked size mismatch.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: a reference picture with dimensions or chroma format differing from the current SPS is accepted because only existence is validated. When mc_chroma later indexes the reference chroma plane using the current picture's block size and subsampling, the read can exceed the smaller reference plane, causing a heap-buffer-overflow.

commit_msg:
On some architectures (like ARM64), it can support CONT-PTE/PMD size
hugetlb, which means it can support not only PMD/PUD size hugetlb (2M and
1G), but also CONT-PTE/PMD size(64K and 32M) if a 4K page size specified.

So when looking up a CONT-PTE size hugetlb page by follow_page(), it will
use pte_offset_map_lock() to get the pte entry lock for the CONT-PTE size
hugetlb in follow_page_pte().  However this pte entry lock is incorrect
for the CONT-PTE size hugetlb, since we should use huge_pte_lock() to get
the correct lock, which is mm->page_table_lock.

That means the pte entry of the CONT-PTE size hugetlb under current pte
lock is unstable in follow_page_pte(), we can continue to migrate or
poison the pte entry of the CONT-PTE size hugetlb, which can cause some
potential race issues, even though they are under the 'pte lock'.

For example, suppose thread A is trying to look up a CONT-PTE size hugetlb
page by move_pages() syscall under the lock, however antoher thread B can
migrate the CONT-PTE hugetlb page at the same time, which will cause
thread A to get an incorrect page, if thread A also wants to do page
migration, then data inconsistency error occurs.

Moreover we have the same issue for CONT-PMD size hugetlb in
follow_huge_pmd().

To fix above issues, rename the follow_huge_pmd() as follow_huge_pmd_pte()
to handle PMD and PTE level size hugetlb, which uses huge_pte_lock() to
get the correct pte entry lock to make the pte entry stable.

Mike said:

Support for CONT_PMD/_PTE was added with bb9dd3df8ee9 ("arm64: hugetlb:
refactor find_num_contig()").  Patch series "Support for contiguous pte
hugepages", v4.  However, I do not believe these code paths were
executed until migration support was added with 5480280d3f2d ("arm64/mm:
enable HugeTLB migration for contiguous bit HugeTLB pages") I would go
with 5480280d3f2d for the Fixes: targe.

Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/635f43bdd85ac2615a58405da82b4d33c6e5eb05.1662017562.git.baolin.wang@linux.alibaba.com
Fixes: 5480280d3f2d ("arm64/mm: enable HugeTLB migration for contiguous bit HugeTLB pages")
Signed-off-by: Baolin Wang <baolin.wang@linux.alibaba.com>
Suggested-by: Mike Kravetz <mike.kravetz@oracle.com>
Reviewed-by: Mike Kravetz <mike.kravetz@oracle.com>
Cc: David Hildenbrand <david@redhat.com>
Cc: Muchun Song <songmuchun@bytedance.com>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\t/*', '\t * Considering PTE level hugetlb, like continuous-PTE hugetlb on', '\t * ARM64 architecture.', '\t */', '\tif (is_vm_hugetlb_page(vma)) {', '\t\tpage = follow_huge_pmd_pte(vma, address, flags);', '\t\tif (page)', '\t\t\treturn page;', '\t\treturn no_page_table(vma, flags);', '\t}', '']}
description: A vulnerability was found in Linux Kernel. It has been declared as problematic. Affected by this vulnerability is the function follow_page_pte of the file mm/gup.c of the component BPF. The manipulation leads to race condition. The attack can be launched remotely. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue. The identifier VDB-211921 was assigned to this vulnerability.

code_evidence: Line 16 acquires the pte lock via pte_offset_map_lock() and reads the pte at line 17 under that lock.
Lines 27-29 release the lock, wait on a migration entry, and retry, showing the pte value is re-read across a lock boundary.
Lines 82-84 unlock via pte_unmap_unlock() on the normal exit path, so the pte is assumed stable while held.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-362 fits because the code sequence requires exclusive access to the shared pte for atomic read/use, but uses the wrong lock, allowing an interfering concurrent sequence to modify the resource. This is improper synchronization of a shared resource, not a memory-safety flaw like use-after-free.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function takes the ordinary pte lock (pte_offset_map_lock) for hugetlb ptes, but contiguous-PTE/PMD hugetlb entries require huge_pte_lock() (mm->page_table_lock). The pte read at line 17 is therefore not protected against concurrent migration or poisoning of the contiguous hugetlb entry, so another thread can alter the entry while this sequence runs, yielding an incorrect page or data inconsistency.

description: mp3dec/SoftMP3.cpp in libstagefright in mediaserver in Android 4.x before 4.4.4, 5.0.x before 5.0.2, 5.1.x before 5.1.1, and 6.x before 2016-06-01 does not validate the relationship between allocated memory and the frame size, which allows attackers to gain privileges via a crafted application, as demonstrated by obtaining Signature or SignatureOrSystem access, aka internal bug 27793371.

code_evidence: Line 34 sets outputFrameSize to a fixed kOutputBufferSize-derived value without checking the actual output buffer allocation from outHeader (line 36).
Lines 61-63 memset the output buffer for outputFrameSize * sizeof(int16_t) bytes regardless of outHeader->nAllocLen.
Lines 80-84 write outHeader->nFilledLen derived from outputFrameSize without constraining it to the allocated output buffer length.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The root cause is missing validation of a size constraint (allocated buffer length versus frame size) before processing, matching CWE-20 improper input validation of metadata/size. The overflow is the consequence of the unvalidated relationship, not a separate validation category.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The decoder output frame size is assumed to fit the OMX output buffer; the actual allocation length (outHeader->nAllocLen) is never validated against the computed frame size. A crafted MP3 stream that yields a large frame causes writes beyond the output buffer, enabling memory corruption and potential privilege escalation.

description: timg v1.4.4 was discovered to contain a memory leak via the function timg::QueryBackgroundColor() at /timg/src/term-query.cc.

code_evidence: Line 18 returns strdup(buffer), which heap-allocates a copy of the assembled color string. The caller receives a newly allocated pointer, but the function itself never frees it and the buffer is not tracked by the function; ownership is implicitly transferred to the caller with no release path here.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The target CWE-401 describes failure to sufficiently track and release allocated memory after use. The strdup allocation returned without any release or ownership mechanism fits this missing-release pattern; it is a memory leak rather than an out-of-bounds or use-after-free issue.

evidence_lines.code: return strdup(buffer);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function allocates memory with strdup on every successful call and relies on the caller to free it, but no ownership contract or cleanup is enforced. Trigger: repeated calls to QueryBackgroundColor() (e.g., on repeated terminal queries) each allocate a new string. Supported consequence: the allocations accumulate, causing memory consumption/leak and potential DoS or instability.

commit_msg:
Fix 697448: Limit the maximum program size to something reasonable.

A regular expression with lots of nested repetition can lead to
integer overflow when calculating the size of the program.

Check max program size when counting the number of instructions required
for a loop, so we can bail before integer overflow can happen.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['static int count(Renode *node)', '\tint min, max;', '\tcase P_CAT: return count(node->x) + count(node->y);', '\tcase P_ALT: return count(node->x) + count(node->y) + 2;', '\t\tif (min == max) return count(node->x) * min;', '\t\tif (max < REPINF) return count(node->x) * max + (max - min);', '\t\treturn count(node->x) * (min + 1) + 2;', '\tcase P_PAR: return count(node->x) + 2;', '\tcase P_PLA: return count(node->x) + 2;', '\tcase P_NLA: return count(node->x) + 2;'], 'added_lines': ['static int count(struct cstate *g, Renode *node)', '\tint min, max, n;', '\tcase P_CAT: return count(g, node->x) + count(g, node->y);', '\tcase P_ALT: return count(g, node->x) + count(g, node->y) + 2;', '\t\tif (min == max) n = count(g, node->x) * min;', '\t\telse if (max < REPINF) n = count(g, node->x) * max + (max - min);', '\t\telse n = count(g, node->x) * (min + 1) + 2;', '\t\tif (n < 0 || n > MAXPROG) die(g, "program too large");', '\t\treturn n;', '\tcase P_PAR: return count(g, node->x) + 2;', '\tcase P_PLA: return count(g, node->x) + 2;', '\tcase P_NLA: return count(g, node->x) + 2;']}
description: An integer overflow vulnerability was observed in the regemit function in regexp.c in Artifex Software, Inc. MuJS before fa3d30fd18c348bb4b1f3858fb860f4fcd4b2045. The attack requires a regular expression with nested repetition. A successful exploitation of this issue can lead to code execution or a denial of service (buffer overflow) condition.

code_evidence: For a P_REP node, the instruction count is computed by multiplying the recursive sub-count by the repetition bound: count(node->x) * min, count(node->x) * max, or count(node->x) * (min + 1). These int multiplications can exceed INT_MAX when the sub-expression count and repetition counts are large (e.g. nested repetition), producing a wrapped result that is then returned and used as the program size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs arithmetic (count * bound) whose result can overflow the int representation, and the pre-fix code assumes the product remains a valid larger value. This is exactly CWE-190; the added n < 0 check confirms the wrapped-negative scenario. It is not merely an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) because the root cause is the unchecked integer multiplication.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: unbounded signed int multiplication of the recursive node count by attacker-controlled repetition bounds in the P_REP case, with no overflow check before returning. Trigger: a regular expression with nested repetition makes count(node->x) and min/max large enough that their product wraps. Consequence: a small or negative program size is propagated, leading to undersized allocation and later out-of-bounds writes (memory corruption/DoS).

commit_msg:
CVE-2017-13002/AODV: Add some missing bounds checks.

In aodv_extension() do a bounds check on the extension header before we
look at it.

This fixes a buffer over-read discovered by Kamil Frankowicz.

Add a test using the capture file supplied by the reporter(s).

While we're at it, add the RFC number, and check the validity of the
length for the Hello extension.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tND_TCHECK(*ep);', '\t\tif (ep->length < 4) {', '\t\t\tND_PRINT((ndo, "\\n\\text HELLO - bad length %u", ep->length));', '\t\t\tbreak;', '\t\t}']}
description: The AODV parser in tcpdump before 4.9.2 has a buffer over-read in print-aodv.c:aodv_extension().

code_evidence: The switch reads ep->type before any ND_TCHECK on the extension header; in the HELLO case ah is cast from ep and ND_TCHECK(*ah) is applied, but the initial ep->type dereference itself is unvalidated.

The length check compares the function's length argument against sizeof(struct aodv_hello) and then EXTRACT_32BITS(&ah->interval) reads the interval field; there is no check of ep->length against the actual extension size before accessing the header fields.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the defect is reading past the end of the available buffer via unvalidated header dereferences; the missing ND_TCHECK/length validation directly enables an out-of-bounds read, not a write or overflow.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the AODV extension header is dereferenced (ep->type, and later ah->interval) without first verifying that the captured buffer contains the full extension structure or that ep->length is consistent with the HELLO header. Trigger: a truncated or malformed AODV packet whose extension length is smaller than the structure reached by the parser. Consequence: out-of-bounds read of packet buffer memory, causing disclosure or a crash.

commit_msg:
SELinux tries to support setting/clearing of /proc/pid/attr attributes
from the shell by ignoring terminating newlines and treating an
attribute value that begins with a NUL or newline as an attempt to
clear the attribute.  However, the test for clearing attributes has
always been wrong; it has an off-by-one error, and this could further
lead to reading past the end of the allocated buffer since commit
bb646cdb12e75d82258c2f2e7746d5952d3e321a ("proc_pid_attr_write():
switch to memdup_user()").  Fix the off-by-one error.

Even with this fix, setting and clearing /proc/pid/attr attributes
from the shell is not straightforward since the interface does not
support multiple write() calls (so shells that write the value and
newline separately will set and then immediately clear the attribute,
requiring use of echo -n to set the attribute), whereas trying to use
echo -n "" to clear the attribute causes the shell to skip the
write() call altogether since POSIX says that a zero-length write
causes no side effects. Thus, one must use echo -n to set and echo
without -n to clear, as in the following example:
$ echo -n unconfined_u:object_r:user_home_t:s0 > /proc/$$/attr/fscreate
$ cat /proc/$$/attr/fscreate
unconfined_u:object_r:user_home_t:s0
$ echo "" > /proc/$$/attr/fscreate
$ cat /proc/$$/attr/fscreate

Note the use of /proc/$$ rather than /proc/self, as otherwise
the cat command will read its own attribute value, not that of the shell.

There are no users of this facility to my knowledge; possibly we
should just get rid of it.

UPDATE: Upon further investigation it appears that a local process
with the process:setfscreate permission can cause a kernel panic as a
result of this bug.  This patch fixes CVE-2017-2618.

Signed-off-by: Stephen Smalley <sds@tycho.nsa.gov>
[PM: added the update about CVE-2017-2618 to the commit description]
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # 3.5: d6ea83ec6864e
Signed-off-by: Paul Moore <paul@paul-moore.com>

Signed-off-by: James Morris <james.l.morris@oracle.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ["\tif (size && str[1] && str[1] != '\\n') {"], 'added_lines': ["\tif (size && str[0] && str[0] != '\\n') {"]}
description: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's handling of clearing SELinux attributes on /proc/pid/attr files before 4.9.10. An empty (null) write to this file can crash the system by causing the system to attempt to access unmapped kernel memory.

code_evidence: Line 26 tests str[1] instead of str[0] to decide whether the attribute value is non-empty; the following block strips a trailing newline and passes value/size to security_context_to_sid().
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The condition uses str[1] where str[0] is intended, an incorrect boundary/index by one element, matching CWE-193. It is not merely a missing length check: size is already validated, but the wrong index causes the misclassification.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The clearing test indexes the second byte, so a one-byte value such as a lone NUL or newline is treated as a real context and reaches security_context_to_sid(), where size-based handling reads past the allocated buffer. Trigger: a short write to /proc/pid/attr/fscreate; consequence: out-of-bounds kernel read leading to crash/panic.

commit_msg:
LWAPP: define a recursion depth limit

Altough the dissection consumes a few ytes each time it is called,
it can trigger a stack overflow for big packets.

commit_msg:
Avoid using stale UserScript pointers

BUG=625393
TEST=Manually. Compile Chrome with ASAN and follow the steps from the bug report.

Review-Url: https://codereview.chromium.org/2116923002
Cr-Commit-Position: refs/heads/master@{#403725}
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  if (changed_hosts.count(host_id_) > 0)'], 'added_lines': ['  if (changed_hosts.count(host_id_) > 0) {', '    script_ = nullptr;', '  }']}
description: Use-after-free vulnerability in extensions/renderer/user_script_injector.cc in the Extensions subsystem in Google Chrome before 52.0.2743.82 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service or possibly have unspecified other impact via vectors related to script deletion.

code_evidence: When the injector's host is among changed_hosts, the function returns early without clearing the stored raw pointer script_.
Otherwise it overwrites script_ with a raw UserScript* taken from the scripts vector without any ownership or lifetime check.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function retains and later reuses a pointer to memory that may have been freed, matching CWE-416. The fix clears script_ to nullptr, confirming the stale-pointer root cause rather than a mere null-dereference or logic error.

evidence_lines.code:
if (changed_hosts.count(host_id_) > 0)
return;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: script_ is a raw pointer to a UserScript. If the host changed, the injection is removed and the backing script may be deleted, but the early return leaves script_ dangling; later use of script_ dereferences freed memory. The trigger is a host change combined with script deletion; the supported consequence is use-after-free (crash/DoS or unspecified impact).

commit_msg:
http_server: v1: metrics: fix potential SIGSEGV by memory allocation errors

This is a follow up on PR 3045. While 3045 fixed the potential SIGSERV
issue caused by memory allocation error in flb_avro, after searching/reviewing
it looks like  src/http_server/api/v1/metrics.c also consists of several
similar issues.

This PR adds proper check to prevent the potential SIGSERV issues.

Signed-off-by: Yong Tang <yong.tang.github@outlook.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    if (!buf->raw_data) {', '        flb_errno();', '        flb_sds_destroy(out_data);', '        flb_free(buf);', '        return;', '    }']}
description: Fluent Bit 1.6.10 has a NULL pointer dereference when an flb_malloc return value is not validated by flb_avro.c or http_server/api/v1/metrics.c.

code_evidence: Line 28 assigns the result of flb_malloc(size) to buf->raw_data without checking for NULL; line 29 immediately passes buf->raw_data to memcpy, which dereferences it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences a pointer expected to be valid but potentially NULL, matching CWE-476. This is distinct from an integer overflow or buffer overflow, since no size arithmetic or bounds issue is involved; the defect is the missing NULL check.

evidence_lines.code:
buf->raw_data = flb_malloc(size);
memcpy(buf->raw_data, data, size);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the allocation result stored in buf->raw_data is never validated. Trigger: flb_malloc returns NULL (e.g., under memory pressure or a large size). Consequence: memcpy dereferences the NULL destination, causing a crash (SIGSEGV).

commit_msg:
While investigating on why a synchronize_net() has been added recently
in ipv6_mc_down(), I found that igmp6_event_query() and igmp6_event_report()
might drop skbs in some cases.

Discussion about removing synchronize_net() from ipv6_mc_down()
will happen in a different thread.

Fixes: f185de28d9ae ("mld: add new workqueues for process mld events")
Signed-off-by: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Cc: Taehee Yoo <ap420073@gmail.com>
Cc: Cong Wang <xiyou.wangcong@gmail.com>
Cc: David Ahern <dsahern@kernel.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220303173728.937869-1-eric.dumazet@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['int igmp6_event_report(struct sk_buff *skb)', '\tif (!idev)', '\t\treturn -EINVAL;', '', '\tif (idev->dead) {', '\t\tkfree_skb(skb);', '\t\treturn -ENODEV;', '\t}', '', '\treturn 0;'], 'added_lines': ['void igmp6_event_report(struct sk_buff *skb)', '\tif (!idev || idev->dead)', '\t\tgoto out;', '\t\tskb = NULL;', 'out:', '\tkfree_skb(skb);']}
description: Memory leak in icmp6 implementation in Linux Kernel 5.13+ allows a remote attacker to DoS a host by making it go out-of-memory via icmp6 packets of type 130 or 131. We recommend upgrading past commit 2d3916f3189172d5c69d33065c3c21119fe539fc.

code_evidence: The function takes ownership of skb. When the queue is at capacity (skb_queue_len >= MLD_MAX_SKBS), the if-body is skipped and the skb is never enqueued nor freed; the function returns 0 at line 17 without kfree_skb(skb), dropping the only reference to the allocation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-401 fits because an allocated skb is neither enqueued for later release nor freed on the overflow path, so its memory becomes unreachable and unavailable for reuse. This is a missing release after effective lifetime, not a use-after-free or double-free.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function returns success after the capacity check fails without releasing the skb it owns. Trigger: repeated MLD report (type 131) packets arriving while idev->mc_report_queue is full. Consequence: each dropped skb leaks its memory, enabling remote memory exhaustion/DoS. The dead-device branch frees the skb, contrasting with the full-queue path that does not.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    pjmedia_rtcp_common *hdr;', '    hdr = (pjmedia_rtcp_common*)buf;', '    pj_memcpy(hdr, &session->rtcp_rr_pkt.common,  sizeof(*hdr));', '    hdr->pt = RTCP_PSFB;', '    hdr->count = 3; /* FMT = 3 */', '    hdr->length = pj_htons((pj_uint16_t)(len/4 - 1));'], 'added_lines': ['    pjmedia_rtcp_fb_common *hdr;', '    hdr = (pjmedia_rtcp_fb_common*)buf;', '    pj_memcpy(hdr, &session->rtcp_fb_com, sizeof(*hdr));', '    hdr->rtcp_common.pt = RTCP_PSFB;', '    hdr->rtcp_common.count = 3; /* FMT = 3 */', '    hdr->rtcp_common.length = pj_htons((pj_uint16_t)(len/4 - 1));']}
description: PJSIP is a free and open source multimedia communication library written in C. PJSIP versions 2.12 and prior do not parse incoming RTCP feedback RPSI (Reference Picture Selection Indication) packet, but any app that directly uses pjmedia_rtcp_fb_parse_rpsi() will be affected. A patch is available in the `master` branch of the `pjsip/pjproject` GitHub repository. There are currently no known workarounds.

code_evidence: Lines 11-15 compute bitlen from rpsi->rpsi_bit_len, derive padlen and len, and reject only if len > *length; this bounds the header-plus-FCI length, not the subsequent raw copies.

Lines 21-30 advance p past the header, write padlen and pt, then memcpy rpsi_bit_len/8 bytes and possibly one extra byte from rpsi->rpsi.ptr, followed by pj_bzero(p, padlen/8); the destination bounds are not rechecked against *length here.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the function can write past the end of the caller-provided buf during FCI serialization. This is a write-side overflow, not merely a read or logic error, and the affected memory is the destination buffer.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The size check at line 14 compares the computed len to the caller-supplied *length, but the later writes at lines 24-30 depend on rpsi->rpsi_bit_len and rpsi->rpsi.ptr, which may be inconsistent with the length used to compute len. If a caller passes a buffer sized to *length while rpsi_bit_len or the pointer content implies more data than len accounts for, the memcpy or extra-byte write can exceed the destination buffer, causing an out-of-bounds write.

commit_msg:
We currently split the close into two, in case we have a ->flush op
that we can't safely handle from non-blocking context. This requires
us to flag the op as uncancelable if we do need to punt it async, and
that means special handling for just this op type.

Use __close_fd_get_file() and grab the files lock so we can get the file
and check if we need to go async in one atomic operation. That gets rid
of the need for splitting this into two steps, and hence the need for
IO_WQ_WORK_NO_CANCEL.

Signed-off-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t/*', '\t * If we queue this for async, it must not be cancellable. That would', "\t * leave the 'file' in an undeterminate state, and here need to modify", '\t * io_wq_work.flags, so initialize io_wq_work firstly.', '\t */', '\tio_req_init_async(req);', '', '\tif ((req->file && req->file->f_op == &io_uring_fops))', '\t\treturn -EBADF;', '', '\treq->close.put_file = NULL;'], 'added_lines': []}
description: A time-of-check to time-of-use issue exists in io_uring subsystem's IORING_OP_CLOSE operation in the Linux kernel's versions 5.6 - 5.11 (inclusive), which allows a local user to elevate their privileges to root. Introduced in b5dba59e0cf7e2cc4d3b3b1ac5fe81ddf21959eb, patched in 9eac1904d3364254d622bf2c771c4f85cd435fc2, backported to stable in 788d0824269bef539fe31a785b1517882eafed93.

code_evidence: Line 3 initializes async work without marking it uncancelable, so a queued close can be cancelled mid-operation.
Lines 11-14 record the fd and defer the actual file lookup to later use, while line 12's f_op check uses req->file, a value not atomically tied to the fd captured at line 11.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-367 fits because a resource state (the fd's target file) is checked at prep time and used later without atomicity, allowing the state to change between check and use. This is not a simple missing validation; the flaw is the non-atomic gap between the f_op check and the deferred close.

evidence_lines.code: io_req_init_async(req);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The fd from the SQE is stored at line 11, and the io_uring_fops check at line 12 inspects req->file rather than resolving the fd atomically. Between this prep-time check and the later actual close, another thread can swap the fd's underlying file, so the check no longer describes the object being closed. This enables a race that can close or act on a different file than validated, supporting privilege escalation.

description:
A use-after-free vulnerability in the Linux kernel's net/sched: sch_qfq component can be exploited to achieve local privilege escalation.

When the plug qdisc is used as a class of the qfq qdisc, sending network packets triggers use-after-free in qfq_dequeue() due to the incorrect .peek handler of sch_plug and lack of error checking in agg_dequeue().

We recommend upgrading past commit 8fc134fee27f2263988ae38920bc03da416b03d8.

code_evidence: Line 4 calls qdisc_dequeue_peeked(cl->qdisc) and discards the returned skb, so a NULL or already-freed buffer is never detected. Lines 5-11 then continue using the class state: line 6 checks cl->qdisc->q.qlen, line 8 invokes cl->qdisc->ops->peek(cl->qdisc) and reads qdisc_pkt_len on its result, and lines 9-10 move the class within the aggregate. No check guards a failed dequeue before these dereferences.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function references memory through cl->qdisc after the underlying skb was freed and the dequeue result discarded, matching CWE-416's reuse of freed memory. This is not merely a NULL dereference: the missing check on qdisc_dequeue_peeked allows access to a freed skb/class state, so CWE-416 fits the demonstrated UAF consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the dequeue return value is ignored, so a non-work-conserving qdisc (plug under qfq) can return NULL after the skb was freed elsewhere, yet agg_dequeue keeps touching the class/qdisc state. Trigger: a packet sent through a qfq class backed by plug causes the peek path to return a freed/NULL skb; the subsequent cl->qdisc->ops->peek and qlen use operate on stale state, yielding the KASAN slab-use-after-free in qfq_dequeue.

commit_msg:
tools/xenstore: remove nodes owned by destroyed domain

In case a domain is removed from Xenstore, remove all nodes owned by
it per default.

This tackles the problem that nodes might be created by a domain
outside its home path in Xenstore, leading to Xenstore hogging more
and more memory. Domain quota don't work in this case if the guest is
rebooting in between.

Since XSA-322 ownership of such stale nodes is transferred to dom0,
which is helping against unintended access, but not against OOM of
Xenstore.

As a fallback for weird cases add a Xenstore start parameter for
keeping today's way to handle stale nodes, adding the risk of Xenstore
hitting an OOM situation.

This is part of XSA-419 / CVE-2022-42322.

Fixes: 496306324d8d ("tools/xenstore: revoke access rights for removed domains")
Signed-off-by: Juergen Gross <jgross@suse.com>
Reviewed-by: Julien Grall <jgrall@amazon.com>

-		 * tested to exist and replaced by domid 0 if not).

description: Xenstore: Cooperating guests can create arbitrary numbers of nodes T[his CNA information record relates to multiple CVEs; the text explains which aspects/vulnerabilities correspond to which CVE.] Since the fix of XSA-322 any Xenstore node owned by a removed domain will be modified to be owned by Dom0. This will allow two malicious guests working together to create an arbitrary number of Xenstore nodes. This is possible by domain A letting domain B write into domain A's local Xenstore tree. Domain B can then create many nodes and reboot. The nodes created by domain B will now be owned by Dom0. By repeating this process over and over again an arbitrary number of nodes can be created, as Dom0's number of nodes isn't limited by Xenstore quota.

description: In ImageMagick 7.0.8-13 Q16, there is a heap-based buffer over-read in the SVGStripString function of coders/svg.c, which allows attackers to cause a denial of service via a crafted SVG image file.

code_evidence: The inner loop scans for a closing '*/' by testing *(p+1) at line 17 while only guaranteeing *p != '\0'; at the string's final character, *(p+1) dereferences the terminating NUL's successor, one byte past the buffer.
When the '*' terminator is found, line 21 advances p by 2 before line 23 dereferences *q++=(*p), so p can point past the end and that read is also out of bounds.
The outer loop's *p != '\0' check at line 12 does not constrain the inner loop's lookahead or the post-match increment.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the function reads memory beyond the intended buffer via the unchecked *(p+1) and post-match *p dereference. It is not CWE-787, since the defect is an out-of-bounds read rather than a write.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the lookahead *(p+1) and the p+=2 skip are performed without verifying that at least two characters remain before the NUL terminator. Trigger: a crafted SVG message ending in '*' or containing '/*' near the buffer end. Consequence: reads past the heap buffer, which the description reports as a heap-based over-read causing a denial of service (crash).

commit_msg:
(uid_t) -1 is still used as placeholder to mean "unset". This is OK, since
there should be no users with such number, see
https://systemd.io/UIDS-GIDS#special-linux-uids.

(uid_t) -1 is used as the default value in class initialization.

When a user or group above INT32_MAX is created, the numeric uid or
gid wraps around to negative when the value is assigned to gint, and
polkit gets confused. Let's accept such gids, except for -1.

A nicer fix would be to change the underlying type to e.g. uint32 to
not have negative values. But this cannot be done without breaking the
API, so likely new functions will have to be added (a
polkit_unix_user_new variant that takes a unsigned, and the same for
_group_new, _set_uid, _get_uid, _set_gid, _get_gid, etc.). This will
require a bigger patch.

Fixes https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/polkit/polkit/issues/74.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  g_return_if_fail (uid != -1);']}
description: A flaw was found in PolicyKit (aka polkit) 0.115 that allows a user with a uid greater than INT_MAX to successfully execute any systemctl command.

code_evidence: polkit_unix_user_set_uid accepts a gint uid parameter (line 3) and stores it directly into user->uid (line 6) after only checking that the object is a PolkitUnixUser. There is no check on the numeric value of uid, so any integer including negative values is accepted and persisted.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function receives a uid input and fails to validate that it is a permitted value (in particular, that it is not the reserved -1 sentinel) before using it. This is improper input validation (CWE-20); the missing constraint on the input's value directly enables the subsequent authorization confusion.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the setter performs no validation of the supplied uid value before assigning it to user->uid. Trigger: a caller passes a uid whose unsigned value exceeds INT32_MAX, which wraps to a negative gint; the special value -1 is used as the 'unset' placeholder. Consequence: the stored negative uid collides with the unset sentinel and confuses polkit's authorization logic, allowing a user with uid > INT_MAX to execute arbitrary systemctl commands.

commit_msg:
The MACVLAN receive handler clones skbs to all matching source MACVLAN
interfaces, before it passes the packet along to match on destination
based MACVLANs.

When using the MACVLAN nodst mode, passing the packet to destination based
MACVLANs is omitted and the handler returns with RX_HANDLER_CONSUMED.
However, the passed skb is not freed, leaking for any packet processed
with the nodst option.

Properly free the skb when consuming packets to fix that leak.

Fixes: 427f0c8c194b ("macvlan: Add nodst option to macvlan type source")
Signed-off-by: Martin Willi <martin@strongswan.org>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tif (macvlan_forward_source(skb, port, eth->h_source))', '\tif (macvlan_forward_source(skb, port, eth->h_source))'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (macvlan_forward_source(skb, port, eth->h_source)) {', '\t\t\tkfree_skb(skb);', '\t\t}', '\tif (macvlan_forward_source(skb, port, eth->h_source)) {', '\t\tkfree_skb(skb);', '\t}']}
description: A vulnerability classified as problematic was found in Linux Kernel. This vulnerability affects the function macvlan_handle_frame of the file drivers/net/macvlan.c of the component skb. The manipulation leads to memory leak. The attack can be initiated remotely. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue. The identifier of this vulnerability is VDB-211024.

code_evidence: At lines 22-23, when macvlan_forward_source() returns true for a multicast packet, the function returns RX_HANDLER_CONSUMED without freeing skb; the skb was either the original or a defragmented clone assigned at line 20.

At lines 38-39, the same pattern occurs for non-multicast packets: a true return from macvlan_forward_source() consumes the skb but returns without releasing it, unlike the IFF_UP failure path at line 49 which calls kfree_skb().
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function allocates/holds an skb and drops it from use on a consumed path without any kfree_skb(), matching CWE-401 (missing release of memory after effective lifetime). This is a resource-lifetime leak, not a use-after-free (CWE-416), since the memory is never freed while still referenced.

evidence_lines.code:
if (macvlan_forward_source(skb, port, eth->h_source))
return RX_HANDLER_CONSUMED;

if (macvlan_forward_source(skb, port, eth->h_source))
return RX_HANDLER_CONSUMED;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the nodst/source-forwarding path returns RX_HANDLER_CONSUMED, signaling the skb is consumed, yet ownership is never released. Trigger: a remotely received frame whose source MAC matches a macvlan interface under the nodst option causes macvlan_forward_source() to return true. Consequence: each such packet leaks its skb, exhausting kernel memory over time.

description: LibVNC before 0.9.12 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in libvncserver/rfbserver.c. The fix for CVE-2018-15127 was incomplete.

code_evidence: The client-controlled uint32_t length is used to size the heap buffer as malloc((uint64_t)length+1) with no upper-bound check before allocation.
After rfbReadExact reads length bytes into buffer, the code unconditionally executes buffer[length]=0, writing a NUL terminator at offset length.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes buffer[length]=0 beyond the allocated buffer, which is exactly an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). It is not merely an integer overflow: the overflow in sizing is the enabler, but the supported consequence is the out-of-bounds heap write.

evidence_lines.code:
if ((n = rfbReadExact(cl, (char *)buffer, length)) <= 0) {
buffer[length]=0;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: length is attacker-controlled and only checked for length>0; the allocation and the terminating write both assume length+1 bytes are available. If length is the maximum uint32_t value, the size computation can wrap or the allocation can be undersized, so the write at buffer[length] lands past the allocated heap object. Trigger: a file-transfer request carrying an oversized length. Consequence: a heap out-of-bounds write, corrupting adjacent memory and potentially enabling code execution or a crash.

commit_msg:
bpf: fix branch pruning logic

when the verifier detects that register contains a runtime constant
and it's compared with another constant it will prune exploration
of the branch that is guaranteed not to be taken at runtime.
This is all correct, but malicious program may be constructed
in such a way that it always has a constant comparison and
the other branch is never taken under any conditions.
In this case such path through the program will not be explored
by the verifier. It won't be taken at run-time either, but since
all instructions are JITed the malicious program may cause JITs
to complain about using reserved fields, etc.
To fix the issue we have to track the instructions explored by
the verifier and sanitize instructions that are dead at run time
with NOPs. We cannot reject such dead code, since llvm generates
it for valid C code, since it doesn't do as much data flow
analysis as the verifier does.

Fixes: 17a5267067f3 ("bpf: verifier (add verifier core)")
Signed-off-by: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@kernel.org>
Acked-by: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>
Signed-off-by: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\tsanitize_dead_code(env);', '', '\tif (ret == 0)']}
description: kernel/bpf/verifier.c in the Linux kernel through 4.14.8 ignores unreachable code, even though it would still be processed by JIT compilers. This behavior, also considered an improper branch-pruning logic issue, could possibly be used by local users for denial of service.

code_evidence: do_check() at line 50 prunes branches the verifier proves unreachable at runtime; those instructions remain in env->prog and are never inspected. After skip_full_check cleanup, the only post-check transformation is convert_ctx_accesses() at line 59, with no sanitization of the dead instructions before the program is handed to the JIT.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The verifier is the input-validation gate for BPF bytecode, and it fails to validate the full instruction stream because pruned code bypasses do_check(). The missing constraint (no sanitization of dead code) is an improper-validation flaw producing the DoS consequence, matching CWE-20.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the verifier's branch-pruning logic treats runtime-constant comparisons as safe to skip, but the pruned instructions are still emitted and JIT-compiled. Trigger: a crafted BPF program whose dead branch contains instructions with reserved fields or otherwise invalid encodings. Consequence: the JIT processes unverified instructions, causing a crash or denial of service.

Lines 95-98 compute match->match_length as match_offset - match->offset + match_length and clamp data_length with yr_min against max_match_data, then lines 99-106 allocate data_length bytes and memcpy match->data_length bytes from match_data - match_offset + match->offset.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The memcpy at lines 103-106 copies into a buffer whose size derives from the same unvalidated configuration value, matching CWE-120's buffer copy without checking input size. It is not merely an out-of-bounds read, so CWE-125 does not fit.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the configured max_match_data value is fetched as a raw buffer without size/type validation, so an attacker-controlled or mismatched configuration can yield an incorrect bound. Trigger: a scan with chained strings where the computed match_length exceeds the allocated/expected size. Consequence: memcpy copies match->data_length bytes into a buffer sized from that same value, permitting out-of-bounds write and crash/DoS.
