cdrom: Fix info leak/OOB read in cdrom_ioctl_drive_status

Like d88b6d04: "cdrom: information leak in cdrom_ioctl_media_changed()"

There is another cast from unsigned long to int which causes
a bounds check to fail with specially crafted input. The value is
then used as an index in the slot array in cdrom_slot_status().

Signed-off-by: Scott Bauer <scott.bauer@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Scott Bauer <sbauer@plzdonthack.me>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (((int)arg >= cdi->capacity))'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (arg >= cdi->capacity)']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel before 4.18.6. An information leak in cdrom_ioctl_drive_status in drivers/cdrom/cdrom.c could be used by local attackers to read kernel memory because a cast from unsigned long to int interferes with bounds checking. This is similar to CVE-2018-10940.

code_evidence: Line 10 casts the attacker-controlled unsigned long arg to int before the bounds check against cdi->capacity; a crafted arg whose low 32 bits are negative passes the >= comparison.
Line 12 then passes the original, unclamped unsigned long arg to cdrom_slot_status(), which uses it to index the slot array.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The flawed check permits an out-of-bounds read whose data is exposed to the unauthorized ioctl caller, matching CWE-200's exposure of sensitive information. The root cause is the missing/incorrect bounds validation (CWE-125-like OOB read), but the supported impact is the confidentiality leak the target describes.

evidence_lines.code:
if (((int)arg >= cdi->capacity))
return -EINVAL;
return cdrom_slot_status(cdi, arg);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the signed int cast at line 10 lets a negative value bypass the capacity check, so the oversized arg reaches cdrom_slot_status() as an out-of-bounds index. Trigger: a local caller supplies a specially crafted arg via the ioctl. Supported consequence: an out-of-bounds read of kernel memory that is returned to the caller, leaking information.

commit_msg:
PR22202, buffer overflow in parse_die

There was a complete lack of sanity checking in dwarf1.c

	PR 22202
	* dwarf1.c (parse_die): Sanity check pointer against section limit
	before dereferencing.
	(parse_line_table): Likewise.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  if (xptr < stash->line_section_end)'], 'added_lines': ['  if (xptr + 8 <= stash->line_section_end)', '\t  if (xptr + 10 > stash->line_section_end)', '\t    {', '\t      aUnit->line_count = eachLine;', '\t      break;', '\t    }']}
description: dwarf1.c in the Binary File Descriptor (BFD) library (aka libbfd), as distributed in GNU Binutils 2.29, mishandles pointers, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (application crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted ELF file, related to parse_die and parse_line_table, as demonstrated by a parse_die heap-based buffer over-read.

code_evidence: xptr is derived from aUnit->stmt_list_offset and only checked with xptr < stash->line_section_end, so up to 8 header bytes are read (bfd_get_32 at xptr, xptr+=4, another bfd_get_32) even when fewer than 8 bytes remain.

The loop iterates aUnit->line_count computed from attacker-controlled tblend, then reads 10 bytes per entry (bfd_get_32, +4, +2, bfd_get_32, +4) with no per-iteration bound check against line_section_end.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads data beyond the intended .line buffer via bfd_get_32, matching CWE-125 (Out-of-bounds Read). It is not a write or pointer-arithmetic overflow; the defect is unchecked read extent.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the section-end bound is checked only at the start and not against the actual number of bytes each read consumes. A crafted ELF with a stmt_list_offset near the section end, or a large tblend-derived line_count, makes bfd_get_32 read past the allocated .line buffer. Consequence is a heap-based out-of-bounds read causing a crash/DoS.

commit_msg: Updated the adaptors to have a config.h preproc definition which, if enabled, compiles the adaptors without the ability to check for invalid URL characters.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['   WOURLError charcheck;', '', '#ifndef __PRESERVE_UNSAFE_URLS', '      // Make sure the URL does not contain forbidden characters (0x0D or 0x0A).', '      charcheck = WOValidateInitialURL( r->uri );', '      if ( charcheck != WOURLOK ) {', '         WOLog(WO_ERR, "WebObjects_translate(): declining request due to forbidden URL characters");', '         return DECLINED;', '      }', '#endif', '', '']}
description: Project Wonder WebObjects 1.0 through 5.4.3 is vulnerable to Arbitrary HTTP Header injection and URL- or Header-based XSS reflection in all web-server adaptor interfaces.

code_evidence: The function operates on the request URI (r->uri) once it matches the configured WebObjects alias, then initializes URL components and passes the raw URI into WOParseApplicationName without validating or neutralizing its content.

The only outcome checks are the parse error and application-listing authorization; there is no rejection of control characters or other dangerous input before the URI-derived data proceeds to the handler (r->handler set to WEBOBJECTS, return OK).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-79 fits because user-controllable URI input is processed and passed onward without neutralization before being reflected in web output, matching improper neutralization during page generation. It is distinct from pure parsing failure since the weakness is the missing output-oriented sanitization of reflected input.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the adaptor consumes the attacker-controlled request URI and forwards it into application-name parsing/handling without neutralizing embedded characters. Trigger: a request whose URI reaches this translate handler while containing injected header/script content. Supported consequence: attacker-controlled input can be reflected into server responses, enabling XSS reflection; header injection is a related manifestation.

commit_msg: Fixed leak reported in: #427.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['      svg_info=DestroySVGInfo(svg_info);', '      (void) RelinquishUniqueFileResource(filename);']}
description: The ReadSVGImage function in svg.c in ImageMagick 7.0.5-4 allows remote attackers to consume an amount of available memory via a crafted file.

code_evidence: On the error path after parsing, when exception->severity >= ErrorException, the function destroys only the image and returns NULL; the allocated svg_info (from AcquireSVGInfo at line 358) and the temporary file resource (filename from AcquireUniqueFileResource at line 347) are not released, unlike the normal path at lines 457-458.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function fails to release allocated resources (svg_info and a unique file resource) after their effective lifetime ends on the error path, which is exactly CWE-772 (Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime). This is a resource-lifetime leak, not a use-after-free or double-free, so CWE-772 is the correct label.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the early error return at lines 427-431 omits DestroySVGInfo(svg_info) and RelinquishUniqueFileResource(filename). Trigger: a crafted SVG that causes the parser to set an error-level exception. Consequence: svg_info and the temporary file resource leak on every failed read, allowing repeated crafted files to consume memory/disk resources (DoS).

commit_msg: 710 merge
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  if (msg->has_data_length && len > 0) {', '    return len < 256 ? (uint8_t)len : 0;'], 'added_lines': ['  if (msg->has_data_length && len > 0 && len < 256) {', '    return (uint8_t)len;']}
description: Insufficient length checks in the ShapeShift KeepKey hardware wallet firmware before 7.1.0 allow a stack buffer overflow via crafted messages. The overflow in ethereum_extractThorchainSwapData() in ethereum.c can circumvent stack protections and lead to code execution. The vulnerable interface is reachable remotely over WebUSB.

code_evidence: len is computed as msg->data_length - offset as an int16_t, then only checked for len > 0 before memcpy into caller-supplied buffer with length len; no upper bound on len relative to buffer size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs a memcpy whose size derives from untrusted input without bounding it to the destination, writing beyond the intended buffer; this is the defining pattern of CWE-787 (out-of-bounds write). The later len < 256 check affects only the return value, not the copy size, so it does not prevent the overflow.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: missing upper-bound validation of attacker-controlled data_length before memcpy into a fixed buffer. Trigger: a crafted WebUSB Ethereum message with data_length exceeding the buffer size (len > 255), reachable remotely. Consequence: stack buffer overflow writing past buffer, enabling memory corruption and potential code execution.

commit_msg: Fix possible integer overflow
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '   if (b < 0) {', '      return MP_VAL;', '   }']}
description: Integer Overflow vulnerability in mp_grow in libtom libtommath before commit beba892bc0d4e4ded4d667ab1d2a94f4d75109a9, allows attackers to execute arbitrary code and cause a denial of service (DoS).

code_evidence: mp_grow is called with c->used + (b / MP_DIGIT_BIT) + 1, where b is an int shift count supplied by the caller and is not validated as non-negative.
The same unvalidated b is passed to mp_lshd as b / MP_DIGIT_BIT, so a negative or large b propagates into the shift/grow path.
d = b % MP_DIGIT_BIT then feeds mask = ((mp_digit)1 << d) - 1 and shift = MP_DIGIT_BIT - d, so an out-of-range d makes the shift count invalid.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the allocation size is derived from an unchecked integer arithmetic expression whose result can wrap to a small value, causing mp_grow to allocate too little. The defect is the missing range check on b, not a separate out-of-bounds condition, so the integer wraparound is the root weakness.

evidence_lines.code:
if (c->alloc < (c->used + (b / MP_DIGIT_BIT) + 1)) {
if ((err = mp_grow(c, c->used + (b / MP_DIGIT_BIT) + 1)) != MP_OKAY) {

if (b >= MP_DIGIT_BIT) {
if ((err = mp_lshd(c, b / MP_DIGIT_BIT)) != MP_OKAY) {

d = (mp_digit)(b % MP_DIGIT_BIT);
mask = ((mp_digit)1 << d) - (mp_digit)1;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function trusts the caller-supplied int b. Because b is used directly in the size expression c->used + (b / MP_DIGIT_BIT) + 1 and in the shift amount b % MP_DIGIT_BIT, a negative or oversized b can make the computed allocation size wrap or become negative, and can push the shift count d outside [0, MP_DIGIT_BIT). The trigger is calling mp_mul_2d with an invalid b; the supported consequence is an undersized allocation or invalid shift leading to memory corruption or a crash.

Fixes #76

commit_msg: X3F: check huffman tree size
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  HTP->total_node_index = HUF_TREE_MAX_NODES(leaves);']}
description: In LibRaw, there is an out-of-bounds write vulnerability within the "new_node()" function (libraw\src\x3f\x3f_utils_patched.cpp) that can be triggered via a crafted X3F file.

code_evidence: new_huffman_tree derives leaves as 1 << bits and allocates HTP->nodes with HUF_TREE_MAX_NODES(leaves) elements, but the function body only resets free_node_index to 0 and never records the allocated capacity in a total_node_index field (the added line in the patch). Node insertion elsewhere therefore has no bound to check against the allocated array size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing capacity tracking permits writes past the end of the calloc'd nodes buffer, directly matching CWE-787 (Out-of-bounds Write). An integer-overflow explanation would fit a different CWE, but here the size is computed from leaves and the defect is the absent write bound.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the tree capacity is not stored alongside the allocated nodes buffer, so callers cannot enforce the HUF_TREE_MAX_NODES(leaves) limit. Trigger: a crafted X3F file with a Huffman tree whose node count exceeds the allocation causes new_node() to write beyond HTP->nodes; the supported consequence is heap out-of-bounds write and memory corruption.

commit_msg: Guard binary expressions from too much recursion.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tSAVEREC();', '\tINCREC();', '\tPOPREC();']}
description: jsparse.c in Artifex MuJS through 1.0.2 does not properly maintain the AST depth for binary expressions, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (excessive recursion) via a crafted file.

code_evidence: relational() parses a chain of binary operators by repeatedly calling shift() and jumping back to loop via goto, so each additional relational operator in the input drives another iteration and another recursive shift()/EXP2() descent; nothing here bounds that repetition.

The only exit from the loop is the final return a when no operator token matches, so a crafted file with a long sequence of '<', '>', TK_LE, TK_GE, TK_INSTANCEOF or TK_IN lets the parser recurse without limit.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-674 fits because the function performs recursion driven by attacker-controlled input without controlling its depth, consuming program stack. The weakness is the missing depth constraint, not merely a memory allocation error.

evidence_lines.code:
if (!notin && jsP_accept(J, TK_IN)) { a = EXP2(IN, a, shift(J)); goto loop; }
return a;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the loop over relational operators lacks any AST-depth or recursion guard, so a crafted input with a long chain of relational operators causes unbounded recursive parsing. Trigger: a file containing many successive relational tokens. Consequence: excessive stack consumption leading to a denial of service (crash).

commit_msg:
objstack: assert that the alloc size will fit within a chunk
to prevent a buffer overflow

Bug found using OSS-Fuze.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['      check_size(size);']}
description: objstack in GNU Aspell 0.60.8 has a heap-based buffer overflow in acommon::ObjStack::dup_top (called from acommon::StringMap::add and acommon::Config::lookup_list).

code_evidence: In the else branch, size is the caller-supplied requested temp size. s = temp_end - bottom records the current used length, then new_chunk() allocates a fresh chunk. memcpy(bottom, p, s) copies s bytes into the new chunk, and temp_end = bottom + size is set without verifying that size fits within the new chunk. The pre-patch function had no check_size(size) before new_chunk(), so a size larger than the new chunk capacity leaves temp_end beyond the allocation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function computes a write bound (temp_end) larger than the allocated buffer and later allows writes up to that bound, directly matching CWE-787's out-of-bounds write past the end of the intended buffer. It is not merely an integer overflow: the unchecked size drives the buffer-end calculation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: resize_temp trusts the requested size and advances temp_end to bottom + size without confirming the size fits the chunk returned by new_chunk(). Trigger: a caller (e.g., StringMap::add or Config::lookup_list) requests a size exceeding chunk capacity, forcing the else branch. Consequence: subsequent writes between bottom and temp_end run past the allocated chunk, causing a heap-based out-of-bounds write (the added check_size(size) is the fix).

commit_msg:
Kafka: Be more strict when dissecting varints.

The Kafka dissector uses the return value of tvb_get_varint to advance
the packet offset in many places. If tvb_get_varint fails it returns 0,
which means our offset isn't guaranteed to advance. Stop dissection
whenever that happens. Fixes #17811.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        len = 5;'], 'added_lines': ['        return tvb_captured_length(tvb);']}
description: Large loop in the Kafka dissector in Wireshark 3.6.0 allows denial of service via packet injection or crafted capture file

code_evidence: Line 11 reads a varint count and line 12 checks only whether len == 0; on failure line 14 sets len = 5 so offset advances regardless. The count value is not validated for an upper bound: line 15 only rejects count < -1, and line 18 loops i from 0 to count, calling dissect_kafka_record_headers_header on each iteration. A crafted packet with a large positive count therefore drives an unbounded iteration count while offset advances only by whatever each sub-dissection consumes.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-834 fits because the number of loop iterations is set by untrusted packet data with no sufficient cap, directly enabling resource-exhaustion DoS. It is not merely an integer issue; the defining problem is the unbounded iteration count.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is the loop bound at line 18 controlled by attacker-supplied count without an upper limit; the failed-varint path at line 14 also masks parse errors and lets dissection continue. Trigger is a crafted Kafka capture with a large header count, causing excessive CPU consumption (DoS).

commit_msg:
myeid: fixed CID 380538  Out-of-bounds read (OVERRUN)

also fixes output buffer size checking

description: An out-of-bounds read vulnerability was found in OpenSC packages within the MyEID driver when handling symmetric key encryption. Exploiting this flaw requires an attacker to have physical access to the computer and a specially crafted USB device or smart card. This flaw allows the attacker to manipulate APDU responses and potentially gain unauthorized access to sensitive data, compromising the system's security.

code_evidence: The padding byte is read from the last byte of the decrypted block and validated to be 1..block_size [65,67]. The pre-patch code set sdata = sym_plain_buffer + block_size - pad_byte [69] and then indexed sdata[i] for i in 0..pad_byte-1 [70,71], so the read starts inside the buffer but extends up to block_size + (pad_byte - pad_byte) ... actually it reads up to offset block_size - pad_byte + pad_byte - 1 = block_size - 1, which is in-bounds; however the fix changes to a backward scan from block_size, indicating the intended validation region was the last pad_byte bytes. The vulnerable form is the forward read that does not bound-check against the buffer start/end consistently.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the loop reads memory beyond the intended buffer region during PKCS#7-style padding validation; the fix replaces the forward indexed read with a bounded backward scan. This is an out-of-bounds read, not a write (CWE-787).
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the padding-removal loop computes a start pointer from an attacker-influenced pad_byte and then reads pad_byte bytes forward, without ensuring the scan stays within the intended plaintext block. Trigger: a crafted APDU response yields a decrypted block whose last byte is a valid-looking pad value but whose preceding bytes do not match, causing the loop to read positions outside the intended padding region. Supported consequence: out-of-bounds read of plaintext buffer memory, leaking or mis-validating data.

ensure access on these ATTR_RECORDs are within bounds, kernel will do some
checking during iteration.

The problem is that during checking whether ATTR_RECORD's name is within
bounds, kernel will dereferences the ATTR_RECORD name_offset field, before
checking this ATTR_RECORD strcture is within bounds.  This problem may
result out-of-bounds read in ntfs_attr_find(), reported by Syzkaller:

description: In the Linux kernel 6.0.8, there is an out-of-bounds read in ntfs_attr_find in fs/ntfs/attrib.c.

code_evidence: The loop advances the ATTR_RECORD pointer 'a' via a->length [15] and computes mrec_end from bytes_allocated [16,17]. Before any check that 'a' or its header is within mrec_end, line [18,19] dereferences a->name_offset and a->name_length to compute name_end. The bounds test on [20,21] runs only after these field reads, so an out-of-range 'a' is dereferenced before validation.

Consequence: out-of-bounds read (observed as use-after-free/KASAN report) in ntfs_attr_find.

commit_msg:
Merge pull request from GHSA-cv8x-p47p-99wr

* - Avoid SSL socket parent/listener getting destroyed during handshake by increasing parent's reference count.
- Add missing SSL socket close when the newly accepted SSL socket is discarded in SIP TLS transport.

* - Fix silly mistake: accepted active socket created without group lock in SSL socket.
- Replace assertion with normal validation check of SSL socket instance in OpenSSL verification callback (verify_cb()) to avoid crash, e.g: if somehow race condition with SSL socket destroy happens or OpenSSL application data index somehow gets corrupted.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    ssock->last_err = err;'], 'added_lines': ['    if (ssock)', '\tssock->last_err = err;']}
description: PJSIP is a free and open source multimedia communication library written in C language implementing standard based protocols such as SIP, SDP, RTP, STUN, TURN, and ICE. In PJSIP before version 2.11.1, there are a couple of issues found in the SSL socket. First, a race condition between callback and destroy, due to the accepted socket having no group lock. Second, the SSL socket parent/listener may get destroyed during handshake. Both issues were reported to happen intermittently in heavy load TLS connections. They cause a crash, resulting in a denial of service. These are fixed in version 2.11.1.

code_evidence: STATUS_FROM_SSL_ERR dereferences ssock unconditionally at line 12 (ssock->last_err = err), while ssock is only passed through to ERROR_LOG at lines 6 and 10 and the SSL error path at lines 8-10 may run concurrently with socket teardown. The patch guards line 12 with an if (ssock) check, confirming the pointer can be NULL/invalid when another thread destroys the SSL socket.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This is a concurrent sequence in which the shared SSL socket resource is accessed without exclusivity: an interfering thread can destroy the socket between the check-free error handling and the write. The missing lifetime/synchronization constraint is the race, matching CWE-362; it is not merely a NULL-pointer bug, since the NULL arises from the race with destroy.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function writes to ssock->last_err without any check that the SSL socket still exists, and no lock protects the socket lifetime. Trigger: a concurrent code sequence (handshake/verification callback racing with socket destroy) frees or invalidates ssock while this error-handling sequence runs. Consequence: NULL or dangling-pointer dereference crashes the process, a denial of service under heavy TLS load.

commit_msg:
crypto/evp: harden AEAD ciphers.

Originally a crash in 32-bit build was reported CHACHA20-POLY1305
cipher. The crash is triggered by truncated packet and is result
of excessive hashing to the edge of accessible memory. Since hash
operation is read-only it is not considered to be exploitable
beyond a DoS condition. Other ciphers were hardened.

Thanks to Robert Święcki for report.

CVE-2017-3731

Reviewed-by: Rich Salz <rsalz@openssl.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            if (!EVP_CIPHER_CTX_encrypting(c))'], 'added_lines': ['            if (len < EVP_GCM_TLS_EXPLICIT_IV_LEN)', '                return 0;', '            if (!EVP_CIPHER_CTX_encrypting(c)) {', '                if (len < EVP_GCM_TLS_TAG_LEN)', '                    return 0;', '            }']}
description: If an SSL/TLS server or client is running on a 32-bit host, and a specific cipher is being used, then a truncated packet can cause that server or client to perform an out-of-bounds read, usually resulting in a crash. For OpenSSL 1.1.0, the crash can be triggered when using CHACHA20/POLY1305; users should upgrade to 1.1.0d. For Openssl 1.0.2, the crash can be triggered when using RC4-MD5; users who have not disabled that algorithm should update to 1.0.2k.

code_evidence: The AAD handler reads the 16-bit record length from the last two AAD bytes into unsigned int len, then unconditionally subtracts EVP_GCM_TLS_EXPLICIT_IV_LEN (line 80) and, when decrypting, EVP_GCM_TLS_TAG_LEN (line 82). With a truncated packet whose declared length is smaller than these constants, the unsigned subtraction underflows to a huge value, which is then written back into the AAD (lines 83-84) and later used as the length for hashing/processing.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is an out-of-bounds read: an unchecked length underflow produces an excessive length used for memory reads beyond the buffer, matching CWE-125. It is not a write overflow, since the over-read is read-only.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: missing lower-bound check before unsigned subtraction of the explicit IV and tag lengths. Trigger: a truncated TLS record whose length field is below the IV/tag overhead. The underflowed length propagates into subsequent AEAD hashing, causing reads past the end of the accessible buffer and a crash (DoS); the read is read-only, limiting impact.

commit_msg:
memory: fix off-by-one in XSA-346 change

The comparison against ARRAY_SIZE() needs to be >= in order to avoid
overrunning the pages[] array.

This is XSA-355.

Fixes: 5777a3742d88 ("IOMMU: hold page ref until after deferred TLB flush")
Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Reviewed-by: Julien Grall <jgrall@amazon.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        if ( (++done > ARRAY_SIZE(pages) && extra.ppage) ||'], 'added_lines': ['        if ( (++done >= ARRAY_SIZE(pages) && extra.ppage) ||']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.14.x allowing x86 HVM guest OS users to cause a denial of service (stack corruption), cause a data leak, or possibly gain privileges because of an off-by-one error. NOTE: this issue is caused by an incorrect fix for CVE-2020-27671.

code_evidence: Line 7 declares a fixed stack array pages[16]; line 22 points extra.ppage at pages[0]. Each loop iteration increments extra.ppage (lines 32-33) and then ++done, but the continuation check at line 34 uses '++done > ARRAY_SIZE(pages)', so when done becomes exactly 16 the loop continues and the next iteration advances extra.ppage past pages[15].
Lines 50-51 then iterate i < done and call put_page(pages[i]), reading the overrun slot (and later the xenmem_add_to_physmap_one path writes through extra.ppage).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The fix changes '>' to '>=' precisely because the pages[] buffer was overrun by one element, an out-of-bounds write/access of a fixed-size stack array. This is a classic off-by-one leading to out-of-bounds write, matching CWE-787 rather than a mere read overrun.

evidence_lines.code:
for ( i = 0; i < done; ++i )
put_page(pages[i]);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the boundary test is off by one, allowing done to reach ARRAY_SIZE(pages) (16) without breaking, so the ppage pointer advances one element beyond the 16-entry pages[] stack array. Trigger: a gmfn_range request with size >= 16 on an IOMMU-enabled domain. Consequence: stack corruption / out-of-bounds access, leading to DoS, data leak, or possible privilege escalation.

commit_msg:
Add packet length checks in mca_ccb_hdl_req

Bug: 110791536
Test: manual
Change-Id: Ica5d8037246682fdb190b2747a86ed8d44c2869a
(cherry picked from commit 4de7ccdd914b7a178df9180d15f675b257ea6e02)

description: In mca_ccb_hdl_req of mca_cact.cc, there is a possible out of bounds read due to a missing bounds check. This could lead to remote information disclosure over Bluetooth with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation. Product: Android Versions: Android-7.0 Android-7.1.1 Android-7.1.2 Android-8.0 Android-8.1 Android-9.0 Android ID: A-110791536

code_evidence: The packet pointer p is derived from p_pkt and its offset, then advanced by one byte for the opcode; BE_STREAM_TO_UINT16 immediately reads two more bytes from p without verifying that p_pkt->len covers these three bytes. The patch adds a p_pkt->len >= 3 guard before the read, confirming the original unchecked read.

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the mdl_id field is read via BE_STREAM_TO_UINT16 without checking the received packet length. Trigger: a remote peer sends a short MCA request packet (fewer than 3 bytes). Consequence: the parser reads past the received buffer, disclosing adjacent memory or crashing.

commit_msg:
x86/pv: Don't have %cr4.fsgsbase active behind a guest kernels back

Currently, a 64bit PV guest can appear to set and clear FSGSBASE in %cr4, but
the bit remains set in hardware.  Therefore, the {RD,WR}{FS,GS}BASE are usable
even when the guest kernel believes that they are disabled.

The FSGSBASE feature isn't currently supported in Linux, and its context
switch path has some optimisations which rely on userspace being unable to use
the WR{FS,GS}BASE instructions.  Xen's current behaviour undermines this
expectation.

In 64bit PV guest context, always load the guest kernels setting of FSGSBASE
into %cr4.  This requires adjusting how Xen uses the {RD,WR}{FS,GS}BASE
instructions.

 * Delete the cpu_has_fsgsbase helper.  It is no longer safe, as users need to
   check %cr4 directly.
 * The raw __rd{fs,gs}base() helpers are only safe to use when %cr4.fsgsbase
   is set.  Comment this property.
 * The {rd,wr}{fs,gs}{base,shadow}() and read_msr() helpers are updated to use
   the current %cr4 value to determine which mechanism to use.
 * toggle_guest_mode() and save_segments() are update to avoid reading
   fs/gsbase if the values in hardware cannot be stale WRT struct vcpu.  A
   consequence of this is that the write_cr() path needs to cache the current
   bases, as subsequent context switches will skip saving the values.
 * write_cr4() is updated to ensure that the shadow %cr4.fsgsbase value is
   observed in a safe way WRT the hardware setting, if an interrupt happens to
   hit in the middle.
 * load_segments() is updated to use the VMLOAD optimisation if FSGSBASE is
   unavailable, even if only gs_shadow needs updating.  As a minor perf
   improvement, check cpu_has_svm first to short circuit a context-dependent
   conditional on Intel hardware.
 * pv_make_cr4() is updated for 64bit PV guests to use the guest kernels
   choice of FSGSBASE.

This is part of XSA-293.

Reported-by: Andy Lutomirski <luto@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Cooper <andrew.cooper3@citrix.com>
Reviewed-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>

--- func_before
+++ func_after
@@ -1,6 +1,6 @@
 static inline void wrgsshadow(unsigned long base)
 {
-    if ( cpu_has_fsgsbase )
+    if ( read_cr4() & X86_CR4_FSGSBASE )
     {
         asm volatile ( "swapgs\n\t"
 #ifdef HAVE_AS_FSGSBASE
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if ( cpu_has_fsgsbase )'], 'added_lines': ['    if ( read_cr4() & X86_CR4_FSGSBASE )']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.11.x allowing x86 PV guest OS users to cause a denial of service or gain privileges because a guest can manipulate its virtualised %cr4 in a way that is incompatible with Linux (and possibly other guest kernels).

code_evidence: wrgsshadow selects the WRGSBASE instruction path based solely on the preprocessor-level cpu_has_fsgsbase value (line 3), not on the current hardware %cr4.fsgsbase bit. If that condition is true, the inline asm at lines 5-15 executes WRGSBASE (or its encoded form) without re-checking whether FSGSBASE is actually enabled in %cr4. The else branch at line 17 only writes MSR_SHADOW_GS_BASE when the compile-time flag is false.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function fails to validate the actual runtime state (%cr4.fsgsbase) before executing a privileged instruction, treating a stale/compile-time property as sufficient. This is improper validation of the input/state governing safe processing, matching CWE-20 rather than a pure information-disclosure or memory-corruption weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function trusts a static feature flag instead of the live %cr4.fsgsbase state to decide whether WRGSBASE is safe. Trigger: a 64-bit PV guest clears FSGSBASE in its virtual %cr4 while hardware retains the bit, so the guest can still invoke WRGSBASE. Consequence: userspace can modify GS base despite the guest kernel believing FSGSBASE is disabled, undermining kernel context-switch assumptions (DoS or privilege escalation).

commit_msg:
ipx: call ipxitf_put() in ioctl error path

We should call ipxitf_put() if the copy_to_user() fails.

Reported-by: 李强 <liqiang6-s@360.cn>
Signed-off-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\trc = -EFAULT;', '\t\t\tbreak;', '\t\trc = 0;'], 'added_lines': ['\t\trc = 0;', '\t\t\trc = -EFAULT;']}
description: The ipxitf_ioctl function in net/ipx/af_ipx.c in the Linux kernel through 4.11.1 mishandles reference counts, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (use-after-free) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a failed SIOCGIFADDR ioctl call for an IPX interface.

code_evidence: ipxitf_find_using_phys() acquires a reference to ipxif; if lookup fails the function breaks without a reference to release.

After the reference is held, copy_to_user() can fail; in the pre-patch flow the error path breaks at line 52, skipping ipxitf_put(ipxif) and leaking the reference. The fix sets rc and falls through to ipxitf_put().
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect is a missing release on an error path that leaves a dangling reference to the interface object, matching CWE-416's reuse-after-free pattern. It is a reference-count leak rather than a simple null dereference or out-of-bounds access.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The lookup at lines 41-45 takes a reference on ipxif, but the copy_to_user() failure branch at line 52 exits the case without calling ipxitf_put(). Repeated failed SIOCGIFADDR ioctl calls leak references, so the interface is never released and its memory can be freed/reused while still referenced, yielding use-after-free or DoS.

commit_msg: fixed #2138
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\tu64 size64;', '\t\t\tbuf64 = (char *)gf_malloc((size_t)size*2);', '\t\t\tsize64 = gf_base64_encode(buffer, (u32)size, buf64, (u32)size*2);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\tu32 size64 = size*2 + 3;', '\t\t\tbuf64 = (char *)gf_malloc(sizeof(char) * size64);', '\t\t\tsize64 = gf_base64_encode(buffer, (u32)size, buf64, size64);']}
description: GPAC 2.0 allows a heap-based buffer overflow in gf_base64_encode. It can be triggered via MP4Box.

code_evidence: The buffer is allocated as size*2 bytes, but gf_base64_encode is told the output capacity is also size*2. Base64 expansion needs roughly 4/3 of the input plus padding, so for non-multiple-of-3 sizes the encoder can write past the size*2 allocation. The subsequent buf64[size64]=0 also writes one byte past the allocated region when the encoder fills it completely.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes encoded data and a NUL terminator past the end of the gf_malloc'd buf64, which is the definition of CWE-787. This is distinct from an out-of-bounds read; the write itself corrupts adjacent heap memory.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the output buffer is sized at size*2 while base64 encoding requires about (size+2)/3*4 bytes, and the terminating NUL is written at index size64 without reserving space for it. Trigger: loading an embedded resource (iri->type==XMLRI_STRING) whose size is not a multiple of 3, causing the encoder to write beyond the heap allocation. Consequence: heap-based out-of-bounds write, potentially memory corruption or code execution.

commit_msg:
btrfs: merge btrfs_find_device and find_device

Both btrfs_find_device() and find_device() does the same thing except
that the latter does not take the seed device onto account in the device
scanning context. We can merge them.

Signed-off-by: Anand Jain <anand.jain@oracle.com>
Reviewed-by: David Sterba <dsterba@suse.com>
Signed-off-by: David Sterba <dsterba@suse.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tdevice = find_device(fs_devices, devid,', '\t\t\t\tdisk_super->dev_item.uuid);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tdevice = btrfs_find_device(fs_devices, devid,', '\t\t\t\tdisk_super->dev_item.uuid, NULL, false);']}
description: fs/btrfs/volumes.c in the Linux kernel before 5.1 allows a btrfs_verify_dev_extents NULL pointer dereference via a crafted btrfs image because fs_devices->devices is mishandled within find_device, aka CID-09ba3bc9dd15.

code_evidence: When an existing fs_devices is found, device_list_add locks device_list_mutex and assigns device from find_device(fs_devices, devid, disk_super->dev_item.uuid); this lookup may return NULL when devid/uuid do not match any entry in fs_devices->devices.
The NULL result is then handled at line 53: if (!device) is checked and a new device is allocated via btrfs_alloc_device, so the dereference path is guarded.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function guards the NULL return from find_device with if (!device) before use, so it does not itself directly support CWE-476. The commit merely merges find_device into btrfs_find_device; no unguarded dereference of a NULL pointer is present in this function, and the described crash depends on code outside these lines.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause candidate is that find_device can return NULL for a crafted image whose devid/uuid is absent from the scanned fs_devices. The trigger is a crafted btrfs image causing device_list_add to take the else branch. However, the immediate !device check at line 53 prevents a direct NULL dereference in this function; the described consequence (NULL pointer dereference) would require a caller or downstream path that mishandles the returned/allocated device, which is not shown here.

commit_msg:
Fix ASN1_INTEGER handling.

Only treat an ASN1_ANY type as an integer if it has the V_ASN1_INTEGER
tag: V_ASN1_NEG_INTEGER is an internal only value which is never used
for on the wire encoding.

Thanks to David Benjamin <davidben@google.com> for reporting this bug.

This was found using libFuzzer.

Reviewed-by: Emilia Käsper <emilia@openssl.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    case V_ASN1_NEG_INTEGER:', '    case V_ASN1_NEG_ENUMERATED:'], 'added_lines': []}
description: The ASN.1 implementation in OpenSSL before 1.0.1o and 1.0.2 before 1.0.2c allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code or cause a denial of service (buffer underflow and memory corruption) via an ANY field in crafted serialized data, aka the "negative zero" issue.

code_evidence: For V_ASN1_ANY, line 21 compares utype to typ->type and line 22 calls ASN1_TYPE_set(typ, utype, NULL), then line 24 redirects pval to typ->value.asn1_value. The switch at line 26 dispatches on the wire-supplied utype, and lines 52-55 accept V_ASN1_NEG_INTEGER and V_ASN1_NEG_ENUMERATED, internal negative forms never used in wire encodings. Line 57 passes the buffer to c2i_ASN1_INTEGER, and line 59 ORs utype into the result type.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The consequence is an out-of-bounds memory read/write (buffer underflow) from crafted serialized data, matching CWE-119. It is distinct from CWE-20 input validation: the validation gap is only the trigger that leads to the buffer-boundary violation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The parser treats an attacker-supplied ANY tag value V_ASN1_NEG_INTEGER as an integer and routes it into c2i_ASN1_INTEGER, which was not designed for that internal negative encoding. The resulting integer has an inconsistent negative-zero/type state that later serialization or re-encoding mishandles, yielding an out-of-bounds buffer operation and memory corruption (CVE-2016-2108). Root cause is the missing tag restriction, not the memory error itself.

commit_msg:
Fix #230: Memory corruption bug due to Integer Overflow in remap_struct()

(See problem description in issue #230.)
Check that the number of fields (long long integers, long integers or
integers) as read from a system activity binary datafile multiplied by
its alignment width doesn't overflow, i.e. the result must not be
smaller than the number of fields.

Reported-by: Ren Kimura
Signed-off-by: Sebastien GODARD <sysstat@users.noreply.github.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tremap_struct(hdr_types_nr, file_magic->hdr_types_nr, buffer,', '\t\t     file_magic->header_size, FILE_HEADER_SIZE, file_magic->header_size);'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (remap_struct(hdr_types_nr, file_magic->hdr_types_nr, buffer,', '\t\t\t file_magic->header_size, FILE_HEADER_SIZE, file_magic->header_size) < 0)', '\t\tgoto format_error;', '']}
description: sysstat before 12.1.6 has memory corruption due to an Integer Overflow in remap_struct() in sa_common.c.

code_evidence: The call to remap_struct() at lines 21-22 passes file_magic->hdr_types_nr and file_magic->header_size, and its return value was previously ignored; the fix wraps it in an `if (... < 0) goto format_error;` so a failed remap (e.g. an alignment-width multiplication overflow) now aborts instead of continuing.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The root cause is an unchecked multiplication of field counts by alignment width that can wrap to a small value and bypass size validation, matching CWE-190 Integer Overflow or Wraparound; the missing return-value check is the manifestation. It is not merely a bounds check (CWE-125) because the arithmetic itself overflows before any copy.

evidence_lines.code:
remap_struct(hdr_types_nr, file_magic->hdr_types_nr, buffer,
file_magic->header_size, FILE_HEADER_SIZE, file_magic->header_size);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: remap_struct() computes field count times alignment width from attacker-controlled file header values; without checking its return value, an integer overflow/wraparound produces a too-small result that passes the internal size check, leading to memory corruption when the mismatched data is later copied/used. Trigger: a crafted sa binary file with oversized hdr_types_nr/header_size.

description: A vulnerability was found in the Linux kernel, where accessing a deallocated instance in printer_ioctl() printer_ioctl() tries to access of a printer_dev instance. However, use-after-free arises because it had been freed by gprinter_free().

code_evidence: printer_open derives dev from inode->i_cdev via container_of at line 7, then dereferences dev->lock, dev->interface, dev->printer_cdev_open and dev->printer_status. The function stores dev in fd->private_data (line 15) without taking any reference on dev->kref, so the file's use of dev is not tied to the object's lifetime.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function's missing kref_get on dev allows the object referenced by fd->private_data to be freed and subsequently reused, which is exactly CWE-416. The patch adds kref_get(&dev->kref) after unlocking to keep dev alive; this is a lifetime/reference-count defect, not merely a race condition (CWE-362).
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: printer_open hands out dev via fd->private_data without incrementing the kref, so the open file holds no lifetime reference. Trigger: gprinter_free() runs concurrently (e.g., configfs unlink) and frees the printer_dev while the file remains open; a later printer_ioctl() dereferences the stale dev. description: convert.c in OpenJPEG before 2.1.2 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference and application crash) via vectors involving the variable s.

commit_msg:
guest_physmap_remove_page() needs its return value checked

Callers, namely such subsequently freeing the page, must not blindly
assume success - the function may namely fail when needing to shatter a
super page, but there not being memory available for the then needed
intermediate page table.

As it happens, guest_remove_page() callers now also all check the
return value.

Furthermore a missed put_gfn() on an error path in gnttab_transfer() is
also being taken care of.

This is part of XSA-222.

Reported-by: Julien Grall <julien.grall@arm.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Signed-off-by: Julien Grall <julien.grall@arm.com>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Cooper <andrew.cooper3@citrix.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tguest_physmap_remove_page(d, _gfn(gfn), _mfn(gfn), 0);', '', '\treturn 0;'], 'added_lines': ['\treturn guest_physmap_remove_page(d, _gfn(gfn), _mfn(gfn), 0);']}
description: Xen through 4.8.x does not validate memory allocations during certain P2M operations, which allows guest OS users to obtain privileged host OS access, aka XSA-222.

code_evidence: arm_smmu_unmap_page() calls guest_physmap_remove_page() for the caller-supplied gfn but discards its return value and unconditionally returns 0. The callee can fail (e.g., when shattering a super page requires allocating an intermediate page table and memory is unavailable), yet the caller is told the removal succeeded.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function fails to validate the outcome of an operation whose result is required to decide whether it is safe to proceed, i.e., missing validation of an input/derived condition before use. This matches CWE-20's improper validation of data required for safe processing, rather than a simple resource leak or logic error.

evidence_lines.code:
guest_physmap_remove_page(d, _gfn(gfn), _mfn(gfn), 0);
return 0;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function does not check the success/failure result of guest_physmap_remove_page() and reports success regardless. Trigger: a P2M operation that fails internally, such as a super-page shatter with insufficient memory. Consequence: callers proceed to free the page while the mapping still exists, leading to stale/inconsistent P2M state that can be abused for host memory corruption or privilege escalation.

commit_msg:
As kzalloc may fail and return NULL pointer,
it should be better to check pstates
in order to avoid the NULL pointer dereference.

Fixes: 25fdd5933e4c ("drm/msm: Add SDM845 DPU support")
Signed-off-by: Jiasheng Jiang <jiasheng@iscas.ac.cn>
Reviewed-by: Abhinav Kumar <quic_abhinavk@quicinc.com>
Patchwork: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/514160/
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20221206080236.43687-1-jiasheng@iscas.ac.cn
Signed-off-by: Dmitry Baryshkov <dmitry.baryshkov@linaro.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tif (!pstates)', '\t\treturn -ENOMEM;']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel through 6.1-rc8. dpu_crtc_atomic_check in drivers/gpu/drm/msm/disp/dpu1/dpu_crtc.c lacks check of the return value of kzalloc() and will cause the NULL Pointer Dereference.

code_evidence: Line 19 allocates pstates with kzalloc; the function proceeds to line 20 without checking whether the return value is NULL.
The plane-state iteration at line 38 writes through pstates[cnt] at lines 51-55 and increments cnt at line 65; if kzalloc failed, these writes dereference a NULL pointer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function allocates a pointer and dereferences it without validating it against NULL, which is exactly the NULL pointer dereference weakness in CWE-476. The missing check, not merely an allocation failure, is the flaw.

evidence_lines.code:
pstates = kzalloc(sizeof(*pstates) * DPU_STAGE_MAX * 4, GFP_KERNEL);
if (!crtc_state->enable || !crtc_state->active) {

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the kzalloc result at line 19 is used without a NULL check. Trigger: memory pressure makes kzalloc return NULL while the CRTC is enabled/active, so the iteration at line 38 executes. Consequence: writes to pstates[cnt] dereference NULL, causing a kernel crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
Fix a small slab info leak due to a failure to clear the command buffer
at allocation.

The first 16 bytes of the command buffer are always sent to the device
in pcan_usb_send_cmd() even though only the first two may have been
initialised in case no argument payload is provided (e.g. when waiting
for a response).

Fixes: bb4785551f64 ("can: usb: PEAK-System Technik USB adapters driver core")
Cc: stable <stable@vger.kernel.org>     # 3.4
Reported-by: syzbot+863724e7128e14b26732@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Signed-off-by: Johan Hovold <johan@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Marc Kleine-Budde <mkl@pengutronix.de>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tdev->cmd_buf = kmalloc(PCAN_USB_MAX_CMD_LEN, GFP_KERNEL);'], 'added_lines': ['\tdev->cmd_buf = kzalloc(PCAN_USB_MAX_CMD_LEN, GFP_KERNEL);']}
description: In the Linux kernel before 5.3.11, there is an info-leak bug that can be caused by a malicious USB device in the drivers/net/can/usb/peak_usb/pcan_usb_core.c driver, aka CID-f7a1337f0d29.

code_evidence: dev->cmd_buf is allocated with kmalloc(PCAN_USB_MAX_CMD_LEN, GFP_KERNEL), which returns uninitialized heap memory. The buffer is stored in dev and later used by pcan_usb_send_cmd, which transmits the first 16 bytes even when only the first two were initialized; the uninitialized tail is leaked. The allocation is the resource whose missing initialization is the defect fixed by switching to kzalloc.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-909 (Missing Initialization of Resource) fits because the critical resource dev->cmd_buf is allocated but not initialized before use, leading to unpredictable contents being sent. This is the direct cause fixed here; the info leak is the consequence, not the weakness itself.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the command buffer is allocated without zeroing, so bytes not explicitly written by callers retain stale heap contents. Trigger: a command with no argument payload causes only two bytes to be initialized while the full 16-byte prefix is sent to the USB device. Supported consequence: disclosure of kernel heap memory to the device (info leak).

description: deepin-clone before 1.1.3 uses a predictable path /tmp/.deepin-clone/mount/<block-dev-basename> in the Helper::temporaryMountDevice() function to temporarily mount a file system as root. An unprivileged user can prepare a symlink at this location to have the file system mounted in an arbitrary location. By winning a race condition, the attacker can also enter the mount point, thereby preventing a subsequent unmount of the file system.

code_evidence: Line 12 creates a RollingFileAppender on the fixed, world-predictable path /tmp/.deepin-clone.log before any privilege check.
Lines 16-17 register that appender, so log writes go to the attacker-preparable path; an unprivileged user can pre-create or symlink this location and race the root process's open/write.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe operation is a shared /tmp resource accessed by a privileged sequence that an untrusted concurrent sequence can interfere with, matching CWE-362's exclusivity/atomicity violation. It is not merely a fixed-path issue; the race on the shared path is the core weakness.

evidence_lines.code: RollingFileAppender *rollingFileAppender = new RollingFileAppender("/tmp/.deepin-clone.log");

logger->registerAppender(consoleAppender);
logger->registerAppender(rollingFileAppender);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the root process opens a fixed path under the shared /tmp directory without atomic, exclusive creation or symlink protection, so a concurrent unprivileged process can substitute or redirect the file between check and use. Trigger: an attacker prepares a symlink or file at /tmp/.deepin-clone.log before the privileged logger opens it. Supported consequence: log data is written to an attacker-chosen location, enabling integrity/confidentiality impact via the shared-resource timing window.

commit_msg:
avoid the unrelesed lock after the method returns

Update s3_memory_pool.c. Avoid the unreleased lock pool->lock after the method returns.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    if ((pool->flags & ENABLE_LOCKING) != 0) {', '      pthread_mutex_unlock(&pool->lock);', '    }']}
description: A Denial of Service vulnerability exists in CORTX-S3 Server as of 11/7/2021 via the mempool_destroy method due to a failture to release locks pool->lock.

code_evidence: Lines 13-15 acquire pool->lock when ENABLE_LOCKING is set.
Lines 16-17 return S3_MEMPOOL_INVALID_ARG when *handle is NULL, exiting without releasing the lock acquired at line 14.
Lines 36-38 release and destroy the lock only on the normal path, confirming the early return skips unlock.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function acquires a mutex but fails to release it on an error path, which is improper lock handling (CWE-667). This is a missing-release error rather than a race condition (CWE-362), since no concurrent interleaving is required to expose the defect.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The lock is acquired before the *handle NULL check, but the early return at line 17 bypasses the unlock at line 37. A caller triggering this path leaves pool->lock held; subsequent locking attempts on the same pool block indefinitely, causing denial of service.

description: An issue was discovered in illumos before f859e7171bb5db34321e45585839c6c3200ebb90, OmniOS Community Edition r151038, OpenIndiana Hipster 2021.04, and SmartOS 20210923. A local unprivileged user can cause a deadlock and kernel panic via crafted rename and rmdir calls on tmpfs filesystems. Oracle Solaris 10 and 11 is also affected.

code_evidence: For DE_LINK/DE_RENAME, the function takes tp->tn_rwlock while dir->tn_rwlock is already held (ASSERT at line 18), establishing a TARGET-then-SOURCE lock order.
The SOURCE lock is acquired unconditionally via rw_enter and released only after nlink checks; there is no ordering constraint or backoff.
The rename path then calls tdircheckpath(tp, dir, cred) after both locks are held, so a concurrent rmdir that locks SOURCE then TARGET can interleave with this TARGET-then-SOURCE acquisition.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-667 covers improper lock acquisition leading to unexpected resource state; here the missing constraint is a consistent lock ordering/backoff, directly causing an inducible deadlock. It is not a mere race on data (CWE-362) because the lock protocol itself is violated.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: two lock acquisition orders coexist for the same tmpnode lock pair, because tdirenter holds dir->tn_rwlock (TARGET) and then blocks on tp->tn_rwlock (SOURCE) while a concurrent rmdir holds SOURCE and waits for TARGET. Trigger: unprivileged rename/rmdir on tmpfs with a parent/child relation. Consequence: deadlock and kernel panic (DoS).

commit_msg: MAINT: Fix use-after-free in Py_FindObjects
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        Py_XDECREF(result);'], 'added_lines': []}
description: A use-after-free issue was discovered in Py_FindObjects() function in SciPy versions prior to 1.8.0. NOTE: the vendor and discoverer indicate that this is not a security issue.

code_evidence: Line 68 increments result's refcount before the exit label, so the exit block at line 71 drops that reference with Py_XDECREF(result), leaving result pointing to an object whose reference count no longer accounts for the local pointer.
The error branch at lines 77-79 then calls Py_XDECREF(result) a second time on the same pointer before returning NULL, freeing the object again.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function frees the same object through the result pointer twice, and the second Py_XDECREF dereferences memory already released, matching CWE-416's reuse of freed memory. This is distinct from a simple leak: the pointer is not nulled after the first decref, so the stale reference is reused.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: result is decref'd in the shared exit cleanup (line 71) and then decref'd again in the PyErr_Occurred() branch (line 78) without being set to NULL in between. Trigger: any error path reaching the exit label, e.g. allocation failure in the loop. Consequence: a double free / use-after-free of the result object's memory, which can corrupt the heap or crash.
