commit_msg: X3F parser possible buffer overrun
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t  utf2char(P[i].name,name);', '\t\t\t  utf2char(P[i].value,value);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t  utf2char(P[i].name,name,sizeof(name));', '\t\t\t  utf2char(P[i].value,value,sizeof(value));']}
description: An issue was discovered in LibRaw 0.18.9. There is a stack-based buffer overflow in the utf2char function in libraw_cxx.cpp.

code_evidence: Fixed-size stack buffers name[100] and value[100] are declared, then passed to utf2char without any length argument. utf2char writes the converted P[i].name/P[i].value strings into these buffers with no bound, so an over-long property string from the X3F file overflows the stack arrays.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes attacker-controlled data past the end of the name/value stack buffers, directly matching CWE-787 (out-of-bounds write). This is a stack buffer overflow; the write beyond the intended buffer is the core issue, distinct from merely reading out of bounds.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is the missing size constraint: the property strings P[i].name and P[i].value come from parsed X3F data and are copied by utf2char into 100-byte stack arrays without a length limit. A crafted file with a long property name/value triggers a stack-based out-of-bounds write, corrupting adjacent stack memory and potentially enabling code execution or a crash.

commit_msg:
Fix assignment lookahead in parser_process_group_expression

This patch fixes #3815 and fixes #3819.

JerryScript-DCO-1.0-Signed-off-by: Robert Fancsik frobert@inf.u-szeged.hu
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['static bool', '  if (context_p->token.type == LEXER_ASSIGN)', '    uint32_t flags = 0;', '#if ENABLED (JERRY_ES2015)', '    if (JERRY_UNLIKELY (token == LEXER_LEFT_PAREN))', '    {', '      flags = PARSER_PATTERN_GROUP_EXPR;', '    }', '    parser_append_binary_single_assignment_token (context_p, flags);', '    lexer_next_token (context_p);', '    return true;', '  }', '  return false;'], 'added_lines': ['static void', '#if ENABLED (JERRY_ES2015)', "  /* Lookahead for anonymous function declaration after '=' token when the assignment base is LHS expression", '     with a single indentifier in it. e.g.: (a) = function () {} */', '  if (JERRY_UNLIKELY (context_p->token.type == LEXER_ASSIGN', '                      && PARSER_IS_PUSH_LITERALS_WITH_THIS (context_p->last_cbc_opcode)', '                      && context_p->last_cbc.literal_type == LEXER_IDENT_LITERAL))', '    parser_stack_push_uint8 (context_p, LEXER_ASSIGN_GROUP_EXPR);', '  }']}
description: There is an Assertion 'context_p->stack_top_uint8 == LEXER_EXPRESSION_START' at js-parser-expr.c:3565 in parser_parse_expression in JerryScript 2.2.0.

code_evidence: After popping the group stack and advancing the lexer, the function checks whether the next token is LEXER_ASSIGN and, if so, appends a binary assignment token and consumes the token again. The assignment handling is gated only on the token type and the prior popped stack entry (token == LEXER_LEFT_PAREN), without the LHS/identifier lookahead constraint added in the patch.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function's unchecked assignment lookahead allows attacker-supplied JavaScript to reach a parser assert that aborts execution, matching CWE-617 (Reachable Assertion). This is not merely a logic error because the observable impact is an application exit triggered by crafted input; the root cause is the missing assignment-base lookahead constraint.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The parser pops its grouping stack and then treats any '=' following a group expression as a binary assignment, appending an assignment token and pushing/consuming lexer state. Because the stack was already popped and no check ensures the expression base is a single identifier literal, malformed parenthesized assignment input drives the parser into a stack state that violates the LEXER_EXPRESSION_START invariant, hitting the assertion at js-parser-expr.c:3565. The consequence is a reachable assertion and parser crash (denial of service).

commit_msg:
nfc: nfcmrvl: main: reorder destructive operations in nfcmrvl_nci_unregister_dev to avoid bugs

There are destructive operations such as nfcmrvl_fw_dnld_abort and
gpio_free in nfcmrvl_nci_unregister_dev. The resources such as firmware,
gpio and so on could be destructed while the upper layer functions such as
nfcmrvl_fw_dnld_start and nfcmrvl_nci_recv_frame is executing, which leads
to double-free, use-after-free and null-ptr-deref bugs.

There are three situations that could lead to double-free bugs.

The first situation is shown below:

   (Thread 1)                 |      (Thread 2)
nfcmrvl_fw_dnld_start         |
 ...                          |  nfcmrvl_nci_unregister_dev
 release_firmware()           |   nfcmrvl_fw_dnld_abort
  kfree(fw) //(1)             |    fw_dnld_over
                              |     release_firmware
  ...                         |      kfree(fw) //(2)
                              |     ...

The second situation is shown below:

   (Thread 1)                 |      (Thread 2)
nfcmrvl_fw_dnld_start         |
 ...                          |
 mod_timer                    |
 (wait a time)                |
 fw_dnld_timeout              |  nfcmrvl_nci_unregister_dev
   fw_dnld_over               |   nfcmrvl_fw_dnld_abort
    release_firmware          |    fw_dnld_over
     kfree(fw) //(1)          |     release_firmware
     ...                      |      kfree(fw) //(2)

The third situation is shown below:

       (Thread 1)               |       (Thread 2)
nfcmrvl_nci_recv_frame          |
 if(..->fw_download_in_progress)|
  nfcmrvl_fw_dnld_recv_frame    |
   queue_work                   |
                                |
fw_dnld_rx_work                 | nfcmrvl_nci_unregister_dev
 fw_dnld_over                   |  nfcmrvl_fw_dnld_abort
  release_firmware              |   fw_dnld_over
   kfree(fw) //(1)              |    release_firmware
                                |     kfree(fw) //(2)

The firmware struct is deallocated in position (1) and deallocated
in position (2) again.

The crash trace triggered by POC is like below:

BUG: KASAN: double-free or invalid-free in fw_dnld_over
Call Trace:
  kfree
  fw_dnld_over
  nfcmrvl_nci_unregister_dev
  nci_uart_tty_close
  tty_ldisc_kill
  tty_ldisc_hangup
  __tty_hangup.part.0
  tty_release
  ...

What's more, there are also use-after-free and null-ptr-deref bugs
in nfcmrvl_fw_dnld_start. If we deallocate firmware struct, gpio or
set null to the members of priv->fw_dnld in nfcmrvl_nci_unregister_dev,
then, we dereference firmware, gpio or the members of priv->fw_dnld in
nfcmrvl_fw_dnld_start, the UAF or NPD bugs will happen.

This patch reorders destructive operations after nci_unregister_device
in order to synchronize between cleanup routine and firmware download
routine.

The nci_unregister_device is well synchronized. If the device is
detaching, the firmware download routine will goto error. If firmware
download routine is executing, nci_unregister_device will wait until
firmware download routine is finished.

Fixes: 3194c6870158 ("NFC: nfcmrvl: add firmware download support")
Signed-off-by: Duoming Zhou <duoming@zju.edu.cn>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tnci_unregister_device(ndev);'], 'added_lines': ['\tnci_unregister_device(ndev);']}
description: A flaw in Linux Kernel found in nfcmrvl_nci_unregister_dev() in drivers/nfc/nfcmrvl/main.c can lead to use after free both read or write when non synchronized between cleanup routine and firmware download routine.

code_evidence: Before the fix the function dereferences priv->ndev->nfc_dev->fw_download_in_progress and calls nfcmrvl_fw_dnld_abort/deinit, then frees reset_n_io, all before nci_unregister_device(ndev). The firmware-download path (e.g. nfcmrvl_fw_dnld_start, fw_dnld_timeout, fw_dnld_rx_work) can concurrently run fw_dnld_over and release_firmware. Because teardown frees firmware/gpio state before the device is unregistered and synchronized, a concurrent download routine can still reference those freed objects.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function's ordering allows memory owned by the firmware-download path to be freed and then referenced by a concurrent routine, which is the definition of CWE-416. The double-free is a related outcome, but the supported weakness here is reuse of freed memory.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: destructive cleanup (fw_dnld_abort/deinit and gpio_free) runs before nci_unregister_device, so it is not synchronized with the firmware download routine. Trigger: a firmware download or its timer/work runs while nfcmrvl_nci_unregister_dev executes. Consequence: the download path dereferences freed firmware/gpio/priv->fw_dnld state, giving use-after-free reads/writes (and related double-free).

commit_msg:
If the device node of dvb_ca_en50221 is open() and the
device is disconnected, a UAF may occur when calling
close() on the device node.

The root cause is that wake_up() and wait_event() for
dvbdev->wait_queue are not implemented.

So implement wait_event() function in dvb_ca_en50221_release()
and add 'remove_mutex' which prevents race condition
for 'ca->exit'.

[mchehab: fix a checkpatch warning]

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/linux-media/20221121063308.GA33821@ubuntu
Signed-off-by: Hyunwoo Kim <v4bel@theori.io>
Signed-off-by: Mauro Carvalho Chehab <mchehab@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tmutex_init(&ca->remove_mutex);']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel through 6.0.10. In drivers/media/dvb-core/dvb_ca_en50221.c, a use-after-free can occur is there is a disconnect after an open, because of the lack of a wait_event.

code_evidence: The function allocates ca with kzalloc, stores it in pubca->private, and registers a device that exposes ca to user space via dvb_register_device; after that, ca can be retained by an open() file descriptor.

mutex_init(&ca->ioctl_mutex) and the signal_pending check run only after registration; the patch adds mutex_init(&ca->remove_mutex) here, but this function itself performs no wait_event and no synchronization against release.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the object ca is freed on release while a still-referencing close path may access it, i.e., memory is reused after being freed. The missing wait_event/remove_mutex coordination is the cause; the dangling access is the use-after-free, not merely a race condition (CWE-362).
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: initialization registers the device (publishing ca) before release-side synchronization exists, and the init function never waits for an in-flight release; if the device node is open()ed and then disconnected, release can free ca while another close path still references it. Trigger: open followed by disconnect/close. Supported consequence: use-after-free of the dvb_ca_private object (crash/DoS, potential memory corruption).

commit_msg:
Fixed Error() instance dumping when "name" prop is not primitive.

Previously, njs_error_to_string2() might be invoked with error argument
pointing to vm->retval.  When "name" prop was not primitive vm->retval
might be overwritten.  As a result error pointer might be referencing a
primitive value.  In turn the second call of njs_object_property()
received an invalid object pointer because it expects only object value
types.

The fix is to ensure that error object pointer is never overwritten.

This closes #615 issue on Github.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    njs_object_property_init(&lhq, &to_json_string, NJS_TO_JSON_HASH);', '    ret = njs_object_property(vm, value, &lhq, &retval);', '    if (njs_slow_path(ret == NJS_ERROR)) {', '        return NULL;', '    return njs_is_function(&retval) ? njs_function(&retval) : NULL;'], 'added_lines': ['    if (njs_is_object(value)) {', '        njs_object_property_init(&lhq, &to_json_string, NJS_TO_JSON_HASH);', '        ret = njs_object_property(vm, njs_object(value), &lhq, &retval);', '        if (njs_slow_path(ret == NJS_ERROR)) {', '            return NULL;', '        }', '', '        return njs_is_function(&retval) ? njs_function(&retval) : NULL;', '    return NULL;']}
description: Nginx NJS v0.7.10 was discovered to contain a segmentation violation via the function njs_lvlhsh_find at src/njs_lvlhsh.c.

code_evidence: njs_object_property_init and njs_object_property are called on value without checking that value is an object; njs_object_property/njs_lvlhsh_find expects an object value and dereferences it. The result of njs_object_property is only checked for NJS_ERROR; the returned function is then extracted from retval.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing njs_is_object guard causes an invalid object pointer to be dereferenced, and the resulting invalid memory read in njs_lvlhsh_find is exactly an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). The later check of ret only handles NJS_ERROR and does not prevent the bad dereference.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function passes a non-object value (e.g. a primitive such as the overwritten vm->retval) into njs_object_property, which reaches njs_lvlhsh_find and interprets the value as an object pointer. Trigger: callers reach this helper when the error's "name" property is non-primitive, leaving value pointing at a primitive. Consequence: njs_lvlhsh_find reads memory out of bounds, causing the segmentation violation reported.

commit_msg:
Fix tvbparse recursion limit check.

When doing recursion check we must also count down when done.

Bug: 14253
Change-Id: Icacc86e8b25e106e151117dbcc2f132b1bbe898e
Reviewed-on: https://code.wireshark.org/review/25226
Petri-Dish: Stig Bjørlykke <stig@bjorlykke.org>
Tested-by: Petri Dish Buildbot
Reviewed-by: Gerald Combs <gerald@wireshark.org>
(cherry picked from commit c51560985a43592a79c29baba4f79f399a8e15dd)
Reviewed-on: https://code.wireshark.org/review/25228
Petri-Dish: Gerald Combs <gerald@wireshark.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '    tt->recursion_depth--;']}
description: In Wireshark 2.4.0 to 2.4.3 and 2.2.0 to 2.2.11, the JSON, XML, NTP, XMPP, and GDB dissectors could crash. This was addressed in epan/tvbparse.c by limiting the recursion depth.

code_evidence: Line 10 increments tt->recursion_depth and returns -1 on exceeding TVBPARSE_MAX_RECURSION_DEPTH, but the increment is never undone before returning.
The do/while loop at lines 12-14 recursively invokes the subelement's condition, which can re-enter cond_until without any decrement of the shared recursion counter.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing decrement causes the recursion guard to fail, enabling unbounded recursion leading to stack/memory corruption and a crash, which matches CWE-119's out-of-bounds memory operations. The root cause is the unbalanced counter, but the supported consequence is memory-buffer violation via stack exhaustion.

evidence_lines.code:
if (++tt->recursion_depth > TVBPARSE_MAX_RECURSION_DEPTH)
return -1;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The recursion counter is incremented on entry but never decremented on the early-return path or after the loop completes, so the depth budget is consumed permanently. Repeated parsing reuses the same tvbparse_t, letting the counter drift until recursion is falsely exhausted or, conversely, the guard no longer bounds actual stack depth, allowing unbounded recursion that can overflow the stack and crash.

commit_msg:
mapLen = (code + 256) & ~255; can wrap and you end up with mapLen < code
that is not what you wanted
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    map = (Unicode *)greallocn(map, mapLen, sizeof(Unicode));', '    for (i = oldLen; i < mapLen; ++i) {', '      map[i] = 0;', '    }'], 'added_lines': ['    if (unlikely(code >= mapLen)) {', '      error(-1, "Illegal code value in CharCodeToUnicode::addMapping");', '      return;', '    } else {', '      map = (Unicode *)greallocn(map, mapLen, sizeof(Unicode));', '      for (i = oldLen; i < mapLen; ++i) {', '        map[i] = 0;', '      }', '\t}']}
description: An integer overflow condition in poppler before 0.16.3 can occur when parsing CharCodes for fonts.

code_evidence: Line 9 computes mapLen = (code + 256) & ~255; if code is near the maximum CharCode value, code + 256 wraps around to a small value, so the rounded mapLen can be less than code. Line 10 then calls greallocn with this wrapped mapLen, and the zero-fill loop at lines 11-13 only covers oldLen..mapLen. Line 20 later writes map[code] = u + offset using the original code, which now exceeds the allocated mapLen.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the defect is an integer wraparound in the mapLen size calculation that is then used as an allocation size, leading to an undersized buffer and out-of-bounds write. It is distinct from an off-by-one error since the arithmetic itself wraps, not merely a boundary comparison.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the size computation (code + 256) & ~255 is performed without checking for integer wraparound before using the result as an allocation size. Trigger: a CharCode value close to the type's maximum causes mapLen to wrap to a small value. Consequence: greallocn allocates too little memory, and the subsequent map[code] store writes out of bounds, corrupting memory or crashing.

commit_msg:
(uid_t) -1 is still used as placeholder to mean "unset". This is OK, since
there should be no users with such number, see
https://systemd.io/UIDS-GIDS#special-linux-uids.

(uid_t) -1 is used as the default value in class initialization.

When a user or group above INT32_MAX is created, the numeric uid or
gid wraps around to negative when the value is assigned to gint, and
polkit gets confused. Let's accept such gids, except for -1.

A nicer fix would be to change the underlying type to e.g. uint32 to
not have negative values. But this cannot be done without breaking the
API, so likely new functions will have to be added (a
polkit_unix_user_new variant that takes a unsigned, and the same for
_group_new, _set_uid, _get_uid, _set_gid, _get_gid, etc.). This will
require a bigger patch.

Fixes https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/polkit/polkit/issues/74.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      unix_user->uid = g_value_get_int (value);'], 'added_lines': ['  gint val;', '      val = g_value_get_int (value);', '      g_return_if_fail (val != -1);', '      unix_user->uid = val;']}
description: A flaw was found in PolicyKit (aka polkit) 0.115 that allows a user with a uid greater than INT_MAX to successfully execute any systemctl command.

code_evidence: In the PROP_UID case, the property value is read via g_value_get_int (line 11) and assigned directly to unix_user->uid with no check that the value is a usable UID. The function never inspects the value for validity before storing it, so any integer (including a wrapped negative representation of a UID above INT32_MAX) becomes the object's uid.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-20 fits because the function receives an input value and fails to validate that it has the properties (non-negative, non-placeholder UID) required for safe processing. The patch adds exactly such a check, confirming the pre-patch code lacked input validation rather than a transformation or encoding defect.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the setter performs no validation of the incoming integer UID before assigning it to unix_user->uid. A caller supplying a value whose gint form is negative (large uid wrapping through g_value_get_int) is accepted, producing a confused uid that downstream authorization logic misinterprets, enabling privilege bypass. The consequence stems from the missing constraint, not from the assignment itself.

commit_msg:
mwifiex: Fix three heap overflow at parsing element in cfg80211_ap_settings

mwifiex_update_vs_ie(),mwifiex_set_uap_rates() and
mwifiex_set_wmm_params() call memcpy() without checking
the destination size.Since the source is given from
user-space, this may trigger a heap buffer overflow.

Fix them by putting the length check before performing memcpy().

This fix addresses CVE-2019-14814,CVE-2019-14815,CVE-2019-14816.

Signed-off-by: Wen Huang <huangwenabc@gmail.com>
Acked-by: Ganapathi Bhat <gbhat@marvell.comg>
Signed-off-by: Kalle Valo <kvalo@codeaurora.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (rate_ie)'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (rate_ie->len > MWIFIEX_SUPPORTED_RATES)', '\t\t\treturn;', '\tif (rate_ie) {', '\t\tif (rate_ie->len > MWIFIEX_SUPPORTED_RATES - rate_len)', '\t\t\treturn;', '\t}']}
description: There is heap-based buffer overflow in kernel, all versions up to, excluding 5.3, in the marvell wifi chip driver in Linux kernel, that allows local users to cause a denial of service(system crash) or possibly execute arbitrary code.

code_evidence: cfg80211_find_ie locates an attacker-controlled rate IE in the beacon head; rate_ie->len is copied into bss_cfg->rates with no check against the destination capacity.
A second IE from the beacon tail is located and copied to bss_cfg->rates + rate_len, again without bounding rate_ie->len against the remaining space.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked length-driven memcpy into a heap-allocated fixed-size buffer is a classic heap-based buffer overflow (CWE-122). It is not merely an out-of-bounds read, since the copy writes attacker-controlled data beyond the heap allocation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The destination bss_cfg->rates is a fixed-size heap-allocated array, but both memcpy calls use the IE length taken from user-supplied beacon data without validating it. A crafted rate IE with an oversized len causes a write past the heap buffer, leading to memory corruption, crash, or possible code execution.

commit_msg:
HID: cp2112: fix sleep-while-atomic

A recent commit fixing DMA-buffers on stack added a shared transfer
buffer protected by a spinlock. This is broken as the USB HID request
callbacks can sleep. Fix this up by replacing the spinlock with a mutex.

Fixes: 1ffb3c40ffb5 ("HID: cp2112: make transfer buffers DMA capable")
Cc: stable <stable@vger.kernel.org>	# 4.9
Signed-off-by: Johan Hovold <johan@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Benjamin Tissoires <benjamin.tissoires@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Jiri Kosina <jkosina@suse.cz>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tspin_lock_init(&dev->lock);'], 'added_lines': ['\tmutex_init(&dev->lock);']}
description: drivers/hid/hid-cp2112.c in the Linux kernel 4.9.x before 4.9.9 uses a spinlock without considering that sleeping is possible in a USB HID request callback, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (deadlock) via unspecified vectors.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function only initializes the lock with spin_lock_init; it contains no resource release/shutdown path, so it does not support CWE-404. The actual defect is calling a sleeping USB HID callback while holding a spinlock, which is a sleep-in-atomic/locking issue, not improper resource release.

commit_msg:
Strict KEX 対応 (CVE-2023-48795)

とりあえず Strict KEX のネゴシエーションとシーケンス番号のリセットに対応。
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\tif (pvar->server_strict_kex) {', '\t\tpvar->ssh_state.receiver_sequence_number = 0;', '\t}']}
description: The SSH transport protocol with certain OpenSSH extensions, found in OpenSSH before 9.6 and other products, allows remote attackers to bypass integrity checks such that some packets are omitted (from the extension negotiation message), and a client and server may consequently end up with a connection for which some security features have been downgraded or disabled, aka a Terrapin attack. This occurs because the SSH Binary Packet Protocol (BPP), implemented by these extensions, mishandles the handshake phase and mishandles use of sequence numbers. For example, there is an effective attack against SSH's use of ChaCha20-Poly1305 (and CBC with Encrypt-then-MAC). The bypass occurs in chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com and (if CBC is used) the -etm@openssh.com MAC algorithms. This also affects Maverick Synergy Java SSH API before 3.1.0-SNAPSHOT, Dropbear through 2022.83, Ssh before 5.1.1 in Erlang/OTP, PuTTY before 0.80, AsyncSSH before 2.14.2, golang.org/x/crypto before 0.17.0, libssh before 0.10.6, libssh2 through 1.11.0, Thorn Tech SFTP Gateway before 3.4.6, Tera Term before 5.1, Paramiko before 3.4.0, jsch before 0.2.15, SFTPGo before 2.5.6, Netgate pfSense Plus through 23.09.1, Netgate pfSense CE through 2.7.2, HPN-SSH through 18.2.0, ProFTPD before 1.3.8b (and before 1.3.9rc2), ORYX CycloneSSH before 2.3.4, NetSarang XShell 7 before Build 0144, CrushFTP before 10.6.0, ConnectBot SSH library before 2.2.22, Apache MINA sshd through 2.11.0, sshj through 0.37.0, TinySSH through 20230101, trilead-ssh2 6401, LANCOM LCOS and LANconfig, FileZilla before 3.66.4, Nova before 11.8, PKIX-SSH before 14.4, SecureCRT before 9.4.3, Transmit5 before 5.10.4, Win32-OpenSSH before 9.5.0.0p1-Beta, WinSCP before 6.2.2, Bitvise SSH Server before 9.32, Bitvise SSH Client before 9.33, KiTTY through 0.76.1.13, the net-ssh gem 7.2.0 for Ruby, the mscdex ssh2 module before 1.15.0 for Node.js, the thrussh library before 0.35.1 for Rust, and the Russh crate before 0.40.2 for Rust.

code_evidence: After receiving NEWKEYS, ssh2_set_newkeys(pvar, MODE_IN) installs the inbound keys and CRYPT_start_encryption switches the receive path to the negotiated MAC/cipher; lines 12-14 then enable MAC and compression. The function never resets or tracks the inbound packet sequence number, so the MAC input sequence continues across the key exchange.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-354 fits because the MAC/integrity check is computed over a sequence-number context that the function fails to re-establish at NEWKEYS, so the received integrity value does not validate the full handshake transcript. This is distinct from a weak MAC algorithm; the defect is missing sequence-state validation, not algorithm strength.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the inbound sequence number used as MAC input is not re-initialized at NEWKEYS on the receive side, so a peer can influence which packets precede the encrypted phase and thereby which packets the MAC covers. Trigger: a handshake where extension/negotiation messages are manipulated before or during key exchange. Supported consequence: the integrity check does not bind the omitted negotiation data, permitting undetected packet omission and feature downgrade (Terrapin).

commit_msg: Fixed memory leak reported in #456.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      ThrowReaderException(CorruptImageError,"UnableToReadImageData");'], 'added_lines': ['      {', '        quantum_info=DestroyQuantumInfo(quantum_info);', '        ThrowReaderException(CorruptImageError,"UnableToReadImageData");', '      }']}
description: In ImageMagick 7.0.5-5, the ReadARTImage function in coders/art.c allows attackers to cause a denial of service (memory leak) via a crafted .art file.

code_evidence: Line 47 allocates quantum_info via AcquireQuantumInfo; if allocation fails, line 49 throws without needing cleanup.

Lines 58-59 read pixel data into the quantum buffer; line 60 checks whether the read count matches length, and line 61 throws CorruptImageError without first destroying quantum_info. The normal path frees it at line 72, but this early-exit path skips that release.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-772 fits because a resource whose lifetime effectively ends at the error exit is never released; the leak is a missing release, not a buffer over-read or use-after-free. The same commit's added DestroyQuantumInfo call confirms the intended cleanup.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the error branch for a short blob read (count != length) exits via ThrowReaderException while quantum_info, allocated at line 47, is still live. Trigger: a crafted .art file whose pixel data ends before the requested length is available. Consequence: the QuantumInfo allocation is leaked on each failed read, supporting memory-consumption denial of service.

commit_msg:
opj_decompress: fix double-free on input directory with mix of valid and invalid images (CVE-2020-15389)

Fixes #1261

Credits to @Ruia-ruia for reporting and analysis.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    opj_image_t* image = NULL;', '    opj_stream_t *l_stream = NULL;              /* Stream */', '    opj_codec_t* l_codec = NULL;                /* Handle to a decompressor */', '    opj_codestream_index_t* cstr_index = NULL;'], 'added_lines': ['        opj_image_t* image = NULL;', '        opj_stream_t *l_stream = NULL;              /* Stream */', '        opj_codec_t* l_codec = NULL;                /* Handle to a decompressor */', '        opj_codestream_index_t* cstr_index = NULL;']}
description: jp2/opj_decompress.c in OpenJPEG through 2.3.1 has a use-after-free that can be triggered if there is a mix of valid and invalid files in a directory operated on by the decompressor. Triggering a double-free may also be possible. This is related to calling opj_image_destroy twice.

code_evidence: image, l_stream, l_codec and cstr_index are declared once at function scope (lines 4-7), so they persist across loop iterations.
The loop over num_images (line 59) reuses these variables; on a skipped file (lines 64-68) the code continues without resetting image, leaving a stale pointer from a prior iteration.
On the upsample failure path (lines 256-262) opj_destroy_codec is called and control jumps to fin without destroying image, so image remains dangling.
On the force_rgb failure path (lines 275-276) opj_image_destroy(image) frees the image and sets it to NULL, but a later iteration may still reference the prior value.
At normal loop end line 367 unconditionally calls opj_image_destroy(image) and line 368 opj_destroy_cstr_index, which can free an already-freed or reused pointer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the same image pointer is reused and passed to opj_image_destroy after its referent may already have been freed on an earlier iteration's error or continue path, so the program dereferences or frees memory no longer owned by it. This is a use-after-free, not merely a resource leak.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the image, codec and stream handles are allocated per-iteration but declared once outside the loop, so error/continue paths leave stale pointers that a subsequent iteration or the loop-exit cleanup frees again. Trigger: a directory mixing valid and invalid images causes an early continue or goto fin while image still holds a prior allocation, then line 367 frees it. Consequence: use-after-free/double-free of the opj_image_t, leading to crash or potential memory corruption.

      [<000000009456679f>] entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x63/0xcd

We can reproduce this issue by creating two AF_UNIX SOCK_STREAM sockets,
send()ing an OOB skb to each other, and close()ing them without consuming
the OOB skbs.

  int skpair[2];

  socketpair(AF_UNIX, SOCK_STREAM, 0, skpair);

  send(skpair[0], "x", 1, MSG_OOB);
  send(skpair[1], "x", 1, MSG_OOB);

  close(skpair[0]);
  close(skpair[1]);

Currently, we free an OOB skb in unix_sock_destructor() which is called via
__sk_free(), but it's too late because the receiver's unix_sk(sk)->oob_skb
is accounted against the sender's sk->sk_wmem_alloc and __sk_free() is
called only when sk->sk_wmem_alloc is 0.

In the repro sequences, we do not consume the OOB skb, so both two sk's
sock_put() never reach __sk_free() due to the positive sk->sk_wmem_alloc.
Then, no one can consume the OOB skb nor call __sk_free(), and we finally
leak the two whole sk.

Thus, we must free the unconsumed OOB skb earlier when close()ing the
socket.

Fixes: 314001f0bf92 ("af_unix: Add OOB support")
Reported-by: syzbot <syzkaller@googlegroups.com>
Signed-off-by: Kuniyuki Iwashima <kuniyu@amazon.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

description: A vulnerability, which was classified as problematic, has been found in Linux Kernel. This issue affects the function unix_sock_destructor/unix_release_sock of the file net/unix/af_unix.c of the component BPF. The manipulation leads to memory leak. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue. The associated identifier of this vulnerability is VDB-211043.

code_evidence: unix_sock_destructor() purges only sk_receive_queue (line 4) and, under CONFIG_AF_UNIX_OOB, frees u->oob_skb and clears the pointer (lines 5-10). This destructor runs only via __sk_free(), which is reached only when sk_wmem_alloc drops to zero.

Line 11 asserts refcount_read(&sk->sk_wmem_alloc) is zero, confirming the destructor assumes the OOB skb's accounted memory has already been released; the OOB cleanup at lines 6-9 is therefore too late to break the accounting cycle.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function directly embodies the leak: it is the sole release site for oob_skb yet is gated behind the very allocation accounting that the OOB skb keeps positive, so memory is never released after its effective lifetime. This is missing release of allocated memory (CWE-401), not a use-after-free or double-free.

evidence_lines.code: DEBUG_NET_WARN_ON_ONCE(refcount_read(&sk->sk_wmem_alloc));

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The receiver's oob_skb is charged against the sender's sk_wmem_alloc, and the only free path for oob_skb is inside unix_sock_destructor(), which itself requires sk_wmem_alloc to reach zero. If an OOB skb is never consumed before close(), the refcount stays positive, __sk_free() is never invoked, and the whole struct sock plus oob_skb leak.

commit_msg:
x86/fpu/xsaves: Fix improper uses of __ex_table

Commit:

  f31a9f7c7169 ("x86/xsaves: Use xsaves/xrstors to save and restore xsave area")

introduced alternative instructions for XSAVES/XRSTORS and commit:

  adb9d526e982 ("x86/xsaves: Add xsaves and xrstors support for booting time")

added support for the XSAVES/XRSTORS instructions at boot time.

Unfortunately both failed to properly protect them against faulting:

The 'xstate_fault' macro will use the closest label named '1'
backward and that ends up in the .altinstr_replacement section
rather than in .text. This means that the kernel will never find
in the __ex_table the .text address where this instruction might
fault, leading to serious problems if userspace manages to
trigger the fault.

Signed-off-by: Quentin Casasnovas <quentin.casasnovas@oracle.com>
Signed-off-by: Jamie Iles <jamie.iles@oracle.com>
[ Improved the changelog, fixed some whitespace noise. ]
Acked-by: Borislav Petkov <bp@alien8.de>
Acked-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Cc: Allan Xavier <mr.a.xavier@gmail.com>
Cc: H. Peter Anvin <hpa@zytor.com>
Cc: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
Fixes: adb9d526e982 ("x86/xsaves: Add xsaves and xrstors support for booting time")
Fixes: f31a9f7c7169 ("x86/xsaves: Use xsaves/xrstors to save and restore xsave area")
Signed-off-by: Ingo Molnar <mingo@kernel.org>

-			: : "D" (fx), "m" (*fx), "a" (lmask), "d" (hmask)
+			     xstate_fault

commit_msg:
It is possible to trigger heap overflows due to an integer overflow
while parsing images and a signedness issue while parsing comments.

The integer overflow occurs because the chosen limit 0x10000 for
dimensions is too large for 32 bit systems, because each pixel takes
4 bytes. Properly chosen values allow an overflow which in turn will
lead to less allocated memory than needed for subsequent reads.

The signedness bug is triggered by reading the length of a comment
as unsigned int, but casting it to int when calling the function
XcursorCommentCreate. Turning length into a negative value allows the
check against XCURSOR_COMMENT_MAX_LEN to pass, and the following
addition of sizeof (XcursorComment) + 1 makes it possible to allocate
less memory than needed for subsequent reads.

Signed-off-by: Tobias Stoeckmann <tobias@stoeckmann.org>
Reviewed-by: Matthieu Herrb <matthieu@herrb.eu>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if (length > XCURSOR_COMMENT_MAX_LEN)'], 'added_lines': ['    if (length < 0 || length > XCURSOR_COMMENT_MAX_LEN)']}
description: libXcursor before 1.1.15 has various integer overflows that could lead to heap buffer overflows when processing malicious cursors, e.g., with programs like GIMP. It is also possible that an attack vector exists against the related code in cursor/xcursor.c in Wayland through 1.14.0.

code_evidence: Line 5 checks only length > XCURSOR_COMMENT_MAX_LEN, so a negative signed int length passes the guard and returns nothing at line 6.
Line 7 computes malloc(sizeof(XcursorComment) + length + 1); with negative length this arithmetic yields a small allocation, and the pointer is later used as a buffer for comment data.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The size computation at line 7 relies on arithmetic that can wrap when length is negative, producing an undersized allocation; this is an integer overflow/wraparound used for memory sizing. It is not merely a missing input-validation issue, since the guard exists but fails to constrain the sign of the operand feeding the size calculation.

evidence_lines.code:
if (length > XCURSOR_COMMENT_MAX_LEN)
return NULL;
comment = malloc (sizeof (XcursorComment) + length + 1);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the length validation omits a lower-bound check on the signed int, so negative values bypass the maximum-length guard. Trigger: a caller passes a negative length derived from an unsigned comment length cast to int. The addition in the malloc size expression then wraps to a small value, allocating less memory than subsequent reads expect, enabling a heap buffer overflow.

The second loop walks the same input string and writes atoi(cp) into (*array)[t++] for each field, with no upper bound check on the parsed value and no re-validation that the number of written fields matches the allocated valcount.

commit_msg:
i2c: fix stack buffer overflow vulnerability in i2c md command

When running "i2c md 0 0 80000100", the function do_i2c_md parses the
length into an unsigned int variable named length. The value is then
moved to a signed variable:

    int nbytes = length;
    #define DISP_LINE_LEN 16
    int linebytes = (nbytes > DISP_LINE_LEN) ? DISP_LINE_LEN : nbytes;
    ret = dm_i2c_read(dev, addr, linebuf, linebytes);

On systems where integers are 32 bits wide, 0x80000100 is a negative
value to "nbytes > DISP_LINE_LEN" is false and linebytes gets assigned
0x80000100 instead of 16.

The consequence is that the function which reads from the i2c device
(dm_i2c_read or i2c_read) is called with a 16-byte stack buffer to fill
but with a size parameter which is too large. In some cases, this could
trigger a crash. But with some i2c drivers, such as drivers/i2c/nx_i2c.c
(used with "nexell,s5pxx18-i2c" bus), the size is actually truncated to
a 16-bit integer. This is because function i2c_transfer expects an
unsigned short length. In such a case, an attacker who can control the
response of an i2c device can overwrite the return address of a function
and execute arbitrary code through Return-Oriented Programming.

Fix this issue by using unsigned integers types in do_i2c_md. While at
it, make also alen unsigned, as signed sizes can cause vulnerabilities
when people forgot to check that they can be negative.

Signed-off-by: Nicolas Iooss <nicolas.iooss+uboot@ledger.fr>
Reviewed-by: Heiko Schocher <hs@denx.de>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tint alen;'], 'added_lines': ['\tuint\talen;']}
description: In Das U-Boot through 2022.07-rc5, an integer signedness error and resultant stack-based buffer overflow in the "i2c md" command enables the corruption of the return address pointer of the do_i2c_md function.

code_evidence: Line 8 declares a fixed 16-byte stack buffer bytes[16]. Line 5 declares alen as signed int; line 18 assigns get_alen() to it, and line 19 checks only alen > 3, so a negative value such as -1 passes. Lines 28-29 read length from argv[3] into unsigned length, and lines 30-31 clamp it to sizeof(bytes). Line 37 calls dm_i2c_read(dev, addr, bytes, length), and line 39 calls i2c_read(chip, addr, alen, bytes, length), passing the buffer with the length.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the function passes a negative, unvalidated alen-derived size to the read routine while the destination is the fixed 16-byte stack buffer bytes, causing a write past the buffer end. The root cause is the missing lower-bound check on the signed alen at line 19, not merely the unsigned length clamp.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The signed alen is only checked for being greater than 3, so a negative offset length (e.g. -1) passes the guard and is passed to i2c_set_chip_offset_len and i2c_read as a size/offset argument; the length clamp at lines 30-31 does not cover alen. The trigger is a crafted negative address-length argument to the i2c command, and the supported consequence is an out-of-bounds write into the 16-byte stack buffer bytes, corrupting the return address and enabling code execution.

commit_msg:
[PATCH] arm: fix handling of F_OFD_... in oabi_fcntl64()

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # 3.15+
Reviewed-by: Jeff Layton <jeff.layton@primarydata.com>
Signed-off-by: Al Viro <viro@zeniv.linux.org.uk>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tstruct oabi_flock64 user;', '\tstruct flock64 kernel;', '\tmm_segment_t fs = USER_DS; /* initialized to kill a warning */', '\tunsigned long local_arg = arg;', '\tint ret;', '', '\t\tif (copy_from_user(&user, (struct oabi_flock64 __user *)arg,', '\t\t\t\t   sizeof(user)))', '\t\t\treturn -EFAULT;', '\t\tkernel.l_type\t= user.l_type;', '\t\tkernel.l_whence\t= user.l_whence;', '\t\tkernel.l_start\t= user.l_start;', '\t\tkernel.l_len\t= user.l_len;', '\t\tkernel.l_pid\t= user.l_pid;', '\t\tlocal_arg = (unsigned long)&kernel;', '\t\tfs = get_fs();', '\t\tset_fs(KERNEL_DS);', '', '\tret = sys_fcntl64(fd, cmd, local_arg);', '', '\tswitch (cmd) {', '\tcase F_GETLK64:', '\t\tif (!ret) {', '\t\t\tuser.l_type\t= kernel.l_type;', '\t\t\tuser.l_whence\t= kernel.l_whence;', '\t\t\tuser.l_start\t= kernel.l_start;', '\t\t\tuser.l_len\t= kernel.l_len;', '\t\t\tuser.l_pid\t= kernel.l_pid;', '\t\t\tif (copy_to_user((struct oabi_flock64 __user *)arg,', '\t\t\t\t\t &user, sizeof(user)))', '\t\t\t\tret = -EFAULT;', '\t\t}', '\tcase F_SETLK64:', '\tcase F_SETLKW64:', '\t\tset_fs(fs);', '\t}', '', '\treturn ret;'], 'added_lines': ['\t\treturn do_locks(fd, cmd, arg);', '', '\tdefault:', '\t\treturn sys_fcntl64(fd, cmd, arg);']}
description: arch/arm/kernel/sys_oabi-compat.c in the Linux kernel before 4.4 allows local users to gain privileges via a crafted (1) F_OFD_GETLK, (2) F_OFD_SETLK, or (3) F_OFD_SETLKW command in an fcntl64 system call.

code_evidence: The switch routes the F_OFD_* commands together with the legacy F_*LK64 commands into one shared handling path.
The handler copies a user-supplied oabi_flock64 into a local struct, then overwrites local_arg with the kernel pointer to `kernel` and raises the address limit via set_fs(KERNEL_DS).
sys_fcntl64 is then invoked with this kernel-space pointer as the lock argument, regardless of which command was requested.

Only F_GETLK64 copies results back and restores fs; F_OFD_GETLK, F_OFD_SETLK, F_OFD_SETLKW, F_SETLK64 and F_SETLKW64 fall through without restoring the segment, and the F_OFD_* commands never copy the kernel lock back to the user.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function mishandles a security-relevant access-control operation (file locking) for unprivileged callers by misrouting F_OFD_* commands into a kernel-pointer path, enabling local privilege gain; this is a permissions/access-control weakness consistent with CWE-264.

evidence_lines.code:
case F_OFD_GETLK:
case F_OFD_SETLK:
case F_OFD_SETLKW:
case F_GETLK64:
case F_SETLK64:
case F_SETLKW64:
ret = sys_fcntl64(fd, cmd, local_arg);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The root cause is conflating the OFD lock commands with the legacy 64-bit lock commands: OFD commands are dispatched with a kernel pointer while the user/kernel address limit is raised and are not handled symmetrically. Triggering an F_OFD_* fcntl64 leaves the address-limit override and lock bookkeeping in an inconsistent state, allowing the caller to influence privileged lock operations and resulting in privilege escalation.

to prevent a buffer overflow

Bug found using OSS-Fuze.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if (bottom > top) {new_chunk(); goto loop;}'], 'added_lines': ['    if (bottom > top) {check_size(size); new_chunk(); goto loop;}']}
description: objstack in GNU Aspell 0.60.8 has a heap-based buffer overflow in acommon::ObjStack::dup_top (called from acommon::StringMap::add and acommon::Config::lookup_list).

code_evidence: alloc_bottom advances bottom by size (line 5) and only compares the new bottom against top (line 6) before calling new_chunk; there is no check that size itself fits within a chunk. The caller receives tmp=bottom (line 4) and can write size bytes there, even when size exceeds the chunk capacity and the overflow check merely triggers a new chunk after the pointer was already advanced.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the missing size constraint allows data to be written past the end of the allocated chunk. This is a direct out-of-bounds write; the added check_size guard in the patch confirms the intended bound.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function accepts an arbitrary size and advances bottom without constraining size to the chunk capacity. Trigger: a large allocation request (e.g., via dup_top/StringMap::add) causes new_chunk/goto loop, but the write using the returned pointer exceeds the chunk. Consequence: heap-based out-of-bounds write past the intended buffer.

commit_msg:
Fix vtrnd pci_vtrnd_notify uninitialized memory use (GHSL-2021-056)

Signed-off-by: Frederic Dalleau <frederic.dalleau@docker.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tint len;', '\t\tvq_getchain(vq, &idx, &iov, 1, NULL);'], 'added_lines': ['\tint len, n;', '\t\tn = vq_getchain(vq, &idx, &iov, 1, NULL);', '\t\tif (n < 0) {', '\t\t\tfprintf(stderr, "vtrnd: vtrnd_notify(): n %d\\r\\n", n);', '\t\t\treturn;', '\t\t}']}
description: HyperKit is a toolkit for embedding hypervisor capabilities in an application. In versions 0.20210107 and prior of HyperKit, the implementation of `qnotify` at `pci_vtrnd_notify` fails to check the return value of `vq_getchain`. This leads to `struct iovec iov;` being uninitialized and used to read memory in `len = (int) read(sc->vrsc_fd, iov.iov_base, iov.iov_len);` when an attacker is able to make `vq_getchain` fail. This issue may lead to a guest crashing the host causing a denial of service and, under certain circumstance, memory corruption. This issue is fixed in commit 41272a980197917df8e58ff90642d14dec8fe948.

code_evidence: iov is declared uninitialized at line 4, and its address is passed to vq_getchain at line 14; the return value of vq_getchain is discarded.
Line 15 then reads sc->vrsc_fd into iov.iov_base with length iov.iov_len, which remain uninitialized/unset when vq_getchain fails.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The root cause is precisely the unchecked return value of vq_getchain (CWE-252): the missing error branch leaves iov uninitialized before use. The uninitialized-memory use is the downstream consequence; the fix adds the n<0 check, confirming the missing-return-value check is the weakness.

evidence_lines.code:
struct iovec iov;
int len;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: vq_getchain may fail (e.g., malformed descriptor chains from the guest) and return a negative value, but the code ignores it and proceeds to call read() with an uninitialized struct iovec. The trigger is a guest forcing vq_getchain to fail; the consequence is a read into an invalid/attacker-influenced base with an uninitialized length, causing host crash (DoS) and possible memory corruption.

commit_msg: Fix BZ #17269 -- _IO_wstr_overflow integer overflow

description: Integer overflow in the _IO_wstr_overflow function in libio/wstrops.c in the GNU C Library (aka glibc or libc6) before 2.22 allows context-dependent attackers to cause a denial of service (application crash) or possibly execute arbitrary code via vectors related to computing a size in bytes, which triggers a heap-based buffer overflow.

A large offset wraps newsize or the byte count to a small value, so the allocation is undersized while later pointer arithmetic and wmemset (lines 44-46) use the full offset, producing a heap-based buffer overflow.

commit_msg:
src/common.c: Fix heap buffer overflows when writing strings in binheader

Fixes the following problems:
 1. Case 's' only enlarges the buffer by 16 bytes instead of size bytes.
 2. psf_binheader_writef() enlarges the header buffer (if needed) prior to the
    big switch statement by an amount (16 bytes) which is enough for all cases
    where only a single value gets added. Cases 's', 'S', 'p' however
    additionally write an arbitrary length block of data and again enlarge the
    buffer to the required amount. However, the required space calculation does
    not take into account the size of the length field which gets output before
    the data.
 3. Buffer size requirement calculation in case 'S' does not account for the
    padding byte ("size += (size & 1) ;" happens after the calculation which
    uses "size").
 4. Case 'S' can overrun the header buffer by 1 byte when no padding is
    involved
    ("memcpy (&(psf->header.ptr [psf->header.indx]), strptr, size + 1) ;" while
    the buffer is only guaranteed to have "size" space available).
 5. "psf->header.ptr [psf->header.indx] = 0 ;" in case 'S' always writes 1 byte
    beyond the space which is guaranteed to be allocated in the header buffer.
 6. Case 's' can overrun the provided source string by 1 byte if padding is
    involved ("memcpy (&(psf->header.ptr [psf->header.indx]), strptr, size) ;"
    where "size" is "strlen (strptr) + 1" (which includes the 0 terminator,
    plus optionally another 1 which is padding and not guaranteed to be
    readable via the source string pointer).

Closes: https://github.com/erikd/libsndfile/issues/292

description: Heap-based Buffer Overflow in the psf_binheader_writef function in common.c in libsndfile through 1.0.28 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (application crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact.

code_evidence: Case 's' computes size = strlen(strptr)+1 then enlarges buffer only by a fixed 16 bytes (line 117) regardless of size, then memcpy's size bytes (line 123), so a long string overflows the header buffer.
Case 'S' checks indx+size against len (line 131) but then memcpy's size+1 bytes (line 137), writing one byte past the guaranteed allocation.

tls allows re-use when some cert validation settings have changed

description: Envoy is an open source edge and service proxy, designed for cloud-native applications. Envoy's tls allows re-use when some cert validation settings have changed from their default configuration. The only workaround for this issue is to ensure that default tls settings are used. Users are advised to upgrade.

code_evidence: The digest incorporates the CA certificate only when ca_cert_ is non-null; the guard skips any contribution when it is null, so the session-ID hash does not reflect the absence of a CA cert.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function computes the session-ID digest that governs whether certificate-validation settings are re-applied; because it fails to account for a validation-relevant state (absent CA cert), certificate validation is incorrectly applied on resumed sessions, matching CWE-295. This is not mere hashing weakness (CWE-328) since the defect is in certificate-validation coverage.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: updateDigestForSessionId builds the TLS session-resumption identifier from certificate-validation settings, but the ca_cert_ branch is conditional and omits the null case, so distinct validation configurations can hash identically. Trigger: a connection reusing a session ID while CA validation state differs from the original handshake. Consequence: TLS session reuse bypasses certificate validation, enabling authentication bypass.

commit_msg:
Fix heap-buffer-overflows when accessing pool

Constants are usually retrieved from the constant pool without verifying
that the pool actually contains them, which may lead to various heap
buffer overflow issues.

In this patch we add a counter keeping track of how many elements the pool
contains, and checks making sure that whenever the pool is accessed, the
constant in present in the pool (constant position < pool counter).

Also, do not return "" when a pointer is excepted (it should be legal to free
this return value).

This patch fixes #112 (CVE-2018-7875), fixes #120 (CVE-2018-7871),
fixes #117 (CVE-2018-7870), fixes #114 (CVE-2018-7872), fixes #122,
fixes #113 (CVE-2018-7868), fixes #123.

commit_msg:
KEYS: Remove key_type::match in favour of overriding default by match_preparse

A previous patch added a ->match_preparse() method to the key type.  This is
allowed to override the function called by the iteration algorithm.
Therefore, we can just set a default that simply checks for an exact match of
the key description with the original criterion data and allow match_preparse
to override it as needed.

The key_type::match op is then redundant and can be removed, as can the
user_match() function.

Signed-off-by: David Howells <dhowells@redhat.com>
Acked-by: Vivek Goyal <vgoyal@redhat.com>

--- func_before
+++ func_after
@@ -10,7 +10,7 @@
 		.index_key.type		= type,
 		.index_key.description	= description,
 		.cred			= current_cred(),
-		.match_data.cmp		= type->match,
+		.match_data.cmp		= key_default_cmp,
 		.match_data.raw_data	= description,
 		.match_data.lookup_type	= KEYRING_SEARCH_LOOKUP_DIRECT,
 	};
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t.match_data.cmp\t\t= type->match,'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t.match_data.cmp\t\t= key_default_cmp,']}
description: The KEYS subsystem in the Linux kernel before 3.18 allows local users to gain privileges or cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference and system crash) via vectors involving a NULL value for a certain match field, related to the keyring_search_iterator function in keyring.c.

Lines 23-29 only invoke match_preparse when present and check its return, but do not validate match_data.cmp before line 30 calls search_process_keyrings(&ctx), which uses the cmp callback during iteration.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function passes an unchecked possibly-NULL function pointer into the search path, and iteration dereferences it, matching CWE-476's NULL pointer dereference. This is not merely a missing return-value check; the defect is the unchecked pointer being consumed.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the search context's comparison callback is initialized from type->match without a NULL check, and match_preparse's optional override is not required to supply one. Trigger: a key type with a NULL match field reaches search_process_keyrings, which dereferences the NULL cmp function pointer. Supported consequence: kernel NULL pointer dereference and crash (DoS), with potential integrity/confidentiality impact from control-flow misuse.

The BACKGROUND disposal path computes row_start from s->last_frame->linesize[0] and writes bpp*width bytes at that offset in diffFrame, again without bounding against diffFrame's allocation.
The PREVIOUS disposal branch performs the same unbounded memcpy from s->prev_frame into diffFrame using prev_frame's linesize and height.

description: TensorFlow is an open source platform for machine learning. When `Unbatch` receives a nonscalar input `id`, it gives a `CHECK` fail that can trigger a denial of service attack. We have patched the issue in GitHub commit 4419d10d576adefa36b0e0a9425d2569f7c0189f. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.10.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.9.1, TensorFlow 2.8.1, and TensorFlow 2.7.2, as these are also affected and still in supported range. There are no known workarounds for this issue.

joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-617 fits because an attacker-controlled nonscalar input reaches an assertion/CHECK that terminates execution. The missing scalar check is the cause; the abort is the consequence. This is a reachable-assertion DoS, not a memory-safety issue.

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the id input from context->input(2) is used directly as a scalar with no rank/shape validation. Trigger: a caller supplies a nonscalar id tensor, causing the scalar accessor to hit a CHECK failure. Supported consequence: the process aborts, giving a denial of service (availability impact).

Fixed Out-of-bound read in glyph_cache_put

CVE-2020-11098 thanks to @antonio-morales for finding this.

description: In FreeRDP before version 2.1.2, there is an out-of-bound read in glyph_cache_put. This affects all FreeRDP clients with `+glyph-cache` option enabled This is fixed in version 2.1.2.

code_evidence: The bounds check rejects only index values strictly greater than glyphCache[id].number, so index == number passes validation and execution continues.
prevGlyph is read from entries[index] and entries[index] is later written; with index equal to number (the count/size boundary), this accesses the entry one past the valid range.

commit_msg:
Fix memory leak when a graph node is invalid.

If a graph node is invalid but a kernel is created then we set the kernel back to `nullptr` but we forget to delete it. Hence, we get a memory leak.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 408968108
Change-Id: I1d8a9d0d8988ed5e08be8b9f2004ce1b4cd11b7c
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['      params_.delete_kernel(item->kernel);']}
description: Tensorflow is an Open Source Machine Learning Framework. If a graph node is invalid, TensorFlow can leak memory in the implementation of `ImmutableExecutorState::Initialize`. Here, we set `item->kernel` to `nullptr` but it is a simple `OpKernel*` pointer so the memory that was previously allocated to it would leak. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.8.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.7.1, TensorFlow 2.6.3, and TensorFlow 2.5.3, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: create_kernel allocates an OpKernel into item->kernel; on failure the code sets item->kernel = nullptr and returns without releasing the previously allocated kernel object, losing the only pointer to it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function fails to release allocated memory on an error path, matching CWE-401 (Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime). This is a resource-lifetime leak, not a use-after-free or double-free, since the pointer is nulled rather than freed.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the error branch overwrites item->kernel with nullptr without freeing the kernel that create_kernel may have allocated before returning a non-OK status. Trigger: a graph node whose kernel creation fails after allocation. Consequence: the allocated OpKernel becomes unreachable and leaks, consuming memory on each such failure.

commit_msg:
The X protocol uses CARD16 values to represent the length so
this would overflow.

CVE-2021-31535

Signed-off-by: Matthieu Herrb <matthieu@herrb.eu>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (n >= USHRT_MAX) {', '\t\t\tUnlockDisplay(dpy);', '\t\t\tSyncHandle();', '\t\t\treturn 0;', '\t\t}']}
description: LookupCol.c in X.Org X through X11R7.7 and libX11 before 1.7.1 might allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary code. The libX11 XLookupColor request (intended for server-side color lookup) contains a flaw allowing a client to send color-name requests with a name longer than the maximum size allowed by the protocol (and also longer than the maximum packet size for normal-sized packets). The user-controlled data exceeding the maximum size is then interpreted by the server as additional X protocol requests and executed, e.g., to disable X server authorization completely. For example, if the victim encounters malicious terminal control sequences for color codes, then the attacker may be able to take full control of the running graphical session.

code_evidence: The loop accumulates the total length n of all directory strings without any upper bound check.
nbytes is derived from n and added to req->length; a large n overflows the CARD16 length field of the request.
Xmalloc(nbytes) allocates the computed size, then Data sends nbytes bytes, so the oversized request length is transmitted.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function copies attacker-controlled directory data into a protocol buffer sized by an unchecked length calculation, allowing the request length to overflow and data to be written past the intended protocol boundary, consistent with a buffer copy lacking input size checking.

evidence_lines.code:
nbytes = (n + 3) & ~3;
req->length += nbytes >> 2;

if ((p = Xmalloc (nbytes))) {
Data (dpy, tmp, nbytes);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the total size of the user-supplied directory name list is summed and encoded into the fixed-width CARD16 request length field without validating against USHRT_MAX. Trigger: a client supplies a color/font path name list whose combined size exceeds 65535 bytes, overflowing req->length and corrupting the X protocol packet framing. Consequence: the server interprets excess bytes as additional X requests, potentially enabling arbitrary command execution.

commit_msg:
compat: fix 4-byte infoleak via uninitialized struct field

Commit 3a4d44b61625 ("ntp: Move adjtimex related compat syscalls to
native counterparts") removed the memset() in compat_get_timex().  Since
then, the compat adjtimex syscall can invoke do_adjtimex() with an
uninitialized ->tai.

If do_adjtimex() doesn't write to ->tai (e.g.  because the arguments are
invalid), compat_put_timex() then copies the uninitialized ->tai field
to userspace.

Fix it by adding the memset() back.

Fixes: 3a4d44b61625 ("ntp: Move adjtimex related compat syscalls to native counterparts")
Signed-off-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Acked-by: Kees Cook <keescook@chromium.org>
Acked-by: Al Viro <viro@zeniv.linux.org.uk>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tmemset(txc, 0, sizeof(struct timex));']}
description: The compat_get_timex function in kernel/compat.c in the Linux kernel before 4.16.9 allows local users to obtain sensitive information from kernel memory via adjtimex.

code_evidence: compat_get_timex declares local struct compat_timex tx32, fills it from userspace via copy_from_user, then copies individual fields into txc. Fields such as tai are not assigned; the function returns 0 without initializing the rest of txc, so any unassigned field retains stale stack/kernel memory.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function returns a partially uninitialized timex struct whose unset fields are later exposed to userspace, directly disclosing sensitive kernel memory to an unauthorized actor, matching CWE-200 information exposure.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: txc is not zeroed before selective field assignment, leaving uninitialized fields (e.g. tai) with residual kernel memory. Trigger: when do_adjtimex does not write tai (e.g. invalid args), compat_put_timex copies it to userspace. Consequence: local users leak kernel stack data (infoleak).

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['                     video_frame->data(media::VideoFrame::kYPlane),', '                     video_frame->data(media::VideoFrame::kUPlane),', '                     video_frame->data(media::VideoFrame::kVPlane),', '    CopyAlphaChannelIntoVideoFrame(temp_data_.data(), video_frame);'], 'added_lines': ['                     video_frame->visible_data(media::VideoFrame::kYPlane),', '                     video_frame->visible_data(media::VideoFrame::kUPlane),', '                     video_frame->visible_data(media::VideoFrame::kVPlane),', '    CopyAlphaChannelIntoVideoFrame(temp_data_.data(), size, video_frame);']}
description: Heap-based buffer overflow in content/renderer/media/canvas_capture_handler.cc in Google Chrome before 51.0.2704.63 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted web site.

code_evidence: CreateFrame allocates the video frame with a visible rect equal to the full size, so visible_data and data initially coincide; the frame dimensions derive from the SkImage size.

ARGBToI420 writes the converted Y/U/V planes through video_frame->data() pointers using the image width/height; when the image size is odd, the allocated plane stride/buffer sizing can be smaller than the amount libyuv writes.
The alpha path passes temp_data_ and the frame to CopyAlphaChannelIntoVideoFrame without a size argument, so it cannot bound the copy to the actual buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs writes into video frame memory buffers without ensuring the destination bounds match the source dimensions, so writes can land outside the intended buffer boundary. firewire: fix potential uaf in outbound_phy_packet_callback()

&e->event and e point to the same address, and &e->event could
be freed in queue_event. So there is a potential uaf issue if
we dereference e after calling queue_event(). Fix this by adding
a temporary variable to maintain e->client in advance, this can
avoid the potential uaf issue.

commit_msg:
drm/v3d: Fix memory leak in v3d_submit_cl_ioctl

In the impelementation of v3d_submit_cl_ioctl() there are two memory
leaks. One is when allocation for bin fails, and the other is when bin
initialization fails. If kcalloc fails to allocate memory for bin then
render->base should be put. Also, if v3d_job_init() fails to initialize
bin->base then allocated memory for bin should be released.

Fixes: a783a09ee76d ("drm/v3d: Refactor job management.")
Signed-off-by: Navid Emamdoost <navid.emamdoost@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Eric Anholt <eric@anholt.net>
Signed-off-by: Daniel Vetter <daniel.vetter@ffwll.ch>
Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20191021185250.26130-1-navid.emamdoost@gmail.com

description: Two memory leaks in the v3d_submit_cl_ioctl() function in drivers/gpu/drm/v3d/v3d_gem.c in the Linux kernel before 5.3.11 allow attackers to cause a denial of service (memory consumption) by triggering kcalloc() or v3d_job_init() failures, aka CID-29cd13cfd762.

code_evidence: When bcl_start differs from bcl_end, bin is allocated with kcalloc at line 30; if allocation fails, line 31-32 returns -ENOMEM without releasing the already-initialized render job, leaking render->base.
If v3d_job_init for bin->base fails at line 33-34, line 36 puts render->base but line 37 returns ret without kfree(bin), leaking the bin allocation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function allocates render and bin objects but does not sufficiently track and release them on specific error paths, matching CWE-401's missing release of memory after effective lifetime. This is not a use-after-free or double-free, since the defect is unreleased memory, not invalid access.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: error paths in v3d_submit_cl_ioctl fail to release already-allocated resources. Trigger: kcalloc failure for bin or v3d_job_init failure for bin->base; the early returns skip v3d_job_put(&render->base) and kfree(bin) respectively. Supported consequence is memory consumption/DoS on repeated failures.

code_evidence: szTmp is a fixed 256-byte stack buffer (line 5). nLength is the attacker-controlled length of pszValue (lines 38-39). The loop at 47-67 copies one input character to one output byte in the plain case, but expands a wildcard character into two bytes ('.' and '*', lines 63-64), so iTmp can reach up to 1 + 2*nLength before the trailing '/' and NUL writes at lines 68-69. joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes beyond the intended bounds of the szTmp memory buffer, matching CWE-119's improper restriction of operations within a memory buffer's boundary. The more specific CWE-121 (stack-based buffer overflow) would also fit, but the target label CWE-119 is directly supported by the out-of-bounds write shown here.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: writes into the fixed-size stack array szTmp are indexed by iTmp, which grows with the length of the attacker-supplied pszValue and can double per wildcard character, with no capacity check. commit_msg: https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/issues/781
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      FT_Done_Glyph(glyph.image);'], 'added_lines': ['          FT_Done_Glyph(glyph.image);']}
description: A use-after-free in RenderFreetype in MagickCore/annotate.c in ImageMagick 7.0.7-4 Q16 allows attackers to crash the application via a crafted font file, because the FT_Done_Glyph function (from FreeType 2) is called at an incorrect place in the ImageMagick code.

code_evidence: At the end of each loop iteration, the current glyph is retained in last_glyph (line 433) while the previous last_glyph.image is released via FT_Done_Glyph (line 432), transferring ownership of the current glyph to last_glyph.

After the loop, last_glyph.image is freed (line 441), but glyph.image still aliases the same object since glyph was assigned to last_glyph. The underscore path then calls FT_Get_Glyph on line 447, overwriting glyph.image only on success; on failure glyph.image remains the freed pointer, and line 463 calls FT_Done_Glyph(glyph.image) unconditionally, causing a double free.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the function frees an FT_Glyph object and then invokes FT_Done_Glyph on the same stale pointer when the reallocation path fails. This is a genuine use-after-free of freed heap memory rather than a mere resource leak or null dereference; the missing guard that glyph.image was reassigned is the defect.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is an ownership/aliasing error: glyph.image and last_glyph.image refer to the same FT_Glyph, which is freed at line 441. When the subsequent FT_Get_Glyph at line 447 fails (e.g., crafted font with missing underscore glyph), glyph.image is not reassigned, and the unconditional FT_Done_Glyph at line 463 operates on freed memory. Trigger is a font/load failure path; consequence is a use-after-free/double-free leading to application crash.

description: An arbitrary memory read vulnerability in Asylo versions up to 0.6.0 allows an untrusted attacker to make a call to enc_untrusted_recvfrom whose return size was not validated against the requested size. The parameter size is unchecked allowing the attacker to read memory locations outside of the intended buffer size including memory addresses within the secure enclave. We recommend upgrading past commit 6e158d558abd3c29a0208e30c97c9a8c5bd4230f

code_evidence: Line 16 reads the untrusted return size into result; lines 18-21 only handle result == -1 and never validate result against len before proceeding.
Line 22 consumes the received buffer and line 23 copies std::min(len, buffer_received.size()) bytes into buf, but result is returned at line 31 without any check that result <= len.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the unchecked result permits reads beyond the intended buffer's end. This is distinct from an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787): the copy itself is bounded by std::min(len, size), but the unvalidated length drives downstream over-reads.

evidence_lines.code:
auto buffer_received = output.next();
memcpy(buf, buffer_received.data(), std::min(len, buffer_received.size()));

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The dispatcher-supplied result (the reported received byte count) is trusted without comparison to the requested len. A malicious or compromised host can return a result larger than len; the function then reports that oversized length to the caller while only len bytes were copied, so the caller may treat result bytes of buf as valid and read past the buffer. The added guard (result > len) confirms the missing constraint; without it, out-of-bounds reads of enclave memory follow.

commit_msg:
Parallel dio write takes a negative refcount of fi->iocachectr and so does
open of file in passthrough mode.

The refcount of passthrough mode is associated with attach/detach of a
fuse_backing object to fuse inode.

For parallel dio write, the backing file is irrelevant, so the call to
fuse_inode_uncached_io_start() passes a NULL fuse_backing object.

Passing a NULL fuse_backing will result in false -EBUSY error if the file
is already open in passthrough mode.

Allow taking negative fi->iocachectr refcount with NULL fuse_backing,
because it does not conflict with an already attached fuse_backing object.

Fixes: 4a90451bbc7f ("fuse: implement open in passthrough mode")
Signed-off-by: Amir Goldstein <amir73il@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Miklos Szeredi <mszeredi@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (oldfb && oldfb != fb) {', '\tif (!oldfb) {'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (fb && oldfb && oldfb != fb) {', '\tif (fb && !oldfb) {']}
description: A use-after-free flaw was found in the Linux kernel’s FUSE filesystem in the way a user triggers write(). This flaw allows a local user to gain unauthorized access to data from the FUSE filesystem, resulting in privilege escalation.

code_evidence: The function reads the current backing pointer via fuse_inode_backing(fi) into oldfb under fi->lock (lines 5-6), then decrements fi->iocachectr (line 15). When oldfb is non-NULL it calls fuse_backing_put(fb) on the caller-supplied fb (line 20), and when oldfb is NULL it stores fb via fuse_inode_backing_set (line 17). The reference-count bookkeeping of the inode's backing object and iocachectr is therefore coupled to the lifetime of the fused backing object.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the function manipulates the reference/lifetime of a fuse_backing object and can leave the inode referencing memory after its reference is released, matching reuse of freed memory. It is not merely a refcount imbalance (CWE-911) because the supported consequence is dereference of freed memory.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the refcount/backing-object handoff is performed without a matching lifetime guarantee for the object referenced by fb, so a caller can pass a backing object whose reference is dropped while the inode still references it. Trigger: a write() path invoking this start function with a stale/parallel fuse_backing. Consequence: the inode retains a dangling backing pointer, later dereferenced, giving use-after-free read/write of freed memory.

commit_msg:
Resource requests from Save-Page-As should go through CanRequestURL checks.

This CL:

- Added checks to ResourceDispatcherHostImpl::BeginSaveFile to verify if
  the renderer process is authorized to access a given resource.

- Removed separate code path for file: URIs that used to be implemented
  in SaveFileManager::SaveLocalFile.  Avoiding a separate code path
  helps consolidate all authorization checks in one place.

BUG=616429

Review-Url: https://codereview.chromium.org/2075273002
Cr-Commit-Position: refs/heads/master@{#408235}
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  std::unique_ptr<ResourceHandler> handler(new SaveFileResourceHandler(', '      render_frame_route_id, url, save_file_manager_.get()));'], 'added_lines': ['  // Check if the renderer is permitted to request the requested URL.', '  using AuthorizationState = SaveFileResourceHandler::AuthorizationState;', '  AuthorizationState authorization_state = AuthorizationState::AUTHORIZED;', '  if (!ChildProcessSecurityPolicyImpl::GetInstance()->CanRequestURL(child_id,', '                                                                    url)) {', '    DVLOG(1) << "Denying unauthorized save of " << url.possibly_invalid_spec();', '    authorization_state = AuthorizationState::NOT_AUTHORIZED;', '    // No need to return here (i.e. okay to begin processing the request below),', '    // because NOT_AUTHORIZED will cause the request to be cancelled.  See also', '    // doc comments for AuthorizationState enum.', '  }', '', '  std::unique_ptr<SaveFileResourceHandler> handler(new SaveFileResourceHandler(', '      render_frame_route_id, url, save_file_manager_.get(),', '      authorization_state));']}
description: The download implementation in Google Chrome before 53.0.2785.89 on Windows and OS X and before 53.0.2785.92 on Linux does not properly restrict saving a file:// URL that is referenced by an http:// URL, which makes it easier for user-assisted remote attackers to discover NetNTLM hashes and conduct SMB relay attacks via a crafted web page that is accessed with the "Save page as" menu choice.

code_evidence: The URL is validated only by IsHandledURL (protocol handled by job factory), not by any authorization check against the requesting renderer (child_id). A file:// URL is a handled URL, so it passes this gate and reaches CreateRequest.

The request is created from the caller-supplied url and handed to a SaveFileResourceHandler and BeginRequestInternal without consulting ChildProcessSecurityPolicyImpl::CanRequestURL for child_id, so the renderer's access rights to the target are never enforced.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing authorization allows a renderer to cause disclosure of local file content it is not permitted to read, matching CWE-200's exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor. It is not merely a confidentiality impact of another flaw; the absent access-control check is the direct cause of the disclosure.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: BeginSaveFile trusts the renderer-supplied URL and only checks that its scheme is handled, omitting a CanRequestURL authorization check for child_id. Trigger: a renderer/remote page causes a save of a file:// URL (e.g., referenced via http://). Consequence: the local file is fetched and saved, exposing its contents and enabling NetNTLM hash discovery / SMB relay.

description: In Wireshark 2.4.0 to 2.4.2 and 2.2.0 to 2.2.10, the NetBIOS dissector could crash. This was addressed in epan/dissectors/packet-netbios.c by ensuring that write operations are bounded by the beginning of a buffer.

code_evidence: After writing the name, the code appends a null terminator at *name_ret (line 24) then decrements name_ret (line 25) before the trailing-space trim loop. The loop at line 26 runs a fixed NETBIOS_NAME_LEN - 1 iterations and decrements name_ret each pass (line 31), with no lower bound tied to the buffer start, so it can walk before name_ret's original position.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The code assumes a trailing non-space character will always terminate the backward scan, an unusual-input condition it fails to check. Consequence: pointer underflow causes reads and the write at *(name_ret + 1) to touch memory before the buffer, crashing the dissector (DoS).

Fix handling of symbolic link ACLs

On Linux ACLs on symbolic links are not supported.
We must avoid calling acl_set_file() on symbolic links as their
targets are modified instead.
