If we have been executed a lot of code then', '           assume this is the case and force an unexpected device disconnect.', '           This is apparently sufficient to beat the drivers into submission.', '         */', '        if (!(s->sien0 & LSI_SIST0_UDC)) {', '            qemu_log_mask(LOG_GUEST_ERROR,', '                          "lsi_scsi: inf. loop with UDC masked");', '        }', '        lsi_script_scsi_interrupt(s, LSI_SIST0_UDC, 0);', '        lsi_disconnect(s);', '        trace_lsi_execute_script_stop();', '        return;', '    }', '    if (s->istat1 & LSI_ISTAT1_SRUN && s->waiting == LSI_NOWAIT) {']}
description: In QEMU 1:4.1-1, 1:2.1+dfsg-12+deb8u6, 1:2.8+dfsg-6+deb9u8, 1:3.1+dfsg-8~deb10u1, 1:3.1+dfsg-8+deb10u2, and 1:2.1+dfsg-12+deb8u12 (fixed), when executing script in lsi_execute_script(), the LSI scsi adapter emulator advances 's->dsp' index to read next opcode. This can lead to an infinite loop if the next opcode is empty. Move the existing loop exit after 10k iterations so that it covers no-op opcodes as well.

code_evidence: Each iteration increments insn_processed, then reads the next opcode via read_dword(s, s->dsp). If the opcode is zero, the code advances s->dsp by 4 and jumps back to again, without any bound check on this path.

The only iteration limit is checked at the bottom of the function, gated additionally by s->waiting == LSI_NOWAIT; the goto again at line 414 re-enters the loop from the top, bypassing this check when empty opcodes keep the dsp advancing.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-835 fits because the function contains an iteration whose exit condition is unreachable on the empty-opcode path: the counter check is bypassed by goto again, so the loop never terminates. This is an availability/DoS weakness, distinct from a simple logic error, matching the infinite-loop description.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the loop-exit guard (insn_processed > 10000) is placed after the opcode dispatch and is skipped by the early goto again taken on empty opcodes. Trigger: a guest supplies a script whose opcodes are zero, so the zero-opcode branch repeatedly advances dsp and re-enters the loop. Consequence: the emulator spins indefinitely, consuming host CPU and denying service.

commit_msg:
Chain binding only requires the rule addition/insertion command within
the same transaction. Removal of rules from chain bindings within the
same transaction makes no sense, userspace does not utilize this
feature. Replace nft_chain_is_bound() check to nft_chain_binding() in
rule deletion commands. Replace command implies a rule deletion, reject
this command too.

Rule flush command can also safely rely on this nft_chain_binding()
check because unbound chains are not allowed since 62e1e94b246e
("netfilter: nf_tables: reject unbound chain set before commit phase").

Fixes: d0e2c7de92c7 ("netfilter: nf_tables: add NFT_CHAIN_BINDING")
Reported-by: Kevin Rich <kevinrich1337@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tif (nft_chain_is_bound(chain))', '\t\t\tif (nft_chain_is_bound(chain))'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (nft_chain_binding(chain))', '\t\t\tif (nft_chain_binding(chain))']}
description:
A use-after-free vulnerability in the Linux kernel's netfilter: nf_tables component can be exploited to achieve local privilege escalation.

Addition and removal of rules from chain bindings within the same transaction causes leads to use-after-free.

We recommend upgrading past commit f15f29fd4779be8a418b66e9d52979bb6d6c2325.

code_evidence: The chain looked up from NFTA_RULE_CHAIN is rejected only when nft_chain_is_bound(chain) is true; a chain that is a binding (nft_chain_binding) but not yet bound is not rejected, so deletion proceeds on it.
With a chain supplied, the code then calls nft_delrule(&ctx, rule) by handle or rule ID, or nft_delrule_by_chain(&ctx), scheduling removal of rules from that chain.
In the no-chain path, chains where nft_chain_is_bound(chain) is true are skipped, but a binding chain that is not yet bound is not skipped; nft_delrule_by_chain(&ctx) then deletes its rules.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the guard failure allows rules to be freed while chain-binding state still refers to them, i.e., memory is reused after being freed. This is not merely a missing validation (CWE-20): the deletion on a binding chain is what creates the dangling reference and the use-after-free consequence.

evidence_lines.code:
if (nft_chain_is_bound(chain))
return -EOPNOTSUPP;

if (nft_chain_is_bound(chain))
continue;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the deletion path guards against bound chains using the narrower nft_chain_is_bound() rather than nft_chain_binding(), so rule deletion is permitted on a chain binding within the same transaction as its rule insertion. Trigger: a userspace transaction that adds a rule to a binding chain and deletes it before commit. The scheduled deletion can free rule state that the binding still references, producing a use-after-free; the supported consequence is memory corruption/possible local privilege escalation.

commit_msg:
Fix buffer overrun due to integer overflow in bcmath

Summary: scale gets passed around as an int inside the library.

Reviewed By: mxw

Differential Revision: D3624520

fbshipit-source-id: d39927413cec24fda2e475a296ad5d9019ccef0a
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  if (scale < 0) scale = BCG(bc_precision);'], 'added_lines': ['  scale = adjust_scale(scale);']}
description: Integer overflow in bcmath in Facebook HHVM before 3.15.0 allows attackers to have unspecified impact via unknown vectors, which triggers a buffer overflow.

code_evidence: The scale parameter is an int64_t accepted directly from the caller and only checked for negativity; any non-negative value, including one beyond the range bc_multiply can safely handle, is passed through unchanged.
The unvalidated scale flows into bc_multiply and is then used to clamp result->n_scale; the code assumes scale is representable in the internal int scale used by the bcmath library.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs no range check on scale and relies on an implicit narrowing conversion, matching CWE-190's integer overflow/wraparound from assuming a value stays representable. The buffer overrun is the downstream consequence, not the root cause.

evidence_lines.code:
int64_t scale ) {
if (scale < 0) scale = BCG(bc_precision);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: caller-controlled scale is not bounded before being narrowed to the library's internal int scale, so a large int64_t value can overflow/wrap. Trigger: bcmul invoked with a very large positive scale. Consequence: wraparound produces an unexpected small or negative scale used in bc_multiply and result->n_scale assignment, which the commit message ties to a buffer overrun.

commit_msg:
Jan Kara's analysis of the syzbot report (edited):

  The reproducer opens a directory on FUSE filesystem, it then attaches
  dnotify mark to the open directory.  After that a fuse_do_getattr() call
  finds that attributes returned by the server are inconsistent, and calls
  make_bad_inode() which, among other things does:

          inode->i_mode = S_IFREG;

  This then confuses dnotify which doesn't tear down its structures
  properly and eventually crashes.

Avoid calling make_bad_inode() on a live inode: switch to a private flag on
the fuse inode.  Also add the test to ops which the bad_inode_ops would
have caught.

This bug goes back to the initial merge of fuse in 2.6.14...

Reported-by: syzbot+f427adf9324b92652ccc@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Signed-off-by: Miklos Szeredi <mszeredi@redhat.com>
Tested-by: Jan Kara <jack@suse.cz>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (is_bad_inode(inode))'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (fuse_is_bad(inode))']}
description: An issue was discovered in the FUSE filesystem implementation in the Linux kernel before 5.10.6, aka CID-5d069dbe8aaf. fuse_do_getattr() calls make_bad_inode() in inappropriate situations, causing a system crash. NOTE: the original fix for this vulnerability was incomplete, and its incompleteness is tracked as CVE-2021-28950.

code_evidence: The early check only tests is_bad_inode(inode) and returns -EIO; it does not recognize the FUSE-private bad-inode state, so a live inode marked bad by the FUSE layer passes through.
The flush path proceeds with inode_lock, fuse_sync_writes, and fuse_simple_request, and on -ENOSYS it sets fm->fc->no_flush and returns success without tearing down related state.
The function returns err after the request; the changed guard no longer reflects the private bad flag, so the flush continues on an inode whose attributes were made inconsistent.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-459 fits because the flush path fails to abort and clean up supporting resources (dnotify/flush state) after the inode is marked bad, resulting in incomplete cleanup and a crash. It is not merely an input-validation error; the weakness is the missing cleanup/abort on the bad-inode path.

evidence_lines.code:
if (is_bad_inode(inode))
return -EIO;

if (fm->fc->no_flush)
goto inval_attr_out;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: fuse_flush relies on a generic is_bad_inode check that does not detect the FUSE-private bad-inode condition, so the flush operation is not aborted. Trigger: FUSE getattr returns inconsistent attributes and marks the inode bad via the private flag while a dnotify mark is attached. Consequence: flush-related structures are not properly cleaned up, leading to a crash (DoS).

description: In Tensorflow before versions 1.15.4, 2.0.3, 2.1.2, 2.2.1 and 2.3.1, changing the TensorFlow's `SavedModel` protocol buffer and altering the name of required keys results in segfaults and data corruption while loading the model. This can cause a denial of service in products using `tensorflow-serving` or other inference-as-a-service installments. Fixed were added in commits f760f88b4267d981e13f4b302c437ae800445968 and fcfef195637c6e365577829c4d67681695956e7d (both going into TensorFlow 2.2.0 and 2.3.0 but not yet backported to earlier versions). However, this was not enough, as #41097 reports a different failure mode. The issue is patched in commit adf095206f25471e864a8e63a0f1caef53a0e3a6, and is released in TensorFlow versions 1.15.4, 2.0.3, 2.1.2, 2.2.1, or 2.3.1.

code_evidence: For each node in graph_def.node(), the function looks up the 'value' attribute and, when a tensor is present, derives PartialTensorShape from the tensor shape and checks node_shape.num_elements() < 0.
If the 'value' attribute is absent and the op is 'Const', it returns FailedPrecondition because no value was provided.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-20 fits because untrusted serialized model data is accepted without validating required properties (tensor shape/element count, presence of Const values) for all embedded nodes, allowing unsafe input to reach downstream processing. This is missing input validation of model data, not a transformation or escaping issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function validates only top-level GraphDef nodes: it rejects negative tensor element counts and Const nodes lacking a value. Nodes inside graph_def.library().function().node_def() are never inspected, so a crafted SavedModel can carry malformed FunctionDef nodes that bypass these checks and later trigger a CHECK-fail, causing denial of service. Root cause is incomplete validation of attacker-controlled model input; the crash is the consequence.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['#ifdef LIBRAW_LIBRARY_BUILD', '  if(offset>ifp->size()-8) // At least 8 bytes for tag/len', '    offset = ifp->size()-8;', '#endif', '', '    if(len < 0)', '      return; // just ignore wrong len?? or raise bad file exception?']}
description: An error within the "parse_minolta()" function (dcraw/dcraw.c) in LibRaw versions prior to 0.18.11 can be exploited to trigger an infinite loop via a specially crafted file.

code_evidence: Line 9 derives the loop bound offset from file data via get4(); lines 10-11 run while ftell(ifp) < offset.
Line 14 reads len via get4(); the switch (15-22) may fseek forward, then line 79 seeks to save+len+8, where save was captured at line 10 before the iteration.

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The loop exit depends on ftell(ifp) reaching offset, but each iteration repositions the stream to save+len+8 using an attacker-controlled len from get4(). If len is negative or otherwise crafted, the seek moves the position backward or keeps it below offset, so the condition at line 10 never becomes false. The trigger is a malformed Minolta file; the supported consequence is CPU consumption from an unbounded loop.

commit_msg:
Fix remote code execution and privilege escalation vulnerability.

CVE-2019-12816

description: Modules.cpp in ZNC before 1.7.4-rc1 allows remote authenticated non-admin users to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary code by loading a module with a crafted name.

code_evidence: LoadModule accepts the caller-supplied sModule string and immediately uses it as a lookup key in FindModule without any syntactic validation of the name.
The unvalidated name is passed to FindModPath and then embedded into sModPath/sDataPath; Info.SetName/SetPath and OpenModule later consume these derived paths.

The loaded module is constructed via Info.GetLoader() with the same sModule and sDataPath, and the resulting path is stored on the module, so a crafted name propagates into module loading and path construction.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function fails to validate the properties (allowed syntax, no traversal) of its module-name input before processing, which is the defining pattern of CWE-20. The path traversal and code execution are consequences of that missing validation rather than a separate encoding or escaping defect.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: sModule is trusted as-is, so characters such as path separators or traversal sequences are never rejected before being combined into module paths. Trigger: an authenticated non-admin user supplies a crafted module name to LoadModule. This lets the derived path escape the intended module directory, enabling loading of attacker-controlled code and privilege escalation.

The code does not modify memory out of bounds, so the target CWE is not directly supported; the weakness aligns better with CWE-125 (out-of-bounds read).

Trigger: crafted HTML producing a MARKUP_NONE node with NULL or empty data. Consequence: out-of-bounds read before the buffer, leading to a crash (DoS) as reported; the fix adds a dereference guard.

commit_msg:
KVM: VMX: Do not BUG() on out-of-bounds guest IRQ

The value of the guest_irq argument to vmx_update_pi_irte() is
ultimately coming from a KVM_IRQFD API call. Do not BUG() in
vmx_update_pi_irte() if the value is out-of bounds. (Especially,
since KVM as a whole seems to hang after that.)

Instead, print a message only once if we find that we don't have a
route for a certain IRQ (which can be out-of-bounds or within the
array).

This fixes CVE-2017-1000252.

Fixes: efc644048ecde54 ("KVM: x86: Update IRTE for posted-interrupts")
Signed-off-by: Jan H. Schönherr <jschoenh@amazon.de>
Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tint idx, ret = -EINVAL;', '\tBUG_ON(guest_irq >= irq_rt->nr_rt_entries);'], 'added_lines': ['\tint idx, ret = 0;', '\tif (guest_irq >= irq_rt->nr_rt_entries ||', '\t    hlist_empty(&irq_rt->map[guest_irq])) {', '\t\tpr_warn_once("no route for guest_irq %u/%u (broken user space?)\\n",', '\t\t\t     guest_irq, irq_rt->nr_rt_entries);', '\t\tgoto out;', '\t}']}

code_evidence: guest_irq, derived from a KVM_IRQFD API call, is used directly as an index into irq_rt->map without any bounds check. BUG_ON only asserts the condition rather than validating and rejecting it, and an out-of-range guest_irq still reaches the hlist_for_each_entry dereference of &irq_rt->map[guest_irq].

It is not a memory-safety weakness like CWE-125/787 because the primary failure is the unchecked index assertion and resulting DoS, not an out-of-bounds read of attacker data.

BUG_ON(guest_irq >= irq_rt->nr_rt_entries);
hlist_for_each_entry(e, &irq_rt->map[guest_irq], link) {

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function trusts the caller-supplied guest_irq and never validates it against irq_rt->nr_rt_entries before indexing the map array; the BUG_ON is an assertion, not a safe rejection path. Trigger: a guest/user passes an out-of-bounds guest_irq through the IRQFD API. Consequence: assertion failure leading to hypervisor hang or crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
cjpeg: Fix OOB read caused by malformed 8-bit BMP

... in which one or more of the color indices is out of range for the
number of palette entries.

Fix partly borrowed from jpeg-9c.  This commit also adopts Guido's
JERR_PPM_OUTOFRANGE enum value in lieu of our project-specific
JERR_PPM_TOOLARGE enum value.

Fixes #258
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    source->cmap_length = (int)biClrUsed;']}
description: get_8bit_row in rdbmp.c in libjpeg-turbo through 1.5.90 and MozJPEG through 3.3.1 allows attackers to cause a denial of service (heap-based buffer over-read and application crash) via a crafted 8-bit BMP in which one or more of the color indices is out of range for the number of palette entries.

The colormap is allocated with exactly biClrUsed entries (line 105) and read_colormap fills that many entries (line 106); the added cmap_length records this count for later index validation. Before the fix, get_8bit_row could index colormap with a file-supplied color index larger than the allocated biClrUsed, causing a heap-based over-read.

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the palette size is derived from biClrUsed and can be smaller than the range of color indices appearing in the 8-bit pixel data. Trigger: a crafted 8-bit BMP with a small biClrUsed and out-of-range indices. Consequence: get_8bit_row reads colormap entries past the allocated buffer, causing a heap over-read and crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
Save stack space while handling errors

Because error handling (luaG_errormsg) uses slots from EXTRA_STACK,
and some errors can recur (e.g., string overflow while creating an
error message in 'luaG_runerror', or a C-stack overflow before calling
the message handler), the code should use stack slots with parsimony.

This commit fixes the bug "Lua-stack overflow when C stack overflows
while handling an error".
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  if (isLua(ci))  /* if Lua function, add source:line information */'], 'added_lines': ['  if (isLua(ci)) {  /* if Lua function, add source:line information */', "    setobjs2s(L, L->top - 2, L->top - 1);  /* remove 'msg' from the stack */", '    L->top--;', '  }']}
description: An issue in the component luaG_runerror of Lua v5.4.4 and below leads to a heap-buffer overflow when a recursive error occurs.

code_evidence: Line 7 pushes the formatted message onto the Lua stack via luaO_pushvfstring, leaving the value at L->top-1. Line 9 checks isLua(ci) and line 10 calls luaG_addinfo, which pushes additional stack slots; the 'msg' object is then no longer at the top and is not removed before luaG_errormsg (line 11) consumes EXTRA_STACK slots while handling the error.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unbalanced stack push causes stack exhaustion and subsequent writes past the intended stack boundary, matching CWE-787 (out-of-bounds write). This is distinct from a mere resource-exhaustion DoS: the memory write past the stack limit is the supported weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: luaG_runerror leaves the formatted 'msg' value on the Lua stack instead of balancing it, so each recursive error (e.g. string overflow while building an error message, or C-stack overflow before the handler) consumes extra stack slots. The trigger is a recursive error path; the supported consequence is a Lua-stack overflow that corrupts/overwrites stack memory, i.e. an out-of-bounds write.

commit_msg:
netlink: limit recursion depth in policy validation

Now that we have nested policies, we can theoretically
recurse forever parsing attributes if a (sub-)policy
refers back to a higher level one. This is a situation
that has happened in nl80211, and we've avoided it there
by not linking it.

Add some code to netlink parsing to limit recursion depth.

Signed-off-by: Johannes Berg <johannes.berg@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t\t    extack, tb);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t\t    extack, tb, 0);']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel before 5.8. lib/nlattr.c allows attackers to cause a denial of service (unbounded recursion) via a nested Netlink policy with a back reference.

code_evidence: The wrapper __nla_parse delegates directly to __nla_validate_parse, passing head, len, maxtype, policy, validate, extack and tb with no depth or recursion counter argument. The call supplies no bound on nested policy traversal; the recursion limit must be carried through this call chain.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-674 fits because the function's delegation of policy validation lacks any recursion-depth control, permitting unbounded recursive descent. This is uncontrolled recursion (resource exhaustion), not merely a memory-safety defect; the missing depth constraint is the weakness.

evidence_lines.code:
return __nla_validate_parse(head, len, maxtype, policy, validate,
extack, tb);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the validation entry point invokes __nla_validate_parse without any recursion-depth state, so nested policies that reference back to a higher-level policy can recurse indefinitely. Trigger: a crafted Netlink policy with a back reference during attribute validation. Consequence: unbounded recursion consumes stack and CPU, causing denial of service.

commit_msg:
The X protocol uses CARD16 values to represent the length so
this would overflow.

CVE-2021-31535

Signed-off-by: Matthieu Herrb <matthieu@herrb.eu>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '    if (strlen(colorname) >= USHRT_MAX)', '        return (0);']}
description: LookupCol.c in X.Org X through X11R7.7 and libX11 before 1.7.1 might allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary code. The libX11 XLookupColor request (intended for server-side color lookup) contains a flaw allowing a client to send color-name requests with a name longer than the maximum size allowed by the protocol (and also longer than the maximum packet size for normal-sized packets). The user-controlled data exceeding the maximum size is then interpreted by the server as additional X protocol requests and executed, e.g., to disable X server authorization completely. For example, if the victim encounters malicious terminal control sequences for color codes, then the attacker may be able to take full control of the running graphical session.

code_evidence: Line 36 casts strlen(colorname) to CARD16, silently truncating any name longer than 65535 bytes before assigning it to req->nbytes. Line 37 computes the request length from the truncated value, and line 38 sends nbytes bytes via _XSend while the actual colorname buffer may be much larger.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function copies a client-supplied string into a fixed-width protocol field without validating that its length fits, causing a size mismatch between the declared and actual copy—the classic buffer-copy-without-size-check pattern of CWE-120. The added strlen guard confirms the intended constraint was absent in this version.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The root cause is the unchecked narrowing cast of the user-controlled color name length to CARD16. When colorname exceeds USHRT_MAX, the protocol length field wraps while the full string is still transmitted, so excess bytes are interpreted by the X server as additional protocol requests, enabling arbitrary protocol injection.

commit_msg:
In the event of a failure in tcf_change_indev(), fw_set_parms() will
immediately return an error after incrementing or decrementing
reference counter in tcf_bind_filter().  If attacker can control
reference counter to zero and make reference freed, leading to
use after free.

In order to prevent this, move the point of possible failure above the
point where the TC_FW_CLASSID is handled.

Fixes: 1da177e4c3f4 ("Linux-2.6.12-rc2")
Reported-by: M A Ramdhan <ramdhan@starlabs.sg>
Signed-off-by: M A Ramdhan <ramdhan@starlabs.sg>
Acked-by: Jamal Hadi Salim <jhs@mojatatu.com>
Reviewed-by: Pedro Tammela <pctammela@mojatatu.com>
Message-ID: <20230705161530.52003-1-ramdhan@starlabs.sg>
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['', '\tif (tb[TCA_FW_CLASSID]) {', '\t\tf->res.classid = nla_get_u32(tb[TCA_FW_CLASSID]);', '\t\ttcf_bind_filter(tp, &f->res, base);', '\t}'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (tb[TCA_FW_CLASSID]) {', '\t\tf->res.classid = nla_get_u32(tb[TCA_FW_CLASSID]);', '\t\ttcf_bind_filter(tp, &f->res, base);', '\t}', '']}
description:
A use-after-free vulnerability in the Linux kernel's net/sched: cls_fw component can be exploited to achieve local privilege escalation.

If tcf_change_indev() fails, fw_set_parms() will immediately return an error after incrementing or decrementing the reference counter in tcf_bind_filter(). If an attacker can control the reference counter and set it to zero, they can cause the reference to be freed, leading to a use-after-free vulnerability.

We recommend upgrading past commit 0323bce598eea038714f941ce2b22541c46d488f.

code_evidence: At [13-16] the TCA_FW_CLASSID branch records f->res.classid and calls tcf_bind_filter(tp, &f->res, base), which increments the filter's reference counter before any later validation. The subsequent TCA_FW_INDEV block at [17-23] calls tcf_change_indev and returns ret on failure at [20-21], leaving the bound reference from [15] in place despite the error return.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The early return after tcf_bind_filter leaves a dangling reference to freed filter memory that may later be dereferenced, which is the reuse of freed memory described by CWE-416. The defect is an ordering/error-path flaw enabling use-after-free rather than a simple reference-count leak.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: fw_set_parms() binds the filter and bumps its reference counter before a later operation (tcf_change_indev) that can fail and return early. Trigger: an attacker supplies a TCA_FW_CLASSID plus an invalid TCA_FW_INDEV so the error path is taken after tcf_bind_filter. Consequence: the reference counter state is inconsistent, allowing the filter to be freed while still referenced, yielding a use-after-free.

commit_msg:
hw/usb/hcd-xhci: Fix unbounded loop in xhci_ring_chain_length() (CVE-2020-14394)

The loop condition in xhci_ring_chain_length() is under control of
the guest, and additionally the code does not check for failed DMA
transfers (e.g. if reaching the end of the RAM), so the loop there
could run for a very long time or even forever. Fix it by checking
the return value of dma_memory_read() and by introducing a maximum
loop length.

Resolves: https://gitlab.com/qemu-project/qemu/-/issues/646
Message-Id: <20220804131300.96368-1-thuth@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Mauro Matteo Cascella <mcascell@redhat.com>
Acked-by: Gerd Hoffmann <kraxel@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Huth <thuth@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    while (1) {', '        dma_memory_read(xhci->as, dequeue, &trb, TRB_SIZE,', '                        MEMTXATTRS_UNSPECIFIED);', '    }'], 'added_lines': ['    do {', '        if (dma_memory_read(xhci->as, dequeue, &trb, TRB_SIZE,', '                        MEMTXATTRS_UNSPECIFIED) != MEMTX_OK) {', '            qemu_log_mask(LOG_GUEST_ERROR, "%s: DMA memory access failed!\\n",', '                          __func__);', '            return -1;', '        }', '', '        /*', '         * According to the xHCI spec, Transfer Ring segments should have', '         * a maximum size of 64 kB (see chapter "6 Data Structures")', '         */', '    } while (length < TRB_LINK_LIMIT * 65536 / TRB_SIZE);', '', '    qemu_log_mask(LOG_GUEST_ERROR, "%s: exceeded maximum tranfer ring size!\\n",', '                          __func__);', '', '    return -1;']}
description: An infinite loop flaw was found in the USB xHCI controller emulation of QEMU while computing the length of the Transfer Request Block (TRB) Ring. This flaw allows a privileged guest user to hang the QEMU process on the host, resulting in a denial of service.

code_evidence: The loop is entered unconditionally with `while (1)` and the DMA read result at lines 11-12 is discarded, so a failed read leaves `trb` uninitialized/unrefreshed while control continues.

A TR_LINK TRB sets `dequeue` from guest-controlled `trb.parameter` and `continue`s; only `link_cnt > TRB_LINK_LIMIT` bounds link hops, and a self-referential or cyclic link can keep the loop iterating.
`length` increments only for non-link TRBs; the normal exit at lines 37-38 requires a TRB with TRB_TR_CH clear and no control TD set, which a guest can avoid indefinitely.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-835 fits: the `while (1)` loop's exit condition depends on guest-controlled TRB data and an unchecked DMA read, so the exit is unreachable for crafted input, causing an infinite loop and DoS. This is the unbounded-iteration root cause, not merely an out-of-bounds access.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The guest controls the TRB chain contents and link addresses read via DMA. Because the DMA read failure is ignored and the loop has no overall iteration/length bound, a guest can supply a cyclic link chain or unreadable DMA region so the termination condition at lines 37-38 is never reached, hanging the QEMU vCPU thread and denying service to the host process.

commit_msg:
When opening files for write, ensure they aren't symbolic links

Issue #1048 identified that if, for example, a non privileged user
created a symbolic link from /etc/keepalvied.data to /etc/passwd,
writing to /etc/keepalived.data (which could be invoked via DBus)
would cause /etc/passwd to be overwritten.

This commit stops keepalived writing to pathnames where the ultimate
component is a symbolic link, by setting O_NOFOLLOW whenever opening
a file for writing.

This might break some setups, where, for example, /etc/keepalived.data
was a symbolic link to /home/fred/keepalived.data. If this was the case,
instead create a symbolic link from /home/fred/keepalived.data to
/tmp/keepalived.data, so that the file is still accessible via
/home/fred/keepalived.data.

There doesn't appear to be a way around this backward incompatibility,
since even checking if the pathname is a symbolic link prior to opening
for writing would create a race condition.

Signed-off-by: Quentin Armitage <quentin@armitage.org.uk>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tchar file_name[21];', '\t\tfp = fopen(file_name, "w");'], 'added_lines': ['\tchar file_name[22];', '\t\tfp = fopen_safe(file_name, "w");']}
description: keepalived 2.0.8 didn't check for pathnames with symlinks when writing data to a temporary file upon a call to PrintData or PrintStats. This allowed local users to overwrite arbitrary files if fs.protected_symlinks is set to 0, as demonstrated by a symlink from /tmp/keepalived.data or /tmp/keepalived.stats to /etc/passwd.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function writes diagnostic keyword data to a predictable /tmp file via fopen without symlink protection, which supports arbitrary file overwrite (CWE-59/CWE-73), not exposure of sensitive information; no unauthorized read or disclosure occurs in this code.

commit_msg:
vgacon: remove software scrollback support

Yunhai Zhang recently fixed a VGA software scrollback bug in commit
ebfdfeeae8c0 ("vgacon: Fix for missing check in scrollback handling"),
but that then made people look more closely at some of this code, and
there were more problems on the vgacon side, but also the fbcon software
scrollback.

We don't really have anybody who maintains this code - probably because
nobody actually _uses_ it any more.  Sure, people still use both VGA and
the framebuffer consoles, but they are no longer the main user
interfaces to the kernel, and haven't been for decades, so these kinds
of extra features end up bitrotting and not really being used.

So rather than try to maintain a likely unused set of code, I'll just
aggressively remove it, and see if anybody even notices.  Maybe there
are people who haven't jumped on the whole GUI badnwagon yet, and think
it's just a fad.  And maybe those people use the scrollback code.

If that turns out to be the case, we can resurrect this again, once
we've found the sucker^Wmaintainer for it who actually uses it.

commit_msg:
blk-mq: fix race between timeout and freeing request

Inside timeout handler, blk_mq_tag_to_rq() is called
to retrieve the request from one tag. This way is obviously
wrong because the request can be freed any time and some
fiedds of the request can't be trusted, then kernel oops
might be triggered[1].

Currently wrt. blk_mq_tag_to_rq(), the only special case is
that the flush request can share same tag with the request
cloned from, and the two requests can't be active at the same
time, so this patch fixes the above issue by updating tags->rqs[tag]
with the active request(either flush rq or the request cloned
from) of the tag.

Also blk_mq_tag_to_rq() gets much simplified with this patch.

Given blk_mq_tag_to_rq() is mainly for drivers and the caller must
make sure the request can't be freed, so in bt_for_each() this
helper is replaced with tags->rqs[tag].

description: In blk_mq_tag_to_rq in blk-mq.c in the upstream kernel, there is a possible use after free due to a race condition when a request has been previously freed by blk_mq_complete_request. This could lead to local escalation of privilege. Product: Android. Versions: Android kernel. Android ID: A-63083046.

code_evidence: bt_for_each iterates bitmap tag words and, for each set bit, retrieves the request at line 12 via blk_mq_tag_to_rq(hctx->tags, off + bit). The retrieved rq is then dereferenced at line 13 (rq->q) and passed to fn at line 14 without any lock or lifetime check on the tag slot.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-362 fits because the flaw is improper synchronization over a shared resource (the tag-to-request mapping): the iteration sequence assumes exclusive access to the tag slot while a concurrent completion sequence can modify/free it. The consequence (use-after-free) is a downstream effect of the race, so the primary weakness is the race condition.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The tag bitmap and the tags->rqs[] array are shared state accessed concurrently by the timeout/iteration path (bt_for_each under blk_mq_tag_busy_iter) and the completion/free path (blk_mq_complete_request). Between reading the set bit and dereferencing the returned request, another CPU can free and reuse that request, so rq at line 12 is stale; line 13 then reads freed memory. This is a use-after-free race causing kernel oops and potential local privilege escalation, not a simple null check failure.

commit_msg:
x86/ept: atomically modify entries in ept_next_level

ept_next_level was passing a live PTE pointer to ept_set_middle_entry,
which was then modified without taking into account that the PTE could
be part of a live EPT table. This wasn't a security issue because the
pages returned by p2m_alloc_ptp are zeroed, so adding such an entry
before actually initializing it didn't allow a guest to access
physical memory addresses it wasn't supposed to access.

This is part of XSA-328.

Reported-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Signed-off-by: Roger Pau Monné <roger.pau@citrix.com>
Reviewed-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        next = ept_set_middle_entry(p2m, ept_entry);', '        /* e is now stale and hence may not be used anymore below. */'], 'added_lines': ['', '    ASSERT(next_level);', '        int rc;', '', '        next = ept_set_middle_entry(p2m, &e);', '', '        rc = atomic_write_ept_entry(p2m, ept_entry, e, next_level);', '        ASSERT(rc == 0);']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.13.x, allowing Intel guest OS users to gain privileges or cause a denial of service because of non-atomic modification of a live EPT PTE. When mapping guest EPT (nested paging) tables, Xen would in some circumstances use a series of non-atomic bitfield writes. Depending on the compiler version and optimisation flags, Xen might expose a dangerous partially written PTE to the hardware, which an attacker might be able to race to exploit. A guest administrator or perhaps even an unprivileged guest user might be able to cause denial of service, data corruption, or privilege escalation. Only systems using Intel CPUs are vulnerable. Systems using AMD CPUs, and Arm systems, are not vulnerable. Only systems using nested paging (hap, aka nested paging, aka in this case Intel EPT) are vulnerable. Only HVM and PVH guests can exploit the vulnerability. The presence and scope of the vulnerability depends on the precise optimisations performed by the compiler used to build Xen. If the compiler generates (a) a single 64-bit write, or (b) a series of read-modify-write operations in the same order as the source code, the hypervisor is not vulnerable. For example, in one test build using GCC 8.3 with normal settings, the compiler generated multiple (unlocked) read-modify-write operations in source-code order, which did not constitute a vulnerability. We have not been able to survey compilers; consequently we cannot say which compiler(s) might produce vulnerable code (with which code-generation options). The source code clearly violates the C rules, and thus should be considered vulnerable.

code_evidence: Line 11 reads the live EPT entry e via atomic_read_ept_entry, and line 18 passes the live ept_entry pointer (which is the slot at line 10) to ept_set_middle_entry, which writes the new middle entry directly into the live table. No atomic publication of the initialized entry occurs; the write at line 18 targets the shared EPT PTE that hardware/other vCPUs may concurrently read.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-362 fits because the function performs a multi-step, non-atomic modification of a shared EPT PTE that concurrent code sequences (hardware page walks or other vCPUs) can access, violating exclusivity/atomicity. The fix replaces the live-pointer write with an atomic_write_ept_entry, confirming the race.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the code sequence initializes a new EPT middle entry by writing non-atomically into a live EPT PTE, violating atomicity of the shared resource update. Trigger: a guest causes a not-present EPT entry to be populated while the EPT table is live; concurrent hardware EPT walks or other vCPUs may observe the partially written PTE. Supported consequence: exposure of a partially written entry enabling data corruption, DoS, or privilege escalation for a racing guest.

commit_msg: WFSSL-51 sessions not removed correctly
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    ssl_methods.SSL_SESSION_free(session);']}
description: A memory leak flaw was found in WildFly OpenSSL in versions prior to 1.1.3.Final, where it removes an HTTP session. It may allow the attacker to cause OOM leading to a denial of service. The highest threat from this vulnerability is to system availability.

code_evidence: The callback obtains the SSL_SESSION pointer via the ctx/session arguments (lines 1-2) and uses it to build a Java sessionId (line 7) and invoke sessionRemove (line 8). After detaching the thread (line 9), the function returns at line 10 without calling SSL_SESSION_free on the session obtained for this callback.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-401 covers failing to release allocated memory after its effective lifetime. Here the session object is used for the callback work but not freed before return, matching the missing-release pattern; the added free line in the diff confirms the intended lifetime ends in this function.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: remove_session_cb never releases the SSL_SESSION it is invoked for, so the OpenSSL session object remains allocated. Trigger: each HTTP session removal invokes this callback repeatedly, causing per-session allocations to accumulate. Consequence: unbounded memory growth leading to OOM and denial of service, as described for the fixed version that adds SSL_SESSION_free(session).

description: GPAC 0.7.1 has a buffer overflow issue in gf_import_message() in media_import.c.

code_evidence: BT_STR_CHECK_ALLOC only reallocates when i==size, growing the buffer by 500 bytes; it does not bound-check writes against size.
The loop breaks on the delimiter but otherwise writes unconditionally into res at index i.
In the UTF-8 branch, res[i] is written, i incremented, then the macro is invoked; the check occurs after the write, so a write at i==size happens before the buffer grows.
The common path res[i] = ...; i++ also writes at i without a preceding capacity check.
Terminating NUL res[i]=0 is written at the final i, which can equal size, again past the allocation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Writes to res[i] at or beyond the allocated size are out-of-bounds writes, matching CWE-787. The off-by-one ordering of the realloc check is the specific cause; this is not merely an integer overflow, since the size arithmetic itself is bounded.

evidence_lines.code:
#defineBT_STR_CHECK_ALLOC\
if (i==size) {\
res = (char*)gf_realloc(res, sizeof(char) * (size+500+1));\
size += 500;\
}\
res[i] = 0;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the allocation macro tests i==size only after the current index has already been written, and some writes (lines 33, 69, 78) occur with no capacity check at all. A long input string or multibyte UTF-8 sequence drives i up to size, so the subsequent store writes one byte past the heap buffer, corrupting adjacent memory and potentially enabling code execution or a crash.

code_evidence: on_header_value indexes data->part[data->num_of_part] for both OGS_SBI_CONTENT_TYPE and OGS_SBI_CONTENT_ID without checking num_of_part against OGS_SBI_MAX_NUM_OF_PART; the guard is only 'if (at && length)' at line 8.

commit_msg:
Fix file descriptor leak.

If the openssl initial negotiation fails, then the rest of
what sslize does doesn't happen.  One of the last things
sslize does is to close the socket at the end of the session.
That needs to happen even if there's no session.

Signed-off-by: Marcus Watts <mwatts@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\telse {', '\t\t\t\tclose_connection(conn);', '\t\t\t}']}
description: A flaw was found in the way civetweb frontend was handling requests for ceph RGW server with SSL enabled. An unauthenticated attacker could create multiple connections to ceph RADOS gateway to exhaust file descriptors for ceph-radosgw service resulting in a remote denial of service.

code_evidence: At line 66 the SSL branch is entered when conn->client.is_ssl is true. If sslize() at 68-71 fails, the condition is false, so the block at 72-86 (which calls process_new_connection and frees client_cert) is skipped. The else at 88-90 handles only non-SSL connections, so on SSL negotiation failure neither process_new_connection nor close_connection is invoked and the accepted socket remains open until the next loop iteration.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The socket descriptor is acquired by consume_socket() and should be released after its lifetime ends; the missing close on the SSL failure path leaves it unreleased, matching CWE-772. This is not CWE-404 generally but specifically failure to release the acquired resource after use.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the failure path of sslize() bypasses all connection cleanup, including closing the accepted socket. Trigger: an unauthenticated client repeatedly opens SSL connections whose handshake fails. Consequence: each failed connection's file descriptor stays open, exhausting the process descriptor table and causing denial of service.

description: An issue was discovered in faad2 through 2.10.0. A stack-buffer-overflow exists in the function ftypin located in mp4read.c. It allows an attacker to cause Code Execution.

code_evidence: The loop copies bytes one at a time from g_fin into txt at index size, bounded by size < sizemax, so writes stay within [0, sizemax-1]. The loop exits early only when a NUL byte is read; if the input fills the buffer without a NUL, no terminator is written and the buffer contents are not guaranteed to be NUL-terminated within sizemax bytes.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the missing terminator leads to out-of-bounds memory access/write past the intended stack buffer during later string handling. The write bound itself is respected; the weakness is the absent NUL constraint that enables the out-of-bounds write downstream, not a pure out-of-bounds read (CWE-125).
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: stringin fills up to sizemax bytes but does not guarantee NUL termination when the input contains no NUL byte within the limit. Trigger: a crafted file whose field reaches sizemax without a NUL. Consequence: downstream string operations read past the stack buffer, producing a stack-buffer-overflow (the commit adds txt[sizemax-1]='\0' to fix it).

commit_msg:
Fix table rowspan and colspan

Origin: https://github.com/tats/w3m/pull/19
Bug-Debian: https://github.com/tats/w3m/issues/8
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tif (rowspan < 1)', '\t    rowspan = 1;', '\tif (colspan < 1)', '\t    colspan = 1;']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Tatsuya Kinoshita w3m fork before 0.5.3-31. The feed_table_tag function in w3m doesn't properly validate the value of table span, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (stack and/or heap buffer overflow) and possibly execute arbitrary code via a crafted HTML page.

code_evidence: ATTR_ROWSPAN is parsed into rowspan and only capped at an upper bound (ATTR_ROWSPAN_MAX); there is no lower-bound check, so a zero or negative rowspan survives.
ATTR_COLSPAN is parsed into colspan and only clamped when it exceeds MAXCOL; a zero or negative colspan is not corrected.
The rowspan/colspan loops index tbl->tabattr[tbl->row + i][tbl->col + j] using these unvalidated values, so negative i or j compute negative array offsets.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked span values drive array indexing outside the intended bounds of tbl->tabattr, which is a memory buffer. This matches CWE-119's out-of-bounds read/write; the added clamps in the patch confirm the missing minimum constraint is the cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the parser accepts attacker-controlled rowspan/colspan values without enforcing a minimum of 1. Trigger: a crafted HTML table cell with rowspan or colspan of 0 or negative. The subsequent nested loops compute out-of-bounds indices into tbl->tabattr (and related cell arrays), producing stack/heap buffer overflow, crash, or possible code execution.

commit_msg:
Add IsScalar / IsVector (rank) checks to input min/max tensors for FakeQuantWithMinMaxVarsPerChannelGradientOp and FakeQuantWithMinMaxVarsGradientOp.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 462542629
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    OP_REQUIRES(', '        context, TensorShapeUtils::IsVector(min.shape()),', '        InvalidArgument("`min` must be rank 1 but is rank ", min.dims()));', '    OP_REQUIRES(', '        context, TensorShapeUtils::IsVector(max.shape()),', '        InvalidArgument("`max` must be rank 1 but is rank ", max.dims()));']}
description: TensorFlow is an open source platform for machine learning. When `tf.quantization.fake_quant_with_min_max_vars_per_channel_gradient` receives input `min` or `max` of rank other than 1, it gives a `CHECK` fail that can trigger a denial of service attack. We have patched the issue in GitHub commit f3cf67ac5705f4f04721d15e485e192bb319feed. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.10.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.9.1, TensorFlow 2.8.1, and TensorFlow 2.7.2, as these are also affected and still in supported range.There are no known workarounds for this issue.

code_evidence: min is read from context->input(2) and its first dimension is compared to depth via min.dim_size(0) without first verifying min is rank 1.
max is read from context->input(3) and max.dim_size(0) is likewise accessed without a rank check.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The reachable CHECK/assertion on malformed min/max rank causes an application exit, matching CWE-617. The fix adds IsVector guards so the condition becomes a handled error instead of a fatal assertion; this is an availability issue, not memory corruption.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function assumes the min and max tensors are rank-1 vectors and calls dim_size(0) directly. A caller supplying a scalar or higher-rank min/max triggers a CHECK failure inside dim_size rather than a graceful InvalidArgument, aborting the process and enabling denial of service.

commit_msg:
display: Exit with failure if loading existing users fails

Given not having users may make GDM to launch initial setup, that
allows to create new users (potentially with sudo capabilities), it's
better to make look_for_existing_users() to return its status and only
if it didn't fail continue the gdm execution.

GHSL-2020-202
CVE-2020-16125

Fixes #642

description: gdm3 versions before 3.36.2 or 3.38.2 would start gnome-initial-setup if gdm3 can't contact the accountservice service via dbus in a timely manner; on Ubuntu (and potentially derivatives) this could be be chained with an additional issue that could allow a local user to create a new privileged account.

code_evidence: Line 8 logs the display being prepared; line 9 calls look_for_existing_users_sync (self) and discards any return value; line 10 then unconditionally computes doing_initial_setup via wants_initial_setup (self), continuing preparation regardless of whether the user lookup succeeded.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-754 fits because the function fails to check an unusual/exceptional condition (lookup failure) and continues normal processing, producing incorrect state. It is not merely a missing exception mechanism; the unchecked exceptional return directly drives the subsequent initial-setup decision.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the return status of look_for_existing_users_sync is not checked, so an exceptional condition (failure to contact the account service via D-Bus) is treated as success. Trigger: accountservice is unavailable or slow, making the lookup fail. Consequence: prepare proceeds and wants_initial_setup runs, which can launch initial setup and allow creation of a privileged account; the failure path is not distinguished from the normal path.

commit_msg:
In vrend clear dispatch function, the 'buffers' is read from
guest. A malicious guest can specify a bad 'buffers' to make
a the function call util_format_is_pure_uint() even the
'ctx->sub->surf[i]' is NULL. This can cause a NULL pointer deref.
Make a sanity check to avoid this.

[airlied: use a define]

Signed-off-by: Li Qiang <liq3ea@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Dave Airlie <airlied@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            if (util_format_is_pure_uint(ctx->sub->surf[i]->format))', '            else if (util_format_is_pure_sint(ctx->sub->surf[i]->format))'], 'added_lines': ['            if (i < PIPE_MAX_COLOR_BUFS && ctx->sub->surf[i] && util_format_is_pure_uint(ctx->sub->surf[i] && ctx->sub->surf[i]->format))', '            else if (i < PIPE_MAX_COLOR_BUFS && ctx->sub->surf[i] && util_format_is_pure_sint(ctx->sub->surf[i] && ctx->sub->surf[i]->format))']}
description: The util_format_is_pure_uint function in vrend_renderer.c in Virgil 3d project (aka virglrenderer) 0.6.0 and earlier allows local guest OS users to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference) via a crafted VIRGL_CCMD_CLEAR command.

code_evidence: Lines 36-39 build a mask only from non-NULL ctx->sub->surf[i] entries, but when that mask differs from buffers>>2, line 41 overwrites it with the guest-supplied buffers>>2. The while loop then scans arbitrary bits, and line 44 dereferences ctx->sub->surf[i]->format without checking that surf[i] is non-NULL; line 47 repeats the same unchecked dereference for the signed path.
The guest-controlled buffers value can set bits for color-buffer indices whose surf[i] is NULL (or beyond nr_cbufs), so the loop reaches a NULL or out-of-range pointer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function directly dereferences ctx->sub->surf[i] without verifying it is non-NULL, which is a NULL pointer dereference (CWE-476). The missing check is the cause; the crash is the consequence. This is not merely an out-of-bounds read, since the primary defect is the unchecked NULL pointer.

evidence_lines.code: else if (util_format_is_pure_sint(ctx->sub->surf[i]->format))

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the guest-controlled buffers mask is trusted after the safe mask is discarded, and surf[i] is dereferenced without a NULL or bounds check. Trigger: a VIRGL_CCMD_CLEAR command with color bits set for an unbound surface slot. Consequence: NULL pointer dereference causing a host crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
Fix jpeg_skip_scanlines() segfault w/merged upsamp

The additional segfault mentioned in #244 was due to the fact that
the merged upsamplers use a different private structure than the
non-merged upsamplers.  jpeg_skip_scanlines() was assuming the latter, so
when merged upsampling was enabled, jpeg_skip_scanlines() clobbered one
of the IDCT method pointers in the merged upsampler's private structure.

For reasons unknown, the test image in #441 did not encounter this
segfault (too small?), but it encountered an issue similar to the one
fixed in 5bc43c7821df982f65aa1c738f67fbf7cba8bd69, whereby it was
necessary to set up a dummy postprocessing function in
read_and_discard_scanlines() when merged upsampling was enabled.
Failing to do so caused either a segfault in merged_2v_upsample() (due
to a NULL pointer being passed to jcopy_sample_rows()) or an error
("Corrupt JPEG data: premature end of data segment"), depending on the
number of scanlines skipped and whether the first scanline skipped was
an odd- or even-numbered row.

Fixes #441
Fixes #244 (for real this time)

Lines 14-17 then read Cr_r_tab, Cb_b_tab, Cr_g_tab and Cb_g_tab through that mismatched type, so the offsets resolve to wrong fields and can yield NULL or garbage pointer values later dereferenced.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits because the incorrect cast leads to dereferencing pointer fields that are not valid for this struct layout, producing a NULL pointer dereference and crash. It is not a simple out-of-bounds read; the defect is using an invalid pointer value obtained from the wrong type.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is a private-structure type mismatch: the merged upsampler's cinfo->upsample is interpreted as the non-merged my_upsample struct. The trigger is decoding with merged upsampling enabled; the misread table pointers are then indexed in the pixel loop, giving a NULL/garbage dereference and crash (or bad memory access).

commit_msg: Fix buffer overrun (issue #678). Add assert for detecting this kind of issues earlier.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '  // make sure that match fits into the data.', '  assert(match_offset + match_length <= callback_args->data_size);']}
description: The yr_arena_write_data function in YARA 3.6.1 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (buffer over-read and application crash) or obtain sensitive information from process memory via a crafted file that is mishandled in the yr_re_fast_exec function in libyara/re.c and the _yr_scan_match_callback function in libyara/scan.c.

code_evidence: match_offset is computed from match_data minus data, and match_length is extended by forward_matches without any bound check against data_size.
The wide-mode full-word check reads *(match_data + match_length) and *(match_data + match_length + 1) after only a '<' comparison against data_size, so the +1 index can equal data_size.
The non-wide full-word check reads *(match_data + match_length) guarded by a strict '<' against data_size.
new_match->data_length is set to min(match_length, MAX_MATCH_DATA) and then match_length bytes are read from match_data into the arena, so an over-long match_length reads past the buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the function reads memory beyond the intended data buffer via match_data indexing and the arena copy, causing DoS or information disclosure. This is an out-of-bounds read, not a write (CWE-787), since the unsafe accesses are loads from match_data.

evidence_lines.code:
size_t match_offset = match_data - callback_args->data;
match_length += callback_args->forward_matches;

if (match_offset + match_length + 1 < callback_args->data_size &&
*(match_data + match_length + 1) == 0 &&
isalnum(*(match_data + match_length)))

if (match_offset + match_length < callback_args->data_size &&
isalnum(*(match_data + match_length)))

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: match_length (extended by forward_matches) and match_offset are used to index match_data without verifying that match_offset + match_length stays within data_size. A crafted file producing a match near the buffer end triggers reads at match_data + match_length (and +1 in wide mode) and a copy of match_length bytes, yielding out-of-bounds reads that crash or leak process memory.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\tmutex_lock(&device->cbuf_lock);', '\tmutex_unlock(&device->cbuf_lock);', '']}
description: roccat_report_event in drivers/hid/hid-roccat.c in the Linux kernel through 5.19.12 has a race condition and resultant use-after-free in certain situations where a report is received while copying a report->value is in progress.

code_evidence: The function indexes the shared ring buffer device->cbuf at device->cbuf_end, frees the previous report->value with kfree, installs new_value, then advances cbuf_end. No lock protects cbuf or report->value during this sequence, so a concurrent roccat_read() holding a pointer to the same report can be freed underneath it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs a non-atomic, unsynchronized read-modify-write on a shared resource (cbuf entry) that another code sequence concurrently accesses, which is exactly CWE-362. The UAF is the resulting consequence, not the labeled weakness itself.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the report buffer slot and its value pointer are mutated without exclusive access. Trigger: a new report arrives while roccat_read() is copying report->value to user space; the kfree(report->value) at [12] races with that copy. Consequence: use-after-free read of freed memory, potentially leaking or corrupting data.

commit_msg:
floppy_revalidate() doesn't perform any error handling on lock_fdc()
result. lock_fdc() might actually be interrupted by a signal (it waits for
fdc becoming non-busy interruptibly). In such case, floppy_revalidate()
proceeds as if it had claimed the lock, but it fact it doesn't.

In case of multiple threads trying to open("/dev/fdX"), this leads to
serious corruptions all over the place, because all of a sudden there is
no critical section protection (that'd otherwise be guaranteed by locked
fd) whatsoever.

While at this, fix the fact that the 'interruptible' parameter to
lock_fdc() doesn't make any sense whatsoever, because we always wait
interruptibly anyway.

Most of the lock_fdc() callsites do properly handle error (and propagate
EINTR), but floppy_revalidate() and floppy_check_events() don't. Fix this.

Spotted by 'syzkaller' tool.

Reported-by: Dmitry Vyukov <dvyukov@google.com>
Tested-by: Dmitry Vyukov <dvyukov@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Jiri Kosina <jkosina@suse.cz>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (lock_fdc(drive, interruptible))'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (lock_fdc(drive))']}
description: A race condition was found in the Linux kernels implementation of the floppy disk drive controller driver software. The impact of this issue is lessened by the fact that the default permissions on the floppy device (/dev/fd0) are restricted to root. If the permissions on the device have changed the impact changes greatly. In the default configuration root (or equivalent) permissions are required to attack this flaw.

code_evidence: lock_fdc(drive, interruptible) is checked and returns -EINTR on failure, but the fix removes the interruptible argument; the pre-fix call could fail after an interruptible wait.

On failure the function returns -EINTR before process_fd_request(); however the commit states floppy_revalidate() (and check_events) proceeded without holding the lock, so the critical section is not actually protected.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing synchronization on the shared FDC lock lets an interfering concurrent sequence access the same resource, matching CWE-362's exclusivity violation. This is a race condition, not merely a resource leak or improper error return.

evidence_lines.code:
if (lock_fdc(drive, interruptible))
return -EINTR;
process_fd_request();

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: lock_fdc() waits interruptibly and can be interrupted by a signal, returning an error while the caller proceeds as if the lock were held. Trigger: multiple threads open /dev/fdX concurrently and a signal interrupts the lock wait. Consequence: the critical section loses exclusivity, allowing concurrent modification of shared controller state and serious corruption.

commit_msg:
pcnet: fix rx buffer overflow(CVE-2015-7512)

Backends could provide a packet whose length is greater than buffer
size. Check for this and truncate the packet to avoid rx buffer
overflow in this case.

Cc: Prasad J Pandit <pjp@fedoraproject.org>
Cc: qemu-stable@nongnu.org
Reviewed-by: Michael S. Tsirkin <mst@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Jason Wang <jasowang@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['                if (size > 4092) {', '#ifdef PCNET_DEBUG_RMD', '                    fprintf(stderr, "pcnet: truncates rx packet.\\n");', '#endif', '                    size = 4092;', '                }']}
description: Buffer overflow in the pcnet_receive function in hw/net/pcnet.c in QEMU, when a guest NIC has a larger MTU, allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (guest OS crash) or execute arbitrary code via a large packet.

code_evidence: At line 61, memcpy(src, buf, size) copies the caller-supplied packet of length size into s->buffer without bounding size; lines 62-66 then write src[size] through src[size+3] and add 4 to size, so any size near the buffer capacity overflows past s->buffer.
size is derived from the external size_ parameter at line 8 and is only rejected for zero/loop conditions at lines 9-12; no upper bound on size is enforced before the copy.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This is a classic buffer copy without input-size validation: memcpy writes size bytes into a fixed destination without verifying size fits, matching CWE-120. It is not merely an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125), since the defect is the unchecked write.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: a packet length controlled by the backend/guest is copied into the fixed s->buffer with no upper-bound check, and the trailing zero/CRC writes extend the overflow. Trigger: a packet larger than the receive buffer reaches this branch. Consequence: out-of-bounds writes corrupt adjacent memory, enabling guest crash or potential code execution.

'node_info->vdev_port.name' should be checked.

Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

description: An issue was discovered in get_vdev_port_node_info in arch/sparc/kernel/mdesc.c in the Linux kernel through 5.1.6. There is an unchecked kstrdup_const of node_info->vdev_port.name, which might allow an attacker to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference and system crash).

commit_msg: X3F parser possible buffer overrun
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['static char *utf2char(utf16_t *str, char *buffer)', '  while (*str != 0x00) {', '  return buffer;'], 'added_lines': ['void utf2char(utf16_t *str, char *buffer, unsigned bufsz)', ' if(bufsz<1) return;', ' buffer[bufsz-1] = 0;', '  while (*str != 0x00 && --bufsz>0)', '  {']}
description: An issue was discovered in LibRaw 0.18.9. There is a stack-based buffer overflow in the utf2char function in libraw_cxx.cpp.

code_evidence: Line 3 aliases the destination as b = buffer. The loop at line 4 advances while *str is nonzero with no bound on the number of iterations. Lines 5-6 cast each utf16_t element to char* and write one byte via *b++ per iteration, so b advances once per input character. Line 9 then writes a terminating NUL at the current b position. Nothing constrains the write count to the destination capacity, so the loop and the final terminator can write past the end of buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes data past the end of the intended buffer, which is exactly CWE-787 (Out-of-bounds Write). The missing length constraint is the cause; the memory corruption is the consequence. A related CWE-125 would involve reading out of bounds, whereas here the unsafe operation is the unbounded write via *b++ and the terminator.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the copy loop lacks a destination-size limit, so output length is driven solely by the input string length. Trigger: a long or unterminated utf16_t input passed with a buffer smaller than the encoded output. Consequence: out-of-bounds writes beyond buffer, corrupting adjacent stack memory and potentially enabling code execution or a crash.

commit_msg:

description: Gobby 0.4.11 allows a NULL pointer dereference in the D-Bus handler for certain set_language calls.

code_evidence: Only a g_assert guards m_current_view before it is used; in builds where assertions are disabled (NDEBUG) the check is removed entirely, so a NULL m_current_view proceeds unguarded.
m_current_view is dereferenced to obtain the text buffer, session, active user and undo grouping; all of these operate on the pointer's target object.
Further dereferences occur at signal_handler_disconnect, gtk_text_buffer_get_iter_at_mark, select_range, delete_mark and scroll_to_cursor_position, each assuming m_current_view is valid.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits because the code dereferences a pointer expected to be valid but that can be NULL, and the fix replaces the assert with an explicit NULL check plus return. This is a null-check omission, not a use-after-free or type confusion.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function relies solely on g_assert to validate m_current_view, which is compiled out in release builds, so an unset current view (e.g. redo invoked via D-Bus with no document open) is dereferenced. Trigger: on_redo called when m_current_view is NULL. Consequence: NULL pointer dereference causing a crash (DoS).

commit_msg: fix #751
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    m_Data.SetDataSize((AP4_Size)size-GetHeaderSize());', '    stream.Read(m_Data.UseData(), m_Data.GetDataSize());'], 'added_lines': ['    AP4_Size header_size = GetHeaderSize();', '    if (size > header_size) {', '        m_Data.SetDataSize((AP4_Size)size-GetHeaderSize());', '        stream.Read(m_Data.UseData(), m_Data.GetDataSize());', '    }']}
description: Buffer overflow vulnerability in function AP4_MemoryByteStream::WritePartial in mp42aac in Bento4 v1.6.0-639, allows attackers to cause a denial of service via a crafted file.

code_evidence: The constructor computes the destination size as (AP4_Size)size-GetHeaderSize() without checking that size exceeds the header size, then passes UseData() and GetDataSize() to stream.Read, which writes into the buffer sized by that unchecked expression.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function copies stream input into a destination buffer whose size is not validated against the input-derived length, matching CWE-120's buffer copy without input size checking. This is a write-side overflow, not merely an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125).

evidence_lines.code:
m_Data.SetDataSize((AP4_Size)size-GetHeaderSize());
stream.Read(m_Data.UseData(), m_Data.GetDataSize());

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the buffer size is derived from an attacker-controlled 64-bit size field minus the header size with no lower-bound check. If size is smaller than GetHeaderSize(), the unsigned subtraction underflows, producing a huge AP4_Size; SetDataSize may fail or allocate inconsistently, and stream.Read then writes attacker-controlled stream bytes into an undersized or invalid buffer, causing memory corruption and denial of service.

description: Asterisk is an open source private branch exchange and telephony toolkit. In Asterisk prior to versions 18.20.1, 20.5.1, and 21.0.1; as well as certified-asterisk prior to 18.9-cert6; Asterisk is susceptible to a DoS due to a race condition in the hello handshake phase of the DTLS protocol when handling DTLS-SRTP for media setup. This attack can be done continuously, thus denying new DTLS-SRTP encrypted calls during the attack. Abuse of this vulnerability may lead to a massive Denial of Service on vulnerable Asterisk servers for calls that rely on DTLS-SRTP. Commit d7d7764cb07c8a1872804321302ef93bf62cba05 contains a fix, which is part of versions 18.20.1, 20.5.1, 21.0.1, amd 18.9-cert6.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The shown function only adds source-address validation against the ICE candidate list to reject unexpected DTLS packets; it contains no concurrent shared-resource access or timing window demonstrating a race condition.

commit_msg:
evtchn: address races with evtchn_reset()

Neither d->evtchn_port_ops nor max_evtchns(d) may be used in an entirely
lock-less manner, as both may change by a racing evtchn_reset(). In the
common case, at least one of the domain's event lock or the per-channel
lock needs to be held. In the specific case of the inter-domain sending
by evtchn_send() and notify_via_xen_event_channel() holding the other
side's per-channel lock is sufficient, as the channel can't change state
without both per-channel locks held. Without such a channel changing
state, evtchn_reset() can't complete successfully.

Lock-free accesses continue to be permitted for the shim (calling some
otherwise internal event channel functions), as this happens while the
domain is in effectively single-threaded mode. Special care also needs
taking for the shim's marking of in-use ports as ECS_RESERVED (allowing
use of such ports in the shim case is okay because switching into and
hence also out of FIFO mode is impossihble there).

As a side effect, certain operations on Xen bound event channels which
were mistakenly permitted so far (e.g. unmask or poll) will be refused
now.

This is part of XSA-343.

Reported-by: Julien Grall <jgrall@amazon.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Acked-by: Julien Grall <jgrall@amazon.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['        unsigned long flags;', '        spin_lock_irqsave(&chn->lock, flags);', '        spin_unlock_irqrestore(&chn->lock, flags);']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.14.x. There are evtchn_reset() race conditions. Uses of EVTCHNOP_reset (potentially by a guest on itself) or XEN_DOMCTL_soft_reset (by itself covered by XSA-77) can lead to the violation of various internal assumptions. This may lead to out of bounds memory accesses or triggering of bug checks. In particular, x86 PV guests may be able to elevate their privilege to that of the host. Host and guest crashes are also possible, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS). Information leaks cannot be ruled out. All Xen versions from 4.5 onwards are vulnerable. Xen versions 4.4 and earlier are not vulnerable.

code_evidence: The function fetches the channel via evtchn_from_port(guest, port) and immediately reads chn->notify_vcpu_id and mutates the channel through evtchn_port_set_pending() without holding chn->lock; the port-validity check and channel lookup are not serialized against a concurrent evtchn_reset().
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The code performs a check-then-use sequence on a shared event-channel resource that another concurrent sequence (evtchn_reset) can modify, violating exclusivity/atomicity; this is precisely a race condition (CWE-362), not a mere missing bounds check.

evidence_lines.code:
struct evtchn *chn = evtchn_from_port(guest, port);
evtchn_port_set_pending(guest, chn->notify_vcpu_id, chn);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the shared evtchn structure and port mapping are accessed without the per-channel lock, so a racing evtchn_reset() can change channel state or the port mapping between the validity check and the pending update. Trigger: a guest issuing EVTCHNOP_reset while another path injects/sends on the port. Consequence: stale or invalid channel use leading to out-of-bounds access, bug checks, host/guest crash, or privilege escalation.

description: nf_tables_newset in net/netfilter/nf_tables_api.c in the Linux kernel before 5.12.13 allows local users to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference and general protection fault) because of the missing initialization for nft_set_elem_expr_alloc. A local user can set a netfilter table expression in their own namespace.

code_evidence: At lines 154-161, nft_set_elem_expr_alloc(&ctx, set, nla[NFTA_SET_EXPR]) is called and its result stored in set->exprs[0] before the set is initialized.

The set fields, including set->flags, are only assigned later at lines 194-204, after expression allocation. nft_set_elem_expr_alloc reads set->flags to test NFT_EXPR_GC, so it observes the zeroed kvzalloc buffer instead of the requested flags.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is improper initialization: a resource (the set) is accessed before its fields are set, matching CWE-665. The consequence is availability impact from the crash, not a separate memory-safety CWE.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the set is used by nft_set_elem_expr_alloc before set->flags (and other fields) are initialized. Trigger: a local user creates a set carrying NFTA_SET_EXPR with the NFT_SET_EVAL flag. The GC flag check reads uninitialized set state, leading to a NULL pointer dereference and kernel crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
media: stv06xx: add missing descriptor sanity checks

Make sure to check that we have two alternate settings and at least one
endpoint before accessing the second altsetting structure and
dereferencing the endpoint arrays.

This specifically avoids dereferencing NULL-pointers or corrupting
memory when a device does not have the expected descriptors.

Note that the sanity checks in stv06xx_start() and pb0100_start() are
not redundant as the driver is mixing looking up altsettings by index
and by number, which may not coincide.

Fixes: 8668d504d72c ("V4L/DVB (12082): gspca_stv06xx: Add support for st6422 bridge and sensor")
Fixes: c0b33bdc5b8d ("[media] gspca-stv06xx: support bandwidth changing")
Cc: stable <stable@vger.kernel.org>     # 2.6.31
Cc: Hans de Goede <hdegoede@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Johan Hovold <johan@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Hans Verkuil <hverkuil-cisco@xs4all.nl>
Signed-off-by: Mauro Carvalho Chehab <mchehab+huawei@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\tif (alt->desc.bNumEndpoints < 1)', '\t\treturn -ENODEV;']}
description: An issue was discovered in the stv06xx subsystem in the Linux kernel before 5.6.1. drivers/media/usb/gspca/stv06xx/stv06xx.c and drivers/media/usb/gspca/stv06xx/stv06xx_pb0100.c mishandle invalid descriptors, as demonstrated by a NULL pointer dereference, aka CID-485b06aadb93.

code_evidence: usb_altnum_to_altsetting() returns an alternate setting whose endpoint array may be empty; only the NULL return of alt itself is checked at line 9. Line 13 then unconditionally dereferences alt->endpoint[0].desc.wMaxPacketSize without verifying that alt->desc.bNumEndpoints >= 1, so a device descriptor with zero endpoints leaves endpoint[0] invalid.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences alt->endpoint[0] while relying only on the earlier alt NULL check, so an out-of-range endpoint element is treated as valid. This directly matches CWE-476 (NULL Pointer Dereference). It is not merely a bounds/index issue, since the unchecked descriptor count makes the endpoint element dereference invalid.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: missing validation that the selected altsetting contains at least one endpoint before indexing endpoint[0]. Trigger: a malicious or malformed USB device supplies an altsetting with bNumEndpoints == 0; stv06xx_start() proceeds past the NULL check and dereferences endpoint[0]. Supported consequence: invalid/NULL pointer dereference leading to a kernel crash (denial of service).

description: The kernel in Amazon Web Services FreeRTOS before 10.4.3 has insufficient bounds checking during management of heap memory.

code_evidence: xWantedSize (caller-controlled size_t) is incremented by xHeapStructSize at line 19 and again by the alignment padding at line 22 without any overflow check; if the addition wraps, xWantedSize becomes a small value that passes the non-zero/alignment assertions.

The wrapped xWantedSize is then compared against xFreeBytesRemaining (line 34) and used to locate and split a free block: line 49 computes pxNewBlockLink as pxBlock + xWantedSize, line 51 writes pxNewBlockLink->xBlockSize, and line 52 sets pxBlock->xBlockSize = xWantedSize, so the block accounting is based on the truncated size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect is an unchecked size computation that lets the allocation logic operate with a buffer length outside the intended boundary, so subsequent use writes past the allocated region, matching CWE-119. The underlying arithmetic flaw is an integer overflow, but the supported consequence here is out-of-bounds memory operation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: integer overflow in the size arithmetic at lines 19 and 22 when xWantedSize is near SIZE_MAX. Trigger: a caller requests a very large allocation. The wrapped small size passes the bound check at line 34 and is used to split the free block, so the heap metadata (xBlockSize at lines 51-52) and the returned buffer are sized inconsistently with the real request, allowing later writes beyond the intended allocation.
