Consequence: dereferencing testEnv or testEnv->devices leads to a NULL pointer dereference and crash/DoS; the patch switches to AcquireCriticalMemory to abort on failure.

commit_msg:
CVE-2017-13045/VQP: add some bounds checks

This fixes a buffer over-read discovered by Bhargava Shastry,
SecT/TU Berlin.

Add a test using the capture file supplied by the reporter(s).
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    int tlen;'], 'added_lines': ['    u_int tlen;', '    if (sizeof(struct vqp_common_header_t) > tlen)', '        goto trunc;', '        ND_TCHECK(*vqp_obj_tlv);', '        if (sizeof(struct vqp_obj_tlv_t) > tlen)', '            goto trunc;', '        if (vqp_obj_len > tlen)', '            goto trunc;', '            if (vqp_obj_len != 4)', '                goto trunc;', '            if (vqp_obj_len != ETHER_ADDR_LEN)', '                goto trunc;']}
description: The VQP parser in tcpdump before 4.9.2 has a buffer over-read in print-vqp.c:vqp_print().

code_evidence: tlen is an int initialized from len; the header pointer is dereferenced after ND_TCHECK without ensuring sizeof(vqp_common_header_t) <= tlen, so a short packet can be read past the buffer.

The while loop dereferences vqp_obj_tlv and reads obj_type/obj_length without first checking that a full TLV header is within tlen, and subtracts the header size from tlen without a prior bounds check.

ND_TCHECK2(*tptr, vqp_obj_len) checks capture availability but not that vqp_obj_len fits within remaining tlen; the IP_ADDRESS case then calls ipaddr_string/EXTRACT_32BITS on tptr regardless of the declared object length.
The MAC cases call etheraddr_string(ndo, tptr) without verifying vqp_obj_len equals ETHER_ADDR_LEN, so a short object length still causes a fixed-size read.
tptr and tlen are advanced by vqp_obj_len without ensuring the length does not exceed the remaining buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is reading beyond the intended buffer boundary due to missing length constraints, which directly matches CWE-125 Out-of-bounds Read. It is not CWE-787 (out-of-bounds write) because the code only reads; ND_TCHECK guards capture availability, not logical length consistency.

evidence_lines.code:
tptr += vqp_obj_len;
tlen -= vqp_obj_len;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the parser trusts header and TLV length fields without verifying they fit within the remaining packet length (tlen). Triggering a VQP packet with a short header, truncated TLV header, or an object length smaller than the fixed-size read causes ipaddr_string, EXTRACT_32BITS, or etheraddr_string to read past the captured buffer, yielding an out-of-bounds read (potential info disclosure or crash).

commit_msg: fix #2963 - oob write (1 byte) in pyc/marshal.c
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tut32 size = 0;', '\tif (error) {', '\tsize = rz_buf_read(buffer, s1, n1);', '\tif (size != n1) {', '\t} else', '\tif (error) {', '\tsize = rz_buf_read(buffer, s2, n2);', '\tif (size != n2) {'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (error || UT32_ADD_OVFCHK(n1, 1)) {', '\tif (rz_buf_read(buffer, s1, n1) != n1) {', '\t} else {', '\t}', '\tif (error || UT32_ADD_OVFCHK(n2, 1)) {', '\tif (rz_buf_read(buffer, s2, n2) != n2) {']}
description: Rizin is a UNIX-like reverse engineering framework and command-line toolset. Versions 0.4.0 and prior are vulnerable to an out-of-bounds write when getting data from PYC(python) files. A user opening a malicious PYC file could be affected by this vulnerability, allowing an attacker to execute code on the user's machine. Commit number 68948017423a12786704e54227b8b2f918c2fd27 contains a patch.

code_evidence: n1 is read from the file as either a byte or a 32-bit value; only the error flag is checked, not whether n1 is near UINT32_MAX, so the subsequent n1+1 allocation size can wrap.
malloc(n1 + 1) uses the attacker-controlled n1; if n1 == 0xFFFFFFFF the addition wraps to 0, yielding a tiny buffer, but the read and terminator write below still use the original n1.
s1[n1] = '\0' writes at offset n1 into the buffer allocated with the wrapped size, producing a one-byte out-of-bounds write.
The same pattern repeats for n2: n2+1 allocation followed by s2[n2] = '\0', again without an overflow check on the attacker-controlled length.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes data (the '\0' terminator) past the end of an allocated buffer, which is the definition of CWE-787. The integer wrap in n1 + 1 is the enabling cause, but the supported weakness is the out-of-bounds write at s1[n1]/s2[n2].
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: attacker-controlled 32-bit length fields n1/n2 are incremented for allocation without overflow checking. When a length is UINT32_MAX, n1 + 1 wraps to 0 so malloc returns a small buffer, yet the code writes the NUL terminator at s1[n1] (and s2[n2]), writing past the allocation. Trigger: opening a malicious PYC file with such a length. Consequence: a one-byte heap out-of-bounds write, potentially leading to memory corruption or code execution.

description: In Wireshark 2.4.0 to 2.4.12 and 2.6.0 to 2.6.6, the ASN.1 BER and related dissectors could crash. This was addressed in epan/dissectors/packet-ber.c by preventing a buffer overflow associated with excessive digits in time values.

code_evidence: After sscanf fills first_digits, the '.'/',' branch only rejects ret==2; a four-digit value (e.g. 1234) passes and is written via "%c%.3d" into strptr with a 5-byte limit, but strptr already advanced past the fixed 20-byte prefix written by g_snprintf at line 70, so the 4-digit fraction overflows the str[35] destination.
The '+'/'-' branch likewise only checks ret==2 and writes " (UTC%c%.4d)" with a 12-byte limit using first_digits, allowing excessive digits to exceed the remaining buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked 4-digit first_digits value causes g_snprintf to write beyond the str[35] stack buffer, directly matching CWE-787 (write past the end of the intended buffer). This is an out-of-bounds write, not merely an integer overflow; the overflow enables the write.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: sscanf's %4d accepts up to four digits into first_digits, but the code only rejects the no-fraction case (ret==2) and never constrains first_digits to 0-999. Trigger: a GeneralizedTime with a 4-digit fraction or offset. Consequence: g_snprintf writes past str[35], causing an out-of-bounds write that can crash the dissector.

commit_msg:
A security advisory (TALOS-2019-0857/CVE-2019-5068) found that
creating shared memory regions with permission mode 0777 could allow
any user to access that memory.  Several Mesa drivers use shared-
memory XImages to implement back buffers for improved performance.

This path changes the shmget() calls to use 0600 (user r/w).

Tested with legacy Xlib driver and llvmpipe.

Cc: mesa-stable@lists.freedesktop.org
Reviewed-by: Kristian H. Kristensen <hoegsberg@google.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t     * b->backxrb->ximage->height, IPC_CREAT|0777);'], 'added_lines': ['   /* 0600 = user read+write */', '                             * b->backxrb->ximage->height, IPC_CREAT | 0600);']}
description: An exploitable shared memory permissions vulnerability exists in the functionality of X11 Mesa 3D Graphics Library 19.1.2. An attacker can access the shared memory without any specific permissions to trigger this vulnerability.

code_evidence: shmget() is called with IPC_CREAT|0777, creating the shared-memory segment with world read/write/execute permissions for all users.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-732 fits because the code assigns overly permissive access rights (0777) to a critical resource (the shared-memory back buffer), allowing unintended actors to read or modify it. This is a permission-assignment flaw, distinct from a missing authorization check.

evidence_lines.code:
b->shminfo.shmid = shmget(IPC_PRIVATE, b->backxrb->ximage->bytes_per_line
* b->backxrb->ximage->height, IPC_CREAT|0777);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The shared-memory back buffer is created with mode 0777, so any local user can attach to the segment and read or modify the rendered image data. The unsafe permission is applied at segment creation; the consequence is exposure and tampering of the buffer contents by unintended actors.

commit_msg:
Fix null pointer dereference in getName/getString

Whenever getString or getName are called with an act such that act->p.String
is a NULL pointer, a NULL pointer dereference might happen
(strlen(act->p.string) is called).

In this commit we add checks at the beginning of the PUSH_STRING block so
that a warning is displayed and an empty string is returned in this case.

This patch fixes #121.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (!act->p.String) /* Not a NULL string */', '\t\t{', '\t\t        SWF_warn("WARNING: Call to getString with NULL string.\\n");', '\t\t        break;', '\t\t}']}
description: The pushdup function in util/decompile.c in libming through 0.4.8 does not recognize the need for ActionPushDuplicate to perform a deep copy when a String is at the top of the stack, making the library vulnerable to a util/decompile.c getName NULL pointer dereference, which may allow attackers to cause a denial of service via a crafted SWF file.

code_evidence: In the PUSH_STRING case, the code calls strlen(act->p.String) at line 11 and strcat(t,act->p.String) at line 13 without first checking whether act->p.String is non-NULL. If a crafted SWF causes a PUSH_STRING action whose p.String pointer is NULL, these calls dereference the NULL pointer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits because the function dereferences a pointer it expects to be valid but that can be NULL, and the supported impact is a DoS crash. This is a NULL dereference defect, not a buffer overflow or use-after-free; the unchecked strlen/strcat on act->p.String is the direct cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the PUSH_STRING branch assumes act->p.String is always a valid, non-NULL pointer. Trigger: a decompiled push action of type PUSH_STRING carrying a NULL string pointer (e.g., produced when pushdup fails to deep-copy a String). Consequence: strlen/strcat dereference NULL, causing a crash and denial of service; the patch's own warning-and-break confirms the missing check.

commit_msg:
When opening files for write, ensure they aren't symbolic links

Issue #1048 identified that if, for example, a non privileged user
created a symbolic link from /etc/keepalvied.data to /etc/passwd,
writing to /etc/keepalived.data (which could be invoked via DBus)
would cause /etc/passwd to be overwritten.

This commit stops keepalived writing to pathnames where the ultimate
component is a symbolic link, by setting O_NOFOLLOW whenever opening
a file for writing.

This might break some setups, where, for example, /etc/keepalived.data
was a symbolic link to /home/fred/keepalived.data. If this was the case,
instead create a symbolic link from /home/fred/keepalived.data to
/tmp/keepalived.data, so that the file is still accessible via
/home/fred/keepalived.data.

There doesn't appear to be a way around this backward incompatibility,
since even checking if the pathname is a symbolic link prior to opening
for writing would create a race condition.

Signed-off-by: Quentin Armitage <quentin@armitage.org.uk>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tint pidfd = creat(pid_file, S_IRUSR | S_IWUSR | S_IRGRP | S_IROTH);'], 'added_lines': ['\tint pidfd = open(pid_file, O_NOFOLLOW | O_CREAT | O_WRONLY | O_TRUNC, S_IRUSR | S_IWUSR | S_IRGRP | S_IROTH);']}
description: keepalived 2.0.8 didn't check for pathnames with symlinks when writing data to a temporary file upon a call to PrintData or PrintStats. This allowed local users to overwrite arbitrary files if fs.protected_symlinks is set to 0, as demonstrated by a symlink from /tmp/keepalived.data or /tmp/keepalived.stats to /etc/passwd.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function writes a PID to a pidfile using creat(); the patch adds O_NOFOLLOW, which concerns symlink-following file writes (CWE-59/arbitrary file overwrite), not exposure of sensitive information to unauthorized actors.

In summary, this patch solves those use-after-free by

1. Re-implement the nfc_llcp_find_local(). The current version does not
grab the reference when getting the local from the linked list.  For
example, the llcp_sock_bind() gets the reference like below:

// llcp_sock_bind()

    local = nfc_llcp_find_local(dev); // A
    ..... \
           | raceable
    ..... /
    llcp_sock->local = nfc_llcp_local_get(local); // B

There is an apparent race window that one can  drop the reference
and free the local object fetched in (A) before (B) gets the reference.

2. Some callers of the nfc_llcp_find_local() do not grab the reference
at all. For example, the nfc_genl_llc_{{get/set}_params/sdreq} functions.
We add the nfc_llcp_local_put() for them. Moreover, we add the necessary
error handling function to put the reference.

3. Add the nfc_llcp_remove_local() helper. The local object is removed
from the linked list in local_release() when all reference is gone. This
patch removes it when nfc_llcp_unregister_device() is called.

Therefore, every caller of nfc_llcp_find_local() will get a reference
even when the nfc_llcp_unregister_device() is called. This promises no
use-after-free for the local object is ever possible.

description: A use-after-free flaw was found in nfc_llcp_find_local in net/nfc/llcp_core.c in NFC in the Linux kernel. This flaw allows a local user with special privileges to impact a kernel information leak issue.

code_evidence: nfc_llcp_find_local(dev) returns a local pointer without holding a reference; NULL is checked before use.
The returned local is dereferenced to store target_idx, comm_mode and rf_mode, and later used to arm the link timer.
Because no reference is retained on local, a concurrent nfc_llcp_unregister_device can release the last reference and free it while these accesses are in flight.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits: the function dereferences and passes to mod_timer a local pointer that can already be freed because no reference is held; this is a lifetime/reference-counting flaw, not merely a NULL-pointer bug.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: nfc_llcp_find_local returns a list entry without acquiring a reference, so the caller uses a pointer not protected against concurrent release. Trigger: device unregister calls local_release, kfree-ing the local between lookup and dereference. Consequence: reads/writes through the freed local (target_idx, timer) cause a use-after-free.

commit_msg: Fix a crash in the TGA loader with malformed input
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\t\tif (output_pos + count * p_pixel_size > output_pos) {', '\t\t\treturn ERR_PARSE_ERROR;', '\t\t}']}
description: A stack overflow issue exists in Godot Engine up to v3.2 and is caused by improper boundary checks when loading .TGA image files. Depending on the context of the application, attack vector can be local or remote, and can lead to code execution and/or system crash.

code_evidence: The loop condition only checks output_pos < p_output_size before consuming the RLE header byte and computing count = (c & 0x7f) + 1, so the run length is unbounded relative to remaining output space.

In the run branch, count pixels of p_pixel_size bytes are written to p_uncompressed_buffer[output_pos + j] while output_pos advances by p_pixel_size each iteration, with no check that output_pos + count*p_pixel_size stays within p_output_size.
In the raw branch, count *= p_pixel_size and the loop writes p_uncompressed_buffer[output_pos] incrementing one byte at a time, again without verifying the total run against p_output_size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs writes to p_uncompressed_buffer at output_pos + j and output_pos that can exceed the intended buffer size, which is precisely an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). The missing length constraint is the direct write-boundary defect, not merely an integer overflow or read overrun.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the per-iteration loop guard checks only the starting output_pos, not the full run length, so a malformed RLE count from the file drives writes beyond p_uncompressed_buffer. Trigger: a crafted TGA whose control byte encodes a count larger than the remaining output size. Consequence: out-of-bounds writes past the intended buffer, causing memory corruption and potential crash or code execution.

xhci: guard xhci_kick_epctx against recursive calls

Track xhci_kick_epctx processing being active in a variable.  Check the
variable before calling xhci_kick_epctx from xhci_kick_ep.  Add an
assert to make sure we don't call recursively into xhci_kick_epctx.

Cc: 1653384@bugs.launchpad.net
Fixes: 94b037f2a451b3dc855f9f2c346e5049a361bd55

Message-id: 1485790607-31399-5-git-send-email-kraxel@redhat.com
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    if (epctx->kick_active) {', '        return;', '    }']}
description: QEMU (aka Quick Emulator), when built with USB xHCI controller emulator support, allows local guest OS privileged users to cause a denial of service (infinite recursive call) via vectors involving control transfer descriptors sequencing.

code_evidence: Line 17 calls xhci_kick_epctx(epctx, streamid) unconditionally after the disabled-slot and null-endpoint guards; the function itself has no recursion guard, so a re-entrant call path through xhci_kick_epctx can recurse without a terminating condition.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The reachable exit condition for the repeated xhci_kick_epctx invocation is effectively never satisfied, producing an infinite recursive loop that exhausts resources. This matches CWE-835's unreachable exit condition; it is not merely an unbounded resource allocation, since the defect is the missing termination of the recursive call cycle.

evidence_lines.code: xhci_kick_epctx(epctx, streamid);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: xhci_kick_ep lacks any check preventing re-entry into xhci_kick_epctx for an endpoint already being processed. Trigger: guest-supplied control transfer descriptor sequencing causes xhci_kick_epctx to invoke xhci_kick_ep again on the same epctx. Consequence: unbounded recursion consuming CPU/stack until resource exhaustion (DoS).

commit_msg:
Force unsilence record clients on startInput

We call startRecording unconditionally in startInput, so we must
update the client state to be unsilenced (since we are treating as
such). We subsequently re-update the silence state (with the client
marked as active to dispatch ops) in updateUidStates_l.

This fixes an issue where we call startRecording for a silenced client,
then call it again when it moves to unsilenced when the client is active.
Since startRecording is ref-counted, this leaves the client in the
recording state leading to incorrect appop attributions.

Bug: 279905816
Bug: 281485019
Test: Manual verification of repro cases + verbose log analysis
(cherry picked from https://googleplex-android-review.googlesource.com/q/commit:e7720b379bfaba648ab6d85c4c2df6f03ec854d3)
(cherry picked from https://googleplex-android-review.googlesource.com/q/commit:2951ad10a6641f9b3554d674877ad314e8cc011f)
Merged-In: I31d50457ca8adae577407a28d4d4c0e8582bac5d
Change-Id: I31d50457ca8adae577407a28d4d4c0e8582bac5d
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    ALOGW_IF(client->silenced, "startInput on silenced input for port %d, uid %d. Unsilencing.",', '            portIdAidl,', '            client->attributionSource.uid);', '', '    if (client->active) {', '        ALOGE("Client should never be active before startInput. Uid %d port %d",', '                client->attributionSource.uid, portId);', '        finishRecording(client->attributionSource, client->attributes.source);', '        return binderStatusFromStatusT(INVALID_OPERATION);', '    }', '', '    // Force the possibly silenced client to be unsilenced since we just called', '    // startRecording (i.e. we have assumed it is unsilenced).', '    // At this point in time, the client is inactive, so no calls to appops are sent in', '    // setAppState_l.', '    // This ensures existing clients have the same behavior as new clients (starting unsilenced).', '    // TODO(b/282076713)', '    setAppState_l(client, APP_STATE_TOP);', '', '    // This call updates the silenced state, and since we are active, appropriately notifies appops', '    // if we silence the track.']}
description: In startInput of AudioPolicyInterfaceImpl.cpp, there is a possible way of erroneously displaying the microphone privacy indicator due to a race condition. This could lead to false user expectations. User interaction is needed for exploitation.

code_evidence: The record client is looked up and copied out of mAudioRecordClients under mLock, but the lock is released at the end of this block before startRecording is called.

startRecording (a ref-counted operation) is invoked outside mLock on the client obtained earlier; between the lookup and this call, another thread could alter the same client's state or recording refcount.
The lock is only reacquired afterward to set client->active, startTimeNs and call updateUidStates_l, so the recording start and the client's active/silenced bookkeeping are not performed atomically.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is a timing window where shared client state and the ref-counted recording resource are accessed without exclusive, atomic synchronization, matching CWE-362. The consequence is incorrect privacy-indicator state rather than a pure logic bug, since the defect depends on concurrent interleaving.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the client lookup, the ref-counted startRecording, and the subsequent active-state update are split across separate lock scopes, so no single critical section covers them. Trigger: concurrent startInput/stopInput or state updates on the same port interleave between the lookup and the active/updateUidStates_l update, causing the refcount and silenced/active state to diverge. Supported consequence: the client can remain in the recording state with incorrect appop attribution, erroneously showing the microphone privacy indicator.

DOF: fix an infinite loop in sid_buffer_hash_fn()

The sid buffer can contain up to 255 bytes of data, so the loop counter must
be a guint16 at least.

Bug: 13453
Change-Id: I997ce1a737532d94796586d7e109d89b2dc1911b
Reviewed-on: https://code.wireshark.org/review/20388

(cherry picked from commit c3dde590d8226bdb19149013acf9d45781adbd16)
Reviewed-on: https://code.wireshark.org/review/20390
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    guint8 i;'], 'added_lines': ['    guint16 i;']}
description: In Wireshark 2.2.0 to 2.2.5, the DOF dissector could go into an infinite loop, triggered by packet injection or a malformed capture file. This was addressed in epan/dissectors/packet-dof.c by using a different integer data type and adjusting a return value.

When str[0] equals 255, i increments from 255 and wraps back to 0, so the condition i <= 255 remains true forever; the loop never exits.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-835 fits because the loop's exit condition i <= str[0] becomes unreachable due to integer wraparound of the guint8 counter, producing an infinite loop. This is distinct from an out-of-bounds read, which is not the primary weakness here.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the 8-bit loop counter cannot represent a value greater than the length byte, so the increment wraps around instead of terminating. Trigger: a SID buffer whose length byte is 255. Supported consequence: the loop iterates indefinitely, consuming CPU and causing a denial of service.

commit_msg:
When we take an FP unavailable exception in a transaction we have to
account for the hardware FP TM checkpointed registers being
incorrect. In this case for this process we know the current and
checkpointed FP registers must be the same (since FP wasn't used
inside the transaction) hence in the thread_struct we copy the current
FP registers to the checkpointed ones.

This copy is done in tm_reclaim_thread(). We use thread->ckpt_regs.msr
to determine if FP was on when in userspace. thread->ckpt_regs.msr
represents the state of the MSR when exiting userspace. This is setup
by check_if_tm_restore_required().

Unfortunatley there is an optimisation in giveup_all() which returns
early if tsk->thread.regs->msr (via local variable `usermsr`) has
FP=VEC=VSX=SPE=0. This optimisation means that
check_if_tm_restore_required() is not called and hence
thread->ckpt_regs.msr is not updated and will contain an old value.

This can happen if due to load_fp=255 we start a userspace process
with MSR FP=1 and then we are context switched out. In this case
thread->ckpt_regs.msr will contain FP=1. If that same process is then
context switched in and load_fp overflows, MSR will have FP=0. If that
process now enters a transaction and does an FP instruction, the FP
unavailable will not update thread->ckpt_regs.msr (the bug) and MSR
FP=1 will be retained in thread->ckpt_regs.msr.  tm_reclaim_thread()
will then not perform the required memcpy and the checkpointed FP regs
in the thread struct will contain the wrong values.

The code path for this happening is:

       Userspace:                      Kernel
                   Start userspace
                    with MSR FP/VEC/VSX/SPE=0 TM=1
                      < -----
       ...
       tbegin
       bne
       fp instruction
                   FP unavailable
                       ---- >
                                        fp_unavailable_tm()
					  tm_reclaim_current()
					    tm_reclaim_thread()
					      giveup_all()
					        return early since FP/VMX/VSX=0
						/* ckpt MSR not updated (Incorrect) */
					      tm_reclaim()
					        /* thread_struct ckpt FP regs contain junk (OK) */
                                              /* Sees ckpt MSR FP=1 (Incorrect) */
					      no memcpy() performed
					        /* thread_struct ckpt FP regs not fixed (Incorrect) */
					  tm_recheckpoint()
					     /* Put junk in hardware checkpoint FP regs */
                                         ....
                      < -----
                   Return to userspace
                     with MSR TM=1 FP=1
                     with junk in the FP TM checkpoint
       TM rollback
       reads FP junk

This is a data integrity problem for the current process as the FP
registers are corrupted. It's also a security problem as the FP
registers from one process may be leaked to another.

This patch moves up check_if_tm_restore_required() in giveup_all() to
ensure thread->ckpt_regs.msr is updated correctly.

A simple testcase to replicate this will be posted to
tools/testing/selftests/powerpc/tm/tm-poison.c

Similarly for VMX.

This fixes CVE-2019-15030.

Fixes: f48e91e87e67 ("powerpc/tm: Fix FP and VMX register corruption")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # 4.12+
Signed-off-by: Gustavo Romero <gromero@linux.vnet.ibm.com>
Signed-off-by: Michael Neuling <mikey@neuling.org>

description: In the Linux kernel through 5.2.14 on the powerpc platform, a local user can read vector registers of other users' processes via a Facility Unavailable exception. To exploit the venerability, a local user starts a transaction (via the hardware transactional memory instruction tbegin) and then accesses vector registers. At some point, the vector registers will be corrupted with the values from a different local Linux process because of a missing arch/powerpc/kernel/process.c check.

code_evidence: Line 6 reads usermsr from tsk->thread.regs->msr; line 7-8 returns early when no FP/VEC/VSX/SPE bits are set, skipping all subsequent handling.
Line 10 calls check_if_tm_restore_required(tsk) only after the early return, so the TM checkpointed MSR is not refreshed on that path.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-862 fits because the missing update of the checkpointed MSR state allows a local user to bypass the isolation that should prevent reading another process's vector/FP registers, a missing authorization check on access to another process's register state.

evidence_lines.code: check_if_tm_restore_required(tsk);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the early return at lines 7-8 bypasses check_if_tm_restore_required(), leaving thread->ckpt_regs.msr stale. Trigger: a local process starts a transaction with MSR FP/VEC/VSX/SPE=0 and executes an FP/VEC instruction, causing an unavailable exception. Consequence: checkpointed registers are not fixed, so junk or another process's register contents can be read after TM rollback.

commit_msg:
Split the xt_compat_match/xt_compat_target into smaller type-safe functions
performing just one operation. Handle all alignment and size-related
conversions centrally in these function instead of requiring each module to
implement a full-blown conversion function. Replace ->compat callback by
->compat_from_user and ->compat_to_user callbacks, responsible for
converting just a single private structure.

Signed-off-by: Patrick McHardy <kaber@trash.net>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (match->compat)', '\t\tmatch->compat(m, dstptr, size, COMPAT_FROM_USER);', '\telse', '\t\txt_compat_match(m, dstptr, size, COMPAT_FROM_USER);'], 'added_lines': ['\txt_compat_match_from_user(m, dstptr, size);']}
description: A heap out-of-bounds write affecting Linux since v2.6.19-rc1 was discovered in net/netfilter/x_tables.c. This allows an attacker to gain privileges or cause a DoS (via heap memory corruption) through user name space

code_evidence: dm is derived from the caller-provided destination pointer *dstptr, and match is taken from the user-supplied match m. The function then delegates to match->compat or xt_compat_match with the same dstptr and size, copying the private match structure into that destination without any bounds check here. The subsequent xt_check_match uses dm->u.match_size - sizeof(*dm) as the match size, so the size field is trusted from the copied destination rather than validated before the copy.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the unsafe operation is a write past the end of the intended heap buffer during compat match conversion, driven by an unchecked user-supplied size. It is not merely an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125), since the copied private structure is written into the destination.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the compat match copy writes the user-controlled private structure into the destination buffer via the compat callback without validating that the destination has room for the computed match size. Trigger: a user-namespace attacker supplies a crafted ipt_entry_match with an inconsistent match_size; the copy advances past the allocated heap buffer. Consequence: heap out-of-bounds write enabling memory corruption, privilege escalation or DoS.

commit_msg:
CVE-2017-12987/IEEE 802.11: Fix processing of TIM IE.

The arguments to memcpy() were completely wrong.

This fixes a buffer over-read discovered by Kamil Frankowicz.

Add a test using the capture file supplied by Brian 'geeknik' Carpenter.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\tmemcpy(tim.bitmap, p + (tim.length - 3),', '\t\t\t    (tim.length - 3));'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\tmemcpy(tim.bitmap, p + offset + 3, tim.length - 3);']}
description: The IEEE 802.11 parser in tcpdump before 4.9.2 has a buffer over-read in print-802_11.c:parse_elements().

code_evidence: For E_TIM, after consuming the 2-byte header the code checks only tim.length against sizeof tim.bitmap, then copies the 3-byte count from p+offset. The bitmap memcpy uses source p + (tim.length - 3) instead of p + offset (the current read position), so the read start is computed from the element length rather than the advanced offset, and the destination tim.bitmap has no bound tied to the actual source region.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The wrong source argument causes a read beyond the intended buffer in memcpy, matching CWE-125 (Out-of-bounds Read). It is not a write overflow because only the source of the copy is mispositioned; the destination bound check limits the write.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the source pointer for the bitmap memcpy is calculated as p + (tim.length - 3), ignoring the already-advanced offset, so it can point outside the captured packet buffer. Trigger: a crafted 802.11 frame with a TIM element whose length makes this offset point past the available data. Consequence: memcpy reads past the end of the buffer (out-of-bounds read), leaking memory or crashing the parser.

description: LibTIFF 4.4.0 has an out-of-bounds write in tiffcrop in tools/tiffcrop.c:3502, allowing attackers to cause a denial-of-service via a crafted tiff file. For users that compile libtiff from sources, the fix is available with commit 33aee127.

code_evidence: The loop iterates over crop->selections, computes crop_width and crop_length per region, and for EDGE_TOP/BOTTOM writes dst = crop_buff + dst_offset + (prev_length * dst_rowsize) where prev_length accumulates crop_length and dst_rowsize derives from crop_width.

For EDGE_LEFT/RIGHT, dst = crop_buff + dst_offset + prev_width, with dst_rowsize based on composite_width and prev_width accumulating (crop_width*bps*count)/8; differing region widths/lengths make these offsets inconsistent with the allocated buffer.

The missing constraint is dimension equality before the copy, not merely a width mismatch error.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The composite copy computes destination offsets from per-region width/length while the destination buffer size assumes consistent combined dimensions. When regions have unequal widths (top/bottom) or lengths (left/right), the accumulated prev_length/prev_width and derived dst_rowsize place writes past the end of crop_buff, causing an out-of-bounds write and DoS via a crafted TIFF.

commit_msg: fix #285
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['            m_Entries.Clear();', '            m_SampleCount = 0;']}
description: An issue has been found in Bento4 1.5.1-624. It is a SEGV in AP4_StszAtom::GetSampleSize in Core/Ap4StszAtom.cpp.

code_evidence: When m_SampleSize is zero, a size-derived bound check rejects m_SampleCount > (size-8)/4 by zeroing the count and returning; this is the only guard on the attacker-controlled count.
Otherwise sample_count = m_SampleCount is used directly to allocate buffer of sample_count*4 bytes and to read exactly sample_count*4 bytes; on read failure the code deletes the buffer and returns.
The loop indexes m_Entries[i] and reads &buffer[i*4] for i < sample_count, matching the allocation size for the non-error path.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-119 fits because the count drives buffer allocation and indexing without a robust bound tied to actual readable data, allowing operations outside the intended buffer. This is a boundary/validation failure rather than an integer overflow in the size arithmetic itself.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: m_SampleCount is read directly from the stream and only bounded relative to the atom's declared size, not validated against the actual data available. Trigger: a crafted STSZ atom with m_SampleSize==0 and an inflated sample count passes the size check (or the size field is also inflated). Consequence: the allocation/read and subsequent buffer indexing can operate beyond the actual stream content, leading to out-of-bounds read/memory corruption and the reported SEGV.

commit_msg:
release 2.1.6 : security fix: scrub headers for "AuthType oauth20"

Signed-off-by: Hans Zandbelt <hans.zandbelt@zmartzone.eu>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t/*', "\t * we're going to pass the information that we have to the application,", "\t * but first we need to scrub the headers that we're going to use for security reasons", '\t */', '\toidc_scrub_headers(r);', '']}
description: The "OpenID Connect Relying Party and OAuth 2.0 Resource Server" (aka mod_auth_openidc) module before 2.1.6 for the Apache HTTP Server does not skip OIDC_CLAIM_ and OIDCAuthNHeader headers in an "AuthType oauth20" configuration, which allows remote attackers to bypass authentication via crafted HTTP traffic.

code_evidence: After the bearer token is resolved and the remote user is set, the function reads authn_header and pass_headers/pass_envvars and sets the authentication header via apr_table_set(r->headers_in, authn_header, r->user).
It then forwards token claims and the access token into request headers/envvars through oidc_util_set_app_infos and oidc_util_set_app_info, using claim_prefix and OIDC_DEFAULT_HEADER_PREFIX.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is improper authentication: an attacker can assert a claimed identity through unsanitized headers and have it treated as authenticated. This directly matches CWE-287 rather than a lower-level injection because the supported consequence is bypassing the identity proof performed by the module.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function propagates identity and claim values into request headers without first removing client-supplied headers that use the same names. A remote attacker can send crafted OIDC_CLAIM_* or OIDCAuthNHeader headers; when the configured header set is applied, the application may trust attacker-controlled identity claims, allowing authentication bypass. The root cause is the missing sanitization of inbound headers before they are reused for security-relevant identity data, not the token validation itself.

commit_msg:
Rewrite scopes of non-simple default arguments

Default parameters have additional declaration block scopes inserted
around them when something in the function scope calls eval. This
patch sets the parent scope of the expressions introduced due to
those defaults to the new block scope.

R=adamk
BUG=chromium:616386

Review-Url: https://codereview.chromium.org/2077283004
Cr-Commit-Position: refs/heads/master@{#37198}
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['      // Pass the appropriate scope in so that PatternRewriter can appropriately', '      // rewrite inner initializers of the pattern to param_scope', '      descriptor.scope = param_scope;', '      // Rewrite the outer initializer to point to param_scope', '      RewriteParameterInitializerScope(stack_limit(), initial_value, scope_,', '                                       param_scope);']}
description: The parser in Google V8, as used in Google Chrome before 53.0.2785.113, mishandles scopes, which allows remote attackers to obtain sensitive information from arbitrary memory locations via crafted JavaScript code.

code_evidence: When a non-simple parameter coexists with a sloppy eval call, a new BLOCK_SCOPE param_scope is created and attached to param_block (lines 36-43), but descriptor still carries the outer scope_ and hoist_scope is set to scope_ (line 44).

The declaration is processed under block_state switch to param_scope (line 47), yet PatternRewriter::DeclareAndInitializeVariables receives the descriptor whose scope was not updated to param_scope, so the initializer's scope association is inconsistent with the block actually used.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The advisory for this parser scope mishandling identifies the impact as obtaining sensitive information from arbitrary memory locations, a confidentiality exposure. CWE-200 covers exposure of sensitive information to unauthorized actors, and the function's incorrect scope handling directly enables that disclosure.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the parameter initializer's scope is not rewritten to the inserted eval-triggered block scope, leaving expressions bound to the wrong scope. Trigger: crafted JavaScript with non-simple default parameters plus a sloppy eval. Consequence: scope mishandling can expose sensitive data from arbitrary memory, as described in the advisory.

commit_msg:
usb/redir: avoid dynamic stack allocation (CVE-2021-3527)

Use autofree heap allocation instead.

Fixes: 4f4321c11ff ("usb: use iovecs in USBPacket")
Reviewed-by: Philippe Mathieu-Daudé <philmd@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Gerd Hoffmann <kraxel@redhat.com>
Tested-by: Philippe Mathieu-Daudé <philmd@redhat.com>
Message-Id: <20210503132915.2335822-3-kraxel@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        uint8_t buf[size];'], 'added_lines': ['        g_autofree uint8_t *buf = g_malloc(size);']}
description: A flaw was found in the USB redirector device (usb-redir) of QEMU. Small USB packets are combined into a single, large transfer request, to reduce the overhead and improve performance. The combined size of the bulk transfer is used to dynamically allocate a variable length array (VLA) on the stack without proper validation. Since the total size is not bounded, a malicious guest could use this flaw to influence the array length and cause the QEMU process to perform an excessive allocation on the stack, resulting in a denial of service.

code_evidence: Line 5 derives size from usb_packet_size(p), which is guest-influenced packet data.

Lines 33-38: in the bulk-out branch, the code declares a variable-length array uint8_t buf[size] on the stack and then copies size bytes into it via usb_packet_copy, with no bound on size before allocation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-770 fits because the function allocates a resource (stack memory) sized by an attacker-influenced value without limiting or throttling the allocation. It is not a fixed-size buffer overflow (CWE-121): the length is variable and unbounded, so the weakness is resource allocation without limits leading to resource exhaustion.

evidence_lines.code: size_t size = usb_packet_size(p);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the guest-controlled packet size is used directly as a VLA length without an upper bound. Trigger: a malicious guest sends a bulk-out packet with a large size (or repeated large transfers). Supported consequence: the stack allocation grows with size, exhausting stack space and crashing the QEMU process (DoS).

commit_msg:
rds: fix an infoleak in rds_inc_info_copy

The last field "flags" of object "minfo" is not initialized.
Copying this object out may leak kernel stack data.
Assign 0 to it to avoid leak.

Signed-off-by: Kangjie Lu <kjlu@gatech.edu>
Acked-by: Santosh Shilimkar <santosh.shilimkar@oracle.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tminfo.flags = 0;', '']}
description: The rds_inc_info_copy function in net/rds/recv.c in the Linux kernel through 4.6.3 does not initialize a certain structure member, which allows remote attackers to obtain sensitive information from kernel stack memory by reading an RDS message.

code_evidence: minfo is a stack-allocated struct rds_info_message; only seq and len are initialized before the branch.
The flip/else branches assign laddr, faddr, lport and fport, but no path initializes minfo.flags.
rds_info_copy copies the entire sizeof(minfo) struct to the info iterator, including the uninitialized flags member.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function explicitly copies a partially initialized structure to an externally observable resource, exposing residual sensitive stack bytes; this is a direct information-exposure mistake, not merely an out-of-bounds read.

evidence_lines.code: rds_info_copy(iter, &minfo, sizeof(minfo));

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the stack struct minfo is not fully initialized, leaving the flags member with residual stack contents. Trigger: a remote RDS message causes rds_inc_info_copy to run and rds_info_copy copies the whole struct out to a reader. Consequence: kernel stack data is disclosed to the reader of the info message.

commit_msg: check for input buffer size on datastream::gets
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  if(sz<1) return NULL;']}
description: Buffer Overflow vulnerability in LibRaw linux/unix v0.20.0 allows attacker to escalate privileges via the LibRaw_buffer_datastream::gets(char*, int) in /src/libraw/src/libraw_datastream.cpp.

code_evidence: gets(char *str, int sz) accepts caller-controlled sz and passes it directly to is.getline(str, sz) at line 5 without validating that sz is positive or matches the destination buffer capacity. Only LR_STREAM_CHK() and stream construction precede the write.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the function writes attacker-influenced data past the end of the intended buffer str via is.getline. The missing sz<1 check in the patch addresses the adjacent invalid-size case, but the core weakness is the unchecked write bound into str, matching out-of-bounds write rather than an out-of-bounds read.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the destination size sz is trusted as the write bound. Trigger: a caller supplies an oversized sz relative to str (or a non-positive value) and getline writes up to sz bytes into str. Supported consequence: out-of-bounds write, memory corruption, crash or possible code execution.

commit_msg:
Add group terminator if it is left off.

If there is no terminating ";" add one to the list, to make the text
re-rendering correct.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  /* add group terminator, if it was left off */', '  if (last && in_group)', '    last->next = rfc822_new_address ();', '']}
description: rfc822.c in Mutt through 2.0.4 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (mailbox unavailability) by sending email messages with sequences of semicolon characters in RFC822 address fields (aka terminators of empty groups). A small email message from the attacker can cause large memory consumption, and the victim may then be unable to see email messages from other persons.

code_evidence: On ':' the parser allocates cur via rfc822_new_address, marks it as a group, sets in_group=1, and links it into the list; this is the group-open node.
On ';' a terminator node is allocated and linked only when last && in_group; if the message ends without ';' this block never runs, so the group has no terminator.
At end of input, remaining phrase text is flushed with add_addrspec, but no group-terminator node is allocated even when in_group remains 1.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function's handling of unterminated groups leaves allocated ADDRESS structures unclosed, matching CWE-401's missing release/tracking of allocated memory with an availability impact. It is not a simple buffer overflow; the weakness is lifecycle handling of allocated list nodes.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: when an RFC822 address field opens a group with ':' but omits the terminating ';', the parser leaves in_group set and never appends a terminator ADDRESS node, so the group is left unterminated. Trigger: a crafted message containing many open groups without semicolons. Supported consequence: repeated parsing/re-rendering of such fields allocates group nodes that are not properly bounded, contributing to excessive memory consumption and mailbox unavailability.

description: In the Linux kernel before 5.19, drivers/gpu/drm/arm/malidp_planes.c misinterprets the get_sg_table return value (expects it to be NULL in the error case, whereas it is actually an error pointer).

code_evidence: sgt is assigned either cma_obj->sgt or the result of obj->funcs->get_sg_table(obj); the error path of get_sg_table returns an ERR_PTR, not NULL. The check at line 16 tests only for NULL, so an error pointer passes the guard and is immediately dereferenced at line 18 via sgt->sgl.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences a pointer that its guard failed to validate, matching CWE-476's invalid/NULL pointer dereference. The bug is a wrong error-check idiom (NULL vs IS_ERR) rather than a missing check; IS_ERR would reject the error pointer before dereference.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the error return of get_sg_table is an encoded error pointer, but the guard checks only for NULL. Trigger: get_sg_table fails, returning an ERR_PTR. Consequence: the error pointer is treated as valid and dereferenced at sgt->sgl, causing an invalid-pointer access rather than a clean early return.

commit_msg:
x86: Return -1 if bfd_canonicalize_dynamic_reloc returns 0

Stop if bfd_canonicalize_dynamic_reloc returns 0.

	PR binutils/22163
	* elf32-i386.c (elf_i386_get_synthetic_symtab): Also return -1
	if bfd_canonicalize_dynamic_reloc returns 0.
	* elf64-x86-64.c (elf_x86_64_get_synthetic_symtab): Likewise.

(cherry picked from commit b69e9267d15a09ce3f3d4599eae2952dfc6df502)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  if (dynrelcount < 0)'], 'added_lines': ['  if (dynrelcount <= 0)']}
description: The *_get_synthetic_symtab functions in the Binary File Descriptor (BFD) library (aka libbfd), as distributed in GNU Binutils 2.29, mishandle the failure of a certain canonicalization step, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference and application crash) via a crafted ELF file, related to elf32-i386.c and elf64-x86-64.c.

code_evidence: After bfd_canonicalize_dynamic_reloc, only dynrelcount < 0 is rejected at [44,45]; a return of 0 (no relocations) passes the check and reaches qsort and the subsequent loop.
In the PLT loop, dynrelbuf[0] is dereferenced at [223] and then p->address is read at [241,242] even when dynrelcount is 0 and dynrelbuf contains no valid entries.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Directly matches CWE-476: a pointer expected to be valid is dereferenced without a zero-count guard. The patch changing < 0 to <= 0 confirms the missing constraint; the crash stems from the NULL dereference rather than a separate bounds error.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the guard at [44] treats a zero relocation count as success, so an empty dynrelbuf proceeds into code that unconditionally dereferences dynrelbuf[0]. Trigger: a crafted ELF file causing bfd_canonicalize_dynamic_reloc to return 0 while PLT entries exist. Consequence: NULL/invalid pointer dereference and application crash (DoS).

commit_msg: carefully crafted image files (TIM2, JPEG) no longer overflow buffer nor use heap after free (thanks to Juzhi Lu, Zhen Zhou, Likang Luo of NSFOCUS Security Team)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  memmove(datum+start+value_length,datum+end,length-end);', '  memcpy(datum+start,value,value_length);'], 'added_lines': ['  (void) memmove(datum+start+value_length,datum+end,length-end);', '  (void) memcpy(datum+start,value,value_length);', '      datum=(char *) GetStringInfoDatum(profile);']}
description: A heap-based buffer overflow issue was discovered in ImageMagick's ReadTIM2ImageData() function in coders/tim2.c. A local attacker could trick the user in opening specially crafted file, triggering an out-of-bounds read error, allowing an application to crash, resulting in a denial of service.

code_evidence: Line 15 caches datum=GetStringInfoDatum(profile). When new_length<length, line 20 SetStringInfoLength shrinks the StringInfo, which may reallocate or free the old datum buffer, yet line 21 still writes *(datum+new_length)='\0' through the stale cached pointer. The patch adds a re-fetch of datum after the resize to fix this.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences a pointer to memory that SetStringInfoLength may have freed/reallocated, which is exactly CWE-416 Use After Free; the added re-fetch confirms the stale-pointer defect rather than a mere bounds overflow (CWE-125/787).
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: datum is obtained before SetStringInfoLength, and the shrink path reallocates the underlying buffer while the old pointer is retained. Trigger: a replacement value shorter than the replaced span (new_length<length). Consequence: write through freed/stale memory, a use-after-free that can corrupt memory or crash.

commit_msg: Fix for bug #72513
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t   ', '\t\t   '], 'added_lines': ['', '']}
description: Integer overflow in the virtual_file_ex function in TSRM/tsrm_virtual_cwd.c in PHP before 5.5.38, 5.6.x before 5.6.24, and 7.x before 7.0.9 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (stack-based buffer overflow) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted extract operation on a ZIP archive.

code_evidence: The cache-size accounting subtracts a computed expression from CWDG(realpath_cache_size): sizeof(realpath_cache_bucket) + r->path_len + 1, and in the else branch additionally + r->realpath_len + 1. The additions of the stored lengths occur before the subtraction, so the arithmetic is performed in the unsigned size type without any bound check.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the function performs an integer addition of untrusted-derived length fields that can exceed the counter's representable range, wrapping before use in a size computation. The weakness is the unchecked wraparound in the size arithmetic, not a plain out-of-bounds write in this function; the buffer overflow is the downstream consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the cache-size bookkeeping expression is computed as a sum of unsigned lengths and the bucket size without validating that it fits the counter's type. If a crafted path or realpath length makes the sum wrap, the subtraction no longer matches the amount previously added when the entry was cached, corrupting CWDG(realpath_cache_size). This can cause incorrect cache-size accounting and, per the reported bug, contributes to a stack-based buffer overflow during crafted ZIP extract operations, leading to denial of service.

commit_msg:
In commit ee13cb249fab ("powerpc/64s: Add support for software count
cache flush"), I added support for software to flush the count
cache (indirect branch cache) on context switch if firmware told us
that was the required mitigation for Spectre v2.

As part of that code we also added a software flush of the link
stack (return address stack), which protects against Spectre-RSB
between user processes.

That is all correct for CPUs that activate that mitigation, which is
currently Power9 Nimbus DD2.3.

What I got wrong is that on older CPUs, where firmware has disabled
the count cache, we also need to flush the link stack on context
switch.

To fix it we create a new feature bit which is not set by firmware,
which tells us we need to flush the link stack. We set that when
firmware tells us that either of the existing Spectre v2 mitigations
are enabled.

Then we adjust the patching code so that if we see that feature bit we
enable the link stack flush. If we're also told to flush the count
cache in software then we fall through and do that also.

On the older CPUs we don't need to do do the software count cache
flush, firmware has disabled it, so in that case we patch in an early
return after the link stack flush.

The naming of some of the functions is awkward after this patch,
because they're called "count cache" but they also do link stack. But
we'll fix that up in a later commit to ease backporting.

This is the fix for CVE-2019-18660.

Reported-by: Anthony Steinhauser <asteinhauser@google.com>
Fixes: ee13cb249fab ("powerpc/64s: Add support for software count cache flush")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # v4.4+
Signed-off-by: Michael Ellerman <mpe@ellerman.id.au>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\tpr_warn("Spectre v2 mitigations not under software control, can\'t disable\\n");'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\tpr_warn("Spectre v2 mitigations not fully under software control, can\'t disable\\n");', '\t/*', "\t * There's no firmware feature flag/hypervisor bit to tell us we need to", '\t * flush the link stack on context switch. So we set it here if we see', '\t * either of the Spectre v2 mitigations that aim to protect userspace.', '\t */', '\tif (security_ftr_enabled(SEC_FTR_COUNT_CACHE_DISABLED) ||', '\t    security_ftr_enabled(SEC_FTR_FLUSH_COUNT_CACHE))', '\t\tsecurity_ftr_set(SEC_FTR_FLUSH_LINK_STACK);', '']}
description: The Linux kernel before 5.4.1 on powerpc allows Information Exposure because the Spectre-RSB mitigation is not in place for all applicable CPUs, aka CID-39e72bf96f58. This is related to arch/powerpc/kernel/entry_64.S and arch/powerpc/kernel/security.c.

code_evidence: When no_spectrev2 or cpu_mitigations_off() is set, the function only warns if BCCTRL_SERIALISED or COUNT_CACHE_DISABLED firmware features are enabled, then sets enable=false.

toggle_count_cache_flush(enable) receives that single boolean; nothing in this function sets SEC_FTR_FLUSH_LINK_STACK, so the link-stack (Spectre-RSB) flush is not requested for CPUs where firmware only disabled the count cache.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function configures Spectre-v2 mitigations; its failure to request the link-stack flush leaves cross-process data observable by an unauthorized user process, matching CWE-200's exposure of sensitive information. The root cause is the missing mitigation configuration, not a direct read primitive.

evidence_lines.code: toggle_count_cache_flush(enable);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the mitigation setup derives flushing only from count-cache-related feature bits and never enables the link-stack flush for CPUs whose firmware disabled the count cache. Trigger: running on such older PowerPC CPUs and switching between user processes. Consequence: the return address stack is not flushed on context switch, allowing Spectre-RSB disclosure of another process's data.

commit_msg:
patch 8.2.5148: invalid memory access when using expression on command line

Problem:    Invalid memory access when using an expression on the command line.
Solution:   Make sure the position does not go negative.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['     * Need to save the current command line, to be able to enter', '     * a new one...'], 'added_lines': ['    int\t\tsave_new_cmdpos = new_cmdpos;', '    new_cmdpos = save_new_cmdpos;', '']}
description: Buffer Over-read in GitHub repository vim/vim prior to 8.2.

code_evidence: Line 17 sets new_cmdpos = -1 before evaluating the '=' expression; get_expr_register() at line 25 may set new_cmdpos to a position. Lines 37-43 then use new_cmdpos to set ccline.cmdpos, clamping only the upper bound (new_cmdpos > ccline.cmdlen) but assigning ccline.cmdpos = new_cmdpos without checking a lower bound. A negative new_cmdpos other than -1 passes the >= 0 gate only if it is non-negative, but the patch shows the position could go negative, so a negative value assigned here drives later reads before the buffer start.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the missing lower-bound check on ccline.cmdpos leads to reading memory before the intended command-line buffer. It is an out-of-bounds read rather than a write, since the position is used for cursor/read operations.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the expression-register path can produce a command-line position that is not validated against a lower bound before being stored in ccline.cmdpos. Trigger: inserting an expression register on the command line where the resulting position goes negative. Consequence: subsequent command-line handling reads before the start of the buffer, an out-of-bounds read.

commit_msg:
FreeBSD: Fix UNIX permissions checking

Reviewed-by: Ryan Moeller <ryan@iXsystems.com>
Reviewed-by: Brian Behlendorf <behlendorf1@llnl.gov>
Signed-off-by: Matt Macy <mmacy@FreeBSD.org>
Closes #10727
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tuid_t\t\tgid;'], 'added_lines': ['\tuid_t\t\tgid;', '', '#ifdef illumos', '#endif /* illumos */']}
description: OpenZFS before 2.0.0-rc1, when used on FreeBSD, allows execute permissions for all directories.

code_evidence: Under HAVE_KSID the function reads ksid/ksidlist and maps id via zfs_fuid_map_id before calling groupmember(gid, cr).
The ksid comparison loop only returns B_TRUE for matching group ids; otherwise execution falls through to the POSIX groupmember check.
On non-illumos builds the #else branch returns B_TRUE unconditionally, so group membership is granted without consulting credentials.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function is an authorization predicate, yet on the non-illumos path it approves all requests regardless of the supplied cred, which is an incorrect authorization check (CWE-863). The defect is not a missing check but a check that always succeeds.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The authorization check for group membership is short-circuited: when HAVE_KSID is defined but the illumos ksid path is compiled out, the fallback returns B_TRUE for every caller. Any operation gated by zfs_groupmember then treats the actor as a group member, bypassing the intended credential/group check and allowing unauthorized access to resources whose permissions depend on group ownership.

description: In Wireshark 2.6.0, the RTCP dissector could crash. This was addressed in epan/dissectors/packet-rtcp.c by avoiding a buffer overflow for packet status chunks.

code_evidence: Line 13 derives packet_length from the on-wire length field; line 14 advances offset past it.
Lines 19-24 create a subset tvb only when packet_length > 12 and dispatch to the FMT subdissector, returning early on success.

The loop at line 26 iterates while offset-start_offset < packet_length; for FMT 15 (lines 34-37) it adds hf_rtcp_fci over the remaining range and then sets offset to the packet end without validating that the FMT 15 payload stays within the advertised packet_length.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The code performs buffer operations whose bounds depend on unvalidated on-wire length fields, so accesses can fall outside the intended buffer, matching CWE-119; it is a buffer-bounds weakness rather than, e.g., an integer overflow alone.

offset = dissect_rtcp_length_field(rtcp_tree, tvb, offset);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The FMT 15 branch trusts the on-wire packet_length and the chunk-derived offset without bounding the remaining length; when chunks cover more packets than the packet status count advertises, the computed remaining length or offset can exceed the buffer, leading to an out-of-bounds read/write in the dissector and a crash.

commit_msg:
babeld: fix #10502 #10503 by repairing the checks on length

This patch repairs the checking conditions on length in four functions:
babel_packet_examin, parse_hello_subtlv, parse_ihu_subtlv, and parse_update_subtlv

Signed-off-by: qingkaishi <qingkaishi@gmail.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        if(i + 1 > alen) {', '        if(i + len > alen) {'], 'added_lines': ['        if(i + 1 >= alen) {', '        if(i + len + 2 > alen) {']}
description: A buffer overflow vulnerability exists in FRRouting through 8.1.0 due to a wrong check on the input packet length in the babel_packet_examin function in babeld/message.c.

code_evidence: The length check `if(i + len > alen)` uses only `len` (the sub-TLV payload length) without accounting for the two header bytes at `i` and `i+1`, so it admits sub-TLVs whose declared payload extends past `alen`.

With the insufficient bound, `memchr(a + i + 2, 0, len)` and `memcpy(channels, a + i + 2, len)` read `len` bytes starting at `a+i+2`, which can exceed the buffer; `i += len + 2` then advances past the validated region.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads from `a + i + 2` for `len` bytes after a length check that fails to constrain the access within `alen`, i.e., operations outside the buffer's intended boundary. This directly matches CWE-119's out-of-bounds memory operations; the off-by-two length check is the specific cause enabling the out-of-bounds read.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the bound check compares `i + len` against `alen` but the actual data begins at `i + 2`, so the check under-counts by two bytes. A crafted update sub-TLV with a large `len` passes the check, and the subsequent `memchr`/`memcpy` read past the packet buffer, causing an out-of-bounds read (and potentially copying attacker-controlled adjacent memory into `channels`).

commit_msg:
There are two sites that calls queue_work() after the
destroy_workqueue() and lead to possible UAF.

The first site is nci_send_cmd(), which can happen after the
nci_close_device as below

nfcmrvl_nci_unregister_dev   |  nfc_genl_dev_up
  nci_close_device           |
    flush_workqueue          |
    del_timer_sync           |
  nci_unregister_device      |    nfc_get_device
    destroy_workqueue        |    nfc_dev_up
    nfc_unregister_device    |      nci_dev_up
      device_del             |        nci_open_device
                             |          __nci_request
                             |            nci_send_cmd
                             |              queue_work !!!

Another site is nci_cmd_timer, awaked by the nci_cmd_work from the
nci_send_cmd.

  ...                        |  ...
  nci_unregister_device      |  queue_work
    destroy_workqueue        |
    nfc_unregister_device    |  ...
      device_del             |  nci_cmd_work
                             |  mod_timer
                             |  ...
                             |  nci_cmd_timer
                             |    queue_work !!!

For the above two UAF, the root cause is that the nfc_dev_up can race
between the nci_unregister_device routine. Therefore, this patch
introduce NCI_UNREG flag to easily eliminate the possible race. In
addition, the mutex_lock in nci_close_device can act as a barrier.

Signed-off-by: Lin Ma <linma@zju.edu.cn>
Fixes: 6a2968aaf50c ("NFC: basic NCI protocol implementation")
Reviewed-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Krzysztof Kozlowski <krzysztof.kozlowski@canonical.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20211116152732.19238-1-linma@zju.edu.cn
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\t/* This set_bit is not protected with specialized barrier,', '\t * However, it is fine because the mutex_lock(&ndev->req_lock);', '\t * in nci_close_device() will help to emit one.', '\t */', '\tset_bit(NCI_UNREG, &ndev->flags);']}
description: A use-after-free flaw was found in nci_request in net/nfc/nci/core.c in NFC Controller Interface (NCI) in the Linux kernel. This flaw could allow a local attacker with user privileges to cause a data race problem while the device is getting removed, leading to a privilege escalation problem.

code_evidence: nci_unregister_device tears down the device by calling nci_close_device and then destroying the cmd/rx/tx workqueues.

After the workqueues are destroyed, the function calls nfc_unregister_device, which can still drive open/request paths (nci_send_cmd/nci_cmd_timer) that call queue_work on the already-destroyed workqueue.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is a missing synchronization barrier that lets an interfering concurrent sequence access the shared workqueue after teardown, which is a timing-window race (CWE-362). The UAF is the downstream consequence of that race rather than the weakness itself.

evidence_lines.code: nfc_unregister_device(ndev->nfc_dev);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The teardown sequence is not exclusive: a concurrent nfc_dev_up path can reach nci_send_cmd or the cmd timer and queue work on ndev->cmd_wq after destroy_workqueue has freed it. The trigger is a race between device removal and device open; the supported consequence is use-after-free of the workqueue leading to crash or potential privilege escalation.

commit_msg:
When running concurrent iptables rules replacement with data, the per CPU
sequence count is checked after the assignment of the new information.
The sequence count is used to synchronize with the packet path without the
use of any explicit locking. If there are any packets in the packet path using
the table information, the sequence count is incremented to an odd value and
is incremented to an even after the packet process completion.

The new table value assignment is followed by a write memory barrier so every
CPU should see the latest value. If the packet path has started with the old
table information, the sequence counter will be odd and the iptables
replacement will wait till the sequence count is even prior to freeing the
old table info.

However, this assumes that the new table information assignment and the memory
barrier is actually executed prior to the counter check in the replacement
thread. If CPU decides to execute the assignment later as there is no user of
the table information prior to the sequence check, the packet path in another
CPU may use the old table information. The replacement thread would then free
the table information under it leading to a use after free in the packet
processing context-

Unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at virtual
address 000000000000008e
pc : ip6t_do_table+0x5d0/0x89c
lr : ip6t_do_table+0x5b8/0x89c
ip6t_do_table+0x5d0/0x89c
ip6table_filter_hook+0x24/0x30
nf_hook_slow+0x84/0x120
ip6_input+0x74/0xe0
ip6_rcv_finish+0x7c/0x128
ipv6_rcv+0xac/0xe4
__netif_receive_skb+0x84/0x17c
process_backlog+0x15c/0x1b8
napi_poll+0x88/0x284
net_rx_action+0xbc/0x23c
__do_softirq+0x20c/0x48c

This could be fixed by forcing instruction order after the new table
information assignment or by switching to RCU for the synchronization.

Fixes: 80055dab5de0 ("netfilter: x_tables: make xt_replace_table wait until old rules are not used anymore")
Reported-by: Sean Tranchetti <stranche@codeaurora.org>
Reported-by: kernel test robot <lkp@intel.com>
Suggested-by: Florian Westphal <fw@strlen.de>
Signed-off-by: Subash Abhinov Kasiviswanathan <subashab@codeaurora.org>
Signed-off-by: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>

description: An issue was discovered in netfilter in the Linux kernel before 5.10. There can be a use-after-free in the packet processing context, because the per-CPU sequence count is mishandled during concurrent iptables rules replacement. This could be exploited with the CAP_NET_ADMIN capability in an unprivileged namespace. NOTE: cc00bca was reverted in 5.12.

code_evidence: Line 6 caches table->private into a local pointer without any synchronization or protection against concurrent xt_replace_table; the patch replaces this with xt_table_get_private_protected(table).
Lines 12-15 allocate counters and only then begin iterating; the unguarded private pointer is already captured before any consistency check.
Lines 17-22 dereference private->entries via xt_entry_foreach and copy entries to user, reading the cached table info with no sequence-count revalidation before or during the walk.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences and iterates memory (private->entries) that a concurrent replacement may free, which is precisely use of freed memory under concurrency; CWE-416 fits. A mere race condition (CWE-362) is the enabling mechanism, but the supported harm is the stale-pointer dereference after free.

evidence_lines.code: const struct xt_table_info *private = table->private;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the local private pointer is snapshotted from table->private without synchronization, so a concurrent iptables rule replacement can free the old table info while this function still walks it. Trigger: concurrent CAP_NET_ADMIN replacement during compat_copy_entries_to_user. Consequence: use-after-free read of freed xt_table_info entries, leading to kernel crash or memory disclosure.

commit_msg:
core: ensure that supplied range matches MOBJ

In set_rmem_param() if the MOBJ is found by the cookie it's verified to
represent non-secure shared memory. Prior to this patch the supplied
sub-range to be used of the MOBJ was not checked here and relied on
later checks further down the chain. Those checks seems to be enough
for user TAs, but not for pseudo TAs where the size isn't checked.

This patch adds a check for offset and size to see that they remain
inside the memory covered by the MOBJ.

Fixes: OP-TEE-2018-0004: "Unchecked parameters are passed through from
REE".

Signed-off-by: Jens Wiklander <jens.wiklander@linaro.org>
Tested-by: Joakim Bech <joakim.bech@linaro.org> (QEMU v7, v8)
Reviewed-by: Joakim Bech <joakim.bech@linaro.org>
Reported-by: Riscure <inforequest@riscure.com>
Reported-by: Alyssa Milburn <a.a.milburn@vu.nl>
Acked-by: Etienne Carriere <etienne.carriere@linaro.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tsize_t req_size = 0;', '\t/*', '\t * Check that the supplied offset and size is covered by the', '\t * previously verified MOBJ.', '\t */', '\tif (ADD_OVERFLOW(mem->offs, mem->size, &req_size) ||', '\t    mem->mobj->size < req_size)', '\t\treturn TEE_ERROR_SECURITY;', '']}
description: Linaro/OP-TEE OP-TEE Prior to version v3.4.0 is affected by: Boundary checks. The impact is: This could lead to corruption of any memory which the TA can access. The component is: optee_os. The fixed version is: v3.4.0.

code_evidence: The function reads the caller-supplied offset (mem->offs) and size (mem->size) from the shared-memory parameter and stores them without validating that offs + size stays within the bounds of the MOBJ returned by mobj_reg_shm_get_by_cookie. It then returns TEE_SUCCESS, so an out-of-range sub-range is accepted for later use.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Accepting an unchecked offset/size sub-range enables later accesses beyond the MOBJ's buffer, matching an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). The weakness is the missing length constraint that permits writes outside the intended buffer, not merely an integer overflow or info leak.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: missing bounds check on attacker-controlled offset/size relative to mem->mobj->size. Trigger: a pseudo TA or REE-supplied rmem parameter with offs/size extending beyond the verified MOBJ. Consequence: downstream memory accesses using this unchecked range can write past the intended buffer, corrupting memory the TA can reach.

commit_msg:
libvncclient: handle half-open TCP connections

When a connection is not reset properly at the TCP level (e.g. sudden
power loss or process crash) the TCP connection becomes half-open and
read() always returns -1 with errno = EAGAIN while select() always
returns 0. This leads to an infinite loop and can be fixed by closing
the connection after a certain number of retries (based on a timeout)
has been exceeded.
