commit_msg:
posix-timers: Sanitize overrun handling

The posix timer overrun handling is broken because the forwarding functions
can return a huge number of overruns which does not fit in an int. As a
consequence timer_getoverrun(2) and siginfo::si_overrun can turn into
random number generators.

The k_clock::timer_forward() callbacks return a 64 bit value now. Make
k_itimer::ti_overrun[_last] 64bit as well, so the kernel internal
accounting is correct. 3Remove the temporary (int) casts.

Add a helper function which clamps the overrun value returned to user space
via timer_getoverrun(2) or siginfo::si_overrun limited to a positive value
between 0 and INT_MAX. INT_MAX is an indicator for user space that the
overrun value has been clamped.

Reported-by: Team OWL337 <icytxw@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
Acked-by: John Stultz <john.stultz@linaro.org>
Cc: Peter Zijlstra <peterz@infradead.org>
Cc: Michael Kerrisk <mtk.manpages@gmail.com>
Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/20180626132705.018623573@linutronix.de
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\ttimr->it_overrun += (unsigned int) hrtimer_forward(timer,', '\t\t\t\t\t\ttimer->base->get_time(),', '\t\t\t\t\t\ttimr->it_interval);'], 'added_lines': ['\ttimr->it_overrun += hrtimer_forward(timer, timer->base->get_time(),', '\t\t\t\t\t    timr->it_interval);']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel through 4.17.3. An Integer Overflow in kernel/time/posix-timers.c in the POSIX timer code is caused by the way the overrun accounting works. Depending on interval and expiry time values, the overrun can be larger than INT_MAX, but the accounting is int based. This basically makes the accounting values, which are visible to user space via timer_getoverrun(2) and siginfo::si_overrun, random. For example, a local user can cause a denial of service (signed integer overflow) via crafted mmap, futex, timer_create, and timer_settime system calls.

code_evidence: Line 4 checks only it_interval; line 6 accumulates hrtimer_forward's return into timr->it_overrun, but casts the result to (unsigned int). hrtimer_forward returns a 64-bit count of overruns; the cast truncates it before accumulation, so the stored accounting wraps/truncates rather than reflecting the true count.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The narrowing cast and accumulation of an unbounded count into a fixed-width integer is exactly an integer overflow/wraparound (CWE-190). It is not merely a logic flaw: the arithmetic result exceeds the storage representation, producing wrapped values.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the 64-bit forward count is narrowed to unsigned int and added to an int-typed accumulator, so when overruns exceed the type range the stored value wraps. Trigger: a POSIX timer with a short interval relative to expiry causes large overrun counts. Consequence: corrupted overrun accounting exposed via timer_getoverrun/si_overrun, yielding nonsensical values and signed-overflow behavior.

description: An issue was discovered in Nginx NJS v0.7.5. The JUMP offset for a break instruction was not set to a correct offset during code generation, leading to a segmentation violation.

code_evidence: When try_block->exit or catch_block->exit is set, the code derives dest_label via njs_generate_jump_destination using NJS_GENERATOR_ALL | NJS_GENERATOR_TRY, then searches for a matching block with the same flags. If no block matches, the block != NULL guard silently skips creating the exit patch, leaving the finally break_offset unpatched.

commit_msg:
Bug 767873 - (CVE-2016-4994) Multiple Use-After-Free when parsing...

...XCF channel and layer properties

The properties PROP_ACTIVE_LAYER, PROP_FLOATING_SELECTION,
PROP_ACTIVE_CHANNEL saves the current object pointer the @info
structure. Others like PROP_SELECTION (for channel) and
PROP_GROUP_ITEM (for layer) will delete the current object and create
a new object, leaving the pointers in @info invalid (dangling).

Therefore, if a property from the first type will come before the
second, the result will be an UaF in the last lines of xcf_load_image
(when it actually using the pointers from @info).

I wasn't able to exploit this bug because that
g_object_instance->c_class gets cleared by the last g_object_unref and
GIMP_IS_{LAYER,CHANNEL} detects that and return FALSE.

(cherry picked from commit 6d804bf9ae77bc86a0a97f9b944a129844df9395)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ["            /* We're going to delete *channel, Don't leave its pointer", '             * in @info. See bug #767873.', '             */', '            if (*channel == info->active_channel)', '              info->active_channel = NULL;', '', '', "            /* Don't restore info->active_channel because the", "             * selection can't be the active channel", '             */']}
description: Use-after-free vulnerability in the xcf_load_image function in app/xcf/xcf-load.c in GIMP allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (program crash) or possibly execute arbitrary code via a crafted XCF file.

code_evidence: PROP_ACTIVE_CHANNEL stores the current channel pointer into info->active_channel, persisting it beyond this property block.

PROP_SELECTION allocates a new mask, transfers tiles, then calls g_object_unref(*channel) at line 31 and reassigns *channel to mask. The previously saved info->active_channel still points to the freed object.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because a stored pointer is reused after the underlying object is freed by g_object_unref; the stale info->active_channel reference is the dangling pointer. This is use-after-free, not a simple double free, since the freed object is later dereferenced.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the channel object referenced by info->active_channel is freed by g_object_unref in PROP_SELECTION, but the info->active_channel pointer is not cleared. Trigger: a crafted XCF supplies PROP_ACTIVE_CHANNEL before PROP_SELECTION. Consequence: later use of info->active_channel dereferences freed memory, enabling crash or potential code execution.

commit_msg:
avcodec/h264_slice: Limit max_contexts when slice_context_count is initialized

Fixes out of array access
Fixes: 1430e9c43fae47a24c179c7c54f94918/signal_sigsegv_421427_2049_f2192b6829ab6e0eefcb035329c03c60.264

Found-by: Mateusz "j00ru" Jurczyk and Gynvael Coldwind
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>

description: The h264_slice_header_init function in libavcodec/h264_slice.c in FFmpeg before 2.8.3 does not validate the relationship between the number of threads and the number of slices, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds array access) or possibly have unspecified other impact via crafted H.264 data.

code_evidence: When nb_slices exceeds H264_MAX_THREADS or h->mb_height, the code clamps it to max_slices and stores that in h->slice_context_count.
The threading branch iterates i < h->slice_context_count and indexes h->slice_ctx[i], so the loop bound is derived from the clamped count.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function indexes the slice_ctx buffer with a count not validated against its bounds, matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds memory operation. This is specifically the slice-context count mismatch rather than a generic integer issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The root cause is that the number of slice contexts used for indexing is not constrained to be consistent with the allocated/supported context count (max_contexts). If a crafted H.264 stream and thread configuration yield a context count larger than the backing slice_ctx array, the loop at line 75 indexes h->slice_ctx[i] out of bounds; the supported consequence is an out-of-bounds array access causing a crash (DoS) or memory corruption.

commit_msg:
In 801c6058d14a ("bpf: Fix leakage of uninitialized bpf stack under
speculation") we replaced masking logic with direct loads of immediates
if the register is a known constant. Given in this case we do not apply
any masking, there is also no reason for the operation to be truncated
under the speculative domain.

Therefore, there is also zero reason for the verifier to branch-off and
simulate this case, it only needs to do it for unknown but bounded scalars.
As a side-effect, this also enables few test cases that were previously
rejected due to simulation under zero truncation.

Signed-off-by: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>
Reviewed-by: Piotr Krysiuk <piotras@gmail.com>
Acked-by: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@kernel.org>

commit_msg: Fix #77369 - memcpy with negative length via crafted DNS response
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tif (dlen == 0) {', '\t\t/* No data in the response - nothing to do */', '\t\treturn NULL;', '\t}', '\t\t\tif ( (size_t) dlen < ((size_t)n) + 2 ) {', '\t\t\t\treturn NULL;', '\t\t\t}']}
description: An issue was discovered in PHP 7.x before 7.1.26, 7.2.x before 7.2.14, and 7.3.x before 7.3.2. dns_get_record misparses a DNS response, which can allow a hostile DNS server to cause PHP to misuse memcpy, leading to read operations going past the buffer allocated for DNS data. This affects php_parserr in ext/standard/dns.c for DNS_CAA and DNS_ANY queries.

code_evidence: In the DNS_T_CAA case, dlen is a u_short attacker-controlled from the DNS response. The loop at line 111 runs while i < 8, but dlen is not used to bound the number of 16-bit reads; CHECKCP(2) only checks against end, not the record's dlen. When dlen is smaller than the bytes the loop consumes, GETSHORT(s, cp) reads past the record data. The added guard (size_t)dlen < n+2 prevents a negative n = dlen - n - 2 but does not constrain the loop's reads to dlen.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the parser reads past the intended record buffer boundary due to missing dlen-based bounds enforcement. It is not CWE-787 (write) since the operation is a read via GETSHORT/add_assoc_string.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the CAA parsing loop consumes up to 8 16-bit words regardless of the record's declared dlen, so a hostile DNS server can supply a short dlen while cp advances beyond the record into subsequent buffer contents. Trigger: DNS_CAA or DNS_ANY response with a truncated record. Consequence: out-of-bounds read of DNS buffer memory, potentially leaking data or crashing.

commit_msg:
Check the max size to read before actually reading

The size check waas also missing from the length parsing
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    } while (!bFound && MaxDataSize > ReadSize);'], 'added_lines': ['      if (MaxDataSize <= ReadSize)', '        break;', '    } while (!bFound);', '        bFound = false;', '        break;', '      }', '      if (MaxDataSize <= ReadSize) {']}
description: libebml before 1.3.6, as used in the MKV module in VideoLAN VLC Media Player binaries before 3.0.3, has a heap-based buffer over-read in EbmlElement::FindNextElement.

code_evidence: The ID-reading loop tracks ReadIndex (bounded only by the assert at line 15) and MaxDataSize via ReadSize. When ReadIndex >= 4, line 30 memmoves and decrements ReadIndex, then line 32 reads one byte into PossibleIdNSize[ReadIndex++] without checking that MaxDataSize has not already been reached; the only loop guard is the while at line 35, so a final read can occur when MaxDataSize <= ReadSize.

commit_msg: Prevent buffer overflow in magick/draw.c
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  for (i=1; (i < number_vertices) && (length >= 0.0); i++)'], 'added_lines': ['  for (i=1; (i < (ssize_t) number_vertices) && (length >= 0.0); i++)']}
description: The DrawDashPolygon function in MagickCore/draw.c in ImageMagick before 6.9.4-0 and 7.x before 7.0.1-2 mishandles calculations of certain vertices integer data, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (buffer overflow and application crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted file.

code_evidence: number_vertices is a size_t derived from the sentinel loop at line 29-30, but the loop counter i is a signed ssize_t; the loop condition compares i < number_vertices, mixing signed and unsigned types.

The guard at line 92 checks (j+1) > (2*number_vertices) before writing dash_polygon[j], but the unchecked writes at lines 113-115 and 119-125 increment and index j without any bounds check against the allocated size 2*number_vertices+1.
The allocation at lines 31-32 is sized 2UL*number_vertices+1, so writes at indices beyond that count overflow the heap buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes past the end of the heap buffer dash_polygon, which is an out-of-bounds memory write within CWE-119's scope. It is not merely an integer-conversion issue; the signed/unsigned comparison is incidental, whereas the missing capacity check on j directly causes the buffer overflow.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the number of dash-segment vertices appended to dash_polygon is not bounded by the allocated capacity; only one inner write is guarded, while the outer-loop writes at lines 113-115 and 119-125 can push j past 2*number_vertices+1. Trigger: a crafted file with many vertices and dash patterns causes repeated appends, producing an out-of-bounds heap write that crashes the application or corrupts memory.

commit_msg:
rtlwifi: prevent memory leak in rtl_usb_probe

In rtl_usb_probe if allocation for usb_data fails the allocated hw
should be released. In addition the allocated rtlpriv->usb_data should
be released on error handling path.

Signed-off-by: Navid Emamdoost <navid.emamdoost@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Kalle Valo <kvalo@codeaurora.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (!rtlpriv->usb_data)'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (!rtlpriv->usb_data) {', '\t\tieee80211_free_hw(hw);', '\t}', '\tkfree(rtlpriv->usb_data);']}
description: Two memory leaks in the rtl_usb_probe() function in drivers/net/wireless/realtek/rtlwifi/usb.c in the Linux kernel through 5.3.11 allow attackers to cause a denial of service (memory consumption), aka CID-3f9361695113.

code_evidence: Lines 10-17 allocate hw via ieee80211_alloc_hw and store it in rtlpriv->hw (also referenced by local hw); if the subsequent kcalloc at lines 18-19 fails, line 20-21 returns -ENOMEM without freeing hw, leaking the earlier allocation.

Error path lines 66-72 releases I/O handler and usb device and completes firmware_loading_complete but never frees rtlpriv->usb_data allocated at lines 18-19, so all error_out/error_out2 jumps leak that buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function allocates memory and fails to release it on error returns, matching CWE-401's missing release of memory after effective lifetime. This is a leak (unreachable/untracked allocation), not use-after-free, because the pointers are simply abandoned rather than reused after freeing.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: error paths in rtl_usb_probe return without releasing memory already allocated. Trigger: kcalloc failure for usb_data leaks hw, while any later failure (init, register) jumps to error_out2 and leaks usb_data. Consequence: repeated probe attempts consume kernel memory, enabling DoS via resource exhaustion.

commit_msg:
evtchn: avoid NULL derefs

Commit fbbd5009e6 ("evtchn: refactor low-level event channel port ops")
added a de-reference of the struct evtchn pointer for a port without
first making sure the bucket pointer is non-NULL. This de-reference is
actually entirely unnecessary, as all relevant callers (beyond the
problematic do_poll()) already hold the port number in their hands, and
the actual leaf functions need nothing else.

For FIFO event channels there's a second problem in that the ordering
of reads and updates to ->num_evtchns and ->event_array[] was so far
undefined (the read side isn't always holding the domain's event lock).
Add respective barriers.

This is XSA-221.

Reported-by: Ankur Arora <ankur.a.arora@oracle.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '    /* Synchronize with evtchn_fifo_word_from_port(). */', '    smp_wmb();', '']}
description: Xen through 4.8.x does not validate the port numbers of polled event channel ports, which allows guest OS users to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference and host OS crash) or possibly obtain sensitive information, aka XSA-221.

code_evidence: Line 13 stores the mapped page pointer into event_array[slot], then line 14 increments num_evtchns, making the new port range visible.
The loop at lines 15-22 iterates the newly added ports, calls port_is_valid and evtchn_from_port, then dereferences evtchn->pending and evtchn->notify_vcpu_id.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The supported consequence is dereferencing a pointer expected valid but NULL (evtchn or event_array-derived), matching CWE-476. The missing memory barrier is the trigger, not the weakness itself; the NULL dereference is the resulting flaw.

evidence_lines.code:
d->evtchn_fifo->event_array[slot] = virt;
d->evtchn_fifo->num_evtchns += EVTCHN_FIFO_EVENT_WORDS_PER_PAGE;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The event_array[slot] pointer and num_evtchns are updated without a barrier, so a concurrent reader such as evtchn_fifo_word_from_port may observe the incremented num_evtchns before the event_array entry is visible, or read a stale/NULL bucket. The loop then obtains an evtchn pointer and dereferences it, causing a NULL pointer dereference and host crash.

commit_msg:
Increase the RX buffer size to 3K when the SBP bit is on. The size of
the RX buffer determines the number of pages allocated which may not
be sufficient for receive frames larger than the set MTU size.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: 89eaefb61dc9 ("igb: Support RX-ALL feature flag.")
Reported-by: Manfred Rudigier <manfred.rudigier@omicronenergy.com>
Signed-off-by: Radoslaw Tyl <radoslawx.tyl@intel.com>
Tested-by: Arpana Arland <arpanax.arland@intel.com> (A Contingent worker at Intel)
Signed-off-by: Tony Nguyen <anthony.l.nguyen@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (adapter->max_frame_size <= IGB_MAX_FRAME_BUILD_SKB)', '\t\treturn;', '', '\tset_ring_uses_large_buffer(rx_ring);'], 'added_lines': ['#if (PAGE_SIZE < 8192)', '\tstruct e1000_hw *hw = &adapter->hw;', '#endif', '', '\tif (adapter->max_frame_size > IGB_MAX_FRAME_BUILD_SKB ||', '\t    rd32(E1000_RCTL) & E1000_RCTL_SBP)', '\t\tset_ring_uses_large_buffer(rx_ring);']}
description: An issue was discovered in drivers/net/ethernet/intel/igb/igb_main.c in the IGB driver in the Linux kernel before 6.5.3. A buffer size may not be adequate for frames larger than the MTU.

code_evidence: The buffer-size decision at [9-12] only enables the large buffer when adapter->max_frame_size exceeds IGB_MAX_FRAME_BUILD_SKB; when the frame size is smaller it returns early, so RX-ALL (SBP) mode with larger receive frames does not get the larger buffer allocation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-131 fits because the code miscalculates the required buffer size, selecting too small an allocation for the actual frame length; this is a size-calculation flaw, not a generic bounds check.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the buffer size chosen for the RX ring is computed from max_frame_size alone, ignoring the SBP (store-bad-packets / RX-ALL) setting. Trigger: enabling RX-ALL while frames larger than IGB_MAX_FRAME_BUILD_SKB arrive. Consequence: insufficiently sized RX buffers, causing overflow/corruption of receive data.

commit_msg:
Fix oob memcpy in matrix_custom_frame methods

Adjust row_length if it exeeds the arguments array

commit_msg:
When a client has a USB device attached over IP, the vhci_hcd driver is
locally leaking a socket pointer address via the

/sys/devices/platform/vhci_hcd/status file (world-readable) and in debug
output when "usbip --debug port" is run.

Fix it to not leak. The socket pointer address is not used at the moment
and it was made visible as a convenient way to find IP address from socket
pointer address by looking up /proc/net/{tcp,tcp6}.

As this opens a security hole, the fix replaces socket pointer address with
sockfd.

Reported-by: Secunia Research <vuln@secunia.com>
Cc: stable <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Shuah Khan <shuahkh@osg.samsung.com>
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tvdev->ud.sockfd     = sockfd;']}
description: The vhci_hcd driver in the Linux Kernel before version 4.14.8 and 4.4.114 allows allows local attackers to disclose kernel memory addresses. Successful exploitation requires that a USB device is attached over IP.

code_evidence: store_attach parses a user-supplied sockfd at line 13 and resolves it with sockfd_lookup at line 34, then stores the resulting socket pointer into vdev->ud.tcp_socket at line 52.
The parsed sockfd and related fields are written to debug/info output at lines 19-20 and 46-47; the commit replaces the leaked socket pointer with sockfd in status/debug output.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is explicit exposure of sensitive internal kernel state (a socket pointer address) to unauthorized readers, matching CWE-200. It is not merely a generic confidentiality impact; the code directly inserts the pointer into accessible output.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the driver stores the kernel socket pointer in vdev->ud.tcp_socket, which is later rendered into the world-readable status file and debug output. Trigger: a local attacker with a USB device attached over IP reads that output. Consequence: kernel pointer disclosure that aids further exploitation; the fix stores sockfd instead of the pointer.

commit_msg: store mode: check for truncation
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        if (data_size - 8 > 64) {'], 'added_lines': ['        if (data_size - 8 > 64 || data_size < 8) {']}
description: An issue was discovered in libbzip3.a in bzip3 before 1.2.3. There is a crash caused by an invalid memmove in bz3_decode_block.

code_evidence: Line 4 bounds data_size above by bz3_bound and rejects negative values, but does not reject small positive values.

When bwt_idx (read from buffer+4) equals -1, line 9 checks only data_size - 8 > 64; for data_size in 0..7 the subtraction underflows/negative and the guard passes, then line 13 calls memmove(buffer, buffer + 8, data_size - 8), reading past the end of buffer and using a negative/huge length.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The memmove operates outside the intended buffer bounds because the size/offset relationship is not validated, which is exactly an improper restriction of operations within a memory buffer (CWE-119); the invalid memmove is the boundary violation, not merely a resultant crash.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the malformed-header guard omits a lower bound on data_size before computing data_size - 8. A crafted block with bwt_idx == -1 and data_size < 8 reaches memmove with a negative length and a source pointer buffer+8 beyond the buffer, causing an out-of-bounds read/memmove and crash.

This was addressed in epan/dissectors/packet-dcerpc-nt.c and epan/dissectors/packet-dcerpc-spoolss.c by using the wmem file scope for private strings.

Lines 33-36 store that packet-scoped pointer into dcv->private_data, a persistent dcerpc_call_value field, without duplicating it.

The patch's wmem_strdup into file scope confirms the lifetime mismatch; this is not merely a memory leak or out-of-bounds read.

s = tvb_get_string_enc(wmem_packet_scope(),
tvb, start_offset + 12, (end_offset - start_offset - 12), ENC_ASCII);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: a pointer to packet-scope memory is retained in persistent call data. Trigger: a later access to dcv->private_data after the packet scope is freed. Consequence: use-after-free, leading to a dissector crash or potential memory corruption.

description: In Exiv2 0.26 and previous versions, PngChunk::readRawProfile in pngchunk_int.cpp may cause a denial of service (application crash due to a heap-based buffer over-read) via a crafted PNG file.

code_evidence: The loop skipping NUL/space/newline advances sp without any bound against text.size_, so sp can move past the end of the text buffer.
The loop scanning to the next space/newline likewise has no size bound, allowing sp to walk beyond the buffer before atol or subsequent reads.
The hex-scanning loop dereferences *sp (and checks *sp == '\0') with no bound on sp, so a truncated profile without a terminating NUL causes reads past the allocated text buffer.
unhex[*sp++] indexes using the byte read from sp; once sp is out of bounds, arbitrary adjacent memory is read and used as an index.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences and indexes sp beyond the intended text buffer, directly matching CWE-125 out-of-bounds read. It is not a write overflow because the reads, not writes to dp, exceed the source buffer bounds.

evidence_lines.code:
while (*sp != ' ' && *sp != '\n')
sp++;

*dp = (unsigned char) (16*unhex[(int) *sp++]);
(*dp++) += unhex[(int) *sp++];

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: pointer sp is advanced through the attacker-controlled PNG text buffer without checking it stays within text.size_. Trigger: a crafted raw profile lacking expected newlines/terminator causes the skip and hex-scan loops to run past the buffer, and unhex[*sp++] then reads out-of-bounds memory. Consequence: heap-based buffer over-read, leading to crash/denial of service.

commit_msg: Use the correct rights.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  rights=AllPolicyRights;'], 'added_lines': ['  rights=ReadPolicyRights|WritePolicyRights;']}
description: ImageMagick is free software delivered as a ready-to-run binary distribution or as source code that you may use, copy, modify, and distribute in both open and proprietary applications. In affected versions and in certain cases, Postscript files could be read and written when specifically excluded by a `module` policy in `policy.xml`. ex. <policy domain="module" rights="none" pattern="PS" />. The issue has been resolved in ImageMagick 7.1.0-7 and in 6.9.12-22. Fortunately, in the wild, few users utilize the `module` policy and instead use the `coder` policy that is also our workaround recommendation: <policy domain="coder" rights="none" pattern="{PS,EPI,EPS,EPSF,EPSI}" />.

code_evidence: The module name is derived from caller input and then normalized via GetCoderInfo (lines 24-27). Line 28 sets rights=AllPolicyRights, so the subsequent IsRightsAuthorized check at line 29 tests the module against every policy right rather than only the rights needed to load it, making a policy that denies a specific right ineffective.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The flaw lets a resource (the Postscript module and its file I/O) be used by actors the policy explicitly excluded, i.e., exposure to the wrong control sphere, matching CWE-668. It is an over-broad authorization check rather than a memory-safety or injection defect.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the authorization check requests AllPolicyRights instead of the read/write rights the module load actually needs. Trigger: a policy.xml module policy that excludes the PS module for certain rights; the over-broad rights value still satisfies the check. Consequence: excluded Postscript modules can be loaded and used, exposing file read/write operations to a control sphere the policy intended to block.

commit_msg:
dir: Refuse to export .desktop files with suspicious uses of @@ tokens

This is either a malicious/compromised app trying to do an attack, or
a mistake that will break handling of %f, %u and so on. Either way,
if we refuse to export the .desktop file, resulting in installation
failing, then it makes the rejection more obvious than quietly
removing the magic tokens.

Signed-off-by: Simon McVittie <smcv@collabora.com>
(cherry picked from commit 46b3ede5241561c7d588951048c687c5075a3eac)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['                g_print (_("Skipping invalid Exec argument %s\\n"), arg);'], 'added_lines': ['                {', '                  flatpak_fail_error (error, FLATPAK_ERROR_EXPORT_FAILED,', '                                     _("Invalid Exec argument %s"), arg);', '                  goto out;', '                }']}
description: Flatpak is a system for building, distributing, and running sandboxed desktop applications on Linux. In Flatpack since version 0.9.4 and before version 1.10.2 has a vulnerability in the "file forwarding" feature which can be used by an attacker to gain access to files that would not ordinarily be allowed by the app's permissions. By putting the special tokens `@@` and/or `@@u` in the Exec field of a Flatpak app's .desktop file, a malicious app publisher can trick flatpak into behaving as though the user had chosen to open a target file with their Flatpak app, which automatically makes that file available to the Flatpak app. This is fixed in version 1.10.2. A minimal solution is the first commit "`Disallow @@ and @@U usage in desktop files`". The follow-up commits "`dir: Reserve the whole @@ prefix`" and "`dir: Refuse to export .desktop files with suspicious uses of @@ tokens`" are recommended, but not strictly required. As a workaround, avoid installing Flatpak apps from untrusted sources, or check the contents of the exported `.desktop` files in `exports/share/applications/*.desktop` (typically `~/.local/share/flatpak/exports/share/applications/*.desktop` and `/var/lib/flatpak/exports/share/applications/*.desktop`) to make sure that literal filenames do not follow `@@` or `@@u`.

code_evidence: The Exec arguments from the .desktop file are parsed into old_argv and each argument is re-emitted into new_exec; arguments equal to %f/%u are wrapped in @@ ... @@ file-forwarding tokens, while any other argument beginning with @@ is only reported via g_print and otherwise passes to the else branch appending it to new_exec.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function builds a downstream command string (Exec) from untrusted .desktop input without neutralizing special @@ elements that the flatpak run parser interprets, matching CWE-74's injection of special elements into output consumed by a downstream component. It is not merely a quoting bug; the unneutralized token syntax alters execution logic.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: externally controlled Exec arguments that already contain the @@ file-forwarding token syntax are not rejected or escaped when the exported .desktop file is constructed. Trigger: a malicious publisher places @@ or @@u tokens in Exec; on export the token is either skipped (leaving adjacent tokens to form forwarding syntax) or appended unchanged, so flatpak run later interprets it as file forwarding and grants the app access to a target file. Consequence: bypass of the app's filesystem permissions (confidentiality/access-control).

commit_msg:
auth: Do not double-expand key in passdb dict when authenticating

Broken by 79042f8c

When 'dict' passdb and userdb were used for user authentication, the username sent by the IMAP/POP3 client was sent through var_expand() to perform %variable expansion. Sending specially crafted %variable fields could result in excessive memory usage causing the process to crash (and restart), or excessive CPU usage causing all authentications to hang.

Line 14 passes key->key->key directly to var_expand() with iter->var_expand_table, so %variable tokens in the client-supplied key are expanded before the key is used.

str_c(path), &key->value, &error);

Trigger: a username/key containing nested % expansions is sent through the dict passdb path. Trigger: a client sends a URI longer than the buffer. Consequence: the one-byte recv writes past the end of _buf, corrupting adjacent memory (the described one-byte overflow).

commit_msg:
mm/rmap: Fix anon_vma->degree ambiguity leading to double-reuse

anon_vma->degree tracks the combined number of child anon_vmas and VMAs
that use the anon_vma as their ->anon_vma.

anon_vma_clone() then assumes that for any anon_vma attached to
src->anon_vma_chain other than src->anon_vma, it is impossible for it to
be a leaf node of the VMA tree, meaning that for such VMAs ->degree is
elevated by 1 because of a child anon_vma, meaning that if ->degree
equals 1 there are no VMAs that use the anon_vma as their ->anon_vma.

This assumption is wrong because the ->degree optimization leads to leaf
nodes being abandoned on anon_vma_clone() - an existing anon_vma is
reused and no new parent-child relationship is created.  So it is
possible to reuse an anon_vma for one VMA while it is still tied to
another VMA.

This is an issue because is_mergeable_anon_vma() and its callers assume
that if two VMAs have the same ->anon_vma, the list of anon_vmas
attached to the VMAs is guaranteed to be the same.  When this assumption
is violated, vma_merge() can merge pages into a VMA that is not attached
to the corresponding anon_vma, leading to dangling page->mapping
pointers that will be dereferenced during rmap walks.

Fix it by separately tracking the number of child anon_vmas and the
number of VMAs using the anon_vma as their ->anon_vma.

Fixes: 7a3ef208e662 ("mm: prevent endless growth of anon_vma hierarchy")
Cc: stable@kernel.org
Acked-by: Michal Hocko <mhocko@suse.com>
Acked-by: Vlastimil Babka <vbabka@suse.cz>
Signed-off-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t/* vma reference or self-parent link for new root */', '\t\tanon_vma->degree++;'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tanon_vma->num_children++; /* self-parent link for new root */', '\t\tanon_vma->num_active_vmas++;']}
description: mm/rmap.c in the Linux kernel before 5.19.7 has a use-after-free related to leaf anon_vma double reuse.

code_evidence: find_mergeable_anon_vma() may return an existing anon_vma that is reused for this VMA; if none is found, a fresh anon_vma is allocated (lines 12-17).

When vma->anon_vma is empty, the reused anon_vma is attached via anon_vma_chain_link and its degree counter is incremented (lines 20-26), but no new parent-child relationship is created for the reused leaf, so the degree bookkeeping no longer reflects actual attachment.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The described consequence is dereferencing freed page->mapping memory during rmap walks, matching CWE-416 use-after-free. The ambiguous degree accounting is the root cause enabling the dangling pointer, not a separate weakness such as CWE-667.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: a single degree counter conflates child anon_vmas and active VMAs, so reusing an existing anon_vma on a leaf abandons the leaf without recording the relationship. Trigger: __anon_vma_prepare reuses a mergeable anon_vma for a VMA while it remains tied to another VMA. Consequence: callers later assume identical ->anon_vma implies identical chains, vma_merge merges pages into a VMA not attached to the anon_vma, leaving dangling page->mapping pointers dereferenced during rmap walks (use-after-free).

v2: FontNames.c  return a NULL list whenever a single
length field from the server is incohent.

Signed-off-by: Tobias Stoeckmann <tobias@stoeckmann.org>
Reviewed-by: Matthieu Herrb <matthieu@herrb.eu>

commit_msg:
Make sure that the xEvent eventT is initialized with zeros, the same way as
in SProcSendEvent.

Some event swapping functions do not overwrite all 32 bytes of xEvent
structure, for example XSecurityAuthorizationRevoked. Two cooperating
clients, one swapped and the other not, can send
XSecurityAuthorizationRevoked event to each other to retrieve old stack data
from X server. This can be potentialy misused to go around ASLR or
stack-protector.

Signed-off-by: Michal Srb <msrb@suse.com>
Reviewed-by: Peter Hutterer <peter.hutterer@who-t.net>
Signed-off-by: Peter Hutterer <peter.hutterer@who-t.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    xEvent eventT;'], 'added_lines': ['    xEvent eventT = { .u.u.type = 0 };']}
description: Uninitialized data in endianness conversion in the XEvent handling of the X.Org X Server before 2017-06-19 allowed authenticated malicious users to access potentially privileged data from the X server.

code_evidence: Line 6 declares eventT without initializing it. Line 23 passes &eventT as the output buffer to the swap procedure, and line 24 copies the whole xEvent back into *eventP. When a swap function does not write all 32 bytes, the untouched bytes remain uninitialized stack data and are propagated to eventP.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-665 fits because the weakness is a resource (the eventT buffer) that is not properly initialized before use, leaving bytes in an unexpected state that are then read and forwarded. This is improper initialization leading to memory disclosure, not a separate out-of-bounds or type-confusion issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the local xEvent eventT is uninitialized before being used as a swap destination. Trigger: a client sends an event whose swap routine (e.g. XSecurityAuthorizationRevoked) writes only part of the structure. Consequence: the remaining stack bytes are copied into the swapped event and can be disclosed to another client, leaking server memory that may help bypass ASLR or stack-protector.

commit_msg:
When expanding the extra isize space, we must never move the
system.data xattr out of the inode body.  For performance reasons, it
doesn't make any sense, and the inline data implementation assumes
that system.data xattr is never in the external xattr block.

This addresses CVE-2018-10880

https://bugzilla.kernel.org/show_bug.cgi?id=200005

Signed-off-by: Theodore Ts'o <tytso@mit.edu>
Cc: stable@kernel.org
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t/* never move system.data out of the inode */', '\t\t\tif ((last->e_name_len == 4) &&', '\t\t\t    (last->e_name_index == EXT4_XATTR_INDEX_SYSTEM) &&', '\t\t\t    !memcmp(last->e_name, "data", 4))', '\t\t\t\tcontinue;']}
description: Linux kernel is vulnerable to a stack-out-of-bounds write in the ext4 filesystem code when mounting and writing to a crafted ext4 image in ext4_update_inline_data(). An attacker could use this to cause a system crash and a denial of service.

code_evidence: The loop walks inode-body xattr entries and computes total_size from each entry's name/value length, then selects an entry to move to the external block based on bfree and isize_diff.
Selection logic accepts any entry whose total_size fits bfree and is smaller than min_total_size; there is no exclusion of the system.data entry, so it can become the chosen entry.
If no fitting entry is found, small_entry (or ENOSPC) is used; otherwise the selected entry is passed to the move path.
The chosen entry is moved via ext4_xattr_move_to_block, and bookkeeping adjusts *total_ino, ifree and bfree, assuming the inode body no longer holds that entry.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Moving system.data out of the inode body breaks the buffer-layout assumption of the inline-data path, causing a write past the intended buffer. This matches CWE-787 (out-of-bounds write); the missing system.data exclusion in selection is the direct cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the entry-selection loop does not prevent the system.data xattr from being chosen for relocation out of the inode body. Trigger: while expanding extra isize space, a crafted ext4 image whose system.data entry fits bfree gets selected and moved. Consequence: the inline-data implementation's invariant that system.data stays in the inode body is violated, leading to an out-of-bounds write and crash/DoS.

commit_msg:
libndp: validate the IPv6 hop limit

None of the NDP messages should ever come from a non-local network; as
stated in RFC4861's 6.1.1 (RS), 6.1.2 (RA), 7.1.1 (NS), 7.1.2 (NA),
and 8.1. (redirect):

  - The IP Hop Limit field has a value of 255, i.e., the packet
    could not possibly have been forwarded by a router.

This fixes CVE-2016-3698.

Reported by: Julien BERNARD <julien.bernard@viagenie.ca>
Signed-off-by: Lubomir Rintel <lkundrak@v3.sk>
Signed-off-by: Jiri Pirko <jiri@mellanox.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tval = 1;', '\tret = setsockopt(sock, IPPROTO_IPV6, IPV6_RECVHOPLIMIT,', '\t\t\t &val, sizeof(val));', '\tif (ret == -1) {', '\t\terr(ndp, "Failed to setsockopt IPV6_RECVHOPLIMIT,.");', '\t\terr = -errno;', '\t\tgoto close_sock;', '\t}', '']}
description: libndp before 1.6, as used in NetworkManager, does not properly validate the origin of Neighbor Discovery Protocol (NDP) messages, which allows remote attackers to conduct man-in-the-middle attacks or cause a denial of service (network connectivity disruption) by advertising a node as a router from a non-local network.

code_evidence: The added block enables IPV6_RECVHOPLIMIT via setsockopt and aborts socket setup on failure, but it only requests that the kernel deliver hop-limit ancillary data; no code here reads, checks, or enforces the received hop limit.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function fails to restrict acceptance of NDP messages to authorized local-link senders, i.e., it does not enforce the access-control policy that only directly connected nodes may participate in NDP. This is a missing enforcement mechanism, matching CWE-284's high-level improper access control.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the socket is opened without any enforcement of the RFC4861 requirement that NDP packets arrive with IP Hop Limit 255, so packets forwarded from non-local networks are not rejected. Trigger: a remote attacker sends NDP messages (e.g., RA/NA) from a non-local network; since the hop limit is never validated, the message is accepted. Supported consequence: spoofed router advertisements enable man-in-the-middle or network connectivity disruption. The added setsockopt is only a prerequisite for validation, not the validation itself.

commit_msg:
proxy: fix buffer overflow with multiget syntax

"get[200 spaces]key1 key2\r\n" would overflow a temporary buffer used to
process multiget syntax.

To exploit this you must first pass the check in try_read_command_proxy:
- The request before the first newline must be less than 1024 bytes.
- If it is more than 1024 bytes there is a limit of 100 spaces.
- The key length is still checked at 250 bytes
- Meaning you have up to 772 spaces and then the key to create stack
  corruption.

So the amount of data you can shove in here isn't unlimited.

The fix caps the amount of data pre-key to be reasonable. Something like
GAT needs space for a 32bit TTL which is at most going to be 15 bytes +
spaces, so we limit it to 20 bytes.

I hate hate hate hate hate the multiget syntax. hate it.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            char temp[KEY_MAX_LENGTH + 30];', '            if (pr.klen > KEY_MAX_LENGTH) {'], 'added_lines': ['            char temp[KEY_MAX_LENGTH + MAX_CMD_PREFIX + 30];', '            if (pr.tokens[pr.keytoken] > MAX_CMD_PREFIX) {', '                if (!resp_start(c)) {', '                    conn_set_state(c, conn_closing);', '                    return;', '                }', '                proxy_out_errstring(c->resp, PROXY_CLIENT_ERROR, "malformed request");', '            } else if (pr.klen > KEY_MAX_LENGTH) {']}
description: In Memcached before 1.6.22, a buffer overflow exists when processing multiget requests in proxy mode, if there are many spaces after the "get" substring.

code_evidence: At line 44 keyoff is taken from pr.tokens[pr.keytoken], the attacker-influenced prefix length before the key. The only length check at line 48 bounds pr.klen, not keyoff. Line 55 copies pr.tokens[pr.keytoken] bytes (the pre-key prefix, e.g. many spaces) into temp, then line 57 appends pr.klen bytes and lines 59-61 add CRLF and NUL. With a large space run, the copy at line 55 exceeds temp's size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs a memcpy of attacker-controlled prefix data into a fixed-size output buffer without checking that the input length fits, matching CWE-120's buffer copy without size validation. This is distinct from an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) because the copy writes past temp's bounds.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the prefix length stored in pr.tokens[pr.keytoken] is copied into the fixed stack buffer temp without being validated; only the key length pr.klen is checked. Trigger: a multiget request like 'get' followed by many spaces and a key. Consequence: stack buffer overflow (memory corruption), potentially leading to crash or code execution.

description: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel. A memory leak problem was found in mbochs_ioctl in samples/vfio-mdev/mbochs.c in Virtual Function I/O (VFIO) Mediated devices. This flaw could allow a local attacker to leak internal kernel information.

code_evidence: The remove callback frees mdev_state->pages, mdev_state->vconfig, and mdev_state after unregistering the group device, but the pre-patch line 4 only decrements the global mbochs_used_mbytes counter; it does not release the memory accounting or address allocation failures elsewhere. The diff shows the fix replaces the non-atomic counter update with atomic_add, indicating the counter was not reliably maintained, so allocated mbytes could remain permanently unavailable for reuse.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-401 fits because the tracked allocation counter is not sufficiently released after use, making the resource unavailable for reallocation. This is an accounting/resource leak rather than a use-after-free (CWE-416) or plain buffer overflow.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: mbochs_used_mbytes is updated with a non-atomic decrement and the accounting is not reliably released on removal/error paths. Trigger: probing/removal races or failed registration leave the usage count inflated. Consequence: mbochs_avail_mbytes stays depleted, so subsequent allocations fail and the resource is effectively leaked (DoS/resource exhaustion).

description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. The fix for CVE-2020-15209(https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2020-15209) missed the case when the target shape of `Reshape` operator is given by the elements of a 1-D tensor. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.5.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.4.2, TensorFlow 2.3.3, TensorFlow 2.2.3 and TensorFlow 2.1.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: Loop over node inputs: when tensor->data.raw is null and bytes>0, the code at [40] exempts the Reshape op's second input (i==1) from the missing-data error and continues. No check that this shape tensor is a scalar/1-D-non-vector, so a null-buffer-backed 1-D shape tensor reaches OpInvoke.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe operation is dereferencing a null data pointer of the shape tensor after the guard exempts it, matching CWE-476. Trigger: a model supplies Reshape with a null-buffer-backed 1-D shape tensor; Invoke's guard is bypassed and the kernel dereferences the null data. description: ok-file-formats through 2018-10-16 has a heap-based buffer overflow in the ok_wav_decode_ms_adpcm_data function in ok_wav.c.

code_evidence: Without a per-block base pointer, the output cursor advances by the actual samples written for each block. When frames_per_block is odd, the nibble loops stop at samples > 0 and write one extra sample beyond the nominal block, so output drifts ahead of the allocation for subsequent blocks.
The two-channel loop writes two samples per input byte; an odd remaining sample count still triggers a full pair write, overshooting the block boundary.
The multi-channel loop likewise writes two samples per iteration while samples is decremented by 2, so an odd count produces one extra write.
remaining_frames is decremented by block_frames, but output was advanced by the actual (larger) writes, so the final block can write past the allocated wav->data buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes decoded samples past the end of the allocated output buffer, matching CWE-787's out-of-bounds write definition. The patch fixes it by using block_output for within-block writes and advancing output only by block_frames*num_channels, confirming the overflow was caused by cursor drift.

evidence_lines.code: remaining_frames -= block_frames;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: output pointer is advanced per written sample rather than reset to a per-block base, and odd block/sample counts cause the decode loops to emit one sample more than block_frames*num_channels. Trigger: a crafted MS ADPCM WAV with odd frames_per_block or odd remaining frames. Consequence: heap-based buffer overflow writing past the wav->data allocation.

description: In LibSass prior to 3.5.5, the function handle_error in sass_context.cpp allows attackers to cause a denial-of-service resulting from a heap-based buffer over-read via a crafted sass file.

code_evidence: The loop condition `start != end` only terminates on exact equality; if `utf8::next` advances `start` beyond `end` (e.g., on a malformed/incomplete UTF-8 sequence), the inequality never becomes false.

`utf8::next(start, end)` then continues decoding with `start` past the valid range, and the loop keeps iterating, reading octets beyond the supplied buffer until an unrelated value coincidentally equals `end`.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads octets outside the intended `[start,end)` buffer because the guard fails to enforce the upper bound, matching CWE-125 (Out-of-bounds Read). This is a read-past-end issue rather than an out-of-bounds write, since only decoding/reading occurs.

while (start != end) {
uint32_t cp = utf8::next(start, end);

}
return result;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is the `start != end` loop guard combined with `utf8::next` advancing past `end` on malformed input; the iterator overshoots the buffer bound and the loop reads out-of-bounds memory. Trigger is a crafted sass file containing an incomplete UTF-8 sequence; the supported consequence is a heap-based out-of-bounds read leading to a denial-of-service crash.

description: GOST engine is a reference implementation of the Russian GOST crypto algorithms for OpenSSL. TLS clients using GOST engine when ciphersuite `TLS_GOSTR341112_256_WITH_KUZNYECHIK_CTR_OMAC` is agreed and the server uses 512 bit GOST secret keys are vulnerable to buffer overflow. GOST engine version 3.0.1 contains a patch for this issue. Disabling ciphersuite `TLS_GOSTR341112_256_WITH_KUZNYECHIK_CTR_OMAC` is a possible workaround.

joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-120 fits because the unwrap routine copies a fixed-size decrypted result into the output buffer with no check that the input size fits the destination. Contrast CWE-125: this is a write past the buffer end, not an out-of-bounds read.

evidence_lines.code: if (!keyUnwrapCryptoPro(&ctx, sharedKey, wrappedKey, key)) {

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function writes a fixed 32-byte unwrapped key into the caller-supplied key buffer without validating that the buffer actually has 32 bytes available; *key_len is only reported, never checked. commit_msg:
The functions that were used in the emulation of fxrstor, fxsave, sgdt and
sidt were originally meant for task switching, and as such they did not
check privilege levels.  This is very bad when the same functions are used
in the emulation of unprivileged instructions.  This is CVE-2018-10853.

The obvious fix is to add a new argument to ops->read_std and ops->write_std,
which decides whether the access is a "system" access or should use the
processor's CPL.

Fixes: 129a72a0d3c8 ("KVM: x86: Introduce segmented_write_std", 2017-01-12)
Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\treturn ctxt->ops->write_std(ctxt, linear, data, size, &ctxt->exception);'], 'added_lines': ['\treturn ctxt->ops->write_std(ctxt, linear, data, size, &ctxt->exception, true);']}
description: A flaw was found in the way Linux kernel KVM hypervisor before 4.18 emulated instructions such as sgdt/sidt/fxsave/fxrstor. It did not check current privilege(CPL) level while emulating unprivileged instructions. An unprivileged guest user/process could use this flaw to potentially escalate privileges inside guest.

code_evidence: linear_write_system calls ctxt->ops->write_std with size and data without any privilege/CPL check; it only forwards to the write_std op with the exception pointer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The root cause is missing privilege management: the function does not assign, track, or check CPL before performing the operation, matching CWE-269. The consequence (privilege escalation inside the guest) follows from that missing check rather than being a separate weakness.

evidence_lines.code: return ctxt->ops->write_std(ctxt, linear, data, size, &ctxt->exception);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The wrapper performs a standard memory write through write_std without verifying the current privilege level of the emulated instruction. If an unprivileged guest invokes instructions such as sgdt/sidt/fxsave/fxrstor that reach this path, the emulator performs the write as if privileged, giving an unprivileged actor access outside its intended sphere of control.

description: libsoup from versions 2.65.1 until 2.68.1 have a heap-based buffer over-read because soup_ntlm_parse_challenge() in soup-auth-ntlm.c does not properly check an NTLM message's length before proceeding with a memcpy.

description: A flaw was found in dovecot 2.0 up to 2.2.33 and 2.3.0. An abort of SASL authentication results in a memory leak in dovecot's auth client used by login processes. The leak has impact in high performance configuration where same login processes are reused and can cause the process to crash due to memory exhaustion.

code_evidence: The function obtains the request from *_request and clears the caller's pointer at line 4, then sends a cancel at line 5 and invokes the callback at line 6. No pool_unref or equivalent release of request->pool occurs on the abort path, so the request's pool resource is never freed.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-772 fits because the resource (request->pool) is not released after its effective lifetime ends at abort. This is a missing-release weakness, not a use-after-free or double-free, since the resource is simply never freed.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the abort path terminates the request's effective lifetime (cancel sent, callback invoked) but does not release the request's memory pool. Trigger: a client aborting SASL authentication (e.g., IMAP AUTHENTICATE then '*') repeatedly on reused login processes. Consequence: the pool leaks on each abort, exhausting memory and potentially crashing the process.

commit_msg:
xen: let alloc_xenballooned_pages() fail if not enough memory free

commit a1078e821b605813b63bf6bca414a85f804d5c66 upstream.

Instead of trying to allocate pages with GFP_USER in
add_ballooned_pages() check the available free memory via
si_mem_available(). GFP_USER is far less limiting memory exhaustion
than the test via si_mem_available().

This will avoid dom0 running out of memory due to excessive foreign
page mappings especially on ARM and on x86 in PVH mode, as those don't
have a pre-ballooned area which can be used for foreign mappings.

As the normal ballooning suffers from the same problem don't balloon
down more than si_mem_available() pages in one iteration. At the same
time limit the default maximum number of retries.

This is part of XSA-300.

Signed-off-by: Juergen Gross <jgross@suse.com>
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tif (credit < 0)', '\t\t\tstate = decrease_reservation(-credit, GFP_BALLOON);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (credit < 0) {', '\t\t\tlong n_pages;', '', '\t\t\tn_pages = min(-credit, si_mem_available());', '\t\t\tstate = decrease_reservation(n_pages, GFP_BALLOON);', '\t\t\tif (state == BP_DONE && n_pages != -credit &&', '\t\t\t    n_pages < totalreserve_pages)', '\t\t\t\tstate = BP_EAGAIN;', '\t\t}']}
description: An issue was discovered in drivers/xen/balloon.c in the Linux kernel before 5.2.3, as used in Xen through 4.12.x, allowing guest OS users to cause a denial of service because of unrestricted resource consumption during the mapping of guest memory, aka CID-6ef36ab967c7.

code_evidence: On a negative credit, the function calls decrease_reservation(-credit, GFP_BALLOON) with the entire requested amount, without bounding it by available memory or any other limit.
The do-while loop at line 19 repeats while credit is nonzero and state is BP_DONE, so each iteration can again balloon down the full credit amount.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-770 fits because the function allocates/reclaims a resource (pages via decrease_reservation) on behalf of an actor without limiting the amount to available memory. The missing bound, not a memory-safety bug, is the weakness; the DoS is its consequence.

evidence_lines.code:
if (credit < 0)
state = decrease_reservation(-credit, GFP_BALLOON);
} while (credit && state == BP_DONE);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the number of pages ballooned down per iteration is not limited by available memory, so a guest-controlled credit can drive unbounded page allocation/reclamation under GFP_BALLOON. Trigger: a large negative credit causes decrease_reservation to process the full amount, repeated by the loop. Supported consequence: resource exhaustion leading to denial of service, as described for guest memory mapping.

commit_msg:
The X protocol uses CARD16 values to represent the length so
this would overflow.

CVE-2021-31535

Signed-off-by: Matthieu Herrb <matthieu@herrb.eu>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '    if (strlen(name) >= USHRT_MAX)', '        return false;']}
description: LookupCol.c in X.Org X through X11R7.7 and libX11 before 1.7.1 might allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary code. The libX11 XLookupColor request (intended for server-side color lookup) contains a flaw allowing a client to send color-name requests with a name longer than the maximum size allowed by the protocol (and also longer than the maximum packet size for normal-sized packets). The user-controlled data exceeding the maximum size is then interpreted by the server as additional X protocol requests and executed, e.g., to disable X server authorization completely. For example, if the victim encounters malicious terminal control sequences for color codes, then the attacker may be able to take full control of the running graphical session.

code_evidence: GetReq(QueryExtension, req) allocates the request buffer based on the fixed xQueryExtensionReq size, then line 13 stores the caller-supplied name length truncated into a 16-bit CARD16 field (req->nbytes). Line 14 extends req->length from that truncated value, and line 15 copies req->nbytes bytes of name via _XSend. The missing check is that strlen(name) must be bounded before it is cast to CARD16 and used to size the copy.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-120 fits because a caller-controlled string is copied into a protocol buffer using an unchecked, truncated length, allowing data to exceed the intended buffer boundary. This is a size-check failure on a copy operation, not merely an out-of-bounds read.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the name length is narrowed to CARD16 without validating that it fits the protocol field, so oversized names wrap and the declared/copied length no longer matches the real data. Trigger: a client passes a name longer than USHRT_MAX. Consequence: the X server interprets trailing user-controlled bytes as additional protocol requests, enabling request injection and potential session compromise.

Avoid closing other connections to prevent deep recursion when a large number of idle connections are closed at the start of a pool drain, when a connection is closed.

Signed-off-by: Yan Avlasov <yavlasov@google.com>

description: Envoy is an open source edge and service proxy, designed for cloud-native applications. When a cluster is deleted via Cluster Discovery Service (CDS) all idle connections established to endpoints in that cluster are disconnected. A recursion was introduced in the procedure of disconnecting idle connections that can lead to stack exhaustion and abnormal process termination when a cluster has a large number of idle connections. This infinite recursion causes Envoy to crash. Users are advised to upgrade.

code_evidence: After removing the closed client from its tracking list, onConnectionEvent calls checkForIdleAndCloseIdleConnsIfDraining() before setting the client state to CLOSED. That call can close other idle connections, whose close events re-enter onConnectionEvent and again invoke checkForIdleAndCloseIdleConnsIfDraining(), chaining calls without a bound.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function's synchronous re-entrant close path produces recursion whose depth scales with the number of idle connections, with no depth bound, matching CWE-674 uncontrolled recursion leading to resource exhaustion.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: during pool drain, every connection-close event triggers closure of further idle connections synchronously, and each of those closures re-enters the same handler. Trigger: a cluster with a large number of idle connections is deleted/drained. Consequence: unbounded recursion consumes the stack, causing stack exhaustion and abnormal process termination (DoS).

description: An issue was discovered in Dropbear through 2020.81. Due to a non-RFC-compliant check of the available authentication methods in the client-side SSH code, it is possible for an SSH server to change the login process in its favor. This attack can bypass additional security measures such as FIDO2 tokens or SSH-Askpass. Thus, it allows an attacker to abuse a forwarded agent for logging on to another server unnoticed.

code_evidence: Inside the loop over server-supplied prompts, the code reads echo via buf_getbool and, when echo is false, obtains the secret through getpass_or_cancel, otherwise through get_response. The patch adds cli_ses.is_trivial_auth = 0 at the loop head so the client no longer treats this keyboard-interactive exchange as trivial authentication. The server controls num_prompts and echo, so it can force prompts that bypass the intended trivial-auth path.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is improper authentication: the client insufficiently proves the server's claimed authentication flow, letting the server alter the login process in its favor. This is CWE-287 rather than a mere input-validation flaw because the supported consequence is authentication bypass.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the client's authentication-method handling let the server manipulate the login flow by choosing prompt/echo behavior. Trigger: a malicious server sends a keyboard-interactive request with echo values that avoid the trivial-auth path. Consequence: additional measures such as FIDO2 tokens or SSH-Askpass can be bypassed, allowing agent abuse to log in elsewhere unnoticed.

commit_msg:
Prevent strrpos and strripos from visiting out-of-bounds memory.

Reviewed By: alexeyt

Differential Revision: D14669668

fbshipit-source-id: 16bb4674bccf83ffd737e60d1fd9fd4a0093f77c
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      ptr = bstrrstr(input, len + pos + s_len, s, s_len);', '      ptr = bstrrcasestr(input, len + pos + s_len, s, s_len);'], 'added_lines': ['      ptr = bstrrstr(input, len + std::min(pos + s_len, 0), s, s_len);', '      ptr = bstrrcasestr(input, len + std::min(pos + s_len, 0), s, s_len);']}
description: Insufficient boundary checks for the strrpos and strripos functions allow access to out-of-bounds memory. This affects all supported versions of HHVM (4.0.3, 3.30.4, and 3.27.7 and below).

code_evidence: Guard only rejects pos < -len or pos > len, so a negative pos with |pos| < len is accepted.

For the negative-pos case, the length passed to bstrrstr is len + pos + s_len; when pos + s_len > 0 this exceeds the remaining buffer, and the call starts at input, allowing the search to read past the end.
Same defective length expression len + pos + s_len is passed to bstrrcasestr, duplicating the out-of-bounds read path.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked length lets the search helper read memory before/after the intended buffer, matching CWE-125 (Out-of-bounds Read). This is not a write or integer overflow; the read itself is the weakness.

evidence_lines.code:
if (!s_len || pos < -len || pos > len) {
return -1;

} else {
ptr = bstrrstr(input, len + pos + s_len, s, s_len);

} else {
ptr = bstrrcasestr(input, len + pos + s_len, s, s_len);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the negative-pos branch computes the search length as len + pos + s_len without clamping, so a negative pos close to zero produces a length larger than the valid region. Trigger: callers supplying a negative pos with |pos| < len and a nonempty needle. Consequence: the substring search reads beyond the input buffer, leaking or crashing on out-of-bounds memory.

commit_msg:
Correctly load/initialize classes when using ConstantPool

- do not load classes in the "ifLoaded" calls
- never intitialize classes in the natives
- do not update the constant pool when querying from the natives

Fixes: #12016

[ci skip]

Signed-off-by: Graham Chapman <graham_chapman@ca.ibm.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (NULL != ramCPEntry) {'], 'added_lines': ['\tif ((NULL != ramCPEntry) && J9_ARE_NO_BITS_SET(resolveFlags, J9_RESOLVE_FLAG_NO_CP_UPDATE)) {']}
description: In Eclipse Openj9 to version 0.25.0, usage of the jdk.internal.reflect.ConstantPool API causes the JVM in some cases to pre-resolve certain constant pool entries. This allows a user to call static methods or access static members without running the class initialization method, and may allow a user to observe uninitialized values.

code_evidence: resolveFlags-derived booleans (jitCompileTimeResolve, canRunJavaCode) gate whether Java code may run during resolution; the JCL ConstantPool path sets J9_RESOLVE_FLAG_JCL_CONSTANT_POOL, which suppresses class-constraint checks at lines 31-33.

The resolved method is cached into ramCPEntry->method whenever ramCPEntry is non-NULL; the patch adds a J9_RESOLVE_FLAG_NO_CP_UPDATE guard so ConstantPool queries do not write the constant pool entry.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-909 fits because a critical resource (the class/static state behind the resolved method) is effectively used without its initialization method having run, due to the entry being cached prematurely. This is a missing-initialization weakness rather than a generic access-control or race issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: When the jdk.internal.reflect.ConstantPool API resolves a special method reference, the function previously stored the resolved method into the RAM constant pool entry unconditionally. That pre-resolves the entry without running class initialization, so later static calls can use a method whose class is not initialized, exposing uninitialized static values or skipping required initialization side effects. Root cause is the missing CP-update suppression during query-only resolution; the consequence is observation of uninitialized state.

commit_msg:
usb: dwc3: gadget: never call ->complete() from ->ep_queue()

This is a requirement which has always existed but, somehow, wasn't
reflected in the documentation and problems weren't found until now
when Tuba Yavuz found a possible deadlock happening between dwc3 and
f_hid. She described the situation as follows:

spin_lock_irqsave(&hidg->write_spinlock, flags); // first acquire
/* we our function has been disabled by host */
if (!hidg->req) {
	free_ep_req(hidg->in_ep, hidg->req);
	goto try_again;
}

[...]

status = usb_ep_queue(hidg->in_ep, hidg->req, GFP_ATOMIC);
=>
	[...]
	=> usb_gadget_giveback_request
		=>
		f_hidg_req_complete
			=>
			spin_lock_irqsave(&hidg->write_spinlock, flags); // second acquire

Note that this happens because dwc3 would call ->complete() on a
failed usb_ep_queue() due to failed Start Transfer command. This is,
anyway, a theoretical situation because dwc3 currently uses "No
Response Update Transfer" command for Bulk and Interrupt endpoints.

It's still good to make this case impossible to happen even if the "No
Reponse Update Transfer" command is changed.

Reported-by: Tuba Yavuz <tuba@ece.ufl.edu>
Signed-off-by: Felipe Balbi <felipe.balbi@linux.intel.com>
Cc: stable <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\treq->started = false;', '\tlist_del(&req->list);', '\treq->remaining = 0;', '', '\tif (req->request.status == -EINPROGRESS)', '\t\treq->request.status = status;', '', '\tif (req->trb)', '\t\tusb_gadget_unmap_request_by_dev(dwc->sysdev,', '\t\t\t\t\t\t&req->request, req->direction);', '', '\treq->trb = NULL;', '', '\ttrace_dwc3_gadget_giveback(req);', '', '\tif (dep->number > 1)', '\t\tpm_runtime_put(dwc->dev);'], 'added_lines': ['\tdwc3_gadget_del_and_unmap_request(dep, req, status);']}
description: In the Linux kernel before 4.16.4, a double-locking error in drivers/usb/dwc3/gadget.c may potentially cause a deadlock with f_hid.

code_evidence: dwc3_gadget_giveback() drops dwc->lock with spin_unlock(&dwc->lock), invokes the gadget completion callback usb_gadget_giveback_request() outside the lock, then reacquires it with spin_lock(&dwc->lock). The callback executes while the caller's context is still inside the queue path, so a completion handler that takes its own lock can re-enter that lock.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function's lock release/reacquire around usb_gadget_giveback_request lets a callback re-enter a lock held by the caller, matching CWE-667's improper locking behavior. CWE-764 (multiple locks) is close, but the defect is the locking discipline of this giveback path, not mere lock ordering.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the completion callback is invoked synchronously from the giveback path during ep_queue, releasing and reacquiring dwc->lock around the call. Trigger: a failed Start Transfer causes dwc3 to call ->complete() from usb_ep_queue(), so f_hid's completion handler reacquires hidg->write_spinlock already held by the queueing caller. Consequence: double-locking deadlock (denial of service).

description: The Array.prototype.concat implementation in builtins.cc in Google V8, as used in Google Chrome before 49.0.2623.108, does not properly consider element data types, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read) or possibly have unspecified other impact via crafted JavaScript code.

description: The get_icu_value_internal function in ext/intl/locale/locale_methods.c in PHP before 5.5.36, 5.6.x before 5.6.22, and 7.x before 7.0.7 does not ensure the presence of a '\0' character, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted locale_get_primary_language call.

code_evidence: The do-loop allocates tag_value with erealloc(tag_value, buflen) and sets tag_value_len = buflen, then passes tag_value_len as the ICU output capacity.
When ICU returns U_BUFFER_OVERFLOW_ERROR, the code resets status and continues without increasing buflen, so the retry reuses the same undersized buffer.

The loop condition buflen > tag_value_len compares the overflow length to the capacity, so after a failed retry it can exit with buflen <= tag_value_len even though ICU never wrote a terminating '\0'.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function returns a buffer whose contents are read beyond the intended bounds because the terminating NUL is absent, which is CWE-125. This is not CWE-787, since the defect is an unterminated read, not a write past the buffer end.

evidence_lines.code: } while( buflen > tag_value_len );

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the overflow path does not reserve space for the required '\0' terminator, so the retried ICU call fills the buffer without a NUL. Trigger: a crafted locale_get_primary_language value makes ICU report U_BUFFER_OVERFLOW_ERROR and then return a length equal to the buffer size; the loop ends and callers read tag_value as a C string. Supported consequence: out-of-bounds read, potentially leaking memory or crashing (DoS).

commit_msg:
evtchn: address races with evtchn_reset()

Neither d->evtchn_port_ops nor max_evtchns(d) may be used in an entirely
lock-less manner, as both may change by a racing evtchn_reset(). In the
common case, at least one of the domain's event lock or the per-channel
lock needs to be held. In the specific case of the inter-domain sending
by evtchn_send() and notify_via_xen_event_channel() holding the other
side's per-channel lock is sufficient, as the channel can't change state
without both per-channel locks held. Without such a channel changing
state, evtchn_reset() can't complete successfully.

Lock-free accesses continue to be permitted for the shim (calling some
otherwise internal event channel functions), as this happens while the
domain is in effectively single-threaded mode. Special care also needs
taking for the shim's marking of in-use ports as ECS_RESERVED (allowing
use of such ports in the shim case is okay because switching into and
hence also out of FIFO mode is impossihble there).

As a side effect, certain operations on Xen bound event channels which
were mistakenly permitted so far (e.g. unmask or poll) will be refused
now.

This is part of XSA-343.

Reported-by: Julien Grall <jgrall@amazon.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Acked-by: Julien Grall <jgrall@amazon.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['static bool_t evtchn_fifo_is_masked(const struct domain *d, evtchn_port_t port)', '    const event_word_t *word = evtchn_fifo_word_from_port(d, port);'], 'added_lines': ['static bool_t evtchn_fifo_is_masked(const struct domain *d,', '                                    const struct evtchn *evtchn)', '    const event_word_t *word = evtchn_fifo_word_from_port(d, evtchn->port);']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.14.x. There are evtchn_reset() race conditions. Uses of EVTCHNOP_reset (potentially by a guest on itself) or XEN_DOMCTL_soft_reset (by itself covered by XSA-77) can lead to the violation of various internal assumptions. This may lead to out of bounds memory accesses or triggering of bug checks. In particular, x86 PV guests may be able to elevate their privilege to that of the host. Host and guest crashes are also possible, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS). Information leaks cannot be ruled out. All Xen versions from 4.5 onwards are vulnerable. Xen versions 4.4 and earlier are not vulnerable.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function is a lock-free read helper that only computes a word pointer and tests a bit; it contains no synchronization, no shared-resource modification, and no evidence of the evtchn_reset() race described in the commit, so CWE-362 is not directly supported by this function.

commit_msg:
WireGuard: fix null pointer crash

It was assumed that the WireGuard dissector is always called on the
first pass before the second pass. That might not be the case when the
heuristics dissector sets a conversation dissector later in the stream.
Be prepared to handle this case. Do not simply abort, the previous
packets may be valid data messages.

description: In Wireshark 3.2.0 to 3.2.1, the WireGuard dissector could crash. This was addressed in epan/dissectors/packet-wireguard.c by handling the situation where a certain data structure intentionally has a NULL value.

Trigger: the WireGuard dissector is invoked on a second pass without a prior first-pass call populating wg_pinfo (e.g., heuristics setting the conversation dissector late). Consequence: NULL pointer dereference causing a crash/DoS.
