commit_msg:
avcodec/pngdec: Fix off by 1 size in decode_zbuf()

Fixes out of array access
Fixes: 444/fuzz-2-ffmpeg_VIDEO_AV_CODEC_ID_PNG_fuzzer

Found-by: continuous fuzzing process https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz/tree/master/targets/ffmpeg
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        av_bprint_get_buffer(bp, 1, &buf, &buf_size);', '        if (!buf_size) {', '        zstream.avail_out = buf_size;'], 'added_lines': ['        av_bprint_get_buffer(bp, 2, &buf, &buf_size);', '        if (buf_size < 2) {', '        zstream.avail_out = buf_size - 1;']}
description: FFmpeg before 2017-01-23 has an out-of-bounds write caused by a stack-based buffer overflow related to the decode_zbuf function in libavcodec/pngdec.c.

code_evidence: av_bprint_get_buffer reserves only 1 byte of guaranteed space and availability is checked with !buf_size, so buf_size can be 1; zstream.avail_out is then set to that full buf_size, allowing inflate to write up to buf_size bytes into the buffer.

After inflate, bp->len is advanced by the produced count and bp->str[bp->len] is written with no trailing NUL. When inflate fills the entire reserved buffer, that terminating write lands one byte past the allocated region.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes a NUL byte beyond the intended buffer allocation, which is a write past the end of the buffer, matching CWE-787. The missing reserved byte is the constraint whose absence permits the out-of-bounds write; this is not merely an out-of-bounds read.

evidence_lines.code:
bp->len += zstream.next_out - buf;
bp->str[bp->len] = 0;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the output buffer is sized for exactly buf_size bytes while inflate is permitted to fill all of them, and the subsequent NUL terminator at bp->str[bp->len] has no reserved slot. Trigger: compressed PNG zlib data that expands to fill the available output buffer during a loop iteration. Consequence: a one-byte out-of-bounds write past the heap buffer, corrupting adjacent memory or crashing.

commit_msg:
Prevent array OOB read/write

PiperOrigin-RevId: 371026165
Change-Id: I26ac6372c87246e03c7eb8c94e84c84d86054b36
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  TF_LITE_ENSURE(context, axis_value >= 0);', '  TF_LITE_ENSURE(context, axis_value < NumDimensions(input));']}
description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. A specially crafted TFLite model could trigger an OOB read on heap in the TFLite implementation of `Split_V`(https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/c59c37e7b2d563967da813fa50fe20b21f4da683/tensorflow/lite/kernels/split_v.cc#L99). If `axis_value` is not a value between 0 and `NumDimensions(input)`, then the `SizeOfDimension` function(https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/102b211d892f3abc14f845a72047809b39cc65ab/tensorflow/lite/kernels/kernel_util.h#L148-L150) will access data outside the bounds of the tensor shape array. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.5.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.4.2, TensorFlow 2.3.3, TensorFlow 2.2.3 and TensorFlow 2.1.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: Line 5 reads axis_value directly from the axis tensor; lines 6-8 only normalize negative values by adding NumDimensions(input), which still leaves an out-of-range value if the magnitude exceeds the rank.
Line 32 calls SizeOfDimension(input, axis_value) with that unvalidated axis_value, indexing the tensor's dimension array.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the unvalidated axis_value is used as an index into the tensor dimension array on line 32, reading memory before/after the buffer. The missing bounds check is the root cause; the OOB read is the consequence.

evidence_lines.code: const int input_size = SizeOfDimension(input, axis_value);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The axis tensor value is attacker-controlled (from a crafted TFLite model) and is never constrained to [0, NumDimensions(input)). Normalization of negative values does not bound the result, so SizeOfDimension indexes the shape array out of bounds, causing an OOB heap read.

commit_msg: Fix incorrect loop condition.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        while ( count < length || !bWroteColor ) {', '            Jp2BoxHeader   subBox = *pSubBox ;'], 'added_lines': ['        while ( count < length && !bWroteColor ) {', "            // pSubBox isn't always an aligned pointer, so use memcpy to do the copy.", '            Jp2BoxHeader   subBox;', '            memcpy(&subBox, pSubBox, sizeof(Jp2BoxHeader));']}
description: Exiv2 is a command-line utility and C++ library for reading, writing, deleting, and modifying the metadata of image files. An out-of-bounds read was found in Exiv2 versions v0.27.4 and earlier. The out-of-bounds read is triggered when Exiv2 is used to write metadata into a crafted image file. An attacker could potentially exploit the vulnerability to cause a denial of service by crashing Exiv2, if they can trick the victim into running Exiv2 on a crafted image file. Note that this bug is only triggered when writing the metadata, which is a less frequently used Exiv2 operation than reading the metadata. For example, to trigger the bug in the Exiv2 command-line application, you need to add an extra command-line argument such as insert. The bug is fixed in version v0.27.5.

code_evidence: Line 10's loop condition uses `||`, so iteration continues even when count >= length; the guard on line 11 only checks `length - count`, which underflows when count exceeds length, and line 12/13 then dereference pSubBox at p+count past the buffer.
With the fixed `&&` condition, count is bounded by length before the header read, and lines 21-22 enforce subBox.length <= length - count before count advances on line 23.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This directly matches CWE-125: a pointer into the box buffer is dereferenced outside the intended bounds due to a faulty loop/guard interaction, yielding an out-of-bounds read. It is not a write primitive, since the out-of-range access is a load of the box header.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the disjunctive loop condition lets count reach or exceed length while bWroteColor is false, and the subtraction length - count underflows, defeating the guard. Trigger: a crafted JP2 box whose sub-box lengths advance count past length during metadata writing. Consequence: pSubBox = p+count points beyond boxBuf, and dereferencing it reads out of bounds, crashing Exiv2 (DoS).

commit_msg:
stb_image: Fix bug on JPEGs with malformed DC deltas

extend_receive implicitly requires n <= 15 (code length);
the maximum that actually makes sense for 8-bit baseline JPEG is
11, but 15 is the natural limit for us because the AC coding path
stores the number of magnitude bits in a nibble.

Check that DC delta bits are in range before attempting to call
extend_receive.

Fixes issue #1108.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['   if (t < 0) return stbi__err("bad huffman code","Corrupt JPEG");'], 'added_lines': ['   if (t < 0 || t > 15) return stbi__err("bad huffman code","Corrupt JPEG");']}
description: Buffer overflow vulnerability in function stbi__extend_receive in stb_image.h in stb 2.26 via a crafted JPEG file.

code_evidence: Line 6 decodes the DC Huffman symbol into t; line 7 rejects only negative values, so t may exceed 15. Line 9 passes t as the bit count to stbi__extend_receive(j, t), whose internal shift/mask logic assumes n <= 15 (per commit message).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unvalidated t produces out-of-range bit manipulation that writes past intended bounds in the decode path, matching CWE-787 (out-of-bounds write). The fix adds t > 15 to the guard on line 7, confirming the missing range constraint as the root cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the DC delta magnitude t from the crafted JPEG is not upper-bounded before being used as a bit count. Trigger: a malformed Huffman symbol yielding t > 15 reaches stbi__extend_receive, causing invalid shifts/reads and corrupting the decoded state; the commit notes this leads to a buffer overflow.

commit_msg:
CVE-2017-12894/In lookup_bytestring(), take the length of the byte string into account.

Otherwise, if, in our search of the hash table, we come across a byte
string that's shorter than the string we're looking for, we'll search
past the end of the string in the hash table.

This fixes a buffer over-read discovered by Forcepoint's security
researchers Otto Airamo & Antti Levomäki.

Add a test using the capture file supplied by the reporter(s).
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tregister struct enamemem *tp;', '\tif (tp->e_name)', '\t\treturn (tp->e_name);', '\ttp->e_name = cp = (char *)malloc(len*3);', '\tif (tp->e_name == NULL)', '\treturn (tp->e_name);'], 'added_lines': ['\tregister struct bsnamemem *tp;', '\tif (tp->bs_name)', '\t\treturn (tp->bs_name);', '\ttp->bs_name = cp = (char *)malloc(len*3);', '\tif (tp->bs_name == NULL)', '\treturn (tp->bs_name);']}
description: Several protocol parsers in tcpdump before 4.9.2 could cause a buffer over-read in addrtoname.c:lookup_bytestring().

code_evidence: lookup_bytestring(ndo, ep, len) returns a table entry that may hold a byte string shorter than len; the function returns that cached e_name without verifying its length matches the requested len.
The loop reads *ep and ep++ for i = len-1 iterations, consuming len bytes from the caller's buffer based on the supplied len; the read extent is driven by len rather than any validated buffer size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads memory beyond the intended buffer bounds, matching CWE-125 Out-of-bounds Read. It is not a write overflow (CWE-787) because the defect is the over-read during lookup/formatting, though this patch's linkaddr_string body mainly reflects the renamed struct member.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the hash lookup compares only the looked-up bytes without accounting for the stored string's length, so a shorter stored entry can be matched and its cached name returned for a longer query. Trigger: parsing a packet whose byte string collides with a shorter cached entry. Consequence: subsequent length-based reads (and the lookup itself) access past the end of the intended buffer, an out-of-bounds read.

commit_msg: Fix int overflows in phar (bug #73764)

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the size check adds a constant to an attacker-supplied 32-bit length without overflow protection. Trigger: a crafted PHAR manifest entry with filename_len near UINT32_MAX. Consequence: the check is bypassed, so parsing reads beyond the manifest buffer, causing crash or memory consumption (DoS) and potentially memory corruption.

commit_msg:
After a failed devlink reload, devlink parameters are still registered,
which means user space can set and get their values. In the case of the
mlxsw "acl_region_rehash_interval" parameter, these operations will
trigger a use-after-free [1].

Fix this by rejecting set and get operations while in the failed state.
Return the "-EOPNOTSUPP" error code which does not abort the parameters
dump, but instead causes it to skip over the problematic parameter.

Another possible fix is to perform these checks in the mlxsw parameter
callbacks, but other drivers might be affected by the same problem and I
am not aware of scenarios where these stricter checks will cause a
regression.

commit_msg: fixed heap buffer overflow in gf_m2ts_sync #1250
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tif (i+188>ts->buffer_size) return ts->buffer_size;'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (i+188>=ts->buffer_size) return ts->buffer_size;', '\t\tif (i+192>=ts->buffer_size) return ts->buffer_size;']}
description: In GPAC before 0.8.0, isomedia/isom_read.c in libgpac.a has a heap-based buffer over-read, as demonstrated by a crash in gf_m2ts_sync in media_tools/mpegts.c.

code_evidence: Loop bound checks only ensure i+188 <= buffer_size; when i+188 == buffer_size, the check passes and line 7 reads ts->buffer[i+188], one byte past the end.
Line 8 reads ts->buffer[i+192] with no preceding bound check for i+192, so indexes up to i+192 can exceed buffer_size whenever the buffer is smaller.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads ts->buffer at indices beyond buffer_size due to off-by-one/insufficient bounds checks, which is a direct out-of-bounds read (CWE-125), not a write or integer overflow.

evidence_lines.code:
break;
if ((ts->buffer[i]==0x47) && (ts->buffer[i+192]==0x47)) {

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The loop guards use strict '>' (and omit a guard for the +192 access), so an index equal to buffer_size is permitted and the subsequent reads at i+188 or i+192 access memory past the buffer. Triggered when parsing a truncated MPEG-2 TS buffer where the sync pattern is near the buffer end, causing an out-of-bounds read (crash/DoS, possible info disclosure).

commit_msg: https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/issues/636
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  /*', '    Free resources.', '  */', '  *msl_info.image_info=DestroyImageInfo(*msl_info.image_info);', '  msl_info.image_info=(ImageInfo **) RelinquishMagickMemory(', '    msl_info.image_info);', '  *msl_info.draw_info=DestroyDrawInfo(*msl_info.draw_info);', '  msl_info.draw_info=(DrawInfo **) RelinquishMagickMemory(msl_info.draw_info);', '  msl_info.image=(Image **) RelinquishMagickMemory(msl_info.image);', '  *msl_info.attributes=DestroyImage(*msl_info.attributes);', '  msl_info.attributes=(Image **) RelinquishMagickMemory(msl_info.attributes);', '  msl_info.group_info=(MSLGroupInfo *) RelinquishMagickMemory(', '    msl_info.group_info);']}
description: The ProcessMSLScript function in coders/msl.c in ImageMagick before 6.9.9-5 and 7.x before 7.0.6-5 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory leak) via a crafted file, related to the WriteMSLImage function.

code_evidence: ProcessMSLScript allocates four heap objects via AcquireMagickMemory: msl_info.image_info, msl_info.draw_info, msl_info.image and msl_info.attributes (group_info is also allocated).
The pointers are then populated with CloneImageInfo, CloneDrawInfo and AcquireImage, so each owns a live resource.

After parsing, only msl_info.group_info is released and the parser context is freed; the image_info, draw_info, image and attributes allocations and their cloned/destroyable contents are never released before the function returns.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-772 fits because resources remain allocated after their effective lifetime ends and are not released on the function's return path. This is a missing-release leak, not a use-after-free or double free: the pointers are simply abandoned without DestroyImageInfo, DestroyDrawInfo, DestroyImage or RelinquishMagickMemory.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the cleanup path frees only group_info and the parser, omitting the four AcquireMagickMemory allocations and their cloned contents. Trigger: any MSL file processed by ProcessMSLScript, including repeated crafted inputs. Consequence: the image_info, draw_info, image and attributes resources leak on each invocation, enabling memory-consumption denial of service.

commit_msg:
drm/amd/display: memory leak

In dcn*_clock_source_create when dcn20_clk_src_construct fails allocated
clk_src needs release.

Signed-off-by: Navid Emamdoost <navid.emamdoost@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Alex Deucher <alexander.deucher@amd.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tkfree(clk_src);']}
description: Memory leaks in *clock_source_create() functions under drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc in the Linux kernel before 5.3.8 allow attackers to cause a denial of service (memory consumption). This affects the dce112_clock_source_create() function in drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/dce112/dce112_resource.c, the dce100_clock_source_create() function in drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/dce100/dce100_resource.c, the dcn10_clock_source_create() function in drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/dcn10/dcn10_resource.c, the dcn20_clock_source_create() function in drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/dcn20/dcn20_resource.c, the dce120_clock_source_create() function in drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/dce120/dce120_resource.c, the dce110_clock_source_create() function in drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/dce110/dce110_resource.c, and the dce80_clock_source_create() function in drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/dce80/dce80_resource.c, aka CID-055e547478a1.

code_evidence: clk_src is allocated with kzalloc at line 9; the NULL check at lines 10-11 is the only early exit that avoids an allocation leak.
When dce110_clk_src_construct fails at line 12-13, the function skips the success return at lines 14-15 and falls to the failure path.
The failure path at lines 17-19 returns NULL without freeing the still-allocated clk_src; the patch adds kfree(clk_src) before BREAK_TO_DEBUGGER.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-401 fits because memory is allocated and then abandoned on an error path without release, making it unavailable for reuse. This is a missing-release leak, not a use-after-free or double-free.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the construct-failure branch returns NULL while the kzalloc'd clk_src remains unreferenced and unreleased. Trigger: dce110_clk_src_construct returns nonzero. Consequence: each failed creation leaks a dce110_clk_src object, enabling memory-consumption DoS over repeated calls.

commit_msg:
gsocketclient: Fix criticals

This ensures the parent GTask is kept alive as long as an enumeration
is running and trying to connect.

Closes #1646
Closes #1649
diff_func:
--- func_before
+++ func_after
@@ -27,9 +27,22 @@
   else
     data->enumerator = g_socket_connectable_enumerate (connectable);
 
+  /* The flow and ownership here isn't quite obvious:
+    - The task starts an async attempt to connect.
+      - Each attempt holds a single ref on task.
+      - Each attempt may create new attempts by timing out (not a failure) so
+        there are multiple attempts happening in parallel.
+      - Upon failure an attempt will start a new attempt that steals its ref
+        until there are no more attempts left and it drops its ref.
+      - Upon success it will cancel all other attempts and continue on
+        to the rest of the connection (tls, proxies, etc) which do not
+        happen in parallel and at the very end drop its ref.
+      - Upon cancellation an attempt drops its ref.
+   */
+
   data->task = g_task_new (client, cancellable, callback, user_data);
   g_task_set_source_tag (data->task, g_socket_client_connect_async);
   g_task_set_task_data (data->task, data, (GDestroyNotify)g_socket_client_async_connect_data_free);
 
-  enumerator_next_async (data);
+  enumerator_next_async (data, FALSE);
 }
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  enumerator_next_async (data);'], 'added_lines': ["  /* The flow and ownership here isn't quite obvious:", '    - The task starts an async attempt to connect.', '      - Each attempt holds a single ref on task.', '      - Each attempt may create new attempts by timing out (not a failure) so', '        there are multiple attempts happening in parallel.', '      - Upon failure an attempt will start a new attempt that steals its ref', '        until there are no more attempts left and it drops its ref.', '      - Upon success it will cancel all other attempts and continue on', '        to the rest of the connection (tls, proxies, etc) which do not', '        happen in parallel and at the very end drop its ref.', '      - Upon cancellation an attempt drops its ref.', '   */', '', '  enumerator_next_async (data, FALSE);']}
description: gio/gsocketclient.c in GNOME GLib 2.59.2 does not ensure that a parent GTask remains alive during the execution of a connection-attempting enumeration, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (g_socket_client_connected_callback mishandling and application crash) via a crafted web site, as demonstrated by GNOME Web (aka Epiphany).

code_evidence: The function creates a GTask and stores it in data->task, then immediately starts the asynchronous connection enumeration via enumerator_next_async(data). The task is only referenced by data->task; nothing in this function keeps the parent GTask alive across the parallel connection attempts that the enumeration may spawn (timeouts/success/failure).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The code fails to account for an unusual but reachable condition (parallel/long-lived connection attempts outliving the initiating call) and omits the check/ref needed to keep the task valid, matching CWE-754. This is a lifetime/ownership omission rather than a generic memory-safety flaw.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the parent GTask's lifetime is not protected while an enumeration runs and may create multiple parallel attempts. Trigger: a connection attempt that times out or otherwise continues the enumeration after the original connect call returns. Consequence: the GTask can be freed while callbacks (g_socket_client_connected_callback) still use it, causing a crash/DoS.

commit_msg:
Chain binding only requires the rule addition/insertion command within
the same transaction. Removal of rules from chain bindings within the
same transaction makes no sense, userspace does not utilize this
feature. Replace nft_chain_is_bound() check to nft_chain_binding() in
rule deletion commands. Replace command implies a rule deletion, reject
this command too.

Rule flush command can also safely rely on this nft_chain_binding()
check because unbound chains are not allowed since 62e1e94b246e
("netfilter: nf_tables: reject unbound chain set before commit phase").

Fixes: d0e2c7de92c7 ("netfilter: nf_tables: add NFT_CHAIN_BINDING")
Reported-by: Kevin Rich <kevinrich1337@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tif (nft_chain_is_bound(chain))', '\t\tif (nft_chain_is_bound(chain))'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (nft_chain_binding(chain))', '\t\tif (nft_chain_binding(chain))']}
description:
A use-after-free vulnerability in the Linux kernel's netfilter: nf_tables component can be exploited to achieve local privilege escalation.

Addition and removal of rules from chain bindings within the same transaction causes leads to use-after-free.

We recommend upgrading past commit f15f29fd4779be8a418b66e9d52979bb6d6c2325.

code_evidence: The first loop iterates table chains and skips only chains for which nft_chain_is_bound(chain) is true at line 11 before calling nft_delrule_by_chain(ctx) at line 14. A chain that is a binding (nft_chain_binding) but not bound can therefore have its rules deleted within the same transaction in which the binding was added, which is the unsafe operation the patch replaces with nft_chain_binding().
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the deleted rules leave the chain binding referencing freed rule memory that may later be reused, matching the described use-after-free. The defect is an insufficient guard condition enabling premature freeing, not merely a logic error.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the guard tests nft_chain_is_bound() instead of nft_chain_binding(), so chain bindings that are not yet bound are processed by nft_delrule_by_chain(). Trigger: a transaction that adds rules to a chain binding and deletes them in the same batch. Consequence: rules referenced by the binding are freed while still reachable, producing a use-after-free.

commit_msg:
Don't allocate a group terminator unless we are in a group-list.

This will reduce memory allocation for garbage/spam address lists.

It also makes no sense to store a terminator when there wasn't a
display-name indicating the start of a group.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  int ws_pending, nl;', '      if (last)'], 'added_lines': ['  int ws_pending, nl, in_group = 0;', '      in_group = 1;', '      if (last && in_group)', '      in_group = 0;']}
description: rfc822.c in Mutt through 2.0.4 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (mailbox unavailability) by sending email messages with sequences of semicolon characters in RFC822 address fields (aka terminators of empty groups). A small email message from the attacker can cause large memory consumption, and the victim may then be unable to see email messages from other persons.

code_evidence: In the ';' branch, when phraselen is zero and no comment applies, no address is added, yet the code unconditionally allocates a new terminator node via rfc822_new_address() and links it after last (lines 119-123). Because each semicolon in the input reaches this branch, a sequence of semicolons allocates one ADDRESS node per character; these nodes are retained on the top/last list and never freed within the parse loop.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-401 fits because the function allocates ADDRESS nodes for each semicolon and keeps them reachable on the list without any corresponding release, so the allocated memory remains unavailable for reuse; the availability impact matches the DoS resource-consumption scope. The patch's in_group guard confirms the unnecessary allocation is the defect, not an out-of-bounds or type issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the semicolon handler allocates a group-terminator node regardless of whether a group (display-name) was actually started. Trigger: an RFC822 address field containing many semicolons, including empty-group terminators. Consequence: memory grows linearly with attacker-supplied input, exhausting memory and making the mailbox unavailable (DoS).

description: An issue was discovered in fs/f2fs/inline.c in the Linux kernel through 4.4. A denial of service (out-of-bounds memory access and BUG) can occur for a modified f2fs filesystem image in which an inline inode contains an invalid reserved blkaddr.

code_evidence: set_new_dnode and f2fs_reserve_block(&dn,0) populate dn.data_blkaddr from the inline inode's reserved block address; the original code immediately proceeds to write the page without checking that the reserved address is valid (NEW_ADDR), so an attacker-controlled corrupted image yields an arbitrary blkaddr used downstream.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The supported consequence is reading memory beyond the sit bitmap boundary, matching CWE-125 (Out-of-bounds Read). The weakness is the absent bounds/validity constraint on the block address, not a write overflow or use-after-free itself.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is the missing validation of the inline inode's reserved blkaddr before the converted page is written out. A crafted f2fs image with an invalid reserved blkaddr triggers use of that address when updating the sit bitmap, causing an out-of-bounds read and KASAN crash (denial of service).

commit_msg:
iio: imu: adis16400: release allocated memory on failure

In adis_update_scan_mode, if allocation for adis->buffer fails,
previously allocated adis->xfer needs to be released.

Signed-off-by: Navid Emamdoost <navid.emamdoost@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Alexandru Ardelean <alexandru.ardelean@analog.com>
Signed-off-by: Jonathan Cameron <Jonathan.Cameron@huawei.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (!adis->buffer)'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (!adis->buffer) {', '\t\tkfree(adis->xfer);', '\t\tadis->xfer = NULL;', '\t}']}
description: A memory leak in the adis_update_scan_mode() function in drivers/iio/imu/adis_buffer.c in the Linux kernel before 5.3.9 allows attackers to cause a denial of service (memory consumption), aka CID-ab612b1daf41.

code_evidence: Line 14 allocates adis->xfer with kcalloc; lines 15-16 return -ENOMEM if that allocation fails, while the earlier frees at lines 9-10 have already released the prior buffer and xfer.

Line 17 allocates adis->buffer; lines 18-19 return -ENOMEM when this second allocation fails, but adis->xfer allocated at line 14 is not freed on this error path (the fix adds kfree(adis->xfer) here).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-401 fits because memory allocated by kcalloc is never released on an error return, leaving it unavailable for reuse; this is a missing-release leak rather than a use-after-free or double-free, since no dangling pointer is accessed.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the adis->buffer allocation failure path returns -ENOMEM without releasing the adis->xfer memory allocated earlier in the same call. Trigger: repeated calls where the xfer allocation succeeds but the buffer kcalloc fails (e.g. under memory pressure). Consequence: the xfer array is leaked and its pointer is overwritten on the next call, causing unbounded memory consumption and denial of service.

commit_msg: imgcodecs: add overflow checks
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['        CV_Assert(size > 0); // overflow, 2Gb limit']}
description: In OpenCV 3.3.1, an assertion failure happens in cv::RBaseStream::setPos in modules/imgcodecs/src/bitstrm.cpp because of an incorrect integer cast.

code_evidence: m_offset and size are read directly from the attacker-controlled BMP stream via getDWord().
After reading header fields, the code calls m_strm.skip( size - 36 ) using the file-supplied size value.
A separate attacker-influenced value, clrused, is guarded by CV_Assert(clrused >= 0 && clrused <= 256), showing reachable assertions in this parser.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-617 fits because an attacker-controlled BMP header can drive the decoder into an assertion failure, terminating the application. This is not a memory-corruption weakness (e.g., CWE-190/787) since the demonstrated effect is an abort triggered by malformed input.

evidence_lines.code: m_strm.skip( size - 36 );
CV_Assert(clrused >= 0 && clrused <= 256);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The BMP 'size' field is read from untrusted input and used to compute a skip offset (size - 36) without validating it. A crafted or truncated stream drives the stream position to an invalid value, and the subsequent parsing/assertion path aborts the process rather than returning a clean parse error. Root cause is trusting an unvalidated header field; the supported consequence is a reachable assertion causing denial of service (crash/exit).

commit_msg:
Bug 699655: Properly check the return value....

...when getting a value from a dictionary
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            code = dict_find_string(op, "Implementation", &pImpl);', '            if (code != 0) {'], 'added_lines': ['            if ((code = dict_find_string(op, "Implementation", &pImpl)) < 0)', '                return code;', '            if (code > 0) {']}
description: In Artifex Ghostscript before 9.24, attackers able to supply crafted PostScript files could use a type confusion in the setcolor function to crash the interpreter or possibly have unspecified other impact.

code_evidence: The result of dict_find_string is tested with code != 0, so both a found entry (>0) and an error (<0) enter the branch; pImpl is then passed to array_get without confirming the lookup succeeded.

When array_get succeeds, the retrieved element is cast to gs_pattern_instance_t via r_ptr and dereferenced by pattern_instance_uses_base_space(cc.pattern), assuming the stored object is a pattern instance.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function retrieves an object and reinterprets it as gs_pattern_instance_t without verifying its actual type, which is an incorrect type conversion/cast (CWE-704). The missing lookup-success check is the enabling defect; the type mismatch is the supported weakness rather than mere input validation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the dictionary lookup return value is not distinguished from an error, so a failed or erroring lookup of "Implementation" leaves pImpl unvalidated while the code proceeds to array_get and treats the result as a pattern instance. Trigger: crafted PostScript supplying a dictionary whose Implementation entry is absent, malformed, or errors. Consequence: the element is used as gs_pattern_instance_t (type confusion), leading to a crash or unspecified impact in setcolor.

commit_msg:
Fix OSS-Fuzz issue 20332: buffer overflow in jbig2_image_compose.

With extreme values of x/y/w/h we can get overflow. Test for this
and exit safely.

Thanks for OSS-Fuzz for reporting.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '    if ((UINT32_MAX - src->width  < (x > 0 ? x : -x)) ||', '        (UINT32_MAX - src->height < (y > 0 ? y : -y)))', '    {', '#ifdef JBIG2_DEBUG', '        jbig2_error(ctx, JBIG2_SEVERITY_DEBUG, -1, "overflow in compose_image");', '#endif', '        return 0;', '    }']}
description: jbig2_image_compose in jbig2_image.c in Artifex jbig2dec before 0.18 has a heap-based buffer overflow.

code_evidence: w/h are taken from src->width/height and adjusted by x/y; the negative-x path computes ss += (-x-1)>>3 and the negative-y path computes syoffset = -y * src->stride, all in uint32_t arithmetic where large magnitudes can wrap.
Clipping only compares (uint32_t)x + w and (uint32_t)y + h against dst dimensions; these sums can wrap, so the clipping does not bound w/h when x or y is extreme.
dd = dst->data + y*dst->stride + leftbyte is computed from the unclipped y, and bytewidth is derived from x+w; the compose_opt_* call then writes h rows using this dd/bytewidth into dst.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The compose_opt_* functions write into dst using a dd pointer and bytewidth computed from unvalidated offsets, producing a write past the intended dst buffer, which is CWE-787. This is not merely an out-of-bounds read because the affected operation stores into dst memory.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: x and y are signed offsets whose magnitudes are combined with uint32_t widths/strides without overflow checks, so clipping and pointer/bytewidth arithmetic wrap. Trigger: extreme x/y values passed to jbig2_image_compose. Consequence: dd and bytewidth can point beyond or before dst->data, and the compose_opt_* loop writes out of bounds on the heap.

commit_msg:
datasets: flag to disable "write" actions

Add a new configuration flag, "datasets.rules.allow-write" to control
if rules can contain "save" or "state" rules which allow write access
to the file system.

Ticket: #6123
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '    int allow_save = 1;', '    if (ConfGetBool("datasets.rules.allow-write", &allow_save)) {', '        if (!allow_save) {', '            SCLogError(SC_ERR_INVALID_SIGNATURE,', '                    "Rules containing save/state datasets have been disabled");', '            return -1;', '        }', '    }']}
description: In Suricata before 6.0.13 (when there is an adversary who controls an external source of rules), a dataset filename, that comes from a rule, may trigger absolute or relative directory traversal, and lead to write access to a local filesystem. This is addressed in 6.0.13 by requiring allow-absolute-filenames and allow-write (in the datasets rules configuration section) if an installation requires traversal/writing in this situation.

code_evidence: The function takes an attacker-influenced `save` path from a dataset rule and only rejects absolute paths or traversal when `allow_absolute` is false; otherwise it skips both checks.
It then builds `path` as `dir/save` via snprintf and copies it back into `save` with strlcpy, so the unvalidated rule-supplied path becomes the filesystem path used for the save operation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function constructs a pathname intended to stay under the configured data directory but fails to properly neutralize absolute paths and traversal sequences, matching CWE-22 path traversal. This is not merely a missing configuration check: the attacker-controlled `save` value directly reaches the final path used for writing.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the path from the rule is used to construct a filesystem location without unconditional neutralization of absolute paths or '..' traversal, and the checks are bypassed when the allow-absolute configuration is enabled. Trigger: an adversary controlling dataset rules supplies an absolute or traversal path. Supported consequence: the resolved path escapes the intended data directory, enabling unauthorized file write.

This reverts commit 9aa4be691f5c73eb3c68606d824c104550c053f7 and removed the
redundant flag setting.

Fixes #19643

Fixes LOW CVE-2022-3996

Reviewed-by: Dmitry Belyavskiy <beldmit@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Tomas Mraz <tomas@openssl.org>
(Merged from https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/19652)

(cherry picked from commit 4d0340a6d2f327700a059f0b8f954d6160f8eef5)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if (ret == -1 && CRYPTO_THREAD_write_lock(x->lock)) {', '        x->ex_flags |= EXFLAG_INVALID_POLICY;', '        CRYPTO_THREAD_unlock(x->lock);', '    }'], 'added_lines': []}
description:
If an X.509 certificate contains a malformed policy constraint and
policy processing is enabled, then a write lock will be taken twice
recursively.  On some operating systems (most widely: Windows) this
results in a denial of service when the affected process hangs.  Policy
processing being enabled on a publicly facing server is not considered
to be a common setup.

Policy processing is enabled by passing the `-policy'
argument to the command line utilities or by calling the
`X509_VERIFY_PARAM_set1_policies()' function.

Update (31 March 2023): The description of the policy processing enablement
was corrected based on CVE-2023-0466.

code_evidence: The bad_mapping label is reached from validation failures, e.g. when a mapping uses NID_any_policy (lines 16-17), which sets ret=-1 and jumps here.

At lines 44-47 the error path calls CRYPTO_THREAD_write_lock(x->lock) and then CRYPTO_THREAD_unlock(x->lock). This lock is acquired inside a function that is itself invoked while the caller already holds x->lock during policy processing, so the same write lock is taken recursively.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-667 covers improper acquisition/release of a lock leading to unexpected state; here the error path takes the same write lock twice, a classic improper locking pattern whose supported impact is DoS. It is not a generic race but a lock-usage defect at the bad_mapping branch.

evidence_lines.code:
ret = -1;
goto bad_mapping;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the error-handling path re-acquires x->lock via CRYPTO_THREAD_write_lock even though the caller already holds it, producing recursive/improper locking on malformed policy constraints. Trigger: a certificate with a malformed policy mapping (ret == -1) while policy processing is enabled. Consequence: on platforms with non-recursive write locks (e.g. Windows) the process deadlocks, causing a denial of service.

commit_msg:
[Merge to 54] Fix CPDFSDK_PageView cleanup.

In https://pdfium.googlesource.com/pdfium/+/461eeafe191068ac8c32f2717907fc6a22a667d2
we moved the map cleanup for the page view to happen before the page view was
destroyed and before we killed the annotation focus.

The map removal must happen before the pageview is destroyed, but must happen
after we've killed the annotation focus in order to not create duplicate page
views which point to the same page.

BUG=chromium:645122
R=tsepez@chromium.org

Review URL: https://codereview.chromium.org/2338893002 .

Review-Url: https://codereview.chromium.org/2320253002
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  pPageView->KillFocusAnnotIfNeeded();'], 'added_lines': ['  // This must happen before we remove |pPageView| from the map because', '  // |KillFocusAnnotIfNeeded| can call into the |GetPage| method which will', "  // look for this page view in the map, if it doesn't find it a new one will", '  // be created. We then have two page views pointing to the same page and', '  // bad things happen.', '  pPageView->KillFocusAnnotIfNeeded();', '']}
description: A heap use after free in PDFium in Google Chrome prior to 54.0.2840.59 for Windows, Mac, and Linux; 54.0.2840.85 for Android allows a remote attacker to potentially exploit heap corruption via crafted PDF files.

code_evidence: Line 8 erases the map entry, dropping the document's reference to pPageView. Line 9 then calls KillFocusAnnotIfNeeded(), which can re-enter GetPage and create a fresh page view for the same page because the map no longer holds it. Line 10 deletes the original pPageView while the newly created view may still reference the same underlying page.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The delete at line 10 frees the page view while a duplicate page view created during focus cleanup may still reference the same underlying page, so subsequent access to that freed object is a use-after-free, matching CWE-416.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the map entry is removed before focus cleanup, so re-entrant GetPage creates a second page view for the same page. Trigger: KillFocusAnnotIfNeeded() calls back into GetPage after erase. Consequence: two page views alias one page and one is deleted, leaving a dangling reference that can be used later, producing heap use-after-free and possible corruption.

commit_msg: Pad keys to avoid memory errors (fixes #147)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    pad_short_parameter(k1, data.getLengthBytes());']}
description: An issue was discovered in QPDF before 7.0.0. There is a stack-based out-of-bounds read in the function iterate_rc4 in QPDF_encryption.cc.

code_evidence: iterate_rc4 is invoked with k1 as the output/input buffer, sized by data.getLengthBytes(), while k1 is only initialized from compute_encryption_key; the patch adds pad_short_parameter(k1, data.getLengthBytes()) immediately before this call to ensure k1 has the required length.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the unsafe operation is reading past the end of the k1 buffer; the root cause is a missing length constraint (now supplied by padding), not writing out of bounds (CWE-787) or a buffer overflow.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: When k1 is shorter than data.getLengthBytes(), iterate_rc4 reads beyond k1's allocated buffer. The trigger is a key-length parameter exceeding the actual k1 size; the supported consequence is a stack-based out-of-bounds read, leaking memory or crashing.

commit_msg:
There is a current use after free possible on a gatt server if a client
disconnects while a WriteValue call is being processed with dbus.

This patch includes the addition of a pending disconnect callback to handle
cleanup better if a disconnect occurs during a write, an acquire write
or read operation using bt_att_register_disconnect with the cb.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tconst char *path = device_get_path(op->device);', '\tserver = btd_device_get_gatt_server(op->device);'], 'added_lines': ['\tstruct btd_device *device = att_get_device(op->att);', '\tconst char *path = device_get_path(device);', '\tserver = btd_device_get_gatt_server(device);']}
description: An issue was discovered in gatt-database.c in BlueZ 5.61. A use-after-free can occur when a client disconnects during D-Bus processing of a WriteValue call.

code_evidence: Line 3 stores the pending_op as user_data; line 4 dereferences op->device to obtain the device path before any lifetime check.

Line 28 later dereferences op->device again to fetch the gatt server, and line 29 passes that server to bt_gatt_server_get_mtu, so both the device and server pointers are consumed without validating that the pending operation's device is still alive.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because a pointer held in the pending operation is dereferenced after the object it references may have been freed by a concurrent disconnect. This is a stale-pointer lifetime defect, not merely a null dereference or a race on an unlocked value.

evidence_lines.code:
struct pending_op *op = user_data;
const char *path = device_get_path(op->device);

server = btd_device_get_gatt_server(op->device);
mtu = bt_gatt_server_get_mtu(server);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: append_options is invoked during D-Bus message construction for a pending WriteValue. If the client disconnects while that write is being processed, the device/pending_op backing op->device can be freed, yet op->device is dereferenced at lines 4 and 28. The stale pointer yields a use-after-free when device_get_path or btd_device_get_gatt_server read freed memory, enabling crash/DoS and potentially memory corruption.

commit_msg:
As part of CVE-2013-4288, the D-Bus clients were allowed (and
encouraged) to submit the UID of the subject of authorization checks
to avoid races against UID changes (notably using executables
set-UID to root).

However, that also allowed any client to submit an arbitrary UID, and
that could be used to bypass "can only ask about / affect the same UID"
checks in CheckAuthorization / RegisterAuthenticationAgent /
UnregisterAuthenticationAgent.  This allowed an attacker:

- With CheckAuthorization, to cause the registered authentication
  agent in victim's session to pop up a dialog, or to determine whether
  the victim currently has a temporary authorization to perform an
  operation.

  (In principle, the attacker can also determine whether JavaScript
  rules allow the victim process to perform an operation; however,
  usually rules base their decisions on information determined from
  the supplied UID, so the attacker usually won't learn anything new.)

- With RegisterAuthenticationAgent, to prevent the victim's
  authentication agent to work (for a specific victim process),
  or to learn about which operations requiring authorization
  the victim is attempting.

To fix this, expose internal _polkit_unix_process_get_owner() /
obsolete polkit_unix_process_get_owner() as a private
polkit_unix_process_get_racy_uid__() (being more explicit about the
dangers on relying on it), and use it in
polkit_backend_session_monitor_get_user_for_subject() to return
a boolean indicating whether the subject UID may be caller-chosen.

Then, in the permission checks that require the subject to be
equal to the caller, fail on caller-chosen UIDs (and continue
through the pre-existing code paths which allow root, or root-designated
server processes, to ask about arbitrary subjects.)

Signed-off-by: Miloslav Trmač <mitr@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  return _polkit_unix_process_get_owner (process, error);'], 'added_lines': ['  return polkit_unix_process_get_racy_uid__ (process, error);']}
description: A flaw was found in polkit before version 0.116. The implementation of the polkit_backend_interactive_authority_check_authorization function in polkitd allows to test for authentication and trigger authentication of unrelated processes owned by other users. This may result in a local DoS and information disclosure.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function is a thin accessor delegating to a UID getter; it contains no authorization decision, resource access, or actor check, so it does not directly demonstrate missing authorization.

commit_msg:
x86/pv: Don't have %cr4.fsgsbase active behind a guest kernels back

Currently, a 64bit PV guest can appear to set and clear FSGSBASE in %cr4, but
the bit remains set in hardware.  Therefore, the {RD,WR}{FS,GS}BASE are usable
even when the guest kernel believes that they are disabled.

The FSGSBASE feature isn't currently supported in Linux, and its context
switch path has some optimisations which rely on userspace being unable to use
the WR{FS,GS}BASE instructions.  Xen's current behaviour undermines this
expectation.

In 64bit PV guest context, always load the guest kernels setting of FSGSBASE
into %cr4.  This requires adjusting how Xen uses the {RD,WR}{FS,GS}BASE
instructions.

 * Delete the cpu_has_fsgsbase helper.  It is no longer safe, as users need to
   check %cr4 directly.
 * The raw __rd{fs,gs}base() helpers are only safe to use when %cr4.fsgsbase
   is set.  Comment this property.
 * The {rd,wr}{fs,gs}{base,shadow}() and read_msr() helpers are updated to use
   the current %cr4 value to determine which mechanism to use.
 * toggle_guest_mode() and save_segments() are update to avoid reading
   fs/gsbase if the values in hardware cannot be stale WRT struct vcpu.  A
   consequence of this is that the write_cr() path needs to cache the current
   bases, as subsequent context switches will skip saving the values.
 * write_cr4() is updated to ensure that the shadow %cr4.fsgsbase value is
   observed in a safe way WRT the hardware setting, if an interrupt happens to
   hit in the middle.
 * load_segments() is updated to use the VMLOAD optimisation if FSGSBASE is
   unavailable, even if only gs_shadow needs updating.  As a minor perf
   improvement, check cpu_has_svm first to short circuit a context-dependent
   conditional on Intel hardware.
 * pv_make_cr4() is updated for 64bit PV guests to use the guest kernels
   choice of FSGSBASE.

This is part of XSA-293.

Reported-by: Andy Lutomirski <luto@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Cooper <andrew.cooper3@citrix.com>
Reviewed-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if ( cpu_has_fsgsbase && !is_pv_32bit_vcpu(v) )'], 'added_lines': ['    /* %fs/%gs bases can only be stale if WR{FS,GS}BASE are usable. */', '    if ( (read_cr4() & X86_CR4_FSGSBASE) && !is_pv_32bit_vcpu(v) )']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.11.x allowing x86 PV guest OS users to cause a denial of service or gain privileges because a guest can manipulate its virtualised %cr4 in a way that is incompatible with Linux (and possibly other guest kernels).

code_evidence: save_segments() gates reading the hardware FS/GS base on cpu_has_fsgsbase, a global CPU capability, rather than on the guest-kernel-controlled %cr4.fsgsbase bit. When the capability exists but the guest has disabled FSGSBASE in its virtualised %cr4, the code still executes __rdfsbase()/__rdgsbase() and copies hardware values into v->arch.pv.fs_base and gs_base_{kernel,user}.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function fails to validate the guest's %cr4.fsgsbase setting before acting on it, using an unvalidated capability flag as a proxy for the actual required property; this is improper validation of guest-controlled state. It is not merely an incorrect transformation, so CWE-20 fits.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the condition trusts a static CPU capability instead of the guest-supplied/controlled %cr4 state, so the hardware bases are read even when the guest kernel believes FSGSBASE is disabled. Trigger: a 64bit PV guest clearing %cr4.fsgsbase while the host CPU supports the feature. Consequence: stale/attacker-influenced bases are cached into vcpu state, letting userspace use WR{FS,GS}BASE despite the guest kernel's expectation, enabling privilege escalation or DoS.

commit_msg:
Fix uudecode buffer overflow.

mutt_decode_uuencoded() used each line's initial "length character"
without any validation.  It would happily read past the end of the
input line, and with a suitable value even past the length of the
input buffer.

As I noted in ticket 404, there are several other changes that could
be added to make the parser more robust.  However, to avoid
accidentally introducing another bug or regression, I'm restricting
this patch to simply addressing the overflow.

Thanks to Tavis Ormandy for reporting the issue, along with a sample
message demonstrating the problem.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    for (c = 0; c < linelen;)', '      for (l = 2; l <= 6; l += 2)'], 'added_lines': ['    for (c = 0; c < linelen && *pt;)', '      for (l = 2; l <= 6 && *pt && *(pt + 1); l += 2)']}
description: Buffer Overflow in uudecoder in Mutt affecting all versions starting from 0.94.13 before 2.2.3 allows read past end of input line

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function performs out-of-bounds reads of the input line via unvalidated length character and pointer advancement, not a buffer copy that writes past an output buffer, so it does not directly support CWE-120.

commit_msg:
Kafka: Limit our decompression size.

Don't assume that the Internet has our best interests at heart when it
gives us the size of our decompression buffer. Assign an arbitrary limit
of 50 MB.

This fixes #16739 in that it takes care of

** (process:17681): WARNING **: 20:03:07.440: Dissector bug, protocol Kafka, in packet 31: ../epan/proto.c:7043: failed assertion "end >= fi->start"

which is different from the original error output. It looks like *that*
might have taken care of in one of the other recent Kafka bug fixes.

The decompression routines return a success or failure status. Use

commit_msg:
(uid_t) -1 is still used as placeholder to mean "unset". This is OK, since
there should be no users with such number, see
https://systemd.io/UIDS-GIDS#special-linux-uids.

(uid_t) -1 is used as the default value in class initialization.

When a user or group above INT32_MAX is created, the numeric uid or
gid wraps around to negative when the value is assigned to gint, and
polkit gets confused. Let's accept such gids, except for -1.

A nicer fix would be to change the underlying type to e.g. uint32 to
not have negative values. But this cannot be done without breaking the
API, so likely new functions will have to be added (a
polkit_unix_user_new variant that takes a unsigned, and the same for
_group_new, _set_uid, _get_uid, _set_gid, _get_gid, etc.). This will
require a bigger patch.

Fixes https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/polkit/polkit/issues/74.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      unix_group->gid = g_value_get_int (value);'], 'added_lines': ['  gint val;', '      val = g_value_get_int (value);', '      g_return_if_fail (val != -1);', '      unix_group->gid = val;']}
description: A flaw was found in PolicyKit (aka polkit) 0.115 that allows a user with a uid greater than INT_MAX to successfully execute any systemctl command.

code_evidence: The PROP_GID setter reads the incoming GValue with g_value_get_int and stores the result directly into unix_group->gid without any range or sentinel check. The value arrives as a signed gint, so a group ID above INT32_MAX wraps to a negative number, including the reserved (gid_t)-1 sentinel that the class uses to mean unset.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-20 fits because the setter fails to validate that the supplied gid is within the permitted domain (non-negative, excluding the -1 sentinel) before storing it. This is improper input validation, not a transformation/filtering flaw.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the setter accepts any signed int from the GValue and assigns it as the group id, so a large gid wraps negative and can equal the -1 placeholder. Trigger: a caller sets PROP_GID with a group id above INT32_MAX. Consequence: the object's gid becomes a negative sentinel, confusing downstream polkit authorization checks that treat -1 as unset; the patch adds val != -1 rejection.

commit_msg:
MBIM: stop pre sizing wmem arrays

In case of malformed packet, this can lead to an insane amount of
memory.
Instead let's use the automatic growth mecanism. This way the malformed
packet is caught by the dissection engine.

Bug: 14056
Change-Id: I7bf5b80a516210b341356f5d495f08d1dba05805
Reviewed-on: https://code.wireshark.org/review/23537

Petri-Dish: Pascal Quantin <pascal.quantin@gmail.com>

description: In Wireshark 2.4.0 to 2.4.1 and 2.2.0 to 2.2.9, the MBIM dissector could crash or exhaust system memory. This was addressed in epan/dissectors/packet-mbim.c by changing the memory-allocation approach.

code_evidence: The packet_filters_count is read directly from the packet via proto_tree_add_item_ret_uint (line 12) and used without validation to pre-size a wmem array: wmem_array_sized_new(..., packet_filters_count) at line 15, guarded only by a nonzero check at line 14.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-400 fits because the function fails to constrain how much memory it consumes based on untrusted input, leading to resource exhaustion. The related CWE-789 (uncontrolled memory allocation) is a more specific child, but the target is the broader uncontrolled-resource-consumption class.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: an attacker-controlled 32-bit count from the malformed MBIM packet is used to pre-allocate memory before any bounds check against the actual remaining packet data. Trigger: a crafted packet declaring an enormous packet_filters_count. Consequence: the dissector allocates an excessive amount of memory, exhausting system memory or crashing Wireshark (DoS).

description: PJSIP is a free and open source multimedia communication library written in C language. In versions prior to and including 2.12 PJSIP there is a stack-buffer overflow vulnerability which only impacts PJSIP users who accept hashed digest credentials (credentials with data_type `PJSIP_CRED_DATA_DIGEST`). This issue has been patched in the master branch of the PJSIP repository and will be included with the next release. Users unable to upgrade need to check that the hashed digest data length must be equal to `PJSIP_MD5STRLEN` before passing to PJSIP.

code_evidence: A fixed-size stack buffer digest_buf[PJSIP_MD5STRLEN] is wrapped by digest with slen set to PJSIP_MD5STRLEN, then passed to pjsip_auth_create_digest().
The only checks are username and realm equality; nothing validates that the credential's digest data length equals PJSIP_MD5STRLEN before the digest is written into the fixed buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-120 fits because an input buffer (credential digest data) is copied into an output stack buffer without a size check, causing a classic stack buffer overflow. The missing constraint is the length equality check; the defect is not merely an out-of-bounds read.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: pjsip_auth_verify passes a fixed-size stack buffer to pjsip_auth_create_digest() without verifying the stored credential digest length. Trigger: a user configured with PJSIP_CRED_DATA_DIGEST whose digest data is longer than PJSIP_MD5STRLEN. The digest creation copies the oversized input into digest_buf, writing past its end and corrupting the stack; the subsequent comparison uses the truncated/corrupted result.

commit_msg:
gvariant: Don’t allow child elements to overlap with each other

If different elements of a variable sized array can overlap with each
other then we can cause a `GVariant` to normalise to a much larger type.

This commit changes the behaviour of `GVariant` with non-normal form data. If
an invalid frame offset is found all subsequent elements are given their
default value.

When retrieving an element at index `n` we scan the frame offsets up to index
`n` and if they are not in order we return an element with the default value
for that type.  This guarantees that elements don't overlap with each
other.  We remember the offset we've scanned up to so we don't need to
repeat this work on subsequent accesses.  We skip these checks for trusted
data.

Unfortunately this makes random access of untrusted data O(n) — at least
on first access.  It doesn't affect the algorithmic complexity of accessing
elements in order, such as when using the `GVariantIter` interface.  Also:
the cost of validation will be amortised as the `GVariant` instance is
continued to be used.

I've implemented this with 4 different functions, 1 for each element size,
rather than looping calling `gvs_read_unaligned_le` in the hope that the
compiler will find it easy to optimise and should produce fairly tight
code.

Fixes: #2121

description: A flaw was found in GLib. GVariant deserialization is vulnerable to an exponential blowup issue where a crafted GVariant can cause excessive processing, leading to denial of service.

code_evidence: gvs_fixed_sized_maybe_is_normal validates a serialised GVariant 'maybe' value: it queries the element's fixed size, requires value.size to equal it, then recurses into the element via g_variant_serialised_is_normal. The function performs validation of untrusted serialised bytes but the diff adds only ordered_offsets_up_to reset in the caller path, not a check here.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-502 fits because the weakness is insufficient validation of untrusted serialised data during deserialization, enabling a DoS via resource consumption. This is deserialization of untrusted data rather than a memory-corruption class, since the supported consequence is excessive processing, not out-of-bounds access.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function validates a deserialised GVariant structure before normalization, but the underlying deserialization path lacked ordering checks on variable-size array frame offsets. Crafted serialised data whose child elements overlap lets normalization produce a much larger type, causing CPU resource exhaustion. The added ordered_offsets_up_to reset supports the fix but the missing constraint is in the array-offset validation, not in this maybe-specific routine.

The data->block[0] variable comes from user and is a number between
0-255. Without proper check, the variable may be very large to cause
an out-of-bounds when performing memcpy in slimpro_i2c_blkwr.

Fix this bug by checking the value of writelen.

Signed-off-by: Wei Chen <harperchen1110@gmail.com>

description: An out-of-bounds write vulnerability was found in the Linux kernel's SLIMpro I2C device driver. The userspace "data->block[0]" variable was not capped to a number between 0-255 and was used as the size of a memcpy, possibly writing beyond the end of dma_buffer. This flaw could allow a local privileged user to crash the system or potentially achieve code execution.

code_evidence: memcpy copies writelen bytes from caller-supplied data into the fixed-size ctx->dma_buffer without any bound check on writelen.
writelen is also passed as the DMA mapping length and later to dma_unmap_single, so the same unchecked length drives the buffer operation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked length in memcpy writes beyond the intended fixed-size buffer, which is exactly an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). This is distinct from a read overflow since the unsafe operation is a write of attacker-influenced length.

evidence_lines.code: dma_unmap_single(ctx->dev, paddr, writelen, DMA_TO_DEVICE);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: writelen (derived from data->block[0], 0-255 from userspace) is used directly as the memcpy size into the fixed dma_buffer with no validation against I2C_SMBUS_BLOCK_MAX. Trigger: a caller supplies a writelen larger than the buffer size, causing memcpy to write past the end of dma_buffer. Consequence: out-of-bounds write corrupting adjacent memory, leading to crash or potential code execution.

commit_msg:
The userspace program could pass any values to the driver through
ioctl() interface. If the driver doesn't check the value of 'pixclock',
it may cause divide error.

Fix this by checking whether 'pixclock' is zero in the function
i740fb_check_var().

The following log reveals it:

divide error: 0000 [#1] PREEMPT SMP KASAN PTI
RIP: 0010:i740fb_decode_var drivers/video/fbdev/i740fb.c:444 [inline]
RIP: 0010:i740fb_set_par+0x272f/0x3bb0 drivers/video/fbdev/i740fb.c:739
Call Trace:
    fb_set_var+0x604/0xeb0 drivers/video/fbdev/core/fbmem.c:1036
    do_fb_ioctl+0x234/0x670 drivers/video/fbdev/core/fbmem.c:1112
    fb_ioctl+0xdd/0x130 drivers/video/fbdev/core/fbmem.c:1191
    vfs_ioctl fs/ioctl.c:51 [inline]
    __do_sys_ioctl fs/ioctl.c:874 [inline]

Signed-off-by: Zheyu Ma <zheyuma97@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Helge Deller <deller@gmx.de>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tif (!var->pixclock)', '\t\treturn -EINVAL;', '']}
description: Found Linux Kernel flaw in the i740 driver. The Userspace program could pass any values to the driver through ioctl() interface. The driver doesn't check the value of 'pixclock', so it may cause a divide by zero error.

code_evidence: i740fb_check_var accepts the caller-controlled fb_var_screeninfo pointer var and validates bits_per_pixel, xres/yres, but never validates var->pixclock before returning success.
The default case returns -EINVAL only for unsupported bits_per_pixel; pixclock is not part of any rejection path, so a zero value passes the check.

The function only clamps virtual resolutions and optionally calls fb_validate_mode; no division or pixclock constraint is enforced here, allowing an unchecked zero pixclock to proceed to later decode logic.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-369 fits because the missing constraint permits a zero divisor to reach a division in the driver's mode-decoding path, producing a divide error. It is not merely an input-validation issue (CWE-20); the specific supported consequence is division by zero.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the validation function omits a zero check on var->pixclock, which is supplied by userspace via ioctl. Trigger: a caller passes pixclock=0, which passes check_var. Consequence: a downstream pixel-clock calculation divides by pixclock, causing a divide-by-zero fault and kernel crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
The rawmidi core allows user to resize the runtime buffer via ioctl,
and this may lead to UAF when performed during concurrent reads or
writes: the read/write functions unlock the runtime lock temporarily
during copying form/to user-space, and that's the race window.

This patch fixes the hole by introducing a reference counter for the
runtime buffer read/write access and returns -EBUSY error when the
resize is performed concurrently against read/write.

Note that the ref count field is a simple integer instead of
refcount_t here, since the all contexts accessing the buffer is
basically protected with a spinlock, hence we need no expensive atomic
ops.  Also, note that this busy check is needed only against read /
write functions, and not in receive/transmit callbacks; the race can
happen only at the spinlock hole mentioned in the above, while the
whole function is protected for receive / transmit callbacks.

Reported-by: butt3rflyh4ck <butterflyhuangxx@gmail.com>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/CAFcO6XMWpUVK_yzzCpp8_XP7+=oUpQvuBeCbMffEDkpe8jWrfg@mail.gmail.com
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/s5heerw3r5z.wl-tiwai@suse.de
Signed-off-by: Takashi Iwai <tiwai@suse.de>

description: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel’s implementation of MIDI, where an attacker with a local account and the permissions to issue ioctl commands to midi devices could trigger a use-after-free issue. A write to this specific memory while freed and before use causes the flow of execution to change and possibly allow for memory corruption or privilege escalation. The highest threat from this vulnerability is to confidentiality, integrity, as well as system availability.

code_evidence: The function takes runtime->lock, then for userbuf it drops the lock at line 36 and calls copy_from_user into runtime->buffer + appl_ptr at line 37 before reacquiring the lock at line 43.

Because the lock is released during the copy, the runtime buffer and its size fields can be changed concurrently; the loop at lines 22-31 computes appl_ptr and buffer offsets from runtime->buffer_size while the buffer is unprotected.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences runtime->buffer after dropping the lock that protects its lifetime, and the buffer can be freed by a concurrent resize, matching CWE-416 use-after-free. This is not merely an out-of-bounds access: the stale pointer refers to memory no longer owned by this operation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the spinlock is released around copy_from_user while the runtime buffer is still referenced, so a concurrent ioctl resize can free/reallocate runtime->buffer. Trigger: a local user performs a write ioctl concurrently with a buffer-resize ioctl. Consequence: copy_from_user writes through a stale pointer into freed memory, causing use-after-free and potential memory corruption or privilege escalation.

commit_msg:
Fixed allocation of large array literals.

Previously, allocation of large array literals may result in
null-pointer dereference. The reason is that njs_array_alloc() may
return a slow array when size is large enough, but the instruction
code assumes that array is always flat.

The fix is to check fast_array flag before accessing array->start.

This closes #473 issue on Github.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            value = array->start;', '            length = array->length;', '            do {', '                njs_set_invalid(value);', '                value++;', '                length--;', '            } while (length != 0);'], 'added_lines': ['            if (array->object.fast_array) {', '                value = array->start;', '                length = array->length;', '                do {', '                    njs_set_invalid(value);', '                    value++;', '                    length--;', '                } while (length != 0);', '            }']}
description: NGINX NJS 0.7.2 was discovered to contain a NULL pointer dereference via the component njs_vmcode_array at /src/njs_vmcode.c.

code_evidence: Line 9 allocates the array via njs_array_alloc, which can return a slow (non-fast) array when code->length is large. Line 10 only checks array != NULL, not whether the array is fast. Lines 12-18 then dereference array->start and array->length and iterate, assuming a flat fast array. For a slow array, start is NULL, so line 12 reads a NULL pointer and lines 15-16 write through it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits because the function dereferences array->start without verifying the array is fast; for slow arrays that pointer is NULL, producing a NULL pointer dereference. This is not an out-of-bounds issue since the failure is a NULL base pointer, not an index overrun.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the code assumes njs_array_alloc always yields a fast array, but a large length produces a slow array whose start pointer is NULL. Trigger: a large array literal with ctor set reaches this branch; line 12 dereferences the NULL start and the loop writes invalid values through it, causing a crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
Make previousLinePosition() not to use dangling RootInlineBox

This patch makes |previousLinePosition()| not to use dangling |RootInlineBox|
pointer to avoid use-after-free.

Before this patch, |isEditablePosition()| is called with |DoUpdateStyle|
parameter to update layout tree if needed. Usually, layout tree isn't updated
by this |isEditablePosition()| call since |previousLinePosition()| updates
layout tree at entry. However, if there are pending style sheet, e.g. @import
directive, and HTML import, e.g link rel=import, layout tree is updated since
document isn't rendering ready, |haveImportLoaded()| &&
|haveRenderBlockingStyleSheetsLoaded()|.

BUG=618237
TEST=LayoutTests/editing/selection/modify_move/move_backward_line_import_crash.html

Review-Url: https://codereview.chromium.org/2082893005
Cr-Commit-Position: refs/heads/master@{#401231}

description: Use-after-free vulnerability in WebKit/Source/core/editing/VisibleUnits.cpp in Blink, as used in Google Chrome before 52.0.2743.82, allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service or possibly have unspecified other impact via crafted JavaScript code involving an @import at-rule in a Cascading Style Sheets (CSS) token sequence in conjunction with a rel=import attribute of a LINK element.

code_evidence: The function caches a RootInlineBox* in `root` from `box->root().prevRootBox()` at [14] and validates it at [15], then dereferences that cached pointer at [29] via `root->closestLeafChildForPoint(...)`.

Between caching and use, line [29] calls `isEditablePosition(p)` without the DoNotUpdateStyle flag; this call can trigger a layout/style update that frees the inline box tree, leaving `root` dangling when dereferenced.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences a pointer to freed layout memory, matching CWE-416 (use after free). The added DoNotUpdateStyle flag confirms the fix removes the layout-update side effect that frees the object, distinguishing it from a mere null-check or out-of-bounds issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: a raw RootInlineBox* is retained across a call that may force style/layout update and free the inline box tree. Trigger: pending @import stylesheets or HTML imports make `isEditablePosition(p)` update layout, invalidating `root`; the subsequent `root->closestLeafChildForPoint` dereference uses freed memory, causing a crash or potentially exploitable use-after-free.

commit_msg:
avcodec/jpeg2000dec: fix error detection in pix_fmt_match()

Fixes out of array accesses with CODEC_FLAG_EMU_EDGE

Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michaelni@gmx.at>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if (s->avctx->pix_fmt == AV_PIX_FMT_NONE) {'], 'added_lines': ['    if (i == possible_fmts_nb) {', '        return AVERROR_PATCHWELCOME;']}
description: A vulnerability was found in FFmpeg 2.0 and classified as problematic. This issue affects the function get_siz of the file libavcodec/jpeg2000dec.c. The manipulation leads to memory corruption. The attack may be initiated remotely. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue.

code_evidence: The loop scans possible_fmts up to possible_fmts_nb and, on a match, assigns s->avctx->pix_fmt and breaks; if nothing matches, i equals possible_fmts_nb and pix_fmt remains unset.

The error check tests s->avctx->pix_fmt == AV_PIX_FMT_NONE, but pix_fmt is not reset to NONE before the loop, so a stale/previous value or an unset field can make the check miss the no-match case and fall through to return 0.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The flaw allows an unsupported pixel format to pass validation and be used in later buffer/array handling, producing out-of-bounds writes (CWE-787). It is a missing validation/incorrect error-detection cause rather than a direct write in get_siz; the supported consequence is memory corruption from the unchecked format.

evidence_lines.code:
if (s->avctx->pix_fmt == AV_PIX_FMT_NONE) {
av_log(s->avctx, AV_LOG_ERROR,
"Unknown pix_fmt, profile: %d, colour_space: %d, "
"components: %d, precision: %d, "
"cdx[1]: %d, cdy[1]: %d, cdx[2]: %d, cdy[2]: %d\n",
s->avctx->profile, s->colour_space, ncomponents, s->precision,
ncomponents > 2 ? s->cdx[1] : 0,
ncomponents > 2 ? s->cdy[1] : 0,
ncomponents > 2 ? s->cdx[2] : 0,
ncomponents > 2 ? s->cdy[2] : 0);
}

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the no-match condition is detected via a possibly preexisting pix_fmt value instead of the loop index. Trigger: a crafted JPEG2000 SIZ with a colour/profile/component combination matching no entry in possible_fmts. Consequence: get_siz returns success with an unsupported pixel format, leading downstream to out-of-bounds array accesses/memory corruption rather than a clean error.

description: The gdImageCreateFromGd2Ctx function in gd_gd2.c in the GD Graphics Library (aka libgd) before 2.2.4 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (application crash) via a crafted image file.

code_evidence: When gdGetInt fails while reading a truecolor pixel, the code substitutes 0 and continues instead of treating the truncated input as an error.
Likewise, a failed gdGetByte silently sets ch to 0, and processing continues with fabricated image data.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The root cause is that the file-derived input is not checked for the required property (complete pixel data) before use; failed reads are silently accepted rather than rejected, matching improper input validation (CWE-20) with availability impact.

This masks truncated/crafted input and leaves the function operating on a state it never verified, leading to a crash/DoS.

commit_msg:
patch 8.2.4217: illegal memory access when undo makes Visual area invalid

Problem:    Illegal memory access when undo makes Visual area invalid.
Solution:   Correct the Visual area after undo.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    if (VIsual_active)', '\tcheck_pos(curbuf, &VIsual);']}
description: Out-of-bounds Read in GitHub repository vim/vim prior to 8.2.

code_evidence: u_undo_end runs after an undo and uses curbuf state without reconciling the Visual area; before the patch no check_pos(curbuf, &VIsual) guards VIsual.
The function dereferences curbuf->b_u_curhead and its uh_next.ptr / uh_seq fields to build the undo message, assuming the undo headers remain consistent with the buffer.
smsg_attr_keep then formats u_oldcount and uhp->uh_seq, reading undo header state that may reference stale positions after undo invalidated the Visual area.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is a read past the intended buffer bounds caused by stale Visual position state after undo; the added check_pos(curbuf, &VIsual) confirms the defect was an unvalidated position used for reading. This is CWE-125 (out-of-bounds read), not a write or use-after-free, because the supported impact is out-of-bounds memory read.

evidence_lines.code:
smsg_attr_keep(0, _("%ld %s; %s #%ld  %s"),
u_oldcount < 0 ? -u_oldcount : u_oldcount,
_(msgstr),
did_undo ? _("before") : _("after"),
uhp == NULL ? 0L : uhp->uh_seq,
msgbuf);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: undo processing leaves the Visual area (VIsual) pointing to positions that are no longer valid in the buffer, and u_undo_end proceeds to read undo-header and buffer state without validating VIsual. Trigger: an undo that shortens or removes lines while Visual mode is active. Supported consequence: an out-of-bounds read when the stale Visual position is later used, matching the commit's illegal memory access report.
