commit_msg:
Right now ovl_permission() calls __inode_permission(realinode), to do
permission checks on real inode and no checks are done on overlay inode.

Modify it to do checks both on overlay inode as well as underlying inode.
Checks on overlay inode will be done with the creds of calling task while
checks on underlying inode will be done with the creds of mounter.

Signed-off-by: Vivek Goyal <vgoyal@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Miklos Szeredi <mszeredi@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\treturn __inode_permission(realinode, mask);'], 'added_lines': ['\tconst struct cred *old_cred;', '\t/*', '\t * Check overlay inode with the creds of task and underlying inode', '\t * with creds of mounter', '\t */', '\terr = generic_permission(inode, mask);', '\tif (err)', '\t\treturn err;', '', '\told_cred = ovl_override_creds(inode->i_sb);', '\terr = __inode_permission(realinode, mask);', '\trevert_creds(old_cred);', '', '\treturn err;']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel before 4.8. Incorrect access checking in overlayfs mounts could be used by local attackers to modify or truncate files in the underlying filesystem.

code_evidence: The overlay inode's own permission check is bypassed: after resolving realinode from the real dentry, the function proceeds directly to checking the underlying inode without ever calling generic_permission on the overlay inode in this path.
The MAY_WRITE branch only rejects writes when is_upper is true and the real inode is read-only; it does not perform an authorization check against the overlay inode's mode/ownership.
The final check calls __inode_permission(realinode, mask) using the caller's credentials against the underlying inode only, so the overlay inode's permission bits are never enforced.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-863 covers authorization checks that are performed but done incorrectly. Here access is gated only on the underlying inode while the overlay inode's permissions are skipped, an incorrect authorization decision rather than a missing check entirely (which would be CWE-862).

evidence_lines.code: return __inode_permission(realinode, mask);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the permission decision is made solely against the real underlying inode, and the overlay inode's own mode/ownership is never checked in the non-default-permissions path. Trigger: a local user requests access (e.g., write/truncate) via an overlayfs mount whose overlay inode denies the operation but whose underlying inode permits it. Consequence: the access check is incomplete, allowing modification or truncation of files in the underlying filesystem.

commit_msg:
The function l2cap_get_conf_opt will return L2CAP_CONF_OPT_SIZE + opt->len
as length value. The opt->len however is in control over the remote user
and can be used by an attacker to gain access beyond the bounds of the
actual packet.

To prevent any potential leak of heap memory, it is enough to check that
the resulting len calculation after calling l2cap_get_conf_opt is not
below zero. A well formed packet will always return >= 0 here and will
end with the length value being zero after the last option has been
parsed. In case of malformed packets messing with the opt->len field the
length value will become negative. If that is the case, then just abort
and ignore the option.

In case an attacker uses a too short opt->len value, then garbage will
be parsed, but that is protected by the unknown option handling and also
the option parameter size checks.

Signed-off-by: Marcel Holtmann <marcel@holtmann.org>
Reviewed-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Johan Hedberg <johan.hedberg@intel.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (len < 0)', '\t\t\tbreak;']}
description: A heap address information leak while using L2CAP_GET_CONF_OPT was discovered in the Linux kernel before 5.1-rc1.

code_evidence: The loop condition checks only len >= L2CAP_CONF_OPT_SIZE, then subtracts the return of l2cap_get_conf_opt, which includes the remote-controlled opt->len; a malformed opt->len can make len negative without terminating the loop.
The switch then dispatches on the attacker-supplied type and uses olen/val derived from the packet.

L2CAP_CONF_RFC and L2CAP_CONF_EFS branches copy olen bytes from (void *)val after only checking olen equals sizeof(rfc)/sizeof(efs), so a crafted option can drive reads beyond the received packet buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads data beyond the intended buffer bounds due to unchecked attacker-controlled length, matching CWE-125 Out-of-bounds Read. The consequence is read-only memory disclosure, distinguishing it from write-based buffer overflows.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the remaining-length accounting trusts the remote opt->len, allowing len to become negative while parsing continues. Trigger: a malformed configuration response with an oversized opt->len. Consequence: option handlers read past the packet buffer, leaking heap memory to the remote peer or crashing.

commit_msg:
In the AEAD interface for AF_ALG, the reference to the "null skcipher"
held by each tfm was being dropped in the wrong place -- when each
af_alg_ctx was freed instead of when the aead_tfm was freed.  As
discovered by syzkaller, a specially crafted program could use this to
cause the null skcipher to be freed while it is still in use.

Fix it by dropping the reference in the right place.

Fixes: 72548b093ee3 ("crypto: algif_aead - copy AAD from src to dst")
Reported-by: syzbot <syzkaller@googlegroups.com>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org> # v4.14+
Signed-off-by: Eric Biggers <ebiggers@google.com>
Reviewed-by: Stephan Mueller <smueller@chronox.de>
Signed-off-by: Herbert Xu <herbert@gondor.apana.org.au>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tcrypto_put_default_null_skcipher2();']}
description: A flaw was found in the crypto subsystem of the Linux kernel before version kernel-4.15-rc4. The "null skcipher" was being dropped when each af_alg_ctx was freed instead of when the aead_tfm was freed. This can cause the null skcipher to be freed while it is still in use leading to a local user being able to crash the system or possibly escalate privileges.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function only frees an AEAD transform and its context; it contains no input handling or validation, so it does not support CWE-20. The described flaw is a reference-lifetime/use-after-free issue, not improper input validation.

commit_msg:
Fix a bug in the verifier's scalar32_min_max_*() functions which leads to
incorrect tracking of 32 bit bounds for the simulation of and/or/xor bitops.
When both the src & dst subreg is a known constant, then the assumption is
that scalar_min_max_*() will take care to update bounds correctly. However,
this is not the case, for example, consider a register R2 which has a tnum
of 0xffffffff00000000, meaning, lower 32 bits are known constant and in this
case of value 0x00000001. R2 is then and'ed with a register R3 which is a
64 bit known constant, here, 0x100000002.

What can be seen in line '10:' is that 32 bit bounds reach an invalid state
where {u,s}32_min_value > {u,s}32_max_value. The reason is scalar32_min_max_*()
delegates 32 bit bounds updates to scalar_min_max_*(), however, that really
only takes place when both the 64 bit src & dst register is a known constant.
Given scalar32_min_max_*() is intended to be designed as closely as possible
to scalar_min_max_*(), update the 32 bit bounds in this situation through
__mark_reg32_known() which will set all {u,s}32_{min,max}_value to the correct
constant, which is 0x00000000 after the fix (given 0x00000001 & 0x00000002 in
32 bit space). This is possible given var32_off already holds the final value
as dst_reg->var_off is updated before calling scalar32_min_max_*().

Before fix, invalid tracking of R2:

  [...]
  9: R0_w=inv1337 R1=ctx(id=0,off=0,imm=0) R2_w=inv(id=0,smin_value=-9223372036854775807 (0x8000000000000001),smax_value=9223372032559808513 (0x7fffffff00000001),umin_value=1,umax_value=0xffffffff00000001,var_off=(0x1; 0xffffffff00000000),s32_min_value=1,s32_max_value=1,u32_min_value=1,u32_max_value=1) R3_w=inv4294967298 R10=fp0
  9: (5f) r2 &= r3
  10: R0_w=inv1337 R1=ctx(id=0,off=0,imm=0) R2_w=inv(id=0,smin_value=0,smax_value=4294967296 (0x100000000),umin_value=0,umax_value=0x100000000,var_off=(0x0; 0x100000000),s32_min_value=1,s32_max_value=0,u32_min_value=1,u32_max_value=0) R3_w=inv4294967298 R10=fp0
  [...]

After fix, correct tracking of R2:

  [...]
  9: R0_w=inv1337 R1=ctx(id=0,off=0,imm=0) R2_w=inv(id=0,smin_value=-9223372036854775807 (0x8000000000000001),smax_value=9223372032559808513 (0x7fffffff00000001),umin_value=1,umax_value=0xffffffff00000001,var_off=(0x1; 0xffffffff00000000),s32_min_value=1,s32_max_value=1,u32_min_value=1,u32_max_value=1) R3_w=inv4294967298 R10=fp0
  9: (5f) r2 &= r3
  10: R0_w=inv1337 R1=ctx(id=0,off=0,imm=0) R2_w=inv(id=0,smin_value=0,smax_value=4294967296 (0x100000000),umin_value=0,umax_value=0x100000000,var_off=(0x0; 0x100000000),s32_min_value=0,s32_max_value=0,u32_min_value=0,u32_max_value=0) R3_w=inv4294967298 R10=fp0
  [...]

Fixes: 3f50f132d840 ("bpf: Verifier, do explicit ALU32 bounds tracking")
Fixes: 2921c90d4718 ("bpf: Fix a verifier failure with xor")
Reported-by: Manfred Paul (@_manfp)
Reported-by: Thadeu Lima de Souza Cascardo <cascardo@canonical.com>
Signed-off-by: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>
Reviewed-by: John Fastabend <john.fastabend@gmail.com>
Acked-by: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t/* Assuming scalar64_min_max_or will be called so it is safe', '\t * to skip updating register for known case.', '\t */', '\tif (src_known && dst_known)'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (src_known && dst_known) {', '\t\t__mark_reg32_known(dst_reg, var32_off.value);', '\t}']}
description: The eBPF ALU32 bounds tracking for bitwise ops (AND, OR and XOR) in the Linux kernel did not properly update 32-bit bounds, which could be turned into out of bounds reads and writes in the Linux kernel and therefore, arbitrary code execution. This issue was fixed via commit 049c4e13714e ("bpf: Fix alu32 const subreg bound tracking on bitwise operations") (v5.13-rc4) and backported to the stable kernels in v5.12.4, v5.11.21, and v5.10.37. The AND/OR issues were introduced by commit 3f50f132d840 ("bpf: Verifier, do explicit ALU32 bounds tracking") (5.7-rc1) and the XOR variant was introduced by 2921c90d4718 ("bpf:Fix a verifier failure with xor") ( 5.10-rc1).

code_evidence: Lines 4-6 compute src_known/dst_known from subreg tnum and var32_off; when both 32-bit subregs are known constants, line 9-10 returns without updating the 32-bit bounds.

Lines 11-15 show the normal path: u32_min_value is max of minima and u32_max_value comes from var32_off. The early return skips these, so dst_reg keeps stale {u,s}32_{min,max}_value that can become min > max (as the commit shows).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The stale/incorrect 32-bit bounds let the eBPF verifier accept programs whose pointer arithmetic exceeds the intended map/stack buffer, so the supported consequence is an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). The defect is incorrect bound tracking, but the impact matching the target is writing past the intended buffer; this is not merely a logic bug without memory-safety consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the known-constant early return in scalar32_min_max_or skips all 32-bit bound updates, leaving dst_reg->u32_min_value/u32_max_value (and s32 bounds) inconsistent after a bitwise OR. Trigger: both subregs known constants, e.g., a tnum with low 32 bits constant OR'ed with a 64-bit constant. Consequence: the verifier tracks wrong 32-bit bounds, so later ALU32/pointer arithmetic may pass checks it should fail, enabling out-of-bounds memory access in the kernel.

commit_msg: Safer std::vector indexing.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ["            if (openMode_[0] == 'r' || openMode_[1] == '+') reopen = false;", "            if (openMode_[0] != 'r' || openMode_[1] == '+') reopen = false;"], 'added_lines': ["            if (openMode_.at(0) == 'r' || openMode_.at(1) == '+') reopen = false;", "            if (openMode_.at(0) != 'r' || openMode_.at(1) == '+') reopen = false;"]}
description: Exiv2 is a command-line utility and C++ library for reading, writing, deleting, and modifying the metadata of image files. An out-of-bounds read was found in Exiv2 versions v0.27.4 and earlier. The out-of-bounds read is triggered when Exiv2 is used to read the metadata of a crafted image file. An attacker could potentially exploit the vulnerability to cause a denial of service, if they can trick the victim into running Exiv2 on a crafted image file. The bug is fixed in version v0.27.5.

code_evidence: In the opRead branch, openMode_[0] and openMode_[1] are indexed directly without verifying openMode_ has at least two characters; a short or empty openMode_ makes index 1 (and possibly index 0) read past the string's buffer.
The opWrite branch repeats the same unchecked indexing of openMode_[0] and openMode_[1], so the same out-of-bounds read can occur on that path.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the function reads data past the end of the openMode_ buffer via unchecked operator[] access. This is a read overrun, not a write, and the missing length constraint is the direct cause.

evidence_lines.code:
if (openMode_[0] == 'r' || openMode_[1] == '+') reopen = false;
break;

if (openMode_[0] != 'r' || openMode_[1] == '+') reopen = false;
break;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the code indexes openMode_ at fixed positions 0 and 1 using operator[] without a length check. Trigger: openMode_ contains fewer than two characters when switchMode is invoked. Consequence: the comparison reads past the string's buffer, producing an out-of-bounds read that may crash or leak memory contents.

commit_msg:
core: Fix Content-Length parsing

Issue discovered during OpenSIPS Security Audit 2022,
        by Alfred Farrugia & Sandro Gauci (Enable Security)

https://github.com/OpenSIPS/opensips/security/advisories/GHSA-c6j5-f4h4-2xrq
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ["\t\tnumber = number*10 + (*p)-'0';", '\t\tif (number<0) {', '\t\t\tLM_ERR("number overflow at pos %d in len number [%.*s]\\n",'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t/* do not actually cause an integer overflow, as it is UB! --liviu */', '\t\tif (number > 214748363) {', '\t\t\tLM_ERR("integer overflow risk at pos %d in len number [%.*s]\\n",', '', "\t\tnumber = number*10 + (*p)-'0';"]}
description: OpenSIPS is a Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) server implementation. Prior to versions 3.1.9 and 3.2.6, a malformed SIP message containing a large _Content-Length_ value and a specially crafted Request-URI causes a segmentation fault in OpenSIPS. This issue occurs when a large amount of shared memory using the `-m` flag was allocated to OpenSIPS, such as 10 GB of RAM. On the test system, this issue occurred when shared memory was set to `2362` or higher. This issue is fixed in versions 3.1.9 and 3.2.6. The only workaround is to guarantee that the Content-Length value of input messages is never larger than `2147483647`.

code_evidence: Line 3 declares `int number`; the digit loop at lines 14-15 accumulates `number = number*10 + (*p)-'0'` with no pre-multiplication bound check. The only guard is the post-hoc `if (number<0)` at lines 16-20, which detects wraparound only after the signed overflow has already occurred (undefined behavior). The accumulated value is then stored through `*length = number` at line 33.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits: the digit-by-digit multiplication/addition at line 15 can wrap a signed integer, and the guard at line 16 runs only after the overflow. This is not merely a bad-length validation issue; the root cause is unchecked integer arithmetic whose result feeds a length value.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: A malformed Content-Length with many digits drives the signed int accumulation past INT_MAX; the overflow is undefined behavior and the post-hoc negativity test does not reliably catch it. The wrapped value reaches `*length`, so a huge attacker-supplied length can be interpreted as a small or negative value, leading to the reported segmentation fault when downstream code trusts it.

commit_msg:
avformat/flvenc: Check audio packet size

Fixes: Assertion failure
Fixes: assert_flvenc.c:941_1.swf

Found-by: #CHEN HONGXU# <HCHEN017@e.ntu.edu.sg>
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
(cherry picked from commit 6b67d7f05918f7a1ee8fc6ff21355d7e8736aa10)
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '    if (enc->codec_type == AVMEDIA_TYPE_AUDIO && !pkt->size) {', '        av_log(s, AV_LOG_WARNING, "Empty audio Packet\\n");', '        return AVERROR(EINVAL);', '    }']}
description: The flv_write_packet function in libavformat/flvenc.c in FFmpeg through 2.8 does not check for an empty audio packet, leading to an assertion failure.

code_evidence: size is initialized from pkt->size at line 8 and used in the audio branch. In the AVMEDIA_TYPE_AUDIO case, get_audio_flags is called and then av_assert0(size) at line 38 asserts the packet size is nonzero.

The empty-audio condition is not rejected before the switch; an incoming audio packet with pkt->size == 0 reaches the assertion. The later size bound check at lines 68-72 only rejects packets that are too large, not empty ones.

Trigger: a caller supplies an audio AVPacket with size zero. Consequence: av_assert0(size) aborts the process, producing a reachable assertion failure (denial of service) rather than a graceful error.

commit_msg:
mlock: fix mlock count can not decrease in race condition

Kefeng reported that when running the follow test, the mlock count in
meminfo will increase permanently:

 [1] testcase
 linux:~ # cat test_mlockal
 grep Mlocked /proc/meminfo
  for j in `seq 0 10`
  do
 	for i in `seq 4 15`
 	do
 		./p_mlockall >> log &
 	done
 	sleep 0.2
 done
 # wait some time to let mlock counter decrease and 5s may not enough
 sleep 5
 grep Mlocked /proc/meminfo

 linux:~ # cat p_mlockall.c
 #include <sys/mman.h>
 #include <stdlib.h>
 #include <stdio.h>

 #define SPACE_LEN	4096

 int main(int argc, char ** argv)
 {
	 	int ret;
	 	void *adr = malloc(SPACE_LEN);
	 	if (!adr)
	 		return -1;

	 	ret = mlockall(MCL_CURRENT | MCL_FUTURE);
	 	printf("mlcokall ret = %d\n", ret);

	 	ret = munlockall();
	 	printf("munlcokall ret = %d\n", ret);

	 	free(adr);
	 	return 0;
	 }

In __munlock_pagevec() we should decrement NR_MLOCK for each page where
we clear the PageMlocked flag.  Commit 1ebb7cc6a583 ("mm: munlock: batch
NR_MLOCK zone state updates") has introduced a bug where we don't
decrement NR_MLOCK for pages where we clear the flag, but fail to
isolate them from the lru list (e.g.  when the pages are on some other
cpu's percpu pagevec).  Since PageMlocked stays cleared, the NR_MLOCK
accounting gets permanently disrupted by this.

Fix it by counting the number of page whose PageMlock flag is cleared.

commit_msg:
KEYS: Fix race between updating and finding a negative key

Consolidate KEY_FLAG_INSTANTIATED, KEY_FLAG_NEGATIVE and the rejection
error into one field such that:

 (1) The instantiation state can be modified/read atomically.

 (2) The error can be accessed atomically with the state.

 (3) The error isn't stored unioned with the payload pointers.

This deals with the problem that the state is spread over three different
objects (two bits and a separate variable) and reading or updating them
atomically isn't practical, given that not only can uninstantiated keys
change into instantiated or rejected keys, but rejected keys can also turn
into instantiated keys - and someone accessing the key might not be using
any locking.

The main side effect of this problem is that what was held in the payload
may change, depending on the state.  For instance, you might observe the
key to be in the rejected state.  You then read the cached error, but if
the key semaphore wasn't locked, the key might've become instantiated
between the two reads - and you might now have something in hand that isn't
actually an error code.

The state is now KEY_IS_UNINSTANTIATED, KEY_IS_POSITIVE or a negative error
code if the key is negatively instantiated.  The key_is_instantiated()
function is replaced with key_is_positive() to avoid confusion as negative
keys are also 'instantiated'.

Additionally, barriering is included:

 (1) Order payload-set before state-set during instantiation.

 (2) Order state-read before payload-read when using the key.

Further separate barriering is necessary if RCU is being used to access the
payload content after reading the payload pointers.

Fixes: 146aa8b1453b ("KEYS: Merge the type-specific data with the payload data")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # v4.4+
Reported-by: Eric Biggers <ebiggers@google.com>
Signed-off-by: David Howells <dhowells@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Eric Biggers <ebiggers@google.com>

description: The KEYS subsystem in the Linux kernel before 4.13.10 does not correctly synchronize the actions of updating versus finding a key in the "negative" state to avoid a race condition, which allows local users to cause a denial of service or possibly have unspecified other impact via crafted system calls.

commit_msg:
Fix flaws in LDAP DN checking

KDB_TL_USER_INFO tl-data is intended to be internal to the LDAP KDB
module, and not used in disk or wire principal entries.  Prevent
kadmin clients from sending KDB_TL_USER_INFO tl-data by giving it a
type number less than 256 and filtering out type numbers less than 256
in kadm5_create_principal_3().  (We already filter out low type
numbers in kadm5_modify_principal()).

In the LDAP KDB module, if containerdn and linkdn are both specified
in a put_principal operation, check both linkdn and the computed
standalone_principal_dn for container membership.  To that end, factor
out the checks into helper functions and call them on all applicable
client-influenced DNs.

CVE-2018-5729:

In MIT krb5 1.6 or later, an authenticated kadmin user with permission
to add principals to an LDAP Kerberos database can cause a null
dereference in kadmind, or circumvent a DN container check, by
supplying tagged data intended to be internal to the database module.
Thanks to Sharwan Ram and Pooja Anil for discovering the potential
null dereference.

CVE-2018-5730:

In MIT krb5 1.6 or later, an authenticated kadmin user with permission
to add principals to an LDAP Kerberos database can circumvent a DN
containership check by supplying both a "linkdn" and "containerdn"
database argument, or by supplying a DN string which is a left
extension of a container DN string but is not hierarchically within
the container DN.

description: An improper computation of p_tx0, p_tx1, p_ty0 and p_ty1 in the function opj_get_encoding_parameters in openjp2/pi.c in OpenJPEG through 2.3.0 can lead to an integer overflow.

code_evidence: Tile extent computations add p_cp->tx0 + p * p_cp->tdx and p_cp->tx0 + (p + 1) * p_cp->tdx using OPJ_UINT32 operands, then cast the result to OPJ_INT32 before opj_int_max/opj_int_min.

joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the function performs arithmetic (p * p_cp->tdx, q * p_cp->tdy, tx0 + ...) whose result is assumed to fit, and wraparound or an out-of-range signed cast corrupts the computed tile extents. This is an integer overflow/wraparound root cause, not merely a downstream bounds-check failure.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the tile offset products and sums are computed without an overflow check and then reinterpreted as signed OPJ_INT32. Trigger: crafted tile/grid parameters (large tdx/tdy, large tx0/ty0, or many tiles) make the unsigned sum exceed its range or the signed cast become negative. Consequence: p_tx0/p_ty0 or p_tx1/p_ty1 become incorrect, so downstream tile and resolution geometry (ceildivpow2, l_pw/l_ph) is computed from bad bounds, supporting out-of-bounds or resource-exhaustion effects.

commit_msg:
debuggerd: verify that traced threads belong to the right process.

Fix two races in debuggerd's PTRACE_ATTACH logic:
  1. The target thread in a crash dump request could exit between the
     /proc/<pid>/task/<tid> check and the PTRACE_ATTACH.
  2. Sibling threads could exit between listing /proc/<pid>/task and the
     PTRACE_ATTACH.

Bug: http://b/29555636
Change-Id: I4dfe1ea30e2c211d2389321bd66e3684dd757591
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  if (ptrace(PTRACE_ATTACH, request.tid, 0, 0) != 0) {'], 'added_lines': ['  if (!ptrace_attach_thread(request.pid, request.tid)) {', '  }', '', '  // DEBUGGER_ACTION_CRASH requests can come from arbitrary processes and the tid field in the', '  // request is sent from the other side. If an attacker can cause a process to be spawned with the', '  // pid of their process, they could trick debuggerd into dumping that process by exiting after', '  // sending the request. Validate the trusted request.uid/gid to defend against this.', '  if (request.action == DEBUGGER_ACTION_CRASH) {', '    pid_t pid;', '    uid_t uid;', '    gid_t gid;', '    if (get_process_info(request.tid, &pid, &uid, &gid) != 0) {', '      ALOGE("debuggerd: failed to get process info for tid \'%d\'", request.tid);', '      exit(1);', '    }', '', '    if (pid != request.pid || uid != request.uid || gid != request.gid) {', '      ALOGE(', '        "debuggerd: attached task %d does not match request: "', '        "expected pid=%d,uid=%d,gid=%d, actual pid=%d,uid=%d,gid=%d",', '        request.tid, request.pid, request.uid, request.gid, pid, uid, gid);', '      exit(1);', '    }']}
description: debuggerd/debuggerd.cpp in Debuggerd in Android 5.0.x before 5.0.2, 5.1.x before 5.1.1, 6.x before 2016-09-01, and 7.0 before 2016-09-01 mishandles the interaction between PTRACE_ATTACH operations and thread exits, which allows attackers to gain privileges via a crafted application, aka internal bug 29555636.

code_evidence: The worker attaches to request.tid with PTRACE_ATTACH using the caller-supplied tid without verifying that the attached task's pid/uid/gid match the trusted request fields.

A crash-dump request is treated as privileged: after attaching, the worker connects to activity_manager and later signals request.pid, but the identity check on request.tid/pid/uid/gid is absent from this pre-patch function.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is improper validation of permissions/identity before a privileged debuggerd operation, fitting the permissions/privileges/access-control category CWE-264. It is not merely a race condition; the missing authorization check is the supported weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the request's tid/pid/uid/gid are trusted and the PTRACE_ATTACH target is not revalidated against the process's actual identity, leaving a race between the /proc check and attach. Trigger: an attacker sends a DEBUGGER_ACTION_CRASH request and causes the tid to exit or be reused. Consequence: debuggerd attaches to and dumps/signals a process it should not, enabling privilege gain.

description: In radare2 before 3.9.0, a command injection vulnerability exists in bin_symbols() in libr/core/cbin.c. By using a crafted executable file, it's possible to execute arbitrary shell commands with the permissions of the victim. This vulnerability is due to an insufficient fix for CVE-2019-14745 and improper handling of symbol names embedded in executables.

code_evidence: The loop copies every character of the attacker-influenced arg into the output buffer a, dropping only '@', '`', '|', ';' and '\n' via the switch cases [9-15]. Any other byte, including '=', '&', '$', '(', ')' or space, reaches the default branch and is copied verbatim to *b++ [16,17].
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function is the neutralization step for data destined for an OS command; its incomplete blacklist lets special elements through, which is exactly CWE-78's incorrect neutralization of special elements in an OS command. It is not merely a generic parsing bug, since the filter exists specifically to prevent shell interpretation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: __filterShell uses a small blacklist of shell metacharacters rather than neutralizing all command separators/expansions, so symbol names from a crafted executable pass through with characters such as '=' or '&' intact. When the filtered result is later interpolated into a shell command, those surviving elements can alter the command, allowing execution of attacker commands under the victim's privileges.

commit_msg: Fix some pipelines to be safe if downstream write fails (fuzz issue 28262)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    getNext()->write(&ch, 1);', ''], 'added_lines': ['    // Reset before calling getNext()->write in case that throws an', '    // exception.', '', '    getNext()->write(&ch, 1);']}
description: QPDF 9.x through 9.1.1 and 10.x through 10.0.4 has a heap-based buffer overflow in Pl_ASCII85Decoder::write (called from Pl_AES_PDF::flush and Pl_AES_PDF::finish) when a certain downstream write fails.

code_evidence: The function writes the decoded byte to the downstream via getNext()->write(&ch, 1) at line 24 and only then resets this->pos and inbuf at lines 25-28. If the downstream write throws, the reset is skipped, leaving pos and inbuf in a partially flushed state for a subsequent flush call.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The target CWE-787 fits because the stale pos/inbuf state after a failed downstream write can drive out-of-bounds writes in the decoder pipeline. The ordering defect is the cause; the out-of-bounds write is the consequence, not a mere null-pointer or logic error.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: state reset (pos and inbuf) occurs after the fallible downstream write, so an exception leaves stale decoder state. Trigger: a downstream write failure/throw during flush. Consequence: subsequent flush processing operates on unreset state, leading to incorrect buffer handling associated with the reported heap overflow.

commit_msg:
Lossless decomp: Range-limit 12-bit samples

12-bit is the only data precision for which the range of the sample data
type exceeds the valid sample range, so it is possible to craft a 12-bit
lossless JPEG image that contains out-of-range 12-bit samples.
Attempting to decompress such an image using color quantization or merged
upsampling (NOTE: libjpeg-turbo cannot generate YCbCr or subsampled
lossless JPEG images, but it can decompress them) caused segfaults or
buffer overruns when those algorithms attempted to use the out-of-range
sample values as array indices.  This commit modifies the lossless
decompressor so that it range-limits the output of the scaler when using
12-bit samples.

Fixes #670
Fixes #672
Fixes #673
Fixes #674
Fixes #675
Fixes #676
Fixes #677
Fixes #678
Fixes #679
Fixes #681
Fixes #683
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['#if BITS_IN_JSAMPLE == 12', '    /* 12-bit is the only data precision for which the range of the sample data', '     * type exceeds the valid sample range.  Thus, we need to range-limit the', '     * samples, because other algorithms may try to use them as array indices.', '     */', '    *output_buf++ = (_JSAMPLE)((*diff_buf++ << cinfo->Al) & 0xFFF);', '#else', '#endif']}
description: A heap-based buffer overflow issue was discovered in libjpeg-turbo in h2v2_merged_upsample_internal() function of jdmrgext.c file. The vulnerability can only be exploited with 12-bit data precision for which the range of the sample data type exceeds the valid sample range, hence, an attacker could craft a 12-bit lossless JPEG image that contains out-of-range 12-bit samples. An application attempting to decompress such image using merged upsampling would lead to segmentation fault or buffer overflows, causing an application to crash.

code_evidence: The loop shifts each differential sample left by cinfo->Al and narrows it to _JSAMPLE without masking; in 12-bit builds the shifted value can exceed 0xFFF and the stored output sample retains out-of-range bits.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The supported consequence is that out-of-range sample values later drive OOB writes, matching CWE-787 (write past intended buffer). The function itself lacks the range constraint, but the out-of-bounds write occurs downstream; it is not an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) or integer overflow alone.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: simple_upscale emits 12-bit samples without range-limiting, so crafted lossless JPEG data produces output samples outside the valid range. Downstream merged upsampling/color-quantization code uses these values as array indices, causing out-of-bounds writes and segfaults. The unsafe operation is the unmasked shift-store at line 6; the trigger is a crafted 12-bit lossless image whose differential samples yield out-of-range values.

commit_msg: Lock down search_path in SPI calls
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\t/* Lock down search_path */', '\trc = SPI_exec("SET LOCAL search_path TO pg_catalog, pg_temp", 0);', '\tif (rc < 0)', '\t\tereport(ERROR, (errcode(ERRCODE_INTERNAL_ERROR), (errmsg("could not set search_path"))));']}
description:
TimescaleDB, an open-source time-series SQL database, has a privilege escalation vulnerability in versions 2.8.0 through 2.9.2. During installation, TimescaleDB creates a telemetry job that is runs as the installation user. The queries run as part of the telemetry data collection were not run with a locked down `search_path`, allowing malicious users to create functions that would be executed by the telemetry job, leading to privilege escalation. In order to be able to take advantage of this vulnerability, a user would need to be able to create objects in a database and then get a superuser to install TimescaleDB into their database. When TimescaleDB is installed as trusted extension, non-superusers can install the extension without help from a superuser.

Version 2.9.3 fixes this issue. As a mitigation, the `search_path` of the user running the telemetry job can be locked down to not include schemas writable by other users. The vulnerability is not exploitable on instances in Timescale Cloud and Managed Service for TimescaleDB due to additional security provisions in place on those platforms.

code_evidence: After SPI_connect_ext, the function runs SPI queries (e.g., invalidation_threshold_set_or_get, process_cagg_invalidations_and_refresh) without setting search_path, so unqualified object names resolve through the caller's search_path.
The function continues executing SPI-based catalog and invalidation logic under the current user's search_path, allowing attacker-controlled schemas to shadow referenced functions/objects.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function fails to constrain the execution context (search_path) of privileged SPI operations, letting an unintended actor influence which objects run under elevated privileges. This is improper privilege management (CWE-269); the escalation is the impact, while the missing search_path constraint is the root cause.

evidence_lines.code:
if ((rc = SPI_connect_ext(SPI_OPT_NONATOMIC) != SPI_OK_CONNECT))
elog(ERROR, "SPI_connect failed: %s", SPI_result_code_string(rc));

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the SPI session used for telemetry/refresh work inherits the invoking user's search_path, so unqualified names can resolve to attacker-created objects. Trigger: a low-privileged user creates shadowing functions/objects in a writable schema, then a privileged telemetry/refresh job invokes this function. Consequence: attacker code executes with the job's privileges, enabling privilege escalation.

When correct 'Signature part' is received by Collectd, configured without
AuthFile option, condition for endless loop occurs due to missing increase
of pointer to next unprocessed part.

This is a forward-port of #2233.

Fixes: CVE-2017-7401
Closes: #2174
Signed-off-by: Florian Forster <octo@collectd.org>

Will accept it.");', '    return (0);', '  }', ''], 'added_lines': ['  }', '', '  if (se->data.server.userdb == NULL) {', '    c_complain(', '        LOG_NOTICE, &complain_no_users,', '        "network plugin: Received signed network packet but can\'t verify it "', '        "because no user DB has been configured. Will accept it.");', '', '    *ret_buffer = buffer + pss_head_length;', '    *ret_buffer_len -= pss_head_length;', '', '    return (0);']}
description: Incorrect interaction of the parse_packet() and parse_part_sign_sha256() functions in network.c in collectd 5.7.1 and earlier allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (infinite loop) of a collectd instance (configured with "SecurityLevel None" and with empty "AuthFile" options) via a crafted UDP packet.

code_evidence: When no user DB is configured, the function logs and returns 0 at line 24 without advancing *ret_buffer or reducing *ret_buffer_len, so the caller's buffer offset is unchanged.
Only the normal verification path updates the output buffer pointer at lines 90-91 (*ret_buffer = buffer + buffer_len; *ret_buffer_len = 0).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing pointer/length advancement prevents the caller's iteration from terminating, matching CWE-835's unreachable exit condition. This is a control-flow/termination flaw, not merely a null dereference or memory corruption.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the early-return path for an unconfigured AuthFile returns success without consuming the signature part, leaving the caller's buffer pointer and length unchanged. Trigger: a crafted signed UDP packet processed with SecurityLevel None and empty AuthFile repeatedly re-enters parsing on the same part, so the loop exit condition is never reached, causing CPU-exhaustion DoS.

commit_msg: Update header handling to RFC 7230
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t/* RFC 2616 allows new lines if followed by SP or HT */', '\t\t\tint illegal_break =', "\t\t\t\t\t(header_line[i+1] != ' ' && header_line[i+1] != '\\t')", '\t\t\t\t\t&& (', "\t\t\t\t\t\theader_line[i] == '\\n'", "\t\t\t\t\t\t|| (header_line[i] == '\\r' && header_line[i+1] != '\\n'));", '\t\t\tif (illegal_break) {'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t/* RFC 7230 ch. 3.2.4 deprecates folding support */', "\t\t\tif (header_line[i] == '\\n' || header_line[i] == '\\r') {"]}
description: The sapi_header_op function in main/SAPI.c in PHP before 5.4.38, 5.5.x before 5.5.22, and 5.6.x before 5.6.6 supports deprecated line folding without considering browser compatibility, which allows remote attackers to conduct cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks against Internet Explorer by leveraging (1) %0A%20 or (2) %0D%0A%20 mishandling in the header function.

code_evidence: The header_line buffer (copied at line 44) is scanned at 67–72; the illegal_break condition only rejects a newline when the next character is neither SP nor HT, so folded sequences such as '\n ' or '\r\n ' pass the check.
After validation, header_line is assigned to sapi_header.header/header_len at 86–87 and passed to sapi_header_add_op, so the folded value is emitted as an HTTP response header.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function fails to neutralize user-controllable input (header value) before it is placed in generated HTTP output served to other users, which is the core of CWE-79. The deprecated folding allowance is the missing constraint that lets the dangerous input cross into the response; the resulting script execution in the browser matches XSS rather than mere header injection.

evidence_lines.code:
sapi_header.header = header_line;
sapi_header.header_len = header_line_len;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the newline safety check permits line folding, so attacker-controlled header values containing %0A%20 or %0D%0A%20 survive validation. Trigger: a script passes such a value to the header function; the folded bytes reach the response header output. Consequence: Internet Explorer interprets the folded content as a new header, enabling injected content to execute in the victim's browser (XSS).

description: An issue was discovered in ImageMagick 7.0.7. A NULL pointer dereference vulnerability was found in the function LoadOpenCLDevices in MagickCore/opencl.c, which allows attackers to cause a denial of service via a crafted file.

Trigger: if AcquireQuantumMemory fails (e.g., length is 0 or memory exhaustion), it returns NULL; the subsequent clGetPlatformInfo call then receives NULL as the output buffer and dereferences it. commit_msg:
Verify decoded kadmin C strings [CVE-2015-8629]

In xdr_nullstring(), check that the decoded string is terminated with
a zero byte and does not contain any internal zero bytes.

CVE-2015-8629:

In all versions of MIT krb5, an authenticated attacker can cause
kadmind to read beyond the end of allocated memory by sending a string
without a terminating zero byte.  Information leakage may be possible
for an attacker with permission to modify the database.

    CVSSv2 Vector: AV:N/AC:H/Au:S/C:P/I:N/A:N/E:POC/RL:OF/RC:C

ticket: 8341 (new)
target_version: 1.14-next
target_version: 1.13-next
tags: pullup
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t  return (xdr_opaque(xdrs, *objp, size));'], 'added_lines': ['\t  if (!xdr_opaque(xdrs, *objp, size))', '\t\t  return FALSE;', '\t  /* Check that the unmarshalled bytes are a C string. */', "\t  if ((*objp)[size - 1] != '\\0')", '\t\t  return FALSE;', "\t  if (memchr(*objp, '\\0', size - 1) != NULL)", '\t\t  return FALSE;', '\t  return TRUE;']}
description: The xdr_nullstring function in lib/kadm5/kadm_rpc_xdr.c in kadmind in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) before 1.13.4 and 1.14.x before 1.14.1 does not verify whether '\0' characters exist as expected, which allows remote authenticated users to obtain sensitive information or cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read) via a crafted string.

code_evidence: On XDR_DECODE, mem_alloc(size) allocates exactly the attacker-supplied size bytes, then xdr_opaque() fills them with decoded data and returns without any check that a terminating zero byte exists.

The size field is read from the wire via xdr_u_int; when size is nonzero, the buffer length and contents are both attacker-controlled and no C-string constraint is enforced before the buffer is treated as a string.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing termination check lets string consumers read beyond the allocated buffer's end, which is exactly CWE-125 (Out-of-bounds Read); the consequence is memory disclosure/DoS, but the cause is the absent bound on reads relative to the buffer length.

evidence_lines.code:
*objp = (char *) mem_alloc(size);
return (xdr_opaque(xdrs, *objp, size));

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the decode path accepts a length-prefixed blob and returns it as a C string without verifying termination or absence of internal NUL bytes. Trigger: an authenticated client sends a string whose size is nonzero but whose last byte is not '\0'. Consumers using strlen/str* then read past the allocated buffer, leaking memory or crashing.

commit_msg:
After commit cea0cc80a677 ("sctp: use the right sk after waking up from
wait_buf sleep"), it may change to lock another sk if the asoc has been
peeled off in sctp_wait_for_sndbuf.

However, the asoc's new sk could be already closed elsewhere, as it's in
the sendmsg context of the old sk that can't avoid the new sk's closing.
If the sk's last one refcnt is held by this asoc, later on after putting
this asoc, the new sk will be freed, while under it's own lock.

This patch is to revert that commit, but fix the old issue by returning
error under the old sk's lock.

Fixes: cea0cc80a677 ("sctp: use the right sk after waking up from wait_buf sleep")
Reported-by: syzbot+ac6ea7baa4432811eb50@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Signed-off-by: Xin Long <lucien.xin@gmail.com>
Acked-by: Neil Horman <nhorman@tuxdriver.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t\tsize_t msg_len, struct sock **orig_sk)', '\tint err = 0;', '\t\tif (sk != asoc->base.sk) {', '\t\t\trelease_sock(sk);', '\t\t\tsk = asoc->base.sk;', '\t\t\tlock_sock(sk);', '\t\t}', '\t*orig_sk = sk;'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t\tsize_t msg_len)', '\tint err = 0;', '\t\tif (sk != asoc->base.sk)', '\t\t\tgoto do_error;']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel before 4.14.16. There is a use-after-free in net/sctp/socket.c for a held lock after a peel off, aka CID-a0ff660058b8.

code_evidence: The function releases the socket lock, sleeps in schedule_timeout, then reacquires the lock. After reacquiring, it checks whether sk still equals asoc->base.sk; if the association was peeled off, it drops the old sk lock, switches sk to asoc->base.sk, and locks the new socket.
The final out path stores the current sk into *orig_sk, propagating whichever socket pointer was last assigned back to the caller.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function returns a socket pointer that may already have been freed after a peel off, and the caller dereferences it. This direct reuse of freed memory matches CWE-416. It is not merely a race on the lock but a stale pointer being propagated and used.

evidence_lines.code: *orig_sk = sk;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The root cause is that after sleeping, the code adopts the association's new sk (asoc->base.sk) and stores it in *orig_sk. That new sk can already be closed by other threads while the old sk's sendmsg context still runs, so the pointer handed back may reference freed socket memory that the caller later uses. The trigger is a peel off during the wait; the supported consequence is a use-after-free of the socket structure.

commit_msg:
block, bfq: fix use-after-free in bfq_idle_slice_timer_body

In bfq_idle_slice_timer func, bfqq = bfqd->in_service_queue is
not in bfqd-lock critical section. The bfqq, which is not
equal to NULL in bfq_idle_slice_timer, may be freed after passing
to bfq_idle_slice_timer_body. So we will access the freed memory.

In addition, considering the bfqq may be in race, we should
firstly check whether bfqq is in service before doing something
on it in bfq_idle_slice_timer_body func. If the bfqq in race is
not in service, it means the bfqq has been expired through
__bfq_bfqq_expire func, and wait_request flags has been cleared in
__bfq_bfqd_reset_in_service func. So we do not need to re-clear the
wait_request of bfqq which is not in service.

If', '\t * the bfqq in race is not in service, it has already been expired', '\t * through __bfq_bfqq_expire func and its wait_request flags has', '\t * been cleared in __bfq_bfqd_reset_in_service func.', '\t */', '', '\tbfq_clear_bfqq_wait_request(bfqq);']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel before 5.6.5. There is a use-after-free in block/bfq-iosched.c related to bfq_idle_slice_timer_body.

code_evidence: The function receives bfqq as an argument and immediately dereferences it at line 3 (bfqd = bfqq->bfqd) without any lifetime check; the caller obtains bfqq from bfqd->in_service_queue outside the lock, so this dereference can touch a queue already freed by another task.

Under the lock, line 7 calls bfq_clear_bfqq_wait_request(bfqq) before the in-service check at line 8, and lines 12+ later read bfqq->queued and call bfq_bfqq_expire on it; all these accesses occur on the possibly-freed bfqq.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences and mutates a bfq_queue pointer whose lifetime is not guaranteed at use time, which is exactly CWE-416 (Use After Free). It is not merely a race condition: the concrete defect is that freed memory is read/written, so the UAF label fits.

evidence_lines.code:
static void bfq_idle_slice_timer_body(struct bfq_queue *bfqq)
struct bfq_data *bfqd = bfqq->bfqd;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: bfqq is fetched without holding bfqd->lock and used (dereferenced and passed to bfq_clear_bfqq_wait_request) inside the timer body without first validating that it is still in service. Trigger: a concurrent completion/expiration frees the bfq_queue between the caller's fetch and the locked body. Consequence: use-after-free reads and writes on freed queue memory, as reported by KASAN.

commit_msg:
Check the mime type of cross-origin CSS fetched via the Service Worker.

BUG=598077

Review URL: https://codereview.chromium.org/1861243002

Cr-Commit-Position: refs/heads/master@{#385441}
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '    // When the response was fetched via the Service Worker, the original URL may not be same as the base URL.', '    // TODO(horo): When we will use the original URL as the base URL, we can remove this check. crbug.com/553535', '    if (cachedStyleSheet->response().wasFetchedViaServiceWorker()) {', '        const KURL originalURL(cachedStyleSheet->response().originalURLViaServiceWorker());', '        // |originalURL| is empty when the response is created in the SW.', '        if (!originalURL.isEmpty() && !securityOrigin->canRequest(originalURL))', '            isSameOriginRequest = false;', '    }', '']}
description: WebKit/Source/core/css/StyleSheetContents.cpp in Blink, as used in Google Chrome before 51.0.2704.63, permits cross-origin loading of CSS stylesheets by a ServiceWorker even when the stylesheet download has an incorrect MIME type, which allows remote attackers to bypass the Same Origin Policy via a crafted web site.

code_evidence: Line 4 derives isSameOriginRequest only from securityOrigin->canRequest(baseURL()); nothing accounts for the Service Worker original URL, so a cross-origin SW-fetched stylesheet can be treated as same-origin.
Line 5 then selects Lax MIME checking when isQuirksModeBehavior(...) && isSameOriginRequest, and line 6 passes that to sheetText, allowing a stylesheet with an incorrect MIME type to be parsed.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function makes an access-control decision (isSameOriginRequest) that incorrectly permits a cross-origin resource, matching CWE-284's improper restriction of access to a resource. The flaw is an enforcement error in origin checking rather than a parsing defect.

evidence_lines.code:
bool isSameOriginRequest = securityOrigin && securityOrigin->canRequest(baseURL());
CSSStyleSheetResource::MIMETypeCheck mimeTypeCheck = isQuirksModeBehavior(m_parserContext.mode()) && isSameOriginRequest ? CSSStyleSheetResource::MIMETypeCheck::Lax : CSSStyleSheetResource::MIMETypeCheck::Strict;

String sheetText = cachedStyleSheet->sheetText(mimeTypeCheck);
const ResourceResponse& response = cachedStyleSheet->response();

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the same-origin decision ignores the true original URL of a response fetched via a Service Worker, so an attacker-controlled cross-origin stylesheet is classified as same-origin. Trigger: a crafted site serving CSS through a Service Worker with a mismatched MIME type in quirks mode. Consequence: the incorrect-MIME stylesheet is accepted, enabling Same Origin Policy bypass.

Add a couple of memory allocation sanity checks, one of which
fixes #17331.

+++ func_after

 	 * memory for it.

-		 */

 		THROW(ReportedBoundsError);
 	}

-	 * No overflow; now make sure we at least have that data.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t * First, check for an overflow.', '\tif ((guint64)elsize * (guint64)num > G_MAXUINT) {', '\t\t/*', '\t\t * We never have more than G_MAXUINT bytes in a tvbuff,', '\t\t * so this will *definitely* fail.', '\t\t */', '\t * No overflow; now make sure we at least have that data.'], 'added_lines': ['\t * First, check for sane values.', '\tif (num > MAX_VT_VECTOR_SIZE) {', '\t * No huge numbers from the wire; now make sure we at least have that data.']}
description: Excessive memory consumption in MS-WSP dissector in Wireshark 3.4.0 to 3.4.4 and 3.2.0 to 3.2.12 allows denial of service via packet injection or crafted capture file

code_evidence: The guard only rejects counts whose byte product exceeds G_MAXUINT; any num below that threshold passes, so a wire-supplied count can still force a very large elsize * num allocation.

After the size check, tvb_ensure_bytes_exist and wmem_alloc use the unchecked elsize * num, and the loop at the caller's count allocates per-element storage proportional to the attacker-controlled num.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-770 fits because the function allocates a resource (packet-scope memory) sized by an attacker-controlled count without an intended upper bound; the overflow guard limits arithmetic, not allocation size. This is distinct from integer overflow (CWE-190), which the patch's MAX_VT_VECTOR_SIZE check addresses.

evidence_lines.code:
tvb_ensure_bytes_exist(tvb, offset, elsize * num);
data = (guint8*)wmem_alloc(wmem_packet_scope(), elsize * num);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: num from the dissected packet is only bounded so the multiplication does not overflow 32 bits, not bounded to a sane maximum. Trigger: a crafted capture or injected packet encoding a large vector count causes wmem_alloc to attempt a huge packet-scope allocation. Consequence: memory exhaustion and denial of service in the dissector.

description: Cygwin before 2.5.0 does not properly handle updating permissions when changing users, which allows attackers to gain privileges.

code_evidence: The function builds a group SID list and uses the auth_luid/auth_pos parameters only to conditionally populate it via get_token_group_sidlist; when usersid equals well_known_system_sid, the caller-supplied auth_pos is set to -1 and the group SID list is not populated from my_grps. The resulting token group set is derived from caller/credential state rather than independently established.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The flaw concerns improper management of permissions and privileges during token/group SID construction, matching CWE-264's category of permissions/privileges/access-control weaknesses. It is not a simple input-validation issue; the defect is in how group privileges are assigned to the resulting security context.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: token/group SID construction depends on the caller-supplied auth_luid/auth_pos and on whether usersid is the system SID, so the privilege/group set for the new token is inherited rather than re-derived. Trigger: creating a token while changing users. Consequence: the new token can retain or acquire group memberships/privileges it should not have, yielding privilege escalation.

commit_msg:
mp4: limit the recursion depth for boxes

Although the dissection of each box header consumes a couple of bytes,
it turned out that it's still possible to crash wireshark with a sample
file that contains a large number of nested boxes. The stack will fill
up before we reach the end of the data bytes.

Keep track of the recursion depth as we walk through the hierarchy of

commit_msg:
x86: Guard against corrupted PLT

There should be only one entry in PLT for a given symbol.  Set howto to
NULL after processing a PLT entry to guard against corrupted PLT so that
the duplicated PLT entries are skipped.

	PR binutils/22170
	 * elf32-i386.c (elf_i386_get_synthetic_symtab): Guard against
	 corrupted PLT.
	 * elf64-x86-64.c (elf_x86_64_get_synthetic_symtab): Likewise.

(cherry picked from commit 61e3bf5f83f7e505b6bc51ef65426e5b31e6e360)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\t/* There should be only one entry in PLT for a given', '\t\t   symbol.  Set howto to NULL after processing a PLT', '\t\t   entry to guard against corrupted PLT.  */', '\t\tp->howto = NULL;']}
description: The *_get_synthetic_symtab functions in the Binary File Descriptor (BFD) library (aka libbfd), as distributed in GNU Binutils 2.29, do not ensure a unique PLT entry for a symbol, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (heap-based buffer overflow and application crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted ELF file, related to elf32-i386.c and elf64-x86-64.c.

code_evidence: The inner loop walks PLT entries and resolves each got_vma against dynrelbuf, then writes a synthetic symbol via '*s = **p->sym_ptr_ptr' and advances s. The number of emitted symbols n (line 250) later drives the names buffer size at line 247/259. The patch adds 'p->howto = NULL' after processing so a duplicated/corrupted PLT entry cannot match the same relocation twice; without that guard, duplicate matches inflate n beyond the allocated asymbol array, so the s++ writes run past the buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Writing synthetic symbols beyond the allocated buffer's intended bounds is a direct out-of-bounds memory-buffer write, matching CWE-119's buffer-boundary violation. The added NULL-ing of howto is the missing uniqueness constraint that prevents the overrun.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function assumes each PLT entry maps to a unique relocation but never enforces uniqueness, so a crafted ELF with duplicated PLT entries causes repeated symbol emission past the count-based allocation. Trigger is a corrupted PLT in an attacker-supplied file; consequence is a heap-based out-of-bounds write and crash/possible code execution.

commit_msg:
netfilter: x_tables: make sure e->next_offset covers remaining blob size

Otherwise this function may read data beyond the ruleset blob.

Signed-off-by: Florian Westphal <fw@strlen.de>
Signed-off-by: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t    (unsigned char *)e + sizeof(struct compat_ip6t_entry) >= limit) {'], 'added_lines': ['\t    (unsigned char *)e + sizeof(struct compat_ip6t_entry) >= limit ||', '\t    (unsigned char *)e + e->next_offset > limit) {']}
description: The IPT_SO_SET_REPLACE setsockopt implementation in the netfilter subsystem in the Linux kernel before 4.6 allows local users to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read) or possibly obtain sensitive information from kernel heap memory by leveraging in-container root access to provide a crafted offset value that leads to crossing a ruleset blob boundary.

code_evidence: The initial bounds check only validates that the fixed-size compat_ip6t_entry header fits before limit (e + sizeof(...) >= limit); it does not verify that the attacker-controlled e->next_offset stays within the remaining blob, so a crafted next_offset can point past limit.
The subsequent check only enforces a minimum next_offset (sizeof entry + compat target) and returns -EINVAL if smaller; there is no maximum/remaining-size constraint tying next_offset to limit.

The function then iterates matches via xt_ematch_foreach and reads compat_ip6t_get_target(e) and t->u.user.name, dereferencing memory at offsets derived from the unvalidated entry layout beyond the buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads struct fields and iterates matches using offsets not constrained to the buffer's intended boundary, which is a memory-buffer out-of-bounds read operation — the defining behavior of CWE-119. The defect is the absent boundary restriction on next_offset, distinct from the separate alignment/size checks that are present.

evidence_lines.code:
if ((unsigned long)e % __alignof__(struct compat_ip6t_entry) != 0 ||
(unsigned char *)e + sizeof(struct compat_ip6t_entry) >= limit) {

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: a missing upper-bound check on the attacker-supplied e->next_offset relative to the ruleset blob limit. Trigger: local root passes a crafted IPT_SO_SET_REPLACE ruleset whose entry declares a next_offset crossing the blob boundary. Consequence: the code follows offsets and reads match/target structures past the buffer, yielding an out-of-bounds read (DoS or kernel heap info leak).

commit_msg:
(uid_t) -1 is still used as placeholder to mean "unset". This is OK, since
there should be no users with such number, see
https://systemd.io/UIDS-GIDS#special-linux-uids.

(uid_t) -1 is used as the default value in class initialization.

When a user or group above INT32_MAX is created, the numeric uid or
gid wraps around to negative when the value is assigned to gint, and
polkit gets confused. Let's accept such gids, except for -1.

A nicer fix would be to change the underlying type to e.g. uint32 to
not have negative values. But this cannot be done without breaking the
API, so likely new functions will have to be added (a
polkit_unix_user_new variant that takes a unsigned, and the same for
_group_new, _set_uid, _get_uid, _set_gid, _get_gid, etc.). This will
require a bigger patch.

Fixes https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/polkit/polkit/issues/74.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['                          gint gid)'], 'added_lines': ['                           gint gid)', '  g_return_if_fail (gid != -1);']}
description: A flaw was found in PolicyKit (aka polkit) 0.115 that allows a user with a uid greater than INT_MAX to successfully execute any systemctl command.

code_evidence: The setter accepts a signed gint gid from the caller and stores it directly in group->gid without checking for the -1 sentinel value. Only the group object type is validated; the numeric gid itself is unchecked before assignment.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function receives an input value (gid) and fails to validate that it conforms to the required domain (non-negative, not the reserved -1 sentinel) before using it. This is a missing input constraint check, matching CWE-20. It is not merely a type-conversion bug: the unsafe operation is the absent validation of the accepted numeric input.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: gid is a signed gint and negative values (notably -1) are accepted and persisted as if they were valid group IDs. A caller supplying a gid above INT32_MAX wraps to a negative value, and -1 collides with the 'unset' placeholder, so downstream polkit authorization logic misinterprets the identity. This can let a user with such a uid/gid bypass policy checks and execute privileged commands.

commit_msg:
Fix usage of custom EVP_CIPHER objects

If a custom EVP_CIPHER object has been passed to EVP_CipherInit() then it
should be used in preference to a fetched cipher.

We also fix a possible NULL pointer deref in the same code for digests.

If the custom cipher passed to EVP_CipherInit() happens to use NID_undef
(which should be a discouraged practice), then in the previous
implementation this could result in the NULL cipher being fetched and
hence NULL encryption being unexpectedly used.

CVE-2022-3358

Fixes #18970

Reviewed-by: Tomas Mraz <tomas@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Paul Dale <pauli@openssl.org>
(Merged from https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/19300)

(cherry picked from commit 25d47cccf203c3b71171e78865e48ea061a039a8)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            || type->origin == EVP_ORIG_METH) {'], 'added_lines': ['            || (type != NULL && type->origin == EVP_ORIG_METH)', '            || (type == NULL && ctx->digest != NULL', '                             && ctx->digest->origin == EVP_ORIG_METH)) {']}
description: OpenSSL supports creating a custom cipher via the legacy EVP_CIPHER_meth_new() function and associated function calls. This function was deprecated in OpenSSL 3.0 and application authors are instead encouraged to use the new provider mechanism in order to implement custom ciphers. OpenSSL versions 3.0.0 to 3.0.5 incorrectly handle legacy custom ciphers passed to the EVP_EncryptInit_ex2(), EVP_DecryptInit_ex2() and EVP_CipherInit_ex2() functions (as well as other similarly named encryption and decryption initialisation functions). Instead of using the custom cipher directly it incorrectly tries to fetch an equivalent cipher from the available providers. An equivalent cipher is found based on the NID passed to EVP_CIPHER_meth_new(). This NID is supposed to represent the unique NID for a given cipher. However it is possible for an application to incorrectly pass NID_undef as this value in the call to EVP_CIPHER_meth_new(). When NID_undef is used in this way the OpenSSL encryption/decryption initialisation function will match the NULL cipher as being equivalent and will fetch this from the available providers. This will succeed if the default provider has been loaded (or if a third party provider has been loaded that offers this cipher). Using the NULL cipher means that the plaintext is emitted as the ciphertext. Applications are only affected by this issue if they call EVP_CIPHER_meth_new() using NID_undef and subsequently use it in a call to an encryption/decryption initialisation function. Applications that only use SSL/TLS are not impacted by this issue. Fixed in OpenSSL 3.0.6 (Affected 3.0.0-3.0.5).

code_evidence: When type is NULL the function falls back to ctx->digest, but if ctx->digest is also NULL it raises NO_DIGEST_SET and returns, so type is non-NULL here.
The condition evaluates type->origin directly; the patch replaces this with NULL guards on type and ctx->digest.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The code dereferences a pointer expected to be valid without a NULL check, matching CWE-476. This is a direct NULL dereference rather than an unrelated weakness such as use-after-free.

evidence_lines.code:
|| (ctx->flags & EVP_MD_CTX_FLAG_NO_INIT) != 0
|| type->origin == EVP_ORIG_METH) {

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the legacy-origin check dereferences type without verifying it is non-NULL, relying on the earlier fallback to guarantee non-NULLness. Trigger: a caller path where neither the supplied type nor ctx->digest is set reaches the condition, causing a NULL pointer dereference and crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
Prevent division by 0.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 370962554
Change-Id: I0b9b62f4d8e1046dd88f9433f8dfeaf61a901680
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  const int input_size = NumElements(input) / SizeOfDimension(input, 0);'], 'added_lines': ['  TF_LITE_ENSURE(context, batch_size != 0);', '  const int input_size = NumElements(input) / batch_size;']}
description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. TFLite's convolution code(https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/09c73bca7d648e961dd05898292d91a8322a9d45/tensorflow/lite/kernels/conv.cc) has multiple division where the divisor is controlled by the user and not checked to be non-zero. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.5.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.4.2, TensorFlow 2.3.3, TensorFlow 2.2.3 and TensorFlow 2.1.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

const int batch_size = SizeOfDimension(input, 0);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the batch dimension obtained from the user-controlled input tensor is used directly as a divisor. description: The Mobile Identity parser in (1) epan/dissectors/packet-ansi_a.c in the ANSI A dissector and (2) epan/dissectors/packet-gsm_a_common.c in the GSM A dissector in Wireshark 1.12.x before 1.12.9 and 2.0.x before 2.0.1 improperly uses the tvb_bcd_dig_to_wmem_packet_str function, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (buffer overflow and application crash) via a crafted packet.

commit_msg:
With write operation on psi files replacing old trigger with a new one,
the lifetime of its waitqueue is totally arbitrary. Overwriting an
existing trigger causes its waitqueue to be freed and pending poll()
will stumble on trigger->event_wait which was destroyed.
Fix this by disallowing to redefine an existing psi trigger. If a write
operation is used on a file descriptor with an already existing psi
trigger, the operation will fail with EBUSY error.
Also bypass a check for psi_disabled in the psi_trigger_destroy as the
flag can be flipped after the trigger is created, leading to a memory
leak.

Fixes: 0e94682b73bf ("psi: introduce psi monitor")
Reported-by: syzbot+cdb5dd11c97cc532efad@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Suggested-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Analyzed-by: Eric Biggers <ebiggers@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Suren Baghdasaryan <surenb@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Peter Zijlstra (Intel) <peterz@infradead.org>
Reviewed-by: Eric Biggers <ebiggers@google.com>
Acked-by: Johannes Weiner <hannes@cmpxchg.org>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220111232309.1786347-1-surenb@google.com
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tpsi_trigger_replace(&seq->private, NULL);'], 'added_lines': ['\tpsi_trigger_destroy(seq->private);']}
description: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's implementation of Pressure Stall Information. While the feature is disabled by default, it could allow an attacker to crash the system or have other memory-corruption side effects.

code_evidence: psi_fop_release obtains the seq_file from file->private_data and passes &seq->private to psi_trigger_replace, which frees or replaces the stored trigger and clears the pointer to NULL. The release path is reached when the psi file descriptor is closed while a trigger may still exist; the waitqueue inside that trigger is then destroyed.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function frees the trigger object via psi_trigger_replace while other code can still hold and use a pointer into it, which is precisely a use-after-free (CWE-416). A simple memory leak would not fit because the flaw is reuse of freed memory, not failure to free.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the release path uses psi_trigger_replace(&seq->private, NULL) to drop the trigger, freeing its embedded event_wait waitqueue without coordinating with pending poll() callers that still reference trigger->event_wait. Trigger: closing the psi file (or overwriting the trigger as described in the commit) frees the trigger while a concurrent poll() holds a pointer to it. Consequence: poll() dereferences freed memory, causing a crash or memory corruption (use after free).

commit_msg:
Fix 2 issues with `Conv3D`.

We have an issue where the dimensions are not matching and this causes Eigen to crash on an assert.

Then, we have an issue where we accidentally do a division by 0.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 369242785
Change-Id: Ie94067b2d41f58699af99ebb5af335ad9defd931
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    OP_REQUIRES(context, filter_depth != 0,', '                errors::InvalidArgument("filter_depth must be non-zero"));']}
description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. A malicious user could trigger a division by 0 in `Conv3D` implementation. The implementation(https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/42033603003965bffac51ae171b51801565e002d/tensorflow/core/kernels/conv_ops_3d.cc#L143-L145) does a modulo operation based on user controlled input. Thus, when `filter` has a 0 as the fifth element, this results in a division by 0. Additionally, if the shape of the two tensors is not valid, an Eigen assertion can be triggered, resulting in a program crash. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.5.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.4.2, TensorFlow 2.3.3, TensorFlow 2.2.3 and TensorFlow 2.1.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: filter_depth is read directly from the user-supplied filter tensor at line 10 (dim_size(3)) with no validation that it is non-zero. Line 12 then computes in_depth % filter_depth, using filter_depth as the divisor. A filter whose fourth dimension is 0 makes the modulo operation divide by zero before any guard rejects it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-369 fits because a user-controlled value is used as the divisor in a modulo operation without a zero check, producing a divide-by-zero. This is a division-by-zero weakness, not merely a shape-mismatch assertion failure, which concerns different validation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the divisor filter_depth is derived from an attacker-controlled tensor shape and is never checked for zero. Trigger: a Conv3D call with a filter tensor whose depth dimension equals 0. Consequence: the modulo at line 12 performs integer division by zero, causing a crash/DoS (the patch adds an explicit non-zero check).

commit_msg:
Commit 086d49058cd8 ("ipv6: annotate some data-races around sk->sk_prot")
fixed some data-races around sk->sk_prot but it was not enough.

Some functions in inet6_(stream|dgram)_ops still access sk->sk_prot
without lock_sock() or rtnl_lock(), so they need READ_ONCE() to avoid
load tearing.

Fixes: 1da177e4c3f4 ("Linux-2.6.12-rc2")
Signed-off-by: Kuniyuki Iwashima <kuniyu@amazon.com>
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t\t/* Paired with READ_ONCE(sk->sk_prot) in net/ipv6/af_inet6.c */', '\t\t\t\t/* Paired with READ_ONCE(sk->sk_prot) in net/ipv6/af_inet6.c */'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t\t/* Paired with READ_ONCE(sk->sk_prot) in inet6_stream_ops */', '\t\t\t\t/* Paired with READ_ONCE(sk->sk_prot) in inet6_dgram_ops */']}
description: A vulnerability has been found in Linux Kernel and classified as problematic. This vulnerability affects the function inet6_stream_ops/inet6_dgram_ops of the component IPv6 Handler. The manipulation leads to race condition. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue. VDB-211090 is the identifier assigned to this vulnerability.

code_evidence: sockopt_lock_sock(sk) is taken, but the commit states inet6_stream_ops/inet6_dgram_ops still read sk->sk_prot without lock_sock() or rtnl_lock(); the check at [41] reads sk->sk_prot directly and is not READ_ONCE-protected.
On the TCP path, sock_prot_inuse_add(net, sk->sk_prot, -1) reads sk->sk_prot, then WRITE_ONCE(sk->sk_prot, &tcp_prot) reassigns the shared pointer while concurrent readers may observe the field.

The datagram path mirrors this: sock_prot_inuse_add(net, sk->sk_prot, -1) reads the shared proto pointer before WRITE_ONCE(sk->sk_prot, prot) publishes the new one, with no exclusivity against unlocked readers.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-362 fits because a shared resource (sk->sk_prot) is accessed concurrently with only partial synchronization; the writer is locked but unlocked readers violate exclusivity/atomicity, a classic race condition. It is not merely a missing bounds check or null dereference.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: sk->sk_prot is a shared field mutated under the setsockopt lock while other IPv6 proto operations read it without lock_sock()/rtnl_lock(), so the read-modify-write sequence is non-atomic. Trigger: concurrent setsockopt(IPV6_ADDRFORM) and proto operations on the same socket. Supported consequence: load tearing/data race on the proto pointer (inconsistent inuse accounting or dereference), which the patch addresses with READ_ONCE on the reader side.

run: Convert all environment variables into bwrap arguments

This avoids some of them being filtered out by a setuid bwrap. It also
means that if they came from an untrusted source, they cannot be used
to inject arbitrary code into a non-setuid bwrap via mechanisms like
LD_PRELOAD.

Because they get bundled into a memfd or temporary file, they do not
actually appear in argv, ensuring that they remain inaccessible to
processes running under a different uid (which is important if their
values are tokens or other secrets).

Signed-off-by: Simon McVittie <smcv@collabora.com>
Part-of: https://github.com/flatpak/flatpak/security/advisories/GHSA-4ppf-fxf6-vxg2

description: Flatpak is a system for building, distributing, and running sandboxed desktop applications on Linux. A bug was discovered in the `flatpak-portal` service that can allow sandboxed applications to execute arbitrary code on the host system (a sandbox escape). This sandbox-escape bug is present in versions from 0.11.4 and before fixed versions 1.8.5 and 1.10.0. The Flatpak portal D-Bus service (`flatpak-portal`, also known by its D-Bus service name `org.freedesktop.portal.Flatpak`) allows apps in a Flatpak sandbox to launch their own subprocesses in a new sandbox instance, either with the same security settings as the caller or with more restrictive security settings. For example, this is used in Flatpak-packaged web browsers such as Chromium to launch subprocesses that will process untrusted web content, and give those subprocesses a more restrictive sandbox than the browser itself. In vulnerable versions, the Flatpak portal service passes caller-specified environment variables to non-sandboxed processes on the host system, and in particular to the `flatpak run` command that is used to launch the new sandbox instance. A malicious or compromised Flatpak app could set environment variables that are trusted by the `flatpak run` command, and use them to execute arbitrary code that is not in a sandbox. As a workaround, this vulnerability can be mitigated by preventing the `flatpak-portal` service from starting, but that mitigation will prevent many Flatpak apps from working correctly. This is fixed in versions 1.8.5 and 1.10.0.

code_evidence: Caller-influenced environment variables are accumulated into bwrap via flatpak_run_apply_env_default/vars/prompt before argv is finalized.
flatpak_bwrap_bundle_args() then bundles the arguments, and command is appended to bwrap->argv; the environment is passed separately to execvpe as bwrap->envp.
execvpe invokes bwrap with bwrap->envp still populated; the patch adds flatpak_bwrap_envp_to_args() to move env vars into --setenv argv entries and asserts envp is empty.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-74 fits because externally influenced environment data is forwarded to a downstream component (bwrap) without neutralizing special elements that alter its interpretation; the fix converts them into explicit --setenv arguments and empties envp.

evidence_lines.code: if (execvpe (flatpak_get_bwrap (), (char **) bwrap->argv->pdata, bwrap->envp) == -1)

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: environment variables influenced by the calling sandboxed app are passed through to the bwrap/`flatpak run` process environment rather than being neutralized into bwrap arguments. Trigger: a malicious app sets variables such as LD_PRELOAD that the downstream bwrap process interprets. Consequence: arbitrary code execution outside the sandbox.
