commit_msg:
commit 0fa3ecd87848c9c93c2c828ef4c3a8ca36ce46c7 upstream.

sgid directories have special semantics, making newly created files in
the directory belong to the group of the directory, and newly created
subdirectories will also become sgid.  This is historically used for
group-shared directories.

But group directories writable by non-group members should not imply
that such non-group members can magically join the group, so make sure
to clear the sgid bit on non-directories for non-members (but remember
that sgid without group execute means "mandatory locking", just to
confuse things even more).

Reported-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Cc: Andy Lutomirski <luto@kernel.org>
Cc: Al Viro <viro@zeniv.linux.org.uk>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Ben Hutchings <ben@decadent.org.uk>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\t\t/* Directories are special, and always inherit S_ISGID */', '\t\telse if ((mode & (S_ISGID | S_IXGRP)) == (S_ISGID | S_IXGRP) &&', '\t\t\t !in_group_p(inode->i_gid) &&', '\t\t\t !capable_wrt_inode_uidgid(dir, CAP_FSETID))', '\t\t\tmode &= ~S_ISGID;']}
description: The inode_init_owner function in fs/inode.c in the Linux kernel through 3.16 allows local users to create files with an unintended group ownership, in a scenario where a directory is SGID to a certain group and is writable by a user who is not a member of that group. Here, the non-member can trigger creation of a plain file whose group ownership is that group. The intended behavior was that the non-member can trigger creation of a directory (but not a plain file) whose group ownership is that group. The non-member can escalate privileges by making the plain file executable and SGID.

code_evidence: When the parent directory has S_ISGID set, the new inode unconditionally inherits the directory's group via inode->i_gid = dir->i_gid, with no check that the caller is a member of that group or holds CAP_FSETID.
Only directories receive S_ISGID propagation; for non-directories the mode is left otherwise unchanged, so a plain file created by a non-member keeps the inherited group.
The else branch assigns current_fsgid() only when the parent is not SGID; combined with line 11, the inherited group from line 6 is persisted with no membership constraint.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function assigns group ownership (a privilege attribute) without checking the actor's authorization, creating an unintended sphere of control for non-members; this is improper privilege management, not merely the downstream escalation impact.

evidence_lines.code:
if (dir && dir->i_mode & S_ISGID) {
inode->i_gid = dir->i_gid;

if (S_ISDIR(mode))
mode |= S_ISGID;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: group inheritance from an SGID directory is applied to all inode types without verifying group membership or CAP_FSETID. Trigger: a non-member of the directory's group creates a plain file in that writable SGID directory. Consequence: the file gets unintended group ownership, enabling later privilege escalation via an executable SGID file.

commit_msg: fix heap-buffer-overflow
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['      if (t >= tend)    return 0;']}
description: Oniguruma through 6.9.3, as used in PHP 7.3.x and other products, has a heap-based buffer over-read in str_lower_case_match in regexec.c.

code_evidence: Inner loop consumes lowbuf via *q++ while dereferencing and advancing *t++ without checking t against tend; the outer loop guard t < tend is only checked before case folding, not per folded byte.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the dereference of *t++ can occur after t reaches tend, reading past the intended buffer. It is a read overrun, not a write (CWE-787), and the root cause is a missing bounds check on the read pointer.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Case folding can produce more bytes (lowlen) than remain between t and tend, so the inner loop advances t past tend and reads out of bounds. Trigger: a target-side string shorter than the folded form of the pattern-side character. Consequence: heap-buffer-over-read (crash/DoS, possible memory disclosure).

HID: corsair: fix DMA buffers on stack

Not all platforms support DMA to the stack, and specifically since v4.9
this is no longer supported on x86 with VMAP_STACK either.

Note that the macro-mode buffer was larger than necessary.

Fixes: 6f78193ee9ea ("HID: corsair: Add Corsair Vengeance K90 driver")
Cc: stable <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Johan Hovold <johan@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Jiri Kosina <jkosina@suse.cz>

description: drivers/hid/hid-corsair.c in the Linux kernel 4.9.x before 4.9.6 interacts incorrectly with the CONFIG_VMAP_STACK option, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (system crash or memory corruption) or possibly have unspecified other impact by leveraging use of more than one virtual page for a DMA scatterlist.

code_evidence: Line 9 declares a fixed 8-byte stack buffer `data` for the backlight state.
Lines 10-14 pass that stack buffer directly to `usb_control_msg` as the DMA destination for an 8-byte IN transfer.
Line 20 reads `data[4]` after the transfer completes, assuming the DMA wrote into the stack buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-119 fits because the function performs a read/write operation on a memory buffer outside its intended boundary: the DMA transfer into the stack buffer can exceed the buffer's bounds under VMAP_STACK. The missing constraint is that DMA targets must be DMA-safe, page-bounded memory rather than an arbitrary stack region.

evidence_lines.code: char data[8];

ret = usb_control_msg(usbdev, usb_rcvctrlpipe(usbdev, 0),
K90_REQUEST_STATUS,
USB_DIR_IN | USB_TYPE_VENDOR |
USB_RECIP_DEVICE, 0, 0, data, 8,
USB_CTRL_SET_TIMEOUT);
brightness = data[4];

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: a stack-allocated buffer is used as the target of a USB control-message DMA transfer. With CONFIG_VMAP_STACK, the stack may span more than one virtual page, so the device/DMA path can write past the buffer's intended boundary; the subsequent read of data[4] then operates on memory whose contents are not reliably bounded. Trigger: a local user causes k90_backlight_get to issue the control transfer. Consequence: system crash or memory corruption.

commit_msg:
Validate that `DataFormat*` attributes form a permutation.

The `src_format` and `dst_format` attributes for the `DataFormatDimMap` and `DataFormatVecPermute` raw ops are supposed to determine a permutation. However, this was not validated and could result in unitialized memory accesses as well as writes outside of bounds and potential crashes.

While here, we also test that the format attributes have the needed length, add tests for all validation failure cases, remove unnecessary calls to `strings::StrCat`, and fix a few grammar errors.

This will be cherry-picked on the supported release branches.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 346135579
Change-Id: I1c76392382c89ad8f072d5bc93d70669851eb404
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    OP_REQUIRES(context, src_format.size() == 4 || src_format.size() == 5,', '                errors::InvalidArgument(', '                    "Source format must be of length 4 or 5, received "', '                    "src_format = ",', '                    src_format));', '    OP_REQUIRES(context, dst_format.size() == 4 || dst_format.size() == 5,', '                errors::InvalidArgument("Destination format must be of length "', '                                        "4 or 5, received dst_format = ",', '                                        dst_format));', '    OP_REQUIRES(', '        context, IsValidPermutation(src_format, dst_format),', '        errors::InvalidArgument(', '            "Destination and source format must determine a permutation, got ",', '            src_format, " and ", dst_format));']}
description: In affected versions of TensorFlow the tf.raw_ops.DataFormatVecPermute API does not validate the src_format and dst_format attributes. The code assumes that these two arguments define a permutation of NHWC. This can result in uninitialized memory accesses, read outside of bounds and even crashes. This is fixed in versions 1.15.5, 2.0.4, 2.1.3, 2.2.2, 2.3.2, and 2.4.0.

code_evidence: The constructor reads the src_format and dst_format attributes via GetAttr and stores them in src_format_ and dst_format_ without any length or permutation validation. Downstream code uses these stored strings to index/permute vectors, so an attacker-supplied format of arbitrary content or length is accepted unchecked.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The described and demonstrated impact is unvalidated format strings driving out-of-bounds memory reads, matching CWE-125 (Out-of-bounds Read). It is distinct from CWE-787 because the primary supported consequence here is reading past buffer bounds.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: missing validation that src_format and dst_format have length 4 or 5 and form a valid permutation. Trigger: a crafted raw-op invocation supplying non-permutation or wrong-length format attributes. Consequence: downstream indexing/permutation logic reads past the end of the intended buffer (and may also write out of bounds or crash).

commit_msg:
opt_go: Tolerate unplanned server death

While debugging some experimental nbdkit code that was triggering an
assertion failure in nbdkit, I noticed a secondary failure of nbdsh
also dying from an assertion:

libnbd: debug: nbdsh: nbd_opt_go: transition: NEWSTYLE.OPT_GO.SEND -> DEAD
libnbd: debug: nbdsh: nbd_opt_go: option queued, ignoring state machine failure
nbdsh: opt.c:86: nbd_unlocked_opt_go: Assertion `nbd_internal_is_state_negotiating (get_next_state (h))' failed.

Although my trigger was from non-production nbdkit code, libnbd should
never die from an assertion failure merely because a server
disappeared at the wrong moment during an incomplete reply to
NBD_OPT_GO or NBD_OPT_INFO.  If this is assigned a CVE, a followup
patch will add mention of it in docs/libnbd-security.pod.

Fixes: bbf1c51392 (api: Give aio_opt_go a completion callback)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    assert (nbd_internal_is_state_negotiating (get_next_state (h)));'], 'added_lines': ['    assert (nbd_internal_is_state_negotiating (get_next_state (h)) ||', '            nbd_internal_is_state_dead (get_next_state (h)));']}
description: A flaw was found in libnbd 1.7.3. An assertion failure in nbd_unlocked_opt_go in ilb/opt.c may lead to denial of service.

code_evidence: wait_for_option returns r==0 while err is set when the server replies with an error to opt_go; the code then asserts the next state is negotiating without tolerating a server that died mid-reply.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function contains a reachable assert() triggered by server-controlled behavior, so an attacker can force an application exit. This matches CWE-617 (Reachable Assertion) rather than a mere logic error, since the consequence is process abort/DoS.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the assert at line 11 assumes the next state must be negotiating whenever r==0 && err, but a server that disappears during an incomplete reply leaves the state DEAD. The attacker-triggered server death reaches this assert, aborting the process and causing denial of service.

commit_msg: Prevent a buffer overflow in cardreader
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if (dirname_end <= dirname_start) break;', '', '    char dosSubdirname[FILENAME_LENGTH];', '    const uint8_t len = dirname_end - dirname_start;'], 'added_lines': ['    const int8_t len = dirname_end - dirname_start;', '    if (len <= 0) break;', '    char dosSubdirname[len + 1];']}
description: Marlin Firmware Marlin version 1.1.x and earlier contains a Buffer Overflow vulnerability in cardreader.cpp (Depending on branch/version) that can result in Arbitrary code execution. This attack appear to be exploitable via Crafted G-Code instruction/file is sent to the printer.

code_evidence: Line 8 only breaks when dirname_end <= dirname_start; strchr may return NULL, and NULL <= dirname_start is false, so execution continues. Line 10 computes len = dirname_end - dirname_start from a NULL pointer; line 11 strncpy copies len bytes into the fixed stack buffer dosSubdirname[FILENAME_LENGTH] declared on line 9, and line 12 writes dosSubdirname[len] = 0 without bounding len against FILENAME_LENGTH.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-119 fits because the function performs a copy into a fixed-size memory buffer without restricting the operation to the buffer's intended boundary, producing an out-of-bounds write.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the length derived from the path segment is never validated against the fixed FILENAME_LENGTH buffer size, and a missing '/' (NULL from strchr) is not rejected. Trigger: a crafted G-Code path segment longer than FILENAME_LENGTH. Consequence: strncpy and the terminating write overflow the stack buffer, potentially corrupting adjacent memory and enabling code execution.

description: GPAC version 2.1-DEV-rev505-gb9577e6ad-master was discovered to contain a memory leak via the gf_isom_box_parse_ex function at box_funcs.c.

code_evidence: When do_uncompress is true, compb is allocated with gf_malloc at line 66 and used for the compressed payload. If gf_gz_decompress_payload fails, lines 70-72 log and return e without freeing compb, leaking the allocation.

After decompression succeeds, uncomp_bs and uncomp_data are created at line 75. The error returns at lines 84-86 (and similarly the incomplete-file return at lines 146-149) exit without freeing uncomp_data or deleting uncomp_bs, leaking the decompression buffer and bitstream.
The later cleanup at lines 160-162 only runs on the normal path; the early returns bypass it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function allocates heap memory and fails to release it on error paths, matching CWE-401 (missing release of memory after effective lifetime). This is a leak of still-referenced-but-abandoned allocations, not a use-after-free or double-free.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: error/early-exit paths after allocating compb and creating uncomp_bs/uncomp_data return without releasing them. Trigger: a malformed compressed box causing decompression failure, or a truncated box/header causing an incomplete-file return. Consequence: repeated parsing leaks memory, enabling resource-consumption DoS.

description: objects.cc in Google V8 before 5.2.361.27, as used in Google Chrome before 52.0.2743.82, does not prevent API interceptors from modifying a store target without setting a property, which allows remote attackers to bypass the Same Origin Policy via a crafted web site.

commit_msg:
Fixed OOB read in ntlm_av_pair_get

CVE-2020-11097 thanks to @antonio-morales for finding this.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\treturn ntlm_av_pair_add(pAvPairList, cbAvPairList, ntlm_av_pair_get_id(pAvPair),', '\t                        ntlm_av_pair_get_value_pointer(pAvPair), ntlm_av_pair_get_len(pAvPair));'], 'added_lines': ['\tUINT16 pair;', '\tsize_t avLen;', '', '\tif (!ntlm_av_pair_get_id(pAvPair, cbAvPair, &pair))', '\t\treturn FALSE;', '', '\tif (!ntlm_av_pair_get_len(pAvPair, cbAvPair, &avLen))', '\t\treturn FALSE;', '', '\treturn ntlm_av_pair_add(pAvPairList, cbAvPairList, pair,', '\t                        ntlm_av_pair_get_value_pointer(pAvPair), avLen);']}
description: In FreeRDP before version 2.1.2, an out of bounds read occurs resulting in accessing a memory location that is outside of the boundaries of the static array PRIMARY_DRAWING_ORDER_FIELD_BYTES. This is fixed in version 2.1.2.

code_evidence: ntlm_av_pair_check validates the pair, but the code then calls ntlm_av_pair_get_id, ntlm_av_pair_get_len and ntlm_av_pair_get_value_pointer on pAvPair without passing cbAvPair or verifying the returned length against the buffer size. The resulting id and length are passed directly to ntlm_av_pair_add.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Reading AV-pair fields and values beyond the validated buffer is an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). It is not a write overflow because the flaw is unchecked reading of the pair data, not writing past a destination buffer.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the length and value pointer are read from attacker-controlled NTLM AV pair data without bounds validation against cbAvPair. A malformed pair whose declared length exceeds the actual buffer triggers reads past the end of pAvPair when the value is consumed, exposing adjacent memory.

commit_msg:
openssl: associate/detach the transfer from connection

CVE-2021-22901

Bug: https://curl.se/docs/CVE-2021-22901.html
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  if(conn)'], 'added_lines': ['  if(conn) {', '    Curl_ssl_detach_conn(data, conn);', '  }']}
description: curl 7.75.0 through 7.76.1 suffers from a use-after-free vulnerability resulting in already freed memory being used when a TLS 1.3 session ticket arrives over a connection. A malicious server can use this in rare unfortunate circumstances to potentially reach remote code execution in the client. When libcurl at run-time sets up support for TLS 1.3 session tickets on a connection using OpenSSL, it stores pointers to the transfer in-memory object for later retrieval when a session ticket arrives. If the connection is used by multiple transfers (like with a reused HTTP/1.1 connection or multiplexed HTTP/2 connection) that first transfer object might be freed before the new session is established on that connection and then the function will access a memory buffer that might be freed. When using that memory, libcurl might even call a function pointer in the object, making it possible for a remote code execution if the server could somehow manage to get crafted memory content into the correct place in memory.

code_evidence: Curl_detach_connnection() clears data->conn after removing the transfer from conn->easyq, but only calls Curl_llist_remove; no call to Curl_ssl_detach_conn() is made to unlink the OpenSSL session-ticket association from this transfer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing SSL detach leaves a dangling reference to a freed Curl_easy object that is later accessed, which is exactly CWE-416. This is not merely a memory leak or null dereference because the freed transfer memory is reused after free.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The connection keeps a pointer to the transfer object for later TLS 1.3 session-ticket retrieval. Detaching only removes the transfer from easyq and nulls data->conn while leaving the SSL-layer pointer registered on the connection; when a session ticket later arrives on that reused connection, the stale pointer to the freed transfer is dereferenced, causing use-after-free.

commit_msg: Bug 698044: restrict font name length to the buffer size.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['xps_load_sfnt_name(xps_font_t *font, char *namep)'], 'added_lines': ['xps_load_sfnt_name(xps_font_t *font, char *namep, const int buflen)', '        length = length > buflen - 1 ? buflen - 1: length;', '']}
description: The xps_load_sfnt_name function in xps/xpsfont.c in Artifex Ghostscript GhostXPS 9.21 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (buffer overflow and application crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted document.

code_evidence: The record's length and offset fields are read directly from the untrusted font data (lines 43-44) and used to copy into namep without any check against the destination buffer capacity (lines 51-52).

For the UTF-16 path, n = length/2 is derived from the attacker-controlled length and the loop writes namep[k] for k < n plus the terminator at namep[k], again unbounded by the actual destination size (lines 60-67).
Similarly the UTF-32 path computes n = length/4 and writes up to n bytes plus a terminator into namep without a capacity constraint (lines 75-82).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs memory writes (memcpy and indexed stores) outside the intended bounds of the destination buffer because the length is unrestricted, which is exactly an improper restriction of operations within a buffer boundary (CWE-119). The patch's added clamp to buflen-1 confirms the missing bound; a more specific descendant such as out-of-bounds write would also fit, but the target class is supported.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function writes attacker-controlled lengths from the font's name table into the caller-supplied namep buffer without validating length against the buffer size. Trigger: a crafted document whose name record has a large length (or whose stringoffset/offset points to attacker data) causes memcpy or the UTF-16/UTF-32 loops to write past namep. Supported consequence: out-of-bounds write leading to memory corruption and application crash (DoS), with possible unspecified impact.

commit_msg:
ipv6: check sk sk_type and protocol early in ip_mroute_set/getsockopt

Commit 5e1859fbcc3c ("ipv4: ipmr: various fixes and cleanups") fixed
the issue for ipv4 ipmr:

  ip_mroute_setsockopt() & ip_mroute_getsockopt() should not
  access/set raw_sk(sk)->ipmr_table before making sure the socket
  is a raw socket, and protocol is IGMP

The same fix should be done for ipv6 ipmr as well.

This patch can fix the panic caused by overwriting the same offset
as ipmr_table as in raw_sk(sk) when accessing other type's socket
by ip_mroute_setsockopt().

Signed-off-by: Xin Long <lucien.xin@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tif (sk->sk_type != SOCK_RAW ||', '\t\t    inet_sk(sk)->inet_num != IPPROTO_ICMPV6)', '\t\t\treturn -EOPNOTSUPP;'], 'added_lines': ['', '\tif (sk->sk_type != SOCK_RAW ||', '\t    inet_sk(sk)->inet_num != IPPROTO_ICMPV6)', '\t\treturn -EOPNOTSUPP;']}
description: An issue was discovered in net/ipv6/ip6mr.c in the Linux kernel before 4.11. By setting a specific socket option, an attacker can control a pointer in kernel land and cause an inet_csk_listen_stop general protection fault, or potentially execute arbitrary code under certain circumstances. The issue can be triggered as root (e.g., inside a default LXC container or with the CAP_NET_ADMIN capability) or after namespace unsharing. This occurs because sk_type and protocol are not checked in the appropriate part of the ip6_mroute_* functions. NOTE: this affects Linux distributions that use 4.9.x longterm kernels before 4.9.187.

code_evidence: Line 9 dereferences raw6_sk(sk)->ip6mr_table and passes it to ip6mr_get_table before any check on the socket type or protocol, so a non-raw/non-ICMPv6 socket's private data is reinterpreted as raw6_sk.

The sk_type/inet_num check at lines 18-20 is only reached inside case MRT6_INIT, leaving all other optnames (MRT6_DONE, MRT6_ADD_MIF, MRT6_TABLE, etc.) to operate on mrt and raw6_sk(sk) without validating the socket.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function accepts socket input without validating the required type/protocol properties before use, matching CWE-20 improper input validation; the missing check, not a transformation flaw, is the defect.

evidence_lines.code: mrt = ip6mr_get_table(net, raw6_sk(sk)->ip6mr_table ? : RT6_TABLE_DFLT);

case MRT6_INIT:
if (sk->sk_type != SOCK_RAW ||
inet_sk(sk)->inet_num != IPPROTO_ICMPV6)
return -EOPNOTSUPP;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: socket type and protocol are validated only for MRT6_INIT, after line 9 has already treated the socket as raw and fetched a table via raw6_sk(sk)->ip6mr_table. Trigger: an attacker invokes ip6_mroute_setsockopt on a non-raw or non-ICMPv6 socket with any optname. Consequence: out-of-type private-data access/overwrite (e.g. ip6mr_table at the wrong offset) leading to a kernel fault or potential memory corruption.

commit_msg:
Color Laserjet device - properly check params

Bug #701796 "Segmentation fault at devices/gdevclj.c:269 in clj_media_size"

The test in clj_media_size() as incorrect, it didn't signal an error if
there was no HWResolution in the param list. This left the parameter
'fres' undefined leading to a potential invalid memory read, or a
divide-by-zero error.

This commit returns an error if we get a param list with no HWResolution
I'm not absolutely certain if this is correct, but at least signalling
an error is better than a seg fault.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if ( (param_read_float_array(plist, "HWResolution", &fres) == 0) &&'], 'added_lines': ['    if ( param_read_float_array(plist, "HWResolution", &fres) != 0 ||']}
description: A null pointer dereference vulnerability in clj_media_size() in devices/gdevclj.c of Artifex Software GhostScript v9.50 allows a remote attacker to cause a denial of service via a crafted PDF file. This is fixed in v9.51.

code_evidence: Lines 8-10 return early only when param_read_float_array succeeds (== 0) AND the resolution is unsupported; if HWResolution is absent the read fails and no error is raised, leaving fres uninitialized.
Lines 17-19 then read fres.data[0] and fres.data[1] to scale HWSize whenever HWSize is present, regardless of whether HWResolution was ever populated.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences fres.data that may never have been initialized to a valid pointer because the missing-HWResolution case is not rejected. This is a pointer dereference of an invalid (effectively NULL) pointer, matching CWE-476 rather than a mere arithmetic divide-by-zero, which is only a secondary symptom.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The guard uses the wrong condition, so a param list lacking HWResolution passes without error while fres remains uninitialized. A later HWSize entry triggers dereference of fres.data (an invalid/NULL pointer), causing a crash or invalid memory read. The root cause is the inverted/miscombined check; the consequence is denial of service via crafted PDF parameters.

commit_msg:
IAX2: Add a timestamp check.

Don't try to process timestamps that are more than 60 seconds apart.
Avoids the infinite loop in bug 13432.

description: In Wireshark 2.2.0 to 2.2.4 and 2.0.0 to 2.0.10, there is an IAX2 infinite loop, triggered by packet injection or a malformed capture file. This was addressed in epan/dissectors/packet-iax2.c by constraining packet lateness.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function under analysis is proto_register_iax2, a registration routine that only populates field/expert arrays and registers dissectors; it contains no loop or timestamp processing, so it cannot demonstrate the CWE-835 infinite loop fixed in the dissector code.

commit_msg:
netfilter: x_tables: fix unconditional helper

Ben Hawkes says:

 In the mark_source_chains function (net/ipv4/netfilter/ip_tables.c) it
 is possible for a user-supplied ipt_entry structure to have a large
 next_offset field. This field is not bounds checked prior to writing a
 counter value at the supplied offset.

Problem is that mark_source_chains should not have been called --
the rule doesn't have a next entry, so its supposed to return
an absolute verdict of either ACCEPT or DROP.

However, the function conditional() doesn't work as the name implies.
It only checks that the rule is using wildcard address matching.

However, an unconditional rule must also not be using any matches
(no -m args).

The underflow validator only checked the addresses, therefore
passing the 'unconditional absolute verdict' test, while
mark_source_chains also tested for presence of matches, and thus
proceeeded to the next (not-existent) rule.

Unify this so that all the callers have same idea of 'unconditional rule'.

Reported-by: Ben Hawkes <hawkes@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Florian Westphal <fw@strlen.de>
Signed-off-by: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>

description: The netfilter subsystem in the Linux kernel through 4.5.2 does not validate certain offset fields, which allows local users to gain privileges or cause a denial of service (heap memory corruption) via an IPT_SO_SET_REPLACE setsockopt call.

code_evidence: The 'unconditional return/END' test at [22,26] accepts a rule as terminal when target_offset equals sizeof(struct ip6t_entry), the target is XT_STANDARD_TARGET, verdict is negative, and unconditional() holds on addresses. It does not require the absence of matches, so a rule with matches passes as terminal.
The loop exit at [54,59] computes size = e->next_offset and advances to entry0 + pos + size, writing e->counters.pcnt at [58], without bounds-checking next_offset against newinfo->size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The counter write at [58] targets memory derived from an unchecked next_offset, an out-of-bounds write within the table buffer, matching CWE-119. The missing next_offset bound check is the direct cause; the flawed unconditional() predicate merely enables reaching that path.

if ((e->target_offset == sizeof(struct ip6t_entry) &&
(strcmp(t->target.u.user.name,
XT_STANDARD_TARGET) == 0) &&
t->verdict < 0 &&
unconditional(&e->ipv6)) || visited) {

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the terminal-rule predicate omits the no-matches condition, so a user-supplied entry with matches is treated as an unconditional absolute verdict and the chain walk proceeds to a non-existent next rule. Trigger: an IPT_SO_SET_REPLACE setsockopt with a large next_offset. Consequence: the computed pointer at [56,57] and counter write at [58] fall outside the table buffer, corrupting heap memory or crashing.

commit_msg:
On unpacking key blob output buffer size should be fixed

Related: CVE-2022-29242
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '    if (key == NULL) {', '        *key_len = 32;', '        return 1;', '    }', '', '    if (key != NULL && *key_len < 32) {', '        GOSTerr(GOST_F_PKEY_GOST2018_ENCRYPT, GOST_R_INVALID_BUFFER_SIZE);', '        return 0;', '    }', '']}
description: GOST engine is a reference implementation of the Russian GOST crypto algorithms for OpenSSL. TLS clients using GOST engine when ciphersuite `TLS_GOSTR341112_256_WITH_KUZNYECHIK_CTR_OMAC` is agreed and the server uses 512 bit GOST secret keys are vulnerable to buffer overflow. GOST engine version 3.0.1 contains a patch for this issue. Disabling ciphersuite `TLS_GOSTR341112_256_WITH_KUZNYECHIK_CTR_OMAC` is a possible workaround.

code_evidence: Line 4 obtains gctx but performs no key_len validation before dispatch; lines 10-12 forward the caller-supplied key buffer and key_len directly to pkey_gost2018_decrypt for kuznyechik_ctr and magma_ctr. The fix adds a key==NULL query path and a *key_len < 32 check, confirming the decrypt path writes 32 bytes into caller memory without a prior bound check.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-120 fits because the decrypt routine copies/writes fixed-size key material into a destination buffer without verifying the output buffer size first; the missing *key_len < 32 constraint is exactly the unchecked size-of-input condition. This is a write overflow, not an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125).
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the dispatcher passes an unvalidated output buffer and size to the GOST 2018 decrypt routine, which writes a fixed 32-byte key. Trigger: a TLS client with the GOST ciphersuite and 512-bit server keys supplies a key_len smaller than 32. Consequence: out-of-bounds write past the caller's buffer, corrupting memory and potentially enabling crash or code execution.

description: Race condition in the audit_log_single_execve_arg function in kernel/auditsc.c in the Linux kernel through 4.7 allows local users to bypass intended character-set restrictions or disrupt system-call auditing by changing a certain string, aka a "double fetch" vulnerability.

code_evidence: sched_feat_write obtains the inode lock (line 16) and then calls sched_feat_set (line 17) while holding it; sched_feat_set enables/disables static keys which acquire cpu_hotplug_lock.rw_sem, and the reverse order is taken elsewhere (cpufreq_init holds cpu_hotplug_lock then takes the inode mutex), forming a lock-order inversion.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function sequences two shared locks in an order that conflicts with a concurrent code sequence, exactly the improper synchronization over a shared resource described by CWE-362; it is not a simple data race on a value but a lock-order race leading to deadlock.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the write path takes the debugfs inode mutex before the cpu_hotplug_lock.rw_sem acquired inside sched_feat_set, while another code path takes them in the opposite order. Trigger: a local user writes to /sys/kernel/debug/sched_features concurrently with cpufreq module loading, yielding a circular locking dependency and potential deadlock (availability impact).

commit_msg:
lldp: fix a buffer overflow when handling management address TLV

When a remote device was advertising a too large management address
while still respecting TLV boundaries, lldpd would crash due to a buffer
overflow. However, the buffer being a static one, this buffer overflow
is not exploitable if hardening was not disabled. This bug exists since
version 0.5.6.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t', '\t\t\tCHECK_TLV_SIZE(4, "Organisational");'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\tif (addr_str_length > sizeof(addr_str_buffer)) {', '\t\t\t\tlog_warnx("lldp", "too large management address on %s",', '\t\t\t\t    hardware->h_ifname);', '\t\t\t\tgoto malformed;', '\t\t\t}', '', '\t\t\tCHECK_TLV_SIZE(1 + (int)sizeof(orgid), "Organisational");']}
description: Buffer overflow in the lldp_decode function in daemon/protocols/lldp.c in lldpd before 0.8.0 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (daemon crash) and possibly execute arbitrary code via vectors involving large management addresses and TLV boundaries.

code_evidence: addr_str_buffer is a fixed 32-byte stack array (line 26). The management-address TLV supplies addr_str_length as an attacker-controlled u_int8_t (line 155). The only bound check, CHECK_TLV_SIZE(1 + addr_str_length, ...) at line 156, validates the size against the remaining TLV frame, not against sizeof(addr_str_buffer).

PEEK_BYTES(addr_str_buffer, addr_str_length) at line 157 then copies addr_str_length bytes into the 32-byte buffer, and line 158 computes addr_length = addr_str_length - 1 and line 159 reads addr_str_buffer[0].
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This is a classic buffer copy without an input-size check: PEEK_BYTES copies an unbounded TLV-derived length into a fixed-size array, matching CWE-120. It is not merely an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125), since the overflow is a write past the destination buffer's end.

evidence_lines.code: mgmt = lldpd_alloc_mgmt(af, addr_ptr, addr_length, iface);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the copy length is taken from the TLV and validated only against TLV/frame length, with no comparison to the destination buffer size. Trigger: a remote LLDP frame advertising a management-address string length greater than 32 while staying within TLV boundaries. Consequence: a stack buffer overflow writing past addr_str_buffer, corrupting adjacent locals and crashing the daemon (potential code execution when hardening is disabled); the added length check prevents it.

commit_msg: [mod_sofia] Fixed a few Usage-of-uninitialized value bugs which may cause information discolsure and bypass ACL check
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tchar network_ip[80];'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tchar network_ip[80] = "";']}
description: An issue was discovered in function sofia_handle_sip_i_notify in sofia.c in SignalWire freeswitch before 1.10.6, may allow attackers to view sensitive information due to an uninitialized value.

code_evidence: network_ip is declared at line 20 without an initializer, so its contents are indeterminate. Line 26 passes it to sofia_glue_get_addr, which may leave it untouched or partially filled on failure. Line 28 then formats network_ip into via_space with switch_snprintf, and line 29 stores that string as the sip_full_via channel variable.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-909 fits because a critical resource, the network_ip buffer, is used without initialization, and the uninitialized value flows into a formatted string that is stored and later read. The consequence is improper exposure of uninitialized memory, not an out-of-bounds write or buffer overflow.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the stack buffer network_ip is uninitialized before being handed to sofia_glue_get_addr, whose output is not verified. Trigger: a re-INVITE whose address extraction fails or partially succeeds, leaving stale stack bytes. Consequence: those bytes are formatted into sip_full_via and exposed to other SIP processing, supporting disclosure of residual memory contents rather than a direct ACL bypass in this function.

references span multiple types of elements.

commit_msg:
[POWERPC] Never panic when taking altivec exceptions from userspace

At the moment we rely on a cpu feature bit or a firmware property to
detect altivec. If we dont have either of these and the cpu does in fact
support altivec we can cause a panic from userspace.

It seems safer to always send a signal if we manage to get an 0xf20
exception from userspace.

Signed-off-by: Anton Blanchard <anton@samba.org>
Signed-off-by: Paul Mackerras <paulus@samba.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['#if !defined(CONFIG_ALTIVEC)', '#endif'], 'added_lines': ['']}
description: The altivec_unavailable_exception function in arch/powerpc/kernel/traps.c in the Linux kernel before 2.6.19 on 64-bit systems mishandles the case where CONFIG_ALTIVEC is defined and the CPU actually supports Altivec, but the Altivec support was not detected by the kernel, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (panic) by triggering execution of an Altivec instruction.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: Target CWE-19 is a prohibited category, not a weakness; the function instead concerns an unreachable userspace signal path causing a kernel panic (denial of service), not a data processing error.

commit_msg:
SOFT: Check the EC Key on C_CreateObject and C_DeriveKey

When constructing an OpenSSL EC public or private key from PKCS#11
attributes or ECDH public data, check that the key is valid, i.e. that
the point is on the curve.

This prevents one from creating an EC key object via C_CreateObject with
invalid key data. It also prevents C_DeriveKey to derive a secret using
ECDH with an EC public key (public data) that uses a different curve
or is invalid by other means.

Signed-off-by: Ingo Franzki <ifranzki@linux.ibm.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    if (!EC_KEY_check_key(ec_key)) {', '        TRACE_ERROR("EC_KEY_check_key failed\\n");', '        rc = CKR_PUBLIC_KEY_INVALID;', '        goto out;', '    }', '']}
description: A flaw was found in openCryptoki. The openCryptoki Soft token does not check if an EC key is valid when an EC key is created via C_CreateObject, nor when C_DeriveKey is used with ECDH public data. This may allow a malicious user to extract the private key by performing an invalid curve attack.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function only parses public EC point data and validates it; it does not itself expose sensitive information, and the diff's missing EC_KEY_check_key is a curve-validation gap whose consequence is private-key extraction, not an information-exposure root cause in this function.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  ECMA_CHECK_STACK_USAGE ();', '']}
description: Jerryscript 3.0.0 was discovered to contain a stack overflow via ecma_lcache_lookup in /jerry-core/ecma/base/ecma-lcache.c.

When fixed files are unregistered, file_alloc_end and alloc_hint
are not cleared. This can later cause a NULL pointer dereference in
io_file_bitmap_get() if auto index selection is enabled via
IORING_FILE_INDEX_ALLOC:

[    6.519129] BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000000
[...]
[    6.541468] RIP: 0010:_find_next_zero_bit+0x1a/0x70
[...]
[    6.560906] Call Trace:
[    6.561322]  <TASK>
[    6.561672]  io_file_bitmap_get+0x38/0x60
[    6.562281]  io_fixed_fd_install+0x63/0xb0
[    6.562851]  ? __pfx_io_socket+0x10/0x10
[    6.563396]  io_socket+0x93/0xf0
[    6.563855]  ? __pfx_io_socket+0x10/0x10
[    6.564411]  io_issue_sqe+0x5b/0x3d0
[    6.564914]  io_submit_sqes+0x1de/0x650
[    6.565452]  __do_sys_io_uring_enter+0x4fc/0xb20
[    6.566083]  ? __do_sys_io_uring_register+0x11e/0xd80
[    6.566779]  do_syscall_64+0x3c/0x90
[    6.567247]  entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x72/0xdc
[...]

To fix the issue, set file alloc range and alloc_hint to zero after
file tables are freed.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: 4278a0deb1f6 ("io_uring: defer alloc_hint update to io_file_bitmap_set()")
Signed-off-by: Savino Dicanosa <sd7.dev@pm.me>
[axboe: add explicit bitmap == NULL check as well]
Signed-off-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\tif (!table->bitmap)', '\t\treturn -ENFILE;']}
description: A NULL pointer dereference was found in io_file_bitmap_get in io_uring/filetable.c in the io_uring sub-component in the Linux Kernel. When fixed files are unregistered, some context information (file_alloc_{start,end} and alloc_hint) is not cleared. A subsequent request that has auto index selection enabled via IORING_FILE_INDEX_ALLOC can cause a NULL pointer dereference. An unprivileged user can use the flaw to cause a system crash.

code_evidence: Line 4 reads the stale ctx->file_alloc_end into nr, and line 7 passes table->bitmap to find_next_zero_bit without checking it for NULL.
Lines 10-13 compare and reset alloc_hint against ctx->file_alloc_start, so the loop's termination depends on stale range/hint state rather than on bitmap validity.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function passes a pointer it assumes is valid (table->bitmap) into a bit-scanning helper without a NULL check, directly matching CWE-476. This is not merely an out-of-bounds read; the defect is dereference of a NULL pointer, so the target CWE fits exactly.

evidence_lines.code:
unsigned long nr = ctx->file_alloc_end;
ret = find_next_zero_bit(table->bitmap, nr, table->alloc_hint);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: after fixed files are unregistered, file_alloc_end and alloc_hint retain stale values while table->bitmap is freed and becomes NULL. A later auto-index install via IORING_FILE_INDEX_ALLOC reaches io_file_bitmap_get, which dereferences the NULL bitmap in find_next_zero_bit. Supported consequence is a kernel crash (availability impact).

commit_msg:
Don't change the state of the ETM flags until CCS processing

Changing the ciphersuite during a renegotiation can result in a crash
leading to a DoS attack. ETM has not been implemented in 1.1.0 for DTLS
so this is TLS only.

The problem is caused by changing the flag indicating whether to use ETM
or not immediately on negotiation of ETM, rather than at CCS. Therefore,
during a renegotiation, if the ETM state is changing (usually due to a
change of ciphersuite), then an error/crash will occur.

Due to the fact that there are separate CCS messages for read and write
we actually now need two flags to determine whether to use ETM or not.

CVE-2017-3733

Reviewed-by: Richard Levitte <levitte@openssl.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        if (!SSL_USE_ETM(s) && mac_size != 0) {', '        if (SSL_USE_ETM(s) && mac_size != 0) {'], 'added_lines': ['        if (!SSL_WRITE_ETM(s) && mac_size != 0) {', '        if (SSL_WRITE_ETM(s) && mac_size != 0) {']}
description: During a renegotiation handshake if the Encrypt-Then-Mac extension is negotiated where it was not in the original handshake (or vice-versa) then this can cause OpenSSL 1.1.0 before 1.1.0e to crash (dependent on ciphersuite). Both clients and servers are affected.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function's change only switches the ETM check from a single SSL_USE_ETM flag to direction-specific SSL_WRITE_ETM flags during record writing; it contains no input parsing or validation of received data, so it does not support CWE-20.

commit_msg:
PKTC must be stricter with its Kerberos application choices.

The PKTC dissector calls the Kerberos dissector assuming certain application values.  Because different application values can have different "private" data, corruption can occur.
Ensure the Kerberos application values match the preceding comments by checking the ber identifier before calling the Kerberos dissector.

description: In radare2 before 3.9.0, a command injection vulnerability exists in bin_symbols() in libr/core/cbin.c. By using a crafted executable file, it's possible to execute arbitrary shell commands with the permissions of the victim. This vulnerability is due to an insufficient fix for CVE-2019-14745 and improper handling of symbol names embedded in executables.

code_evidence: The loop iterates over every byte of attacker-influenced arg and copies it to the output buffer in the default branch.
Only space, '=', '\r' and '\n' are dropped; double-quote and backslash fall through to default and are copied verbatim into the returned string.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-78 fits because the function is the neutralization step for untrusted data placed into an OS command, and it incompletely removes shell-significant elements. This is command injection rather than simple output encoding: the surviving metacharacters modify the downstream shell command.

evidence_lines.code:
*b = 0;
return a;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the shell-quoting filter whitelists too few shell metacharacters, so embedded '"' and '\\' survive sanitization. Trigger: a crafted executable whose symbol name contains these characters reaches the command built from the filtered string. Consequence: the injected characters can break out of quoting and alter the intended OS command, enabling command execution.

description: In the KeepKey firmware before 7.3.2,Flaws in the supervisor interface can be exploited to bypass important security restrictions on firmware operations. Using these flaws, malicious firmware code can elevate privileges, permanently make the device inoperable or overwrite the trusted bootloader code to compromise the hardware wallet across reboots or storage wipes.

commit_msg:
ServiceManager: Allow system services running as secondary users to add services

This should be reverted when all system services have been cleaned up to not
do this. A process looking up a service while running in the background will
see the service registered by the active user (assuming the service is
registered on every user switch), not the service registered by the user that
the process itself belongs to.

BUG: 30795333
Change-Id: I1b74d58be38ed358f43c163692f9e704f8f31dbe
(cherry picked from commit e6bbe69ba739c8a08837134437aaccfea5f1d943)

description: cmds/servicemanager/service_manager.c in ServiceManager in Android 5.0.x before 5.0.2, 5.1.x before 5.1.1, 6.x before 2016-10-01, and 7.0 before 2016-10-01 does not properly restrict service registration, which allows attackers to gain privileges via a crafted application, aka internal bug 29431260.

Consequence: the app-id check is bypassed and the service registration restriction fails, letting the app register services it should not, supporting privilege gain.

commit_msg: Suspend exception processing if there are too many exceptions
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  if (CheckMemoryOverflow(count,quantum) != MagickFalse)'], 'added_lines': ['  if (HeapOverflowSanityCheck(count,quantum) != MagickFalse)']}
description: magick/memory.c in ImageMagick before 6.9.4-5 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (application crash) via vectors involving "too many exceptions," which trigger a buffer overflow.

code_evidence: Line 11 gates the allocation on CheckMemoryOverflow(count,quantum); if it reports no overflow, line 15 computes size=count*quantum and line 16 rounds it up, then lines 17-18 reject only size==0, bad alignment, or extent<size. The guard depends entirely on the overflow predicate correctly catching product wraparound.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function's central defect is an unchecked size computation that can produce a buffer smaller than the intended extent, matching CWE-119's improper restriction of operations within a memory buffer's bounds. The fix renames the guard to HeapOverflowSanityCheck, indicating the prior predicate failed to enforce the overflow constraint; CWE-190 would describe the arithmetic cause, but the supported consequence here is out-of-bounds memory access.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the multiplication count*quantum can wrap before any bounds check, and the subsequent extent<size test cannot detect that the wrapped size is smaller than the true product. Trigger: attacker-controlled count/quantum large enough to overflow size_t. Consequence: an undersized buffer is allocated while callers may use the nominal count*quantum extent, leading to out-of-bounds memory operations and a crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
ipv6: avoid overflow of offset in ip6_find_1stfragopt

In some cases, offset can overflow and can cause an infinite loop in
ip6_find_1stfragopt(). Make it unsigned int to prevent the overflow, and
cap it at IPV6_MAXPLEN, since packets larger than that should be invalid.

This problem has been here since before the beginning of git history.

Signed-off-by: Sabrina Dubroca <sd@queasysnail.net>
Acked-by: Hannes Frederic Sowa <hannes@stressinduktion.org>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tu16 offset = sizeof(struct ipv6hdr);', '\t\toffset += ipv6_optlen(exthdr);'], 'added_lines': ['\tunsigned int offset = sizeof(struct ipv6hdr);', '\t\tunsigned int len;', '\t\tlen = ipv6_optlen(exthdr);', '\t\tif (len + offset >= IPV6_MAXPLEN)', '\t\t\treturn -EINVAL;', '\t\toffset += len;']}
description: The ip6_find_1stfragopt function in net/ipv6/output_core.c in the Linux kernel through 4.12.3 allows local users to cause a denial of service (integer overflow and infinite loop) by leveraging the ability to open a raw socket.

code_evidence: offset is declared as a 16-bit u16 initialized to sizeof(struct ipv6hdr), so it can hold at most 65535.
The loop condition compares this narrow offset against the unsigned int packet_len, allowing iteration while offset fits.
The guard checks offset + sizeof(struct ipv6_opt_hdr) > packet_len but does not constrain the accumulated offset before the addition.
exthdr is derived from skb_network_header(skb) + offset, then offset += ipv6_optlen(exthdr) accumulates the attacker-influenced extension-header length into the u16.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This is CWE-190: an integer increment is stored in a representation too small for the result, and the code assumes offset grows monotonically. The wrap is the root cause; the infinite loop is the resulting DoS consequence. The missing cap at IPV6_MAXPLEN confirms the arithmetic constraint was absent rather than a memory-safety flaw like out-of-bounds read.

evidence_lines.code: u16 offset = sizeof(struct ipv6hdr);
while (offset <= packet_len) {

if (offset + sizeof(struct ipv6_opt_hdr) > packet_len)
return -EINVAL;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the running offset is stored in a u16, so repeated addition of ipv6_optlen(exthdr) values from a raw-socket-supplied packet can wrap the counter to a small value. Trigger: a crafted IPv6 extension-header chain whose accumulated length exceeds 65535. Consequence: offset becomes small again, the loop re-processes headers and can spin indefinitely, causing a denial of service (CPU consumption/hang).

commit_msg:
[security] Fix int overflow in RaggedRangeOp.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 461749624
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      rt_nested_splits(row + 1) =', '          rt_nested_splits(row) + RangeSize(start, limit, delta);'], 'added_lines': ['      int64_t size;  // The number of elements in the specified range.', '      if (((delta > 0) && (limit < start)) ||', '          ((delta < 0) && (limit > start))) {', '        size = 0;', '      } else if (std::is_integral<T>::value) {', '        // The following is copied from tensorflow::RangeOp::Compute().', '        size = Eigen::divup(Eigen::numext::abs(limit - start),', '                            Eigen::numext::abs(delta));', '      } else {', '        // The following is copied from tensorflow::RangeOp::Compute().', '        auto size_auto =', '            Eigen::numext::ceil(Eigen::numext::abs((limit - start) / delta));', '        OP_REQUIRES(', '            context, size_auto <= std::numeric_limits<int64_t>::max(),', '            errors::InvalidArgument("Requires ((limit - start) / delta) <= ",', '                                    std::numeric_limits<int64_t>::max()));', '        size = static_cast<int64_t>(size_auto);', '      }', '      rt_nested_splits(row + 1) = rt_nested_splits(row) + size;']}
description: TensorFlow is an open source platform for machine learning. The `RaggedRangOp` function takes an argument `limits` that is eventually used to construct a `TensorShape` as an `int64`. If `limits` is a very large float, it can overflow when converted to an `int64`. This triggers an `InvalidArgument` but also throws an abort signal that crashes the program. We have patched the issue in GitHub commit 37cefa91bee4eace55715eeef43720b958a01192. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.10.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.9.1, TensorFlow 2.8.1, and TensorFlow 2.7.2, as these are also affected and still in supported range. There are no known workarounds for this issue.

code_evidence: rt_nested_splits(row + 1) is computed as the previous split plus RangeSize(start, limit, delta); for a very large float limit, RangeSize converts/rounds the float range size into SPLITS_TYPE (int64), so the addition and the size conversion can overflow or produce a value that later feeds TensorShape({nvals}) at line 43.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the calculation of the split offset and range size can exceed int64 and wrap, violating the assumption that the split count grows safely; the crash/abort is a consequence of the unchecked integer overflow, not a separate weakness.

evidence_lines.code:
rt_nested_splits(row + 1) =
rt_nested_splits(row) + RangeSize(start, limit, delta);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the range size for each row is added to the running split offset without bounding the float-to-int64 conversion or the cumulative sum. Trigger: caller supplies a very large float limit (or delta/start combination) making RangeSize exceed int64 range. Consequence: integer overflow/wraparound produces an invalid or negative split value, causing InvalidArgument, an abort, or a crash when the value is used as a TensorShape dimension.

commit_msg:
x86/spec-ctrl: Add spec-ctrl=unpriv-mmio

Per Xen's support statement, PCI passthrough should be to trusted domains
because the overall system security depends on factors outside of Xen's
control.

As such, Xen, in a supported configuration, is not vulnerable to DRPW/SBDR.

However, users who have risk assessed their configuration may be happy with
the risk of DoS, but unhappy with the risk of cross-domain data leakage.  Such
users should enable this option.

On CPUs vulnerable to MDS, the existing mitigations are the best we can do to
mitigate MMIO cross-domain data leakage.

On CPUs fixed to MDS but vulnerable MMIO stale data leakage, this option:

 * On CPUs susceptible to FBSDP, mitigates cross-domain fill buffer leakage
   using FB_CLEAR.
 * On CPUs susceptible to SBDR, mitigates RNG data recovery by engaging the
   srb-lock, previously used to mitigate SRBDS.

Both mitigations require microcode from IPU 2022.1, May 2022.

This is part of XSA-404.

Signed-off-by: Andrew Cooper <andrew.cooper3@citrix.com>
Reviewed-by: Roger Pau Monné <roger.pau@citrix.com>

commit_msg:
mm/rmap: Fix anon_vma->degree ambiguity leading to double-reuse

anon_vma->degree tracks the combined number of child anon_vmas and VMAs
that use the anon_vma as their ->anon_vma.

anon_vma_clone() then assumes that for any anon_vma attached to
src->anon_vma_chain other than src->anon_vma, it is impossible for it to
be a leaf node of the VMA tree, meaning that for such VMAs ->degree is
elevated by 1 because of a child anon_vma, meaning that if ->degree
equals 1 there are no VMAs that use the anon_vma as their ->anon_vma.

This assumption is wrong because the ->degree optimization leads to leaf
nodes being abandoned on anon_vma_clone() - an existing anon_vma is
reused and no new parent-child relationship is created.  So it is
possible to reuse an anon_vma for one VMA while it is still tied to
another VMA.

This is an issue because is_mergeable_anon_vma() and its callers assume
that if two VMAs have the same ->anon_vma, the list of anon_vmas
attached to the VMAs is guaranteed to be the same.  When this assumption
is violated, vma_merge() can merge pages into a VMA that is not attached
to the corresponding anon_vma, leading to dangling page->mapping
pointers that will be dereferenced during rmap walks.

Fix it by separately tracking the number of child anon_vmas and the
number of VMAs using the anon_vma as their ->anon_vma.

Fixes: 7a3ef208e662 ("mm: prevent endless growth of anon_vma hierarchy")
Cc: stable@kernel.org
Acked-by: Michal Hocko <mhocko@suse.com>
Acked-by: Vlastimil Babka <vbabka@suse.cz>
Signed-off-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>

description: The grub_ext2_read_block function in fs/ext2.c in GNU GRUB before 2013-11-12, as used in shlr/grub/fs/ext2.c in radare2 1.5.0, allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (excessive stack use and application crash) via a crafted binary file, related to use of a variable-size stack array.

code_evidence: In the indirect block branch, `indir[blksz / 4]` is a variable-length stack array sized from the disk-derived block size; `grub_disk_read` fills the entire `blksz` into it, then indexes `indir[fileblock - INDIRECT_BLOCKS]` without bounding that index against `blksz / 4`.

The double- and triple-indirect branches repeat the same `grub_uint32_t indir[blksz / 4]` stack array and index it with attacker-derived `rblock` shifts/masks (`indir[rblock >> log_perblock]`, `indir[(rblock >> log_perblock) >> log_perblock]`) without validating indices against the array length.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads memory outside the intended `indir` buffer boundary, matching CWE-119's improper restriction of operations within a memory buffer. The variable-size stack array and unchecked indices directly produce out-of-bounds access rather than a mere integer issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: a variable-size stack array sized by `blksz` is populated from disk and indexed by fileblock-derived offsets that are not checked against the array bounds. A crafted ext2 image with an inconsistent block size/fileblock causes out-of-bounds reads of `indir`, and the oversized stack allocation can exhaust the stack, crashing the application.

commit_msg:
dvb_register_device() dynamically allocates fops with kmemdup()
to set the fops->owner.
And these fops are registered in 'file->f_ops' using replace_fops()
in the dvb_device_open() process, and kfree()d in dvb_free_device().

However, it is not common to use dynamically allocated fops instead
of 'static const' fops as an argument of replace_fops(),
and UAF may occur.
These UAFs can occur on any dvb type using dvb_register_device(),
such as dvb_dvr, dvb_demux, dvb_frontend, dvb_net, etc.

So, instead of kfree() the fops dynamically allocated in
dvb_register_device() in dvb_free_device() called during the
.disconnect() process, kfree() it collectively in exit_dvbdev()
called when the dvbdev.c module is removed.

Reported-by: kernel test robot <lkp@intel.com>
Reported-by: Dan Carpenter <error27@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Mauro Carvalho Chehab <mchehab@kernel.org>

description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel through 6.0.9. drivers/media/dvb-core/dvbdev.c has a use-after-free, related to dvb_register_device dynamically allocating fops.

code_evidence: The function serializes registration with mutex_lock(&dvbdev_register_lock) at line 10, allocates dvbdev at line 17, and duplicates template->fops into dvbdevfops at line 22. The duplicated fops are attached to dvbdev->fops (line 34), its owner is set (line 36), and dvbdev is published on adap->device_list (line 37) while the lock is still held.
The error path at lines 43-48 frees dvbdevfops and dvbdev after list_del.
The media-registration failure path at lines 57-65 also frees dvbdevfops and dvbdev after dvb_media_device_free and list_del, without any additional lifetime coordination for the published fops.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-362 fits because the shared resource (dvbdev->fops) is published and then freed in concurrent registration/error paths without proper synchronization against a concurrent open sequence, violating exclusivity/atomicity. The use-after-free is the consequence of this race, not a separate target weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The duplicated fops are installed into the device and published under the registration lock, but the error paths free them immediately after removing the device from the list. A concurrent open path using replace_fops() can obtain a reference to dvbdev->fops while registration or teardown frees that memory, so the fops pointer is used after release. The root cause is the lack of exclusive lifetime synchronization between registration/error cleanup and concurrent device-open users of the shared fops; the supported consequence is use-after-free of the file_operations object.

commit_msg:
apparmor: fix oops, validate buffer size in apparmor_setprocattr()

When proc_pid_attr_write() was changed to use memdup_user apparmor's
(interface violating) assumption that the setprocattr buffer was always
a single page was violated.

The size test is not strictly speaking needed as proc_pid_attr_write()
will reject anything larger, but for the sake of robustness we can keep
it in.

SMACK and SELinux look safe to me, but somebody else should probably
have a look just in case.

Based on original patch from Vegard Nossum <vegard.nossum@oracle.com>
modified for the case that apparmor provides null termination.

description: The apparmor_setprocattr function in security/apparmor/lsm.c in the Linux kernel before 4.6.5 does not validate the buffer size, which allows local users to gain privileges by triggering an AppArmor setprocattr hook.

code_evidence: When the caller-supplied buffer is not NUL-terminated, the code writes a terminator at args[size]; this assumes the buffer has room for size+1 bytes and that size < PAGE_SIZE, otherwise it writes past the buffer end.

After trimming and splitting the command, arg_size is computed from size and the pointer into value, so a non-NUL-terminated buffer or an off-by-one terminator can lead to parsing beyond the intended range.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs a write at args[size] outside the supplied buffer's intended bounds, and subsequent parsing can read past the buffer, matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds memory operation. The missing size constraint is the cause; the out-of-bounds access is the supported consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function assumes value points to a PAGE_SIZE buffer and writes args[size]='\0' without ensuring size+1 bytes are available. Trigger: a local user calls setprocattr with a non-NUL-terminated buffer whose size equals the allocation boundary. Consequence: out-of-bounds write/read of memory, enabling corruption or privilege escalation.

commit_msg:
PR22307, Heap out of bounds read in _bfd_elf_parse_gnu_properties

When adding an unbounded increment to a pointer, you can't just check
against the end of the buffer but also must check that overflow
doesn't result in "negative" pointer movement.  Pointer comparisons
are signed.  Better, check the increment against the space left using
an unsigned comparison.

	PR 22307
	* elf-properties.c (_bfd_elf_parse_gnu_properties): Compare datasz
	against size left rather than comparing pointers.  Reorganise loop.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  while (1)', '      unsigned int type = bfd_h_get_32 (abfd, ptr);', '      unsigned int datasz = bfd_h_get_32 (abfd, ptr + 4);', '      if ((ptr + datasz) > ptr_end)', '      if (ptr == ptr_end)', '\tbreak;', '', '      if (ptr > (ptr_end - 8))', '\tgoto bad_size;'], 'added_lines': ['  while (ptr != ptr_end)', '      unsigned int type;', '      unsigned int datasz;', '      if ((size_t) (ptr_end - ptr) < 8)', '\tgoto bad_size;', '', '      type = bfd_h_get_32 (abfd, ptr);', '      datasz = bfd_h_get_32 (abfd, ptr + 4);', '      if (datasz > (size_t) (ptr_end - ptr))']}
description: The _bfd_elf_parse_gnu_properties function in elf-properties.c in the Binary File Descriptor (BFD) library (aka libbfd), as distributed in GNU Binutils 2.29.1, does not prevent negative pointers, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read and application crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted ELF file.

code_evidence: The loop reads type and datasz at ptr and ptr+4 with bfd_h_get_32 before any bounds check, so when fewer than 8 bytes remain these reads go past ptr_end (line 18-19). The only guard is the pointer comparison (ptr + datasz) > ptr_end at line 22, which is signed and can be defeated by overflow when datasz is large, so the read at line 19 still occurs out of bounds.

After processing, ptr advances by an aligned datasz (line 91). The termination checks compare ptr == ptr_end and ptr > (ptr_end - 8). With a large datasz causing pointer wrap, ptr can become less than ptr_end and the loop continues, leading to further out-of-bounds reads.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads 4-byte fields from a buffer without validating that the remaining space is sufficient, and the flawed signed pointer comparison permits reading beyond the intended buffer. This matches CWE-125 (Out-of-bounds Read), whose consequence is read memory and DoS crash.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: bounds checks use signed pointer arithmetic and are performed after the header read. A crafted ELF note with an oversized datasz causes ptr + datasz to overflow or wrap, bypassing the check; the subsequent bfd_h_get_32 reads and the aligned ptr increment then read past the descdata buffer, causing an out-of-bounds read and crash.

commit_msg:
Fix bug #77563 - Uninitialized read in exif_process_IFD_in_MAKERNOTE

Also fix for bug #77659
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (maker_note->offset >= value_len) {'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (value_len < 2 || maker_note->offset >= value_len - 1) {', '\t\t\tdata_len = value_len;']}
description: An issue was discovered in the EXIF component in PHP before 7.1.27, 7.2.x before 7.2.16, and 7.3.x before 7.3.3. There is an uninitialized read in exif_process_IFD_in_MAKERNOTE because of mishandling the maker_note->offset relationship to value_len.

code_evidence: The bounds check only rejects maker_note->offset >= value_len, so an offset equal to value_len-1 passes and dir_start is set to value_ptr + maker_note->offset.

dir_start is then dereferenced by php_ifd_get16u at line 47 (reading two bytes) and later passed to exif_process_IFD_TAG; the offset_mode default case leaves data_len uninitialized, so the downstream tag processing uses an indeterminate length.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the function reads past the end of the maker-note value buffer via the off-by-one offset check and the 16-bit dereference. It is not an out-of-bounds write, since the observed unsafe operation is a read.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the guard permits maker_note->offset to equal value_len-1, leaving only one byte before the buffer end, and the MN_OFFSET_NORMAL path never initializes data_len. Trigger: a MAKERNOTE value whose offset is value_len-1 causes php_ifd_get16u to read two bytes starting at the last valid byte, reading one byte past the intended value buffer; the uninitialized data_len further misleads IFD_TAG bounds checks. Consequence: out-of-bounds read of adjacent memory.

commit_msg: Block GIF images with a code size > 12 (Issue #463)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  while ((code = gif_get_code (fp, code_size, 0)) >= 0)'], 'added_lines': ['  while ((code = gif_get_code(fp, code_size, 0)) >= 0)']}
description: A vulnerability was found in htmldoc version 1.9.15 where the stack out-of-bounds read takes place in gif_get_code() and occurs when opening a malicious GIF file, which can result in a crash (segmentation fault).

code_evidence: Declares fixed-size table[2][4096] and stack[8192], with sp starting at stack; these bounds are never checked against code values.
incode = code is accepted from gif_get_code without validating it is below 4096; when code >= max_code, firstcode is pushed and code is replaced with oldcode.

The unwind loop indexes table[1][code] and table[0][code] while code >= clear_code; code originates from the untrusted stream and is only bounded by the clear_code comparison, not by the 4096 table size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads table entries using an attacker-controlled code index without validating it against 4096, which is a read past the end of the intended buffer, matching CWE-125. The stack pushes are a related overflow, but the supported read-out-of-bounds behavior is the target weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the LZW decoder trusts code values read from the GIF stream and uses them directly to index table[2][4096] and write stack[8192] without an upper-bound check. Trigger: a malicious GIF supplies code values exceeding the table bounds (as the commit notes, code size > 12). Consequence: out-of-bounds table reads in the unwind loop, and unchecked stack pushes can overflow, causing a crash/segmentation fault.

commit_msg:
settings: Add support for defaults to keyfile backend

Stacked databases and locks are dconf features that allow
management software like Fleet Commander to set system-wide
defaults and overrides centrally for applications.

This patch adds minimal support for the same to the keyfile
backend. We look for a keyfile named 'defaults' and a
lock-list named 'locks'.

Suitable files can be produced from a dconf database with
dconf dump and dconf list-locks, respectively.

The default location for these files is /etc/glib-2.0/settings/.
For test purposes, this can be overwritten with the
GSETTINGS_DEFAULTS_DIR environment variable.

Writes always go to the per-user keyfile.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '  load_system_settings (kfsb);']}
description: The keyfile settings backend in GNOME GLib (aka glib2.0) before 2.60.0 creates directories using g_file_make_directory_with_parents (kfsb->dir, NULL, NULL) and files using g_file_replace_contents (kfsb->file, contents, length, NULL, FALSE, G_FILE_CREATE_REPLACE_DESTINATION, NULL, NULL, NULL). Consequently, it does not properly restrict directory (and file) permissions. Instead, for directories, 0777 permissions are used; for files, default file permissions are used. This is similar to CVE-2019-12450.

code_evidence: kfsb->dir is derived from the configured keyfile path, then g_file_make_directory_with_parents is called with NULL permission arguments, creating the settings directory with default (0777/umask-dependent) permissions rather than restricted ones.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Assigning loose default permissions to a security-critical configuration directory is exactly CWE-732; it is not a missing authorization check (CWE-285), since the weakness is the permission assignment itself.

evidence_lines.code:
kfsb->dir = g_file_get_parent (kfsb->file);
g_file_make_directory_with_parents (kfsb->dir, NULL, NULL);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the backend creates its configuration directory without specifying restrictive permissions, so the resulting mode permits group/other access. Trigger: construction of the keyfile backend creates or reuses the directory. Consequence: unintended local users may read or modify the per-user settings file stored there.

commit_msg:
Disallow namespace nodes in XPointer ranges

Namespace nodes must be copied to avoid use-after-free errors.
But they don't necessarily have a physical representation in a
document, so simply disallow them in XPointer ranges.

Found with afl-fuzz.

Fixes CVE-2016-4658.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    ret = (xmlXPathObjectPtr) xmlMalloc(sizeof(xmlXPathObject));', '    if (ret == NULL) {', '        xmlXPtrErrMemory("allocating range");', '\treturn(NULL);', '    }', '    memset(ret, 0 , (size_t) sizeof(xmlXPathObject));', '    ret->type = XPATH_RANGE;', '    ret->user = start;', '    ret->index = -1;', '    ret->user2 = end;', '    ret->index2 = -1;'], 'added_lines': ['    ret = xmlXPtrNewRangeInternal(start, -1, end, -1);']}
description: xpointer.c in libxml2 before 2.9.5 (as used in Apple iOS before 10, OS X before 10.12, tvOS before 10, and watchOS before 3, and other products) does not forbid namespace nodes in XPointer ranges, which allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code or cause a denial of service (use-after-free and memory corruption) via a crafted XML document.

code_evidence: The function allocates an xmlXPathObject via xmlMalloc and zeroes it with memset, then stores the caller-supplied start and end node pointers directly into ret->user and ret->user2 and sets XPATH_RANGE type. xmlXPtrRangeCheckOrder(ret) is then called on this range without any check that start or end is a namespace node.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The supported consequence is memory corruption from operations outside intended object boundaries, matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds memory operations. The root cause is the absent node-kind restriction, but the resulting out-of-bounds/use-after-free behavior is the memory-buffer boundary violation CWE-119 describes.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Namespace nodes have no physical document representation, so a range built from them is later copied/processed under the assumption of a real buffer-backed node. The missing constraint on node kind lets a crafted XPointer range reach that path, producing a use-after-free and out-of-bounds memory operations. Cause is the absent namespace-node rejection; the memory corruption is the consequence.

commit_msg:
ipv6: Prevent overrun when parsing v6 header options

The KASAN warning repoted below was discovered with a syzkaller
program.  The reproducer is basically:
  int s = socket(AF_INET6, SOCK_RAW, NEXTHDR_HOP);
  send(s, &one_byte_of_data, 1, MSG_MORE);
  send(s, &more_than_mtu_bytes_data, 2000, 0);

The socket() call sets the nexthdr field of the v6 header to
NEXTHDR_HOP, the first send call primes the payload with a non zero
byte of data, and the second send call triggers the fragmentation path.

The fragmentation code tries to parse the header options in order
to figure out where to insert the fragment option.  Since nexthdr points
to an invalid option, the calculation of the size of the network header
can made to be much larger than the linear section of the skb and data
is read outside of it.

This fix makes ip6_find_1stfrag return an error if it detects
running out-of-bounds.
