commit_msg:
libsepol/cil: Check for statements not allowed in optional blocks

While there are some checks for invalid statements in an optional
block when resolving the AST, there are no checks when building the
AST.

OSS-Fuzz found the following policy which caused a null dereference
in cil_tree_get_next_path().
  (blockinherit b3)
  (sid SID)
  (sidorder(SID))
  (optional o
    (ibpkeycon :(1 0)s)
    (block b3
      (filecon""block())
      (filecon""block())))

The problem is that the blockinherit copies block b3 before
the optional block is disabled. When the optional is disabled,
block b3 is deleted along with everything else in the optional.
Later, when filecon statements with the same path are found an
error message is produced and in trying to find out where the block
was copied from, the reference to the deleted block is used. The
error handling code assumes (rightly) that if something was copied
from a block then that block should still exist.

It is clear that in-statements, blocks, and macros cannot be in an
optional, because that allows nodes to be copied from the optional
block to somewhere outside even though the optional could be disabled
later. When optionals are disabled the AST is reset and the
resolution is restarted at the point of resolving macro calls, so
anything resolved before macro calls will never be re-resolved.
This includes tunableifs, in-statements, blockinherits,
blockabstracts, and macro definitions. Tunable declarations also
cannot be in an optional block because they are needed to resolve
tunableifs. It should be fine to allow blockinherit statements in
an optional, because that is copying nodes from outside the optional
to the optional and if the optional is later disabled, everything
will be deleted anyway.

Check and quit with an error if a tunable declaration, in-statement,
block, blockabstract, or macro definition is found within an
optional when either building or resolving the AST.

Signed-off-by: James Carter <jwcart2@gmail.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t/* tuanbles and macros are not allowed in optionals*/'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\tnode->flavor == CIL_IN ||', '\t\t\tnode->flavor == CIL_BLOCK ||', '\t\t\tnode->flavor == CIL_BLOCKABSTRACT ||']}
description: The CIL compiler in SELinux 3.2 has a heap-based buffer over-read in ebitmap_match_any (called indirectly from cil_check_neverallow). This occurs because there is sometimes a lack of checks for invalid statements in an optional block.

code_evidence: The optional-block guard only rejects CIL_TUNABLE and CIL_MACRO flavors; it omits CIL_IN, CIL_BLOCK and CIL_BLOCKABSTRACT, so such statements are permitted inside an optional and can be copied out via blockinherit before the optional is disabled.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The supported consequence is reading memory past the intended buffer (heap over-read) from a stale reference, matching CWE-125. It is not CWE-476 null dereference, since the described crash path is an out-of-bounds read, not a null pointer use.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the optional-block check is incomplete, allowing blocks and in-statements to be copied out of an optional that may later be disabled and deleted. Trigger: a policy placing a block (with filecon children) and blockinherit inside an optional; on later error handling the dangling copied-from reference is used, producing the out-of-bounds read in ebitmap_match_any via cil_check_neverallow.

commit_msg:
RAR reader: fix use after free

If read_data_compressed() returns ARCHIVE_FAILED, the caller is allowed
to continue with next archive headers. We need to set rar->start_new_table
after the ppmd7_context got freed, otherwise it won't be allocated again.

Reported by: OSS-Fuzz issue 2582
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if (ret != ARCHIVE_OK && ret != ARCHIVE_WARN)'], 'added_lines': ['    if (ret != ARCHIVE_OK && ret != ARCHIVE_WARN) {', '      rar->start_new_table = 1;', '    }']}
description: archive_read_format_rar_read_data in archive_read_support_format_rar.c in libarchive before 3.4.0 has a use-after-free in a certain ARCHIVE_FAILED situation, related to Ppmd7_DecodeSymbol.

code_evidence: read_data_compressed() is called and its return value stored in ret. When ret is neither ARCHIVE_OK nor ARCHIVE_WARN (e.g., ARCHIVE_FAILED), Ppmd7_Free(&rar->ppmd7_context) releases the PPMd7 context, but rar->start_new_table is left unchanged, so the freed context is not marked for reallocation before the caller continues with subsequent archive headers.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function frees rar->ppmd7_context and fails to force reallocation, allowing the dangling pointer to be reused, which is the definition of CWE-416. This is not merely a missing-initialization issue: the object is explicitly freed and later referenced.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: on an ARCHIVE_FAILED return, the PPMd7 context is freed without resetting rar->start_new_table, so later decoding may reuse the stale context pointer. Trigger: a compressed entry whose read_data_compressed() fails and the caller proceeds to the next header. Supported consequence: the freed PPMd7 context is referenced again, yielding a use-after-free (crash, memory corruption, or read of freed memory).

commit_msg:
x86/mm: alloc/free_lN_table: Retain partial_flags on -EINTR

When validating or de-validating pages (in alloc_lN_table and
free_lN_table respectively), the `partial_flags` local variable is
used to keep track of whether the "current" PTE started the entire
operation in a "may be partial" state.

One of the patches in XSA-299 addressed the fact that it is possible
for a previously-partially-validated entry to subsequently be found to
have invalid entries (indicated by returning -EINVAL); in which case
page->partial_flags needs to be set to indicate that the current PTE
may have the partial bit set (and thus _put_page_type() should be
called with PTF_partial_set).

Unfortunately, the patches in XSA-299 assumed that once
put_page_from_lNe() returned -ERESTART on a page, it was not possible
for it to return -EINTR.  This turns out to be true for
alloc_lN_table() and free_lN_table, but not for _get_page_type() and
_put_page_type(): both can return -EINTR when called on pages with
PGT_partial set.  In these cases, the pages PGT_partial will still be
set; failing to set partial_flags appropriately may allow an attacker
to do a privilege escalation similar to those described in XSA-299.

Fix this by always copying the local partial_flags variable into
page->partial_flags when exiting early.

NB that on the "get" side, no adjustment to nr_validated_entries is
needed: whether pte[i] is partially validated or entirely
un-validated, we want nr_validated_entries = i.  On the "put" side,
however, we need to adjust nr_validated_entries appropriately: if
pte[i] is entirely validated, we want nr_validated_entries = i + 1; if
pte[i] is partially validated, we want nr_validated_entries = i.

This is part of XSA-310.

Signed-off-by: George Dunlap <george.dunlap@citrix.com>
Reviewed-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            page->partial_flags = 0;'], 'added_lines': ['            page->partial_flags = partial_flags;;']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.12.x allowing x86 PV guest OS users to gain host OS privileges by leveraging race conditions in pagetable promotion and demotion operations, because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2019-18421. XSA-299 addressed several critical issues in restartable PV type change operations. Despite extensive testing and auditing, some corner cases were missed. A malicious PV guest administrator may be able to escalate their privilege to that of the host. All security-supported versions of Xen are vulnerable. Only x86 systems are affected. Arm systems are not affected. Only x86 PV guests can leverage the vulnerability. x86 HVM and PVH guests cannot leverage the vulnerability. Note that these attacks require very precise timing, which may be difficult to exploit in practice.

code_evidence: Line 8 caches page->partial_flags into the local partial_flags, and line 11 resets it to 0 after the first iteration. Line 25 passes partial_flags into get_page_from_l2e, which can return -EINTR on a PGT_partial page while the page's partial state persists. On the -EINTR path at lines 27-31, the code resets page->partial_flags to 0 instead of retaining the cached partial_flags, discarding the partial state.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function mutates shared pagetable state (page->partial_flags) across restartable operations, and the discarded state creates an inconsistent window exploitable via precise timing during concurrent promotion/demotion, matching CWE-362's improper synchronization of a shared resource.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the early-exit path on -EINTR overwrites page->partial_flags with 0, losing the partial-validation state that the page still carries. Trigger: a hypercall preemption or partial page type returns -EINTR during pagetable allocation, causing the operation to restart with inconsistent page state. Consequence: the restartable type-change sequence operates on mismatched partial state, enabling a PV guest to corrupt pagetable state and escalate to host privilege.

commit_msg:
mm: avoid setting up anonymous pages into file mapping

Reading page fault handler code I've noticed that under right
circumstances kernel would map anonymous pages into file mappings: if
the VMA doesn't have vm_ops->fault() and the VMA wasn't fully populated
on ->mmap(), kernel would handle page fault to not populated pte with
do_anonymous_page().

Let's change page fault handler to use do_anonymous_page() only on
anonymous VMA (->vm_ops == NULL) and make sure that the VMA is not
shared.

For file mappings without vm_ops->fault() or shred VMA without vm_ops,
page fault on pte_none() entry would lead to SIGBUS.

Signed-off-by: Kirill A. Shutemov <kirill.shutemov@linux.intel.com>
Acked-by: Oleg Nesterov <oleg@redhat.com>
Cc: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>
Cc: Willy Tarreau <w@1wt.eu>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t/* The VMA was not fully populated on mmap() or missing VM_DONTEXPAND */', '\tif (!vma->vm_ops->fault)', '\t\treturn VM_FAULT_SIGBUS;']}
description: mm/memory.c in the Linux kernel before 4.1.4 mishandles anonymous pages, which allows local users to gain privileges or cause a denial of service (page tainting) via a crafted application that triggers writing to page zero.

code_evidence: do_fault() derives pgoff from address/vma fields, unmaps the page table, then dispatches to do_read_fault/do_cow_fault/do_shared_fault based only on FAULT_FLAG_WRITE and VM_SHARED, without checking that vma->vm_ops provides a fault handler for the file-backed VMA.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The handler processes a page-fault request on a VMA without validating the required mapping property (presence of vm_ops->fault), matching CWE-20's missing validation of required input properties before unsafe processing. The later patch adds exactly this check and returns VM_FAULT_SIGBUS.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the fault path fails to validate that the VMA is a valid file mapping with vm_ops->fault before invoking the file fault handlers. Trigger: a crafted application faults on a pte_none entry of a VMA lacking vm_ops->fault, causing anonymous pages to be installed into a file mapping. Supported consequence: page tainting and potential local privilege gain or denial of service.

commit_msg:
x509: excessive resource use verifying policy constraints

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if (tdata != NULL)', '      tlen = strlen((char *)tdata);', '', '      if (talloc)', '      {', '\tfree(talloc);', '\ttalloc = NULL;', '      }'], 'added_lines': ['    tlen = tdata ? strlen((char *)tdata) : 0;', '', '    if (tdata != NULL && tlen > 0)', '    }', '    if (talloc)', '    {', '      free(talloc);', '      talloc = NULL;']}
description: HTMLDoc v1.9.15 was discovered to contain a heap overflow via (write_header) /htmldoc/htmldoc/html.cxx:273.

code_evidence: For a non-NULL tdata, tlen = strlen(tdata) is computed, then the buffer is sized as realloc(s, 1 + slen + tlen) or malloc(1 + tlen), and memcpy copies tlen bytes at offset slen. The 1 byte is reserved only for the terminating NUL; slen is the accumulated length of prior concatenations. The allocation and copy use the same tlen, so sizing is internally consistent for this block.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 requires a write past the buffer boundary. The visible code allocates 1 + slen + tlen bytes and writes exactly tlen bytes at offset slen, leaving room for the NUL. The description's heap overflow is attributed to write_header in html.cxx:273, a different function; no over-write is evidenced here.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause would be an incorrect size computation relative to the copied length, e.g., integer overflow of 1 + slen + tlen or a tlen that exceeds the allocated space. The function computes tlen from strlen and uses it consistently in both allocation and memcpy, so no out-of-bounds write is demonstrated. The commit addresses an empty-title crash (tdata non-NULL but empty), not a heap overflow in this function.

commit_msg:
If the beginning of the inode bitmap area is corrupted on disk, an inode
with the same inode number as the root inode can be allocated and fail
soon after.  In this case, the subsequent call to nilfs_clear_inode() on
that bogus root inode will wrongly decrement the reference counter of
struct nilfs_root, and this will erroneously free struct nilfs_root,
causing kernel oopses.

This fixes the problem by changing nilfs_new_inode() to skip reserved
inode numbers while repairing the inode bitmap.

Signed-off-by: Ryusuke Konishi <konishi.ryusuke@gmail.com>

Tested-by: Ryusuke Konishi <konishi.ryusuke@gmail.com>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>

commit_msg:
sg_write()/bsg_write() is not fit to be called under KERNEL_DS

Both damn things interpret userland pointers embedded into the payload;
worse, they are actually traversing those.  Leaving aside the bad
API design, this is very much _not_ safe to call with KERNEL_DS.
Bail out early if that happens.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Al Viro <viro@zeniv.linux.org.uk>

description: The sg implementation in the Linux kernel through 4.9 does not properly restrict write operations in situations where the KERNEL_DS option is set, which allows local users to read or write to arbitrary kernel memory locations or cause a denial of service (use-after-free) by leveraging access to a /dev/sg device, related to block/bsg.c and drivers/scsi/sg.c.  NOTE: this vulnerability exists because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2016-9576.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The shown bsg_write function only lacks a KERNEL_DS guard and forwards to __bsg_write; it contains no free, pointer reuse, or use-after-free operation, so CWE-416 is not supported by the function body.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        ThrowReaderException(CorruptImageError,"InsufficientImageDataInFile");'], 'added_lines': ['        {', '          dib_colormap=(unsigned char *) RelinquishMagickMemory(dib_colormap);', '          ThrowReaderException(CorruptImageError,"InsufficientImageDataInFile");', '        }']}
description: The ReadDIBImage function in coders/dib.c in ImageMagick before 6.9.9-0 and 7.x before 7.0.6-1 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory leak) via a crafted file.

code_evidence: Lines 153-154 allocate dib_colormap with AcquireQuantumMemory; lines 155-156 return on allocation failure.

Line 158 reads the colormap into dib_colormap; lines 159-160 throw CorruptImageError when the read is short, without freeing dib_colormap (the normal free is at line 170, which is skipped by the throw).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function allocates a resource (dib_colormap) and fails to release it on the error path, matching CWE-772. The fix adds RelinquishMagickMemory before throwing. This is distinct from an out-of-bounds read: the weakness is the missing release, not improper buffer access.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: dib_colormap is heap-allocated at line 153 and only released at line 170 after the successful read path. A crafted DIB whose color-table read is truncated makes count mismatch at line 159, so the error branch throws before line 170. Each crafted file thus leaks the allocated colormap buffer, causing memory exhaustion/DoS.

commit_msg:
x86/EPT: ept_set_middle_entry() related adjustments

ept_split_super_page() wants to further modify the newly allocated
table, so have ept_set_middle_entry() return the mapped pointer rather
than tearing it down and then getting re-established right again.

Similarly ept_next_level() wants to hand back a mapped pointer of
the next level page, so re-use the one established by
ept_set_middle_entry() in case that path was taken.

Pull the setting of suppress_ve ahead of insertion into the higher level
table, and don't have ept_split_super_page() set the field a 2nd time.

This is part of XSA-328.

Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Reviewed-by: Roger Pau Monné <roger.pau@citrix.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['static int ept_set_middle_entry(struct p2m_domain *p2m, ept_entry_t *ept_entry)', '        return 0;', '    table = map_domain_page(mfn);', '', '    for ( i = 0; i < EPT_PAGETABLE_ENTRIES; i++ )', '        table[i].suppress_ve = 1;', '', '    unmap_domain_page(table);', '', '    return 1;'], 'added_lines': ['static ept_entry_t *ept_set_middle_entry(struct p2m_domain *p2m,', '                                         ept_entry_t *ept_entry)', '        return NULL;', '', '    table = map_domain_page(mfn);', '', '    for ( i = 0; i < EPT_PAGETABLE_ENTRIES; i++ )', '        table[i].suppress_ve = 1;', '    return table;']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.13.x, allowing Intel guest OS users to gain privileges or cause a denial of service because of non-atomic modification of a live EPT PTE. When mapping guest EPT (nested paging) tables, Xen would in some circumstances use a series of non-atomic bitfield writes. Depending on the compiler version and optimisation flags, Xen might expose a dangerous partially written PTE to the hardware, which an attacker might be able to race to exploit. A guest administrator or perhaps even an unprivileged guest user might be able to cause denial of service, data corruption, or privilege escalation. Only systems using Intel CPUs are vulnerable. Systems using AMD CPUs, and Arm systems, are not vulnerable. Only systems using nested paging (hap, aka nested paging, aka in this case Intel EPT) are vulnerable. Only HVM and PVH guests can exploit the vulnerability. The presence and scope of the vulnerability depends on the precise optimisations performed by the compiler used to build Xen. If the compiler generates (a) a single 64-bit write, or (b) a series of read-modify-write operations in the same order as the source code, the hypervisor is not vulnerable. For example, in one test build using GCC 8.3 with normal settings, the compiler generated multiple (unlocked) read-modify-write operations in source-code order, which did not constitute a vulnerability. We have not been able to survey compilers; consequently we cannot say which compiler(s) might produce vulnerable code (with which code-generation options). The source code clearly violates the C rules, and thus should be considered vulnerable.

code_evidence: Lines 9-14 build the live EPT PTE in ept_entry through a series of separate bitfield writes: clearing epte, then assigning mfn, access, r/w/x, a, and suppress_ve individually. This entry is the shared resource that hardware/other code may read concurrently; there is no single atomic store or synchronization around these writes.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function modifies shared EPT state through a non-atomic sequence, so an interfering concurrent reader can observe intermediate values—this is CWE-362. It is not merely a missing bounds check; the issue is lack of atomicity/exclusivity on the shared PTE.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the middle-level EPT entry is assembled with multiple non-atomic bitfield assignments rather than one atomic write. Trigger: a concurrent reader (hardware EPT walk) observes ept_entry while it is only partially initialized. Supported consequence: a dangerous partially written PTE is exposed, enabling a race that can cause DoS, data corruption, or privilege escalation.

description: Integer Overflow vulnerability in mp_grow in libtom libtommath before commit beba892bc0d4e4ded4d667ab1d2a94f4d75109a9, allows attackers to execute arbitrary code and cause a denial of service (DoS).

code_evidence: digs is used to size the destination: if c->alloc < digs the code calls mp_grow(c, digs) without first validating the sign of digs.
pa = MP_MIN(digs, a->used + b->used) bounds the loop count by the caller-supplied digs value.

evidence_lines.code: pa = MP_MIN(digs, a->used + b->used);
MP_ZERO_DIGITS(tmpc, olduse - ix);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: digs, a caller-controlled int, is used as a size for mp_grow and for loop/clear-length arithmetic without a lower-bound check. A negative or wrapped value makes the mp_grow comparison and the olduse - ix length computation inconsistent, so allocation or clearing can use a wrong size, leading to out-of-bounds memory writes. commit_msg:
x86/HVM: prefill partially used variable on emulation paths

Certain handlers ignore the access size (vioapic_write() being the
example this was found with), perhaps leading to subsequent reads
seeing data that wasn't actually written by the guest. For
consistency and extra safety also do this on the read path of
hvm_process_io_intercept(), even if this doesn't directly affect what
guests get to see, as we've supposedly already dealt with read handlers
leaving data completely unitialized.

This is XSA-239.

Reported-by: Roger Pau Monné <roger.pau@citrix.com>
Reviewed-by: Roger Pau Monné <roger.pau@citrix.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>

+++ func_after
@@ -12,7 +12,7 @@

         .dir = dir,
         .df = df,
-        .data = data,
+        .data = data_is_addr ? data : 0,
         .data_is_ptr = data_is_addr, /* ioreq_t field name is misleading */
         .state = STATE_IOREQ_READY,

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        .data = data,'], 'added_lines': ['        .data = data_is_addr ? data : 0,']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.9.x allowing x86 HVM guest OS users to obtain sensitive information from the host OS (or an arbitrary guest OS) because intercepted I/O operations can cause a write of data from uninitialized hypervisor stack memory.

code_evidence: The ioreq_t initializer copies the raw data argument into p.data at line 15, while data_is_addr only controls the separate data_is_ptr field at line 16. On a write, line 50 checks !data_is_addr and only then memcpy's size bytes from p_data into p.data; when data_is_addr is true this copy is skipped, leaving p.data as the address value rather than written guest data.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The supported consequence is disclosure of sensitive host/hypervisor memory to a guest, matching CWE-200's confidentiality exposure. The commit's fix (zeroing data when data_is_addr) confirms the omission of initialization, distinguishing it from a mere logic error.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: p.data is populated from the data parameter regardless of whether data is an address or a value, and the write path's memcpy at line 51 is conditional on !data_is_addr, so for address-form writes p.data retains the pointer value. A handler that ignores the access size can then expose that uninitialized/stale stack-derived content to a reader, disclosing hypervisor memory across the guest boundary.

description: PJSIP is a free and open source multimedia communication library written in C. A buffer overflow vulnerability in versions 2.12 and prior affects applications that use PJSIP DNS resolution. It doesn't affect PJSIP users who utilize an external resolver. This vulnerability is related to CVE-2023-27585. The difference is that this issue is in parsing the query record `parse_rr()`, while the issue in CVE-2023-27585 is in `parse_query()`. A patch is available in the `master` branch of the `pjsip/pjproject` GitHub repository. A workaround is to disable DNS resolution in PJSIP config (by setting `nameserver_count` to zero) or use an external resolver instead.

code_evidence: label_len is read from the packet byte *p and the only bound check is pkt+label_len > max, which does not account for the length octet at p+1 or the terminating byte; the copy then writes label_len bytes to name->ptr + name->slen.

After the copy, p advances by label_len+1, and the code dereferences *p and writes '.' plus increments name->slen without validating that p (or the write position) remains within max or the destination buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function copies an attacker-controlled packet buffer into name->ptr via pj_memcpy without verifying the input length fits the destination, which is exactly a buffer copy without checking input size (CWE-120). It is not merely an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125), since the copy writes past the destination.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the length check compares the packet base plus label_len against max rather than p+1+label_len (plus terminator), so an attacker-controlled DNS label length passes validation while the copy and subsequent dots write beyond name->ptr. Trigger: a crafted DNS response with an oversized label. Consequence: heap buffer overflow (out-of-bounds write) leading to memory corruption or crash.

description: The ReadSGIImage function in sgi.c in ImageMagick 7.0.5-4 allows remote attackers to consume an amount of available memory via a crafted file.

code_evidence: When AcquireQuantumMemory for scanline fails, control jumps via ThrowReaderException without releasing the already-allocated pixel_info (AcquireVirtualMemory at 111-112), leaking that virtual-memory resource.

If offsets, runlength, or packet_info allocation fails, the handler only relinquishes the buffer whose pointer is NULL; the non-NULL buffers (and pixel_info) are not released before ThrowReaderException.
When a runlength exceeds the header bound, ThrowReaderException exits without releasing offsets, runlength, packet_info, or pixel_info.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function acquires resources and fails to release them after their effective lifetime on error paths, matching CWE-772's missing resource release. This is a resource-lifetime leak rather than an out-of-bounds access or double free.

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: error/exception paths abandon previously acquired memory resources (pixel_info, offsets, runlength, packet_info) instead of releasing them before throwing. Trigger: a crafted SGI file causing an allocation failure or an out-of-range runlength. Consequence: leaked memory per failed parse, enabling resource-consumption denial of service.

description: In CollectValuesOrEntriesImpl of elements.cc, there is possible remote code execution due to type confusion. This could lead to remote escalation of privilege with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is needed for exploitation. Product: Android. Versions: Android-7.0 Android-7.1.1 Android-7.1.2 Android-8.0 Android-8.1 Android-9.0 Android ID: A-111274046

code_evidence: Line 6 captures object->map() and line 7-8 casts object->elements() to FixedArray, caching both before the loop.
Lines 10-11 call GetEntryForIndexImpl using the cached parameter_map while the live object may have changed during iteration.
Lines 15-16 fetch element_k via Subclass::GetImpl from the cached parameter_map and entry, then line 17 tests IsAccessorPair on it.

commit_msg:
bgo#738050 - Handle the case where a list of coordinate pairs has an odd number of elements

Lists of points come in coordinate pairs, but we didn't have any checking for that.
It was possible to try to fetch the 'last' coordinate in a list, i.e. the y coordinate
of an x,y pair, that was in fact missing, leading to an out-of-bounds array read.

In that case, we now reuse the last-known y coordinate.

Fixes https://bugzilla.gnome.org/show_bug.cgi?id=738050

Signed-off-by: Federico Mena Quintero <federico@gnome.org>

But if there is a', "         * missing part of one pair in a corrupt SVG, we'll have an incomplete", '         * list.  In that case, we reuse the last-known Y coordinate.', '         */', '        if (i + 1 < pointlist_len)', '            p = pointlist[i + 1];', '        else', '            p = pointlist[i - 1];', '', '        g_string_append (d, g_ascii_dtostr (buf, sizeof (buf), p));']}
description: The _rsvg_node_poly_build_path function in rsvg-shapes.c in librsvg before 2.40.7 allows context-dependent attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds heap read) via an odd number of elements in a coordinate pair in an SVG document.

code_evidence: Line 10 parses an attacker-controlled SVG number list into pointlist with a length. Line 13 checks only that the length is at least 2, not that it is a multiple of 2 (even). The loop at line 22 increments i by 2 up to pointlist_len, so when pointlist_len is odd the final iteration has i == pointlist_len - 1 and line 26 reads pointlist[i + 1], which is one past the allocated array.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function accepts input that lacks a required structural property (coordinate pairs) and processes it unsafely; this is improper validation of input consistency/length, matching CWE-20. The out-of-bounds read is the consequence of the missing even-length check, not a separate weakness class.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function validates a minimum length but not the required even-pair property of the coordinate list. Trigger: a corrupt SVG with an odd number of coordinate values. Consequence: an out-of-bounds heap read at pointlist[i + 1], causing a denial of service (crash).

commit_msg:
Bug 706506: Fix infinite recursion in mutool info.

2 separate problems here.

Firstly, pdf_mark_list_push fails to copy the pushed data
from local_list to the newly malloced block when we first
move from local storage to malloced storage.

(Also, while we are here, there is no point in storing
0 entries in the list as they will never be checked!)

Secondly, while gatherresourceinfo is supposed to be
called with indirected objects, it can (as is the case
with the given fuzzed file) be called with direct
references. These don't put anything sane in the cycle
checker.

Thus by using (legal) indirections from (say) the Font
resource entry back to something that contains the
original resource entry, we can get cycles that we don't
detect.

Fix this by pushing such entries onto the mark list.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (num > 0)', '\t{', '\t\t/* Note: this is slow, if the mark list is expected to be big use pdf_mark_bits instead! */', '\t\tfor (i = 0; i < marks->len; ++i)', '\t\t\tif (marks->list[i] == num)', '\t\t\t\treturn 1;', '\t}'], 'added_lines': ['\t/* If object is not an indirection, then no record to store, or check. */', '\tif (num == 0)', '\t\treturn 0;', '', '\t/* Note: this is slow, if the mark list is expected to be big use pdf_mark_bits instead! */', '\tfor (i = 0; i < marks->len; ++i)', '\t\tif (marks->list[i] == num)', '\t\t\treturn 1;', '\t\t{', '\t\t\tmemcpy(marks->list, marks->local_list, sizeof(marks->local_list));', '\t\t}']}
description: MuPDF v1.21.1 was discovered to contain an infinite recursion in the component pdf_mark_list_push. This vulnerability allows attackers to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) via a crafted PDF file.

code_evidence: The cycle check is guarded by `if (num > 0)`, so direct objects (num == 0) are never searched in the mark list and never treated as already marked.

When the mark list moves from local storage to a malloced buffer, `marks->list = fz_malloc_array(ctx, newsize, int)` is called without copying `marks->local_list`, so previously recorded entries are lost before `marks->list[marks->len++] = num` is written.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function is the cycle-detection primitive whose failure permits unbounded recursion in resource gathering; the resulting stack exhaustion is the resource-consumption consequence CWE-674 describes. The flaw is not merely an allocation bug (e.g., CWE-787) but a missing constraint that would stop recursive traversal.

evidence_lines.code:
if (marks->list == marks->local_list)
marks->list = fz_malloc_array(ctx, newsize, int);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: direct references are not recorded in the cycle checker and the first growth from local storage discards existing marks. Trigger: a crafted PDF whose resource entries use legal indirections to revisit the original resource structure. Because cycles are not detected, `gatherresourceinfo` recurses without a working termination condition, exhausting the stack and causing a denial of service.

commit_msg:
* src/http.c (skip_short_body): Return error on negative chunk size

Reported-by: Antti Levomäki, Christian Jalio, Joonas Pihlaja from Forcepoint
Reported-by: Juhani Eronen from Finnish National Cyber Security Centre
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '              if (remaining_chunk_size < 0)', '                return false;']}
description: The http.c:skip_short_body() function is called in some circumstances, such as when processing redirects. When the response is sent chunked in wget before 1.19.2, the chunk parser uses strtol() to read each chunk's length, but doesn't check that the chunk length is a non-negative number. The code then tries to skip the chunk in pieces of 512 bytes by using the MIN() macro, but ends up passing the negative chunk length to connect.c:fd_read(). As fd_read() takes an int argument, the high 32 bits of the chunk length are discarded, leaving fd_read() with a completely attacker controlled length argument.

code_evidence: Line 24 parses the chunk length with strtol() into remaining_chunk_size, but the function never validates that the value is non-negative before using it. Line 33 computes contlen = MIN(remaining_chunk_size, SKIP_SIZE); for a negative value this yields the negative chunk size, which line 36 passes as the length argument to fd_read() together with the 513-byte dlbuf.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked negative length flows into fd_read() as the size argument for the fixed dlbuf buffer, so the memory operation is performed outside the buffer's intended bounds, matching CWE-119. The underlying defect is a missing sign check on the length, but the supported consequence is an out-of-bounds buffer operation rather than a pure integer issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the attacker-controlled chunk length is not constrained to be non-negative. Trigger: a chunked response whose chunk-size line encodes a negative value. Consequence: the negative length reaches fd_read(), where it is narrowed to an int and used as a buffer length against dlbuf, producing an out-of-bounds memory operation on the fixed stack buffer.

commit_msg:
x86/mm: Don't reset linear_pt_count on partial validation

"Linear pagetables" is a technique which involves either pointing a
pagetable at itself, or to another pagetable the same or higher level.
Xen has limited support for linear pagetables: A page may either point
to itself, or point to another page of the same level (i.e., L2 to L2,
L3 to L3, and so on).

XSA-240 introduced an additional restriction that limited the "depth"
of such chains by allowing pages to either *point to* other pages of
the same level, or *be pointed to* by other pages of the same level,
but not both.  To implement this, we keep track of the number of
outstanding times a page points to or is pointed to another page
table, to prevent both from happening at the same time.

Unfortunately, the original commit introducing this reset this count
when resuming validation of a partially-validated pagetable, dropping
some "linear_pt_entry" counts.

On debug builds on systems where guests used this feature, this might
lead to crashes that look like this:

    Assertion 'oc > 0' failed at mm.c:874

Worse, if an attacker could engineer such a situation to occur, they
might be able to make loops or other abitrary chains of linear
pagetables, leading to the denial-of-service situation outlined in
XSA-240.

This is XSA-309.

Reported-by: Manuel Bouyer <bouyer@antioche.eu.org>
Signed-off-by: George Dunlap <george.dunlap@citrix.com>
Reviewed-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        page->linear_pt_count = 0;'], 'added_lines': ['            page->linear_pt_count = 0;']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.12.x allowing x86 PV guest OS users to cause a denial of service via degenerate chains of linear pagetables, because of an incorrect fix for CVE-2017-15595. "Linear pagetables" is a technique which involves either pointing a pagetable at itself, or to another pagetable of the same or higher level. Xen has limited support for linear pagetables: A page may either point to itself, or point to another pagetable of the same level (i.e., L2 to L2, L3 to L3, and so on). XSA-240 introduced an additional restriction that limited the "depth" of such chains by allowing pages to either *point to* other pages of the same level, or *be pointed to* by other pages of the same level, but not both. To implement this, we keep track of the number of outstanding times a page points to or is pointed to another page table, to prevent both from happening at the same time. Unfortunately, the original commit introducing this reset this count when resuming validation of a partially-validated pagetable, incorrectly dropping some "linear_pt_entry" counts. If an attacker could engineer such a situation to occur, they might be able to make loops or other arbitrary chains of linear pagetables, as described in XSA-240. A malicious or buggy PV guest may cause the hypervisor to crash, resulting in Denial of Service (DoS) affecting the entire host. Privilege escalation and information leaks cannot be excluded. All versions of Xen are vulnerable. Only x86 systems are affected. Arm systems are not affected. Only x86 PV guests can leverage the vulnerability. x86 HVM and PVH guests cannot leverage the vulnerability. Only systems which have enabled linear pagetables are vulnerable. Systems which have disabled linear pagetables, either by selecting CONFIG_PV_LINEAR_PT=n when building the hypervisor, or adding pv-linear-pt=false on the command-line, are not vulnerable.

code_evidence: At line 99 the code checks whether the new type_info nx is still unvalidated. Inside, lines 101-105 reset nr_validated_ptes and partial_flags only when the prior value x was not PGT_partial, i.e. on a fresh (not resuming) validation. However line 106 unconditionally sets page->linear_pt_count = 0, even when x had PGT_partial set and validation is being resumed for a partially-validated pagetable.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The counter update is a security-critical calculation whose result (linear_pt_count) is later used to enforce the linear-pagetable depth restriction. Resetting it unconditionally in the partial-resume path produces an incorrect count, so the enforcement check operates on wrong data, matching CWE-682. This is an incorrect calculation feeding a resource/DoS decision, not merely a missing bounds check.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the linear_pt_count bookkeeping counter is reset on every entry into the unvalidated branch, including the partial-resume path, rather than only when starting a fresh validation. Trigger: a PV guest creates a linear pagetable, gets it partially validated (PGT_partial set), then resumes validation. The reset drops outstanding linear_pt_entry counts, defeating the XSA-240 depth restriction and allowing degenerate chains/loops of linear pagetables, leading to hypervisor crash/DoS.

Fixed OOB read in update_read_cache_bitmap_v3_order

description: In FreeRDP before version 2.1.2, there is a global OOB read in update_read_cache_bitmap_v3_order. As a workaround, one can disable bitmap cache with -bitmap-cache (default). This is fixed in version 2.1.2.

joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the unchecked attacker-influenced index into BPP_BMF causes a read beyond the intended buffer bounds. The fix replaces the raw index with get_bpp_bmf, which validates bpp and returns a failure flag, confirming the missing bounds constraint rather than a write-side overflow (CWE-787).

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: cache_brush->bpp is used directly as an index into BPP_BMF with no range check. Trigger: a caller supplies a bpp value outside the array's valid index range, causing a read past the end (or before the start) of the global array. Supported consequence: out-of-bounds read of global memory, which may disclose adjacent data or crash.

passing invalid pointers to a pseudo TA.

Fixes: OP-TEE-2018-0007: "Buffer checks missing when calling pseudo
TAs".

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['static void utee_param_to_param(struct tee_ta_param *p, struct utee_params *up)', '\t\tcase TEE_PARAM_TYPE_MEMREF_INPUT:'], 'added_lines': ['static TEE_Result utee_param_to_param(struct user_ta_ctx *utc,', '\t\t\t\t      struct tee_ta_param *p,', '\t\t\t\t      struct utee_params *up)', '\t\tuint32_t flags = TEE_MEMORY_ACCESS_READ |', '\t\t\t\t TEE_MEMORY_ACCESS_ANY_OWNER;', '\t\t\tflags |= TEE_MEMORY_ACCESS_WRITE;', '\t\t\t/*FALLTHROUGH*/', '\t\tcase TEE_PARAM_TYPE_MEMREF_INPUT:', '\t\t\tif (tee_mmu_check_access_rights(utc, flags, a, b))', '\t\t\t\treturn TEE_ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED;', '', '\treturn TEE_SUCCESS;']}
description: Linaro/OP-TEE OP-TEE 3.3.0 and earlier is affected by: Buffer Overflow. The impact is: Memory corruption and disclosure of memory content. The component is: optee_os. The fixed version is: 3.4.0 and later.

code_evidence: Lines 7-8 read attacker-controlled parameter values a (offset/pointer) and b (size) from up->vals without any validation.
Lines 10-16 accept MEMREF_INPUT/OUTPUT/INOUT types and directly copy a and b into p->u[n].mem.offs and p->u[n].mem.size, with no check that [a, a+b) is a valid, accessible user mapping.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-20 fits because the function processes externally supplied parameters (offsets and sizes) without validating they are safe to use, which is precisely missing input validation; the downstream overflow is a consequence of this unchecked input.

commit_msg:
http: make length/offset-related variables unsigned.

Fixes #5992, reported and found by Paul Cher <paulcher@icloud.com>.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    int64_t old_off = s->off;', '    else if ((s->filesize == -1 && whence == SEEK_END))'], 'added_lines': ['    uint64_t old_off = s->off;', '    else if ((s->filesize == UINT64_MAX && whence == SEEK_END))']}
description: Heap-based buffer overflow in libavformat/http.c in FFmpeg before 2.8.10, 3.0.x before 3.0.5, 3.1.x before 3.1.6, and 3.2.x before 3.2.2 allows remote web servers to execute arbitrary code via a negative chunk size in an HTTP response.

code_evidence: old_off is declared int64_t and s->filesize is compared against -1, so the length/offset state is signed and a negative size sentinel can be confused with a valid offset.
For SEEK_END, off is computed as off += s->filesize; the subsequent off < 0 check and s->off = off assignment treat the resulting offset as signed, allowing a negative chunk size to flow through.

old_buf_size is derived from s->buf_end - s->buf_ptr and used in memcpy(old_buf, s->buf_ptr, old_buf_size); if the offset/size state is corrupted, the copied length is not bounded against BUFFER_SIZE, producing an out-of-bounds write.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs a memcpy into a fixed-size stack buffer using a length that can exceed the buffer bound, which is an out-of-bounds write within CWE-119. The signedness flaw is the root cause, but the supported consequence is the memory-buffer boundary violation described by CWE-119.

evidence_lines.code:
int64_t old_off = s->off;
else if ((s->filesize == -1 && whence == SEEK_END))

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: signed offset/size arithmetic and a signed -1 filesize sentinel allow a remote HTTP response with a negative chunk size to corrupt the seek offset. Trigger: seeking with SEEK_END or SEEK_CUR using the attacker-controlled size. Consequence: the computed old_buf_size can exceed BUFFER_SIZE, so memcpy writes past old_buf, yielding a heap-based buffer overflow that may lead to code execution.

commit_msg:
mp4: limit the recursion depth for boxes

Although the dissection of each box header consumes a couple of bytes,
it turned out that it's still possible to crash wireshark with a sample
file that contains a large number of nested boxes. The stack will fill
up before we reach the end of the data bytes.

Keep track of the recursion depth as we walk through the hierarchy of
boxes. Abort if we reach the (locally defined) upper limit.

description: GPAC version 2.1-DEV-rev505-gb9577e6ad-master was discovered to contain a memory leak via the afrt_box_read function at box_code_adobe.c.

code_evidence: asrt_box_read allocates tmp_str with gf_malloc at line 13 and reads bytes into it in the while loop (lines 16-23). The pointer is only inserted into ptr->quality_segment_url_modifiers at line 24, after the loop. If the loop's ISOM_DECREASE_SIZE at line 18 triggers an early return while tmp_strsize remains nonzero, the function exits before line 24, so tmp_str is never stored in the list and never freed.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This is a missing release of memory after its effective lifetime: an allocated buffer becomes unreachable on an error path without being freed. It is not a use-after-free or double-free, since the buffer is neither used nor released after the early return; the supported impact is resource consumption/DoS from repeated leaks.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the malloc'd buffer is registered for ownership only after the read loop, but the loop can return early via ISOM_DECREASE_SIZE on malformed/truncated input. Trigger: a box whose declared size runs out mid-string. The consequence is an unreachable allocation that is never released, leaking memory on each parse of malformed data.

commit_msg:
asymcute: don't make the assumption that req->arg is non-NULL

This fixes a denial of service where an attacker would be able to cause
a NULL pointer dereference by sending a spoofed packet. This attack only
requires knowledge about pending message ids.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['        if (topic == NULL) {', '            return;', '        }', '']}
description: RIOT 2019.07 contains a NULL pointer dereference in the MQTT-SN implementation (asymcute), potentially allowing an attacker to crash a network node running RIOT. This requires spoofing an MQTT server response. To do so, the attacker needs to know the MQTT MsgID of a pending MQTT protocol message and the ephemeral port used by RIOT's MQTT implementation. Additionally, the server IP address is required for spoofing the packet.

code_evidence: req->arg is cast directly to asymcute_topic_t * and dereferenced at lines 13-14 without checking whether it is NULL; the cast does not validate the pointer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences a pointer expected to be valid but which may be NULL, matching CWE-476. This is a missing NULL check, not a type-confusion or use-after-free issue.

Trigger: a spoofed REGACK with MQTTSN_ACCEPTED and a known pending MsgID reaches a request whose arg is NULL. Consequence: NULL pointer dereference, crashing the node (DoS).

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tu32 elem_size = sizeof(struct stack_map_bucket) + smap->map.value_size;'], 'added_lines': ['\tu64 elem_size = sizeof(struct stack_map_bucket) +', '\t\t\t(u64)smap->map.value_size;']}
description: prealloc_elems_and_freelist in kernel/bpf/stackmap.c in the Linux kernel before 5.14.12 allows unprivileged users to trigger an eBPF multiplication integer overflow with a resultant out-of-bounds write.

code_evidence: elem_size is declared u32 from sizeof(struct stack_map_bucket) plus the user-influenced smap->map.value_size; the allocation size is then computed as elem_size * smap->map.max_entries, another user-controlled map attribute, in the same u32 arithmetic domain.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the size calculation can wrap to a small value that is then used for memory allocation, leading to an undersized buffer and out-of-bounds write. This is integer overflow affecting allocation size, not merely a missing bounds check.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the product elem_size * max_entries is evaluated in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic, so a large value_size or max_entries wraps the requested allocation size to a small value. Trigger: unprivileged user creates a stack map with crafted attributes. Consequence: bpf_map_area_alloc allocates a too-small region, and pcpu_freelist_populate later writes beyond it, producing an out-of-bounds write.

commit_msg: Fix #522
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  BLOSC_ERROR_NULL(cparams, BLOSC2_ERROR_NULL_POINTER);', '  BLOSC_ERROR_NULL(cparams->schunk, BLOSC2_ERROR_NULL_POINTER);']}
description: C-blosc2 before 2.9.3 was discovered to contain a NULL pointer dereference in ndlz/ndlz8x8.c via a NULL pointer to memset.

code_evidence: The function receives cparams as a pointer parameter and does not validate it before use. Line 6 dereferences cparams via cparams->schunk when calling blosc2_meta_get, so a NULL cparams directly causes a NULL dereference.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits because the function dereferences a pointer (cparams) that may be NULL without a validity check, leading to a crash. This is a base-level NULL pointer dereference rather than an unrelated memory-safety issue, since the missing constraint is specifically a NULL check on the pointer being dereferenced.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: no NULL check on the cparams argument before its member schunk is accessed. Trigger: caller passes cparams == NULL; the member access cparams->schunk at line 6 dereferences the NULL pointer. Supported consequence: crash/DoS. The patch confirms this by adding BLOSC_ERROR_NULL guards for cparams and cparams->schunk.

commit_msg:
netfilter: add back stackpointer size checks

The rationale for removing the check is only correct for rulesets
generated by ip(6)tables.

In iptables, a jump can only occur to a user-defined chain, i.e.
because we size the stack based on number of user-defined chains we
cannot exceed stack size.

However, the underlying binary format has no such restriction,
and the validation step only ensures that the jump target is a
valid rule start point.

IOW, its possible to build a rule blob that has no user-defined
chains but does contain a jump.

If this happens, no jump stack gets allocated and crash occurs
because no jumpstack was allocated.

Fixes: 7814b6ec6d0d6 ("netfilter: xtables: don't save/restore jumpstack offset")
Reported-by: syzbot+e783f671527912cd9403@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Signed-off-by: Florian Westphal <fw@strlen.de>
Signed-off-by: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t    !(e->ip.flags & IPT_F_GOTO))'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t    !(e->ip.flags & IPT_F_GOTO)) {', '\t\t\t\tif (unlikely(stackidx >= private->stacksize)) {', '\t\t\t\t\tverdict = NF_DROP;', '\t\t\t\t\tbreak;', '\t\t\t\t}', '\t\t\t}']}
description: The netfilter subsystem in the Linux kernel through 4.15.7 mishandles the case of a rule blob that contains a jump but lacks a user-defined chain, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference) by leveraging the CAP_NET_RAW or CAP_NET_ADMIN capability, related to arpt_do_table in net/ipv4/netfilter/arp_tables.c, ipt_do_table in net/ipv4/netfilter/ip_tables.c, and ip6t_do_table in net/ipv6/netfilter/ip6_tables.c.

code_evidence: At [78,79,80] a non-goto jump stores the current entry into jumpstack[stackidx++] without verifying stackidx is within private->stacksize.
At [30,31,32,33] jumpstack is derived from private->jumpstack[cpu], which is NULL when no user-defined chains caused a jump stack allocation.
At [69,70,71,72,73,74] the XT_RETURN path pops jumpstack[--stackidx], dereferencing the unvalidated stack.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences a jumpstack pointer expected to be valid but left NULL by the missing size check, matching CWE-476. The weakness is the unchecked jump-stack index/pointer, not merely an out-of-bounds index.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the jump path writes to jumpstack without bounding stackidx by private->stacksize, so a crafted rule blob containing a jump but no user-defined chains leaves jumpstack NULL. Trigger: a packet traversing such a rule causes the unchecked store, and a later XT_RETURN pops and dereferences the NULL pointer, producing a crash/DoS.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    while(bin)', '    numones = CLIP3(numones, 0, 16);'], 'added_lines': ['    while(bin && (numones <= 16))']}
description: A remote code execution vulnerability in libhevc in Mediaserver could enable an attacker using a specially crafted file to cause memory corruption during media file and data processing. This issue is rated as Critical due to the possibility of remote code execution within the context of the Mediaserver process. Product: Android. Versions: 5.0.2, 5.1.1, 6.0, 6.0.1, 7.0, 7.1.1. Android ID: A-33966031.

code_evidence: The while(bin) loop at [12] reads bypass bins and accumulates u4_sym += bin << numones++ at [15], incrementing numones without any bound on the shift count. After the loop, numones is clamped by CLIP3(numones, 0, 16) at [18], but the shift at [15] has already executed with the unclamped value.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unconstrained shift count causes an out-of-bounds write relative to the u4_sym buffer/word, matching CWE-119's improper restriction of operations within memory bounds. The fix moves the numones <= 16 check into the loop condition, confirming the missing bound is the root cause rather than a mere integer issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: When the decoded bypass bins keep bin nonzero for more than 32 iterations, numones exceeds the width of UWORD32/WORD32 and the shift bin << numones at [15] becomes undefined and writes outside the intended bit range of u4_sym. The clamp at [18] occurs too late to constrain the shift. The trigger is attacker-controlled bitstream data reaching this EGk decoder; the supported consequence is memory corruption leading to possible code execution.

commit_msg:
Prevent negative indent value in feed_table_block_tag()

Bug-Debian: https://github.com/tats/w3m/issues/88
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    if (tbl->indent < 0)', '\ttbl->indent = 0;', '\tif (offset < 0)', '\t    offset = 0;']}
description: w3m through 0.5.3 is prone to an infinite recursion flaw in HTMLlineproc0 because the feed_table_block_tag function in table.c does not prevent a negative indent value.

code_evidence: On the indent == -1 branch, mode->indent_level is decremented and tbl->indent is reduced by INDENT_INCR whenever mode->indent_level < MAX_INDENT_LEVEL, with no lower bound on tbl->indent.
offset is then copied from tbl->indent and further reduced by INDENT_INCR for HTML_DT; nothing clamps it, and the guarded block at lines 28-31 only runs when tbl->indent > 0.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-835 fits because the unchecked negative indent prevents the recursion in HTMLlineproc0 from reaching its exit condition, yielding a non-terminating loop. This is a termination/exit-condition defect, not merely an integer underflow, which alone would not describe the DoS.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: tbl->indent (and offset) can become negative because the decrement paths lack a lower-bound check. Repeated end-tag processing drives the indent below zero, so the positive-indent guard at line 28 never restores progress, and the caller's HTMLlineproc0 recursion does not terminate, consuming CPU. The missing constraint is the cause; resource exhaustion is the consequence.

commit_msg:
Fix wild free.

`huffdata` is initially allocated using `aligned_dealloc` but can be
replaced with `data2` which is allocated using `custom_calloc`.
This can cause a wild free when `aligned_dealloc(huffdata)` is called.
Fix by replacing allocation sites with aligned_alloc.

Noticed and fixed a similar problem with `hdrdata`.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    custom_free( hdrdata );'], 'added_lines': ['    aligned_dealloc( hdrdata );']}
description: Dropbox Lepton v1.2.1-185-g2a08b77 was discovered to contain a heap-buffer-overflow in the function aligned_dealloc():src/lepton/bitops.cc:108.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function's only write is a bounded copy (to_copy = min(len, hdrs - hpos)) into an abytewriter; the actual change is a free/dealloc mismatch, not an out-of-bounds write, so the function does not support CWE-787.

commit_msg:
patch 8.1.0633: crash when out of memory while opening a terminal window

Problem:    Crash when out of memory while opening a terminal window.
Solution:   Handle out-of-memory more gracefully.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  if(screen->buffers[1])', '    vterm_allocator_free(screen->vt, screen->buffers[1]);', '', ''], 'added_lines': ['  vterm_allocator_free(screen->vt, screen->buffers[1]);']}
description: libvterm through 0+bzr726, as used in Vim and other products, mishandles certain out-of-memory conditions, leading to a denial of service (application crash), related to screen.c, state.c, and vterm.c.

code_evidence: Unconditionally frees screen->buffers[0], which may be NULL when allocation failed during terminal window opening.
The guard if(screen->buffers[1]) protects the second buffer free, showing the code expects buffers[1] can be NULL but not buffers[0].
Frees screen itself, so any prior failure path leading here with a partially initialized screen is relevant.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function expects screen->buffers[0] to be valid but passes it to free without verifying it is non-NULL, directly matching CWE-476 (NULL Pointer Dereference). This is a missing NULL constraint, not a use-after-free.

evidence_lines.code: vterm_allocator_free(screen->vt, screen->buffers[0]);

if(screen->buffers[1])
vterm_allocator_free(screen->vt, screen->buffers[1]);
vterm_allocator_free(screen->vt, screen);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: vterm_screen_free dereferences screen and passes buffers[0] to the allocator without a NULL check, so an out-of-memory condition during screen setup leaves buffers[0] NULL. The allocator or dereference of that NULL pointer then crashes the application.

commit_msg: fixed #1883
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\tgf_isom_text_get_encoded_tx3g(tkHint->file, tkHint->TrackNum, i+1, GF_RTP_TX3G_SIDX_OFFSET, &tx3g, &tx3g_len);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\tGF_Err e;', '\t\t\te = gf_isom_text_get_encoded_tx3g(tkHint->file, tkHint->TrackNum, i+1, GF_RTP_TX3G_SIDX_OFFSET, &tx3g, &tx3g_len);', '\t\t\tif (e) {', '\t\t\t\tif (i) continue;', '\t\t\t\treturn GF_ISOM_INVALID_FILE;', '\t\t\t}']}
description: The gf_hinter_track_finalize function in GPAC 1.0.1 allows attackers to cause a denial of service via a crafted file in the MP4Box command.

code_evidence: The loop calls gf_isom_text_get_encoded_tx3g without checking its return value; if it fails, tx3g and tx3g_len are left uninitialized. Line 69 then passes tx3g and tx3g_len to gf_base64_encode, and line 70 frees tx3g, both using uninitialized values. The patched version captures the GF_Err and returns/continues on failure, confirming the missing check.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-908 fits because the code uses tx3g and tx3g_len without verifying they were initialized by the failed call, directly matching 'use of uninitialized resource'. This is not merely a null-pointer dereference; the values are undefined on the error path.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the return status of gf_isom_text_get_encoded_tx3g is ignored, so on error the output pointers tx3g/tx3g_len remain uninitialized. Trigger: a crafted MP4 file causing the tx3g encoding to fail. Consequence: gf_base64_encode reads uninitialized memory and gf_free frees an uninitialized pointer, leading to crash/denial of service (CWE-908 consequence).

commit_msg:
x86/spec-ctrl: Add spec-ctrl=unpriv-mmio

Per Xen's support statement, PCI passthrough should be to trusted domains
because the overall system security depends on factors outside of Xen's
control.

As such, Xen, in a supported configuration, is not vulnerable to DRPW/SBDR.

However, users who have risk assessed their configuration may be happy with
the risk of DoS, but unhappy with the risk of cross-domain data leakage.  Such
users should enable this option.

On CPUs vulnerable to MDS, the existing mitigations are the best we can do to
mitigate MMIO cross-domain data leakage.

On CPUs fixed to MDS but vulnerable MMIO stale data leakage, this option:

 * On CPUs susceptible to FBSDP, mitigates cross-domain fill buffer leakage
   using FB_CLEAR.
 * On CPUs susceptible to SBDR, mitigates RNG data recovery by engaging the
   srb-lock, previously used to mitigate SRBDS.

Both mitigations require microcode from IPU 2022.1, May 2022.

This is part of XSA-404.

Reviewed-by: Roger Pau Monné <roger.pau@citrix.com>

commit_msg:
The commit 47677e51e2a4("[media] em28xx: Only deallocate struct
em28xx after finishing all extensions") adds kref_get to many init
functions (e.g., em28xx_audio_init). However, kref_init is called too
late in em28xx_usb_probe, since em28xx_init_dev before will invoke
those init functions and call kref_get function. Then refcount bug
occurs in my local syzkaller instance.

Fix it by moving kref_init before em28xx_init_dev. This issue occurs
not only in dev but also dev->dev_next.

Fixes: 47677e51e2a4 ("[media] em28xx: Only deallocate struct em28xx after finishing all extensions")
Reported-by: syzkaller <syzkaller@googlegroups.com>
Signed-off-by: Dongliang Mu <mudongliangabcd@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Hans Verkuil <hverkuil-cisco@xs4all.nl>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['', '\t\tkref_init(&dev->dev_next->ref);', '\t}', '', '\tkref_init(&dev->ref);'], 'added_lines': ['\tkref_init(&dev->ref);', '', '\t\tkref_init(&dev->dev_next->ref);', '', '\t}']}
description: A flaw use after free in the Linux kernel video4linux driver was found in the way user triggers em28xx_usb_probe() for the Empia 28xx based TV cards. A local user could use this flaw to crash the system or potentially escalate their privileges on the system.

code_evidence: Line 130 calls em28xx_init_dev before any kref_init(&dev->ref); the reference is only initialized at line 214, after em28xx_init_dev has already run and invoked init functions (e.g., em28xx_audio_init) that call kref_get on the still-uninitialized refcount.
Similarly, em28xx_init_dev is called for dev->dev_next at lines 176-177 before kref_init(&dev->dev_next->ref) at line 212, so the secondary device's refcount is used uninitialized.
The late kref_init at lines 212/214 follows the earlier kref_get calls, leaving the refcount state inconsistent and allowing premature release of the em28xx structures.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect is an erroneous reference-count lifecycle that permits the em28xx object to be freed while still referenced, matching CWE-416 use after free. It is not merely an integer overflow or NULL dereference; the supported consequence is reuse of freed memory.

evidence_lines.code:
kref_init(&dev->dev_next->ref);
kref_init(&dev->ref);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: kref_init(&dev->ref) and kref_init(&dev->dev_next->ref) are performed after em28xx_init_dev, which already calls kref_get on those refcounts. The trigger is probing an em28xx device whose init path invokes kref_get; the resulting broken refcount leads to premature freeing and later use of the em28xx structures, causing the reported use-after-free/crash.

commit_msg: Add an HTTP/2 related rate limiting
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  if (cstate.get_received_ping_frame_count() > Http2::max_ping_frames_per_minute) {'], 'added_lines': ['  if (cstate.configured_max_ping_frames_per_minute != 0 &&', '      cstate.get_received_ping_frame_count() > cstate.configured_max_ping_frames_per_minute) {']}
description: The HTTP/2 protocol allows a denial of service (server resource consumption) because request cancellation can reset many streams quickly, as exploited in the wild in August through October 2023.

code_evidence: Each received PING frame increments the per-connection counter at line 15, and the only throttling gate at line 16 compares that counter against the fixed Http2::max_ping_frames_per_minute constant. There is no per-connection configurable limit or early rate check before the counter grows, so the enforcement threshold is global rather than tunable per connection.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function is the resource-tracking point for a protocol message and fails to properly bound throttling of that resource, matching CWE-400's 'lack of throttling for the number of allocated resources.' It is not merely a consequence report: the missing per-connection limit constraint is the defect.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: PING-frame processing increments a counter and enforces only a fixed constant rate limit, with no configurable per-connection throttle. Trigger: a peer sends many PING frames rapidly; the counter and associated processing/state grow until the fixed threshold (or indefinitely if the constant is large) is reached. Supported consequence: uncontrolled consumption of server CPU/memory resources, enabling denial of service.

commit_msg:
patch 9.0.0260: using freed memory when using 'quickfixtextfunc' recursively

Problem:    Using freed memory when using 'quickfixtextfunc' recursively.
Solution:   Do not allow for recursion.

description: Use After Free in GitHub repository vim/vim prior to 9.0.0260.

code_evidence: Line 13 allocates dictionary d and returns NULL on failure; on success d is later passed via args[0] to the user callback at line 24.

After the callback returns a list, line 28-29 copies rettv.vval.v_list into qftf_list and bumps its refcount, then line 33 unrefs d. A recursive callback re-entering this function can free or reallocate state that the outer invocation still references.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Re-entrant callback execution leads to a pointer being used after the memory it referenced was freed, which is exactly CWE-416 (Use After Free). A mere lack of a recursion limit would not by itself be a memory-safety weakness; the supported consequence here is use of freed memory.

evidence_lines.code:
if ((d = dict_alloc_lock(VAR_FIXED)) == NULL)
return NULL;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function invokes a user-supplied 'quickfixtextfunc' callback without guarding against recursion. A callback that re-enters quickfix text generation can free memory still referenced by the outer invocation, so subsequent use of that memory by the outer call operates on freed/reallocated storage.

commit_msg:
Mach-o defend against bad crafted input

https://github.com/upx/upx/issues/146
	modified:   p_mach.cpp
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        ptr += (unsigned) ((Mach_segment_command const *)ptr)->cmdsize;'], 'added_lines': ['        ptr += (unsigned) ((Mach_command const *)ptr)->cmdsize;']}
description: p_mach.cpp in UPX 3.94 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (invalid memory access and application crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted Mach-O file, related to canPack and unpack functions. NOTE: the vendor has stated "there is no security implication whatsoever.

code_evidence: ncmds is read from the decompressed Mach header (line 44) and used to allocate msegcmd (line 45). The loop iterates j < ncmds while advancing ptr by the cmdsize of each command (line 50); the only bound check occurs after the pointer has already been advanced (lines 51-52), and memcpy at line 48 reads sizeof(Mach_segment_command) bytes from ptr before validating that the command record is fully within the decompressed buffer. Crafted cmdsize values can make ptr advance past ph.u_len, so subsequent iterations read/dereference out-of-bounds memory.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-119 fits because the function performs memcpy reads and pointer dereferences on a memory buffer without ensuring the accessed locations remain within the intended ph.u_len boundary. The missing constraint on cmdsize relative to the buffer is the direct cause of out-of-bounds memory operations.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the command-walking loop trusts attacker-controlled cmdsize/ncmds and dereferences/reads ptr before confirming the current command lies within the ph.u_len buffer; the check is performed only after advancing. Trigger: a crafted Mach-O file whose compressed header decompresses to commands with oversized or inconsistent cmdsize. Consequence: out-of-bounds reads and invalid memory access, leading to crash or other memory-safety impact.

commit_msg:
Fix 697497: Ensure array length is positive.

As a side effect when changing to using regular integers (and avoid the
nightmare of mixing signed and unsigned) we accidentally allowed negative
array lengths.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\tif (newlen != rawlen)'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\tif (newlen != rawlen || newlen < 0)']}
description: An issue was discovered in Artifex Software, Inc. MuJS before 4006739a28367c708dea19aeb19b8a1a9326ce08. The jsR_setproperty function in jsrun.c lacks a check for a negative array length. This leads to an integer overflow in the js_pushstring function in jsrun.c when parsing a specially crafted JS file.

code_evidence: Line 9 converts the supplied 'length' value to a double; line 10 truncates it to an int newlen. Line 11 only rejects newlen when it differs from rawlen, so a negative integral value such as -1 passes validation and reaches jsV_resizearray at line 13 with a negative length.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because a negative array length admitted here feeds later integer arithmetic that can wrap, producing an incorrect size. This is distinct from a simple bounds-check omission: the missing sign constraint permits the overflow-producing value.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the array 'length' setter accepts a negative integer because the validation at line 11 checks only integrality, not sign. Trigger: parsing a crafted JS file that assigns a negative length to an array. The negative length is stored via jsV_resizearray, and downstream size/length arithmetic can overflow, yielding incorrect small values used in string handling.

commit_msg:
Bug #48427 UDN: Forbid vulnerable GET_DN for VERSION >= 3

UDL using PROTOCOL_3 must no longer use GET_DN but WAIT_DN - if it is
still used this is a protocol violation. UDL simply will not get an
answer.

When UCRV 'notifier/protocol/version is set to 3, any old client still
using PROTOCOL_2 will get rejected while negotiating the protocol
version, so it is asserted that "version >= network_procotol_version".
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t} else if ( !strncmp(network_line, "GET_DN ", strlen("GET_DN ")) && msg_id != UINT32_MAX && network_client_get_version(fd) > 0) {'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t} else if ( !strncmp(network_line, "GET_DN ", strlen("GET_DN ")) && msg_id != UINT32_MAX && version > PROTOCOL_UNKNOWN && version < PROTOCOL_3) {']}
description: Univention Corporate Server univention-directory-notifier 12.0.1-3 and earlier is affected by: CWE-213: Intentional Information Exposure. The impact is: Loss of Confidentiality. The component is: function data_on_connection() in src/callback.c. The attack vector is: network connectivity. The fixed version is: 12.0.1-4 and later.

code_evidence: The GET_DN branch is gated only by msg_id and network_client_get_version(fd) > 0; once entered it parses the requested id and answers with the DN (line 90/92) for cached or transaction DNs.

The version is initialized from the stored client version (line 10) and later overwritten from the Version: line (line 45), with lower versions rejected (49) and future versions clamped (52), then stored (56).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function explicitly sends DN data (sensitive directory information) to a requester whose negotiated protocol should not permit that request, matching CWE-200's exposure of information to an unauthorized actor. The bug is an over-permissive request gate, not a memory-safety or injection weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the GET_DN handler accepts the request whenever any positive protocol version is negotiated, including PROTOCOL_3 clients that are supposed to use WAIT_DN. Trigger: a network client negotiates version 3 and sends GET_DN with a valid MSGID; the server returns the DN data for the requested id. Supported consequence: directory DN information is exposed to a client that should not receive it under the newer protocol.

commit_msg:
x509: excessive resource use verifying policy constraints

A security vulnerability has been identified in all supported versions
of OpenSSL related to the verification of X.509 certificate chains
that include policy constraints.  Attackers may be able to exploit this
vulnerability by creating a malicious certificate chain that triggers
exponential use of computational resources, leading to a denial-of-service
(DoS) attack on affected systems.

Fixes CVE-2023-0464

Reviewed-by: Tomas Mraz <tomas@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Shane Lontis <shane.lontis@oracle.com>
(Merged from https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/20570)

description:
A security vulnerability has been identified in all supported versions

of OpenSSL related to the verification of X.509 certificate chains
that include policy constraints.  Attackers may be able to exploit this
vulnerability by creating a malicious certificate chain that triggers
exponential use of computational resources, leading to a denial-of-service

commit_msg:
PR22187, infinite loop in find_abstract_instance_name

This patch prevents the simple case of infinite recursion in
find_abstract_instance_name by ensuring that the attributes being
processed are not the same as the previous call.

The patch also does a little cleanup, and leaves in place some changes
to the nested_funcs array that I made when I wrongly thought looping
might occur in scan_unit_for_symbols.

	PR 22187
	* dwarf2.c (find_abstract_instance_name): Add orig_info_ptr and
	pname param.  Return status.  Make name const.  Don't abort,
	return an error.  Formatting.  Exit if current info_ptr matches
	orig_info_ptr.  Update callers.
	(scan_unit_for_symbols): Start at nesting_level of zero.  Make
	nested_funcs an array of structs for extensibility.  Formatting.

code_evidence: The loop at line 16 is controlled by nesting_level, initialized to 1 at line 7; it decreases only when abbrev_number is zero (lines 31-33). The loop condition 'while (nesting_level)' terminates only if nesting_level reaches zero.

commit_msg:
Kafka: Be more strict when dissecting varints.

The Kafka dissector uses the return value of tvb_get_varint to advance
the packet offset in many places. If tvb_get_varint fails it returns 0,
which means our offset isn't guaranteed to advance. Stop dissection
whenever that happens. Fixes #17811.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function contains no loop or iteration construct; it only returns a non-advancing offset on varint failure, so CWE-834 excessive iteration is not directly supported.
