commit_msg:
The 'num_elements' can be controlled by the guest but the
'vrend_vertex_element_array' has a fixed 'elements' field.
This can cause a heap overflow. Add sanity check of 'num_elements'.

Signed-off-by: Li Qiang <liq3ea@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Marc-André Lureau <marcandre.lureau@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Dave Airlie <airlied@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '   if (num_elements > PIPE_MAX_ATTRIBS)', '      return EINVAL;']}
description: Heap-based buffer overflow in the vrend_create_vertex_elements_state function in vrend_renderer.c in virglrenderer before 0.6.0 allows local guest OS users to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds array access and crash) via the num_elements parameter.

code_evidence: v->count is set to the caller-controlled num_elements without any upper-bound validation; the loop then copies elements[i] into v->elements[i], where elements is a fixed-size array in vrend_vertex_element_array, for every i < num_elements.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The loop writes to a memory location beyond the fixed elements buffer's intended boundary, matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds memory operation. The added PIPE_MAX_ATTRIBS check confirms the missing constraint; the more specific heap overflow is a consequence of this improper bounds restriction.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is the missing bound check on num_elements before indexing the fixed elements array. A guest supplying num_elements larger than the array capacity triggers the memcpy loop to write past v->elements, causing a heap out-of-bounds write and possible crash or memory corruption.

commit_msg:
If the target ring is configured with IOPOLL, then we always need to hold
the target ring uring_lock before posting CQEs. We could just grab it
unconditionally, but since we don't expect many target rings to be of this
type, make grabbing the uring_lock conditional on the ring type.

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/io-uring/Y8krlYa52%2F0YGqkg@ip-172-31-85-199.ec2.internal/
Reported-by: Xingyuan Mo <hdthky0@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (current->flags & PF_EXITING)', '\telse if (!io_post_aux_cqe(target_ctx, msg->user_data, msg->len, 0))', '\t\tret = -EOVERFLOW;'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (current->flags & PF_EXITING) {', '\t} else {', '\t\t/*', '\t\t * If the target ring is using IOPOLL mode, then we need to be', '\t\t * holding the uring_lock for posting completions. Other ring', '\t\t * types rely on the regular completion locking, which is', '\t\t * handled while posting.', '\t\t */', '\t\tif (target_ctx->flags & IORING_SETUP_IOPOLL)', '\t\t\tmutex_lock(&target_ctx->uring_lock);', '\t\tif (!io_post_aux_cqe(target_ctx, msg->user_data, msg->len, 0))', '\t\t\tret = -EOVERFLOW;', '\t\tif (target_ctx->flags & IORING_SETUP_IOPOLL)', '\t\t\tmutex_unlock(&target_ctx->uring_lock);', '\t}']}
description: A vulnerability was found due to missing lock for IOPOLL flaw in io_cqring_event_overflow() in io_uring.c in Linux Kernel. This flaw allows a local attacker with user privilege to trigger a Denial of Service threat.

code_evidence: The function posts an auxiliary CQE via io_post_aux_cqe(target_ctx, ...) without acquiring target_ctx->uring_lock, even though IOPOLL target rings require that lock to be held while posting completions. The only guard is the PF_EXITING check; there is no mutex_lock/mutex_unlock around the posting call.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-667 fits because the code performs a shared-resource operation (posting CQEs to an IOPOLL ring) without following the required locking discipline. A related race condition could be argued, but the direct defect is the missing lock acquisition for IOPOLL rings, which the patch adds.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the completion-posting path omits the required uring_lock for IOPOLL target rings. Trigger: a local user submits a message targeting an IOPOLL ring, causing io_post_aux_cqe to run without holding target_ctx->uring_lock, racing with the target ring's completion handling. Supported consequence: inconsistent ring state leading to a denial of service.

joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads outside the intended bounds of the types array via an unchecked index, matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds memory buffer read. It is not a plain null-dereference or type-confusion issue; the defect is the missing array element combined with unvalidated indexing.

evidence_lines.code:
static const njs_value_t  *types[NJS_VALUE_TYPE_MAX] = {
&njs_string_object,
&njs_string_object,
&njs_string_function,
&njs_string_object,
&njs_string_object,
&njs_string_object,
&njs_string_object,
&njs_string_object,
&njs_string_object,
vm->retval = *types[value->type];

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the typeof dispatch table lacks an entry for the DataView value type while being indexed by the full value->type range with no bounds check. Trigger: calling typeof on a DataView object yields a type index beyond the array's intended contents, so types[value->type] reads out of bounds. Supported consequence: out-of-bounds read of a pointer subsequently dereferenced into vm->retval, potentially crashing or exposing internal memory.

commit_msg:
Currently CONFIG_TIMER_STATS exposes process information across namespaces:

kernel/time/timer_list.c print_timer():

        SEQ_printf(m, ", %s/%d", tmp, timer->start_pid);

 #11: <0000000000000000>, hrtimer_wakeup, S:01, do_nanosleep, cron/2570

removes CONFIG_TIMER_STATS.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['', '#ifdef CONFIG_TIMER_STATS', '\ttimer->start_site = NULL;', '\ttimer->start_pid = -1;', '\tmemset(timer->start_comm, 0, TASK_COMM_LEN);', '#endif'], 'added_lines': []}
description: The time subsystem in the Linux kernel through 4.9.9, when CONFIG_TIMER_STATS is enabled, allows local users to discover real PID values (as distinguished from PID values inside a PID namespace) by reading the /proc/timer_list file, related to the print_timer function in kernel/time/timer_list.c and the __timer_stats_timer_set_start_info function in kernel/time/timer.c.

code_evidence: The CONFIG_TIMER_STATS block initializes timer->start_pid to -1 and clears start_comm/start_site, which are the fields later populated with process identity (real PID and comm) and exposed via /proc/timer_list. This function is the initialization site for those statistics fields, so the patch removing the block is the change that eliminates the exposure path's data source.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is explicit exposure of sensitive process-identity metadata to unprivileged local readers, matching CWE-200's 'code explicitly inserts sensitive information into resources accessible to unauthorized actors.' It is not a memory-safety flaw; the defect is the design that publishes real PIDs/comm through a world-readable interface.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: timer statistics fields (start_pid, start_comm, start_site) are maintained in the hrtimer structure and printed through /proc/timer_list without PID-namespace translation, so a local user reading that file learns real host PIDs and process names. Trigger: reading /proc/timer_list while CONFIG_TIMER_STATS is enabled. Consequence: disclosure of process identity across PID namespaces.

commit_msg:
Prevent stack overflow when FunctionLib in GraphDef has a self-recursive function.

It is likely that no recursivity is supported, but we should handle this separately.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 414860329
Change-Id: I02a2270e86282b37362ddd485eeef16fb986a9e0
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '      // Also check that there is no recursivity in the library', '      // TODO(mihaimaruseac): Do more than self-recursivity', '      TF_RETURN_IF_ERROR(ValidateFunctionNotRecursive(function));']}
description: Tensorflow is an Open Source Machine Learning Framework. The `GraphDef` format in TensorFlow does not allow self recursive functions. The runtime assumes that this invariant is satisfied. However, a `GraphDef` containing a fragment such as the following can be consumed when loading a `SavedModel`. This would result in a stack overflow during execution as resolving each `NodeDef` means resolving the function itself and its nodes. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.8.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.7.1, TensorFlow 2.6.3, and TensorFlow 2.5.3, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: ValidateSavedTensors iterates over every function in graph_def.library() and, for each, validates only the function's node_def() entries via ValidateNode. It never inspects or bounds function references among those nodes, so a function whose node references the enclosing function (self-recursion) passes validation unchanged.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-674 fits because the function fails to control recursion depth when validating library functions, and the accepted self-recursive definition leads to uncontrolled recursion at resolve time. This is the missing constraint, not merely a malformed-node issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the library loop performs no recursion/self-reference check, so a GraphDef containing a self-recursive FunctionDef is accepted. Trigger: loading a SavedModel whose function nodes resolve back to the same function; each NodeDef resolution re-enters the function. Supported consequence: unbounded recursion during execution exhausts the program stack (stack overflow/DoS).

commit_msg:
nfc: replace improper check device_is_registered() in netlink related functions

The device_is_registered() in nfc core is used to check whether
nfc device is registered in netlink related functions such as
nfc_fw_download(), nfc_dev_up() and so on. Although device_is_registered()
is protected by device_lock, there is still a race condition between
device_del() and device_is_registered(). The root cause is that
kobject_del() in device_del() is not protected by device_lock.

   (cleanup task)         |     (netlink task)
                          |
nfc_unregister_device     | nfc_fw_download
 device_del               |  device_lock
  ...                     |   if (!device_is_registered)//(1)
  kobject_del//(2)        |   ...
 ...                      |  device_unlock

The device_is_registered() returns the value of state_in_sysfs and
the state_in_sysfs is set to zero in kobject_del(). If we pass check in
position (1), then set zero in position (2). As a result, the check
in position (1) is useless.

This patch uses bool variable instead of device_is_registered() to judge
whether the nfc device is registered, which is well synchronized.

Fixes: 3e256b8f8dfa ("NFC: add nfc subsystem core")
Signed-off-by: Duoming Zhou <duoming@zju.edu.cn>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (!device_is_registered(&dev->dev)) {'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (dev->shutting_down) {']}
description: A use-after-free flaw was found in the Linux kernel's NFC core functionality due to a race condition between kobject creation and delete. This vulnerability allows a local attacker with CAP_NET_ADMIN privilege to leak kernel information.

code_evidence: nfc_disable_se() takes device_lock and then calls device_is_registered(&dev->dev) at line 7 as a guard before proceeding to dereference dev->dev_up and dev->ops. device_is_registered() reads state_in_sysfs, which is cleared by kobject_del() inside device_del() without holding device_lock.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function checks resource state (device_is_registered) and then uses the resource (dev->dev_up, dev->ops, se lookup, dev->ops->disable_se) while the state can change between check and use, matching CWE-367 TOCTOU. This is a race between the guard and subsequent use, not merely a missing lock around a single operation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the registration state checked under device_lock can be invalidated concurrently by nfc_unregister_device()/device_del(), because kobject_del() clears state_in_sysfs outside the lock. Trigger: a cleanup task unregisters the device while a netlink caller passes the check at line 7. The stale check lets execution continue against a device being torn down, supporting use-after-free/information leak consequences.

commit_msg:
Don't use sp<>&

because they may end up pointing to NULL after a NULL check was performed.

Bug: 28166152
Change-Id: Iab2ea30395b620628cc6f3d067dd4f6fcda824fe
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    const sp<IMediaPlayerService>& service(getMediaPlayerService());'], 'added_lines': ['    const sp<IMediaPlayerService> service(getMediaPlayerService());']}
description: libmedia in mediaserver in Android 4.x before 4.4.4, 5.0.x before 5.0.2, 5.1.x before 5.1.1, and 6.x before 2016-08-01 has certain incorrect declarations, which allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code or cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference or memory corruption) via a crafted media file, aka internal bug 28166152.

code_evidence: Line 4 binds the result of getMediaPlayerService() to a reference to an sp<IMediaPlayerService>; the reference may alias a temporary that is destroyed after the full expression, leaving it pointing to NULL. Line 5 checks service != NULL, but that check is not stable because the reference target can become NULL afterward. Line 6 then dereferences service via service->createMediaRecorder() after the check.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This is a NULL pointer dereference (CWE-476): a pointer is checked for NULL and then dereferenced, but the check is defeated by reference aliasing. It is not merely an uninitialized or dangling pointer issue; the exploitable operation is the NULL dereference at service->createMediaRecorder().
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: holding the smart-pointer result by reference rather than by value allows the referenced sp to become NULL after the NULL check. Trigger: getMediaPlayerService() returns a temporary whose lifetime ends at the end of line 4. Consequence: the service-> call can dereference a NULL pointer, causing a crash (DoS) and, in the described media context, possible memory-corruption impact.

commit_msg:
Consider the exit family when applying guard restrictions.

When the new path selection logic went into place, I accidentally
dropped the code that considered the _family_ of the exit node when
deciding if the guard was usable, and we didn't catch that during
code review.

This patch makes the guard_restriction_t code consider the exit
family as well, and adds some (hopefully redundant) checks for the
case where we lack a node_t for a guard but we have a bridge_info_t
for it.

Fixes bug 22753; bugfix on 0.3.0.1-alpha. Tracked as TROVE-2016-006
and CVE-2017-0377.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  // Only one kind of restriction exists right now'], 'added_lines': ['  // Only one kind of restriction exists right now: excluding an exit', '  // ID and all of its family.', '  const node_t *node = node_get_by_id((const char*)rst->exclude_id);', '  if (node && guard_in_node_family(guard, node))', '    return 0;', '']}
description: Tor 0.3.x before 0.3.0.9 has a guard-selection algorithm that only considers the exit relay (not the exit relay's family), which might allow remote attackers to defeat intended anonymity properties by leveraging the existence of large families.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function implements guard-restriction logic (identity/family comparison) whose flaw is anonymity degradation, not explicit exposure of sensitive information; no disclosure of data to an unauthorized actor is shown in the function.

commit_msg: Fix potential BMP stack overflow (Issue #453)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  {', '  }', '  else if (colors_used > 256)', '    return (-1);']}
description: A stack-based buffer overflow in image_load_bmp() in HTMLDOC <= 1.9.13 results in remote code execution if the victim converts an HTML document linking to a crafted BMP file.

code_evidence: Line 19 declares a fixed local buffer colormap[256][4] on the stack.
Line 35 reads colors_used as an attacker-controlled 32-bit DWORD from the BMP header with no upper bound.
Lines 42-44: colors_used is only defaulted when zero and depth<=8; otherwise the raw value is passed as the element count to fread into colormap, so colors_used>256 overflows the 256-entry buffer.
Lines 55-58 later index colormap[color] for color=colors_used-1, also out of bounds when colors_used exceeds 256.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes past the end of the intended stack buffer colormap due to an unchecked size derived from input, which is precisely CWE-787 (out-of-bounds write). The patch's added colors_used>256 check confirms the missing bound; this is the write itself rather than a mere read overrun.

evidence_lines.code: ucharcolormap[256][4];
colors_used      = (int)read_dword(fp);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the BMP header field colors_used is trusted without an upper bound, so fread writes colors_used*4 bytes into the fixed 256x4 stack buffer colormap. A crafted BMP with a large colors_used triggers a stack-based out-of-bounds write, corrupting adjacent stack memory and enabling remote code execution or crash when the image is loaded.

commit_msg:
prismpaint: Fixed a buffer overrun bug

Ref: GitHub issue #52
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tfor(i=0; i<d->pal_size; i++) {', '\t\tif(i<256) {', '\t\t\tpal1[i] = clr;', '\t\t}', '\tfor(i=0; i<d->pal_size; i++) {'], 'added_lines': ['\ti64 num_entries_to_read;', '\tnum_entries_to_read = de_min_int(d->pal_size, 256);', '\tfor(i=0; i<num_entries_to_read; i++) {', '\t\tpal1[i] = clr;', '\tfor(i=0; i<num_entries_to_read; i++) {']}
description: Deark v.1.6.2 was discovered to contain a stack overflow via the do_prism_read_palette() function at /modules/atari-img.c.

code_evidence: pal1 is a fixed 256-element u32 array [6]. The first loop iterates i up to d->pal_size [10], and the conditional write pal1[i] = clr [22] is guarded only by i<256 [21], so when d->pal_size exceeds 256 the guard prevents the write but the loop continues.
The second loop [25] again iterates to d->pal_size and writes d->pal[i] [26] using an index derived from i, exceeding the destination palette buffer when pal_size is large.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes palette data past the end of fixed-size buffers due to unchecked loop bounds, which is exactly an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). It is not merely an out-of-bounds read, since the defect is the memory-modifying store.

evidence_lines.code:
for(i=0; i<d->pal_size; i++) {
d->pal[i] = pal1[map_vdi_pal(adata->bpp, (unsigned int)i)];

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: loop bounds are taken from the attacker-influenced d->pal_size without clamping to the fixed 256-entry pal1 array and the d->pal buffer size. Trigger: a crafted Atari image with pal_size > 256. Consequence: out-of-bounds writes to pal1 (mitigated only partially by the i<256 check) and to d->pal, causing stack/buffer overflow and possible code execution or crash.

commit_msg: Fix integer overflows and harden memory allocator.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['checked_xmalloc (size_t size)', '    alloc_limit_assert ("checked_xmalloc", size);', '    return xmalloc (size);'], 'added_lines': ['checked_xmalloc (size_t num, size_t size)', '    size_t res;', '    if (check_mul_overflow(num, size, &res))', '        abort();', '', '    alloc_limit_assert ("checked_xmalloc", res);', '    return xmalloc (num, size);']}
description: An issue was discovered in tnef before 1.4.13. Several Integer Overflows, which can lead to Heap Overflows, have been identified in the functions that wrap memory allocation.

code_evidence: The function accepts a single size_t size and passes it directly to alloc_limit_assert and xmalloc without any arithmetic or bounds validation. No multiplication or size computation occurs inside this function, so no integer overflow can be triggered here.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 requires a calculation that can wrap to a smaller value. This function contains no such arithmetic; the fix adds check_mul_overflow to a new two-argument signature, which is not present in the analyzed func. The overflow is introduced by callers multiplying num by size, so this function alone does not directly support CWE-190.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: This pre-patch function performs no calculation on its argument; it simply forwards size to the allocator. The integer overflow described in the commit arises in callers that compute an allocation size from multiple factors, not within checked_xmalloc itself. The function only applies a limit assertion and allocation, so it neither causes nor guards against a wraparound.

commit_msg: fix multiple memory leak in ReadYUVImage
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      ThrowReaderException(ResourceLimitError,"MemoryAllocationFailed");', '      ThrowReaderException(ResourceLimitError,"MemoryAllocationFailed");'], 'added_lines': ['      {', '        scanline=(unsigned char *) RelinquishMagickMemory(scanline); ', '        ThrowReaderException(ResourceLimitError,"MemoryAllocationFailed");', '      }', '            scanline=(unsigned char *) RelinquishMagickMemory(scanline); ', '            scanline=(unsigned char *) RelinquishMagickMemory(scanline); ', '              scanline=(unsigned char *) RelinquishMagickMemory(scanline); ', '      {', '        scanline=(unsigned char *) RelinquishMagickMemory(scanline);   ', '        ThrowReaderException(ResourceLimitError,"MemoryAllocationFailed");', '      }', '            scanline=(unsigned char *) RelinquishMagickMemory(scanline); ']}
description: ImageMagick version 7.0.7-2 contains a memory leak in ReadYUVImage in coders/yuv.c.

code_evidence: scanline is allocated once via AcquireQuantumMemory before the do-loop and only released at line 372 after the loop completes.
If CloneImage returns NULL at line 94, ThrowReaderException jumps out without releasing scanline, leaking the buffer.
If OpenBlob fails at line 106 during PartitionInterlace, the function destroys the image list and returns at line 109, skipping the RelinquishMagickMemory at line 372.
If ResizeImage returns NULL at line 318, ThrowReaderException exits without freeing scanline.
If AcquireNextImage yields no next image at line 360, the function returns at line 363 without freeing scanline.
The single cleanup at line 372 is bypassed by every early-return path above.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-772 fits because the allocated scanline resource outlives its effective use on error paths and is never released. This is a missing-release weakness, not a buffer overflow or use-after-free; the defect is the absent deallocation on early exits.

evidence_lines.code: scanline=(unsigned char *) RelinquishMagickMemory(scanline);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: scanline is a long-lived allocation whose release is placed only on the normal exit path. Trigger: any allocation, blob-open, resize, or image-list failure inside the loop causes an early return or exception throw. Consequence: the scanline buffer is leaked, and repeated malformed or resource-constrained inputs can exhaust memory (DoS).

commit_msg:
x86/spec-ctrl: Mitigate Speculative Return Stack Overflow

On native, synthesise the SRSO bits by probing various hardware properties as
given by AMD.

Extend the IBPB-on-entry mitigations to Zen3/4 CPUs.  There is a microcode
prerequisite to make this an effective mitigation.

This is part of XSA-434 / CVE-2023-20569

Signed-off-by: Andrew Cooper <andrew.cooper3@citrix.com>
Reviewed-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Reviewed-by: Roger Pau Monné <roger.pau@citrix.com>
diff_func:
--- func_before
+++ func_after
@@ -25,6 +25,15 @@
          * Confusion.  Mitigate with IBPB-on-entry.
          */
         if ( !boot_cpu_has(X86_FEATURE_BTC_NO) )
+            def_ibpb_entry = true;
+
+        /*
+         * Further to BTC, Zen3/4 CPUs suffer from Speculative Return Stack
+         * Overflow in most configurations.  Mitigate with IBPB-on-entry if we
+         * have the microcode that makes this an effective option.
+         */
+        if ( !boot_cpu_has(X86_FEATURE_SRSO_NO) &&
+             boot_cpu_has(X86_FEATURE_IBPB_BRTYPE) )
             def_ibpb_entry = true;
     }
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['            def_ibpb_entry = true;', '', '        /*', '         * Further to BTC, Zen3/4 CPUs suffer from Speculative Return Stack', '         * Overflow in most configurations.  Mitigate with IBPB-on-entry if we', '         * have the microcode that makes this an effective option.', '         */', '        if ( !boot_cpu_has(X86_FEATURE_SRSO_NO) &&', '             boot_cpu_has(X86_FEATURE_IBPB_BRTYPE) )']}
description: A side channel vulnerability on some of the AMD CPUs may allow an attacker to influence the return address prediction. This may result in speculative execution at an attacker-controlled address, potentially leading to information disclosure.

code_evidence: For AMD/HYGON CPUs, lines 12-13 force X86_BUG_IBPB_NO_RET when IBPB_RET is absent, and lines 14-15 set def_ibpb_entry when BTC_NO is absent, enabling the IBPB-on-entry mitigation path used later at lines 17-27.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-203 fits because the root weakness is a timing/behavioral discrepancy observable to an unauthorized actor (speculative execution side channel), addressed here by mitigation selection. It is not a direct memory-safety flaw; the observable discrepancy enables information disclosure.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function selects IBPB-on-entry mitigation based on CPU feature probing. On affected AMD CPUs lacking BTC_NO (and later SRSO_NO with IBPB_BRTYPE), the mitigation is enabled; if features are misdetected or microcode prerequisites unmet, the side-channel state remains observable to an attacker, enabling speculative return-address prediction and potential information disclosure.

commit_msg:
Fix inappropriate fetch of entities content

For https://bugzilla.gnome.org/show_bug.cgi?id=761430

libfuzzer regression testing exposed another case where the parser would
fetch content of an external entity while not in validating mode.
Plug that hole
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t    xmlLoadEntityContent(ctxt, ent);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t    /*', '\t\t     * Note: external parsed entities will not be loaded,', '\t\t     * it is not required for a non-validating parser to', '\t\t     * complete external PEreferences coming from the', '\t\t     * internal subset', '\t\t     */', '\t\t    if (((ctxt->options & XML_PARSE_NOENT) != 0) ||', '\t\t\t((ctxt->options & XML_PARSE_DTDVALID) != 0) ||', '\t\t\t(ctxt->validate != 0)) {', '\t\t\txmlLoadEntityContent(ctxt, ent);', '\t\t    } else {', '\t\t\txmlWarningMsg(ctxt, XML_ERR_ENTITY_PROCESSING,', '\t\t  "not validating will not read content for PE entity %s\\n",', '\t\t                      ent->name, NULL);', '\t\t    }']}
description: XML external entity (XXE) vulnerability in the xmlStringLenDecodeEntities function in parser.c in libxml2 before 2.9.4, when not in validating mode, allows context-dependent attackers to read arbitrary files or cause a denial of service (resource consumption) via unspecified vectors.

code_evidence: At line 98 the parser resolves an input '%' PE reference to an entity via xmlParseStringPEReference. Lines 104-107 then, when ent->content is NULL, unconditionally call xmlLoadEntityContent(ctxt, ent) without checking whether the parser is in validating mode or whether XML_PARSE_NOENT/XML_PARSE_DTDVALID is set. The entity's external content is therefore fetched based solely on attacker-controlled document input.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function fails to validate the parser's processing state (validating mode / XML_PARSE_NOENT / XML_PARSE_DTDVALID) before acting on input, allowing unsafe processing of untrusted entity references. This is improper input/state validation (CWE-20); the external-entity read is the consequence, not a distinct validation of entity content.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the parser processes an attacker-supplied parameter-entity reference and loads external entity content without requiring validating mode or explicit entity-loading options. Trigger: a crafted XML document containing a '%' PE reference to an external entity while not in validating mode. Consequence: the parser fetches external content, enabling file disclosure or resource-consumption DoS.

commit_msg: Fixed: check cookie injection
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '    if (http_has_crlf(value, value_len)) {', '        RETURN_FALSE;', '    }', '']}
description: A HTTP response header injection vulnerability in Swoole v4.5.2 allows attackers to execute arbitrary code via supplying a crafted URL.

code_evidence: Before the patch, only the cookie name is validated against the special-element set (line 23); the value is never checked.

The non-encoded branch (line 41) concatenates the externally supplied value directly into the cookie header via snprintf (line 44), with no CRLF/control-character filtering, so the value reaches the downstream HTTP header verbatim.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-74 fits because the function builds part of an output record (the Set-Cookie header) from externally influenced input without neutralizing special elements that the downstream HTTP parser interprets. The missing http_has_crlf check on value is the concrete neutralization gap; the weakness is injection into a downstream component, not the encoding itself.

description: An attacker can modify the address to point to trusted memory to overwrite arbitrary trusted memory. It is recommended to update past 0.6.2 or git commit https://github.com/google/asylo/commit/53ed5d8fd8118ced1466e509606dd2f473707a5c

code_evidence: After Malloc, the untrusted input pointer and size are read directly from sgx_params (lines 20-21) for the IsOutsideEnclave check, then the same sgx_params->input field is reread at line 25 for Serialize. Because sgx_params lives in untrusted memory, the attacker can change sgx_params->input between the check and the use, so Serialize writes to an address that was never validated.

This is the resource-exposure pattern of CWE-668; TOCTOU (CWE-367) is the mechanism, but the supported consequence is exposure of trusted memory to the wrong sphere.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: a security-relevant pointer is read from an untrusted structure both for the boundary check and for the subsequent write, so the check and use are not atomic over the same value. Trigger: an attacker racing to overwrite sgx_params->input after IsOutsideEnclave passes. Consequence: Serialize writes attacker-chosen data into trusted enclave memory, crossing the intended trust boundary.

description: The printDefineFont2 function (util/listfdb.c) in libming through 0.4.8 is vulnerable to a heap-based buffer overflow, which may allow attackers to cause a denial of service or unspecified other impact via a crafted FDB file.

code_evidence: nGlyphs is read directly from the crafted FDB file via readUInt16(f) and used as the element count for malloc(nGlyphs*sizeof(int)); the multiplication can also overflow, producing a smaller allocation than needed.
The loop iterates i from 0 to nGlyphs-1 and writes offset[i] = off-nGlyphs*4-4 on each iteration, with no bound check tying the loop to the actual allocated size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes attacker-influenced data beyond the bounds of a heap allocation, matching CWE-787's out-of-bounds write. The root cause is the missing size validation/integer-overflow guard, not merely an out-of-bounds read, so CWE-787 fits rather than CWE-125.

nGlyphs = readUInt16(f);
offset = (unsigned int *)malloc(nGlyphs*sizeof(int));

for(i=0; i<nGlyphs; ++i)
offset[i] = off-nGlyphs*4-4;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: an untrusted glyph count controls both the allocation size and the write-loop bound without validation. Trigger: a crafted FDB file supplies a large nGlyphs (or one causing integer overflow in nGlyphs*sizeof(int)), so the loop writes offset[i] past the end of the heap buffer. Consequence: heap-based out-of-bounds write, enabling memory corruption, denial of service, or possibly further impact.

commit_msg:
Always generate DH keys for ephemeral DH cipher suites

Modified version of the commit ffaef3f15 in the master branch by Stephen
Henson. This makes the SSL_OP_SINGLE_DH_USE option a no-op and always
generates a new DH key for every handshake regardless.

CVE-2016-0701 (fix part 2 or 2)

Issue reported by Antonio Sanso

Reviewed-by: Viktor Dukhovni <viktor@openssl.org>

description: The DH_check_pub_key function in crypto/dh/dh_check.c in OpenSSL 1.0.2 before 1.0.2f does not ensure that prime numbers are appropriate for Diffie-Hellman (DH) key exchange, which makes it easier for remote attackers to discover a private DH exponent by making multiple handshakes with a peer that chose an inappropriate number, as demonstrated by a number in an X9.42 file.

code_evidence: When SSL_OP_SINGLE_DH_USE is unset and dhp already holds pub_key/priv_key, the else branch copies the static DH keys with BN_dup into the per-handshake dh instead of generating fresh ones.
The condition at line 94 gates key regeneration on an option flag, so the default path reuses the same private DH exponent across handshakes.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is explicit reuse of secret key material that becomes observable to a remote unauthorized actor, matching CWE-200's exposure of sensitive information. The cause is the flawed key-reuse behavior, not merely a downstream confidentiality impact.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the server reuses a fixed DH private/public key pair across handshakes unless SSL_OP_SINGLE_DH_USE is set, rather than always generating an ephemeral key. Trigger: a peer performs multiple handshakes with the same peer parameters, allowing private-exponent recovery through repeated observations. Consequence: the server's DH private exponent is exposed, enabling decryption of past/future sessions (confidentiality loss).

description: An exploitable heap buffer overflow vulnerability exists in the data structure persistence functionality of OpenCV, before version 4.2.0. A specially crafted JSON file can cause a buffer overflow, resulting in multiple heap corruptions and potentially code execution. An attacker can provide a specially crafted file to trigger this vulnerability.

code_evidence: The string-parsing loop copies each segment into the fixed buffer `buf` at offset `i` via `memcpy(buf + i, beg, sz)` and then advances `i += sz`, without any check that `i + sz` stays within the buffer capacity.
On the '\\0' case, another `memcpy(buf + i, beg, sz); i += sz;` appends the segment before fetching the next line, again with no bound check on `i`.

The '"' case performs the same unchecked `memcpy(buf + i, beg, sz); i += sz;` append, and escape handling writes single bytes via `buf[i++] = *ptr` (e.g., lines 131-136), with no capacity check before each increment.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes attacker-controlled data past the end of the intended buffer `buf`, which is exactly CWE-787 (Out-of-bounds Write). The missing length check before `memcpy`/indexed writes is the direct cause; this is a write overflow, not merely an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125).
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the parser accumulates decoded string content into a fixed-size buffer `buf` using an index `i` that is never validated against the buffer size before `memcpy`/`buf[i++]`. Trigger: a crafted JSON string with many characters or escape sequences causes `i` to grow past the buffer capacity, and the subsequent write goes out of bounds. Consequence: heap buffer overflow and memory corruption, potentially leading to code execution.

commit_msg:
Patch series "Fix several device private page reference counting issues",
v2

This series aims to fix a number of page reference counting issues in
drivers dealing with device private ZONE_DEVICE pages.  These result in
use-after-free type bugs, either from accessing a struct page which no
longer exists because it has been removed or accessing fields within the
struct page which are no longer valid because the page has been freed.

During normal usage it is unlikely these will cause any problems.  However
without these fixes it is possible to crash the kernel from userspace. 
These crashes can be triggered either by unloading the kernel module or
unbinding the device from the driver prior to a userspace task exiting. 
In modules such as Nouveau it is also possible to trigger some of these
issues by explicitly closing the device file-descriptor prior to the task
exiting and then accessing device private memory.

This involves some minor changes to both PowerPC and AMD GPU code. 
Unfortunately I lack hardware to test either of those so any help there
would be appreciated.  The changes mimic what is done in for both Nouveau
and hmm-tests though so I doubt they will cause problems.


This patch (of 8):

When the CPU tries to access a device private page the migrate_to_ram()
callback associated with the pgmap for the page is called.  However no
reference is taken on the faulting page.  Therefore a concurrent migration
of the device private page can free the page and possibly the underlying
pgmap.  This results in a race which can crash the kernel due to the
migrate_to_ram() function pointer becoming invalid.  It also means drivers
can't reliably read the zone_device_data field because the page may have
been freed with memunmap_pages().

Close the race by getting a reference on the page while holding the ptl to
ensure it has not been freed.  Unfortunately the elevated reference count
will cause the migration required to handle the fault to fail.  To avoid
this failure pass the faulting page into the migrate_vma functions so that
if an elevated reference count is found it can be checked to see if it's
expected or not.

description: A vulnerability was found in Linux Kernel. It has been classified as problematic. Affected is an unknown function of the file mm/memory.c of the component Driver Handler. The manipulation leads to use after free. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue. The identifier of this vulnerability is VDB-211020.

code_evidence: migrate_vma_check_page takes a page and computes an expected extra reference count; the function only validates the reference count before migration proceeds.
For zone-device pages an additional reference is assumed (extra++), but the function does not itself acquire a reference on the page.

The check compares page_count(page) - extra against page_mapcount(page); if the count matches the assumption it returns true, allowing migration to proceed while no caller-held reference guarantees the page stays alive.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the function's reference-count check permits continued use of a page that can be freed concurrently, i.e., memory is referenced after release. This is a use-after-free, not merely an integer/refcount arithmetic error, since the consequence is invalid access to freed page structures.

if (is_zone_device_page(page))

Trigger: CPU fault on a device private page racing with migration. Consequence: use-after-free of struct page / pgmap, leading to kernel crash or invalid function-pointer use.

Track xhci_kick_epctx processing being active in a variable.  Check the
variable before calling xhci_kick_epctx from xhci_kick_ep.  Add an
assert to make sure we don't call recursively into xhci_kick_epctx.

description: QEMU (aka Quick Emulator), when built with USB xHCI controller emulator support, allows local guest OS privileged users to cause a denial of service (infinite recursive call) via vectors involving control transfer descriptors sequencing.

code_evidence: The function has no guard against re-entry: after the trace at line 11 it proceeds directly into setup/ring processing, and the main loop at line 71 repeatedly fetches TRBs and fires transfers.

Inside the loop, control transfers are fired via xhci_fire_ctl_transfer (line 87) and other transfers via xhci_fire_transfer (line 89); these can synchronously call back into xhci_kick_epctx (via xhci_kick_ep) before the loop makes progress, re-entering the same epctx.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This matches CWE-835: the loop at line 71 plus recursive re-entry forms an iteration whose exit condition is never reached, consuming CPU until the guest causes a DoS. A simple bounded loop bug would not fit; the recursion-driven non-termination is the distinguishing feature.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: xhci_kick_epctx lacks a re-entrancy guard, so a control transfer fired inside its loop can recursively invoke xhci_kick_epctx on the same endpoint. The recursion is triggered by guest-controlled control transfer descriptor sequencing, producing unbounded recursion/iteration and a host CPU denial of service.

description: When sending malicous data to kernel by ioctl cmd FBIOPUT_VSCREENINFO,kernel will write memory out of bounds.

code_evidence: The charcount check rejects values other than 256 or 512 before any sizing or copy occurs.

size is computed from h, pitch and charcount, then new_data is allocated with that size and filled by a loop copying h*pitch bytes per character from data. The copy count and destination size depend on the same font-supplied dimensions, so a font whose height exceeds the screen resolution can drive the allocation/copy relationship out of bounds.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes font data into a heap buffer sized from font dimensions; unvalidated dimensions cause writes beyond that buffer, matching CWE-787 Out-of-bounds Write. A mere integer issue is not indicated; the defect is the missing size constraint relative to the screen and the resulting copy overflow.

evidence_lines.code:
if (charcount != 256 && charcount != 512)
return -EINVAL;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: font width/height from the user-supplied console_font are not constrained against the current screen resolution before CALC_FONTSZ and the per-character memcpy. Trigger: an ioctl setting a font larger than the screen. Consequence: allocation and copy sizes derived from unchecked dimensions lead to out-of-bounds memory writes, as described by KASAN reports.

commit_msg: Fixed bug #71331 - Uninitialized pointer in phar_make_dirstream()
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\tif (entry.filename_len == UINT_MAX) {'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\tif (entry.filename_len == UINT_MAX || entry.filename_len == 0) {']}
description: The phar_make_dirstream function in ext/phar/dirstream.c in PHP before 5.6.18 and 7.x before 7.0.3 mishandles zero-size ././@LongLink files, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (uninitialized pointer dereference) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted TAR archive.

code_evidence: When a TAR header has typeflag 'L' (GNU longlink), entry.filename_len is set from entry.uncompressed_filesize; the check only rejects UINT_MAX, so a zero-length longlink passes. pemalloc(0+1) is called and php_stream_read(fp, entry.filename, 0) returns 0, matching filename_len, so the error path at 138 is skipped and filename[0]='\0' is written.

After the longlink branch, last_was_longlink is reset at 205 and phar_add_virtual_dirs(myphar, entry.filename, entry.filename_len) is called with a zero-length name; the subsequent entry is parsed without a valid longlink name.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing zero-size guard allows a pointer-derived filename to be accessed without being initialized with meaningful data, matching CWE-824 access of an uninitialized pointer. This is distinct from a simple buffer overflow; the flaw is the unvalidated zero-length longlink leading to use of uninitialized pointer content.

evidence_lines.code:
last_was_longlink = 0;
phar_add_virtual_dirs(myphar, entry.filename, entry.filename_len TSRMLS_CC);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the longlink size check omits the zero-length case, so a crafted TAR 'L' entry with size 0 yields a filename buffer that is never filled with a real name. Trigger: a remote attacker supplies a zero-size ././@LongLink entry. Supported consequence: downstream use of the empty/uninitialized name path leads to a null or uninitialized pointer dereference, causing denial of service (bug 71331).

commit_msg:
nfsd: fix undefined behavior in nfsd4_layout_verify

  UBSAN: Undefined behaviour in fs/nfsd/nfs4proc.c:1262:34
  shift exponent 128 is too large for 32-bit type 'int'

Depending on compiler+architecture, this may cause the check for
layout_type to succeed for overly large values (which seems to be the
case with amd64). The large value will be later used in de-referencing
nfsd4_layout_ops for function pointers.

Reported-by: Jani Tuovila <tuovila@synopsys.com>
Signed-off-by: Ari Kauppi <ari@synopsys.com>
[colin.king@canonical.com: use LAYOUT_TYPE_MAX instead of 32]
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Reviewed-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Reviewed-by: Christoph Hellwig <hch@lst.de>
Signed-off-by: J. Bruce Fields <bfields@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (!(exp->ex_layout_types & (1 << layout_type))) {'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (layout_type >= LAYOUT_TYPE_MAX ||', '\t    !(exp->ex_layout_types & (1 << layout_type))) {']}
description: The NFSv4 server in the Linux kernel before 4.11.3 does not properly validate the layout type when processing the NFSv4 pNFS GETDEVICEINFO or LAYOUTGET operand in a UDP packet from a remote attacker. This type value is uninitialized upon encountering certain error conditions. This value is used as an array index for dereferencing, which leads to an OOPS and eventually a DoS of knfsd and a soft-lockup of the whole system.

code_evidence: Line 8 uses the caller-supplied layout_type directly as a shift amount in (1 << layout_type) without bounding it to a valid range. Lines 9-11 only report and return NULL when the resulting bit test fails; no check rejects an out-of-range layout_type.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-129 fits: an untrusted value is used as an array index (nfsd4_layout_ops[layout_type]) and as a shift operand without validating it lies within bounds, and the flawed check permits out-of-range indices. This is an index-validation flaw, not merely a missing-length or integer-overflow issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: layout_type from the remote NFSv4 request is never validated against the valid layout-type range before being used as a shift amount and array index. A value >= the bit width makes the shift undefined, so the membership test can incorrectly pass; the value then flows to nfsd4_layout_ops[layout_type] (line 13), an out-of-bounds index. Trigger: attacker sends an oversized layout type. Consequence: out-of-bounds function-pointer dereference, causing an OOPS and knfsd DoS.

commit_msg:
fix writev regression: pan hanging unkillable and un-straceable

Frederik Himpe reported an unkillable and un-straceable pan process.

Zero length iovecs can go into an infinite loop in writev, because the
iovec iterator does not always advance over them.

The sequence required to trigger this is not trivial. I think it
requires that a zero-length iovec be followed by a non-zero-length iovec
which causes a pagefault in the atomic usercopy. This causes the writev
code to drop back into single-segment copy mode, which then tries to
copy the 0 bytes of the zero-length iovec; a zero length copy looks like
a failure though, so it loops.

Put a test into iov_iter_advance to catch zero-length iovecs. We could
just put the test in the fallback path, but I feel it is more robust to
skip over zero-length iovecs throughout the code (iovec iterator may be
used in filesystems too, so it should be robust).

Signed-off-by: Nick Piggin <npiggin@suse.de>
Signed-off-by: Ingo Molnar <mingo@elte.hu>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tiov_iter_advance(i, copied);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tiov_iter_advance(i, copied);']}
description: mm/filemap.c in the Linux kernel before 2.6.25 allows local users to cause a denial of service (infinite loop) via a writev system call that triggers an iovec of zero length, followed by a page fault for an iovec of nonzero length.

code_evidence: Line 32 copies user data into the page via iov_iter_copy_from_user_atomic; line 39 replaces 'copied' with the write_end status. If 'copied' becomes 0 (line 41), the code recomputes 'bytes' from iov_iter_single_seg_count(i) (lines 42-43) and jumps back to 'again' (line 44), never advancing the iovec iterator. Because iov_iter_advance(i, copied) is only reached at line 46 after the zero-copy branch, a zero-length iovec is never consumed.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function fails to validate that the iovec length is non-zero before entering the retry path, so a zero-length input is mishandled rather than rejected or skipped, matching CWE-20's improper validation of input properties (length). The DoS follows from this missing length constraint, not from a buffer overflow or memory-safety defect.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the loop assumes a zero-byte copy is a transient failure and retries the same iovec, but a zero-length iovec legitimately yields copied==0 and the iterator does not advance over it. Trigger: a writev with a zero-length iovec followed by a non-zero iovec causing a page fault in the atomic usercopy path. Consequence: infinite loop in generic_perform_write, causing an unkillable, un-straceable process and CPU-exhaustion DoS.

jp2_dec: fix `numchans` mixup

When iterating over `dec->cdef->data.cdef.ents`, we need to use its
`numchans` variable, not the one in `jp2_dec_t`.

Fixes CVE-2018-19543
Fixes CVE-2017-9782

Closes https://github.com/jasper-maint/jasper/issues/13
Closes https://github.com/jasper-maint/jasper/issues/18
Closes https://github.com/mdadams/jasper/issues/140

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tfor (i = 0; i < dec->numchans; ++i) {'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tfor (i = 0; i < dec->cdef->data.cdef.numchans; ++i) {']}
description: JasPer 2.0.12 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (heap-based buffer over-read and application crash) via a crafted image, related to the jp2_decode function in libjasper/jp2/jp2_dec.c.

code_evidence: Line 178 creates a color-management profile from an attacker-supplied ICC profile; line 179 asserts the returned pointer is non-null, aborting if profile creation failed.

Lines 254-261 iterate over CDEF channel entries using dec->numchans as the loop bound while indexing ents[i]; an inconsistent CDEF numchans can drive out-of-bounds reads before the channo check at line 256.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function contains a reachable assert() whose condition depends on attacker-controlled input, and failure causes process termination, matching CWE-617. The CDEF loop over-read is a separate memory-safety issue, not the assertion weakness, so it does not support CWE-617.

evidence_lines.code:
dec->image->cmprof_ = jas_cmprof_createfromiccprof(iccprof);
assert(dec->image->cmprof_);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: an assert() on a value derived from untrusted ICC-profile parsing. If jas_cmprof_createfromiccprof returns NULL for a crafted profile, the assert fires and terminates the process. Trigger: a JP2 image with a malformed ICC-based COLR box; consequence is application abort (DoS), not memory corruption.

description: A use-after-free exists in the Linux Kernel in tc_new_tfilter that could allow a local attacker to gain privilege escalation. The exploit requires unprivileged user namespaces. We recommend upgrading past commit 04c2a47ffb13c29778e2a14e414ad4cb5a5db4b5

commit_msg:
Fix/improve buffer overflow in MSG_ReadBits/MSG_WriteBits

Prevent reading past end of message in MSG_ReadBits. If read past
end of msg->data buffer (16348 bytes) the engine could SEGFAULT.
Make MSG_WriteBits use an exact buffer overflow check instead of
possibly failing with a few bytes left.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ["\t// this isn't an exact overflow check, but close enough", '\tif ( msg->maxsize - msg->cursize < 4 ) {', '\t\tmsg->overflowed = qtrue;', '\t\t\t\tHuff_offsetTransmit( &msgHuff.compressor, (value & 0xff), msg->data, &msg->bit );'], 'added_lines': ['\tif ( msg->overflowed ) {', '\t\tif ( msg->cursize + ( bits >> 3 ) > msg->maxsize ) {', '\t\t\tmsg->overflowed = qtrue;', '\t\t\treturn;', '\t\t}', '', '\t\t\tif ( msg->bit + nbits > msg->maxsize << 3 ) {', '\t\t\t\tmsg->overflowed = qtrue;', '\t\t\t\treturn;', '\t\t\t}', '\t\t\t\tHuff_offsetTransmit( &msgHuff.compressor, (value & 0xff), msg->data, &msg->bit, msg->maxsize << 3 );', '', '\t\t\t\tif ( msg->bit > msg->maxsize << 3 ) {', '\t\t\t\t\tmsg->overflowed = qtrue;', '\t\t\t\t\treturn;', '\t\t\t\t}']}
description: Buffer overflow in ioquake3 before 2017-08-02 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (application crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted packet.

code_evidence: The only bounds guard is an approximate check `msg->maxsize - msg->cursize < 4`, which does not account for the actual `bits` count and can allow writes that extend past `maxsize`.
In the out-of-band path, the 8-bit write `msg->data[msg->cursize] = value` relies solely on the loose guard above; no per-write check against `msg->maxsize` exists before indexing the buffer.

In the Huffman path, `Huff_offsetTransmit(...)` writes compressed bits into `msg->data` via `msg->bit` without verifying `msg->bit` stays within `msg->maxsize << 3`, so the bit position can advance beyond the buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes to msg->data at offsets that are not restricted to the buffer's intended boundary, matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds write within a memory buffer. The approximate guard and missing bit-capacity check are the specific constraints whose absence permits the out-of-bounds operation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the bounds check is approximate (reserving only 4 bytes) rather than exact, and the bit-level Huffman writes are not bounded against the buffer's bit capacity. Trigger: a crafted call writing values whose bit length exceeds remaining space. Consequence: out-of-bounds writes to msg->data, causing memory corruption or a crash.

commit_msg:
i2c: fix stack buffer overflow vulnerability in i2c md command

When running "i2c md 0 0 80000100", the function do_i2c_md parses the
length into an unsigned int variable named length. The value is then
moved to a signed variable:

    int nbytes = length;
    #define DISP_LINE_LEN 16
    int linebytes = (nbytes > DISP_LINE_LEN) ? DISP_LINE_LEN : nbytes;
    ret = dm_i2c_read(dev, addr, linebuf, linebytes);

On systems where integers are 32 bits wide, 0x80000100 is a negative
value to "nbytes > DISP_LINE_LEN" is false and linebytes gets assigned
0x80000100 instead of 16.

The consequence is that the function which reads from the i2c device
(dm_i2c_read or i2c_read) is called with a 16-byte stack buffer to fill
but with a size parameter which is too large. In some cases, this could
trigger a crash. But with some i2c drivers, such as drivers/i2c/nx_i2c.c
(used with "nexell,s5pxx18-i2c" bus), the size is actually truncated to
a 16-bit integer. This is because function i2c_transfer expects an
unsigned short length. In such a case, an attacker who can control the
response of an i2c device can overwrite the return address of a function
and execute arbitrary code through Return-Oriented Programming.

Fix this issue by using unsigned integers types in do_i2c_md. While at
it, make also alen unsigned, as signed sizes can cause vulnerabilities
when people forgot to check that they can be negative.

Signed-off-by: Nicolas Iooss <nicolas.iooss+uboot@ledger.fr>
Reviewed-by: Heiko Schocher <hs@denx.de>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tint\talen;', '\tint\tcount;'], 'added_lines': ['\tuint\talen;', '\tuint\tcount;']}
description: In Das U-Boot through 2022.07-rc5, an integer signedness error and resultant stack-based buffer overflow in the "i2c md" command enables the corruption of the return address pointer of the do_i2c_md function.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The provided function is do_i2c_mw, which only writes a single byte (dm_i2c_write/i2c_write with size 1) and contains no fixed-size buffer or out-of-bounds write; the described overflow concerns do_i2c_md, not this function.

commit_msg:
ext4: fix use-after-free in ext4_xattr_set_entry

Hulk Robot reported a issue:
==================================================================
BUG: KASAN: use-after-free in ext4_xattr_set_entry+0x18ab/0x3500
Write of size 4105 at addr ffff8881675ef5f4 by task syz-executor.0/7092

CPU: 1 PID: 7092 Comm: syz-executor.0 Not tainted 4.19.90-dirty #17
Call Trace:
[...]
 memcpy+0x34/0x50 mm/kasan/kasan.c:303
 ext4_xattr_set_entry+0x18ab/0x3500 fs/ext4/xattr.c:1747
 ext4_xattr_ibody_inline_set+0x86/0x2a0 fs/ext4/xattr.c:2205
 ext4_xattr_set_handle+0x940/0x1300 fs/ext4/xattr.c:2386
 ext4_xattr_set+0x1da/0x300 fs/ext4/xattr.c:2498
 __vfs_setxattr+0x112/0x170 fs/xattr.c:149
 __vfs_setxattr_noperm+0x11b/0x2a0 fs/xattr.c:180
 __vfs_setxattr_locked+0x17b/0x250 fs/xattr.c:238
 vfs_setxattr+0xed/0x270 fs/xattr.c:255
 setxattr+0x235/0x330 fs/xattr.c:520
 path_setxattr+0x176/0x190 fs/xattr.c:539
 __do_sys_lsetxattr fs/xattr.c:561 [inline]
 __se_sys_lsetxattr fs/xattr.c:557 [inline]
 __x64_sys_lsetxattr+0xc2/0x160 fs/xattr.c:557
 do_syscall_64+0xdf/0x530 arch/x86/entry/common.c:298
 entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x44/0xa9
RIP: 0033:0x459fe9
RSP: 002b:00007fa5e54b4c08 EFLAGS: 00000246 ORIG_RAX: 00000000000000bd
RAX: ffffffffffffffda RBX: 000000000051bf60 RCX: 0000000000459fe9
RDX: 00000000200003c0 RSI: 0000000020000180 RDI: 0000000020000140
RBP: 000000000051bf60 R08: 0000000000000001 R09: 0000000000000000
R10: 0000000000001009 R11: 0000000000000246 R12: 0000000000000000
R13: 00007ffc73c93fc0 R14: 000000000051bf60 R15: 00007fa5e54b4d80
[...]
==================================================================

Above issue may happen as follows:
-------------------------------------
ext4_xattr_set
  ext4_xattr_set_handle
    ext4_xattr_ibody_find
      >> s->end < s->base
      >> no EXT4_STATE_XATTR
      >> xattr_check_inode is not executed
    ext4_xattr_ibody_set
      ext4_xattr_set_entry
       >> size_t min_offs = s->end - s->base
       >> UAF in memcpy

we can easily reproduce this problem with the following commands:
    mkfs.ext4 -F /dev/sda
    mount -o debug_want_extra_isize=128 /dev/sda /mnt
    touch /mnt/file
    setfattr -n user.cat -v `seq -s z 4096|tr -d '[:digit:]'` /mnt/file

In ext4_xattr_ibody_find, we have the following assignment logic:
  header = IHDR(inode, raw_inode)
         = raw_inode + EXT4_GOOD_OLD_INODE_SIZE + i_extra_isize
  is->s.base = IFIRST(header)
             = header + sizeof(struct ext4_xattr_ibody_header)
  is->s.end = raw_inode + s_inode_size

In ext4_xattr_set_entry
  min_offs = s->end - s->base
           = s_inode_size - EXT4_GOOD_OLD_INODE_SIZE - i_extra_isize -
	     sizeof(struct ext4_xattr_ibody_header)
  last = s->first
  free = min_offs - ((void *)last - s->base) - sizeof(__u32)
       = s_inode_size - EXT4_GOOD_OLD_INODE_SIZE - i_extra_isize -
         sizeof(struct ext4_xattr_ibody_header) - sizeof(__u32)

In the calculation formula, all values except s_inode_size and
i_extra_size are fixed values. When i_extra_size is the maximum value
s_inode_size - EXT4_GOOD_OLD_INODE_SIZE, min_offs is -4 and free is -8.
The value overflows. As a result, the preceding issue is triggered when
memcpy is executed.

Therefore, when finding xattr or setting xattr, check whether
there is space for storing xattr in the inode to resolve this issue.

Cc: stable@kernel.org
Reported-by: Hulk Robot <hulkci@huawei.com>
Signed-off-by: Baokun Li <libaokun1@huawei.com>
Reviewed-by: Ritesh Harjani (IBM) <ritesh.list@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Jan Kara <jack@suse.cz>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220616021358.2504451-3-libaokun1@huawei.com
Signed-off-by: Theodore Ts'o <tytso@mit.edu>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (EXT4_I(inode)->i_extra_isize == 0)'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (!EXT4_INODE_HAS_XATTR_SPACE(inode))', '']}
description: A use-after-free vulnerability was found in the Linux kernel's ext4 filesystem in the way it handled the extra inode size for extended attributes. This flaw could allow a privileged local user to cause a system crash or other undefined behaviors.

code_evidence: The guard at [7,8] only returns early when i_extra_isize == 0, so any nonzero extra-isize value proceeds. Lines [9,10,11,12,13] then compute s.base from IHDR/IFIRST and s.end from raw_inode + s_inode_size without validating that the header/extra-isize leaves room, so s.end can fall below s.base and the xattr region becomes invalid.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function's unchecked base/end computation leads to the stale-region write reported as a use-after-free, matching CWE-416. It is not merely an integer overflow: the overflowed size feeds a write through an invalid pointer, which is the use-after-free consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: missing validation that the inode has space for xattrs when i_extra_isize is large (up to s_inode_size - EXT4_GOOD_OLD_INODE_SIZE). Trigger: a crafted setxattr on an inode with maximal extra_isize makes s.end < s.base, so the find/set logic computes a negative free space; the subsequent memcpy writes through a stale/invalid region, producing the reported use-after-free. Consequence: memory corruption, crash, or undefined behavior.

The inner loops at 117 and 121 iterate x up to images->columns and index Ar[i], Ai[i], Br[i], Bi[i] before advancing pointers at 173-176; if an input image's columns are fewer than images->columns, those reads exceed the fetched row.

commit_msg:
grant_table: fix GNTTABOP_cache_flush handling

Don't fall over a NULL grant_table pointer when the owner of the domain
is a system domain (DOMID_{XEN,IO} etc).

This is CVE-2017-14318 / XSA-232.

Reported-by: Matthew Daley <mattd@bugfuzz.com>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Cooper <andrew.cooper3@citrix.com>
Reviewed-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if ( !owner )'], 'added_lines': ['    if ( !owner || !owner->grant_table )']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen 4.5.x through 4.9.x. The function `__gnttab_cache_flush` handles GNTTABOP_cache_flush grant table operations. It checks to see if the calling domain is the owner of the page that is to be operated on. If it is not, the owner's grant table is checked to see if a grant mapping to the calling domain exists for the page in question. However, the function does not check to see if the owning domain actually has a grant table or not. Some special domains, such as `DOMID_XEN`, `DOMID_IO` and `DOMID_COW` are created without grant tables. Hence, if __gnttab_cache_flush operates on a page owned by these special domains, it will attempt to dereference a NULL pointer in the domain struct.

code_evidence: Line 26 obtains owner via page_get_owner_and_reference; line 27 only guards against a NULL owner, not against an owner lacking a grant_table.
When d != owner (line 32), lines 34 and 35 dereference owner->grant_table for grant_read_lock and grant_map_exists without verifying it is non-NULL.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe dereference of owner->grant_table without a NULL check directly matches CWE-476. It is distinct from an authorization flaw: the defect is the missing NULL validation, not the grant mapping check itself.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the check at line 27 validates only owner != NULL, so an owner domain created without a grant table (DOMID_XEN/IO/COW) passes. Trigger: a cache_flush on a page owned by such a domain where d != owner causes grant_read_lock(owner->grant_table) on a NULL pointer. Consequence: NULL dereference in the hypervisor, crashing the host (DoS).

description: In ZeroMQ before version 4.3.3, there is a denial-of-service vulnerability. Users with TCP transport public endpoints, even with CURVE/ZAP enabled, are impacted. If a raw TCP socket is opened and connected to an endpoint that is fully configured with CURVE/ZAP, legitimate clients will not be able to exchange any message. Handshakes complete successfully, and messages are delivered to the library, but the server application never receives them. This is patched in version 4.3.3.

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the engine is constructed without deferring the peer pipe connection, so a raw TCP peer that completes the ZMTP greeting but performs no further legitimate exchange occupies the endpoint. Trigger: an attacker opens a raw TCP socket to a CURVE/ZAP endpoint. Consequence: the endpoint's pending/connection resources are held by the unauthenticated peer, blocking legitimate clients from exchanging messages (denial of service).

commit_msg:
decode_font: fix subtraction broken by change to unsigned type

This caused a one-byte buffer overwrite and an assertion failure.

Regression in commit 910211f1c0078e37546f73e95306724358b89be2.

Discovered by OSS-Fuzz.

Fixes https://bugs.chromium.org/p/oss-fuzz/issues/detail?id=26674.
Fixes https://bugs.chromium.org/p/oss-fuzz/issues/detail?id=26678.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    buf = malloc(size / 4 * 3 + FFMAX(size % 4 - 1, 0));', '    assert(dsize == size / 4 * 3 + FFMAX(size % 4 - 1, 0));'], 'added_lines': ['    buf = malloc(size / 4 * 3 + FFMAX(size % 4, 1) - 1);', '    assert(dsize == size / 4 * 3 + FFMAX(size % 4, 1) - 1);']}
description: libass 0.15.x before 0.15.1 has a heap-based buffer overflow in decode_chars (called from decode_font and process_text) because the wrong integer data type is used for subtraction.

code_evidence: size is size_t (unsigned). The allocation computes size/4*3 + FFMAX(size % 4 - 1, 0); when size % 4 == 0 the subtraction size % 4 - 1 underflows to SIZE_MAX, but FFMAX picks 0, so the tail allowance is 0.

The decode loop writes 3 output bytes per full 4-byte group (i < size/4), and the trailing size%4==2/3 branches write 2 or 3 more bytes via decode_chars into q. The allocation must cover exactly these writes.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes decoded bytes via decode_chars into a heap buffer whose size is computed with a broken unsigned subtraction, allowing writes past the end of the intended buffer. This is an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787); it is not merely an integer issue because the supported consequence is memory corruption beyond the allocation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The allocation size and the assert both rely on the unsigned subtraction size % 4 - 1. For size % 4 == 0 this wraps to SIZE_MAX and FFMAX yields 0, which is correct only by accident; the real regression cause is the expression mixing unsigned arithmetic with a subtraction that cannot represent the intended 'tail-1' value, so the malloc size can diverge from the bytes written by the decode loop. The subsequent decode_chars writes can then exceed the allocated buffer, producing a one-byte heap overwrite (and assertion failure).

commit_msg:

Fixing that highlighted a problem with the error handling in

commit_msg:
_asn1_extract_der_octet: properly account the bytes read through indefinite encodings

This prevents infinite recursions in the function loop.
Reported by Pascal Cuoq.

description: The _asn1_extract_der_octet function in lib/decoding.c in GNU Libtasn1 before 4.8, when used without the ASN1_DECODE_FLAG_STRICT_DER flag, allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (infinite recursion) via a crafted certificate.

code_evidence: The structured branch loops in a while(1) that advances counter and totals tot_len based on nested OCTET STRING lengths; for indefinite encodings it only breaks on a two-byte zero terminator, otherwise it continues consuming the DER buffer based on attacker-controlled lengths.
The recursive call _asn1_extract_der_octet is invoked with the original der and orig_der_len rather than the consumed/remaining length, so the loop/recursion does not account for bytes already read.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-399 covers resource management errors; uncontrolled recursion leading to stack exhaustion is a resource-consumption weakness, matching the reported infinite recursion denial of service.

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the loop over indefinite/nested OCTET STRING encodings advances without correctly accounting for bytes consumed, and the recursive extraction is called with the original buffer and length. A crafted certificate with nested indefinite encodings triggers repeated recursion without progress, exhausting the stack and causing a denial of service.

commit_msg:
glocalfileoutputstream: Fix CREATE_REPLACE_DESTINATION with symlinks

The `G_FILE_CREATE_REPLACE_DESTINATION` flag is equivalent to unlinking
the destination file and re-creating it from scratch. That did
previously work, but in the process the code would call `open(O_CREAT)`
on the file. If the file was a dangling symlink, this would create the
destination file (empty). That’s not an intended side-effect, and has
security implications if the symlink is controlled by a lower-privileged
process.

Fix that by not opening the destination file if it’s a symlink, and
adjusting the rest of the code to cope with
 - the fact that `fd == -1` is not an error iff `is_symlink` is true,
 - and that `original_stat` will contain the `lstat()` results for the
   symlink now, rather than the `stat()` results for its target (again,
   iff `is_symlink` is true).

This means that the target of the dangling symlink is no longer created,
which was the bug. The symlink itself continues to be replaced (as
before) with the new file — this is the intended behaviour of
`g_file_replace()`.

The behaviour for non-symlink cases, or cases where the symlink was not
dangling, should be unchanged.

Includes a unit test.

Signed-off-by: Philip Withnall <pwithnall@endlessos.org>

Fixes: #2325

description: An issue was discovered in GNOME GLib before 2.66.8. When g_file_replace() is used with G_FILE_CREATE_REPLACE_DESTINATION to replace a path that is a dangling symlink, it incorrectly also creates the target of the symlink as an empty file, which could conceivably have security relevance if the symlink is attacker-controlled. (If the path is a symlink to a file that already exists, then the contents of that file correctly remain unchanged.)

code_evidence: [26-46] With O_NOFOLLOW, a symlink makes g_open fail with ELOOP; the code marks is_symlink and re-opens with g_open(filename, open_flags, mode) without O_NOFOLLOW, following the link. The non-O_NOFOLLOW branch also opens the path directly and only probes with g_file_test afterward.
[56-88] After following the symlink, fstat(fd) describes the symlink's target, so the S_ISREG/S_ISDIR checks validate the unintended target rather than the link itself.

[235-263] When replace_destination_set is set, the function closes fd, unlinks filename, and re-opens with O_CREAT. Because the earlier open already created a dangling symlink's target, that empty target file persists as an unintended side effect.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-59 fits because file access is performed on a path without preventing the filename from resolving through a symlink to an unintended resource. The open follows the link before any link-aware check, so the operation affects the link target rather than only the named link.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function opens the destination path before distinguishing a symlink, so a dangling attacker-controlled symlink causes O_CREAT to create the link's target. Trigger: calling g_file_replace() with G_FILE_CREATE_REPLACE_DESTINATION on a path that is a dangling symlink. Consequence: an unintended empty file is created at the symlink target, a file-system side effect outside the intended replacement of the link itself.

description: Xen maintains the _GTF_{read,writ}ing bits as appropriate, to inform the guest that a grant is in use. A guest is expected not to modify the grant details while it is in use, whereas the guest is free to modify/reuse the grant entry when it is not in use. Under some circumstances, Xen will clear the status bits too early, incorrectly informing the guest that the grant is no longer in use. A guest may prematurely believe that a granted frame is safely private again, and reuse it in a way which contains sensitive information, while the domain on the far end of the grant is still using the grant. Xen 4.9, 4.8, 4.7, 4.6, and 4.5 are affected.

code_evidence: Line 145 increments act->pin with either GNTPIN_hstr_inc or GNTPIN_hstw_inc, but the unlock_out_clear path at 153-155 clears _GTF_writing based only on GNTPIN_hstw_mask, ignoring GNTPIN_devw_mask; line 156-157 then clears _GTF_reading whenever act->pin is zero.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The premature status-flag clearing lets one domain reuse a frame still accessible through another domain's active grant, disclosing that domain's sensitive data to the far-end grant holder; this is the confidentiality exposure described in CWE-200.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the status-flag fixup tests an incomplete pin mask, so device-write pins (GNTPIN_devw) are not considered when deciding to clear _GTF_writing. Trigger: an error path (unlock_out_clear) reaches this fixup while a device-write pin remains held. Consequence: Xen clears the in-use status flag early, the guest believes the grant is free and reuses the frame, exposing its contents to the still-active remote grant holder.
