config->http2.latency_optimization.min_rtt = 50;     config->http2.latency_optimization.max_additional_delay = 10;
config->http2.latency_optimization.max_cwnd = 65535;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the HTTP/2 configuration lacks a mechanism to constrain the rate of stream resets during suspicious behavior, so rapid request cancellation can consume server CPU/memory. Trigger: a client opens and cancels many streams quickly. Consequence: resource exhaustion leading to denial of service. The added dos_delay default only mitigates; it does not itself enforce a hard resource limit in this init function.

commit_msg:
Fix handling of symbolic link ACLs

On Linux ACLs on symbolic links are not supported.
We must avoid calling acl_set_file() on symbolic links as their
targets are modified instead.

While here, do not try to set default ACLs on non-directories.

Fixes #1565
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    struct archive_acl *abstract_acl,', ''], 'added_lines': ['    struct archive_acl *abstract_acl, __LA_MODE_T mode,', '', '        if (S_ISLNK(mode)) {', '                /* Skip ACLs on symbolic links */', '\t\tret = ARCHIVE_OK;', '\t\tgoto exit_free;', '        }']}
description: An improper link resolution flaw while extracting an archive can lead to changing the access control list (ACL) of the target of the link. An attacker may provide a malicious archive to a victim user, who would trigger this flaw when trying to extract the archive. A local attacker may use this flaw to change the ACL of a file on the system and gain more privileges.

code_evidence: set_acl receives only name/fd and an ACL type; the mode argument that the patch adds to distinguish symlinks is absent here, so the function cannot detect link entries.
ACL entries are collected from abstract_acl and, when there are entries, aclp is allocated for the subsequent set operation.

The ACL is applied by path via acl(name, cmd, ...) when fd is negative; this follows the named path, so a symbolic link name would resolve to its target and modify the target's ACL rather than the link.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-59 fits because file access is performed via acl(name, ...) on a name that may identify a symlink, causing the operation to act on the unintended target resource.

evidence_lines.code:
struct archive_acl *abstract_acl,
int ae_requested_type, const char *tname)

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function applies an ACL using the caller-supplied path name without checking whether that name is a symbolic link, and without a mode to make that check. Trigger: archive extraction supplies a symlink entry whose name is passed to set_acl with fd < 0. Consequence: acl() resolves the link and changes the target file's ACL, enabling access-control modification.

commit_msg:
Fix wild free.

`huffdata` is initially allocated using `aligned_dealloc` but can be
replaced with `data2` which is allocated using `custom_calloc`.
This can cause a wild free when `aligned_dealloc(huffdata)` is called.
Fix by replacing allocation sites with aligned_alloc.

Noticed and fixed a similar problem with `hdrdata`.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if ( fmem )\tcustom_free( data2 );'], 'added_lines': ['    if ( fmem )\taligned_dealloc( data2 );']}
description: Dropbox Lepton v1.2.1-185-g2a08b77 was discovered to contain a heap-buffer-overflow in the function aligned_dealloc():src/lepton/bitops.cc:108.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function only frees data2 in the destructor; it contains no buffer write or indexing, so it does not support CWE-787 (out-of-bounds write). The described issue is a mismatched/incorrect free, not a write past a buffer boundary.

commit_msg:
ExifParse: Don't run outside exif information

When parsing exif information the number of entries could be tainted. Make
sure to not run behind the exif data by properly checking out of bounds.

Upstream? fix: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/external/jhead/+/34a2564d3268a5ca1472c5076675782fbaf724d6
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '    // Fix from aosp 34a2564d3268a5ca1472c5076675782fbaf724d6', '    if (DirEntry + 12 > OffsetBase + ExifLength)', '    {', '      ErrNonfatal("GPS info directory goes past end of exif", 0, 0);', '      return;', '    }']}
description: A heap buffer overflow vulnerability in Kodi Home Theater Software up to 19.5 allows attackers to cause a denial of service due to an improper length of the value passed to the offset argument.

code_evidence: NumDirEntries from Get16(DirStart) bounds the loop; DirEntry is computed from DirStart without validating it lies within the exif buffer before dereference.

Get16/Get32 read Tag, Format, Components and OffsetVal from DirEntry and DirEntry+8; OffsetVal+ByteCount is checked against ExifLength but ValuePtr = OffsetBase+OffsetVal is not verified against DirStart/ExifLength boundaries, and DirEntry+8 itself may be past the buffer.
GPS_LAT_REF/LONG_REF write ValuePtr[0] into m_ExifInfo->GpsLat/GpsLong without confirming ValuePtr points to at least one valid byte.
GPS_ALT_REF reads ValuePtr[0] to decide sign, again with no bound check on ValuePtr.
GPS_ALT uses sprintf into temp[18] and strcat onto m_ExifInfo->GpsAlt without limiting the destination length, allowing overflow of the fixed GpsAlt buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes attacker-influenced data (GPS strings via sprintf/strcat and GpsLat/GpsLong bytes) into fixed-size destination buffers without bounds validation, which is a direct out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). The missing directory/value-pointer bounds check is the enabling condition, but the supported consequence is memory corruption from writing past the buffer end.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the GPS directory entries and their value pointers are trusted without verifying they fall inside the exif buffer. A crafted JPEG with a large NumDirEntries or an out-of-range OffsetVal causes DirEntry/ValuePtr to point past the buffer; subsequent reads and the unchecked sprintf/strcat into m_ExifInfo->GpsAlt write beyond the intended buffer, corrupting heap memory and potentially causing a crash or code execution.

commit_msg: Fix denial-of-service attack when reading corrupt PDF files.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  PDFIO_DEBUG("_pdfioTokenRead: Read \'%s\'.\\n", buffer);'], 'added_lines': ['//  PDFIO_DEBUG("_pdfioTokenRead: Read \'%s\'.\\n", buffer);']}
description: PDFio is a C library for reading and writing PDF files. In versions prior to 1.1.0 a denial of service (DOS) vulnerability exists in the pdfio parser. Crafted pdf files can cause the program to run at 100% utilization and never terminate. The pdf which causes this crash found in testing is about 28kb in size and was discovered via fuzzing. Anyone who uses this library either as a standalone binary or as a library can be DOSed when attempting to parse this type of file. Web servers or other automated processes which rely on this code to turn pdf submissions into plaintext can be DOSed when an attacker uploads the pdf. Please see the linked GHSA for an example pdf. Users are advised to upgrade. There are no known workarounds for this vulnerability.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The only change disables a debug print; the function's loops all have reachable exit conditions (EOF, whitespace, delimiters, or buffer-full error returns), and no line in func shows an exit condition that cannot be reached.

commit_msg:
schema tree BUGFIX freeing nodes with no module set

Context must be passed explicitly for these cases.
Fixes #1452
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    lys_node_free(retval, NULL, 0);'], 'added_lines': ['    lys_node_free(ctx, retval, NULL, 0);']}
description: In function lys_node_free() in libyang <= v1.0.225, it asserts that the value of node->module can't be NULL. But in some cases, node->module can be null, which triggers a reachable assertion (CWE-617).

code_evidence: The error path at line 173-175 calls lys_node_free(retval, NULL, 0) without passing the context, while the fix adds ctx as the first argument. The function obtains ctx from module->ctx at line 5, so the context is available but omitted on cleanup. The changed line is the only call to lys_node_free in this function and is reached from many earlier goto error statements, e.g., after read_yin_common or child parsing failures.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function's error path can invoke an assert via lys_node_free with an unset module, matching CWE-617's reachable assertion leading to crash/exit. It is not a null-pointer dereference (CWE-476) because the failure mode is an assertion abort, not a memory access fault.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the cleanup call passes a NULL context to lys_node_free, which internally asserts that node->module is non-NULL; when parsing fails before the node's module is set, the assertion fires. Trigger: malformed or failing YIN leaf input reaches any of the error jumps. Consequence: reachable assertion aborts the process, causing denial of service rather than a graceful parse error.

commit_msg:
patch 9.0.0211: invalid memory access when compiling :lockvar

Problem:    Invalid memory access when compiling :lockvar.
Solution:   Don't read past the end of the line.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tchar *cmd = eap->cmdidx == CMD_lockvar ? "lockvar" : "unlockvar";', ''], 'added_lines': ['    char\t*cmd = eap->cmdidx == CMD_lockvar ? "lockvar" : "unlockvar";', '', '    if (*p == NUL)', '    {', '\tsemsg(_(e_argument_required_for_str), cmd);', '\treturn FAIL;', '    }']}
description: Heap-based Buffer Overflow in GitHub repository vim/vim prior to 9.0.0211.

code_evidence: Line 11 sets p to lvp->ll_name; line 18 immediately reads p[1] without first ensuring the string has at least one character, so an empty argument makes p[1] read past the end of the name buffer (the pre-patch path; the added *p == NUL guard addresses this).
Lines 34-36 terminate the name at name_end, compute len = name_end - p + 20 and heap-allocate buf; lines 43/45 then vim_snprintf cmd plus p into that heap buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-122 fits because the overflow occurs on the heap buffer allocated at line 36 and written by vim_snprintf at lines 43/45, with the length derived from the unvalidated name range. A plain out-of-bounds read alone would be CWE-125; here the missing empty-argument check feeds the heap allocation/write path, matching heap-based buffer overflow.

evidence_lines.code:
char_u*p = lvp->ll_name;
if (p[1] != ':')

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function dereferences p[1] and builds the name before validating that the lockvar/unlockvar argument is non-empty. Trigger: compiling :lockvar/:unlockvar with an empty or immediately-terminating argument, so name_end points at or before p and the pointer arithmetic/length derivation is based on an empty range. Supported consequence: out-of-bounds read past the name buffer and, from the resulting length/name handling, heap buffer overrun (crash or memory corruption).

commit_msg:
Because group consistency is non-atomic between parent (filedesc) and children
(inherited) events, it is possible for PERF_FORMAT_GROUP read() to try and sum
non-matching counter groups -- with non-sensical results.

Add group_generation to distinguish the case where a parent group removes and
adds an event and thus has the same number, but a different configuration of
events as inherited groups.

This became a problem when commit fa8c269353d5 ("perf/core: Invert
perf_read_group() loops") flipped the order of child_list and sibling_list.
Previously it would iterate the group (sibling_list) first, and for each
sibling traverse the child_list. In this order, only the group composition of
the parent is relevant. By flipping the order the group composition of the
child (inherited) events becomes an issue and the mis-match in group
composition becomes evident.

That said; even prior to this commit, while reading of a group that is not
equally inherited was not broken, it still made no sense.

(Ab)use ECHILD as error return to indicate issues with child process group
composition.

Fixes: fa8c269353d5 ("perf/core: Invert perf_read_group() loops")
Reported-by: Budimir Markovic <markovicbudimir@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Peter Zijlstra (Intel) <peterz@infradead.org>
Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/20231018115654.GK33217@noisy.programming.kicks-ass.net
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\tevent->group_leader->group_generation++;']}
description:
A heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the Linux kernel's Linux Kernel Performance Events (perf) component can be exploited to achieve local privilege escalation.

If perf_read_group() is called while an event's sibling_list is smaller than its child's sibling_list, it can increment or write to memory locations outside of the allocated buffer.

We recommend upgrading past commit 32671e3799ca2e4590773fd0e63aaa4229e50c06.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The shown function only detaches events and updates counters/generation; it contains no buffer indexing or write that can go out of bounds, so CWE-787 is not directly supported by this code.

commit_msg:
blk-mq: fix race between timeout and freeing request

Inside timeout handler, blk_mq_tag_to_rq() is called
to retrieve the request from one tag. This way is obviously
wrong because the request can be freed any time and some
fiedds of the request can't be trusted, then kernel oops
might be triggered[1].

Currently wrt. blk_mq_tag_to_rq(), the only special case is
that the flush request can share same tag with the request
cloned from, and the two requests can't be active at the same
time, so this patch fixes the above issue by updating tags->rqs[tag]
with the active request(either flush rq or the request cloned
from) of the tag.

Also blk_mq_tag_to_rq() gets much simplified with this patch.

Given blk_mq_tag_to_rq() is mainly for drivers and the caller must
make sure the request can't be freed, so in bt_for_each() this
helper is replaced with tags->rqs[tag].

description: In blk_mq_tag_to_rq in blk-mq.c in the upstream kernel, there is a possible use after free due to a race condition when a request has been previously freed by blk_mq_complete_request. This could lead to local escalation of privilege. Product: Android. Versions: Android kernel. Android ID: A-63083046.

code_evidence: The function computes fq from flush_rq->mq_ctx at line 8 and only takes fq->mq_flush_lock when q->mq_ops is set (lines 9-10). Under that lock it only sets flush_rq->tag = -1 (line 11); it never updates the tag's rqs[] entry back to the request cloned from (fq->orig_rq), so the shared tag table still points at the flush request after it is freed.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The tag table is shared state modified by the timeout and completion paths, and flush_end_io's critical section fails to restore tags->rqs[tag] to fq->orig_rq, leaving a timing window where a concurrently freed request is still reachable. This improper synchronization of a shared resource matches CWE-362; the missing ownership update, not the resulting oops, is the weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: flush_end_io clears flush_rq->tag without restoring the tag's ownership to fq->orig_rq, while the timeout path reads tags->rqs[tag] under only the tag lock. Trigger: a timeout fires concurrently with or after flush completion, so blk_mq_tag_to_rq returns a freed flush request; dereferencing it gives a NULL-pointer/oops crash and, per the report, possible local privilege escalation.

description: mod_auth_openidc is an authentication/authorization module for the Apache 2.x HTTP server that functions as an OpenID Connect Relying Party, authenticating users against an OpenID Connect Provider. In mod_auth_openidc before version 2.4.9, there is an XSS vulnerability in when using `OIDCPreservePost On`.

code_evidence: apr_psprintf builds an HTML/JavaScript response by interpolating oidc_get_redirect_uri(r, c) directly into a single-quoted JS string literal (window.top.location.href = '%s?session=logout') without escaping.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function generates a web page and places a non-neutralized value into it, matching CWE-79's improper neutralization of input during web page generation. The call to oidc_util_javascript_escape in the patched line confirms the intended constraint (JS-context escaping) was absent here, distinguishing it from mere output formatting.

evidence_lines.code:
char *java_script = apr_psprintf(r->pool,
"    <script type=\"text/javascript\">\n"
"      window.top.location.href = '%s?session=logout';\n"
"    </script>\n", oidc_get_redirect_uri(r, c));

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The redirect URI value is embedded verbatim in a JavaScript string inside a page returned to the browser. If that value contains a quote or script-breaking characters, it can terminate the string and inject arbitrary script, which the victim's browser executes. Root cause is missing output encoding of the URI for the JavaScript/HTML context; the consequence is script execution in the victim's session.

description: In libssh2 before 1.9.0, kex_method_diffie_hellman_group_exchange_sha256_key_exchange in kex.c has an integer overflow that could lead to an out-of-bounds read in the way packets are read from the server. A remote attacker who compromises a SSH server may be able to disclose sensitive information or cause a denial of service condition on the client system when a user connects to the server. This is related to an _libssh2_check_length mistake, and is different from the various issues fixed in 1.8.1, such as CVE-2019-3855.

code_evidence: Line 3 computes the remaining buffer size as `(buf->data + buf->len) - buf->dataptr` and casts the pointer-difference result to size_t before comparing with `len`. If `buf->dataptr` lies beyond `buf->data + buf->len`, the subtraction yields a negative value that wraps when cast to size_t, producing a huge 'remaining' length.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the negative pointer difference is converted to size_t and wraps to a large value that the logic treats as a valid remaining length, bypassing the length check. This is integer wraparound, not merely a pointer-arithmetic flaw.

evidence_lines.code: return (len <= (size_t)((buf->data + buf->len) - buf->dataptr));

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the pointer difference is cast to size_t without validating that dataptr is within [data, data+len], so a negative difference wraps to a very large unsigned value. Trigger: a caller passes a buf whose dataptr advanced past the end. Consequence: the bounds check returns success for an overlong length, enabling out-of-bounds reads downstream.

commit_msg:
Reject fonts with invalid ranges in cmap

A corrupt or malicious font may have a negative size in its cmap
range, which in turn could lead to memory corruption. This patch
detects the case and rejects the font, and also includes an assertion
in the sparse bit set implementation if we missed any such case.

External issue:
https://code.google.com/p/android/issues/detail?id=192618

Bug: 26413177
Change-Id: Icc0c80e4ef389abba0964495b89aa0fae3e9f4b2
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['        LOG_ALWAYS_FATAL_IF(end < start);  // make sure range size is nonnegative']}
description: The Minikin library in Android 5.0.x before 5.0.2, 5.1.x before 5.1.1, and 6.x before 2016-04-01 does not properly consider negative size values in font data, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory corruption and reboot loop) via a crafted font, aka internal bug 26413177.

code_evidence: The function reads start and end from the caller-supplied ranges array without checking that end >= start; endPage is derived as (end - 1) >> kLogValuesPerPage and nElements as (end - (start & ~kElMask) + kElMask) >> kLogBitsPerEl.
With a negative (wrapped) range size, nElements and the page-index computations become inconsistent, so the loop writes mBitmaps[index + j] and mIndices[j] at attacker-influenced offsets.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect is missing validation of a structural property of untrusted input (range ordering/size), which is exactly CWE-20: the code accepts data lacking required properties and processes it unsafely. The out-of-bounds write is the consequence, not the root cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: initFromRanges trusts the cmap range pairs and performs no validation that end >= start. A crafted font with an inverted range makes derived size/page values wrap, causing out-of-bounds writes into mBitmaps and mIndices; the supported consequence is memory corruption leading to crash/DoS.

commit_msg:
knc: fix a couple of memory leaks.

One of these can be remotely triggered during the authentication
phase which leads to a remote DoS possibility.

Pointed out by: Imre Rad <radimre83@gmail.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\treturn -1;', '\t\t\treturn -1;', '\t\treturn -1;', '\t\t\treturn -1;', '\t\treturn -1;', '\t\treturn -1;'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\tgoto bail;', '\t\t\tgoto bail;', '\t\tgoto bail;', '\t\t\tgoto bail;', '', '\t\tgoto bail;', '\t\tgoto bail;', '', 'bail:', '\tfree(tmpbuf);', '\ttmpbuf = NULL;', '', '\treturn -1;']}
description: The read_packet function in knc (Kerberised NetCat) before 1.11-1 is vulnerable to denial of service (memory exhaustion) that can be exploited remotely without authentication, possibly affecting another services running on the targeted host.

code_evidence: tmpbuf is a function-static heap buffer allocated once via malloc(len) when the first packet is read; it persists across calls.

On read failure or EOF, the function returns -1 without freeing tmpbuf, leaving the allocation reachable only through the static pointer; subsequent calls reuse it but the error path never releases it before returning.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function fails to control maintenance of a heap resource, leaking/reusing tmpbuf on error exits, matching CWE-400's resource-exhaustion scope. The patch confirms the fix by adding a bail label that frees tmpbuf and nulls it, evidencing the missing release as the defect.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: error paths return -1 without releasing the statically held tmpbuf allocation. Trigger: a remote peer during authentication can cause read errors/EOF after tmpbuf is allocated, and repeated failed reads leave/leak the buffer or let allocated length be re-driven. Supported consequence: unbounded memory consumption leading to remote DoS.

commit_msg:
n_tty: fix EXTPROC vs ICANON interaction with TIOCINQ (aka FIONREAD)

We added support for EXTPROC back in 2010 in commit 26df6d13406d ("tty:
Add EXTPROC support for LINEMODE") and the intent was to allow it to
override some (all?) ICANON behavior.  Quoting from that original commit
message:

         There is a new bit in the termios local flag word, EXTPROC.
         When this bit is set, several aspects of the terminal driver
         are disabled.  Input line editing, character echo, and mapping
         of signals are all disabled.  This allows the telnetd to turn
         off these functions when in linemode, but still keep track of
         what state the user wants the terminal to be in.

but the problem turns out that "several aspects of the terminal driver
are disabled" is a bit ambiguous, and you can really confuse the n_tty
layer by setting EXTPROC and then causing some of the ICANON invariants
to no longer be maintained.

This fixes at least one such case (TIOCINQ) becoming unhappy because of
the confusion over whether ICANON really means ICANON when EXTPROC is set.

This basically makes TIOCINQ match the case of read: if EXTPROC is set,
we ignore ICANON.  Also, make sure to reset the ICANON state ie EXTPROC
changes, not just if ICANON changes.

Fixes: 26df6d13406d ("tty: Add EXTPROC support for LINEMODE")
Reported-by: Tetsuo Handa <penguin-kernel@i-love.sakura.ne.jp>
Reported-by: syzkaller <syzkaller@googlegroups.com>
Cc: Jiri Slaby <jslaby@suse.com>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

description: drivers/tty/n_tty.c in the Linux kernel before 4.14.11 allows local attackers (who are able to access pseudo terminals) to hang/block further usage of any pseudo terminal devices due to an EXTPROC versus ICANON confusion in TIOCINQ.

commit_msg:
[sipmsgops] fix codec_delete_XX() parsing

Issue discovered during OpenSIPS Security Audit 2021,
        by Alfred Farrugia & Sandro Gauci (Enable Security)

https://github.com/OpenSIPS/opensips/security/advisories/GHSA-xj5x-g52f-548h
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t\t\tif( delete_sdp_line( msg, payload->rtp_enc.s) < 0 )', '\t\t\t\t\tif( delete_sdp_line( msg, payload->fmtp_string.s) < 0 )'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t\t\tif( delete_sdp_line( msg, payload->rtp_enc.s, cell) < 0 )', '\t\t\t\t\tif( delete_sdp_line( msg, payload->fmtp_string.s, cell) < 0 )']}
description:
OpenSIPS is a Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) server implementation. Prior to versions 3.1.7 and 3.2.4, OpenSIPS crashes when a malformed SDP body is received and is processed by the `delete_sdp_line` function in the sipmsgops module. This issue can be reproduced by calling the function with an SDP body that does not terminate by a line feed (i.e. `\n`).

The vulnerability was found while performing black-box fuzzing against an OpenSIPS server running a configuration that made use of the functions `codec_delete_except_re` and `codec_delete_re`. The same issue was also discovered while performing coverage guided fuzzing on the function `codec_delete_except_re`. The crash happens because the function `delete_sdp_line` expects that an SDP line is terminated by a line feed (`\n`):

By abusing this vulnerability, an attacker is able to crash the server. It affects configurations containing functions that rely on the affected code, such as the function `codec_delete_except_re`. Due to the sanity check that is performed in the `del_lump` function, exploitation of this issue will generate an `abort` in the lumps processing function, resulting in a Denial of Service. This issue has been fixed in versions 3.1.7 and 3.2.4.

code_evidence: On DELETE, stream_process calls delete_sdp_line with payload->rtp_enc.s and payload->fmtp_string.s but passes no bounds/termination context; the SDP body contents are attacker-supplied and are not checked to ensure each attribute line ends with a line feed before deletion.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function forwards malformed SDP input to delete_sdp_line without validating the required line-termination property, so the weakness is improper validation of input structure (CWE-20). The crash is the resulting consequence, not the root cause; the missing well-formedness check on the SDP line is the supported weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the caller relies on delete_sdp_line assuming a '\n'-terminated SDP line, and the malformed body lacking a trailing line feed is not validated before these calls. Trigger: a received SDP whose attribute line has no terminating '\n' reaching DELETE. Consequence: delete_sdp_line mishandles the unterminated line, leading to a crash/abort in lump processing and a denial of service.

commit_msg:
ext4: fix data exposure after a crash

Huang has reported that in his powerfail testing he is seeing stale
block contents in some of recently allocated blocks although he mounts
ext4 in data=ordered mode. After some investigation I have found out
that indeed when delayed allocation is used, we don't add inode to
transaction's list of inodes needing flushing before commit. Originally
we were doing that but commit f3b59291a69d removed the logic with a
flawed argument that it is not needed.

The problem is that although for delayed allocated blocks we write their
contents immediately after allocating them, there is no guarantee that
the IO scheduler or device doesn't reorder things and thus transaction
allocating blocks and attaching them to inode can reach stable storage
before actual block contents. Actually whenever we attach freshly
allocated blocks to inode using a written extent, we should add inode to
transaction's ordered inode list to make sure we properly wait for block
contents to be written before committing the transaction. So that is
what we do in this patch. This also handles other cases where stale data
exposure was possible - like filling hole via mmap in
data=ordered,nodelalloc mode.

The only exception to the above rule are extending direct IO writes where
blkdev_direct_IO() waits for IO to complete before increasing i_size and
thus stale data exposure is not possible. For now we don't complicate
the code with optimizing this special case since the overhead is pretty
low. In case this is observed to be a performance problem we can always
handle it using a special flag to ext4_map_blocks().

CC: stable@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: f3b59291a69d0b734be1fc8be489fef2dd846d3d
Reported-by: "HUANG Weller (CM/ESW12-CN)" <Weller.Huang@cn.bosch.com>
Tested-by: "HUANG Weller (CM/ESW12-CN)" <Weller.Huang@cn.bosch.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Kara <jack@suse.cz>
Signed-off-by: Theodore Ts'o <tytso@mit.edu>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\t\t/*', '\t\t * Inodes with freshly allocated blocks where contents will be', "\t\t * visible after transaction commit must be on transaction's", '\t\t * ordered data list.', '\t\t */', '\t\tif (map->m_flags & EXT4_MAP_NEW &&', '\t\t    !(map->m_flags & EXT4_MAP_UNWRITTEN) &&', '\t\t    !(flags & EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_ZERO) &&', '\t\t    !IS_NOQUOTA(inode) &&', '\t\t    ext4_should_order_data(inode)) {', '\t\t\tret = ext4_jbd2_file_inode(handle, inode);', '\t\t\tif (ret)', '\t\t\t\treturn ret;', '\t\t}']}
description: fs/ext4/inode.c in the Linux kernel before 4.6.2, when ext4 data=ordered mode is used, mishandles a needs-flushing-before-commit list, which allows local users to obtain sensitive information from other users' files in opportunistic circumstances by waiting for a hardware reset, creating a new file, making write system calls, and reading this file.

code_evidence: ext4_map_blocks allocates blocks via ext4_ext_map_blocks/ext4_ind_map_blocks (lines 88-91) and returns the new mapping, but before returning at line 144 it only checks block validity (lines 139-143) and inserts the extent status (lines 123-131); it never calls ext4_jbd2_file_inode to place the inode on the transaction's ordered-data list when freshly allocated blocks are attached. The patch adds this ordering call after allocation, confirming the function previously returned with new blocks attached but without the flush-before-commit constraint.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The supported consequence is disclosure of other users' residual file data to an unauthorized local reader, which is an exposure of sensitive information (CWE-200). The weakness is the missing flush-before-commit ordering constraint that permits stale data to become visible; the patch's added ext4_jbd2_file_inode call addresses this exposure directly.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: when delayed allocation attaches freshly allocated blocks to an inode, the inode is not added to the transaction's ordered inode list, so block contents are not guaranteed to reach stable storage before the transaction commit. Trigger: a crash/hardware reset after the allocating transaction commits but before the data write completes; on remount, the inode references blocks whose contents were never written, exposing stale on-disk data from other users' files. Consequence: confidentiality loss via stale block contents being readable from the new file.

description: Cygwin before 2.5.0 does not properly handle updating permissions when changing users, which allows attackers to gain privileges.

code_evidence: Line 11 initializes auth_luid to SYSTEM_LUID, so the token-creation path bases the logon identity on the SYSTEM account rather than on the caller being authenticated.
Lines 62-67 declare auth_pos and pass auth_luid/auth_pos into get_setgroups_sidlist and get_initgroups_sidlist, propagating the SYSTEM LUID into the group SID list construction.
Line 183 then converts the resulting user_token into a full privileged inheritable token, so the privilege set derived from the SYSTEM-based logon is carried forward.

evidence_lines.code: LUID auth_luid = SYSTEM_LUID;

commit_msg:
Bug 702582, CVE 2020-15900 Memory Corruption in Ghostscript 9.52

Fix the 'rsearch' calculation for the 'post' size to give the correct
size.  Previous calculation would result in a size that was too large,
and could underflow to max uint32_t. Also fix 'rsearch' to return the
correct 'pre' string with empty string match.

A future change may 'undefine' this undocumented, non-standard operator
during initialization as we do with the many other non-standard internal
PostScript operators and procedures.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    op->value.bytes = ptr;', '    r_set_size(op, size);', '    op[-1] = *op1;', '    r_set_size(op - 1, ptr - op[-1].value.bytes);', '    op1->value.bytes = ptr + size;', '    r_set_size(op1, count + (!forward ? (size - 1) : 0));'], 'added_lines': ['    op->value.bytes = ptr;\t\t\t\t/* match */', '    op->tas.rsize = size;\t\t\t\t/* match */', '    op[-1] = *op1;\t\t\t\t\t/* pre */', '    op[-3].value.bytes = ptr + size;\t\t\t/* post */', '    if (forward) {', '        op[-1].tas.rsize = ptr - op[-1].value.bytes;\t/* pre */', '        op[-3].tas.rsize = count;\t\t\t/* post */', '    } else {', '        op[-1].tas.rsize = count;\t\t\t/* pre */', '        op[-3].tas.rsize -= count + size;\t\t/* post */', '    }']}
description: A memory corruption issue was found in Artifex Ghostscript 9.50 and 9.52. Use of a non-standard PostScript operator can allow overriding of file access controls. The 'rsearch' calculation for the 'post' size resulted in a size that was too large, and could underflow to max uint32_t. This was fixed in commit 5d499272b95a6b890a1397e11d20937de000d31b.

code_evidence: At the found label, the match pointer and sizes are written into the operand stack. Line 37 sets the match string size to size, line 40 computes the 'pre' size as ptr - op[-1].value.bytes, and line 42 computes the 'post' size from count plus an adjustment for backward search. These derived sizes are stored without validating against the actual string extent.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The root cause is an incorrect length calculation that produces an oversized string size, enabling subsequent out-of-bounds memory access. This directly supports CWE-787 because the bad size can lead to writes/reads past the intended buffer.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The 'post' substring size is computed as count + (!forward ? (size - 1) : 0), which can be too large and, for backward search with certain size/count values, underflows to max uint32_t. The result is stored as an rsize on a string object, so later string reads/writes trust an out-of-range length, causing memory corruption.

description: A memory leak in the qrtr_tun_write_iter() function in net/qrtr/tun.c in the Linux kernel before 5.3 allows attackers to cause a denial of service (memory consumption), aka CID-a21b7f0cff19.

code_evidence: Line 8 allocates kbuf with kzalloc(len, GFP_KERNEL). The copy_from_iter_full failure branch at lines 11-12 returns -EFAULT without freeing kbuf. On the success path, lines 13-14 call qrtr_endpoint_post and return without freeing kbuf.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-401 fits because allocated memory is never released after its effective lifetime; the pointer goes out of scope on return, leaving the allocation unreachable. This is a memory leak, not a use-after-free or double-free, since no stale pointer is dereferenced or freed twice.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function allocates kbuf but has no kfree on either the copy-failure return or the normal return path. The trigger is any call to qrtr_tun_write_iter, including malformed input causing copy_from_iter_full to fail; each invocation leaks the len-sized allocation, exhausting kernel memory and causing denial of service.

commit_msg:
acpi: Disable ACPI table override if securelevel is set

From the kernel documentation (initrd_table_override.txt):

  If the ACPI_INITRD_TABLE_OVERRIDE compile option is true, it is possible
  to override nearly any ACPI table provided by the BIOS with an
  instrumented, modified one.

When securelevel is set, the kernel should disallow any unauthenticated
changes to kernel space. ACPI tables contain code invoked by the kernel, so
do not allow ACPI tables to be overridden if securelevel is set.

Signed-off-by: Linn Crosetto <linn@hpe.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\treserve_initrd();', '', '#if defined(CONFIG_ACPI) && defined(CONFIG_BLK_DEV_INITRD)', '\tacpi_initrd_override((void *)initrd_start, initrd_end - initrd_start);', '#endif', '', '\tvsmp_init();', '', '\tio_delay_init();', ''], 'added_lines': ['', '\treserve_initrd();', '', '#if defined(CONFIG_ACPI) && defined(CONFIG_BLK_DEV_INITRD)', '\tacpi_initrd_override((void *)initrd_start, initrd_end - initrd_start);', '#endif', '', '\tvsmp_init();', '', '\tio_delay_init();']}
description: The Linux kernel, as used in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7.2 and Red Hat Enterprise MRG 2 and when booted with UEFI Secure Boot enabled, allows local users to bypass intended Secure Boot restrictions and execute untrusted code by appending ACPI tables to the initrd.

code_evidence: setup_arch calls reserve_initrd() and then acpi_initrd_override((void *)initrd_start, initrd_end - initrd_start) to load ACPI tables from the initrd at lines 171-174. The securelevel check that calls set_securelevel(1) when boot_params.secure_boot is set appears only afterward at lines 177-181, so the override executes before any securelevel restriction is established.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function mismanages a security feature: securelevel is meant to block unauthenticated kernel-space changes, but the override runs first, defeating that access restriction. This is a permissions/security-feature enforcement failure consistent with CWE-264; it is not merely a memory-safety bug.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the ordering places acpi_initrd_override before the EFI secure-boot securelevel enforcement, so an attacker-supplied initrd can inject ACPI tables that the kernel later parses and executes. Trigger: booting with UEFI Secure Boot enabled while appending ACPI tables to the initrd. Consequence: intended Secure Boot restrictions are bypassed, allowing untrusted code execution in kernel space.

description: Infinite loop in the F5 Ethernet Trailer protocol dissector in Wireshark 3.6.0 to 3.6.7 and 3.4.0 to 3.4.15 allows denial of service via packet injection or crafted capture file

code_evidence: The while loop at line 12 iterates while any reported bytes remain, reading type/len/ver via tvb_get_guint8. The guard at lines 16-18 only enters the switch when the length/type/version checks pass.
If the guard fails, processed is never updated; line 54 advances offset by processed, which remains 0, so offset never changes and the loop condition stays true indefinitely.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The loop's exit condition (offset reaching the reported length) becomes unreachable because offset never advances on the invalid-input path, matching CWE-835's infinite loop with unreachable exit condition. This is not merely a length-validation bug (CWE-20); the direct weakness is the non-terminating iteration.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the loop's only offset advance (offset += processed, line 54) occurs outside the validated branch, so when the length/type/version check fails, processed stays 0 and offset is not incremented. Trigger: a crafted packet/capture whose trailer bytes fail the sanity check. Consequence: the dissector spins forever, consuming CPU (DoS).

commit_msg: fixed #2285
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t//we may have one root desc remaining if error', '\tif (gf_list_count(parser->descriptors)) {', '\t\tGF_Descriptor *desc = gf_list_get(parser->descriptors, 0);', '\t\tgf_odf_desc_del(desc);', '\t}']}
description: GPAC v2.1-DEV-rev368-gfd054169b-master was discovered to contain a memory leak via the component gf_odf_new_iod at odf/odf_code.c.

code_evidence: The cleanup path deletes the list containers with gf_list_del for parser->descriptors and the other lists, but it never retrieves and releases the GF_Descriptor elements held inside parser->descriptors.

After the lists are deleted, parser itself is freed and load->loader_priv is nulled, so any descriptor objects still referenced only by the descriptors list become unreachable and cannot be released later.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-401 fits because allocated GF_Descriptor memory is never released after its effective lifetime, and the pointer is lost when the list container and parser are freed. This is a missing-release leak, not a use-after-free or double-free, since no freed descriptor is subsequently accessed.

evidence_lines.code:
gf_free(parser);
load->loader_priv = NULL;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the teardown routine frees the list wrapper but not the descriptor objects it owns, so on the load-completion/error path a remaining root descriptor is orphaned. Trigger: a parsing session ending with an entry left in parser->descriptors. Consequence: unreachable heap memory accumulates across repeated loads, supporting memory-consumption DoS.

commit_msg:
BACapp: Add a nesting / recursion check.

Track our recursion depth in fAbstractSyntaxNType. It calls several
functions which in turn call it, which makes it easy to overflow the
stack.

Fixes: e2f34481b24d ("cifsd: add server-side procedures for SMB3")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Reported-by: zdi-disclosures@trendmicro.com # ZDI-CAN-17817
Signed-off-by: Hyunchul Lee <hyc.lee@gmail.com>
Acked-by: Namjae Jeon <linkinjeon@kernel.org>

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tif (((struct smb2_write_req *)hdr)->DataOffset) {', '\t\t\t*off = le16_to_cpu(((struct smb2_write_req *)hdr)->DataOffset);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (((struct smb2_write_req *)hdr)->DataOffset ||', '\t\t    ((struct smb2_write_req *)hdr)->Length) {', '\t\t\t*off = max_t(unsigned int,', '\t\t\t\t     le16_to_cpu(((struct smb2_write_req *)hdr)->DataOffset),', '\t\t\t\t     offsetof(struct smb2_write_req, Buffer));']}
description: An issue was discovered in ksmbd in the Linux kernel 5.15 through 5.19 before 5.19.2. There is an out-of-bounds read and OOPS for SMB2_WRITE, when there is a large length in the zero DataOffset case.

code_evidence: For SMB2_WRITE, the code only uses DataOffset when it is nonzero; if DataOffset is 0 it falls through to WriteChannelInfoOffset/Length and ignores the attacker-controlled Length field. No lower bound is enforced on the write data offset, so a compound request with DataOffset 0 and a large Length can yield an offset/length pair pointing before the valid buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function computes an attacker-influenced offset/length used to read request data without a minimum-offset constraint, directly enabling reading past the intended buffer boundary. This is an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125); the crash is the consequence, not the root cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the SMB2_WRITE branch does not constrain the computed data offset to at least the SMB2_WRITE header size and ignores Length when DataOffset is zero. Trigger: a crafted compound SMB2_WRITE with DataOffset 0 and large Length. The later copy_page_from_iter_atomic read then accesses memory out of bounds, causing an OOB read and kernel oops.

commit_msg:
PyACL - Fixing integer overflows that occur when resizing ACLs

Fixes #1700
CVE-2021-32559
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        unsigned short required_size = psacl->AclSize + sizeof(SYSTEM_AUDIT_ACE) + (unsigned short)GetLengthSid(psid);', '        psacl_padded->AclSize = required_size;'], 'added_lines': ['        unsigned int required_size = psacl->AclSize + sizeof(SYSTEM_AUDIT_ACE) + GetLengthSid(psid);', '        // max ACL size is USHRT_MAX', '        if (required_size > USHRT_MAX)', '            return PyErr_Format(PyExc_OverflowError, "%s: adding ACE would put ACL over size limit", __FUNCTION__ );', '        psacl_padded->AclSize = (unsigned short)required_size;']}
description: An integer overflow exists in pywin32 prior to version b301 when adding an access control entry (ACE) to an access control list (ACL) that would cause the size to be greater than 65535 bytes. An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could crash the vulnerable process.

code_evidence: Line 24 computes required_size in an unsigned short, summing psacl->AclSize, sizeof(SYSTEM_AUDIT_ACE), and (unsigned short)GetLengthSid(psid); the narrow type truncates the sum before allocation.

Line 25 uses the truncated required_size for malloc, while lines 28-30 ZeroMemory and memcpy copy psacl->AclSize bytes and store required_size into AclSize, so an oversized ACL yields an undersized buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the size calculation wraps around in a narrow integer type, producing a small value used for allocation and copying. This is an integer overflow leading to heap overflow, not merely an oversized allocation or missing bounds check on input.

evidence_lines.code:
unsigned short required_size = psacl->AclSize + sizeof(SYSTEM_AUDIT_ACE) + (unsigned short)GetLengthSid(psid);
psacl_padded = (ACL *)malloc(required_size);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the ACL size arithmetic is performed in unsigned short, so adding a large SID or ACE to an existing ACL wraps the required_size value. Trigger: AddAuditAccessAceEx is called on an ACL whose grown size exceeds 65535 bytes. Consequence: malloc and ZeroMemory allocate/clear a too-small buffer, and memcpy of psacl->AclSize bytes overflows it, causing memory corruption and a crash.

commit_msg:
Correctly compare EdiPartyName in GENERAL_NAME_cmp()

If a GENERAL_NAME field contained EdiPartyName data then it was
incorrectly being handled as type "other". This could lead to a
segmentation fault.

Many thanks to David Benjamin from Google for reporting this issue.

CVE-2020-1971

Reviewed-by: Tomas Mraz <tmraz@fedoraproject.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        result = ASN1_TYPE_cmp(a->d.other, b->d.other);'], 'added_lines': ['        result = ASN1_TYPE_cmp(a->d.x400Address, b->d.x400Address);', '        break;', '', '        result = edipartyname_cmp(a->d.ediPartyName, b->d.ediPartyName);']}
description: The X.509 GeneralName type is a generic type for representing different types of names. One of those name types is known as EDIPartyName. OpenSSL provides a function GENERAL_NAME_cmp which compares different instances of a GENERAL_NAME to see if they are equal or not. This function behaves incorrectly when both GENERAL_NAMEs contain an EDIPARTYNAME. A NULL pointer dereference and a crash may occur leading to a possible denial of service attack. OpenSSL itself uses the GENERAL_NAME_cmp function for two purposes: 1) Comparing CRL distribution point names between an available CRL and a CRL distribution point embedded in an X509 certificate 2) When verifying that a timestamp response token signer matches the timestamp authority name (exposed via the API functions TS_RESP_verify_response and TS_RESP_verify_token) If an attacker can control both items being compared then that attacker could trigger a crash. For example if the attacker can trick a client or server into checking a malicious certificate against a malicious CRL then this may occur. Note that some applications automatically download CRLs based on a URL embedded in a certificate. This checking happens prior to the signatures on the certificate and CRL being verified. OpenSSL's s_server, s_client and verify tools have support for the "-crl_download" option which implements automatic CRL downloading and this attack has been demonstrated to work against those tools. Note that an unrelated bug means that affected versions of OpenSSL cannot parse or construct correct encodings of EDIPARTYNAME. However it is possible to construct a malformed EDIPARTYNAME that OpenSSL's parser will accept and hence trigger this attack. All OpenSSL 1.1.1 and 1.0.2 versions are affected by this issue. Other OpenSSL releases are out of support and have not been checked. Fixed in OpenSSL 1.1.1i (Affected 1.1.1-1.1.1h). Fixed in OpenSSL 1.0.2x (Affected 1.0.2-1.0.2w).

code_evidence: The GEN_EDIPARTY case falls through to the same statement as GEN_X400 and calls ASN1_TYPE_cmp(a->d.other, b->d.other). However, for an EdiPartyName GENERAL_NAME, the union member holding the name is d.ediPartyName, not d.other; the code reads the wrong union arm and passes a pointer that is not the EdiPartyName structure to ASN1_TYPE_cmp.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits because the switch uses the wrong union member for EdiPartyName, causing a pointer that is not the valid name structure to be dereferenced, with the described NULL dereference and crash. This is a type/union confusion leading to a NULL dereference, not a simple missing NULL check.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the GEN_EDIPARTY branch shares the GEN_X400 comparison and dereferences the wrong union member (d.other instead of d.ediPartyName). Trigger: comparing two GENERAL_NAMEs whose type is GEN_EDIPARTY, e.g. a malicious certificate checked against a malicious CRL. Consequence: the mismatched pointer is dereferenced inside ASN1_TYPE_cmp, producing a NULL pointer dereference and crash (denial of service).

commit_msg:
A NULL pointer dereference was reported by Wei Chen:

  BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000000
  RIP: 0010:__list_del_entry_valid+0x26/0x80
  Call Trace:
   <TASK>
   sctp_sched_dequeue_common+0x1c/0x90
   sctp_sched_prio_dequeue+0x67/0x80
   __sctp_outq_teardown+0x299/0x380
   sctp_outq_free+0x15/0x20
   sctp_association_free+0xc3/0x440
   sctp_do_sm+0x1ca7/0x2210
   sctp_assoc_bh_rcv+0x1f6/0x340

This happens when calling sctp_sendmsg without connecting to server first.
In this case, a data chunk already queues up in send queue of client side
when processing the INIT_ACK from server in sctp_process_init() where it
calls sctp_stream_init() to alloc stream_in. If it fails to alloc stream_in
all stream_out will be freed in sctp_stream_init's err path. Then in the
asoc freeing it will crash when dequeuing this data chunk as stream_out
is missing.

As we can't free stream out before dequeuing all data from send queue, and
this patch is to fix it by moving the err path stream_out/in freeing in
sctp_stream_init() to sctp_stream_free() which is eventually called when
freeing the asoc in sctp_association_free(). This fix also makes the code
in sctp_process_init() more clear.

Note that in sctp_association_init() when it fails in sctp_stream_init(),
sctp_association_free() will not be called, and in that case it should
go to 'stream_free' err path to free stream instead of 'fail_init'.

Fixes: 5bbbbe32a431 ("sctp: introduce stream scheduler foundations")
Reported-by: Wei Chen <harperchen1110@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Xin Long <lucien.xin@gmail.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/831a3dc100c4908ff76e5bcc363be97f2778bc0b.1658787066.git.lucien.xin@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (sctp_stream_init(&asoc->stream, asoc->c.sinit_num_ostreams,', '\t\t\t     0, gfp))', '\t\tgoto fail_init;'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (sctp_stream_init(&asoc->stream, asoc->c.sinit_num_ostreams, 0, gfp))', '\t\tgoto stream_free;']}
description: A null pointer dereference issue was found in the sctp network protocol in net/sctp/stream_sched.c in Linux Kernel. If stream_in allocation is failed, stream_out is freed which would further be accessed. A local user could use this flaw to crash the system or potentially cause a denial of service.

code_evidence: sctp_stream_init is invoked with the association's stream; on failure the original code jumped to fail_init, leaving the partially initialized stream state (including freed stream_out) reachable during later association teardown.

The added stream_free label calls sctp_stream_free on the stream before generic cleanup, so the failed stream is released through the proper teardown path rather than leaving dangling stream_out for the outqueue dequeue path.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function's error path governs stream lifetime; the fix routes failure to stream_free to prevent a later dereference of a NULL/dangling stream_out. This matches CWE-476 (dereference of a pointer expected valid but NULL), not a generic memory leak.

evidence_lines.code:
stream_free:
sctp_stream_free(&asoc->stream);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: after sctp_stream_init fails, stream_out could be freed while the send queue still holds a queued data chunk, so later dequeue dereferenced a missing stream_out (NULL). Trigger: sctp_sendmsg before connect queues a chunk, then INIT_ACK processing calls sctp_stream_init which fails allocation. Consequence: NULL pointer dereference and kernel crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
binding: Moves the check for the first access to the initial document into BindingSecurity.

Checks the access to the initial document and reports it not only at
securityCheck() in V8Window.cpp but also at every call to
BindingSecurity::shouldAllowAccessTo() because V8 only calls back
securityCheck() on property lookups, and not for function invocation.

BindingSecurity::shouldAllowAccessTo() is called with every possible
cross-origin window, which means every possible new window.  Thus,
shouldAllowAccessTo() should be the right place to check the access
to the initial document.

BUG=630662
TBR=benwells@chromium.org

Review-Url: https://codereview.chromium.org/2209303002
Cr-Commit-Position: refs/heads/master@{#412195}
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    return canAccessFrame(isolate, accessingWindow, frame->securityContext()->getSecurityOrigin(), frame->domWindow(), exceptionState);'], 'added_lines': ['    return canAccessFrame(accessingWindow, frame->securityContext()->getSecurityOrigin(), frame->domWindow(), exceptionState);']}
description: Google Chrome before 53.0.2785.89 on Windows and OS X and before 53.0.2785.92 on Linux does not properly validate access to the initial document, which allows remote attackers to spoof the address bar via a crafted web site.

code_evidence: shouldAllowAccessTo() derives the target frame and its security context, returns false only when either is missing, and otherwise delegates the cross-origin decision to canAccessFrame() with the accessing window, target origin and target DOM window.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-254 (7PK - Security Features) is a Category covering security-feature topics such as access control; the function implements an access-control decision that omits validation of the initial document, matching that category's access-control theme. It is not a distinct weakness type, but the target label is supported by the missing access constraint.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the access decision for the initial document is delegated to canAccessFrame() without any check specific to the initial document, so callers relying on this function for cross-origin window access do not get that validation. Trigger: a crafted site invoking functions on a cross-origin window, where V8 does not call securityCheck(). Supported consequence: improper access validation enabling address-bar spoofing.

commit_msg:
Add handshake mode switch check in FINISH and PSK_FINISH.

Reference: DMTF-2023-0001

Fix: https://github.com/DMTF/libspdm/issues/2005

Signed-off-by: Jiewen Yao <jiewen.yao@intel.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['                                               response_size, response);', '    }', '    if (session_info->use_psk) {', '        return libspdm_generate_error_response(spdm_context,', '                                               SPDM_ERROR_CODE_UNEXPECTED_REQUEST, 0,']}
description:
libspdm is a sample implementation that follows the DMTF SPDM specifications. A vulnerability has been identified in SPDM session establishment in libspdm prior to version 2.3.1. If a device supports both DHE session and PSK session with mutual
authentication, the attacker may be able to establish the session with `KEY_EXCHANGE` and `PSK_FINISH` to bypass the mutual authentication. This is most likely to happen when the Requester begins a session using one method (DHE, for example) and then uses the other method's finish (PSK_FINISH in this example) to establish the session. The session hashes would be expected to fail in this case, but the condition was not detected.

This issue only impacts the SPDM responder, which supports `KEY_EX_CAP=1 and `PSK_CAP=10b` at same time with mutual authentication requirement. The SPDM requester is not impacted. The SPDM responder is not impacted if `KEY_EX_CAP=0` or `PSK_CAP=0` or `PSK_CAP=01b`. The SPDM responder is not impacted if mutual authentication is not required.

libspdm 1.0, 2.0, 2.1, 2.2, 2.3 are all impacted. Older branches are not maintained, but users of the 2.3 branch may receive a patch in version 2.3.2. The SPDM specification (DSP0274) does not contain this vulnerability.

code_evidence: The function resolves session_info from the session id but, before the patch, only checks for NULL; it does not reject a session whose use_psk flag indicates a PSK session when handling SPDM_FINISH. The added check at lines 64-69 returns an error if session_info->use_psk is set, preventing a FINISH request from being processed on a PSK-established session context.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing mode check lets an actor complete session establishment with a finish message that does not correspond to the authentication method actually performed, so the claimed identity/authentication is not properly proven. That is improper authentication (CWE-287), not merely a protocol parsing error.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the responder does not verify that the session's authentication mode matches the FINISH message type, so a session started with KEY_EXCHANGE (DHE) can be finished with PSK_FINISH. Trigger: attacker begins a DHE session and sends a PSK_FINISH instead of the expected FINISH; consequence: the mutual-authentication requirement is bypassed and the session is established without the intended authentication.

commit_msg:
x86/PV: writes of %fs and %gs base MSRs require canonical addresses

Commit c42494acb2 ("x86: fix FS/GS base handling when using the
fsgsbase feature") replaced the use of wrmsr_safe() on these paths
without recognizing that wr{f,g}sbase() use just wrmsrl() and that the
WR{F,G}SBASE instructions also raise #GP for non-canonical input.

Similarly arch_set_info_guest() needs to prevent non-canonical
addresses from getting stored into state later to be loaded by context
switch code. For consistency also check stack pointers and LDT base.
DR0..3, otoh, already get properly checked in set_debugreg() (albeit
we discard the error there).

The SHADOW_GS_BASE check isn't strictly necessary, but I think we
better avoid trying the WRMSR if we know it's going to fail.

This is CVE-2016-9385 / XSA-193.

Reported-by: Andrew Cooper <andrew.cooper3@citrix.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Reviewed-by: Andrew Cooper <andrew.cooper3@citrix.com>

+++ func_after

-            if ( !is_canonical_address(c.nat->user_regs.eip) ||
+            if ( !is_canonical_address(c.nat->user_regs.rip) ||
+                 !is_canonical_address(c.nat->user_regs.rsp) ||
+                 !is_canonical_address(c.nat->kernel_sp) ||
+                 (c.nat->ldt_ents && !is_canonical_address(c.nat->ldt_base)) ||
+                 !is_canonical_address(c.nat->fs_base) ||
+                 !is_canonical_address(c.nat->gs_base_kernel) ||

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            if ( !is_canonical_address(c.nat->user_regs.eip) ||'], 'added_lines': ['            if ( !is_canonical_address(c.nat->user_regs.rip) ||', '                 !is_canonical_address(c.nat->user_regs.rsp) ||', '                 !is_canonical_address(c.nat->kernel_sp) ||', '                 (c.nat->ldt_ents && !is_canonical_address(c.nat->ldt_base)) ||', '                 !is_canonical_address(c.nat->fs_base) ||', '                 !is_canonical_address(c.nat->gs_base_kernel) ||', '                 !is_canonical_address(c.nat->gs_base_user) ||']}
description: The x86 segment base write emulation functionality in Xen 4.4.x through 4.7.x allows local x86 PV guest OS administrators to cause a denial of service (host crash) by leveraging lack of canonical address checks.

code_evidence: In the non-compat PV branch, the entry check only validates user_regs.eip and three callback EIPs, returning -EINVAL on failure; it does not validate the FS/GS base values or stack pointers.

Later, the same unvalidated fields are copied directly into persistent vCPU state: fs_base, gs_base_kernel and gs_base_user are stored from c.nat->fs_base/gs_base_kernel/gs_base_user, and kernel_sp via line 157. These stored values are later loaded on context switch.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function receives structured guest input and fails to validate required properties (canonical address form) before safely storing it, matching CWE-20 improper input validation. The added canonical checks in the patch confirm the missing validation is the defect, rather than a transformation/filtering issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: guest-supplied segment base and stack pointer fields are accepted without canonical-address validation before being persisted into vCPU state. Trigger: a local PV guest administrator submits non-canonical fs_base/gs_base (or rsp/kernel_sp) via arch_set_info_guest. Consequence: later WRMSR/context-switch loading of non-canonical addresses raises #GP, crashing the host (DoS).

commit_msg:
Prevent a heap-buffer overrun

Bug #701791 "global-buffer-overflow at devices/gdevpjet.c:177 in pj_common_print_page"

We were not setting the unused bytes at the end of a line to 0, which
later caused us to read uninitialised data from the line, and attempt
to use that as the index into an 8-byte table. If the uninitialised
data was greater than 16 then we would read off the end of the table.

Its 'probably' benign since we aren't using tis data, and we probably
won't try to read from an invalid address, but its poor practice and
its easily fixed. Setting the buffer to 0x00 before we start ensures
that any padding bytes are in the valid range for the table.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['        memset(data, 0x00, DATA_SIZE);']}
description: A buffer overflow vulnerability in pj_common_print_page() in devices/gdevpjet.c of Artifex Software GhostScript v9.50 allows a remote attacker to cause a denial of service via a crafted PDF file. This is fixed in v9.51.

code_evidence: The loop copies each scan line into data with gdev_prn_copy_scan_lines using line_size, then trims trailing zero bytes and memset(end_data, 0, 7) to zero only 7 bytes of padding.

The inner loop then indexes 8-byte tables spr40/spr8/spr2 with dp[0]..dp[7] for i up to DATA_SIZE, so any padding byte beyond the 7 zeroed bytes retains uninitialised heap content and is used as a table index.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Although the copy itself uses line_size, the uninitialized padding is later consumed as an index into fixed 8-byte tables, producing an out-of-bounds access; the commit's memset fix aligns with a buffer-boundary weakness. CWE-120 is the assigned target, though the read-index mechanism is closer to CWE-125.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the buffer data is allocated but never initialized, and only a fixed 7-byte tail is cleared, leaving padding bytes uninitialized. Trigger: a crafted PDF line whose trailing bytes after trimming are not all zeroed, yielding a table index above 7. Consequence: out-of-bounds read of the 8-byte tables, causing a heap/global buffer overrun and denial of service.

commit_msg:
Patch series "Fix several device private page reference counting issues",
v2

This series aims to fix a number of page reference counting issues in
drivers dealing with device private ZONE_DEVICE pages.  These result in
use-after-free type bugs, either from accessing a struct page which no
longer exists because it has been removed or accessing fields within the
struct page which are no longer valid because the page has been freed.

During normal usage it is unlikely these will cause any problems.  However
without these fixes it is possible to crash the kernel from userspace. 
These crashes can be triggered either by unloading the kernel module or
unbinding the device from the driver prior to a userspace task exiting. 
In modules such as Nouveau it is also possible to trigger some of these
issues by explicitly closing the device file-descriptor prior to the task
exiting and then accessing device private memory.

This involves some minor changes to both PowerPC and AMD GPU code. 
Unfortunately I lack hardware to test either of those so any help there
would be appreciated.  The changes mimic what is done in for both Nouveau
and hmm-tests though so I doubt they will cause problems.


This patch (of 8):

When the CPU tries to access a device private page the migrate_to_ram()
callback associated with the pgmap for the page is called.  However no
reference is taken on the faulting page.  Therefore a concurrent migration
of the device private page can free the page and possibly the underlying
pgmap.  This results in a race which can crash the kernel due to the
migrate_to_ram() function pointer becoming invalid.  It also means drivers
can't reliably read the zone_device_data field because the page may have
been freed with memunmap_pages().

Close the race by getting a reference on the page while holding the ptl to
ensure it has not been freed.  Unfortunately the elevated reference count
will cause the migration required to handle the fault to fail.  To avoid
this failure pass the faulting page into the migrate_vma functions so that
if an elevated reference count is found it can be checked to see if it's
expected or not.

commit_msg:
KEYS: Fix race between updating and finding a negative key

Consolidate KEY_FLAG_INSTANTIATED, KEY_FLAG_NEGATIVE and the rejection
error into one field such that:

 (1) The instantiation state can be modified/read atomically.

 (2) The error can be accessed atomically with the state.

 (3) The error isn't stored unioned with the payload pointers.

This deals with the problem that the state is spread over three different
objects (two bits and a separate variable) and reading or updating them
atomically isn't practical, given that not only can uninstantiated keys
change into instantiated or rejected keys, but rejected keys can also turn
into instantiated keys - and someone accessing the key might not be using
any locking.

The main side effect of this problem is that what was held in the payload
may change, depending on the state.  For instance, you might observe the
key to be in the rejected state.  You then read the cached error, but if
the key semaphore wasn't locked, the key might've become instantiated
between the two reads - and you might now have something in hand that isn't
actually an error code.

The state is now KEY_IS_UNINSTANTIATED, KEY_IS_POSITIVE or a negative error
code if the key is negatively instantiated.  The key_is_instantiated()
function is replaced with key_is_positive() to avoid confusion as negative
keys are also 'instantiated'.

Additionally, barriering is included:

 (1) Order payload-set before state-set during instantiation.

 (2) Order state-read before payload-read when using the key.

Further separate barriering is necessary if RCU is being used to access the
payload content after reading the payload pointers.

Fixes: 146aa8b1453b ("KEYS: Merge the type-specific data with the payload data")

Reviewed-by: Eric Biggers <ebiggers@google.com>

commit_msg:
Use correct origin when prompting for proxy authentication.

Since M49, Chrome has been prompting for proxy authentication
credentials using the target origin instead of the origin of the proxy
server. Even if the proxy origin was displayed correctly, a mischievous
network operator could still spoof the proxy server origin. To mitigate
these problems, this CL:

* Fixes the origin used in the proxy authentication login prompt to use
  the origin of the proxy server.

* Indicate if the proxy server connection is insecure.

* Always throw up an interstitial and clear the omnibox when showing a
  proxy auth prompt.

* Use the correct origin when saving proxy authentication credentials.

description: TensorFlow is an open source platform for machine learning. If `QuantizedInstanceNorm` is given `x_min` or `x_max` tensors of a nonzero rank, it results in a segfault that can be used to trigger a denial of service attack. We have patched the issue in GitHub commit 785d67a78a1d533759fcd2f5e8d6ef778de849e0. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.10.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.9.1, TensorFlow 2.8.1, and TensorFlow 2.7.2, as these are also affected and still in supported range. There are no known workarounds for this issue.

code_evidence: The function reads `x_min` and `x_max` via `context->input(1).flat<float>()(0)` and `context->input(2).flat<float>()(0)` without checking that those tensors are rank-0 scalars. `flat<float>()` on a nonzero-rank tensor followed by unchecked indexing `(0)` accesses data outside the validated scalar assumption, producing a segfault when the op is given non-scalar min/max tensors.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The crash arises from an unchecked assertion-like assumption (scalar rank) being violated by attacker-controlled input, matching CWE-617's reachable assertion leading to application exit/crash. It is not a memory-corruption class per se; the supported impact is DoS via crash.

evidence_lines.code:
float input_min = context->input(1).flat<float>()(0);
float input_max = context->input(2).flat<float>()(0);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: missing rank/shape validation on the min/max input tensors before flat indexing. Trigger: an attacker supplies x_min or x_max with nonzero rank. Consequence: out-of-bounds/segfault crash leading to denial of service; the patch adds IsScalar OP_REQUIRES checks, confirming the missing constraint.

description: The CFM parser in tcpdump before 4.9.2 has a buffer over-read in print-cfm.c:cfm_print().

code_evidence: For CFM_CHASSIS_ID_MAC_ADDRESS, etheraddr_string(ndo, tptr + 1) reads six bytes without verifying chassis_id_length equals ETHER_ADDR_LEN; the earlier check only ensures cfm_tlv_len >= chassis_id_length, so a short declared chassis ID still causes a 6-byte read past the TLV buffer.
For CFM_CHASSIS_ID_NETWORK_ADDRESS, cfm_network_addr_print(ndo, tptr) is called without passing chassis_id_length, so the callee cannot bound its reads to the declared buffer size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads memory beyond the intended buffer during parsing of attacker-controlled packet data, matching CWE-125 Out-of-bounds Read. It is not a write (CWE-787) because only read access to the buffer occurs.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the chassis ID length is validated only against the TLV length, not against the fixed size required by the address format. Trigger: a Sender ID TLV with a MAC-address chassis ID whose declared length is less than 6, or a network-address chassis ID lacking a length argument. Consequence: the printer reads past the end of the captured TLV buffer, an out-of-bounds read.

commit_msg:
Add sanity check for tile coordinates (#823)

Coordinates are casted from OPJ_UINT32 to OPJ_INT32
Add sanity check for negative values and upper bound becoming lower
than lower bound.
See also
https://pdfium.googlesource.com/pdfium/+/b6befb2ed2485a3805cddea86dc7574510178ea9
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ["\t/* all those OPJ_UINT32 are casted to OPJ_INT32, let's do some sanity check */", '\tif ((l_tile->x0 < 0) || (l_tile->x1 <= l_tile->x0)) {', '\t\topj_event_msg(manager, EVT_ERROR, "Tile X coordinates are not supported\\n");', '\t\treturn OPJ_FALSE;', '\t}', "\t/* all those OPJ_UINT32 are casted to OPJ_INT32, let's do some sanity check */", '\tif ((l_tile->y0 < 0) || (l_tile->y1 <= l_tile->y0)) {', '\t\topj_event_msg(manager, EVT_ERROR, "Tile Y coordinates are not supported\\n");', '\t\treturn OPJ_FALSE;', '\t}', '\t']}
description: Heap-based buffer overflow in the opj_dwt_interleave_v function in dwt.c in OpenJPEG, as used in PDFium in Google Chrome before 53.0.2785.89 on Windows and OS X and before 53.0.2785.92 on Linux, allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via crafted coordinate values in JPEG 2000 data.

code_evidence: l_tx0/l_ty0 are computed as OPJ_UINT32 and then cast to OPJ_INT32 into l_tile->x0/x1/y0/y1. If the unsigned value exceeds INT32_MAX, the cast yields a negative or wrapped coordinate, so l_tile->x1 can become <= l_tile->x0 (or x0 < 0). These tile bounds then feed the component/resolution/band/precinct/code-block coordinate computations (lines 49-58, 112-128, 198-213) and the allocation size l_data_size = (x1-x0)*(y1-y0).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked coordinate conversion lets buffer size and index computations diverge from the actual intended extent, so later operations access memory outside the allocated buffer, matching CWE-119. The integer truncation is the root cause; the out-of-bounds memory operation is the supported consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: unchecked OPJ_UINT32-to-OPJ_INT32 truncation of attacker-controlled tile coordinates. Trigger: crafted JPEG 2000 data with large tx0/tdx or ty0/tdy producing tile bounds above INT32_MAX. Supported consequence: wrapped/negative tile extents corrupt the derived data_size and code-block counts, leading to undersized buffer allocation and subsequent out-of-bounds read/write (heap overflow).

description: The Zone::New function in zone.cc in Google V8 before 5.0.71.47, as used in Google Chrome before 50.0.2661.102, does not properly determine when to expand certain memory allocations, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (buffer overflow) or possibly have unspecified other impact via crafted JavaScript code.

code_evidence: Line 2 rounds size up and line 4 performs alignment correction on position_, which can push position_ past limit_ as the patch comment notes. Line 9 computes size_with_redzone by adding kASanRedzoneBytes to size. Line 10 checks bounds as limit_ < position_ + size_with_redzone, an addition that can wrap when position_ is near the address-space maximum, and it does not account for position_ already exceeding limit_. On a false check, lines 13-14 advance position_ and the allocation at result is used, so the bounds test fails to detect exhaustion.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The faulty bounds check permits memory operations beyond the intended buffer boundary, matching CWE-119. It is a bounds-restriction weakness rather than a pure integer issue because the defect manifests as an out-of-bounds buffer allocation/use.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the boundary test uses pointer-plus-size arithmetic that can overflow and omits the case where position_ exceeds limit_ after alignment. Trigger: a crafted allocation request/size and alignment state near the buffer limit. Consequence: the function treats an out-of-bounds allocation as valid and returns a buffer outside the intended region, enabling overflow.

Extend it to also check that targetoff is >= sizeof(xt_entry).
