description: The read_image_tga function in gd_tga.c in the GD Graphics Library (aka libgd) before 2.2.3 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read) via a crafted TGA image.

code_evidence: The RLE loop reads decompression_buffer[buffer_caret] and derives encoded_pixels from the crafted byte; the inner loop then reads decompression_buffer[buffer_caret + j] without verifying that buffer_caret plus the run length stays within image_block_size, the size of the allocated decompression_buffer.

The non-RLE branch similarly computes encoded_pixels = decompression_buffer[buffer_caret] + 1 and reads decompression_buffer[buffer_caret + j] with no bounds check on buffer_caret relative to image_block_size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads decompression_buffer beyond its allocated image_block_size, which is an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). It is not an out-of-bounds write, since the copied value is assigned to tga->bitmap rather than the source buffer.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: attacker-controlled RLE run counts advance buffer_caret and index decompression_buffer without validating the run against image_block_size. Trigger: a crafted TGA image whose packet header claims more pixels than remain. Consequence: reads past the allocated buffer, causing a crash/DoS (and potential memory disclosure).

commit_msg: check rootseek after correction #41
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            { d = (void*)(fd_map+zz_fd_gap+zz_offset); } /* fd_map+fd_gap==u_rootseek */', '        else'], 'added_lines': ['', '    if (zz_entries < 0 || zz_rootseek < 0 || zz_rootseek < 0)', '        return ZZIP_CORRUPTED;', '        {', '            d = (void*)(fd_map+zz_fd_gap+zz_offset); /* fd_map+fd_gap==u_rootseek */', '        } else']}
description: An issue was discovered in ZZIPlib 0.13.68. There is a bus error caused by the __zzip_parse_root_directory function of zip.c. Attackers could leverage this vulnerability to cause a denial of service via a crafted zip file.

code_evidence: zz_entries, zz_rootsize and zz_rootseek are taken directly from the disk trailer and corrected, without validating that they are non-negative before use.
zz_rootsize is passed to malloc as a size; a crafted negative/garbage root size yields an undersized or invalid allocation.

The loop uses zz_entries as the entry bound and computes d = fd_map+zz_fd_gap+zz_offset (mmap) or reads into dirent via seeks at zz_rootseek+zz_offset, with no check that zz_rootseek points inside the mapped/allocated region.
The bounds check compares zz_offset+sizeof(*d) against zz_rootsize, but both derive from attacker-controlled trailer fields, so the check can pass while the actual mapped buffer is smaller.
Name bounds check uses zz_offset + sizeof(*d) + u_namlen against zz_rootsize, again trusting the unvalidated root size.

memcpy(hdr->d_name, fd_map+zz_fd_gap+zz_offset+sizeof(*d), u_namlen) reads from the mapped region using offsets that may exceed the actual mapping, causing an out-of-bounds read (bus error) and possibly an out-of-bounds write into hdr.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs reads from fd_map and writes into the hdr buffer at offsets derived from unvalidated trailer fields, i.e., operations outside the intended buffer boundaries, which matches CWE-119. The specific out-of-bounds read/write is the buffer-bounds violation; integer/off-by-one subclasses would be more precise, but CWE-119 is the target.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: trailer-derived zz_entries, zz_rootsize and zz_rootseek are used to size the allocation and to index the mmap/read region without validating them against the real file/mapping size. Trigger: a crafted zip file with a malicious disk trailer. Consequence: out-of-bounds memory access (bus error / crash), supporting denial of service.

description: Jsish v3.5.0 was discovered to contain a heap-use-after-free via jsi_wswebsocketObjFree in src/jsiWebSocket.c. This vulnerability can lead to a Denial of Service (DoS).

code_evidence: dptr is copied from uobj->data at line 15, then the hash entry is deleted at line 18, and freefun(interp, dptr) releases the user object at line 20, yet uobj->data still references the freed block; the patch adds uobj->data = NULL to break that dangling reference.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because a stored pointer is dereferenced after the memory it points to has been released by freefun; the defect is retained-reference-after-free, not a simple double free or buffer overflow.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The root cause is that the user object's data pointer is freed via ptr->reg->freefun without being cleared, leaving uobj->data dangling. A later access through uobj->data (or a second free path) references the released allocation, producing a heap-use-after-free that can crash or corrupt memory (DoS).

commit_msg:
dm: Reset virtio device before release

With virtio polling mode enabled, a timer is running in the virtio
backend service. And the timer will also be triggered if its frondend
driver didn't do the device reset in shutdown. A freed virtio device
will be accessed in the polling timer handler.

Do the virtio reset() callback specifically to clear the polling timer
before the free.

Tracked-On: #6147
Signed-off-by: Shuo A Liu <shuo.a.liu@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Yonghua Huang <yonghua.huang@intel.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\tvirtio_reset_dev(&blk->base);']}
description: The polling timer handler in ACRN before 2.5 has a use-after-free for a freed virtio device, related to devicemodel/hw/pci/virtio/*.c.

code_evidence: Line 14 frees the virtio_blk object blk and line 15 closes the enclosing if block; no virtio reset or timer cancellation precedes free(blk).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because memory for blk is freed while a lingering timer handler can still access it, exactly the reuse of freed memory. This is a lifetime/ownership flaw, not merely a null-pointer dereference.

}
free(blk);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the deinit path releases blk without stopping the virtio polling timer, so a timer handler may still reference the freed device. commit_msg:
stb_image: Reject fractional JPEG component subsampling ratios

The component resamplers are not written to support this and I've
never seen it happen in a real (non-crafted) JPEG file so I'm
fine rejecting this as outright corrupt.

Fixes issue #1178.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['   }', '', "   // check that plane subsampling factors are integer ratios; our resamplers can't deal with fractional ratios", "   // and I've never seen a non-corrupted JPEG file actually use them", '   for (i=0; i < s->img_n; ++i) {', '      if (h_max % z->img_comp[i].h != 0) return stbi__err("bad H","Corrupt JPEG");', '      if (v_max % z->img_comp[i].v != 0) return stbi__err("bad V","Corrupt JPEG");']}
description: stb_image.h 2.27 has a heap-based buffer over in stbi__jpeg_load, leading to Information Disclosure or Denial of Service.

code_evidence: The first loop derives h_max/v_max from the per-component sampling factors but performs no divisibility check, so fractional subsampling ratios (e.g. h_max=3 with a component h=2) pass through.
The second loop then computes per-component dimensions from these maxima: x = ceil(img_x*h/h_max), w2 = img_mcu_x*h*8, and allocates raw_data of size w2*h2.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is an out-of-bounds write: insufficient validation of subsampling ratios leads to undersized allocations that later receive decoded data beyond their bounds. This is a write past the end of the intended buffer, matching CWE-787 rather than a pure read-side or integer-only weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the header parser accepts component sampling factors whose ratios to h_max/v_max are non-integer, while the downstream resampler and buffer sizing assume integer ratios. When such a crafted JPEG is decoded, the computed per-component dimensions and subsequent resampling disagree with the allocated buffers, so decoded writes run past the end of the component buffer, causing heap corruption, information disclosure, or a crash.

commit_msg:
Fix NPE in restoring code.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 388303253
Change-Id: Ia8c68568cb854bca538909a182b31a618d68ce55
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            size, "elements"));'], 'added_lines': ['            size, " elements"));', '  {', '    const int64_t size = tensor_name_t.NumElements();', '    OP_REQUIRES(context, size > restore_index,', '                errors::InvalidArgument(', '                    "Input 1 (file_pattern) must be a have at least ",', '                    restore_index + 1, " elements"));', '  }']}
description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. When restoring tensors via raw APIs, if the tensor name is not provided, TensorFlow can be tricked into dereferencing a null pointer. Alternatively, attackers can read memory outside the bounds of heap allocated data by providing some tensor names but not enough for a successful restoration. The [implementation](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/47a06f40411a69c99f381495f490536972152ac0/tensorflow/core/kernels/save_restore_tensor.cc#L158-L159) retrieves the tensor list corresponding to the `tensor_name` user controlled input and immediately retrieves the tensor at the restoration index (controlled via `preferred_shard` argument). This occurs without validating that the provided list has enough values. If the list is empty this results in dereferencing a null pointer (undefined behavior). If, however, the list has some elements, if the restoration index is outside the bounds this results in heap OOB read. We have patched the issue in GitHub commit 9e82dce6e6bd1f36a57e08fa85af213e2b2f2622. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.6.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.5.1, TensorFlow 2.4.3, and TensorFlow 2.3.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: Input 1 (tensor_name_t) is user-controlled, but line 15 indexes flat<tstring>() at restore_index without checking that the tensor has enough elements. If the tensor is empty, the underlying data pointer is null and the access dereferences it; if it has fewer elements than restore_index, the access is out of bounds.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The empty-tensor case directly produces a NULL pointer dereference, matching CWE-476. The same missing check also enables an OOB read, but CWE-476 captures the null-dereference behavior described here.

evidence_lines.code:
const Tensor& tensor_name_t = context->input(1);
const string& tensor_name = tensor_name_t.flat<tstring>()(restore_index);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is the missing bounds check on tensor_name_t before indexing at restore_index. Trigger: an empty tensor_name input (null data pointer) or a restoration index beyond the element count. Supported consequence: null pointer dereference (undefined behavior/crash), and for non-empty short lists a heap out-of-bounds read.

description: A stack-based buffer under-read in htmldoc before 1.9.12, allows attackers to cause a denial of service via a crafted BMP image to image_load_bmp.

code_evidence: img->width and img->height are read directly from the BMP header via read_long and stored without validation.
depth and colors_used come from the file; when colors_used is 0 and depth <= 8 it is set to 1 << depth, and that count drives fread into the fixed colormap[256][4] array.
In the 4-bit RLE path, temp is assigned getc(fp) when color < 0, with no check that the byte is within the 256-entry colormap.
temp is then used as an index (temp >> 4, temp & 15) into colormap, so an attacker-controlled byte selects the array row.

This is distinct from an out-of-bounds write, since the observed unsafe accesses are reads from colormap rather than stores.

img->width       = read_long(fp);
img->height      = read_long(fp);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The root cause is missing bounds validation on header-derived values before they index or size fixed buffers. A crafted BMP can yield out-of-range colormap indices or an oversized colors_used, causing reads past the colormap array bounds; the added width/height and getc masking checks confirm the unvalidated-input trigger. The supported consequence is a crash/denial of service (and possible memory disclosure).

commit_msg:
Fix heap OOB / undefined behavior in `RaggedTensorToTensor`

PiperOrigin-RevId: 373244623
Change-Id: I2d6cbbc8c67b238a8815bf58097f7586d87c54f2
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        CalculateOutputIndexValueRowID(', '            context, row_partition_tensor, parent_output_index,', '            output_index_multiplier, output_size, result);', '        return tensorflow::Status::OK();', '        CalculateOutputIndexRowSplit(', '            context, row_partition_tensor, parent_output_index,', '            output_index_multiplier, output_size, result);', '        return tensorflow::Status::OK();'], 'added_lines': ['        return CalculateOutputIndexValueRowID(', '            row_partition_tensor, parent_output_index, output_index_multiplier,', '            output_size, result);', '        return CalculateOutputIndexRowSplit(', '            row_partition_tensor, parent_output_index, output_index_multiplier,', '            output_size, result);']}
description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. Due to lack of validation in `tf.raw_ops.RaggedTensorToTensor`, an attacker can exploit an undefined behavior if input arguments are empty. The implementation(https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/656e7673b14acd7835dc778867f84916c6d1cac2/tensorflow/core/kernels/ragged_tensor_to_tensor_op.cc#L356-L360) only checks that one of the tensors is not empty, but does not check for the other ones. There are multiple `DCHECK` validations to prevent heap OOB, but these are no-op in release builds, hence they don't prevent anything. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.5.0. We will also cherrypick these commits on TensorFlow 2.4.2, TensorFlow 2.3.3, TensorFlow 2.2.3 and TensorFlow 2.1.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: The ROW_SPLITS branch validates only that row_partition_tensor.size() - 1 does not exceed parent_output_index.size(), a one-sided size check that does not constrain the actual buffer sizes used by CalculateOutputIndexRowSplit.
The VALUE_ROWIDS branch calls CalculateOutputIndexValueRowID and unconditionally returns OK without any size validation of row_partition_tensor against parent_output_index.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is an incorrect/insufficient calculation and validation of buffer sizes before use, matching CWE-131. It is not merely a missing length check on a single value but a failure to correctly bound the sizes of buffers passed to the calculation helpers, enabling OOB.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function performs incomplete size validation, checking only one relation for ROW_SPLITS and none for VALUE_ROWIDS before invoking index-calculation helpers that write into result. Trigger: crafted ragged partition tensors with mismatched/empty dimensions. Consequence: incorrect buffer-size assumptions lead to heap out-of-bounds access, as the real checks were only DCHECKs disabled in release builds.

commit_msg:
Fix CVE-2022-3786 in punycode decoder.

Fixed the ossl_a2ulabel() function which also contained a potential
buffer overflow, albeit without control of the contents.
This overflow could result in a crash (causing a denial of service).

The function also did not NUL-terminate the output in some cases.

The two issues fixed here were dentified and reported
by Viktor Dukhovni while researching CVE-2022-3602.

Reviewed-by: Matt Caswell <matt@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Tomas Mraz <tomas@openssl.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['', '                (written_out - i) * sizeof *pDecoded);'], 'added_lines': ['                (written_out - i) * sizeof(*pDecoded));']}
description: A buffer overrun can be triggered in X.509 certificate verification, specifically in name constraint checking. Note that this occurs after certificate chain signature verification and requires either a CA to have signed a malicious certificate or for an application to continue certificate verification despite failure to construct a path to a trusted issuer. An attacker can craft a malicious email address in a certificate to overflow an arbitrary number of bytes containing the `.' character (decimal 46) on the stack. This buffer overflow could result in a crash (causing a denial of service). In a TLS client, this can be triggered by connecting to a malicious server. In a TLS server, this can be triggered if the server requests client authentication and a malicious client connects.

code_evidence: Line 16-17 bounds-check only basic_count against max_out before the loop at 18-23 writes pDecoded[loop] for each basic code point.

The insertion path at 53-56 checks written_out >= max_out, then memmoves (written_out - i) elements and writes pDecoded[i]; the check does not account for the shift destination pDecoded + i + 1 exceeding max_out.
max_out is taken from *pout_length at line 8, the caller-supplied output capacity, so the constraint is the declared output size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This is a buffer copy into pDecoded without ensuring the input size (written_out+1) fits the output capacity max_out, matching CWE-120's classic copy-without-size-check pattern. It is not merely an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) because the memmove and assignment write beyond the destination buffer.

evidence_lines.code:
if (basic_count > max_out)
return 0;
unsigned int max_out = *pout_length;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The decoder copies decoded code points into pDecoded while using max_out as capacity, but the memmove/write at 55-57 can place data at index i+1 up to written_out+1 without verifying that written_out+1 <= max_out; i is derived from attacker-controlled punycode digits. Triggering an encoded label whose insertion index shifts existing entries past the buffer writes past pDecoded, causing a stack buffer overflow and crash.

commit_msg:
In emac_probe, &adpt->work_thread is bound with
emac_work_thread. Then it will be started by timeout
handler emac_tx_timeout or a IRQ handler emac_isr.

If we remove the driver which will call emac_remove
  to make cleanup, there may be a unfinished work.

The possible sequence is as follows:

Fix it by finishing the work before cleanup in the emac_remove
and disable timeout response.

CPU0                  CPU1

                    |emac_work_thread
emac_remove         |
free_netdev         |
kfree(netdev);      |
                    |emac_reinit_locked
                    |emac_mac_down
                    |//use netdev
Fixes: b9b17debc69d ("net: emac: emac gigabit ethernet controller driver")
Signed-off-by: Zheng Wang <zyytlz.wz@163.com>

Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tnetif_carrier_off(netdev);', '\tnetif_tx_disable(netdev);', '', '', '\tfree_irq(adpt->irq.irq, &adpt->irq);', '\tcancel_work_sync(&adpt->work_thread);']}
description: The Linux kernel before 6.2.9 has a race condition and resultant use-after-free in drivers/net/ethernet/qualcomm/emac/emac.c if a physically proximate attacker unplugs an emac based device.

code_evidence: emac_remove unregisters the netdev and deletes the NAPI instance, then calls free_netdev(netdev) at line 13 without first stopping the work item bound to adpt->work_thread. The work item can be queued by the timeout or IRQ path and run emac_reinit_locked/emac_mac_down against netdev concurrently with this teardown.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-362 fits because two concurrent sequences (device removal and the work handler) access the shared netdev without exclusive access; the missing cancel_work_sync before free_netdev leaves a timing window. This is a race leading to UAF, not merely a generic memory-safety bug.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: teardown frees the netdev while the work_thread work item may still be executing or pending, with no synchronization. Trigger: device removal racing with the timeout/IRQ handler scheduling the work. Consequence: use-after-free of netdev, causing crash or memory corruption.

description: An out-of-memory flaw was found in libtiff. Passing a crafted tiff file to TIFFOpen() API may allow a remote attacker to cause a denial of service via a craft input with size smaller than 379 KB.

code_evidence: The directory count is read from the file (ReadOK into dircount16) and only sanity-checked against 4096, not against the actual file size.
_TIFFCheckMalloc allocates dircount16 * dirsize bytes based solely on the file-supplied count; no comparison with tif_size or file length is made before allocation.
In the mapped path, dircount16 is similarly bounded only by 4096 before allocation and the subsequent tif_size check at lines 171-173 occurs after the allocation.
A crafted TIFF with a large directory count relative to a tiny file causes a large heap allocation to be attempted before any size relationship to the file is validated.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-400 fits because the function fails to restrict a file-controlled resource (heap allocation) to a size consistent with the input, allowing an attacker to force excessive memory consumption. This is uncontrolled resource consumption rather than a memory-safety corruption, since the allocation succeeds but exhausts memory.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the directory count from the file drives _TIFFCheckMalloc without verifying the requested size against the actual file size. Trigger: a small crafted TIFF declaring a large dircount (up to 4096 entries) causes a disproportionate allocation; the missing size-vs-filesize constraint permits memory exhaustion. Consequence: denial of service via out-of-memory when processing the file.

Check for multiplication overflow in MSADPCM decodeSample

Check for multiplication overflow (using __builtin_mul_overflow
if available) in MSADPCM.cpp decodeSample and return an empty
decoded block if an error occurs.

This fixes the 00193-audiofile-signintoverflow-MSADPCM case of #41

code_evidence: Line 4-5 computes linearSample from products of state.sample1/sample2 and coefficients, then line 6 adds a product of the sign-extended code and state.delta; these signed int multiplications and additions have no bounds check before clamping. Line 8 multiplies state.delta by adaptationTable[code] with no overflow guard, and the result feeds state.delta for subsequent samples.

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: signed int multiplications (coefficient products and delta*adaptationTable[code]) are performed without overflow checks on attacker-influenced state and code values. Trigger: a crafted MSADPCM file drives delta/sample values so a product exceeds INT range, producing a wrapped value that is clamped or stored back into state.delta, corrupting decode state and potentially crashing. Consequence: denial of service via crash/instability.

commit_msg:
Generating strings for XKB data used a single shared static buffer,
which offered several opportunities for errors. Use a ring of
resizable buffers instead, to avoid problems when strings end up
longer than anticipated.

Reviewed-by: Michal Srb <msrb@suse.com>
Signed-off-by: Keith Packard <keithp@keithp.com>
Signed-off-by: Julien Cristau <jcristau@debian.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if (len >= BUFFER_SIZE)', '        len = BUFFER_SIZE - 1;'], 'added_lines': []}
description: In X.Org Server (aka xserver and xorg-server) before 1.19.4, a local attacker authenticated to the X server could overflow a global buffer, causing crashes of the X server or potentially other problems by injecting large or malformed XKB related atoms and accessing them via xkbcomp.

code_evidence: Line 22 computes len = strlen(tmp)+1 from attacker-influenced atom data; line 24 adds 4 for XkbCFile format. The buffer is sized with tbGetBuffer(len) at line 27, then line 29 writes the 5-byte literal "vmod_" into it via strcpy, while line 30 copies len-4 bytes starting at offset 5. For non-CFile format, line 33 copies len bytes from tmp.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs write operations beyond the intended boundary of a heap buffer, which is the definition of CWE-119. The defect is an incorrect size computation feeding tbGetBuffer rather than a pure length truncation issue, so an out-of-bounds write class fits better than a simple off-by-one label.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: buffer length accounting is inconsistent with the actual copy sizes. In the XkbCFile branch, strcpy writes 6 bytes including the NUL while the buffer is only len bytes and strncpy writes len-4 bytes at offset 5, so writes can extend past the allocation. Trigger: a large or malformed XKB virtual-modifier atom name reaching NameForAtom. Supported consequence: out-of-bounds write on the heap buffer, causing crashes or memory corruption.

commit_msg:
9pfs: fix information leak in xattr read

9pfs uses g_malloc() to allocate the xattr memory space, if the guest
reads this memory before writing to it, this will leak host heap memory
to the guest. This patch avoid this.

Signed-off-by: Li Qiang <liqiang6-s@360.cn>
Reviewed-by: Greg Kurz <groug@kaod.org>
Signed-off-by: Greg Kurz <groug@kaod.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    xattr_fidp->fs.xattr.value = g_malloc(size);'], 'added_lines': ['    xattr_fidp->fs.xattr.value = g_malloc0(size);']}
description: The v9fs_xattrcreate function in hw/9pfs/9p.c in QEMU (aka Quick Emulator) allows local guest OS administrators to obtain sensitive host heap memory information by reading xattribute values before writing to them.

code_evidence: Line 13 unmarshals a guest-controlled size into local variable size. Line 26 stores size as the xattr length, and line 30 allocates that many bytes with g_malloc(size), which does not zero-initialize the buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Returning uninitialized host heap bytes to the guest exposes sensitive memory to an unauthorized actor, matching CWE-200's confidentiality impact. The fix to g_malloc0 confirms the uninitialized buffer was the disclosure source rather than a bounds error.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The xattr value buffer is allocated uninitialized and its length is exposed to the guest; if the guest reads the xattr before writing it, uninitialized host heap contents are returned. Root cause is missing zero-initialization of guest-accessible memory; the supported consequence is disclosure of host heap data.

In bnxt_re_create_srq(), when ib_copy_to_udata() fails allocated memory
should be released by goto fail.

Fixes: 37cb11acf1f7 ("RDMA/bnxt_re: Add SRQ support for Broadcom adapters")
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20190910222120.16517-1-navid.emamdoost@gmail.com

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\tgoto exit;'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\tgoto fail;']}
description: A memory leak in the bnxt_re_create_srq() function in drivers/infiniband/hw/bnxt_re/ib_verbs.c in the Linux kernel through 5.3.11 allows attackers to cause a denial of service (memory consumption) by triggering copy to udata failures, aka CID-4a9d46a9fe14.

code_evidence: On the udata path, after bnxt_qplib_create_srq succeeds, ib_copy_to_udata failure is handled by destroying the qplib SRQ and then jumping to exit.
The fail label at line 59 releases srq->umem via ib_umem_release, but the error path instead reaches exit at line 61, skipping that release while returning rc.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-401 fits because an allocated memory object (the user SRQ umem) is not released after its effective lifetime on an error path, leaving it unavailable for reuse. This is a missing-release leak rather than a use-after-free or double-free.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The root cause is an incorrect goto target on the ib_copy_to_udata error path: the user SRQ's umem is released only at fail, but the code jumps to exit. Triggered by a copy-to-udata failure, the allocated umem is not released, causing a memory leak and resource-consumption DoS on repeated failures.

commit_msg:
Commit bdcf0a423ea1 ("kernel: make groups_sort calling a responsibility
group_info allocators") appears to break nfsd rootsquash in a pretty
major way.

It adds a call to groups_sort() inside the loop that copies/squashes
gids, which means the valid gids are sorted along with the following
garbage.  The net result is that the highest numbered valid gids are
replaced with any lower-valued garbage gids, possibly including 0.

We should sort only once, after filling in all the gids.

Fixes: bdcf0a423ea1 ("kernel: make groups_sort calling a responsibility ...")
Signed-off-by: Ben Hutchings <ben.hutchings@codethink.co.uk>
Acked-by: J. Bruce Fields <bfields@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t/* Each thread allocates its own gi, no race */', '\t\t\tgroups_sort(gi);', '\t\t}'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t}', '\t\t/* Each thread allocates its own gi, no race */', '\t\tgroups_sort(gi);']}
description: Linux kernel version after commit bdcf0a423ea1 - 4.15-rc4+, 4.14.8+, 4.9.76+, 4.4.111+ contains a Incorrect Access Control vulnerability in NFS server (nfsd) that can result in remote users reading or writing files they should not be able to via NFS. This attack appear to be exploitable via NFS server must export a filesystem with the "rootsquash" options enabled. This vulnerability appears to have been fixed in after commit 1995266727fa.

code_evidence: The ROOTSQUASH branch allocates gi sized to rqgi->ngroups (line 27), then copies/squashes each gid into gi->gid[i] inside the loop. groups_sort(gi) is called inside that same loop at line 35, before all entries have been written, so uninitialized trailing gid slots participate in the sort and can displace valid squashed gids, including with 0 (root).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The flaw misassigns the effective privilege set (supplementary groups) after root squashing, giving the actor an unintended sphere of control, matching CWE-269 Improper Privilege Management. It is not merely a data-integrity bug because the corrupted gid list directly changes access-control decisions made with the resulting credential.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: sorting the partially filled group_info inside the fill loop mixes uninitialized garbage gids with valid ones. Trigger: an NFS export with rootsquash where the client sends multiple supplementary groups. Consequence: the resulting credential group list is corrupted, potentially reinserting gid 0 or other unintended gids, granting the squashed user file access beyond the intended anon identity.

commit_msg:
[gsm] Delay the creation of the GsmXSMPClient until it really exists

We used to create the GsmXSMPClient before the XSMP connection is really
accepted. This can lead to some issues, though. An example is:
https://bugzilla.gnome.org/show_bug.cgi?id=598211#c19. Quoting:

 "What is happening is that a new client (probably metacity in your
 case) is opening an ICE connection in the GSM_MANAGER_PHASE_END_SESSION
 phase, which causes a new GsmXSMPClient to be added to the client
 store. The GSM_MANAGER_PHASE_EXIT phase then begins before the client
 has had a chance to establish a xsmp connection, which means that
 client->priv->conn will not be initialized at the point that xsmp_stop
 is called on the new unregistered client."

The fix is to create the GsmXSMPClient object when there's a real XSMP
connection. This implies moving the timeout that makes sure we don't
have an empty client to the XSMP server.

https://bugzilla.gnome.org/show_bug.cgi?id=598211
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        IceListenObj    listener;', '        GsmClient      *client;', '        GsmXsmpServer  *server;', '', '        listener = data->listener;', '        server = data->server;', '        ice_conn = IceAcceptConnection (listener, &status);', '        client = gsm_xsmp_client_new (ice_conn);', '        ice_conn->context = client;', '', '        gsm_store_add (server->priv->client_store, gsm_client_peek_id (client), G_OBJECT (client));', '        /* the store will own the ref */', '        g_object_unref (client);'], 'added_lines': ['        ice_conn = IceAcceptConnection (data->listener, &status);', '        auth_ice_connection (ice_conn);']}
description: Bad reference counting in the context of accept_ice_connection() in gsm-xsmp-server.c in old versions of gnome-session up until version 2.29.92 allows a local attacker to establish ICE connections to gnome-session with invalid authentication data (an invalid magic cookie). Each failed authentication attempt will leak a file descriptor in gnome-session. When the maximum number of file descriptors is exhausted in the gnome-session process, it will enter an infinite loop trying to communicate without success, consuming 100% of the CPU. The graphical session associated with the gnome-session process will stop working correctly, because communication with gnome-session is no longer possible.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The shown function only accepts an ICE connection and creates a client; it contains no loop, so it does not directly demonstrate an infinite loop (CWE-835). The described CPU-exhaustion loop and file-descriptor leak are not visible in this function.

commit_msg:
win: fix unsavory rwlock fallback implementation

Before this patch an uv_mutex_t (backed by a critical section) could be
released by a tread different from the thread that acquired it, which is
not allowed. This is fixed by using a semaphore instead.

Note that the affected code paths were used on Windows XP and Windows
Server 2003 only.

This is a back-port of commits 3eb6764, 1ad6ad7, 9a4fd26, 9823922
85adf43 and bd1777f from the v1.x branch.

Fixes: https://github.com/libuv/libuv/issues/515
Refs: https://github.com/libuv/libuv/pull/525
PR-URL: https://github.com/libuv/libuv/pull/903
Reviewed-By: Ben Noordhuis <info@bnoordhuis.nl>
Reviewed-By: Bert Belder <bertbelder@gmail.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  if (r && r != EBUSY && r != EAGAIN)', '    abort();', '', '  if (r)', '  else', '    return 0;'], 'added_lines': ['  if (r) {', '    if (r != EBUSY && r != EAGAIN)', '      abort();', '  }', '  return 0;']}
description: The uv_rwlock_t fallback implementation for Windows XP and Server 2003 in libuv before 1.7.4 does not properly prevent threads from releasing the locks of other threads, which allows attackers to cause a denial of service (deadlock) or possibly have unspecified other impact by leveraging a race condition.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function is a POSIX pthread_rwlock_trywrlock wrapper; it contains no Windows fallback rwlock implementation, no lock release logic, and no shared-resource synchronization sequence, so it does not support the described cross-thread release race (CWE-362).

commit_msg:
Handle empty Tight gradient rects

We always assumed there would be one pixel per row so a rect with
a zero width would result in us writing to unknown memory.

This could theoretically be used by a malicious server to inject
code in to the viewer process.

Issue found by Pavel Cheremushkin from Kaspersky Lab.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    /* First pixel in a row */', '    for (c = 0; c < 3; c++) {', '      pix[c] = inbuf[y*rectWidth*3+c] + prevRow[c];', '      thisRow[c] = pix[c];', '    }', '    pf.bufferFromRGB((rdr::U8*)&outbuf[y*stride], pix, 1);', '    /* Remaining pixels of a row */', '    for (x = 1; x < rectWidth; x++) {'], 'added_lines': ['    for (x = 0; x < rectWidth; x++) {', '      /* First pixel in a row */', '      if (x == 0) {', '        for (c = 0; c < 3; c++) {', '          pix[c] = inbuf[y*rectWidth*3+c] + prevRow[c];', '          thisRow[c] = pix[c];', '        }', '        pf.bufferFromRGB((rdr::U8*)&outbuf[y*stride], pix, 1);', '        continue;', '      }']}
description: TigerVNC version prior to 1.10.1 is vulnerable to heap buffer overflow, which occurs in TightDecoder::FilterGradient. Exploitation of this vulnerability could potentially result into remote code execution. This attack appear to be exploitable via network connectivity.

code_evidence: For every row y, the pre-patch code unconditionally reads inbuf[y*rectWidth*3+c] and writes outbuf[y*stride] for the first pixel even when rectWidth is 0, so the row has no pixels.

The inner loop starts at x=1 and indexes prevRow[x*3+c] and thisRow[x*3+c]; with rectWidth 0 the first-pixel write still occurs, and memcpy copies thisRow whose length is not tied to the actual row width.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the function writes decoded pixel data past the intended buffer when a zero-width rect is processed; the missing width constraint is the cause, and memory corruption is the consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the gradient filter assumes at least one pixel per row and performs a first-pixel read/write without checking rectWidth. Trigger: a malicious server sends a Tight gradient rect with zero width. The unconditional write to outbuf[y*stride] and fixed-size thisRow/prevRow handling write outside the intended row buffer, giving a heap out-of-bounds write that may permit code injection in the viewer.

commit_msg:
Fix integer overflows in PAC parsing

In krb5_parse_pac(), check for buffer counts large enough to threaten
integer overflow in the header length and memory length calculations.
Avoid potential integer overflows when checking the length of each
buffer.  Credit to OSS-Fuzz for discovering one of the issues.

CVE-2022-42898:

In MIT krb5 releases 1.8 and later, an authenticated attacker may be
able to cause a KDC or kadmind process to crash by reading beyond the
bounds of allocated memory, creating a denial of service.  A
privileged attacker may similarly be able to cause a Kerberos or GSS
application service to crash.  On 32-bit platforms, an attacker can
also cause insufficient memory to be allocated for the result,
potentially leading to remote code execution in a KDC, kadmind, or GSS
or Kerberos application server process.  An attacker with the
privileges of a cross-realm KDC may be able to extract secrets from a
KDC process's memory by having them copied into the PAC of a new
ticket.

target_version: 1.19-next

description: PAC parsing in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) before 1.19.4 and 1.20.x before 1.20.1 has integer overflows that may lead to remote code execution (in KDC, kadmind, or a GSS or Kerberos application server) on 32-bit platforms (which have a resultant heap-based buffer overflow), and cause a denial of service on other platforms. This occurs in krb5_pac_parse in lib/krb5/krb/pac.c. Heimdal before 7.7.1 has "a similar bug."

commit_msg:
delta: fix overflow when computing limit

When checking whether a delta base offset and length fit into the base
we have in memory already, we can trigger an overflow which breaks the
check. This would subsequently result in us reading memory from out of
bounds of the base.

The issue is easily fixed by checking for overflow when adding `off` and
`len`, thus guaranteeting that we are never indexing beyond `base_len`.
This corresponds to the git patch 8960844a7 (check patch_delta bounds
more carefully, 2006-04-07), which adds these overflow checks.

Reported-by: Riccardo Schirone <rschiron@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\tsize_t off = 0, len = 0;', '\t\t\tif (base_len < off + len || res_sz < len)'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\tsize_t off = 0, len = 0, end;', '\t\t\tif (GIT_ADD_SIZET_OVERFLOW(&end, off, len) ||', '\t\t\t    base_len < end || res_sz < len)', '']}
description: A flaw was found in libgit2 before version 0.27.3. It has been discovered that an unexpected sign extension in git_delta_apply function in delta.c file may lead to an integer overflow which in turn leads to an out of bound read, allowing to read before the base object. An attacker may use this flaw to leak memory addresses or cause a Denial of Service.

code_evidence: ADD_DELTA shifts an unsigned byte left by 0/8/16/24 bits and ORs it into size_t off/len; byte shifts 24 and 16 can set the sign bit, and assignment/accumulation into the wider size_t sign-extends the value.
The bounds check base_len < off + len then adds off and len without overflow protection, so a wrapped sum can pass and memcpy(res_dp, base + off, len) reads out of bounds of base.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The root cause is an incorrect numeric conversion: signed shifting/accumulation values are converted to size_t with sign extension, producing unexpected negative-like magnitudes rather than the intended unsigned offset/length. This matches CWE-681; the subsequent overflow and OOB read are consequences, not a separate integer-overflow label.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The delta stream supplies 32-bit little-endian offset/length fields through the shifting ADD_DELTA macro, whose signed intermediate values are sign-extended when stored into size_t. A crafted large offset causes off + len to overflow, defeating the base_len check, so memcpy reads before or beyond the base buffer; the consequence is an out-of-bounds read (memory disclosure or crash).

commit_msg:
tightvnc-filetransfer: fix heap use-after-free

One can only guess what the intended semantics were here, but as every
other rfbCloseClient() call in this file is followed by an immediate
return, let's assume this was forgotton in this case.

Anyway, don't forget to clean up to not leak memory.

Closes #241
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t    free(reason);', '\t    return;']}
description: LibVNC before commit ca2a5ac02fbbadd0a21fabba779c1ea69173d10b contains heap use-after-free vulnerability in server code of file transfer extension that can result remote code execution.

code_evidence: When rfbReadExact fails (n <= 0), the error path logs and calls rfbCloseClient(cl) but does not return, so execution falls through.
The function then logs reason via %s even though the read into it failed, and continues.
The only free of reason is later at lines 38-41, so the earlier fall-through does not itself free before use; however the missing early return after rfbCloseClient is the defect fixed in the patch.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the function continues to operate on client resources after rfbCloseClient has released them, and the patch's added return prevents that post-close use.

evidence_lines.code:
rfbLog("File [%s]: Method [%s]: File Download Cancel Request received:"
" reason <%s>\n", __FILE__, __FUNCTION__, reason);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: After rfbCloseClient(cl) on a read error, the function does not return and continues executing with a client that has been closed. The intended fix adds free(reason) and return immediately after rfbCloseClient, indicating the original code kept using state associated with the closed client, leading to use-after-free.

commit_msg:
crypto: mcryptd - Check mcryptd algorithm compatibility

Algorithms not compatible with mcryptd could be spawned by mcryptd
with a direct crypto_alloc_tfm invocation using a "mcryptd(alg)" name
construct.  This causes mcryptd to crash the kernel if an arbitrary
"alg" is incompatible and not intended to be used with mcryptd.  It is
an issue if AF_ALG tries to spawn mcryptd(alg) to expose it externally.
But such algorithms must be used internally and not be exposed.

We added a check to enforce that only internal algorithms are allowed
with mcryptd at the time mcryptd is spawning an algorithm.

Link: http://marc.info/?l=linux-crypto-vger&m=148063683310477&w=2
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Reported-by: Mikulas Patocka <mpatocka@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Tim Chen <tim.c.chen@linux.intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Herbert Xu <herbert@gondor.apana.org.au>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tmcryptd_check_internal(tb, &type, &mask);'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (!mcryptd_check_internal(tb, &type, &mask))', '\t\treturn -EINVAL;']}
description: crypto/mcryptd.c in the Linux kernel before 4.8.15 allows local users to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference and system crash) by using an AF_ALG socket with an incompatible algorithm, as demonstrated by mcryptd(md5).

code_evidence: mcryptd_check_internal(tb, &type, &mask) is called but its return value is discarded, so an incompatible algorithm name is not rejected. Execution continues to ahash_attr_alg(tb[1], type, mask); the returned halg is only checked with IS_ERR, not for a NULL result, and line 15 then dereferences it as &halg->base.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 matches because the function dereferences halg via halg->base without validating that the pointer is non-NULL, producing the described NULL pointer dereference DoS. This is a missing NULL check, distinct from merely ignoring an error return code.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the compatibility check's failure result is ignored, allowing an algorithm not intended for mcryptd (e.g. mcryptd(md5)) to proceed. The trigger is an AF_ALG request with such an incompatible name; the hash lookup then yields a value that is not an ERR_PTR but is invalid/NULL, and dereferencing halg->base causes a NULL pointer dereference and kernel crash.

commit_msg:
io_uring: fix race between timeout flush and removal

io_flush_timeouts() assumes the timeout isn't in progress of triggering
or being removed/canceled, so it unconditionally removes it from the
timeout list and attempts to cancel it.

Leave it on the list and let the normal timeout cancelation take care
of it.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # 5.5+
Signed-off-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\twhile (!list_empty(&ctx->timeout_list)) {', '\t\tstruct io_kiocb *req = list_first_entry(&ctx->timeout_list,', '\t\t\t\t\t\tstruct io_kiocb, timeout.list);', '\t\tlist_del_init(&req->timeout.list);'], 'added_lines': ['\tstruct io_kiocb *req, *tmp;', '\tlist_for_each_entry_safe(req, tmp, &ctx->timeout_list, timeout.list) {']}
description: In the Linux kernel before 5.17.3, fs/io_uring.c has a use-after-free due to a race condition in io_uring timeouts. This can be triggered by a local user who has no access to any user namespace; however, the race condition perhaps can only be exploited infrequently.

code_evidence: io_flush_timeouts iterates ctx->timeout_list while holding only ctx->timeout_lock and pulls the first entry with list_first_entry, treating it as a stable head of the list.
It then calls list_del_init(&req->timeout.list) to unlink the entry and immediately io_kill_timeout(req, 0), assuming no other path is concurrently triggering or removing that same timeout request.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The flaw is improper synchronization over the shared ctx->timeout_list/io_kiocb: the flush sequence is neither exclusive nor atomic against concurrent removal, matching CWE-362. It is not merely a logic bug because the defect depends on a concurrent interfering code sequence.

evidence_lines.code:
list_del_init(&req->timeout.list);
io_kill_timeout(req, 0);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the flush path assumes exclusive ownership of a timeout entry and unconditionally unlinks and kills it, while a concurrent timeout trigger/removal path can operate on the same io_kiocb. Trigger: a local user drives io_uring timeout completion racing with io_flush_timeouts. Consequence: the request is freed/killed twice or after removal, yielding a use-after-free and possible crash or instability.

for (count = 0; count < metadata->NumberOfStreams; count++) {

commit_msg:
encode: protect from stack under-flow

From GH #178 fuzzing
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  if (byte[i] & 0x40)'], 'added_lines': ['  if (byte[i] & 0x40 && i > 0)']}
description: An issue was discovered in GNU LibreDWG through 0.9.3. Crafted input will lead to a stack overflow in bits.c, possibly related to bit_read_TF.

code_evidence: The scan loop finds the first non-zero byte index i (0..3), then line 20 decrements i when bit 0x40 is set. Without the guard, when i==0 the decrement makes i negative, and line 22 writes byte[-1] &= 0x7f, an out-of-bounds write before the array.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes through a negative index to a stack array, which is a write before the beginning of the intended buffer, matching CWE-787. It is not a read overrun (CWE-125) because the faulty operation is the assignment byte[i] &= 0x7f.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the sign-extension adjustment decrements the buffer index without a lower-bound check. Trigger: crafted input where byte[0] has bit 0x40 set, causing i to become -1. Consequence: byte[i] &= 0x7f writes before the start of the 5-byte stack buffer byte[5], corrupting stack memory (stack underflow).

commit_msg:
(for 4.9.3) CVE-2018-14879/fix -V to fail invalid input safely

get_next_file() did not check the return value of strlen() and
underflowed an array index if the line read by fgets() from the file
started with \0. This caused an out-of-bounds read and could cause a
write. Add the missing check.

This vulnerability was discovered by Brian Carpenter & Geeknik Labs.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ["\tif (ptr[strlen(ptr) - 1] == '\\n')", "\t\tptr[strlen(ptr) - 1] = '\\0';"], 'added_lines': ['\tsize_t len;', '\tlen = strlen (ptr);', "\tif (len > 0 && ptr[len - 1] == '\\n')", "\t\tptr[len - 1] = '\\0';"]}
description: The command-line argument parser in tcpdump before 4.9.3 has a buffer overflow in tcpdump.c:get_next_file().

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function performs no buffer copy; the flaw is an out-of-bounds read/write from strlen(ptr)-1 underflowing to index -1 when ptr begins with a NUL byte, not a classic buffer copy overflow (CWE-120).

commit_msg: add checks for return value of limitMalloc (#392)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    *sect_buff_ptr = sect_buff;', '  if (!sect_buff)', '    {', '    TIFFError("createImageSection", "Unable to allocate/reallocate section buffer");', '    return (-1);', '    }'], 'added_lines': ['    if (!sect_buff)', '    {', '        TIFFError("createImageSection", "Unable to allocate/reallocate section buffer");', '        return (-1);', '    }', '      if (!sect_buff)', '      {', '          TIFFError("createImageSection", "Unable to allocate/reallocate section buffer");', '          return (-1);', '      }']}
description: Unchecked Return Value to NULL Pointer Dereference in tiffcrop in libtiff 4.3.0 allows attackers to cause a denial-of-service via a crafted tiff file. For users that compile libtiff from sources, the fix is available with commit f2b656e2.

code_evidence: limitMalloc(sectsize) return value is stored in sect_buff, assigned to *sect_buff_ptr, and immediately passed to _TIFFmemset without any NULL check in this branch.

The realloc path stores _TIFFrealloc into new_buff and checks it, but the fallback limitMalloc(sectsize) result is written to sect_buff and used in _TIFFmemset at line 26; only the later check at line 29 guards it, after the memset has already run.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function fails to check the return value of limitMalloc before using the resulting pointer, matching CWE-252 Unchecked Return Value. This differs from a pure NULL-dereference CWE because the defect is the omitted return-value validation enabling the failure to go undetected.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The allocation return values are consumed (dereferenced via _TIFFmemset) before being validated. When limitMalloc fails and returns NULL, the unchecked result is passed to memset, causing a NULL pointer dereference and crash (DoS). The root cause is the missing check at the point of use; the crash is the consequence.

commit_msg:
dccp/tcp: fix routing redirect race

As Eric Dumazet pointed out this also needs to be fixed in IPv6.
v2: Contains the IPv6 tcp/Ipv6 dccp patches as well.

We have seen a few incidents lately where a dst_enty has been freed
with a dangling TCP socket reference (sk->sk_dst_cache) pointing to that
dst_entry. If the conditions/timings are right a crash then ensues when the
freed dst_entry is referenced later on. A Common crashing back trace is:

 #8 [] page_fault at ffffffff8163e648
    [exception RIP: __tcp_ack_snd_check+74]
.
.
 #9 [] tcp_rcv_established at ffffffff81580b64
#10 [] tcp_v4_do_rcv at ffffffff8158b54a
#11 [] tcp_v4_rcv at ffffffff8158cd02
#12 [] ip_local_deliver_finish at ffffffff815668f4
#13 [] ip_local_deliver at ffffffff81566bd9
#14 [] ip_rcv_finish at ffffffff8156656d
#15 [] ip_rcv at ffffffff81566f06
#16 [] __netif_receive_skb_core at ffffffff8152b3a2
#17 [] __netif_receive_skb at ffffffff8152b608
#18 [] netif_receive_skb at ffffffff8152b690
#19 [] vmxnet3_rq_rx_complete at ffffffffa015eeaf [vmxnet3]
#20 [] vmxnet3_poll_rx_only at ffffffffa015f32a [vmxnet3]
#21 [] net_rx_action at ffffffff8152bac2
#22 [] __do_softirq at ffffffff81084b4f
#23 [] call_softirq at ffffffff8164845c
#24 [] do_softirq at ffffffff81016fc5
#25 [] irq_exit at ffffffff81084ee5
#26 [] do_IRQ at ffffffff81648ff8

Of course it may happen with other NIC drivers as well.

It's found the freed dst_entry here:

 224 static bool tcp_in_quickack_mode(struct sock *sk)↩
 225 {↩
 226 ▹       const struct inet_connection_sock *icsk = inet_csk(sk);↩
 227 ▹       const struct dst_entry *dst = __sk_dst_get(sk);↩
 228 ↩
 229 ▹       return (dst && dst_metric(dst, RTAX_QUICKACK)) ||↩
 230 ▹       ▹       (icsk->icsk_ack.quick && !icsk->icsk_ack.pingpong);↩
 231 }↩

But there are other backtraces attributed to the same freed dst_entry in
netfilter code as well.

All the vmcores showed 2 significant clues:

- Remote hosts behind the default gateway had always been redirected to a
different gateway. A rtable/dst_entry will be added for that host. Making
more dst_entrys with lower reference counts. Making this more probable.

- All vmcores showed a postitive LockDroppedIcmps value, e.g:

LockDroppedIcmps                  267

A closer look at the tcp_v4_err() handler revealed that do_redirect() will run
regardless of whether user space has the socket locked. This can result in a
race condition where the same dst_entry cached in sk->sk_dst_entry can be
decremented twice for the same socket via:

do_redirect()->__sk_dst_check()-> dst_release().

Which leads to the dst_entry being prematurely freed with another socket
pointing to it via sk->sk_dst_cache and a subsequent crash.

To fix this skip do_redirect() if usespace has the socket locked. Instead let
the redirect take place later when user space does not have the socket
locked.

The dccp/IPv6 code is very similar in this respect, so fixing it there too.

As Eric Garver pointed out the following commit now invalidates routes. Which
can set the dst->obsolete flag so that ipv4_dst_check() returns null and
triggers the dst_release().

Fixes: ceb3320610d6 ("ipv4: Kill routes during PMTU/redirect updates.")
Cc: Eric Garver <egarver@redhat.com>
Cc: Hannes Sowa <hsowa@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Jon Maxwell <jmaxwell37@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tdccp_do_redirect(skb, sk);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (!sock_owned_by_user(sk))', '\t\t\tdccp_do_redirect(skb, sk);']}
description: Race condition in the audit_log_single_execve_arg function in kernel/auditsc.c in the Linux kernel through 4.7 allows local users to bypass intended character-set restrictions or disrupt system-call auditing by changing a certain string, aka a "double fetch" vulnerability.

code_evidence: bh_lock_sock() acquires the socket lock, but sock_owned_by_user() only records a LINUX_MIB_LOCKDROPPEDICMPS statistic; execution continues regardless of whether user space owns the socket.
In the ICMP_REDIRECT case, dccp_do_redirect() is called unconditionally while the socket may be owned by user space, so it runs concurrently with user-space socket operations.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function allows a concurrent code sequence (user space operating on the socket) to modify shared socket/dst state while dccp_do_redirect() runs, violating exclusive access; this is exactly CWE-362. It is not merely a missing input check, since the defect is the unsynchronized access window rather than a validation gap.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the redirect path is invoked without checking sock_owned_by_user(), unlike the adjacent PMTU path at line 56. Trigger: an ICMP redirect arriving while user space holds the socket lock. The concurrent dccp_do_redirect() performs a dst check/release that can race with user-space processing, causing the cached dst_entry to be released twice and freed prematurely, leading to a use-after-free and kernel crash.

commit_msg:
f2fs: support swap file w/ DIO

Signed-off-by: Jaegeuk Kim <jaegeuk@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tstruct inode *inode = page->mapping->host;', '\t\tret = f2fs_mpage_readpages(page->mapping, NULL, page, 1, false);'], 'added_lines': ['\tstruct inode *inode = page_file_mapping(page)->host;', '\t\tret = f2fs_mpage_readpages(page_file_mapping(page),', '\t\t\t\t\t\tNULL, page, 1, false);']}
description: In the Linux kernel 5.0.21, mounting a crafted f2fs filesystem image can cause a NULL pointer dereference in f2fs_recover_fsync_data in fs/f2fs/recovery.c. This is related to F2FS_P_SB in fs/f2fs/f2fs.h.

code_evidence: Line 3 dereferences page->mapping without checking it for NULL before accessing ->host; page->mapping can be NULL for pages not associated with an address space (e.g., swap-backed or DIO pages).
Line 9 passes page->mapping to f2fs_mpage_readpages, propagating the potentially NULL mapping into further code.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The code dereferences page->mapping (via ->host) without a NULL check, matching CWE-476's NULL pointer dereference; the added page_file_mapping() change addresses exactly this unguarded mapping access.

evidence_lines.code: struct inode *inode = page->mapping->host;
ret = f2fs_mpage_readpages(page->mapping, NULL, page, 1, false);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function assumes page->mapping is always non-NULL and immediately dereferences it to obtain the inode. Trigger: a page whose mapping is NULL (as occurs for swap/DIO pages handled by this commit) reaches f2fs_read_data_page. Consequence: NULL pointer dereference causing a kernel crash/DoS.

commit_msg: add safety in avc/hevc/vvc sps/pps/vps ID check - cf #1720 #1721 #1722
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (pps->sps_id >= 16) {'], 'added_lines': ['\tif ((pps->sps_id<0) || (pps->sps_id >= 16)) {']}
description: There is a integer overflow in media_tools/av_parsers.c in the hevc_parse_slice_segment function in GPAC 1.0.1 which results in a crash.

code_evidence: Line 16 reads sps_id as an unsigned Exp-Golomb value into pps->sps_id; the check on line 17 only rejects values >= 16, so a negative result is accepted.
Line 22 then assigns the unvalidated sps_id to hevc->sps_active_idx, propagating the bad index.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing lower-bound check permits a negative index that is later used to access a buffer, matching CWE-787 (write past the end/before the beginning of the intended buffer). This is an index-validation defect leading to out-of-bounds access, distinct from a mere logic error.

evidence_lines.code: hevc->sps_active_idx = pps->sps_id;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the SPS ID read from the bitstream is validated only against the upper bound (>=16), so a negative value passes and is stored in hevc->sps_active_idx. Downstream code using this index to access the SPS array can write outside the intended buffer, causing memory corruption or a crash.

commit_msg:
Restrict PixelBuffer dimensions to safe values

We do a lot of calculations based on pixel coordinates and we need
to make sure they do not overflow. Restrict the maximum dimensions
we support rather than try to switch over all calculations to use
64 bit integers.

This prevents attackers from from injecting code by specifying a
huge framebuffer size and relying on the values overflowing to
access invalid areas of the heap.

This primarily affects the client which gets both the screen
dimensions and the pixel contents from the remote side. But the
server might also be affected as a client can adjust the screen
dimensions, as can applications inside the session.

Issue found by Pavel Cheremushkin from Kaspersky Lab.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  if ((width < 0) || (width > maxPixelBufferWidth))', '    throw rfb::Exception("Invalid PixelBuffer width of %d pixels requested", width);', '  if ((height < 0) || (height > maxPixelBufferHeight))', '    throw rfb::Exception("Invalid PixelBuffer height of %d pixels requested", height);', '  if ((stride_ < 0) || (stride_ > maxPixelBufferStride) || (stride_ < width))', '    throw rfb::Exception("Invalid PixelBuffer stride of %d pixels requested", stride_);', '  if ((width != 0) && (height != 0) && (data_ == NULL))', '    throw rfb::Exception("PixelBuffer requested without a valid memory area");', '']}
description: TigerVNC version prior to 1.10.1 is vulnerable to heap buffer overflow. Vulnerability could be triggered from CopyRectDecoder due to incorrect value checks. Exploitation of this vulnerability could potentially result into remote code execution. This attack appear to be exploitable via network connectivity.

code_evidence: The function accepts caller-controlled width, height, data_ and stride_ and stores them directly: setSize(width, height) at line 4, stride = stride_ at line 5, and data = data_ at line 6, with no validation of ranges or consistency between dimensions and stride.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the unchecked dimensions/stride are used for pixel addressing that writes past the allocated pixel buffer; the weakness is the missing bounds constraint enabling out-of-bounds writes, not merely an integer overflow. The patch adds exactly these dimension/stride limits.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: setBuffer trusts attacker-supplied framebuffer dimensions and stride without bounds checks, so downstream pixel-coordinate calculations can overflow and index outside the allocated heap area. Trigger: a remote peer (or application) supplies huge width/height values via CopyRectDecoder; consequence is a heap out-of-bounds write that may lead to code execution or crash.

commit_msg:
It turns out that currently we rely only on sysfs attribute
permissions:

  $ ll /sys/bus/rbd/{add*,remove*}
  --w------- 1 root root 4096 Sep  3 20:37 /sys/bus/rbd/add
  --w------- 1 root root 4096 Sep  3 20:37 /sys/bus/rbd/add_single_major
  --w------- 1 root root 4096 Sep  3 20:37 /sys/bus/rbd/remove
  --w------- 1 root root 4096 Sep  3 20:38 /sys/bus/rbd/remove_single_major

This means that images can be mapped and unmapped (i.e. block devices
can be created and deleted) by a UID 0 process even after it drops all
privileges or by any process with CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE in its user namespace
as long as UID 0 is mapped into that user namespace.

Be consistent with other virtual block devices (loop, nbd, dm, md, etc)
and require CAP_SYS_ADMIN in the initial user namespace for mapping and
unmapping, and also for dumping the configuration string and refreshing
the image header.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Ilya Dryomov <idryomov@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\tif (!capable(CAP_SYS_ADMIN))', '\t\treturn -EPERM;']}
description: The rbd block device driver in drivers/block/rbd.c in the Linux kernel through 5.8.9 used incomplete permission checking for access to rbd devices, which could be leveraged by local attackers to map or unmap rbd block devices, aka CID-f44d04e696fe.

code_evidence: do_rbd_remove parses a user-supplied device id and optional force option, then proceeds directly to locating and removing the rbd device.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs a privileged action (device unmapping) without correctly authorizing the caller, matching CWE-863 incorrect authorization. CWE-862 (missing authorization) is related, but here the weakness is an incorrect/insufficient check relying on file permissions rather than proper capability validation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the handler performs no capability/privilege check before unmapping a device; it relies solely on sysfs attribute permissions. Trigger: a UID 0 process that dropped privileges, or a process with CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE in a user namespace mapping UID 0, writes to remove. Consequence: unauthorized removal (and forced removal) of rbd block devices.

commit_msg:
net: rds: force to destroy connection if t_sock is NULL in rds_tcp_kill_sock().

When it is to cleanup net namespace, rds_tcp_exit_net() will call
rds_tcp_kill_sock(), if t_sock is NULL, it will not call
rds_conn_destroy(), rds_conn_path_destroy() and rds_tcp_conn_free() to free
connection, and the worker cp_conn_w is not stopped, afterwards the net is freed in
net_drop_ns(); While cp_conn_w rds_connect_worker() will call rds_tcp_conn_path_connect()
and reference 'net' which has already been freed.

In rds_tcp_conn_path_connect(), rds_tcp_set_callbacks() will set t_sock = sock before
sock->ops->connect, but if connect() is failed, it will call
rds_tcp_restore_callbacks() and set t_sock = NULL, if connect is always
failed, rds_connect_worker() will try to reconnect all the time, so
rds_tcp_kill_sock() will never to cancel worker cp_conn_w and free the
connections.

Therefore, the condition !tc->t_sock is not needed if it is going to do
cleanup_net->rds_tcp_exit_net->rds_tcp_kill_sock, because tc->t_sock is always
NULL, and there is on other path to cancel cp_conn_w and free
connection. So this patch is to fix this.

rds_tcp_kill_sock():
...
if (net != c_net || !tc->t_sock)
...

description: An issue was discovered in rds_tcp_kill_sock in net/rds/tcp.c in the Linux kernel before 5.0.8. There is a race condition leading to a use-after-free, related to net namespace cleanup.

code_evidence: The loop walks rds_tcp_conn_list under rds_tcp_conn_lock and skips entries when net != c_net OR tc->t_sock is NULL, so connections whose t_sock was cleared by a failed connect are never placed on tmp_list.
After unlocking, only connections on tmp_list are passed to rds_conn_destroy(), so skipped connections retain their worker and are never freed.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect is improper synchronization between netns teardown and the reconnect worker: the t_sock check creates a timing window where cleanup skips a live connection that the worker concurrently keeps reconnecting. CWE-362 captures this shared-resource race; the use-after-free is the consequence, not the root weakness.

evidence_lines.code:
list_for_each_entry_safe(tc, _tc, &tmp_list, t_tcp_node)
rds_conn_destroy(tc->t_cpath->cp_conn);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: rds_tcp_conn_path_connect() sets t_sock before connect and rds_tcp_restore_callbacks() clears it on failure, so a persistently failing reconnect leaves t_sock NULL. rds_tcp_kill_sock()'s !tc->t_sock guard then skips that connection during netns cleanup, so cp_conn_w keeps running and later dereferences the freed net namespace, yielding the reported use-after-free.

commit_msg: fixed 2 possible heap overflows (inc. #1088)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (p->nameUTF8 && (u32) p->nameUTF8[0] == strlen(p->nameUTF8+1)) {'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (p->nameUTF8 && (u32) p->nameUTF8[0] == strlen(p->nameUTF8)-1) {']}
description: An issue was discovered in MP4Box in GPAC 0.7.1. The function urn_Read in isomedia/box_code_base.c has a heap-based buffer over-read.

code_evidence: Line 5 computes strlen(p->nameUTF8+1), which starts at the second byte of the nameUTF8 buffer and reads until a NUL. If nameUTF8 is a one-byte string or the length byte is not followed by a NUL-terminated payload, strlen walks past the allocated buffer. The result is used only for a comparison and to select which fprintf branch prints nameUTF8+1 (line 6) or nameUTF8 (line 8).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the defect is a read past the end of the intended nameUTF8 buffer, not a write. The fix changes the strlen operand to strlen(p->nameUTF8)-1, avoiding the over-read; a CWE-787 write would not describe this behavior.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the length byte at nameUTF8[0] is compared against strlen() of the remaining string rather than the total string length, and strlen on nameUTF8+1 has no bound tied to the allocation. Trigger: a crafted hdlr box where nameUTF8+1 is not NUL-terminated within the buffer. Consequence: an out-of-bounds read during dump, potentially crashing or disclosing adjacent memory through the fprintf output.

description: An issue was discovered in button_open in login/logind-button.c in systemd before 243. When executing the udevadm trigger command, a memory leak may occur.

code_evidence: button_open() holds an event source reference in b->io_event_source. Line 22 overwrites this field with sd_event_add_io() without first releasing any prior source; on failure (lines 23-25) the function jumps to fail, which only closes b->fd (line 30) and never unrefs the event source. The added fix line (sd_event_source_unref) is absent from this before-version, confirming the missing release.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-401 fits because a reference to an allocated event source is not released after its effective lifetime, leaving memory unavailable for reuse. This is a resource-release defect rather than a use-after-free, since the stale source is simply dropped without being freed.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the previous b->io_event_source reference is neither unref'd before re-registration nor cleaned up on the error path. Trigger: button_open() called repeatedly (e.g., udevadm trigger producing change events) or sd_event_add_io() failing. Consequence: each iteration leaks an sd_event_source, growing memory usage over time.

Bug: 28673410

description: The ih264d decoder in mediaserver in Android 6.x before 2016-08-01 mishandles slice numbers, which allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code or cause a denial of service (memory corruption) via a crafted media file, aka internal bug 28673410.

code_evidence: The function initializes the slice buffer pointers ps_parse_cur_slice, ps_decode_cur_slice and ps_computebs_cur_slice to ps_dec_slice_buf[0] at lines 165-167, but u2_cur_slice_num is not reset alongside them here.

The reset of u2_cur_slice_num occurs only later at line 329, after substantial picture setup; the patch moves this reset up to line 168 so the slice counter is consistent with the slice buffer pointers at picture start.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The stale slice counter can drive indexing into ps_dec_slice_buf outside its intended boundary, matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds memory operation. The fix resets the counter at picture start to keep it within bounds.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the current-slice counter is initialized out of sync with the slice buffer pointers, so a stale slice number from a prior picture/error clip can index the slice buffer beyond its intended bounds. Trigger: decoding a crafted media file with error clips that preserves a nonzero slice number. Consequence: out-of-bounds memory access, leading to memory corruption and potential code execution or denial of service.
