commit_msg:
Fix CVE-2022-3602 in punycode decoder.

An off by one error in the punycode decoder allowed for a single unsigned int
overwrite of a buffer which could cause a crash and possible code execution.

Reviewed-by: Matt Caswell <matt@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Tomas Mraz <tomas@openssl.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        if (written_out > max_out)'], 'added_lines': ['        if (written_out >= max_out)']}
description: A buffer overrun can be triggered in X.509 certificate verification, specifically in name constraint checking. Note that this occurs after certificate chain signature verification and requires either a CA to have signed the malicious certificate or for the application to continue certificate verification despite failure to construct a path to a trusted issuer. An attacker can craft a malicious email address to overflow four attacker-controlled bytes on the stack. This buffer overflow could result in a crash (causing a denial of service) or potentially remote code execution. Many platforms implement stack overflow protections which would mitigate against the risk of remote code execution. The risk may be further mitigated based on stack layout for any given platform/compiler. Pre-announcements of CVE-2022-3602 described this issue as CRITICAL. Further analysis based on some of the mitigating factors described above have led this to be downgraded to HIGH. Users are still encouraged to upgrade to a new version as soon as possible. In a TLS client, this can be triggered by connecting to a malicious server. In a TLS server, this can be triggered if the server requests client authentication and a malicious client connects. Fixed in OpenSSL 3.0.7 (Affected 3.0.0,3.0.1,3.0.2,3.0.3,3.0.4,3.0.5,3.0.6).

code_evidence: The bounds check uses `written_out > max_out` instead of `>=`, so when `written_out == max_out` the check passes and execution continues to `memmove(pDecoded + i + 1, pDecoded + i, (written_out - i) * sizeof *pDecoded)` followed by `pDecoded[i] = n`. With `written_out` already equal to the output capacity `max_out`, the write at `pDecoded[i]` and the memmove target `pDecoded + i + 1` can land at or beyond the buffer end.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes `pDecoded[i]` and memmoves into `pDecoded + i + 1` without ensuring room beyond `max_out`, which is a write past the end of the intended buffer, matching CWE-787. The adjacent CWE-125 (out-of-bounds read) does not apply because the defect is an out-of-bounds store, not a load.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: an off-by-one in the capacity guard permits one extra decoded code point when the output buffer is already full. Trigger: a crafted punycode string whose decoded length reaches `max_out`. Consequence: an out-of-bounds write of an attacker-influenced unsigned int past the stack buffer, causing a crash or potential code execution.

commit_msg:
ipv6: Use result arg in fib_lookup_arg consistently

arg.result is sometimes used as fib6_result and sometimes used to
hold the rt6_info. Add rt6_info to fib6_result and make the use
of arg.result consistent through ipv6 rules.

The rt6 entry is filled in for lookups returning a dst_entry, but not
for direct fib_lookups that just want a fib6_info.

Fixes: effda4dd97e8 ("ipv6: Pass fib6_result to fib lookups")
Signed-off-by: David Ahern <dsahern@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tstruct rt6_info *rt = (struct rt6_info *) arg->result;'], 'added_lines': ['\tstruct fib6_result *res = arg->result;', '\tstruct rt6_info *rt = res->rt6;', '', '\tif (!rt)', '\t\treturn false;']}
description: A flaw was found in the IPv6 module of the Linux kernel. The arg.result was not used consistently in fib6_rule_lookup, sometimes holding rt6_info and other times fib6_info. This was not accounted for in other parts of the code where rt6_info was expected unconditionally, potentially leading to a kernel panic in fib6_rule_suppress.

code_evidence: Line 3 casts arg->result directly to struct rt6_info*, but the commit notes arg->result may instead hold a fib6_info for direct fib lookups.
Lines 5-7 immediately dereference rt->rt6i_idev and rt->rt6i_dst.plen, and line 13 passes rt to ip6_rt_put, all assuming the object is an rt6_info.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function accesses a resource (arg->result) using a type incompatible with the type actually stored, which is exactly type confusion (CWE-843). It is not merely a null-pointer dereference: the missing constraint is the object's real type, and the consequence is memory misread/crash.

evidence_lines.code: ip6_rt_put(rt);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: fib6_rule_suppress unconditionally reinterprets arg->result as rt6_info without checking which structure the caller stored. Trigger: a lookup path that places a fib6_info into arg->result. The dereferences at lines 5-7 and the ip6_rt_put at line 13 then read fields at rt6_info offsets, causing invalid access and a possible kernel panic.

commit_msg:
sr: pass down correctly sized SCSI sense buffer

We're casting the CDROM layer request_sense to the SCSI sense
buffer, but the former is 64 bytes and the latter is 96 bytes.
As we generally allocate these on the stack, we end up blowing
up the stack.

Fix this by wrapping the scsi_execute() call with a properly
sized sense buffer, and copying back the bits for the CDROM
layer.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Reported-by: Piotr Gabriel Kosinski <pg.kosinski@gmail.com>
Reported-by: Daniel Shapira <daniel@twistlock.com>
Tested-by: Kees Cook <keescook@chromium.org>
Fixes: 82ed4db499b8 ("block: split scsi_request out of struct request")
Signed-off-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t      cgc->buffer, cgc->buflen,', '\t\t\t      (unsigned char *)cgc->sense, &sshdr,'], 'added_lines': ['\tunsigned char sense_buffer[SCSI_SENSE_BUFFERSIZE], *senseptr = NULL;', '', '\tif (cgc->sense)', '\t\tsenseptr = sense_buffer;', '\t\t\t      cgc->buffer, cgc->buflen, senseptr, &sshdr,', '', '\tif (cgc->sense)', '\t\tmemcpy(cgc->sense, sense_buffer, sizeof(*cgc->sense));']}
description: The sr_do_ioctl function in drivers/scsi/sr_ioctl.c in the Linux kernel through 4.16.12 allows local users to cause a denial of service (stack-based buffer overflow) or possibly have unspecified other impact because sense buffers have different sizes at the CDROM layer and the SCSI layer, as demonstrated by a CDROMREADMODE2 ioctl call.

code_evidence: scsi_execute is passed (unsigned char *)cgc->sense as its sense buffer argument, with no size parameter or bounds check relating cgc->sense's allocation to the SCSI sense buffer size. The SCSI layer writes up to SCSI_SENSE_BUFFERSIZE bytes into this pointer, while the CDROM layer's cgc->sense is only 64 bytes, so the write exceeds the caller-provided buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the SCSI layer writes beyond the end of the undersized cgc->sense buffer passed at lines 12-15. The flaw is a size mismatch causing an out-of-bounds write; a mere type confusion would not by itself place the write past the buffer boundary.

evidence_lines.code:
result = scsi_execute(SDev, cgc->cmd, cgc->data_direction,
cgc->buffer, cgc->buflen,
(unsigned char *)cgc->sense, &sshdr,
cgc->timeout, IOCTL_RETRIES, 0, 0, NULL);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the CDROM request_sense buffer (64 bytes) is cast to and used as the SCSI sense buffer (96 bytes) without size reconciliation. Trigger: a CDROMREADMODE2 ioctl reaching sr_do_ioctl with a cgc->sense allocation of the smaller size causes scsi_execute to write past it. Supported consequence: stack-based out-of-bounds write leading to denial of service and possible memory corruption.

Line 38 writes into it with snprintf using a format containing %s bound to gplot->rootname, and line 47 writes formatted floats; both use the buffer size as the snprintf limit, so these specific calls are size-bounded and do not themselves overflow.

commit_msg:
Use correct origin when prompting for proxy authentication.

Since M49, Chrome has been prompting for proxy authentication
credentials using the target origin instead of the origin of the proxy
server. Even if the proxy origin was displayed correctly, a mischievous
network operator could still spoof the proxy server origin. To mitigate
these problems, this CL:

* Fixes the origin used in the proxy authentication login prompt to use
  the origin of the proxy server.

* Indicate if the proxy server connection is insecure.

* Always throw up an interstitial and clear the omnibox when showing a
  proxy auth prompt.

* Use the correct origin when saving proxy authentication credentials.

BUG=613626, 620737

Review-Url: https://codereview.chromium.org/2067933002

joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-287 fits because the prompt fails to reliably establish the claimed identity of the proxy server before credentials are entered. This is improper authentication of a remote party, not merely improper input validation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the constructor passes an unformatted challenger origin to the login prompt, so the displayed identity is not normalized for security display. Trigger: a man-in-the-middle modifies the proxy authentication challenge so the challenger string spoofs a trusted origin. commit_msg:
Add several sanity checks for nft_set_desc_concat_parse():

- validate desc->field_count not larger than desc->field_len array.
- field length cannot be larger than desc->field_len (ie. U8_MAX)
- total length of the concatenation cannot be larger than register array.

Joint work with Florian Westphal.

Fixes: f3a2181e16f1 ("netfilter: nf_tables: Support for sets with multiple ranged fields")
Reported-by: <zhangziming.zzm@antgroup.com>
Reviewed-by: Stefano Brivio <sbrivio@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Florian Westphal <fw@strlen.de>
Signed-off-by: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['', '\tif (len * BITS_PER_BYTE / 32 > NFT_REG32_COUNT)', '\t\treturn -E2BIG;'], 'added_lines': ['', '\tif (desc->field_count >= ARRAY_SIZE(desc->field_len))', '\t\treturn -E2BIG;', '\tif (!len || len > U8_MAX)', '\t\treturn -EINVAL;']}
description: A vulnerability was found in the Linux kernel's nft_set_desc_concat_parse() function .This flaw allows an attacker to trigger a buffer overflow via nft_set_desc_concat_parse() , causing a denial of service and possibly to run code.

code_evidence: Line 13 reads the attacker-controlled field length from the netlink attribute. Line 14 only bounds len*BITS_PER_BYTE/32 against NFT_REG32_COUNT, which does not constrain len itself to fit a u8. Line 16 then stores len into desc->field_len[desc->field_count++] with no check that field_count is within the array bounds.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-121 fits because desc->field_len is a fixed-size array within the nft_set_desc structure and the unchecked index and value cause out-of-bounds stack/struct writes. This is a bounds-check weakness, not merely an integer overflow, since the write itself exceeds the array limits.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the element value len and the index field_count are written into the desc->field_len array without validating that field_count stays below the array size. Trigger: a set description with many concatenated fields, or an oversized len value, repeatedly invokes this parse routine. Consequence: out-of-bounds writes past the array, corrupting adjacent memory and potentially enabling code execution or denial of service.

description: In libgraphite2 in graphite2 1.3.11, a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability was found in Segment.cpp during a dumbRendering operation, which may allow attackers to cause a denial of service or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted .ttf file.

code_evidence: When dumb_font is true, the entire Glat/Gloc validation block is skipped, yet m_pGlat and m_pGloc remain uninitialized/default and no table is loaded.
The validation block is the only path that populates m_pGlat/m_pGloc and verifies they are non-NULL with m_pGloc.size() >= 8 before reading.
Later reads use p = m_pGlat and be::read on m_pGlat without any NULL or size check when dumb_font bypassed the earlier guard.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads through m_pGlat (p = m_pGlat; be::read) after the guarding block was bypassed by dumb_font, so a NULL Glat pointer can be dereferenced. This is a direct NULL pointer dereference (CWE-476), not merely an out-of-bounds read, because the missing constraint is a NULL check on the pointer being used.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the dumb_font branch skips the only code that assigns and validates m_pGlat/m_pGloc, leaving the Glat pointer unchecked before reads. Trigger: a crafted .ttf processed with dumbRendering/dumb_font=true reaches the Glat version read. Consequence: NULL pointer dereference causing a crash/DoS.

commit_msg:
patch 9.0.2068: [security] overflow in :history

Problem:  [security] overflow in :history
Solution: Check that value fits into int

The get_list_range() function, used to parse numbers for the :history
and :clist command internally uses long variables to store the numbers.
However function arguments are integer pointers, which can then
overflow.

Check that the return value from the vim_str2nr() function is not larger
than INT_MAX and if yes, bail out with an error. I guess nobody uses a
cmdline/clist history that needs so many entries... (famous last words).

It is only a moderate vulnerability, so impact should be low.

Github Advisory:
https://github.com/vim/vim/security/advisories/GHSA-q22m-h7m2-9mgm

Signed-off-by: Christian Brabandt <cb@256bit.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t    *str = skipwhite(*str + len);'], 'added_lines': ['\t// overflow', '\tif (num > INT_MAX)', '\t    return FAIL;', '', '\t    *str = skipwhite(*str + len);', '\t    // overflow', '\t    if (num > INT_MAX)', '\t\treturn FAIL;', '']}
description: Vim is an improved version of the good old UNIX editor Vi. Heap-use-after-free in memory allocated in the function `ga_grow_inner` in in the file `src/alloc.c` at line 748, which is freed in the file `src/ex_docmd.c` in the function `do_cmdline` at line 1010 and then used again in `src/cmdhist.c` at line 759. When using the `:history` command, it's possible that the provided argument overflows the accepted value. Causing an Integer Overflow and potentially later an use-after-free. This vulnerability has been patched in version 9.0.2068.

code_evidence: vim_str2nr parses the input into the wide varnumber_T num, then the code advances *str by len without any range check.
After the comma, vim_str2nr again fills num and len, and the value is stored directly with *num2 = (int)num without checking whether it fits in int.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the code performs a narrowing conversion whose result can wrap when the parsed value exceeds the int range, and the logic assumes the cast preserves the value. The fix adds num > INT_MAX checks before each cast, confirming the overflow is the targeted root cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: values parsed by vim_str2nr into the wider num are narrowed to int via casts with no INT_MAX bound. Trigger: a user-supplied :history or :clist argument with a number exceeding INT_MAX. Consequence: the cast wraps to a small or negative int, producing an incorrect history range that later leads to out-of-bounds/use-after-free behavior.

commit_msg:
Remove support for pre-authentication compression. Doing compression
early in the protocol probably seemed reasonable in the 1990s, but
today it's clearly a bad idea in terms of both cryptography (cf.
multiple compression oracle attacks in TLS) and attack surface.

Moreover, to support it across privilege-separation zlib needed
the assistance of a complex shared-memory manager that made the
required attack surface considerably larger.

Prompted by Guido Vranken pointing out a compiler-elided security
check in the shared memory manager found by Stack
(http://css.csail.mit.edu/stack/); ok deraadt@ markus@

NB. pre-auth authentication has been disabled by default in sshd
for >10 years.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t    (r = sshbuf_put_u32(b, comp->enabled)) != 0 ||'], 'added_lines': []}
description: The shared memory manager (associated with pre-authentication compression) in sshd in OpenSSH before 7.4 does not ensure that a bounds check is enforced by all compilers, which might allows local users to gain privileges by leveraging access to a sandboxed privilege-separation process, related to the m_zback and m_zlib data structures.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function only serializes newkeys fields into an sshbuf using checked sshbuf_put_* calls; it contains no memory-buffer bounds operation or unchecked access related to the described m_zback/m_zlib shared-memory manager issue.

commit_msg:
Detect infinite recursion in parameter entities

When expanding a parameter entity in a DTD, infinite recursion could
lead to an infinite loop or memory exhaustion.

Thanks to Wei Lei for the first of many reports.

Fixes bug 759579.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t    if (xmlPushInput(ctxt, input) < 0)'], 'added_lines': ['\t    if (xmlPushInput(ctxt, input) < 0) {', '                xmlFreeInputStream(input);', '            }']}
description: parser.c in libxml2 before 2.9.5 does not prevent infinite recursion in parameter entities.

code_evidence: Line 65 creates a new entity input for the parameter entity and line 66 pushes it onto the parser context. No depth counter or recursion guard is checked before pushing; the only failure path is xmlPushInput returning < 0. Because the function recursively re-enters xmlParsePEReference when the pushed entity content is parsed, a self-referential parameter entity causes unbounded pushes.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing recursion bound lets the entity-expansion iteration never reach its exit condition, matching CWE-835's unreachable-exit infinite loop. The diff only frees the input on push failure, not the recursion cause, confirming the loop is the weakness rather than a plain memory leak (CWE-401).
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: expansion of a parameter entity recurses via xmlPushInput without any recursion-depth or cycle constraint. Trigger: a DTD declaring a parameter entity that references itself (directly or indirectly). Consequence: each expansion pushes another input, so the parser loops indefinitely or exhausts memory, supporting a denial of service.

commit_msg:
Fix handling of symbolic link ACLs

On Linux ACLs on symbolic links are not supported.
We must avoid calling acl_set_file() on symbolic links as their
targets are modified instead.

While here, do not try to set default ACLs on non-directories.

Fixes #1565
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\tret = set_acl(a, fd, name, abstract_acl,', '\t\t\tret = set_acl(a, fd, name, abstract_acl,', '\t\tret = set_acl(a, fd, name, abstract_acl,'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\tret = set_acl(a, fd, name, abstract_acl, mode,', '\t\t\tret = set_acl(a, fd, name, abstract_acl, mode,', '\t\tret = set_acl(a, fd, name, abstract_acl, mode,']}
description: An improper link resolution flaw while extracting an archive can lead to changing the access control list (ACL) of the target of the link. An attacker may provide a malicious archive to a victim user, who would trigger this flaw when trying to extract the archive. A local attacker may use this flaw to change the ACL of a file on the system and gain more privileges.

code_evidence: When POSIX1e ACL types are present, the function calls set_acl() with the entry name and fd without any check that the entry is a symbolic link; set_acl() then applies the ACL to whatever path name resolves to.
The default-ACL branch likewise invokes set_acl() for ARCHIVE_ENTRY_ACL_TYPE_DEFAULT without verifying the entry is a directory, so a symlink entry can cause ACL modification on the link target.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-59 fits because the weakness is file access via a name that resolves through a link to an unintended resource; the ACL is set on the link target rather than the link entry itself, consistent with improper link resolution before file access.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: archive_write_disk_set_acls() applies ACLs by name/fd without first rejecting symbolic-link entries, so the OS resolves the link and modifies the target's ACL. Trigger: a malicious archive containing a symlink entry with ACL data, extracted by a victim. Supported consequence: the ACL of an unintended file is changed, potentially granting the attacker more privileges.

commit_msg: class.c: add `obj->c` check before `prepare_singleton_class()`.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  if (obj->c == NULL) return NULL;']}
description: mruby is vulnerable to NULL Pointer Dereference

code_evidence: obj is obtained from mrb_basic_ptr(v) and passed unconditionally to prepare_singleton_class; obj->c is then returned without any NULL check. If mrb_basic_ptr(v) yields a NULL object pointer, both the call and the dereference operate on NULL.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences a pointer expected to be valid but never checks it for NULL, matching CWE-476's NULL Pointer Dereference. It is not merely a missing return-value check on an unrelated call; the unchecked pointer is the object being dereferenced and returned.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the default path assumes mrb_basic_ptr(v) returns a non-NULL RBasic pointer and never validates it before use. Trigger: a value reaching the default case whose basic pointer is NULL. Consequence: NULL dereference inside prepare_singleton_class or at obj->c, causing a crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
ohci: allocate timer only once.

Allocate timer once, at init time, instead of allocating/freeing
it all the time when starting/stopping the bus.  Simplifies the
code, also fixes bugs (memory leak) due to missing checks whenever
the time is already allocated or not.

Cc: Prasad J Pandit <pjp@fedoraproject.org>
Reported-by: Zuozhi Fzz <zuozhi.fzz@alibaba-inc.com>
Signed-off-by: Gerd Hoffmann <kraxel@redhat.com>

description: The ohci_bus_start function in the USB OHCI emulation support (hw/usb/hcd-ohci.c) in QEMU allows local guest OS administrators to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference and QEMU process crash) via vectors related to multiple eof_timers.

description: An out-of-bounds read/write vulnerability when executing lazily compiled inner generator functions in Facebook Hermes prior to commit 091835377369c8fd5917d9b87acffa721ad2a168 allows attackers to potentially execute arbitrary code via crafted JavaScript. Note that this is only exploitable if the application using Hermes permits evaluation of untrusted JavaScript. Hence, most React Native applications are not affected.

code_evidence: The inner ES5 function is built by genES5Function outside the enclosing FunctionContext scope, so any generator flag or context state set during its construction is not associated with the lexically enclosing outerFn context.

emitFunctionPrologue and createCreateGeneratorInst(innerFn) then run inside the outerFnContext, but innerFn was already finalized without correct generator/context information, so the emitted code treats it as a regular function rather than a generator.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The supported consequence is a memory write/read past the intended buffer caused by incorrect function generation, matching CWE-787's out-of-bounds write scope; the cause is improper context handling rather than a direct bounds check, but the resulting out-of-bounds memory modification is the weakness mapped.

evidence_lines.code:
auto *innerFn = genES5Function(
genAnonymousLabelName(originalName.isValid() ? originalName.str() : ""),
lazyClosureAlias,
functionNode,
true);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the inner function is generated before the outerFnContext is established, so lazily compiled inner generators lose their generator status and are reconstituted as plain functions. Trigger: executing such a crafted inner generator causes the generated code to mismanage the generator frame/state, leading to out-of-bounds memory access. Consequence: memory corruption potentially enabling arbitrary code execution.

commit_msg:
LINE6 drivers allocate the buffers based on the value returned from
usb_maxpacket() calls.  The manipulated device may return zero for
this, and this results in the kmalloc() with zero size (and it may
succeed) while the other part of the driver code writes the packet
data with the fixed size -- which eventually overwrites.

This patch adds a simple sanity check for the invalid buffer size for
avoiding that problem.

Reported-by: syzbot+219f00fb49874dcaea17@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Takashi Iwai <tiwai@suse.de>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tif (!line6pcm->max_packet_size_in || !line6pcm->max_packet_size_out) {', '\t\tdev_err(line6pcm->line6->ifcdev,', '\t\t\t"cannot get proper max packet size\\n");', '\t\treturn -EINVAL;', '\t}']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel before 5.1.17. There is a NULL pointer dereference caused by a malicious USB device in the sound/usb/line6/pcm.c driver.

code_evidence: The function derives max_packet_size_in and max_packet_size_out from usb_maxpacket() on device-supplied endpoints without checking the returned values.
The returned sizes are then used by line6_create_audio_out_urbs() and line6_create_audio_in_urbs(), whose failures are only checked for negative errors.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The fix guards against the invalid size before use; the underlying defect is that the driver trusts a device-controlled value and proceeds to use the resulting buffers, matching CWE-476 for NULL/invalid pointer dereference arising from the unchecked size.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: A malicious USB device can report zero or invalid endpoint packet sizes, so usb_maxpacket() returns 0. That value flows into the URB creation paths, where buffer allocation based on the zero size may succeed while later packet handling assumes a fixed nonzero size, leading to invalid access and crash.

description: PJSIP is a free and open source multimedia communication library written in C. A denial-of-service vulnerability affects applications on a 32-bit systems that use PJSIP versions 2.12 and prior to play/read invalid WAV files. The vulnerability occurs when reading WAV file data chunks with length greater than 31-bit integers. The vulnerability does not affect 64-bit apps and should not affect apps that only plays trusted WAV files. A patch is available on the `master` branch of the `pjsip/project` GitHub repository. As a workaround, apps can reject a WAV file received from an unknown source or validate the file first.

code_evidence: The do/while(1) loop at [63,71] only exits via break at line 130; for a non-matching stream it advances the file with pj_file_setpos(ch.len) then continues.
ch.len is a 32-bit unsigned subchunk length read from the file at [84,90]; fport->pad is derived from its low bit.
At [94,106] when stream_id != fport->stream_id, pj_file_setpos(fport->fd, ch.len, PJ_SEEK_CUR) is called without validating ch.len; continue re-enters the loop.
At [108,120] fport->size_left = ch.len and subsequent reads consume from the file based on this length.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-835 fits because the loop in avi_get_frame has no reachable exit when the attacker-controlled subchunk length produces an invalid/backward seek, so it iterates indefinitely. This is the loop-termination weakness itself, not merely an integer conversion error (CWE-190), which is the enabling cause.

evidence_lines.code:
if (fport->size_left > 0 && fport->size_left < size_to_read) {
if (fport->size_left == 0) {

if (cid[0] >= '0' && cid[0] <= '9' &&
fport->pad = (pj_uint8_t)ch.len & 1;

if (stream_id != fport->stream_id) {
continue;

fport->size_left = ch.len;
fport->size_left -= size_to_read;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: ch.len from the WAV/AVI subchunk header is trusted as a signed seek offset without an overflow check. On 32-bit systems a length with the high bit set becomes a negative pj_off_t, so pj_file_setpos seeks backwards or fails, and the loop's continue keeps re-reading subchunks without reaching a terminating size_left==0/EOF condition. Trigger: an invalid WAV file with a chunk length greater than 31 bits. Consequence: the do/while(1) loop never exits, causing CPU denial of service.

commit_msg:
Jann Horn points out that there is another possible race wrt Unix domain
socket garbage collection, somewhat reminiscent of the one fixed in
commit cbcf01128d0a ("af_unix: fix garbage collect vs MSG_PEEK").

See the extended comment about the garbage collection requirements added
to unix_peek_fds() by that commit for details.

The race comes from how we can locklessly look up a file descriptor just
as it is in the process of being closed, and with the right artificial
timing (Jann added a few strategic 'mdelay(500)' calls to do that), the
Unix domain socket garbage collector could see the reference count
decrement of the close() happen before fget() took its reference to the
file and the file was attached onto a new file descriptor.

This is all (intentionally) correct on the 'struct file *' side, with
RCU lookups and lockless reference counting very much part of the
design.  Getting that reference count out of order isn't a problem per
se.

But the garbage collector can get confused by seeing this situation of
having seen a file not having any remaining external references and then
seeing it being attached to an fd.

In commit cbcf01128d0a ("af_unix: fix garbage collect vs MSG_PEEK") the
fix was to serialize the file descriptor install with the garbage
collector by taking and releasing the unix_gc_lock.

That's not really an option here, but since this all happens when we are
in the process of looking up a file descriptor, we can instead simply
just re-check that the file hasn't been closed in the meantime, and just
re-do the lookup if we raced with a concurrent close() of the same file
descriptor.

Reported-and-tested-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Acked-by: Miklos Szeredi <mszeredi@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\telse if (files_lookup_fd_raw(files, fd) != file) {', '\t\t\tfput_many(file, refs);', '\t\t\tgoto loop;', '\t\t}']}
description: A read-after-free memory flaw was found in the Linux kernel's garbage collection for Unix domain socket file handlers in the way users call close() and fget() simultaneously and can potentially trigger a race condition. This flaw allows a local user to crash the system or escalate their privileges on the system. This flaw affects Linux kernel versions prior to 5.16-rc4.

code_evidence: Under RCU, __fget_files locklessly looks up the fd's struct file (line 7) and then takes a reference with get_file_rcu_many (line 11). Between these operations another thread can close() the fd and drop its reference; the lookup result is not revalidated against the current fd table entry, so the reference may be acquired on a file that was concurrently detached.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-362 fits: a shared resource (the fd table entry and file refcount) is accessed without exclusive synchronization, and a timing window lets an interfering close() sequence modify it between lookup and reference acquisition. This is a concurrency race, not merely a generic use-after-free; the use-after-free is the downstream consequence of the race.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the fd-table lookup and the reference acquisition are not atomic with respect to a concurrent close(). Trigger: a second thread closes the same fd between files_lookup_fd_rcu and get_file_rcu_many, so the refcount decrement is observed before fget()'s reference. Consequence: the Unix domain socket garbage collector sees a file with no external references that is then attached to an fd, causing mis-collection and a read-after-free that can crash the system or escalate privileges.

commit_msg:
get_pipe() routine doesn't validate the input endpoint number
and uses to reference ep_in and ep_out arrays. Invalid endpoint
number can trigger BUG(). Range check the epnum and returning
error instead of calling BUG().

Change caller stub_recv_cmd_submit() to handle the get_pipe()
error return.

Reported-by: Secunia Research <vuln@secunia.com>
Cc: stable <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Shuah Khan <shuahkh@osg.samsung.com>
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (!ep) {', '\t\tdev_err(&sdev->udev->dev, "no such endpoint?, %d\\n",', '\t\t\tepnum);', '\t\tBUG();', '\t}', '\tdev_err(&sdev->udev->dev, "get pipe, epnum %d\\n", epnum);', '\treturn 0;'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (epnum < 0 || epnum > 15)', '\t\tgoto err_ret;', '', '\tif (!ep)', '\t\tgoto err_ret;', 'err_ret:', '\tdev_err(&sdev->udev->dev, "get pipe() invalid epnum %d\\n", epnum);', '\treturn -1;']}
description: The "get_pipe()" function (drivers/usb/usbip/stub_rx.c) in the Linux Kernel before version 4.14.8, 4.9.71, and 4.4.114 allows attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read) via a specially crafted USB over IP packet.

code_evidence: The dir value selects ep_in or ep_out, but the array index is epnum masked with 0x7f, so an attacker-controlled epnum (e.g., 128 or larger) is reduced to an in-range-looking index rather than being validated against the array bounds.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the unchecked epnum leads to reading memory outside the intended endpoint array before use. This is an out-of-bounds read, distinct from a write-based weakness; the patch adds an epnum range check to prevent it.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: get_pipe() indexes udev->ep_in/ep_out using an unvalidated, attacker-supplied endpoint number from a USB/IP packet. Trigger: a crafted packet with an out-of-range epnum reaches this indexing. Consequence: an out-of-bounds read of the endpoint array yields a bogus pointer that is later dereferenced, causing a crash (the pre-patch BUG() path).

description: A HTTP response header injection vulnerability in Swoole v4.5.2 allows attackers to execute arbitrary code via supplying a crafted URL.

code_evidence: Iterates over the user-controlled trailer array (line 14) and reads each key and value. Lines 15-18 only skip null entries; no validation rejects CR or LF characters in the key or value. Line 20-21 formats them directly with sw_snprintf into "%.*s: %.*s\r\n", and line 22 appends the result to the response.

Trigger: an attacker supplies a trailer key or value containing \r\n followed by crafted header or body content. Consequence: the injected special elements are interpreted by the downstream HTTP parser, enabling response header injection/splitting and potentially arbitrary code execution as described.

description: The blockchain node in FISCO-BCOS V2.7.2 may have a bug when dealing with unformatted packet and lead to a crash. A malicious node can send a packet continuously. The packet is in an incorrect format and cannot be decoded by the node correctly. As a result, the node may consume the memory sustainably and crash. More details are shown at: https://github.com/FISCO-BCOS/FISCO-BCOS/issues/1951

code_evidence: Line 8 reads a 32-bit length field directly from the network buffer and converts it with ntohl, so m_length is fully attacker-controlled. Lines 9-12 only compare this claimed length against the actual received size and return PACKET_INCOMPLETE when the buffer is shorter; there is no upper bound or sanity check on m_length before it is used.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-20 fits because the function receives attacker-controlled packet metadata and fails to validate that the declared length is within required bounds before processing. The issue is improper validation of input, not a transformation or encoding flaw.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The decoded length is accepted without validating it against a maximum. A forged packet can declare a large length while the peer keeps sending data, so the length is never rejected and buffering continues, causing sustained memory consumption and node crash. The root cause is missing upper-bound validation of an untrusted header field; the consequence is resource exhaustion/DoS.

description: An issue was discovered in QPDF before 7.0.0. There is a stack-based out-of-bounds read in the function iterate_rc4 in QPDF_encryption.cc.

code_evidence: k1 is produced by compute_encryption_key at line 6 and passed directly as the key buffer to iterate_rc4 at lines 9-11, with data.getLengthBytes() as the length argument. No check or padding ensures k1 actually contains that many bytes before iterate_rc4 reads it.

Trigger: a key shorter than the declared length causes iterate_rc4 to read past the end of k1's storage, producing a stack-based out-of-bounds read. Consequence: memory disclosure or crash from reading beyond the buffer.

Get rid of the global big_buffer.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  char message_loc[1024];', '    flogger_mutex_lock(&lock_bigbuffer);', '    if (big_buffer_alloced < (query_len * 2 + csize))', '    {', '      big_buffer_alloced= (query_len * 2 + csize + 4095) & ~4095L;', '      big_buffer= realloc(big_buffer, big_buffer_alloced);', '      if (big_buffer == NULL)', '      {', '        big_buffer_alloced= 0;', '        return 0;', '      }', '    }', '  if (message == big_buffer)', '    flogger_mutex_unlock(&lock_bigbuffer);'], 'added_lines': ['  char message_loc[2048];', '  char *big_buffer= NULL;', '    size_t big_buffer_alloced= (query_len * 2 + csize + 4095) & ~4095L;', '    if(!(big_buffer= malloc(big_buffer_alloced)))', '      return 0;', '  if (big_buffer)', '    free(big_buffer);']}
description: MariaDB Server before 10.7 is vulnerable to Denial of Service. While executing the plugin/server_audit/server_audit.c method log_statement_ex, the held lock lock_bigbuffer is not released correctly, which allows local users to trigger a denial of service due to the deadlock.

code_evidence: The large-message path acquires lock_bigbuffer before examining or growing the shared big_buffer, then copies the header into it and redirects message to the locked shared buffer.
If realloc fails, the function returns 0 immediately while lock_bigbuffer is still held; no unlock occurs on this error path.
On success, message is set to big_buffer and message_size to big_buffer_alloced, so the buffer is used for the remainder of the logging.
The only unlock is guarded by message == big_buffer at function exit; the earlier error return bypasses it entirely.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function directly fails to properly release an acquired lock on the shared big_buffer on an error path, matching CWE-667's improper lock acquisition/release. This is a lock-release defect rather than a data race, since the lock is taken but never balanced.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the mutex is acquired at line 85 but the realloc-failure branch returns at line 93 without releasing it. Trigger: a query large enough to exceed the stack buffer combined with allocation failure. Consequence: lock_bigbuffer remains held, so subsequent log_statement_ex calls block, producing a deadlock and denial of service for local users.

description: A vulnerability, which was classified as problematic, was found in GPAC 2.3-DEV-rev35-gbbca86917-master. This affects the function gf_m2ts_process_sdt of the file media_tools/mpegts.c. The manipulation leads to heap-based buffer overflow. Attacking locally is a requirement. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue. The identifier VDB-223293 was assigned to this vulnerability.

code_evidence: descs_size is decoded from untrusted section bytes at data[pos+3]/data[pos+4] and pos advances by 5 without verifying that pos+descs_size stays within data_size.
The descriptor loop reads data[pos+d_pos] and data[pos+d_pos+1] bounded only by descs_size, so an attacker-controlled length can drive reads beyond the section buffer.

ulen values are read from the descriptor payload and used to allocate provider/service buffers, then memcpy copies ulen bytes from data+pos+d_pos regardless of remaining data_size; pos += descs_size then moves the outer loop past the buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe copies into gf_malloc-allocated provider/service buffers with attacker-controlled lengths directly cause memory corruption in heap memory, which is CWE-122. It is not merely an out-of-bounds read because the copied data overwrites heap-allocated buffers.

evidence_lines.code: pos += descs_size;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the descriptor length and inner ulen fields are trusted without checking them against the actual section size. Trigger: a crafted SDT section whose descs_size or descriptor lengths exceed data_size. Consequence: heap buffers sized from ulen are overflowed, and out-of-bounds reads/writes occur, matching the reported heap-based buffer overflow.

description: In Wireshark 2.2.7, PROFINET IO data with a high recursion depth allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (stack exhaustion) in the dissect_IODWriteReq function in plugins/profinet/packet-dcerpc-pn-io.c.

code_evidence: When the IODWrite block index equals 0xe040, the code enters a loop over the remaining capture and recursively calls dissect_IODWriteReq on each iteration, with no depth counter or bound on the recursion. The recursion terminates only when the captured length is exhausted, so a crafted packet with many nested write blocks drives unbounded stack growth.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-674 fits because the function controls the amount of recursion only through the input length, not a depth cap, allowing excessive stack consumption. It is not a simple infinite loop; the recursion is bounded by attacker-controlled data volume, which is exactly uncontrolled recursion.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the recursive call in the IODWriteMultipleReq branch lacks any recursion-depth limit. Trigger: attacker-supplied PROFINET IO data whose index 0xe040 causes repeated self-invocation for each remaining byte. Consequence: stack exhaustion and a crash (DoS).

PR23994, libbfd integer overflow

	PR 23994
	* aoutx.h: Include limits.h.
	(get_reloc_upper_bound): Detect long overflow and return a file
	too big error if it occurs.
	* elf.c: Include limits.h.
	(_bfd_elf_get_symtab_upper_bound): Detect long overflow and return
	a file too big error if it occurs.
	(_bfd_elf_get_dynamic_symtab_upper_bound): Likewise.
	(_bfd_elf_get_dynamic_reloc_upper_bound): Likewise.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  long symcount;'], 'added_lines': ['  bfd_size_type symcount;', '  if (symcount >= LONG_MAX / sizeof (asymbol *))', '    {', '      bfd_set_error (bfd_error_file_too_big);', '      return -1;', '    }']}
description: binutils version 2.32 and earlier contains a Integer Overflow vulnerability in objdump, bfd_get_dynamic_reloc_upper_bound,bfd_canonicalize_dynamic_reloc that can result in Integer overflow trigger heap overflow. Successful exploitation allows execution of arbitrary code.. This attack appear to be exploitable via Local. This vulnerability appears to have been fixed in after commit 3a551c7a1b80fca579461774860574eabfd7f18f.

code_evidence: symcount is a signed long holding hdr->sh_size / sizeof_sym, an attacker-influenced ELF header value. Line 13 computes (symcount + 1) * sizeof(asymbol *) in signed long arithmetic without checking whether symcount is near LONG_MAX, so the multiplication can overflow and wrap.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs an unchecked arithmetic size computation whose result can wrap, exactly matching CWE-190 (Integer Overflow or Wraparound). The fix confirms this by adding a LONG_MAX / sizeof(asymbol *) guard before the multiplication; this is an overflow of a size value, not a mere truncation or off-by-one.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the size calculation (symcount + 1) * sizeof(asymbol *) is performed in signed long with no upper-bound check on symcount. Trigger: a crafted ELF dynamic symbol table header with a huge sh_size yields a large symcount, so the product wraps to a small or negative value. Consequence: the returned symtab_size understates the required buffer, enabling undersized allocation and later heap overflow when symbols are written.

commit_msg: Fix some pipelines to be safe if downstream write fails (fuzz issue 28262)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    getNext()->write(outbuf, this->pos - 1);', ''], 'added_lines': ['    // Reset before calling getNext()->write in case that throws an', '    // exception.', '    auto t = this->pos - 1;', '', '    getNext()->write(outbuf, t);']}
description: QPDF 9.x through 9.1.1 and 10.x through 10.0.4 has a heap-based buffer overflow in Pl_ASCII85Decoder::write (called from Pl_AES_PDF::flush and Pl_AES_PDF::finish) when a certain downstream write fails.

code_evidence: outbuf is a fixed 4-byte stack buffer, filled from lval in the loop above.

The write length is computed as this->pos - 1 and passed to getNext()->write; state (this->pos, inbuf) is only reset after this call returns. If write throws, pos retains its prior value and inbuf is left unreset, so a retry of flush can reuse stale pos with the 4-byte outbuf.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect is a length/state mismatch causing a write beyond the fixed outbuf bounds, matching CWE-787 (out-of-bounds write). It is not merely an uninitialized-state issue; the overflow stems from writing with a length exceeding the buffer.

evidence_lines.code:
unsigned char outbuf[4];
memset(outbuf, 0, 4);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: flush mutates decoder state (this->pos, inbuf) only after the downstream write, so an exception leaves pos nonzero and inbuf stale. A subsequent flush then writes outbuf using a length derived from resumed pos while outbuf is only 4 bytes, allowing a write past its end. Consequence is memory corruption in the downstream write path.

commit_msg:
Fix NULL dereference triggered via dbus (#183)

Instead of crashing, print the following warning message and ignore it
when no current view exists.
dbus should not be called when there is no document open.

** (gobby-0.5:78328): WARNING **: 10:01:05.468: No current view exists.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tg_assert(m_current_view != NULL);'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (!m_current_view) {', '\t\tg_warning("No current view exists.");', '\t\treturn;', '\t}', '']}
description: Gobby 0.4.11 allows a NULL pointer dereference in the D-Bus handler for certain set_language calls.

code_evidence: Line 4 only asserts m_current_view is non-NULL; assertions like g_assert abort in debug builds but are compiled out under NDEBUG, leaving no runtime guard. Line 5 then dereferences m_current_view via get_active_user() without any null check, and the result feeds the comparison that may enable the undo action on line 6.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits because the function dereferences a pointer expected to be valid but which can be NULL, as confirmed by the added guard. This is a direct null dereference, not a type-confusion or use-after-free weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function dereferences m_current_view (line 5) while relying solely on a g_assert (line 4), which is not a reliable runtime constraint. Trigger: on_can_undo_changed is invoked via D-Bus when no document/view is open, so m_current_view is NULL. Consequence: NULL pointer dereference causing a crash (availability DoS); the patch replaces the assert with an explicit null check and early return.

commit_msg:
teredo: be stricter on what to consider valid teredo

Invalid Teredo can lead to valid DNS traffic (or other UDP traffic)
being misdetected as Teredo. This leads to false negatives in the
UDP payload inspection.

Make the teredo code only consider a packet teredo if the encapsulated
data was decoded without any 'invalid' events being set.

Bug #2736.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if (unlikely(ret != TM_ECODE_OK)) {', '        /* Not a tunnel packet, just a pseudo packet */'], 'added_lines': ['    if (unlikely(ret != TM_ECODE_OK) ||', '            (proto == DECODE_TUNNEL_IPV6_TEREDO && (p->flags & PKT_IS_INVALID)))', '    {', '        /* Not a (valid) tunnel packet */', '        SCLogDebug("tunnel packet is invalid");', '']}
description: Open Information Security Foundation Suricata prior to version 4.1.2 is affected by: Denial of Service - DNS detection bypass. The impact is: An attacker can evade a signature detection with a specialy formed network packet. The component is: app-layer-detect-proto.c, decode.c, decode-teredo.c and decode-ipv6.c (https://github.com/OISF/suricata/pull/3590/commits/11f3659f64a4e42e90cb3c09fcef66894205aefe, https://github.com/OISF/suricata/pull/3590/commits/8357ef3f8ffc7d99ef6571350724160de356158b). The attack vector is: An attacker can trigger the vulnerability by sending a specifically crafted network request. The fixed version is: 4.1.2.

code_evidence: DecodeTunnel decodes the encapsulated tunnel payload into p, returning ret; the function only rejects the packet when ret != TM_ECODE_OK.

On success the code marks the packet as a tunnel, increments the tunnel counter and disables payload inspection on the parent, so the decoded payload is trusted without checking whether decoding set invalid flags.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function accepts attacker-controlled network input as valid without validating the decoded content's correctness (the invalid-event flags), which is improper input validation (CWE-20). The consequence is a detection bypass rather than a direct memory-safety flaw.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the return code of DecodeTunnel is treated as the sole validity check, without inspecting per-packet validity flags set during decoding. Trigger: a crafted Teredo/UDP packet that decodes with 'invalid' events but returns TM_ECODE_OK. Consequence: the malformed packet is accepted as a valid tunnel and payload inspection is suppressed on the parent, enabling DNS detection bypass.

description: wiretap/nettrace_3gpp_32_423.c in the 3GPP TS 32.423 Trace file parser in Wireshark 2.0.x before 2.0.2 does not ensure that a '\0' character is present at the end of certain strings, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (stack-based buffer overflow and application crash) via a crafted file.

description: TensorFlow is an open source platform for machine learning. The security vulnerability results in FractionalMax(AVG)Pool with illegal pooling_ratio. Attackers using Tensorflow can exploit the vulnerability. They can access heap memory which is not in the control of user, leading to a crash or remote code execution. We have patched the issue in GitHub commit 216525144ee7c910296f5b05d214ca1327c9ce48. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.11.0. We will also cherry pick this commit on TensorFlow 2.10.1.

code_evidence: pooling_ratio_ is read from the op attribute at line 3 without any validation of individual element values. Lines 6-8 only check the vector has 4 dimensions; lines 9-12 only constrain dimensions 0 and 3 to equal 1. Nothing here rejects a pooling_ratio_[i] below 1 (e.g., zero or negative) for the spatial dimensions 1 and 2, so such values flow onward into the fractional pooling computation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing lower-bound check permits ratios that drive downstream buffer index arithmetic out of range, matching CWE-787's out-of-bounds write. It is not merely an input-validation issue: the accepted illegal ratio propagates into memory writes, which is the defining CWE-787 behavior.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the constructor accepts non-positive pooling_ratio_ entries because only length and the batch/channel-ratio constraints are enforced. Trigger: a crafted FractionalAvgPool op with pooling_ratio_[1] or [2] < 1 passes these checks and is used in downstream size/index computations. Consequence: those computations can produce out-of-range offsets, yielding an out-of-bounds write (heap corruption, crash, or potential code execution).

commit_msg:
Jann Horn reported a problem with commit eb1231f73c4d ("selinux:
clarify task subjective and objective credentials") where some LSM
hooks were attempting to access the subjective credentials of a task
other than the current task.  Generally speaking, it is not safe to
access another task's subjective credentials and doing so can cause
a number of problems.

Further, while looking into the problem, I realized that Smack was
suffering from a similar problem brought about by a similar commit
1fb057dcde11 ("smack: differentiate between subjective and objective
task credentials").

This patch addresses this problem by restoring the use of the task's
objective credentials in those cases where the task is other than the
current executing task.  Not only does this resolve the problem
reported by Jann, it is arguably the correct thing to do in these
cases.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: eb1231f73c4d ("selinux: clarify task subjective and objective credentials")
Fixes: 1fb057dcde11 ("smack: differentiate between subjective and objective task credentials")
Reported-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Acked-by: Eric W. Biederman <ebiederm@xmission.com>
Acked-by: Casey Schaufler <casey@schaufler-ca.com>
Signed-off-by: Paul Moore <paul@paul-moore.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t    task_sid_subj(parent), task_sid_obj(current),'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t    task_sid_obj(parent), task_sid_obj(current),']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel before 5.14.8. A use-after-free in selinux_ptrace_traceme (aka the SELinux handler for PTRACE_TRACEME) could be used by local attackers to cause memory corruption and escalate privileges, aka CID-a3727a8bac0a. This occurs because of an attempt to access the subjective credentials of another task.

code_evidence: selinux_ptrace_traceme receives an arbitrary task_struct *parent, not necessarily the current task, and passes task_sid_subj(parent) into the permission check. Accessing another task's subjective credentials dereferences state that is only valid for the current task's subjective context.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the unsafe operation is dereferencing credential memory through a task other than the current one, where that subjective pointer is no longer valid and may have been freed. This is a use-after-free rather than a mere permission-check logic error; the patch swaps to task_sid_obj(parent) to avoid the invalid reference.

evidence_lines.code:
static int selinux_ptrace_traceme(struct task_struct *parent)
task_sid_subj(parent), task_sid_obj(current),

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the hook uses the subjective credentials of a non-current task rather than its objective credentials. When PTRACE_TRACEME is invoked with a parent that is not the current task, the subjective credential pointer is stale/unreliable, leading to a use-after-free of the referenced credential memory. Supported consequence: memory corruption that a local attacker could leverage for privilege escalation.

commit_msg:
ASAN SFTP Fixes
When decoding SFTP messages, fix the size checks so they don't wrap. (ZD12766)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if (sz + idx > maxSz) {'], 'added_lines': ['    if (sz > maxSz - idx) {']}
description: WolfSSH v1.4.7 was discovered to contain an integer overflow via the function wolfSSH_SFTP_RecvRMDIR.

code_evidence: Line 14 reads an attacker-controlled 32-bit length sz from the SFTP request and advances idx by UINT32_SZ. Line 15's guard computes sz + idx before comparing to maxSz; since both are word32, a large sz near UINT32_MAX wraps to a small value, so the check at 15-17 passes and the oversized sz is trusted downstream (WMALLOC at 18, WMEMCPY at 22).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The guard itself performs an unchecked 32-bit addition (sz + idx) whose wraparound defeats the size validation, exactly matching CWE-190. The safe form sz > maxSz - idx avoids the overflow; this is a wraparound in size computation, not merely a missing bounds check.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the bounds check adds sz and idx in 32-bit arithmetic, so the sum can wraparound and the comparison no longer reflects the true required size. Trigger: a crafted STAT request whose declared name length is near UINT32_MAX. Consequence: the length check is bypassed, allowing oversized allocation/copy operations and memory corruption or DoS.

commit_msg:
Patch series "Fix several device private page reference counting issues",
v2

This series aims to fix a number of page reference counting issues in
drivers dealing with device private ZONE_DEVICE pages.  These result in
use-after-free type bugs, either from accessing a struct page which no
longer exists because it has been removed or accessing fields within the
struct page which are no longer valid because the page has been freed.

During normal usage it is unlikely these will cause any problems.  However
without these fixes it is possible to crash the kernel from userspace. 
These crashes can be triggered either by unloading the kernel module or
unbinding the device from the driver prior to a userspace task exiting. 
In modules such as Nouveau it is also possible to trigger some of these
issues by explicitly closing the device file-descriptor prior to the task
exiting and then accessing device private memory.

This involves some minor changes to both PowerPC and AMD GPU code. 
Unfortunately I lack hardware to test either of those so any help there
would be appreciated.  The changes mimic what is done in for both Nouveau
and hmm-tests though so I doubt they will cause problems.


This patch (of 8):

When the CPU tries to access a device private page the migrate_to_ram()
callback associated with the pgmap for the page is called.  However no
reference is taken on the faulting page.  Therefore a concurrent migration
of the device private page can free the page and possibly the underlying
pgmap.  This results in a race which can crash the kernel due to the
migrate_to_ram() function pointer becoming invalid.  It also means drivers
can't reliably read the zone_device_data field because the page may have
been freed with memunmap_pages().

Close the race by getting a reference on the page while holding the ptl to
ensure it has not been freed.  Unfortunately the elevated reference count
will cause the migration required to handle the fault to fail.  To avoid
this failure pass the faulting page into the migrate_vma functions so that
if an elevated reference count is found it can be checked to see if it's
expected or not.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The shown function only retries migration and calls svm_migrate_ram_to_vram; it contains no page reference acquisition or dereference of a potentially freed page, so the CWE-416 race described in the commit is not evidenced in this function.

commit_msg: capture: validate frame has at least IP header before assembly #431
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    // Check frame has at least IP header length', '    if (ip_ver == 4 && header->caplen < link_hl + sizeof(struct ip))', '        return NULL;', '', '#ifdef USE_IPV6', '    if (ip_ver == 6 && header->caplen < link_hl + sizeof(struct ip6_hdr))', '        return NULL;', '#endif', '']}
description: Sngrep v1.6.0 was discovered to contain a heap buffer overflow via the function capture_packet_reasm_ip at /src/capture.c.

code_evidence: The reassembly loop dereferences ip4 = (struct ip *)(packet + link_hl) and reads ip4->ip_v while only checking *size >= sizeof(struct ip), not that the captured frame actually contains a full IP header at link_hl; the patch adds the missing caplen check.
Lines 89-90 overwrite *caplen and *size from the attacker-controlled ip_len and ip_hl fields before any length verification.
ip_cap_len is accumulated from ip_len - ip_hl (line 119) and ip_exp_len from ip_frag_off + ip_len - ip_hl (line 126), both derived from header fields rather than actual captured bytes.
When ip_cap_len equals ip_exp_len, len_data is summed and memset(packet, 0, link_hl + ip_hl + len_data) is executed after only a len_data > MAX_CAPTURE_LEN check.
The memcpy at lines 161-163 copies ntohs(frame_ip->ip_len) - frame_ip->ip_hl * 4 bytes to packet + link_hl + ip_hl + offset*8, with no check that the destination lies within the buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs a memcpy whose destination offset and length derive from attacker-controlled IP header fields, and the buffer is sized from related but unvalidated values, so data is written beyond the intended buffer. This is an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787); the missing caplen check is the entry condition that lets malformed short frames reach this path.

evidence_lines.code:
*caplen = link_hl + ip_len;
*size = *caplen - link_hl - ip_hl;

pkt->ip_cap_len += ip_len - ip_hl;
pkt->ip_exp_len = ip_frag_off + ip_len - ip_hl;

if (pkt->ip_cap_len == pkt->ip_exp_len) {
memset(packet, 0, link_hl + ip_hl + len_data);

while ((frame = vector_iterator_next(&it))) {
ntohs(frame_ip->ip_len) - frame_ip->ip_hl * 4);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: frame lengths and fragment offsets from untrusted IP headers are used to compute the reassembly buffer size and copy offsets without validating the actual captured frame length. Trigger: a crafted fragmented packet whose ip_len/ip_off values produce a len_data smaller than the real copied payload. Consequence: the memcpy writes past the allocated packet buffer, corrupting heap memory.

commit_msg: try fix null pointer deference
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    if (!stream) return EOF;']}
description: The function bitstr_tell at bitstr.c in ffjpeg commit 4ab404e has a NULL pointer dereference.

code_evidence: Line 3 dereferences the caller-supplied void *stream as *(int*)stream to read the type tag, with no NULL check before the dereference. Lines 4-5 then dispatch on that type value to mbitstr_close/fbitstr_close.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits directly: the function dereferences a pointer it expects to be valid, but the pointer is never checked, and the patch adds exactly the missing NULL guard. This is a NULL dereference, not an uninitialized-pointer or type-confusion issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: bitstr_close unconditionally dereferences stream to obtain the type field, so a NULL stream causes a NULL pointer dereference at line 3 before any validation. Trigger: calling bitstr_close(NULL). Supported consequence is a crash/DoS; no memory-safety or code-execution consequence is shown here.
