description: The function tee_obj_free in Samsung mTower through 0.3.0 allows a trusted application to trigger a Denial of Service (DoS) by invoking the function TEE_AllocateOperation with a disturbed heap layout, related to utee_cryp_obj_alloc.

code_evidence: Line 3 computes sz from the caller-supplied size_bits via mpa_StaticVarSizeInU32(size_bits) * sizeof(uint32_t); no check constrains size_bits or the resulting sz. Line 4 passes sz to calloc(1, sz) to size the allocation, and line 7 derives bn->alloc = sz - MPA_NUMBASE_METADATA_SIZE_IN_U32 * sizeof(uint32_t) from the same unchecked quantity. The only guard, lines 5-6, tests the allocation result, not the quantity.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-1284 fits because size_bits is an input expected to specify a quantity (size), and the function neither validates its required properties nor the derived sz before using it for allocation and arithmetic. This is a quantity-validation issue, not merely a missing NULL check.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the size quantity size_bits is converted to sz and used for allocation and metadata arithmetic without validating its range or magnitude. Trigger: a trusted application supplies a disturbed/oversized size_bits. Consequence: an undersized or overflowed allocation layout, leading to availability impact (DoS) when downstream TEE_AllocateOperation/utee_cryp_obj_alloc uses the object.

commit_msg: ok_png: Disallow multiple IHDR chunks (#15)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['            if (hdr_found) {', '                ok_png_error(png, OK_PNG_ERROR_INVALID, "Multiple IHDR chunks not allowed");', '                return;', '            }']}
description: David Brackeen ok-file-formats 203defd is vulnerable to Buffer Overflow. When the function of the ok-file-formats project is used, a heap-buffer-overflow occurred in function ok_png_transform_scanline() in "/ok_png.c:712".

code_evidence: Line 28 checks only the chunk type; when an IHDR chunk is seen it unconditionally sets hdr_found = true at line 29 and calls ok_png_read_header at line 30, with no guard against a second IHDR.

hdr_found is initialized false at line 13 and gates the 'IHDR must appear first' check at line 24, but the loop at line 15 never rejects a repeated IHDR, so a second header is parsed and overwrites the first header's state.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The supported consequence is an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787): re-parsed header values drive later scanline writes past the allocated buffer. This is not merely a parsing/validation issue (CWE-20); the missing duplicate check is the cause, and the write past the buffer is the weakness realized.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the IHDR branch at lines 28-30 lacks a duplicate-chunk check, so a crafted PNG with a second IHDR re-invokes ok_png_read_header and overwrites width/height/format state. Trigger: an attacker-supplied PNG containing multiple IHDR chunks. Consequence: inconsistent header state leads to a heap-buffer-overflow in ok_png_transform_scanline, i.e., an out-of-bounds write.

commit_msg:
Fix DoS in PE/QNX/DYLDCACHE/PSX parsers ##crash

* Reported by lazymio
* Reproducer: AAA4AAAAAB4=
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t\t} else if (!*name) {'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t\t}', '\t\t\t\tif (!*name) {']}
description: Denial of Service in GitHub repository radareorg/radare2 prior to 5.6.4.

code_evidence: The parser loops over import-table entries with only import_ordinal >= UT16_MAX as an upper bound; there is no limit tied to the actual input size or entry count.

r_buf_read_at reads PE_NAME_LENGTH bytes; when len < 1 the code jumps to error, but when the read succeeds with an empty name (!*name) it breaks. The diff separates these checks, yet the loop continues for every non-empty import entry.
The do-while(import_table) condition keeps iterating while import_table is non-zero, allowing a crafted PE to drive many iterations.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Unbounded iteration and repeated allocation driven by attacker-controlled import-table data match CWE-400's uncontrolled resource consumption. It is not a simple out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) because the reads are bounds-checked; the weakness is lack of throttling on work performed.

evidence_lines.code: } while (import_table);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the loop bound is the 16-bit ordinal counter rather than a resource/count limit, so a malformed PE with a long chain of import entries forces repeated reads and reallocations. Trigger: crafted import table (as in the supplied reproducer). Consequence: excessive CPU/memory consumption leading to DoS.

commit_msg:
ltc: remove LTC_LINARO_FIX_RSAWITHOUTCRT

LTC_LINARO_FIX_RSAWITHOUTCRT is used to handle the case where the CRT
optimized algorithm cannot be used because the optimized parameters are
missing. In the official LibTomCrypt tree, there is an official fix for
this.

Please see commits (official LibTomCrypt tree):
    01f184540232 ("harden RSA CRT by implementing the proposed
                   countermeasure from ch. 1.3 of [1]")
    a6e89d58d4fb ("RSA in CRT optimization parameters are empty")
    2bb3f0246f65 ("RSA in case CRT optimization parameters are not
                   populated")

Those patches were brought into OP-TEE with this patch
    a50cb361d9e5 ("ltc: sync from official develop branch")

And therefore there is no need to keep the LTC_LINARO_FIX_RSAWITHOUTCRT
any longer, hence this patch removes the flag and the code related to
that particular flag.

Signed-off-by: Joakim Bech <joakim.bech@linaro.org>
Reviewed-by: Jerome Forissier <jerome.forissier@linaro.org>
Reviewed-by: Jens Wiklander <jens.wiklander@linaro.org>
Acked-by: Etienne Carriere <etienne.carriere@linaro.org>
Tested-by: Jerome Forissier <jerome.forissier@linaro.org> (HiKey, GP)
Tested-by: Etienne Carriere <etienne.carriere@linaro.org> (b2260, GP)

commit_msg: Bug 698056: make bounds check in gx_ttfReader__Read more robust
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            r->error = (r->glyph_data.bits.size - r->pos < n ?'], 'added_lines': ['            r->error = ((r->pos >= r->glyph_data.bits.size ||', '                        r->glyph_data.bits.size - r->pos < n) ?']}
description: The gx_ttfReader__Read function in base/gxttfb.c in Artifex Ghostscript GhostXPS 9.21 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (heap-based buffer over-read and application crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted document.

code_evidence: q is computed as r->glyph_data.bits.data + r->pos before any bound check on r->pos [7]. The pre-patch guard only checks size - r->pos < n [8,9]; if r->pos exceeds size, the unsigned subtraction wraps, the comparison passes, and memcpy(p, q, n) [11] reads from q beyond the buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe memcpy with q derived from an unchecked offset reads data past the intended glyph buffer, matching CWE-125. It is a read (not CWE-787 write) because memcpy's destination p is caller-provided and the flaw is the source-side over-read.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the bounds check uses the unsigned expression size - r->pos without first verifying r->pos < size, so an attacker-influenced position past the end wraps and bypasses the check. Trigger: a crafted document driving extra_glyph_index path with r->pos >= glyph_data.bits.size. Consequence: heap-based out-of-bounds read at q during memcpy, causing crash/DoS and possible memory disclosure.

commit_msg:
When opening files for write, ensure they aren't symbolic links

Issue #1048 identified that if, for example, a non privileged user
created a symbolic link from /etc/keepalvied.data to /etc/passwd,
writing to /etc/keepalived.data (which could be invoked via DBus)
would cause /etc/passwd to be overwritten.

This commit stops keepalived writing to pathnames where the ultimate
component is a symbolic link, by setting O_NOFOLLOW whenever opening
a file for writing.

This might break some setups, where, for example, /etc/keepalived.data
was a symbolic link to /home/fred/keepalived.data. If this was the case,
instead create a symbolic link from /home/fred/keepalived.data to
/tmp/keepalived.data, so that the file is still accessible via
/home/fred/keepalived.data.

There doesn't appear to be a way around this backward incompatibility,
since even checking if the pathname is a symbolic link prior to opening
for writing would create a race condition.

Signed-off-by: Quentin Armitage <quentin@armitage.org.uk>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tFILE *fp = fopen("/tmp/smtp-alert.log", "a");'], 'added_lines': ['\tFILE *fp = fopen_safe("/tmp/smtp-alert.log", "a");']}
description: keepalived 2.0.8 didn't check for pathnames with symlinks when writing data to a temporary file upon a call to PrintData or PrintStats. This allowed local users to overwrite arbitrary files if fs.protected_symlinks is set to 0, as demonstrated by a symlink from /tmp/keepalived.data or /tmp/keepalived.stats to /etc/passwd.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function only appends SMTP alert log text to a fixed /tmp path via fopen; the patch changes it to fopen_safe for symlink protection, but no sensitive information is exposed or disclosed by this function, so CWE-200 is not directly supported.

commit_msg:
Fix uninitialized read with UTF-8 grouping chars

The character type in xsltFormatNumberConversion was too narrow and
an invalid character/length combination could be passed to
xsltNumberFormatDecimal, resulting in an uninitialized read.

Found by OSS-Fuzz.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tpchar = xsltGetUTF8Char(self->grouping, &len);', '\t\t\t\tpchar, len);'], 'added_lines': ['        int gchar;', '\tgchar = xsltGetUTF8Char(self->grouping, &len);', '\t\t\t\tgchar, len);']}
description: In numbers.c in libxslt 1.1.33, a type holding grouping characters of an xsl:number instruction was too narrow and an invalid character/length combination could be passed to xsltNumberFormatDecimal, leading to a read of uninitialized stack data.

code_evidence: Line 11 declares pchar as a single xmlChar (8-bit) to hold the grouping character.

Lines 278-285: when self->grouping is non-empty, len is set to the UTF-8 byte length and xsltGetUTF8Char returns a multi-byte Unicode code point that is stored into the narrow pchar, truncating it; pchar and len are then passed to xsltNumberFormatDecimal.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The value is produced as one type (int code point) but reinterpreted/truncated through an incompatible narrower type (xmlChar), matching CWE-843 type confusion; this is not merely a length error since the type mismatch is the root cause.

evidence_lines.code: xmlChar pchar;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: a Unicode code point (int-sized) returned by xsltGetUTF8Char is stored in an xmlChar, so the value and its associated length become inconsistent. Trigger: a grouping character whose UTF-8 encoding exceeds one byte. Consequence: xsltNumberFormatDecimal receives a mismatched character/length pair and reads uninitialized stack data.

commit_msg:
Bug 699665 "memory corruption in aesdecode"

The specimen file calls aesdecode without specifying the key to be
used, though it does manage to do enough work with the PDF interpreter
routines to get access to aesdecode (which isn't normally available).

This causes us to read uninitialised memory, which can (and often does)
lead to a segmentation fault.

In this commit we set the key to NULL explicitly during intialisation
and then check it before we read it. If its NULL we just return.

It seems bizarre that we don't return error codes, we should probably
look into that at some point, but this prevents the code trying to
read uninitialised memory.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '    if (ctx == NULL || ctx->rk == NULL)', '        return;']}
description: In Artifex Ghostscript 9.23 before 2018-08-24, attackers able to supply crafted PostScript could use uninitialized memory access in the aesdecode operator to crash the interpreter or potentially execute code.

code_evidence: Line 15 unconditionally reads ctx->rk into RK; no check that ctx or ctx->rk is non-NULL or initialized.
Lines 16-19 dereference RK via *RK++ to XOR the input block, consuming the round-key array.
Line 22 reads ctx->nr to bound the decryption loop, relying on ctx being a valid initialized context.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-908 covers using or accessing a resource not initialized; here the round-key pointer/array is read before initialization, matching the uninitialized-resource read. This is not a NULL-pointer dereference alone: the missing constraint is initialization of the key material, not merely a null check.

evidence_lines.code: RK = ctx->rk;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: aes_crypt_ecb assumes ctx and its rk round-key array are initialized, but the aesdecode operator can be reached without a key being set, so ctx->rk is uninitialized. Trigger: crafted PostScript invoking aesdecode without a key. The code then reads *RK and ctx->nr from uninitialized memory, causing invalid reads, crashes, or potentially code execution.

commit_msg:
virtio-gpu: fix memory leak in set scanout

In virtio_gpu_set_scanout function, when creating the 'rect'
its refcount is set to 2, by pixman_image_create_bits and
qemu_create_displaysurface_pixman function. This can lead
a memory leak issues. This patch avoid this issue.

Signed-off-by: Li Qiang <liqiang6-s@360.cn>
Reviewed-by: Marc-André Lureau <marcandre.lureau@redhat.com>
Message-id: 5884626f.5b2f6b0a.1bfff.3037@mx.google.com
Signed-off-by: Gerd Hoffmann <kraxel@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['        pixman_image_unref(rect);']}
description: Memory leak in the virtio_gpu_set_scanout function in hw/display/virtio-gpu.c in QEMU (aka Quick Emulator) allows local guest OS users to cause a denial of service (memory consumption) via a large number of "VIRTIO_GPU_CMD_SET_SCANOUT:" commands.

code_evidence: Line 69 declares pixman_image_t *rect; lines 71-72 create it via pixman_image_create_bits, giving it a refcount. Line 73 refs res->image and line 74 attaches a destroy function to rect. Line 76 wraps rect in a display surface via qemu_create_displaysurface_pixman, which itself takes a reference, leaving rect with an extra reference that is never released on the normal path (line 81). The error path at lines 77-79 also returns without unref'ing rect.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-401 fits because the function allocates a pixman image and fails to release its reference after use, leaking memory on every invocation. This is a missing-release weakness rather than a use-after-free or double-free, since the object remains allocated but unreachable for reuse.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: rect is allocated and referenced but the extra reference obtained through pixman_image_create_bits is never dropped after the surface is installed. Trigger: each guest VIRTIO_GPU_CMD_SET_SCANOUT command that recreates the scanout surface. Consequence: unbounded memory consumption, allowing a local guest to cause denial of service.

commit_msg:
acpi: acpica: fix acpi operand cache leak in dswstate.c

I found an ACPI cache leak in ACPI early termination and boot continuing case.

When early termination occurs due to malicious ACPI table, Linux kernel
terminates ACPI function and continues to boot process. While kernel terminates
ACPI function, kmem_cache_destroy() reports Acpi-Operand cache leak.

Boot log of ACPI operand cache leak is as follows:
>[    0.585957] ACPI: Added _OSI(Module Device)
>[    0.587218] ACPI: Added _OSI(Processor Device)
>[    0.588530] ACPI: Added _OSI(3.0 _SCP Extensions)
>[    0.589790] ACPI: Added _OSI(Processor Aggregator Device)
>[    0.591534] ACPI Error: Illegal I/O port address/length above 64K: C806E00000004002/0x2 (20170303/hwvalid-155)
>[    0.594351] ACPI Exception: AE_LIMIT, Unable to initialize fixed events (20170303/evevent-88)
>[    0.597858] ACPI: Unable to start the ACPI Interpreter
>[    0.599162] ACPI Error: Could not remove SCI handler (20170303/evmisc-281)
>[    0.601836] kmem_cache_destroy Acpi-Operand: Slab cache still has objects
>[    0.603556] CPU: 0 PID: 1 Comm: swapper/0 Not tainted 4.12.0-rc5 #26
>[    0.605159] Hardware name: innotek GmbH VirtualBox/VirtualBox, BIOS VirtualBox 12/01/2006
>[    0.609177] Call Trace:
>[    0.610063]  ? dump_stack+0x5c/0x81
>[    0.611118]  ? kmem_cache_destroy+0x1aa/0x1c0
>[    0.612632]  ? acpi_sleep_proc_init+0x27/0x27
>[    0.613906]  ? acpi_os_delete_cache+0xa/0x10
>[    0.617986]  ? acpi_ut_delete_caches+0x3f/0x7b
>[    0.619293]  ? acpi_terminate+0xa/0x14
>[    0.620394]  ? acpi_init+0x2af/0x34f
>[    0.621616]  ? __class_create+0x4c/0x80
>[    0.623412]  ? video_setup+0x7f/0x7f
>[    0.624585]  ? acpi_sleep_proc_init+0x27/0x27
>[    0.625861]  ? do_one_initcall+0x4e/0x1a0
>[    0.627513]  ? kernel_init_freeable+0x19e/0x21f
>[    0.628972]  ? rest_init+0x80/0x80
>[    0.630043]  ? kernel_init+0xa/0x100
>[    0.631084]  ? ret_from_fork+0x25/0x30
>[    0.633343] vgaarb: loaded
>[    0.635036] EDAC MC: Ver: 3.0.0
>[    0.638601] PCI: Probing PCI hardware
>[    0.639833] PCI host bridge to bus 0000:00
>[    0.641031] pci_bus 0000:00: root bus resource [io  0x0000-0xffff]
> ... Continue to boot and log is omitted ...

I analyzed this memory leak in detail and found acpi_ds_obj_stack_pop_and_
delete() function miscalculated the top of the stack. acpi_ds_obj_stack_push()
function uses walk_state->operand_index for start position of the top, but
acpi_ds_obj_stack_pop_and_delete() function considers index 0 for it.
Therefore, this causes acpi operand memory leak.

This cache leak causes a security threat because an old kernel (<= 4.9) shows
memory locations of kernel functions in stack dump. Some malicious users
could use this information to neutralize kernel ASLR.

I made a patch to fix ACPI operand cache leak.

Signed-off-by: Seunghun Han <kkamagui@gmail.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    AcpiDsObjStackPopAndDelete (ArgCount, WalkState);'], 'added_lines': ['    UINT32                  PrevNumOperands = WalkState->NumOperands;', '    UINT32                  NewNumOperands;', '    NewNumOperands = Index;', '    WalkState->NumOperands = i;', '    AcpiDsObjStackPopAndDelete (NewNumOperands, WalkState);', '', '    /* Restore operand count */', '    WalkState->NumOperands = PrevNumOperands;']}
description: The acpi_ds_create_operands() function in drivers/acpi/acpica/dsutils.c in the Linux kernel through 4.12.9 does not flush the operand cache and causes a kernel stack dump, which allows local users to obtain sensitive information from kernel memory and bypass the KASLR protection mechanism (in the kernel through 4.9) via a crafted ACPI table.

code_evidence: Index is initialized from WalkState->NumOperands and incremented while walking arguments; Arguments[Index] and WalkState->Operands[Index] are populated from that base, so the operand stack top is NumOperands+ArgCount, not 0.

On AcpiDsCreateOperand failure the Cleanup path calls AcpiDsObjStackPopAndDelete(ArgCount) from index 0, popping/deleting the wrong entries relative to the pushed operands, leaving operand objects allocated.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The description and commit show the leak leads to a stack dump disclosing kernel addresses to local users, which is exposure of sensitive information. CWE-200 fits as the stated impact; the underlying miscalculation is the mechanism.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the cleanup path pops/deletes ArgCount entries starting at stack index 0 while push used WalkState->NumOperands as the base, so on early failure the operand cache objects are not released. Trigger: a crafted/invalid ACPI table causing AcpiDsCreateOperand to fail. Supported consequence: leaked Acpi-Operand cache objects, and the resulting kernel stack dump can expose kernel addresses enabling KASLR bypass.

commit_msg:
Fixed bug: barriers cannot be active during sweep

Barriers cannot be active during sweep, even in generational mode.
(Although gen. mode is not incremental, it can hit a barrier when
deleting a thread and closing its upvalues.)  The colors of objects are
being changed during sweep and, therefore, cannot be trusted.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['          p = next;  /* go to next element */', '        else {  /* not touched in this cycle */', '          /* else, object is white: just remove it from this list */'], 'added_lines': ['          p = next;  /* keep it in the list and go to next element */', '        else {  /* everything else is removed */', '          /* white objects are simply removed */']}
description: lgc.c in Lua 5.4.0 mishandles the interaction between barriers and the sweep phase, leading to a memory access violation involving collectgarbage.

code_evidence: For G_TOUCHED1 objects the list pointer is advanced with p = next (line 11), keeping the object in the gray list and continuing traversal from its gclist.

For non-touched objects, line 20 executes *p = *next, unlinking curr from the gray list by overwriting the pointer slot; when curr is white it is removed, and when non-white its age/color is rewritten before removal.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect is incorrect release/unlink of a memory-management structure: the gray-list removal at line 20 uses the wrong pointer state, matching CWE-763 (Release of Invalid Pointer or Reference). It is not merely a missing check; the release operation itself is performed on invalid linkage.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: correctgraylist manipulates gray-list linkage during sweep, when object colors are unstable. The unlink at line 20 writes through *p using *next from getgclist(curr); if a barrier has altered curr's color/age or list linkage during sweep, this release logic removes or relinks the wrong node, corrupting the gray list and later causing an invalid memory access (e.g., during collectgarbage).

commit_msg:
Use copyDataProperties slow path for objects with accessors

Summary:
Fix a bug present in `hermesBuiltinCopyDataProperties`.
`hermesBuiltinCopyDataProperties` is meant to copy an object. It does
this by iterating over all the properties in the source object, and
then writing the key-value pair into a new object which is returned.The
iteration is done using `JSObject::forEachOwnPropertyWhile`, providing
a callback to process each property. It will take the property id, look
it up in the source object using `getNamedPropertyValue_RJS`, then take
that resulting value and write it into the target. However, that API
explicitly states the following:

> Obviously the callbacks shouldn't be  doing naughty things like modifying
the property map or creating new hidden classes (even implicitly)

But, `getNamedPropertyValue_RJS` can
perform arbitrary JS execution if it is a getter, including
adding/deleting new properties, which would modify the object's
HiddenClass, thus violating `JSObject::forEachOwnPropertyWhile`'s
precondition.Therefore, the fix is to use the correct, but slower path,
whenever there is an accessor on the object. This code path is more 1:1
to the spec. At the beginning, it will simply find all the properties
of the source object using `JSObject::getOwnPropertyKeys` and then
iterate on those, rather than use `JSObject::forEachOwnPropertyWhile`.
This way, we are allowed to manipulate the source object however we
wish, which is necessary in order to call `getNamedPropertyValue_RJS`.

Reviewed By: neildhar

Differential Revision: D41701871

fbshipit-source-id: c4be179f57d52827f12ca26b1ab8d17cdccd7447
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  if (source->isProxyObject()) {', '        auto cr =', '            JSObject::getNamedPropertyValue_RJS(source, runtime, source, desc);', '        if (LLVM_UNLIKELY(cr == ExecutionStatus::EXCEPTION))', '          return false;', '', '        valueHandle = std::move(*cr);'], 'added_lines': ['  // We cannot use the fast path if the object is a proxy, host object, or when', '  // there could potentially be an accessor defined on the object. This is', '  // because in order to use JSObject::forEachOwnPropertyWhile, we must not', '  // modify the underlying property map or hidden class. However, if we have an', '  // accessor, we cannot guarantee that condition, so we use the slow path.', '  if (source->isProxyObject() || source->isHostObject() ||', '      source->getClass(runtime)->getMayHaveAccessor()) {', '        SmallHermesValue shv =', '            JSObject::getNamedSlotValueUnsafe(*source, runtime, desc);', '        valueHandle = runtime.makeHandle(shv.unboxToHV(runtime));']}
description: An error in Hermes' algorithm for copying objects properties prior to commit a00d237346894c6067a594983be6634f4168c9ad could be used by a malicious attacker to execute arbitrary code via type confusion. Note that this is only exploitable in cases where Hermes is used to execute untrusted JavaScript. Hence, most React Native applications are not affected.

code_evidence: The pre-patch code only diverts to the slow path for proxy sources; objects with accessors (getters) still enter the fast path below.
The fast path uses JSObject::forEachOwnPropertyWhile, whose callback contract forbids modifying the property map or hidden class during iteration.

Inside the named-property callback, getNamedPropertyValue_RJS invokes the getter, which can execute arbitrary JS and mutate the source's HiddenClass while forEachOwnPropertyWhile is still iterating, invalidating the descriptor/iteration state.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The vulnerability is that the object is iterated/accessed under one assumed HiddenClass/type while a getter reconfigures it to an incompatible layout, matching CWE-843's access of a resource using an incompatible type. The diff's slow-path guard and switch to getNamedSlotValueUnsafe confirm the fast path relied on a type/layout invariant that accessors violate.

source,
runtime,
[&source,
&target,
&excludedItems,
&nameHandle,
&valueHandle,
&tmpSymbolStorage](
Runtime &runtime, uint32_t index, ComputedPropertyDescriptor desc) {

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the fast-path iteration assumes an immutable property map, but the callback can run a getter that mutates the object's HiddenClass. Trigger: a source object with an accessor passed to copyDataProperties. The iterator then continues over stale descriptor state, treating the mutated object per an incompatible layout, which can yield type confusion and, per the description, attacker-controlled code execution.

commit_msg:
Fix heap-buffer-overflows when accessing pool

Constants are usually retrieved from the constant pool without verifying
that the pool actually contains them, which may lead to various heap
buffer overflow issues.

In this patch we add a counter keeping track of how many elements the pool
contains, and checks making sure that whenever the pool is accessed, the
constant in present in the pool (constant position < pool counter).

Also, do not return "" when a pointer is excepted (it should be legal to free
this return value).

This patch fixes #112 (CVE-2018-7875), fixes #120 (CVE-2018-7871),
fixes #117 (CVE-2018-7870), fixes #114 (CVE-2018-7872), fixes #122,
fixes #113 (CVE-2018-7868), fixes #123.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tpoolcounter = sact->Count;']}
description: There is a heap-based buffer over-read in the getName function of util/decompile.c in libming 0.4.8 for CONSTANT8 data. A Crafted input will lead to a denial of service attack.

code_evidence: The function assigns the constant pool pointer from sact->ConstantPool into the global pool variable, and the patch adds poolcounter = sact->Count. Nothing here bounds subsequent indexing of pool by constant positions; the pool is captured without validating that any later-accessed constant index is less than Count.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe behavior is reading a memory buffer outside its intended boundary, which is the core of CWE-119. This function supplies the pool/count used by such accesses; the missing bounds constraint is the buffer-boundary violation rather than a separate logic error.

pool=sact->ConstantPool;
}

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the decompiler stores the pool pointer and count but does not itself enforce that constant indices used when reading pool entries are within Count. Trigger: a crafted SWF with a constant-pool reference index exceeding the number of entries. Consequence: out-of-bounds read of heap memory (heap-buffer-overflow/over-read), leading to crash or information disclosure.

commit_msg:
mp4: limit the recursion depth for boxes

Although the dissection of each box header consumes a couple of bytes,
it turned out that it's still possible to crash wireshark with a sample
file that contains a large number of nested boxes. The stack will fill
up before we reach the end of the data bytes.

Keep track of the recursion depth as we walk through the hierarchy of
boxes. Abort if we reach the (locally defined) upper limit.

Bug: 13777
Change-Id: I0f67245a5c74131f10d0f9d99b39ad31711b9775
Reviewed-on: https://code.wireshark.org/review/26167
Reviewed-by: Martin Kaiser <wireshark@kaiser.cx>
Petri-Dish: Martin Kaiser <wireshark@kaiser.cx>
Tested-by: Petri Dish Buildbot
Reviewed-by: Anders Broman <a.broman58@gmail.com>
(cherry picked from commit 620f69a74b18908e3424920c7bb01cb5e4cbd8b1)
Reviewed-on: https://code.wireshark.org/review/26204
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        ret = dissect_mp4_box(BOX_TYPE_NONE, tvb, offset, pinfo, mp4_tree);'], 'added_lines': ['        ret = dissect_mp4_box(BOX_TYPE_NONE, 0, tvb, offset, pinfo, mp4_tree);']}
description: In Wireshark 2.4.0 to 2.4.5 and 2.2.0 to 2.2.13, the MP4 dissector could crash. This was addressed in epan/dissectors/file-mp4.c by restricting the box recursion depth.

code_evidence: The while loop iterates over all remaining bytes and calls dissect_mp4_box for each box starting at the current offset. The return value ret controls advancement via offset += ret; the only guard is ret <= 0, which breaks the loop. There is no bound on nesting depth or total box count passed into the recursive dissector, so attacker-controlled box structure drives unbounded recursion.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function processes untrusted file structure without validating a required property (nesting depth/count) before recursive processing, matching improper input validation (CWE-20). A more specific resource-exhaustion label could apply, but the target is CWE-20 and the missing constraint is a validation gap on input-derived structure.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the top-level box walker invokes the recursive box dissector without any depth or count limit. Trigger: a crafted MP4 file containing a large number of nested boxes causes dissect_mp4_box to recurse for each nested header. Supported consequence: stack exhaustion leading to a crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
Since resplen and respoffs are signed integers sufficiently
large values of unsigned int len and offset members of RNDIS
response will result in negative values of prior variables.
This may be utilized to bypass implemented security checks
to either extract memory contents by manipulating offset or
overflow the data buffer via memcpy by manipulating both
offset and len.

Additionally assure that sum of resplen and respoffs does not
overflow so buffer boundaries are kept.

Fixes: 80f8c5b434f9 ("rndis_wlan: copy only useful data from rndis_command respond")
Signed-off-by: Szymon Heidrich <szymon.heidrich@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Alexander Duyck <alexanderduyck@fb.com>
Signed-off-by: Kalle Valo <kvalo@kernel.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20230111175031.7049-1-szymon.heidrich@gmail.com
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tint ret, buflen;', '\tint resplen, respoffs, copylen;', '\t\t\tnetdev_dbg(dev->net, "%s(%s): received invalid "', '\t\t\t\t"data offset: %d > %d\\n", __func__,', '\t\t\t\toid_to_string(oid), respoffs, buflen);', '\t\tif ((resplen + respoffs) > buflen) {', '\t\t\t/* Device would have returned more data if buffer would', '\t\t\t * have been big enough. Copy just the bits that we got.', '\t\t\t */', '\t\t\tcopylen = buflen - respoffs;', '\t\t} else {', '\t\t\tcopylen = resplen;', '\t\t}'], 'added_lines': ['\tint ret;', '\tsize_t buflen, resplen, respoffs, copylen;', '\t\t\tnetdev_dbg(dev->net,', '\t\t\t\t   "%s(%s): received invalid data offset: %zu > %zu\\n",', '\t\t\t\t   __func__, oid_to_string(oid), respoffs, buflen);', '\t\tcopylen = min(resplen, buflen - respoffs);']}
description: In rndis_query_oid in drivers/net/wireless/rndis_wlan.c in the Linux kernel through 6.1.5, there is an integer overflow in an addition.

code_evidence: resplen, respoffs, and copylen are declared as signed int, while buflen is also int derived from *len plus sizeof(*u.get).
resplen and respoffs are read from device-controlled le32 fields (u.get_c->len and u.get_c->offset + 8) and stored into signed ints, so large unsigned values become negative.
The check (resplen + respoffs) > buflen performs signed addition; a negative respoffs or resplen can make the sum small or negative, bypassing the boundary check and selecting copylen = resplen.
copylen is only clamped to *len, then used as the size argument to memcpy from u.buf + respoffs, where respoffs may be negative and copylen may exceed the actual buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The signed addition resplen + respoffs can wrap to a small or negative value, and the subsequent logic assumes the sum reflects the true size, exactly matching CWE-190. This is distinct from a simple missing bounds check: the boundary comparison itself is defeated by the integer wraparound, and the wrapped value feeds the memcpy length/offset computation.

evidence_lines.code:
int ret, buflen;
int resplen, respoffs, copylen;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: device-supplied 32-bit len/offset values are stored in signed int and summed without overflow/negative checks. Trigger: a response with large offset or len yields negative respoffs/resplen, so the (resplen + respoffs) > buflen guard is bypassed. Consequence: memcpy with attacker-influenced negative offset and oversized copylen reads out of bounds or overflows the destination buffer, enabling memory disclosure or corruption.

commit_msg:
No upstream commit exists.

This imports the io_uring codebase from 5.15.85, wholesale. Changes

commit_msg:
guest_physmap_remove_page() needs its return value checked

Callers, namely such subsequently freeing the page, must not blindly
assume success - the function may namely fail when needing to shatter a
super page, but there not being memory available for the then needed
intermediate page table.

As it happens, guest_remove_page() callers now also all check the
return value.

Furthermore a missed put_gfn() on an error path in gnttab_transfer() is
also being taken care of.

This is part of XSA-222.

Reported-by: Julien Grall <julien.grall@arm.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Signed-off-by: Julien Grall <julien.grall@arm.com>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Cooper <andrew.cooper3@citrix.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    guest_physmap_remove_page(d, _gfn(gfn), _mfn(mfn), PAGE_ORDER_4K);'], 'added_lines': ['', '    ret = guest_physmap_remove_page(d, _gfn(gfn), _mfn(mfn), PAGE_ORDER_4K);', '    if ( ret )', '    {', '        printk(XENLOG_G_ERR "Failed to remove Dom%d\'s shared_info frame %lx\\n",', '               d->domain_id, gfn);', '        free_domheap_page(new_page);', '        goto exit_put_gfn;', '    }']}
description: Xen through 4.8.x does not validate memory allocations during certain P2M operations, which allows guest OS users to obtain privileged host OS access, aka XSA-222.

code_evidence: new_page is allocated and checked for NULL (lines 38-45), and guest_physmap_add_page's return is validated (lines 47-54). However, the result of guest_physmap_remove_page at line 46 is discarded; the function proceeds to add the replacement page regardless of whether removal succeeded, and the caller cannot learn that the P2M update failed.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function fails to validate the outcome of a critical operation before continuing, matching CWE-20's failure to check that required preconditions/inputs hold before safe processing. It is not a memory-safety defect like CWE-416; the flaw is the missing validation of an operation's result.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the return value of guest_physmap_remove_page is not checked, so a failure (e.g., allocation failure while shattering a super page) goes unnoticed. Trigger: a P2M operation that fails internally during the reset. Consequence: the caller assumes the shared_info frame was removed and proceeds to add the new page, leaving inconsistent P2M state that can enable privileged host access.

commit_msg:
x86/hvm/ioreq: fix page referencing

The code does not take a page reference in hvm_alloc_ioreq_mfn(), only a
type reference. This can lead to a situation where a malicious domain with
XSM_DM_PRIV can engineer a sequence as follows:

- create IOREQ server: no pages as yet.
- acquire resource: page allocated, total 0.
- decrease reservation: -1 ref, total -1.

This will cause Xen to hit a BUG_ON() in free_domheap_pages().

This patch fixes the issue by changing the call to get_page_type() in
hvm_alloc_ioreq_mfn() to a call to get_page_and_type(). This change
in turn requires an extra put_page() in hvm_free_ioreq_mfn() in the case
that _PGC_allocated is still set (i.e. a decrease reservation has not
occurred) to avoid the page being leaked.

This is part of XSA-276.

Reported-by: Julien Grall <julien.grall@arm.com>
Signed-off-by: Paul Durrant <paul.durrant@citrix.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    iorp->page = alloc_domheap_page(s->emulator, MEMF_no_refcount);', '    if ( !iorp->page )', '    if ( !get_page_type(iorp->page, PGT_writable_page) )', '        goto fail1;', '    iorp->va = __map_domain_page_global(iorp->page);', '        goto fail2;', ' fail2:', '    put_page_type(iorp->page);', '', ' fail1:', '    put_page(iorp->page);', '    iorp->page = NULL;'], 'added_lines': ['    struct page_info *page;', '    page = alloc_domheap_page(s->emulator, MEMF_no_refcount);', '    if ( !page )', '    if ( !get_page_and_type(page, s->emulator, PGT_writable_page) )', '    {', '        /*', "         * The domain can't possibly know about this page yet, so failure", '         * here is a clear indication of something fishy going on.', '         */', '        domain_crash(s->emulator);', '        return -ENODATA;', '    }', '    iorp->va = __map_domain_page_global(page);', '        goto fail;', '    iorp->page = page;', ' fail:', '    if ( test_and_clear_bit(_PGC_allocated, &page->count_info) )', '        put_page(page);', '    put_page_and_type(page);']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen 4.11 allowing HVM guest OS users to cause a denial of service (host OS crash) or possibly gain host OS privileges because x86 IOREQ server resource accounting (for external emulators) was mishandled.

code_evidence: The page is allocated with MEMF_no_refcount, so its refcount is not incremented, and only get_page_type() is called, which takes a type reference but no ordinary page reference.

On the mapping failure path, fail2/fail1 only drop the type reference via put_page_type() and then put_page(); with the missing page reference, the page can be freed while accounting still shows it in use.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The reachable BUG_ON()/assertion in the allocator is triggered by the attacker-controlled resource-accounting sequence, producing a host denial of service, which matches CWE-617 (Reachable Assertion). The underlying refcount mishandling is the cause; the supported consequence is the reachable assertion crash.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: hvm_alloc_ioreq_mfn() allocates with MEMF_no_refcount but acquires only a type reference, leaving the page reference count unaccounted. A domain with XSM_DM_PRIV can drive the reservation accounting negative, so the page is freed with inconsistent refcounts and Xen reaches BUG_ON() in free_domheap_pages(), causing a host crash (and potentially privilege escalation).

commit_msg:
Fix a bug in transient object property assignment and getUTF16Ref

Summary:
The returned `UTF16Ref` from `StringView::getUTF16Ref` can be invalidated by
appending more contents to the same allocator.
This case was encountered in `transientObjectPutErrorMessage`, resulting in
using free'd memory.

Reviewed By: tmikov

Differential Revision: D23034855

fbshipit-source-id: 4c25a5369934bf3bdfc5582385503f4b87de3792
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  SmallU16String<32> tmp;', '      baseTypeAsString.getUTF16Ref(tmp) + " \'" +', '      valueAsStringPrintable.getUTF16Ref(tmp) + "\'");'], 'added_lines': ['  SmallU16String<32> tmp1;', '  SmallU16String<32> tmp2;', '      baseTypeAsString.getUTF16Ref(tmp1) + " \'" +', '      valueAsStringPrintable.getUTF16Ref(tmp2) + "\'");']}
description: A use after free in hermes, while emitting certain error messages, prior to commit d86e185e485b6330216dee8e854455c694e3a36e allows attackers to potentially execute arbitrary code via crafted JavaScript. Note that this is only exploitable if the application using Hermes permits evaluation of untrusted JavaScript. Hence, most React Native applications are not affected.

code_evidence: A single SmallU16String<32> tmp buffer is declared and passed to getUTF16Ref for both baseTypeAsString and valueAsStringPrintable within the same TwineChar16 expression. The first getUTF16Ref(tmp) may append/copy into tmp, and the second getUTF16Ref(tmp) call can reallocate or mutate tmp, invalidating the UTF16Ref returned by the first call while the Twine still references it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function retains a reference (UTF16Ref) into a buffer that is subsequently invalidated by a second operation on the same buffer before use, matching CWE-416 use after free rather than a simple buffer overflow.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: two UTF16Ref views share one transient buffer tmp, so the second conversion can reallocate/free tmp's storage while the first view is still used in the concatenated error message. Trigger: raising this TypeError with operands requiring dynamic UTF-16 conversion. Consequence: the Twine reads freed memory, a use-after-free that can crash or, per the report, potentially enable code execution.

commit_msg:
gvariant: Don’t allow child elements to overlap with each other

If different elements of a variable sized array can overlap with each
other then we can cause a `GVariant` to normalise to a much larger type.

This commit changes the behaviour of `GVariant` with non-normal form data. If
an invalid frame offset is found all subsequent elements are given their
default value.

When retrieving an element at index `n` we scan the frame offsets up to index
`n` and if they are not in order we return an element with the default value
for that type.  This guarantees that elements don't overlap with each
other.  We remember the offset we've scanned up to so we don't need to
repeat this work on subsequent accesses.  We skip these checks for trusted
data.

Unfortunately this makes random access of untrusted data O(n) — at least
on first access.  It doesn't affect the algorithmic complexity of accessing
elements in order, such as when using the `GVariantIter` interface.  Also:
the cost of validation will be amortised as the `GVariant` instance is
continued to be used.

I've implemented this with 4 different functions, 1 for each element size,
rather than looping calling `gvs_read_unaligned_le` in the hope that the
compiler will find it easy to optimise and should produce fairly tight
code.

Fixes: #2121
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['      value->contents.serialised.ordered_offsets_up_to = G_MAXSIZE;']}
description: A flaw was found in GLib. GVariant deserialization is vulnerable to an exponential blowup issue where a crafted GVariant can cause excessive processing, leading to denial of service.

code_evidence: When the variant is not yet serialised, g_variant_ensure_serialised allocates a buffer sized by value->size (line 10), serialises children into it (line 11), then wraps the buffer via g_bytes_new_take and stores the resulting data pointer (lines 13-15). The patch adds initialization of ordered_offsets_up_to to G_MAXSIZE for this freshly serialised representation, marking the frame offsets as already trusted/ordered.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function finalises deserialised GVariant data and the fix concerns validating untrusted serialised input; missing validation of child-element offsets during deserialisation matches CWE-502. It is not merely a bounds bug: the weakness is trusting malformed deserialised structure, causing resource-consumption DoS.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the serialised representation is constructed from a GVariant whose child elements may overlap (non-normal form), and the code marks offsets as fully ordered (G_MAXSIZE) without validating frame-offset ordering. Trigger: deserialising crafted untrusted GVariant data with overlapping variable-sized array elements. Consequence: subsequent element access trusts the ordering, allowing normalisation to a much larger type and excessive processing (CPU/resource exhaustion).

commit_msg: capture: properly validate WS packet payload size #438
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    // Check we have payload', '    if (size_payload == 0)'], 'added_lines': ['    // Check we have enough payload (base)', '    if (size_payload == 0 || size_payload <= 2)', '    // Check we have enough payload (base + extended payload headers)', '    if ((int32_t) size_payload - ws_off <= 0) {', '        return 0;', '    }', '', '        // Check we have enough payload (base + extended payload headers + mask)', '        if ((int32_t) size_payload - ws_off - 4 <= 0) {', '            return 0;', '        }']}
description: Sngrep v1.6.0 was discovered to contain a heap buffer overflow via the function capture_ws_check_packet at /src/capture.c.

code_evidence: Only size_payload == 0 is rejected, so a one-byte payload passes; line 20 then reads *(payload + ws_off) with ws_off already 1, reading one byte past the payload buffer.
The length switch advances ws_off by 2 or 8 based on ws_len without verifying that size_payload actually contains those extended length bytes.
The masking key is copied from payload + ws_off for 4 bytes with no check that ws_off + 4 stays within size_payload.

size_payload is reduced by ws_off, but this is uint32_t; if ws_off exceeds size_payload the subtraction underflows to a huge value, making the cast check at line 38 unreliable before sng_malloc/memcpy at 40-41.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked offsets let memcpy at line 41 and the mask-key copy at line 34 write/read past the intended payload region, matching CWE-787 out-of-bounds write. The fix's added size checks confirm the missing constraint; this is a bounds bug, not merely an integer sign issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is missing bounds validation of ws_off against the actual payload size before indexed reads and memcpy. A malformed WebSocket frame with a short payload plus extended length or mask bits drives ws_off beyond size_payload, causing out-of-bounds reads and, via unsigned underflow at line 37, an oversized allocation/copy path.

Fixes trac issue #8718.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    if (output_operand->length <= 0)', '        return -1;']}
description: Buffer Overflow vulnerability in FFMpeg 4.2.3 in dnn_execute_layer_pad in libavfilter/dnn/dnn_backend_native_layer_pad.c due to a call to memcpy without length checks, which could let a remote malicious user execute arbitrary code.

code_evidence: new_channels, output_linesize, by_linesize and x_linesize are computed from attacker-influenced dims and block_size with no validation; block_size can be zero or produce inconsistent sizes.

output_operand->length is computed at line 24 and used directly in av_realloc at line 25 without a positive/lower-bound check; the loop at line 34 then writes output[by*by_linesize + x*x_linesize + bx*new_channels + ch] based on these derived strides, which need not match the allocated length.

description: In rw_i93_send_to_upper of rw_i93.cc, there is a possible out of bounds write due to an integer overflow. This could lead to local escalation of privilege with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

code_evidence: Line 3 derives length as uint16_t from p_resp->len; line 19 decrements it by one after consuming the flags byte. For the multi-block read/security cases reaching line 48, line 49 computes (uint16_t)(length + NFC_HDR_SIZE) as the GKI_getbuf allocation size. If length is large enough that length + NFC_HDR_SIZE exceeds UINT16_MAX, the uint16_t cast wraps to a small value, allocating a small buffer. Lines 51-53 then set p_buff->len = length and memcpy length bytes into (p_buff + 1), writing far past the undersized allocation.

This is an integer overflow directly driving an out-of-bounds write, not merely a bounds-check omission.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the allocation size at line 49 is computed with a 16-bit addition that can wrap, while the copy length at line 53 uses the unwrapped length. Trigger: a response whose length is near UINT16_MAX reaching the multi-block cases. Consequence: heap out-of-bounds write of attacker-influenced length, enabling memory corruption and potential local privilege escalation.

joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The vulnerable operation is a read from smp.pSample8 beyond its allocated length, matching CWE-125 (out-of-bounds read). The additive checks that should constrain the read are overflow-prone, so the missing constraint directly enables the out-of-range read rather than a write or type confusion.

evidence_lines.code:
if((newSmp.nLength + info.loopLength > MAX_SAMPLE_LENGTH) ||
(info.loopLength > MAX_SAMPLE_LENGTH) ||
(info.loopStart + info.loopLength > smp.nLength))

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is the overflow-prone additive validation of loopStart and loopLength, which fails to ensure loopStart is within smp.nLength and that loopStart+loopLength stays inside the source buffer. A malformed STP file supplying large loopStart/loopLength values bypasses the check, and the subsequent memcpy reads past the sample buffer, causing an out-of-bounds read.

commit_msg: Don't crash if s > size.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            assert(s <= size);', '            if (len < s) len = s;', '            i->copy(buf.pData_ + i->tag()*2, byteOrder);'], 'added_lines': ['            if (s <= size) {', '                if (len < s) len = s;', '                i->copy(buf.pData_ + i->tag()*2, byteOrder);', '            }']}
description: Exiv2 is a command-line utility and C++ library for reading, writing, deleting, and modifying the metadata of image files. The assertion failure is triggered when Exiv2 is used to modify the metadata of a crafted image file. An attacker could potentially exploit the vulnerability to cause a denial of service, if they can trick the victim into running Exiv2 on a crafted image file. Note that this bug is only triggered when modifying the metadata, which is a less frequently used Exiv2 operation than reading the metadata. For example, to trigger the bug in the Exiv2 command-line application, you need to add an extra command-line argument such as `fi`. ### Patches The bug is fixed in version v0.27.5. ### References Regression test and bug fix: #1739 ### For more information Please see our [security policy](https://github.com/Exiv2/exiv2/security/policy) for information about Exiv2 security.

code_evidence: Line 13 computes s from attacker-controlled tag and size values. Line 14 asserts s <= size, where size is the fixed 1024-byte buffer.
Lines 15-16 then use s to set len and copy into buf.pData_ + i->tag()*2, so the bounds check exists only as an assertion.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function relies on assert(s <= size) to enforce a buffer bound that attacker-controlled metadata can violate, producing an abort/DoS. This matches CWE-617 (Reachable Assertion); the missing runtime check is the root cause, and the crash is the consequence.

evidence_lines.code:
const uint16_t s = i->tag()*2 + static_cast<uint16_t>(i->size());
assert(s <= size);

if (len < s) len = s;
i->copy(buf.pData_ + i->tag()*2, byteOrder);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: A crafted image yields an Exif entry whose tag*2 + size exceeds the 1024-byte buffer, so the assert on line 14 fails. In release builds where assert is compiled out, the subsequent copy on line 16 can also overrun the buffer; the patch replaces the assertion with a real s <= size guard.

Improve to cover scale value greater than one

description: TensorFlow is an open source platform for machine learning. Prior to versions 2.9.0, 2.8.1, 2.7.2, and 2.6.4, certain TFLite models that were created using TFLite model converter would crash when loaded in the TFLite interpreter. The culprit is that during quantization the scale of values could be greater than 1 but code was always assuming sub-unit scaling. Thus, since code was calling `QuantizeMultiplierSmallerThanOneExp`, the `TFLITE_CHECK_LT` assertion would trigger and abort the process. Versions 2.9.0, 2.8.1, 2.7.2, and 2.6.4 contain a patch for this issue.

code_evidence: The function passes each input tensor's scale (input1->params.scale / input2->params.scale) directly into QuantizeMultiplierSmallerThanOneExp without checking that the scale is below one; that helper asserts the sub-unit precondition and aborts on larger scales.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function consumes model-supplied scale metadata but fails to validate its required range (scale < 1) before processing, which matches CWE-20 improper input validation. The missing constraint, not merely a logic error, is the cause; the crash is the availability consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the code assumes every tensor scale is smaller than one and never validates that property before choosing the sub-unit quantization routine. Trigger: a TFLite model whose quantization scale exceeds one reaches this comparison kernel. Consequence: the internal TFLITE_CHECK_LT assertion fires and aborts the interpreter process (DoS).

commit_msg:
ARM: dma-mapping: don't allow DMA mappings to be marked executable

DMA mapping permissions were being derived from pgprot_kernel directly
without using PAGE_KERNEL.  This causes them to be marked with executable
permission, which is not what we want.  Fix this.

Signed-off-by: Russell King <rmk+kernel@arm.linux.org.uk>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tpgprot_t prot = __get_dma_pgprot(attrs, pgprot_kernel);'], 'added_lines': ['\tpgprot_t prot = __get_dma_pgprot(attrs, PAGE_KERNEL);']}
description: arch/arm/mm/dma-mapping.c in the Linux kernel before 3.13 on ARM platforms, as used in Android before 2016-08-05 on Nexus 5 and 7 (2013) devices, does not prevent executable DMA mappings, which might allow local users to gain privileges via a crafted application, aka Android internal bug 28803642 and Qualcomm internal bug CR642735.

code_evidence: Line 4 derives the DMA page protection from pgprot_kernel, which carries executable permission bits; this prot value is passed unchanged into __dma_alloc at line 8 and applied to the returned mapping (line 9).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function mishandles a permission attribute (executable bit) when establishing a memory mapping, matching CWE-264's scope of improper management of permissions. The defect is the permission value chosen at line 4, not a memory-corruption bug.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the DMA allocation protection is built from pgprot_kernel rather than PAGE_KERNEL, so executable permission is inherited by the DMA mapping. Trigger: any caller invoking arm_dma_alloc obtains a mapping that is executable. Supported consequence: executable DMA memory weakens the intended non-executable permission constraint on kernel/DMA memory, potentially enabling code execution in that region.

commit_msg:
Fix line wrapping mode 0/3 bugs

This fixes two separate bugs:

a) Don't move a linebreak into the first symbol. This results in a empty
   line at the front, which does not help to equalize line lengths at all.
   Instead, merge line with the second one.
b) When moving a linebreak into a symbol that already is a break, the
   number of lines must be decremented. Otherwise, uninitialized memory
   is possibly used for later layout operations.

Found by fuzzer test case
id:000085,sig:11,src:003377+003350,op:splice,rep:8.

This might also affect and hopefully fix libass#229.

v2: change semantics according to review
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['                        w->linebreak = 1;'], 'added_lines': ['                        if (w->linebreak || w == text_info->glyphs)', '                            text_info->n_lines--;', '                        if (w != text_info->glyphs)', '                            w->linebreak = 1;']}
description: The wrap_lines_smart function in ass_render.c in libass before 0.13.4 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read) via unspecified vectors, related to "0/3 line wrapping equalization."

code_evidence: The equalization loop picks a glyph w inside the current line and sets w->linebreak = 1 and s2->linebreak = 0 without updating text_info->n_lines when w already had a linebreak or w is the first glyph; the while loop at 67-69 can also move w back to s1.

The later layout loop iterates over all glyphs with linebreak set (114) and indexes text_info->lines[cur_line] and [cur_line - 1] (117-122) while incrementing cur_line; if the actual number of linebreak glyphs exceeds the recorded n_lines, cur_line runs past the allocated lines array.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the flaw causes reads past the end of the text_info->lines buffer via cur_line indexing. It is not CWE-787 since no data is written out of bounds; the consequence is an out-of-bounds read.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: moving a linebreak to a glyph that already is a break (or to the first glyph) without decrementing text_info->n_lines leaves the line count inconsistent with the number of linebreak-marked glyphs. Trigger: input causing the DIFF test to succeed on such a glyph. Consequence: the subsequent layout loop indexes text_info->lines beyond n_lines, reading out-of-bounds memory (crash/DoS).

commit_msg: Handle NO response without message properly
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    mutt_error("%s", s + 3);'], 'added_lines': ['    mutt_error("%s", s + 2);']}
description: An issue was discovered in Mutt before 1.10.1 and NeoMutt before 2018-07-16. imap/command.c mishandles a NO response without a message.

code_evidence: The NO branch matches a server response beginning with "NO" via mutt_str_strncasecmp(s, "NO", 2), then passes s + 3 to mutt_error without confirming that a space and message text follow the two-character token. For a bare "NO" response the buffer holds only "NO" plus terminator, so s + 3 points past the string terminator and mutt_error's %s reads beyond the allocated buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function consumes an external IMAP response but fails to validate its required properties (presence of a message after "NO") before deriving an offset into it, matching CWE-20's improper input validation. The defect is a missing well-formedness check rather than a filtering or encoding mistake.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the handler assumes every untagged NO reply is followed by a separator and message, skipping three bytes without validating the reply's length or format. Trigger: a server returns a NO response with no message text. Consequence: the pointer lands past the buffer, and formatting it with %s causes an out-of-bounds read, potentially crashing the client or exposing adjacent memory.

description: There is a heap out of bounds read in radare2 2.6.0 in _6502_op() in libr/anal/p/anal_6502.c via a crafted iNES ROM binary file.

code_evidence: In the conditional-branch case (opcodes 0x10–0xf0), op->type is set to R_ANAL_OP_TYPE_CJMP and then data[1] is dereferenced unconditionally at lines 241–243 to compute the jump target, without any check that len > 1 before reading the second byte.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Reading data[1] without first confirming len > 1 is a direct out-of-bounds read past the intended buffer, matching CWE-125. It is not merely a logic error in jump computation, since the read itself exceeds the buffer bounds.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function receives a caller-supplied instruction buffer of length len and reads data[1] to compute the relative branch target. When a crafted iNES ROM ends with a single-byte branch opcode, len is 1 but data[1] is still read, accessing memory past the end of the buffer; the supported consequence is an out-of-bounds read (crash/info disclosure).

commit_msg:
avformat/mvdec: Fix DoS due to lack of eof check

Fixes: loop.mv

Found-by: Xiaohei and Wangchu from Alibaba Security Team
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['            if (avio_feof(pb))', '                return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;']}
description: In libavformat/mvdec.c in FFmpeg 3.3.3, a DoS in mv_read_header() due to lack of an EOF (End of File) check might cause huge CPU and memory consumption. When a crafted MV file, which claims a large "nb_frames" field in the header but does not contain sufficient backing data, is provided, the loop over the frames would consume huge CPU and memory resources, since there is no EOF check inside the loop.

code_evidence: Line 22 reads attacker-controlled vst->nb_frames from the file; line 41 copies it to ast->nb_frames. The loop at line 61 iterates i from 0 to vst->nb_frames without any EOF/limit check. Each iteration reads pos/asize/vsize (62-64), skips 8 bytes (65) and adds two index entries (66-67), so a large claimed frame count with no backing data drives many iterations.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-834 covers loops whose iteration count is not sufficiently limited; here the unbounded, attacker-influenced nb_frames loop with per-iteration allocations and no EOF guard matches that weakness. The missing EOF check is the mechanism enabling the excessive iteration, not a separate out-of-bounds issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the frame-index loop bound comes directly from the untrusted nb_frames header field and is never validated against available input or a sane maximum. Trigger: a crafted MV file declares a huge nb_frames but supplies little data, so avio_rb32 returns zeros/EOF while the loop keeps running, each pass allocating index entries. Supported consequence: excessive CPU and memory consumption (DoS).

description: When there are multiple ranges in a range request, Apache Traffic Server (ATS) will read the entire object from cache. This can cause performance problems with large objects in cache. This affects versions 6.0.0 to 6.2.2 and 7.0.0 to 7.1.3. Consequence: disproportionate CPU/memory work per request, enabling resource-consumption denial of service.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\tif (f2fs_has_extra_attr(inode) &&', '\t\t\t!f2fs_sb_has_extra_attr(sbi->sb)) {', '\t\tset_sbi_flag(sbi, SBI_NEED_FSCK);', '\t\tf2fs_msg(sbi->sb, KERN_WARNING,', '\t\t\t"%s: inode (ino=%lx) is with extra_attr, "', '\t\t\t"but extra_attr feature is off",', '\t\t\t__func__, inode->i_ino);', '\t\treturn false;', '\t}']}
description: An issue was discovered in fs/f2fs/inode.c in the Linux kernel through 4.17.3. A denial of service (slab out-of-bounds read and BUG) can occur for a modified f2fs filesystem image in which FI_EXTRA_ATTR is set in an inode.

code_evidence: sanity_check_inode reads the inode's extra-attr state via f2fs_has_extra_attr(inode) at line 5 and validates it only against the flexible-inline-xattr superblock feature (line 4). There is no check that f2fs_sb_has_extra_attr(sbi->sb) is set when the inode carries FI_EXTRA_ATTR, so an inconsistent on-disk inode passes validation and returns true at line 12.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked inconsistency lets attacker-controlled metadata drive an address beyond the intended page buffer, producing an out-of-bounds memory read (CWE-125). This is a read overrun rather than a write, so CWE-787 does not apply.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the inode sanity check omits the cross-check between the inode's FI_EXTRA_ATTR bit and the filesystem's extra_attr feature. Trigger: a crafted f2fs image sets FI_EXTRA_ATTR while the extra_attr feature is off, causing i_addr[0] to be misparsed as i_extra_isize and inline data addressing to exceed the page. Consequence: out-of-bounds read during inode/dentry access, leading to a crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
Bluetooth: L2CAP: Fix accepting connection request for invalid SPSM

The Bluetooth spec states that the valid range for SPSM is from
0x0001-0x00ff so it is invalid to accept values outside of this range:

  BLUETOOTH CORE SPECIFICATION Version 5.3 | Vol 3, Part A
  page 1059:
  Table 4.15: L2CAP_LE_CREDIT_BASED_CONNECTION_REQ SPSM ranges

CVE: CVE-2022-42896
CC: stable@vger.kernel.org
Reported-by: Tamás Koczka <poprdi@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Luiz Augusto von Dentz <luiz.von.dentz@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Tedd Ho-Jeong An <tedd.an@intel.com>

description:
There are use-after-free vulnerabilities in the Linux kernel's net/bluetooth/l2cap_core.c's l2cap_connect and l2cap_le_connect_req functions which may allow code execution and leaking kernel memory (respectively) remotely via Bluetooth. A remote attacker could execute code leaking kernel memory via Bluetooth if within proximity of the victim.

We recommend upgrading past commit   https://www.google.com/url  https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/711f8c3fb3db61897080468586b970c87c61d9e4 https://www.google.com/url

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function validates the SPSM range before channel lookup and does not free or reuse freed memory; no use-after-free operation is present in the shown code.

commit_msg: Fix boundary checking error in markup search, that could cause buffer over-read with corrupt input
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ["                if (*(data - 1) == '/' && *data == '>') {"], 'added_lines': ["                if (data <= data_end && *(data - 1) == '/' && *data == '>') {"]}
description: Buffer Over-read in GitHub repository bfabiszewski/libmobi prior to 0.11.

code_evidence: The attribute-value loop at [40] stops when data exceeds data_end, reaches whitespace, hits '>', or fills the buffer; the post-loop check at [43] then unconditionally dereferences *data and *(data-1) without verifying that data still points within [data_start, data_end].
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 covers reading past the end of an intended buffer. Here the missing bound check before dereferencing *data produces exactly such a read; the fix adds a data <= data_end guard, confirming the boundary-check omission as root cause rather than a write overflow or use-after-free.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: When the loop terminates because data advanced past data_end (no terminator found within the buffer), the condition at [43] reads *data one element beyond the intended end. With corrupt or unterminated input, this is an out-of-bounds read of the supplied buffer, potentially disclosing adjacent memory or crashing.

commit_msg:
Make sure binding security checks don't pass if the frame is remote.

Blink assumes that remote frames will always fail the security origin
check. Unfortunately, reality is not that simple. There are several
instances where this assumption fails to hold. For example:

  1. Navigate to a.com.
  2. a.com opens a new window.
  3. Navigate the new window to b.com via the omnibox.
  4. Click a link to c.com in both windows.

Because browser-initiated navigations go cross-process but
renderer-initiated navigations do not [1], the two c.com windows will
end up in different renderer processes.

Both windows have the same origin but see each other as RemoteFrames.
This means that SecurityOrigin's canAccess check will pass… but this
ends up violating many assumptions in Blink that passing the security
check implies a local frame.

[1] https://www.chromium.org/developers/design-documents/process-models#Caveats

BUG=601629
CQ_INCLUDE_TRYBOTS=tryserver.chromium.linux:linux_site_isolation

Review URL: https://codereview.chromium.org/1887553002

Cr-Commit-Position: refs/heads/master@{#387087}
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    ASSERT(!activeOrigin->canAccessCheckSuborigins(targetOrigin));'], 'added_lines': ["    // It's possible for a remote frame to be same origin with respect to a", '    // local frame, but it must still be treated as a disallowed cross-domain', '    // access. See https://crbug.com/601629.', '    ASSERT(frame()->isRemoteFrame() || !activeOrigin->canAccessCheckSuborigins(targetOrigin));']}
description: Blink, as used in Google Chrome before 50.0.2661.94, does not ensure that frames satisfy a check for the same renderer process in addition to a Same Origin Policy check, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory corruption) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted web site, related to BindingSecurity.cpp and DOMWindow.cpp.

code_evidence: The function derives activeOrigin and targetOrigin from the calling and target frames, then asserts that the active origin cannot access the target origin. This assertion embodies the assumption that a passing same-origin check implies a local frame, without any validation of frame locality. The patched assertion shows the missing constraint: a remote frame may be same-origin yet must be treated as disallowed.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-20 fits because the function fails to validate a required property of the frame (its locality/process identity) before trusting the origin check. The missing constraint is an input-validation gap on frame metadata, not an output-encoding issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the code validates only the security-origin relationship and never checks whether the target frame is remote, so a same-origin RemoteFrame passes the access assumption. Trigger: a crafted site where two windows share an origin but reside in different renderer processes. Supported consequence: the violated assumption leads to memory corruption or denial of service.

commit_msg:
commit 95a762e2c8c942780948091f8f2a4f32fce1ac6f upstream.

Distinguish between
BPF_ALU64|BPF_MOV|BPF_K (load 32-bit immediate, sign-extended to 64-bit)
and BPF_ALU|BPF_MOV|BPF_K (load 32-bit immediate, zero-padded to 64-bit);
only perform sign extension in the first case.

This patch differs from the mainline one because the verifier's internals
have changed in the meantime. Mainline tracks register values as 64-bit
values; however, 4.4 still stores tracked register values as 32-bit
values with sign extension. Therefore, in the case of a 32-bit op with
negative immediate, the value can't be tracked; leave the register as
UNKNOWN_VALUE (set by the preceding check_reg_arg() call).


I have manually tested this patch on top of 4.4.122. For the following BPF
bytecode:

        BPF_MOV64_IMM(BPF_REG_1, 1),
        BPF_JMP_IMM(BPF_JEQ, BPF_REG_1, 1, 1),
        BPF_EXIT_INSN(),

        BPF_MOV32_IMM(BPF_REG_1, 1),
        BPF_JMP_IMM(BPF_JEQ, BPF_REG_1, 1, 1),
        BPF_EXIT_INSN(),

        BPF_MOV64_IMM(BPF_REG_1, -1),
        BPF_JMP_IMM(BPF_JEQ, BPF_REG_1, -1, 1),
        BPF_EXIT_INSN(),

        BPF_MOV32_IMM(BPF_REG_1, -1),
        BPF_JMP_IMM(BPF_JEQ, BPF_REG_1, -1, 2),
        BPF_MOV32_IMM(BPF_REG_0, 42),
        BPF_EXIT_INSN(),

        BPF_MOV32_IMM(BPF_REG_0, 43),
        BPF_EXIT_INSN()

Verifier output on 4.4.122 without this patch:

0: (b7) r1 = 1
1: (15) if r1 == 0x1 goto pc+1
3: (b4) (u32) r1 = (u32) 1
4: (15) if r1 == 0x1 goto pc+1
6: (b7) r1 = -1
7: (15) if r1 == 0xffffffff goto pc+1
9: (b4) (u32) r1 = (u32) -1
10: (15) if r1 == 0xffffffff goto pc+2
13: (b4) (u32) r0 = (u32) 43
14: (95) exit

Verifier output on 4.4.122+ with this patch:

0: (b7) r1 = 1
1: (15) if r1 == 0x1 goto pc+1
3: (b4) (u32) r1 = (u32) 1
4: (15) if r1 == 0x1 goto pc+1
6: (b7) r1 = -1
7: (15) if r1 == 0xffffffff goto pc+1
9: (b4) (u32) r1 = (u32) -1
10: (15) if r1 == 0xffffffff goto pc+2
 R1=inv R10=fp
11: (b4) (u32) r0 = (u32) 42
12: (95) exit

from 10 to 13: R1=imm-1 R10=fp
13: (b4) (u32) r0 = (u32) 43
14: (95) exit


Signed-off-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Acked-by: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t} else {'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t} else if (BPF_CLASS(insn->code) == BPF_ALU64 ||', '\t\t\t   insn->imm >= 0) {']}
description: The check_alu_op function in kernel/bpf/verifier.c in the Linux kernel through 4.4 allows local users to cause a denial of service (memory corruption) or possibly have unspecified other impact by leveraging incorrect sign extension.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The MOV-immediate branch (lines 63-66) records an immediate as CONST_IMM without sign-extension handling, but the function contains no memory buffer access, bounds computation, or pointer arithmetic that would demonstrate an out-of-bounds read/write; the mis-tracked register value is a soundness/type-confusion issue, not a directly evidenced CWE-119 memory-boundary operation.
