So have patched up to avoid', "        this, but without any proper idea about what's going on. */", '        if(H>256 && H<768){\t\t/* green correct */']}
description: A buffer overflow vulnerability in mj_color_correct() in contrib/japanese/gdevmjc.c of Artifex Software GhostScript v9.50 allows a remote attacker to cause a denial of service via a crafted PDF file. This is fixed in v9.51.

code_evidence: Lines 32,36,40,46,50,54 compute H by scaling a channel difference with *256/D; for R>G and G>=B, H=(G-B)*256/D with D=R-B, so H stays in [0,256], but other branches can produce H up to ~1024 (e.g. line 40 H=1024+(R-G)*256/D, line 54 H=1024-(G-R)*256/D).

Lines 77-82 guard green correction with H>256 && H<1024 and index grnsep2[H-256] at line 79. Since H can reach up to about 1024, H-256 can reach 768, exceeding the 512-element grnsep2[] and writing/reading out of bounds.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The code uses an unchecked, attacker-influenced index to access a fixed 512-element array, causing an out-of-bounds write/read consistent with a classic buffer overflow (CWE-120). It differs from pure out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) because the index also feeds C/M/Y adjustments that can write past grnsep2's bounds.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the H value derived from input color channels is not bounded to the grnsep2[] table size before indexing. Trigger: a crafted PDF yields color values where H falls in (256,1024) but H-256 >= 512, e.g. H near 1024. The out-of-range grnsep2 access can corrupt memory or crash, supporting denial of service (and potentially memory modification).

commit_msg: RLE check for pixel offset less than 0 (heap overflow report from Craig Young)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    offset,', '          if (offset+((size_t) operand*number_planes) > pixel_info_length)', '          if (offset+((size_t) operand*number_planes) > pixel_info_length)'], 'added_lines': ['    offset,', '          if ((offset < 0) ||', '              (offset+((size_t) operand*number_planes) > pixel_info_length))', '          if ((offset < 0) ||', '              (offset+((size_t) operand*number_planes) > pixel_info_length))']}
description: Heap-based buffer overflow in the ReadRLEImage function in coders/rle.c in ImageMagick 6.9.4-8 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (application crash) or have other unspecified impact via a crafted RLE file.

code_evidence: ByteDataOp computes offset from attacker-influenced y, x, plane and number_planes; only the upper bound offset+operand*number_planes is checked against pixel_info_length, so a negative offset passes and p=pixels+offset points before the buffer, then *p=pixel writes there.
RunDataOp has the identical pattern: offset derived from y/x/plane, upper-bound-only check, then p=pixels+offset and *p=pixel in the write loop.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs a write through a pointer derived from an unchecked offset, accessing memory outside the pixel_info buffer, which matches CWE-119's out-of-bounds memory operations. The missing negative-offset constraint is the underlying cause, distinct from a mere integer overflow.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is a signed size_t offset computed from image coordinates without validating that it is non-negative; the bound check only rejects offsets beyond pixel_info_length. A crafted RLE stream (e.g., large y via SkipLinesOp or large x via SkipPixelsOp) makes offset negative, so p points outside the allocated pixel buffer and the loops write past its start, corrupting heap memory.

commit_msg:
guest_physmap_remove_page() needs its return value checked

Callers, namely such subsequently freeing the page, must not blindly
assume success - the function may namely fail when needing to shatter a
super page, but there not being memory available for the then needed
intermediate page table.

As it happens, guest_remove_page() callers now also all check the
return value.

Furthermore a missed put_gfn() on an error path in gnttab_transfer() is
also being taken care of.

This is part of XSA-222.

Reported-by: Julien Grall <julien.grall@arm.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Signed-off-by: Julien Grall <julien.grall@arm.com>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Cooper <andrew.cooper3@citrix.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            guest_physmap_remove_page(d, _gfn(gfn), _mfn(mfn), 0);'], 'added_lines': ['            if ( guest_physmap_remove_page(d, _gfn(gfn), _mfn(mfn), 0) )', '                domain_crash(d);']}
description: Xen through 4.8.x does not validate memory allocations during certain P2M operations, which allows guest OS users to obtain privileged host OS access, aka XSA-222.

code_evidence: The loop removes each page from in_chunk_list, clears _PGC_allocated, derives gfn via mfn_to_gmfn, and calls guest_physmap_remove_page(d, _gfn(gfn), _mfn(mfn), 0) at line 150 without examining its return value; the following put_page(page) at line 151 then frees the page regardless of whether the P2M removal succeeded.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function fails to validate the outcome (status) of a memory-management operation before acting on the data, matching CWE-20's incorrect validation of required properties. The missing check is the validation defect; the stale mapping is its consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the return status of guest_physmap_remove_page() is ignored, so a failed P2M teardown (e.g. super-page shatter allocation failure) is treated as success. Trigger: a guest invokes XENMEM_exchange such that removal fails; the code then put_page()s a page still mapped in the P2M, leaving a stale mapping whose freed page can be reallocated. Supported consequence: inconsistent P2M state enabling privileged host access.

description: In ImageMagick 7.0.5-5, the ReadEPTImage function in ept.c allows attackers to cause a denial of service (memory leak) via a crafted file.

code_evidence: ept_info.postscript is allocated via AcquireQuantumMemory; on allocation failure for tiff the ThrowReaderException path exits without releasing postscript.
ept_info.tiff is allocated via AcquireQuantumMemory after postscript; both buffers must be freed on later error paths.
When tiff_offset is invalid (offset < 30), ThrowReaderException(CorruptImageError) is thrown without freeing the already-allocated tiff and postscript buffers.
Similarly, when postscript_offset is invalid, ThrowReaderException exits without freeing the allocated buffers, leaking them.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-772 fits because the function allocates resources whose lifetime ends on early exception exits, yet the buffers are not released on those paths. The patch adds RelinquishMagickMemory calls on the error branches, confirming the missing-release root cause rather than a different memory-safety weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: error/exception paths abort the reader before the allocated ept_info.tiff and ept_info.postscript buffers are relinquished. Trigger: a crafted EPT file with a bad tiff_offset or postscript_offset (or a tiff allocation failure) reaches ThrowReaderException. Consequence: the heap buffers are leaked, enabling memory-consumption denial of service across repeated reads.

description: In Eclipse Openj9 to version 0.25.0, usage of the jdk.internal.reflect.ConstantPool API causes the JVM in some cases to pre-resolve certain constant pool entries. This allows a user to call static methods or access static members without running the class initialization method, and may allow a user to observe uninitialized values.

code_evidence: When internalFindClassUTF8 returns NULL, the failure path marks the class reference permanently unresolvable (modifiers = -1) and caches this state in the constant pool even when resolution was requested without CP update/class load semantics.
After successful lookup, the resolved class and access modifiers are written back to ramClassRefWrapper unconditionally, caching a class that may not have been initialized.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The root cause is that a critical resource (the class reference/constant pool entry) is committed to a resolved state without ensuring the class was initialized, matching CWE-909 Missing Initialization of Resource. This is distinct from an access-control flaw; the consequence is observation of uninitialized values and possible DoS.

evidence_lines.code:
ramClassRefWrapper->value = resolvedClass;
ramClassRefWrapper->modifiers = accessModifiers;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The resolveClassRef helper caches resolution results (failure markers and resolved class values) into the shared constant pool entry regardless of whether the caller requested NO_CP_UPDATE or NO_CLASS_LOAD. A caller using the ConstantPool reflection API can therefore trigger pre-resolution of an entry; later static access uses the cached class without running class initialization, so uninitialized static fields may be observed.

commit_msg:
Check that the array index isn't negative. This fixes CVE-2023-43641.

Signed-off-by: Kevin Backhouse <kevinbackhouse@github.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (i > MAXINDEX) {'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (i < 0 || i > MAXINDEX) {']}
description: libcue provides an API for parsing and extracting data from CUE sheets. Versions 2.2.1 and prior are vulnerable to out-of-bounds array access. A user of the GNOME desktop environment can be exploited by downloading a cue sheet from a malicious webpage. Because the file is saved to `~/Downloads`, it is then automatically scanned by tracker-miners. And because it has a .cue filename extension, tracker-miners use libcue to parse the file. The file exploits the vulnerability in libcue to gain code execution. This issue is patched in version 2.3.0.

code_evidence: The guard only rejects i > MAXINDEX, so a negative index i passes the check and reaches the write.
Line 7 writes track->index[i] = ind, indexing the array with the unchecked (possibly negative) i, writing before the start of the buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs a write through an array subscript that can be negative, writing before the intended buffer, which is exactly CWE-787 (out-of-bounds write). This is a write weakness rather than a read, so it is not CWE-125.

evidence_lines.code: track->index[i] = ind;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the bounds check omits the lower bound, so negative i is accepted. Trigger: a caller supplies a negative index (e.g., from a crafted CUE sheet's INDEX value). Consequence: track->index[i] writes out of bounds before the array, corrupting memory and enabling the code-execution described.

description: Clara Genomics Analysis before 0.2.0 has an integer overflow for cudapoa memory management in allocate_block.cpp.

commit_msg:
netfilter: add back stackpointer size checks

The rationale for removing the check is only correct for rulesets
generated by ip(6)tables.

In iptables, a jump can only occur to a user-defined chain, i.e.
because we size the stack based on number of user-defined chains we
cannot exceed stack size.

However, the underlying binary format has no such restriction,
and the validation step only ensures that the jump target is a
valid rule start point.

IOW, its possible to build a rule blob that has no user-defined
chains but does contain a jump.

If this happens, no jump stack gets allocated and crash occurs
because no jumpstack was allocated.

Fixes: 7814b6ec6d0d6 ("netfilter: xtables: don't save/restore jumpstack offset")
Reported-by: syzbot+e783f671527912cd9403@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Signed-off-by: Florian Westphal <fw@strlen.de>
Signed-off-by: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t\tif (unlikely(stackidx >= private->stacksize)) {', '\t\t\t\t\tverdict = NF_DROP;', '\t\t\t\t\tbreak;', '\t\t\t\t}']}
description: The netfilter subsystem in the Linux kernel through 4.15.7 mishandles the case of a rule blob that contains a jump but lacks a user-defined chain, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference) by leveraging the CAP_NET_RAW or CAP_NET_ADMIN capability, related to arpt_do_table in net/ipv4/netfilter/arp_tables.c, ipt_do_table in net/ipv4/netfilter/ip_tables.c, and ip6t_do_table in net/ipv6/netfilter/ip6_tables.c.

code_evidence: Line 27 loads jumpstack from private->jumpstack[cpu]; when the rule blob defines no user-defined chains, no jump stack is allocated for this table, so jumpstack is NULL (or the per-cpu slot is unset). Lines 28-29 only adjust the pointer for tee duplication and do not validate it.
Lines 73-74 detect a jump to a non-sequential target without IP6T_F_GOTO; line 75 then writes jumpstack[stackidx++] without any stacksize or NULL check, dereferencing the unallocated jumpstack.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe write through an unallocated jumpstack pointer is a direct NULL pointer dereference (CWE-476), matching the reported NULL dereference DoS. The missing stacksize bound and the NULL allocation are distinct; the supported weakness is the dereference of the NULL jumpstack, not an out-of-bounds write.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function assumes a jumpstack was allocated whenever a jump target exists, but the binary rule format permits a jump with zero user-defined chains, leaving jumpstack unallocated. Trigger: a crafted rule blob with a jump but no user-defined chain is traversed by ip6t_do_table. Consequence: the write to jumpstack[stackidx++] dereferences a NULL pointer, causing a kernel crash (denial of service).

commit_msg:
evtchn: address races with evtchn_reset()

Neither d->evtchn_port_ops nor max_evtchns(d) may be used in an entirely
lock-less manner, as both may change by a racing evtchn_reset(). In the
common case, at least one of the domain's event lock or the per-channel
lock needs to be held. In the specific case of the inter-domain sending
by evtchn_send() and notify_via_xen_event_channel() holding the other
side's per-channel lock is sufficient, as the channel can't change state
without both per-channel locks held. Without such a channel changing
state, evtchn_reset() can't complete successfully.

Lock-free accesses continue to be permitted for the shim (calling some
otherwise internal event channel functions), as this happens while the
domain is in effectively single-threaded mode. Special care also needs
taking for the shim's marking of in-use ports as ECS_RESERVED (allowing
use of such ports in the shim case is okay because switching into and
hence also out of FIFO mode is impossihble there).

As a side effect, certain operations on Xen bound event channels which
were mistakenly permitted so far (e.g. unmask or poll) will be refused
now.

This is part of XSA-343.

Reported-by: Julien Grall <jgrall@amazon.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Acked-by: Julien Grall <jgrall@amazon.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['static bool_t evtchn_fifo_is_busy(const struct domain *d, evtchn_port_t port)', '    const event_word_t *word = evtchn_fifo_word_from_port(d, port);'], 'added_lines': ['static bool_t evtchn_fifo_is_busy(const struct domain *d,', '                                  const struct evtchn *evtchn)', '    const event_word_t *word = evtchn_fifo_word_from_port(d, evtchn->port);']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.14.x. There are evtchn_reset() race conditions. Uses of EVTCHNOP_reset (potentially by a guest on itself) or XEN_DOMCTL_soft_reset (by itself covered by XSA-77) can lead to the violation of various internal assumptions. This may lead to out of bounds memory accesses or triggering of bug checks. In particular, x86 PV guests may be able to elevate their privilege to that of the host. Host and guest crashes are also possible, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS). Information leaks cannot be ruled out. All Xen versions from 4.5 onwards are vulnerable. Xen versions 4.4 and earlier are not vulnerable.

code_evidence: The function takes only a port number and derives the event word through evtchn_fifo_word_from_port(d, port), then reads the shared FIFO word with guest_test_bit(d, EVTCHN_FIFO_LINKED, word). No event lock or per-channel lock is acquired, so the port-to-word mapping and the LINKED bit are read without synchronization against a concurrent evtchn_reset().
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-362 fits because the function accesses a shared resource (the event channel FIFO word) without the required exclusive access, creating a timing window for a concurrent reset to interfere. The patch passes the evtchn pointer and relies on callers holding locking, confirming the missing synchronization is the weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: evtchn_fifo_is_busy() performs an unsynchronized lookup and bit test on the port's FIFO word, while evtchn_reset() can concurrently change the port/channel state. Trigger: a racing reset changes or frees the channel while this function reads the derived word. Consequence: a stale or invalid word is examined, violating internal assumptions and leading to out-of-bounds accesses or bug checks (host/guest crash, possible privilege escalation).

commit_msg:
smacker: add sanity check for length in smacker_decode_tree()

Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michaelni@gmx.at>

Bug-Id: 1098
Cc: libav-stable@libav.org
Signed-off-by: Sean McGovern <gseanmcg@gmail.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    if (length > SMKTREE_DECODE_MAX_RECURSION) {', '        av_log(NULL, AV_LOG_ERROR, "Maximum tree recursion level exceeded.\\n");', '        return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;', '    }', '']}
description: In Libav through 11.11 and 12.x through 12.1, the smacker_decode_tree function in libavcodec/smacker.c does not properly restrict tree recursion, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (bitstream.c:build_table() out-of-bounds read and application crash) via a crafted Smacker stream.

code_evidence: The else branch increments length and recurses into smacker_decode_tree twice (lines 22 and 25) without any bound on length. The function's own parameter length is the recursion depth, which is also stored as hc->lengths[hc->current] and used to compute prefix bit shifts; unbounded growth lets crafted bitstreams drive depth arbitrarily deep.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The consequence is an out-of-bounds memory read caused by an unconstrained buffer index derived from unbounded recursion, matching CWE-119's scope of reading outside a buffer's intended boundary. CWE-674 (uncontrolled recursion) describes the root cause, but the target here is the out-of-bounds memory operation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: missing recursion-depth constraint on the tree builder, so a crafted Smacker stream produces an excessively deep Huffman tree. The resulting lengths overflow the intended table bounds used later by build_table(), triggering an out-of-bounds read and crash.

commit_msg:
ipv4: fix a race in ip4_datagram_release_cb()

Alexey gave a AddressSanitizer[1] report that finally gave a good hint
at where was the origin of various problems already reported by Dormando
in the past [2]

Problem comes from the fact that UDP can have a lockless TX path, and
concurrent threads can manipulate sk_dst_cache, while another thread,
is holding socket lock and calls __sk_dst_set() in
ip4_datagram_release_cb() (this was added in linux-3.8)

It seems that all we need to do is to use sk_dst_check() and
sk_dst_set() so that all the writers hold same spinlock
(sk->sk_dst_lock) to prevent corruptions.

TCP stack do not need this protection, as all sk_dst_cache writers hold
the socket lock.

https://code.google.com/p/address-sanitizer/wiki/AddressSanitizerForKernel

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (! __sk_dst_get(sk) || __sk_dst_check(sk, 0))', '', '\trcu_read_lock();', '\tif (!IS_ERR(rt))', '\t\t__sk_dst_set(sk, &rt->dst);'], 'added_lines': ['\tstruct dst_entry *dst;', '\trcu_read_lock();', '', '\tdst = __sk_dst_get(sk);', '\tif (!dst || !dst->obsolete || dst->ops->check(dst, 0)) {', '\t\trcu_read_unlock();', '\t}', '', '\tdst = !IS_ERR(rt) ? &rt->dst : NULL;', '\tsk_dst_set(sk, dst);', '']}
description: Race condition in the ip4_datagram_release_cb function in net/ipv4/datagram.c in the Linux kernel before 3.15.2 allows local users to gain privileges or cause a denial of service (use-after-free) by leveraging incorrect expectations about locking during multithreaded access to internal data structures for IPv4 UDP sockets.

code_evidence: Lines 8-9 read the cached destination via __sk_dst_get()/__sk_dst_check() and return early without taking sk->sk_dst_lock, so the existence check is not synchronized with concurrent writers.

Line 10 only takes the RCU read lock, and lines 18-19 publish the new route with __sk_dst_set(), the lockless variant, instead of sk_dst_set() which acquires sk->sk_dst_lock. Concurrent lockless UDP TX writers can therefore free/replace the same sk_dst_cache entry between the check and the set.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs a check-then-act on a shared resource (sk_dst_cache) without holding the same lock as concurrent writers, exactly a race condition violating exclusivity/atomicity. The use-after-free is the consequence, not the root cause; CWE-362 fits the improper synchronization.

evidence_lines.code:
if (! __sk_dst_get(sk) || __sk_dst_check(sk, 0))
return;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The release callback tests and replaces sk_dst_cache using the lockless __sk_dst_get/__sk_dst_set helpers, while the UDP lockless TX path concurrently modifies the same field under sk_dst_lock. The check-then-set sequence is non-atomic, so another thread can free the cached dst after the check, and the subsequent routing/set operates on a freed dst, causing use-after-free and DoS or privilege escalation.

commit_msg:
Fix heap-buffer-overflows when accessing pool

Constants are usually retrieved from the constant pool without verifying
that the pool actually contains them, which may lead to various heap
buffer overflow issues.

In this patch we add a counter keeping track of how many elements the pool
contains, and checks making sure that whenever the pool is accessed, the
constant in present in the pool (constant position < pool counter).

Also, do not return "" when a pointer is excepted (it should be legal to free
this return value).

This patch fixes #112 (CVE-2018-7875), fixes #120 (CVE-2018-7871),
fixes #117 (CVE-2018-7870), fixes #114 (CVE-2018-7872), fixes #122,
fixes #113 (CVE-2018-7868), fixes #123.

description: A vulnerability has been found in MZ Automation libiec61850 up to 1.4 and classified as critical. This vulnerability affects unknown code of the file src/mms/iso_mms/client/mms_client_files.c of the component MMS File Services. The manipulation of the argument filename leads to path traversal. Upgrading to version 1.5 is able to address this issue. The name of the patch is 10622ba36bb3910c151348f1569f039ecdd8786f. It is recommended to upgrade the affected component. The identifier of this vulnerability is VDB-213556.

code_evidence: The function declares a fixed 256-byte filename buffer and fills it via mmsMsg_parseFileName from attacker-supplied PDU bytes (tag 0xa0), setting hasFileName without any traversal validation.

Once hasFileName is true, the filename is passed directly to the configured fileAccessHandler and then to openFile under the filesystem base path; no check rejects '..' or absolute path elements before the file is opened.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-22 fits because external input builds a pathname intended to stay beneath the base directory, but special elements are not neutralized, permitting escape. This is path traversal rather than mere missing authorization.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: remotely supplied filename is used to construct a path under the server base directory without neutralizing traversal sequences. Trigger: a client sends an MMS file-open request whose filename contains '../' or an absolute path. Consequence: openFile resolves outside the restricted directory, allowing read/access of unintended files.

description: mediaserver in Android 6.x before 2016-03-01 allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code or cause a denial of service (memory corruption) via a crafted media file, related to decoder/ih264d_parse_islice.c and decoder/ih264d_parse_pslice.c, aka internal bug 25928803.

code_evidence: In the CABAC inter-slice loop each parsed macroblock increments u1_num_mbs and previously u2_total_mbs_coded per MB [159,160]; the patch relocates the total count so it is updated only by the transfer amount u1_num_mbs when the group is flushed [193,194].
u1_num_mbs is reset to 0 on u1_tfr_n_mb and u1_mb_idx is re-synchronized [193,194,195,196], so the count of coded MBs must track transferred groups rather than individual increments.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness concerns operations on a memory buffer whose intended boundary is mis-tracked, matching CWE-119. The per-MB versus per-group count mismatch is the cause, and out-of-bounds memory access is the supported consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the running total u2_total_mbs_coded was advanced per macroblock while the transfer/group boundaries reset u1_num_mbs, desynchronizing the reported count from the actual buffer progress. Trigger: crafted slice data driving group transfers; consequence is an inconsistent MB count that can lead to out-of-bounds buffer access/memory corruption during decoding.

not bounds checked, causing a potential OOB write.

Check these functions against bounds of the destination array.

Bug: 275895309

Tag: #security
Ignore-AOSP-First: Security
(cherry picked from https://googleplex-android-review.googlesource.com/q/commit:46803ae95d63ee133eae83d885e7c051964dc8ed)

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  for (; i <= length / sampleSize; i++) {'], 'added_lines': ['  for (; i < std::min(trackHolder->bufferLength, length / sampleSize); i++) {']}
description: In transcodeQ*ToFloat of btif_avrcp_audio_track.cc, there is a possible out of bounds write due to a missing bounds check. This could lead to paired device escalation of privilege with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

code_evidence: Loop bound uses i <= length / sampleSize, so the final iteration runs with i == length/sampleSize; offset = i * sampleSize then reaches length, and the read at buffer + offset - 1 is the last in-bounds read.

That same final iteration writes trackHolder->buffer[i] at index length/sampleSize, which can equal or exceed the destination array's capacity; the loop is not constrained by trackHolder->bufferLength.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe store trackHolder->buffer[i] writes beyond the destination buffer because the index bound ignores bufferLength, matching CWE-787's out-of-bounds write. This is a write-side overflow, not merely an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125), since the destination store is the security-relevant operation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the loop condition is bounded only by the input length and uses <=, while the destination trackHolder->buffer has its own capacity (bufferLength) that is never checked. Trigger: a length/sampleSize ratio reaching or exceeding bufferLength, or a length not a multiple of sampleSize, causes the final write to land past the end of the buffer. Supported consequence: out-of-bounds write into the track buffer, corrupting adjacent memory.

commit_msg:
CVE-2022-23606

Avoid closing other connections to prevent deep recursion when a large number of idle connections are closed at the start of a pool drain, when a connection is closed.

Signed-off-by: Yan Avlasov <yavlasov@google.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  if (isIdleImpl()) {', '    ENVOY_LOG(debug, "invoking idle callbacks - is_draining_for_deletion_={}",', '              is_draining_for_deletion_);', '    for (const Instance::IdleCb& cb : idle_callbacks_) {', '      cb();', '    }', '  }'], 'added_lines': ['  checkForIdleAndNotify();']}
description: Envoy is an open source edge and service proxy, designed for cloud-native applications. When a cluster is deleted via Cluster Discovery Service (CDS) all idle connections established to endpoints in that cluster are disconnected. A recursion was introduced in the procedure of disconnecting idle connections that can lead to stack exhaustion and abnormal process termination when a cluster has a large number of idle connections. This infinite recursion causes Envoy to crash. Users are advised to upgrade.

code_evidence: When is_draining_for_deletion_ is set, the function calls closeIdleConnectionsForDrainingPool(), which closes idle connections and can re-enter this same check as each connection is closed.

After that call, isIdleImpl() is evaluated and each idle callback in idle_callbacks_ is invoked; these callbacks can trigger further connection closure and re-enter the idle-check path without any recursion-depth or re-entrancy guard.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function permits unbounded recursive re-entry through closeIdleConnectionsForDrainingPool() and the idle callbacks, consuming the program stack until exhaustion. This is uncontrolled recursion (CWE-674), not merely a resource leak or infinite loop, because the termination is driven by stack growth from nested calls.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the drain-close path and idle callback loop lack a re-entrancy/depth guard, so closing one connection re-invokes the same idle-closing logic. Trigger: a cluster with many idle connections is deleted via CDS, causing repeated nested calls. Consequence: stack exhaustion and abnormal process termination (denial of service).

commit_msg:
Make DH_check_pub_key() and DH_generate_key() safer yet

We already check for an excessively large P in DH_generate_key(), but not in
DH_check_pub_key(), and none of them check for an excessively large Q.

This change adds all the missing excessive size checks of P and Q.

It's to be noted that behaviours surrounding excessively sized P and Q
differ.  DH_check() raises an error on the excessively sized P, but only
sets a flag for the excessively sized Q.  This behaviour is mimicked in
DH_check_pub_key().

Reviewed-by: Tomas Mraz <tomas@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Matt Caswell <matt@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Hugo Landau <hlandau@openssl.org>
(Merged from https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/22518)

(cherry picked from commit ddeb4b6c6d527e54ce9a99cba785c0f7776e54b6)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['        return 0;', '    }', '', '    if (dh->params.q != NULL', '        && BN_num_bits(dh->params.q) > OPENSSL_DH_MAX_MODULUS_BITS) {', '        ERR_raise(ERR_LIB_DH, DH_R_Q_TOO_LARGE);']}
description:
Issue summary: Generating excessively long X9.42 DH keys or checking
excessively long X9.42 DH keys or parameters may be very slow.

Impact summary: Applications that use the functions DH_generate_key() to
generate an X9.42 DH key may experience long delays.  Likewise, applications
that use DH_check_pub_key(), DH_check_pub_key_ex() or EVP_PKEY_public_check()
to check an X9.42 DH key or X9.42 DH parameters may experience long delays.
Where the key or parameters that are being checked have been obtained from
an untrusted source this may lead to a Denial of Service.

While DH_check() performs all the necessary checks (as of CVE-2023-3817),
DH_check_pub_key() doesn't make any of these checks, and is therefore
vulnerable for excessively large P and Q parameters.

Likewise, while DH_generate_key() performs a check for an excessively large
P, it doesn't check for an excessively large Q.

An application that calls DH_generate_key() or DH_check_pub_key() and
supplies a key or parameters obtained from an untrusted source could be
vulnerable to a Denial of Service attack.

DH_generate_key() and DH_check_pub_key() are also called by a number of
other OpenSSL functions.  An application calling any of those other
functions may similarly be affected.  The other functions affected by this
are DH_check_pub_key_ex(), EVP_PKEY_public_check(), and EVP_PKEY_generate().

Also vulnerable are the OpenSSL pkey command line application when using the
"-pubcheck" option, as well as the OpenSSL genpkey command line application.

The OpenSSL SSL/TLS implementation is not affected by this issue.

The OpenSSL 3.0 and 3.1 FIPS providers are not affected by this issue.

code_evidence: Lines 10-13 reject only an excessively large modulus p, returning 0; there is no analogous bound on dh->params.q before key generation proceeds.
When a non-NID group is used, line 40-42 accepts any non-NULL q and only compares dh->length against BN_num_bits(q); an attacker-supplied oversized q passes this guard.

Lines 66-69 call ossl_ffc_params_simple_validate and then ossl_ffc_generate_private_key with BN_num_bits(dh->params.q) as the bit length, so the unchecked q size directly drives expensive bignum work.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The code fails to check an unusual, attacker-controllable exceptional condition (oversized q) before proceeding, matching CWE-754's improper check for unusual conditions. This is distinct from CWE-400 resource exhaustion, which describes the resulting impact rather than the missing validation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function validates the size of p but omits an upper bound check on q, so an untrusted X9.42 parameter set with an excessively large q is accepted. Trigger: a caller supplies such parameters with no private key, causing private-key generation over the oversized q; the supported consequence is a long delay (denial of service), not memory corruption.

commit_msg:
Check if auth_user is set.

Fixes a crash if password packet appears before startup packet (#42).
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\t/* too early */', '\t\tif (!client->auth_user) {', '\t\t\tdisconnect_client(client, true, "client password pkt before startup packet");', '\t\t\treturn false;', '\t\t}', '']}
description: PgBouncer before 1.5.5 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference and crash) by sending a password packet before a startup packet.

code_evidence: Case 'p' (PasswordMessage) is handled without first verifying that client->auth_user was established by a prior startup packet. The code proceeds to mbuf_get_string on pkt->data and then check_client_passwd(client, passwd), which dereferences client->auth_user. The only guard before these calls is cf_auth_type <= AUTH_TRUST, which does not imply auth_user is non-NULL.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits because a pointer expected to be valid (client->auth_user) is NULL when the password packet arrives first, and it is dereferenced downstream without a check. This is a direct NULL dereference rather than a general input-validation or logic flaw.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the password-packet branch lacks a precondition that a startup packet has already set client->auth_user. Trigger: a remote client sends a PasswordMessage before any startup packet. Consequence: check_client_passwd dereferences the NULL auth_user, causing a NULL pointer dereference and crash (DoS).

description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel before 5.14.15. There is an array-index-out-of-bounds flaw in the detach_capi_ctr function in drivers/isdn/capi/kcapi.c.

code_evidence: ctr->cnr is used directly as an array subscript (cnr - 1) into capi_controller at lines 6 and 10 without any prior bounds check on the controller number. If cnr is 0 or negative, the index is -1 or lower; if cnr exceeds CAPI_MAXCONTR, the index is past the 32-element array.

Trigger: a controller/session whose cnr is 0 or out of range (as in the cmtp path) reaches this function. The out-of-bounds access at line 6 reads memory before the array, which UBSAN reports and which can crash or corrupt control flow.

commit_msg:
fix(swagger/security): ensure that the requested file is in the UI directory

The Rest::Swagger class didn't check if the file asked from the user was
contained in the UI directory, thus allowing users to access arbitrary
files in the filesystem.

Thanks to Kirill Efimov (@Kirill89) and the Snyk Security team for
finding and reporting the vulnerability to the Pistache team.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['     * @Export might be useful for routing also. Make it public or merge it with', '     * the Fragment class', '     */', '                auto path = uiDir.join(file);', '                Http::serveFile(response, path);', '                return Route::Result::Ok;'], 'added_lines': ['             * @Export might be useful for routing also. Make it public or merge it with', '             * the Fragment class', '             */', '                auto path = std::filesystem::canonical(uiDir.join(file)).string();', '', '                // Check if the requested file is contained in the uiDirectory', '                // to prevent path traversal vulnerabilities.', '                // In C++20, use std::string::starts_with()', '                if (path.rfind(uiDirectory_, 0) == 0)', '                {', '                    Http::serveFile(response, path);', '                    return Route::Result::Ok;', '                }', '                else', '                {', '                    response.send(Http::Code::Not_Found);', '                    return Route::Result::Failure;', '                }']}
description: This affects the package pistacheio/pistache before 0.0.3.20220425. It is possible to traverse directories to fetch arbitrary files from the server.

code_evidence: When the request resource is a prefix of the UI path, the handler strips the UI prefix from the user-controlled resource (line 78) and joins the remainder onto the configured UI directory (line 79). The result is passed directly to Http::serveFile (line 80) with no normalization or containment check, so a resource such as a traversal sequence can escape the UI directory.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-22 fits because external request input constructs a pathname intended to stay under the UI directory, but special elements are not neutralized, letting the resolved path escape that restricted parent. This is path traversal, not merely a routing or file-not-found issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: user-controlled request resource is concatenated to uiDirectory_ via Path::join without neutralizing '..' or absolute-path elements. Trigger: a request whose resource is a UI prefix followed by traversal segments. Consequence: Http::serveFile resolves the constructed path outside the restricted UI directory, allowing arbitrary files to be read from the server filesystem.

commit_msg:
A recent fuzzed filesystem image cached random dcache corruption
when the reproducer was run. This often showed up as panics in
lookup_slow() on a null inode->i_ops pointer when doing pathwalks.

BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at 0000000000000000
....
Call Trace:
 lookup_slow+0x44/0x60
 walk_component+0x3dd/0x9f0
 link_path_walk+0x4a7/0x830
 path_lookupat+0xc1/0x470
 filename_lookup+0x129/0x270
 user_path_at_empty+0x36/0x40
 path_listxattr+0x98/0x110
 SyS_listxattr+0x13/0x20
 do_syscall_64+0xf5/0x280
 entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x42/0xb7

but had many different failure modes including deadlocks trying to
lock the inode that was just allocated or KASAN reports of
use-after-free violations.

The cause of the problem was a corrupt INOBT on a v4 fs where the
root inode was marked as free in the inobt record. Hence when we
allocated an inode, it chose the root inode to allocate, found it in
the cache and re-initialised it.

We recently fixed a similar inode allocation issue caused by inobt
record corruption problem in xfs_iget_cache_miss() in commit
ee457001ed6c ("xfs: catch inode allocation state mismatch
corruption"). This change adds similar checks to the cache-hit path
to catch it, and turns the reproducer into a corruption shutdown
situation.

Reported-by: Wen Xu <wen.xu@gatech.edu>
Signed-Off-By: Dave Chinner <dchinner@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Christoph Hellwig <hch@lst.de>
Reviewed-by: Carlos Maiolino <cmaiolino@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Darrick J. Wong <darrick.wong@oracle.com>
[darrick: fix typos in comment]
Signed-off-by: Darrick J. Wong <darrick.wong@oracle.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t * If we are allocating a new inode, then check what was returned is', '\t * actually a free, empty inode. If we are not allocating an inode,', "\t * the check we didn't find a free inode.", '\tif (flags & XFS_IGET_CREATE) {', '\t\tif (VFS_I(ip)->i_mode != 0) {', '\t\t\txfs_warn(mp,', '"Corruption detected! Free inode 0x%llx not marked free on disk",', '\t\t\t\tino);', '\t\t\terror = -EFSCORRUPTED;', '\t\t\tgoto out_destroy;', '\t\t}', '\t\tif (ip->i_d.di_nblocks != 0) {', '\t\t\txfs_warn(mp,', '"Corruption detected! Free inode 0x%llx has blocks allocated!",', '\t\t\t\tino);', '\t\t\terror = -EFSCORRUPTED;', '\t\t\tgoto out_destroy;', '\t\t}', '\t} else if (VFS_I(ip)->i_mode == 0) {', '\t\terror = -ENOENT;', '\t}'], 'added_lines': ['\t * Check the inode free state is valid. This also detects lookup', '\t * racing with unlinks.', '\terror = xfs_iget_check_free_state(ip, flags);', '\tif (error)']}
description: An issue was discovered in fs/xfs/xfs_icache.c in the Linux kernel through 4.17.3. There is a NULL pointer dereference and panic in lookup_slow() on a NULL inode->i_ops pointer when doing pathwalks on a corrupted xfs image. This occurs because of a lack of proper validation that cached inodes are free during allocation.

code_evidence: xfs_iread reads the on-disk inode and, on error, jumps to out_destroy.
For non-create lookups, if the cached inode's mode is zero (free), the code sets -ENOENT and jumps to out_destroy.
out_destroy calls __destroy_inode/xfs_inode_free and returns the error, but the caller's *ipp is never set.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits because the supported consequence is dereferencing a NULL/uninitialized inode pointer, causing a crash. The missing free-state validation is the corruption trigger, not the weakness class itself; the dereference of the invalid pointer is the NULL-pointer weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function returns an error without setting *ipp, so callers that do not check the return value (or treat the inode as valid) use an uninitialized/NULL inode pointer. Trigger: a corrupted v4 inobt marks the root inode free; during lookup the mode==0 path returns -ENOENT. Consequence: a later dereference of the bogus inode leads to NULL-pointer panic in lookup_slow, matching the reported crash.

commit_msg: https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/issues/143
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  pixels=(unsigned char *) AcquireQuantumMemory(packets+256UL,image->rows*'], 'added_lines': ['  pixels=(unsigned char *) AcquireQuantumMemory(packets+257UL,image->rows*']}
description: MagickCore/memory.c in ImageMagick allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds access) via a crafted PDB file.

code_evidence: packets is computed from bits_per_pixel and image->columns; the buffer is allocated with AcquireQuantumMemory(packets+256UL, image->rows*sizeof(*pixels)), reserving only 256 bytes of slack beyond the row-packet size.

DecodeImage is given packets*image->rows as the buffer length, and for the 1-bit case the loop reads *p while advancing p++ per 8 pixels, so a crafted PDB can drive reads to the end of the allocated region.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function allocates a pixel buffer and then reads from it based on attacker-influenced dimensions without ensuring reads stay within bounds, which is an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). The fixed-size pad is insufficient to guarantee safety, so the read past the intended buffer matches this weakness rather than a write-based overflow.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The allocation size is derived from packets and image->rows with a fixed 256-byte pad, but decoding consumes/reads pixel data based on the crafted image dimensions. When the crafted PDB causes the decoder to read beyond the allocated pixel buffer, an out-of-bounds read occurs, leading to a crash/denial of service.

            complicated.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tchar_u\t\t**line_to_free,', '\tif (*eap->cmdlinep == *line_to_free)', '\tvim_free(*line_to_free);', '\t*line_to_free = theline;'], 'added_lines': ['\tgarray_T\t*lines_to_free,', '\tif (lines_to_free->ga_len > 0', '\t\t&& *eap->cmdlinep == ((char_u **)lines_to_free->ga_data)', '\t\t\t\t\t\t   [lines_to_free->ga_len - 1])', '\tga_add_string(lines_to_free, theline);']}
description: vim is vulnerable to Use After Free

code_evidence: On non-NULL input, the code compares *eap->cmdlinep against *line_to_free, conditionally repoints cmdlinep to the new line, then unconditionally frees *line_to_free and overwrites the pointer with theline.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the code explicitly frees memory with vim_free while other pointers may retain the same address, and no invalidation of those aliases occurs. This is a dangling-reference problem, not merely a double free or null dereference.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function frees the buffer referenced by *line_to_free and reassigns that pointer to the newly returned line. Any other reference that still aliases the freed buffer (for example a stored cmdlinep or caller-held pointer not updated by the conditional assignment) continues to point to freed memory; later reads or writes through it are use-after-free, potentially causing memory corruption or crash.

commit_msg:
Fix assignment lookahead in parser_process_group_expression

This patch fixes #3815 and fixes #3819.

JerryScript-DCO-1.0-Signed-off-by: Robert Fancsik frobert@inf.u-szeged.hu
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['parse_unary_expression:', '        if (parser_process_group_expression (context_p, &grouping_level))', '        {', '          goto parse_unary_expression;', '        }'], 'added_lines': ['        parser_process_group_expression (context_p, &grouping_level);']}
description: There is an Assertion 'context_p->stack_top_uint8 == LEXER_EXPRESSION_START' at js-parser-expr.c:3565 in parser_parse_expression in JerryScript 2.2.0.

code_evidence: When a right paren closes a group, parser_process_group_expression is called; if it returns true the code jumps back to parse_unary_expression via goto, re-running unary parsing without the corresponding stack bookkeeping. The fixed version removes this control-flow jump and just continues.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reaches JERRY_ASSERT(context_p->stack_top_uint8 == LEXER_EXPRESSION_START) due to attacker-influenced parser control flow, causing an abort. This directly matches CWE-617 (Reachable Assertion); it is not merely a logic error because the observable impact is a process exit from a reachable assert.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The goto re-enters the unary-expression path after a group expression has already been processed, leaving the parser stack in an inconsistent state so that LEXER_EXPRESSION_START is no longer on top. A crafted parenthesized expression triggers this condition, and the final assertion at line 0087 aborts the process, giving a reachable assertion and denial of service.

commit_msg:
NetKVM: BZ#1169718: Checking the length only on read

Signed-off-by: Joseph Hindin <yhindin@rehat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    tTcpIpPacketParsingResult res = QualifyIpPacket(pIpHeader, ulDataLength);'], 'added_lines': ['                                                BOOLEAN verifyLength,', '    tTcpIpPacketParsingResult res = QualifyIpPacket(pIpHeader, ulDataLength, verifyLength);']}
description: The NetKVM Windows Virtio driver allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (guest crash) via a crafted length value in an IP packet, as demonstrated by a value that does not account for the size of the IP options.

code_evidence: pIpHeader is derived from the packet buffer at ulStartOffset, and ulDataLength is passed directly to QualifyIpPacket. The only subsequent guard checks ipStatus==ppresNotIP or ipCheckSum==ppresIPTooShort, but the packet length field is never validated against IP options size before parsing/checksum processing.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function accepts network-supplied length metadata and fails to validate it before use, matching CWE-20's improper validation of derived/implied size properties. The DoS arises from the missing length constraint, not from a separate memory-corruption primitive.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function forwards attacker-controlled packet data and length to QualifyIpPacket without verifying that ulDataLength accounts for IP options. Trigger: a crafted IP packet whose length value is shorter than the actual header/options. Consequence: parsing proceeds on inconsistent length metadata, causing a guest crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
evtchn: convert per-channel lock to be IRQ-safe

... in order for send_guest_{global,vcpu}_virq() to be able to make use
of it.

This is part of XSA-343.

Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Acked-by: Julien Grall <jgrall@amazon.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['static void double_evtchn_lock(struct evtchn *lchn, struct evtchn *rchn)', '    if ( lchn < rchn )', '        spin_lock(&lchn->lock);', '        spin_lock(&rchn->lock);', '        if ( lchn != rchn )', '            spin_lock(&rchn->lock);'], 'added_lines': ['static unsigned long double_evtchn_lock(struct evtchn *lchn,', '                                        struct evtchn *rchn)', '    unsigned long flags;', '', '    if ( lchn <= rchn )', '        spin_lock_irqsave(&lchn->lock, flags);', '        if ( lchn != rchn )', '            spin_lock(&rchn->lock);', '        spin_lock_irqsave(&rchn->lock, flags);', '', '    return flags;']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.14.x. There are evtchn_reset() race conditions. Uses of EVTCHNOP_reset (potentially by a guest on itself) or XEN_DOMCTL_soft_reset (by itself covered by XSA-77) can lead to the violation of various internal assumptions. This may lead to out of bounds memory accesses or triggering of bug checks. In particular, x86 PV guests may be able to elevate their privilege to that of the host. Host and guest crashes are also possible, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS). Information leaks cannot be ruled out. All Xen versions from 4.5 onwards are vulnerable. Xen versions 4.4 and earlier are not vulnerable.

code_evidence: When lchn < rchn, the function acquires lchn->lock then rchn->lock using plain spin_lock, which does not disable interrupts on the local CPU.

In the else branch, rchn->lock is taken first (only when lchn != rchn) and then lchn->lock, again with plain spin_lock; the ordering differs from the first branch, so the two branches take the two locks in opposite orders.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-362 fits because concurrent execution can interleave with the lock acquisition sequence, violating exclusivity of the shared evtchn resource; the missing IRQ-safety and inconsistent ordering are the synchronization defects enabling that race, not merely a performance issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The per-channel locks are acquired with interrupt-enabled spin_lock calls, and the lock ordering is inconsistent between the two branches. An IRQ handler or another concurrent path can interrupt a holder of one lock and attempt to acquire the other, producing a lock-order inversion and a timing window in which the evtchn state is not exclusively protected. The supported consequence is a race on the shared evtchn state, leading to corrupted internal assumptions, out-of-bounds accesses or bug checks.

description: RIOT-OS, an operating system that supports Internet of Things devices, contains a network stack with the ability to process 6LoWPAN frames. An attacker can send a crafted frame to the device resulting in a large out of bounds write beyond the packet buffer. The write will create a hard fault exception after reaching the last page of RAM. The hard fault is not handled and the system will be stuck until reset. Thus the impact is denial of service. Version 2022.10 fixes this issue. As a workaround, apply the patch manually.

code_evidence: The decoder return value payload_offset is only rejected when zero; no upper bound against sixlo->size is enforced before use.
The memcpy copies sixlo->size - payload_offset bytes from sixlo->data + payload_offset into ipv6->data + uncomp_hdr_len, assuming payload_offset <= sixlo->size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked offset leads to writing past the end of the ipv6 packet buffer, matching CWE-787 out-of-bounds write. The integer underflow is the trigger, but the supported consequence is an out-of-bounds write, not merely an integer error.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: payload_offset from _iphc_ipv6_decode is not validated against the received frame size. A crafted 6LoWPAN IPHC/NHC header can yield payload_offset larger than sixlo->size, making the size subtraction underflow to a huge length; the memcpy then writes far beyond the packet buffer, causing memory corruption and a hard fault (DoS).

commit_msg: parse_qt: possible integer overflow
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    if ((int)size < 0) return; // 2+GB is too much', '    if (save + size < save) return; // 32bit overflow']}
description: An integer overflow error within the "parse_qt()" function (internal/dcraw_common.cpp) in LibRaw versions prior to 0.18.12 can be exploited to trigger an infinite loop via a specially crafted Apple QuickTime file.

code_evidence: size is an unsigned value read from the file via get4() and only checked against the lower bound 8; no upper bound constrains it.
save+size is used as a file offset for the recursive parse_qt() call and for fseek(); with a large size this unsigned addition can wrap to a small value.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe operation is an unsigned integer addition (save+size) whose wraparound is unchecked, matching CWE-190's integer overflow/wraparound. The impact is resource-consumption DoS via altered execution logic, consistent with the CWE scope; this is arithmetic wraparound rather than a mere out-of-bounds read.

fseek (ifp, save+size, SEEK_SET);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: size, an attacker-controlled unsigned 32-bit value from the QuickTime file, is combined with save without an overflow check. Trigger: a crafted tag with a size near UINT_MAX makes save+size wrap to a small offset. Consequence: fseek()/recursion operate on a wrapped offset, so the loop can fail to advance and iterate indefinitely, causing the described infinite loop/DoS.

commit_msg:
stream_out: rtp: don't use VLA for user controlled data

It should fix a possible invalid memory access

When streaming ogg-files via rtp, an ogg-file can trigger an invalid
write access using an overly long 'configuration' string.

The original code attemps to allocate space to hold the string on the stack
and hence, cannot verify if allocation succeeds. Instead, we now allocate the
buffer on the heap and return if allocation fails.

In detail, rtp_packetize_xiph_config allocates a buffer on the stack at (1) where
the size depends on the local variable 'len'. The variable 'len' is
calculated at (0) to be the length of a string contained in a specially
crafted Ogg Vorbis file, and therefore, it is attacker-controlled.

Signed-off-by: Jean-Baptiste Kempf <jb@videolan.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    char b64[len + 1];'], 'added_lines': ['', '    char *b64 = malloc(len + 1);', '    if(!b64)', '        return VLC_EGENERIC;', '', '    free(b64);']}
description: The rtp_packetize_xiph_config function in modules/stream_out/rtpfmt.c in VideoLAN VLC media player before 2.1.6 uses a stack-allocation approach with a size determined by arbitrary input data, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory corruption) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted length value.

code_evidence: Line 9-10 locate the ';' terminator and assert it exists; line 11 computes len as the distance from the attacker-supplied 'configuration=' value to that terminator, so len is fully attacker-controlled. Line 12 then declares a stack VLA of len+1 bytes, and lines 13-14 memcpy len bytes and write b64[len] into it without any bound check against available stack space.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs a memcpy/terminator write into a buffer whose size derives from untrusted input, so the write can fall outside the buffer's intended boundary, matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds memory operation. The unbounded length (CWE-129/789) is the upstream cause, but the resulting unsafe buffer operation is the CWE-119 weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: a variable-length stack array sized directly by an attacker-controlled length derived from the Ogg 'configuration' string. Trigger: a crafted file with an overly long configuration value makes the allocation exceed available stack; the subsequent memcpy and terminator write then operate outside the intended buffer bounds, causing memory corruption or a crash. The consequence is invalid memory write, not merely an allocation failure.

commit_msg:
vga: fix display update region calculation

vga display update mis-calculated the region for the dirty bitmap
snapshot in case the scanlines are padded.  This can triggere an
assert in cpu_physical_memory_snapshot_get_dirty().

Fixes: fec5e8c92becad223df9d972770522f64aafdb72
Reported-by: Kevin Wolf <kwolf@redhat.com>
Reported-by: 李强 <liqiang6-s@360.cn>
Signed-off-by: Gerd Hoffmann <kraxel@redhat.com>
Message-id: 20170509104839.19415-1-kraxel@redhat.com
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['                                                      bwidth * height,'], 'added_lines': ['                                                      line_offset * height,']}
description: The vga display update in mis-calculated the region for the dirty bitmap snapshot in case split screen mode is used causing a denial of service (assertion failure) in the cpu_physical_memory_snapshot_get_dirty function.

code_evidence: Line 145 computes bwidth as the packed line width in bytes, but line 138 captures line_offset, the actual VRAM stride used to advance addr1 (line 194).

When full_update is false, lines 152-154 snapshot dirty VRAM over the range addr1..addr1+bwidth*height. The loop's per-line dirty query at lines 172-173 uses page0=addr and page1=addr+bwidth-1, where addr is derived from the strided addr1.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function drives a snapshot API whose precondition is violated by the mis-sized range, reaching an internal assert() and terminating the process. This matches CWE-617 (Reachable Assertion): an attacker-reachable assertion causing a crash/DoS, rather than a memory-corruption consequence.

evidence_lines.code:
update = memory_region_snapshot_get_dirty(&s->vram, snap,
page0, page1 - page0);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the snapshot extent uses bwidth*height (contiguous packed size) instead of line_offset*height, so when the VRAM scanlines are padded (line_offset > bwidth) the snapshot region is too small. Lines in the strided display can then reference offsets beyond the snapshotted range, and memory_region_snapshot_get_dirty() hits its internal assert, aborting QEMU. Trigger: non-full update with padded line_offset; consequence: guest-triggerable denial of service via assertion failure.

commit_msg:
index: error out on unreasonable prefix-compressed path lengths

When computing the complete path length from the encoded
prefix-compressed path, we end up just allocating the complete path
without ever checking what the encoded path length actually is. This can
easily lead to a denial of service by just encoding an unreasonable long
path name inside of the index. Git already enforces a maximum path
length of 4096 bytes. As we also have that enforcement ready in some
places, just make sure that the resulting path is smaller than
GIT_PATH_MAX.

Reported-by: Krishna Ram Prakash R <krp@gtux.in>
Reported-by: Vivek Parikh <viv0411.parikh@gmail.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\t\tif (path_len > GIT_PATH_MAX)', '\t\t\treturn index_error_invalid("unreasonable path length");', '']}
description: Integer overflow in the index.c:read_entry() function while decompressing a compressed prefix length in libgit2 before v0.26.2 allows an attacker to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read) via a crafted repository index file.

code_evidence: git_decode_varint reads an attacker-controlled strip_len from the index buffer; last_len = strlen(last) is compared against strip_len, and prefix_len = last_len - strip_len is computed. suffix_len = strlen(path_ptr + varint_len) derives from the untrusted entry bytes. path_len is then built with GITERR_CHECK_ALLOC_ADD(prefix_len, suffix_len) and +1, and passed to git__malloc; the patched function adds a GIT_PATH_MAX guard before allocation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is an unchecked length calculation feeding memory allocation, matching CWE-190's concern that size arithmetic can produce an unreasonable result used in allocation/copy. The added GIT_PATH_MAX check confirms the missing constraint on path_len. It is not merely an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125), since the root cause is the unsanitized length computation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The path length arithmetic combines a prefix length derived from the encoded varint and the suffix length of the stored path. Without an upper bound on the resulting path_len, an index entry can encode an unreasonable length that drives the allocation and subsequent path handling. The trigger is a crafted repository index with an oversized prefix-compressed path; the supported consequence is a denial of service via excessive allocation/resource consumption or out-of-bounds read.

commit_msg:
Use EVP_PKEY_size() to allocate correct size of signature buffer. (#18)

Do not use fixed buffer size for signature, EVP_SignFinal() requires
buffer for signature at least  EVP_PKEY_size(pkey) bytes in size.

Fixes crash when using 4K RSA signatures (https://github.com/OpenSC/pam_p11/issues/16, https://github.com/OpenSC/pam_p11/issues/15)

|| !EVP_SignFinal(md_ctx, signature, &siglen, privkey)

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the signature buffer size is fixed at 256 bytes instead of being derived from the key size, while EVP_SignFinal writes a signature whose length depends on the key. Trigger: a smart card/key producing a signature longer than 256 bytes (e.g., 4096-bit RSA). Consequence: an out-of-bounds stack write, causing memory corruption and a crash.

commit_msg:
Jann Horn points out that our TLB flushing was subtly wrong for the
mremap() case.  What makes mremap() special is that we don't follow the
usual "add page to list of pages to be freed, then flush tlb, and then
free pages".  No, mremap() obviously just _moves_ the page from one page
table location to another.

That matters, because mremap() thus doesn't directly control the
lifetime of the moved page with a freelist: instead, the lifetime of the
page is controlled by the page table locking, that serializes access to
the entry.

As a result, we need to flush the TLB not just before releasing the lock
for the source location (to avoid any concurrent accesses to the entry),
but also before we release the destination page table lock (to avoid the
TLB being flushed after somebody else has already done something to that
page).

This also makes the whole "need_flush" logic unnecessary, since we now
always end up flushing the TLB for every valid entry.

Reported-and-tested-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Acked-by: Will Deacon <will.deacon@arm.com>
Tested-by: Ingo Molnar <mingo@kernel.org>
Acked-by: Peter Zijlstra (Intel) <peterz@infradead.org>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

Both old and new PTL matter: the old one', '\t\t * for racing with page_mkclean(), the new one to', '\t\t * make sure the physical page stays valid until', '\t\t * the TLB entry for the old mapping has been', '\t\t * flushed.', '\t\tif (pte_present(pte))', '\tif (force_flush)', '\t\tflush_tlb_range(vma, old_end - len, old_end);']}
description: Since Linux kernel version 3.2, the mremap() syscall performs TLB flushes after dropping pagetable locks. If a syscall such as ftruncate() removes entries from the pagetables of a task that is in the middle of mremap(), a stale TLB entry can remain for a short time that permits access to a physical page after it has been released back to the page allocator and reused. This is fixed in the following kernel versions: 4.9.135, 4.14.78, 4.18.16, 4.19.

code_evidence: At [25,26] the loop sets force_flush only when pte_present(pte) && pte_dirty(pte); a present but clean PTE moved to a new location leaves force_flush false.

At [31,32,33,34,35,36,37,38,39] the destination page-table lock new_ptl is released at line 33 and the destination PTE is unmapped at line 34 before the TLB flush at line 36; when force_flush is false the code instead sets *need_flush=true at line 38, deferring the flush until after the locks are dropped.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-459 fits because the function fails to clean up the stale TLB translation for a moved PTE at the required synchronization point; the missing flush is the incomplete cleanup of a supporting resource (the TLB entry). The deferred *need_flush path leaves the stale mapping in place, matching incomplete cleanup rather than a simple locking bug.

evidence_lines.code:
if (pte_present(pte) && pte_dirty(pte))
force_flush = true;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the TLB flush for the moved entry is not performed while the destination page-table lock is still held, and clean present PTEs skip the immediate flush entirely. Trigger: a concurrent syscall such as ftruncate() operates on the pagetable during mremap(); because the destination lock is released before flush_tlb_range, a stale TLB entry survives. Consequence: access to a physical page after it is freed and reused, enabling read/modify of reused memory.

commit_msg:
evtchn: convert per-channel lock to be IRQ-safe

... in order for send_guest_{global,vcpu}_virq() to be able to make use
of it.

This is part of XSA-343.

Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Acked-by: Julien Grall <jgrall@amazon.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['static void double_evtchn_unlock(struct evtchn *lchn, struct evtchn *rchn)', '    spin_unlock(&lchn->lock);', '        spin_unlock(&rchn->lock);'], 'added_lines': ['static void double_evtchn_unlock(struct evtchn *lchn, struct evtchn *rchn,', '                                 unsigned long flags)', '        spin_unlock(&lchn->lock);', '    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&rchn->lock, flags);']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.14.x. There are evtchn_reset() race conditions. Uses of EVTCHNOP_reset (potentially by a guest on itself) or XEN_DOMCTL_soft_reset (by itself covered by XSA-77) can lead to the violation of various internal assumptions. This may lead to out of bounds memory accesses or triggering of bug checks. In particular, x86 PV guests may be able to elevate their privilege to that of the host. Host and guest crashes are also possible, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS). Information leaks cannot be ruled out. All Xen versions from 4.5 onwards are vulnerable. Xen versions 4.4 and earlier are not vulnerable.

code_evidence: double_evtchn_unlock releases lchn->lock unconditionally, then only releases rchn->lock when the channels differ, using plain spin_unlock rather than an IRQ-safe variant. The lock ordering and irq-restore state are not coordinated with the corresponding acquire path, so the exclusive region is not maintained across the two-channel case.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function implements a synchronization sequence for a shared evtchn resource, and its unlock logic leaves a window where an interfering concurrent sequence can access the resource, matching CWE-362. The IRQ-safety and ordering defects are the mechanism of the race, not a separate memory-safety class.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the unlock helper drops the per-channel spinlocks without IRQ-safe restoration and with an asymmetric release order, so an interrupt or concurrent evtchn_reset path can interleave between the two unlocks. Trigger: a reset racing with evtchn send/unlock on the same or different channels. Supported consequence: violated evtchn internal assumptions, out-of-bounds access or bug checks.

commit_msg:
Correctly load/initialize classes when using ConstantPool

- do not load classes in the "ifLoaded" calls
- never intitialize classes in the natives
- do not update the constant pool when querying from the natives

Fixes: #12016

[ci skip]

Signed-off-by: Graham Chapman <graham_chapman@ca.ibm.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (NULL != ramCPEntry)', '\t{'], 'added_lines': ['\tif ((NULL != ramCPEntry) && J9_ARE_NO_BITS_SET(resolveFlags, J9_RESOLVE_FLAG_NO_CP_UPDATE)) {']}
description: In Eclipse Openj9 to version 0.25.0, usage of the jdk.internal.reflect.ConstantPool API causes the JVM in some cases to pre-resolve certain constant pool entries. This allows a user to call static methods or access static members without running the class initialization method, and may allow a user to observe uninitialized values.

code_evidence: Lines 95-118 conditionally initialize the resolved method's class via initializeClass only when J9_RESOLVE_FLAG_NO_CLASS_INIT is clear; if jitCompileTimeResolve and init not succeeded, method is nulled (98-101). Otherwise the class init runs (105) before the method is cached.

Lines 119-122 write the resolved method pointer into ramCPEntry unconditionally (before patch); the patch adds J9_RESOLVE_FLAG_NO_CP_UPDATE guard so callers requesting no CP update (e.g. JCL ConstantPool queries) do not cache the method.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-909 (Missing Initialization of Resource) fits because the cached RAM static-method entry is made usable without the class-initialization step that should precede its use, allowing access to uninitialized static state. The patch's NO_CP_UPDATE guard prevents this premature caching, confirming the missing-initialization dependency.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: resolveStaticMethodRefInto caches the resolved static method into ramCPEntry even when the caller requested J9_RESOLVE_FLAG_NO_CP_UPDATE, so a ConstantPool query pre-resolves the entry without ensuring class initialization in the caller's context. Trigger: a user queries jdk.internal.reflect.ConstantPool, causing the entry to be resolved and cached; later execution of the static member uses the cached entry and skips initializeClass. Consequence: static methods/members may be invoked before the class initializer runs, exposing uninitialized static values.

commit_msg: Fix a crash in the TGA loader with malformed input
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tconst size_t buffer_size = (tga_header.image_width * tga_header.image_height) * pixel_size;', '\t\t\terr = convert_to_image(p_image, buffer, tga_header, palette_r, is_monochrome);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tsize_t buffer_size = (tga_header.image_width * tga_header.image_height) * pixel_size;', '\t\t\tbuffer_size = src_image_len;', '\t\t\terr = convert_to_image(p_image, buffer, tga_header, palette_r, is_monochrome, buffer_size);']}

code_evidence: buffer_size is computed from the untrusted 16-bit header fields image_width*image_height*pixel_size at line 59, and uncompressed_buffer is resized to that value at line 61. For RLE-encoded input, decode_tga_rle writes into uncompressed_buffer_w using buffer_size at line 66.

This is a boundary-check failure rather than a pure out-of-bounds read, since the size mismatch drives writes past the buffer end.

Trigger: a malformed TGA whose dimensions/pixel depth imply a size larger than the file contents. Consequence: decode/convert routines operate beyond the intended buffer, corrupting memory or crashing.

commit_msg:
Prevent KDC unset status assertion failures

Assign status values if S4U2Self padata fails to decode, if an
S4U2Proxy request uses invalid KDC options, or if an S4U2Proxy request
uses an evidence ticket which does not match the canonicalized request
server principal name.  Reported by Samuel Cabrero.

If a status value is not assigned during KDC processing, default to
"UNKNOWN_REASON" rather than failing an assertion.  This change will
prevent future denial of service bugs due to similar mistakes, and
will allow us to omit assigning status values for unlikely errors such
as small memory allocation failures.

CVE-2017-11368:

In MIT krb5 1.7 and later, an authenticated attacker can cause an
assertion failure in krb5kdc by sending an invalid S4U2Self or
S4U2Proxy request.

  CVSSv3 Vector: AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H/E:H/RL:O/RC:C

ticket: 8599 (new)
target_version: 1.15-next
target_version: 1.14-next
tags: pullup
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if (code)'], 'added_lines': ['    if (code) {', '        *status = "DECODE_PA_FOR_USER";', '    }']}
description: In MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.7 and later, an authenticated attacker can cause a KDC assertion failure by sending invalid S4U2Self or S4U2Proxy requests.

code_evidence: decode_krb5_pa_for_user() parses attacker-supplied pa_data contents; on failure the function returns the error code without assigning *status, leaving the caller's status pointer unset.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The patch adds *status = "DECODE_PA_FOR_USER" to the decode-failure branch precisely to avoid a reachable assertion in the KDC. The weakness is a reachable assertion triggered by attacker-controlled input, matching CWE-617; it is not merely an input-validation error since the impact is an abort.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the decode-failure path returns without setting *status. Trigger: an authenticated client sends a malformed PA-FOR-USER padata in an S4U2Self request. The caller later asserts that status is assigned, so the unset status causes a KDC assertion failure and process abort (DoS).

commit_msg:
When opening files for write, ensure they aren't symbolic links

Issue #1048 identified that if, for example, a non privileged user
created a symbolic link from /etc/keepalvied.data to /etc/passwd,
writing to /etc/keepalived.data (which could be invoked via DBus)
would cause /etc/passwd to be overwritten.

This commit stops keepalived writing to pathnames where the ultimate
component is a symbolic link, by setting O_NOFOLLOW whenever opening
a file for writing.

This might break some setups, where, for example, /etc/keepalived.data
was a symbolic link to /home/fred/keepalived.data. If this was the case,
instead create a symbolic link from /home/fred/keepalived.data to
/tmp/keepalived.data, so that the file is still accessible via
/home/fred/keepalived.data.

There doesn't appear to be a way around this backward incompatibility,
since even checking if the pathname is a symbolic link prior to opening
for writing would create a race condition.

Signed-off-by: Quentin Armitage <quentin@armitage.org.uk>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tif ((tf = fopen(tfile->file_path, "w"))) {'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif ((tf = fopen_safe(tfile->file_path, "w"))) {']}
description: keepalived 2.0.8 didn't check for pathnames with symlinks when writing data to a temporary file upon a call to PrintData or PrintStats. This allowed local users to overwrite arbitrary files if fs.protected_symlinks is set to 0, as demonstrated by a symlink from /tmp/keepalived.data or /tmp/keepalived.stats to /etc/passwd.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function opens a configured track file for writing and writes an integer init value; it does not read or expose sensitive information, and the described symlink-following issue is an arbitrary file overwrite (CWE-59/CWE-73 class), not information exposure.

commit_msg:
mmu_gather: Force tlb-flush VM_PFNMAP vmas

Jann reported a race between munmap() and unmap_mapping_range(), where
unmap_mapping_range() will no-op once unmap_vmas() has unlinked the
VMA; however munmap() will not yet have invalidated the TLBs.

Therefore unmap_mapping_range() will complete while there are still
(stale) TLB entries for the specified range.

Mitigate this by force flushing TLBs for VM_PFNMAP ranges.

Signed-off-by: Peter Zijlstra (Intel) <peterz@infradead.org>
Acked-by: Will Deacon <will@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
diff_func:
--- func_before
+++ func_after
@@ -1,13 +1,19 @@
 static inline void tlb_end_vma(struct mmu_gather *tlb, struct vm_area_struct *vma)
 {
-	if (tlb->fullmm || IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_MMU_GATHER_MERGE_VMAS))
+	if (tlb->fullmm)
 		return;
 
 	/*
-	 * Do a TLB flush and reset the range at VMA boundaries; this avoids
-	 * the ranges growing with the unused space between consecutive VMAs,
-	 * but also the mmu_gather::vma_* flags from tlb_start_vma() rely on
-	 * this.
+	 * VM_PFNMAP is more fragile because the core mm will not track the
+	 * page mapcount -- there might not be page-frames for these PFNs after
+	 * all. Force flush TLBs for such ranges to avoid munmap() vs
+	 * unmap_mapping_range() races.
 	 */
-	tlb_flush_mmu_tlbonly(tlb);
+	if (tlb->vma_pfn || !IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_MMU_GATHER_MERGE_VMAS)) {
+		/*
+		 * Do a TLB flush and reset the range at VMA boundaries; this avoids
+		 * the ranges growing with the unused space between consecutive VMAs.
+		 */
+		tlb_flush_mmu_tlbonly(tlb);
+	}
 }
