commit_msg:
x86/mm: alloc/free_lN_table: Retain partial_flags on -EINTR

When validating or de-validating pages (in alloc_lN_table and
free_lN_table respectively), the `partial_flags` local variable is
used to keep track of whether the "current" PTE started the entire
operation in a "may be partial" state.

One of the patches in XSA-299 addressed the fact that it is possible
for a previously-partially-validated entry to subsequently be found to
have invalid entries (indicated by returning -EINVAL); in which case
page->partial_flags needs to be set to indicate that the current PTE
may have the partial bit set (and thus _put_page_type() should be
called with PTF_partial_set).

Unfortunately, the patches in XSA-299 assumed that once
put_page_from_lNe() returned -ERESTART on a page, it was not possible
for it to return -EINTR.  This turns out to be true for
alloc_lN_table() and free_lN_table, but not for _get_page_type() and
_put_page_type(): both can return -EINTR when called on pages with
PGT_partial set.  In these cases, the pages PGT_partial will still be
set; failing to set partial_flags appropriately may allow an attacker
to do a privilege escalation similar to those described in XSA-299.

Fix this by always copying the local partial_flags variable into
page->partial_flags when exiting early.

NB that on the "get" side, no adjustment to nr_validated_entries is
needed: whether pte[i] is partially validated or entirely
un-validated, we want nr_validated_entries = i.  On the "put" side,
however, we need to adjust nr_validated_entries appropriately: if
pte[i] is entirely validated, we want nr_validated_entries = i + 1; if
pte[i] is partially validated, we want nr_validated_entries = i.

This is part of XSA-310.

Signed-off-by: George Dunlap <george.dunlap@citrix.com>
Reviewed-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            page->partial_flags = 0;'], 'added_lines': ['            page->partial_flags = partial_flags;']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.12.x allowing x86 PV guest OS users to gain host OS privileges by leveraging race conditions in pagetable promotion and demotion operations, because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2019-18421. XSA-299 addressed several critical issues in restartable PV type change operations. Despite extensive testing and auditing, some corner cases were missed. A malicious PV guest administrator may be able to escalate their privilege to that of the host. All security-supported versions of Xen are vulnerable. Only x86 systems are affected. Arm systems are not affected. Only x86 PV guests can leverage the vulnerability. x86 HVM and PVH guests cannot leverage the vulnerability. Note that these attacks require very precise timing, which may be difficult to exploit in practice.

code_evidence: Line 8 snapshots page->partial_flags into the local partial_flags before the validation loop.
Line 14 clears partial_flags after the first iteration, so it reflects only the current PTE's may-be-partial state.
Lines 17-18 allow hypercall_preempt_check() to abort the loop with -EINTR while a page type change is in progress.
Lines 44-49 handle -EINTR after the loop began: they set nr_validated_ptes but reset page->partial_flags to 0 instead of preserving partial_flags.
Lines 62-63 show the correct preservation path in the other early-exit branch, confirming the omitted constraint.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-362 fits because the flaw is a timing-dependent window in a preemptible, restartable shared page-table operation where an interfering sequence observes inconsistent partial state, violating exclusivity/atomicity. It is not merely improper input validation; the root cause is missing synchronization of shared partial_flags state across concurrent restarts.

evidence_lines.code: unsigned int   partial_flags = page->partial_flags;
i++, partial_flags = 0 )

if ( i > page->nr_validated_ptes && hypercall_preempt_check() )
rc = -EINTR;

page->nr_validated_ptes = i;
page->partial_flags = partial_flags;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The page's type-change state is shared across preempted/restarted operations. When alloc_l3_table is interrupted mid-validation (-EINTR), the code resets page->partial_flags to 0 even though the page may still have PGT_partial set. A subsequent concurrent operation then misinterprets the page's partial state and calls _put_page_type() without PTF_partial_set, breaking the atomicity of the type-change sequence and enabling privilege escalation like XSA-299/310.

description: The binary MP4Box in Gpac 1.0.1 has a null pointer dereference vulnerability in the gf_isom_get_payt_count function in hint_track.c, which allows attackers to cause a denial of service.

joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads hmhd->type while hmhd may be NULL, which is exactly a NULL pointer dereference (CWE-476). This is a missing null check, not an out-of-bounds or use-after-free issue, so CWE-476 is the precise fit.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the InfoHeader pointer is dereferenced on line 4 before being validated. Trigger: a track whose Media information InfoHeader is NULL (e.g., malformed/missing hint media header). Consequence: NULL pointer dereference causing a crash/DoS, matching the reported gf_isom_get_payt_count path.

description: In Wireshark 2.6.0 to 2.6.5 and 2.4.0 to 2.4.11, the P_MUL dissector could crash. This was addressed in epan/dissectors/packet-p_mul.c by rejecting the invalid sequence number of zero.

code_evidence: The Data_PDU branch reads seq_no from the packet with tvb_get_ntohs and adds it to the tree, but performs no check that seq_no is nonzero before using it.

Later, seq_no is passed to fragment_add_seq_check as seq_no - 1; with seq_no == 0 this underflows the guint16 to 0xFFFF, an invalid fragment index. The patch adds an expert warning for seq_no == 0, confirming zero was not validated.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is missing validation of a protocol field (sequence number) that must satisfy a domain rule (nonzero) before safe processing, matching CWE-20. The underflow is the consequence of failing to reject the invalid input, not an independent integer weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the dissector accepts a network-supplied Data PDU sequence number without validating that it is nonzero. Trigger: a Data PDU whose sequence field is 0. Consequence: seq_no - 1 underflows to 65535, feeding an invalid sequence into reassembly and contributing to the reported dissector crash/DoS.

description: An issue was discovered in the Tatsuya Kinoshita w3m fork before 0.5.3-31. w3m allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory corruption, segmentation fault, and crash) via a crafted HTML page.

code_evidence: After locating the textarea line l, the loop walks l via l = l->next for each of rows iterations (lines 60, 72) while using l in columnPos(l, col), retrieveAnchor(...l->linenumber...) and form_update_line(l, ...). The pre-patch guard only reset epos when spos > epos; the patch adds epos >= l->len and breaks, indicating epos derived from a->end.pos could exceed the current line buffer length before form_update_line reads/writes it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe operation is a read/write over a line buffer at an offset beyond its intended length (epos >= l->len), matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds buffer access. The patch constrains epos by breaking the loop, confirming the boundary violation rather than a mere logic error.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: epos from the anchor can exceed the length of the current line l, and the loop passes it to form_update_line which operates on l->lineBuf without a bounds check. Trigger: a crafted HTML page whose textarea/anchor positions or multi-line layout produce epos >= l->len. Consequence: out-of-bounds memory access leading to corruption and a segmentation fault/crash (DoS).

description: epan/crypt/airpdcap.c in the IEEE 802.11 dissector in Wireshark 2.x before 2.0.4 mishandles certain length values, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (application crash) via a crafted packet.

code_evidence: Line 20 computes eapol_len - sizeof(EAPOL_RSN_KEY), which underflows when eapol_len is smaller than the EAPOL_RSN_KEY size, making the upper-bound comparison ineffective.

szEncryptedKey = (guint8 *)g_memdup(key_data, key_bytes_len);

commit_msg:
Commit 086d49058cd8 ("ipv6: annotate some data-races around sk->sk_prot")
fixed some data-races around sk->sk_prot but it was not enough.

Some functions in inet6_(stream|dgram)_ops still access sk->sk_prot
without lock_sock() or rtnl_lock(), so they need READ_ONCE() to avoid
load tearing.

Fixes: 1da177e4c3f4 ("Linux-2.6.12-rc2")
Signed-off-by: Kuniyuki Iwashima <kuniyu@amazon.com>
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tstruct sock *sk1 = sock->sk;', '\tstruct sock *sk2 = sk1->sk_prot->accept(sk1, flags, &err, kern);'], 'added_lines': ['\tstruct sock *sk1 = sock->sk, *sk2;', '\t/* IPV6_ADDRFORM can change sk->sk_prot under us. */', '\tsk2 = READ_ONCE(sk1->sk_prot)->accept(sk1, flags, &err, kern);']}
description: A vulnerability has been found in Linux Kernel and classified as problematic. This vulnerability affects the function inet6_stream_ops/inet6_dgram_ops of the component IPv6 Handler. The manipulation leads to race condition. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue. VDB-211090 is the identifier assigned to this vulnerability.

code_evidence: inet_accept loads sock->sk into sk1 and then dereferences sk1->sk_prot to fetch the accept handler and invoke it, with no lock_sock() or rtnl_lock() protecting sk_prot.
The result sk2 is only locked after the indirect call returns, so the sk_prot read and the call occur during an unlocked window.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs a shared-resource access (sk->sk_prot) that requires temporary exclusivity but is not synchronized against an interfering concurrent modification, matching CWE-362. The patch's READ_ONCE only addresses load tearing; it is a data-race mitigation rather than a different weakness class.

evidence_lines.code:
if (!sk2)
goto do_err;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: sk1->sk_prot is read and dereferenced without synchronization while another code sequence (IPV6_ADDRFORM) can change sk->sk_prot concurrently. Trigger: a concurrent setsockopt IPV6_ADDRFORM on the same socket while inet_accept executes. This can yield a torn or stale proto pointer, leading to a wrong or invalid accept handler invocation and a possible crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
tools/xenstore: remove nodes owned by destroyed domain

In case a domain is removed from Xenstore, remove all nodes owned by
it per default.

This tackles the problem that nodes might be created by a domain
outside its home path in Xenstore, leading to Xenstore hogging more
and more memory. Domain quota don't work in this case if the guest is
rebooting in between.

Since XSA-322 ownership of such stale nodes is transferred to dom0,
which is helping against unintended access, but not against OOM of
Xenstore.

As a fallback for weird cases add a Xenstore start parameter for
keeping today's way to handle stale nodes, adding the risk of Xenstore
hitting an OOM situation.

This is part of XSA-419 / CVE-2022-42322.

description: Xenstore: Cooperating guests can create arbitrary numbers of nodes T[his CNA information record relates to multiple CVEs; the text explains which aspects/vulnerabilities correspond to which CVE.] Since the fix of XSA-322 any Xenstore node owned by a removed domain will be modified to be owned by Dom0. commit_msg: util-lib: use MODE_INVALID as invalid value for mode_t everywhere
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['                        touch_file(t->stamp_path, true, USEC_INFINITY, UID_INVALID, GID_INVALID, 0);'], 'added_lines': ['                        touch_file(t->stamp_path, true, USEC_INFINITY, UID_INVALID, GID_INVALID, MODE_INVALID);']}
description: A flaw in systemd v228 in /src/basic/fs-util.c caused world writable suid files to be created when using the systemd timers features, allowing local attackers to escalate their privileges to root. This is fixed in v229.

code_evidence: When the stamp file path exists but stat() fails with ENOENT, the code calls touch_file() passing literal 0 as the mode argument. This hard-coded mode value is the only permission specification for the newly created stamp file; no validation or safe default is applied.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Passing a literal 0 mode to a file-creation call mismanages permission bits, directly falling under CWE-264's permissions/privileges management category. The fix replaces 0 with MODE_INVALID, confirming the mode argument is the access-control-relevant defect; this is permission assignment, not a separate memory or input-validation weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: touch_file() is invoked with mode 0 instead of an invalid sentinel, so the callee cannot distinguish 'no mode change requested' from an explicit zero mode. Trigger: timer start when the stamp file is absent (stat returns ENOENT). Supported consequence: the stamp file is created with unintended/unsafe permission bits, which under the described flaw yields world-writable suid files enabling local privilege escalation.

commit_msg: irc: fix parsing of DCC filename
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if (length > 0)'], 'added_lines': ['    if (length > 1)']}
description: WeeChat before 1.7.1 allows a remote crash by sending a filename via DCC to the IRC plugin. This occurs in the irc_ctcp_dcc_filename_without_quotes function during quote removal, with a buffer overflow.

code_evidence: length = strlen(filename) sets the buffer length. The guard is only length > 0, so a one-character string passes. For filename = "\"", filename[0] and filename[length-1] are both the quote, so the branch is taken and weechat_strndup(filename+1, length-2) is called with length-2 = -1.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The subtraction produces a negative length that is used as a buffer size, so the copy operates outside the intended buffer bounds, matching CWE-119. The fix (length > 1) shows the missing boundary constraint. CWE-125 is a narrower read-only variant, but the negative-size operation is the buffer-boundary violation captured by CWE-119.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the length check does not exclude strings of length 1 before computing length-2. Trigger: a remote DCC filename consisting of a single double-quote. The negative size passed to weechat_strndup causes an out-of-bounds read/copy, leading to a crash (DoS) and possibly reading adjacent memory.

commit_msg: http://www.imagemagick.org/discourse-server/viewtopic.php?f=3&t=26838
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    sun_data=(unsigned char *) AcquireQuantumMemory((size_t) sun_info.length,', '      sizeof(*sun_data));', '        bytes_per_line=sun_info.width*sun_info.depth;'], 'added_lines': ['    bytes_per_line=sun_info.width*sun_info.depth;', '    sun_data=(unsigned char *) AcquireQuantumMemory((size_t) MagickMax(', '      sun_info.length,bytes_per_line*sun_info.width),sizeof(*sun_data));']}
description: Buffer overflow in ImageMagick before 6.9.0-4 Beta allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (application crash) via a crafted SUN file.

code_evidence: number_pixels is computed from image->columns*image->rows, and the guard rejects only when number_pixels*((depth+7)/8) exceeds sun_info.length for non-encoded data.
sun_data is allocated with only sun_info.length bytes (line 182-183), so its size is bounded by the attacker-controlled header length field.
ReadBlob fills sun_data with exactly sun_info.length bytes, establishing the buffer extent as sun_info.length.
For RT_ENCODED, bytes_per_line=sun_info.width*sun_info.depth is computed independently of the sun_data allocation size.
DecodeImage is called with sun_data, sun_info.length as source length, and bytes_per_line*height as destination size; the source buffer is only sun_info.length bytes.
Later pixel loops validate length against sun_info.length or bytes_per_line*rows, but these checks occur after decoding and do not constrain the decode input.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Reading beyond the allocated sun_data buffer is an operation outside the intended memory boundary, matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds memory access class. The root cause is the unvalidated relationship between the encoded raster dimensions and the source buffer length, distinct from an integer overflow (CWE-190) since the allocation size itself is the length field.

evidence_lines.code:
sun_data=(unsigned char *) AcquireQuantumMemory((size_t) sun_info.length,
sizeof(*sun_data));

(void) DecodeImage(sun_data,sun_info.length,sun_pixels,bytes_per_line*
height);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The buffer sun_data is allocated to sun_info.length bytes, but for RT_ENCODED images the decoder is driven by width/depth-derived output sizing rather than the actual source allocation. A crafted SUN file with an encoded type and mismatched length/width/depth can make DecodeImage read past the end of sun_data, causing an out-of-bounds read and crash.

commit_msg:
In ql_alloc_large_buffers, a new skb is allocated via netdev_alloc_skb.
This skb should be released if pci_dma_mapping_error fails.

Fixes: 0f8ab89e825f ("qla3xxx: Check return code from pci_map_single() in ql_release_to_lrg_buf_free_list(), ql_populate_free_queue(), ql_alloc_large_buffers(), and ql3xxx_send()")
Signed-off-by: Navid Emamdoost <navid.emamdoost@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t\tdev_kfree_skb_irq(skb);']}
description: A memory leak in the ql_alloc_large_buffers() function in drivers/net/ethernet/qlogic/qla3xxx.c in the Linux kernel before 5.3.5 allows local users to cause a denial of service (memory consumption) by triggering pci_dma_mapping_error() failures, aka CID-1acb8f2a7a9f.

code_evidence: Line 9-10 allocates a new skb via netdev_alloc_skb and stores it in the local skb variable.

Line 21 stores that skb into lrg_buf_cb->skb, but on the pci_dma_mapping_error failure path at lines 29-34 the function logs, calls ql_free_large_buffers, and returns -ENOMEM without releasing the newly allocated skb itself.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-401 fits because an allocated resource (the skb) is not released on an error path, making memory unavailable for reuse. This is an error-condition memory leak, not a use-after-free or double-free.

evidence_lines.code:
skb = netdev_alloc_skb(qdev->ndev,
qdev->lrg_buffer_len);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the DMA-mapping error branch returns early without freeing the freshly allocated skb. Trigger: pci_dma_mapping_error() reports a mapping failure after netdev_alloc_skb succeeds. Consequence: the skb allocation is leaked, and repeated failures exhaust memory, causing denial of service.

commit_msg:
Zero and sanity check all dynamic allocs.

This addresses the memory issues in Issue #6 expressed in
calloc_some.pdf and malloc_some.pdf
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    data = malloc(blk_sz * n_blks);', '    memset(data, 0, blk_sz * n_blks);'], 'added_lines': ['    data = safe_calloc(blk_sz * n_blks);']}
description: An issue was discovered in PDFResurrect before 0.18. pdf_load_pages_kids in pdf.c doesn't validate a certain size value, which leads to a malloc failure and out-of-bounds write.

code_evidence: The initial buffer is allocated with malloc(blk_sz * n_blks) and zeroed; there is no check that malloc/realloc returned non-NULL, so data may be NULL.
fread writes into data+total_sz, then total_sz is advanced and *(data + total_sz) is written; the terminator write relies on the buffer having spare room.

The growth check occurs only after the read and terminator write, and realloc's return is assigned directly without a NULL check, so a failed realloc loses the pointer and later writes target freed/NULL memory.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes through a pointer whose allocation success is not validated and whose resize check lags the write, producing a write outside the intended buffer, which matches CWE-787. A NULL-dereference-only framing would miss the out-of-bounds write consequence.

evidence_lines.code:
data = malloc(blk_sz * n_blks);
memset(data, 0, blk_sz * n_blks);

if (total_sz + blk_sz >= (blk_sz * n_blks))
data = realloc(data, blk_sz * (++n_blks));

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: unchecked allocation results combined with a write that occurs before the buffer-growth check. Trigger: an object whose data fills the current block causes the terminator write at data+total_sz, and a failed allocation (e.g., large n_blks) leaves data NULL or stale. Consequence: writes past the allocated buffer boundary, corrupting memory or crashing.

commit_msg:
coredump: fix race condition between mmget_not_zero()/get_task_mm() and core dumping

The core dumping code has always run without holding the mmap_sem for
writing, despite that is the only way to ensure that the entire vma
layout will not change from under it.  Only using some signal
serialization on the processes belonging to the mm is not nearly enough.
This was pointed out earlier.  For example in Hugh's post from Jul 2017:

  https://lkml.kernel.org/r/alpine.LSU.2.11.1707191716030.2055@eggly.anvils

  "Not strictly relevant here, but a related note: I was very surprised
   to discover, only quite recently, how handle_mm_fault() may be called
   without down_read(mmap_sem) - when core dumping. That seems a
   misguided optimization to me, which would also be nice to correct"

In particular because the growsdown and growsup can move the
vm_start/vm_end the various loops the core dump does around the vma will
not be consistent if page faults can happen concurrently.

Pretty much all users calling mmget_not_zero()/get_task_mm() and then
taking the mmap_sem had the potential to introduce unexpected side
effects in the core dumping code.

Adding mmap_sem for writing around the ->core_dump invocation is a
viable long term fix, but it requires removing all copy user and page
faults and to replace them with get_dump_page() for all binary formats
which is not suitable as a short term fix.

For the time being this solution manually covers the places that can
confuse the core dump either by altering the vma layout or the vma flags
while it runs.  Once ->core_dump runs under mmap_sem for writing the
function mmget_still_valid() can be dropped.

Allowing mmap_sem protected sections to run in parallel with the
coredump provides some minor parallelism advantage to the swapoff code
(which seems to be safe enough by never mangling any vma field and can
keep doing swapins in parallel to the core dumping) and to some other
corner case.

In order to facilitate the backporting I added "Fixes: 86039bd3b4e6"
however the side effect of this same race condition in /proc/pid/mem
should be reproducible since before 2.6.12-rc2 so I couldn't add any
other "Fixes:" because there's no hash beyond the git genesis commit.

Because find_extend_vma() is the only location outside of the process
context that could modify the "mm" structures under mmap_sem for
reading, by adding the mmget_still_valid() check to it, all other cases
that take the mmap_sem for reading don't need the new check after
mmget_not_zero()/get_task_mm().  The expand_stack() in page fault
context also doesn't need the new check, because all tasks under core
dumping are frozen.

Link: http://lkml.kernel.org/r/20190325224949.11068-1-aarcange@redhat.com
Fixes: 86039bd3b4e6 ("userfaultfd: add new syscall to provide memory externalization")
Signed-off-by: Andrea Arcangeli <aarcange@redhat.com>
Reported-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Suggested-by: Oleg Nesterov <oleg@redhat.com>
Acked-by: Peter Xu <peterx@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Mike Rapoport <rppt@linux.ibm.com>
Reviewed-by: Oleg Nesterov <oleg@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Acked-by: Jason Gunthorpe <jgg@mellanox.com>
Acked-by: Michal Hocko <mhocko@suse.com>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (!mmget_still_valid(mm))', '\t\t\tgoto skip_mm;', '\tskip_mm:']}
description: The coredump implementation in the Linux kernel before 5.0.10 does not use locking or other mechanisms to prevent vma layout or vma flags changes while it runs, which allows local users to obtain sensitive information, cause a denial of service, or possibly have unspecified other impact by triggering a race condition with mmget_not_zero or get_task_mm calls. This is related to fs/userfaultfd.c, mm/mmap.c, fs/proc/task_mmu.c, and drivers/infiniband/core/uverbs_main.c.

code_evidence: mmget_not_zero(mm) at line 13 takes a reference to the mm, then line 24 acquires mmap_sem for writing and line 37 releases it before line 38 drops the reference with mmput; in the patched function a mmget_still_valid(mm) check gates the locked section so a concurrent core dump that invalidated the mm is detected before the vma list is walked and zapped.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is improper locking: the lock is acquired but the protected state can still be altered concurrently because validity of the mm is not checked under the lock, matching CWE-667's incorrect synchronization of a shared resource.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The code takes an mm reference and then later acquires mmap_sem without verifying the mm is still valid for the dumping state; a concurrent core dump can change the vma layout or flags between the reference acquisition and the locked manipulation, so the loop at lines 26-35 may operate on an inconsistent vma list, leading to memory corruption or denial of service.

commit_msg:
Prevent null dereference read in `GetInitOp`.

We have a map of maps. We test that the key exists in the first map but then we don't have any validation that this also means the second map has the needed key. In the scenarios where this is not the case, we'll dereference a nullptr, if we don't have this check

PiperOrigin-RevId: 408739325
Change-Id: If9bb7ed759aba1f3b56a34913f209508dbaf65ce
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    *init_op_name = init_op_sig_it->second.outputs()', '                        .find(kSavedModelInitOpSignatureKey)', '                        ->second.name();'], 'added_lines': ['    const auto& sig_def_outputs = init_op_sig_it->second.outputs();', '    const auto& sig_def_outputs_it =', '        sig_def_outputs.find(kSavedModelInitOpSignatureKey);', '    if (sig_def_outputs_it == sig_def_outputs.end()) {', '      return errors::FailedPrecondition("Could not find output ",', '                                        kSavedModelInitOpSignatureKey);', '    }', '    *init_op_name = sig_def_outputs_it->second.name();']}
description: Tensorflow is an Open Source Machine Learning Framework. The implementation of `GetInitOp` is vulnerable to a crash caused by dereferencing a null pointer. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.8.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.7.1, TensorFlow 2.6.3, and TensorFlow 2.5.3, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: The code checks only that kSavedModelInitOpSignatureKey exists in sig_def_map (line 6). Inside that branch it calls .find(kSavedModelInitOpSignatureKey) on the outputs map at lines 7-8 and immediately dereferences the returned iterator with ->second.name() at line 9, without comparing it to outputs().end().
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits because the function dereferences a find() result that may be end()/NULL when the inner key is absent, matching a null pointer dereference. It is not merely a missing-key logic error, since the unchecked dereference is the concrete unsafe operation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the presence of the signature key in the outer map does not guarantee the same key exists in the inner outputs map. When the inner find returns end(), the chained ->second dereferences an invalid/NULL iterator, crashing the process (DoS) during GetInitOp.

commit_msg:

Chrome's Edit Bookmark dialog formats urls for display such that a
url of http://javascript:scripttext@host.com is later converted to a
javascript url scheme, allowing persistence of a script injection
attack within the user's bookmarks.

This fix prevents such misinterpretations by always showing the
scheme when a userinfo component is present within the url.

However, it's", '  return url_formatter::FormatUrl(', '      url, url_formatter::kFormatUrlOmitAll &', '               ~url_formatter::kFormatUrlOmitUsernamePassword,', '      net::UnescapeRule::SPACES, nullptr, nullptr, nullptr);'], 'added_lines': ["  // and trailing slash, and unescape most characters. However, it's", '  url_formatter::FormatUrlTypes format_types =', '      url_formatter::kFormatUrlOmitAll &', '      ~url_formatter::kFormatUrlOmitUsernamePassword;', '', '  // If username is present, we must not omit the scheme because FixupURL() will', '  // subsequently interpret the username as a scheme. crbug.com/639126', '  if (url.has_username())', '    format_types &= ~url_formatter::kFormatUrlOmitHTTP;', '', '  return url_formatter::FormatUrl(url, format_types, net::UnescapeRule::SPACES,', '                                  nullptr, nullptr, nullptr);']}
description: Bookmark handling in Google Chrome prior to 54.0.2840.59 for Windows, Mac, and Linux; 54.0.2840.85 for Android had insufficient validation of supplied data, which allowed a remote attacker to inject arbitrary scripts or HTML (UXSS) via crafted HTML pages, as demonstrated by an interpretation conflict between userinfo and scheme in an http://javascript:payload@example.com URL.

code_evidence: The function formats a bookmark URL for display using url_formatter::FormatUrl with kFormatUrlOmitAll, omitting the scheme while preserving username/password. For a URL like http://javascript:payload@host.com, the omitted scheme plus retained userinfo can be re-parsed by FixupURL() as a javascript: scheme, turning stored userinfo into executable script content.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function produces output (bookmark display text) from attacker-influenced URL input without neutralizing the scheme/userinfo ambiguity, enabling script execution in a web context, which is the improper input neutralization central to CWE-79. It is not merely a URL parsing bug because the unsafe output is later rendered/executed as a web page.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the display formatting drops the http scheme without accounting for a userinfo component, so the serialized bookmark text is ambiguous and re-parses as a script scheme. Trigger: a crafted bookmark URL containing a javascript: string in userinfo is displayed and later fixed up. Consequence: script injection/XSS when the persisted bookmark is opened.

commit_msg:
softmmu: Always initialize xlat in address_space_translate_for_iotlb

The bug is an uninitialized memory read, along the translate_fail
path, which results in garbage being read from iotlb_to_section,
which can lead to a crash in io_readx/io_writex.

The bug may be fixed by writing any value with zero
in ~TARGET_PAGE_MASK, so that the call to iotlb_to_section using
the xlat'ed address returns io_mem_unassigned, as desired by the
translate_fail path.

It is most useful to record the original physical page address,
which will eventually be logged by memory_region_access_valid
when the access is rejected by unassigned_mem_accepts.

Resolves: https://gitlab.com/qemu-project/qemu/-/issues/1065
Signed-off-by: Richard Henderson <richard.henderson@linaro.org>
Reviewed-by: Peter Maydell <peter.maydell@linaro.org>
Message-Id: <20220621153829.366423-1-richard.henderson@linaro.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['address_space_translate_for_iotlb(CPUState *cpu, int asidx, hwaddr addr,'], 'added_lines': ['address_space_translate_for_iotlb(CPUState *cpu, int asidx, hwaddr orig_addr,', '    hwaddr addr = orig_addr;', '    /*', '     * We should be given a page-aligned address -- certainly', '     * tlb_set_page_with_attrs() does so.  The page offset of xlat', '     * is used to index sections[], and PHYS_SECTION_UNASSIGNED = 0.', '     * The page portion of xlat will be logged by memory_region_access_valid()', '     * when this memory access is rejected, so use the original untranslated', '     * physical address.', '     */', '    assert((orig_addr & ~TARGET_PAGE_MASK) == 0);', '    *xlat = orig_addr;']}
description: softmmu/physmem.c in QEMU through 7.0.0 can perform an uninitialized read on the translate_fail path, leading to an io_readx or io_writex crash. NOTE: a third party states that the Non-virtualization Use Case in the qemu.org reference applies here, i.e., "Bugs affecting the non-virtualization use case are not considered security bugs at this time.

code_evidence: When IOMMU translation clears all permission bits, the loop jumps to translate_fail without ever assigning *xlat; the successful path only writes *xlat at line 37.

The translate_fail block returns the unassigned section without initializing the caller's *xlat output. The caller (tlb_set_page_with_attrs) then uses that uninitialized xlat to index iotlb_to_section, producing a garbage section pointer and a crash in io_readx/io_writex.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function returns to its caller with an output resource (*xlat) never initialized on the translate_fail path; the caller then uses that uninitialized value, matching CWE-908's use of an uninitialized resource. This is distinct from an out-of-bounds read, since no bounds violation is needed—the value is simply never written.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the translate_fail path omits an assignment to the *xlat out-parameter. Trigger: an IOMMU translation whose permissions lack both IOMMU_RO and IOMMU_WO (or otherwise clear *prot). Consequence: the caller reads uninitialized stack memory as the translated address, indexes iotlb_to_section with garbage, and crashes on subsequent memory access.

commit_msg:
Fix a possible integer overflow problem when examining corrupt binaries using a 32-bit binutil.

	PR 24005
	* objdump.c (load_specific_debug_section): Check for integer
	overflow before attempting to allocate contents.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  section->user_data = sec;', '  if (amt == 0', '      || section->start == NULL'], 'added_lines': ['  section->user_data = sec;', '  if (amt == 0 || amt > bfd_get_file_size (abfd))', '    {', '      section->start = NULL;', '      free_debug_section (debug);', '      printf (_("\\nSection \'%s\' has an invalid size: %#llx.\\n"),', '\t      section->name, (unsigned long long) section->size);', '      return FALSE;', '    }', '  if (section->start == NULL']}
description: load_specific_debug_section in objdump.c in GNU Binutils through 2.31.1 contains an integer overflow vulnerability that can trigger a heap-based buffer overflow via a crafted section size.

code_evidence: Line 19 stores the attacker-controlled section size from bfd_get_section_size into section->size; line 20 computes amt = section->size + 1 in bfd_size_type, which wraps to 0 when size equals the maximum representable value.
Line 21 passes the wrapped amt to malloc, and the guard at lines 23-30 checks amt == 0 only after allocation, so the overflowed size is not rejected before allocation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe operation is an integer wraparound in a size calculation (section->size + 1) that feeds a memory allocation, which is the defining pattern of CWE-190. The later heap corruption is the consequence; the root cause remains the unchecked integer overflow.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the increment section->size + 1 on line 20 can wrap to zero for a crafted section size, and malloc(amt) is attempted on line 21 before any size validation. Trigger: a corrupt binary whose debug section size is the maximum bfd_size_type value. Consequence: a zero/tiny allocation is used as if it held the full section, so the subsequent write of the NUL terminator and content copy can corrupt heap memory.

commit_msg:
rgw: Remove assertions in IAM Policy

A couple of them could be triggered by user input.

Signed-off-by: Adam C. Emerson <aemerson@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  ceph_assert(shift > 0);'], 'added_lines': []}
description: RADOS Gateway in Ceph 12.1.0 through 12.2.1 allows remote authenticated users to cause a denial of service (assertion failure and application exit) by leveraging "full" (not necessarily admin) privileges to post an invalid profile to the admin API, related to rgw/rgw_iam_policy.cc, rgw/rgw_basic_types.h, and rgw/rgw_iam_types.h.

code_evidence: The prefix values of both MaskedIP operands are subtracted from their address width (128 for IPv6, 32 for IPv4), and std::max selects the larger resulting shift.

ceph_assert(shift > 0) aborts the process when the computed shift is zero or negative, which occurs when either operand's prefix equals or exceeds its address width (e.g., prefix >= 32 for IPv4 or >= 128 for IPv6).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-617 fits because the function contains an assert reachable through user-controlled prefix values, converting an input validation gap into an application exit. The weakness is the reachable assertion, not merely the missing prefix bound.

evidence_lines.code:
auto shift = std::max((l.v6 ? 128 : 32) - l.prefix,
(r.v6 ? 128 : 32) - r.prefix);
ceph_assert(shift > 0);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the equality operator trusts prefix values from policy input without bounding them, then asserts that the derived shift is positive. Trigger: a remote authenticated user submits an IAM policy containing a MaskedIP with an out-of-range prefix, causing shift <= 0. Consequence: ceph_assert fires, terminating the gateway process and denying service.

commit_msg:
In saa7134_initdev, it will call saa7134_hwinit1. There are three
function invoking here: saa7134_video_init1, saa7134_ts_init1
and saa7134_vbi_init1.

All of them will init a timer with same function. Take
saa7134_video_init1 as an example. It'll bound &dev->video_q.timeout
with saa7134_buffer_timeout.

In buffer_activate, the timer funtcion is started.

If we remove the module or device which will call saa7134_finidev
to make cleanup, there may be a unfinished work. The
possible sequence is as follows, which will cause a
typical UAF bug.

Fix it by canceling the timer works accordingly before cleanup in
saa7134_finidev.

CPU0                  CPU1

                    |saa7134_buffer_timeout
saa7134_finidev     |
  kfree(dev);       |
                    |
                    | saa7134_buffer_next
                    | //use dev

Fixes: 1e7126b4a86a ("media: saa7134: Convert timers to use timer_setup()")
Signed-off-by: Zheng Wang <zyytlz.wz@163.com>
Signed-off-by: Hans Verkuil <hverkuil-cisco@xs4all.nl>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tdel_timer_sync(&dev->video_q.timeout);']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel before 6.3.2. A use-after-free was found in saa7134_finidev in drivers/media/pci/saa7134/saa7134-core.c.

code_evidence: saa7134_video_fini frees page tables and control handlers for dev->video_q/vbi_q without first stopping the dev->video_q.timeout timer; the post-fix diff adds del_timer_sync(&dev->video_q.timeout) before these frees, confirming the timer is still armed during teardown.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The teardown lacks synchronization against the concurrently executing timer callback, so shared dev state is freed while another execution sequence still accesses it—a race condition (CWE-362) whose consequence is UAF.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The timer callback saa7134_buffer_timeout can run concurrently on another CPU while fini releases dev resources; without del_timer_sync, the callback reaches saa7134_buffer_next and dereferences freed dev memory, a use-after-free. Trigger is module/device removal racing an active buffer timer.

commit_msg:
Fix double-free in gdImageWebPtr()

The issue is that gdImageWebpCtx() (which is called by gdImageWebpPtr() and
the other WebP output functions to do the real work) does not return whether
it succeeded or failed, so this is not checked in gdImageWebpPtr() and the
function wrongly assumes everything is okay, which is not, in this case,
because there is a size limitation for WebP, namely that the width and
height must by less than 16383.

We can't change the signature of gdImageWebpCtx() for API compatibility
reasons, so we introduce the static helper _gdImageWebpCtx() which returns
success respective failure, so gdImageWebpPtr() and gdImageWebpPtrEx() can
check the return value. We leave it solely to libwebp for now to report
warnings regarding the failing write.

This issue had been reported by Ibrahim El-Sayed to security@libgd.org.

CVE-2016-6912
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tgdImageWebpCtx(im, out, -1);'], 'added_lines': ['\t_gdImageWebpCtx(im, out, -1);']}
description: Double free vulnerability in the gdImageWebPtr function in the GD Graphics Library (aka libgd) before 2.2.4 allows remote attackers to have unspecified impact via large width and height values.

code_evidence: Line 7 calls gdImageWebpCtx(im, out, -1) without checking any return status; the commit notes this helper does not report success/failure. Line 8 then unconditionally calls out->gd_free(out), releasing the gdIOCtx even when the WebP write failed (e.g., width/height exceeding the 16383 limit).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function frees out via gd_free without validating that the preceding WebP operation succeeded, so the same allocation can be released twice along the failing path, matching CWE-415's definition of calling free() twice on the same address. This is a double free rather than a plain resource leak because the buffer is still freed after the failed write.

evidence_lines.code:
gdImageWebpCtx(im, out, -1);
out->gd_free(out);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the void-returning gdImageWebpCtx can fail on oversized dimensions, but its result is ignored, so out is freed unconditionally afterward. Trigger: large width/height values causing the WebP encode to fail. Supported consequence: the output buffer is released on a failed path, leading to a double free whose impact is memory corruption.

commit_msg:
mime-actions: use file metadata for trusting desktop files

Currently we only trust desktop files that have the executable bit
set, and don't replace the displayed icon or the displayed name until
it's trusted, which prevents for running random programs by a malicious
desktop file.

However, the executable permission is preserved if the desktop file
comes from a compressed file.

To prevent this, add a metadata::trusted metadata to the file once the
user acknowledges the file as trusted. This adds metadata to the file,
which cannot be added unless it has access to the computer.

Also remove the SHEBANG "trusted" content we were putting inside the
desktop file, since that doesn't add more security since it can come
with the file itself.

https://bugzilla.gnome.org/show_bug.cgi?id=777991
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            mark_desktop_file_trusted (job,', '                                       job->cancellable,', '                                       dest,', '                                       FALSE);'], 'added_lines': ['            mark_desktop_file_executable (job,', '                                          job->cancellable,', '                                          dest,', '                                          FALSE);']}
description: GNOME Nautilus before 3.23.90 allows attackers to spoof a file type by using the .desktop file extension, as demonstrated by an attack in which a .desktop file's Name field ends in .pdf but this file's Exec field launches a malicious "sh -c" command. In other words, Nautilus provides no UI indication that a file actually has the potentially unsafe .desktop extension; instead, the UI only shows the .pdf extension. One (slightly) mitigating factor is that an attack requires the .desktop file to have execute permission. The solution is to ask the user to confirm that the file is supposed to be treated as a .desktop file, and then remember the user's answer in the metadata::trusted field.

code_evidence: The trust decision for a copied .desktop file rests on is_trusted_desktop_file(src,...) combined with the destination being the desktop directory; the source's trust state is the only gate.

On success, mark_desktop_file_trusted is invoked on dest, propagating trust (and thus executable/launch behavior) to the copied file without validating the file's actual type or Name/Exec consistency.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function accepts file metadata (the .desktop extension and exec/trust state) as sufficient evidence of safety and does not validate the file's actual type or Name-vs-Exec consistency before propagating trust. That is improper validation of input properties (CWE-20), not merely a display or escaping issue.

evidence_lines.code:
if (copy_job->desktop_location != NULL &&
g_file_equal (copy_job->desktop_location, dest_dir) &&
is_trusted_desktop_file (src, job->cancellable))
{

mark_desktop_file_trusted (job,
job->cancellable,
dest,
FALSE);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the copy path trusts a source desktop file based on its existing trusted/executable state rather than validating the file's content or type metadata. Trigger: an attacker supplies a .desktop file (e.g., Name ending in .pdf, Exec launching sh -c) that carries execute permission, e.g., from a compressed archive; copying it to the desktop marks the destination trusted. Consequence: the spoofed .desktop file remains launchable while the UI shows a benign extension, enabling execution of attacker commands.

commit_msg:
Fix a possible double file close when decoder initialization fails.

Public issue https://github.com/mackron/miniaudio/issues/319
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['        pDecoder->backend.vfs.file = NULL;']}
description: Miniaudio 0.10.35 has a Double free vulnerability that could cause a buffer overflow in ma_default_vfs_close__stdio in miniaudio.h.

code_evidence: The uninit path closes the VFS file whenever onRead is ma_decoder__on_read_vfs, but the original code did not clear backend.vfs.file after closing. A subsequent uninit call (or a failure path calling uninit twice) re-enters this branch and closes the same handle again.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-415 covers calling free twice on the same address; here the same VFS file handle is released twice because no NULL reset guards the second close. This is distinct from a generic use-after-free, since the defect is the repeated release itself.

Trigger: ma_decoder_uninit is invoked twice, or decoder initialization fails after the file was opened and cleanup runs again. Consequence: the same file handle is closed/liberated twice, i.e. a double free of the underlying resource.

commit_msg:
correctly check return value of X509_check_host

CVE-2020-7041 incorrect use of X509_check_host (regarding return value)
is fixed with this commit.

The flaw came in with #242 and prevented proper host name verification
when openssl >= 1.0.2 was in use since openfortivpn 1.7.0.
diff_func:
--- func_before
+++ func_after
@@ -23,7 +23,8 @@
 
 #ifdef HAVE_X509_CHECK_HOST
 	// Use OpenSSL native host validation if v >= 1.0.2.
-	if (X509_check_host(cert, common_name, FIELD_SIZE, 0, NULL))
+	// correctly check return value of X509_check_host
+	if (X509_check_host(cert, common_name, FIELD_SIZE, 0, NULL) == 1)
 		cert_valid = 1;
 #else
 	// Use explicit Common Name check if native validation not available.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (X509_check_host(cert, common_name, FIELD_SIZE, 0, NULL))'], 'added_lines': ['\t// correctly check return value of X509_check_host', '\tif (X509_check_host(cert, common_name, FIELD_SIZE, 0, NULL) == 1)']}
description: An issue was discovered in openfortivpn 1.11.0 when used with OpenSSL 1.0.2 or later. tunnel.c mishandles certificate validation because an X509_check_host negative error code is interpreted as a successful return value.

code_evidence: Line 21 treats any nonzero X509_check_host return as success; OpenSSL returns -1 on internal error and 0 on mismatch, so only 1 means a match.
Lines 31-34 then set ret = 0 (validation succeeded) when cert_valid is set and the chain result is X509_V_OK, so a negative error code is accepted as a valid host.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function is the certificate-validation routine, and its incorrect handling of the host-check result causes improper certificate validation, matching CWE-295. Contrast with CWE-252 (unchecked return value): here the return is checked but misinterpreted, so the defect is in validation logic.

evidence_lines.code:
if (X509_check_host(cert, common_name, FIELD_SIZE, 0, NULL))
cert_valid = 1;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the boolean test of X509_check_host conflates the match value 1 with negative error codes. Trigger: X509_check_host returns -1 (e.g., internal failure), setting cert_valid = 1. Consequence: host-name verification is bypassed and the certificate is accepted, enabling impersonation of the gateway.

commit_msg:
userfaultfd: non-cooperative: fix fork use after free

When reading the event from the uffd, we put it on a temporary
fork_event list to detect if we can still access it after releasing and
retaking the event_wqh.lock.

If fork aborts and removes the event from the fork_event all is fine as
long as we're still in the userfault read context and fork_event head is
still alive.

We've to put the event allocated in the fork kernel stack, back from
fork_event list-head to the event_wqh head, before returning from
userfaultfd_ctx_read, because the fork_event head lifetime is limited to
the userfaultfd_ctx_read stack lifetime.

Forgetting to move the event back to its event_wqh place then results in
__remove_wait_queue(&ctx->event_wqh, &ewq->wq); in
userfaultfd_event_wait_completion to remove it from a head that has been
already freed from the reader stack.

This could only happen if resolve_userfault_fork failed (for example if
there are no file descriptors available to allocate the fork uffd).  If
it succeeded it was put back correctly.

Furthermore, after find_userfault_evt receives a fork event, the forked
userfault context in fork_nctx and uwq->msg.arg.reserved.reserved1 can
be released by the fork thread as soon as the event_wqh.lock is
released.  Taking a reference on the fork_nctx before dropping the lock
prevents an use after free in resolve_userfault_fork().

If the fork side aborted and it already released everything, we still
try to succeed resolve_userfault_fork(), if possible.

Fixes: 893e26e61d04eac9 ("userfaultfd: non-cooperative: Add fork() event")

commit_msg:
KEYS: fix keyctl_set_reqkey_keyring() to not leak thread keyrings

This fixes CVE-2017-7472.

Running the following program as an unprivileged user exhausts kernel
memory by leaking thread keyrings:

	#include <keyutils.h>

	int main()
	{
		for (;;)
			keyctl_set_reqkey_keyring(KEY_REQKEY_DEFL_THREAD_KEYRING);
	}

Fix it by only creating a new thread keyring if there wasn't one before.
To make things more consistent, make install_thread_keyring_to_cred()
and install_process_keyring_to_cred() both return 0 if the corresponding
keyring is already present.

Fixes: d84f4f992cbd ("CRED: Inaugurate COW credentials")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # 2.6.29+
Signed-off-by: Eric Biggers <ebiggers@google.com>
Signed-off-by: David Howells <dhowells@redhat.com>
diff_func:
--- func_before
+++ func_after
@@ -1,6 +1,9 @@
 int install_thread_keyring_to_cred(struct cred *new)
 {
 	struct key *keyring;
+
+	if (new->thread_keyring)
+		return 0;
 
 	keyring = keyring_alloc("_tid", new->uid, new->gid, new,
 				KEY_POS_ALL | KEY_USR_VIEW,
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\tif (new->thread_keyring)', '\t\treturn 0;']}
description: The KEYS subsystem in the Linux kernel before 4.10.13 allows local users to cause a denial of service (memory consumption) via a series of KEY_REQKEY_DEFL_THREAD_KEYRING keyctl_set_reqkey_keyring calls.

code_evidence: The function unconditionally calls keyring_alloc() to create a new thread keyring and assigns it to new->thread_keyring without first checking whether one already exists; the added guard is absent in this version.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-404 covers failure to release or properly manage a resource across repeated paths. Here each invocation allocates a keyring that is never freed or reused, matching improper resource release leading to resource-consumption DoS; it is a resource-lifetime issue, not a bounds or type flaw.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: no check for an existing new->thread_keyring before allocating. Trigger: repeated keyctl_set_reqkey_keyring(KEY_REQKEY_DEFL_THREAD_KEYRING) calls by an unprivileged user. Consequence: each call allocates a fresh keyring that is not released, leaking kernel memory and causing DoS; the allocation is the cause, memory exhaustion the consequence.

description: Integer overflow vulnerability in function Jsi_ObjSetLength in jsish before 3.0.6, allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code.

code_evidence: Line 9 and line 18 obtain the array length through Jsi_ObjGetLength, which the commit replaces with jsi_SizeOfArray, the overflow-safe size accessor.
Line 22 iterates i from 0 to argc, where argc is the raw length from Jsi_ObjGetLength; line 24 reads each element with Jsi_ValueArrayIndex and line 32 appends its string form.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The flaw is an integer overflow in the length calculation feeding a loop bound and index access, matching CWE-190. The patch swaps in jsi_SizeOfArray to avoid the wraparound; this is not merely a bounds-check omission (CWE-125), because the corrupted length value is the root cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the array length is read via Jsi_ObjGetLength, which can return a wrapped or negative value for an oversized array. Trigger: joining an array whose length overflows the integer representation. The loop bound and per-index element access then use the corrupted length, causing out-of-bounds reads and a crash or memory corruption rather than a correctly bounded iteration.

description: OpenCV (Open Source Computer Vision Library) 3.3 has an out-of-bounds write error in the function FillColorRow1 in utils.cpp when reading an image file by using cv::imread. NOTE: this vulnerability exists because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2017-12597.

code_evidence: Line 3 computes end = data + len; the loop at line 4 advances data by 8 and writes eight bytes at data-8..data-1, so when len is not a multiple of 8 the final advance can move data past end while writes still occur at offsets that may exceed the intended buffer.

Line 16 shifts indices[0] left by 24 into a signed int, which is undefined behavior for values with the high bit set; the loop at lines 17-19 then writes data[0] for each iteration while data < end, using data -= 8 as its start.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes through data-derived pointers without bounding each write to the buffer end; the overshoot in the loop condition allows writes before/outside the intended region, matching CWE-787's out-of-bounds write. The signed shift is a separate UB issue, not the buffer-overflow cause.

evidence_lines.code:
uchar* end = data + len;
while( (data += 8) < end )

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the loop condition (data += 8) < end permits data to overshoot end before the eight in-bounds writes at data-8..data-1, and the signed shift at line 16 is undefined behavior. Trigger: a len value not divisible by 8, or an index byte with the high bit set. Consequence: writes at data-8..data-1 can fall outside the allocated buffer, corrupting memory past the intended bounds.

commit_msg:
ext4: make orphan functions be no-op in no-journal mode

Instead of checking whether the handle is valid, we check if journal
is enabled. This avoids taking the s_orphan_lock mutex in all cases
when there is no journal in use, including the error paths where
ext4_orphan_del() is called with a handle set to NULL.

Signed-off-by: Anatol Pomozov <anatol.pomozov@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: "Theodore Ts'o" <tytso@mit.edu>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t/* ext4_handle_valid() assumes a valid handle_t pointer */', '\tif (handle && !ext4_handle_valid(handle))', '\tif (sbi->s_journal && !handle)'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (!EXT4_SB(inode->i_sb)->s_journal)', '\tif (!handle)']}
description: fs/ext4/namei.c in the Linux kernel before 3.7 allows physically proximate attackers to cause a denial of service (system crash) via a crafted no-journal filesystem, a related issue to CVE-2013-2015.

code_evidence: Line 9 only short-circuits when a non-NULL handle is invalid; a NULL handle passes through to line 11, taking s_orphan_lock and continuing.
Line 19 exits only when sbi->s_journal is set and handle is NULL; with no journal (s_journal NULL) and a NULL handle, execution proceeds to line 21.
Line 21 calls ext4_reserve_inode_write(handle, inode, &iloc) with handle == NULL; on error it jumps to out_err and ext4_std_error at line 49.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function mishandles a resource (journal/transaction handle) by operating on an invalid NULL handle in the no-journal configuration, leading to a crash; this improper resource management is what CWE-399 categorizes. It is not a memory-safety bug like CWE-476 per se, but failure to guard the handle resource path.

evidence_lines.code:
if (handle && !ext4_handle_valid(handle))
return 0;

if (sbi->s_journal && !handle)
goto out;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the early-return guard in ext4_orphan_del keys off handle validity rather than journal presence, so in a no-journal filesystem a NULL handle is not filtered. Trigger: error paths call ext4_orphan_del with handle NULL while s_journal is NULL. The function then dereferences the NULL handle through ext4_reserve_inode_write and journal helpers, causing a system crash (denial of service) instead of a clean no-op.

description: The FrameLoader::startLoad function in WebKit/Source/core/loader/FrameLoader.cpp in Blink, as used in Google Chrome before 51.0.2704.79, does not prevent frame navigations during DocumentLoader detach operations, which allows remote attackers to bypass the Same Origin Policy via crafted JavaScript code.

Detaching a DocumentLoader can fire events that re-enter navigation code; nothing here prevents a frame navigation from being initiated during that detach window.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-284 fits because the missing navigation restriction during DocumentLoader detach is a failure to enforce an intended access-control policy (frame navigation/origin boundary), allowing unauthorized cross-origin access. It is broader than a pure memory-safety issue, matching the access-control enforcement failure.

detachDocumentLoader(m_provisionalDocumentLoader);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the detach of the provisional DocumentLoader proceeds while the frame remains free to start new navigations, so re-entrant JavaScript/event handlers can trigger a navigation during detach. Trigger: crafted JavaScript causing an event to fire inside detachDocumentLoader. Supported consequence: a frame navigation occurs outside the intended access-control boundary, enabling Same Origin Policy bypass as described in the commit.

commit_msg:
xfrm: fix crash in XFRM_MSG_GETSA netlink handler

If we hit any of the error conditions inside xfrm_dump_sa(), then
xfrm_state_walk_init() never gets called. However, we still call
xfrm_state_walk_done() from xfrm_dump_sa_done(), which will crash
because the state walk was never initialized properly.

We can fix this by setting cb->args[0] only after we've processed the
first element and checking this before calling xfrm_state_walk_done().

Fixes: d3623099d3 ("ipsec: add support of limited SA dump")
Cc: Nicolas Dichtel <nicolas.dichtel@6wind.com>
Cc: Steffen Klassert <steffen.klassert@secunet.com>
Signed-off-by: Vegard Nossum <vegard.nossum@oracle.com>
Acked-by: Nicolas Dichtel <nicolas.dichtel@6wind.com>
Signed-off-by: Steffen Klassert <steffen.klassert@secunet.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tcb->args[0] = 1;', ''], 'added_lines': ['\t\tcb->args[0] = 1;']}
description: A NULL pointer dereference vulnerability was found in netlink_dump. This issue can occur when the Netlink socket receives the message(sendmsg) for the XFRM_MSG_GETSA, XFRM_MSG_GETPOLICY type message, and the DUMP flag is set and can cause a denial of service or possibly another unspecified impact. Due to the nature of the flaw, privilege escalation cannot be fully ruled out, although it is unlikely.

code_evidence: At line 12 the first-dump branch is entered when cb->args[0] is zero; line 17 sets cb->args[0] = 1 before any parsing or walk initialization occurs. If nlmsg_parse fails at line 18, line 21 returns err with cb->args[0] still 1 but xfrm_state_walk_init at line 30 never executed, leaving walk (aliased to cb->args[1] at line 4) uninitialized. The filter allocation failure at line 26 and the early return path likewise leave the walk uninitialized while args[0] already marks it as initialized.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The flaw yields a dereference of an uninitialized/NULL pointer in the dump-done path, matching CWE-476 (NULL Pointer Dereference). It is a state-ordering bug rather than a missing bounds check or type confusion, so the NULL-dereference label is the direct fit.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the initialized flag cb->args[0] is set before xfrm_state_walk_init() succeeds, so parse/attribute errors return early with the flag set but the walk structure still zero/uninitialized. Trigger: a malformed XFRM_MSG_GETSA dump request causing nlmsg_parse to fail; the subsequent xfrm_dump_sa_done path then uses the uninitialized walk, leading to a NULL/invalid pointer dereference and kernel crash (DoS).

commit_msg: Guard binary expressions from too much recursion.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tSAVEREC();', '\tINCREC();', '\tPOPREC();']}
description: jsparse.c in Artifex MuJS through 1.0.2 does not properly maintain the AST depth for binary expressions, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (excessive recursion) via a crafted file.

code_evidence: additive() builds a left-associative binary expression by looping with goto, calling multiplicative(J) and EXP2(ADD/SUB, ...) on each iteration. There is no depth counter or recursion limit around this loop, so a crafted input with a long chain of '+'/'-' operators drives unbounded parser recursion via multiplicative().
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-674 fits because the function's missing depth constraint lets recursion grow with input, consuming the program stack and causing a DoS; this is uncontrolled recursion, not merely a resource leak or memory corruption.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the parser does not track or bound AST/recursion depth while consuming a chain of additive operators, so each operator triggers a fresh multiplicative() descent. Trigger: a crafted file with many consecutive binary operators. Consequence: excessive stack consumption leading to denial of service (crash).

commit_msg:
Fix a padding oracle in PKCS7_dataDecode and CMS_decrypt_set1_pkey

An attack is simple, if the first CMS_recipientInfo is valid but the
second CMS_recipientInfo is chosen ciphertext. If the second
recipientInfo decodes to PKCS #1 v1.5 form plaintext, the correct
encryption key will be replaced by garbage, and the message cannot be
decoded, but if the RSA decryption fails, the correct encryption key is
used and the recipient will not notice the attack.

As a work around for this potential attack the length of the decrypted
key must be equal to the cipher default key length, in case the
certifiate is not given and all recipientInfo are tried out.

The old behaviour can be re-enabled in the CMS code by setting the
CMS_DEBUG_DECRYPT flag.

Reviewed-by: Matt Caswell <matt@openssl.org>
(Merged from https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/9777)

(cherry picked from commit 5840ed0cd1e6487d247efbc1a04136a41d7b3a37)

description: In situations where an attacker receives automated notification of the success or failure of a decryption attempt an attacker, after sending a very large number of messages to be decrypted, can recover a CMS/PKCS7 transported encryption key or decrypt any RSA encrypted message that was encrypted with the public RSA key, using a Bleichenbacher padding oracle attack. Applications are not affected if they use a certificate together with the private RSA key to the CMS_decrypt or PKCS7_decrypt functions to select the correct recipient info to decrypt. Fixed in OpenSSL 1.1.1d (Affected 1.1.1-1.1.1c). Fixed in OpenSSL 1.1.0l (Affected 1.1.0-1.1.0k). Fixed in OpenSSL 1.0.2t (Affected 1.0.2-1.0.2s).

commit_msg:
arm32: handle async aborts delivered while at HYP

If guest generates an asynchronous abort and then traps into HYP
(by HVC or IRQ) before the abort has been delivered, the hypervisor
could not catch it, because the PSTATE.A bit is masked all the time
in hypervisor. So this asynchronous abort may be slipped to next
running guest with PSTATE.A bit unmasked.

In order to avoid this, it is necessary to take the abort at HYP, by
clearing the PSTATE.A bit. In this patch, we unmask the PSTATE.A bit
to open a window to catch guest-generated asynchronous abort in all
Guest -> HYP switch paths. If we caught such asynchronous abort in
checking window, the HYP data abort exception will be triggered and
the abort source guest will be crashed.

This is part of XSA-201.

Signed-off-by: Wei Chen <Wei.Chen@arm.com>
Reviewed-by: Julien Grall <julien.grall@arm.com>
Acked-by: Stefano Stabellini <sstabellini@kernel.org>

description:
A heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the Linux kernel's Performance Events system component can be exploited to achieve local privilege escalation.

A perf_event's read_size can overflow, leading to an heap out-of-bounds increment or write in perf_read_group().

We recommend upgrading past commit 382c27f4ed28f803b1f1473ac2d8db0afc795a1b.

code_evidence: The function computes event->read_size via __perf_event_read_size(event, group_leader->nr_siblings + 1), then adds read_size + header_size + id_header_size + sizeof(struct perf_event_header) and rejects only if the total >= 16*1024. It validates only the newly added event's sizes, never recomputing the read_size of existing siblings whose read_format may differ, so a group whose combined sizes overflow the limit passes validation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the unchecked size overflow produces a write past the intended heap buffer during group read. The defect is a missing size constraint (incomplete validation), and the supported consequence is an out-of-bounds write, not merely an integer overflow.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: validation is scoped to the single new event while group read_size depends on all siblings' read_format. Trigger: attach an event to a group containing siblings with different read_format, causing the group's total read_size to exceed the 64k record limit after perf_group_attach() recomputes sizes. Consequence: read_size overflow leads to heap out-of-bounds increment/write in perf_read_group().

commit_msg:
lvmetad: fix heap memory leak

error could be reproduced by calling pvs periodically:
    #!/bin/bash
    while :
    do
        pvs
        sleep 1
    done

use top command to watch RES memory of lvmetad. After a few minutes,
its RES memory will grow for a few KB. Then stop calling pvs, while
its RES will not decrease.

This is because, when lvmetad make reponse for clent request, it
will malloc new chunk for s->vgid_to_metadata, while actually the
new chunk should be added to the reponse dm_config_tree, or it will
make the chunk list of s->vgid_to_metadata keep growing.

Signed-off-by: wangjufeng <wangjufeng@huawei.com>
Reviewed-by: liuzhiqiang <liuzhiqiang26@huawei.com>
Reviewed-by: guiyao <guiyao@huawei.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (!(n->v = dm_config_create_value(cft)))'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (!(n->v = dm_config_create_value(res.cft)))']}
description: vg_lookup in daemons/lvmetad/lvmetad-core.c in LVM2 2.02 mismanages memory, leading to an lvmetad memory leak, as demonstrated by running pvs. NOTE: RedHat disputes CVE-2020-8991 as not being a vulnerability since there’s no apparent route to either privilege escalation or to denial of service through the bug

code_evidence: res.cft is created via dm_config_create() at line 47; the response config node n is created under res.cft at line 49. At line 51 the value node is created with dm_config_create_value(cft), where cft is the cached metadata tree from s->vgid_to_metadata (line 42), not res.cft. This attaches the allocated value to the wrong config tree, so the response's ownership chain does not include it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-401 fits because memory allocated for the value node is not tracked by the response tree that is later freed, leaving it attached to a long-lived cached tree and never released. This is a missing-release ownership bug, not a use-after-free or double free.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: dm_config_create_value is passed the cached metadata tree cft instead of the newly created response tree res.cft, so each vg_lookup call allocates a value chunk owned by s->vgid_to_metadata. Trigger: repeated client requests (e.g., periodic pvs). Consequence: the metadata tree's chunk list grows without bound and the memory is never released, an unbounded memory leak.

commit_msg:
Preserve GSS context on init/accept failure

After gss_init_sec_context() or gss_accept_sec_context() has created a
context, don't delete the mechglue context on failures from subsequent
calls, even if the mechanism deletes the mech-specific context (which
is allowed by RFC 2744 but not preferred).  Check for union contexts
with no mechanism context in each GSS function which accepts a
gss_ctx_id_t.

CVE-2017-11462:

RFC 2744 permits a GSS-API implementation to delete an existing
security context on a second or subsequent call to
gss_init_sec_context() or gss_accept_sec_context() if the call results
in an error.  This API behavior has been found to be dangerous,
leading to the possibility of memory errors in some callers.  For
safety, GSS-API implementations should instead preserve existing
security contexts on error until the caller deletes them.

All versions of MIT krb5 prior to this change may delete acceptor
contexts on error.  Versions 1.13.4 through 1.13.7, 1.14.1 through
1.14.5, and 1.15 through 1.15.1 may also delete initiator contexts on
error.

description: The cdxl_decode_frame function in libavcodec/cdxl.c in FFmpeg 2.8.x before 2.8.12, 3.0.x before 3.0.8, 3.1.x before 3.1.8, 3.2.x before 3.2.5, and 3.3.x before 3.3.1 does not exclude the CHUNKY format, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (heap-based buffer overflow and application crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted file.

commit_msg:
arm64: KVM: pmu: Fix AArch32 cycle counter access

We're missing the handling code for the cycle counter accessed
from a 32bit guest, leading to unexpected results.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # 4.6+
Signed-off-by: Wei Huang <wei@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Marc Zyngier <marc.zyngier@arm.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\tBUG();', '\t\tBUG();'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\treturn false;', '\t} else if (r->CRn == 0 && r->CRm == 9) {', '\t\t/* PMCCNTR */', '\t\tif (pmu_access_event_counter_el0_disabled(vcpu))', '\t\t\treturn false;', '', '\t\tidx = ARMV8_PMU_CYCLE_IDX;', '\t\treturn false;']}
description: The access_pmu_evcntr function in arch/arm64/kvm/sys_regs.c in the Linux kernel before 4.8.11 allows privileged KVM guest OS users to cause a denial of service (assertion failure and host OS crash) by accessing the Performance Monitors Cycle Count Register (PMCCNTR).

code_evidence: The else branch for r->CRn==9 && r->CRm==13 with an unexpected Op2 value (not 2 or 0) unconditionally executes BUG().
The final else branch for any register encoding other than CRn==9/CRm==13 or CRn==14/CRm&12==8 also unconditionally executes BUG().
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function contains BUG() assertions reachable via attacker-controlled guest register encodings, and the fix replaces them with return false, exactly matching CWE-617 (reachable assertion causing crash). It is distinct from a memory-safety issue: the defect is the assertion itself, not the counter value handling.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function dispatches on guest-controlled system-register fields (CRn, CRm, Op2) and calls BUG() on unrecognized encodings instead of returning false. A privileged KVM guest can issue a PMCCNTR access whose encoding (e.g., CRn==0/CRm==9) falls through to the else branch, triggering the assertion. Consequence: the BUG() aborts the host kernel, a denial of service, rather than returning a trap response to the guest.

commit_msg:
The path prefix check can be circumvented by regular users by passing
relative path component like so:

$ dbus-send --system --print-reply --dest=org.freedesktop.Accounts \
        /org/freedesktop/Accounts/User1000 \
        org.freedesktop.Accounts.User.SetIconFile \
        string:/usr/share/../../tmp/test

This results in a user controlled path being stored in the
accountsservice. Clients of accountsservice may unwittingly trust this
path.

To fix that situation this commit canonicalizes the input path before
the prefix comparison.

Some small changes to patch by Ray Strode.

https://bugs.freedesktop.org/show_bug.cgi?id=107085

--- func_before
+++ func_after
@@ -34,6 +34,14 @@
         }
 
         file = g_file_new_for_path (filename);
+        g_clear_pointer (&filename, g_free);
+
+        /* Canonicalize path so we can call g_str_has_prefix on it
+         * below without concern for ../ path components moving outside
+         * the prefix
+         */
+        filename = g_file_get_path (file);
+
         info = g_file_query_info (file, G_FILE_ATTRIBUTE_UNIX_MODE ","
                                         G_FILE_ATTRIBUTE_STANDARD_TYPE ","

description: Directory Traversal with ../ sequences occurs in AccountsService before 0.6.50 because of an insufficient path check in user_change_icon_file_authorized_cb() in user.c.

code_evidence: The user-supplied filename is wrapped in a GFile (line 29) but the prefix check at lines 48-49 runs g_str_has_prefix on the raw filename string, not on any canonicalized path. A value such as /usr/share/../../tmp/test passes the DATADIR prefix test while resolving outside it.
When the prefix check is bypassed, the raw filename is passed as argv[1] to /bin/cat (lines 71-75), which reads the traversed path as the caller and splices its contents into the icon output stream.

The mode/readability gate at line 47 and the copy path at lines 86-87 store the resulting path via accounts_user_set_icon_file (line 90), so a user-controlled path escapes the intended ICONDIR/DATADIR restriction.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This is exactly CWE-22: external input constructs a pathname intended to stay under a restricted parent, but '..' elements are not neutralized, letting it resolve outside. The commit's fix canonicalizes the path before the prefix comparison, confirming the uncanonicalized check is the weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the restricted-directory check compares the uncanonicalized filename against DATADIR/ICONDIR with g_str_has_prefix, so embedded '../' components are not neutralized. Trigger: an authorized caller submits a path with a valid prefix followed by '../' sequences. Consequence: the prefix check passes and the traversed file is read and its path stored, allowing access outside the restricted directory.

description: In radare2 2.5.0, there is a heap-based buffer over-read in the r_hex_bin2str function (libr/util/hex.c). Remote attackers could leverage this vulnerability to cause a denial of service via a crafted DEX file. This issue is different from CVE-2017-15368.

commit_msg:
Fix SRI bypass by loading same resource twice in same origin.

This fixes a bug where the memory cache was bypassing subresource
integrity checks when a resource is loaded for a second time in the same
origin. The resource in the memory cache was correctly storing that an
integrity check had already been done so whene it was retrieved later,
it wouldn't need to be checked again, but it didn't store the fact that
this was a *failure*, so when the load happened a second time, it
assumed it was a good integrity.

This modifies the resources to store a disposition for the integrity
check, rather than just that the integrity check occurred. On a reload
of the resource, if the integrity had failed the first time, the
resource will fail to load.

BUG=584155

Review URL: https://codereview.chromium.org/1675183003

Cr-Commit-Position: refs/heads/master@{#374336}
(cherry picked from commit bf24693238d407f90bec71453b18aae8dd1c0f43)

Review URL: https://codereview.chromium.org/1713093002 .

Cr-Commit-Position: refs/branch-heads/2623@{#452}
Cr-Branched-From: 92d77538a86529ca35f9220bd3cd512cbea1f086-refs/heads/master@{#369907}
