commit_msg:
sunrpc: Avoid use-after-free read access in clntudp_call [BZ #21115]

After commit bc779a1a5b3035133024b21e2f339fe4219fb11c
(CVE-2016-4429: sunrpc: Do not use alloca in clntudp_call
[BZ #20112]), ancillary data is stored on the heap,
but it is accessed after it has been freed.

The test case must be run under a heap debugger such as valgrind
to observe the invalid access.  A malloc implementation which
immediately calls munmap on free would catch this bug as well.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t  free (cbuf);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t  free (cbuf);']}
description: Use-after-free vulnerability in the clntudp_call function in sunrpc/clnt_udp.c in the GNU C Library (aka glibc or libc6) before 2.26 allows remote attackers to have unspecified impact via vectors related to error path.

code_evidence: At line 136 cbuf is freed, then lines 137-138 read CMSG_DATA(cmsg) and e->ee_errno; cmsg points into the control buffer cbuf (msg.msg_control = cbuf at line 119), so this dereferences freed memory.

cbuf is malloc'd at line 105 and used as msg.msg_control with length 256 at lines 119-120; __recvmsg fills it, and the loop at lines 132-135 iterates cmsgs within that buffer before the free at line 136.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The code dereferences a pointer (e->ee_errno via CMSG_DATA(cmsg)) into memory already released by free(cbuf), which is exactly CWE-416 Use After Free. This is not a double free or leak; the defect is post-free read access.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the IP_RECVERR branch frees the heap control buffer cbuf before reading the extended error record that resides inside it. Trigger: a POLLERR on the RPC socket with a matching MSG_ERRQUEUE reply causes CMSG_DATA(cmsg) to be dereferenced after free. Supported consequence is an invalid read of freed heap memory (use-after-free).

commit_msg:
Fix size check for large input shape and rates.

To address a check failure for exceedingly large output shapes, we need to
`AppendShapeWithStatus`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 462885894
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    samples_shape.AppendShape(rate_t.shape());'], 'added_lines': ['    OP_REQUIRES_OK(ctx, samples_shape.AppendShapeWithStatus(rate_t.shape()));']}
description: TensorFlow is an open source platform for machine learning. When `RandomPoissonV2` receives large input shape and rates, it gives a `CHECK` fail that can trigger a denial of service attack. We have patched the issue in GitHub commit 552bfced6ce4809db5f3ca305f60ff80dd40c5a3. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.10.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.9.1, TensorFlow 2.8.1, and TensorFlow 2.7.2, as these are also affected and still in supported range. There are no known workarounds for this issue.

code_evidence: The function builds samples_shape from the user-supplied shape input via tensor::MakeShape, then appends rate_t.shape() using AppendShape. AppendShape internally CHECK-fails on shape overflow or invalid dimensions rather than returning a status, so an exceedingly large input shape combined with a large rate shape can trigger a fatal CHECK.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The failure is a reachable assertion/CHECK in TensorFlow's shape handling triggered by attacker-controlled input, matching CWE-617. The patch replaces AppendShape with AppendShapeWithStatus to return an error instead of aborting, confirming the assertion-based crash.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: unchecked shape combination using AppendShape, which aborts on overflow instead of propagating an error. Trigger: attacker supplies very large shape and rate tensors so samples_shape.AppendShape(rate_t.shape()) encounters an invalid/overflowing dimension. Consequence: process abort (CHECK failure), enabling denial of service.

commit_msg: [FG-VD-19-136] ImageMagick Convert SVG MacOS Denial Of Service
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      (void) xmlCtxtUseOptions(svg_info->parser,XML_PARSE_HUGE);'], 'added_lines': ['      const char', '        *value;', '', '      value=GetImageOption(image_info,"svg:xml-parse-huge");', '      if ((value != (char *) NULL) && (IsStringTrue(value) != MagickFalse))', '        (void) xmlCtxtUseOptions(svg_info->parser,XML_PARSE_HUGE);']}
description: ImageMagick before 7.0.9-0 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service because XML_PARSE_HUGE is not properly restricted in coders/svg.c, related to SVG and libxml2.

code_evidence: Creates a libxml2 push parser context and unconditionally enables XML_PARSE_HUGE, which removes libxml2's default limits on document size and recursion depth.
The parser is then fed attacker-controlled chunks via xmlParseChunk in a loop, so the unlimited parser processes the entire supplied SVG document.
The parser context is finalized with xmlParseChunk(...,0,1) and SVGEndDocument; nested/recursive entity or element structures in the input are parsed without depth limits.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-674 fits because the parser performs recursion driven by attacker-controlled nesting with no bound, causing resource exhaustion. The missing constraint (depth limit) is the cause; the DoS is the consequence. This is uncontrolled recursion, not merely oversized allocation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the code enables XML_PARSE_HUGE with no depth or size restriction, disabling libxml2's recursion and entity limits. Trigger: an attacker supplies an SVG with deeply nested or recursive structures so the libxml2 parser recurses without bound. Consequence: excessive stack/memory consumption leading to a denial of service (crash or hang).

commit_msg:
Patched DoS vulnerability CVE-2022-41985 / TALOS-2022-1680. Fixed bug
within FTPs_Init() that could cause an invalid socket ID to be pased to
the FTPs Server Task.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            if (ftp_session.CtrlState == FTPs_STATE_LOGOUT) {'], 'added_lines': ['            if (ftp_session.CtrlState != FTPs_STATE_LOGIN) {']}
description: An authentication bypass vulnerability exists in the Authentication functionality of Weston Embedded uC-FTPs v 1.98.00. A specially crafted set of network packets can lead to authentication bypass and denial of service. An attacker can send a sequence of unauthenticated packets to trigger this vulnerability.

code_evidence: After command lookup, line 94 checks whether the command is disallowed in the current context. On the pre-patch path, line 95 only treats FTPs_STATE_LOGOUT as 'not logged in'; any other non-LOGIN state falls to line 98, which sends a bad-sequence reply and then sets ftp_session.CtrlState = FTPs_STATE_LOGIN at line 99. This lets a context-rejected command force the session into the authenticated state without any credential verification.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-287 fits because the function grants the authenticated LOGIN state without proving identity; the state flag is set by a rejected command rather than by credential validation. This is an authentication-state flaw, not merely a bad command sequence or generic DoS.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the context check conflates 'not logged in' with only the LOGOUT state and assigns LOGIN in the else branch. Trigger: an unauthenticated client sends a command whose CmdCntxt entry is DEF_OFF while CtrlState is not LOGOUT. Consequence: CtrlState becomes FTPs_STATE_LOGIN, so later commands pass the context gate and are processed as authenticated, enabling bypass and denial of service via the control task.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tpriv->set->use++;'], 'added_lines': ['\tnf_tables_activate_set(ctx, priv->set);']}
description: In the Linux kernel through 6.3.1, a use-after-free in Netfilter nf_tables when processing batch requests can be abused to perform arbitrary read and write operations on kernel memory. Unprivileged local users can obtain root privileges. This occurs because anonymous sets are mishandled.

code_evidence: nft_objref_map_activate() obtains the bound set via priv->set and directly increments priv->set->use, which only bumps the reference count and does not reactivate the set in the current generation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function operates on priv->set without ensuring the set is still live in the current generation, allowing subsequent operations to reference freed set memory. This matches CWE-416 (Use After Free); it is not merely a reference-count leak, since the missing activation leads to reuse of freed memory.

evidence_lines.code:
struct nft_objref_map *priv = nft_expr_priv(expr);
priv->set->use++;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the activate path only increments the set's use counter instead of calling nf_tables_activate_set(), so a bound anonymous set that was deactivated/deleted in the same transaction is not properly reactivated. Trigger: a batch transaction that removes the anonymous set and then performs an element update on it. Consequence: the stale set reference is used after it has been freed, yielding use-after-free reads/writes on kernel memory.

commit_msg:
Default initialize fixed point Eigen types.

In certain cases, tensors are filled with default values of the type. But, for these fixed point types, these values were uninitialized. Thus, we would have uninitialized memory access bugs, some of which were caught by MSAN.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 344101137
Change-Id: I14555fda74dca3b5f1582da9008901937e3f14e2
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['QInt16() {}'], 'added_lines': ['QInt16() : value(0) {}']}
description: In affected versions of TensorFlow under certain cases a saved model can trigger use of uninitialized values during code execution. This is caused by having tensor buffers be filled with the default value of the type but forgetting to default initialize the quantized floating point types in Eigen. This is fixed in versions 1.15.5, 2.0.4, 2.1.3, 2.2.2, 2.3.2, and 2.4.0.

code_evidence: The QInt16 default constructor body is empty and does not initialize its value member, so a default-constructed QInt16 leaves the underlying storage uninitialized.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-908 (Use of Uninitialized Resource) fits because the constructor creates an object whose resource (the value member) is never initialized, and later use reads that uninitialized memory. This is distinct from an out-of-bounds or type-confusion issue; the defect is the missing initialization itself.

evidence_lines.code: QInt16() {}

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the default constructor fails to initialize the value member. Trigger: code default-constructs QInt16 (e.g., when tensor buffers are filled with the type's default value). Consequence: subsequent reads of the object access uninitialized memory, producing indeterminate values and MSAN-detectable uninitialized memory reads.

commit_msg:
* src/type1/t1parse.c (T1_Get_Private_Dict): Assure `cur' doesn't
point to end of file buffer.

description: In FreeType before 2.6.1, a buffer over-read occurs in type1/t1parse.c on function T1_Get_Private_Dict where there is no check that the new values of cur and limit are sensible before going to Again.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tif (!N) {', '\t\t/* No program? */', '\t\tret = -EINVAL;', '\t\tparse_error(pe, FILT_ERR_NO_FILTER, ptr - str);', '\t\tgoto out_free;', '\t}', '']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel through 4.17.2. The filter parsing in kernel/trace/trace_events_filter.c could be called with no filter, which is an N=0 case when it expected at least one line to have been read, thus making the N-1 index invalid. This allows attackers to cause a denial of service (slab out-of-bounds write) or possibly have unspecified other impact via crafted perf_event_open and mmap system calls.

code_evidence: After the parse loop, the code unconditionally indexes prog[N] and prog[N+1] and writes prog[N-1] without verifying N>0. N is initialized to 0 at line 15 and only incremented inside the while(*ptr) loop; an empty filter string leaves ptr pointing at the NUL, so the loop body never runs and N remains 0. At line 115 prog[0] is written, at 117 prog[1], and line 119 writes prog[-1], a negative index before the allocated prog_stack buffer. The subsequent loop at line 121 uses N-1 as the start index, and line 129 compares prog[i].target <= i with i underflowing.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the function writes through prog[N-1] with N=0, i.e., before the allocated prog_stack array, and indexes prog[N+1] beyond the parsed region; the missing N>0 check directly causes an out-of-bounds write. A mere NULL/invalid-pointer dereference (CWE-476) is not the issue since prog is valid; the defect is the unchecked index.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the parser assumes at least one predicate was parsed but never checks N before computing prog[N-1] and prog[N+1]. Trigger: a caller passes an empty/no filter string so the parse loop is skipped and N stays 0. Consequence: writes at prog[-1] and prog[0..1] occur outside the intended element range, yielding a slab out-of-bounds write (memory corruption / DoS).

offset++ and len-- after reading pad, so a len==0 input underflows len (guint32) to a huge value.

if ((pad == 0) && (len == 1)) {

offset++;
len--;

[tflite] Ensure inputs and outputs don't overlap.

If a model uses the same tensor for both an input and an output then this can result in data loss and memory corruption. This should not happen.

it is assuming that the event has fixed size and gives the swapping function
xEvent-sized buffer.

A GenericEvent would be later rejected by ProcXSendExtensionEvent anyway.

Reviewed-by: Peter Hutterer <peter.hutterer@who-t.net>

commit_msg:
openssl: associate/detach the transfer from connection

CVE-2021-22901

Bug: https://curl.se/docs/CVE-2021-22901.html
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  Curl_ssl_associate_conn(data, conn);']}
description: curl 7.75.0 through 7.76.1 suffers from a use-after-free vulnerability resulting in already freed memory being used when a TLS 1.3 session ticket arrives over a connection. A malicious server can use this in rare unfortunate circumstances to potentially reach remote code execution in the client. When libcurl at run-time sets up support for TLS 1.3 session tickets on a connection using OpenSSL, it stores pointers to the transfer in-memory object for later retrieval when a session ticket arrives. If the connection is used by multiple transfers (like with a reused HTTP/1.1 connection or multiplexed HTTP/2 connection) that first transfer object might be freed before the new session is established on that connection and then the function will access a memory buffer that might be freed. When using that memory, libcurl might even call a function pointer in the object, making it possible for a remote code execution if the server could somehow manage to get crafted memory content into the correct place in memory.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The shown function only attaches a transfer to a connection and registers it in the connection's easyq; it contains no free, pointer retention across free, or later dereference of freed memory, so CWE-416 use-after-free is not directly evidenced in this code.

buffer protected by a spinlock. This is broken as the USB HID request
callbacks can sleep. Fix this up by replacing the spinlock with a mutex.

commit_msg:
Revised handling of TIFFTAG_INKNAMES and related TIFFTAG_NUMBEROFINKS value

In order to solve the buffer overflow issues related to TIFFTAG_INKNAMES and related TIFFTAG_NUMBEROFINKS value, a revised handling of those tags within LibTiff is proposed:

Behaviour for writing:
    `NumberOfInks`  MUST fit to the number of inks in the `InkNames` string.
    `NumberOfInks` is automatically set when `InkNames` is set.
    If `NumberOfInks` is different to the number of inks within `InkNames` string, that will be corrected and a warning is issued.
    If `NumberOfInks` is not equal to samplesperpixel only a warning will be issued.

Behaviour for reading:
    When reading `InkNames` from a TIFF file, the `NumberOfInks` will be set automatically to the number of inks in `InkNames` string.
    If `NumberOfInks` is different to the number of inks within `InkNames` string, that will be corrected and a warning is issued.
    If  `NumberOfInks` is not equal to samplesperpixel only a warning will be issued.

This allows the safe use of the NumberOfInks value to read out the InkNames without buffer overflow

This MR will close the following issues:  #149, #150, #152, #168 (to be checked), #250, #269, #398 and #456.

It also fixes the old bug at http://bugzilla.maptools.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2599, for which the limitation of `NumberOfInks = SPP` was introduced, which is in my opinion not necessary and does not solve the general issue.

description: A vulnerability was found in the libtiff library. This flaw causes a heap buffer overflow issue via the TIFFTAG_INKNAMES and TIFFTAG_NUMBEROFINKS values.

code_evidence: The InkNames printing block iterates with i = td->td_samplesperpixel (line 153) rather than the number of inks, and advances cp via strchr(cp,'\0')+1 (line 157). If the ink names string lacks enough NUL separators, strchr returns NULL and the +1 yields an invalid pointer; the loop condition cp < td->td_inknames + td->td_inknameslen (line 156) is then evaluated on an out-of-bounds pointer. The bounded print computes max_chars = td->td_inknameslen - (cp - td->td_inknames) (lines 158-159), which underflows if cp has moved past the buffer end, so _TIFFprintAsciiBounded (line 161) reads/writes past the intended buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the unterminated/over-advanced pointer combined with the underflowed max_chars causes the print routine to operate past the end of the allocated ink names buffer, an out-of-bounds write/read. This is distinct from a mere integer overflow: the buffer-boundary violation is the direct weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the loop count is tied to samplesperpixel and the pointer advances without verifying a NUL was found, so cp can move beyond the ink names buffer. Trigger: a crafted TIFF where InkNames contains fewer NUL separators than samplesperpixel. Consequence: out-of-bounds pointer arithmetic and an underflowing length passed to the bounded printer, enabling a heap buffer overflow/over-read.

commit_msg:
net: e1000e: fix an infinite loop issue

This issue is like the issue in e1000 network card addressed in
this commit:
e1000: eliminate infinite loops on out-of-bounds transfer start.

Signed-off-by: Li Qiang <liqiang6-s@360.cn>
Reviewed-by: Dmitry Fleytman <dmitry@daynix.com>
Signed-off-by: Jason Wang <jasowang@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    return core->mac[r->dh] == core->mac[r->dt];'], 'added_lines': ['    return core->mac[r->dh] == core->mac[r->dt] ||', '                core->mac[r->dt] >= core->mac[r->dlen] / E1000_RING_DESC_LEN;']}
description: QEMU (aka Quick Emulator), when built with the e1000e NIC emulation support, allows local guest OS privileged users to cause a denial of service (infinite loop) via vectors related to setting the initial receive / transmit descriptor head (TDH/RDH) outside the allocated descriptor buffer.

code_evidence: The ring-empty predicate returns true only when the head (r->dh) equals the tail (r->dt); it never checks whether r->dt lies outside the allocated descriptor buffer. If a privileged guest sets RDH/TDH outside the buffer, the equality test can fail indefinitely while callers keep looping over the ring, so the exit condition is never satisfied.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-835 fits because the unchecked descriptor index makes the ring-empty exit condition unreachable, producing an infinite loop. This is not merely an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125): the supported consequence is the non-terminating iteration driven by the missing bound check.

evidence_lines.code: return core->mac[r->dh] == core->mac[r->dt];

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the loop-exit predicate lacks a bound check on the descriptor tail/head against r->dlen. Trigger: guest sets the initial RDH/TDH outside the allocated descriptor buffer. Consequence: callers such as the e1000e transmit/receive loops spin forever, consuming CPU and causing a denial of service.

commit_msg:
Fix type confusion in nc_match_single()

This function assumes that if the "gen" is an OtherName, then the "base"
is a rfc822Name constraint. This assumption is not true in all cases.
If the end-entity certificate contains an OtherName SAN of any type besides
SmtpUtf8Mailbox and the CA certificate contains a name constraint of
OtherName (of any type), then "nc_email_eai" will be invoked, with the
OTHERNAME "base" being incorrectly interpreted as a ASN1_IA5STRING.

Reported by Corey Bonnell from Digicert.

description:
A read buffer overrun can be triggered in X.509 certificate verification,
specifically in name constraint checking. Note that this occurs
after certificate chain signature verification and requires either a
CA to have signed the malicious certificate or for the application to
continue certificate verification despite failure to construct a path
to a trusted issuer.

The read buffer overrun might result in a crash which could lead to
a denial of service attack. In theory it could also result in the disclosure
of private memory contents (such as private keys, or sensitive plaintext)
although we are not aware of any working exploit leading to memory
contents disclosure as of the time of release of this advisory.

In a TLS client, this can be triggered by connecting to a malicious
server. In a TLS server, this can be triggered if the server requests
client authentication and a malicious client connects.

code_evidence: When gen->type is GEN_OTHERNAME, the code unconditionally calls nc_email_eai(gen->d.otherName->value, base->d.rfc822Name) without checking that base is actually a rfc822Name/email constraint. base->d.rfc822Name is thus interpreted as an ASN1_IA5STRING regardless of base's real GENERAL_NAME type.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked union-member reinterpretation causes a buffer to be read with the wrong type/length, producing a read past the intended buffer, which is CWE-125. The type confusion is the mechanism; the memory over-read is the supported weakness outcome.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the GEN_OTHERNAME branch assumes base is an email constraint and reads base->d.rfc822Name as an IA5STRING. Trigger: an OtherName SAN of a type other than SmtpUtf8Mailbox combined with an OtherName name constraint, causing nc_email_eai to process a mismatched union member. Supported consequence: out-of-bounds read during name-constraint checking, leading to crash/DoS or potential memory disclosure.

commit_msg:
ALSA: pcm: Move rwsem lock inside snd_ctl_elem_read to prevent UAF

Takes rwsem lock inside snd_ctl_elem_read instead of snd_ctl_elem_read_user
like it was done for write in commit 1fa4445f9adf1 ("ALSA: control - introduce
snd_ctl_notify_one() helper"). Doing this way we are also fixing the following
locking issue happening in the compat path which can be easily triggered and
turned into an use-after-free.

64-bits:
snd_ctl_ioctl
  snd_ctl_elem_read_user
    [takes controls_rwsem]
    snd_ctl_elem_read [lock properly held, all good]
    [drops controls_rwsem]

32-bits:
snd_ctl_ioctl_compat
  snd_ctl_elem_write_read_compat
    ctl_elem_write_read
      snd_ctl_elem_read [missing lock, not good]

CVE-2023-0266 was assigned for this issue.

Cc: stable@kernel.org # 5.13+
Signed-off-by: Clement Lecigne <clecigne@google.com>
Reviewed-by: Jaroslav Kysela <perex@perex.cz>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20230113120745.25464-1-tiwai@suse.de
Signed-off-by: Takashi Iwai <tiwai@suse.de>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tdown_read(&card->controls_rwsem);', '\tup_read(&card->controls_rwsem);'], 'added_lines': []}
description: A use after free vulnerability exists in the ALSA PCM package in the Linux Kernel. SNDRV_CTL_IOCTL_ELEM_{READ|WRITE}32 is missing locks that can be used in a use-after-free that can result in a priviledge escalation to gain ring0 access from the system user. We recommend upgrading past commit 56b88b50565cd8b946a2d00b0c83927b7ebb055e

code_evidence: snd_ctl_elem_read_user takes down_read(&card->controls_rwsem), calls snd_ctl_elem_read(card, control), then releases the lock before returning; the lock scope brackets the read call itself.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The reported consequence is reuse of freed control memory through an unlocked read path, which is CWE-416. This is a locking/serialization defect enabling UAF, not merely a race or info leak, so CWE-416 is the appropriate target.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is lock placement: the controls_rwsem is held only around snd_ctl_elem_read here, while the compat path ctl_elem_write_read reaches snd_ctl_elem_read without taking the lock. That missing serialization lets a control be freed concurrently while the read still dereferences it, producing a use-after-free (CVE-2023-0266). The patch moves locking inside snd_ctl_elem_read so every caller is covered.

description: The php_wddx_push_element function in ext/wddx/wddx.c in PHP before 5.6.26 and 7.x before 7.0.11 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (invalid pointer access and out-of-bounds read) or possibly have unspecified other impact via an incorrect boolean element in a wddxPacket XML document, leading to mishandling in a wddx_deserialize call.

code_evidence: In the EL_CHAR branch, the loop condition atts[i] is evaluated, then atts[++i] pre-increments i inside the strcmp guard; when the attribute value is missing, atts[i] after the increment may point past the NULL terminator, and strtol/strlen then read past the attribute array.
The EL_BOOLEAN branch uses the same atts[++i] pattern and passes atts[i] to php_wddx_process_data with strlen(atts[i]), so a boolean element lacking a value attribute reads out of bounds.
The EL_VAR branch duplicates the pre-increment and estrdup(atts[i]) copies the out-of-range pointer.
The EL_FIELD branch similarly uses atts[++i] and passes atts[i] into zend_hash_find with strlen(atts[i])+1, reading beyond the attribute array.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-119 fits because the code reads memory outside the bounds of the atts pointer array due to the pre-increment exceeding the terminator. This is a bounds violation on a memory buffer rather than a separate logic flaw; the missing bound check on i directly enables the out-of-bounds read.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The loop checks atts[i] before the strcmp guard, but the guard's atts[++i] advances i past the terminating NULL when the named attribute is the last entry. Subsequent atts[i][0], strtol, strlen, estrdup and zend_hash_find then dereference the out-of-bounds slot, causing an invalid pointer access/out-of-bounds read on attacker-controlled wddxPacket XML during wddx_deserialize.

commit_msg:
Bug 767873 - (CVE-2016-4994) Multiple Use-After-Free when parsing...

...XCF channel and layer properties

The properties PROP_ACTIVE_LAYER, PROP_FLOATING_SELECTION,
PROP_ACTIVE_CHANNEL saves the current object pointer the @info
structure. Others like PROP_SELECTION (for channel) and
PROP_GROUP_ITEM (for layer) will delete the current object and create
a new object, leaving the pointers in @info invalid (dangling).

Therefore, if a property from the first type will come before the
second, the result will be an UaF in the last lines of xcf_load_image
(when it actually using the pointers from @info).

I wasn't able to exploit this bug because that
g_object_instance->c_class gets cleared by the last g_object_unref and
GIMP_IS_{LAYER,CHANNEL} detects that and return FALSE.

(cherry picked from commit 6d804bf9ae77bc86a0a97f9b944a129844df9395)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['            gboolean   is_active_layer;', '', "            /* We're going to delete *layer, Don't leave its pointers", "             * in @info.  After that, we'll restore them back with the", '             * new pointer. See bug #767873.', '             */', '            is_active_layer = (*layer == info->active_layer);', '            if (is_active_layer)', '              info->active_layer = NULL;', '', '            if (*layer == info->floating_sel)', '              info->floating_sel = NULL;', '', '            if (is_active_layer)', '              info->active_layer = *layer;', '', "            /* Don't restore info->floating_sel because group layers", "             * can't be floating selections", '             */']}
description: Use-after-free vulnerability in the xcf_load_image function in app/xcf/xcf-load.c in GIMP allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (program crash) or possibly execute arbitrary code via a crafted XCF file.

code_evidence: PROP_ACTIVE_LAYER stores the current *layer pointer into info->active_layer, which is retained beyond this property's lifetime.
PROP_FLOATING_SELECTION similarly stores *layer into info->floating_sel and reads an offset, leaving another dangling pointer in info.
PROP_GROUP_ITEM saves *layer, refs it, unrefs it, then replaces *layer with a new group layer; the unref frees the old layer while info->active_layer/floating_sel may still point to it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function frees a layer object while retaining stale pointers to it in info, and those pointers are subsequently reused; this is exactly reuse of memory after free, matching CWE-416. It is not merely a NULL dereference because the stale pointer references freed, potentially reallocated memory.

evidence_lines.code:
case PROP_ACTIVE_LAYER:
info->active_layer = *layer;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: PROP_GROUP_ITEM frees the old layer via g_object_unref and replaces it, but earlier PROP_ACTIVE_LAYER/PROP_FLOATING_SELECTION properties already stored that old pointer in info. When a crafted XCF orders the saving property before PROP_GROUP_ITEM, info retains a dangling pointer later dereferenced in xcf_load_image, causing a use-after-free (crash or possibly code execution).

commit_msg: Fix a crash bug with bogus text (Issue #426)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ["\t  if (t->data[strlen((char *)t->data) - 1] == '\\n')"], 'added_lines': ["\t  if (t->data[0] && t->data[strlen((char *)t->data) - 1] == '\\n')"]}
description: HTMLDoc v1.9.15 was discovered to contain a heap overflow via (write_header) /htmldoc/htmldoc/html.cxx:273.

code_evidence: In the preformatted branch, after t->data is confirmed non-NULL at line 17, the loop at line 21 writes characters and line 23 indexes t->data[strlen((char *)t->data) - 1]. If t->data is an empty string, strlen returns 0, so the index becomes -1, reading before the start of the buffer. The patch adds a t->data[0] guard, confirming the empty-string case was the crash trigger.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect is an index computed as strlen-1 without a non-empty check, producing an out-of-bounds access before the buffer start. That matches out-of-bounds memory access; CWE-787 (out-of-bounds write) is only a partial fit because the faulty operation here is a read/index, not a write, so the mapping is weak.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the length-derived index strlen(t->data)-1 is used without first verifying the string is non-empty. Trigger: a preformatted text node whose data is an empty string reaches this branch. Consequence: an out-of-bounds access at index -1 on the heap buffer, causing the reported crash; this is an out-of-bounds read/access rather than a write past the buffer.

commit_msg:
nstrace: Allow opening of files that are not multiples of 16kB
in size.

Wireshark/Tshark hangs when netscaler trace file smaller than 16KB is opened. 
It also hangs when a gzipped trace file is opened. With this fix, 
Files with sizes that are not multiple of 16KB and gzipped files can be opened.

Bug: 12083
Change-Id: I26b2fc406edafcb2f1f6161d69064ba5662ddf29
Reviewed-on: https://code.wireshark.org/review/13721
Reviewed-by: Michael Mann <mmann78@netscape.net>
(cherry picked from commit 875d95ea605758308fc2369d83a41a34a6adbe53)

description: In Wireshark 2.2.0 to 2.2.4 and 2.0.0 to 2.0.10, there is a Netscaler file parser infinite loop, triggered by a malformed capture file. This was addressed in wiretap/netscaler.c by changing the restrictions on file size.

code_evidence: The outer do-loop at line 14 relies on the while condition at line 66, which continues while bytes_read equals nstrace_buflen. The inner while at lines 22-24 advances nstrace_buf_offset only via nspr_getv20recordsize(hdp) at line 58 (default case). If the record size is zero, nstrace_buf_offset never advances, so the inner loop spins forever when nstrace_buf[nstrace_buf_offset] stays nonzero. commit_msg:
vc2enc_dwt: pad the temporary buffer by the slice size

Since non-Haar wavelets need to look into pixels outside the frame, we
need to pad the buffer. The old factor of two seemed to be a workaround
that fact and only padded to the left and bottom. This correctly pads
by the slice size and as such reduces memory usage and potential
exploits.
Reported by Liu Bingchang.

Ideally, there should be no temporary buffer but the encoder is designed
to deinterleave the coefficients into the classical wavelet structure
with the lower frequency values in the top left corner.

Signed-off-by: Rostislav Pehlivanov <atomnuker@gmail.com>
(cherry picked from commit 3228ac730c11eca49d5680d5550128e397061c85)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['av_cold int ff_vc2enc_init_transforms(VC2TransformContext *s, int p_width, int p_height)', '    s->buffer = av_malloc(2*p_width*p_height*sizeof(dwtcoef));'], 'added_lines': ['av_cold int ff_vc2enc_init_transforms(VC2TransformContext *s, int p_stride,', '                                      int p_height, int slice_w, int slice_h)', '    /* Pad by the slice size, only matters for non-Haar wavelets */', '    s->buffer = av_calloc((p_stride + slice_w)*(p_height + slice_h), sizeof(dwtcoef));', '    s->padding = (slice_h >> 1)*p_stride + (slice_w >> 1);', '    s->buffer += s->padding;', '']}
description: The VC-2 Video Compression encoder in FFmpeg 3.0 and 3.4 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read) because of incorrect buffer padding for non-Haar wavelets, related to libavcodec/vc2enc.c and libavcodec/vc2enc_dwt.c.

code_evidence: Allocates the temporary DWT buffer with av_malloc(2*p_width*p_height*sizeof(dwtcoef)), sizing it only from the padded frame width/height. No slice-size or offset padding is added, so the allocation does not account for the extra rows/columns non-Haar wavelets access outside the frame; the only failure check is for a NULL pointer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the undersized buffer permits reads before or past its bounds during wavelet processing, matching the out-of-bounds read description. It is not an out-of-bounds write; the function only sizes memory, and the unsafe access is a read by the transform.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The buffer allocation is too small for non-Haar wavelet transforms that read pixels outside the frame boundary. When such a transform runs, it indexes before/after the allocated buffer, causing an out-of-bounds read that can crash or leak memory. The root cause is the missing slice-size padding in the allocation, not the NULL check.

commit_msg:
net: Fix double free and memory corruption in get_net_ns_by_id()

(I can trivially verify that that idr_remove in cleanup_net happens
 after the network namespace count has dropped to zero --EWB)

Function get_net_ns_by_id() does not check for net::count
after it has found a peer in netns_ids idr.

It may dereference a peer, after its count has already been
finaly decremented. This leads to double free and memory
corruption:

put_net(peer)                                   rtnl_lock()
atomic_dec_and_test(&peer->count) [count=0]     ...
__put_net(peer)                                 get_net_ns_by_id(net, id)
  spin_lock(&cleanup_list_lock)
  list_add(&net->cleanup_list, &cleanup_list)
  spin_unlock(&cleanup_list_lock)
queue_work()                                      peer = idr_find(&net->netns_ids, id)
  |                                               get_net(peer) [count=1]
  |                                               ...
  |                                               (use after final put)
  v                                               ...
  cleanup_net()                                   ...
    spin_lock(&cleanup_list_lock)                 ...
    list_replace_init(&cleanup_list, ..)          ...
    spin_unlock(&cleanup_list_lock)               ...
    ...                                           ...
    ...                                           put_net(peer)
    ...                                             atomic_dec_and_test(&peer->count) [count=0]
    ...                                               spin_lock(&cleanup_list_lock)
    ...                                               list_add(&net->cleanup_list, &cleanup_list)
    ...                                               spin_unlock(&cleanup_list_lock)
    ...                                             queue_work()
    ...                                           rtnl_unlock()
    rtnl_lock()                                   ...
    for_each_net(tmp) {                           ...
      id = __peernet2id(tmp, peer)                ...
      spin_lock_irq(&tmp->nsid_lock)              ...
      idr_remove(&tmp->netns_ids, id)             ...
      ...                                         ...
      net_drop_ns()                               ...
	net_free(peer)                            ...
    }                                             ...
  |
  v
  cleanup_net()
    ...
    (Second free of peer)

Also, put_net() on the right cpu may reorder with left's cpu
list_replace_init(&cleanup_list, ..), and then cleanup_list
will be corrupted.

Since cleanup_net() is executed in worker thread, while
put_net(peer) can happen everywhere, there should be
enough time for concurrent get_net_ns_by_id() to pick
the peer up, and the race does not seem to be unlikely.
The patch fixes the problem in standard way.

(Also, there is possible problem in peernet2id_alloc(), which requires
check for net::count under nsid_lock and maybe_get_net(peer), but
in current stable kernel it's used under rtnl_lock() and it has to be
safe. Openswitch begun to use peernet2id_alloc(), and possibly it should
be fixed too. While this is not in stable kernel yet, so I'll send
a separate message to netdev@ later).

Cc: Nicolas Dichtel <nicolas.dichtel@6wind.com>
Signed-off-by: Kirill Tkhai <ktkhai@virtuozzo.com>
Fixes: 0c7aecd4bde4 "netns: add rtnl cmd to add and get peer netns ids"
Reviewed-by: Andrey Ryabinin <aryabinin@virtuozzo.com>
Reviewed-by: "Eric W. Biederman" <ebiederm@xmission.com>
Signed-off-by: Eric W. Biederman <ebiederm@xmission.com>
Reviewed-by: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Acked-by: Nicolas Dichtel <nicolas.dichtel@6wind.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tget_net(peer);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tpeer = maybe_get_net(peer);']}
description: A use-after-free vulnerability was found in network namespaces code affecting the Linux kernel before 4.14.11. The function get_net_ns_by_id() in net/core/net_namespace.c does not check for the net::count value after it has found a peer network in netns_ids idr, which could lead to double free and memory corruption. This vulnerability could allow an unprivileged local user to induce kernel memory corruption on the system, leading to a crash. Due to the nature of the flaw, privilege escalation cannot be fully ruled out, although it is thought to be unlikely.

code_evidence: idr_find returns the peer under nsid_lock, but the reference is merely resurrected with get_net(peer), which unconditionally increments net::count without verifying the peer is still alive. If the peer's count already reached zero and cleanup_net queued its final free, this increment races with teardown, so the returned peer is used after its final put.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The flaw is a timing window in which a concurrent code sequence (put_net/cleanup_net) modifies the shared peer's count between lookup and reference acquisition, violating atomicity. This is a race condition (CWE-362); the use-after-free is its consequence, not the target label.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the lookup and reference acquisition do not atomically test whether net::count is nonzero. Trigger: concurrent put_net drops the peer's count to zero while get_net_ns_by_id holds nsid_lock and calls get_net. The consequence is a use-after-free/double free of the network namespace, causing kernel memory corruption or crash.

The CRC block is guarded only by MIN(tvb_len, tvb_reported_length(tvb)) >= mac_len, so a mac_len value smaller than sizeof(mac_crc) still passes and reaches wimax_mac_calc_crc32 with a size of mac_len - sizeof(mac_crc), which underflows to a huge unsigned value.

Trigger: a crafted WiMax DLMAP packet with a small mac_len (<= sizeof(mac_crc)). Consequence: the subtraction mac_len - sizeof(mac_crc) underflows, producing an enormous length passed to tvb_get_ptr/wimax_mac_calc_crc32, leading to a crash (DoS).

description: UnRAR 5.6.1.2 and 5.6.1.3 has a heap-based buffer overflow in Unpack::CopyString (called from Unpack::Unpack5 and CmdExtract::ExtractCurrentFile).

The destination capacity is CmtLength+1, but the conversion count and source length are derived from the same attacker-controlled CmtLength, so the write bound is tied to the input length rather than the destination size. The patch replaces CmtLength with CmtData->Size() at the call, showing the original count could exceed the allocated destination.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CharToWide writes into CmtData->Addr(0) bounded by a value not derived from the destination allocation, allowing writes past the intended buffer. This is a direct out-of-bounds write (CWE-787), distinct from a mere read overflow.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the CharToWide destination length argument is the source-derived CmtLength instead of the destination buffer size. Trigger: a crafted comment whose length/conversion causes CharToWide to write more than CmtLength+1 elements, overflowing the heap buffer allocated at line 102. Supported consequence: heap out-of-bounds write, memory corruption or crash.

commit_msg:
We recently had an oops reported on a 4.14 kernel in
xfs_reclaim_inodes_count() where sb->s_fs_info pointed to garbage
and so the m_perag_tree lookup walked into lala land.

Essentially, the machine was under memory pressure when the mount
was being run, xfs_fs_fill_super() failed after allocating the
xfs_mount and attaching it to sb->s_fs_info. It then cleaned up and
freed the xfs_mount, but the sb->s_fs_info field still pointed to
the freed memory. Hence when the superblock shrinker then ran
it fell off the bad pointer.

With the superblock shrinker problem fixed at teh VFS level, this
stale s_fs_info pointer is still a problem - we use it
unconditionally in ->put_super when the superblock is being torn
down, and hence we can still trip over it after a ->fill_super
call failure. Hence we need to clear s_fs_info if
xfs-fs_fill_super() fails, and we need to check if it's valid in
the places it can potentially be dereferenced after a ->fill_super
failure.

Signed-Off-By: Dave Chinner <dchinner@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Darrick J. Wong <darrick.wong@oracle.com>
Signed-off-by: Darrick J. Wong <darrick.wong@oracle.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tsb->s_fs_info = NULL;']}
description: An issue was discovered in fs/xfs/xfs_super.c in the Linux kernel before 4.18. A use after free exists, related to xfs_fs_fill_super failure.

code_evidence: Line 13 stores the allocated xfs_mount pointer in sb->s_fs_info; the failure path at [129,130,131] reaches kfree(mp) via out_free_fsname without clearing sb->s_fs_info, leaving the superblock field dangling.
Lines [14,15,16] show xfs_parseargs can fail and jump directly to out_free_fsname, so sb->s_fs_info is set to mp before any validation and mp is freed while sb still references it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function leaves a pointer to freed heap memory reachable through sb->s_fs_info and later dereferenced, which is exactly CWE-416 use after free. This is not merely a NULL-pointer dereference; the added NULL assignment prevents the stale freed pointer from being used.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: sb->s_fs_info is assigned the xfs_mount at line 13, but the cleanup labels free mp via kfree without resetting the field; the patch adds sb->s_fs_info = NULL at out_free_fsname. Trigger: xfs_parseargs, xfs_open_devices, or later mount steps fail, freeing mp while sb->s_fs_info still points to freed memory. Consequence: later teardown/shrinker code dereferences the stale pointer, causing the reported oops (use-after-free).

commit_msg:
Fixed Error() instance dumping when "name" prop is not primitive.

Previously, njs_error_to_string2() might be invoked with error argument
pointing to vm->retval.  When "name" prop was not primitive vm->retval
might be overwritten.  As a result error pointer might be referencing a
primitive value.  In turn the second call of njs_object_property()
received an invalid object pointer because it expects only object value
types.

The fix is to ensure that error object pointer is never overwritten.

This closes #615 issue on Github.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    if (njs_slow_path(!njs_is_object(error))) {', '        njs_type_error(vm, "\\"error\\" is not an object");', '        return NJS_ERROR;', '    }', '']}
description: Nginx NJS v0.7.10 was discovered to contain a segmentation violation via the function njs_lvlhsh_find at src/njs_lvlhsh.c.

code_evidence: njs_error_to_string forwards its caller-supplied error pointer directly to njs_error_to_string2 without verifying that error is an object value; njs_error_to_string2 later performs object property reads on it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the unchecked non-object value leads to reading through an invalid object pointer, which is an out-of-bounds memory read. A type-confusion or NULL-pointer label would describe the intermediate state, but the supported observed consequence is an out-of-bounds read.

evidence_lines.code: return njs_error_to_string2(vm, retval, error, 1);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function passes an unvalidated error value to njs_error_to_string2, which expects an object and reads object properties from it. When a non-object (e.g., primitive) value is supplied, those property lookups interpret the value as an object, producing an invalid pointer access and a crash/out-of-bounds read. The missing precondition check is the root cause; the invalid memory access is the consequence.

commit_msg:
evtchn: avoid NULL derefs

Commit fbbd5009e6 ("evtchn: refactor low-level event channel port ops")
added a de-reference of the struct evtchn pointer for a port without
first making sure the bucket pointer is non-NULL. This de-reference is
actually entirely unnecessary, as all relevant callers (beyond the
problematic do_poll()) already hold the port number in their hands, and
the actual leaf functions need nothing else.

For FIFO event channels there's a second problem in that the ordering
of reads and updates to ->num_evtchns and ->event_array[] was so far
undefined (the read side isn't always holding the domain's event lock).
Add respective barriers.

This is XSA-221.

Reported-by: Ankur Arora <ankur.a.arora@oracle.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['                                           const struct evtchn *evtchn)', '    return d->evtchn_port_ops->is_masked(d, evtchn);'], 'added_lines': ['                                           evtchn_port_t port)', '    return d->evtchn_port_ops->is_masked(d, port);']}
description: Xen through 4.8.x does not validate the port numbers of polled event channel ports, which allows guest OS users to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference and host OS crash) or possibly obtain sensitive information, aka XSA-221.

code_evidence: evtchn_port_is_masked takes a struct evtchn pointer and forwards it unvalidated to the port-ops is_masked callback; the pointer is dereferenced downstream with no NULL check at this boundary.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function's role is to forward a pointer that is expected valid but is not checked, and the patch removes this pointer parameter entirely because the dereference was unnecessary. This directly matches CWE-476: dereferencing a pointer assumed valid but NULL; it is not a bounds or type-confusion issue since no array indexing or cast occurs here.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The wrapper passes a caller-supplied evtchn pointer straight into d->evtchn_port_ops->is_masked without confirming it is non-NULL. When a caller such as the polling path obtains a port whose bucket lookup failed, the NULL pointer reaches the leaf operation and is dereferenced, crashing the host. The cause is the missing validity constraint on the pointer argument; the consequence is a host denial of service (and potentially information exposure).

description: coders/dds.c in ImageMagick before 6.9.0-4 Beta allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (CPU consumption) via a crafted DDS file.

code_evidence: The mipmap loop computes a per-level byte offset from attacker-controlled width/height and texel_size (line 25) and advances the blob cursor with SeekBlob (line 26). The return value of SeekBlob is discarded by the (void) cast, so a failed or out-of-range seek does not stop the loop; w and h are then halved and iteration continues while i < mipmapcount.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-399 covers improper management of system resources; here unchecked seek failure and unbounded iteration over attacker-supplied mipmapcount cause excessive CPU use. This is resource-consumption behavior rather than a memory-safety defect such as an out-of-bounds write.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the seek result is ignored, so no bound or error condition terminates processing of a crafted DDS file. Trigger: a DDS header with a large mipmapcount and dimensions causing repeated seeks over the image. The loop keeps iterating, consuming CPU proportional to the crafted level count instead of aborting on the failed seek; the supported consequence is CPU consumption (denial of service).

commit_msg:
Fix #77973: Uninitialized read in gdImageCreateFromXbm

We have to ensure that `sscanf()` does indeed read a hex value here,
and bail out otherwise.

(cherry picked from commit ed6dee9a198c904ad5e03113e58a2d2c200f5184)

description: When using the gdImageCreateFromXbm() function in the GD Graphics Library (aka LibGD) 2.2.5, as used in the PHP GD extension in PHP versions 7.1.x below 7.1.30, 7.2.x below 7.2.19 and 7.3.x below 7.3.6, it is possible to supply data that will cause the function to use the value of uninitialized variable. This may lead to disclosing contents of the stack that has been left there by previous code.

code_evidence: b is declared as an uninitialized unsigned int and is only ever written by the return of sscanf.
.h[0] and h[1] are filled from getc, and h[2]/h[3] are only filled when max_bit == 32768; no check ensures the bytes form a valid hex string.
sscanf(h, "%x", &b) is called and its return value is ignored, so if the buffer does not parse as hex, b is never assigned.
b is then read in (b & bit) to set pixels, propagating the indeterminate value.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads a local variable that may never have been assigned, which is exactly use of an uninitialized resource (CWE-908). This is not an out-of-bounds issue: the buffer is bounded, but the conversion failure leaves b indeterminate before its use.

sscanf(h, "%x", &b);

for (bit = 1; bit <= max_bit; bit = bit << 1) {
gdImageSetPixel(im, x++, y, (b & bit) ? 1 : 0);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the return value of sscanf is not checked, so a non-hex or malformed input line leaves the local b uninitialized. Trigger: crafted XBM data whose pixel bytes do not parse as %x. Consequence: the uninitialized stack value is used to compute pixel bits, potentially disclosing stack contents into the decoded image.

commit_msg:
KVM: MTRR: remove MSR 0x2f8

MSR 0x2f8 accessed the 124th Variable Range MTRR ever since MTRR support
was introduced by 9ba075a664df ("KVM: MTRR support").

0x2f8 became harmful when 910a6aae4e2e ("KVM: MTRR: exactly define the
size of variable MTRRs") shrinked the array of VR MTRRs from 256 to 8,
which made access to index 124 out of bounds.  The surrounding code only
WARNs in this situation, thus the guest gained a limited read/write
access to struct kvm_arch_vcpu.

0x2f8 is not a valid VR MTRR MSR, because KVM has/advertises only 16 VR
MTRR MSRs, 0x200-0x20f.  Every VR MTRR is set up using two MSRs, 0x2f8
was treated as a PHYSBASE and 0x2f9 would be its PHYSMASK, but 0x2f9 was
not implemented in KVM, therefore 0x2f8 could never do anything useful
and getting rid of it is safe.

This fixes CVE-2016-3713.

Fixes: 910a6aae4e2e ("KVM: MTRR: exactly define the size of variable MTRRs")

Reported-by: David Matlack <dmatlack@google.com>

Signed-off-by: Radim Krčmář <rkrcmar@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>

0005 | case MSR_MTRRfix64K_00000:

description: The msr_mtrr_valid function in arch/x86/kvm/mtrr.c in the Linux kernel before 4.6.1 supports MSR 0x2f8, which allows guest OS users to read or write to the kvm_arch_vcpu data structure, and consequently obtain sensitive information or cause a denial of service (system crash), via a crafted ioctl call.

code_evidence: The switch explicitly accepts MSR 0x2f8 and returns true, validating it as a permitted MTRR MSR despite it not being part of the advertised variable-range MTRR set.

The legitimate variable MTRR range is covered by 0x200 ... 0x200 + 2*KVM_NR_VAR_MTRR - 1 and the fixed MTRRs/defType/PAT cases, so 0x2f8 is an out-of-range, unauthorized MSR that bypasses the intended set.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function fails to restrict access to a resource (valid MTRR MSRs) from an unauthorized guest actor, granting access to an out-of-range MSR; this matches improper access control/authorization rather than a memory-safety label.

case 0x200 ... 0x200 + 2 * KVM_NR_VAR_MTRR - 1:

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: msr_mtrr_valid authorizes MSR 0x2f8, which is not a valid VR MTRR MSR, so the guest can reach MTRR handling indexed beyond the shrunk VR MTRR array. Trigger: a guest ioctl accessing MSR 0x2f8. Supported consequence: out-of-bounds read/write of struct kvm_arch_vcpu, enabling information disclosure or a host crash.

commit_msg:
replace dangerous tvb_get_ptr with safer string function.

Using tvb_get_ptr to get a string is always dangerous in the face of
malformed packets. Instead using string functions allow for safe handling
of these.

Bug: 12242
Change-Id: I059c186032492aae9c90a69858ea3fc59e21313f
Reviewed-on: https://code.wireshark.org/review/14714
Reviewed-by: Michael Mann <mmann78@netscape.net>
Petri-Dish: Michael Mann <mmann78@netscape.net>
Tested-by: Petri Dish Buildbot <buildbot-no-reply@wireshark.org>
Reviewed-by: Alexis La Goutte <alexis.lagoutte@gmail.com>

description: epan/dissectors/packet-pktc.c in the PKTC dissector in Wireshark 1.12.x before 1.12.11 and 2.0.x before 2.0.3 misparses timestamp fields, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read and application crash) via a crafted packet.

code_evidence: timestr is a raw pointer returned by tvb_get_ptr for 13 bytes; it is then consumed by proto_tree_add_string_format_value as a C string and indexed as timestr+2 through timestr+10 for %.2s conversions. tvb_get_ptr does not guarantee NUL termination, so the string reads can extend past the 13-byte region.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads memory outside the intended 13-byte buffer boundary through unbounded string operations, matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds read. The patch replaces tvb_get_ptr with tvb_get_string_enc to enforce bounded string handling, confirming the boundary defect.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the 13-byte timestamp is treated as a NUL-terminated string without a bounded copy or terminator guarantee. A malformed packet whose timestamp field lacks a NUL within the captured region causes the string-formatting reads to walk beyond the intended buffer, producing an out-of-bounds read and possible crash.

virtio-gpu-3d: fix memory leak in resource attach backing

If the virgl_renderer_resource_attach_iov function fails the
'res_iovs' will be leaked. Add check of the return value to
free the 'res_iovs' when failing.

Signed-off-by: Li Qiang <liq3ea@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Marc-André Lureau <marcandre.lureau@redhat.com>
Message-id: 1482999086-59795-1-git-send-email-liq3ea@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Gerd Hoffmann <kraxel@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    virgl_renderer_resource_attach_iov(att_rb.resource_id,', '                                       res_iovs, att_rb.nr_entries);'], 'added_lines': ['    ret = virgl_renderer_resource_attach_iov(att_rb.resource_id,', '                                             res_iovs, att_rb.nr_entries);', '', '    if (ret != 0)', '        virtio_gpu_cleanup_mapping_iov(res_iovs, att_rb.nr_entries);']}
description: Memory leak in the virgl_resource_attach_backing function in hw/display/virtio-gpu-3d.c in QEMU (aka Quick Emulator) allows local guest OS users to cause a denial of service (host memory consumption) via a large number of VIRTIO_GPU_CMD_RESOURCE_ATTACH_BACKING commands.

code_evidence: virtio_gpu_create_mapping_iov allocates res_iovs and returns nonzero on failure; that error path returns without freeing res_iovs. On success, virgl_renderer_resource_attach_iov is called but its return value is ignored; if it fails, res_iovs is never released because no cleanup or error branch exists before the function returns.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-401 fits because allocated memory (res_iovs) is not released on the attach-failure path, matching missing release of memory after effective lifetime. It is distinct from CWE-476/double-free since the flaw is failure to free, not dereferencing or freeing twice.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the return value of virgl_renderer_resource_attach_iov is unchecked, so a failed attach leaves the allocated res_iovs mapping unreleased. Trigger: repeated VIRTIO_GPU_CMD_RESOURCE_ATTACH_BACKING commands whose attach fails. Consequence: host memory is leaked, enabling resource-consumption denial of service by a local guest.

description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel before 5.1.8. There is a NULL pointer dereference caused by a malicious USB device in the drivers/usb/misc/sisusbvga/sisusb.c driver.

code_evidence: At line 14 usb_register_dev() is called and its failure is checked at line 15. The error branch at lines 16-18 logs via &sisusb->sisusb_dev->dev, but sisusb_dev is only assigned at line 22, after the registration succeeds. Since sisusb is kzalloc'd (line 9), sisusb_dev is NULL on the error path, so the dev_err dereference of NULL->dev triggers the fault.
Line 22 shows the assignment sisusb->sisusb_dev = dev placed after the usb_register_dev check, confirming the pointer is unset whenever the error branch is taken.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences a NULL struct member pointer (sisusb_dev) on an error path, matching CWE-476's definition of dereferencing a pointer expected to be valid but NULL. This is distinct from an uninitialized-variable issue because kzalloc zeroes the struct, making the pointer deterministically NULL.

evidence_lines.code: sisusb->sisusb_dev = dev;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the sisusb_dev field is initialized only after successful registration, yet the registration-failure branch dereferences it through &sisusb->sisusb_dev->dev. Trigger: a malicious/failing USB device makes usb_register_dev() return an error, taking lines 16-18 where sisusb_dev is still NULL. Consequence: NULL pointer dereference, causing a crash/DoS.

description: An issue was discovered in libsixel 1.8.4. There is a heap-based buffer overflow in the function gif_out_code at fromgif.c.

code_evidence: Lines 18-21 read attacker-controlled x, y, w, h from the GIF image descriptor. Line 22 checks only x+w>g->w and y+h>g->h, without rejecting x>=g->w or y>=g->h, and without guarding integer overflow in x+w or y+h.
Lines 29-32 then store start_x/start_y and compute max_x=start_x+w, max_y=start_y+h, which later drive raster writes into the image buffer allocated for g->w by g->h.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function accepts image geometry that exceeds the destination buffer and propagates it to raster processing, directly enabling writes beyond the allocated buffer, matching CWE-787. The missing offset check is the cause; the out-of-bounds write is the consequence, not merely an integer issue (CWE-190).

A crafted GIF with large or overflowing x/y/w/h values passes validation, so max_x/max_y exceed the allocated image dimensions and subsequent raster rendering writes past the buffer, giving a heap-based out-of-bounds write.

commit_msg:
KEYS: Fix race between updating and finding a negative key

Consolidate KEY_FLAG_INSTANTIATED, KEY_FLAG_NEGATIVE and the rejection
error into one field such that:

 (1) The instantiation state can be modified/read atomically.

 (2) The error can be accessed atomically with the state.

 (3) The error isn't stored unioned with the payload pointers.

This deals with the problem that the state is spread over three different
objects (two bits and a separate variable) and reading or updating them
atomically isn't practical, given that not only can uninstantiated keys
change into instantiated or rejected keys, but rejected keys can also turn
into instantiated keys - and someone accessing the key might not be using
any locking.

The main side effect of this problem is that what was held in the payload
may change, depending on the state.  For instance, you might observe the
key to be in the rejected state.  You then read the cached error, but if
the key semaphore wasn't locked, the key might've become instantiated
between the two reads - and you might now have something in hand that isn't
actually an error code.

The state is now KEY_IS_UNINSTANTIATED, KEY_IS_POSITIVE or a negative error
code if the key is negatively instantiated.  The key_is_instantiated()
function is replaced with key_is_positive() to avoid confusion as negative
keys are also 'instantiated'.

Additionally, barriering is included:

 (1) Order payload-set before state-set during instantiation.

 (2) Order state-read before payload-read when using the key.

Further separate barriering is necessary if RCU is being used to access the
payload content after reading the payload pointers.

Fixes: 146aa8b1453b ("KEYS: Merge the type-specific data with the payload data")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # v4.4+
Reported-by: Eric Biggers <ebiggers@google.com>
Signed-off-by: David Howells <dhowells@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Eric Biggers <ebiggers@google.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tif (test_bit(KEY_FLAG_INSTANTIATED, &key->flags)) {'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (key->state != KEY_IS_UNINSTANTIATED) {']}
description: The KEYS subsystem in the Linux kernel before 4.13.10 does not correctly synchronize the actions of updating versus finding a key in the "negative" state to avoid a race condition, which allows local users to cause a denial of service or possibly have unspecified other impact via crafted system calls.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function's only relevant change replaces a flag-bit test with a state-field comparison; the described race is an atomicity/synchronization issue, not improper validation of input, so CWE-20 is not supported.

commit_msg: Fix integer overflow for multiframe gifs.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    int buffer_size = 0;', '          buffer_size = num_frames * height * width * channels;'], 'added_lines': ['    ptrdiff_t buffer_size = 0;', '          buffer_size = ptrdiff_t(num_frames) * height * width * channels;']}
description: TensorFlow is an open source platform for machine learning. Prior to versions 2.12.0 and 2.11.1, integer overflow occurs when `2^31 <= num_frames * height * width * channels < 2^32`, for example Full HD screencast of at least 346 frames. A fix is included in TensorFlow version 2.12.0 and version 2.11.1.

code_evidence: buffer_size is declared as a 32-bit int (line 17) and computed as num_frames * height * width * channels in int arithmetic (line 22); for large multiframe GIFs the product can exceed INT_MAX and wrap. The wrapped value is then passed to new uint8[buffer_size] (line 52), so the allocated buffer is smaller than the data the decoder writes based on the true frame dimensions.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is an integer wraparound in a size computation that feeds memory allocation, matching CWE-190's core case where a size/offset calculation exceeds the integer representation. The fix widens buffer_size to ptrdiff_t and casts num_frames, confirming the overflow was the defect rather than a separate out-of-bounds write.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the frame-buffer size is computed in 32-bit signed int without an overflow check, so num_frames*height*width*channels wraps when it reaches 2^31..2^32. Trigger: decoding a large multiframe GIF with enough frames/dimensions. Consequence: new uint8[] allocates an undersized buffer while the decoder fills it per true dimensions, causing out-of-bounds heap writes.

commit_msg: Fix for heap vulnerability
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    map = (Unicode *)greallocn(map, mapLen, sizeof(Unicode));', '    for (i = oldLen; i < mapLen; ++i) {', '      map[i] = 0;'], 'added_lines': ['    if (unlikely(code >= mapLen)) {', '      error(-1, "Illegal code value in CharCodeToUnicode::addMapping");', '      return;', '    } else {', '      map = (Unicode *)greallocn(map, mapLen, sizeof(Unicode));', '      for (i = oldLen; i < mapLen; ++i) {', '        map[i] = 0;', '      }']}
description: Buffer overflow in pdf2json 0.69 allows local users to execute arbitrary code by converting a crafted PDF file.

code_evidence: When code >= mapLen, mapLen is recomputed as (code + 256) & ~255 and map is reallocated to that size, then initialized in the loop.
The parsed code is later used directly as an index: map[code] = u + offset (line 20) and map[code] = 0 (line 27), with no bound check against mapLen.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes to map[code] without verifying that code is within the allocated mapLen, producing an out-of-bounds buffer write driven by unchecked input. This is a classic buffer overflow (CWE-120): a size/validation failure on an input-derived index leads to writing past the buffer end.

evidence_lines.code:
map[code] = u + offset;
map[code] = 0;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the mapping array is sized from an attacker-controlled CharCode value while the write index derives from the same value, and integer truncation in the CharCode type can make the recomputed mapLen smaller than code. Trigger: a crafted PDF ToUnicode CMap supplies a large code; the subsequent map[code] write lands outside the allocated map. Consequence: heap out-of-bounds write enabling memory corruption and potential code execution.

description: In Wireshark 2.2.0 to 2.2.4 and 2.0.0 to 2.0.10, there is an IAX2 infinite loop, triggered by packet injection or a malformed capture file. This was addressed in epan/dissectors/packet-iax2.c by constraining packet lateness.

code_evidence: The function reads a 16-bit timestamp from the packet (ts = tvb_get_ntohs), strips the marker bit, and passes the resulting timestamp to iax2_add_ts_fields and dissect_payload.
The timestamp value is taken directly from attacker-controlled packet bytes and forwarded without any bounds or lateness check.
Processing then continues into payload dissection and updates first_time, so the timestamp drives subsequent state handling.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-835 fits because the observable consequence is an unreachable exit condition causing an infinite loop during packet processing. This is not merely a numeric overflow; the defect is failure to bound timestamp progression, leading to non-terminating iteration.

evidence_lines.code:
iax2_add_ts_fields(pinfo, iax2_tree, iax_packet, (guint16)ts);
iax2_add_ts_fields(pinfo, iax2_tree, iax_packet, (guint16)ts);

dissect_payload(tvb, offset, pinfo, iax2_tree, main_tree, ts, TRUE, iax_packet);
iax_packet->first_time = FALSE;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the packet timestamp is consumed and propagated with no constraint on its relation to the previous timestamp, so timestamp-based state transitions in the called code can fail to advance. Trigger: a malformed or injected IAX2 mini video packet carrying an out-of-range timestamp. Supported consequence: the dissector can loop indefinitely, consuming CPU (DoS). The timestamp check itself lives in the callee, but this function is the source of the unvalidated value.

commit_msg:
tools/xenstore: remove nodes owned by destroyed domain

In case a domain is removed from Xenstore, remove all nodes owned by
it per default.

This tackles the problem that nodes might be created by a domain
outside its home path in Xenstore, leading to Xenstore hogging more
and more memory. Domain quota don't work in this case if the guest is
rebooting in between.

Since XSA-322 ownership of such stale nodes is transferred to dom0,
which is helping against unintended access, but not against OOM of
Xenstore.

As a fallback for weird cases add a Xenstore start parameter for
keeping today's way to handle stale nodes, adding the risk of Xenstore
hitting an OOM situation.

This is part of XSA-419 / CVE-2022-42322.

Fixes: 496306324d8d ("tools/xenstore: revoke access rights for removed domains")
Signed-off-by: Juergen Gross <jgross@suse.com>
Reviewed-by: Julien Grall <jgrall@amazon.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (domain_adjust_node_perms(conn, node))'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (domain_adjust_node_perms(node))']}
description: Xenstore: Cooperating guests can create arbitrary numbers of nodes T[his CNA information record relates to multiple CVEs; the text explains which aspects/vulnerabilities correspond to which CVE.] Since the fix of XSA-322 any Xenstore node owned by a removed domain will be modified to be owned by Dom0. This will allow two malicious guests working together to create an arbitrary number of Xenstore nodes. This is possible by domain A letting domain B write into domain A's local Xenstore tree. Domain B can then create many nodes and reboot. The nodes created by domain B will now be owned by Dom0. By repeating this process over and over again an arbitrary number of nodes can be created, as Dom0's number of nodes isn't limited by Xenstore quota.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function only serializes and writes a node; it contains no allocation whose lifetime is mismanaged, and the diff merely changes the domain_adjust_node_perms signature, so no missing-release weakness is evidenced.

Update utfcpp to v2.3.6

Fixes #2657

Incorporates the following utfcpp patches:

1. Sass addition of `retreat`.
   https://github.com/nemtrif/utfcpp/pull/20

2. Fix for `replace_invalid` throwing on incomplete sequence at the end

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['        if (it == end)', '            return NOT_ENOUGH_ROOM;', '']}
description: In LibSass prior to 3.5.5, the function handle_error in sass_context.cpp allows attackers to cause a denial-of-service resulting from a heap-based buffer over-read via a crafted sass file.

code_evidence: validate_next receives the current iterator it and the end sentinel, saves original_it, then immediately calls utf8::internal::sequence_length(it) before any check that it is still within the input range.

sequence_length dereferences it to inspect the lead byte, so an iterator already equal to end (or advanced past the valid data) triggers a read beyond the intended buffer; the switch then dispatches get_sequence_N and on failure restores it = original_it and returns err.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the function reads a byte through it without confirming the iterator is within the input bounds, an out-of-bounds read. It is not CWE-787 since the defect is a read, not a write past the buffer.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: no guard verifies it != end before sequence_length reads the lead octet. Trigger: an incomplete or truncated UTF-8 sequence positioned at end-of-input. Consequence: the lead-byte read and subsequent sequence decoding access memory past the intended buffer, producing a heap-based out-of-bounds read that can crash (denial of service).

description: A stack overflow vulnerability exists in gpac 1.1.0 via the gf_bifs_dec_proto_list function, which causes a segmentation fault and application crash.

code_evidence: The loop reads one byte at a time from the bitstream and stores it with name[i] = gf_bs_read_int(bs, 8) without any check that index i is within the allocated buffer. i is incremented on every non-NUL byte, so a long or unterminated input string keeps writing past the end of name.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the function writes attacker-derived bytes past the end of the intended name buffer. This is a direct out-of-bounds write, not merely an out-of-bounds read or an integer issue; the missing bound on i is the write-side flaw.

Trigger: attacker-controlled bitstream data supplies a name with no early NUL byte or a length exceeding the destination allocation. Consequence: out-of-bounds writes to adjacent memory, causing memory corruption and the reported segmentation fault/crash.

commit_msg: Moved global resource creation to startup instead of context creation. Fixes #645.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tlcGetPiecesLibrary()->UploadTextures(Context);'], 'added_lines': []}
description: LeoCAD before 21.03 sometimes allows a use-after-free during the opening of a new document.

code_evidence: lcScene::Draw calls lcGetPiecesLibrary()->UpdateBuffers(Context) and then UploadTextures(Context), both operating on the passed Context during scene drawing.

The function then issues many draw operations (e.g. DrawOpaqueMeshes and DrawTranslucentMeshes) that use the same Context; the patch removes line 4, indicating texture upload through Context during drawing was the problematic reuse.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the function dereferences and passes the Context pointer to library and draw calls after it may have been freed. This is a use-after-free, not merely a null dereference or leak, since the stale pointer is reused for operations.

evidence_lines.code:
lcGetPiecesLibrary()->UpdateBuffers(Context);
lcGetPiecesLibrary()->UploadTextures(Context);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function performs resource uploads on a Context that may already have been released, then continues to use that same Context for drawing. description: In ImageMagick 7.0.5-5, the ReadPICTImage function in pict.c allows attackers to cause a denial of service (memory leak) via a crafted file.

code_evidence: After tile_image is created by CloneImage at line 263, a failed ReadRectangle on source or destination throws without releasing tile_image.

In the alpha-undefined branch, the pixel-bound check throws without freeing tile_image or pixels.

description: The sanity_check_ckpt function in fs/f2fs/super.c in the Linux kernel before 4.12.4 does not validate the blkoff and segno arrays, which allows local users to gain privileges via unspecified vectors.

code_evidence: sanity_check_ckpt reads checkpoint fields from the on-disk image and compares derived segment counts: fsmeta accumulates rsvd_segment_count (line 11) and is checked against total (line 13), but no per-index validation of cur_node_segno/cur_node_blkoff or cur_data_segno/cur_data_blkoff exists in this function.

The segment and block-offset arrays (cur_*_segno, cur_*_blkoff) are later used as array indices without being bounded against main_segs and blocks_per_seg, so a crafted image with out-of-range values causes out-of-bounds indexing and memory corruption that can be escalated to privilege gain.

description: The VTP parser in tcpdump before 4.9.2 has a buffer over-read in print-vtp.c:vtp_print().

code_evidence: At line 54 EXTRACT_32BITS(tptr) reads four bytes from the config revision without first verifying that four bytes remain in the captured buffer; only after consuming them (line 55) does the loop at line 56 begin.
