commit_msg:
Correctly compare EdiPartyName in GENERAL_NAME_cmp()

If a GENERAL_NAME field contained EdiPartyName data then it was
incorrectly being handled as type "other". This could lead to a
segmentation fault.

Many thanks to David Benjamin from Google for reporting this issue.

CVE-2020-1971

Reviewed-by: Tomas Mraz <tmraz@fedoraproject.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        return a->d.other;'], 'added_lines': ['        return a->d.x400Address;', '', '        return a->d.ediPartyName;']}
description: The X.509 GeneralName type is a generic type for representing different types of names. One of those name types is known as EDIPartyName. OpenSSL provides a function GENERAL_NAME_cmp which compares different instances of a GENERAL_NAME to see if they are equal or not. This function behaves incorrectly when both GENERAL_NAMEs contain an EDIPARTYNAME. A NULL pointer dereference and a crash may occur leading to a possible denial of service attack. OpenSSL itself uses the GENERAL_NAME_cmp function for two purposes: 1) Comparing CRL distribution point names between an available CRL and a CRL distribution point embedded in an X509 certificate 2) When verifying that a timestamp response token signer matches the timestamp authority name (exposed via the API functions TS_RESP_verify_response and TS_RESP_verify_token) If an attacker can control both items being compared then that attacker could trigger a crash. For example if the attacker can trick a client or server into checking a malicious certificate against a malicious CRL then this may occur. Note that some applications automatically download CRLs based on a URL embedded in a certificate. This checking happens prior to the signatures on the certificate and CRL being verified. OpenSSL's s_server, s_client and verify tools have support for the "-crl_download" option which implements automatic CRL downloading and this attack has been demonstrated to work against those tools. Note that an unrelated bug means that affected versions of OpenSSL cannot parse or construct correct encodings of EDIPARTYNAME. However it is possible to construct a malformed EDIPARTYNAME that OpenSSL's parser will accept and hence trigger this attack. All OpenSSL 1.1.1 and 1.0.2 versions are affected by this issue. Other OpenSSL releases are out of support and have not been checked. Fixed in OpenSSL 1.1.1i (Affected 1.1.1-1.1.1h). Fixed in OpenSSL 1.0.2x (Affected 1.0.2-1.0.2w).

code_evidence: The switch dispatches on a->type, but cases GEN_X400 and GEN_EDIPARTY fall through to a single shared return of a->d.other. For a GENERAL_NAME whose type is GEN_EDIPARTY, the union member actually populated is d.ediPartyName, not d.other, so the returned pointer does not correspond to the active union member.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The incorrect union member selection causes an invalid/NULL pointer to be returned and subsequently dereferenced, matching CWE-476's NULL pointer dereference with availability impact. It is not merely a type-confusion issue, since the supported consequence is dereference of an invalid pointer.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the GEN_EDIPARTY case is grouped with GEN_X400 and returns the wrong union member (d.other) instead of d.ediPartyName. Trigger: a caller invokes GENERAL_NAME_get0_value (or comparison logic using it) on a GENERAL_NAME of type GEN_EDIPARTY. The mismatched union member yields an invalid pointer that downstream code dereferences, causing a crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
Patch series "Fix several device private page reference counting issues",
v2

This series aims to fix a number of page reference counting issues in
drivers dealing with device private ZONE_DEVICE pages.  These result in
use-after-free type bugs, either from accessing a struct page which no
longer exists because it has been removed or accessing fields within the
struct page which are no longer valid because the page has been freed.

During normal usage it is unlikely these will cause any problems.  However
without these fixes it is possible to crash the kernel from userspace. 
These crashes can be triggered either by unloading the kernel module or
unbinding the device from the driver prior to a userspace task exiting. 
In modules such as Nouveau it is also possible to trigger some of these
issues by explicitly closing the device file-descriptor prior to the task
exiting and then accessing device private memory.

This involves some minor changes to both PowerPC and AMD GPU code. 
Unfortunately I lack hardware to test either of those so any help there
would be appreciated.  The changes mimic what is done in for both Nouveau
and hmm-tests though so I doubt they will cause problems.


This patch (of 8):

When the CPU tries to access a device private page the migrate_to_ram()
callback associated with the pgmap for the page is called.  However no
reference is taken on the faulting page.  Therefore a concurrent migration
of the device private page can free the page and possibly the underlying
pgmap.  This results in a race which can crash the kernel due to the
migrate_to_ram() function pointer becoming invalid.  It also means drivers
can't reliably read the zone_device_data field because the page may have
been freed with memunmap_pages().

Close the race by getting a reference on the page while holding the ptl to
ensure it has not been freed.  Unfortunately the elevated reference count
will cause the migration required to handle the fault to fail.  To avoid
this failure pass the faulting page into the migrate_vma functions so that
if an elevated reference count is found it can be checked to see if it's
expected or not.

description: A vulnerability was found in Linux Kernel. It has been classified as problematic. Affected is an unknown function of the file mm/memory.c of the component Driver Handler. The manipulation leads to use after free. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue. The identifier of this vulnerability is VDB-211020.

code_evidence: The function declares struct migrate_vma mig, zero-initializes it, and passes it to migrate_vma_setup at line 20. It then reads *mig.src at lines 33-34 and writes *mig.dst at line 42 before calling migrate_vma_pages and migrate_vma_finalize on the same mig. The page faulting into device memory is migrated without holding any reference on the source page, so a concurrent migration can free it and its pgmap while mig still references it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the function continues to operate on a struct page after a concurrent free, and the patch note explicitly describes use-after-free from accessing freed pages. This is not merely a missing NULL check; the defect is lifetime of the referenced page across the migration sequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: migrate_vma_setup selects the device-private source page without taking a reference, so nothing prevents a concurrent migration from freeing the page and underlying pgmap. Trigger: a CPU access to device-private memory races with migration/unload. Consequence: migrate_pfn_to_page, migrate_vma_pages or migrate_vma_finalize dereference freed struct page or pgmap state, yielding use-after-free crashes or invalid function-pointer access.

commit_msg:
babeld: fix #10487 by adding a check on packet length

The body length of a packet should satisfy the condition:
packetlen >= bodylen + 4. Otherwise, heap overflows may happen.

Signed-off-by: whichbug <whichbug@github.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['', '    if(bodylen + 4 > packetlen) {', '        flog_err(EC_BABEL_PACKET, "Received truncated packet (%d + 4 > %d).",', '                 bodylen, packetlen);', '        bodylen = packetlen - 4;', '    }'], 'added_lines': []}
description: A buffer overflow vulnerability exists in FRRouting through 8.1.0 due to missing a check on the input packet length in the babel_packet_examin function in babeld/message.c.

code_evidence: Line 37 reads the attacker-controlled body length from packet+2 into bodylen. Lines 38-42 clamp bodylen to packetlen-4 when bodylen+4 exceeds packetlen, so the declared quantity is validated before use.
The loop at 43-44 iterates i<bodylen over the now-bounded body; message is packet+4+i, and line 266 advances i by len+2, keeping parsing within the validated body length.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-1284 fits because the function consumes an input-specified length (bodylen) and must validate it against the received packet size before using it to control iteration and pointer arithmetic. The clamp is exactly validation of that specified quantity; a missing check yields the related out-of-bounds read/write.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the message body length field decoded from the packet is a specified quantity that must be checked against the actual packet length. Without the clamp at lines 38-42, an oversized bodylen lets the loop and message accesses read past the buffer; the check bounds bodylen to packetlen-4, preventing out-of-bounds access.

commit_msg:
AMD/IOMMU: Cease using a dynamic height for the IOMMU pagetables

update_paging_mode() has multiple bugs:

 1) Booting with iommu=debug will cause it to inform you that that it called
    without the pdev_list lock held.
 2) When growing by more than a single level, it leaks the newly allocated
    table(s) in the case of a further error.

Furthermore, the choice of default level for a domain has issues:

 1) All HVM guests grow from 2 to 3 levels during construction because of the
    position of the VRAM just below the 4G boundary, so defaulting to 2 is a
    waste of effort.
 2) The limit for PV guests doesn't take memory hotplug into account, and
    isn't dynamic at runtime like HVM guests.  This means that a PV guest may
    get RAM which it can't map in the IOMMU.

The dynamic height is a property unique to AMD, and adds a substantial
quantity of complexity for what is a marginal performance improvement.  Remove
the complexity by removing the dynamic height.

PV guests now get 3 or 4 levels based on any hotplug regions in the host.
This only makes a difference for hardware which previously had all RAM below
the 512G boundary, and a hotplug region above.

HVM guests now get 4 levels (which will be sufficient until 256TB guests
become a thing), because we don't currently have the information to know when
3 would be safe to use.

The overhead of this extra level is not expected to be noticeable.  It costs
one page (4k) per domain, and one extra IO-TLB paging structure cache entry
which is very hot and less likely to be evicted.

This is XSA-311.

Signed-off-by: Andrew Cooper <andrew.cooper3@citrix.com>
Acked-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>

description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.12.x allowing x86 AMD HVM guest OS users to cause a denial of service or possibly gain privileges by triggering data-structure access during pagetable-height updates. When running on AMD systems with an IOMMU, Xen attempted to dynamically adapt the number of levels of pagetables (the pagetable height) in the IOMMU according to the guest's address space size. The code to select and update the height had several bugs. Notably, the update was done without taking a lock which is necessary for safe operation. A malicious guest administrator can cause Xen to access data structures while they are being modified, causing Xen to crash. Privilege escalation is thought to be very difficult but cannot be ruled out. Additionally, there is a potential memory leak of 4kb per guest boot, under memory pressure. Only Xen on AMD CPUs is vulnerable. Xen running on Intel CPUs is not vulnerable. ARM systems are not vulnerable. Only systems where guests are given direct access to physical devices are vulnerable. Systems which do not use PCI pass-through are not vulnerable. Only HVM guests can exploit the vulnerability. PV and PVH guests cannot. All versions of Xen with IOMMU support are vulnerable.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The shown function only assigns a paging_mode value and returns; it contains no memory allocation or release, so it cannot demonstrate a missing release of allocated memory (CWE-401).

description: In Wireshark 2.6.0, 2.4.0 to 2.4.6, and 2.2.0 to 2.2.14, the GSM A DTAP dissector could crash. This was addressed in epan/dissectors/packet-gsm_a_dtap.c by fixing an off-by-one error that caused a buffer overflow.

code_evidence: Line 26 computes ia5_string_len from the remaining packet length, then line 27 duplicates that many bytes and line 28 allocates exactly ia5_string_len bytes for the output address string.
The loop at lines 30-38 converts each byte; line 39 calls IA5_7BIT_decode on the buffer sized without room for a terminator, and line 40 uses the result as a string for the tree item.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The allocation at line 28 is one byte too small for the terminator written at line 39, producing a write outside the intended buffer boundary, which is CWE-119. This is an off-by-one allocation sizing error rather than an unbounded copy or a read overrun.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The output buffer is allocated with exactly ia5_string_len bytes, but IA5_7BIT_decode writes a NUL terminator after decoding, so the write extends one byte past the allocation. A packet with a type-of-subaddress field of zero and AFI 0x50 triggers this path; the resulting heap write can corrupt adjacent memory and crash the dissector.

commit_msg:
specrec: better handle unexpected PS

Parametric Stereo (PS) can arrive at any moment in input files. PS
changes the number of output channels and therefore requires more
allocated memory in various structures from hDecoder.

The current faad2 code attempts to perform allocation surgery in
hDecoder to recover from this. This works well when there is only one
frame channel, else it creates large number of memory corruption
issues.

If there is more than one input channel, return cleanly with error
code. It would be nice to handle this, but this is likely to be a lot
of work and is beyond the scope of a security fix.

This commit addresses CVE-2018-20360 and CVE-2018-20199 (fixes #32,
fixes #24).
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        /* element inconsistency */', '', '        /* this only happens if PS is actually found but not in the first frame', '        /* reset the allocation */', '        hDecoder->element_alloced[hDecoder->fr_ch_ele] = 0;', '', '        hDecoder->element_output_channels[hDecoder->fr_ch_ele] = output_channels;', '', '        //return 21;'], 'added_lines': ['        /* element inconsistency', '         * this only happens if PS is actually found but not in the first frame', '        if (hDecoder->fr_channels == 1) {', '            /* reset the allocation */', '            hDecoder->element_alloced[hDecoder->fr_ch_ele] = 0;', '            hDecoder->element_output_channels[hDecoder->fr_ch_ele] = output_channels;', '        } else {', '            return 21;', '        }']}
description: An invalid memory address dereference was discovered in the sbr_process_channel function of libfaad/sbr_dec.c in Freeware Advanced Audio Decoder 2 (FAAD2) 2.8.8. The vulnerability causes a segmentation fault and application crash, which leads to denial of service.

code_evidence: PS presence selects output_channels=2, otherwise 1, based on hDecoder->ps_used[hDecoder->fr_ch_ele].
If element_output_channels was previously set to a different value, the code zeroes element_alloced and overwrites element_output_channels with the new count, discarding the old allocation state.
Because element_alloced is reset, allocate_single_channel is re-invoked with the new output_channels, reallocating buffers sized for a different channel count.

When PS is later absent but element_output_channels is 2, memcpy writes into hDecoder->time_out[ch+1] copying frame_size bytes from time_out[ch], without verifying that ch+1 buffer exists and is large enough.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs a memcpy into hDecoder->time_out[ch+1] and relies on channel-count bookkeeping that can be reset, allowing operations beyond the intended buffer boundary. This is a memory-buffer bounds violation matching CWE-119; CWE-787/125 would be more specific, but the target class encompasses the out-of-bounds read/write behavior.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function reallocates channel buffers whenever the PS-derived output channel count changes, but downstream code still indexes time_out[ch+1] under the assumption it was allocated for two channels. Trigger: PS appears after the first frame or disappears mid-stream, causing element_output_channels and element_alloced to be reset inconsistently with actual allocated buffer sizes. Consequence: out-of-bounds memory access/corruption, leading to crash or denial of service.

commit_msg:
bn/bn_exp.c: constant-time MOD_EXP_CTIME_COPY_FROM_PREBUF.

Performance penalty varies from platform to platform, and even
key length. For rsa2048 sign it was observed to reach almost 10%.

CVE-2016-0702

Reviewed-by: Richard Levitte <levitte@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Rich Salz <rsalz@openssl.org>
(cherry picked from master)

Resolved conflicts:
	crypto/bn/bn_exp.c
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['                                        int width)', '    size_t i, j;', '    for (i = 0, j = idx; i < top * sizeof b->d[0]; i++, j += width) {', '        buf[j] = ((unsigned char *)b->d)[i];'], 'added_lines': ['                                        int window)', '    int i, j;', '    int width = 1 << window;', '    BN_ULONG *table = (BN_ULONG *)buf;', '    for (i = 0, j = idx; i < top; i++, j += width) {', '        table[j] = b->d[i];']}
description: The MOD_EXP_CTIME_COPY_FROM_PREBUF function in crypto/bn/bn_exp.c in OpenSSL 1.0.1 before 1.0.1s and 1.0.2 before 1.0.2g does not properly consider cache-bank access times during modular exponentiation, which makes it easier for local users to discover RSA keys by running a crafted application on the same Intel Sandy Bridge CPU core as a victim and leveraging cache-bank conflicts, aka a "CacheBleed" attack.

code_evidence: The precomputed table is copied byte-by-byte into buf at index j = idx + i*width, where width is the table stride. The copy loop iterates up to top*sizeof(b->d[0]) bytes and writes buf[j] one byte at a time at a fixed stride, so the memory access pattern and cache-bank usage depend on the secret exponent-derived table index and the BIGNUM contents.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function's secret-dependent access pattern leaks private key information to an unauthorized local observer, directly supporting exposure of sensitive information (CWE-200). The weakness is the side-channel disclosure itself; CWE-200 fits as the information-exposure outcome grounded in the observable copy behavior.

evidence_lines.code:
for (i = 0, j = idx; i < top * sizeof b->d[0]; i++, j += width) {
buf[j] = ((unsigned char *)b->d)[i];

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the table copy performs secret-dependent memory accesses (byte-wise writes at a secret-derived stride/offset) during modular exponentiation, so the data written and the cache-bank timing vary with the private key. Trigger: an attacker co-resident on the same Sandy Bridge core measures cache-bank conflicts while the victim signs. Consequence: RSA private-key bits are disclosed through the timing side channel (CacheBleed).

Fixed invalid memory access bugs when decoding JPEG Exif data

description: The iw_get_ui16le function in imagew-util.c:405:23 in libimageworsener.a in ImageWorsener 1.3.1 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (invalid read and SEGV) via a crafted image, related to imagew-jpeg.c.

code_evidence: Line 10 bounds-checks ifd but computes e->d_len-18 without first ensuring e->d_len>=18, so a short buffer underflows the unsigned subtraction and admits an out-of-range ifd. Line 11 then reads a 16-bit tag count at &e->d[ifd]. Line 15 derives tag_pos and reads a 16-bit tag id at &e->d[tag_pos], with only a tag_pos+12>e->d_len guard and no lower-bound validation.

It is not merely an integer underflow (CWE-191); the underflow is the enabling cause of the out-of-bounds read itself.

Trigger is a truncated Exif buffer; the supported consequence is an invalid out-of-bounds read, causing a crash/SEGV (denial of service) and potential disclosure of adjacent memory.

commit_msg:
Avoid buffer read overflow on vcl_error and -sfile

The file stevedore may return a buffer larger than asked for when
requesting storage. Due to lack of check for this condition, the code
to copy the synthetic error memory buffer from vcl_error would overrun
the buffer.

Patch by @shamger

Fixes: #2429
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (l > ll)', '\t\t\tl = ll;']}
description: vbf_stp_error in bin/varnishd/cache/cache_fetch.c in Varnish HTTP Cache 4.1.x before 4.1.9 and 5.x before 5.2.1 allows remote attackers to obtain sensitive information from process memory because a VFP_GetStorage buffer is larger than intended in certain circumstances involving -sfile Stevedore transient objects.

code_evidence: l is initialized to the remaining length ll, then VFP_GetStorage may increase l to a value larger than requested; the returned l is used directly as the memcpy length into ptr and to advance o and ll without any bound check.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The memcpy length l derives from a storage backend and is not constrained to the source buffer's remaining length, so a read operation crosses the intended buffer boundary, matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds memory operation. The missing l > ll clamp is the direct cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the code trusts VFP_GetStorage to leave l no larger than the requested size, but -sfile Stevedore can return a larger buffer. Trigger: a synthetic vcl_error body stored via -sfile returns l > ll. Consequence: memcpy reads beyond the synth_body VSB buffer, copying adjacent process memory into the object, causing out-of-bounds read and information disclosure.

commit_msg:
Blamed commit changed:
    ptr = kmalloc(size);
    if (ptr)
      size = ksize(ptr);

to:
    size = kmalloc_size_roundup(size);
    ptr = kmalloc(size);

This allowed various crash as reported by syzbot [1]
and Kyle Zeng.

Problem is that if @size is bigger than 0x80000001,
kmalloc_size_roundup(size) returns 2^32.

kmalloc_reserve() uses a 32bit variable (obj_size),
so 2^32 is truncated to 0.

kmalloc(0) returns ZERO_SIZE_PTR which is not handled by
skb allocations.

Following trace can be triggered if a netdev->mtu is set
close to 0x7fffffff

We might in the future limit netdev->mtu to more sensible
limit (like KMALLOC_MAX_SIZE).

This patch is based on a syzbot report, and also a report
and tentative fix from Kyle Zeng.

Fixes: 12d6c1d3a2ad ("skbuff: Proactively round up to kmalloc bucket size")
Reported-by: syzbot <syzkaller@googlegroups.com>
Reported-by: Kyle Zeng <zengyhkyle@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Cc: Kees Cook <keescook@chromium.org>
Cc: Vlastimil Babka <vbabka@suse.cz>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tunsigned int obj_size;', '\t*size = obj_size = kmalloc_size_roundup(obj_size);'], 'added_lines': ['\tsize_t obj_size;', '', '\tobj_size = kmalloc_size_roundup(obj_size);', '\t/* The following cast might truncate high-order bits of obj_size, this', '\t * is harmless because kmalloc(obj_size >= 2^32) will fail anyway.', '\t */', '\t*size = (unsigned int)obj_size;', '']}
description: An integer overflow flaw was found in the Linux kernel. This issue leads to the kernel allocating `skb_shared_info` in the userspace, which is exploitable in systems without SMAP protection since `skb_shared_info` contains references to function pointers.

code_evidence: Line 5 stores the allocation size in a 32-bit unsigned int obj_size. Line 7 rounds *size up via SKB_HEAD_ALIGN, which can exceed 0xffffffff. Line 20 assigns kmalloc_size_roundup(obj_size) back into the 32-bit obj_size and *size; for values above 0x80000001 the roundup yields 2^32, which truncates to 0 in the 32-bit variable. Lines 21-23 then call kmalloc_node_track_caller with that truncated obj_size, so a zero-size allocation (ZERO_SIZE_PTR) is returned while callers assume a valid buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the size computation produces a value (2^32) that cannot be represented in the unsigned int obj_size and wraps to a small value, which then drives a memory allocation. This is distinct from a pure bounds check omission: the unsafe behavior stems from the integer wraparound of the computed allocation size.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the rounded allocation size is stored in a 32-bit unsigned int, so a roundup result of 2^32 wraps to 0. Trigger: a caller supplies a size (e.g. netdev->mtu near 0x7fffffff) whose SKB_HEAD_ALIGN/roundup result is 2^32. Consequence: kmalloc of size 0 returns ZERO_SIZE_PTR, and subsequent skb_shared_info writes land in user-accessible low memory, causing crashes and potential memory corruption/exploitation.

commit_msg:
Problem: pointer overflow in zmq::v2_decoder_t::size_ready leading to remote code execution (issue #3351)

Solution: refactor bounds check arithmetic such that no overflow shall occur

Signed-off-by: Guido Vranken <guidovranken@gmail.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['                  || ((unsigned char *) read_pos_ + msg_size_', '                      > (allocator.data () + allocator.size ())))) {'], 'added_lines': ['                  || msg_size_ > allocator.data () + allocator.size () - read_pos_ )) {']}
description: A pointer overflow, with code execution, was discovered in ZeroMQ libzmq (aka 0MQ) 4.2.x and 4.3.x before 4.3.1. A v2_decoder.cpp zmq::v2_decoder_t::size_ready integer overflow allows an authenticated attacker to overwrite an arbitrary amount of bytes beyond the bounds of a buffer, which can be leveraged to run arbitrary code on the target system. The memory layout allows the attacker to inject OS commands into a data structure located immediately after the problematic buffer (i.e., it is not necessary to use a typical buffer-overflow exploitation technique that changes the flow of control).

code_evidence: The bounds check computes `(unsigned char *) read_pos_ + msg_size_` and compares the resulting pointer against `allocator.data () + allocator.size ()`. Because `msg_size_` is an attacker-controlled uint64_t accepted after only a max-size and size_t-narrowing check, the pointer addition can wrap around the address space, so the comparison may evaluate false and the zero-copy path is taken.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the defect is an integer/pointer arithmetic wraparound in size validation, which the logic assumes yields a larger address. The fix rewrites the comparison as subtraction so no overflow occurs. This is distinct from a plain out-of-bounds write, which is the consequence rather than the root cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the size/offset arithmetic in the arena bounds check can overflow because the sum `read_pos_ + msg_size_` is formed before validation. Trigger: a v2 message declaring a very large size that passes the earlier checks. Consequence: the check is bypassed, `_in_progress.init` references an out-of-bounds region, enabling arbitrary memory overwrite beyond the buffer.

commit_msg:
avcodec/x86/mpegvideodsp: Fix signedness bug in need_emu

Fixes: out of array read
Fixes: 3516/attachment-311488.dat

Found-by: Insu Yun, Georgia Tech.
Tested-by: wuninsu@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
(cherry picked from commit 58cf31cee7a456057f337b3102a03206d833d5e8)
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    int need_emu  =  (unsigned) ix >= width  - w ||', '                     (unsigned) iy >= height - h;'], 'added_lines': ['    int need_emu  =  (unsigned) ix >= width  - w || width < w ||', '                     (unsigned) iy >= height - h || height< h', '                     ;']}
description: The gmc_mmx function in libavcodec/x86/mpegvideodsp.c in FFmpeg 2.3 and 3.4 does not properly validate widths and heights, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (integer signedness error and out-of-array read) via a crafted MPEG file.

code_evidence: need_emu decides whether the block lies outside the frame, but it only tests (unsigned)ix >= width - w and (unsigned)iy >= height - h; when width < w or height < h, these subtractions wrap, so need_emu can be false even though the block does not fit in the frame.

Because need_emu is false, the guard at line 38 is skipped and src += ix + iy * stride (line 37) is used directly by the MMX reads of src[0], src[1], src[stride], src[stride+1] without the edge-emulation buffer that would clamp accesses to the frame.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads source pixels through a pointer computed without validating that the block fits within width/height, so memory beyond the intended buffer is read, which is exactly CWE-125. The signedness/underflow is the cause; the out-of-bounds read is the supported consequence, not a separate integer-overflow label.

evidence_lines.code:
int need_emu  =  (unsigned) ix >= width  - w ||
(unsigned) iy >= height - h;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the bounds check treats width - w and height - h as unsigned, so when a crafted MPEG file supplies a height smaller than the fixed block height h, the underflow makes need_emu false. Trigger: a frame/block where height < h (or width < w). The unchecked src pointer then feeds the MMX load, reading past the end of the source buffer, causing an out-of-array read and denial of service.

commit_msg:
mm/rmap: Fix anon_vma->degree ambiguity leading to double-reuse

anon_vma->degree tracks the combined number of child anon_vmas and VMAs
that use the anon_vma as their ->anon_vma.

anon_vma_clone() then assumes that for any anon_vma attached to
src->anon_vma_chain other than src->anon_vma, it is impossible for it to
be a leaf node of the VMA tree, meaning that for such VMAs ->degree is
elevated by 1 because of a child anon_vma, meaning that if ->degree
equals 1 there are no VMAs that use the anon_vma as their ->anon_vma.

This assumption is wrong because the ->degree optimization leads to leaf
nodes being abandoned on anon_vma_clone() - an existing anon_vma is
reused and no new parent-child relationship is created.  So it is
possible to reuse an anon_vma for one VMA while it is still tied to
another VMA.

This is an issue because is_mergeable_anon_vma() and its callers assume
that if two VMAs have the same ->anon_vma, the list of anon_vmas
attached to the VMAs is guaranteed to be the same.  When this assumption
is violated, vma_merge() can merge pages into a VMA that is not attached
to the corresponding anon_vma, leading to dangling page->mapping
pointers that will be dereferenced during rmap walks.

Fix it by separately tracking the number of child anon_vmas and the
number of VMAs using the anon_vma as their ->anon_vma.

Fixes: 7a3ef208e662 ("mm: prevent endless growth of anon_vma hierarchy")
Cc: stable@kernel.org
Acked-by: Michal Hocko <mhocko@suse.com>
Acked-by: Vlastimil Babka <vbabka@suse.cz>
Signed-off-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tanon_vma->parent->degree++;'], 'added_lines': ['\tanon_vma->num_active_vmas++;', '\tanon_vma->parent->num_children++;']}
description: mm/rmap.c in the Linux kernel before 5.19.7 has a use-after-free related to leaf anon_vma double reuse.

code_evidence: anon_vma_fork allocates a new anon_vma and an avc; on avc allocation failure it jumps to out_error_free_anon_vma and frees the freshly allocated anon_vma via put_anon_vma (lines 29-30).
On success, the new anon_vma is linked to the VMA and the parent's degree is incremented (line 26), the counter that the flawed clone logic relied on to infer leaf status.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The supported consequence is dereferencing freed page->mapping memory during rmap traversal, matching CWE-416. The defect is an accounting error enabling stale references, not an out-of-bounds access or double-free itself.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The fork path increments only the combined parent->degree counter when a new child anon_vma is created, so the count cannot distinguish child anon_vmas from VMAs directly using the anon_vma. anon_vma_clone then misjudges leaf status and may reuse an anon_vma still tied to another VMA; merging pages into an unattached VMA leaves dangling page->mapping pointers that are dereferenced during rmap walks, causing use-after-free.

description: In QEMU 4.1.0, an out-of-bounds read flaw was found in the ATI VGA implementation. It occurs in the ati_cursor_define() routine while handling MMIO write operations through the ati_mm_write() callback. A malicious guest could abuse this flaw to crash the QEMU process, resulting in a denial of service.

code_evidence: The source pointer is computed directly from guest-controlled register values: src = s->vga.vram_ptr + s->regs.cur_offset - (s->regs.cur_hv_offs >> 16) - (s->regs.cur_hv_offs & 0xffff) * 16. No bounds check constrains cur_offset or cur_hv_offs against the VRAM size.
The loops then dereference src at i*16+j and i*16+j+8 for i up to 63 and j up to 7, reading up to 1024 bytes from that unchecked offset.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the function performs out-of-bounds reads of guest VRAM via unchecked pointer arithmetic and dereference. It is not CWE-787 since no out-of-bounds write occurs here; the flaw is a read past the intended buffer.

evidence_lines.code:

(s->regs.cur_hv_offs >> 16) - (s->regs.cur_hv_offs & 0xffff) * 16;

data[idx] = src[i * 16 + j];
data[512 + idx] = src[i * 16 + j + 8];

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the cursor source offset is derived from attacker-controlled MMIO registers without validating it lies within video memory, and raw pointer arithmetic is used instead of a bounded accessor. Trigger: a guest writes cursor registers so the computed offset falls outside VRAM. Consequence: the host reads past the intended buffer, potentially crashing QEMU (DoS) or leaking adjacent memory.

description: Net-SNMP through 5.8 has Improper Privilege Management because SNMP WRITE access to the EXTEND MIB provides the ability to run arbitrary commands as root.

code_evidence: The write-handling switch is guarded only by #ifndef NETSNMP_NO_WRITE_SUPPORT, so when write support is compiled in, the SET path is active by default. MODE_SET_RESERVE1 reads idx from the attacker-supplied var_val and accepts it when it equals 1, then MODE_SET_COMMIT calls netsnmp_cache_check_and_reload on exten->efix_entry->cache, which re-executes the configured extend command. No additional privilege or access constraint gates this path.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe operation is missing privilege restriction on a privileged action (command execution via SNMP SET), i.e. improper management of who may exercise that capability. This matches CWE-269 at the class level; the diff's added ENABLE_EXTEND_WRITE_ACCESS gate confirms the write path was not properly privilege-restricted.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the EXTEND MIB SET handler is enabled by default whenever write support exists, without a dedicated opt-in restriction. Trigger: an SNMP principal with WRITE access issues a SET with integer value 1, reaching MODE_SET_COMMIT and reloading the extend cache, which runs the configured command. Consequence: the command executes with the agent's privileges (root), yielding an unintended sphere of control.

joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function's error path leaves *outBox NULL while signaling a skippable condition; the downstream dereference of that NULL pointer is the NULL Pointer Dereference described by CWE-476. The fix maps GF_SKIP_BOX to GF_ISOM_INVALID_FILE for root boxes, preventing the NULL output from being used.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the error path clears *outBox and returns GF_SKIP_BOX for a root box, so the caller receives NULL output but no invalid-file indication. Trigger: a root-level box whose size is 0 and is not at file level returns GF_SKIP_BOX. Supported consequence: the caller dereferences the NULL box pointer, causing a denial-of-service crash.

patch 8.0.0378: possible overflow when reading corrupted undo file

The allocation size is computed as sizeof(char_u *) * uep->ue_size without checking that the multiplication can overflow, so a corrupted ue_size can wrap the product to a small value.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The multiplication sizeof(char_u *) * uep->ue_size is an integer calculation that can overflow or wrap when ue_size is large, matching CWE-190. The wrapped allocation size then feeds a heap buffer write loop, distinguishing this from a plain missing bounds check.

vim_memset(array, 0, sizeof(char_u *) * uep->ue_size);
for (i = 0; i < uep->ue_size; ++i)

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the unchecked file-controlled ue_size is multiplied by the pointer size when computing the allocation length, so a large value wraps the product. Trigger: reading a corrupted undo file whose ue_size makes the multiplication exceed the integer range. Consequence: U_ALLOC_LINE receives a too-small size, but the loop at line 33 still iterates ue_size times writing array[i], causing out-of-bounds writes.

commit_msg: capture: properly validate capture length calculated from IP headers #430
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    // Check maximum capture len', '    if (*caplen > MAX_CAPTURE_LEN)', '        return NULL;', '']}
description: Sngrep v1.6.0 was discovered to contain a stack buffer overflow via the function packet_set_payload at /src/packet.c.

code_evidence: *caplen is set from link_hl + ip_len where ip_len comes from the IP header, so an attacker-controlled header can produce a large capture length.
When reassembly completes, len_data is summed from frame IP lengths and is only compared against MAX_CAPTURE_LEN before the buffer is memset and filled.
The IPv4 memcpy writes frame payload at packet + link_hl + ip_hl + fragment offset for ntohs(ip_len)-ip_hl*4 bytes without checking against the allocated capture buffer.
The IPv6 memcpy similarly writes at packet + link_hl + ip_hl + sizeof(ip6_frag) + fragment offset with the IPv6 payload length.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs memcpy writes into a packet buffer using attacker-influenced offsets and lengths, which can write past the end of the intended buffer, directly matching CWE-787 (Out-of-bounds Write).

evidence_lines.code:
*caplen = link_hl + ip_len;
*size = *caplen - link_hl - ip_hl;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: IP header length fields (ip_len and per-frame payload lengths) drive the destination offsets and copy sizes in the reassembly memcpy calls, while the destination buffer size is derived from the same untrusted values. A crafted fragmented IP packet can make the computed offset plus payload length exceed the intended buffer, causing an out-of-bounds write.

commit_msg:
When the link layer is terminating, x25->neighbour will be set to NULL
in x25_disconnect(). As a result, it could cause null-ptr-deref bugs in
x25_sendmsg(),x25_recvmsg() and x25_connect(). One of the bugs is
shown below.

    (Thread 1)                 |  (Thread 2)
x25_link_terminated()          | x25_recvmsg()
 x25_kill_by_neigh()           |  ...
  x25_disconnect()             |  lock_sock(sk)
   ...                         |  ...
   x25->neighbour = NULL //(1) |
   ...                         |  x25->neighbour->extended //(2)

The code sets NULL to x25->neighbour in position (1) and dereferences
x25->neighbour in position (2), which could cause null-ptr-deref bug.

This patch adds lock_sock() in x25_kill_by_neigh() in order to synchronize
with x25_sendmsg(), x25_recvmsg() and x25_connect(). What`s more, the
sock held by lock_sock() is not NULL, because it is extracted from x25_list
and uses x25_list_lock to synchronize.

Fixes: 4becb7ee5b3d ("net/x25: Fix x25_neigh refcnt leak when x25 disconnect")
Signed-off-by: Duoming Zhou <duoming@zju.edu.cn>
Reviewed-by: Lin Ma <linma@zju.edu.cn>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tsk_for_each(s, &x25_list)', '\t\tif (x25_sk(s)->neighbour == nb)', ''], 'added_lines': ['\tsk_for_each(s, &x25_list) {', '\t\tif (x25_sk(s)->neighbour == nb) {', '\t\t\twrite_unlock_bh(&x25_list_lock);', '\t\t\tlock_sock(s);', '\t\t\trelease_sock(s);', '\t\t\twrite_lock_bh(&x25_list_lock);', '\t\t}', '\t}']}
description: A NULL pointer dereference flaw was found in the Linux kernel’s X.25 set of standardized network protocols functionality in the way a user terminates their session using a simulated Ethernet card and continued usage of this connection. This flaw allows a local user to crash the system.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The shown function only iterates x25_list and calls x25_disconnect under x25_list_lock with no NULL dereference; the NULL x25->neighbour dereference occurs in x25_sendmsg/recvmsg/connect, which are not in this function.

commit_msg:
copyin_link() tries to allocate (unsigned int)c_filesize + 1 bytes.
If c_filesize == UINT_MAX, this works out as 0 bytes, resulting in a
null pointer and a subsequent SIGSEGV.

The previous commit made this impossible on 32-bit systems.

CVE-2021-31871

Signed-off-by: Ben Hutchings <ben@decadent.org.uk>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tlink_name = (char *)xmalloc((unsigned int)file_hdr->c_filesize + 1);'], 'added_lines': ['\tlink_name = (char *)xmalloc(file_hdr->c_filesize + 1);']}
description: An issue was discovered in klibc before 2.0.9. An integer overflow in the cpio command may result in a NULL pointer dereference on 64-bit systems.

code_evidence: Line 5 computes the allocation size as (unsigned int)file_hdr->c_filesize + 1, truncating the 64-bit c_filesize to 32 bits before adding one. When c_filesize is UINT_MAX, the addition wraps to 0, so xmalloc(0) returns a null or minimal pointer. Line 6 then indexes link_name[c_filesize] and line 7 reads c_filesize bytes into it, dereferencing the undersized buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is an integer overflow/wraparound in a memory-size calculation that the logic assumes yields a larger value; the wrapped result is then used for allocation and indexing. This matches CWE-190 rather than merely a NULL dereference, which is the downstream consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the size calculation truncates c_filesize to unsigned int and then adds 1, allowing wraparound to zero for c_filesize == UINT_MAX. Trigger: a crafted cpio archive header with that size. Consequence: xmalloc(0) yields a null/invalid pointer, and the subsequent write at index c_filesize causes a NULL pointer dereference and crash (SIGSEGV), and potentially memory corruption.

commit_msg:
CVE-2017-13008/IEEE 802.11: Fix TIM bitmap copy to copy from p + offset.

offset has already been advanced to point to the bitmap; we shouldn't
add the amount to advance again.

This fixes a buffer over-read discovered by Brian 'geeknik' Carpenter.

Add a test using the capture file supplied by the reporter(s).

While we're at it, remove some redundant tests - we've already checked,
before the case statement, whether we have captured the entire
information element and whether the entire information element is
present in the on-the-wire packet; in the cases for particular IEs, we
only need to make sure we don't go past the end of the IE.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t\tif (!ND_TTEST2(*(p + offset), ssid.length))', '\t\t\t\t\treturn 0;', '\t\t\t\tif (length < ssid.length)', '\t\t\t\t\treturn 0;', '\t\t\t\t\treturn 0;', '\t\t\t\tif (!ND_TTEST2(*(p + offset), challenge.length))', '\t\t\t\t\treturn 0;', '\t\t\t\tif (length < challenge.length)', '\t\t\t\t\treturn 0;', '\t\t\t\tif (!ND_TTEST2(*(p + offset), rates.length))', '\t\t\t\t\treturn 0;', '\t\t\t\tif (length < rates.length)', '\t\t\tmemcpy(tim.bitmap, p + offset + 3, tim.length - 3);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\tmemcpy(tim.bitmap, p + offset, tim.length - 3);']}
description: The IEEE 802.11 parser in tcpdump before 4.9.2 has a buffer over-read in print-802_11.c:parse_elements().

code_evidence: In the E_TIM case, after the two-byte IE header is consumed (offset += 2), tim.length is checked only against sizeof tim.bitmap at [137], and tim.count is copied at [139] with length 3, then offset is advanced by 3 at [140]. The bitmap copy at [142] uses p + offset + 3 while offset already points past the count bytes, so the read starts 3 bytes beyond the intended bitmap start and extends tim.length - 3 bytes, reaching up to 3 bytes past the validated region.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The faulty pointer arithmetic causes a read of memory beyond the intended buffer bound, matching CWE-125 Out-of-bounds Read. It is a read overrun, not a write or unbounded length, so CWE-125 fits rather than an out-of-bounds write.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the bitmap source pointer double-applies the 3-byte count offset (p + offset + 3) after offset was already advanced by 3. Trigger: an E_TIM information element with tim.length > 3 and a bitmap length that passes the size check. Consequence: memcpy reads past the validated on-wire element, causing an out-of-bounds read (buffer over-read).

commit_msg: https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/issues/1641
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  error_manager->profile=NULL;'], 'added_lines': ['  error_manager->profile=NULL;']}
description: ImageMagick before 7.0.8-55 has a use-after-free in DestroyStringInfo in MagickCore/string.c because the error manager is mishandled in coders/jpeg.c.

code_evidence: Line 54 stores the newly allocated StringInfo in error_manager->profile, making it reachable from the persistent ErrorManager. Lines 65-72 handle the short-read case: profile is freed via DestroyStringInfo at line 67, an exception is thrown, and the function returns FALSE. In the original code error_manager->profile=NULL was placed only after this block (line 73), so the dangling pointer remains in error_manager->profile throughout the error path.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because a heap object is freed at line 67 while a surviving reference (error_manager->profile) still points to it, and that reference is later reused. This is use-after-free, not a double free: the defect is the stale pointer surviving the free, not freeing the same pointer twice.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the error path frees the StringInfo but does not clear error_manager->profile before returning, leaving a stale pointer in the shared ErrorManager. Trigger: truncated/insufficient ICC profile data causes i != length. Consequence: later use of error_manager->profile (e.g., DestroyStringInfo in MagickCore/string.c) dereferences freed memory, giving use-after-free (crash or memory corruption). The patch moves the NULL assignment before the error return.

commit_msg:
A recent fuzzed filesystem image cached random dcache corruption
when the reproducer was run. This often showed up as panics in
lookup_slow() on a null inode->i_ops pointer when doing pathwalks.

BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at 0000000000000000
....
Call Trace:
 lookup_slow+0x44/0x60
 walk_component+0x3dd/0x9f0
 link_path_walk+0x4a7/0x830
 path_lookupat+0xc1/0x470
 filename_lookup+0x129/0x270
 user_path_at_empty+0x36/0x40
 path_listxattr+0x98/0x110
 SyS_listxattr+0x13/0x20
 do_syscall_64+0xf5/0x280
 entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x42/0xb7

but had many different failure modes including deadlocks trying to
lock the inode that was just allocated or KASAN reports of
use-after-free violations.

The cause of the problem was a corrupt INOBT on a v4 fs where the
root inode was marked as free in the inobt record. Hence when we
allocated an inode, it chose the root inode to allocate, found it in
the cache and re-initialised it.

We recently fixed a similar inode allocation issue caused by inobt
record corruption problem in xfs_iget_cache_miss() in commit
ee457001ed6c ("xfs: catch inode allocation state mismatch
corruption"). This change adds similar checks to the cache-hit path
to catch it, and turns the reproducer into a corruption shutdown
situation.

Reported-by: Wen Xu <wen.xu@gatech.edu>
Signed-Off-By: Dave Chinner <dchinner@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Christoph Hellwig <hch@lst.de>
Reviewed-by: Carlos Maiolino <cmaiolino@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Darrick J. Wong <darrick.wong@oracle.com>
[darrick: fix typos in comment]
Signed-off-by: Darrick J. Wong <darrick.wong@oracle.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t * If lookup is racing with unlink return an error immediately.', '\tif (VFS_I(ip)->i_mode == 0 && !(flags & XFS_IGET_CREATE)) {', '\t\terror = -ENOENT;', '\t}'], 'added_lines': ['\t * Check the inode free state is valid. This also detects lookup', '\t * racing with unlinks.', '\terror = xfs_iget_check_free_state(ip, flags);', '\tif (error)']}
description: An issue was discovered in fs/xfs/xfs_icache.c in the Linux kernel through 4.17.3. There is a NULL pointer dereference and panic in lookup_slow() on a NULL inode->i_ops pointer when doing pathwalks on a corrupted xfs image. This occurs because of a lack of proper validation that cached inodes are free during allocation.

code_evidence: Lines 25-28 only check VFS_I(ip)->i_mode == 0 to detect a free inode when XFS_IGET_CREATE is not set; the cached inode's on-disk free state is never validated against the inobt record.

Lines 29-38 then treat the cached inode as reclaimable, set XFS_IRECLAIM, release locks and call xfs_reinit_inode() to reinitialise it, even though the root inode was marked free by corrupted inobt data.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The supported consequence is a NULL pointer dereference: the unchecked reuse of a corrupt cached inode leaves inode->i_ops NULL, which lookup_slow() dereferences and crashes. This is directly CWE-476 rather than a generic corruption issue, since the observable weakness is dereferencing a NULL pointer.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the cache-hit path reuses a cached inode based only on the VFS i_mode check and XFS_IRECLAIMABLE flag, without verifying the inode's free state against the inobt. Trigger: a corrupted v4 inobt records the root inode as free, so allocation selects it, finds it cached and reinitialises it. Consequence: the reinitialised inode has a NULL i_ops pointer, and a later pathwalk in lookup_slow() dereferences it, causing a NULL pointer dereference and kernel panic.

commit_msg:
net: rose: fix UAF bugs caused by timer handler

There are UAF bugs in rose_heartbeat_expiry(), rose_timer_expiry()
and rose_idletimer_expiry(). The root cause is that del_timer()
could not stop the timer handler that is running and the refcount
of sock is not managed properly.

One of the UAF bugs is shown below:

    (thread 1)          |        (thread 2)
                        |  rose_bind
                        |  rose_connect
                        |    rose_start_heartbeat
rose_release            |    (wait a time)
  case ROSE_STATE_0     |
  rose_destroy_socket   |  rose_heartbeat_expiry
    rose_stop_heartbeat |
    sock_put(sk)        |    ...
  sock_put(sk) // FREE  |
                        |    bh_lock_sock(sk) // USE

The sock is deallocated by sock_put() in rose_release() and
then used by bh_lock_sock() in rose_heartbeat_expiry().

Although rose_destroy_socket() calls rose_stop_heartbeat(),
it could not stop the timer that is running.

The KASAN report triggered by POC is shown below:

Write of size 4 at addr ffff88800ae59098 by task swapper/3/0
...
Call Trace:

 print_address_description+0x7b/0x440
 print_report+0x101/0x230
 ? irq_work_single+0xbb/0x140
 ? _raw_spin_lock+0x5a/0x110
 kasan_report+0xed/0x120
 ? _raw_spin_lock+0x5a/0x110
 kasan_check_range+0x2bd/0x2e0

description: There are use-after-free vulnerabilities caused by timer handler in net/rose/rose_timer.c of linux that allow attackers to crash linux kernel without any privileges.

code_evidence: The function starts the socket's t2 timer by calling del_timer() directly on rose->timer, but del_timer() only removes a pending timer; it does not synchronize with a handler that is already executing and does not hold any reference on the owning sock.

The timer is then armed with add_timer() after setting its function and expiry. The timer handler runs asynchronously and accesses sk without the socket's refcount being incremented here, so the sock can be freed by rose_release()/sock_put() while the handler still runs.

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: timer start/stop uses plain del_timer()/add_timer() without taking a sock reference for the lifetime of the timer callback. Trigger: a timer expires concurrently with socket release, which frees the sock. Consequence: the timer handler dereferences freed sock memory, producing a use-after-free that can crash or corrupt the kernel.

commit_msg:
tracing/syscalls: Ignore numbers outside NR_syscalls' range

ARM has some private syscalls (for example, set_tls(2)) which lie
outside the range of NR_syscalls.  If any of these are called while
syscall tracing is being performed, out-of-bounds array access will
occur in the ftrace and perf sys_{enter,exit} handlers.

 # trace-cmd record -e raw_syscalls:* true && trace-cmd report
 ...
 true-653   [000]   384.675777: sys_enter:            NR 192 (0, 1000, 3, 4000022, ffffffff, 0)
 true-653   [000]   384.675812: sys_exit:             NR 192 = 1995915264
 true-653   [000]   384.675971: sys_enter:            NR 983045 (76f74480, 76f74000, 76f74b28, 76f74480, 76f76f74, 1)
 true-653   [000]   384.675988: sys_exit:             NR 983045 = 0
 ...

 # trace-cmd record -e syscalls:* true
 [   17.289329] Unable to handle kernel paging request at virtual address aaaaaace
 [   17.289590] pgd = 9e71c000
 [   17.289696] [aaaaaace] *pgd=00000000
 [   17.289985] Internal error: Oops: 5 [#1] PREEMPT SMP ARM
 [   17.290169] Modules linked in:
 [   17.290391] CPU: 0 PID: 704 Comm: true Not tainted 3.18.0-rc2+ #21
 [   17.290585] task: 9f4dab00 ti: 9e710000 task.ti: 9e710000
 [   17.290747] PC is at ftrace_syscall_enter+0x48/0x1f8
 [   17.290866] LR is at syscall_trace_enter+0x124/0x184

Fix this by ignoring out-of-NR_syscalls-bounds syscall numbers.

added the check for less than zero, but it should have also checked
for greater than NR_syscalls.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # 2.6.33+

description: TensorFlow is an open source platform for machine learning. The implementation of `BlockLSTMGradV2` does not fully validate its inputs. This results in a a segfault that can be used to trigger a denial of service attack. We have patched the issue in GitHub commit 2a458fc4866505be27c62f81474ecb2b870498fa. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.10.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.9.1, TensorFlow 2.8.1, and TensorFlow 2.7.2, as these are also affected and still in supported range. There are no known workarounds for this issue.

These unvalidated shapes are then used to allocate outputs and temporaries (e.g., w_tensor->shape() at line 65, b_tensor->shape() at line 77, and batch_cell_shape at lines 78-112) before the functor consumes them.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function accepts tensor inputs and fails to validate their required rank/shape properties before using them, which is improper input validation (CWE-20); the crash is the consequence of the missing check, not a separate memory-safety root cause. The missing rank constraint is the direct defect.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the kernel validates x's rank but not the ranks of w and b before calling dim_size(1)/dim_size(0) on them. Trigger: a caller supplies a w or b tensor of insufficient rank; the out-of-range dim_size access causes a crash. Supported consequence: denial of service via segfault, consistent with the commit description.

commit_msg:
As part of CVE-2013-4288, the D-Bus clients were allowed (and
encouraged) to submit the UID of the subject of authorization checks
to avoid races against UID changes (notably using executables
set-UID to root).

However, that also allowed any client to submit an arbitrary UID, and
that could be used to bypass "can only ask about / affect the same UID"
checks in CheckAuthorization / RegisterAuthenticationAgent /
UnregisterAuthenticationAgent.  This allowed an attacker:

- With CheckAuthorization, to cause the registered authentication
  agent in victim's session to pop up a dialog, or to determine whether
  the victim currently has a temporary authorization to perform an
  operation.

  (In principle, the attacker can also determine whether JavaScript
  rules allow the victim process to perform an operation; however,
  usually rules base their decisions on information determined from
  the supplied UID, so the attacker usually won't learn anything new.)

- With RegisterAuthenticationAgent, to prevent the victim's
  authentication agent to work (for a specific victim process),
  or to learn about which operations requiring authorization
  the victim is attempting.

To fix this, expose internal _polkit_unix_process_get_owner() /
obsolete polkit_unix_process_get_owner() as a private
polkit_unix_process_get_racy_uid__() (being more explicit about the
dangers on relying on it), and use it in
polkit_backend_session_monitor_get_user_for_subject() to return
a boolean indicating whether the subject UID may be caller-chosen.

Then, in the permission checks that require the subject to be
equal to the caller, fail on caller-chosen UIDs (and continue
through the pre-existing code paths which allow root, or root-designated
server processes, to ask about arbitrary subjects.)

Signed-off-by: Miloslav Trmač <mitr@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      process->uid = _polkit_unix_process_get_owner (process, &error);'], 'added_lines': ['      process->uid = polkit_unix_process_get_racy_uid__ (process, &error);']}
description: A flaw was found in polkit before version 0.116. The implementation of the polkit_backend_interactive_authority_check_authorization function in polkitd allows to test for authentication and trigger authentication of unrelated processes owned by other users. This may result in a local DoS and information disclosure.

code_evidence: When the process UID is unset (process->uid == -1), the constructor obtains it via _polkit_unix_process_get_owner() and stores the result in process->uid. This UID is later consumed by polkit_backend_session_monitor_get_user_for_subject() and the CheckAuthorization/RegisterAuthenticationAgent permission checks to decide whether the subject UID matches the caller.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is a missing authorization check: the same-UID constraint that should gate access to another user's authorization state is not enforced. CWE-862 fits because the subject UID is trusted without verification, letting an actor act on resources belonging to other users. This is not merely a race (CWE-367); the defect is the absent authorization constraint on caller-chosen UIDs.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function resolves a process owner UID through a racy lookup and records it without any indication that the UID is caller-chosen or verified. A caller can therefore supply an arbitrary UID that propagates into the subject used by authorization checks, which lack a constraint rejecting caller-chosen UIDs. Trigger: invoking CheckAuthorization/RegisterAuthenticationAgent with a forged subject UID; consequence: the same-UID authorization restriction is bypassed, enabling authentication prompts or information disclosure about other users.

commit_msg:
Fix left shift of a negative value in readSBits.

Check for !number before left-shifting by (number-1).

This commit fixes CVE-2018-5294 (fixes #97).
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  if(num & (1<<(number-1)))'], 'added_lines': ['  if(number && num & (1<<(number-1)))']}
description: In libming 0.4.8, there is an integer signedness error vulnerability (left shift of a negative value) in the readSBits function (util/read.c). Remote attackers can leverage this vulnerability to cause a denial of service via a crafted swf file.

code_evidence: Line 4 left-shifts 1 by (number-1) and masks it against num to test the sign bit; line 5 then left-shifts 1 by number to sign-extend. When number is 0, both shifts use a negative shift count (number-1 = -1) and the sign-extension subtracts 1<<0, producing an incorrect value from the int conversion logic.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs numeric type/bit-width conversion of the read value into a signed integer, and the missing guard causes that conversion to produce unexpected values, matching CWE-681's incorrect conversion between numeric types. A shift-count issue alone would be CWE-682/190; here the defect is in the signed-value conversion.

evidence_lines.code:
if(num & (1<<(number-1)))
return num - (1<<number);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: number is not validated before being used as a shift amount, so a zero (or otherwise invalid) bit width drives left shifts by negative/out-of-range counts. Trigger: a crafted SWF causing readSBits to be called with number=0. Supported consequence: undefined shift behavior yields an unexpected integer result, which can cause denial of service; the patch guards with number &&.

commit_msg:
Add check for DataBuf.size_ in Jp2Image::readMetadata()

When parsing a subBox that is a ColorHeader, a length is extracted
from the input file and fed directly into DataBuf() (which calls
malloc). A crafted input file can provide arbitrarily (up to
max(uint32_t)-8) large values and result in excessive memory
allocation.

This commit adds a check for the new size of DataBuf so that it is not
larger than the remaining size of the file.

This fixes #202 aka CVE-2018-4868

Line 60 then reads data.size_ bytes from the input. No comparison against the remaining file size or any allocation cap occurs before the allocation.

It is not CWE-789 (uncontrolled memory allocation) alone: the missing constraint is the lack of any limit or throttle on the requested allocation.

commit_msg:
Fixed a buffer overrun problem in the QMFB code in the JPC codec
that was caused by a buffer being allocated with a size that was too small
in some cases.
Added a new regression test case.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tint hstartcol;', '\t\thstartcol = (numrows + 1 - parity) >> 1;', '\t\t// ORIGINAL (WRONG): m = (parity) ? hstartcol : (numrows - hstartcol);', '\t\tm = numrows - hstartcol;', '\t\tdstptr = &a[hstartcol * stride];'], 'added_lines': ['\tint hstartrow;', '\t\thstartrow = (numrows + 1 - parity) >> 1;', '\t\t// ORIGINAL (WRONG): m = (parity) ? hstartrow : (numrows - hstartrow);', '\t\tm = numrows - hstartrow;', '\t\tdstptr = &a[hstartrow * stride];']}
description: A heap-buffer overflow vulnerability was found in QMFB code in JPC codec caused by buffer being allocated with too small size. jasper versions before 2.0.0 are affected.

code_evidence: hstartcol is computed as (numrows+1-parity)>>1 and used to offset dstptr into a at line 36; the variable name suggests a column index but it is used as a row offset (hstartrow in the fix).
bufsize is JPC_CEILDIVPOW2(numrows,1) and splitbuf is a fixed QMFB_SPLITBUFSIZE array; when bufsize exceeds it, a heap buffer of bufsize elements is allocated.
The loop writes m elements from buf into a starting at a[hstartcol*stride], so the write range depends on hstartcol and stride rather than on the allocated bufsize.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-119 fits because the function performs writes through dstptr into a at an offset not constrained to the buffer's intended boundary, allowing operations outside the memory buffer. The root cause is an incorrect offset/index computation rather than a simple integer overflow, so the buffer-bounds class applies.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The offset hstartcol is derived from numrows/parity and used to place the highpass samples at a[hstartcol*stride]; with the wrong start position the destination region can extend beyond the intended bounds of a, and the split buffer allocation sizing/writes are not consistently tied to the actual range written. commit_msg:
mqueue: fix a use-after-free in sys_mq_notify()

The retry logic for netlink_attachskb() inside sys_mq_notify()
is nasty and vulnerable:

1) The sock refcnt is already released when retry is needed
2) The fd is controllable by user-space because we already
   release the file refcnt

so we when retry but the fd has been just closed by user-space
during this small window, we end up calling netlink_detachskb()
on the error path which releases the sock again, later when
the user-space closes this socket a use-after-free could be
triggered.

Setting 'sock' to NULL here should be sufficient to fix it.

Reported-by: GeneBlue <geneblue.mail@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Cong Wang <xiyou.wangcong@gmail.com>
Cc: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>
Cc: Manfred Spraul <manfred@colorfullife.com>
Cc: stable@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\tif (ret == 1)'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\tif (ret == 1) {', '\t\t\t\tsock = NULL;', '\t\t\t}']}
description: The mq_notify function in the Linux kernel through 4.11.9 does not set the sock pointer to NULL upon entry into the retry logic. During a user-space close of a Netlink socket, it allows attackers to cause a denial of service (use-after-free) or possibly have unspecified other impact.

code_evidence: netlink_attachskb() returns 1 to request a retry; the code jumps back to retry without clearing sock, so the stale sock pointer survives across the retry.
At the out label, a non-NULL sock causes netlink_detachskb(sock, nc), which releases the socket reference again.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect is a stale pointer to a freed socket that is dereferenced/released again, which is precisely CWE-416 Use After Free; the missing sock = NULL on the retry path is the root cause, distinct from a simple NULL-pointer bug.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: When netlink_attachskb() signals retry, the previously obtained sock reference is already released, but sock is not reset to NULL before goto retry. If user-space closes the netlink fd during the retry window, the error path still calls netlink_detachskb() on the stale sock, releasing it a second time; subsequent use of that socket yields a use-after-free, enabling DoS or other impact.

description: In ZeroMQ before version 4.3.3, there is a denial-of-service vulnerability. Users with TCP transport public endpoints, even with CURVE/ZAP enabled, are impacted. If a raw TCP socket is opened and connected to an endpoint that is fully configured with CURVE/ZAP, legitimate clients will not be able to exchange any message. Handshakes complete successfully, and messages are delivered to the library, but the server application never receives them. This is patched in version 4.3.3.

Here the base engine is constructed in its default (pre-handshake connect) mode.

It is not a memory-safety bug; the flaw is improper lifecycle/resource control, making CWE-400 the fitting class.

Consequence: denial of service (availability loss) for legitimate clients on that endpoint.

description: In ImageMagick 7.0.8-3 Q16, ReadDIBImage and WriteDIBImage in coders/dib.c allow attackers to cause an out of bounds write via a crafted file.

commit_msg:
mm/madvise.c: fix madvise() infinite loop under special circumstances

MADVISE_WILLNEED has always been a noop for DAX (formerly XIP) mappings.
Unfortunately madvise_willneed() doesn't communicate this information
properly to the generic madvise syscall implementation.  The calling
convention is quite subtle there.  madvise_vma() is supposed to either
return an error or update &prev otherwise the main loop will never
advance to the next vma and it will keep looping for ever without a way
to get out of the kernel.

It seems this has been broken since introduction.  Nobody has noticed
because nobody seems to be using MADVISE_WILLNEED on these DAX mappings.

description: In FFmpeg 3.3.3, a DoS in asf_read_marker() due to lack of an EOF (End of File) check might cause huge CPU and memory consumption. When a crafted ASF file, which claims a large "name_len" or "count" field in the header but does not contain sufficient backing data, is provided, the loops over the name and markers would consume huge CPU and memory resources, since there is no EOF check inside these loops.

commit_msg:
Avoid ldbl-96 stack corruption from range reduction of pseudo-zero (bug 25487).

Bug 25487 reports stack corruption in ldbl-96 sinl on a pseudo-zero
argument (an representation where all the significand bits, including
the explicit high bit, are zero, but the exponent is not zero, which
is not a valid representation for the long double type).

Although this is not a valid long double representation, existing
practice in this area (see bug 4586, originally marked invalid but
subsequently fixed) is that we still seek to avoid invalid memory
accesses as a result, in case of programs that treat arbitrary binary
data as long double representations, although the invalid
representations of the ldbl-96 format do not need to be consistently
handled the same as any particular valid representation.

This patch makes the range reduction detect pseudo-zero and unnormal
representations that would otherwise go to __kernel_rem_pio2, and
returns a NaN for them instead of continuing with the range reduction
process.  (Pseudo-zero and unnormal representations whose unbiased
exponent is less than -1 have already been safely returned from the
function before this point without going through the rest of range
reduction.)  Pseudo-zero representations would previously result in
the value passed to __kernel_rem_pio2 being all-zero, which is
definitely unsafe; unnormal representations would previously result in
a value passed whose high bit is zero, which might well be unsafe
since that is not a form of input expected by __kernel_rem_pio2.

Tested for x86_64.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  if ((i0 & 0x80000000) == 0)', '    {', '      /* Pseudo-zero and unnormal representations are not valid', '\t representations of long double.  We need to avoid stack', '\t corruption in __kernel_rem_pio2, which expects input in a', '\t particular normal form, but those representations do not need', '\t to be consistently handled like any particular floating-point', '\t value.  */', '      y[1] = y[0] = __builtin_nanl ("");', '      return 0;', '    }', '']}
description: The GNU C Library (aka glibc or libc6) before 2.32 could overflow an on-stack buffer during range reduction if an input to an 80-bit long double function contains a non-canonical bit pattern, a seen when passing a 0x5d414141414141410000 value to sinl on x86 targets. This is related to sysdeps/ieee754/ldbl-96/e_rem_pio2l.c.

code_evidence: GET_LDOUBLE_WORDS extracts se, i0, i1 from x; j0 is computed from the biased exponent and the sign bit is kept in sx. The only early exits cover j0 < -1 and j0 >= 0x8000, so a non-canonical 80-bit pattern with all significand bits zero but a nonzero in-range exponent passes through.
The mantissa is split directly from i0 and i1 into tx[0..2] and passed to __kernel_rem_pio2 with exp = j0 - 23. No check rejects an all-zero or high-bit-zero significand before this call.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The supported weakness is an out-of-bounds write: a malformed but accepted input reaches a kernel that writes past its stack buffer. This is CWE-787, not merely improper input validation, because the demonstrated consequence is a write beyond the intended buffer bounds.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the range-reduction path accepts pseudo-zero/unnormal ldbl-96 representations and forwards an all-zero or high-bit-zero mantissa to __kernel_rem_pio2, which expects normal-form input. Trigger: calling sinl with a non-canonical bit pattern such as 0x5d414141414141410000. Consequence: __kernel_rem_pio2 overflows an on-stack buffer, corrupting memory.

commit_msg:
Security: update Lua struct package for security.

During an auditing Apple found that the "struct" Lua package
we ship with Redis (http://www.inf.puc-rio.br/~roberto/struct/) contains
a security problem. A bound-checking statement fails because of integer
overflow. The bug exists since we initially integrated this package with
Lua, when scripting was introduced, so every version of Redis with
EVAL/EVALSHA capabilities exposed is affected.

Instead of just fixing the bug, the library was updated to the latest
version shipped by the author.

description: An Integer Overflow issue was discovered in the struct library in the Lua subsystem in Redis before 3.2.12, 4.x before 4.0.10, and 5.x before 5.0 RC2, leading to a failure of bounds checking.

code_evidence: Line 6 derives pos from an attacker-controlled optional integer, and line 12 adds gettoalign() to pos without validating pos before the check; line 13 checks pos+size <= ld, but pos+size can wrap around for large pos, so the comparison passes even though data+pos is far out of bounds.

In the 'c' case, when size==0 the size is taken from a previous numeric result (line 44) and then used in pos+size <= ld (line 46) and lua_pushlstring(data+pos, size) (line 48); a large size can overflow pos+size and bypass the bounds check, leading to an out-of-bounds read.

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: bounds checks use the expression pos+size <= ld, which can overflow or wrap when pos and size are large, so the check is satisfied for invalid offsets. Trigger: a crafted format string and data/position values cause pos+size to exceed SIZE_MAX. Consequence: the subsequent data+pos access and lua_pushlstring read past the input buffer, causing information disclosure or a crash.

commit_msg:
KVM: avoid NULL pointer dereference in kvm_dirty_ring_push

kvm_vcpu_release() will call kvm_dirty_ring_free(), freeing
ring->dirty_gfns and setting it to NULL.  Afterwards, it calls
kvm_arch_vcpu_destroy().

However, if closing the file descriptor races with KVM_RUN in such away
that vcpu->arch.st.preempted == 0, the following call stack leads to a
NULL pointer dereference in kvm_dirty_run_push():

 mark_page_dirty_in_slot+0x192/0x270 arch/x86/kvm/../../../virt/kvm/kvm_main.c:3171
 kvm_steal_time_set_preempted arch/x86/kvm/x86.c:4600 [inline]
 kvm_arch_vcpu_put+0x34e/0x5b0 arch/x86/kvm/x86.c:4618
 vcpu_put+0x1b/0x70 arch/x86/kvm/../../../virt/kvm/kvm_main.c:211
 vmx_free_vcpu+0xcb/0x130 arch/x86/kvm/vmx/vmx.c:6985
 kvm_arch_vcpu_destroy+0x76/0x290 arch/x86/kvm/x86.c:11219
 kvm_vcpu_destroy arch/x86/kvm/../../../virt/kvm/kvm_main.c:441 [inline]

The fix is to release the dirty page ring after kvm_arch_vcpu_destroy
has run.

Reported-by: Qiuhao Li <qiuhao@sysec.org>
Reported-by: Gaoning Pan <pgn@zju.edu.cn>
Reported-by: Yongkang Jia <kangel@zju.edu.cn>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tkvm_arch_vcpu_destroy(vcpu);'], 'added_lines': ['\tkvm_arch_vcpu_destroy(vcpu);']}
description: A NULL pointer dereference issue was found in KVM when releasing a vCPU with dirty ring support enabled. This flaw allows an unprivileged local attacker on the host to issue specific ioctl calls, causing a kernel oops condition that results in a denial of service.

code_evidence: kvm_vcpu_destroy() frees the dirty ring via kvm_dirty_ring_free(&vcpu->dirty_ring) before calling kvm_arch_vcpu_destroy(vcpu). kvm_dirty_ring_free releases ring->dirty_gfns and sets it to NULL, so the subsequent teardown path reaches dirty-ring push code with a NULL ring buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function's ordering exposes a pointer that later code dereferences after it has been freed and set to NULL, matching CWE-476. A use-after-free contrast does not fit because the ring pointer is explicitly nulled, not left dangling.

evidence_lines.code:
kvm_dirty_ring_free(&vcpu->dirty_ring);
kvm_arch_vcpu_destroy(vcpu);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is the teardown ordering: dirty-ring storage is freed and nulled before arch vCPU destruction, which can still record dirty pages (e.g., via kvm_steal_time_set_preempted during vcpu_put). The trigger is concurrent vCPU release with KVM_RUN leaving preempted == 0; the consequence is a NULL dereference and kernel oops, causing host denial of service.

commit_msg: http://www.imagemagick.org/discourse-server/viewtopic.php?f=3&t=26861
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        (void) SeekBlob(image, offset, SEEK_CUR);', ''], 'added_lines': ['        if (SeekBlob(image,offset,SEEK_CUR) < 0)', '          break;']}
description: coders/dds.c in ImageMagick before 6.9.0-4 Beta allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (CPU consumption) via a crafted DDS file.
