commit_msg:
ksmbd: validate length in smb2_write()

The SMB2 Write packet contains data that is to be written
to a file or to a pipe. Depending on the client, there may
be padding between the header and the data field.
Currently, the length is validated only in the case padding
is present.

Since the DataOffset field always points to the beginning
of the data, there is no need to have a special case for
padding. By removing this, the length is validated in both
cases.

Signed-off-by: Marios Makassikis <mmakassikis@freebox.fr>
Acked-by: Namjae Jeon <linkinjeon@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Steve French <stfrench@microsoft.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tif (le16_to_cpu(req->DataOffset) ==', '\t\t    offsetof(struct smb2_write_req, Buffer)) {', '\t\t\tdata_buf = (char *)&req->Buffer[0];', '\t\t} else {', '\t\t\tif ((u64)le16_to_cpu(req->DataOffset) + length >', '\t\t\t    get_rfc1002_len(work->request_buf)) {', '\t\t\t\tpr_err("invalid write data offset %u, smb_len %u\\n",', '\t\t\t\t       le16_to_cpu(req->DataOffset),', '\t\t\t\t       get_rfc1002_len(work->request_buf));', '\t\t\t\terr = -EINVAL;', '\t\t\t\tgoto out;', '\t\t\t}', '', '\t\t\tdata_buf = (char *)(((char *)&req->hdr.ProtocolId) +', '\t\t\t\t\tle16_to_cpu(req->DataOffset));'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif ((u64)le16_to_cpu(req->DataOffset) + length >', '\t\t    get_rfc1002_len(work->request_buf)) {', '\t\t\tpr_err("invalid write data offset %u, smb_len %u\\n",', '\t\t\t       le16_to_cpu(req->DataOffset),', '\t\t\t       get_rfc1002_len(work->request_buf));', '\t\t\terr = -EINVAL;', '\t\t\tgoto out;', '\t\tdata_buf = (char *)(((char *)&req->hdr.ProtocolId) +', '\t\t\t\t    le16_to_cpu(req->DataOffset));']}
description: An issue was discovered in ksmbd in the Linux kernel 5.15 through 5.18 before 5.18.18. fs/ksmbd/smb2pdu.c lacks length validation in the non-padding case in smb2_write.

code_evidence: length is taken from the client-controlled req->Length and only checked against max_write_size, not against the remaining request buffer size.

In the non-RDMA branch, when DataOffset equals offsetof(smb2_write_req, Buffer) the code sets data_buf to &req->Buffer[0] without validating that DataOffset+length stays within get_rfc1002_len(work->request_buf); validation occurs only in the else branch.
ksmbd_vfs_write then consumes length bytes from data_buf, which may extend past the end of the received request buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing length/offset check lets the write path read data past the end of the intended request buffer, matching CWE-125. It is not CWE-787 because the immediate defect is an over-read of the source buffer, not an out-of-bounds write.

evidence_lines.code:
err = ksmbd_vfs_write(work, fp, data_buf, length, &offset,
writethrough, &nbytes);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the padding case (DataOffset == offsetof(Buffer)) skips the bounds check that the else branch performs, so length is not validated against the actual request buffer size. Trigger: a client sends an SMB2 Write with DataOffset at Buffer and a length larger than the data actually present. Consequence: ksmbd_vfs_write reads beyond the request buffer, causing an out-of-bounds read (potential crash or memory disclosure).

commit_msg: fix for #187

description: The AP4_HdlrAtom class in Core/Ap4HdlrAtom.cpp in Bento4 version 1.5.0-617 uses an incorrect character data type, leading to a heap-based buffer over-read and application crash in AP4_BytesToUInt32BE in Core/Ap4Utils.h.

The signed char comparison in line 18 mishandles the boundary/underflow case, and the subsequent pointer arithmetic and handler-name handling operate on an invalid length, leading to an out-of-bounds read and crash as reported.

description: LookupCol.c in X.Org X through X11R7.7 and libX11 before 1.7.1 might allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary code. commit_msg:
run: Prevent TIOCLINUX ioctl, the same as TIOCSTI

The TIOCLINUX ioctl is only available on Linux virtual consoles such as
/dev/tty1. It has several Linux-specific functions, one of which is a
copy/paste operation which can be used for attacks similar to TIOCSTI.

This vulnerability does not affect typical graphical terminal emulators
such as xterm, gnome-terminal and Konsole, and Flatpak is primarily
designed to be run from a Wayland or X11 graphical environment, so this
is relatively unlikely to be a practical problem.

CVE-2023-28100, GHSA-7qpw-3vjv-xrqp

Resolves: https://github.com/flatpak/flatpak/security/advisories/GHSA-7qpw-3vjv-xrqp
Signed-off-by: Simon McVittie <smcv@debian.org>

description: Flatpak is a system for building, distributing, and running sandboxed desktop applications on Linux. Versions prior to 1.10.8, 1.12.8, 1.14.4, and 1.15.4 contain a vulnerability similar to CVE-2017-5226, but using the `TIOCLINUX` ioctl command instead of `TIOCSTI`. If a Flatpak app is run on a Linux virtual console such as `/dev/tty1`, it can copy text from the virtual console and paste it into the command buffer, from which the command might be run after the Flatpak app has exited. Ordinary graphical terminal emulators like xterm, gnome-terminal and Konsole are unaffected. This vulnerability is specific to the Linux virtual consoles `/dev/tty1`, `/dev/tty2` and so on. A patch is available in versions 1.10.8, 1.12.8, 1.14.4, and 1.15.4. As a workaround, don't run Flatpak on a Linux virtual console. Flatpak is primarily designed to be used in a Wayland or X11 graphical environment.

code_evidence: Line 41 adds a seccomp blocklist entry that blocks ioctl only when argument 1 equals TIOCSTI, using a masked-equality comparison.

Lines 119-133 iterate syscall_blocklist and install each rule via seccomp_rule_add, applying SCMP_ACT_ERRNO(EPERM) with the single argument comparator; entries with an arg filter on that argument, others match any argument.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function validates the ioctl request argument against an allow/deny expectation but covers only one value, leaving other dangerous request codes unvalidated; this incomplete input validation matches CWE-20. It is not a generic filtering/encoding issue but a missing constraint on the request value.

evidence_lines.code: {SCMP_SYS (ioctl), EPERM, &SCMP_A1 (SCMP_CMP_MASKED_EQ, 0xFFFFFFFFu, (int) TIOCSTI)},

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The filter constrains only one recognized dangerous ioctl request (TIOCSTI); ioctl's request argument is attacker-controlled and other requests such as TIOCLINUX are not checked, so a sandboxed app on a Linux virtual console can still issue the copy/paste ioctl to inject input into the controlling tty. Root cause is incomplete validation of the ioctl request value; consequence is command injection into the terminal after the app exits.

description: LibTIFF 4.0.7 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (divide-by-zero error and application crash) via a crafted TIFF image, related to libtiff/tif_read.c:351:22.

Line 24 computes stripsperplane as (td_imagelength+rowsperstrip-1)/rowsperstrip, and the sum can overflow uint32; overflowed values combined with rowsperstrip drive the division. Lines 25 and 26 then use stripsperplane as a divisor (strip%stripsperplane and strip/stripsperplane).

commit_msg:
vc2enc_dwt: pad the temporary buffer by the slice size

Since non-Haar wavelets need to look into pixels outside the frame, we
need to pad the buffer. The old factor of two seemed to be a workaround
that fact and only padded to the left and bottom. This correctly pads
by the slice size and as such reduces memory usage and potential
exploits.
Reported by Liu Bingchang.

Ideally, there should be no temporary buffer but the encoder is designed
to deinterleave the coefficients into the classical wavelet structure
with the lower frequency values in the top left corner.

Signed-off-by: Rostislav Pehlivanov <atomnuker@gmail.com>
(cherry picked from commit 3228ac730c11eca49d5680d5550128e397061c85)

description: The VC-2 Video Compression encoder in FFmpeg 3.0 and 3.4 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read) because of incorrect buffer padding for non-Haar wavelets, related to libavcodec/vc2enc.c and libavcodec/vc2enc_dwt.c.

commit_msg:
smart_pkt: verify packet length exceeds PKT_LEN_SIZE

Each packet line in the Git protocol is prefixed by a four-byte
length of how much data will follow, which we parse in
`git_pkt_parse_line`. The transmitted length can either be equal
to zero in case of a flush packet or has to be at least of length
four, as it also includes the encoded length itself. Not
checking this may result in a buffer overflow as we directly pass
the length to functions which accept a `size_t` length as
parameter.

Fix the issue by verifying that non-flush packets have at least a
length of `PKT_LEN_SIZE`.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\t/*', '\t * The length has to be exactly 0 in case of a flush', '\t * packet or greater than PKT_LEN_SIZE, as the decoded', '\t * length includes its own encoded length of four bytes.', '\t */', '\tif (len != 0 && len < PKT_LEN_SIZE)', '\t\treturn GIT_ERROR;']}
description: Buffer overflow in the git_pkt_parse_line function in transports/smart_pkt.c in the Git Smart Protocol support in libgit2 before 0.24.6 and 0.25.x before 0.25.1 allows remote attackers to have unspecified impact via a crafted non-flush packet.

code_evidence: parse_len(line) decodes a four-byte length into int32_t len; the only bound check at [17,18] rejects a short buffer but does not reject a small nonzero len such as 1-3.

After line += PKT_LEN_SIZE, len is decremented at [29]; for len < 4 this underflows and the resulting negative len is passed to data_pkt, sideband_*_pkt, ack_pkt, err_pkt, comment_pkt, ok_pkt, ng_pkt, unpack_pkt or ref_pkt, which take size_t lengths, so the negative value converts to a huge size_t. *out = line + len at [52] also advances by a negative offset.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-119 fits because the missing length validation lets the code compute an out-of-bounds length and operate on memory beyond the intended buffer. The concrete underflow is an integer issue, but the supported consequence is an out-of-bounds memory operation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: git_pkt_parse_line accepts a nonzero packet length below PKT_LEN_SIZE. Trigger: a crafted non-flush packet whose encoded length is 1-3. Consequence: len -= PKT_LEN_SIZE underflows to a negative int32_t, which is passed as a size_t length to the packet constructors, enabling out-of-bounds reads/writes and a buffer overflow.

commit_msg:
Input: sunkbd - avoid use-after-free in teardown paths

We need to make sure we cancel the reinit work before we tear down the
driver structures.

Reported-by: Bodong Zhao <nopitydays@gmail.com>
Tested-by: Bodong Zhao <nopitydays@gmail.com>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Dmitry Torokhov <dmitry.torokhov@gmail.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\twait_event_interruptible_timeout(sunkbd->wait, sunkbd->reset >= 0, HZ);', '\tserio_write(sunkbd->serio, SUNKBD_CMD_SETLED);', '\tserio_write(sunkbd->serio,', '\t\t(!!test_bit(LED_CAPSL,   sunkbd->dev->led) << 3) |', '\t\t(!!test_bit(LED_SCROLLL, sunkbd->dev->led) << 2) |', '\t\t(!!test_bit(LED_COMPOSE, sunkbd->dev->led) << 1) |', '\t\t !!test_bit(LED_NUML,    sunkbd->dev->led));', '\tserio_write(sunkbd->serio,', '\t\tSUNKBD_CMD_NOCLICK - !!test_bit(SND_CLICK, sunkbd->dev->snd));', '\tserio_write(sunkbd->serio,', '\t\tSUNKBD_CMD_BELLOFF - !!test_bit(SND_BELL, sunkbd->dev->snd));'], 'added_lines': ['\t/*', '\t * It is OK that we check sunkbd->enabled without pausing serio,', '\t * as we only want to catch true->false transition that will', '\t * happen once and we will be woken up for it.', '\t */', '\twait_event_interruptible_timeout(sunkbd->wait,', '\t\t\t\t\t sunkbd->reset >= 0 || !sunkbd->enabled,', '\t\t\t\t\t HZ);', '\tif (sunkbd->reset >= 0 && sunkbd->enabled)', '\t\tsunkbd_set_leds_beeps(sunkbd);']}
description: A vulnerability was found in the Linux Kernel where the function sunkbd_reinit having been scheduled by sunkbd_interrupt before sunkbd being freed. Though the dangling pointer is set to NULL in sunkbd_disconnect, there is still an alias in sunkbd_reinit causing Use After Free.

code_evidence: Derives sunkbd via container_of from the work item and waits only for sunkbd->reset, with no check that the device is still enabled or being torn down.
Unconditionally dereferences sunkbd->serio and sunkbd->dev->led to issue SETLED and LED state writes.
Reads sunkbd->dev->snd for NOCLICK; note the commented line is not part of the actual code.
Reads sunkbd->dev->snd for BELLOFF, all without any liveness guard on the sunkbd object.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the reinit work references sunkbd and its serio/dev members after the object may have been freed during teardown. The added enabled check and cancellation are the fix; this is not merely a race on a live object but access to freed memory.

evidence_lines.code:
struct sunkbd *sunkbd = container_of(work, struct sunkbd, tq);
wait_event_interruptible_timeout(sunkbd->wait, sunkbd->reset >= 0, HZ);

serio_write(sunkbd->serio,
SUNKBD_CMD_NOCLICK - !!test_bit(SND_CLICK, sunkbd->dev->snd));

serio_write(sunkbd->serio,
SUNKBD_CMD_BELLOFF - !!test_bit(SND_BELL, sunkbd->dev->snd));

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: sunkbd_reinit runs as a scheduled work item. If teardown frees sunkbd while this work is still queued, the function's wait condition does not observe shutdown, and it proceeds to dereference sunkbd->serio and sunkbd->dev, accessing freed memory. Root cause is the missing cancellation/synchronization plus the absent enabled check; the supported consequence is use-after-free read/write on freed driver structures.

commit_msg:
dm: virtio: check for paddr_guest2host return value

paddr_guest2host can return NULL, but code paths in virtio
are not checking the return value.
_vq_record() initializes iov_base pointer using paddr_guest2host()
but there is nothing in the flow that checks for NULL.
Chane _vq_record to return -1 in case the address translation
has failed.

Tracked-On: #5452
Signed-off-by: Tomas Winkler <tomas.winkler@intel.com>
Acked-by: Wang, Yu1 <yu1.wang@intel.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['static inline void', '\t\treturn;', '\tiov[i].iov_base = paddr_guest2host(ctx, vd->addr, vd->len);'], 'added_lines': ['static inline int', '\tvoid *host_addr;', '', '\t\treturn -1;', '\thost_addr = paddr_guest2host(ctx, vd->addr, vd->len);', '\tif (!host_addr)', '\t\treturn -1;', '\tiov[i].iov_base = host_addr;', '\treturn 0;']}
description: ACRN through 2.2 has a devicemodel/hw/pci/virtio/virtio.c NULL Pointer Dereference.

code_evidence: Line 6 assigns the result of paddr_guest2host(ctx, vd->addr, vd->len) directly to iov[i].iov_base without any NULL check; the function returns void and cannot signal failure.
Line 7 then stores vd->len into iov[i].iov_len and the caller proceeds to use the iovec, so a NULL iov_base from a failed address translation is carried forward as if valid.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked NULL return is stored as a pointer that later code expects to be valid, matching CWE-476's NULL pointer dereference. The fix's added 'if (!host_addr) return -1;' confirms the missing constraint; this is not merely an out-of-bounds index issue (the i >= n_iov check is separate).

evidence_lines.code: iov[i].iov_base = paddr_guest2host(ctx, vd->addr, vd->len);
iov[i].iov_len = vd->len;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the return value of paddr_guest2host, which can be NULL when guest-to-host translation fails, is stored unchecked into iov[i].iov_base. Trigger: a guest supplies a vring descriptor whose address cannot be translated. Consequence: downstream virtio I/O paths use the NULL iov_base, causing a crash/DoS (and potentially memory access issues).

commit_msg:
Fix invalid assertion CESU8-UTF8 buffer copy

The UTF8 buffer size can be smaller then the CESU8 string's size so the UTF8 output is may truncated. Therefore we cannot ensure that the CESU8 buffer is read until the end.
This patch fixes #4920.

description: There is an Assertion 'cesu8_cursor_p == cesu8_end_p' failed at /jerry-core/lit/lit-strings.c in JerryScript 3.0.0.

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the buffer-capacity check breaks out of the conversion loop without consuming all CESU-8 input, yet the postcondition asserts full consumption. commit_msg:
The dvb-core tries to sync the releases of opened files at
dvb_dmxdev_release() with two refcounts: dvbdev->users and
dvr_dvbdev->users.  A problem is present in those two syncs: when yet
another dvb_demux_open() is called during those sync waits,
dvb_demux_open() continues to process even if the device is being
closed.  This includes the increment of the former refcount, resulting
in the leftover refcount after the sync of the latter refcount at
dvb_dmxdev_release().  It ends up with use-after-free, since the
function believes that all usages were gone and releases the
resources.

This patch addresses the problem by adding the check of dmxdev->exit
flag at dvb_demux_open(), just like dvb_dvr_open() already does.  With
the exit flag check, the second call of dvb_demux_open() fails, hence
the further corruption can be avoided.

Also for avoiding the races of the dmxdev->exit flag reference, this
patch serializes the dmxdev->exit set up and the sync waits with the
dmxdev->mutex lock at dvb_dmxdev_release().  Without the mutex lock,
dvb_demux_open() (or dvb_dvr_open()) may run concurrently with
dvb_dmxdev_release(), which allows to skip the exit flag check and
continue the open process that is being closed.

CVE-2022-41218 is assigned to those bugs above.

Reported-by: Hyunwoo Kim <imv4bel@gmail.com>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/20220908132754.30532-1-tiwai@suse.de
Signed-off-by: Takashi Iwai <tiwai@suse.de>
Signed-off-by: Hans Verkuil <hverkuil-cisco@xs4all.nl>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tmutex_lock(&dmxdev->mutex);', '\tmutex_unlock(&dmxdev->mutex);', '']}
description: In drivers/media/dvb-core/dmxdev.c in the Linux kernel through 5.19.10, there is a use-after-free caused by refcount races, affecting dvb_demux_open and dvb_dmxdev_release.

code_evidence: dvb_dmxdev_release() sets dmxdev->exit and then waits for the dvbdev and dvr_dvbdev refcounts to drop to 1 before proceeding.
After the waits, it unregisters both devices, frees dmxdev->filter and closes the demux, tearing down resources.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The refcount race allows resources to be released while a concurrent open still uses them, which is the CWE-416 use-after-free pattern; the missing mutex serialization is the root cause, and the resulting stale reference is the consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The exit flag is set without holding dmxdev->mutex, and the waits are also unsynchronized, so a concurrent dvb_demux_open() can pass the exit-flag check and increment dvbdev->users after the wait condition is satisfied. The release then unregisters and frees the device resources while the racing open still holds a reference, yielding a use-after-free.

commit_msg:
Fix xsltNumberFormatGetMultipleLevel

Namespace nodes are actually an xmlNs, not an xmlNode. They must be
special-cased in xsltNumberFormatGetMultipleLevel to avoid an
out-of-bounds heap access.

Move the test whether a node matches the "count" pattern to a separate
function to make the code more readable. As a side effect, we also
compare expanded names when walking up the ancestor axis, fixing an
insignificant bug.

The count-match test dereferences ancestor->type, ancestor->name and calls xsltTestCompMatchList on ancestor without distinguishing namespace nodes.

commit_msg:
x86: limit linear page table use to a single level

That's the only way that they're meant to be used. Without such a
restriction arbitrarily long chains of same-level page tables can be
built, tearing down of which may then cause arbitrarily deep recursion,
causing a stack overflow. To facilitate this restriction, a counter is
being introduced to track both the number of same-level entries in a
page table as well as the number of uses of a page table in another
same-level one (counting into positive and negative direction
respectively, utilizing the fact that both counts can't be non-zero at
the same time).

Note that the added accounting introduces a restriction on the number
of times a page can be used in other same-level page tables - more than
32k of such uses are no longer possible.

Note also that some put_page_and_type[_preemptible]() calls are
replaced with open-coded equivalents.  This seemed preferrable to
adding "parent_table" to the matrix of functions.

Note further that cross-domain same-level page table references are no
longer permitted (they probably never should have been).

This is XSA-240.

Reported-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Signed-off-by: George Dunlap <george.dunlap@citrix.com>

commit_msg:
ASAN SFTP Fixes
When decoding SFTP messages, fix the size checks so they don't wrap. (ZD12766)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if (rSz > WOLFSSH_MAX_FILENAME || (int)(rSz + UINT32_SZ) > maxSz) {'], 'added_lines': ['    if (rSz >= WOLFSSH_MAX_FILENAME || (int)(rSz + UINT32_SZ) > maxSz) {']}
description: WolfSSH v1.4.7 was discovered to contain an integer overflow via the function wolfSSH_SFTP_RecvRMDIR.

code_evidence: Line 17-19 only ensures maxSz is at least UINT32_SZ before reading the length field.

Line 20 reads attacker-controlled rSz from the request; line 21 checks (int)(rSz + UINT32_SZ) > maxSz. Because rSz is a word32, rSz + UINT32_SZ can wrap before the cast, so the size check can be bypassed. Line 25 then copies rSz bytes into the fixed r[WOLFSSH_MAX_FILENAME] buffer, and line 26 writes r[rSz] = '\0'.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The root cause is an integer wraparound in the size calculation (rSz + UINT32_SZ) that defeats the bounds check before a copy, matching CWE-190. The buffer overflow is the consequence, not the primary weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The length rSz is read from the message and used in an addition that wraps when rSz is near UINT32_MAX; the comparison against maxSz is then evaluated on the wrapped result. A crafted request can pass the check, causing WMEMCPY to copy an oversized amount into the fixed-size stack buffer and the terminator write to overflow it, leading to memory corruption or crash.

commit_msg:
Fix out of bound access in DequantizeOp by adding check for axis < input dimension

PiperOrigin-RevId: 411214268
Change-Id: I3249d2a69ddc82f182c589a3a5bbfb71543f4b29
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '    OP_REQUIRES(', '        ctx, axis_ < input.dims(),', '        errors::InvalidArgument("Axis must be less than input dimension(",', '                                input.dims(), "), got ", axis_));']}
description: Tensorflow is an Open Source Machine Learning Framework. The implementation of `Dequantize` does not fully validate the value of `axis` and can result in heap OOB accesses. The `axis` argument can be `-1` (the default value for the optional argument) or any other positive value at most the number of dimensions of the input. Unfortunately, the upper bound is not checked and this results in reading past the end of the array containing the dimensions of the input tensor. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.8.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.7.1, TensorFlow 2.6.3, and TensorFlow 2.5.3, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: The function derives num_slices from input.dim_size(axis_) whenever axis_ > -1, with no check that axis_ is a valid dimension index; dim_size performs an unchecked index into the tensor's dimension array, so an axis_ >= input.dims() reads past the end of that array.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This is a read past the end of the buffer holding the tensor's dimensions, matching CWE-125 (out-of-bounds read). It is not a write (CWE-787) because only the dimension array is read; the missing upper-bound check is the cause, not the weakness class itself.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the attacker-controlled axis_ is used to index input dimensions without validating axis_ < input.dims(). Trigger: a Dequantize op with axis_ greater than or equal to the input rank. Consequence: an out-of-bounds read of the dimension array (heap OOB), yielding an incorrect slice count and possibly a crash or memory disclosure.

commit_msg:
The expired catchall element is not deactivated and removed from GC sync
path. This path holds mutex so just call nft_setelem_data_deactivate()
and nft_setelem_catchall_remove() before queueing the GC work.

Fixes: 4a9e12ea7e70 ("netfilter: nft_set_pipapo: call nft_trans_gc_queue_sync() in catchall GC")
Reported-by: lonial con <kongln9170@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tstruct nft_set_elem_catchall *catchall;', '\tlist_for_each_entry_rcu(catchall, &set->catchall_list, list) {', '\t\tnft_trans_gc_elem_add(gc, catchall->elem);'], 'added_lines': ['\tstruct nft_set_elem_catchall *catchall, *next;', '\tstruct nft_elem_priv *elem_priv;', '\tlist_for_each_entry_safe(catchall, next, &set->catchall_list, list) {', '\t\telem_priv = catchall->elem;', '\t\tif (sync) {', '\t\t\tnft_setelem_data_deactivate(gc->net, gc->set, elem_priv);', '\t\t\tnft_setelem_catchall_destroy(catchall);', '\t\t}', '', '\t\tnft_trans_gc_elem_add(gc, elem_priv);']}
description:
A use-after-free vulnerability in the Linux kernel's netfilter: nf_tables component can be exploited to achieve local privilege escalation.

The function nft_trans_gc_catchall did not remove the catchall set element from the catchall_list when the argument sync is true, making it possible to free a catchall set element many times.

We recommend upgrading past commit 93995bf4af2c5a99e2a87f0cd5ce547d31eb7630.

code_evidence: The loop iterates the catchall list with the RCU iterator and, for an expired element in sync mode, queues GC work via nft_trans_gc_queue_sync() and adds catchall->elem to the transaction at line 22. In the pre-fix function the element is neither removed from catchall_list nor deactivated before being queued, so the same catchall entry remains reachable and can be queued/freed again on a later GC pass.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the stale catchall_list linkage allows an already-queued element to be freed and subsequently referenced again, which is reuse of freed memory. This is not merely a double-free pattern alone: the retained list reference is what enables later use of the freed element.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the sync GC path queues the expired catchall element for freeing without unlinking it from set->catchall_list or deactivating its data. Trigger: repeated GC traversal (sync=true) revisits the still-linked catchall entry and adds the same element again, so the element is freed multiple times and later accesses use freed memory. Supported consequence: memory corruption/use-after-free, potentially local privilege escalation.

commit_msg:
Force value conversion in case of TypedArray filter method

During the execution of the TypedArray filter method it is possible
to have a different sized output TypedArray than the input one.
When copying the data to the output array the values must be
correctly converted to the output TypedArray's value range.

description: A buffer overflow in ecma_builtin_typedarray_prototype_filter() in JerryScript version fe3a5c0 allows an attacker to construct a fake object or a fake arraybuffer with unlimited size.

code_evidence: A local scratch buffer is allocated with size info_p->length * info_p->element_size, sized to the input typed array.

For each element the callback returns true, memcpy copies info_p->element_size bytes into pass_value_p and advances it; the number of copies equals the number of passing elements, bounded only by the input length.
pass_num is derived from the advanced pointer and used to create the output typed array via species_create, whose element type/size may differ from the input.
memcpy then copies (pass_value_p - pass_value_list_p) bytes into ecma_typedarray_get_buffer(obj_p) without checking that this byte count fits the output buffer's size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The vulnerable operation is a buffer copy (memcpy at lines 52–54) into an output buffer whose size is never compared against the copied size, matching CWE-120's classic buffer copy without input-size checking. It is not merely an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125); the write past the destination buffer is the defect.

lit_utf8_byte_t *pass_value_p = pass_value_list_p;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the filter copies the input-sized byte span into the species-created output buffer without verifying the output buffer's byte capacity. Trigger: a subclass overrides Symbol.species so the output typed array has a smaller element size (or size) than the input, while the callback returns true for many elements. Consequence: memcpy writes past the end of the output arraybuffer, corrupting memory, enabling fake object/arraybuffer construction or a crash.

commit_msg:
UDP IPv6 packets auto flowlabels are using a 32bit secret
(static u32 hashrnd in net/core/flow_dissector.c) and
apply jhash() over fields known by the receivers.

Attackers can easily infer the 32bit secret and use this information
to identify a device and/or user, since this 32bit secret is only
set at boot time.

Really, using jhash() to generate cookies sent on the wire
is a serious security concern.

Trying to change the rol32(hash, 16) in ip6_make_flowlabel() would be
a dead end. Trying to periodically change the secret (like in sch_sfq.c)
could change paths taken in the network for long lived flows.

Let's switch to siphash, as we did in commit df453700e8d8
("inet: switch IP ID generator to siphash")

Using a cryptographically strong pseudo random function will solve this
privacy issue and more generally remove other weak points in the stack.

Packet schedulers using skb_get_hash_perturb() benefit from this change.

Fixes: b56774163f99 ("ipv6: Enable auto flow labels by default")
Fixes: 42240901f7c4 ("ipv6: Implement different admin modes for automatic flow labels")
Fixes: 67800f9b1f4e ("ipv6: Call skb_get_hash_flowi6 to get skb->hash in ip6_make_flowlabel")
Fixes: cb1ce2ef387b ("ipv6: Implement automatic flow label generation on transmit")
Signed-off-by: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Reported-by: Jonathan Berger <jonathann1@walla.com>
Reported-by: Amit Klein <aksecurity@gmail.com>
Reported-by: Benny Pinkas <benny@pinkas.net>
Cc: Tom Herbert <tom@herbertland.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tq->perturbation = prandom_u32();'], 'added_lines': ['\tget_random_bytes(&q->perturbation, sizeof(q->perturbation));']}
description: The flow_dissector feature in the Linux kernel 4.3 through 5.x before 5.3.10 has a device tracking vulnerability, aka CID-55667441c84f. This occurs because the auto flowlabel of a UDP IPv6 packet relies on a 32-bit hashrnd value as a secret, and because jhash (instead of siphash) is used. The hashrnd value remains the same starting from boot time, and can be inferred by an attacker. This affects net/core/flow_dissector.c and related code.

code_evidence: Line 8 initializes q->perturbation with prandom_u32(), a non-cryptographic PRNG output. This value seeds the HHF qdisc's hash perturbation, which is used to derive flow hashes observable on the wire.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-330 fits because a security-relevant secret (hash perturbation) is produced from insufficiently random values. This is distinct from weak hashing alone; the flaw is the predictable randomness source seeding the perturbation.

evidence_lines.code: q->perturbation = prandom_u32();

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the perturbation secret is generated with prandom_u32() rather than a cryptographically strong RNG, making the 32-bit value predictable/inferable. Trigger: an attacker observes flow hashes influenced by this perturbation. Consequence: device/user tracking via stable, guessable hashes; the patch replaces it with get_random_bytes().

commit_msg:
Prevent small subgroup attacks on DH/DHE

Historically OpenSSL only ever generated DH parameters based on "safe"
primes. More recently (in version 1.0.2) support was provided for
generating X9.42 style parameter files such as those required for RFC
5114 support. The primes used in such files may not be "safe". Where an
application is using DH configured with parameters based on primes that
are not "safe" then an attacker could use this fact to find a peer's
private DH exponent. This attack requires that the attacker complete
multiple handshakes in which the peer uses the same DH exponent.

A simple mitigation is to ensure that y^q (mod p) == 1

CVE-2016-0701 (fix part 1 of 2)

Issue reported by Antonio Sanso.

Reviewed-by: Viktor Dukhovni <viktor@openssl.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    BIGNUM *q = NULL;', '    q = BN_new();', '    if (q == NULL)', '    BN_set_word(q, 1);', '    if (BN_cmp(pub_key, q) <= 0)', '    BN_copy(q, dh->p);', '    BN_sub_word(q, 1);', '    if (BN_cmp(pub_key, q) >= 0)', '    if (q != NULL)', '        BN_free(q);'], 'added_lines': ['    BIGNUM *tmp = NULL;', '    BN_CTX *ctx = NULL;', '    ctx = BN_CTX_new();', '    if (ctx == NULL)', '    BN_CTX_start(ctx);', '    tmp = BN_CTX_get(ctx);', '    if (tmp == NULL)', '        goto err;', '    BN_set_word(tmp, 1);', '    if (BN_cmp(pub_key, tmp) <= 0)', '    BN_copy(tmp, dh->p);', '    BN_sub_word(tmp, 1);', '    if (BN_cmp(pub_key, tmp) >= 0)', '', '    if (dh->q != NULL) {', '        /* Check pub_key^q == 1 mod p */', '        if (!BN_mod_exp(tmp, pub_key, dh->q, dh->p, ctx))', '            goto err;', '        if (!BN_is_one(tmp))', '            *ret |= DH_CHECK_PUBKEY_INVALID;', '    }', '    if (ctx != NULL) {', '        BN_CTX_end(ctx);', '        BN_CTX_free(ctx);', '    }']}
description: The DH_check_pub_key function in crypto/dh/dh_check.c in OpenSSL 1.0.2 before 1.0.2f does not ensure that prime numbers are appropriate for Diffie-Hellman (DH) key exchange, which makes it easier for remote attackers to discover a private DH exponent by making multiple handshakes with a peer that chose an inappropriate number, as demonstrated by a number in an X9.42 file.

code_evidence: The function only validates pub_key against the bounds 1 < pub_key < p-1 by comparing it to 1 and p-1.
It never verifies that pub_key lies in the correct subgroup, i.e., no check that pub_key^q mod p == 1, so an attacker-supplied value from a small subgroup is accepted.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing subgroup constraint causes leakage of the secret private exponent to a remote actor, which is exposure of sensitive information (CWE-200). The weakness is the absent validation allowing secret-dependent state to be inferred, not a generic confidentiality impact of another flaw.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the peer public value is only range-checked, not validated against the DH subgroup order q. Trigger: an attacker repeatedly sends crafted small-subgroup public values during handshakes using the same private exponent. Consequence: information about the peer's private DH exponent leaks across handshakes, enabling its recovery.

commit_msg:
x86/spec-ctrl: Mitigate Gather Data Sampling

This is part of XSA-435 / CVE-2022-40982

Signed-off-by: Andrew Cooper <andrew.cooper3@citrix.com>
Reviewed-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    gds_calculations();', '']}
description: Information exposure through microarchitectural state after transient execution in certain vector execution units for some Intel(R) Processors may allow an authenticated user to potentially enable information disclosure via local access.

code_evidence: The function performs microarchitectural mitigation setup. Line 116 calls srso_calculations(), line 141 calls mds_calculations(), and lines 173-175 configure MCU_OPT_CTRL_RNGDS_MITG_DIS based on opt_srb_lock. The patch inserts gds_calculations() at the position shown in diff_func, after the srb-lock MCU control block and before print_details(thunk) at line 176. This call is the mitigation decision for Gather Data Sampling.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-203 fits because the weakness is an observable discrepancy: differing microarchitectural behavior across transient execution states enables an unauthorized local actor to infer data. The function's role is to enable the mitigation that removes this observable difference; the missing call is the defect being fixed.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: without the gds_calculations() invocation, the boot-time mitigation selection for Gather Data Sampling is absent, so the hypervisor may leave vector execution units in a state where transient execution leaks microarchitectural data. Trigger: local authenticated execution of vector instructions on affected Intel processors. Supported consequence: information disclosure through observable microarchitectural state differences.

commit_msg:
tty: n_gsm: fix the UAF caused by race condition in gsm_cleanup_mux

In commit 9b9c8195f3f0 ("tty: n_gsm: fix UAF in gsm_cleanup_mux"), the UAF
problem is not completely fixed. There is a race condition in
gsm_cleanup_mux(), which caused this UAF.

The UAF problem is triggered by the following race:
task[5046]                     task[5054]
-----------------------        -----------------------
gsm_cleanup_mux();
dlci = gsm->dlci[0];
mutex_lock(&gsm->mutex);
                               gsm_cleanup_mux();
			       dlci = gsm->dlci[0]; //Didn't take the lock
gsm_dlci_release(gsm->dlci[i]);
gsm->dlci[i] = NULL;
mutex_unlock(&gsm->mutex);
                               mutex_lock(&gsm->mutex);
			       dlci->dead = true; //UAF

Fix it by assigning values after mutex_lock().

Link: https://syzkaller.appspot.com/text?tag=CrashReport&x=176188b5a80000
Cc: stable <stable@kernel.org>
Fixes: 9b9c8195f3f0 ("tty: n_gsm: fix UAF in gsm_cleanup_mux")
Fixes: aa371e96f05d ("tty: n_gsm: fix restart handling via CLD command")
Signed-off-by: Yi Yang <yiyang13@huawei.com>
Co-developed-by: Qiumiao Zhang <zhangqiumiao1@huawei.com>
Signed-off-by: Qiumiao Zhang <zhangqiumiao1@huawei.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20230811031121.153237-1-yiyang13@huawei.com
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tstruct gsm_dlci *dlci = gsm->dlci[0];'], 'added_lines': ['\tstruct gsm_dlci *dlci;', '\tdlci = gsm->dlci[0];']}
description: A race condition was found in the GSM 0710 tty multiplexor in the Linux kernel. This issue occurs when two threads execute the GSMIOC_SETCONF ioctl on the same tty file descriptor with the gsm line discipline enabled, and can lead to a use-after-free problem on a struct gsm_dlci while restarting the gsm mux. This could allow a local unprivileged user to escalate their privileges on the system.

code_evidence: Line 4 reads the shared pointer gsm->dlci[0] into dlci before mutex_lock on line 7, so the dereference at line 13 (dlci->dead = true) and the check at line 9 operate on a pointer captured outside the critical section. Lines 25-26 release and NULL gsm->dlci[i] under the mutex, so a concurrent gsm_cleanup_mux can free the object that the first caller still holds in dlci; the later dlci->dead write then touches freed memory. The patch moves the assignment after mutex_lock so the pointer is acquired under the lock.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-362 fits because a shared resource (gsm->dlci[0]) is accessed without proper exclusive synchronization, creating a timing window where an interfering concurrent sequence frees it. This is a race condition; the UAF is the downstream consequence, not the root weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the shared pointer gsm->dlci[0] is read before acquiring gsm->mutex, so the pointer is not synchronized with the release path (lines 25-26). Trigger: two concurrent cleanup/restart sequences, one releasing and NULLing the DLCI while the other holds the stale pointer. Consequence: use-after-free when dlci->dead is written, enabling crash or privilege escalation.

commit_msg:
Jan Kara's analysis of the syzbot report (edited):

  The reproducer opens a directory on FUSE filesystem, it then attaches
  dnotify mark to the open directory.  After that a fuse_do_getattr() call
  finds that attributes returned by the server are inconsistent, and calls
  make_bad_inode() which, among other things does:

          inode->i_mode = S_IFREG;

  This then confuses dnotify which doesn't tear down its structures
  properly and eventually crashes.

Avoid calling make_bad_inode() on a live inode: switch to a private flag on
the fuse inode.  Also add the test to ops which the bad_inode_ops would
have caught.

This bug goes back to the initial merge of fuse in 2.6.14...

commit_msg:
Prevent double free by crafted fences.

If client sent fence with some data, followed by fence with no data (length 0), the original fence data were freed, but the pointer kept pointing at them. Sending one more fence would attempt to free them again.

commit_msg:
commit: always initialize commit message

When parsing a commit, we will treat all bytes left after parsing
the headers as the commit message. When no bytes are left, we
leave the commit's message uninitialized. While uncommon to have
a commit without message, this is the right behavior as Git
unfortunately allows for empty commit messages.

Given that this scenario is so uncommon, most programs acting on
the commit message will never check if the message is actually
set, which may lead to errors. To work around the error and not
lay the burden of checking for empty commit messages to the
developer, initialize the commit message with an empty string
when no commit message is given.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (buffer <= buffer_end) {', '\t\tGITERR_CHECK_ALLOC(commit->raw_message);', '\t}'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (buffer <= buffer_end)', '\telse', '\t\tcommit->raw_message = git__strdup("");', '\tGITERR_CHECK_ALLOC(commit->raw_message);']}
description: The git_commit_message function in oid.c in libgit2 before 0.24.3 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read) via a cat-file command with a crafted object file.

code_evidence: The pre-fix guard only assigns commit->raw_message inside `if (buffer <= buffer_end)`; when no bytes remain after the header, the field stays uninitialized/NULL. The allocation check is also inside that branch, so the empty-message path returns 0 without setting a valid message.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect is a pointer expected to be valid but left NULL and later dereferenced, matching CWE-476. It is not merely an unchecked return value; the missing initialization directly produces the NULL dereference.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the empty commit-message path skips assignment, leaving commit->raw_message NULL. Trigger: parsing a crafted commit object with no message bytes. Consequence: callers such as git_commit_message dereference the NULL pointer, causing an out-of-bounds read/crash (DoS).

channel) and 16 bits (5 bits per color channel and 1 bit for alpha), and

Maybe there exist more variants, but if they do exist, we simply don't

description: In GIMP 2.8.22, there is a heap-based buffer over-read in ReadImage in plug-ins/common/file-tga.c (related to bgr2rgb.part.1) via an unexpected bits-per-pixel value for an RGBA image.

code_evidence: header[16] supplies info.bpp and header[17] supplies info.alphaBits directly from the file; info.bytes is derived as (bpp+7)/8.
The TGA_TYPE_COLOR case validates only bpp against {15,16,24,32} but does not constrain alphaBits, so combinations such as 32 bpp with an unexpected alpha value pass validation.
ReadImage is then called with the unvalidated info, and downstream decoding (bgr2rgb) reads per-pixel data assuming the validated layout.

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The root cause is that the color-image validation checks bits-per-pixel but ignores the alpha-bit field, so a crafted TGA can declare an RGBA layout whose actual pixel size differs from what the decoder expects. When ReadImage processes such input, its pixel-conversion loop reads beyond the allocated/read pixel buffer, causing a heap-based out-of-bounds read.

commit_msg:
pk7_doit.c: Check return of BIO_set_md() calls

These calls invoke EVP_DigestInit() which can fail for digests
with implicit fetches. Subsequent EVP_DigestUpdate() from BIO_write()
or EVP_DigestFinal() from BIO_read() will segfault on NULL
dereference. This can be triggered by an attacker providing
PKCS7 data digested with MD4 for example if the legacy provider
is not loaded.

If BIO_set_md() fails the md BIO cannot be used.

CVE-2023-0401

Reviewed-by: Paul Dale <pauli@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Dmitry Belyavskiy <beldmit@gmail.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            BIO_set_md(btmp, md);'], 'added_lines': ['            if (BIO_set_md(btmp, md) <= 0) {', '                EVP_MD_free(evp_md);', '                ERR_raise(ERR_LIB_PKCS7, ERR_R_BIO_LIB);', '                goto err;', '            }']}
description:
A NULL pointer can be dereferenced when signatures are being
verified on PKCS7 signed or signedAndEnveloped data. In case the hash
algorithm used for the signature is known to the OpenSSL library but
the implementation of the hash algorithm is not available the digest
initialization will fail. There is a missing check for the return
value from the initialization function which later leads to invalid
usage of the digest API most likely leading to a crash.

The unavailability of an algorithm can be caused by using FIPS
enabled configuration of providers or more commonly by not loading
the legacy provider.

PKCS7 data is processed by the SMIME library calls and also by the
time stamp (TS) library calls. The TLS implementation in OpenSSL does
not call these functions however third party applications would be
affected if they call these functions to verify signatures on untrusted
data.

code_evidence: BIO_set_md(btmp, md) is called at line 109 without checking its return value; its result is ignored and execution continues to EVP_MD_free and BIO_push. BIO_set_md invokes EVP_DigestInit, which fails when the digest (e.g., MD4) is known but its implementation is unavailable (legacy provider not loaded). The md BIO then has a NULL digest context, and later BIO_write/BIO_read on the chain dereferences it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked call leads to a NULL pointer being dereferenced during digest processing, matching CWE-476 (NULL Pointer Dereference). It is not merely a missing-error-handling style issue; the concrete effect is a NULL dereference of the digest context.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: unchecked return of BIO_set_md leaves the BIO_f_md filter with an uninitialized/NULL digest context. Trigger: attacker-supplied PKCS7 data naming a digest whose implementation is not fetchable. Consequence: NULL dereference (crash) when the chained BIO later processes data, a denial of service.

commit_msg:
dm: Reset virtio device before release

With virtio polling mode enabled, a timer is running in the virtio
backend service. And the timer will also be triggered if its frondend
driver didn't do the device reset in shutdown. A freed virtio device
will be accessed in the polling timer handler.

Do the virtio reset() callback specifically to clear the polling timer
before the free.

Tracked-On: #6147
Signed-off-by: Shuo A Liu <shuo.a.liu@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Yonghua Huang <yonghua.huang@intel.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tvirtio_ipu_reset(ipu);']}
description: The polling timer handler in ACRN before 2.5 has a use-after-free for a freed virtio device, related to devicemodel/hw/pci/virtio/*.c.

code_evidence: The deinit path only tears down the backend (k_stop/k_reset, close fd) when ipu_kstatus == VIRTIO_DEV_STARTED; otherwise it skips all device reset and backend shutdown.
After that conditional block, the mutex is destroyed and the ipu structure is freed unconditionally.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function's unconditional free(ipu) leaves a freed object reachable by the still-active polling timer, which is exactly reuse of freed memory (CWE-416). The added virtio_ipu_reset(ipu) before free is the fix, confirming the missing reset as the cause rather than a plain double free or leak.

evidence_lines.code:
pthread_mutex_destroy(&ipu->mtx);
free(ipu);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function frees ipu without ensuring the virtio backend's polling timer is stopped/reset, because backend reset is gated on VIRTIO_DEV_STARTED. Trigger: the polling timer fires (or remains active) after free(ipu). Consequence: the timer handler dereferences the freed virtio device, a use-after-free that can corrupt memory or crash.

description: In Wireshark 2.4.0 to 2.4.2 and 2.2.0 to 2.2.10, the CIP Safety dissector could crash. This was addressed in epan/dissectors/packet-cipsafety.c by validating the packet length.

commit_msg:
swtpm: Check header size indicator against expected size (CID 375869)

This fix addresses Coverity issue CID 375869.

Check the header size indicated in the header of the state against the
expected size and return an error code in case the header size indicator
is different. There was only one header size so far since blobheader was
introduced, so we don't need to deal with different sizes.

Without this fix a specially craft header could have cause out-of-bounds
accesses on the byte array containing the swtpm's state.

Signed-off-by: Stefan Berger <stefanb@linux.ibm.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    *dataoffset = ntohs(bh->hdrsize);'], 'added_lines': ['    uint16_t hdrsize;', '    hdrsize = ntohs(bh->hdrsize);', '    if (hdrsize != sizeof(blobheader)) {', '        logprintf(STDERR_FILENO,', '                  "bad header size: %u != %zu\\n",', '                  hdrsize, sizeof(blobheader));', '        return TPM_BAD_DATASIZE;', '    }', '', '    *dataoffset = hdrsize;']}
description: swtpm is a libtpms-based TPM emulator with socket, character device, and Linux CUSE interface. Versions prior to 0.5.3, 0.6.2, and 0.7.1 are vulnerable to out-of-bounds read. A specially crafted header of swtpm's state, where the blobheader's hdrsize indicator has an invalid value, may cause an out-of-bounds access when the byte array representing the state of the TPM is accessed. This will likely crash swtpm or prevent it from starting since the state cannot be understood. Users should upgrade to swtpm v0.5.3, v0.6.2, or v0.7.1 to receive a patch. There are currently no known workarounds.

code_evidence: Line 6 casts the untrusted input buffer to blobheader without validating the header's own size field. Line 7 checks only length against sizeof(bh) (pointer size), not sizeof(blobheader), and line 13 validates totlen but never checks bh->hdrsize. Line 29 assigns the attacker-controlled hdrsize to *dataoffset, which callers use to index the state byte array.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked hdrsize directly yields reads beyond the intended buffer, matching CWE-125. It is not merely an integer or input-validation issue: the concrete effect is an out-of-bounds read during state parsing.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the header's hdrsize indicator is trusted and propagated to *dataoffset without being constrained to the actual header size. A crafted state blob sets hdrsize to a value larger than the buffer, and the caller then uses dataoffset to access the state byte array, reading past its end. Supported consequence: out-of-bounds read, likely crash or failure to start.

commit_msg:
In the function fgetwln() there's a 4 byte heap overflow.

There is a while loop that has this check to see whether there's still
enough space in the buffer:

		if (!fb->len || wused > fb->len) {

If this is true more memory gets allocated. However this test won't be
true if wused == fb->len, but at that point wused already points out
of the buffer. Some lines later there's a write to the buffer:

		fb->wbuf[wused++] = wc;

This bug was found with the help of address sanitizer.

Warned-by: ASAN
Fixes: https://bugs.freedesktop.org/show_bug.cgi?id=93881
Signed-off-by: Guillem Jover <guillem@hadrons.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tif (!fb->len || wused > fb->len) {'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (!fb->len || wused >= fb->len) {']}
description: Off-by-one vulnerability in the fgetwln function in libbsd before 0.8.2 allows attackers to have unspecified impact via unknown vectors, which trigger a heap-based buffer overflow.

code_evidence: Line 15 guards reallocation with wused > fb->len, so when wused equals fb->len the buffer is not grown; line 28 then writes fb->wbuf[wused++] at index fb->len, one past the last valid element, advancing wused beyond capacity.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes to a memory location outside the buffer's intended boundary, matching CWE-119. The specific off-by-one is a child weakness, but the target CWE-119 correctly captures the out-of-bounds buffer write and its memory-corruption impact.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the capacity check uses a strict greater-than instead of >=, so the reallocation path is skipped when the buffer is exactly full. Trigger: fgetwc returns a character while wused == fb->len. Consequence: line 28 writes one wchar_t past the heap allocation, corrupting adjacent heap memory (a 4-byte heap overflow).

Because the user->release_barrier.rda is freed in ipmi_destroy_user(), but
the refcount is not zero, when acquire_ipmi_user() uses user->release_barrier.rda
in __srcu_read_lock(), it causes oops.
Fix this by calling cleanup_srcu_struct() when the refcount is zero.

Fixes: e86ee2d44b44 ("ipmi: Rework locking and shutdown for hot remove")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # 4.18
Signed-off-by: Yang Yingliang <yangyingliang@huawei.com>

Signed-off-by: Corey Minyard <cminyard@mvista.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tcleanup_srcu_struct(&user->release_barrier);'], 'added_lines': []}
description: In the Linux kernel before 4.20.5, attackers can trigger a drivers/char/ipmi/ipmi_msghandler.c use-after-free and OOPS by arranging for certain simultaneous execution of the code, as demonstrated by a "service ipmievd restart" loop.

code_evidence: _ipmi_destroy_user(user) tears down the user's SRCU state while the object is still referenced by kref_put's refcount; cleanup_srcu_struct(&user->release_barrier) is then called unconditionally, freeing the SRCU structure before the last kref reference is released. Concurrent acquire_ipmi_user() paths that take the refcount and call __srcu_read_lock on user->release_barrier.rda can therefore touch the already-destroyed SRCU struct.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function frees SRCU-backed memory (via cleanup_srcu_struct) and later code paths still reference it through user->release_barrier.rda, matching CWE-416 use-after-free rather than a simple race condition, since the core defect is reuse of freed memory.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is that cleanup_srcu_struct is invoked in ipmi_destroy_user regardless of whether other references to the user remain, so the release_barrier SRCU structure is freed while users can still acquire the object. A racing acquire_ipmi_user/__srcu_read_lock dereferences the freed rda, producing an OOPS/use-after-free; the fix defers cleanup until the refcount reaches zero.

commit_msg:
Fix SDCA optimizer crash.

Validates size of the dense_features and example state_data_inputs.
Other validation already verifies that sizes are otherwise consistent.

This looks to be a v1-only op that isn't used internally at all outside
of `contrib`, and no tests.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 478073762
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  for (int i = 0; i < dense_features_inputs.size(); ++i) {', '    if (!TensorShapeUtils::IsMatrix(dense_features_inputs[i].shape())) {', '      return errors::InvalidArgument("Dense features at index ", i,', '                                     " must be rank 2 but is rank ",', '                                     dense_features_inputs[i].dims());', '    }', '  }']}
description: TensorFlow is an open source platform for machine learning. Inputs `dense_features` or `example_state_data` not of rank 2 will trigger a `CHECK` fail in `SdcaOptimizer`. We have patched the issue in GitHub commit 80ff197d03db2a70c6a111f97dcdacad1b0babfa. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.11. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.10.1, 2.9.3, and TensorFlow 2.8.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: The function obtains the `dense_features` input list and, without validating each tensor's rank, proceeds to resize per-example `dense_vectors_` to `num_dense_features` and later calls `CreateDenseFeatureRepresentation` with these inputs. The missing rank check on `dense_features_inputs[i]` allows malformed rank-2 assumptions to reach downstream code.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unvalidated input reaches an assertion/`CHECK` that aborts the process, matching CWE-617 (Reachable Assertion): attacker-controlled input triggers a fatal assertion leading to application exit.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: no validation that each `dense_features` tensor is rank 2 before use. Trigger: an attacker supplies a `dense_features` tensor of rank other than 2. Consequence: downstream `CHECK`/assert failure terminates the process, causing denial of service (crash).

commit_msg:
PNRP: Exit our main loop.

Make sure our main loop offset advances. Fixes #17684.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    gint offset;', '    guint16 data_length;', ''], 'added_lines': ['    int offset, start_offset;', '    unsigned data_length;', '    start_offset = offset;', '        // SPLIT_CONTROLS might reset our offset.', '        if (start_offset <= offset) {', '            THROW(ReportedBoundsError);', '        }']}
description: Large loop in the PNRP dissector in Wireshark 3.4.0 to 3.4.9 and 3.2.0 to 3.2.17 allows denial of service via packet injection or crafted capture file

code_evidence: The main loop at line 54 continues while reported bytes remain, and each iteration advances offset by data_length (or data_length+padding) without any loop-iteration cap.

In the SPLIT_CONTROLS branch, after offset += data_length, reassembly can replace tvb and reset offset = 0 at line 280, so the next loop iteration re-parses from the start of the reassembled buffer rather than advancing.
No counter or termination guard bounds how many times the while loop can execute.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-834 covers iterations not sufficiently limited in count. Here the while loop has no iteration bound and a path that can repeatedly reset progress, directly matching excessive iteration with availability impact.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the loop termination depends solely on offset advancement, but the SPLIT_CONTROLS path can reset offset to 0 when a fragment is reassembled, so progress is not guaranteed. An attacker-supplied crafted capture/packet that triggers this reset makes the dissector repeatedly re-parse the buffer, consuming excessive CPU and hanging the process (DoS).

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    /*', '     * If the file is uncompressed, zz_csize and zz_usize should be the same', '     * If they are not, we cannot guarantee that either is correct, so ...', '     */', '    if (item->zz_compr == ZZIP_IS_STORED && item->zz_csize != item->zz_usize)', '    {', '        goto error;', '    }']}
description: In ZZIPlib 0.13.67, 0.13.66, 0.13.65, 0.13.64, 0.13.63, 0.13.62, 0.13.61, 0.13.60, 0.13.59, 0.13.58, 0.13.57 and 0.13.56 there is a segmentation fault caused by invalid memory access in the zzip_disk_fread function (zzip/mmapped.c) because the size variable is not validated against the amount of file->stored data.

code_evidence: Lines 24-25 read zz_csize and zz_usize from the disk entry without any cross-check; the new added validation (which would reject stored entries where csize != usize) is absent in this function as shown.
Lines 28-31 only validate that the comment and name strings exist before proceeding; there is no check tying zz_csize to the actual stored data extent, so the size fields are propagated unchecked.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing size consistency check lets a later operation use a size value that exceeds the intended buffer extent, matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds memory access. CWE-20 (input validation) is the underlying cause, but the supported weakness here is the resulting improper restriction of operations within buffer bounds.

evidence_lines.code:
item->zz_csize = zzip_disk_entry_get_csize(entry);
item->zz_usize = zzip_disk_entry_get_usize(entry);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function copies the on-disk compressed and uncompressed sizes into the entry without verifying that a stored (uncompressed) entry's csize equals usize or that csize fits the available data. Trigger: a crafted ZIP with ZZIP_IS_STORED compression and mismatched size fields. Consequence: downstream code uses the unvalidated size to address/read file data, producing out-of-bounds reads and a segmentation fault.

Fixes: 10cdd7e63e7f66e3e66273939e0863dd-asan_heap-oob_1a4ff32_7078_cov_4056274555_mov_h264_aac__mp4box_frag.mp4

description: A vulnerability was found in FFmpeg 2.0. It has been rated as problematic. This issue affects the function ff_init_buffer_info of the file utils.c. The manipulation leads to memory corruption. The attack may be initiated remotely. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue.

code_evidence: In the AVMEDIA_TYPE_VIDEO branch, frame->format is only initialized from avctx->pix_fmt when frame->format < 0. A pre-existing non-negative frame->format is left untouched, so the frame's format can remain inconsistent with the codec context's pix_fmt before downstream buffer allocation and pixel processing.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The commit fixes out-of-array accesses caused by an inconsistent frame format that feeds buffer sizing; the supported consequence is a write beyond the intended buffer, matching CWE-787. This is not merely an information-disclosure or uninitialized-read issue, since the format drives memory layout and writes.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the conditional guard skips overwriting frame->format, allowing a stale or inconsistent format value to persist into the video decode path. Trigger: a remotely supplied stream causes frame->format to be set to a value inconsistent with avctx->pix_fmt. Consequence: downstream code sizing or indexing per-format buffers uses the wrong format, producing out-of-array accesses and heap memory corruption.

commit_msg:
Return bad identity error if identity is unset

When the server-identity property of GTlsClientConnection is unset, the
documentation sasy we need to fail the certificate verification with
G_TLS_CERTIFICATE_BAD_IDENTITY. This is important because otherwise,
it's easy for applications to fail to specify server identity.

Unfortunately, we did not correctly implement the intended, documented
behavior. When server identity is missing, we check the validity of the
TLS certificate, but do not check if it corresponds to the expected
server (since we have no expected server). Then we assume the identity
is good, instead of returning bad identity, as documented. This means,
for example, that evil.com can present a valid certificate issued to
evil.com, and we would happily accept it for paypal.com.

Fixes #135
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  GSocketConnectable *peer_identity;', '  GTlsCertificateFlags errors;', '  if (!is_client)', '    peer_identity = NULL;', '  else if (!g_tls_connection_base_is_dtls (tls))', '    peer_identity = g_tls_client_connection_get_server_identity (G_TLS_CLIENT_CONNECTION (tls));', '  else', '    peer_identity = g_dtls_client_connection_get_server_identity (G_DTLS_CLIENT_CONNECTION (tls));', '  errors = 0;'], 'added_lines': ['  GSocketConnectable *peer_identity = NULL;', '  GTlsCertificateFlags errors = 0;', '  if (is_client)', '    {', '      if (!g_tls_connection_base_is_dtls (tls))', '        peer_identity = g_tls_client_connection_get_server_identity (G_TLS_CLIENT_CONNECTION (tls));', '      else', '        peer_identity = g_dtls_client_connection_get_server_identity (G_DTLS_CLIENT_CONNECTION (tls));', '      if (!peer_identity)', '        errors |= G_TLS_CERTIFICATE_BAD_IDENTITY;', '    }']}
description: In GNOME glib-networking through 2.64.2, the implementation of GTlsClientConnection skips hostname verification of the server's TLS certificate if the application fails to specify the expected server identity. This is in contrast to its intended documented behavior, to fail the certificate verification. Applications that fail to provide the server identity, including Balsa before 2.5.11 and 2.6.x before 2.6.1, accept a TLS certificate if the certificate is valid for any host.

code_evidence: Lines 10-16 compute peer_identity: for non-client connections it is set to NULL, and for client connections it is taken from the connection's server identity without any check that the result is non-NULL.

Line 21 calls g_tls_certificate_verify with peer_identity passed as the expected hostname, and lines 26-30 pass the same peer_identity to g_tls_database_verify_chain; when peer_identity is NULL there is no expected server name to compare the certificate against.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-295 covers failing to correctly validate a certificate. Here the certificate is not checked against the expected server identity, so hostname validation is skipped and a valid-but-wrong certificate is accepted, which is improper certificate validation rather than a pure trust-store issue.

evidence_lines.code:
errors |= g_tls_certificate_verify (peer_certificate, peer_identity, NULL);
errors |= g_tls_database_verify_chain (database, peer_certificate,
is_client ?
G_TLS_DATABASE_PURPOSE_AUTHENTICATE_SERVER :
G_TLS_DATABASE_PURPOSE_AUTHENTICATE_CLIENT,
peer_identity,

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: when a client connection has no server identity set, peer_identity remains NULL and the code does not add G_TLS_CERTIFICATE_BAD_IDENTITY, so the certificate chain is verified for validity but not against any expected host. Trigger: an application that fails to set the server identity. Consequence: a valid certificate issued to any host (e.g., evil.com) is accepted for the intended target (e.g., paypal.com), bypassing hostname authentication.

commit_msg:
CVE-2021-43825

Response filter manager crash

Signed-off-by: Yan Avlasov <yavlasov@google.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  if (stream.response_encoder_ != nullptr &&', '      (!stream.filter_manager_.remoteComplete() || !stream.state_.codec_saw_local_complete_)) {', '  bool request_complete = stream.filter_manager_.remoteComplete();'], 'added_lines': ['  if (stream.response_encoder_ != nullptr && (!stream.filter_manager_.remoteDecodeComplete() ||', '                                              !stream.state_.codec_saw_local_complete_)) {', '  bool request_complete = stream.filter_manager_.remoteDecodeComplete();']}
description: Envoy is an open source edge and service proxy, designed for cloud-native applications. Sending a locally generated response must stop further processing of request or response data. Envoy tracks the amount of buffered request and response data and aborts the request if the amount of buffered data is over the limit by sending 413 or 500 responses. However when the buffer overflows while response is processed by the filter chain the operation may not be aborted correctly and result in accessing a freed memory block. If this happens Envoy will crash resulting in a denial of service.

code_evidence: Line 3-4 gate stream reset and destruction on response_encoder_ being non-null and filter_manager_.remoteComplete() being false; if remoteComplete() returns true the stream is not reset and falls through to deferred destruction.
Line 33 similarly derives request_complete from filter_manager_.remoteComplete(), which reports completion of the whole filter-manager chain rather than decode completion of the remote data.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function's incorrect completion check lets destruction proceed while the filter manager still holds references, yielding a use-after-free; the supported consequence is a crash/DoS, matching CWE-416. It is not merely improper resource shutdown but access to freed memory, so the target CWE fits.

evidence_lines.code:
if (stream.response_encoder_ != nullptr &&
(!stream.filter_manager_.remoteComplete() || !stream.state_.codec_saw_local_complete_)) {
bool request_complete = stream.filter_manager_.remoteComplete();

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The completion predicate conflates full filter-manager completion with remote decode completion. When a locally generated response (e.g. buffer-overflow 413/500) is being processed, remoteComplete() can report true prematurely, so doEndStream skips resetting the stream and proceeds to doDeferredStreamDestroy while the filter chain still references the stream. Subsequent filter processing accesses the freed stream, causing a crash and denial of service.

When early abort is occurred due to invalid ACPI information, Linux kernel
terminates ACPI by calling acpi_terminate() function. The function calls
acpi_ut_delete_caches() function to delete local caches (acpi_gbl_namespace_
cache, state_cache, operand_cache, ps_node_cache, ps_node_ext_cache).

slab caches using kmem_cache_destroy() function, therefore the cache
objects should be flushed before acpi_ut_delete_caches() function.

function, acpi_ps_parse_loop(). The function should have flush codes to
handle an error state due to invalid AML codes.

This cache leak has a security threat because an old kernel (<= 4.9) shows
memory locations of kernel functions in stack dump. Some malicious users
could use this information to neutralize kernel ASLR.

To fix ACPI cache leak for enhancing security, I made a patch which has
flush codes in acpi_ps_parse_loop() function.

I hope that this patch improves the security of Linux kernel.

Thank you.

Signed-off-by: Seunghun Han <kkamagui@gmail.com>
