commit_msg:
The current code performs the cancel of a delayed work at the late
stage of disconnection procedure, which may lead to the access to the
already cleared state.

This patch assures to call cancel_delayed_work_sync() at the beginning
of the disconnection procedure for avoiding that race.  The delayed
work object is now assigned in the common line6 object instead of its
derivative, so that we can call cancel_delayed_work_sync().

Along with the change, the startup function is called via the new
callback instead.  This will make it easier to port other LINE6
drivers to use the delayed work for startup in later patches.

Reported-by: syzbot+5255458d5e0a2b10bbb9@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Fixes: 7f84ff68be05 ("ALSA: line6: toneport: Fix broken usage of timer for delayed execution")
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Takashi Iwai <tiwai@suse.de>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tINIT_DELAYED_WORK(&toneport->pcm_work, toneport_start_pcm);'], 'added_lines': ['\tline6->startup = toneport_startup;']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel before 5.1.8. There is a NULL pointer dereference caused by a malicious USB device in the sound/usb/line6/driver.c driver.

code_evidence: Line 7 schedules delayed work toneport_start_pcm via INIT_DELAYED_WORK on toneport->pcm_work, but only line6->disconnect is registered at line 8; no cancel_delayed_work_sync is arranged here, so the work can run after teardown clears state.

Line 9 calls line6_init_pcm; on failure lines 10-11 return early while the delayed work from line 7 remains initialized and potentially pending, leaving it to fire against partially initialized/cleared state.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function's unsynchronized delayed work leads to dereferencing a pointer expected valid but NULL after teardown, matching CWE-476. It is not merely a use-after-free ordering bug: the supported consequence is a NULL dereference crash.

evidence_lines.code:
INIT_DELAYED_WORK(&toneport->pcm_work, toneport_start_pcm);
line6->disconnect = line6_toneport_disconnect;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The delayed work is initialized and can execute without being synchronized against disconnection or early init failure, so it dereferences line6/PCM state that may already be NULL or freed. Trigger: malicious USB device causing disconnect or init error racing the pending work; consequence: NULL pointer dereference and kernel crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
Track byteSize of HeaderMap internally.

Introduces a cached byte size updated internally in HeaderMap. The value
is stored as an optional, and is cleared whenever a non-const pointer or
reference to a HeaderEntry is accessed. The cached value can be set with
refreshByteSize() which performs an iteration over the HeaderMap to sum
the size of each key and value in the HeaderMap.

Signed-off-by: Asra Ali <asraa@google.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['uint64_t HeaderMapImpl::byteSize() const {', '  uint64_t byte_size = 0;', '  for (const HeaderEntryImpl& header : headers_) {', '    byte_size += header.key().size();', '    byte_size += header.value().size();', '  }', '', '  return byte_size;', '}'], 'added_lines': ['absl::optional<uint64_t> HeaderMapImpl::byteSize() const { return cached_byte_size_; }']}
description: Upon receiving each incoming request header data, Envoy will iterate over existing request headers to verify that the total size of the headers stays below a maximum limit. The implementation in versions 1.10.0 through 1.11.1 for HTTP/1.x traffic and all versions of Envoy for HTTP/2 traffic had O(n^2) performance characteristics. A remote attacker may craft a request that stays below the maximum request header size but consists of many thousands of small headers to consume CPU and result in a denial-of-service attack.

code_evidence: byteSize() recomputes the total by iterating over every entry in headers_ on each call, summing key().size() and value().size() with no caching or memoization. Because the loop is O(n) in the number of headers and the function is invoked per incoming request header, repeated calls over a growing header set yield O(n^2) work.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function's per-call full iteration causes unbounded CPU consumption driven by attacker-controlled header count, matching CWE-400's resource-consumption scope. The defect is algorithmic resource exhaustion, not a memory-safety issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the size check recomputes the full header sum on every header added, so cost grows quadratically with header count. Trigger: a remote client sends many small headers staying under the size limit. Consequence: excessive CPU consumption leading to denial of service.

commit_msg:
bpf: fix incorrect tracking of register size truncation

Properly handle register truncation to a smaller size.

The old code first mirrors the clearing of the high 32 bits in the bitwise
tristate representation, which is correct. But then, it computes the new
arithmetic bounds as the intersection between the old arithmetic bounds and
the bounds resulting from the bitwise tristate representation. Therefore,
when coerce_reg_to_32() is called on a number with bounds
[0xffff'fff8, 0x1'0000'0007], the verifier computes
[0xffff'fff8, 0xffff'ffff] as bounds of the truncated number.
This is incorrect: The truncated number could also be in the range [0, 7],
and no meaningful arithmetic bounds can be computed in that case apart from
the obvious [0, 0xffff'ffff].

Starting with v4.14, this is exploitable by unprivileged users as long as
the unprivileged_bpf_disabled sysctl isn't set.

Debian assigned CVE-2017-16996 for this issue.

v2:
 - flip the mask during arithmetic bounds calculation (Ben Hutchings)
v3:
 - add CVE number (Ben Hutchings)

Fixes: b03c9f9fdc37 ("bpf/verifier: track signed and unsigned min/max values")
Signed-off-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Acked-by: Edward Cree <ecree@solarflare.com>
Signed-off-by: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tcoerce_reg_to_32(dst_reg);', '\t\tcoerce_reg_to_32(&src_reg);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tcoerce_reg_to_size(dst_reg, 4);', '\t\tcoerce_reg_to_size(&src_reg, 4);']}
description: kernel/bpf/verifier.c in the Linux kernel through 4.14.8 allows local users to cause a denial of service (memory corruption) or possibly have unspecified other impact by leveraging register truncation mishandling.

code_evidence: For non-ALU64 (32-bit) ALU ops, the verifier coerces dst_reg and src_reg with coerce_reg_to_32(), which narrows register tracking state (var_off and bounds) rather than the actual 64-bit register. This truncation of tracking metadata is the operation whose incorrect bounds computation is fixed in the commit.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The verifier's flawed truncation tracking lets a BPF program pass validation with memory accesses outside the intended buffer, matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds read/write within an intended boundary. The root cause is the bounds-tracking error at lines 11-14, not a distinct arithmetic bug alone.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the register-bound coercion used for 32-bit ALU operations produces incorrect arithmetic bounds after truncation, so the verifier's tracked range for a register no longer over-approximates the real value. Trigger: an unprivileged BPF program performs a 32-bit ALU operation on a register whose pre-truncation bounds straddle the 32-bit boundary; subsequent operations rely on the too-narrow bounds. Consequence: the verifier accepts out-of-bounds pointer/access computations, leading to memory corruption (CVE-2017-16996).

That meant a maliciously constructed string could cause deserialization to recurse, leading to stack exhaustion. This issue affected HHVM prior to v4.32.3, between versions 4.33.0 and 4.56.0, 4.57.0, 4.58.0, 4.58.1, 4.59.0, 4.60.0, 4.61.0, 4.62.0.

joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-674 fits because the function performs recursive deserialization with no depth limit, and the loop's unconditional recursive call is the direct cause of uncontrolled recursion. This is a recursion-depth control flaw rather than merely excessive input size.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: unserializeList recurses through unserializeThing without tracking or capping nesting depth. Trigger: a maliciously constructed serialized string containing deeply nested lists. Consequence: each nesting level adds stack frames, exhausting the stack and causing denial of service (stack exhaustion/crash).

commit_msg: Fixes to leaks and race conditions in VoiceMail plugin

description: An issue was discovered in Janus through 0.9.1. plugins/janus_voicemail.c in the VoiceMail plugin has a race condition that could cause a server crash.

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: started and stopping are written non-atomically in a session that is concurrently accessible after insertion into the shared sessions table. Trigger: another thread reads or modifies these flags while this thread performs the plain store. Consequence: torn/inconsistent flag state can cause the voice-mail session to be mishandled, supporting the reported server crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
Prevent null pointer dereference in constant folding.

Under certain conditions, an invalid protobuf saved model with invalid nodes would be loaded. During optimization phase, Grappler optimizer will then dereference a null pointer.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 409683530
Change-Id: I1f10340a7ec384bc9bc587300390f1078cf5caa0
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  if (mul_left_child == nullptr || mul_right_child == nullptr) {', '    return false;', '  }']}
description: Tensorflow is an Open Source Machine Learning Framework. Under certain scenarios, Grappler component of TensorFlow can trigger a null pointer dereference. There are 2 places where this can occur, for the same malicious alteration of a `SavedModel` file (fixing the first one would trigger the same dereference in the second place). First, during constant folding, the `GraphDef` might not have the required nodes for the binary operation. If a node is missing, the correposning `mul_*child` would be null, and the dereference in the subsequent line would be incorrect. We have a similar issue during `IsIdentityConsumingSwitch`. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.8.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.7.1, TensorFlow 2.6.3, and TensorFlow 2.5.3, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: node_map_->GetNode may return nullptr for a missing input; the results are stored in mul_left_child and mul_right_child. Both are then unconditionally dereferenced by IsReallyConstant(*mul_left_child) and IsReallyConstant(*mul_right_child) with no null check.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits: a pointer expected to be valid is NULL and is dereferenced without a guard, causing a crash. This is a missing null check, not an out-of-bounds or type-confusion issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the return value of GetNode is not validated before dereference. Trigger: a crafted SavedModel GraphDef in which a Mul node references an input name absent from the node map. Consequence: null pointer dereference/DoS during constant folding; later dereferences (e.g., lines 16-17) share the same unchecked values.

The loop bound and accumulator use int arithmetic: (++n + clen) is computed as a signed int before comparison to interp->maxArrayList, so a large clen or accumulated n can overflow before the size check.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs integer addition (++n + clen) whose result is assumed to grow, but can wrap when lengths are large, matching CWE-190. The missing overflow-safe constraint, not merely an out-of-range index, is the supported weakness.

Trigger: flattening an array whose element count or combined length approaches INT_MAX causes (++n + clen) to wrap to a small or negative value, passing the maxArrayList guard. Supported consequence: the size limit is bypassed, allowing excessive array growth (memory/instability) rather than guaranteed code execution.

commit_msg: Fix strncat/cpy bounding issues (fix #1425)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      strncpy(str, "", len);'], 'added_lines': ['    str[len-1] = 0;', '      str[0] = 0;']}
description: Espruino before 1.99 allows attackers to cause a denial of service (application crash) and a potential Escalation of Privileges with a user crafted input file via a Buffer Overflow during syntax parsing, because strncat is misused.

code_evidence: Line 4 copies up to len bytes of the constant string into str with strncpy, which does not append a terminator when the source is at least len bytes; line 5 then returns strlen(s) based on the source, not the bounded copy.
Lines 18-19 guard the character-data loop with l--<=1 and write a terminator, bounding writes to len.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs a bounded copy but leaves the destination buffer unterminated, enabling reads/writes outside the buffer's intended boundary; this is a memory-buffer bounds issue matching CWE-119. It is not merely a logic error, since the buffer boundary constraint is violated.

strncpy(str, s, len);
return strlen(s);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: For a constant string whose length is >= len, strncpy fills all len bytes of str without a NUL terminator. The caller receives a non-terminated buffer, so subsequent string operations read past the intended boundary, producing out-of-bounds reads and possible crash. The later character-data path is bounded, so the constant-string branch is the trigger.

commit_msg:
ALSA: timer: Fix leak in events via snd_timer_user_tinterrupt

The stack object “r1” has a total size of 32 bytes. Its field
“event” and “val” both contain 4 bytes padding. These 8 bytes
padding bytes are sent to user without being initialized.

Signed-off-by: Kangjie Lu <kjlu@gatech.edu>
Signed-off-by: Takashi Iwai <tiwai@suse.de>

description: sound/core/timer.c in the Linux kernel through 4.6 does not initialize certain r1 data structures, which allows local users to obtain sensitive information from kernel stack memory via crafted use of the ALSA timer interface, related to the (1) snd_timer_user_ccallback and (2) snd_timer_user_tinterrupt functions.

code_evidence: Stack object r1 is declared uninitialized at line 6. In the resolution branch, only event, tstamp and val are assigned (24-26) before &r1 is appended to the user-visible tqueue (27).
The tick branch likewise sets only event, tstamp and val (45-47) and appends the same partially initialized r1 (48). Struct padding bytes never receive a value.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function explicitly copies an under-initialized structure into a buffer exposed to userspace, leaking kernel stack contents; this is a direct disclosure of sensitive information, matching CWE-200.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the local struct snd_timer_tread r1 is not zeroed, so its 8 padding bytes remain uninitialized stack contents. Trigger: a user enables the resolution or tick filter and the event is appended to the queue, which is readable through the ALSA timer interface. Consequence: kernel stack memory is disclosed to the local user.

description: The "OpenID Connect Relying Party and OAuth 2.0 Resource Server" (aka mod_auth_openidc) module before 2.1.6 for the Apache HTTP Server does not skip OIDC_CLAIM_ and OIDCAuthNHeader headers in an "AuthType oauth20" configuration, which allows remote attackers to bypass authentication via crafted HTTP traffic.

commit_msg:
list-objects: pass full pathname to callbacks

When we find a blob at "a/b/c", we currently pass this to
our show_object_fn callbacks as two components: "a/b/" and
"c". Callbacks which want the full value then call
path_name(), which concatenates the two. But this is an
inefficient interface; the path is a strbuf, and we could
simply append "c" to it temporarily, then roll back the
length, without creating a new copy.

So we could improve this by teaching the callsites of
path_name() this trick (and there are only 3). But we can
also notice that no callback actually cares about the
broken-down representation, and simply pass each callback
the full path "a/b/c" as a string. The callback code becomes
even simpler, then, as we do not have to worry about freeing
an allocated buffer, nor rolling back our modification to
the strbuf.

This is theoretically less efficient, as some callbacks
would not bother to format the final path component. But in
practice this is not measurable. Since we use the same
strbuf over and over, our work to grow it is amortized, and
we really only pay to memcpy a few bytes.

Signed-off-by: Jeff King <peff@peff.net>
Signed-off-by: Junio C Hamano <gitster@pobox.com>

commit_msg:
Prevent heap OOB read in TFLite's `gather_nd.cc`.

Passing negative indices is illegal but there was a missing check so that resulted in OOB accesses.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 387208551
Change-Id: I6b7a8a62d3e7c13a16d81619e5bc23ae2cdbc7fd
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  bool indices_has_only_positive_elements = true;', '  const auto* indices_values = GetTensorData<IndicesT>(indices);', '  const size_t num_indices = indices->bytes / sizeof(IndicesT);', '  for (size_t i = 0; i < num_indices; i++) {', '    if (indices_values[i] < 0) {', '      indices_has_only_positive_elements = false;', '      break;', '    }', '  }', '  TF_LITE_ENSURE(context, indices_has_only_positive_elements);', '']}
description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. In affected versions TFLite's [`GatherNd` implementation](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/149562d49faa709ea80df1d99fc41d005b81082a/tensorflow/lite/kernels/gather_nd.cc#L124) does not support negative indices but there are no checks for this situation. Hence, an attacker can read arbitrary data from the heap by carefully crafting a model with negative values in `indices`. Similar issue exists in [`Gather` implementation](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/149562d49faa709ea80df1d99fc41d005b81082a/tensorflow/lite/kernels/gather.cc). We have patched the issue in GitHub commits bb6a0383ed553c286f87ca88c207f6774d5c4a8f and eb921122119a6b6e470ee98b89e65d721663179d. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.6.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.5.1, TensorFlow 2.4.3, and TensorFlow 2.3.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: EvalGatherNd dispatches to GatherNd<...> for each params type using the caller-supplied indices tensor; no validation of indices values occurs before the dispatch, so negative index values flow into the gather computation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Reading data before the intended buffer via negative array offsets is an out-of-bounds read, matching CWE-125. It is not CWE-787 because the defect is an unchecked read index rather than a write past a buffer bound.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function trusts indices tensor element values without checking that they are non-negative. Trigger: a crafted model supplies negative values in indices. These reach GatherNd, which uses them to compute offsets, producing an out-of-bounds heap read (information disclosure).

commit_msg:
Revised handling of TIFFTAG_INKNAMES and related TIFFTAG_NUMBEROFINKS value

In order to solve the buffer overflow issues related to TIFFTAG_INKNAMES and related TIFFTAG_NUMBEROFINKS value, a revised handling of those tags within LibTiff is proposed:

Behaviour for writing:
    `NumberOfInks`  MUST fit to the number of inks in the `InkNames` string.
    `NumberOfInks` is automatically set when `InkNames` is set.
    If `NumberOfInks` is different to the number of inks within `InkNames` string, that will be corrected and a warning is issued.
    If `NumberOfInks` is not equal to samplesperpixel only a warning will be issued.

Behaviour for reading:
    When reading `InkNames` from a TIFF file, the `NumberOfInks` will be set automatically to the number of inks in `InkNames` string.
    If `NumberOfInks` is different to the number of inks within `InkNames` string, that will be corrected and a warning is issued.
    If  `NumberOfInks` is not equal to samplesperpixel only a warning will be issued.

This allows the safe use of the NumberOfInks value to read out the InkNames without buffer overflow

This MR will close the following issues:  #149, #150, #152, #168 (to be checked), #250, #269, #398 and #456.

It also fixes the old bug at http://bugzilla.maptools.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2599, for which the limitation of `NumberOfInks = SPP` was introduced, which is in my opinion not necessary and does not solve the general issue.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t\t\tgoto bad;', '\t\t\t}', '\t\t\tif (TIFFFieldSet(tif, FIELD_NUMBEROFINKS))', '\t\t\t{', '\t\t\t\tif (!TIFFWriteDirectoryTagShort(tif, &ndir, dir, TIFFTAG_NUMBEROFINKS, tif->tif_dir.td_numberofinks))']}
description: A vulnerability was found in the libtiff library. This flaw causes a heap buffer overflow issue via the TIFFTAG_INKNAMES and TIFFTAG_NUMBEROFINKS values.

code_evidence: When FIELD_INKNAMES is set, the code calls TIFFWriteDirectoryTagAscii with tif->tif_dir.td_inknameslen as the count and tif->tif_dir.td_inknames as the buffer, without checking that the length is consistent with the related TIFFTAG_NUMBEROFINKS value.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the unsafe operation is a write past the end of the intended buffer driven by an unvalidated length. The weakness is the missing consistency check between InkNames length and NumberOfInks, not merely an integer overflow.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The directory writer trusts td_inknameslen and td_inknames without validating them against the number of inks. If a caller sets an InkNames length larger than the actual ink-name buffer (or inconsistent with NumberOfInks), the tag-writing routine copies past the end of the buffer, causing an out-of-bounds write.

commit_msg:
dm: Reset virtio device before release

With virtio polling mode enabled, a timer is running in the virtio
backend service. And the timer will also be triggered if its frondend
driver didn't do the device reset in shutdown. A freed virtio device
will be accessed in the polling timer handler.

Do the virtio reset() callback specifically to clear the polling timer
before the free.

Tracked-On: #6147
Signed-off-by: Shuo A Liu <shuo.a.liu@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Yonghua Huang <yonghua.huang@intel.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\tvirtio_console_reset(console);']}
description: The polling timer handler in ACRN before 2.5 has a use-after-free for a freed virtio device, related to devicemodel/hw/pci/virtio/*.c.

code_evidence: The destroy function frees console->config and then frees the console object itself without first invoking virtio_console_reset(console). The commit message states a virtio polling timer keeps running in the backend and can fire after the device is freed, so the timer handler dereferences freed console memory.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function releases the console object while an external timer retains a reference used later, matching CWE-416 (reusing memory after it has been freed). This is not a simple double free or leak; the defect is an outstanding reference surviving deallocation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: teardown frees the virtio_console and its config while the polling timer remains active. Trigger: the timer fires after free() and its handler accesses the released device. Supported consequence: use-after-free read/modify of freed memory, leading to crash or memory corruption; the patch adds reset() before free to clear the timer.

commit_msg:
Trap for overly large input to XmlRPCPP which could cause problems with int <-> size_t conversions.

 - In XmlRpcClient, XmlRpcServerConnection and XmlRpcSocket, recognize when incoming or outgoing data is too large, generate an error and discard the data when practical.
 - Use the safe strtol() rather than atoi() to decode an incoming content-length header, and generate an error if the length is invalid or too large.
 - In XmlRpcUtil, prevent attempts to parse overly large XML input.
 - Add tests where they can reasonably be inserted into existing test routines.

Although this fix could be cleaner the update is written to make the update ABI compatible.

This fix addresses CVE-2020-16124 / Integer overflow in ros_comm.

Signed-off-by: Sid Faber <sid.faber@canonical.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  // Watch for integer overrun', '  if (s.length() > size_t(__INT_MAX__)) {', '    XmlRpcUtil::error("XmlRpcSocket::nbWrite: text size (%u) exceeds the maximum allowed size(%s)",', '                      s.length(), __INT_MAX__);', '    return false;', '  }']}
description: Integer Overflow or Wraparound vulnerability in the XML RPC library of OpenRobotics ros_comm communications packages allows unauthenticated network traffic to cause unexpected behavior. This issue affects: OpenRobotics ros_comm communications packages Noetic and prior versions. Fixed in https://github.com/ros/ros_comm/pull/2065.

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the size_t-to-int conversion in line 4 assumes the serialized string always fits in int. Trigger: an oversized outgoing XML-RPC payload (attacker-influenced data) makes int(s.length()) wrap to a negative or small value. Consequence: nToWrite is negative so the write loop never sends the data, or the computed length is inconsistent, causing failed/incorrect transmission and possible instability/DoS.

description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. An attacker can force accesses outside the bounds of heap allocated arrays by passing in invalid tensor values to `tf.raw_ops.RaggedCross`. This is because the implementation(https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/efea03b38fb8d3b81762237dc85e579cc5fc6e87/tensorflow/core/kernels/ragged_cross_op.cc#L456-L487) lacks validation for the user supplied arguments. Each of the above branches call a helper function after accessing array elements via a `*_list[next_*]` pattern, followed by incrementing the `next_*` index. However, as there is no validation that the `next_*` values are in the valid range for the corresponding `*_list` arrays, this results in heap OOB reads. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.5.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.4.2, TensorFlow 2.3.3, TensorFlow 2.2.3 and TensorFlow 2.1.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: Loop iterates over each character of input_order_ and, for 'R', indexes ragged_values_list[next_ragged] and ragged_splits_list[next_ragged] before incrementing next_ragged, with no check that next_ragged is within the list sizes.
For 'S', indexes sparse_indices_list[next_sparse] and sparse_values_list[next_sparse] before incrementing, without validating next_sparse against the array bounds.
For 'D', indexes dense_list[next_dense++] without checking next_dense against dense_list.size().
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the unchecked *_list[next_*] accesses read past the end of the heap-allocated input lists. This is not CWE-129 (improper validation of array index) alone; the concrete supported weakness is the resulting out-of-bounds read.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the counters next_ragged, next_sparse and next_dense are incremented per matching character in the user-supplied input_order_, but are never bounded against the corresponding OpInputList sizes. Trigger: an input_order_ containing more 'R', 'S' or 'D' characters than provided tensors. Consequence: heap out-of-bounds reads when the indexed list element is accessed and passed to the builder helpers.

commit_msg:
[CVE-2022-23308] Use-after-free of ID and IDREF attributes

If a document is parsed with XML_PARSE_DTDVALID and without
XML_PARSE_NOENT, the value of ID attributes has to be normalized after
potentially expanding entities in xmlRemoveID. Otherwise, later calls
to xmlGetID can return a pointer to previously freed memory.

ID attributes which are empty or contain only whitespace after
entity expansion are affected in a similar way. This is fixed by
not storing such attributes in the ID table.

The test to detect streaming mode when validating against a DTD was
broken. In connection with the defects above, this could result in a
use-after-free when using the xmlReader interface with validation.
Fix detection of streaming mode to avoid similar issues. (This changes
the expected result of a test case. But as far as I can tell, using the
XML reader with XIncludes referencing the root document never worked
properly, anyway.)

All of these issues can result in denial of service. Using xmlReader
with validation could result in disclosure of memory via the error
channel, typically stderr. The security impact of xmlGetID returning
a pointer to freed memory depends on the application. The typical use
case of calling xmlGetID on an unmodified document is not affected.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if ((ctxt != NULL) && (ctxt->vstateNr != 0)) {'], 'added_lines': ['    if (xmlIsStreaming(ctxt)) {']}
description: valid.c in libxml2 before 2.9.13 has a use-after-free of ID and IDREF attributes.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: xmlAddRef only allocates and appends an xmlRef entry; the streaming-mode check affects whether the attribute name or attribute pointer is stored, but no free or reuse of freed memory occurs within this function, so CWE-416 is not directly supported here.

commit_msg:
xsk: Add missing check on user supplied headroom size

Add a check that the headroom cannot be larger than the available
space in the chunk. In the current code, a malicious user can set the
headroom to a value larger than the chunk size minus the fixed XDP
headroom. That way packets with a length larger than the supported
size in the umem could get accepted and result in an out-of-bounds
write.

Fixes: c0c77d8fb787 ("xsk: add user memory registration support sockopt")
Reported-by: Bui Quang Minh <minhquangbui99@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Magnus Karlsson <magnus.karlsson@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>
Link: https://bugzilla.kernel.org/show_bug.cgi?id=207225
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/bpf/1586849715-23490-1-git-send-email-magnus.karlsson@intel.com
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tint size_chk, err;', '\tsize_chk = chunk_size - headroom - XDP_PACKET_HEADROOM;', '\tif (size_chk < 0)'], 'added_lines': ['\tint err;', '\tif (headroom >= chunk_size - XDP_PACKET_HEADROOM)']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel before 5.6.7. xdp_umem_reg in net/xdp/xdp_umem.c has an out-of-bounds write (by a user with the CAP_NET_ADMIN capability) because of a lack of headroom validation.

code_evidence: Line 4 reads user-supplied chunk_size and headroom from the registration struct. Lines 29-31 compute size_chk = chunk_size - headroom - XDP_PACKET_HEADROOM and reject only if size_chk < 0. Because size_chk is a signed int and the subtraction is performed in unsigned arithmetic before assignment, a headroom larger than chunk_size - XDP_PACKET_HEADROOM wraps to a positive value and passes. Lines 36-37 then store the oversized headroom and compute chunk_size_nohr = chunk_size - headroom, which underflows.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The accepted oversized headroom leads to an underflowed chunk size and subsequent out-of-bounds memory writes, matching CWE-787. It is not merely an integer overflow (CWE-190); the security-relevant effect is writing beyond the intended buffer.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the validation compares a wrapped signed result instead of constraining headroom directly against chunk_size minus the fixed XDP headroom. Trigger: a privileged user registers a umem with headroom exceeding the permitted space. Consequence: chunk_size_nohr underflows, later packet length checks accept oversized packets, and writes past the umem buffer occur (out-of-bounds write).

commit_msg:
KEYS: Fix race between updating and finding a negative key

Consolidate KEY_FLAG_INSTANTIATED, KEY_FLAG_NEGATIVE and the rejection
error into one field such that:

 (1) The instantiation state can be modified/read atomically.

 (2) The error can be accessed atomically with the state.

 (3) The error isn't stored unioned with the payload pointers.

This deals with the problem that the state is spread over three different
objects (two bits and a separate variable) and reading or updating them
atomically isn't practical, given that not only can uninstantiated keys
change into instantiated or rejected keys, but rejected keys can also turn
into instantiated keys - and someone accessing the key might not be using
any locking.

The main side effect of this problem is that what was held in the payload
may change, depending on the state.  For instance, you might observe the
key to be in the rejected state.  You then read the cached error, but if
the key semaphore wasn't locked, the key might've become instantiated
between the two reads - and you might now have something in hand that isn't
actually an error code.

The state is now KEY_IS_UNINSTANTIATED, KEY_IS_POSITIVE or a negative error
code if the key is negatively instantiated.  The key_is_instantiated()
function is replaced with key_is_positive() to avoid confusion as negative
keys are also 'instantiated'.

Additionally, barriering is included:

 (1) Order payload-set before state-set during instantiation.

 (2) Order state-read before payload-read when using the key.

Further separate barriering is necessary if RCU is being used to access the
payload content after reading the payload pointers.

Fixes: 146aa8b1453b ("KEYS: Merge the type-specific data with the payload data")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # v4.4+
Reported-by: Eric Biggers <ebiggers@google.com>
Signed-off-by: David Howells <dhowells@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Eric Biggers <ebiggers@google.com>

commit_msg:
drm/amd/display: memory leak

In dcn*_clock_source_create when dcn20_clk_src_construct fails allocated
clk_src needs release.

Signed-off-by: Navid Emamdoost <navid.emamdoost@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Alex Deucher <alexander.deucher@amd.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tkfree(clk_src);']}
description: Memory leaks in *clock_source_create() functions under drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc in the Linux kernel before 5.3.8 allow attackers to cause a denial of service (memory consumption). This affects the dce112_clock_source_create() function in drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/dce112/dce112_resource.c, the dce100_clock_source_create() function in drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/dce100/dce100_resource.c, the dcn10_clock_source_create() function in drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/dcn10/dcn10_resource.c, the dcn20_clock_source_create() function in drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/dcn20/dcn20_resource.c, the dce120_clock_source_create() function in drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/dce120/dce120_resource.c, the dce110_clock_source_create() function in drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/dce110/dce110_resource.c, and the dce80_clock_source_create() function in drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/dce80/dce80_resource.c, aka CID-055e547478a1.

code_evidence: Line 8-9 allocates clk_src with kzalloc and stores the only reference in the local variable.

Lines 12-13 call dce112_clk_src_construct; on failure the function falls through to BREAK_TO_DEBUGGER and returns NULL at line 18 without freeing clk_src, so the allocation is leaked on the error path.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-401 matches: memory is allocated and, on the failure path, never released after its effective lifetime ends because the local pointer is discarded. This is a missing-release error-path leak, not a use-after-free or double-free.

evidence_lines.code:
struct dce110_clk_src *clk_src =
kzalloc(sizeof(*clk_src), GFP_KERNEL);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the error branch after dce112_clk_src_construct fails returns NULL without releasing the kzalloc'd clk_src. Trigger: repeated calls where construction fails; each leaks sizeof(*clk_src) bytes, leading to memory exhaustion (DoS).

commit_msg: kernel: harden the signature check (#1027)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tif (is_manager_apk(cwd) == 0) {'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (is_manager_apk(cwd)) {']}
description: Incorrect Authorization in GitHub repository tiann/kernelsu prior to v0.6.9.

code_evidence: The authorization branch calls is_manager_apk(cwd) and only grants manager privileges (ksu_set_manager_uid(uid); result = true) when the condition holds; otherwise it logs 'manager signature invalid!' and breaks. The diff changes the polarity from == 0 to a truthy test, so the acceptance path depends entirely on is_manager_apk's return convention.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-863 fits because the code performs an authorization check (signature validation) but evaluates it incorrectly, allowing an unauthorized actor to be granted manager privileges. It is not merely a signature-verification flaw (CWE-347); the defect is the misapplied authorization decision controlling privilege assignment.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the authorization decision at line 41 inverts/relies on the boolean semantics of is_manager_apk, so a signature-validity check is evaluated with the wrong polarity (the pre-patch == 0 form). Trigger: a caller/APK whose signature is not the manager's passes the check and reaches ksu_set_manager_uid. Consequence: the process assumes manager identity and gains privileged access, bypassing the intended signature authorization.

commit_msg: fixed mqtt variable length header issue
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        m->props_size = decode_variable_length((char *) p, &len_len);'], 'added_lines': ['        len_len = (uint32_t) decode_varint(p, (size_t) (end - p), &m->props_size);', '        if (!len_len) return MQTT_MALFORMED;']}
description: Due to a failure in validating the length of a provided MQTT_CMD_PUBLISH parsed message with a variable length header, Cesanta Mongoose, an embeddable web server, version 7.10 is susceptible to a heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in the default configuration. Version 7.9 and prior does not appear to be vulnerable. This issue is resolved in version 7.11.

code_evidence: At line 51 the code enters the v5 properties branch whenever p+2 < end, but line 52 calls decode_variable_length on p without bounding the available bytes to end. The returned length len_len is used unvalidated at lines 53-54 to advance p by len_len + props_size; if decoding runs past end or yields an oversized props_size, p is advanced beyond end. Line 56 checks p > end only after the pointer was already moved using the unchecked size, and m->props_start is also computed from the unchecked len_len.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the unchecked decoded length drives pointer advancement and subsequent buffer handling past the intended end, enabling memory corruption. This is the out-of-bounds write consequence; the underlying missing length validation is the cause, but the supported weakness is the OOB write.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the variable-length properties header is decoded without limiting input to end and without validating len_len/props_size. Trigger: a crafted MQTT_CMD_PUBLISH v5 packet with a malformed variable-length header. Consequence: pointer/length arithmetic derived from attacker-controlled values can exceed the buffer, yielding out-of-bounds writes/reads consistent with heap-based buffer overflow.

description: The HTTP/2 protocol allows a denial of service (server resource consumption) because request cancellation can reset many streams quickly, as exploited in the wild in August through October 2023.

description: sysstat through 12.7.2 allows a multiplication integer overflow in check_overflow in common.c. NOTE: this issue exists because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2022-39377.

code_evidence: The overflow check multiplies all three unsigned int operands after casting each to unsigned long long, then compares the 64-bit product against UINT_MAX. if ((unsigned long long) val1 * (unsigned long long) val2 *
(unsigned long long) val3 > UINT_MAX) {

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the guard relies on a multiplication whose result can itself wrap in the widened type. Trigger: callers supply large val1, val2, val3 whose 64-bit product overflows. Consequence: the overflow is not detected, so exit(4) is skipped and downstream size/length logic may proceed with a wrapped value.

commit_msg: daemon: fix read overflow when parsing CDP addresses
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t\taddresses_len -= address_len;']}
description: An issue was discovered in lldpd before 1.0.17. By crafting a CDP PDU packet with specific CDP_TLV_ADDRESSES TLVs, a malicious actor can remotely force the lldpd daemon to perform an out-of-bounds read on heap memory. This occurs in cdp_decode in daemon/protocols/cdp.c.

code_evidence: addresses_len is derived from the attacker-controlled TLV length (143) and bounds the address sub-TLV loop (144). The check at 157 verifies addresses_len against address_len+2, but after PEEK_DISCARD(address_len) at 164 the code consumes the 2-byte protocol length via PEEK_UINT16 (166) and decrements addresses_len (167) before validating it against address_len (168). Because addresses_len is never reduced by the earlier address_len bytes, the running budget overstates the remaining sub-TLV space, so the subsequent PEEK_DISCARD(address_len) at 175 can advance pos beyond the TLV/frame end.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The PEEK macros read from the received frame using the unvalidated position, so the missing budget decrement allows reads past the intended buffer end, matching CWE-125 Out-of-bounds Read. It is not an out-of-bounds write because no write beyond the buffer is shown.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the address sub-TLV byte budget is not decremented by the consumed address bytes, so the length consistency checks at 157 and 168 compare against an inflated remaining size. Trigger: a crafted CDP_TLV_ADDRESSES TLV with mismatched sub-TLV lengths drives PEEK_DISCARD past the buffer, causing an out-of-bounds heap read (and potential crash) in cdp_decode.

description: Out-of-bounds Read in r_bin_ne_get_entrypoints function in GitHub repository radareorg/radare2 prior to 5.6.8. This vulnerability may allow attackers to read sensitive information or cause a crash.

code_evidence: The loop is bounded by EntryTableLength and a buffer-size check at [28-31], but that check uses tableat+off+4 and does not account for the post-increment reads inside the bundle loop.

In the 0xff bundle branch, off is incremented by 2 and then a segnum byte plus a 16-bit segoff are read at [54-56] from entry_table+off; no bound check precedes these reads, and segnum is used to index segment_entries at [58] without validating it against SegCount.
In the fixed branch, a 16-bit value is read at [62] from entry_table+off after off was incremented at [49], again without checking off against EntryTableLength or the buffer size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences entry_table at offsets not proven to be within the table/buffer, which is a read past the intended buffer, matching CWE-125. The unbounded segnum index at [58] is a related indexing issue, but the direct weakness is the unchecked out-of-bounds read.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the per-bundle reads of segnum, segoff and the fixed delta occur without validating off against EntryTableLength or the underlying buffer, and the earlier check at [29] does not cover these offsets. Trigger: a crafted NE EntryTable whose bundle_length/type cause off to advance near or past the table end. Consequence: out-of-bounds reads of entry_table, leaking memory or crashing.

Proposed patch for bug #71270

+++ func_after
@@ -5,7 +5,7 @@
 	size_t estimate = (4 * l) + 3;
 
 
-	cmd = zend_string_alloc(4 * l + 2, 0); /* worst case */

description: Multiple integer overflows in ext/standard/exec.c in PHP 7.x before 7.0.2 allow remote attackers to cause a denial of service or possibly have unspecified other impact via a long string to the (1) php_escape_shell_cmd or (2) php_escape_shell_arg function, leading to a heap-based buffer overflow.

code_evidence: Line 3 computes l as a signed int from strlen; line 5 computes an unchecked size_t estimate = (4 * l) + 3, and line 6 allocates 4 * l + 2 bytes using the same unchecked multiplication. No overflow check exists before the allocation size is used.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is improper calculation of a numeric size before allocation, matching the numeric-errors category. The overflow of 4*l+2 is the direct cause; the heap overflow is its consequence rather than a separate weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the allocation size 4*l+2 is computed from an attacker-controlled length without checking integer overflow, so a very long string wraps the multiplication. The undersized heap buffer is then written past its end by the quoting loop (lines 12-37) and terminator at line 51, causing a heap-based buffer overflow and possible denial of service or other impact.

commit_msg:
Do not dereference PKCS7 object data if not set

Fixes CVE-2023-0216

Reviewed-by: Shane Lontis <shane.lontis@oracle.com>
Reviewed-by: Paul Dale <pauli@openssl.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    STACK_OF(PKCS7_RECIP_INFO) *rinfos = pkcs7_get_recipient_info(p7);', '    STACK_OF(PKCS7_SIGNER_INFO) *sinfos = PKCS7_get_signer_info(p7);', '    STACK_OF(X509) *certs = pkcs7_get_signer_certs(p7);', '    if (ctx == NULL)'], 'added_lines': ['    STACK_OF(PKCS7_RECIP_INFO) *rinfos;', '    STACK_OF(PKCS7_SIGNER_INFO) *sinfos;', '    STACK_OF(X509) *certs;', '    if (ctx == NULL || p7->d.ptr == NULL)', '', '    rinfos = pkcs7_get_recipient_info(p7);', '    sinfos = PKCS7_get_signer_info(p7);', '    certs = pkcs7_get_signer_certs(p7);']}
description:
An invalid pointer dereference on read can be triggered when an
application tries to load malformed PKCS7 data with the
d2i_PKCS7(), d2i_PKCS7_bio() or d2i_PKCS7_fp() functions.

The result of the dereference is an application crash which could
lead to a denial of service attack. The TLS implementation in OpenSSL
does not call this function however third party applications might
call these functions on untrusted data.

code_evidence: Lines 7-9 call pkcs7_get_recipient_info, PKCS7_get_signer_info and pkcs7_get_signer_certs before any validity check on the PKCS7 object.
Lines 10-11 only guard ctx == NULL; they do not verify that p7->d.ptr is set, so a malformed PKCS7 union with an unset data pointer passes through.
Lines 12-16 then use the returned stacks, dereferencing ri->cert and iterating certs, which depend on the PKCS7 data being present.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The root cause is a missing NULL check before dereferencing the PKCS7 data pointer, leading to a NULL pointer dereference (CWE-476). It is not a generic input-validation issue: the concrete unsafe operation is the unchecked pointer dereference.

evidence_lines.code:
if (ctx == NULL)
return;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function accesses PKCS7 union data without confirming that p7->d.ptr is non-NULL; when malformed PKCS7 input leaves the data pointer unset, the helper accessors and the subsequent stack dereferences operate on invalid data, causing a NULL-pointer read and application crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
Air Icy reported:

  UBSAN: Undefined behaviour in kernel/time/alarmtimer.c:811:7
  signed integer overflow:
  1529859276030040771 + 9223372036854775807 cannot be represented in type 'long long int'
  Call Trace:
   alarm_timer_nsleep+0x44c/0x510 kernel/time/alarmtimer.c:811
   __do_sys_clock_nanosleep kernel/time/posix-timers.c:1235 [inline]
   __se_sys_clock_nanosleep kernel/time/posix-timers.c:1213 [inline]
   __x64_sys_clock_nanosleep+0x326/0x4e0 kernel/time/posix-timers.c:1213
   do_syscall_64+0xb8/0x3a0 arch/x86/entry/common.c:290

alarm_timer_nsleep() uses ktime_add() to add the current time and the
relative expiry value. ktime_add() has no sanity checks so the addition
can overflow when the relative timeout is large enough.

Use ktime_add_safe() which has the necessary sanity checks in place and
limits the result to the valid range.

Fixes: 9a7adcf5c6de ("timers: Posix interface for alarm-timers")
Reported-by: Team OWL337 <icytxw@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
Cc: John Stultz <john.stultz@linaro.org>
Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/alpine.DEB.2.21.1807020926360.1595@nanos.tec.linutronix.de
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\texp = ktime_add(now, exp);'], 'added_lines': ['', '\t\texp = ktime_add_safe(now, exp);']}
description: The alarm_timer_nsleep function in kernel/time/alarmtimer.c in the Linux kernel through 4.17.3 has an integer overflow via a large relative timeout because ktime_add_safe is not used.

code_evidence: Line 16 converts the user-supplied relative timeout tsreq into ktime_t exp. When flags are not TIMER_ABSTIME, lines 17-20 add the current alarm-base time now to exp using ktime_add(), which performs no overflow/saturation check. A large user-chosen exp near the ktime_t maximum makes now + exp wrap around.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This is a direct integer overflow/wraparound: an arithmetic sum exceeds the ktime_t (signed 64-bit) range because the code assumed the result would remain valid. The fix replaces ktime_add with ktime_add_safe to clamp the value, confirming the missing overflow constraint is the root cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The relative timeout from userspace is added to the current time with unchecked ktime_add(). A large relative expiry triggers signed integer overflow, producing a wrapped (very small/negative) absolute expiration that is then passed to alarmtimer_do_nsleep, causing incorrect timer behavior rather than the intended long sleep.

commit_msg:
Validate intermediate symlinks during installation, CVE-2021-35939

Whenever directory changes during unpacking, walk the entire tree from
starting from / and validate any symlinks crossed, fail the install
on invalid links.

This is the first of step of many towards securing our file operations
against local tamperers and besides plugging that one CVE, paves the way
for the next step by adding the necessary directory fd tracking.
This also bumps the rpm OS requirements to a whole new level by requiring
the *at() family of calls from POSIX-1.2008.

This necessarily does a whole lot of huffing and puffing we previously
did not do. It should be possible to cache secure (ie root-owned)
directory structures to avoid validating everything a million times
but for now, just keeping things simple.

description: It was found that the fix for CVE-2017-7500 and CVE-2017-7501 was incomplete: the check was only implemented for the parent directory of the file to be created. A local unprivileged user who owns another ancestor directory could potentially use this flaw to gain root privileges. The highest threat from this vulnerability is to data confidentiality and integrity as well as system availability.

code_evidence: fsmMkdir dereferences the caller-supplied path with mkdir(path, mode & 07777); it performs no validation of intermediate path components.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-59 fits because the filename is used for a file-system operation without preventing a link in the path from resolving to an unintended resource; the missing ancestor-link validation, not merely a missing parent-directory check, is the weakness.

int rc = mkdir(path, (mode & 07777));

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function resolves the full path relative to the process CWD and creates a directory without checking whether any ancestor component is a symlink controlled by an unprivileged user. Trigger: an attacker owns an ancestor directory and replaces it with a symlink to a privileged location before installation reaches this call. Consequence: mkdir follows the link and creates the directory in the unintended target, enabling privilege escalation.

commit_msg:
When opening files for write, ensure they aren't symbolic links

Issue #1048 identified that if, for example, a non privileged user
created a symbolic link from /etc/keepalvied.data to /etc/passwd,
writing to /etc/keepalived.data (which could be invoked via DBus)
would cause /etc/passwd to be overwritten.

This commit stops keepalived writing to pathnames where the ultimate
component is a symbolic link, by setting O_NOFOLLOW whenever opening
a file for writing.

This might break some setups, where, for example, /etc/keepalived.data
was a symbolic link to /home/fred/keepalived.data. If this was the case,
instead create a symbolic link from /home/fred/keepalived.data to
/tmp/keepalived.data, so that the file is still accessible via
/home/fred/keepalived.data.

There doesn't appear to be a way around this backward incompatibility,
since even checking if the pathname is a symbolic link prior to opening
for writing would create a race condition.

Signed-off-by: Quentin Armitage <quentin@armitage.org.uk>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tlog_file = fopen(file_name, "a");'], 'added_lines': ['\tlog_file = fopen_safe(file_name, "a");']}
description: keepalived 2.0.8 didn't check for pathnames with symlinks when writing data to a temporary file upon a call to PrintData or PrintStats. This allowed local users to overwrite arbitrary files if fs.protected_symlinks is set to 0, as demonstrated by a symlink from /tmp/keepalived.data or /tmp/keepalived.stats to /etc/passwd.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function opens a log/data file for append; the symlink-following issue causes arbitrary file overwrite (integrity impact), not exposure of sensitive information, so CWE-200 is not supported.

commit_msg:
Fix #73003: Integer Overflow in gdImageWebpCtx of gd_webp.c

We add the missing integer overflow check to avoid potential buffer overflows.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\tif (overflow2(width, height)) {', '\t\treturn;', '\t}', '\t/* simplification possible, because WebP must not be larger than 16384**2 */', '\tif (overflow2(width * height, 2 * sizeof(unsigned char))) {', '\t\treturn;', '\t}', '']}
description: Integer overflow in the gdImageWebpCtx function in gd_webp.c in the GD Graphics Library (aka libgd) through 2.2.3, as used in PHP through 7.0.11, allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (heap-based buffer overflow) or possibly have unspecified other impact via crafted imagewebp and imagedestroy calls.

code_evidence: width and height are taken directly from attacker-influenced image dimensions (im->sx, im->sy) and multiplied to compute yuv_nbytes without any overflow check.

yuv_nbytes, a signed int, is passed as the element count to gdCalloc; then U and V are set to Y + width*height and U + yuv_width*yuv_height, reusing the same overflow-prone products as pointer offsets.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the unchecked integer multiplication and addition produce a wraparound value that is then used as an allocation size and pointer offset, directly violating the assumption that the computed size exceeds its operands. This is the root cause; the heap overflow and DoS are consequences of that wraparound, not a separate weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the size computation width*height + 2*yuv_width*yuv_height is performed in signed int with no overflow guard. When crafted dimensions make the product wrap to a small or negative value, gdCalloc allocates an undersized (or huge) buffer while the subsequent Y/U/V offset arithmetic and gd_RGBAToYUV420/WebPEncode writes use the un-wrapped logical dimensions, causing a heap-based buffer overflow.

commit_msg:
bpf: don't let ldimm64 leak map addresses on unprivileged

The patch fixes two things at once:

1) It checks the env->allow_ptr_leaks and only prints the map address to
   the log if we have the privileges to do so, otherwise it just dumps 0
   as we would when kptr_restrict is enabled on %pK. Given the latter is
   off by default and not every distro sets it, I don't want to rely on
   this, hence the 0 by default for unprivileged.

2) Printing of ldimm64 in the verifier log is currently broken in that
   we don't print the full immediate, but only the 32 bit part of the
   first insn part for ldimm64. Thus, fix this up as well; it's okay to
   access, since we verified all ldimm64 earlier already (including just
   constants) through replace_map_fd_with_map_ptr().

Fixes: 1be7f75d1668 ("bpf: enable non-root eBPF programs")
Fixes: cbd357008604 ("bpf: verifier (add ability to receive verification log)")
Reported-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>
Acked-by: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['static void print_bpf_insn(struct bpf_insn *insn)', '\t\t} else if (BPF_MODE(insn->code) == BPF_IMM) {', '\t\t\tverbose("(%02x) r%d = 0x%x\\n",', '\t\t\t\tinsn->code, insn->dst_reg, insn->imm);'], 'added_lines': ['static void print_bpf_insn(const struct bpf_verifier_env *env,', '\t\t\t   const struct bpf_insn *insn)', '\t\t} else if (BPF_MODE(insn->code) == BPF_IMM &&', '\t\t\t   BPF_SIZE(insn->code) == BPF_DW) {', '\t\t\t/* At this point, we already made sure that the second', '\t\t\t * part of the ldimm64 insn is accessible.', '\t\t\t */', '\t\t\tu64 imm = ((u64)(insn + 1)->imm << 32) | (u32)insn->imm;', '\t\t\tbool map_ptr = insn->src_reg == BPF_PSEUDO_MAP_FD;', '', '\t\t\tif (map_ptr && !env->allow_ptr_leaks)', '\t\t\t\timm = 0;', '', '\t\t\tverbose("(%02x) r%d = 0x%llx\\n", insn->code,', '\t\t\t\tinsn->dst_reg, (unsigned long long)imm);']}
description: The do_check function in kernel/bpf/verifier.c in the Linux kernel before 4.11.1 does not make the allow_ptr_leaks value available for restricting the output of the print_bpf_insn function, which allows local users to obtain sensitive address information via crafted bpf system calls.

code_evidence: For a BPF_LD instruction with BPF_IMM mode, the verifier log prints insn->imm via verbose() without any check on the caller's privilege level. This immediate is the map pointer value for ldimm64 pseudo map-fd loads, so the address is emitted into the verification log that unprivileged users can read.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function explicitly writes sensitive internal address data into a log accessible to unauthorized actors, which is a deliberate information-exposure mistake in handling sensitive data, matching CWE-200. It is not merely a downstream confidentiality impact of another memory-safety bug.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: print_bpf_insn formats and logs the 32-bit immediate of an ldimm64 instruction with no allow_ptr_leaks gate, so a map address reaches the verifier log. Trigger: an unprivileged user submits a crafted BPF program containing a pseudo map-fd ldimm64 load and reads the verifier log. Consequence: kernel map addresses are disclosed, aiding further attacks.

commit_msg:
x86/ioreq server: correctly handle bogus XEN_DMOP_{,un}map_io_range_to_ioreq_server arguments

Misbehaving device model can pass incorrect XEN_DMOP_map/
unmap_io_range_to_ioreq_server arguments, namely end < start when
specifying address range. When this happens we hit ASSERT(s <= e) in
rangeset_contains_range()/rangeset_overlaps_range() with debug builds.
Production builds will not trap right away but may misbehave later
while handling such bogus ranges.

This is XSA-238.

Signed-off-by: Vitaly Kuznetsov <vkuznets@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '    if ( start > end )', '        return -EINVAL;']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen 4.5.x through 4.9.x allowing attackers (who control a stub domain kernel or tool stack) to cause a denial of service (host OS crash) because of a missing comparison (of range start to range end) within the DMOP map/unmap implementation.

code_evidence: The function accepts caller-supplied start and end range bounds (lines 1-3) and passes them into rangeset operations without any check that start <= end.
At line 33 rangeset_overlaps_range(r, start, end) is called, and line 35 calls rangeset_add_range(r, start, end), both using the unvalidated bounds.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is absent validation of input properties (ordering of range bounds) before processing, matching CWE-20. The crash is the consequence, not the cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function validates neither the ordering nor consistency of the start/end arguments before using them as a range. Trigger: a device model passes end < start. The rangeset helpers assert on or mishandle the inverted range, causing a host crash in debug builds and possible misbehavior in production builds (DoS).

commit_msg:
If the state is not idle then rdma_bind_addr() will immediately fail and
no change to global state should happen.

For instance if the state is already RDMA_CM_LISTEN then this will corrupt
the src_addr and would cause the test in cma_cancel_operation():

		if (cma_any_addr(cma_src_addr(id_priv)) && !id_priv->cma_dev)

To view a mangled src_addr, eg with a IPv6 loopback address but an IPv4
family, failing the test.

This would manifest as this trace from syzkaller:

  BUG: KASAN: use-after-free in __list_add_valid+0x93/0xa0 lib/list_debug.c:26
  Read of size 8 at addr ffff8881546491e0 by task syz-executor.1/32204

  CPU: 1 PID: 32204 Comm: syz-executor.1 Not tainted 5.12.0-rc8-syzkaller #0
  Hardware name: Google Google Compute Engine/Google Compute Engine, BIOS Google 01/01/2011
  Call Trace:
   __dump_stack lib/dump_stack.c:79 [inline]
   dump_stack+0x141/0x1d7 lib/dump_stack.c:120
   print_address_description.constprop.0.cold+0x5b/0x2f8 mm/kasan/report.c:232
   __kasan_report mm/kasan/report.c:399 [inline]
   kasan_report.cold+0x7c/0xd8 mm/kasan/report.c:416
   __list_add_valid+0x93/0xa0 lib/list_debug.c:26
   __list_add include/linux/list.h:67 [inline]
   list_add_tail include/linux/list.h:100 [inline]
   cma_listen_on_all drivers/infiniband/core/cma.c:2557 [inline]
   rdma_listen+0x787/0xe00 drivers/infiniband/core/cma.c:3751
   ucma_listen+0x16a/0x210 drivers/infiniband/core/ucma.c:1102
   ucma_write+0x259/0x350 drivers/infiniband/core/ucma.c:1732
   vfs_write+0x28e/0xa30 fs/read_write.c:603
   ksys_write+0x1ee/0x250 fs/read_write.c:658
   do_syscall_64+0x2d/0x70 arch/x86/entry/common.c:46
   entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x44/0xae

Which is indicating that an rdma_id_private was destroyed without doing
cma_cancel_listens().

Instead of trying to re-use the src_addr memory to indirectly create an
any address build one explicitly on the stack and bind to that as any
other normal flow would do.

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/0-v1-9fbb33f5e201+2a-cma_listen_jgg@nvidia.com
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: 732d41c545bb ("RDMA/cma: Make the locking for automatic state transition more clear")
Reported-by: syzbot+6bb0528b13611047209c@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Tested-by: Hao Sun <sunhao.th@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Leon Romanovsky <leonro@nvidia.com>
Signed-off-by: Jason Gunthorpe <jgg@nvidia.com>

description: A flaw in the Linux kernel's implementation of RDMA communications manager listener code allowed an attacker with local access to setup a socket to listen on a high port allowing for a list element to be used after free. Given the ability to execute code, a local attacker could leverage this use-after-free to crash the system or possibly escalate privileges on the system.

code_evidence: When cma_comp_exch fails to transition RDMA_CM_ADDR_BOUND to RDMA_CM_LISTEN, the fallback path mutates the existing id->route.addr.src_addr.ss_family in place and then calls rdma_bind_addr() using cma_src_addr(id_priv). If the id is already in RDMA_CM_LISTEN, this overwrites the stored source address family, corrupting state that cma_cancel_operation() later tests via cma_any_addr(cma_src_addr(id_priv)).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The reported and described consequence is a use-after-free: an rdma_id_private is destroyed without cma_cancel_listens(), so a list node is referenced after free. The corrupted src_addr is the enabling cause, but the supported weakness class is CWE-416, not merely a state/validation flaw.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the fallback rebinds using and mutating the same src_addr memory even when the state is not IDLE, corrupting the identity's stored address. Trigger: a local user calls rdma_listen on an id already in RDMA_CM_LISTEN. Consequence: the mangled src_addr defeats the cma_any_addr() check, so cma_cancel_listens() is skipped and a list element is used after free, yielding a KASAN UAF and potential crash or privilege escalation.

commit_msg:
wifi: wilc1000: validate pairwise and authentication suite offsets

There is no validation of 'offset' which can trigger an out-of-bounds
read when extracting RSN capabilities.

Signed-off-by: Phil Turnbull <philipturnbull@github.com>
Tested-by: Ajay Kathat <ajay.kathat@microchip.com>
Acked-by: Ajay Kathat <ajay.kathat@microchip.com>
Signed-off-by: Kalle Valo <kvalo@kernel.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20221123153543.8568-2-philipturnbull@github.com
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tparam->mode_802_11i = 2;', '\t\tparam->rsn_found = true;', '\t\toffset += (rsn_ie[offset] * 4) + 2;', '\t\toffset += (rsn_ie[offset] * 4) + 2;', '\t\tmemcpy(param->rsn_cap, &rsn_ie[offset], 2);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tint rsn_ie_len = sizeof(struct element) + rsn_ie[1];', '\t\tif (offset < rsn_ie_len) {', '\t\t\t/* skip over pairwise suites */', '\t\t\toffset += (rsn_ie[offset] * 4) + 2;', '', '\t\t\tif (offset < rsn_ie_len) {', '\t\t\t\t/* skip over authentication suites */', '\t\t\t\toffset += (rsn_ie[offset] * 4) + 2;', '', '\t\t\t\tif (offset + 1 < rsn_ie_len) {', '\t\t\t\t\tparam->mode_802_11i = 2;', '\t\t\t\t\tparam->rsn_found = true;', '\t\t\t\t\tmemcpy(param->rsn_cap, &rsn_ie[offset], 2);', '\t\t\t\t}', '\t\t\t}', '\t\t}']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel before 6.0.11. Missing offset validation in drivers/net/wireless/microchip/wilc1000/hif.c in the WILC1000 wireless driver can trigger an out-of-bounds read when parsing a Robust Security Network (RSN) information element from a Netlink packet.

code_evidence: rsn_ie is obtained from cfg80211_find_ie over the Netlink-supplied IEs; its length byte rsn_ie[1] is not checked before use. offset starts at 8, then line 101 reads rsn_ie[offset] and scales it by 4, and line 102 reads rsn_ie[offset] again at the newly computed offset. Line 103 then memcpy's two bytes from &rsn_ie[offset] into param->rsn_cap, with no comparison of offset against the actual RSN element length.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe memcpy at line 103 reads two bytes from &rsn_ie[offset] where offset is attacker-influenced and unvalidated against the element size, which is precisely an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). The added length checks in the patch confirm the missing bound is the defect, not a write overflow.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the RSN pairwise/authentication suite counts read from rsn_ie drive offset arithmetic without any bound check against rsn_ie[1] or ies->len. A crafted RSN IE with a short body or large suite counts makes the second read and final memcpy index past the element buffer, causing an out-of-bounds read of adjacent kernel memory copied into the join parameter.

description: The make_response function in drivers/block/xen-blkback/blkback.c in the Linux kernel before 4.11.8 allows guest OS users to obtain sensitive information from host OS (or other guest OS) kernel memory by leveraging the copying of uninitialized padding fields in Xen block-interface response structures, aka XSA-216.

code_evidence: A stack-local struct blkif_response resp is declared; only the id, operation, and status fields are initialized, leaving padding bytes uninitialized.
memcpy copies sizeof(resp) bytes, including the uninitialized padding, into the shared native response ring.
The same full-size copy occurs for the x86_32 response ring.
The same full-size copy occurs for the x86_64 response ring, exposing the uninitialized stack bytes to the guest.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function explicitly transfers sensitive stack contents into a shared ring accessible to an unauthorized guest actor, matching CWE-200's exposure of sensitive information. The weakness is the uninitialized-padding copy, not an out-of-bounds access.

evidence_lines.code:
memcpy(RING_GET_RESPONSE(&blk_rings->native, blk_rings->native.rsp_prod_pvt),
&resp, sizeof(resp));

memcpy(RING_GET_RESPONSE(&blk_rings->x86_32, blk_rings->x86_32.rsp_prod_pvt),
&resp, sizeof(resp));

memcpy(RING_GET_RESPONSE(&blk_rings->x86_64, blk_rings->x86_64.rsp_prod_pvt),
&resp, sizeof(resp));

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the local response structure is only partially initialized, yet the whole structure size is copied into the shared ring. Trigger: a guest-visible block response is posted, copying uninitialized stack padding into memory the guest can read. Consequence: host kernel stack data leaks to the guest (confidentiality loss).

commit_msg:
[builtins] Fix Array.prototype.concat bug

Array.prototype.concat did not work correct with complex elements on the
receiver or the prototype chain.

BUG=chromium:594574
LOG=y

Review URL: https://codereview.chromium.org/1804963002

Cr-Commit-Position: refs/heads/master@{#34798}
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  if (!isolate->IsFastArrayConstructorPrototypeChainIntact()) {', '    return MaybeHandle<JSArray>();', '  }', '    Object* array_proto = isolate->array_function()->prototype();', '      if (!array->HasFastElements()) return MaybeHandle<JSArray>();', '      PrototypeIterator iter(isolate, *array);', '      if (iter.GetCurrent() != array_proto) return MaybeHandle<JSArray>();'], 'added_lines': ['      if (!HasOnlySimpleReceiverElements(isolate, JSObject::cast(arg))) {', '        return MaybeHandle<JSArray>();', '      }', '      // TODO(cbruni): support fast concatenation of DICTIONARY_ELEMENTS.', '      if (!JSObject::cast(arg)->HasFastElements()) {', '        return MaybeHandle<JSArray>();', '      }']}
description: The Array.prototype.concat implementation in builtins.cc in Google V8, as used in Google Chrome before 49.0.2623.108, does not properly consider element data types, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read) or possibly have unspecified other impact via crafted JavaScript code.

code_evidence: The loop accepts any JSArray argument and only checks arg->IsJSArray(), HasFastElements(), prototype identity and concat-spreadable before reading Smi::cast(array->length())->value() and accumulating result_len.

It does not verify that the receiver and each argument's elements have simple/consistent element kinds; the removed prototype-chain guard is replaced only by per-argument checks in the patched version, while this version relies on the global IsFastArrayConstructorPrototypeChainIntact() check.

The total result_len is passed to ElementsAccessor::Concat(isolate, args, n_arguments), which copies element data based on the computed length and element types without re-validating element data types for complex elements.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect leads to reading element storage beyond its intended bounds because element data types are not properly considered, matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds read. It is not merely a length overflow (CWE-190), since the missing constraint is element-type/layout validation before buffer access.

evidence_lines.code: return ElementsAccessor::Concat(isolate, args, n_arguments);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: Fast_ArrayConcat trusts the element representation of receiver/arguments and computes a combined length from Smi lengths without validating complex element data types. Trigger: crafted JavaScript builds arrays with mixed/complex elements (or altered prototype chain) so Concat reads element storage assuming a layout that does not hold. Consequence: out-of-bounds read of heap memory, causing denial of service or unspecified impact.

description: Liblouis 3.5.0 has a stack-based Buffer Overflow in the function parseChars in compileTranslationTable.c, a different vulnerability than CVE-2018-11440.

code_evidence: After decoding the multibyte sequence, line 106 writes result->chars[out++] before the bounds check at line 107; the prior check at lines 93-96 only guards the loop iterations, so a final iteration can increment out to MAXSTRING and then write at index MAXSTRING.

The single-byte path at line 79 also writes result->chars[out++] before its own check at line 80, but here the write occurs at index out which equals MAXSTRING only after increment, showing the same post-increment ordering pattern.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the function writes past the end of result->chars, an intended fixed-size buffer, due to a missing bounds check before the write. The commit explicitly fixes this ordering, confirming an out-of-bounds write rather than an unrelated weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the UTF-8 branch writes the decoded character (line 106) before verifying out < MAXSTRING, so when out already equals MAXSTRING-1 the post-increment write lands one element past the array. Trigger: a token containing a valid multibyte UTF-8 sequence that decodes at the boundary of the result buffer. Consequence: stack-based out-of-bounds write of a widechar, corrupting adjacent memory.

Fixes: 7549ae3e81cc ("9p: Use the i_size_[read, write]() macros instead of using inode->i_size directly.")
Reported-by: Xing Gaopeng <xingaopeng@huawei.com>

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tstruct super_block *sb)', '\ti_size_write(inode, stat->length);', '\tinode->i_blocks = (i_size_read(inode) + 512 - 1) >> 9;'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t struct super_block *sb, unsigned int flags)', '\tif (!(flags & V9FS_STAT2INODE_KEEP_ISIZE))', '\t\tv9fs_i_size_write(inode, stat->length);', '\tinode->i_blocks = (stat->length + 512 - 1) >> 9;']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel before 5.0.4. The 9p filesystem did not protect i_size_write() properly, which causes an i_size_read() infinite loop and denial of service on SMP systems.

code_evidence: Line 32 updates the inode size via i_size_write() without holding inode->i_lock, so the seqcount protecting i_size is not serialized against concurrent readers. Line 33 then calls i_size_read(), which spins in read_seqcount_begin() until the seqcount is stable; a concurrent i_size_write() can keep changing the sequence, so the reader never observes a consistent value.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The seqcount retry loop in i_size_read() has an exit condition that concurrent unprotected writes prevent from being reached, an unreachable-exit loop causing DoS. This matches CWE-835; the missing lock is the cause, but the resulting infinite retry loop is the weakness type.

evidence_lines.code:
i_size_write(inode, stat->length);
inode->i_blocks = (i_size_read(inode) + 512 - 1) >> 9;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: i_size_write() is performed without the inode->i_lock, breaking the seqcount write-side serialization that i_size_read() relies on. Trigger: concurrent v9fs_vfs_getattr/getattr_dotl calls on SMP (32-bit) update and read i_size simultaneously. Consequence: the reader loops indefinitely in read_seqcount_begin(), causing a soft lockup and CPU-consumption denial of service.
