Check bounds for reads and writes in scatter_nd

PiperOrigin-RevId: 463365479
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      return ScatterNd<IndicesT, float>(indices, updates, output);', '      return ScatterNd<IndicesT, uint8_t>(indices, updates, output);', '      return ScatterNd<IndicesT, bool>(indices, updates, output);', '      return ScatterNd<IndicesT, int8_t>(indices, updates, output);', '      return ScatterNd<IndicesT, int32_t>(indices, updates, output);', '      return ScatterNd<IndicesT, int64_t>(indices, updates, output);'], 'added_lines': ['  TfLiteStatus status = kTfLiteError;', '      status = ScatterNd<IndicesT, float>(indices, updates, output);', '      break;', '      status = ScatterNd<IndicesT, uint8_t>(indices, updates, output);', '      break;', '      status = ScatterNd<IndicesT, bool>(indices, updates, output);', '      break;', '      status = ScatterNd<IndicesT, int8_t>(indices, updates, output);', '      break;', '      status = ScatterNd<IndicesT, int32_t>(indices, updates, output);', '      break;', '      status = ScatterNd<IndicesT, int64_t>(indices, updates, output);', '      break;', '  if (status != kTfLiteOk) {', '    TF_LITE_KERNEL_LOG(context, "scatter_nd index out of bounds");', '  }', '  return status;']}
description: TensorFlow is an open source platform for machine learning. The `ScatterNd` function takes an input argument that determines the indices of of the output tensor. An input index greater than the output tensor or less than zero will either write content at the wrong index or trigger a crash. We have patched the issue in GitHub commit b4d4b4cb019bd7240a52daa4ba61e3cc814f0384. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.10.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.9.1, TensorFlow 2.8.1, and TensorFlow 2.7.2, as these are also affected and still in supported range. There are no known workarounds for this issue.

code_evidence: The switch dispatches updates types to ScatterNd<IndicesT, T>(indices, updates, output), which writes updates values into output at offsets derived from the untrusted indices tensor; the return value propagates ScatterNd's status.
ScatterNd is invoked for int64 indices as well, so index values originate from model input data without visible clamping in this function.
The only validation before dispatch is CheckShapes/ResizeOutputTensor, which handle output shape, not per-index bounds against the output tensor.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the unchecked index drives a write past the end or before the beginning of the output buffer. It is distinct from CWE-125 (read) since the operation modifies memory at the computed offset.

evidence_lines.code:
case kTfLiteInt64:
return ScatterNd<IndicesT, int64_t>(indices, updates, output);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: EvalScatterNd passes the indices tensor to ScatterNd without verifying each index lies within the output tensor bounds. Trigger: a model supplies an index >= output size or < 0. Consequence: ScatterNd writes updates content at an out-of-range offset, corrupting memory or crashing; the patch merely surfaces the returned error status.

commit_msg:
mm/pagewalk.c: report holes in hugetlb ranges

This matters at least for the mincore syscall, which will otherwise copy
uninitialized memory from the page allocator to userspace.  It is
probably also a correctness error for /proc/$pid/pagemap, but I haven't
tested that.

Removing the `walk->hugetlb_entry` condition in walk_hugetlb_range() has
no effect because the caller already checks for that.

This only reports holes in hugetlb ranges to callers who have specified
a hugetlb_entry callback.

This issue was found using an AFL-based fuzzer.

v2:
 - don't crash on ->pte_hole==NULL (Andrew Morton)
 - add Cc stable (Andrew Morton)

Fixes: 1e25a271c8ac ("mincore: apply page table walker on do_mincore()")
Signed-off-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tif (pte && walk->hugetlb_entry)'], 'added_lines': ['', '\t\tif (pte)', '\t\telse if (walk->pte_hole)', '\t\t\terr = walk->pte_hole(addr, next, walk);', '']}
description: The walk_hugetlb_range function in mm/pagewalk.c in the Linux kernel before 4.14.2 mishandles holes in hugetlb ranges, which allows local users to obtain sensitive information from uninitialized kernel memory via crafted use of the mincore() system call.

code_evidence: Line 13 resolves pte for the hugetlb range; line 14 only invokes the callback when pte is non-NULL, and line 15 reports the entry. When huge_pte_offset returns NULL (a hole in the hugetlb range), no callback is made and err stays 0.
The loop at lines 16-18 advances to next and continues, so holes are silently skipped and walk_hugetlb_range returns success without ever notifying the caller (pte_hole) that the range was unmapped.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing hole report lets mincore return uninitialized kernel memory to a local user, which is an exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor, matching CWE-200. The defect is the silent skip of unmapped ranges, not a bounds error.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the walker treats an absent hugetlb pte as a successful walk instead of reporting a hole, so callers such as mincore believe the range is backed. Trigger: a local user calls mincore() over a hugetlb range containing holes; the callback is never invoked, leaving caller-supplied buffers uninitialized. Supported consequence: uninitialized kernel memory is copied to userspace, disclosing sensitive data.

Syzbot found an issue in usbmon module, where the user space client can
corrupt the monitor's internal memory, causing the usbmon module to

commit_msg:
UDP IPv6 packets auto flowlabels are using a 32bit secret
(static u32 hashrnd in net/core/flow_dissector.c) and
apply jhash() over fields known by the receivers.

Attackers can easily infer the 32bit secret and use this information
to identify a device and/or user, since this 32bit secret is only
set at boot time.

Really, using jhash() to generate cookies sent on the wire
is a serious security concern.

Trying to change the rol32(hash, 16) in ip6_make_flowlabel() would be
a dead end. Trying to periodically change the secret (like in sch_sfq.c)
could change paths taken in the network for long lived flows.

Let's switch to siphash, as we did in commit df453700e8d8
("inet: switch IP ID generator to siphash")

Using a cryptographically strong pseudo random function will solve this
privacy issue and more generally remove other weak points in the stack.

Packet schedulers using skb_get_hash_perturb() benefit from this change.

Fixes: b56774163f99 ("ipv6: Enable auto flow labels by default")
Fixes: 42240901f7c4 ("ipv6: Implement different admin modes for automatic flow labels")
Fixes: 67800f9b1f4e ("ipv6: Call skb_get_hash_flowi6 to get skb->hash in ip6_make_flowlabel")
Fixes: cb1ce2ef387b ("ipv6: Implement automatic flow label generation on transmit")
Signed-off-by: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Reported-by: Jonathan Berger <jonathann1@walla.com>
Reported-by: Amit Klein <aksecurity@gmail.com>
Reported-by: Benny Pinkas <benny@pinkas.net>
Cc: Tom Herbert <tom@herbertland.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tfq->perturbation = prandom_u32();'], 'added_lines': ['\tget_random_bytes(&fq->perturbation, sizeof(fq->perturbation));']}
description: The flow_dissector feature in the Linux kernel 4.3 through 5.x before 5.3.10 has a device tracking vulnerability, aka CID-55667441c84f. This occurs because the auto flowlabel of a UDP IPv6 packet relies on a 32-bit hashrnd value as a secret, and because jhash (instead of siphash) is used. The hashrnd value remains the same starting from boot time, and can be inferred by an attacker. This affects net/core/flow_dissector.c and related code.

code_evidence: fq_init seeds fq->perturbation with prandom_u32(). This value is the per-flow perturbation mixed into skb_get_hash_perturb() for packet scheduling, so its unpredictability protects flow-to-queue mapping. prandom_u32() is a non-cryptographic PRNG whose output is predictable from observed values.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function supplies a security-relevant value (fq->perturbation) from an insufficiently random generator, matching CWE-330's use of insufficiently random values in a security context. The fix replaces prandom_u32() with get_random_bytes(), confirming the randomness weakness rather than a logic or bounds flaw.

evidence_lines.code:

network plugin: Fix heap overflow in parse_packet().

Emilien Gaspar has identified a heap overflow in parse_packet(), the
function used by the network plugin to parse incoming network packets.

This is a vulnerability in collectd, though the scope is not clear at
this point. At the very least specially crafted network packets can be
used to crash the daemon. We can't rule out a potential remote code

description: Heap-based buffer overflow in the parse_packet function in network.c in collectd before 5.4.3 and 5.x before 5.5.2 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (daemon crash) or possibly execute arbitrary code via a crafted network packet.

Subsequent iterations therefore validate pkg_length against a stale, too-large buffer_size and read part headers via memcpy beyond the actual packet buffer, causing a heap out-of-bounds read that can crash the daemon.

commit_msg:
ide: ahci: reset ncq object to unused on error

When processing NCQ commands, AHCI device emulation prepares a
NCQ transfer object; To which an aio control block(aiocb) object
is assigned in 'execute_ncq_command'. In case, when the NCQ
command is invalid, the 'aiocb' object is not assigned, and NCQ
transfer object is left as 'used'. This leads to a use after
free kind of error in 'bdrv_aio_cancel_async' via 'ahci_reset_port'.
Reset NCQ transfer object to 'unused' to avoid it.

[Maintainer edit: s/ACHI/AHCI/ in the commit message. --js]

Reported-by: Qinghao Tang <luodalongde@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Prasad J Pandit <pjp@fedoraproject.org>
Reviewed-by: John Snow <jsnow@redhat.com>
Message-id: 1452282511-4116-1-git-send-email-ppandit@redhat.com
Signed-off-by: John Snow <jsnow@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    ncq_tfs->used = 0;']}
description: Use-after-free vulnerability in hw/ide/ahci.c in QEMU, when built with IDE AHCI Emulation support, allows guest OS users to cause a denial of service (instance crash) or possibly execute arbitrary code via an invalid AHCI Native Command Queuing (NCQ) AIO command.

code_evidence: ncq_err marks the error status and sets the tag's error bit in scr_err, but the shown function body never clears ncq_tfs->used; the patch adds that clearing statement after the scr_err update.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function leaves a transfer object in a state that is later reused after free, matching CWE-416 (Use After Free). The missing reset of used is the missing constraint; the later reference to freed memory is the consequence, not a separate weakness.

evidence_lines.code:
ncq_tfs->drive->port_regs.scr_err |= (1 << ncq_tfs->tag);
}

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: an invalid NCQ command reaches ncq_err while the NCQ transfer object remains marked used, so no aiocb is assigned but the object is still treated as live. Trigger: the invalid NCQ/AIO command path. This stale used state lets the port reset path later cancel/reference the transfer object after it has been freed, causing a use-after-free crash or possible code execution.

commit_msg:
x86/mm: Add barriers and document switch_mm()-vs-flush synchronization

When switch_mm() activates a new PGD, it also sets a bit that
tells other CPUs that the PGD is in use so that TLB flush IPIs
will be sent.  In order for that to work correctly, the bit
needs to be visible prior to loading the PGD and therefore
starting to fill the local TLB.

Document all the barriers that make this work correctly and add
a couple that were missing.

Signed-off-by: Andy Lutomirski <luto@kernel.org>
Cc: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>
Cc: Andy Lutomirski <luto@amacapital.net>
Cc: Borislav Petkov <bp@alien8.de>
Cc: Brian Gerst <brgerst@gmail.com>
Cc: Dave Hansen <dave.hansen@linux.intel.com>
Cc: Denys Vlasenko <dvlasenk@redhat.com>
Cc: H. Peter Anvin <hpa@zytor.com>
Cc: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Cc: Peter Zijlstra <peterz@infradead.org>
Cc: Rik van Riel <riel@redhat.com>
Cc: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
Cc: linux-mm@kvack.org
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Ingo Molnar <mingo@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\t/* This is an implicit full barrier that synchronizes with switch_mm. */', '']}
description: Race condition in arch/x86/mm/tlb.c in the Linux kernel before 4.4.1 allows local users to gain privileges by triggering access to a paging structure by a different CPU.

code_evidence: The function performs a local TLB flush (line 6) but the commit notes this flush must act as an implicit full barrier synchronizing with switch_mm; without that ordering guarantee the PGD-in-use bit may not be visible before the local TLB is filled.

After flushing, the function reads mm_cpumask(mm) and conditionally sends remote flushes (lines 8-9), so the local and remote flush sequence depends on ordering with concurrent switch_mm activity on other CPUs.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function participates in a concurrent sequence where TLB state and the mm_cpumask bit are shared resources accessed without sufficient ordering, permitting an interfering switch_mm to race the flush. This is improper synchronization in concurrent execution, matching CWE-362 rather than an out-of-bounds or injection weakness.

evidence_lines.code:
count_vm_tlb_event(NR_TLB_LOCAL_FLUSH_ALL);
local_flush_tlb();

if (cpumask_any_but(mm_cpumask(mm), smp_processor_id()) < nr_cpu_ids)
flush_tlb_others(mm_cpumask(mm), mm, 0UL, TLB_FLUSH_ALL);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: a missing synchronization barrier between setting the PGD-in-use bit and loading the PGD/flushing the local TLB. Trigger: a local user causes switch_mm on another CPU while this task flushes; the bit may not be visible before TLB entries are populated. Consequence: a stale TLB entry survives the flush, allowing access to a paging structure by a different CPU and privilege escalation.

commit_msg:
nfsd: stricter decoding of write-like NFSv2/v3 ops

The NFSv2/v3 code does not systematically check whether we decode past
the end of the buffer.  This generally appears to be harmless, but there
are a few places where we do arithmetic on the pointers involved and
don't account for the possibility that a length could be negative.  Add
checks to catch these.

Reported-by: Tuomas Haanpää <thaan@synopsys.com>
Reported-by: Ari Kauppi <ari@synopsys.com>
Reviewed-by: NeilBrown <neilb@suse.com>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: J. Bruce Fields <bfields@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tif ((void *)old > vec->iov_base + vec->iov_len)', '\t\treturn 0;']}
description: The NFSv2 and NFSv3 server implementations in the Linux kernel through 4.10.13 lack certain checks for the end of a buffer, which allows remote attackers to trigger pointer-arithmetic errors or possibly have unspecified other impact via crafted requests, related to fs/nfsd/nfs3xdr.c and fs/nfsd/nfsxdr.c.

code_evidence: old is set to the decoded pointer p and vec is the head request buffer; avail is computed as vec->iov_len - (old - vec->iov_base) with no check that old lies within [iov_base, iov_base+iov_len].
If old is past the buffer end, the unsigned subtraction underflows to a huge avail, so the loop reads *old and copies bytes from memory beyond the request buffer into new (the symlink target page).

The second loop can then switch old to page_address(rqstp->rq_arg.pages[0]) and continue copying up to min(page_len, PAGE_SIZE) bytes, again without validating the offset, so the out-of-bounds read extends across the page.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs memory reads outside the intended buffer boundary because the pointer/length constraint is missing; this is an improper restriction of operations within a buffer (CWE-119). The commit adds exactly the missing bound check before the subtraction, confirming the out-of-bounds read is the defect addressed.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the decode path advances p without confirming it remains within the head iovec before deriving avail. Trigger: a crafted NFSv2/v3 symlink request whose variable-length fields push the pointer past the buffer end. Consequence: unsigned underflow yields a large avail and the function reads/copies attacker-influenced bytes from beyond the intended request buffer into the symlink target, causing out-of-bounds memory reads.

commit_msg:
Prevent EBCDIC overread for very long strings

ASN1 Strings that are over 1024 bytes can cause an overread in
applications using the X509_NAME_oneline() function on EBCDIC systems.
This could result in arbitrary stack data being returned in the buffer.

Issue reported by Guido Vranken.

CVE-2016-2176

Reviewed-by: Andy Polyakov <appro@openssl.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            ascii2ebcdic(ebcdic_buf, q, (num > sizeof ebcdic_buf)', '                         ? sizeof ebcdic_buf : num);'], 'added_lines': ['            if (num > (int)sizeof(ebcdic_buf))', '                num = sizeof(ebcdic_buf);', '            ascii2ebcdic(ebcdic_buf, q, num);']}
description: The X509_NAME_oneline function in crypto/x509/x509_obj.c in OpenSSL before 1.0.1t and 1.0.2 before 1.0.2h allows remote attackers to obtain sensitive information from process stack memory or cause a denial of service (buffer over-read) via crafted EBCDIC ASN.1 data.

code_evidence: A fixed 1024-byte stack buffer ebcdic_buf is declared at [14]. The ASN.1 entry length is read into num at [46] and only rejected against NAME_ONELINE_MAX at [47-50], which is larger than 1024. For EBCDIC string types [53-57], ascii2ebcdic copies min(num, sizeof ebcdic_buf) bytes into ebcdic_buf and sets q=ebcdic_buf [58-61]. However the later loops at [76] and [110] iterate j < num, indexing q[j] (e.g. os_toascii[q[j]] at [123]) beyond the 1024-byte buffer when num exceeds 1024.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads memory outside the intended bounds of ebcdic_buf, matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds memory operation. It is a buffer over-read rather than an over-write, but CWE-119 covers reads outside buffer boundaries; the length mismatch between copy and use is the direct cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the copy into ebcdic_buf is truncated to 1024 bytes but num remains the full untruncated length, so subsequent loops over j<num read past the buffer. Trigger: crafted EBCDIC ASN.1 string longer than 1024 bytes on EBCDIC builds. Consequence: out-of-bounds stack read returning arbitrary stack data or a crash.

commit_msg:
GHSL-2023-011: Out-of-bounds read when decoding

Out-of-bounds read when decoding target information (GHSL-2023-011)

Fixes defect GHSL-2023-011 found by the GitHub Security Lab team via
oss-fuzz.

The lenght of the av_pair is not checked properly for two of the
elements. In case the lenght is shorter than requires this may cause an
out-of-bound read that either reads garbage or may cause a crash by
reading unmapped memory.

This can be exploited to crash the service causing a DoS.

Signed-off-by: Simo Sorce <simo@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['            if (av_len < sizeof(timestamp)) {', '                ret = ERR_DECODE;', '                goto done;', '            }', '            if (av_len < sizeof(flags)) {', '                ret = ERR_DECODE;', '                goto done;', '            }']}
description: GSS-NTLMSSP, a mechglue plugin for the GSSAPI library that implements NTLM authentication, has an out-of-bounds read when decoding target information prior to version 1.2.0. The length of the `av_pair` is not checked properly for two of the elements which can trigger an out-of-bound read. The out-of-bounds read can be triggered via the main `gss_accept_sec_context` entry point and could cause a denial-of-service if the memory is unmapped. The issue is fixed in version 1.2.0.

code_evidence: For MSV_AV_TIMESTAMP, after checking only that av_timestamp is non-null, memcpy copies sizeof(timestamp) bytes from av_pair->value without verifying av_len is at least 8.
For MSV_AV_FLAGS, after checking only that av_flags is non-null, memcpy copies sizeof(flags) bytes from av_pair->value without verifying av_len is at least 4.
The loop-level check at line 29 only ensures av_len does not exceed the remaining buffer; it does not ensure av_len is large enough for the fixed-size memcpy reads, so a short av_pair passes.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads past the end of the intended av_pair value buffer via memcpy with a fixed size exceeding av_len, which is exactly an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). The missing length constraint causes the read; the crash/garbage disclosure is its consequence, not the weakness itself.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the per-element av_len is validated only against the upper bound of remaining buffer length, not against the fixed sizes (8 and 4 bytes) required by the timestamp and flags memcpy calls. Trigger: an attacker-supplied target-info AV pair with MSV_AV_TIMESTAMP or MSV_AV_FLAGS and a short av_len that still fits in the buffer. Consequence: out-of-bounds read of adjacent memory, yielding garbage or a crash (DoS) if unmapped.

commit_msg:
Fix a dangerous integer overflow and a malloc of negative size.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 371254154
Change-Id: I250a98a3df26328770167025670235a963a72da0
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  TF_LITE_ENSURE(context, output_shape != nullptr);']}
description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. The TFLite code for allocating `TFLiteIntArray`s is vulnerable to an integer overflow issue(https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/4ceffae632721e52bf3501b736e4fe9d1221cdfa/tensorflow/lite/c/common.c#L24-L27). An attacker can craft a model such that the `size` multiplier is so large that the return value overflows the `int` datatype and becomes negative. In turn, this results in invalid value being given to `malloc`(https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/4ceffae632721e52bf3501b736e4fe9d1221cdfa/tensorflow/lite/c/common.c#L47-L52). In this case, `ret->size` would dereference an invalid pointer. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.5.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.4.2, TensorFlow 2.3.3, TensorFlow 2.2.3 and TensorFlow 2.1.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: output_rank is computed from attacker-influenced rank dimensions and passed to TfLiteIntArrayCreate without validating a positive/non-overflowing size.
The loop multiplies embedding_size by each value dimension; large dimensions wrap the signed int and can make embedding_size negative or small.
output_size = lookup_size * embedding_size is then used as TfLiteTensorRealloc(output_size * sizeof(float), output), so a wrapped/negative size reaches allocation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits: the function performs size calculations assumed to grow but can wrap to negative values, and the wrapped value directly determines an allocation size. This is integer overflow feeding allocation, not merely an out-of-bounds index check.

evidence_lines.code:
const int output_rank = (lookup_rank - 1) + (embedding_rank - 1);
TfLiteIntArray* output_shape = TfLiteIntArrayCreate(output_rank);

const int output_size = lookup_size * embedding_size;
TfLiteTensorRealloc(output_size * sizeof(float), output);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: signed integer multiplications (lookup_size *= dim, embedding_size *= dim, lookup_size * embedding_size) are unchecked. Trigger: a crafted model with large dimension values causes wraparound; the resulting negative/small output_size is passed to TfLiteTensorRealloc. Supported consequence: invalid allocation size, and subsequent std::fill_n / indexed writes against an undersized buffer can corrupt memory or crash.

commit_msg:
oauth2: do not blindly accept requests with a token in the Authorization headera (781)

The logic was broken because it assumed an additional call would be
performed to the auth server, which isn't the case. Per the filter
documentation, a request is only considered subsequently authenticated
if there's valid cookie that was set after the access token was received
from the auth server:

https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/configuration/http/http_filters/oauth2_filter

More info about how to validate an access token (which we don't do, per
above):

https://www.oauth.com/oauth2-servers/token-introspection-endpoint/
https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7662

Also fix the fact that ee shouldn't be calling continueDecoding() after
decoder_callbacks_->encodeHeaders().

commit_msg:
KVM: x86: avoid calling x86 emulator without a decoded instruction

Whenever x86_decode_emulated_instruction() detects a breakpoint, it
returns the value that kvm_vcpu_check_breakpoint() writes into its
pass-by-reference second argument.  Unfortunately this is completely
bogus because the expected outcome of x86_decode_emulated_instruction
is an EMULATION_* value.

Then, if kvm_vcpu_check_breakpoint() does "*r = 0" (corresponding to
a KVM_EXIT_DEBUG userspace exit), it is misunderstood as EMULATION_OK
and x86_emulate_instruction() is called without having decoded the
instruction.  This causes various havoc from running with a stale
emulation context.

The fix is to move the call to kvm_vcpu_check_breakpoint() where it was
before commit 4aa2691dcbd3 ("KVM: x86: Factor out x86 instruction
emulation with decoding") introduced x86_decode_emulated_instruction().
The other caller of the function does not need breakpoint checks,
because it is invoked as part of a vmexit and the processor has already
checked those before executing the instruction that #GP'd.

This fixes CVE-2022-1852.

Reported-by: Qiuhao Li <qiuhao@sysec.org>
Reported-by: Gaoning Pan <pgn@zju.edu.cn>
Reported-by: Yongkang Jia <kangel@zju.edu.cn>
Fixes: 4aa2691dcbd3 ("KVM: x86: Factor out x86 instruction emulation with decoding")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Sean Christopherson <seanjc@google.com>
Message-Id: <20220311032801.3467418-2-seanjc@google.com>
[Rewrote commit message according to Qiuhao's report, since a patch
 already existed to fix the bug. - Paolo]
Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tint r = EMULATION_OK;', '', '\t/*', '\t * We will reenter on the same instruction since we do not set', '\t * complete_userspace_io. This does not handle watchpoints yet,', '\t * those would be handled in the emulate_ops.', '\t */', '\tif (!(emulation_type & EMULTYPE_SKIP) &&', '\t    kvm_vcpu_check_breakpoint(vcpu, &r))', '\t\treturn r;'], 'added_lines': ['\tint r;']}
description: A NULL pointer dereference flaw was found in the Linux kernel’s KVM module, which can lead to a denial of service in the x86_emulate_insn in arch/x86/kvm/emulate.c. This flaw occurs while executing an illegal instruction in guest in the Intel CPU.

code_evidence: Line 4 initializes r to EMULATION_OK; lines 7-9 call kvm_vcpu_check_breakpoint(vcpu, &r) and, on a breakpoint, return r (which may be 0 from a KVM_EXIT_DEBUG userspace exit) without decoding the instruction; line 10 then decodes only when the branch is not taken, so the return value conflates emulation status with breakpoint status.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The misreported status skips x86_decode_insn, leaving the emulation context without a decoded instruction; the subsequent emulation dereferences a pointer expected to be valid but NULL, matching CWE-476. This is a NULL-dereference consequence, not merely an incorrect return value.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: x86_decode_emulated_instruction returns the breakpoint-check value as if it were an EMULATION_* status, so a 0 (KVM_EXIT_DEBUG) is misread as EMULATION_OK. Trigger: a guest breakpoint causes kvm_vcpu_check_breakpoint to write 0. Consequence: the caller invokes x86_emulate_instruction without a decoded instruction, running with a stale emulation context and leading to a NULL pointer dereference/DoS.

commit_msg:
vc2enc_dwt: pad the temporary buffer by the slice size

Since non-Haar wavelets need to look into pixels outside the frame, we
need to pad the buffer. The old factor of two seemed to be a workaround
that fact and only padded to the left and bottom. This correctly pads
by the slice size and as such reduces memory usage and potential
exploits.
Reported by Liu Bingchang.

Ideally, there should be no temporary buffer but the encoder is designed
to deinterleave the coefficients into the classical wavelet structure
with the lower frequency values in the top left corner.

Signed-off-by: Rostislav Pehlivanov <atomnuker@gmail.com>
(cherry picked from commit 3228ac730c11eca49d5680d5550128e397061c85)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['                                        s->plane[0].coef_stride,', '                                        s->plane[0].dwt_height))'], 'added_lines': ['                                      s->plane[i].coef_stride,', '                                      s->plane[i].dwt_height,', '                                      s->slice_width, s->slice_height))']}
description: The VC-2 Video Compression encoder in FFmpeg 3.0 and 3.4 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read) because of incorrect buffer padding for non-Haar wavelets, related to libavcodec/vc2enc.c and libavcodec/vc2enc_dwt.c.

code_evidence: The plane buffer is allocated as coef_stride*dwt_height, where dwt_width/height are only FFALIGN-ed to the wavelet depth and stride to 32; no padding for the slice size or for non-Haar wavelet taps is included.

ff_vc2enc_init_transforms is passed s->plane[0].coef_stride and s->plane[0].dwt_height (plane 0) for every plane i, and no slice_width/slice_height, so transform setup receives dimensions that do not account for the extra boundary padding the DWT needs.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect is insufficient buffer padding that lets DWT reads index before/after the intended buffer, matching CWE-125 (out-of-bounds read). It is not a write (CWE-787) because the unsafe access is a read of coefficient data.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the temporary coefficient buffer and transform arguments lack the padding required by non-Haar wavelets, which read neighbors outside the frame. Trigger: encoding with a non-Haar wavelet and a non-zero slice size causes transform taps to access indices beyond the allocated buffer. Supported consequence: out-of-bounds read, leading to a crash/DoS and potential disclosure.

description: A remote code execution vulnerability in libhevc in Mediaserver could enable an attacker using a specially crafted file to cause memory corruption during media file and data processing. This issue is rated as Critical due to the possibility of remote code execution within the context of the Mediaserver process. Product: Android. Versions: 5.0.2, 5.1.1, 6.0, 6.0.1, 7.0, 7.1.1, 7.1.2. The added guard compares (UWORD8 *)ps_bitstrm->pu4_buf against ps_bitstrm->pu1_buf_max and returns IHEVCD_INVALID_PARAMETER before further parsing.

description: tif_pixarlog.c in libtiff 4.0.6 has out-of-bounds write vulnerabilities in heap allocated buffers. Reported as MSVR 35094, aka "PixarLog horizontalDifference heap-buffer-overflow."

code_evidence: In the else branch (stride not 3 or 4), pointers are first advanced to the end via ip += n - 1 and wp += n - 1, then the loop walks backward with wp-- and ip--. The write wp[stride] -= wp[0] and wp[stride] &= mask targets an offset relative to the current wp, and the final backward REPEAT at line 51 writes wp[0] after the decrements. The traversal direction and index arithmetic are not bounded against the buffer extent, so writes can land outside the allocated heap buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the defect is a write past the end/before the beginning of the intended heap buffer, matching the out-of-bounds write definition. It is not merely an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) since wp[stride] and wp[0] are assigned.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the backward traversal computes write locations via wp[stride] and wp[0] with pointer decrements that are not validated against the buffer bounds. Trigger: calling horizontalDifferenceF with a stride other than 3 or 4 and an n/stride combination that causes the pointer arithmetic to step past the allocated region. Consequence: heap out-of-bounds write, corrupting adjacent memory.

commit_msg: add parentheses for define expression
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['#define MAX_TABLEFILE_SIZE MAXSTRING * sizeof(char) * 2'], 'added_lines': ['#define MAX_TABLEFILE_SIZE (MAXSTRING * sizeof(char) * 2)']}
description: Buffer Overflow vulnerability found in Liblouis Lou_Trace v.3.24.0 allows a remote attacker to cause a denial of service via the resolveSubtable function at compileTranslationTabel.c.

code_evidence: Line 5 defines MAX_TABLEFILE_SIZE as an unparenthesized macro MAXSTRING * sizeof(char) * 2; line 7 uses it as the malloc size, so the allocated size depends on how the macro expands in context.

Line 10 checks strlen(base) against MAX_TABLEFILE_SIZE, then line 11 strcpy copies base into tableFile; the bound comparison uses the macro expression, coupling the copy guard to the allocation arithmetic.
Line 15 checks combined lengths against the macro before line 16 strcat appends table; the guard and the buffer size share the same macro expression.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Line 11 (and line 16) copy input into tableFile after a size check whose correctness is undermined by the macro's lack of parentheses, matching CWE-120's buffer copy without a reliable input-size check. This is a copy-size/validation flaw, not merely an out-of-bounds read.

evidence_lines.code:
#define MAX_TABLEFILE_SIZE MAXSTRING * sizeof(char) * 2
tableFile = (char *)malloc(MAX_TABLEFILE_SIZE);

if (strlen(base) >= MAX_TABLEFILE_SIZE) goto failure;
strcpy(tableFile, base);

if (strlen(tableFile) + strlen(table) >= MAX_TABLEFILE_SIZE) goto failure;
strcat(tableFile, table);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The buffer size and the length guards both derive from the same unparenthesized macro. When the macro is substituted into an expression, operator precedence can change the computed size or comparison, so a length check may pass while the actual allocated buffer is smaller, and the subsequent strcpy/strcat writes past it, causing memory corruption or a crash (DoS).

description: ImageMagick before 7.0.8-50 has an integer overflow vulnerability in the function TIFFSeekCustomStream in coders/tiff.c.

code_evidence: In the SEEK_CUR case, profile->offset (a signed MagickOffsetType) is added to the caller-supplied offset without any bound check before the sum is compared to zero. The comparison (profile->offset+offset) < 0 is itself evaluated on the possibly-overflowed sum, so an addition that wraps to a small or negative value is not detected, and profile->offset+=offset then stores the wrapped result.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function computes profile->offset+offset on signed integers without detecting wraparound, exactly the integer-overflow condition described by CWE-190. The added SEEK_CUR guard in the patch confirms the missing constraint; this is overflow of a computed offset, not an underflow of an unsigned length.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the offset addition is performed before any overflow check, so the guard tests the already-wrapped value. Trigger: a crafted TIFF profile causes TIFFSeekCustomStream to be called with a large positive offset that makes profile->offset+offset exceed SSIZE_MAX. The wrapped offset is returned and used for subsequent stream positioning, allowing out-of-bounds reads/writes and resulting in memory corruption or a crash.

Bug-Debian: https://github.com/tats/w3m/issues/7 [CVE-2016-9430]
Origin: https://anonscm.debian.org/cgit/collab-maint/w3m.git/commit/?id=59b91cd8e30c86f23476fa81ae005cabff49ebb6

description: An issue was discovered in the Tatsuya Kinoshita w3m fork before 0.5.3-31. w3m allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (segmentation fault and crash) via a crafted HTML page.

code_evidence: p defaults to "text" but is overwritten by the ATTR_TYPE value via parsedtag_get_value; the type string is attacker-controlled from the HTML input tag.
formtype(p) is called on that type string; if it returns FORM_UNKNOWN the function returns NULL, otherwise processing continues.

When no ATTR_VALUE is given, q may remain NULL for types not covered by the default switch (e.g. a nonstandard/malformed type that formtype maps to a known form but is not in this switch), so q stays NULL.
Only when q is non-NULL are qq and qlen set; qlen = get_strwidth(q) is skipped otherwise.
The Sprintf builds the input_alt markup using p (the type string) and qq; the original code interpolated the raw type without quoting.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect is a missing NULL guard on a pointer (q) that the code assumes is valid, leading to a segmentation fault on crafted input, matching CWE-476. The fix additionally quotes the type string, but the crash is a NULL-dereference rather than improper output encoding (CWE-79).
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The type attribute is attacker-controlled and passed as p into formtype and later into markup generation. If a crafted type value yields a form type not handled by the default-value switch, q remains NULL while downstream code paths (notably textfieldrep/get_strwidth usage and the unquoted type interpolation) process it without a NULL check, causing a NULL pointer dereference and crash.

description: Google V8 before 5.2.361.32, as used in Google Chrome before 52.0.2743.82, does not properly process left-trimmed objects, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory corruption) or possibly have unspecified other impact via crafted JavaScript code.

code_evidence: The only handle-uniqueness guard, SLOW_DCHECK(CountHandlesForObject(object) <= 1), is a debug-only check and does not enforce the constraint in release builds.

new_start is computed as object->address() + bytes_to_trim, and CreateFillerObjectAt overwrites the trimmed prefix; bytes_to_trim derives from caller-supplied elements_to_trim without a runtime bound check beyond a DCHECK.
CanMoveObjectStart(object) is also only a DCHECK, so movement is not prevented at runtime.

former_start[new_start_index] and the following index write the map and length into the shifted backing store using computed offsets, so any stale handle to the old address now points outside the new object's bounds.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The stale handle causes operations on memory outside the relocated buffer's intended boundary, matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds memory operation; it is not merely a logic error because the supported consequence is memory corruption via out-of-bounds access.

evidence_lines.code: SLOW_DCHECK(CountHandlesForObject(object) <= 1);
DCHECK(CanMoveObjectStart(object));

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Left-trimming relocates the object start while stale handles still reference the original address; because the uniqueness and movability constraints are debug-only checks, release builds can leave handles pointing at the trimmed prefix, leading to out-of-bounds reads/writes and heap memory corruption.

commit_msg:
ksmbd: check nt_len to be at least CIFS_ENCPWD_SIZE in ksmbd_decode_ntlmssp_auth_blob

"nt_len - CIFS_ENCPWD_SIZE" is passed directly from
ksmbd_decode_ntlmssp_auth_blob to ksmbd_auth_ntlmv2. Malicious requests
can set nt_len to less than CIFS_ENCPWD_SIZE, which results in a negative
number (or large unsigned value) used for a subsequent memcpy in
ksmbd_auth_ntlvm2 and can cause a panic.

Fixes: e2f3448 ("cifsd: add server-side procedures for SMB3")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: William Liu <will@willsroot.io>
Signed-off-by: Hrvoje Mišetić <misetichrvoje@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Namjae Jeon <linkinjeon@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (blob_len < (u64)dn_off + dn_len || blob_len < (u64)nt_off + nt_len)'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (blob_len < (u64)dn_off + dn_len || blob_len < (u64)nt_off + nt_len ||', '\t    nt_len < CIFS_ENCPWD_SIZE)']}
description: A bug affects the Linux kernel’s ksmbd NTLMv2 authentication and is known to crash the OS immediately in Linux-based systems.

code_evidence: Lines 23-24 read attacker-controlled nt_off and nt_len from the NTLMSSP authenticate blob. Lines 27-28 validate only that nt_off + nt_len fits within blob_len; they do not require nt_len to be at least CIFS_ENCPWD_SIZE.

Lines 52-55 pass nt_len - CIFS_ENCPWD_SIZE to ksmbd_auth_ntlmv2 together with a pointer into the blob at nt_off. When nt_len < CIFS_ENCPWD_SIZE the subtraction underflows to a large unsigned value, which the downstream memcpy uses as a length.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing minimum-length constraint permits an underflowed length that drives an out-of-bounds write in the downstream copy, matching CWE-787. It is not merely an integer issue: the underflow directly enables the memory write past the buffer boundary.

evidence_lines.code:
ret = ksmbd_auth_ntlmv2(conn, sess,
(struct ntlmv2_resp *)((char *)authblob + nt_off),
nt_len - CIFS_ENCPWD_SIZE,
domain_name, conn->ntlmssp.cryptkey);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function validates the response offset/length against the blob size but omits a lower-bound check on nt_len. commit_msg:
passthrough: quarantine PCI devices

When a PCI device is assigned to an untrusted domain, it is possible for
that domain to program the device to DMA to an arbitrary address. The
IOMMU is used to protect the host from malicious DMA by making sure that
the device addresses can only target memory assigned to the guest. However,
when the guest domain is torn down the device is assigned back to dom0,
thus allowing any in-flight DMA to potentially target critical host data.

This patch introduces a 'quarantine' for PCI devices using dom_io. When
the toolstack makes a device assignable (by binding it to pciback), it
will now also assign it to DOMID_IO and the device will only be assigned
back to dom0 when the device is made unassignable again. Whilst device is
assignable it will only ever transfer between dom_io and guest domains.
dom_io is actually only used as a sentinel domain for quarantining purposes;
it is not configured with any IOMMU mappings. Assignment to dom_io simply
means that the device's initiator (requestor) identifier is not present in
the IOMMU's device table and thus any DMA transactions issued will be
terminated with a fault condition.

In addition, a fix to assignment handling is made for VT-d.  Failure
during the assignment step should not lead to a device still being
associated with its prior owner. Hand the device to DomIO temporarily,
until the assignment step has completed successfully.  Remove the PI
hooks from the source domain then earlier as well.

Failure of the recovery reassign_device_ownership() may not go silent:
There e.g. may still be left over RMRR mappings in the domain assignment
to which has failed, and hence we can't allow that domain to continue
executing.

NOTE: This patch also includes one printk() cleanup; the
      "XEN_DOMCTL_assign_device: " tag is dropped in iommu_do_pci_domctl(),
      since similar printk()-s elsewhere also don't log such a tag.

This is XSA-302.

Signed-off-by: Paul Durrant <paul.durrant@citrix.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Signed-off-by: Ian Jackson <ian.jackson@eu.citrix.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '    /* dom_io is used as a sentinel for quarantined devices */', '    if ( domain == dom_io )', '        return;']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.12.x allowing attackers to gain host OS privileges via DMA in a situation where an untrusted domain has access to a physical device. This occurs because passed through PCI devices may corrupt host memory after deassignment. When a PCI device is assigned to an untrusted domain, it is possible for that domain to program the device to DMA to an arbitrary address. The IOMMU is used to protect the host from malicious DMA by making sure that the device addresses can only target memory assigned to the guest. However, when the guest domain is torn down, or the device is deassigned, the device is assigned back to dom0, thus allowing any in-flight DMA to potentially target critical host data. An untrusted domain with access to a physical device can DMA into host memory, leading to privilege escalation. Only systems where guests are given direct access to physical devices capable of DMA (PCI pass-through) are vulnerable. Systems which do not use PCI pass-through are not vulnerable.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function manipulates AMD IOMMU device-table entries and ATS state; it contains no OS command construction or execution, so it cannot support CWE-78.

commit_msg:
The following sequence can be used to trigger a UAF:

    int fscontext_fd = fsopen("cgroup");
    int fd_null = open("/dev/null, O_RDONLY);
    int fsconfig(fscontext_fd, FSCONFIG_SET_FD, "source", fd_null);
    close_range(3, ~0U, 0);

The cgroup v1 specific fs parser expects a string for the "source"
parameter.  However, it is perfectly legitimate to e.g.  specify a file
descriptor for the "source" parameter.  The fs parser doesn't know what
a filesystem allows there.  So it's a bug to assume that "source" is
always of type fs_value_is_string when it can reasonably also be
fs_value_is_file.

This assumption in the cgroup code causes a UAF because struct
fs_parameter uses a union for the actual value.  Access to that union is
guarded by the param->type member.  Since the cgroup paramter parser
didn't check param->type but unconditionally moved param->string into
fc->source a close on the fscontext_fd would trigger a UAF during
put_fs_context() which frees fc->source thereby freeing the file stashed
in param->file causing a UAF during a close of the fd_null.

Fix this by verifying that param->type is actually a string and report
an error if not.

In follow up patches I'll add a new generic helper that can be used here
and by other filesystems instead of this error-prone copy-pasta fix.
But fixing it in here first makes backporting a it to stable a lot
easier.

Fixes: 8d2451f4994f ("cgroup1: switch to option-by-option parsing")
Reported-by: syzbot+283ce5a46486d6acdbaf@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Cc: Christoph Hellwig <hch@lst.de>
Cc: Alexander Viro <viro@zeniv.linux.org.uk>
Cc: Dmitry Vyukov <dvyukov@google.com>
Cc: <stable@kernel.org>
Cc: syzkaller-bugs <syzkaller-bugs@googlegroups.com>
Signed-off-by: Christian Brauner <christian.brauner@ubuntu.com>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\tif (param->type != fs_value_is_string)', '\t\t\t\treturn invalf(fc, "Non-string source");']}
description: A use-after-free flaw was found in cgroup1_parse_param in kernel/cgroup/cgroup-v1.c in the Linux kernel's cgroup v1 parser. A local attacker with a user privilege could cause a privilege escalation by exploiting the fsconfig syscall parameter leading to a container breakout and a denial of service on the system.

code_evidence: For the "source" key, the code unconditionally treats param->string as the active union member: it checks only fc->source, assigns fc->source = param->string, then NULLs param->string. It never checks param->type, so when the parameter is fs_value_is_file the union actually holds a file pointer, and that pointer is stored into fc->source and later freed by put_fs_context().
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function stores a union member of the wrong active type into fc->source and that pointer is subsequently freed and reused, matching CWE-416 (reuse of memory after free). The added type check confirms the defect is the unchecked union access, not merely a type-confusion error.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: missing type discrimination before reading the fs_parameter union. Trigger: fsconfig(fscontext_fd, FSCONFIG_SET_FD, "source", fd) supplies a file-typed parameter that is copied into fc->source; closing the fscontext frees it while the underlying file remains referenced by fd, causing a use-after-free on later close of that fd. Consequence: memory corruption potentially enabling privilege escalation or denial of service.

commit_msg:
The check_interval file in

  /sys/devices/system/machinecheck/machinecheck<cpu number>

directory is a global timer value for MCE polling. If it is changed by one
CPU, mce_restart() broadcasts the event to other CPUs to delete and restart
the MCE polling timer and __mcheck_cpu_init_timer() reinitializes the
mce_timer variable.

If more than one CPU writes a specific value to the check_interval file
concurrently, mce_timer is not protected from such concurrent accesses and
all kinds of explosions happen. Since only root can write to those sysfs
variables, the issue is not a big deal security-wise.

However, concurrent writes to these configuration variables is void of
reason so the proper thing to do is to serialize the access with a mutex.

Boris:

 - Make store_int_with_restart() use device_store_ulong() to filter out
   negative intervals
 - Limit min interval to 1 second
 - Correct locking
 - Massage commit message

NOTE: a third party has indicated that this report is not security relevant

code_evidence: set_cmci_disabled reads and writes the shared global mca_cfg.cmci_disabled and broadcasts on_each_cpu() to all CPUs without any lock protecting the check-then-act sequence. The conditional at line 8 tests cmci_disabled and the body mutates it, so concurrent sysfs writers can interleave between the test and the update.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-362 fits because concurrent code sequences access a shared resource without exclusive, atomic access, violating both exclusivity and atomicity. The patch's added mutex_lock/mutex_unlock confirms the missing synchronization; this is a race condition, not merely a missing input-validation issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is the unsynchronized check-then-act on the shared mca_cfg.cmci_disabled state, combined with per-CPU mce_disable_cmci/mce_enable_ce broadcasts. Trigger: two or more concurrent writes to the check_interval sysfs file. Consequence: interleaved enable/disable broadcasts and inconsistent state, causing instability or panic (DoS).

commit_msg:
Fix SRI bypass by loading same resource twice in same origin.

This fixes a bug where the memory cache was bypassing subresource
integrity checks when a resource is loaded for a second time in the same
origin. The resource in the memory cache was correctly storing that an
integrity check had already been done so whene it was retrieved later,
it wouldn't need to be checked again, but it didn't store the fact that
this was a *failure*, so when the load happened a second time, it
assumed it was a good integrity.

This modifies the resources to store a disposition for the integrity
check, rather than just that the integrity check occurred. On a reload
of the resource, if the integrity had failed the first time, the
resource will fail to load.

commit_msg: tif_lzw.c: fix potential out-of-bounds error when trying to read in the same tile/strip after an error has occured (fixes #410)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tsp->read_error = 0;']}
description: LibTIFF master branch has an out-of-bounds read in LZWDecode in libtiff/tif_lzw.c:619, allowing attackers to cause a denial-of-service via a crafted tiff file. For users that compile libtiff from sources, the fix is available with commit b4e79bfa.

code_evidence: LZWPreDecode reads tif->tif_rawdata[0] and [1] when tif_rawcc >= 2, inspecting the compressed input header.
The decoder state is reset here: dec_restart, dec_bitsleft, old_tif_rawcc are cleared and dec_free_entp is set to dec_codetab - 1, a pointer one element before the table.
dec_oldcodep and dec_maxcodep are initialized to table boundaries; the added sp->read_error = 0 clears the prior error flag so a subsequent decode is permitted.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This matches CWE-125: the function clears the read_error flag and reinitializes decoder state, enabling a subsequent LZWDecode to read beyond the compressed input buffer when the same tile/strip is processed again after an error, producing an out-of-bounds read and DoS.

evidence_lines.code:
if (tif->tif_rawcc >= 2 &&
tif->tif_rawdata[0] == 0 && (tif->tif_rawdata[1] & 0x1)) {

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function resets decoder pointers and counters but resets read_error to 0, allowing a re-decode of the same tile/strip after a prior error. Because dec_free_entp is set to dec_codetab - 1 and state is reinitialized without validating that the prior decode did not leave the input position inconsistent, a crafted TIFF that triggers an error and then re-reads the tile/strip can cause LZWDecode to read past the end of the buffer. The added reset removes the guard that prevented this out-of-bounds read.

commit_msg:
Fix heap overflow with unmatched closing parens

This bug can trigger vulnerable code in find_fixedlength for forward reference
within backward assertion with excess closing parenthesis.

+++ func_after
@@ -483,7 +483,7 @@

 length, and set their lengths. */
 
-if (cd->check_lookbehind)
+if (errorcode == 0 && cd->check_lookbehind)
   {
   pcre_uchar *cc = (pcre_uchar *)codestart;
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['if (cd->check_lookbehind)'], 'added_lines': ['if (errorcode == 0 && cd->check_lookbehind)']}
description: An issue was discovered in Erlang/OTP 18.x. Erlang's generation of compiled regular expressions is vulnerable to a heap overflow. Regular expressions using a malformed extpattern can indirectly specify an offset that is used as an array index. This ordinal permits arbitrary regions within the erts_alloc arena to be both read and written to.

code_evidence: After compilation, when cd->check_lookbehind is set, the loop walks brackets via find_bracket and computes 'be = cc - 1 - LINK_SIZE + GET(cc, -LINK_SIZE)', then calls find_fixedlength and writes the result with PUT(cc, 1, fixed_length). This block runs unconditionally even if compile_regex already set errorcode (e.g., unmatched closing parens), so it operates on a malformed/partially built code buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe operation is a read/write beyond intended buffer boundaries driven by a malformed offset, matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds memory access. The fix gates the pass on errorcode==0, confirming the boundary violation stems from processing an invalid buffer; this is the memory-safety consequence rather than a separate logic flaw.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the lookbehind-fixup pass executes without checking that compilation succeeded, so a malformed extpattern with excess closing parens yields an inconsistent code buffer and an attacker-influenced offset. Trigger: compiling such a regex invokes find_fixedlength on corrupt bracket links. Consequence: out-of-bounds read/write within allocated memory (heap overflow), allowing memory modification or crash.

commit_msg:
avformat/rtmppkt: Check for packet size mismatches

Fixes out of array access

Found-by: Paul Cher <paulcher@icloud.com>
Reviewed-by: Paul Cher <paulcher@icloud.com>
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    if (prev_pkt[channel_id].read && size != prev_pkt[channel_id].size) {', '        av_log(NULL, AV_LOG_ERROR, "RTMP packet size mismatch %d != %d\\n",', '                size,', '                prev_pkt[channel_id].size);', '        ff_rtmp_packet_destroy(&prev_pkt[channel_id]);', '        prev_pkt[channel_id].read = 0;', '    }', '']}
description: Heap-based buffer overflow in libavformat/rtmppkt.c in FFmpeg before 2.8.10, 3.0.x before 3.0.5, 3.1.x before 3.1.6, and 3.2.x before 3.2.2 allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code by leveraging failure to check for RTMP packet size mismatches.

code_evidence: size is initialized from prev_pkt[channel_id].size (line 24) and overwritten from the wire via AV_RB24 (line 38); when the packet is not yet in progress, ff_rtmp_packet_create allocates a buffer for this size (lines 60-63) and stores it in prev_pkt[channel_id].size (line 84).

On continuation, p->size/p->offset/p->data are copied from prev (lines 68-78); size is recomputed as size - p->offset (line 86), toread = FFMIN(size, chunk_size) (line 87), and data is written at p->data + p->offset (line 88). The size stored at line 84 can differ from the buffer allocated earlier, so the offset arithmetic and write can exceed the allocation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The write at line 88 operates on p->data using offset/size derived from an unvalidated size, performing a memory-buffer operation outside the intended allocation boundary, which is CWE-119. The missing size-equality check is the specific root cause; the buffer overflow is the supported consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the continuation path trusts a newly parsed size (line 38) stored at line 84 without verifying it equals the size used to allocate p->data. Trigger: an RTMP chunk with a mismatched size on an in-progress channel. Consequence: p->data + p->offset at line 88 writes past the heap buffer, enabling out-of-bounds access and potential code execution.

commit_msg:
dm: Reset virtio device before release

With virtio polling mode enabled, a timer is running in the virtio
backend service. And the timer will also be triggered if its frondend
driver didn't do the device reset in shutdown. A freed virtio device
will be accessed in the polling timer handler.

Do the virtio reset() callback specifically to clear the polling timer
before the free.

Tracked-On: #6147
Signed-off-by: Shuo A Liu <shuo.a.liu@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Yonghua Huang <yonghua.huang@intel.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tvirtio_coreu_reset(vcoreu);']}
description: The polling timer handler in ACRN before 2.5 has a use-after-free for a freed virtio device, related to devicemodel/hw/pci/virtio/*.c.

code_evidence: The deinit function destroys the mutexes and condition variable, joins the rx thread, then frees vcoreu at line 11 without resetting the virtio device. The polling timer in the backend can still be running and reference vcoreu after free; the fix adds virtio_coreu_reset before free, which is absent here.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function frees vcoreu while a timer can still reference it, matching CWE-416's reuse of memory after free. The weakness is the missing reset/teardown ordering, not merely a resource leak.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: deinit frees vcoreu without first stopping the virtio polling timer that holds a reference to it. Trigger: with polling mode enabled, the timer fires after free and dereferences the freed device. Consequence: use-after-free, potentially memory corruption or crash.

commit_msg: imgcodecs: remove assert() usage
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    assert( bytes >= 0 );'], 'added_lines': ['    CV_Assert(bytes >= 0);']}
description: In OpenCV 3.3.1, an assertion failure happens in cv::RBaseStream::setPos in modules/imgcodecs/src/bitstrm.cpp because of an incorrect integer cast.

joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function contains a reachable assert() on an input-controlled value, so a crafted input can force the assertion to fail and terminate the application, matching CWE-617. This is a denial-of-service via abort rather than memory corruption (CWE-787), which the assertion itself does not establish here.

m_current += bytes;

In release builds the assertion is compiled out, and when the argument is negative the check either aborts the process (debug) or is bypassed, allowing m_current to be moved backwards. commit_msg:
Set optlen for UDP-encap check in XfrmController

When setting the socket owner for an encap socket XfrmController will
first attempt to verify that the socket has the UDP-encap socket option
set. When doing so it would pass in an uninitialized optlen parameter
which could cause the call to not modify the option value if the optlen
happened to be too short. So for example if the stack happened to
contain a zero where optlen was located the check would fail and the
socket owner would not be changed.

Fix this by setting optlen to the size of the option value parameter.

Test: run cts -m CtsNetTestCases
BUG: 111650288
Change-Id: I57b6e9dba09c1acda71e3ec2084652e961667bd9
(cherry picked from commit fc42a105147310bd680952d4b71fe32974bd8506)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    socklen_t optlen;'], 'added_lines': ['    socklen_t optlen = sizeof(optval);']}
description: In ipSecSetEncapSocketOwner of XfrmController.cpp, there is a possible failure to initialize a security feature due to uninitialized data. This could lead to local denial of service of IPsec on sockets with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation. Product: Android Versions: Android-9.0 Android ID: A-111650288

code_evidence: optval is declared but not initialized at line 15, and optlen is declared without initialization at line 16. Both are then passed by address to getsockopt at line 18, which writes optval only if the caller-supplied optlen is large enough; the uninitialized optlen value determines whether the option value is actually read.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-909 fits because a critical resource (the sockopt length/value pair driving a security check) is used without initialization, producing unpredictable behavior. This is not merely a logic error: the missing initialization is the direct cause of the check unpredictably rejecting a valid socket.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: optlen is an uninitialized socklen_t used as the in/out length for getsockopt. Trigger: when the stack contents make optlen too small, getsockopt does not populate optval, so the subsequent UDP_ENCAP check at line 22 evaluates against uninitialized optval and returns EINVAL, preventing fchown from setting the socket owner. Supported consequence: the IPsec encap socket-owner security operation fails (local denial of service of IPsec).

description: In JerryScript 2.3.0, there is an out-of-bounds read in main_print_unhandled_exception in the main-utils.c file.

commit_msg:
cryp: prevent direct calls to update and final functions

With inconsistent or malformed data it has been possible to call
"update" and "final" crypto functions directly. Using a fuzzer tool [1]
we have seen that this results in asserts, i.e., a crash that
potentially could leak sensitive information.

By setting the state (initialized) in the crypto context (i.e., the
tee_cryp_state) at the end of all syscall_*_init functions and then add
a check of the state at the beginning of all update and final functions,
  we prevent direct entrance to the "update" and "final" functions.

[1] https://github.com/MartijnB/optee_fuzzer

Fixes: OP-TEE-2019-0021

Signed-off-by: Joakim Bech <joakim.bech@linaro.org>
Reported-by: Martijn Bogaard <bogaard@riscure.com>
Acked-by: Jerome Forissier <jerome.forissier@linaro.org>

commit_msg:
Jan Kara's analysis of the syzbot report (edited):

  The reproducer opens a directory on FUSE filesystem, it then attaches
  dnotify mark to the open directory.  After that a fuse_do_getattr() call
  finds that attributes returned by the server are inconsistent, and calls
  make_bad_inode() which, among other things does:

          inode->i_mode = S_IFREG;

  This then confuses dnotify which doesn't tear down its structures
  properly and eventually crashes.

Avoid calling make_bad_inode() on a live inode: switch to a private flag on
the fuse inode.  Also add the test to ops which the bad_inode_ops would
have caught.

This bug goes back to the initial merge of fuse in 2.6.14...

Reported-by: syzbot+f427adf9324b92652ccc@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Signed-off-by: Miklos Szeredi <mszeredi@redhat.com>
Tested-by: Jan Kara <jack@suse.cz>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tif (is_bad_inode(inode)) {'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (fuse_is_bad(inode)) {']}
description: An issue was discovered in the FUSE filesystem implementation in the Linux kernel before 5.10.6, aka CID-5d069dbe8aaf. fuse_do_getattr() calls make_bad_inode() in inappropriate situations, causing a system crash. NOTE: the original fix for this vulnerability was incomplete, and its incompleteness is tracked as CVE-2021-28950.

code_evidence: When a lookup finds an existing dentry, the code obtains inode = d_inode(dentry) and checks is_bad_inode(inode) at line 47. If the inode was marked bad (e.g., by make_bad_inode() setting i_mode = S_IFREG), the path dput()s the dentry and returns -EIO without releasing or resetting the associated dnotify/inotify structures attached to the still-live inode.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-459 fits because the function's error path fails to clean up the supporting dnotify resources after the inode is marked bad, matching incomplete cleanup of temporary/supporting resources. It is not merely a bad-value check; the defect is the missing teardown on the abort path.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the bad-inode check aborts the lookup path via dput() but does not tear down supporting resources (dnotify marks) associated with the inode that make_bad_inode() left in place. Trigger: a FUSE server returns inconsistent attributes so fuse_do_getattr() calls make_bad_inode(), then a readdirplus lookup hits the is_bad_inode() branch. Consequence: dangling dnotify structures lead to a system crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
KEYS: Remove key_type::match in favour of overriding default by match_preparse

A previous patch added a ->match_preparse() method to the key type.  This is
allowed to override the function called by the iteration algorithm.
Therefore, we can just set a default that simply checks for an exact match of
the key description with the original criterion data and allow match_preparse
to override it as needed.

The key_type::match op is then redundant and can be removed, as can the
user_match() function.

Signed-off-by: David Howells <dhowells@redhat.com>
Acked-by: Vivek Goyal <vgoyal@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t.match_data.cmp\t\t= type->match,', '', '\tif (!ctx.match_data.cmp)', '\t\treturn ERR_PTR(-ENOKEY);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t.match_data.cmp\t\t= key_default_cmp,']}
description: The KEYS subsystem in the Linux kernel before 3.18 allows local users to gain privileges or cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference and system crash) via vectors involving a NULL value for a certain match field, related to the keyring_search_iterator function in keyring.c.

code_evidence: Line 9 initializes ctx.match_data.cmp from type->match, which may be NULL if a key type does not provide a match function.
Lines 16-17 guard against a NULL cmp by returning -ENOKEY before any search occurs, but this guard is the only protection against a NULL comparator.
Lines 18-23 call type->match_preparse to override match_data, then invoke keyring_search_aux; if match_preparse does not set a valid cmp, the search proceeds with a possibly NULL comparator.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits because the code permits a NULL function pointer in ctx.match_data.cmp to reach a call site instead of enforcing a non-NULL comparator. This is a direct NULL dereference of an expected-valid pointer, distinct from a mere missing error check on an ordinary value.

evidence_lines.code: .match_data.cmp= type->match,

if (!ctx.match_data.cmp)
return ERR_PTR(-ENOKEY);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the comparator field match_data.cmp can be NULL when a key type supplies no match function and match_preparse fails to install one. Trigger: a local user requests a keyring search for such a type. The iteration path may call the NULL comparator, causing a NULL pointer dereference and system crash (DoS) or, per the advisory, possible privilege gain.

commit_msg:
Fix #230: Memory corruption bug due to Integer Overflow in remap_struct()

(See problem description in issue #230.)
Check that the number of fields (long long integers, long integers or
integers) as read from a system activity binary datafile multiplied by
its alignment width doesn't overflow, i.e. the result must not be
smaller than the number of fields.

Reported-by: Ren Kimura
Signed-off-by: Sebastien GODARD <sysstat@users.noreply.github.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (ftypes_nr[0] * ULL_ALIGNMENT_WIDTH < ftypes_nr[0])', '\t\t\t/* Overflow */', '\t\t\treturn -1;', '', '', '\t\tif (ftypes_nr[1] * UL_ALIGNMENT_WIDTH < ftypes_nr[1])', '\t\t\t/* Overflow */', '\t\t\treturn -1;', '', '', '\t\tif (ftypes_nr[2] * U_ALIGNMENT_WIDTH < ftypes_nr[2])', '\t\t\t/* Overflow */', '\t\t\treturn -1;', '', '']}
description: sysstat before 12.1.6 has memory corruption due to an Integer Overflow in remap_struct() in sa_common.c.

code_evidence: The alignment-width products (ftypes_nr[0]*ULL_ALIGNMENT_WIDTH and gtypes_nr[0]*ULL_ALIGNMENT_WIDTH) are computed with unsigned int values into size_t; if ftypes_nr[0] is large the multiplication wraps. The wrapped values feed the size checks at lines 12-15 and the memmove offsets at lines 16-17, so the bounds validation can pass while the copy offset/length is inconsistent, producing an out-of-bounds memmove.

The second block subtracts multiple wrapped products from f_size/g_size at lines 25-28 and uses wrapped sums in the checks at lines 29-35 and memmove offsets at lines 36-39. A wrapped product can defeat the b_size guard and shift the destination/source pointer beyond the buffer.

The third block similarly computes ftypes_nr[2]*U_ALIGNMENT_WIDTH and gtypes_nr[2]*U_ALIGNMENT_WIDTH at lines 48-53, uses wrapped sums in the guards at lines 54-63, and passes wrapped offsets to memmove at lines 64-69. The overflow is the root cause; the resulting out-of-bounds copy is the consequence.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function's unsafe behavior is an integer multiplication that can overflow before being used as an offset/size in memory operations, matching CWE-190. The downstream out-of-bounds memmove is the impact of that overflow rather than a separate weakness label.

commit_msg:
Fix loop in blocking read on transport timeout

The loop was cased by an incorrect errno if the transport read in
mgs_transport_read() fails with an APR TIMEUP status, as happens when
mod_reqtimeout limits are exceeded. Setting the transport errno to
EGAIN meant that a blocking read would be retried endlessly, setting
ETIMEDOUT instead makes the read fail as it should.

The bug was introduced in commit 92cb0cca41af946055307e373b6ab6d76d34f356,
first release to include it was 0.9.0.

Many thanks to Félix Arreola Rodríguez for the detailed analysis [1]
on the Debian bug tracker!

[1] https://bugs.debian.org/cgi-bin/bugreport.cgi?bug=942737#25
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['            } else if (rc == GNUTLS_E_PULL_ERROR', '                       && APR_STATUS_IS_TIMEUP(ctxt->input_rc)) {', '                ap_log_cerror(', '                    APLOG_MARK, APLOG_TRACE2, ctxt->input_rc, ctxt->c,', '                    "%s: transport read timed out", __func__);']}
description: Mod_gnutls is a TLS module for Apache HTTPD based on GnuTLS. Versions from 0.9.0 to 0.12.0 (including) did not properly fail blocking read operations on TLS connections when the transport hit timeouts. Instead it entered an endless loop retrying the read operation, consuming CPU resources. This could be exploited for denial of service attacks. If trace level logging was enabled, it would also produce an excessive amount of log output during the loop, consuming disk space. The problem has been fixed in commit d7eec4e598158ab6a98bf505354e84352f9715ec, please update to version 0.12.1. There are no workarounds, users who cannot update should apply the errno fix detailed in the security advisory.

code_evidence: The function enters an unconditional while(1) loop and calls gnutls_record_recv on each iteration.
When gnutls_record_recv returns GNUTLS_E_INTERRUPTED or GNUTLS_E_AGAIN and input_block is not APR_NONBLOCK_READ, the code executes continue, restarting the loop without any terminating condition.

Other non-fatal errors fall into the else branch; when input_rc remains APR_SUCCESS, it is set to APR_EGENERAL and the loop breaks. The added timeout branch does not alter input_rc or break, so the loop continues after a transport timeout.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The while(1) loop's exit depends on input_rc becoming non-success or a break; the timeout path neither sets a failing input_rc nor breaks, so the exit condition is unreachable for that case, matching CWE-835. This is distinct from merely mishandling an error code, since the observable defect is the non-terminating iteration.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: a blocking read retries indefinitely because a transport timeout (GNUTLS_E_PULL_ERROR with APR_STATUS_IS_TIMEUP) is logged but never converted into a terminating error status or a break. Trigger: a client exceeding mod_reqtimeout limits causes the transport read to time out repeatedly. Consequence: the while(1) loop spins, consuming CPU and producing excessive trace log output (disk exhaustion), a denial of service.

commit_msg: Use the correct rights.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  rights=AllPolicyRights;'], 'added_lines': ['  rights=ReadPolicyRights|WritePolicyRights;']}
description: ImageMagick is free software delivered as a ready-to-run binary distribution or as source code that you may use, copy, modify, and distribute in both open and proprietary applications. In affected versions and in certain cases, Postscript files could be read and written when specifically excluded by a `module` policy in `policy.xml`. ex. <policy domain="module" rights="none" pattern="PS" />. The issue has been resolved in ImageMagick 7.1.0-7 and in 6.9.12-22. Fortunately, in the wild, few users utilize the `module` policy and instead use the `coder` policy that is also our workaround recommendation: <policy domain="coder" rights="none" pattern="{PS,EPI,EPS,EPSF,EPSI}" />.

code_evidence: RegisterStaticModule sets rights=AllPolicyRights at line 19, then passes those rights to IsRightsAuthorized for ModulePolicyDomain at line 20. A policy that grants only read or only write (e.g. rights="none" for a module) is evaluated against AllPolicyRights, so the authorization check does not reflect the actual operation being registered; on failure it sets errno=EPERM and throws NotAuthorized (lines 22-25).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function fails to enforce the module policy's intended access boundary, letting a restricted module be used, which matches CWE-668's exposure of a resource to the wrong control sphere. It is not merely a generic access-control flaw; the specific mistake is evaluating rights against an over-broad set, so the resource escapes its intended policy sphere.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the module authorization check uses the maximum rights set (AllPolicyRights) rather than the read/write rights the operation actually requires, so a module policy restricting rights is not enforced as intended. Trigger: a policy.xml module policy that denies or limits read/write for a module such as PS. Consequence: the module can still be registered and PostScript files read/written despite the policy exclusion, exposing that resource beyond the intended control sphere.
