commit_msg:
ASAN SFTP Fixes
When decoding SFTP messages, fix the size checks so they don't wrap. (ZD12766)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        if (localIdx + sz > maxIdx) {', '        if (localIdx + sz > maxIdx) {'], 'added_lines': ['        if (sz > maxIdx - localIdx) {', '        if (sz > maxIdx - localIdx) {']}
description: WolfSSH v1.4.7 was discovered to contain an integer overflow via the function wolfSSH_SFTP_RecvRMDIR.

code_evidence: sz is read from the network buffer via ato32 (lines 18/38) and is attacker-controlled. The bound check localIdx + sz > maxIdx (lines 22 and 42) adds two word32 values; if sz is near UINT32_MAX, localIdx + sz wraps to a small value and the check passes.
WMALLOC(sz + 1) then also wraps to a tiny allocation, and WMEMCPY(s, buf + localIdx, sz) copies sz bytes, overflowing the heap buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs an addition-based bounds check whose result can wrap, directly matching CWE-190; the fix rewrites it as sz > maxIdx - localIdx to avoid overflow. This is distinct from a simple off-by-one length error because the arithmetic itself wraps.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the size validation uses addition localIdx + sz without guarding against word32 wraparound. Trigger: a crafted SFTP status/language string length near UINT32_MAX. Consequence: the check is bypassed, allocation under-sizes, and the subsequent memcpy writes out of bounds, enabling heap corruption/crash.

commit_msg:
In commit ee13cb249fab ("powerpc/64s: Add support for software count
cache flush"), I added support for software to flush the count
cache (indirect branch cache) on context switch if firmware told us
that was the required mitigation for Spectre v2.

As part of that code we also added a software flush of the link
stack (return address stack), which protects against Spectre-RSB
between user processes.

That is all correct for CPUs that activate that mitigation, which is
currently Power9 Nimbus DD2.3.

What I got wrong is that on older CPUs, where firmware has disabled
the count cache, we also need to flush the link stack on context
switch.

To fix it we create a new feature bit which is not set by firmware,
which tells us we need to flush the link stack. We set that when
firmware tells us that either of the existing Spectre v2 mitigations
are enabled.

Then we adjust the patching code so that if we see that feature bit we
enable the link stack flush. If we're also told to flush the count
cache in software then we fall through and do that also.

On the older CPUs we don't need to do do the software count cache
flush, firmware has disabled it, so in that case we patch in an early
return after the link stack flush.

The naming of some of the functions is awkward after this patch,
because they're called "count cache" but they also do link stack. But
we'll fix that up in a later commit to ease backporting.

This is the fix for CVE-2019-18660.

Reported-by: Anthony Steinhauser <asteinhauser@google.com>
Fixes: ee13cb249fab ("powerpc/64s: Add support for software count cache flush")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # v4.4+
Signed-off-by: Michael Ellerman <mpe@ellerman.id.au>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (!enable || !security_ftr_enabled(SEC_FTR_FLUSH_COUNT_CACHE)) {', '\t\tcount_cache_flush_type = COUNT_CACHE_FLUSH_NONE;', '\t\tpr_info("count-cache-flush: software flush disabled.\\n");'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (!security_ftr_enabled(SEC_FTR_FLUSH_COUNT_CACHE) &&', '\t    !security_ftr_enabled(SEC_FTR_FLUSH_LINK_STACK))', '\t\tenable = false;', '', '\tif (!enable) {', '\t\tpr_info("link-stack-flush: software flush disabled.\\n");', '\t\tlink_stack_flush_enabled = false;', '\t\tno_count_cache_flush();', '\t// This enables the branch from _switch to flush_count_cache', '', '\tpr_info("link-stack-flush: software flush enabled.\\n");', '\tlink_stack_flush_enabled = true;', '', '\t// If we just need to flush the link stack, patch an early return', '\tif (!security_ftr_enabled(SEC_FTR_FLUSH_COUNT_CACHE)) {', '\t\tpatch_instruction_site(&patch__flush_link_stack_return, PPC_INST_BLR);', '\t\tno_count_cache_flush();', '\t\treturn;', '\t}']}
description: The Linux kernel before 5.4.1 on powerpc allows Information Exposure because the Spectre-RSB mitigation is not in place for all applicable CPUs, aka CID-39e72bf96f58. This is related to arch/powerpc/kernel/entry_64.S and arch/powerpc/kernel/security.c.

code_evidence: Line 3 gates the entire flush configuration on `enable` and `SEC_FTR_FLUSH_COUNT_CACHE`; when firmware disables the count cache but the link-stack mitigation is still required, the early branch at line 3-7 patches the call site to NOP and returns, leaving the link stack unflushed.

Lines 9-10 only patch the branch to `flush_count_cache` when the function does not return early; the link-stack flush is coupled to the count-cache feature bit rather than an independent link-stack requirement.

Lines 11-16 configure the count-cache flush sequence, but this block is only reached after the link-stack branch has been patched, so the missing independent link-stack enablement is the root of the exposure.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-200 fits because the missing link-stack flush permits speculative execution to leak sensitive data across process boundaries, directly violating confidentiality. The weakness is a mitigation-configuration error whose supported consequence is information exposure, not a memory-safety flaw.

evidence_lines.code: if (!enable || !security_ftr_enabled(SEC_FTR_FLUSH_COUNT_CACHE)) {

patch_branch_site(&patch__call_flush_count_cache,
(u64)&flush_count_cache, BRANCH_SET_LINK);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function ties enabling the link-stack (return-address stack) flush to `SEC_FTR_FLUSH_COUNT_CACHE`, so on CPUs where firmware disables the count cache but Spectre-RSB mitigation is still required, the function patches the flush call to NOP and returns. Trigger: a context switch on such a CPU leaves the link stack unflushed. Consequence: cross-process return-address prediction allows speculative information exposure between user processes.

code_evidence: At line 226 the MPLS-extension branch is entered when plen > ICMP_EXTD_MINLEN, and line 227 only checks the fixed ext_dp header. commit_msg:
netfilter: x_tables: fix unconditional helper

Ben Hawkes says:

 In the mark_source_chains function (net/ipv4/netfilter/ip_tables.c) it
 is possible for a user-supplied ipt_entry structure to have a large
 next_offset field. This field is not bounds checked prior to writing a
 counter value at the supplied offset.

Problem is that mark_source_chains should not have been called --
the rule doesn't have a next entry, so its supposed to return
an absolute verdict of either ACCEPT or DROP.

However, the function conditional() doesn't work as the name implies.
It only checks that the rule is using wildcard address matching.

However, an unconditional rule must also not be using any matches
(no -m args).

The underflow validator only checked the addresses, therefore
passing the 'unconditional absolute verdict' test, while
mark_source_chains also tested for presence of matches, and thus
proceeeded to the next (not-existent) rule.

Unify this so that all the callers have same idea of 'unconditional rule'.

Reported-by: Ben Hawkes <hawkes@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Florian Westphal <fw@strlen.de>
Signed-off-by: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t\tpr_err("Underflows must be unconditional and "', '\t\t\t\t       "use the STANDARD target with "', '\t\t\t\t       "ACCEPT/DROP\\n");'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t\tpr_debug("Underflows must be unconditional and "', '\t\t\t\t\t "use the STANDARD target with "', '\t\t\t\t\t "ACCEPT/DROP\\n");']}
description: The netfilter subsystem in the Linux kernel through 4.5.2 does not validate certain offset fields, which allows local users to gain privileges or cause a denial of service (heap memory corruption) via an IPT_SO_SET_REPLACE setsockopt call.

code_evidence: Lines 11-13 bound e->next_offset against limit but only relative to the current entry pointer; the underflow path below relies on the unconditional-rule decision to avoid walking to a non-existent next entry.

Lines 31-38 accept an underflow entry when check_underflow(e) passes; if that check wrongly classifies a rule with matches as unconditional, the caller proceeds past the last entry and later writes counters at the attacker-controlled next_offset, outside the buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is an out-of-bounds memory write driven by an unvalidated offset, matching CWE-119's improper restriction of operations within a buffer boundary. The absent constraint on next_offset relative to the table bounds, not merely a logic error, is what enables the out-of-bounds access.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the validator's notion of an unconditional rule diverges from the caller's, so a rule with matches but a large next_offset passes validation. Trigger: a crafted IPT_SO_SET_REPLACE table whose underflow entry has matches and a large next_offset. Consequence: mark_source_chains follows the out-of-range next_offset and writes counter data outside the allocated table, giving heap memory corruption.

commit_msg:
settings: Add support for defaults to keyfile backend

Stacked databases and locks are dconf features that allow
management software like Fleet Commander to set system-wide
defaults and overrides centrally for applications.

This patch adds minimal support for the same to the keyfile
backend. We look for a keyfile named 'defaults' and a
lock-list named 'locks'.

Suitable files can be produced from a dconf database with
dconf dump and dconf list-locks, respectively.

The default location for these files is /etc/glib-2.0/settings/.
For test purposes, this can be overwritten with the
GSETTINGS_DEFAULTS_DIR environment variable.

Writes always go to the per-user keyfile.

description: The keyfile settings backend in GNOME GLib (aka glib2.0) before 2.60.0 creates directories using g_file_make_directory_with_parents (kfsb->dir, NULL, NULL) and files using g_file_replace_contents (kfsb->file, contents, length, NULL, FALSE, G_FILE_CREATE_REPLACE_DESTINATION, NULL, NULL, NULL). commit_msg:
vmx does not restore GDT.LIMIT to the host value, instead it sets it to 64KB.
This means host userspace can learn a few bits of host memory.

Fix by reloading GDTR when we load other host state.

Signed-off-by: Avi Kivity <avi@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Marcelo Tosatti <mtosatti@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tstore_gdt(&__get_cpu_var(host_gdt));', '']}
description: A flaw was found in Linux kernel's KVM virtualization subsystem. The VMX code does not restore the GDT.LIMIT to the previous host value, but instead sets it to 64KB. With a corrupted GDT limit a host's userspace code has an ability to place malicious entries in the GDT, particularly to the per-cpu variables. An attacker can use this to escalate their privileges.

code_evidence: hardware_enable enables VMX by setting X86_CR4_VMXE and, when vmm_exclusive is set, executes kvm_cpu_vmxon() and ept_sync_global() before returning success at line 22. No store_gdt() call exists in this function to capture the host GDTR before VMX operation begins.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-665 fits because the function fails to initialize/preserve a required resource, the host GDTR, during VMX setup, leaving it in an unexpected state on later access. This is improper initialization of host state rather than a bounds-check omission alone.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the VMX-enable path initializes VMX state (CR4.VMXE and, under vmm_exclusive, VMXON/EPT) without saving the host GDT descriptor. When VMX later loads host state, GDT.LIMIT is set to 64KB rather than the original host value, leaving the host in an incorrectly initialized descriptor-table state. The trigger is enabling VMX and subsequently running host userspace, which can then observe or manipulate GDT entries beyond the real limit, supporting information disclosure and privilege escalation.

code_evidence: A private wmem allocator strpool is created at function entry via wmem_allocator_new(WMEM_ALLOCATOR_SIMPLE).

description: h2o is an open source http server. In code prior to the `8c0eca3` commit h2o may attempt to access uninitialized memory. When receiving QUIC frames in certain order, HTTP/3 server-side implementation of h2o can be misguided to treat uninitialized memory as HTTP/3 frames that have been received. When h2o is used as a reverse proxy, an attacker can abuse this vulnerability to send internal state of h2o to backend servers controlled by the attacker or third party. Also, if there is an HTTP endpoint that reflects the traffic sent from the client, an attacker can use that reflector to obtain internal state of h2o. This internal state includes traffic of other connections in unencrypted form and TLS session tickets. This vulnerability exists in h2o server with HTTP/3 support, between commit 93af138 and d1f0f65. None of the released versions of h2o are affected by this vulnerability. There are no known workarounds. Users of unreleased versions of h2o using HTTP/3 are advised to upgrade immediately.

code_evidence: bytes_avail is derived solely from src_end - *src and clamped to bytes_left_in_data_frame; the function never checks that the frame parser has actually received/initialized the data before the payload is consumed.

The clamped bytes_avail is appended from *src into stream->req_body and the request entity/body size is advanced by that count, so uninitialized payload bytes are incorporated into the request body if the caller's buffer region has not been filled.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is direct use of a resource (the source buffer region) that has not been initialized, matching CWE-908. It is not merely an out-of-bounds read because the length is bounded by the frame counter; the defect is the missing initialization guarantee before the buffer is consumed.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the payload handler trusts the caller-supplied source range and frame byte counter without confirming the data frame's payload was initialized. Trigger: receiving QUIC/HTTP-3 frames in an order that leaves the input region uninitialized while bytes_left_in_data_frame is nonzero. Consequence: uninitialized memory is appended to req_body and later forwarded to backend or reflected, leaking internal state.

commit_msg:
win: fix unsavory rwlock fallback implementation

Before this patch an uv_mutex_t (backed by a critical section) could be
released by a tread different from the thread that acquired it, which is
not allowed. This is fixed by using a semaphore instead.

Note that the affected code paths were used on Windows XP and Windows
Server 2003 only.

This is a back-port of commits 3eb6764, 1ad6ad7, 9a4fd26, 9823922
85adf43 and bd1777f from the v1.x branch.

Fixes: https://github.com/libuv/libuv/issues/515
Refs: https://github.com/libuv/libuv/pull/525
PR-URL: https://github.com/libuv/libuv/pull/903
Reviewed-By: Ben Noordhuis <info@bnoordhuis.nl>
Reviewed-By: Bert Belder <bertbelder@gmail.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  if (r && r != EBUSY && r != EAGAIN)', '    abort();', '', '  if (r)', '  else', '    return 0;'], 'added_lines': ['  if (r) {', '    if (r != EBUSY && r != EAGAIN)', '      abort();', '  }', '  return 0;']}
description: The uv_rwlock_t fallback implementation for Windows XP and Server 2003 in libuv before 1.7.4 does not properly prevent threads from releasing the locks of other threads, which allows attackers to cause a denial of service (deadlock) or possibly have unspecified other impact by leveraging a race condition.

code_evidence: The function calls pthread_mutex_trylock on the caller-supplied mutex and inspects the return code r. Lines 4-5 abort on unexpected errors, while lines 6-9 map any nonzero result (including EBUSY/EAGAIN) to -1 and success to 0; the function performs no ownership check and does not record which thread acquired the lock.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-362 fits because the shared mutex is accessed by concurrent code sequences without a constraint guaranteeing exclusive, owner-only release, creating an interfering-access window. This is improper synchronization rather than a simple error-handling bug: the return-code branching is correct, but the lock's exclusivity property is violated.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the trylock wrapper exposes a lock whose ownership is not enforced, so a thread other than the acquirer can release it. Trigger: concurrent threads race on the shared mutex, allowing a non-owner thread to free a lock still held by another; the supported consequence is a deadlock or lock-state corruption leading to denial of service.

commit_msg:
xen: let alloc_xenballooned_pages() fail if not enough memory free

commit a1078e821b605813b63bf6bca414a85f804d5c66 upstream.

Instead of trying to allocate pages with GFP_USER in
add_ballooned_pages() check the available free memory via
si_mem_available(). GFP_USER is far less limiting memory exhaustion
than the test via si_mem_available().

This will avoid dom0 running out of memory due to excessive foreign
page mappings especially on ARM and on x86 in PVH mode, as those don't
have a pre-ballooned area which can be used for foreign mappings.

As the normal ballooning suffers from the same problem don't balloon
down more than si_mem_available() pages in one iteration. At the same
time limit the default maximum number of retries.

This is part of XSA-300.

Signed-off-by: Juergen Gross <jgross@suse.com>
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tballoon_stats.max_retry_count = RETRY_UNLIMITED;'], 'added_lines': ['\tballoon_stats.max_retry_count = 4;']}
description: An issue was discovered in drivers/xen/balloon.c in the Linux kernel before 5.2.3, as used in Xen through 4.12.x, allowing guest OS users to cause a denial of service because of unrestricted resource consumption during the mapping of guest memory, aka CID-6ef36ab967c7.

code_evidence: balloon_init sets balloon_stats.retry_count to 1 but assigns balloon_stats.max_retry_count = RETRY_UNLIMITED, so the balloon driver's retry loop has no cap on the number of retry iterations it may perform.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-770 fits because the initialization explicitly removes a limit on how many times a reusable resource operation (retries/allocations) may occur, enabling unbounded resource consumption. This is a missing-throttle issue rather than a memory-safety flaw.

evidence_lines.code:
balloon_stats.retry_count = 1;
balloon_stats.max_retry_count = RETRY_UNLIMITED;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the maximum retry count for the balloon driver is initialized to RETRY_UNLIMITED, removing any bound on repeated allocation/ballooning attempts. Trigger: a guest causes ballooning to retry repeatedly while memory is scarce. Consequence: unbounded resource consumption leading to a denial of service, as reflected by the upstream change to a finite limit of 4.

commit_msg:
make_mmu_pages_available() must be called with mmu_lock held for write.
However, if the TDP MMU is used, it will be called with mmu_lock held for
read.
This function does nothing unless shadow pages are used, so there is no
race unless nested TDP is used.
Since nested TDP uses shadow pages, old shadow pages may be zapped by this
function even when the TDP MMU is enabled.
Since shadow pages are never allocated by kvm_tdp_mmu_map(), a race
condition can be avoided by not calling make_mmu_pages_available() if the
TDP MMU is currently in use.

I encountered this when repeatedly starting and stopping nested VM.
It can be artificially caused by allocating a large number of nested TDP
SPTEs.

For example, the following BUG and general protection fault are caused in
the host kernel.

Fixes: a2855afc7ee8 ("KVM: x86/mmu: Allow parallel page faults for the TDP MMU")
Signed-off-by: Kazuki Takiguchi <takiguchi.kazuki171@gmail.com>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tlockdep_assert_held_write(&kvm->mmu_lock);']}
description: A race condition in the x86 KVM subsystem in the Linux kernel through 6.1-rc6 allows guest OS users to cause a denial of service (host OS crash or host OS memory corruption) when nested virtualisation and the TDP MMU are enabled.

code_evidence: __kvm_mmu_prepare_zap_page mutates shared KVM MMU state without any synchronization: it unlinks children and parents (lines 9-11), unaccounts shadow pages (line 14), moves or deletes sp->link on the invalid_list (lines 20-25), and flips sp->role.invalid (line 30). The added lockdep assertion in the patch confirms the caller must hold mmu_lock for write, but the function itself performs no locking, so the correctness depends entirely on callers.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function modifies shared MMU lists and page state with no enforced exclusive locking, and the fix adds a lockdep write-hold assertion, matching CWE-362's concurrent sequence lacking exclusivity. This is a synchronization race, not merely a memory-safety flaw: the corruption follows from the missing write lock, so CWE-362 fits the root cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the zap path assumes exclusive write access to mmu_lock, but when the TDP MMU is active mmu_lock is held only for read, so concurrent readers can execute this shared-resource mutation. Trigger: nested virtualization with TDP MMU allocates many nested SPTEs and repeatedly starts/stops a nested VM, causing a parallel page fault to zap shadow pages. Consequence: list corruption in pte_list_remove and kvm_mmu_commit_zap_page, producing a host kernel BUG/general protection fault (DoS) and possible host memory corruption.

commit_msg:
CVE-2016-0798: avoid memory leak in SRP

The SRP user database lookup method SRP_VBASE_get_by_user had confusing
memory management semantics; the returned pointer was sometimes newly
allocated, and sometimes owned by the callee. The calling code has no
way of distinguishing these two cases.

Specifically, SRP servers that configure a secret seed to hide valid
login information are vulnerable to a memory leak: an attacker
connecting with an invalid username can cause a memory leak of around
300 bytes per connection.

Servers that do not configure SRP, or configure SRP but do not configure
a seed are not vulnerable.

In Apache, the seed directive is known as SSLSRPUnknownUserSeed.

To mitigate the memory leak, the seed handling in SRP_VBASE_get_by_user
is now disabled even if the user has configured a seed.

Applications are advised to migrate to SRP_VBASE_get1_by_user. However,
note that OpenSSL makes no strong guarantees about the
indistinguishability of valid and invalid logins. In particular,
computations are currently not carried out in constant time.

Reviewed-by: Rich Salz <rsalz@openssl.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['                        SRP_VBASE_get_by_user(srp_callback_parm.vb,', '                                              srp_callback_parm.login);', '                        SRP_VBASE_get_by_user(srp_callback_parm.vb,', '                                              srp_callback_parm.login);'], 'added_lines': ['                    SRP_user_pwd_free(srp_callback_parm.user);', '                        SRP_VBASE_get1_by_user(srp_callback_parm.vb,', '                                               srp_callback_parm.login);', '                    SRP_user_pwd_free(srp_callback_parm.user);', '                        SRP_VBASE_get1_by_user(srp_callback_parm.vb,', '                                               srp_callback_parm.login);']}
description: Memory leak in the SRP_VBASE_get_by_user implementation in OpenSSL 1.0.1 before 1.0.1s and 1.0.2 before 1.0.2g allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory consumption) by providing an invalid username in a connection attempt, related to apps/s_server.c and crypto/srp/srp_vfy.c.

code_evidence: In the SSL_ERROR_WANT_X509_LOOKUP retry loop, line 255 overwrites srp_callback_parm.user with the result of SRP_VBASE_get_by_user without freeing the previous value; the returned pointer may be newly allocated (seed-based unknown-user path), so each iteration of the loop leaks the prior allocation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-399 covers improper resource management; the leak of heap allocations on each lookup retry is a resource-management error that exhausts memory. It is distinct from CWE-476 (null deref) or CWE-416 (use-after-free), since the defect is failure to release allocated memory.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the lookup returns a pointer with ambiguous ownership, sometimes newly allocated, and the caller stores it into a long-lived field without releasing the prior value. Trigger: an attacker repeatedly causing the X509 lookup retry loop (e.g., invalid username with a configured seed) re-enters line 255, overwriting and leaking the previous allocation. Consequence: unbounded memory consumption leading to denial of service.

commit_msg:
Use spinlocks to deal with workers introducing a wrapper
bigben_schedule_work(), and several spinlock checks.
Otherwise, bigben_set_led() may schedule bigben->worker after the
structure has been freed, causing a use-after-free.

Fixes: 4eb1b01de5b9 ("HID: hid-bigbenff: fix race condition for scheduled work during removal")
Signed-off-by: Pietro Borrello <borrello@diag.uniroma1.it>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20230125-hid-unregister-leds-v4-3-7860c5763c38@diag.uniroma1.it
Signed-off-by: Benjamin Tissoires <benjamin.tissoires@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['', '\tif (bigben->removed)', '\t\treturn;'], 'added_lines': []}
description: The Linux kernel through 6.1.9 has a Use-After-Free in bigben_remove in drivers/hid/hid-bigbenff.c via a crafted USB device because the LED controllers remain registered for too long.

code_evidence: bigben_worker derives its bigben pointer from the work struct via container_of and immediately dereferences bigben->report->field[0].
The only guard against operating on a torn-down device is the removed flag check; when set it returns early.
Under the spinlock the worker reads work_led and writes report_field->value[] then calls hid_output_report on bigben->report.
A second locked block does the same for work_ff, again dereferencing bigben->report and report_field.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the function performs reads and writes through bigben and report_field pointers that may already refer to freed memory after device removal. It is not merely a race or null-dereference: the worker operates on memory whose owner has been deallocated.

evidence_lines.code:
if (bigben->removed)
return;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the worker dereferences bigben and its report/field state without a lifetime guarantee tying the scheduled work to the device. Trigger: bigben_set_led() can schedule this worker after bigben_remove has freed the bigben structure; the removed flag alone does not prevent the work from running against freed memory. Supported consequence: use-after-free writes to report_field->value[] and reads of bigben->report, yielding memory corruption or crash.

commit_msg:
Limit client cut text length to 1 MB

This patch constrains a client cut text length to 1 MB. Otherwise
a client could make server allocate 2 GB of memory and that seems to
be to much to classify it as a denial of service.

The limit also prevents from an integer overflow followed by copying
an uninitilized memory when processing msg.cct.length value larger
than SIZE_MAX or INT_MAX - sz_rfbClientCutTextMsg.

This patch also corrects accepting length value of zero (malloc(0) is
interpreted on differnet systems differently).

CVE-2018-7225
<https://github.com/LibVNC/libvncserver/issues/218>

description: An issue was discovered in LibVNCServer through 0.9.11. rfbProcessClientNormalMessage() in rfbserver.c does not sanitize msg.cct.length, leading to access to uninitialized and potentially sensitive data or possibly unspecified other impact (e.g., an integer overflow) via specially crafted VNC packets.

code_evidence: Line 480 swaps msg.cct.length into a uint32_t derived from the client-supplied rfbClientCutTextMsg. Line 481 passes it directly to malloc()'s size_t argument with no upper bound; line 487 passes the same value to rfbReadExact()'s int length; line 494 adds sz_rfbClientCutTextMsg to it for rfbStatRecordMessageRcvd(); line 496 forwards it to setXCutText()'s int argument. No validation constrains the length before these conversions.

commit_msg:
Fix double-free in KDC TGS processing

When issuing a ticket for a TGS renew or validate request, copy only
the server field from the outer part of the header ticket to the new
ticket.  Copying the whole structure causes the enc_part pointer to be
aliased to the header ticket until krb5_encrypt_tkt_part() is called,
resulting in a double-free if handle_authdata() fails.

[ghudson@mit.edu: changed the fix to avoid aliasing enc_part rather
than check for aliasing before freeing; rewrote commit message]

CVE-2023-39975:

In MIT krb5 release 1.21, an authenticated attacker can cause a KDC to
free the same pointer twice if it can induce a failure in
authorization data handling.

ticket: 9101 (new)
tags: pullup
target_version: 1.21-next
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        /* Copy the whole header ticket except for authorization data. */', '        ticket_reply = *t->header_tkt;'], 'added_lines': ['        /* Copy the header ticket server and all enc-part fields except for', '         * authorization data. */', '        ticket_reply.server = t->header_tkt->server;']}
description: kdc/do_tgs_req.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.21 before 1.21.2 has a double free that is reachable if an authenticated user can trigger an authorization-data handling failure. Incorrect data is copied from one ticket to another.

code_evidence: For VALIDATE/RENEW, the whole header ticket is copied with `ticket_reply = *t->header_tkt`, so ticket_reply.enc_part aliases the header ticket's enc_part pointer.
handle_authdata() is called with &enc_tkt_reply; on failure it jumps to cleanup before ticket_reply.enc_part2 is reassigned.
ticket_reply.enc_part2 is only set to &enc_tkt_reply after handle_authdata succeeds; the aliased enc_part remains from the struct copy on the failure path.
cleanup frees ticket_reply.enc_part.ciphertext.data and separately frees enc_tkt_reply.authorization_data, which may overlap the aliased header data.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function frees the same memory address twice on the handle_authdata failure path, matching CWE-415's double free. It is not merely a use-after-free because the supported defect is repeated deallocation of the aliased buffer.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the full-struct copy aliases ticket_reply's enc_part ciphertext to the header ticket's enc_part instead of copying only the server field. Trigger: an authenticated TGS renew/validate request that makes handle_authdata() fail, reaching cleanup. Consequence: the same ciphertext buffer is freed twice, corrupting heap state and potentially enabling memory corruption or denial of service.

commit_msg:
CHANGES: snmpd: Stop reading and writing the mib_indexes/* files

Caching directory contents is something the operating system should do
and is not something Net-SNMP should do. Instead of storing a copy of
the directory contents in ${tmp_dir}/mib_indexes/${n}, always scan a
MIB directory.

description: Net-SNMP through 5.7.3 allows Escalation of Privileges because of UNIX symbolic link (symlink) following.

Each parsed token is concatenated into tmpstr1 as "%s/%s" and passed to new_module, so the index file contents drive which paths are later accessed.
netsnmp_mibindex_new(dirname) creates/opens the mib_indexes file for writing and the FILE* ip is handed to add_mibfile, which writes index entries to that path.

if (add_mibfile(filenames[i], strrchr(filenames[i], '/'), ip) == 0)

Trigger: a local user places a symlink at the index path pointing to a privileged file. Consequence: the daemon reads from or truncates/writes to the link target, enabling disclosure or modification of files with the daemon's privileges.

commit_msg:
Fix #73280: Stack Buffer Overflow in GD dynamicGetbuf

We make sure to never pass a negative `rlen` as size to memcpy().

Cf. <https://github.com/libgd/libgd/commit/53110871>.

(cherry picked from commit cc08cbc84d46933c1e9e0149633f1ed5d19e45e9)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tif (remain == 0) {'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (remain <= 0) {']}
description: Integer signedness error in the dynamicGetbuf function in gd_io_dp.c in the GD Graphics Library (aka libgd) through 2.2.3, as used in PHP before 5.6.28 and 7.x before 7.0.13, allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (stack-based buffer overflow) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted imagecreatefromstring call.

code_evidence: Line 8 computes remain as logicalSize - pos, which can be negative when pos exceeds logicalSize. The guard at line 12 only checks remain == 0, so a negative remain falls through to line 15 where rlen = remain becomes negative. Line 17 then passes that negative rlen to memcpy as a size_t, producing a huge copy length into the stack buffer buf.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: memcpy writes outside the intended bounds of buf, matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds memory operation. The signedness/underflow is the underlying cause; CWE-119 captures the resulting buffer-boundary violation and its memory-corruption consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the bounds check tests only equality with zero, missing negative remain values caused by pos > logicalSize. Trigger: a crafted imagecreatefromstring call advancing pos past logicalSize. The negative rlen is converted to a large size_t in memcpy, overflowing the caller's buffer buf and causing stack-based buffer overflow/DoS.

joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The assert at line 73 is reachable from remote packet input and terminates the process rather than following the malformed-packet cleanup path, matching CWE-617. It is not merely improper error handling; the explicit assertion causes the crash.

Trigger: a malformed packet drives decoding to the mgmt allocation path and lldpd_alloc_mgmt fails with a non-ENOMEM error. Consequence: the daemon aborts, causing remote denial of service.

commit_msg:
Fixed heap-buffer-overflow while parsing regexp literals.

This closes #174 issue on Github.
description: njs through 0.3.3, used in NGINX, has a heap-based buffer over-read in nxt_vsprintf in nxt/nxt_sprintf.c during error handling, as demonstrated by an njs_regexp_literal call that leads to an njs_parser_lexer_error call and then an njs_parser_scope_error call.

code_evidence: In the character-class scan, the loop condition `++p < lexer->end && *p != ']'` advances p and dereferences it only when still in bounds, but the escape case `if (++p < lexer->end && (*p == '\n' || *p == '\r'))` advances p; when the post-increment makes p equal lexer->end, the `< lexer->end` test fails and the body is skipped, yet p now points one past the buffer and is later used in the failed error path.

The top-level escape case at line 30 has the same pattern: `++p` moves past lexer->end when the backslash is the final byte, then `(*p == ...)` short-circuits so no dereference occurs here, but the out-of-range p propagates to the `failed` label.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the function permits reading memory past the end of the lexer buffer via an unvalidated pointer advance. This is an out-of-bounds read, not a write; the buffer is only read during error formatting, so the defect is a read overrun rather than CWE-787.

evidence_lines.code:
if (++p < lexer->end && (*p == '\n' || *p == '\r')) {
goto failed;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the escape handling increments p before validating that the next position is within lexer->end, allowing p to advance to end+1. Trigger: a RegExp literal ending in a backslash (or a backslash at the end of a character class). Consequence: the out-of-range pointer reaches the error path where `p - (lexer->start - 1)` is computed and the buffer is read for the error message, producing an out-of-bounds read.

commit_msg:
xen/arm: p2m: Avoid aliasing guest physical frame

The P2M helpers implementation is quite lax and will end up to ignore
the unused top bits of a guest physical frame.

This effectively means that p2m_set_entry() will create a mapping for a
different frame (it is always equal to gfn & (mask unused bits)). Yet
p2m->max_mapped_gfn will be updated using the original frame.

At the moment, p2m_get_entry() and p2m_resolve_translation_fault()
assume that p2m_get_root_pointer() will always return a non-NULL pointer
when the GFN is smaller than p2m->max_mapped_gfn.

Unfortunately, because of the aliasing described above, it would be
possible to set p2m->max_mapped_gfn high enough so it covers frame that
would lead p2m_get_root_pointer() to return NULL.

As we don't sanity check the guest physical frame provided by a guest, a
malicious guest could craft a series of hypercalls that will hit the
BUG_ON() and therefore DoS Xen.

To prevent aliasing, the function p2m_get_root_pointer() is now reworked
to return NULL If any of the unused top bits are not zero. The caller
can then decide what's the appropriate action to do. Since the two paths
(i.e. P2M_ROOT_PAGES == 1 and P2M_ROOT_PAGES != 1) are now very
similarly, take the opportunity to consolidate them making the code a
bit simpler.

With this change, p2m_get_entry() will not try to insert a mapping as
the root pointer is invalid.

Note that root_table is now switch to unsigned long as unsigned int is
not enough to hold part of a GFN.

This is part of XSA-301.

Reported-by: Julien Grall <Julien.Grall@arm.com>
Signed-off-by: Julien Grall <julien.grall@arm.com>
Reviewed-by: Stefano Stabellini <sstabellini@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    unsigned int root_table;', '', '    if ( P2M_ROOT_PAGES == 1 )', '        return __map_domain_page(p2m->root);', '     * Concatenated root-level tables. The table number will be the', '     * offset at the previous level. It is not possible to', '     * concatenate a level-0 root.', '    ASSERT(P2M_ROOT_LEVEL > 0);', '', '    root_table = gfn_x(gfn) >> (level_orders[P2M_ROOT_LEVEL - 1]);', '    root_table &= LPAE_ENTRY_MASK;', ''], 'added_lines': ['    unsigned long root_table;', '     * While the root table index is the offset from the previous level,', "     * we can't use (P2M_ROOT_LEVEL - 1) because the root level might be", '     * 0. Yet we still want to check if all the unused bits are zeroed.', '    root_table = gfn_x(gfn) >> (level_orders[P2M_ROOT_LEVEL] + LPAE_SHIFT);']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.12.x allowing ARM guest OS users to cause a denial of service via a XENMEM_add_to_physmap hypercall. p2m->max_mapped_gfn is used by the functions p2m_resolve_translation_fault() and p2m_get_entry() to sanity check guest physical frame. The rest of the code in the two functions will assume that there is a valid root table and check that with BUG_ON(). The function p2m_get_root_pointer() will ignore the unused top bits of a guest physical frame. This means that the function p2m_set_entry() will alias the frame. However, p2m->max_mapped_gfn will be updated using the original frame. It would be possible to set p2m->max_mapped_gfn high enough to cover a frame that would lead p2m_get_root_pointer() to return NULL in p2m_get_entry() and p2m_resolve_translation_fault(). Additionally, the sanity check on p2m->max_mapped_gfn is off-by-one allowing "highest mapped + 1" to be considered valid. However, p2m_get_root_pointer() will return NULL. The problem could be triggered with a specially crafted hypercall XENMEM_add_to_physmap{, _batch} followed by an access to an address (via hypercall or direct access) that passes the sanity check but cause p2m_get_root_pointer() to return NULL. A malicious guest administrator may cause a hypervisor crash, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS). Xen version 4.8 and newer are vulnerable. Only Arm systems are vulnerable. x86 systems are not affected.

code_evidence: The root table index is derived by shifting gfn_x(gfn) right by level_orders[P2M_ROOT_LEVEL - 1], then masking with LPAE_ENTRY_MASK, so the unused top bits of the GFN are discarded rather than validated.

The bounds check root_table >= P2M_ROOT_PAGES is the only guard before using root_table as an offset into p2m->root; because the discarded bits were never checked, distinct GFNs can alias to the same root_table value.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-193 fits because the function's index/bounds calculation mishandles the boundary between valid and invalid GFNs: the shift/mask admits values one step beyond the representable root-table range, letting the root_table check and max_mapped_gfn disagree. This is a boundary-calculation error, not a generic integer overflow.

evidence_lines.code:
root_table = gfn_x(gfn) >> (level_orders[P2M_ROOT_LEVEL - 1]);
root_table &= LPAE_ENTRY_MASK;

if ( root_table >= P2M_ROOT_PAGES )
return NULL;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: p2m_get_root_pointer() truncates the GFN's unused top bits via shift and mask without requiring them to be zero, so an oversized GFN is accepted and aliases a smaller frame. Trigger: a malicious guest supplies a crafted GFN through XENMEM_add_to_physmap, raising p2m->max_mapped_gfn using the original frame while mapping a different one. Consequence: later lookups pass the max_mapped_gfn sanity check yet p2m_get_root_pointer() returns NULL, hitting BUG_ON() and crashing/DoS'ing Xen.

commit_msg:
x86/insn-eval: Fix use-after-free access to LDT entry

get_desc() computes a pointer into the LDT while holding a lock that
protects the LDT from being freed, but then drops the lock and returns the
(now potentially dangling) pointer to its caller.

Fix it by giving the caller a copy of the LDT entry instead.

Fixes: 670f928ba09b ("x86/insn-eval: Add utility function to get segment descriptor")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tstruct desc_struct *desc;', '\tdesc = get_desc(sel);', '\tif (!desc)', '\treturn get_desc_base(desc);'], 'added_lines': ['\tstruct desc_struct desc;', '\tif (!get_desc(&desc, sel))', '\treturn get_desc_base(&desc);']}
description: In arch/x86/lib/insn-eval.c in the Linux kernel before 5.1.9, there is a use-after-free for access to an LDT entry because of a race condition between modify_ldt() and a #BR exception for an MPX bounds violation.

code_evidence: desc is a raw pointer returned by get_desc(sel), which computes a pointer into the LDT while holding the LDT lock but drops it before returning. The caller dereferences this pointer at line 25 via get_desc_base(desc) after the lock is gone, with no copy or validation that the entry still exists.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect is a synchronization flaw: a shared resource (LDT entry) is accessed without exclusive/atomic protection across the lock release, allowing an interfering concurrent code sequence to modify it. CWE-362 captures this race; the use-after-free is the downstream consequence, not the root weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: get_desc returns a dangling pointer to an LDT entry instead of copying it under the lock. Trigger: a concurrent modify_ldt() frees/replaces the LDT between get_desc returning and get_desc_base dereferencing it (e.g. during a #BR MPX bounds exception). Consequence: use-after-free read of freed descriptor memory, yielding stale base or memory-safety impact.

Proper global init/deinit of GnuTLS

These are reference counted so it is important to retain symmetry
between the calls. Failure to do so will result in bad memory access
and crashes.

description: PJSIP is a free and open source multimedia communication library written in C. PJSIP versions 2.12 and prior do not parse incoming RTCP feedback RPSI (Reference Picture Selection Indication) packet, but any app that directly uses pjmedia_rtcp_fb_parse_rpsi() will be affected. A patch is available in the `master` branch of the `pjsip/pjproject` GitHub repository. There are currently no known workarounds.

code_evidence: The size check at [12,13,14] computes len = (3 + sli_cnt) * 4 and compares it against *length, so the caller-supplied buffer capacity is validated before writing.
At [15,16] the header is copied into buf and at [19,20] the write pointer p is derived from sizeof(*hdr); the loop at [21,28] then writes exactly 4 bytes per SLI entry into buf.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 requires a write past the buffer bounds. Here the length check bounds the header plus 4*sli_cnt bytes before the loop writes them, and the patch only changes the header struct type; the function does not itself exhibit an out-of-bounds write, so CWE-787 is not directly supported.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function writes the RTCP FB SLI header and sli_cnt four-byte FCI records into the caller's buffer. The only guard is the len > *length check at [12,13,14], and len is derived from sli_cnt, so the total written bytes match the validated size; no missing constraint or attacker-controlled size mismatch is present in this function.

commit_msg: fs: Don't try to delete the file when copying. It could cause a security issue if the file exists and doesn't allow other's to read/write. delete could allow someone to create the file and have access to the data.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tif (M_fs_perms_can_access(p2, M_FS_PERMS_MODE_NONE) == M_FS_ERROR_SUCCESS)', '\t\t{'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (M_fs_perms_can_access(p2, M_FS_PERMS_MODE_NONE) == M_FS_ERROR_SUCCESS) {']}
description: mstdlib (aka the M Standard Library for C) 1.2.0 has incorrect file access control in situations where M_fs_perms_can_access attempts to delete an existing file (that lacks public read/write access) during a copy operation, related to fs/m_fs.c and fs/m_fs_path.c. An attacker could create the file and then would have access to the data.

code_evidence: When p1 is not a directory, the function tests whether p2 is accessible with M_FS_PERMS_MODE_NONE. If that access check succeeds, ret is set to M_FALSE and control jumps to done, so overwrite is refused. Otherwise execution continues to basename/join and a second p2-based access check at line 23; the delete/create race described in the commit is not implemented by this function, which only decides whether overwrite is permitted.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The target CWE-732 concerns incorrect permission assignment for a critical resource. The evidence shows a permission/access check gating overwrite, but not the assignment of loose permissions; the actual exposure arises from deletion behavior in a callee. The function alone does not directly establish a permission-assignment flaw, so support is weak and indirect.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The root cause is that the overwrite-permission decision relies on M_fs_perms_can_access, which the commit message says can delete an existing file lacking public read/write access. The trigger is a non-directory p1 with an existing p2 that fails the access check; the consequence is file deletion and recreation by an attacker who can then read the copied data. This function expresses the check, but the unsafe operation occurs in M_fs_perms_can_access, not in these lines.

commit_msg: Bug 698044: restrict font name length to the buffer size.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        xps_load_sfnt_name(font, (char*)p42->font_name.chars);'], 'added_lines': ['        xps_load_sfnt_name(font, (char*)p42->font_name.chars, sizeof(p42->font_name.chars));']}
description: The xps_load_sfnt_name function in xps/xpsfont.c in Artifex Ghostscript GhostXPS 9.21 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (buffer overflow and application crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted document.

code_evidence: Line 43 zeroes the fixed-size font_name buffer, then line 44 calls xps_load_sfnt_name with only the destination pointer and no size argument, so the callee cannot bound how many name bytes it writes.
Line 45 immediately derives the length with strlen, and line 47 copies that buffer into key_name with unbounded strcpy, propagating any overlong name.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Writing name data beyond the intended bounds of the fixed-size font_name.chars buffer is an out-of-bounds memory-buffer operation, matching CWE-119. CWE-120 (unbounded copy) is the more specific root cause, but the target label CWE-119 correctly captures the resulting improper restriction of operations within the buffer's bounds.

evidence_lines.code:
memset(p42->key_name.chars, 0, sizeof(p42->key_name.chars));
strcpy((char*)p42->key_name.chars, (char*)p42->font_name.chars);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the pre-patch call at line 44 passes the fixed-size font_name.chars buffer to xps_load_sfnt_name without conveying its capacity, allowing a crafted font name in the document to write past the buffer. Trigger: a malicious XPS document with an oversized sfnt name. Supported consequence: out-of-bounds write, application crash (DoS) and possible memory corruption; the later strlen/strcpy at lines 45 and 47 compound the overrun.

commit_msg:
ASTERIX: Avoid an integer overflow.

Count using a guint instead of a guint8.

Bug: 13344
Change-Id: Ic7d337dbb29b92ebb8332f50fd47b5ba2aa3f41e
Reviewed-on: https://code.wireshark.org/review/19746
Petri-Dish: Gerald Combs <gerald@wireshark.org>
Tested-by: Petri Dish Buildbot <buildbot-no-reply@wireshark.org>
Reviewed-by: Gerald Combs <gerald@wireshark.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['static guint8 asterix_fspec_len (tvbuff_t *tvb, guint offset)', '    guint8 i;', '    for (i = 0; (tvb_get_guint8 (tvb, offset + i) & 1) && i < tvb_reported_length (tvb) - offset; i++);'], 'added_lines': ['static guint asterix_fspec_len (tvbuff_t *tvb, guint offset)', '    guint i;', '    guint max_length = tvb_reported_length (tvb) - offset;', '    for (i = 0; (tvb_get_guint8 (tvb, offset + i) & 1) && i < max_length; i++);']}
description: In Wireshark 2.2.0 to 2.2.3 and 2.0.0 to 2.0.9, the ASTERIX dissector could go into an infinite loop, triggered by packet injection or a malformed capture file. This was addressed in epan/dissectors/packet-asterix.c by changing a data type to avoid an integer overflow.

code_evidence: The loop counter i is declared as guint8, so it wraps to 0 after 255 iterations. The loop condition reads tvb_get_guint8(tvb, offset+i) before checking the length bound, and the bound tvb_reported_length(tvb)-offset can exceed the guint8 range, so i never reliably reaches it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the counter increment exceeds the guint8 representation and wraps to a small value, defeating the loop termination check. This is integer wraparound; the missing bound on the counter's range, not a buffer over-read, is the supported weakness.

evidence_lines.code:
guint8 i;
for (i = 0; (tvb_get_guint8 (tvb, offset + i) & 1) && i < tvb_reported_length (tvb) - offset; i++);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the 8-bit counter cannot represent lengths beyond 255, so incrementing past 255 wraps to 0. Because the byte read precedes the bound check and the bound is not clamped to the counter's range, a malformed packet with 0x01 bytes at the end of a long tvb keeps the loop condition true indefinitely, causing an infinite loop and CPU exhaustion/DoS.

commit_msg: fixed #2138
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tnode->name = gf_malloc(sizeof(u8) * subs_size * 2);', '\t\tsubs_size = gf_base64_encode(aux_data + subs_offset, subs_size, (u8*) node->name, subs_size * 2);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tu64 size_64 = (subs_size * 2) + 3;', '\t\tnode->name = gf_malloc(sizeof(char) * size_64);', '\t\tsubs_size = gf_base64_encode(aux_data + subs_offset, subs_size, (u8*) node->name, size_64);']}
description: GPAC 2.0 allows a heap-based buffer overflow in gf_base64_encode. It can be triggered via MP4Box.

code_evidence: Line 94 allocates node->name with exactly subs_size*2 bytes, but line 99 calls gf_base64_encode with that same subs_size*2 as the output capacity. Base64 encoding of subs_size input bytes produces 4*ceil(subs_size/3) output bytes, which exceeds 2*subs_size for most sizes; the encoder can therefore write past the allocation. Line 100 then writes the terminating NUL at node->name[subs_size], which is also beyond the buffer when the encoder filled it to capacity.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes encoded bytes and a NUL past the end of a heap allocation, directly matching CWE-787 (out-of-bounds write). The patch confirms this by enlarging the allocation to (subs_size*2)+3 and passing that size to the encoder; a related CWE-122 heap overflow is the same defect at a more specific memory region, but CWE-787 is the target base weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the destination buffer for base64 output is sized as 2*n instead of the required ~4*ceil(n/3) (plus terminator). Trigger: a subsample with a valid src index and size passes checks at lines 25 and 51, reaching the encode call with attacker-influenced subs_size. Consequence: heap-based out-of-bounds write of encoded data and the NUL terminator, corrupting adjacent heap memory.

commit_msg:
Security: update Lua struct package for security.

During an auditing Apple found that the "struct" Lua package
we ship with Redis (http://www.inf.puc-rio.br/~roberto/struct/) contains
a security problem. A bound-checking statement fails because of integer
overflow. The bug exists since we initially integrated this package with
Lua, when scripting was introduced, so every version of Redis with
EVAL/EVALSHA capabilities exposed is affected.

Instead of just fixing the bug, the library was updated to the latest
version shipped by the author.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      int a = getnum(L, fmt, MAXALIGN);'], 'added_lines': ['      int a = getnum(fmt, MAXALIGN);']}
description: An Integer Overflow issue was discovered in the struct library in the Lua subsystem in Redis before 3.2.12, 4.x before 4.0.10, and 5.x before 5.0 RC2, leading to a failure of bounds checking.

code_evidence: controloptions parses the alignment option '!' by calling getnum(L, fmt, MAXALIGN) and stores the returned int in a at line 8. The only validation applied to a is isp2(a) at line 9, followed by assignment h->align = a at line 11. No check constrains the numeric parse result or prevents a wraparound/overflow in the value returned by getnum before it is used as the alignment bound.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the root cause is an integer overflow/wraparound in the parsed alignment value that defeats bound checking, exactly the described weakness. It is not merely a logic error in isp2; the numeric calculation itself can overflow before validation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The alignment value is obtained from a format string via getnum and accepted into h->align after only a power-of-two test; an overflowing numeric input can yield a small or negative value that passes or subverts the intended bound-checking logic. This weakens later size/offset bounds checks in struct operations, enabling out-of-bounds memory access.

commit_msg:
Prevent array index out of bounds for symbol

Bug-Debian: https://github.com/tats/w3m/issues/38
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\taddstr(graph2_symbol[(int)c]);', '\t\taddch(*graph_symbol[(int)c]);', '\t    addstr(symbol[(int)c]);', '\t    addch(*symbol[(int)c]);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\taddstr(graph2_symbol[(unsigned char)c % N_GRAPH_SYMBOL]);', '\t\taddch(*graph_symbol[(unsigned char)c % N_GRAPH_SYMBOL]);', '\t    addstr(symbol[(unsigned char)c % N_SYMBOL]);', '\t    addch(*symbol[(unsigned char)c % N_SYMBOL]);']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Tatsuya Kinoshita w3m fork before 0.5.3-33. w3m allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (heap buffer overflow and crash) via a crafted HTML page.

code_evidence: Line 19 derives index c from input via wtf_get_code masked to 0x7f then offset by SYMBOL_BASE; c is a signed char. Line 23 guards only c < N_GRAPH_SYMBOL, so negative c passes. Lines 30 and 33 index graph2_symbol/graph_symbol with (int)c without a lower bound. Lines 38 and 41 index symbol with (int)c in the else branch, also unguarded against negative values.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Indexing arrays with an unchecked negative index reads outside the buffer's intended boundary, matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds memory operation. The fix applies modulo with unsigned char to force a valid in-range index; this is a bounds restriction rather than a type-confusion or integer-overflow issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The index c is computed from attacker-influenced HTML character data and stored in a signed char; the only bound check is an upper bound. A crafted value yielding a negative c passes the check and is used to index symbol arrays, causing an out-of-bounds read that can crash or corrupt memory (heap buffer overflow).

commit_msg:
Fixed bugs of stack reallocation x GC

Macro 'checkstackGC' was doing a GC step after resizing the stack;
the GC could shrink the stack and undo the resize. Moreover, macro
'checkstackp' also does a GC step, which could remove the preallocated
CallInfo when calling a function. (Its name has been changed to
'checkstackGCp' to emphasize that it calls the GC.)
diff_func:
--- func_before
+++ func_after
@@ -509,7 +509,7 @@
         while (!ttisfunction(s2v(ra))) {  /* not a function? */
           luaD_tryfuncTM(L, ra);  /* try '__call' metamethod */
           b++;  /* there is now one extra argument */
-          checkstackp(L, 1, ra);
+          checkstackGCp(L, 1, ra);
         }
         if (!ttisLclosure(s2v(ra))) {  /* C function? */
           luaD_call(L, ra, LUA_MULTRET);  /* call it */
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['          checkstackp(L, 1, ra);'], 'added_lines': ['          checkstackGCp(L, 1, ra);']}
description: Lua through 5.4.0 mishandles the interaction between stack resizes and garbage collection, leading to a heap-based buffer overflow, heap-based buffer over-read, or use-after-free.

code_evidence: In the OP_TAILCALL handler, the loop calls luaD_tryfuncTM(L, ra) to insert a '__call' metamethod, then increments the argument count b and calls checkstackp(L, 1, ra) to ensure one extra stack slot. checkstackp performs a GC step after resizing; that GC can shrink the stack or free the preallocated CallInfo, so the space reserved for the new argument/metamethod is removed before the next iteration writes to ra and b is used further.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe write occurs when the loop writes argument slots at ra after the GC has invalidated the prior stack resize, which is an out-of-bounds write past the intended stack buffer. This is a missing-ordering/reservation issue, not merely a null dereference or integer overflow, so CWE-787 fits the supported consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the stack is resized and then a GC step runs, which may shrink the stack and undo the reservation, so subsequent writes at ra (the added argument/metamethod slot) and the CallInfo use go past the valid stack buffer. Trigger: a tail call whose object is not a function and whose '__call' metamethod chain forces the loop. Consequence: heap-based out-of-bounds write/read or use-after-free of the CallInfo.

commit_msg:
Fix nullptr exception in QuantizedMaxPool op when empty list is sent to min_input or max_input parameters.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 413960973
Change-Id: I9e3ded593f3c4eabf0d6d5dc356e6a19a3ad2682
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    auto min_input_tensor = context->input(1);', '    auto max_input_tensor = context->input(2);', '    OP_REQUIRES(', '        context, min_input_tensor.NumElements() == 1,', '        errors::InvalidArgument(', '            "min_input must be a scalar float value, got tensor with shape ",', '            min_input_tensor.shape()));', '    OP_REQUIRES(', '        context, max_input_tensor.NumElements() == 1,', '        errors::InvalidArgument(', '            "max_input must be a scalar float value, got tensor with shape ",', '            max_input_tensor.shape()));']}
description: Tensorflow is an Open Source Machine Learning Framework. The implementation of `QuantizedMaxPool` has an undefined behavior where user controlled inputs can trigger a reference binding to null pointer. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.8.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.7.1, TensorFlow 2.6.3, and TensorFlow 2.5.3, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: Lines 2-3 read min_input and max_input via context->input(1)/(2).flat<float>()(0) with no check that those inputs are non-empty scalars; if the caller supplies an empty tensor, index (0) dereferences an out-of-range/null data pointer.

Lines 6-10 allocate output tensors with OP_REQUIRES_OK, which returns early on failure, but then immediately dereference output_min and output_max via flat<float>()(0) without verifying allocation succeeded.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits because the unsafe element-0 access on an empty tensor yields a null/invalid pointer dereference for user-controlled input; the fix adds NumElements()==1 checks, confirming the missing validity constraint. Related CWE-125 (out-of-bounds read) is less apt since the observed failure is a null pointer binding.

evidence_lines.code:
const float min_input = context->input(1).flat<float>()(0);
const float max_input = context->input(2).flat<float>()(0);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function unconditionally indexes element 0 of the min/max input tensors and of the freshly allocated output tensors without validating element count or allocation success. Trigger: a user passes an empty min_input or max_input list (or output allocation fails). Consequence: reference binding/dereference of an invalid pointer, causing a crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
Use spinlocks to deal with workers introducing a wrapper
bigben_schedule_work(), and several spinlock checks.
Otherwise, bigben_set_led() may schedule bigben->worker after the
structure has been freed, causing a use-after-free.

Fixes: 4eb1b01de5b9 ("HID: hid-bigbenff: fix race condition for scheduled work during removal")
Signed-off-by: Pietro Borrello <borrello@diag.uniroma1.it>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20230125-hid-unregister-leds-v4-3-7860c5763c38@diag.uniroma1.it
Signed-off-by: Benjamin Tissoires <benjamin.tissoires@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tschedule_work(&bigben->worker);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tbigben_schedule_work(bigben);']}
description: The Linux kernel through 6.1.9 has a Use-After-Free in bigben_remove in drivers/hid/hid-bigbenff.c via a crafted USB device because the LED controllers remain registered for too long.

code_evidence: Under bigben->lock the function updates the motor state and sets bigben->work_ff, then releases the lock.
Immediately after releasing the lock, it calls schedule_work(&bigben->worker) on the bigben object without any lifetime or removal guard.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The code dereferences and schedules work through the bigben pointer after its lifetime may have ended, which is exactly CWE-416. This is a lifetime/race flaw, not merely a missing NULL check or a double free.

evidence_lines.code: schedule_work(&bigben->worker);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: scheduling bigben->worker is not synchronized with device teardown, so the worker can be queued against a bigben structure that bigben_remove is concurrently freeing. Trigger: a crafted USB device drives an FF_RUMBLE effect whose magnitudes change while removal occurs. Supported consequence: the queued work runs on freed memory, a use-after-free.

commit_msg:
CVE-2017-13690/IKEv2: Fix some bounds checks.

Use a pointer of the correct type in ND_TCHECK(), or use ND_TCHECK2()
and provide the correct length.

While we're at it, remove the blank line between some checks and the
UNALIGNED_MEMCPY()s they protect.

Also, note the places where we print the entire payload.

This fixes a buffer over-read discovered by Bhargava Shastry,
SecT/TU Berlin.

Add a test using the capture file supplied by the reporter(s).
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\t/* Print the entire payload in hex */']}
description: The IKEv2 parser in tcpdump before 4.9.2 has a buffer over-read in print-isakmp.c, several functions.

code_evidence: Line 9 checks only a single byte via ND_TCHECK(*ext), then line 10 copies sizeof(e) bytes from ext into e, so the bounds check does not cover the full struct read. Line 11 computes ntohs(e.len)-4 and lines 12-14 pass ntohs(e.len)-4 as the length to rawprint starting at ext+1, without verifying the payload length against the captured buffer or ep. Line 17 returns ext+ntohs(e.len), advancing by the attacker-controlled length.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the function reads memory beyond the intended buffer via an unchecked attacker-controlled length and an undersized bounds check; the consequence is memory disclosure/crash, not a write, so it is not an out-of-bounds write.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The root cause is an insufficient bounds check: ND_TCHECK(*ext) validates only one byte before UNALIGNED_MEMCPY reads sizeof(struct isakmp_gen), and the payload length from the packet is trusted. A truncated IKEv2 HASH payload triggers reads past the captured/enclosing buffer in the memcpy and rawprint, causing an out-of-bounds read (buffer over-read).

commit_msg:
syntax.c: check for syntax element inconsistencies

Implicit channel mapping reconfiguration is explicitely forbidden by
ISO/IEC 13818-7:2006 (8.5.3.3). Decoders should be able to detect such
files and reject them. FAAD2 does not perform any kind of checks
regarding this.

This leads to security vulnerabilities when processing crafted AAC
files performing such reconfigurations.

Add checks to decode_sce_lfe and decode_cpe to make sure such
inconsistencies are detected as early as possible.

These checks first read hDecoder->frame: if this is not the first
frame then we make sure that the syntax element at the same position
in the previous frame also had element_id id_syn_ele. If not, return
21 as this is a fatal file structure issue.

This patch addresses CVE-2018-20362 (fixes #26) and possibly other
related issues.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '    if (hDecoder->frame && hDecoder->element_id[hDecoder->fr_ch_ele] != id_syn_ele) {', '        /* element inconsistency */', '        hInfo->error = 21;', '        return;', '    }']}
description: A NULL pointer dereference was discovered in ifilter_bank of libfaad/filtbank.c in Freeware Advanced Audio Decoder 2 (FAAD2) 2.8.8. The vulnerability causes a segmentation fault and application crash because adding to windowed output is mishandled in the EIGHT_SHORT_SEQUENCE case.

code_evidence: Bounds on channels and fr_ch_ele are checked before indexing element_id and element_output_channels.
element_id[fr_ch_ele] is written, then single_lfe_channel_element fills element_output_channels[fr_ch_ele]; no consistency check on id_syn_ele vs prior frame.
internal_channel is indexed by channels and pce.sce_channel[tag], then fr_channels is advanced by element_output_channels[fr_ch_ele], potentially beyond MAX_CHANNELS.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the unchecked channel count and pce index produce writes past the end of internal_channel and related arrays; the added element_id consistency check is the missing constraint preventing the reconfiguration that leads to the out-of-bounds write.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function trusts element_output_channels and pce.sce_channel[tag] to stay within internal_channel bounds; a crafted AAC stream reconfiguring syntax elements can make channels advance past MAX_CHANNELS, so subsequent writes to internal_channel/channels overflow the fixed-size arrays and corrupt memory or crash.

commit_msg:
Budimir noted that perf_event_validate_size() only checks the size of
the newly added event, even though the sizes of all existing events
can also change due to not all events having the same read_format.

When we attach the new event, perf_group_attach(), we do re-compute
the size for all events.

Fixes: a723968c0ed3 ("perf: Fix u16 overflows")
Reported-by: Budimir Markovic <markovicbudimir@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Peter Zijlstra (Intel) <peterz@infradead.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t__perf_event_read_size(event,', '\t\t\t       event->group_leader->nr_siblings);'], 'added_lines': ['\tevent->read_size =', '\t\t__perf_event_read_size(event->attr.read_format,', '\t\t\t\t       event->group_leader->nr_siblings);']}
description:
A heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the Linux kernel's Performance Events system component can be exploited to achieve local privilege escalation.

A perf_event's read_size can overflow, leading to an heap out-of-bounds increment or write in perf_read_group().

We recommend upgrading past commit 382c27f4ed28f803b1f1473ac2d8db0afc795a1b.

code_evidence: The function computes the event's read_size by calling __perf_event_read_size(event, event->group_leader->nr_siblings) and discarding the return value; the resulting size is not stored back into event->read_size. The count of siblings from the group leader feeds the size computation without any bound being enforced here.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The described consequence is a write past the end of an allocated buffer (heap out-of-bounds write) in perf_read_group, matching CWE-787. The unchecked size computation here is the enabling condition rather than a mere integer overflow (CWE-190), which is only the precursor.

evidence_lines.code:
__perf_event_read_size(event,
event->group_leader->nr_siblings);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the computed read size is not persisted into event->read_size for this event, so the stored size can remain inconsistent with the actual group read_format and sibling count. When perf_read_group() later uses the stale/underestimated read_size to index or copy per-event data, the mismatch allows an out-of-bounds increment or write in the heap buffer.

commit_msg:
avcodec/idctdsp: Transmit studio_profile to init instead of using AVCodecContext profile

These 2 fields are not always the same, it is simpler to always use the same field
for detecting studio profile

Fixes: null pointer dereference
Fixes: ffmpeg_crash_3.avi

Found-by: Thuan Pham <thuanpv@comp.nus.edu.sg>, Marcel Böhme, Andrew Santosa and Alexandru RazvanCaciulescu with AFLSmart
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>

description: libavcodec in FFmpeg 4.0 may trigger a NULL pointer dereference if the studio profile is incorrectly detected while converting a crafted AVI file to MPEG4, leading to a denial of service, related to idctdsp.c and mpegvideo.c.

code_evidence: ff_mpv_idct_init dereferences the MpegEncContext pointer s (s->idsp, s->avctx, s->alternate_scan) and passes s->avctx into ff_idctdsp_init without any null check on s or s->avctx. sockets.cpp was branching on whether a socket close function was
local_socket_close in order to avoid a potential deadlock if the socket
list lock was held while closing a peer socket.

Bug: http://b/28347842
Change-Id: I5e56f17fa54275284787f0f1dc150d1960256ab3
(cherry picked from commit 9b587dec6d0a57c8fe1083c1c543fbeb163d65fa)

commit_msg:
schema tree BUGFIX freeing nodes with no module set

Context must be passed explicitly for these cases.
Fixes #1452

description: In function lys_node_free() in libyang <= v1.0.225, it asserts that the value of node->module can't be NULL. But in some cases, node->module can be null, which triggers a reachable assertion (CWE-617).

code_evidence: The error path calls lys_node_free(retval, NULL, 0) without passing ctx, so the node is freed with a NULL context; per the commit, lys_node_free asserts that node->module is non-NULL, and this cleanup path can reach that assertion when module was never set.

commit_msg: Fix possible integer overflow
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '   if (b < 0) {', '      return MP_VAL;', '   }']}
description: Integer Overflow vulnerability in mp_grow in libtom libtommath before commit beba892bc0d4e4ded4d667ab1d2a94f4d75109a9, allows attackers to execute arbitrary code and cause a denial of service (DoS).

code_evidence: Line 5 computes the allocation size as (b / MP_DIGIT_BIT) + 1 and passes it to mp_grow; line 8 stores the same computed count in a->used; line 9 indexes a->dp with b / MP_DIGIT_BIT. The function takes b as a signed int and performs no bounds check on it before these calculations.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is integer overflow/wraparound: arithmetic on b produces a small or negative value used as a size and offset, exactly the CWE-190 pattern where size calculations become security-critical. It is not merely a missing validation issue, because the computed value feeds allocation and indexing.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the signed argument b is used directly in size and index arithmetic without a lower-bound check. A negative b yields a negative or zero quotient, so (b / MP_DIGIT_BIT) + 1 can be zero or negative; mp_grow may allocate a too-small or invalid buffer, while line 8 sets an inconsistent used count and line 9 writes through a negative index. The supported consequence is an out-of-bounds write that can corrupt memory or crash.

commit_msg:
The "rb_per_cpu_empty()" misinterpret the condition (as not-empty) when
"head_page" and "commit_page" of "struct ring_buffer_per_cpu" points to
the same buffer page, whose "buffer_data_page" is empty and "read" field
is non-zero.

An error scenario could be constructed as followed (kernel perspective):

1. All pages in the buffer has been accessed by reader(s) so that all of
them will have non-zero "read" field.

2. Read and clear all buffer pages so that "rb_num_of_entries()" will
return 0 rendering there's no more data to read. It is also required
that the "read_page", "commit_page" and "tail_page" points to the same
page, while "head_page" is the next page of them.

3. Invoke "ring_buffer_lock_reserve()" with large enough "length"
so that it shot pass the end of current tail buffer page. Now the
"head_page", "commit_page" and "tail_page" points to the same page.

4. Discard current event with "ring_buffer_discard_commit()", so that
"head_page", "commit_page" and "tail_page" points to a page whose buffer
data page is now empty.

When the error scenario has been constructed, "tracing_read_pipe" will
be trapped inside a deadloop: "trace_empty()" returns 0 since
"rb_per_cpu_empty()" returns 0 when it hits the CPU containing such
constructed ring buffer. Then "trace_find_next_entry_inc()" always
return NULL since "rb_num_of_entries()" reports there's no more entry
to read. Finally "trace_seq_to_user()" returns "-EBUSY" spanking
"tracing_read_pipe" back to the start of the "waitagain" loop.

I've also written a proof-of-concept script to construct the scenario
and trigger the bug automatically, you can use it to trace and validate
my reasoning above:

  https://github.com/aegistudio/RingBufferDetonator.git

Tests has been carried out on linux kernel 5.14-rc2
(2734d6c1b1a089fb593ef6a23d4b70903526fe0c), my fixed version
of kernel (for testing whether my update fixes the bug) and
some older kernels (for range of affected kernels). Test result is
also attached to the proof-of-concept repository.

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/linux-trace-devel/YPaNxsIlb2yjSi5Y@aegistudio/
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/linux-trace-devel/YPgrN85WL9VyrZ55@aegistudio

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: bf41a158cacba ("ring-buffer: make reentrant")
Suggested-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linuxfoundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Haoran Luo <www@aegistudio.net>
Signed-off-by: Steven Rostedt (VMware) <rostedt@goodmis.org>
diff_func:
--- func_before
+++ func_after
@@ -8,8 +8,28 @@
 	if (unlikely(!head))
 		return true;
 
-	return reader->read == rb_page_commit(reader) &&
-		(commit == reader ||
-		 (commit == head &&
-		  head->read == rb_page_commit(commit)));
+	/* Reader should exhaust content in reader page */
+	if (reader->read != rb_page_commit(reader))
+		return false;
+
+	/*
+	 * If writers are committing on the reader page, knowing all
+	 * committed content has been read, the ring buffer is empty.
+	 */
+	if (commit == reader)
+		return true;
+

commit_msg:
journalctl: verify sealed log epochs are continuous

Currently empty epochs are not sealed. This allows an attacker to truncate
a sealed log and continue it without any problems showing when verifying the
log.

This partially addresses CVE-2023-31438. One way to extend this change to
address CVE-2023-31438 completely, would be to verify that there is exactly
one seal per epoch (and not sealing when the epoch has not ended yet).

the change also adds a journal-file flag: HEADER_COMPATIBLE_SEALED_CONTINUOUS
this flag indicates that a journal file is sealed continuously and decides whether
any missing crypto epochs should trigger a warning or an error.

description: An issue was discovered in systemd 253. An attacker can truncate a sealed log file and then resume log sealing such that checking the integrity shows no error, despite modifications. NOTE: the vendor reportedly sent "a reply denying that any of the finding was a security vulnerability."

After each tag, last_epoch is set to the tag's epoch and n_tags increments, so the verifier's state moves to the jumped epoch and never detects the missing intermediate epoch.

The OBJECT_TAG case additionally requires the tag sequence number to equal n_tags+1, showing that sequence continuity is enforced for tags but the analogous epoch continuity is not enforced for epochs.

Here the epoch sequence is part of the seal verification, and failing to require consecutive epochs means the integrity check is incompletely validated, allowing modified/truncated data to pass verification.
