joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is the unbounded variable-size stack array whose size derives directly from the attacker-controlled currpath length. A crafted binary/name with a very long path causes excessive stack allocation, and the subsequent copy fills that stack region, triggering stack exhaustion and application crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
* NEWS: Document this.
* src/extract.c (extract_archive): Skip members whose names
contain "..".
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  bool skip_dotdot_name;', '  skip_dotdot_name = (!absolute_names_option', '\t\t      && contains_dot_dot (current_stat_info.orig_file_name));', '  if (skip_dotdot_name)', '    ERROR ((0, 0, _("%s: Member name contains \'..\'"),', '\t    quotearg_colon (current_stat_info.orig_file_name)));', '', '      || skip_dotdot_name']}
description: Directory traversal vulnerability in the safer_name_suffix function in GNU tar 1.14 through 1.29 might allow remote attackers to bypass an intended protection mechanism and write to arbitrary files via vectors related to improper sanitization of the file_name parameter, aka POINTYFEATHER.

code_evidence: The function decides whether to skip an archive member using only current_stat_info.file_name[0] being empty or an interactive confirm; it does not inspect the member path for '..' components before proceeding.

description: GNOME GdkPixbuf (aka GDK-PixBuf) before 2.42.8 allows a heap-based buffer overflow when compositing or clearing frames in GIF files, as demonstrated by io-gif-animation.c composite_frame. This overflow is controllable and could be abused for code execution, especially on 32-bit systems.

code_evidence: The GDK_PIXBUF_FRAME_DISPOSE loop computes a destination pointer as pixels + y * gdk_pixbuf_get_rowstride(anim->last_frame_data) + anim->last_frame->x_offset * 4 and then calls memset on that pointer for (x_end - x_offset) * 4 bytes. The multiplication and addition are performed in an unchecked expression, so attacker-controlled GIF frame offsets/dimensions can make the computed offset wrap.

Trigger: a GIF whose frame y_offset/x_offset/rowstride values cause the products or sum to exceed the addressable integer range. Supported consequence: the wrapped offset points outside the intended frame buffer, and the following memset writes attacker-influenced length at that location, producing heap memory corruption (the diff confirms the fix adds g_size_checked_mul/add around this calculation).

commit_msg: closes bpo-34656: Avoid relying on signed overflow in _pickle memos. (GH-9261)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['_Unpickler_ResizeMemoList(UnpicklerObject *self, Py_ssize_t new_size)', '    Py_ssize_t i;'], 'added_lines': ['_Unpickler_ResizeMemoList(UnpicklerObject *self, size_t new_size)', '    size_t i;']}
description: Modules/_pickle.c in Python before 3.7.1 has an integer overflow via a large LONG_BINPUT value that is mishandled during a "resize to twice the size" attempt. This issue might cause memory exhaustion, but is only relevant if the pickle format is used for serializing tens or hundreds of gigabytes of data. This issue is fixed in: v3.4.10, v3.4.10rc1; v3.5.10, v3.5.10rc1, v3.5.7, v3.5.7rc1, v3.5.8, v3.5.8rc1, v3.5.8rc2, v3.5.9; v3.6.10, v3.6.10rc1, v3.6.11, v3.6.11rc1, v3.6.12, v3.6.7, v3.6.7rc1, v3.6.7rc2, v3.6.8, v3.6.8rc1, v3.6.9, v3.6.9rc1; v3.7.1, v3.7.1rc1, v3.7.1rc2, v3.7.2, v3.7.2rc1, v3.7.3, v3.7.3rc1, v3.7.4, v3.7.4rc1, v3.7.4rc2, v3.7.5, v3.7.5rc1, v3.7.6, v3.7.6rc1, v3.7.7, v3.7.7rc1, v3.7.8, v3.7.8rc1, v3.7.9.

code_evidence: The resize helper takes new_size and loop index i as signed Py_ssize_t, then passes new_size to PyMem_RESIZE and stores it into self->memo_size.

The only guard is the assert(new_size > self->memo_size); callers compute new_size by doubling the memo size, so a large LONG_BINPUT can make the doubling wrap in signed arithmetic before this function is reached.
The loop `for (i = self->memo_size; i < new_size; i++)` and the assignment `self->memo_size = new_size` assume new_size is a positive, larger value; a wrapped negative size violates that assumption.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The signed doubling of the memo size is a calculation assumed to grow but can wrap to a small or negative value, which is exactly integer overflow/wraparound (CWE-190). A mere allocation failure would be CWE-770, but here the size arithmetic itself is the defect.

evidence_lines.code:
_Unpickler_ResizeMemoList(UnpicklerObject *self, Py_ssize_t new_size)
Py_ssize_t i;

assert(new_size > self->memo_size);
PyMem_RESIZE(memo_new, PyObject *, new_size);

for (i = self->memo_size; i < new_size; i++)
self->memo_size = new_size;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: memo sizes are handled as signed Py_ssize_t and doubled without overflow checking, so a huge LONG_BINPUT index produces a wrapped/negative new_size. Trigger: a crafted pickle stream with a very large memo index forces the resize path; the assert may be compiled out in release builds, so the wrapped value reaches PyMem_RESIZE and the initialization loop, causing undersized allocation or out-of-bounds writes and memory exhaustion/corruption.

commit_msg:
Harden ASN.1 BIO handling of large amounts of data.

If the ASN.1 BIO is presented with a large length field read it in
chunks of increasing size checking for EOF on each read. This prevents
small files allocating excessive amounts of data.

CVE-2016-2109

Thanks to Brian Carpenter for reporting this issue.

Reviewed-by: Viktor Dukhovni <viktor@openssl.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['                if (!BUF_MEM_grow_clean(b, len + want)) {', '                    ASN1err(ASN1_F_ASN1_D2I_READ_BIO, ERR_R_MALLOC_FAILURE);', '                    goto err;', '                }', '                    i = BIO_read(in, &(b->data[len]), want);', '                    if (i <= 0) {', '                        ASN1err(ASN1_F_ASN1_D2I_READ_BIO,', '                                ASN1_R_NOT_ENOUGH_DATA);', '                    len += i;', '                    want -= i;'], 'added_lines': ['                size_t chunk_max = ASN1_CHUNK_INITIAL_SIZE;', '', '                    /*', '                     * Read content in chunks of increasing size', '                     * so we can return an error for EOF without', '                     * having to allocate the entire content length', '                     * in one go.', '                     */', '                    size_t chunk = want > chunk_max ? chunk_max : want;', '', '                    if (!BUF_MEM_grow_clean(b, len + chunk)) {', '                        ASN1err(ASN1_F_ASN1_D2I_READ_BIO, ERR_R_MALLOC_FAILURE);', '                    want -= chunk;', '                    while (chunk > 0) {', '                        i = BIO_read(in, &(b->data[len]), chunk);', '                        if (i <= 0) {', '                            ASN1err(ASN1_F_ASN1_D2I_READ_BIO,', '                                    ASN1_R_NOT_ENOUGH_DATA);', '                            goto err;', '                        }', '                        len += i;', '                        chunk -= i;', '                    }', '                    if (chunk_max < INT_MAX/2)', '                        chunk_max *= 2;']}
description: The asn1_d2i_read_bio function in crypto/asn1/a_d2i_fp.c in the ASN.1 BIO implementation in OpenSSL before 1.0.1t and 1.0.2 before 1.0.2h allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory consumption) via a short invalid encoding.

code_evidence: When the ASN.1 length field slen is large, want is set to slen and the code allocates BUF_MEM_grow_clean(b, len + want) for the entire declared length before reading any content. The read loop then only learns of EOF after the full allocation; a short invalid encoding with a huge length therefore allocates excessive memory.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This is improper management of a system resource (memory) driven by untrusted length data, which fits CWE-399 Resource Management Errors. The concrete allocation-before-validation is the resource-handling defect; the resulting memory exhaustion is the consequence, not the cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the buffer is grown to the attacker-declared length up front, before verifying that the stream actually contains that many bytes. Trigger: a short invalid ASN.1 encoding with a large length field. Consequence: large memory allocation and denial of service via memory consumption.

commit_msg:
KVM: x86: Reload pit counters for all channels when restoring state

Currently if userspace restores the pit counters with a count of 0
on channels 1 or 2 and the guest attempts to read the count on those
channels, then KVM will perform a mod of 0 and crash.  This will ensure
that 0 values are converted to 65536 as per the spec.

This is CVE-2015-7513.

Signed-off-by: Andy Honig <ahonig@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tkvm_pit_load_count(kvm, 0, kvm->arch.vpit->pit_state.channels[0].count, start);'], 'added_lines': ['\tint i;', '\tfor (i = 0; i < 3; i++)', '\t\tkvm_pit_load_count(kvm, i, kvm->arch.vpit->pit_state.channels[i].count, start);']}
description: arch/x86/kvm/x86.c in the Linux kernel before 4.4 does not reset the PIT counter values during state restoration, which allows guest OS users to cause a denial of service (divide-by-zero error and host OS crash) via a zero value, related to the kvm_vm_ioctl_set_pit and kvm_vm_ioctl_set_pit2 functions.

code_evidence: Copies all three PIT channel states, including attacker-supplied count values, from userspace ps->channels into the kernel's pit_state.
Loads only channel 0's count via kvm_pit_load_count; channels 1 and 2 counts are copied but never reloaded/validated, so a restored count of 0 remains in kernel state.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is a divide-by-zero driven by an unvalidated zero counter value, matching CWE-369. It is not merely a missing range check; the concrete consequence is division by zero in the PIT count path, affecting host availability.

evidence_lines.code:
memcpy(&kvm->arch.vpit->pit_state.channels, &ps->channels,
sizeof(kvm->arch.vpit->pit_state.channels));
kvm_pit_load_count(kvm, 0, kvm->arch.vpit->pit_state.channels[0].count, start);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Userspace can restore PIT channel 1 or 2 with a count of 0; because only channel 0 is reloaded, the zero persists. When the guest later reads that channel's count, the PIT handler computes a modulo/division by the zero count, causing a divide-by-zero that crashes the host (DoS).

description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. The implementation of `tf.raw_ops.AvgPool3DGrad` is vulnerable to a heap buffer overflow. The implementation(https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/d80ffba9702dc19d1fac74fc4b766b3fa1ee976b/tensorflow/core/kernels/pooling_ops_3d.cc#L376-L450) assumes that the `orig_input_shape` and `grad` tensors have similar first and last dimensions but does not check that this assumption is validated. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.5.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.4.2, TensorFlow 2.3.3, TensorFlow 2.2.3 and TensorFlow 2.1.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: The function zeroes output and derives each spatial input_size from tensor_in_shape.dim_size(3..1), but never validates that tensor_in_shape's batch (dim 0) and channel (dim 4) dimensions match out_backprop's.
The loops iterate over out_backprop.dim_size(3..1) and build src slices from out_backprop.shape() with fixed first/last slices {0,-1}, while dst slices are built from tensor_in_shape.

FillIndicesAndSizes on out_backprop.shape() and tensor_in_shape yields indices/sizes, and the output tensor slice is written via += slices.broadcast(bcast), so mismatched outer dimensions produce inconsistent slice sizes and an out-of-bounds write into output.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked dimension assumption leads directly to writing beyond the output buffer's bounds, which is the definition of CWE-787. It is not merely an incorrect-shape rejection (CWE-1284); the supported consequence is an out-of-bounds heap write.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the launch kernel assumes out_backprop and tensor_in_shape share batch and channel dimensions without checking them. Trigger: callers supply orig_input_shape whose first or last dimension differs from grad. The mismatched slice extents then cause the broadcasted accumulation to write past the intended output buffer, corrupting heap memory (crash or potential code execution).

commit_msg:
Preserve GSS context on init/accept failure

After gss_init_sec_context() or gss_accept_sec_context() has created a
context, don't delete the mechglue context on failures from subsequent
calls, even if the mechanism deletes the mech-specific context (which
is allowed by RFC 2744 but not preferred).  Check for union contexts
with no mechanism context in each GSS function which accepts a
gss_ctx_id_t.

CVE-2017-11462:

RFC 2744 permits a GSS-API implementation to delete an existing
security context on a second or subsequent call to
gss_init_sec_context() or gss_accept_sec_context() if the call results
in an error.  This API behavior has been found to be dangerous,
leading to the possibility of memory errors in some callers.  For
safety, GSS-API implementations should instead preserve existing
security contexts on error until the caller deletes them.

All versions of MIT krb5 prior to this change may delete acceptor
contexts on error.  Versions 1.13.4 through 1.13.7, 1.14.1 through
1.14.5, and 1.15 through 1.15.1 may also delete initiator contexts on
error.

commit_msg:
Fix jpeg_skip_scanlines() segfault w/merged upsamp

The additional segfault mentioned in #244 was due to the fact that
the merged upsamplers use a different private structure than the
non-merged upsamplers.  jpeg_skip_scanlines() was assuming the latter, so
when merged upsampling was enabled, jpeg_skip_scanlines() clobbered one
of the IDCT method pointers in the merged upsampler's private structure.

For reasons unknown, the test image in #441 did not encounter this
segfault (too small?), but it encountered an issue similar to the one
fixed in 5bc43c7821df982f65aa1c738f67fbf7cba8bd69, whereby it was
necessary to set up a dummy postprocessing function in
read_and_discard_scanlines() when merged upsampling was enabled.
Failing to do so caused either a segfault in merged_2v_upsample() (due
to a NULL pointer being passed to jcopy_sample_rows()) or an error
("Corrupt JPEG data: premature end of data segment"), depending on the
number of scanlines skipped and whether the first scanline skipped was
an odd- or even-numbered row.

Fixes #441
Fixes #244 (for real this time)

description: A crafted input file could cause a null pointer dereference in jcopy_sample_rows() when processed by libjpeg-turbo.

code_evidence: Line 7 casts cinfo->upsample to my_upsample_ptr, but merged upsamplers actually use my_merged_upsample_ptr, so field offsets are misinterpreted.

When spare_full is set (line 10), size is read from upsample->out_row_width (line 11) and jcopy_sample_rows copies from upsample->spare_row (lines 14-15); with the wrong struct type, spare_row/spare_full are not the merged upsampler's actual fields.
In the else branch, work_ptrs[1] = upsample->spare_row (line 29) and upmethod is invoked (line 32); a mis-resolved spare_row or upmethod pointer can be NULL.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe operation is a pointer dereference (spare_row passed to jcopy_sample_rows, or upmethod call) that can be NULL due to the struct-type mismatch, matching CWE-476. This is a NULL dereference rather than a simple out-of-bounds read because the immediate fault is on a NULL pointer value.

evidence_lines.code: my_upsample_ptr upsample = (my_upsample_ptr)cinfo->upsample;

work_ptrs[1] = upsample->spare_row;
(*upsample->upmethod) (cinfo, input_buf, *in_row_group_ctr, work_ptrs);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function assumes the non-merged upsampler private layout, but when merged upsampling is enabled the private structure differs, so field accesses like spare_row and upmethod resolve to wrong/NULL values. Trigger: a crafted JPEG whose skipping path sets spare_full or leaves spare_row NULL, then jcopy_sample_rows or the upmethod call dereferences the NULL pointer, causing a crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
Skip 0-length ACL fields

Currently, it is possible to create an archive that crashes bsdtar
with a malformed ACL:

Program received signal SIGSEGV, Segmentation fault.
archive_acl_from_text_l (acl=<optimised out>, text=0x7e2e92 "", want_type=<optimised out>, sc=<optimised out>) at libarchive/archive_acl.c:1726
1726				switch (*s) {
(gdb) p n
$1 = 1
(gdb) p field[n]
$2 = {start = 0x0, end = 0x0}

Stop this by checking that the length is not zero before beginning
the switch statement.

I am pretty sure this is the bug mentioned in the qsym paper [1],
and I was able to replicate it with a qsym + AFL + afl-rb setup.

[1] https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenixsecurity18/presentation/yun
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\tif (len == 0) {', '\t\t\t\tret = ARCHIVE_WARN;', '\t\t\t\tcontinue;', '\t\t\t}', '']}
description: libarchive version commit 379867ecb330b3a952fb7bfa7bffb7bbd5547205 onwards (release v3.3.0 onwards) contains a CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference vulnerability in ACL parser - libarchive/archive_acl.c, archive_acl_from_text_l() that can result in Crash/DoS. This attack appear to be exploitable via the victim must open a specially crafted archive file.

code_evidence: After splitting the ACL text into fields, the code sets s = field[n].start, st = field[n].start + 1, len = field[n].end - field[n].start, then immediately dereferences *s in the switch.
When a field is empty, start and end are equal (or both set to NULL by the fill loop at lines 41-42), so len is 0 and s may be NULL; the switch dereference then has no validity check.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe operation is a direct dereference of a pointer expected to be valid but which can be NULL for zero-length ACL fields, matching CWE-476. The fix's len==0 guard confirms the missing non-NULL/non-empty constraint; this is a NULL dereference rather than an out-of-bounds read.

evidence_lines.code:
for (n = fields; n < numfields; ++n)
field[n].start = field[n].end = NULL;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the parser computes a field length but dereferences the field pointer without ensuring the field is non-empty. Trigger: a crafted archive containing an ACL entry with a zero-length field (e.g. leading ':' or empty text) makes field[n].start NULL/equal to end. Consequence: *s dereferences NULL, causing a SIGSEGV crash (denial of service) when opening the archive.

commit_msg:
Fixed njs_vmcode_interpreter() when await fails.

Previously, while interpreting a user function, njs_vmcode_interpreter()
might return prematurely when an error happens in await instruction.
This is not correct because the current frame has to be unwound (or
exception caught) first.

The fix is to exit through only 5 appropriate exit points to ensure
proper unwinding.

The patch correctly fixes issue reported in 07ef6c1f04f1 (0.7.3).

This closes #506 issue on Github.

description: Nginx NJS v0.7.4 was discovered to contain an out-of-bounds read via njs_scope_value at njs_scope.h.

code_evidence: Line 13 obtains value via njs_scope_value/njs_scope_valid_value using await->retval as index without visible bounds checking here; line 14 only checks the returned pointer for NULL, returning NJS_ERROR at line 15, and the patch adds an error report before that return.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the weakness is a read past the intended buffer boundary during the scope-value lookup, with only a post-hoc NULL guard rather than an index/bounds constraint.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the scope value lookup indexed by await->retval can read outside the intended scope buffer; the NULL check at line 14 does not validate the index before the read occurs. Trigger: an invalid/out-of-range await->retval. Supported consequence: out-of-bounds read of scope memory, potentially yielding an invalid pointer that is then dereferenced by downstream promise operations.

commit_msg:
When running concurrent iptables rules replacement with data, the per CPU
sequence count is checked after the assignment of the new information.
The sequence count is used to synchronize with the packet path without the
use of any explicit locking. If there are any packets in the packet path using
the table information, the sequence count is incremented to an odd value and
is incremented to an even after the packet process completion.

The new table value assignment is followed by a write memory barrier so every
CPU should see the latest value. If the packet path has started with the old
table information, the sequence counter will be odd and the iptables
replacement will wait till the sequence count is even prior to freeing the
old table info.

However, this assumes that the new table information assignment and the memory
barrier is actually executed prior to the counter check in the replacement
thread. If CPU decides to execute the assignment later as there is no user of
the table information prior to the sequence check, the packet path in another
CPU may use the old table information. The replacement thread would then free
the table information under it leading to a use after free in the packet
processing context-

Unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at virtual
address 000000000000008e
pc : ip6t_do_table+0x5d0/0x89c
lr : ip6t_do_table+0x5b8/0x89c
ip6t_do_table+0x5d0/0x89c
ip6table_filter_hook+0x24/0x30
nf_hook_slow+0x84/0x120
ip6_input+0x74/0xe0
ip6_rcv_finish+0x7c/0x128
ipv6_rcv+0xac/0xe4
__netif_receive_skb+0x84/0x17c
process_backlog+0x15c/0x1b8
napi_poll+0x88/0x284
net_rx_action+0xbc/0x23c
__do_softirq+0x20c/0x48c

This could be fixed by forcing instruction order after the new table
information assignment or by switching to RCU for the synchronization.

Fixes: 80055dab5de0 ("netfilter: x_tables: make xt_replace_table wait until old rules are not used anymore")
Reported-by: Sean Tranchetti <stranche@codeaurora.org>
Reported-by: kernel test robot <lkp@intel.com>
Suggested-by: Florian Westphal <fw@strlen.de>
Signed-off-by: Subash Abhinov Kasiviswanathan <subashab@codeaurora.org>
Signed-off-by: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tstruct xt_table_info *private = t->private;'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tstruct xt_table_info *private = xt_table_get_private_protected(t);']}
description: An issue was discovered in netfilter in the Linux kernel before 5.10. There can be a use-after-free in the packet processing context, because the per-CPU sequence count is mishandled during concurrent iptables rules replacement. This could be exploited with the CAP_NET_ADMIN capability in an unprivileged namespace. NOTE: cc00bca was reverted in 5.12.

code_evidence: xt_find_table_lock returns the table t, and line 17 reads t->private directly without the protected accessor, then dereferences private->size at line 18 and passes private to copy_entries_to_user at lines 19-20. The table is only unlocked at line 24, after these uses.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences t->private and private->size after the replacement thread may have freed that xt_table_info, which is exactly reusing freed memory (CWE-416). This is not merely a data race: the supported harm is access to memory whose lifetime ended.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the per-CPU sequence-count synchronization does not guarantee the new table-info assignment is ordered before the counter check, so a concurrent rules replacement can free the old xt_table_info while this path still holds and dereferences t->private. Trigger: concurrent iptables replacement with packet-path/readers accessing the table. Supported consequence: use-after-free read of private->size/entries, leading to crash or memory disclosure.

commit_msg:
Fixed Error() instance dumping when "name" prop is not primitive.

Previously, njs_error_to_string2() might be invoked with error argument
pointing to vm->retval.  When "name" prop was not primitive vm->retval
might be overwritten.  As a result error pointer might be referencing a
primitive value.  In turn the second call of njs_object_property()
received an invalid object pointer because it expects only object value
types.

The fix is to ensure that error object pointer is never overwritten.

This closes #615 issue on Github.

description: Nginx NJS v0.7.10 was discovered to contain a segmentation violation via the function njs_lvlhsh_find at src/njs_lvlhsh.c.

code_evidence: Guard confirms desc must be an object before use, but the raw desc value is later passed directly to njs_object_property().
njs_object_property() is invoked with desc rather than a validated njs_object_t pointer; the same raw desc is reused for the "get"/"set" lookups.
The "value" lookup likewise passes desc, so the object pointer expected by the callee depends on desc still holding an object type at call time.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe dereference of a stale/non-object pointer during property lookup causes reads through an invalid object, matching CWE-125 (out-of-bounds read). It is not a write-side corruption (CWE-787); the supported impact is an invalid read and crash.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function passes the descriptor value desc to njs_object_property(), which expects an object pointer, without re-validating its type after prior property lookups. If a lookup (e.g. the "name" property) overwrites the underlying value so desc no longer holds an object, subsequent lookups dereference an invalid/non-object pointer. Consequence: out-of-bounds/invalid memory read leading to a crash (segmentation violation).

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  int  was_read;', '    ', '  free(line);'], 'added_lines': ['  int  was_read, backslashed;', '    backslashed = 0;', '          backslashed = 1;', '', '  if(!backslashed)', '    free(line);']}
description: The foreach function in ext/ccsv.c in Ccsv 1.1.0 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (double free and application crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted file.

code_evidence: When an escaped line is joined, new_line is allocated and assigned to line (line 84), then line itself is freed at line 88 before continue.
The final free(line) at line 157 then runs on the same pointer that was already freed in the join path, since line still references the freed new_line buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function calls free() on the same address twice: once inside the join branch and again at function exit. This matches CWE-415 Double Free; it is not merely a use-after-free because the second explicit free of the same pointer is the core defect.

evidence_lines.code: free(line);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the escaped-line join path frees line after reassigning it to the newly allocated new_line buffer, but does not clear or replace the pointer, so the loop-exit cleanup frees it again. commit_msg:
patch 8.1.0633: crash when out of memory while opening a terminal window

Problem:    Crash when out of memory while opening a terminal window.
Solution:   Handle out-of-memory more gracefully.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  if(buffer)', '    vterm_allocator_free(screen->vt, buffer);'], 'added_lines': ['  vterm_allocator_free(screen->vt, buffer);']}
description: libvterm through 0+bzr726, as used in Vim and other products, mishandles certain out-of-memory conditions, leading to a denial of service (application crash), related to screen.c, state.c, and vterm.c.

code_evidence: Line 3 allocates new_buffer via vterm_allocator_malloc but never checks whether the allocation returned NULL.
Line 7 computes new_cell from new_buffer and lines 8-9 dereference it when copying existing cells, with no NULL guard on new_buffer.
Lines 16-17 free the old buffer unconditionally; the patch's change only removes the if(buffer) guard around the free, not the missing allocation check.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences a pointer (new_buffer) that it expects to be valid but may be NULL after a failed allocation, which is exactly CWE-476. The defect is not a use-after-free or buffer overflow; the unchecked NULL from malloc is the direct weakness.

evidence_lines.code: ScreenCell *new_buffer = vterm_allocator_malloc(screen->vt, sizeof(ScreenCell) * new_rows * new_cols);

if(buffer)
vterm_allocator_free(screen->vt, buffer);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Under an out-of-memory condition, vterm_allocator_malloc returns NULL, but realloc_buffer proceeds to compute new_cell and dereference it in the copy loop, causing a crash. The root cause is the missing NULL check on the allocation result; the supported consequence is a denial-of-service crash.

commit_msg:
Fix #354: Signed Integer Overflow gd_io.c

GD2 stores the number of horizontal and vertical chunks as words (i.e. 2
byte unsigned). These values are multiplied and assigned to an int when
reading the image, what can cause integer overflows. We have to avoid
that, and also make sure that either chunk count is actually greater
than zero. If illegal chunk counts are detected, we bail out from
reading the image.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (*ncx <= 0 || *ncy <= 0 || *ncx > INT_MAX / *ncy) {', '\t\t\tGD2_DBG(printf ("Illegal chunk counts: %d * %d\\n", *ncx, *ncy));', '\t\t\tgoto fail1;', '\t\t}']}
description: Integer overflow in gd_io.c in the GD Graphics Library (aka libgd) before 2.2.4 allows remote attackers to have unspecified impact via vectors involving the number of horizontal and vertical chunks in an image.

code_evidence: For compressed GD2 images, *ncx and *ncy are attacker-controlled 16-bit word values read from the file (lines 61,65). Line 70 computes nc = (*ncx) * (*ncy) in a signed int with no prior range check, so the product can overflow/wrap before it is used as an allocation count for cidx and as the loop bound at line 83.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe arithmetic at line 70 is exactly an integer overflow/wraparound: the code assumes *ncx * *ncy always yields a valid positive int, but the multiplication can exceed INT_MAX and wrap. This matches CWE-190 rather than a pure out-of-bounds write, since the overflow is the root cause feeding the size calculation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the multiplication of two chunk counts is performed in a signed int without validating that the product fits in int. Trigger: a crafted GD2 header with large horizontal/vertical chunk counts. Consequence: nc wraps to a small or negative value, so the downstream allocation and index loop operate on an incorrect size, leading to out-of-bounds memory access or resource exhaustion.

commit_msg: properly cast double to size_t (https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/issues/6341)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    height=(size_t) floor(metrics.ascent-metrics.descent+0.5);'], 'added_lines': ['    height=CastDoubleToUnsigned(metrics.ascent-metrics.descent+0.5);']}
description: A vulnerability was found in ImageMagick. This security flaw ouccers as an undefined behaviors of casting double to size_t in svg, mvg and other coders (recurring bugs of CVE-2022-32546).

code_evidence: Line 103 converts the double expression metrics.ascent-metrics.descent+0.5, after floor, directly to size_t. metrics is populated by GetTypeMetrics at line 102 using font/text metrics, so the value depends on input-controlled text and font data. An out-of-range or negative double makes the (size_t) cast undefined behavior; the patched version replaces this cast with CastDoubleToUnsigned. height is then used in offset computations and in the rectangle primitive at line 257.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The flaw is an integer conversion whose result can wrap or be undefined, matching CWE-190 (integer overflow/wraparound) when a value cannot be represented in the target integer type. It is distinguished from a pure type-confusion issue because the unsafe operation is numeric range conversion, not misuse of a pointer or object type.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: an unchecked floating-point-to-unsigned conversion of font metrics into height. Trigger: crafted text or font metrics yielding a value outside the size_t range. Consequence: undefined behavior/incorrect height, which propagates into drawing offsets and a rectangle primitive, potentially causing instability or memory corruption.

commit_msg:
Sanity check ticket length.

If a ticket callback changes the HMAC digest to SHA512 the existing
sanity checks are not sufficient and an attacker could perform a DoS
attack with a malformed ticket. Add additional checks based on
HMAC size.

Thanks to Shi Lei for reporting this bug.

CVE-2016-6302

Reviewed-by: Viktor Dukhovni <viktor@openssl.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    /* Need at least keyname + iv + some encrypted data */', '    if (eticklen < 48)', '        return 2;'], 'added_lines': ['', '        goto err;', '    }', '    /* Sanity check ticket length: must exceed keyname + IV + HMAC */', '    if (eticklen <=', '        TLSEXT_KEYNAME_LENGTH + EVP_CIPHER_CTX_iv_length(ctx) + mlen) {', '        ret = 2;']}
description: The tls_decrypt_ticket function in ssl/t1_lib.c in OpenSSL before 1.1.0 does not consider the HMAC size during validation of the ticket length, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service via a ticket that is too short.

code_evidence: The only length check on the attacker-supplied ticket is the fixed threshold eticklen < 48, which does not account for the actual HMAC digest size returned by HMAC_size(hctx).
mlen is computed from HMAC_size and, when positive, subtracted from eticklen without verifying that eticklen still covers keyname, IV and HMAC.

The HMAC comparison and the pointer/offset computation at etick + 16 + iv_length, followed by OPENSSL_malloc(eticklen) and EVP_DecryptUpdate over eticklen bytes, rely on the unvalidated remaining length.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function accepts externally supplied ticket data but fails to validate that its length is sufficient for the actual keyname, IV and HMAC sizes, which is improper input validation of a size property. The consequence is a DoS, consistent with CWE-20's availability scope.

evidence_lines.code:
if (eticklen < 48)
return 2;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the ticket length is validated against a hard-coded constant instead of the derived HMAC size, so a ticket callback that selects SHA512 makes mlen large while eticklen stays small. Trigger: a remote attacker sends a too-short malformed ticket. The derived remaining length underflows or becomes invalid, leading to out-of-bounds reads or excessive allocation in the decrypt path, causing a denial of service.

commit_msg:
Fix EditingStyle::mergeStyle()'s handling of custom properties

This patch fixes the logic of EditingStyle::mergeStyle() to correctly
handle custom properties. Currently it serializes the CSSValue and then
reparses it, which, aside from being inefficient, doesn't work for
custom properties as the custom property name is lost (since we only
have the enum value CSSPropertyVariable).

BUG=622420

Review-Url: https://codereview.chromium.org/2103043004
Cr-Commit-Position: refs/heads/master@{#410614}
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            m_mutableStyle->setProperty(property.id(), property.value().cssText(), property.isImportant());'], 'added_lines': ['            m_mutableStyle->setProperty(property.toCSSProperty());']}
description: The EditingStyle::mergeStyle function in WebKit/Source/core/editing/EditingStyle.cpp in Blink, as used in Google Chrome before 53.0.2785.89 on Windows and OS X and before 53.0.2785.92 on Linux, mishandles custom properties, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted web site that leverages "type confusion" in the StylePropertySerializer class.

code_evidence: Line 11 obtains a PropertyReference that may represent a custom property whose name is not recoverable from property.id() (CSSPropertyVariable). Line 12 looks up the value by enum id, and line 21 reconstructs the property via property.id() and property.value().cssText(), dropping the custom property name and relying on enum-based identity.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This matches CWE-704: the function incorrectly converts a property reference into a generic enum-plus-text form, losing its actual type/identity rather than preserving the custom-property representation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The code treats a PropertyReference as if its enum id plus serialized cssText fully describes the property, but custom properties carry a name distinct from the CSSPropertyVariable enum. On a crafted stylesheet containing custom properties, the merge path re-serializes and re-parses with the wrong identity, producing type/identity confusion in the serializer and corrupting style state, with denial-of-service or unspecified impact.

commit_msg:
Allow fuse device clones to refer to be distinguished.  This patch just
adds the infrastructure by associating a separate "struct fuse_dev" with
each clone.

Signed-off-by: Miklos Szeredi <mszeredi@suse.cz>
Reviewed-by: Ashish Samant <ashish.samant@oracle.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tnew->private_data = fuse_conn_get(fc);'], 'added_lines': ['\tstruct fuse_dev *fud;', '', '\tfud = fuse_dev_alloc(fc);', '\tif (!fud)', '\t\treturn -ENOMEM;', '', '\tnew->private_data = fud;']}
description: Memory leak in the cuse_channel_release function in fs/fuse/cuse.c in the Linux kernel before 4.4 allows local users to cause a denial of service (memory consumption) or possibly have unspecified other impact by opening /dev/cuse many times.

code_evidence: fuse_device_clone stores a reference obtained from fuse_conn_get(fc) into new->private_data at line 5, but the function returns immediately after line 6 with no failure path and no record of the allocation beyond private_data; there is no release logic in this function. The only guard is the existing private_data check at lines 3-4.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-399 covers improper management of system resources; the acquired reference at line 5 is a resource whose lifetime is not balanced within this function, matching that category. It is not a generic input-validation issue, since the flaw is resource acquisition without corresponding release.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function acquires a fuse_conn reference via fuse_conn_get and assigns it to the cloned file's private_data, but the management of that reference is left entirely to other code paths. If the associated release path does not drop the reference obtained here (as the described cuse_channel_release leak indicates), repeated cloning via opening /dev/cuse accumulates unreleased references, causing resource exhaustion/denial of service.

commit_msg:
usb: gadget: f_fs: Fix use-after-free

When using asynchronous read or write operations on the USB endpoints the
issuer of the IO request is notified by calling the ki_complete() callback
of the submitted kiocb when the URB has been completed.

Calling this ki_complete() callback will free kiocb. Make sure that the
structure is no longer accessed beyond that point, otherwise undefined
behaviour might occur.

Fixes: 2e4c7553cd6f ("usb: gadget: f_fs: add aio support")
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org> # v3.15+
Signed-off-by: Lars-Peter Clausen <lars@metafoo.de>
Signed-off-by: Felipe Balbi <felipe.balbi@linux.intel.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (io_data->ffs->ffs_eventfd &&', '\t    !(io_data->kiocb->ki_flags & IOCB_EVENTFD))', '\tio_data->kiocb->private = NULL;'], 'added_lines': ['\tbool kiocb_has_eventfd = io_data->kiocb->ki_flags & IOCB_EVENTFD;', '\tif (io_data->ffs->ffs_eventfd && !kiocb_has_eventfd)']}
description: Use-after-free vulnerability in the ffs_user_copy_worker function in drivers/usb/gadget/function/f_fs.c in the Linux kernel before 4.5.3 allows local users to gain privileges by accessing an I/O data structure after a certain callback call.

code_evidence: Line 14 invokes io_data->kiocb->ki_complete(), which per the commit frees the kiocb. Lines 15-16 then re-read io_data->kiocb->ki_flags, and line 19 writes io_data->kiocb->private = NULL, both dereferencing the kiocb after its completion callback has released it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences and writes through io_data->kiocb after ki_complete() has freed it, which is precisely reuse of freed memory, matching CWE-416. This is not merely a NULL/dangling pointer check; the object is explicitly released by the callback before the later accesses.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the completion callback ki_complete() frees the kiocb, but the worker keeps using the io_data->kiocb pointer afterward to test ki_flags and clear private. Trigger: any asynchronous read/write completion reaching this worker. Consequence: use-after-free read/write on freed kiocb memory, enabling memory corruption or privilege escalation.

commit_msg: fixed #2138
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t\tu32 b64_size;', '\t\t\t\tb64 = (char *)gf_malloc(samp->dataLength*3);', '\t\t\t\tb64_size = gf_base64_encode(samp->data, samp->dataLength, b64, samp->dataLength*3);', '\t\t\t\tif (b64_size != (u32)-1) {', '\t\t\t\t\tb64[b64_size] = 0;', '\t\t\t\t\tgf_fprintf(vtt, "%s\\n", b64);', '\t\t\t\t}'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t\tu32 b64_size = samp->dataLength*2 + 3;', '\t\t\t\tb64 = (char *)gf_malloc(sizeof(char)*b64_size);', '\t\t\t\tb64_size = gf_base64_encode(samp->data, samp->dataLength, b64, b64_size);', '\t\t\t\tb64[b64_size] = 0;', '\t\t\t\tgf_fprintf(vtt, "%s\\n", b64);']}
description: GPAC 2.0 allows a heap-based buffer overflow in gf_base64_encode. It can be triggered via MP4Box.

code_evidence: The non-text branch allocates b64 with gf_malloc(samp->dataLength*3) and passes the same size as the output capacity to gf_base64_encode. The returned b64_size is then used to write the NUL terminator at b64[b64_size]. If the encoder returns a size equal to or greater than the allocation (e.g., truncation or an encoder that reports required length), this write is out of bounds; the only guard is b64_size != (u32)-1.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes past the end of the intended heap buffer b64, matching CWE-787 (out-of-bounds write). Contrast with CWE-125 (out-of-bounds read): the unsafe operation is a write at an unvalidated index, not a read.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the terminator index b64_size is trusted without verifying it is smaller than the allocated buffer size. Trigger: a sample whose base64 encoding produces a size at or beyond the allocated capacity. Consequence: a heap-based out-of-bounds write of a NUL byte, corrupting adjacent heap memory (potential crash or code execution).

commit_msg:
Fix ANSI Escape Sequence Injection vulns via DWARF ##vuln

* Reported by @solid-snail via huntrdev
* BountyID: 583133af-7ae6-4a21-beef-a4b0182cf82e
* Reproducer: dwarf_test_func_patched
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\tconst char *name = attribute->string.content;', '\t\t\tsdb_set (sdb, "DW_AT_comp_dir", name, 0);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\tchar *name = strdup (attribute->string.content);', '\t\t\tr_str_ansi_strip (name);', "\t\t\tr_str_replace_ch (name, '\\n', 0, true);", "\t\t\tr_str_replace_ch (name, '\\t', 0, true);", '\t\t\tsdb_set_owned (sdb, "DW_AT_comp_dir", name, 0);']}
description: Failure to Sanitize Special Elements into a Different Plane (Special Element Injection) in GitHub repository radareorg/radare2 prior to 5.8.2.

code_evidence: DW_AT_comp_dir string content from parsed DWARF is passed unmodified into sdb_set under the key DW_AT_comp_dir, with no neutralization of ANSI escapes or control characters.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-74 fits because externally-influenced DWARF input is placed into a record used by a downstream component without neutralizing special elements that alter interpretation. It is not just a generic string issue: the stored value crosses a trust boundary into an interpreting consumer, matching injection semantics.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The compiler-unit directory string is attacker-influenced DWARF data; it is stored raw into the SDB record. A downstream consumer that prints this value interprets embedded ANSI escape sequences, allowing terminal/control-sequence injection. Root cause is missing sanitization of special elements before the value enters the downstream data store; consequence is escape-sequence injection in output consumers.

commit_msg:
acpi: Disable ACPI table override if securelevel is set

From the kernel documentation (initrd_table_override.txt):

  If the ACPI_INITRD_TABLE_OVERRIDE compile option is true, it is possible
  to override nearly any ACPI table provided by the BIOS with an
  instrumented, modified one.

When securelevel is set, the kernel should disallow any unauthenticated
changes to kernel space. ACPI tables contain code invoked by the kernel, so
do not allow ACPI tables to be overridden if securelevel is set.

Signed-off-by: Linn Crosetto <linn@hpe.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tif (get_securelevel() > 0) {', '\t\tpr_notice(PREFIX', '\t\t\t"securelevel enabled, ignoring table override\\n");', '\t\treturn;', '\t}', '']}
description: The Linux kernel, as used in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7.2 and Red Hat Enterprise MRG 2 and when booted with UEFI Secure Boot enabled, allows local users to bypass intended Secure Boot restrictions and execute untrusted code by appending ACPI tables to the initrd.

code_evidence: The function processes caller-supplied initrd data (data, size) and, after parsing ACPI tables, proceeds to allocate and reserve kernel memory at acpi_tables_addr without checking any privilege or securelevel state.
Only a null/empty-input check and a table_nr==0 early return guard the path; no authorization gate exists before the override work begins.
memblock_find_in_range, memblock_reserve and arch_reserve_mem_area commit kernel memory to the attacker-influenced ACPI tables, which the kernel later executes.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing permission/privilege restriction on a security-relevant operation (ACPI table override) fits CWE-264's permissions/privileges/access-control category. It is not a memory-safety flaw; the weakness is the absent access-control constraint, not malformed parsing.

evidence_lines.code:
if (data == NULL || size == 0)
return;

if (table_nr == 0)
return;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the override path lacks any securelevel/privilege check before consuming attacker-supplied initrd ACPI tables. Trigger: a local user boots with a modified initrd containing crafted ACPI tables while securelevel is set. Consequence: the kernel reserves and later invokes untrusted ACPI table code, bypassing intended Secure Boot restrictions.

commit_msg:
speakup: Do not let the line discipline be used several times

Speakup has only one speakup_tty variable to store the tty it is managing. This
makes sense since its codebase currently assumes that there is only one user who
controls the screen reading.

That however means that we have to forbid using the line discipline several
times, otherwise the second closure would try to free a NULL ldisc_data, leading to

general protection fault: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN PTI
RIP: 0010:spk_ttyio_ldisc_close+0x2c/0x60
Call Trace:
 tty_ldisc_release+0xa2/0x340
 tty_release_struct+0x17/0xd0
 tty_release+0x9d9/0xcc0
 __fput+0x231/0x740
 task_work_run+0x12c/0x1a0
 do_exit+0x9b5/0x2230
 ? release_task+0x1240/0x1240
 ? __do_page_fault+0x562/0xa30
 do_group_exit+0xd5/0x2a0
 __x64_sys_exit_group+0x35/0x40
 do_syscall_64+0x89/0x2b0
 ? page_fault+0x8/0x30
 entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x44/0xa9

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Reported-by: 秦世松 <qinshisong1205@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Samuel Thibault <samuel.thibault@ens-lyon.org>
Tested-by: Shisong Qin <qinshisong1205@gmail.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20201110183541.fzgnlwhjpgqzjeth@function
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (!ldisc_data)'], 'added_lines': ['', '\tmutex_lock(&speakup_tty_mutex);', '\tif (speakup_tty) {', '\t\tmutex_unlock(&speakup_tty_mutex);', '\t\treturn -EBUSY;', '\t}', '\tif (!ldisc_data) {', '\t\tspeakup_tty = NULL;', '\t\tmutex_unlock(&speakup_tty_mutex);', '\t}', '\tmutex_unlock(&speakup_tty_mutex);']}
description: An issue was discovered in drivers/accessibility/speakup/spk_ttyio.c in the Linux kernel through 5.9.9. Local attackers on systems with the speakup driver could cause a local denial of service attack, aka CID-d41227544427. This occurs because of an invalid free when the line discipline is used more than once.

code_evidence: The function unconditionally assigns the global speakup_tty = tty (line 6) without checking whether a previous line-discipline instance already registered a tty. It then allocates ldisc_data (line 7), returns -ENOMEM on failure (lines 8-9), or stores it in speakup_tty->disc_data (line 12). On a second open, the global is overwritten, so the second close frees/clears the shared ldisc_data while the first tty still references it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The supported consequence is release of an invalid pointer: the shared ldisc_data is freed twice or freed via a stale reference, matching CWE-763 (Release of Invalid Pointer or Reference). This is not merely a NULL-pointer dereference; the defect is incorrect release of a resource through aliased state.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: no mutual exclusion or single-instance constraint on the global speakup_tty, so opening the line discipline twice overwrites the shared pointer. Trigger: a local user attaches the ldisc a second time; the second close releases the shared ldisc_data, leaving a stale/NULL reference, and the first close then performs an invalid free, causing a general protection fault and local DoS.

commit_msg: SA79000 advisory fix
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['#ifdef LIBRAW_LIBRARY_BUILD', '  if(!image)', '    throw LIBRAW_EXCEPTION_IO_CORRUPT;', '#endif']}
description: An error within the "LibRaw::unpack()" function (src/libraw_cxx.cpp) in LibRaw versions prior to 0.18.7 can be exploited to trigger a NULL pointer dereference.

code_evidence: The nested loops over height and width index into image[row * width + col] and pass the result by reference to read_shorts without any check that image is non-NULL; the function relies entirely on the caller to provide a valid buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The code dereferences the image pointer that it expects to be valid but may be NULL, matching CWE-476. This is a NULL-dereference availability issue, not a buffer overflow, since the weakness is the missing NULL check rather than an out-of-bounds index.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function assumes image points to allocated memory. Trigger: image is NULL (e.g., failed allocation or unpack path entering this loader without a buffer) while height/width are nonzero. Consequence: the first read_shorts call dereferences NULL, causing a crash/DoS; the patch adds an explicit !image guard throwing IO_CORRUPT.

commit_msg:
btsdp: Keep offset advancing

hf_data_element_value is a FT_NONE, so we can add the item with
the expected length and get_hfi_length() will adjust the length
without throwing an exception. There's no need to add it with
zero length and call proto_item_set_len. Also, don't increment
the offset by 0 instead of the real length when there isn't
enough data in the packet, as that can lead to failing to advance
the offset.

When dissecting a sequence type (sequence or alternative) and
recursing into the sequence member, instead of using the main
packet tvb directly, create a subset using the indicated length
of the sequence. That will properly throw an exception if a
contained item is larger than the containing sequence, instead of
dissecting the same bytes as several different items (inside
the sequence recursively, as well in the outer loop.)

Fix #19258

description: An issue was discovered in Exiv2 0.27. There is infinite recursion at BigTiffImage::printIFD in the file bigtiffimage.cpp. This can be triggered by a crafted file. It allows an attacker to cause Denial of Service (Segmentation fault) or possibly have unspecified other impact.

commit_msg:
rar: file split across multi-part archives must match

Fuzzing uncovered some UAF and memory overrun bugs where a file in a
single file archive reported that it was split across multiple
volumes. This was caused by ppmd7 operations calling
rar_br_fillup. This would invoke rar_read_ahead, which would in some
situations invoke archive_read_format_rar_read_header.  That would
check the new file name against the old file name, and if they didn't
match up it would free the ppmd7 buffer and allocate a new
one. However, because the ppmd7 decoder wasn't actually done with the
buffer, it would continue to used the freed buffer. Both reads and
writes to the freed region can be observed.

This is quite tricky to solve: once the buffer has been freed it is
too late, as the ppmd7 decoder functions almost universally assume
success - there's no way for ppmd_read to signal error, nor are there
good ways for functions like Range_Normalise to propagate them. So we
can't detect after the fact that we're in an invalid state - e.g. by
checking rar->cursor, we have to prevent ourselves from ever ending up
there. So, when we are in the dangerous part or rar_read_ahead that
assumes a valid split, we set a flag force read_header to either go
down the path for split files or bail. This means that the ppmd7
decoder keeps a valid buffer and just runs out of data.

Found with a combination of AFL, afl-rb and qsym.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  else if (rar->filename_must_match)', '  {', '    archive_set_error(&a->archive, ARCHIVE_ERRNO_FILE_FORMAT,', '      "Mismatch of file parts split across multi-volume archive");', '    return (ARCHIVE_FATAL);', '  }']}
description: libarchive version commit 416694915449219d505531b1096384f3237dd6cc onwards (release v3.1.0 onwards) contains a CWE-416: Use After Free vulnerability in RAR decoder - libarchive/archive_read_support_format_rar.c that can result in Crash/DoS - it is unknown if RCE is possible. This attack appear to be exploitable via the victim must open a specially crafted RAR archive.

code_evidence: When the incoming filename matches the saved split-part name, the function returns early at line 269, leaving the existing ppmd7 context intact. If the name does not match, execution reaches lines 271-275, which reallocate filename_save and free rar->dbo, and then lines 345-346 call Ppmd7_Free and clear ppmd_valid. The new guard added in the diff prevents read_header from being re-entered via rar_read_ahead during ppmd7 decoding, which is what previously triggered this mismatch path and freed the buffer still in use.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is CWE-416: the ppmd7 buffer is freed at line 345 but the decoder continues to use it. The added filename_must_match guard blocks the re-entry that leads to the free, addressing the use-after-free rather than a separate weakness such as an out-of-bounds read.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: read_header can free the ppmd7 context (line 345) and rar->dbo while the ppmd7 decoder still holds pointers into them, because the split-name mismatch path does not check whether decoding is in progress. Trigger: a crafted multi-volume RAR whose parts have mismatched names causes rar_read_ahead to invoke read_header mid-decode. Consequence: the decoder reads and writes freed memory, causing UAF crash/DoS and possible memory corruption.

commit_msg: Bug #703 safeguard against corrupt packet lengths in checksum functions
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['fix_ipv6_checksums(tcpedit_t *tcpedit, struct pcap_pkthdr *pkthdr, ipv6_hdr_t *ip6_hdr)', '    if (pkthdr->caplen < sizeof(*ip6_hdr)) {', '        if (ip6_hdr->ip_len < ipv6_header_length(ip6_hdr, pkthdr->len)) {', '            tcpedit_setwarn(tcpedit, "Unable to checksum IPv6 packet with invalid length %u",', '                    ip6_hdr->ip_len);', '            return TCPEDIT_WARN;'], 'added_lines': ['fix_ipv6_checksums(tcpedit_t *tcpedit, struct pcap_pkthdr *pkthdr,', '                   ipv6_hdr_t *ip6_hdr, const size_t l2len)', '    if (pkthdr->caplen < (sizeof(*ip6_hdr) + l2len)) {', '        int ip6_len = ipv6_header_length(ip6_hdr, pkthdr->len, l2len);', '        if (ip6_hdr->ip_len < ip6_len) {', '            tcpedit_seterr(tcpedit, "Unable to checksum IPv6 packet with invalid length %u",', '                        ip6_hdr->ip_len);', '            return TCPEDIT_ERROR;']}
description: Tcpreplay v4.4.1 has a heap-based buffer overflow in do_checksum_math at /tcpedit/checksum.c.

code_evidence: The length guard only compares pkthdr->caplen against sizeof(*ip6_hdr); it does not account for l2len, so a captured frame whose caplen covers the IPv6 header but not the L2 prefix passes validation and ip6_hdr points into a shorter buffer.

When caplen == len, the code compares ip6_hdr->ip_len against ipv6_header_length(ip6_hdr, pkthdr->len) without the L2 offset and treats an invalid length only as a warning (TCPEDIT_WARN), so processing continues past a corrupt length.
do_checksum is then called with ip6_hdr->ip_nh and htons(ip6_hdr->ip_len); the attacker-controlled ip_len drives the checksum walker (do_checksum_math) beyond the allocated packet buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the unchecked length reaches a checksum routine that writes beyond the intended packet buffer. It is a concrete out-of-bounds write; the length-check flaw is the enabling cause, not merely a generic input-validation issue.

evidence_lines.code:
ret = do_checksum(tcpedit, (u_char *)ip6_hdr, ip6_hdr->ip_nh,
htons(ip6_hdr->ip_len));

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the caplen and ip_len validation omits the L2 offset (l2len), so a crafted packet with a corrupt IPv6 payload length is accepted. Trigger: caplen == len and an ip_len larger than the actual captured data. Consequence: do_checksum walks past the packet buffer and writes/reads out of bounds, giving a heap overflow.

commit_msg:
Bug 701785: fixed sanitizer heap-buffer-overflow in lprn_is_black().

In contrib/lips4/gdevlprn.c:lprn_is_black(), it seems that bpl is not
necessarily a multiple of lprn->nBw, so we need to explicitly avoid straying
into the next line's data.

This also avoids accessing beyond our buffer if we are already on the last
line, and so fixes the sanitizer error.

Fixes:
    ./sanbin/gs -sOutputFile=tmp -sDEVICE=lips2p ../bug-701785.pdf
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        for (x = 0; x < lprn->nBw; x++)'], 'added_lines': ['        for (x = 0; x < lprn->nBw; x++) {', "            /* bpl isn't necessarily a multiple of lprn->nBw, so", '            we need to explicitly stop after the last byte in this', "            line to avoid accessing either the next line's data or", '            going off the end of our buffer completely. This avoids', '            https://bugs.ghostscript.com/show_bug.cgi?id=701785. */', '            if (bx * lprn->nBw + x >= bpl)  break;', '        }']}
description: A buffer overflow vulnerability in lprn_is_black() in contrib/lips4/gdevlprn.c of Artifex Software GhostScript v9.50 allows a remote attacker to cause a denial of service via a crafted PDF file. This is fixed in v9.51.

code_evidence: Line 12 computes a row pointer with offset (y0 + y) * bpl + bx * lprn->nBw, then line 13 iterates x over nBw bytes and line 14 reads p[x] without checking whether bx * lprn->nBw + x has exceeded the row length bpl.

bpl from gdev_mem_bytes_per_scan_line (line 6) is not necessarily a multiple of lprn->nBw, so the pointer at line 12 plus the nBw-byte scan at line 13 can run past the current line into the next line or beyond the ImageBuf on the last line.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the loop reads past the end of the intended line/buffer, an out-of-bounds memory access driven by the missing bpl bound; the patch adds exactly the bx*nBw+x >= bpl guard. The access is a read rather than a write, but the code fails to bound the buffer access as described.

evidence_lines.code:
int bpl = gdev_mem_bytes_per_scan_line(pdev);
p = &lprn->ImageBuf[(y0 + y) * bpl + bx * lprn->nBw];

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the inner loop bound nBw is used without constraining the column offset against the actual bytes-per-line bpl. Trigger: a crafted PDF producing a block whose bpl is not a multiple of nBw, especially at the final line. Consequence: out-of-bounds read of ImageBuf, causing a sanitizer-detected heap-buffer-overflow and denial of service.

commit_msg:
Issue 4609 - CVE - info disclosure when authenticating

Description:  If you bind as a user that does not exist.  Error 49 is returned
              instead of error 32.  As error 32 discloses that the entry does
              not exist.  When you bind as an entry that does not have userpassword
              set then error 48 (inappropriate auth) is returned, but this
              discloses that the entry does indeed exist.  Instead we should
              always return error 49, even if the password is not set in the
              entry.  This way we do not disclose to an attacker if the Bind
              DN exists or not.

Relates: https://github.com/389ds/389-ds-base/issues/4609

Reviewed by: tbordaz(Thanks!)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        slapi_send_ldap_result(pb, LDAP_NO_SUCH_OBJECT, NULL, NULL, 0, NULL);', '            slapi_send_ldap_result(pb, LDAP_INAPPROPRIATE_AUTH, NULL, NULL, 0, NULL);'], 'added_lines': ['        slapi_pblock_set(pb, SLAPI_PB_RESULT_TEXT, "Entry does not exist");', '        slapi_send_ldap_result(pb, LDAP_INVALID_CREDENTIALS, NULL, NULL, 0, NULL);', '            slapi_pblock_set(pb, SLAPI_PB_RESULT_TEXT, "Entry does not have userpassword set");', '            slapi_send_ldap_result(pb, LDAP_INVALID_CREDENTIALS, NULL, NULL, 0, NULL);', '            slapi_pblock_set(pb, SLAPI_PB_RESULT_TEXT, "Invalid credentials");']}
description: When binding against a DN during authentication, the reply from 389-ds-base will be different whether the DN exists or not. This can be used by an unauthenticated attacker to check the existence of an entry in the LDAP database.

code_evidence: dse_get_entry_copy returns NULL when the bind DN does not exist, and the function replies with LDAP_NO_SUCH_OBJECT, a distinct result code from other failures.
When the entry exists but has no userpassword attribute, slapi_entry_attr_find fails and the function replies with LDAP_INAPPROPRIATE_AUTH, a different code than the missing-entry path.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-203 covers observable discrepancies in responses that reveal otherwise hidden state. Here the differing LDAP result codes for nonexistent versus existing-but-passwordless entries are directly observable to an unauthorized binder, matching the target weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The bind handler returns distinguishable LDAP result codes depending on whether the target DN exists and whether it has a password. An unauthenticated attacker can send bind requests and compare the replies to enumerate entries in the database. The root cause is the use of different error codes across these branches; the consequence is disclosure of entry existence.

description: The ReadOneJNGImage function in coders/png.c in ImageMagick through 6.9.9-0 and 7.x through 7.0.6-1 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (large loop and CPU consumption) via a malformed JNG file.

Lines 96-100 allocate a buffer sized to that length, and the loop at lines 101-102 then iterates once per length byte, calling ReadBlobByte each time. commit_msg:
It's possible for a request to invalidate a fscache_cookie will come in
while we're already processing an invalidation. If that happens we
currently take an extra access reference that will leak. Only call
__fscache_begin_cookie_access if the FSCACHE_COOKIE_DO_INVALIDATE bit
was previously clear.

Also, ensure that we attempt to clear the bit when the cookie is
"FAILED" and put the reference to avoid an access leak.

Fixes: 85e4ea1049c7 ("fscache: Fix invalidation/lookup race")
Suggested-by: David Howells <dhowells@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: David Howells <dhowells@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t__fscache_begin_cookie_access(cookie, fscache_access_invalidate_cookie);', '\t\tset_bit(FSCACHE_COOKIE_DO_INVALIDATE, &cookie->flags);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (!test_and_set_bit(FSCACHE_COOKIE_DO_INVALIDATE, &cookie->flags))', '\t\t\t__fscache_begin_cookie_access(cookie, fscache_access_invalidate_cookie);']}
description: A vulnerability was found in Linux Kernel. It has been rated as problematic. This issue affects some unknown processing of the file fs/fscache/cookie.c of the component IPsec. The manipulation leads to memory leak. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue. The associated identifier of this vulnerability is VDB-211931.

code_evidence: In the LOOKING_UP case, the function unconditionally calls __fscache_begin_cookie_access to take an access reference and then sets FSCACHE_COOKIE_DO_INVALIDATE. Because the bit is set after the reference is taken and without checking whether an invalidation is already pending, a concurrent/second invalidation re-entering this state takes an additional access reference each time, and the previously taken reference is never released on that path.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-401 fits because the function fails to release an acquired access reference (allocation/lifetime tracking) on the duplicate-invalidation path, causing memory to remain unavailable for reuse. This is a leak of a tracked reference, not a use-after-free or double-free.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the access reference is acquired unconditionally before the DO_INVALIDATE bit is tested/set, so repeated invalidations while already processing an invalidation acquire extra references that are not balanced by a put. Trigger: a request invalidates a fscache_cookie that is in LOOKING_UP state while an invalidation is already in progress. Consequence: the leaked access reference keeps the cookie object alive, exhausting memory/resources over repeated occurrences.

code_evidence: buf is cast to pjmedia_rtcp_common and hdr->pt/hdr->count are read at line 9, but the only length check at line 7 requires length >= 12 and PJ_ASSERT_RETURN(buf,...) at line 6 is the sole pointer guard; the cast occurs before the buffer validation and the struct read is not bounded by the actual packet layout.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 covers writes past the intended buffer, but this function only reads hdr fields; the supported consequence is an out-of-bounds read, not a write, so the target CWE is not directly supported by the shown code.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function dereferences the caller-supplied buffer through a cast to pjmedia_rtcp_common without ensuring the buffer contains that structure's fields; a short or malformed RTCP packet triggers an out-of-bounds read. The patch changes the cast to pjmedia_rtcp_fb_common and accesses hdr->rtcp_common fields, indicating the prior layout mismatch caused the OOB access.

commit_msg:
xhci: limit the number of link trbs we are willing to process

Needed to avoid we run in circles forever in case the guest builds
an endless loop with link trbs.

Reported-by: Li Qiang <liqiang6-s@360.cn>
Tested-by: P J P <ppandit@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Gerd Hoffmann <kraxel@redhat.com>
Message-id: 1476096382-7981-1-git-send-email-kraxel@redhat.com
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    uint32_t link_cnt = 0;', '            if (++link_cnt > TRB_LINK_LIMIT) {', '                return -length;', '            }']}
description: The xhci_ring_fetch function in hw/usb/hcd-xhci.c in QEMU (aka Quick Emulator) allows local guest OS administrators to cause a denial of service (infinite loop and QEMU process crash) by leveraging failure to limit the number of link Transfer Request Blocks (TRB) to process.

code_evidence: The unbounded while(1) loop reads TRBs via pci_dma_read and, when a TR_LINK TRB is encountered, sets dequeue to the guest-controlled trb.parameter and continues without any counter limiting link traversals. The loop can therefore follow guest-supplied link pointers indefinitely.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function processes an unbounded number of guest-controlled link TRBs, i.e., allocates/consumes an unlimited reusable resource (CPU processing iterations) without throttling, matching CWE-770's resource exhaustion without limits. The consequence is a DoS rather than memory corruption.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the ring-walk loop follows TR_LINK TRBs with guest-controlled targets and no cap on link count. A guest can build a cyclic or endless chain of link TRBs, causing the loop to spin forever and consuming CPU until the QEMU process hangs or crashes.

commit_msg:
NetKVM: BZ#1169718: More rigoruous testing of incoming packet

Signed-off-by: Joseph Hindin <yhindin@rehat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    if (res.ipStatus == ppresNotIP || res.ipCheckSum == ppresIPTooShort)', '        return res;', '']}
description: The NetKVM Windows Virtio driver allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (guest crash) via a crafted length value in an IP packet, as demonstrated by a value that does not account for the size of the IP options.

code_evidence: The packet header pointer is derived directly from the received buffer at ulStartOffset, and the packet is qualified only through QualifyIpPacket before any status gate.
The function proceeds to checksum verification (VerifyIpChecksum, VerifyTcpChecksum, VerifyUdpChecksum) based on ipStatus/xxpStatus without first rejecting a non-IP or too-short packet result.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function accepts externally supplied packet data and proceeds without validating that the parsed status is processable, matching CWE-20's improper input validation of derived length/status properties. A length-specific CWE would be narrower, but the target is the class-level validation failure.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the incoming packet's parsed status is not validated for the not-IP and too-short cases before checksum processing, so a crafted length value that ignores IP options yields an inconsistent packet description. Trigger: a remote attacker sends a malformed IP packet with a length that does not account for IP options. Consequence: the checksum routines operate on the misparsed packet, causing a guest crash (DoS).

code_evidence: On the success path, lydict_insert_zc() consumes the caller's buffer at lines 19/48, and line 49 sets the local pointer value to NULL so the function no longer owns it.

The error label at line 84 unconditionally calls free(value); since the local variable is only nulled at line 49 after a successful insert, an empty/missing description reaching the error path frees a buffer that the caller/dictionary still references.

The root cause is the ambiguous ownership of value across success and error paths, not merely a memory leak (CWE-401) or use-after-free without the duplicate release.

When parsing an empty description triggers the error branch, the buffer is freed here while remaining owned elsewhere, and the caller subsequently frees it again, producing a double free that can crash or corrupt memory.

commit_msg:
Add a one-word sentinel value of 0x0 at the end of each buf_t chunk

This helps protect against bugs where any part of a buf_t's memory
is passed to a function that expects a NUL-terminated input.

It also closes TROVE-2016-10-001 (aka bug 20384).
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  size_t memlen_orig = chunk->memlen;', '  chunk = tor_realloc(chunk, CHUNK_ALLOC_SIZE(sz));', '  tor_assert(chunk->DBG_alloc == CHUNK_ALLOC_SIZE(memlen_orig));', '  chunk->DBG_alloc = CHUNK_ALLOC_SIZE(sz);', '  total_bytes_allocated_in_chunks +=', '    CHUNK_ALLOC_SIZE(sz) - CHUNK_ALLOC_SIZE(memlen_orig);'], 'added_lines': ['  const size_t memlen_orig = chunk->memlen;', '  const size_t orig_alloc = CHUNK_ALLOC_SIZE(memlen_orig);', '  const size_t new_alloc = CHUNK_ALLOC_SIZE(sz);', '  chunk = tor_realloc(chunk, new_alloc);', '  tor_assert(chunk->DBG_alloc == orig_alloc);', '  chunk->DBG_alloc = new_alloc;', '  total_bytes_allocated_in_chunks += new_alloc - orig_alloc;', '  CHUNK_SET_SENTINEL(chunk, new_alloc);']}
description: Tor before 0.2.8.9 and 0.2.9.x before 0.2.9.4-alpha had internal functions that were entitled to expect that buf_t data had NUL termination, but the implementation of or/buffers.c did not ensure that NUL termination was present, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (client, hidden service, relay, or authority crash) via crafted data.

code_evidence: chunk_grow reallocates the chunk to CHUNK_ALLOC_SIZE(sz) and sets chunk->memlen = sz, but never initializes the byte at the new end of the buffer as a NUL terminator. The offset/data pointer is preserved, so subsequent callers can read the buffer as a NUL-terminated string.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing NUL termination lets string operations read beyond the buffer's intended boundary, matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds memory access. The root cause is the absent sentinel constraint in chunk_grow, distinct from a simple allocation-size error.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function grows a buffer without guaranteeing a terminating NUL byte within the intended bounds. When callers treat the chunk data as a C string, string routines read past the allocated region, causing out-of-bounds reads and crashes (DoS) on crafted data.

description: TensorFlow is an open source platform for machine learning. If a list of quantized tensors is assigned to an attribute, the pywrap code fails to parse the tensor and returns a `nullptr`, which is not caught. An example can be seen in `tf.compat.v1.extract_volume_patches` by passing in quantized tensors as input `ksizes`. We have patched the issue in GitHub commit e9e95553e5411834d215e6770c81a83a3d0866ce. for (int i = 0; i < num_values; ++i) {                                  \
tensorflow::Safe_PyObjectPtr py_value(PySequence_ITEM(py_list, i));   \
