commit_msg:
x86/mm: relinquish_memory: Grab an extra type ref when setting PGT_partial

The PGT_partial bit in page->type_info holds both a type count and a
general ref count.  During domain tear-down, when free_page_type()
returns -ERESTART, relinquish_memory() correctly handles the general
ref count, but fails to grab an extra type count when setting
PGT_partial.  When this bit is eventually cleared, type_count underflows
and triggers the following BUG in page_alloc.c:free_domheap_pages():

    BUG_ON((pg[i].u.inuse.type_info & PGT_count_mask) != 0);

As far as we can tell, this page underflow cannot be exploited any any
other way: The page can't be used as a pagetable by the dying domain
because it's dying; it can't be used as a pagetable by any other
domain since it belongs to the dying domain; and ownership can't
transfer to any other domain without hitting the BUG_ON() in
free_domheap_pages().

(steal_page() won't work on a page in this state, since it requires
PGC_allocated to be set, and PGC_allocated will already have been
cleared.)

Fix this by grabbing an extra type ref if setting PGT_partial in
relinquish_memory.

This is part of XSA-310.

Signed-off-by: George Dunlap <george.dunlap@citrix.com>
Acked-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
diff_func:
--- func_before
+++ func_after
@@ -97,6 +97,25 @@
                     goto out;
                 case -ERESTART:
                     page_list_add(page, list);
+                    /*
+                     * PGT_partial holds a type ref and a general ref.
+                     * If we came in with PGT_partial set, then we 1)
+                     * don't need to grab an extra type count, and 2)
+                     * do need to drop the extra page ref we grabbed
+                     * at the top of the loop.  If we didn't come in
+                     * with PGT_partial set, we 1) do need to drab an
+                     * extra type count, but 2) can transfer the page
+                     * ref we grabbed above to it.
+                     *
+                     * Note that we must increment type_info before
+                     * setting PGT_partial.  Theoretically it should
+                     * be safe to drop the page ref before setting
+                     * PGT_partial, but do it afterwards just to be
+                     * extra safe.
+                     */
+                    if ( !(x & PGT_partial) )
+                        page->u.inuse.type_info++;
+                    smp_wmb();
                     page->u.inuse.type_info |= PGT_partial;
                     if ( x & PGT_partial )
                         put_page(page);

description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.12.x allowing x86 PV guest OS users to gain host OS privileges by leveraging race conditions in pagetable promotion and demotion operations, because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2019-18421. XSA-299 addressed several critical issues in restartable PV type change operations. Despite extensive testing and auditing, some corner cases were missed. A malicious PV guest administrator may be able to escalate their privilege to that of the host. All security-supported versions of Xen are vulnerable. Only x86 systems are affected. Arm systems are not affected. Only x86 PV guests can leverage the vulnerability. x86 HVM and PVH guests cannot leverage the vulnerability. Note that these attacks require very precise timing, which may be difficult to exploit in practice.

code_evidence: On the -ERESTART path the function adds the page back to the list and sets PGT_partial, but before the fix it does not increment the type ref when the incoming value x lacked PGT_partial. The shared field page->u.inuse.type_info is read into x in the loop at line 41 and modified here without an atomic update.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect is an improper synchronization/refcount update around shared page type state on a restartable, concurrent pagetable type-change path, matching CWE-362's concurrent access to a shared resource with a timing window. The incomplete refcount accounting is the concrete manifestation, but the target class is the race-prone concurrent sequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: PGT_partial is documented to hold both a type ref and a general ref. When free_page_type returns -ERESTART and the page was not already partial, setting PGT_partial without taking the extra type ref leaves the type count short. When the bit is later cleared, type_count underflows and trips the BUG_ON in free_domheap_pages. The trigger is the restartable PV type-change path; the consequence is a host crash/DoS, not a straightforward privilege escalation.

commit_msg:
CVE-2017-13689/IKEv1: Fix addr+subnet length check.

An IPv6 address plus subnet mask is 32 bytes, not 20 bytes.
16 bytes of IPv6 address, 16 bytes of subnet mask.

This fixes a buffer over-read discovered by Bhargava Shastry,
SecT/TU Berlin.

Add a test using the capture file supplied by the reporter(s).

description: The IKEv1 parser in tcpdump before 4.9.2 has a buffer over-read in print-isakmp.c:ikev1_id_print().

code_evidence: len is derived from item_len - sizeof(*p) (lines 26), i.e., attacker-controlled packet length. For IPSECDOI_ID_IPV6_ADDR_SUBNET the guard only requires len >= 20, but the else branch reads mask[0..15] starting at data + sizeof(struct in6_addr) (16 bytes), requiring 32 bytes total. With len between 20 and 31, the 16 mask byte reads at lines 113-116 and the ip6addr_string at 112 access up to data+31, past the validated len bytes.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function validates fewer bytes than it subsequently reads, so the read goes past the intended buffer, matching CWE-125 (Out-of-bounds Read). This is a length-validation error enabling over-read, distinct from an out-of-bounds write.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the pre-fix length check (len < 20) undercounts the required 32 bytes for an IPv6 address plus 16-byte subnet mask. Trigger: a crafted IKEv1 ID payload of type IPV6_ADDR_SUBNET with len in [20,31]. Consequence: out-of-bounds read of up to 12 bytes past the buffer via mask[] indices and ip6addr_string, potentially disclosing memory or crashing tcpdump.

commit_msg:
Don't lower lastStreamID_

Summary:
This could throw off the logic about what is headers/trailers
CVE-2018-6347

Reviewed By: avasylev, bolekk

Differential Revision: D13521704

description: An issue in the Proxygen handling of HTTP2 parsing of headers/trailers can lead to a denial-of-service attack. This affects Proxygen prior to v2018.12.31.00.

commit_msg:
libdw, readelf: Make sure there is enough data to read full aranges header.

dwarf_getaranges didn't check if there was enough data left to read both
the address and segment size. readelf didn't check there was enough data
left to read the segment size.

https://sourceware.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=23541

Signed-off-by: Mark Wielaard <mark@klomp.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['      /* Next up two bytes for address and segment size.  */', '      if (readp + 2 > readendp)', '\tgoto invalid;', '']}
description: dwarf_getaranges in dwarf_getaranges.c in libdw in elfutils before 2018-08-18 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (heap-based buffer over-read) via a crafted file.

code_evidence: After __libdw_read_offset_inc advances readp, the code dereferences *readp++ to obtain address_size and then *readp++ again for segment_size without first verifying that two bytes remain before readendp. The diff adds exactly the missing 'readp + 2 > readendp' guard (goto invalid) before these reads.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads bytes beyond the intended buffer end via unchecked pointer dereference, exactly matching CWE-125 out-of-bounds read. Contrast with CWE-787 write, which is not present since only reads occur.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the loop bounds check is only applied to earlier header fields; after the offset read, readp may equal or exceed readendp, yet lines 65 and 68 unconditionally read and advance. Trigger: a crafted .debug_aranges section whose header ends immediately after the offset field. Consequence: heap-based out-of-bounds read of the section buffer, potentially crashing (DoS) or exposing adjacent memory.

description: In the Linux kernel before 5.3.12, there is a use-after-free bug that can be caused by a malicious USB device in the drivers/input/ff-memless.c driver, aka CID-fa3a5a1880c9.

code_evidence: ml_ff_destroy() frees the per-device private buffer via kfree(ml->private) and returns without stopping ml->timer. The timer callback operates on the same ml_device/private data, so after this teardown the timer can still fire and dereference freed memory.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function releases memory that an active timer still references, so subsequent timer execution accesses freed memory, directly matching CWE-416 (use after free). This is not merely a resource leak: the stale timer retains a live reference to freed storage.

evidence_lines.code:
struct ml_device *ml = ff->private;
kfree(ml->private);

commit_msg:
x86/vpt: fix race when migrating timers between vCPUs

The current vPT code will migrate the emulated timers between vCPUs
(change the pt->vcpu field) while just holding the destination lock,
either from create_periodic_time or pt_adjust_global_vcpu_target if
the global target is adjusted. Changing the periodic_timer vCPU field
in this way creates a race where a third party could grab the lock in
the unlocked region of pt_adjust_global_vcpu_target (or before
create_periodic_time performs the vcpu change) and then release the
lock from a different vCPU, creating a locking imbalance.

Introduce a per-domain rwlock in order to protect periodic_time
migration between vCPU lists. Taking the lock in read mode prevents
any timer from being migrated to a different vCPU, while taking it in
write mode allows performing migration of timers across vCPUs. The
per-vcpu locks are still used to protect all the other fields from the
periodic_timer struct.

Note that such migration shouldn't happen frequently, and hence
there's no performance drop as a result of such locking.

This is XSA-336.

Reported-by: Igor Druzhinin <igor.druzhinin@citrix.com>
Tested-by: Igor Druzhinin <igor.druzhinin@citrix.com>
Signed-off-by: Roger Pau Monné <roger.pau@citrix.com>
Reviewed-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    struct vcpu *v;', '', '    for ( ; ; )', '    {', '        v = pt->vcpu;', '        spin_lock(&v->arch.hvm.tm_lock);', '        if ( likely(pt->vcpu == v) )', '            break;', '        spin_unlock(&v->arch.hvm.tm_lock);', '    }'], 'added_lines': ['    /*', '     * We cannot use pt_vcpu_lock here, because we need to acquire the', '     * per-domain lock first and then (re-)fetch the value of pt->vcpu, or', '     * else we might be using a stale value of pt->vcpu.', '     */', '    read_lock(&pt->vcpu->domain->arch.hvm.pl_time->pt_migrate);', '    spin_lock(&pt->vcpu->arch.hvm.tm_lock);']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.14.x. There is a race condition when migrating timers between x86 HVM vCPUs. When migrating timers of x86 HVM guests between its vCPUs, the locking model used allows for a second vCPU of the same guest (also operating on the timers) to release a lock that it didn't acquire. The most likely effect of the issue is a hang or crash of the hypervisor, i.e., a Denial of Service (DoS). All versions of Xen are affected. Only x86 systems are vulnerable. Arm systems are not vulnerable. Only x86 HVM guests can leverage the vulnerability. x86 PV and PVH cannot leverage the vulnerability. Only guests with more than one vCPU can exploit the vulnerability.

code_evidence: pt_lock caches pt->vcpu in local v, then locks that vCPU's tm_lock and only breaks if pt->vcpu still equals v; otherwise it unlocks and retries. The check and lock are not atomic with respect to a concurrent migration of pt->vcpu, so another vCPU can change pt->vcpu between the read at 6 and the lock at 7, or after the check at 8.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-362 fits because the exclusive-access protocol over the shared periodic_time/vCPU lock is not atomic: an interfering migration sequence can modify pt->vcpu during the lock sequence, violating exclusivity. The defect is improper synchronization, not a simple missing bounds check.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the per-vCPU lock is acquired based on a snapshot of pt->vcpu that can change concurrently, and there is no lock covering the migration itself. Trigger: one vCPU migrates the timer while another calls pt_lock; the retry loop can then unlock a tm_lock belonging to a different vCPU than the one that acquired it, creating a locking imbalance and leaving structures unprotected. Supported consequence: hypervisor hang or crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
evtchn: address races with evtchn_reset()

Neither d->evtchn_port_ops nor max_evtchns(d) may be used in an entirely
lock-less manner, as both may change by a racing evtchn_reset(). In the
common case, at least one of the domain's event lock or the per-channel
lock needs to be held. In the specific case of the inter-domain sending
by evtchn_send() and notify_via_xen_event_channel() holding the other
side's per-channel lock is sufficient, as the channel can't change state
without both per-channel locks held. Without such a channel changing
state, evtchn_reset() can't complete successfully.

Lock-free accesses continue to be permitted for the shim (calling some
otherwise internal event channel functions), as this happens while the
domain is in effectively single-threaded mode. Special care also needs
taking for the shim's marking of in-use ports as ECS_RESERVED (allowing
use of such ports in the shim case is okay because switching into and
hence also out of FIFO mode is impossihble there).

As a side effect, certain operations on Xen bound event channels which
were mistakenly permitted so far (e.g. unmask or poll) will be refused
now.

This is part of XSA-343.

Reported-by: Julien Grall <jgrall@amazon.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Acked-by: Julien Grall <jgrall@amazon.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['static bool evtchn_2l_is_pending(const struct domain *d, evtchn_port_t port)'], 'added_lines': ['static bool evtchn_2l_is_pending(const struct domain *d,', '                                 const struct evtchn *evtchn)', '    evtchn_port_t port = evtchn->port;']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.14.x. There are evtchn_reset() race conditions. Uses of EVTCHNOP_reset (potentially by a guest on itself) or XEN_DOMCTL_soft_reset (by itself covered by XSA-77) can lead to the violation of various internal assumptions. This may lead to out of bounds memory accesses or triggering of bug checks. In particular, x86 PV guests may be able to elevate their privilege to that of the host. Host and guest crashes are also possible, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS). Information leaks cannot be ruled out. All Xen versions from 4.5 onwards are vulnerable. Xen versions 4.4 and earlier are not vulnerable.

code_evidence: evtchn_2l_is_pending reads d's shared_info evtchn_pending bitmap via guest_test_bit(d, port, ...) without taking the domain event lock or the per-channel lock. The port bound is derived from max_ports = BITS_PER_EVTCHN_WORD(d)^2, a value the commit states can change under a racing evtchn_reset(). The read of the pending bit and the max_ports bound are not protected against concurrent modification.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs a shared-resource access (event-channel pending bitmap and max_ports) without exclusive access, so an interfering evtchn_reset() sequence can modify the resource between the bound check and the read. This is a concurrent shared-resource synchronization flaw, matching CWE-362; it is not merely a missing bounds check, since the bound itself is race-sensitive.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the pending-bit test and its max_ports bound use domain state (max_evtchns/shared info) without synchronization. Trigger: a concurrent evtchn_reset() changes max_evtchns while this function evaluates the port bound and reads the bitmap. Consequence: the ASSERT and bound check can be bypassed, leading to out-of-bounds bitmap access or inconsistent state, supporting crash/DoS and potential privilege escalation per the advisory.

IOMMU/x86: fix type ref-counting race upon IOMMU page table construction

When arch_iommu_populate_page_table() gets invoked for an already
running guest, simply looking at page types once isn't enough, as they
may change at any time. Add logic to re-check the type after having
mapped the page, unmapping it again if needed.

This is XSA-285.

Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Tentatively-Acked-by: Andrew Cooper <andrew.cooper3@citrix.com>

description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. In affected versions an attacker can cause denial of service in applications serving models using `tf.raw_ops.UnravelIndex` by triggering a division by 0. The [implementation](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/460e000de3a83278fb00b61a16d161b1964f15f4/tensorflow/core/kernels/unravel_index_op.cc#L36) does not check that the tensor subsumed by `dims` is not empty. Hence, if one element of `dims` is 0, the implementation does a division by 0. We have patched the issue in GitHub commit a776040a5e7ebf76eeb7eb923bf1ae417dd4d233. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.6.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.5.1, TensorFlow 2.4.3, and TensorFlow 2.3.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: Line 14 obtains the dims vector directly from attacker-controlled input(1); lines 15-16 compute dims_prod = product of dims, and lines 19-20 use it only as an upper bound for indices, so a zero element in dims is never rejected.

In the scalar branch line 49 divides by strides_shifted, and in the vector branch lines 68-70 divide by strides_shifted.reshape(...).broadcast(...). These divisors derive from a reversed scan/product of dims, so any zero dim makes the divisor zero.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs division by a value derived from unchecked input that can be zero, matching CWE-369 (Divide By Zero). The issue is the missing zero-dim check, not merely an out-of-bounds index check (CWE-125/787), since the consequence is a division by zero causing DoS.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the kernel accepts a dims tensor containing a 0 and computes strides/strides_shifted from it without validating nonzero elements. Trigger: an attacker supplies dims with a zero entry to tf.raw_ops.UnravelIndex. Consequence: the division at line 49 or 68-70 divides by zero, producing inf/NaN or a crash, a denial of service.

vmsvga: correct bitmap and pixmap size checks

When processing svga command DEFINE_CURSOR in vmsvga_fifo_run,
the computed BITMAP and PIXMAP size are checked against the
'cursor.mask[]' and 'cursor.image[]' array sizes in bytes.
Correct these checks to avoid OOB memory access.

Reported-by: Qinghao Tang <luodalongde@gmail.com>
Reported-by: Li Qiang <liqiang6-s@360.cn>
Signed-off-by: Prasad J Pandit <pjp@fedoraproject.org>
Message-id: 1473338754-15430-1-git-send-email-ppandit@redhat.com
Signed-off-by: Gerd Hoffmann <kraxel@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            if (cursor.width > 256 ||', '                cursor.height > 256 ||', '                cursor.bpp > 32 ||', '                SVGA_BITMAP_SIZE(x, y) > sizeof cursor.mask ||', '                SVGA_PIXMAP_SIZE(x, y, cursor.bpp) > sizeof cursor.image) {'], 'added_lines': ['            if (cursor.width > 256', '                || cursor.height > 256', '                || cursor.bpp > 32', '                || SVGA_BITMAP_SIZE(x, y)', '                    > sizeof(cursor.mask) / sizeof(cursor.mask[0])', '                || SVGA_PIXMAP_SIZE(x, y, cursor.bpp)', '                    > sizeof(cursor.image) / sizeof(cursor.image[0])) {']}
description: The vmsvga_fifo_run function in hw/display/vmware_vga.c in QEMU (aka Quick Emulator) allows local guest OS administrators to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds write and QEMU process crash) via vectors related to cursor.mask[] and cursor.image[] array sizes when processing a DEFINE_CURSOR svga command.

code_evidence: Guest-supplied x, y, and bpp from the FIFO are used to compute args and are only rejected if width/height exceed 256, bpp exceeds 32, or the computed sizes exceed sizeof cursor.mask / sizeof cursor.image (byte sizes, not element counts).
The loop writes cursor.mask[args] for args < SVGA_BITMAP_SIZE(x,y), using the computed size as an array index without validating it against the element count of cursor.mask.
Similarly, cursor.image[args] is written for args < SVGA_PIXMAP_SIZE(x,y,bpp), again using an unvalidated computed size as an index into cursor.image.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function uses guest-controlled computed sizes as array indices (cursor.mask[args], cursor.image[args]) while the guard incorrectly validates the index bound, matching CWE-129. It is not merely a buffer-size comparison bug; the index is not validated against the valid array element range.

evidence_lines.code:
for (args = 0; args < SVGA_BITMAP_SIZE(x, y); args++) {
cursor.mask[args] = vmsvga_fifo_read_raw(s);

for (args = 0; args < SVGA_PIXMAP_SIZE(x, y, cursor.bpp); args++) {
cursor.image[args] = vmsvga_fifo_read_raw(s);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the size checks compare the computed bitmap/pixmap sizes against the byte size of the mask/image arrays rather than their element counts, so an oversized guest-controlled index passes validation. Trigger: a DEFINE_CURSOR command with crafted x/y/bpp. Consequence: out-of-bounds writes into cursor.mask/cursor.image, causing memory corruption and a QEMU crash.

commit_msg:
usb: check RNDIS buffer offsets & length

When processing remote NDIS control message packets,
the USB Net device emulator uses a fixed length(4096) data buffer.
The incoming informationBufferOffset & Length combination could
overflow and cross that range. Check control message buffer
offsets and length to avoid it.

Reported-by: Qinghao Tang <luodalongde@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Prasad J Pandit <pjp@fedoraproject.org>
Message-id: 1455648821-17340-3-git-send-email-ppandit@redhat.com
Signed-off-by: Gerd Hoffmann <kraxel@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        if (offs + size <= len)'], 'added_lines': ['        if (offs < len && size < len && offs + size <= len) {', '        }']}
description: Multiple integer overflows in the USB Net device emulator (hw/usb/dev-network.c) in QEMU before 2.5.1 allow local guest OS administrators to cause a denial of service (QEMU process crash) or obtain sensitive host memory information via a remote NDIS control message packet that is mishandled in the (1) rndis_query_response, (2) rndis_set_response, or (3) usb_net_handle_dataout function.

code_evidence: len is taken from the guest-supplied MessageLength and only checked against s->out_ptr at [24]; nothing constrains MessageLength relative to the 4096-byte out_buf or to the packet's actual payload.

At [28] offs = 8 + DataOffset and size = DataLength are both guest-controlled uint32 values; the guard at [30] computes offs + size in uint32, which can wrap before the comparison, and offs is never checked against len.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect is an improper numeric calculation: summation of untrusted offsets/lengths without overflow protection, allowing the range check to be bypassed. The fix adds offs < len && size < len, confirming integer overflow as the cause, matching CWE-189 numeric errors.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the bounds check offs + size <= len performs an unchecked 32-bit addition of two attacker-controlled fields, so a large DataOffset/DataLength wraps to a small value and passes. Trigger: a crafted RNDIS_PACKET_MSG with overflowing offset/length. Consequence: qemu_send_packet reads out of bounds from s->out_buf, leaking host memory or crashing QEMU.

commit_msg:
journalctl: verify sealed log epochs are continuous

Currently empty epochs are not sealed. This allows an attacker to truncate
a sealed log and continue it without any problems showing when verifying the
log.

This partially addresses CVE-2023-31438. One way to extend this change to
address CVE-2023-31438 completely, would be to verify that there is exactly
one seal per epoch (and not sealing when the epoch has not ended yet).

the change also adds a journal-file flag: HEADER_COMPATIBLE_SEALED_CONTINUOUS
this flag indicates that a journal file is sealed continuously and decides whether
any missing crypto epochs should trigger a warning or an error.
diff_func:
--- func_before
+++ func_after
@@ -21,7 +21,7 @@
                                 keyed_hash_requested() * HEADER_INCOMPATIBLE_KEYED_HASH |
                                 compact_mode_requested() * HEADER_INCOMPATIBLE_COMPACT),
                 .compatible_flags = htole32(
-                                (seal * HEADER_COMPATIBLE_SEALED) |
+                                (seal * (HEADER_COMPATIBLE_SEALED | HEADER_COMPATIBLE_SEALED_CONTINUOUS) ) |
                                 HEADER_COMPATIBLE_TAIL_ENTRY_BOOT_ID),
         };
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['                                (seal * HEADER_COMPATIBLE_SEALED) |'], 'added_lines': ['                                (seal * (HEADER_COMPATIBLE_SEALED | HEADER_COMPATIBLE_SEALED_CONTINUOUS) ) |']}
description: An issue was discovered in systemd 253. An attacker can truncate a sealed log file and then resume log sealing such that checking the integrity shows no error, despite modifications. NOTE: the vendor reportedly sent "a reply denying that any of the finding was a security vulnerability."

code_evidence: Line 10 sets seal from file flags and FSS key load; line 19 writes the compatible header flag HEADER_COMPATIBLE_SEALED into the new journal header only when seal is true, alongside the tail-entry boot-id flag at line 20.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-354 covers failure to validate integrity check values so tampering is not detected. Here the sealing metadata written at line 19 lacks the continuity information needed for verification to detect a truncated-and-resumed epoch, so the integrity check reports no error despite modification. This is integrity-check validation weakness, not a checksum algorithm error.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The header initialization records only a generic sealed flag, with no per-epoch continuity marker or count. Because empty epochs need not be sealed, a truncated sealed log can be re-sealed and reopened, and verification finds no gap in the integrity metadata. Root cause is the missing continuity constraint in the seal flag; the consequence is that truncation/modification of a sealed journal is not detected (integrity check fails to detect tampering).

description: In Wireshark 2.2.0 to 2.2.5 and 2.0.0 to 2.0.11, the WSP dissector could go into an infinite loop, triggered by packet injection or a malformed capture file. This was addressed in epan/dissectors/packet-wsp.c by adding a length check.

code_evidence: The while loop at [22] advances offset using len returned by tvb_get_guintvar at [24]. capaValueLen and capaLen are derived from that varint, and the loop's final advance is offset = capaStart + capaLen at [170].
For textual capabilities, offset is set to capaStart + capaLen at [54] and the loop continues at [55].
For well-known capabilities the offset is incremented by one at [66], but no constraint ties capaLen to the actual remaining buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-835 fits because the dissector loop has an exit condition (offset >= tvb_len) that cannot be reached when malformed length fields prevent offset advancement. This is a loop-termination defect, not merely an out-of-bounds read, and matches the reported infinite-loop DoS.

evidence_lines.code: offset = capaStart + capaLen;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The loop termination depends on offset advancing past tvb_len, but capaLen is computed from attacker-controlled varint fields without a bound check against tvb_len. If capaLen resolves to zero (or a value that does not advance offset), the continue at [55] or the final offset = capaStart + capaLen leaves offset unchanged, so the while condition at [22] never becomes false, causing an infinite loop and CPU exhaustion.

commit_msg:
Correctly compare EdiPartyName in GENERAL_NAME_cmp()

If a GENERAL_NAME field contained EdiPartyName data then it was
incorrectly being handled as type "other". This could lead to a
segmentation fault.

Many thanks to David Benjamin from Google for reporting this issue.

CVE-2020-1971

Reviewed-by: Tomas Mraz <tmraz@fedoraproject.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        a->d.other = value;'], 'added_lines': ['        a->d.x400Address = value;', '        break;', '', '        a->d.ediPartyName = value;']}
description: The X.509 GeneralName type is a generic type for representing different types of names. One of those name types is known as EDIPartyName. OpenSSL provides a function GENERAL_NAME_cmp which compares different instances of a GENERAL_NAME to see if they are equal or not. This function behaves incorrectly when both GENERAL_NAMEs contain an EDIPARTYNAME. A NULL pointer dereference and a crash may occur leading to a possible denial of service attack. OpenSSL itself uses the GENERAL_NAME_cmp function for two purposes: 1) Comparing CRL distribution point names between an available CRL and a CRL distribution point embedded in an X509 certificate 2) When verifying that a timestamp response token signer matches the timestamp authority name (exposed via the API functions TS_RESP_verify_response and TS_RESP_verify_token) If an attacker can control both items being compared then that attacker could trigger a crash. For example if the attacker can trick a client or server into checking a malicious certificate against a malicious CRL then this may occur. Note that some applications automatically download CRLs based on a URL embedded in a certificate. This checking happens prior to the signatures on the certificate and CRL being verified. OpenSSL's s_server, s_client and verify tools have support for the "-crl_download" option which implements automatic CRL downloading and this attack has been demonstrated to work against those tools. Note that an unrelated bug means that affected versions of OpenSSL cannot parse or construct correct encodings of EDIPARTYNAME. However it is possible to construct a malformed EDIPARTYNAME that OpenSSL's parser will accept and hence trigger this attack. All OpenSSL 1.1.1 and 1.0.2 versions are affected by this issue. Other OpenSSL releases are out of support and have not been checked. Fixed in OpenSSL 1.1.1i (Affected 1.1.1-1.1.1h). Fixed in OpenSSL 1.0.2x (Affected 1.0.2-1.0.2w).

code_evidence: For both GEN_X400 and GEN_EDIPARTY the same fall-through case stores the incoming value into a->d.other (line 6), so an EdiPartyName value is placed in the wrong union member and a->d.ediPartyName is never initialized.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect causes a pointer that consumers expect to be valid to remain NULL and be dereferenced, matching CWE-476. It is a wrong-union-member initialization, not merely a logic/type-confusion issue, because the observable effect is dereferencing a NULL pointer.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: GEN_EDIPARTY is conflated with GEN_X400 and the value is written to a->d.other instead of a->d.ediPartyName, leaving the ediPartyName pointer unset. Trigger: a GENERAL_NAME of type GEN_EDIPARTY is created via this setter and later consumed by GENERAL_NAME_cmp(), which reads the uninitialized/NULL ediPartyName and dereferences it. Supported consequence: NULL pointer dereference leading to a crash (denial of service).

commit_msg:
mnt: Add a per mount namespace limit on the number of mounts

CAI Qian <caiqian@redhat.com> pointed out that the semantics
of shared subtrees make it possible to create an exponentially
increasing number of mounts in a mount namespace.

    mkdir /tmp/1 /tmp/2
    mount --make-rshared /
    for i in $(seq 1 20) ; do mount --bind /tmp/1 /tmp/2 ; done

Will create create 2^20 or 1048576 mounts, which is a practical problem
as some people have managed to hit this by accident.

As such CVE-2016-6213 was assigned.

Ian Kent <raven@themaw.net> described the situation for autofs users
as follows:

> The number of mounts for direct mount maps is usually not very large because of
> the way they are implemented, large direct mount maps can have performance
> problems. There can be anywhere from a few (likely case a few hundred) to less
> than 10000, plus mounts that have been triggered and not yet expired.
>
> Indirect mounts have one autofs mount at the root plus the number of mounts that
> have been triggered and not yet expired.
>
> The number of autofs indirect map entries can range from a few to the common
> case of several thousand and in rare cases up to between 30000 and 50000. I've
> not heard of people with maps larger than 50000 entries.
>
> The larger the number of map entries the greater the possibility for a large
> number of active mounts so it's not hard to expect cases of a 1000 or somewhat
> more active mounts.

So I am setting the default number of mounts allowed per mount
namespace at 100,000.  This is more than enough for any use case I
know of, but small enough to quickly stop an exponential increase
in mounts.  Which should be perfect to catch misconfigurations and
malfunctioning programs.

For anyone who needs a higher limit this can be changed by writing
to the new /proc/sys/fs/mount-max sysctl.

Tested-by: CAI Qian <caiqian@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: "Eric W. Biederman" <ebiederm@xmission.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\tnew_ns->mounts++;']}
description: fs/namespace.c in the Linux kernel before 4.9 does not restrict how many mounts may exist in a mount namespace, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (memory consumption and deadlock) via MS_BIND mount system calls, as demonstrated by a loop that triggers exponential growth in the number of mounts.

code_evidence: copy_mnt_ns allocates a new mount namespace via alloc_mnt_ns and populates it by copying the entire mount tree with copy_tree. The loop then walks the copied mounts, assigning q->mnt_ns = new_ns for each; the patch adds new_ns->mounts++ here, showing this loop is the point where the namespace's mount count is tracked. Before the patch no counter was incremented, so the copied namespace's mount total was not bounded.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-400 fits because the function is responsible for tracking how many mounts a namespace holds, yet the pre-patch code did not increment or enforce any limit, permitting uncontrolled resource consumption. commit_msg:
ax25: improve the incomplete fix to avoid UAF and NPD bugs

The previous commit 1ade48d0c27d ("ax25: NPD bug when detaching
AX25 device") introduce lock_sock() into ax25_kill_by_device to
prevent NPD bug. But the concurrency NPD or UAF bug will occur,
when lock_sock() or release_sock() dereferences the ax25_cb->sock.

The NULL pointer dereference bug can be shown as below:

ax25_kill_by_device()        | ax25_release()
                             |   ax25_destroy_socket()
                             |     ax25_cb_del()
  ...                        |     ...
                             |     ax25->sk=NULL;
  lock_sock(s->sk); //(1)    |
  s->ax25_dev = NULL;        |     ...
  release_sock(s->sk); //(2) |
  ...                        |

The root cause is that the sock is set to null before dereference
site (1) or (2). Therefore, this patch extracts the ax25_cb->sock
in advance, and uses ax25_list_lock to protect it, which can synchronize
with ax25_cb_del() and ensure the value of sock is not null before
dereference sites.

The concurrency UAF bug can be shown as below:

ax25_kill_by_device()        | ax25_release()
                             |   ax25_destroy_socket()
  ...                        |   ...
                             |   sock_put(sk); //FREE
  lock_sock(s->sk); //(1)    |
  s->ax25_dev = NULL;        |   ...
  release_sock(s->sk); //(2) |
  ...                        |

The root cause is that the sock is released before dereference
site (1) or (2). Therefore, this patch uses sock_hold() to increase
the refcount of sock and uses ax25_list_lock to protect it, which
can synchronize with ax25_cb_del() in ax25_destroy_socket() and
ensure the sock wil not be released before dereference sites.

Signed-off-by: Duoming Zhou <duoming@zju.edu.cn>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\tlock_sock(s->sk);', '\t\t\trelease_sock(s->sk);', ''], 'added_lines': ['\tstruct sock *sk;', '\t\t\tsk = s->sk;', '\t\t\tsock_hold(sk);', '\t\t\tlock_sock(sk);', '\t\t\trelease_sock(sk);', '\t\t\tsock_put(sk);']}
description: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel. This flaw allows an attacker to crash the Linux kernel by simulating amateur radio from the user space, resulting in a null-ptr-deref vulnerability and a use-after-free vulnerability.

code_evidence: The list lock is dropped at line 11, then s->sk is dereferenced by lock_sock at line 12 and release_sock at line 14 without holding a reference to the socket; a concurrent ax25_release/ax25_cb_del can free the sock via sock_put between unlock and these dereferences.

After reacquiring the list lock at line 16, the code loops back to again and continues iterating s, but the entry may already have been removed by ax25_cb_del, so subsequent list traversal can operate on freed memory.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences s->sk and later s after the protecting lock is released, allowing the underlying object to be freed concurrently and then reused. This is a use-after-free (CWE-416); the NULL-pointer variant is a separate consequence, whereas here the freed sock is still referenced.

evidence_lines.code: ax25_disconnect(s, ENETUNREACH);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the socket pointer (and list entry) is used outside the list lock without a lifetime reference. Trigger: a concurrent ax25_release/ax25_destroy_socket frees the sock or removes the ax25_cb while ax25_kill_by_device is between unlock and lock_sock/release_sock. Consequence: use-after-free, leading to kernel crash or memory corruption.

strlen(NULL) in a very common use-case -- wrong CWD path.  Causing
segfault, which for some users lead to loss of further service.

commit_msg:
Fix for integer/buffer overflow CVE-2021-32765

This fix prevents hiredis from trying to allocate more than `SIZE_MAX`
bytes, which would result in a buffer overrun.

[Full Details](https://github.com/redis/hiredis/security/advisories/GHSA-hfm9-39pp-55p2)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ["        if (SIZE_MAX / sizeof(redisReply*) < elements) return NULL;  /* Don't overflow */"]}
description: Hiredis is a minimalistic C client library for the Redis database. In affected versions Hiredis is vulnurable to integer overflow if provided maliciously crafted or corrupted `RESP` `mult-bulk` protocol data. When parsing `multi-bulk` (array-like) replies, hiredis fails to check if `count * sizeof(redisReply*)` can be represented in `SIZE_MAX`. If it can not, and the `calloc()` call doesn't itself make this check, it would result in a short allocation and subsequent buffer overflow. Users of hiredis who are unable to update may set the [maxelements](https://github.com/redis/hiredis#reader-max-array-elements) context option to a value small enough that no overflow is possible.

code_evidence: When elements > 0, the function requests hi_calloc(elements, sizeof(redisReply*)) without first verifying that the product fits in size_t; elements is an attacker-influenced multibulk count.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe multiplication feeding a size argument is an integer-overflow/wraparound condition (CWE-190), which the patch fixes by rejecting elements when SIZE_MAX / sizeof(redisReply*) < elements. It is the arithmetic flaw enabling the later buffer overrun, distinct from the out-of-bounds write itself.

evidence_lines.code:
if (elements > 0) {
r->element = hi_calloc(elements,sizeof(redisReply*));

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the allocation size is computed as elements * sizeof(redisReply*) with no pre-multiplication bounds check. A malicious RESP multibulk count large enough to wrap size_t yields a short allocation; subsequent writes to parent->element[task->idx] then overrun the buffer. The consequence is memory corruption, not merely allocation failure.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t\t\t\twhile(!IsNewline(*ioBuf.ptr)) ++ioBuf.ptr;'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t\t\t\twhile(ioBuf.ptr < ioBuf.limit &&', '                                                      !IsNewline(*ioBuf.ptr))', '                                                    ++ioBuf.ptr;']}
description: An issue was discovered in Exempi through 2.4.4. There is a stack-based buffer over-read in the PostScript_MetaHandler::ParsePSFile() function in XMPFiles/source/FileHandlers/PostScript_Handler.cpp.

code_evidence: After matching the '%%Tra' prefix and 'iler' bytes, the code advances ioBuf.ptr by 4 (line 209) and then enters a loop that dereferences *ioBuf.ptr while scanning for a newline (line 210). This loop has no bound against ioBuf.limit and no CheckFileSpace call, so if the trailer comment reaches the end of the buffer/file without a newline, the pointer walks past the valid buffer and *ioBuf.ptr reads out-of-bounds memory. Line 211 then computes token length from the overrun pointer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 (Out-of-bounds Read) fits because the function reads memory beyond the intended buffer via *ioBuf.ptr in an unbounded loop. It is a read overrun, not a write (CWE-787), since no store occurs past the boundary.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the newline-scanning loop at line 210 dereferences ioBuf.ptr without checking ioBuf.ptr < ioBuf.limit or refilling the buffer. Trigger: a PostScript file containing a '%%Trailer' comment that is not terminated by a newline before the buffer/file end. Consequence: stack-based out-of-bounds read (crash/DoS and possible memory disclosure).

description: Contiki-NG is an open-source, cross-platform operating system for internet of things devices. It is possible to cause an out-of-bounds write in versions of Contiki-NG prior to 4.6 when transmitting a 6LoWPAN packet with a chain of extension headers. Unfortunately, the written header is not checked to be within the available space, thereby making it possible to write outside the buffer. The problem has been patched in Contiki-NG 4.6. commit_msg:
syscalls: arm: Fix possible overflow in is_in_region function

This function is widely used by functions that validate memory
buffers. Macros used to check permissions, like Z_SYSCALL_MEMORY_READ
and Z_SYSCALL_MEMORY_WRITE, use these functions to check that a
pointers passed by user threads in a syscall.

Signed-off-by: Flavio Ceolin <flavio.ceolin@intel.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (start >= r_addr_start && (start + size - 1) <= r_addr_end) {'], 'added_lines': ['\tu32_t end;', '\tsize = size == 0 ? 0 : size - 1;', '\tif (__builtin_add_overflow(start, size, &end)) {', '\t\treturn 0;', '\t}', '', '\tif ((start >= r_addr_start) && (end <= r_addr_end)) {']}
description: A malicious userspace application can cause a integer overflow and bypass security checks performed by system call handlers. The impact would depend on the underlying system call and can range from denial of service to information leak to memory corruption resulting in code execution within the kernel. See NCC-ZEP-005 This issue affects: zephyrproject-rtos zephyr version 1.14.1 and later versions. version 2.1.0 and later versions.

code_evidence: The bounds check computes start + size - 1 in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic and compares it against r_addr_end. If size is large (e.g., near UINT32_MAX) or start + size wraps, the sum wraps to a small value that can fall within the MPU region, so the function returns 1 despite the buffer extending far beyond the region.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the function performs an unchecked 32-bit addition whose wraparound directly defeats an access-control validation. The overflow is the cause; the bypass of Z_SYSCALL_MEMORY_READ/WRITE checks is the consequence. A plain out-of-bounds comparison (CWE-125-style) would not capture the arithmetic wraparound root cause.

evidence_lines.code: if (start >= r_addr_start && (start + size - 1) <= r_addr_end) {

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the addition start + size - 1 is performed without overflow detection, and the logic assumes the sum is always larger than start. Trigger: a userspace syscall passes a large size (or a start near the top of the address space) so the addition wraps. Consequence: the region check is bypassed, letting unvalidated buffers pass permission macros, enabling memory corruption, information leak, or DoS depending on the syscall.

commit_msg:
media: rc: Fix use-after-free bugs caused by ene_tx_irqsim()

When the ene device is detaching, function ene_remove() will
be called. But there is no function to cancel tx_sim_timer
in ene_remove(), the timer handler ene_tx_irqsim() could race
with ene_remove(). As a result, the UAF bugs could happen,
the process is shown below.

    (cleanup routine)          |        (timer routine)
                               | mod_timer(&dev->tx_sim_timer, ..)
ene_remove()                   | (wait a time)
                               | ene_tx_irqsim()
                               |   dev->hw_lock //USE
                               |   ene_tx_sample(dev) //USE

Fix by adding del_timer_sync(&dev->tx_sim_timer) in ene_remove(),
The tx_sim_timer could stop before ene device is deallocated.

What's more, The rc_unregister_device() and del_timer_sync()
should be called first in ene_remove() and the deallocated
functions such as free_irq(), release_region() and so on
should be called behind them. Because the rc_unregister_device()
is well synchronized. Otherwise, race conditions may happen. The
situations that may lead to race conditions are shown below.

Firstly, the rx receiver is disabled with ene_rx_disable()
before rc_unregister_device() in ene_remove(), which means it
can be enabled again if a process opens /dev/lirc0 between
ene_rx_disable() and rc_unregister_device().

Secondly, the irqaction descriptor is freed by free_irq()
before the rc device is unregistered, which means irqaction
descriptor may be accessed again after it is deallocated.

Thirdly, the timer can call ene_tx_sample() that can write
to the io ports, which means the io ports could be accessed
again after they are deallocated by release_region().

Therefore, the rc_unregister_device() and del_timer_sync()
should be called first in ene_remove().

Suggested by: Sean Young <sean@mess.org>

Fixes: 9ea53b74df9c ("V4L/DVB: STAGING: remove lirc_ene0100 driver")
Signed-off-by: Duoming Zhou <duoming@zju.edu.cn>
Signed-off-by: Sean Young <sean@mess.org>
Signed-off-by: Mauro Carvalho Chehab <mchehab@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\trc_unregister_device(dev->rdev);'], 'added_lines': ['\trc_unregister_device(dev->rdev);', '\tdel_timer_sync(&dev->tx_sim_timer);']}
description: A flaw use after free in the Linux kernel integrated infrared receiver/transceiver driver was found in the way user detaching rc device. A local user could use this flaw to crash the system or potentially escalate their privileges on the system.

code_evidence: ene_remove() frees the IRQ with free_irq() and releases the I/O region with release_region() before unregistering the rc device and before any timer cancellation; kfree(dev) then releases the device memory. No del_timer_sync(&dev->tx_sim_timer) exists in this function, so the tx_sim_timer handler ene_tx_irqsim() can still run and dereference dev->hw_lock and call ene_tx_sample(dev) after the device is freed.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This is CWE-416 because the timer handler references and operates on the device structure after ene_remove() has freed it. The missing cancellation is the cause; the post-free access by ene_tx_irqsim() is the use-after-free, distinct from a mere race or resource leak.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: ene_remove() deallocates dev (kfree) and its resources without synchronizing with the tx_sim_timer, which can be re-armed via mod_timer. Trigger: detaching the rc device while the timer is pending or fires concurrently. Consequence: ene_tx_irqsim() uses freed dev memory (hw_lock, ene_tx_sample), causing a use-after-free that can crash the system or potentially lead to privilege escalation.

commit_msg:
avcodec/jpegxl_parser: fix OOB read regression

In f7ac3512f5b5cb8eb149f37300b43461d8e93af3 the size of the dynamically
allocated buffer was shrunk, but it was made too small for very small
alphabet sizes. This patch restores the size to prevent an OOB read.

Reported-by: Cole Dilorenzo <coolkingcole@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Leo Izen <leo.izen@gmail.com>

description: FFmpeg prior to commit bf814 was discovered to contain an out of bounds read via the dist->alphabet_size variable in the read_vlc_prefix() function.

code_evidence: The level2 buffers are sized from dist->alphabet_size, and the sub-buffer pointers are computed at offsets based on dist->alphabet_size, so a small alphabet_size makes the allocation too small for the subsequent indexed writes/reads.

The loop iterates i < dist->alphabet_size, decoding len via get_vlc2, then for len==16 computes extra and, before the fix, only rejects when i+extra exceeds alphabet_size; the bounds check is present in this version.
For len==17, extra is computed and i is advanced by extra-1 with level2_codecounts[0] += extra, without clamping extra to the remaining alphabet_size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads level2_lens and level2_codecounts at indices derived from attacker-controlled repeat counts and alphabet_size, past the allocated/valid region; this is a read past the intended buffer, matching CWE-125. It is not a write overflow because the observed unsafety is reading lengths for VLC initialization.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: buffer size and sub-buffer offsets derive from dist->alphabet_size, which can be very small, while the repeat-expansion logic (len 16/17) can advance i or accumulate counts beyond the intended level2 region. Trigger: crafted JPEG XL bitstream with a small alphabet_size and repeat codes. Consequence: out-of-bounds read of level2_lens/codecounts during VLC construction.

commit_msg:
Make Transpose's shape inference function validate that negative `perm` values are within the tensor's rank.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 403252853
Change-Id: Ia6b31b45b237312668bb31c2c3b3c7bbce2d2610

description: TensorFlow is an open source platform for machine learning. In affected versions the shape inference function for `Transpose` is vulnerable to a heap buffer overflow. This occurs whenever `perm` contains negative elements. The shape inference function does not validate that the indices in `perm` are all valid. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.7.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.6.1, TensorFlow 2.5.2, and TensorFlow 2.4.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: Loop over perm values reads in_idx = data[i] and checks only in_idx >= rank before indexing dims[i] = c->Dim(input, in_idx). A negative in_idx passes the check and is used as a dimension index.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing lower-bound constraint allows an index before the start of the intended buffer, matching CWE-787 out-of-bounds write. It is not merely a logic error because the unchecked index is used to access memory outside the valid dimension range.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The bound check omits negative perm values, so a negative index reaches c->Dim(input, in_idx), an out-of-bounds access on the rank-sized shape. Trigger: a Transpose perm containing a negative value; the supported consequence is an out-of-bounds read/write consistent with the described heap buffer overflow during shape inference.

commit_msg:
debuggerd: verify that traced threads belong to the right process.

Fix two races in debuggerd's PTRACE_ATTACH logic:
  1. The target thread in a crash dump request could exit between the
     /proc/<pid>/task/<tid> check and the PTRACE_ATTACH.
  2. Sibling threads could exit between listing /proc/<pid>/task and the
     PTRACE_ATTACH.

Bug: http://b/29555636
Change-Id: I4dfe1ea30e2c211d2389321bd66e3684dd757591
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    char buf[64];', '    struct stat s;', '    snprintf(buf, sizeof buf, "/proc/%d/task/%d", out_request->pid, out_request->tid);', '    if (stat(buf, &s)) {', '      ALOGE("tid %d does not exist in pid %d. ignoring debug request\\n",', '          out_request->tid, out_request->pid);', '  } else if (cr.uid == 0', '            || (cr.uid == AID_SYSTEM && msg.action == DEBUGGER_ACTION_DUMP_BACKTRACE)) {'], 'added_lines': ['    // This check needs to happen again after ptracing the requested thread to prevent a race.', '    if (!pid_contains_tid(out_request->pid, out_request->tid)) {', '      ALOGE("tid %d does not exist in pid %d. ignoring debug request\\n", out_request->tid,', '            out_request->pid);', '  } else if (cr.uid == 0 || (cr.uid == AID_SYSTEM && msg.action == DEBUGGER_ACTION_DUMP_BACKTRACE)) {']}
description: debuggerd/debuggerd.cpp in Debuggerd in Android 5.0.x before 5.0.2, 5.1.x before 5.1.1, 6.x before 2016-09-01, and 7.0 before 2016-09-01 mishandles the interaction between PTRACE_ATTACH operations and thread exits, which allows attackers to gain privileges via a crafted application, aka internal bug 29555636.

code_evidence: The client-supplied msg.tid is stored into out_request->tid (line 32) while out_request->pid comes from SO_PEERCRED (line 33). For DEBUGGER_ACTION_CRASH, the only validation builds '/proc/%d/task/%d' from those values and calls stat() (lines 39-42); a successful stat merely proves the tid existed at that instant and is not tied to an open reference, so the tid may exit and be reused before the later PTRACE_ATTACH performed by the caller.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The flaw is a missing access-control check on the target of a privileged ptrace operation: debuggerd fails to ensure the attached thread still belongs to the requesting process, so authorization of the target is bypassed. This is a permissions/privilege-management weakness, matching CWE-264 rather than a memory-corruption class.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the crash path checks tid existence via a racy path-based stat() and never re-verifies the traced thread after ptrace attach. Trigger: an unprivileged crafted application sends a crash request whose tid exits (or whose sibling threads exit) between the /proc check and PTRACE_ATTACH, letting debuggerd attach to a thread of another process. Consequence: the privileged debuggerd process operates on an unintended target, enabling privilege gain.

description: rootdir/init.rc in Android 4.x before 4.4.4 does not ensure that the /data/tombstones directory exists for the Debuggerd component, which allows attackers to gain privileges via a crafted application, aka internal bug 26403620.

code_evidence: The function creates TOMBSTONE_DIR with mode 0755 and only logs failure; it does not abort, so execution continues even if the directory could not be created or already existed with attacker-controlled attributes.
It then calls chown(TOMBSTONE_DIR, AID_SYSTEM, AID_SYSTEM) and again only logs on failure, leaving ownership unchanged if the call fails.
It restores the SELinux context and only proceeds to find_and_open_tombstone when restorecon returns 0; on failure it logs and skips, but the directory's existence/ownership was never guaranteed.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-264 covers weaknesses in permission and privilege management. Here the code manages directory creation, ownership (chown to AID_SYSTEM) and SELinux context but does not enforce these constraints, directly matching improper permission handling; it is not a buffer or integer issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the tombstone directory's existence, ownership and security context are set up with best-effort calls whose failures are ignored, and the directory is not guaranteed to exist. Trigger: a crafted application causes a crash while /data/tombstones is missing or improperly owned/labeled. Consequence: the tombstone open path proceeds under incorrect permissions/ownership, enabling privilege or access-control problems rather than a memory-safety issue.

Note that this is only exploitable if the application using Hermes permits evaluation of untrusted JavaScript. Hence, most React Native applications are not affected.

commit_msg:
lib/node.c: Limit recursion in ri-records (CVE-2021-3622)

Windows Registry hive "ri"-records are arbitrarily nested B-tree-like
structures:

  +-------------+
  | ri          |
  |-------------|
  | nr_offsets  |
  |   offset[0] ------>  points to another lf/lh/li/ri block
  |   offset[1] ------>
  |   offset[2] ------>
  +-------------+

It is possible to construct a hive with a very deeply nested tree of
ri-records, causing the internal _get_children function to recurse to
any depth which can cause programs linked to hivex to crash with a
stack overflow.

Since it is not thought that deeply nested ri-records occur in real
hives, limit recursion depth.  If you hit this limit you will see the
following error and the operation will return an error instead of
crashing:

  \> ls
  hivex: _get_children: returning EINVAL because: ri-record nested to depth >= 32
  ls: Invalid argument

Thanks to Jeremy Galindo for finding and reporting this bug.

Reported-by: Jeremy Galindo, Sr Security Engineer, Datto.com
Signed-off-by: Richard W.M. Jones <rjones@redhat.com>
Fixes: CVE-2021-3622
Fixes: https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1975489
(cherry picked from commit 781a12c4a49dd81365c9c567c5aa5e19e894ba0e)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['               int flags)', '      if (_get_children (h, offset, children, blocks, flags) == -1)'], 'added_lines': ['               int flags, unsigned depth)', '      /* Although in theory hive ri records might be nested to any', '       * depth, in practice this is unlikely.  Recursing here caused', '       * CVE-2021-3622.  Thus limit the depth we will recurse to', '       * something small.', '       */', '      if (depth >= 32) {', '        SET_ERRNO (EINVAL, "ri-record nested to depth >= %u", depth);', '        return -1;', '      }', '', '      if (_get_children (h, offset, children, blocks, flags, depth+1) == -1)']}
description: A flaw was found in the hivex library. This flaw allows an attacker to input a specially crafted Windows Registry (hive) file, which would cause hivex to recursively call the _get_children() function, leading to a stack overflow. The highest threat from this vulnerability is to system availability.

code_evidence: In the 'ri' branch, _get_children parses nr_offsets from the attacker-controlled hive block, bounds it against len, then for each offset computes a subkey and validates it as a block. It then unconditionally calls _get_children recursively on that offset with no depth argument or limit, so a crafted hive with ri-records pointing to further ri-records drives unbounded recursion.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-400 fits because the function fails to throttle a limited resource (call-stack depth) consumed in proportion to attacker-controlled nesting, leading to resource-exhaustion DoS. This is uncontrolled resource consumption, not a memory-corruption or bounds bug.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the recursive call at line 77 lacks any depth bound, so attacker-supplied ri-record offset chains control the recursion depth. Trigger: a hive file containing deeply nested ri-record blocks. Consequence: stack exhaustion and crash of the linked program, an availability impact.

commit_msg:
9pfs: handle walk of ".." in the root directory

The 9P spec at http://man.cat-v.org/plan_9/5/intro says:

All directories must support walks to the directory .. (dot-dot) meaning
parent directory, although by convention directories contain no explicit
entry for .. or . (dot).  The parent of the root directory of a server's
tree is itself.

This means that a client cannot walk further than the root directory
exported by the server. In other words, if the client wants to walk
"/.." or "/foo/../..", the server should answer like the request was
to walk "/".

This patch just does that:
- we cache the QID of the root directory at attach time
- during the walk we compare the QID of each path component with the root
  QID to detect if we're in a "/.." situation
- if so, we skip the current component and go to the next one

Signed-off-by: Greg Kurz <groug@kaod.org>
Reviewed-by: Eric Blake <eblake@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Peter Maydell <peter.maydell@linaro.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    memcpy(&s->root_qid, &qid, sizeof(qid));']}
description: Directory traversal vulnerability in hw/9pfs/9p.c in QEMU (aka Quick Emulator) allows local guest OS administrators to access host files outside the export path via a .. (dot dot) in an unspecified string.

code_evidence: The attach handler resolves the export root with v9fs_co_name_to_path(pdu, NULL, "/", &fidp->path), then derives the root QID via fid_to_qid into local qid and stores it in s->root_qid; this QID is later used by the walk code to detect a '/..' that would escape the export root.

The patch records the root directory's QID at attach time so that subsequent walks can compare each component against the root and clamp '..' at the root instead of traversing above it; without this cached root QID, a client-supplied '..' component could resolve outside the exported tree.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-22 fits because client-supplied path input ('..' components) is intended to stay under the restricted export root, but the code does not neutralize the special element; caching the root QID is the constraint that enables clamping. A related weakness like CWE-23 is a child of CWE-22, but the target is the parent path-traversal entry.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the server lacks a stored identity for the export root, so client-controlled path components containing '..' cannot be recognized as attempts to ascend past the root. Trigger: a guest sends an attach followed by a walk such as '/..' or '/foo/../..'. Supported consequence: path traversal outside the export directory, allowing access to host files beyond the shared tree.

commit_msg:
Fixed bug of old finalized objects in the GC

When an object aged OLD1 is finalized, it is moved from the list
'finobj' to the *beginning* of the list 'allgc'. So, this part of the
list (and not only the survival list) must be visited by 'markold'.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  markold(g, g->survival, g->reallyold);'], 'added_lines': ['  markold(g, g->allgc, g->reallyold);']}
description: Lua 5.4.0 has a getobjname heap-based buffer over-read because youngcollection in lgc.c uses markold for an insufficient number of list members.

code_evidence: youngcollection calls markold(g, g->survival, g->reallyold), restricting the old-object marking traversal to the survival list. Finalized OLD1 objects are moved to the beginning of allgc, so they lie outside the survival range and are not marked old here; markold(g, g->finobj, g->finobjrold) only covers the finalization list.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect produces reads beyond the intended buffer during later object-name resolution, matching CWE-125's out-of-bounds read. It is not merely incorrect garbage-collection bookkeeping; the supported consequence is an out-of-bounds memory read.

evidence_lines.code:
markold(g, g->survival, g->reallyold);
markold(g, g->finobj, g->finobjrold);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the markold traversal starts from g->survival instead of g->allgc, so finalized OLD1 objects relocated to the head of allgc are skipped during the young-collection marking pass. When getobjname later relies on this incomplete marking/state, it can traverse an object list whose members were not correctly aged, reading past the intended buffer and causing a heap-based out-of-bounds read.

disconnects while a WriteValue call is being processed with dbus.

commit_msg:
Kafka: Be more strict when dissecting varints.

The Kafka dissector uses the return value of tvb_get_varint to advance
the packet offset in many places. If tvb_get_varint fails it returns 0,
which means our offset isn't guaranteed to advance. Stop dissection
whenever that happens. Fixes #17811.

On the failure path (len==0), the returned offset equals the input offset, so the caller's offset is not guaranteed to advance; lines 21-24 show the normal path advancing offset by len+length, contrasting with the non-advancing failure return.

It is not merely a bad-value error; the key defect is that iteration count is not bounded because the offset fails to advance.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: when the varint is malformed (len==0), the function returns the unchanged offset instead of signaling termination. Trigger: a crafted Kafka packet/capture with a bad varint causes the caller's dissection loop to re-enter at the same offset indefinitely, consuming CPU.

commit_msg:
avcodec/vp3: Add missing check for av_malloc

Since the av_malloc() may fail and return NULL pointer,
it is needed that the 's->edge_emu_buffer' should be checked
whether the new allocation is success.

Fixes: d14723861b ("VP3: fix decoding of videos with stride > 2048")
Reviewed-by: Peter Ross <pross@xvid.org>
Signed-off-by: Jiasheng Jiang <jiasheng@iscas.ac.cn>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if (!s->edge_emu_buffer)'], 'added_lines': ['    if (!s->edge_emu_buffer) {', '        if (!s->edge_emu_buffer) {', '            ret = AVERROR(ENOMEM);', '            goto error;', '        }', '    }']}
description: An issue was discovered in the FFmpeg package, where vp3_decode_frame in libavcodec/vp3.c lacks check of the return value of av_malloc() and will cause a null pointer dereference, impacting availability.

code_evidence: Line 81 checks only whether s->edge_emu_buffer is already set; line 82 assigns the result of av_malloc(9 * FFABS(s->current_frame.f->linesize[0])) to it without verifying the return value. If av_malloc fails, the field remains NULL and execution continues into the subsequent decode path.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked allocation leads to a pointer expected to be valid being NULL and subsequently dereferenced, directly matching CWE-476. This is not merely an unchecked return value (CWE-252); the supported consequence is dereference of the NULL pointer.

evidence_lines.code:
if (!s->edge_emu_buffer)
s->edge_emu_buffer = av_malloc(9 * FFABS(s->current_frame.f->linesize[0]));

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the allocation return value is stored directly into s->edge_emu_buffer with no NULL check. Trigger: av_malloc fails under memory pressure. Consequence: later decoding code uses the still-NULL edge_emu_buffer, producing a NULL pointer dereference and availability loss (crash).

commit_msg:
fix possible overflow in effect wrappers.

Add checks on parameter size field in effect command handlers
to avoid overflow leading to invalid comparison with min allowed
size for command and reply buffers.

Bug: 26347509.
Change-Id: I20e6a9b6de8e5172b957caa1ac9410b9752efa4d
(cherry picked from commit ad1bd92a49d78df6bc6e75bee68c517c1326f3cf)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [''], 'added_lines': ['            if (SIZE_MAX - sizeof(effect_param_t) < (size_t)p->psize) {', '                android_errorWriteLog(0x534e4554, "26347509");', '                return -EINVAL;', '            }']}
description: Multiple integer overflows in libeffects in mediaserver in Android 4.x before 4.4.4, 5.x before 5.1.1 LMY49H, and 6.x before 2016-03-01 allow attackers to gain privileges via a crafted application, as demonstrated by obtaining Signature or SignatureOrSystem access, related to EffectBundle.cpp and EffectReverb.cpp, aka internal bug 26347509.

code_evidence: Line 63 casts the caller-controlled pCmdData to effect_param_t; lines 64-67 validate cmdSize against sizeof(effect_param_t) plus p->psize, but p->psize is attacker-controlled and the addition can wrap, so the comparison may pass when it should fail.
Line 71 then memcpy's sizeof(effect_param_t) + p->psize bytes into pReplyData, and line 73 computes voffset from p->psize, propagating the wrapped size into a buffer copy.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The root cause is an unchecked integer addition of an untrusted size field, matching the Numeric Errors category (integer overflow in size calculation). It is not merely a missing length check: the check exists but is bypassed because the arithmetic wraps.

evidence_lines.code:
memcpy(pReplyData, pCmdData, sizeof(effect_param_t) + p->psize);
int voffset = ((p->psize - 1) / sizeof(int32_t) + 1) * sizeof(int32_t);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The size check adds a caller-supplied psize to a fixed header size without checking for overflow. A crafted psize near SIZE_MAX makes the sum wrap to a small value that satisfies the cmdSize/replySize comparisons, so the subsequent memcpy and voffset arithmetic operate on an inconsistent length, leading to out-of-bounds memory access.

commit_msg:
http: make length/offset-related variables unsigned.

Fixes #5992, reported and found by Paul Cher <paulcher@icloud.com>.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    s->chunksize = -1;'], 'added_lines': ['    s->chunksize = UINT64_MAX;']}
description: Heap-based buffer overflow in libavformat/http.c in FFmpeg before 2.8.10, 3.0.x before 3.0.5, 3.1.x before 3.1.6, and 3.2.x before 3.2.2 allows remote web servers to execute arbitrary code via a negative chunk size in an HTTP response.

code_evidence: Line 6 initializes s->chunksize to -1, a signed sentinel that later chunk-size handling treats as a length/offset value; the commit changes this to UINT64_MAX to make the variable unsigned.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-119 fits because the missing unsigned restriction on the chunk-size field permits operations outside the intended memory buffer. The signed sentinel itself is the root cause; the out-of-bounds heap access is the resultant bound violation described by CWE-119, rather than a distinct weakness class.

evidence_lines.code: s->chunksize = -1;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The root cause is a signed -1 sentinel assigned to a length/offset field that downstream HTTP chunk parsing uses without an unsigned bounds check. A malicious server supplying a negative chunk size can drive the value into an out-of-bounds buffer operation, supporting heap corruption and potential code execution.

commit_msg:
ALSA: control: code refactoring for ELEM_READ/ELEM_WRITE operations

ALSA control core handles ELEM_READ/ELEM_WRITE requests within lock
acquisition of a counting semaphore. The lock is acquired in helper
functions in the end of call path before calling implementations of each
driver.

ioctl(2) with SNDRV_CTL_ELEM_READ
...
->snd_ctl_ioctl()
  ->snd_ctl_elem_read_user()
    ->snd_ctl_elem_read()
      ->down_read(controls_rwsem)
      ->snd_ctl_find_id()
      ->struct snd_kcontrol.get()
      ->up_read(controls_rwsem)

ioctl(2) with SNDRV_CTL_ELEM_WRITE
...
->snd_ctl_ioctl()
  ->snd_ctl_elem_write_user()
    ->snd_ctl_elem_write()
      ->down_read(controls_rwsem)
      ->snd_ctl_find_id()
      ->struct snd_kcontrol.put()
      ->up_read(controls_rwsem)

This commit moves the lock acquisition to middle of the call graph to
simplify the helper functions. As a result:

ioctl(2) with SNDRV_CTL_ELEM_READ
...
->snd_ctl_ioctl()
  ->snd_ctl_elem_read_user()
    ->down_read(controls_rwsem)
    ->snd_ctl_elem_read()
      ->snd_ctl_find_id()
      ->struct snd_kcontrol.get()
    ->up_read(controls_rwsem)

ioctl(2) with SNDRV_CTL_ELEM_WRITE
...
->snd_ctl_ioctl()
  ->snd_ctl_elem_write_user()
    ->down_read(controls_rwsem)
    ->snd_ctl_elem_write()
      ->snd_ctl_find_id()
      ->struct snd_kcontrol.put()
    ->up_read(controls_rwsem)

Signed-off-by: Takashi Sakamoto <o-takashi@sakamocchi.jp>
Signed-off-by: Takashi Iwai <tiwai@suse.de>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (result >= 0)'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (result >= 0) {', '\t\tdown_read(&card->controls_rwsem);', '\t\tup_read(&card->controls_rwsem);', '\t}']}
description: A use after free vulnerability exists in the ALSA PCM package in the Linux Kernel. SNDRV_CTL_IOCTL_ELEM_{READ|WRITE}32 is missing locks that can be used in a use-after-free that can result in a priviledge escalation to gain ring0 access from the system user. We recommend upgrading past commit 56b88b50565cd8b946a2d00b0c83927b7ebb055e

code_evidence: The read path invokes snd_ctl_elem_read(card, control) under only snd_power_lock, without holding card->controls_rwsem; the driver's get() callback and snd_ctl_find_id() run unlocked, so the control object looked up can be concurrently removed/freed.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing lock permits the control object to be freed while still in use, matching CWE-416 (reuse/reference of memory after free). It is not merely a race condition: the supported consequence is dereference of freed memory.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: control element lookup and access occur without the controls_rwsem that serializes removal of controls. Trigger: a concurrent ioctl removing the element while ELEM_READ runs. Consequence: the get() callback dereferences freed control memory, giving a use-after-free that may be exploited for privilege escalation.

commit_msg:
Release "3.0.10": Fix issues #12, #13, and #14.

FossilOrigin-Name: 70747c8d1c4e7bf176bec8cfb9d3cac3e64a696e7df0b1e3712d3f6b952164c3
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if (maa>3)', '        vobjs[1] = (maa>1?Jsi_ValueNewNumber(interp, i):NULL);'], 'added_lines': ['    if (maa>3 || fptr->type == FC_BUILDIN)', '        vobjs[1] = (maa>1?Jsi_ValueNewNumber(interp, i):interp->NullValue);']}
description: An issue found in Jsish v.3.0.11 allows a remote attacker to cause a denial of service via the Jsi_ValueIsNumber function in ./src/jsiValue.c file.

code_evidence: vobjs is a fixed-size stack array of 4 Jsi_Value pointers (line 28). maa derives from the callback's declared argument count (line 30) and is clamped to 3 only when maa>3 (lines 31-32); a builtin with zero/unknown argnames yields maa=0. Jsi_ObjNewArray is then called with maa and the vobjs contents (line 38), so the array size handed to the constructor is driven by the unvalidated argCnt rather than the actual number of populated entries (vobjs[0..2] are always set at lines 35-37).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the fixed vobjs[4] stack buffer is indexed/sized using maa derived from unvalidated callback metadata, permitting a write/read past the intended buffer bounds. This is a bounds-violation root cause, not merely a null-dereference or type confusion.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the argument-count clamp assumes maa<=3 for all callbacks, but builtins can report a different/zero argCnt, so maa can mismatch the fixed vobjs[4] buffer and the number of initialized elements. Trigger: Array.prototype.filter is invoked with a builtin callback whose argnames metadata yields maa outside the expected 0–3 range. The mismatch can cause the array constructor to read past the initialized vobjs entries or size the array inconsistently, leading to out-of-bounds access/memory corruption and a crash (DoS).
