description: The overlayfs implementation in the Linux kernel through 4.5.2 does not properly maintain POSIX ACL xattr data, which allows local users to gain privileges by leveraging a group-writable setgid directory.

code_evidence: lookup_one_len returns a dentry that may be negative (no inode); the code only guards against IS_ERR, not against a negative dentry, then calls ovl_cleanup with dentry->d_inode potentially NULL.

Only entries flagged is_whiteout are processed, and the loop iterates over the cache list under the upper inode mutex, so the negative-dentry path is reachable for whiteout entries whose lookup misses.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-269 concerns improper assignment, tracking, or checking of privileges and control spheres. Here the missing positivity check lets a negative dentry enter cleanup, but the code does not itself assign, modify, or check any privilege for an actor; privilege gain is only a downstream impact of the ACL/xattr description, not a root cause visible in this function, so CWE-269 is not directly supported.

evidence_lines.code:
if (!p->is_whiteout)
continue;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function assumes a successful lookup yields a positive dentry and passes it to ovl_cleanup without checking dentry->d_inode. Trigger: a whiteout cache entry whose name no longer resolves to an inode causes a negative dentry to flow into cleanup. Supported consequence: inconsistent cleanup of whiteout entries, contributing to improper maintenance of directory metadata rather than an explicit privilege decision.

commit_msg: opj_t2_encode_packet(): fix potential write heap buffer overflow (#992)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['        if (length < 6) {', '            if (p_t2_mode == FINAL_PASS) {', '                opj_event_msg(p_manager, EVT_ERROR,', '                              "opj_t2_encode_packet(): only %u bytes remaining in "', '                              "output buffer. %u needed.\\n",', '                              length, 6);', '            }', '            return OPJ_FALSE;', '        }', '        if (length < 2) {', '            if (p_t2_mode == FINAL_PASS) {', '                opj_event_msg(p_manager, EVT_ERROR,', '                              "opj_t2_encode_packet(): only %u bytes remaining in "', '                              "output buffer. %u needed.\\n",', '                              length, 2);', '            }', '            return OPJ_FALSE;', '        }']}
description: A heap-based buffer overflow was discovered in the opj_t2_encode_packet function in lib/openjp2/t2.c in OpenJPEG 2.2.0. The vulnerability causes an out-of-bounds write, which may lead to remote denial of service or possibly unspecified other impact.

code_evidence: When the J2K_CP_CSTY_SOP style flag is set, the code unconditionally writes six bytes c[0]..c[5] and then does c += 6; length -= 6 without checking that length >= 6, so a buffer smaller than six bytes is overrun.

Similarly, when J2K_CP_CSTY_EPH is set, it writes c[0]=255 and c[1]=146 and advances/ decrements by two with no prior check that at least two bytes remain, allowing a two-byte out-of-bounds write at the end of the output buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the writes at c[0..5] and c[0..1] can occur past the end of the intended dest buffer when length is smaller than the fixed marker size, an out-of-bounds write. It is not merely an integer issue; the missing length guard directly permits writing beyond the allocated buffer.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the SOP and EPH marker emissions write a fixed number of bytes into the caller-provided dest buffer without verifying that the remaining length is sufficient. Trigger: a codestream enabling J2K_CP_CSTY_SOP or J2K_CP_CSTY_EPH combined with a small or nearly-full output buffer. Consequence: heap out-of-bounds write past dest, corrupting memory and potentially causing a crash or other impact.

net: rose: fix UAF bugs caused by timer handler

There are UAF bugs in rose_heartbeat_expiry(), rose_timer_expiry()
and rose_idletimer_expiry(). The root cause is that del_timer()
could not stop the timer handler that is running and the refcount
of sock is not managed properly.

One of the UAF bugs is shown below:

    (thread 1)          |        (thread 2)
                        |  rose_bind
                        |  rose_connect
                        |    rose_start_heartbeat
rose_release            |    (wait a time)
  case ROSE_STATE_0     |
  rose_destroy_socket   |  rose_heartbeat_expiry
    rose_stop_heartbeat |
    sock_put(sk)        |    ...
  sock_put(sk) // FREE  |
                        |    bh_lock_sock(sk) // USE

The sock is deallocated by sock_put() in rose_release() and
then used by bh_lock_sock() in rose_heartbeat_expiry().

add_timer(&rose->idletimer);

commit_msg:
Patch series "Fix several device private page reference counting issues",
v2

This series aims to fix a number of page reference counting issues in
drivers dealing with device private ZONE_DEVICE pages.  These result in
use-after-free type bugs, either from accessing a struct page which no
longer exists because it has been removed or accessing fields within the
struct page which are no longer valid because the page has been freed.

During normal usage it is unlikely these will cause any problems.  However
without these fixes it is possible to crash the kernel from userspace. 
These crashes can be triggered either by unloading the kernel module or
unbinding the device from the driver prior to a userspace task exiting. 
In modules such as Nouveau it is also possible to trigger some of these
issues by explicitly closing the device file-descriptor prior to the task
exiting and then accessing device private memory.

This involves some minor changes to both PowerPC and AMD GPU code. 
Unfortunately I lack hardware to test either of those so any help there
would be appreciated.  The changes mimic what is done in for both Nouveau
and hmm-tests though so I doubt they will cause problems.


This patch (of 8):

When the CPU tries to access a device private page the migrate_to_ram()
callback associated with the pgmap for the page is called.  However no
reference is taken on the faulting page.  Therefore a concurrent migration
of the device private page can free the page and possibly the underlying
pgmap.  This results in a race which can crash the kernel due to the
migrate_to_ram() function pointer becoming invalid.  It also means drivers
can't reliably read the zone_device_data field because the page may have
been freed with memunmap_pages().

Close the race by getting a reference on the page while holding the ptl to
ensure it has not been freed.  Unfortunately the elevated reference count
will cause the migration required to handle the fault to fail.  To avoid
this failure pass the faulting page into the migrate_vma functions so that
if an elevated reference count is found it can be checked to see if it's
expected or not.

description: A vulnerability was found in Linux Kernel. It has been classified as problematic. Affected is an unknown function of the file mm/memory.c of the component Driver Handler. The manipulation leads to use after free. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue. The identifier of this vulnerability is VDB-211020.

code_evidence: Under only mmap_read_lock, the function resolves the gfn to a user HVA and locates the vma, then calls kvmppc_svm_page_out(vma, start, end, page_shift, kvm, gpa, NULL) without taking any reference on the faulting page.

The patch only adds a NULL argument to that call, so the faulting page is not passed to the migration path and no page reference is pinned; the mmap read lock and srcu lock are released without any page reference being held.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function invokes a callback that dereferences a device-private page whose lifetime is not protected, matching CWE-416: memory is referenced after it may have been freed. This is not merely a missing NULL check; the defect is absent lifetime/refcount protection across concurrent migration, which is the use-after-free root cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the page-out path operates on a device-private page without acquiring a reference while holding the ptl, so a concurrent migration/memunmap_pages can free the page and pgmap. Trigger: a CPU fault on a device-private page races with migration or driver unbind/module unload; the migrate_to_ram callback or zone_device_data is then used after the page is freed. Supported consequence: use-after-free of the struct page/pgmap, leading to kernel crash or invalid function-pointer dereference.

Trigger: attacker-supplied media with a header that fails to decode but leaves bytes_remaining positive. Consequence: out-of-bounds buffer access during frame decode/format conversion, enabling memory corruption and potential remote code execution.

Merge pull request from GHSA-8hcp-hm38-mfph

* Check hostname during TLS transport selection

description: PJSIP is a free and open source multimedia communication library written in C language implementing standard based protocols such as SIP, SDP, RTP, STUN, TURN, and ICE. In version 2.10 and earlier, PJSIP transport can be reused if they have the same IP address + port + protocol. However, this is insufficient for secure transport since it lacks remote hostname authentication. Suppose we have created a TLS connection to `sip.foo.com`, which has an IP address `100.1.1.1`. If we want to create a TLS connection to another hostname, say `sip.bar.com`, which has the same IP address, then it will reuse that existing connection, even though `100.1.1.1` does not have certificate to authenticate as `sip.bar.com`. The vulnerability allows for an insecure interaction without user awareness. It affects users who need access to connections to different destinations that translate to the same address, and allows man-in-the-middle attack if attacker can route a connection to another destination such as in the case of DNS spoofing.

code_evidence: Line 26 stores the dialog pointer in tdata->mod_data but the function never records the destination hostname used for the created request.
Lines 35-39 build the request (auth init) and then lines 40-41 return tdata without associating any hostname with the transport selection data.
The request is created from dlg->target (line 16) but no hostname is propagated into tdata->dest_info.name, leaving transport reuse keyed only on address/port/protocol.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-295 fits because the missing hostname binding means the TLS peer certificate is not validated against the intended destination, allowing a connection authenticated for one host to serve another. This is improper certificate/hostname validation rather than a generic transport-reuse bug.

evidence_lines.code: tdata->mod_data[dlg->ua->id] = dlg;

*p_tdata = tdata;
return PJ_SUCCESS;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the created transaction data carries no destination hostname, so the later transport selection cannot authenticate the remote host beyond IP/port/protocol. Trigger: a dialog targeting a hostname that resolves to an already-connected IP causes reuse of the existing TLS connection. Consequence: certificate identity for the intended hostname is never checked, enabling a man-in-the-middle via DNS spoofing.

commit_msg:
The VT_DISALLOCATE ioctl can free a virtual console while tty_release()
is still running, causing a use-after-free in con_shutdown().  This
occurs because VT_DISALLOCATE considers a virtual console's
'struct vc_data' to be unused as soon as the corresponding tty's
refcount hits 0.  But actually it may be still being closed.

Fix this by making vc_data be reference-counted via the embedded
'struct tty_port'.  A newly allocated virtual console has refcount 1.
Opening it for the first time increments the refcount to 2.  Closing it
for the last time decrements the refcount (in tty_operations::cleanup()
so that it happens late enough), as does VT_DISALLOCATE.

Reproducer:
	#include <fcntl.h>
	#include <linux/vt.h>
	#include <sys/ioctl.h>
	#include <unistd.h>

	int main()
	{
		if (fork()) {
			for (;;)
				close(open("/dev/tty5", O_RDWR));
		} else {
			int fd = open("/dev/tty10", O_RDWR);

			for (;;)
				ioctl(fd, VT_DISALLOCATE, 5);
		}
	}

description: A race condition in the Linux kernel before 5.6.2 between the VT_DISALLOCATE ioctl and closing/opening of ttys could lead to a use-after-free.

code_evidence: vt_disallocate takes console_lock() and checks vt_busy(vc_num), then calls vc_deallocate() under that lock, releases the lock with console_unlock(), and afterwards frees the vc_data via tty_port_destroy() and kfree(vc). The busy check and deallocation are serialized, but the final teardown of vc->port and vc occurs after the lock is dropped, so it is not covered by the same exclusive section.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function's shared vc_data is freed outside the console_lock critical section that guarded the busy check, allowing an interfering concurrent tty close to access it; this is improper synchronization of a shared resource, matching CWE-362. The use-after-free is the downstream consequence, not the root cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the decision that a console is unused and its subsequent destruction are not atomic with respect to tty_release(), which may still be closing the same tty. Trigger: VT_DISALLOCATE races a concurrent close/open of the tty so vc_deallocate() returns the vc_data while tty_release() continues, and the unlocked tty_port_destroy()/kfree() frees it. Consequence: use-after-free in con_shutdown(), leading to a crash or memory corruption.

commit_msg:
Fix segmentation fault when closing an element

Reported in issue #19. The error happened when the node passed to elm_close
wasn't an element as it was supposed to.

In the example files reported with the issue, the node causing the crash
was a comment.

Now, elm_close will exit with an error if the node it receives isn't
an element. Some calls that could potentially call it with something else
check the node type before calling it.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      elm_close(nodo);', '\telm_close(nodo);', '\telm_close(nodo);'], 'added_lines': ['      if (nodo->tipo == Node_element) {', '        elm_close(nodo);', '      }', '        if (nodo->tipo == Node_element) {', '          elm_close(nodo);', '        }', '        if (nodo->tipo == Node_element) {', '          elm_close(nodo);', '        }']}
description: html2xhtml v1.3 was discovered to contain an Out-Of-Bounds read in the function static void elm_close(tree_node_t *nodo) at procesador.c. This vulnerability allows attackers to access sensitive files or cause a Denial of Service (DoS) via a crafted html file.

code_evidence: Each loop walks nodo up the padre chain from actual_element and calls elm_close(nodo) without verifying nodo->tipo is an element.
The loop guard only checks nodo non-NULL and nodo!=html; a comment or other non-element node in the ancestor chain is passed directly to elm_close.
The same unguarded elm_close call appears in the BODY and FRAMESET insertion branches, so the missing type check is systematic.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The patch adds nodo->tipo == Node_element guards before elm_close, confirming the pre-patch code operated on a non-element node and read beyond its intended structure. This is an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125), distinct from a null-pointer dereference because the node is non-NULL but of the wrong type.

evidence_lines.code:
for (nodo=actual_element; nodo && (nodo!=html); nodo=nodo->padre)
elm_close(nodo);

for(nodo=actual_element; nodo && (nodo!=html); nodo=nodo->padre)
elm_close(nodo);

for(nodo=actual_element; nodo && (nodo!=html); nodo=nodo->padre)
elm_close(nodo);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the traversal invokes elm_close on any ancestor node without confirming it is an element. Trigger: a crafted HTML file leaves a comment (or other non-element) node in the actual_element ancestor chain. elm_close then treats that node as an element and reads element-specific fields past the intended structure, producing an out-of-bounds read that can crash or leak memory.

commit_msg:
Avoid Segfault for scalar shapes.

Calling tensor::FromElementsOp with an empty vector of elements and no type
causes a segfault. We need to let the FromElementsOp know which scalar type it
should have.
Also add back the DynamicBroadcastInDimOp canonicalization patterns, which
previously prevented this bug from happening.
Add a regression test that demonstrates the bug.

Change-Id: I6d1d6cfb71aabbad6102422625a00bbe253ac95a

description: Tensorflow is an Open Source Machine Learning Framework. The `simplifyBroadcast` function in the MLIR-TFRT infrastructure in TensorFlow is vulnerable to a segfault (hence, denial of service), if called with scalar shapes. If all shapes are scalar, then `maxRank` is 0, so we build an empty `SmallVector`. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.8.0. This is the only affected version.

code_evidence: maxRank is initialized to 0 and only updated from shape sizes; for scalar shapes every found_shape->size() is 0, so maxRank stays 0. The code then constructs joined_dimensions and shape_and_rank_for_dim with size 0 without special-casing the empty-rank case.
The is_splat check on shape_and_rank_for_dim is followed by indexing shape_and_rank_for_dim[0], and the final FromElementsOp is built from the possibly empty elements vector without a scalar type.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function fails to check for the unusual but reachable condition of zero total rank before indexing and constructing operations, matching CWE-754's improper check for unusual/exceptional conditions leading to a crash. The fix explicitly guards maxRank == 0, confirming the missing condition check rather than a different weakness class.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function assumes at least one non-scalar dimension exists and does not handle the exceptional all-scalar case (maxRank == 0). Trigger: callers pass all-scalar shapes, producing zero-sized SmallVectors; indexing [0] and building FromElementsOp with an empty element list (and no type) cause a segfault, i.e., denial of service.

description:

commit_msg:
Bug 739133 - (CVE-2017-17785) Heap overflow while parsing FLI files.

It is possible to trigger a heap overflow while parsing FLI files. The
RLE decoder is vulnerable to out of boundary writes due to lack of
boundary checks.

The variable "framebuf" points to a memory area which was allocated
with fli_header->width * fli_header->height bytes. The RLE decoder
therefore must never write beyond that limit.

If an illegal frame is detected, the parser won't stop, which means
that the next valid sequence is properly parsed again. This should
allow GIMP to parse FLI files as good as possible even if they are
broken by an attacker or by accident.

While at it, I changed the variable xc to be of type size_t, because
the multiplication of width and height could overflow a 16 bit type.

Signed-off-by: Tobias Stoeckmann <tobias@stoeckmann.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tunsigned short xc, pc, pcnt;', '\t\t\t\tfor (len=-(signed char)ps; len>0; len--) {', '\t\t\t\tmemset(&(pos[xc]), val, ps);', '\t\t\t\txc+=ps;'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tunsigned short pc, pcnt;', '\t\tsize_t n, xc;', '\t\tn=(size_t)fli_header->width * (fli_header->height-yc);', '\t\t\t\tfor (len=-(signed char)ps; len>0 && xc<n; len--) {', '\t\t\t\tsize_t len;', '\t\t\t\tlen=MIN(n-xc,ps);', '\t\t\t\tmemset(&(pos[xc]), val, len);', '\t\t\t\txc+=len;']}
description: In GIMP 2.8.22, there is a heap-based buffer overflow in the fli_read_brun function in plug-ins/file-fli/fli.c.

code_evidence: Literal RLE run: the loop writes pos[xc++] for each byte read, with no check that xc stays below the row/framebuffer bound, so a long run advances xc past the allocated framebuf.
Copy run: memset writes ps bytes at &pos[xc] and then xc+=ps, where ps is an attacker-controlled unsigned short; neither the write length nor the resulting xc is bounded by the framebuffer size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the decoder writes beyond the intended heap buffer via unchecked run-length indices. It is not merely a read overflow; the unsafe operation is the out-of-bounds store in pos[xc] and memset.

evidence_lines.code:
for (len=-(signed char)ps; len>0; len--) {
pos[xc++]=fli_read_char(f);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is the absence of any bound on xc relative to the framebuffer allocated as width*height. Triggered by crafted FLI RLE run lengths (ps or negative-ps run) that exceed the remaining row/plane, causing writes past the heap buffer; this yields heap corruption and potential code execution or crash.

commit_msg:
Fix OOB access due to multiple backspaces

Commit 419ca82d57 (Fix m17n backspace handling causes out-of-bounds
write in checkType) introduced an incomplete fix.

In function checkType we store the length of the previous multi-char
character in a buffer plens_buffer with pointer plens pointing to the
current position inside the buffer. When encountering a backspace plens
is set to the previous position without a bounds check. This will lead
to plens being out of bounds if we get more backspaces than we have
processed multi-char characters before.

If we are at the beginning of the buffer do not decrement and set plen
(the current length) to 0.

This also fixes GH Issue #270 [BUG] Out of bound read in Strnew_size ,
Str.c:61

If the above explanation does sound weird it's because I didn't fully
grok that function. :-)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t    plen = *(--plens);', '\t\t\t    plen = *(--plens);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t    if (plens == plens_buffer)', '\t\t\t\tplen = 0;', '\t\t\t    else', '\t\t\t\tplen = *(--plens);', '\t\t\t    if (plens == plens_buffer)', '\t\t\t\tplen = 0;', '\t\t\t    else', '\t\t\t\tplen = *(--plens);']}
description: An out-of-bounds write issue has been discovered in the backspace handling of the checkType() function in etc.c within the W3M application. This vulnerability is triggered by supplying a specially crafted HTML file to the w3m binary. Exploitation of this flaw could lead to application crashes, resulting in a denial of service condition.

code_evidence: On backspace handling, plens is decremented and dereferenced (plen = *(--plens)) after Strshrink/prop adjustments, with no check that plens is still within plens_buffer.
A second identical backspace branch repeats plen = *(--plens) at line 183 without any lower-bound check.
plens starts at plens_buffer (line 37); repeated backspaces can drive plens before the buffer start, and the dereference reads/writes out of bounds.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the unchecked pointer decrement and dereference writes/reads before the intended plens_buffer bounds, an out-of-bounds memory access. It is not merely a logic error; the missing lower-bound constraint directly enables memory corruption.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: plens is decremented past plens_buffer when more backspaces occur than previously stored multi-char lengths. Trigger: crafted HTML with excessive backspace sequences in checkType. Consequence: out-of-bounds access causing crash/DoS and unexpected state, matching the reported OOB write/read.

description: TensorFlow is an open source platform for machine learning. Prior to versions 2.9.0, 2.8.1, 2.7.2, and 2.6.4, the implementation of `tf.raw_ops.SparseTensorDenseAdd` does not fully validate the input arguments. code_evidence: The function checks only that a_indices is a matrix, without validating that its second dimension (ndims) matches a_shape's length or that its first dimension (nnz) matches a_values' length.
Vector checks confirm a_values and a_shape are vectors but never verify their element counts are consistent with each other or with a_indices.
Rank is compared against the dense tensor b, but no check ensures a_shape_flat(didx) is a valid bound for indices stored in a_indices.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-20 fits because the function is an input-validation routine that fails to check required properties (dimension consistency and index bounds) of its arguments before processing. The missing constraints allow malformed SparseTensorDenseAdd inputs to reach unsafe kernel operations; the weakness is the absent validation, distinct from the resulting memory-safety consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: ValidateInputs omits consistency checks between a_indices shape, a_values length, and a_shape length. A caller can supply mismatched dimensions so that a_indices rows/columns exceed a_values or a_shape, or indices reference positions outside a_shape_flat. Downstream kernel code then dereferences a reference bound to nullptr or indexes arrays out of bounds, producing undefined behavior and a crash.

commit_msg:
Fix `tf.io.decode_raw` bugs and update documentation.

Fixes cases where specifying `fixed_length` resulted in data loss and even segfault and corruption of the Python interpreter. The fix is subtle but needed due to pointer arithmetic rules.

Makes sure that `fixed_length` does not change the output when present but not needed.

Eliminates needless copy and cast in the main codepath.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 371322725
Change-Id: I514ef67a2961c86422f69d05122d31615e87896c
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        const T* in_data = reinterpret_cast<const T*>(flat_in(i).data());', '', '        if (flat_in(i).size() > fixed_length) {', '          memcpy(out_data, in_data, fixed_length);', '        } else {', '          memcpy(out_data, in_data, flat_in(i).size());', '        }', '        out_data += fixed_length;', '        out_data += fixed_length;'], 'added_lines': ['        const auto to_copy =', '            std::min(flat_in(i).size(), static_cast<size_t>(fixed_length));', '        memcpy(out_data, flat_in(i).data(), to_copy);', "        // Note: increase out_data by width since it's already of type T* so", '        // each shift amount is implicitly multiplied by sizeof(T) according to', '        // pointer arithmetic rules.', '        out_data += width;', "        // Note: increase out_data by width since it's already of type T* so", '        // each shift amount is implicitly multiplied by sizeof(T) according to', '        // pointer arithmetic rules.', '        out_data += width;']}
description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. The implementation of `tf.io.decode_raw` produces incorrect results and crashes the Python interpreter when combining `fixed_length` and wider datatypes. The implementation of the padded version(https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/1d8903e5b167ed0432077a3db6e462daf781d1fe/tensorflow/core/kernels/decode_padded_raw_op.cc) is buggy due to a confusion about pointer arithmetic rules. First, the code computes(https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/1d8903e5b167ed0432077a3db6e462daf781d1fe/tensorflow/core/kernels/decode_padded_raw_op.cc#L61) the width of each output element by dividing the `fixed_length` value to the size of the type argument. The `fixed_length` argument is also used to determine the size needed for the output tensor(https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/1d8903e5b167ed0432077a3db6e462daf781d1fe/tensorflow/core/kernels/decode_padded_raw_op.cc#L63-L79). This is followed by reencoding code(https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/1d8903e5b167ed0432077a3db6e462daf781d1fe/tensorflow/core/kernels/decode_padded_raw_op.cc#L85-L94). The erroneous code is the last line above: it is moving the `out_data` pointer by `fixed_length * sizeof(T)` bytes whereas it only copied at most `fixed_length` bytes from the input. This results in parts of the input not being decoded into the output. Furthermore, because the pointer advance is far wider than desired, this quickly leads to writing to outside the bounds of the backing data. This OOB write leads to interpreter crash in the reproducer mentioned here, but more severe attacks can be mounted too, given that this gadget allows writing to periodically placed locations in memory. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.5.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.4.2, TensorFlow 2.3.3, TensorFlow 2.2.3 and TensorFlow 2.1.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: out_data is a T* pointing into the output tensor sized for width elements per input string; memset clears fixed_length*flat_in.size() bytes.
In the direct-copy branch, memcpy copies at most fixed_length bytes but out_data is advanced by fixed_length elements (fixed_length*sizeof(T) bytes), overshooting the per-element slot.
In the endianness branch, the loop copies fixed_length bytes but out_data += fixed_length also advances by fixed_length elements rather than width.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes through out_data beyond the allocated output tensor, which is precisely an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). The defect is the insufficient pointer-arithmetic constraint on the write cursor, not merely incorrect decoding; the supported consequence is memory corruption/DoS.

evidence_lines.code:
T* out_data = out.data();
memset(out_data, 0, fixed_length * flat_in.size());

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is pointer-advance confusion: out_data is T* so += fixed_length moves fixed_length*sizeof(T) bytes per input string while only width (fixed_length/sizeof(T)) elements were allocated and at most fixed_length bytes copied. With wider datatypes and nonzero fixed_length, repeated iterations advance past the output buffer, causing out-of-bounds writes that corrupt memory and crash the interpreter.

commit_msg:
Avoid overflow in EVP_EncodeUpdate

An overflow can occur in the EVP_EncodeUpdate function which is used for
Base64 encoding of binary data. If an attacker is able to supply very large
amounts of input data then a length check can overflow resulting in a heap
corruption. Due to the very large amounts of data involved this will most
likely result in a crash.

Internally to OpenSSL the EVP_EncodeUpdate function is primarly used by the
PEM_write_bio* family of functions. These are mainly used within the
OpenSSL command line applications, so any application which processes
data from an untrusted source and outputs it as a PEM file should be
considered vulnerable to this issue.

User applications that call these APIs directly with large amounts of
untrusted data may also be vulnerable.

Issue reported by Guido Vranken.

CVE-2016-2105

Reviewed-by: Richard Levitte <levitte@openssl.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if ((ctx->num + inl) < ctx->length) {'], 'added_lines': ['    if (ctx->length - ctx->num > inl) {']}
description: Integer overflow in the EVP_EncodeUpdate function in crypto/evp/encode.c in OpenSSL before 1.0.1t and 1.0.2 before 1.0.2h allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (heap memory corruption) via a large amount of binary data.

code_evidence: Line 10 computes ctx->num + inl as a signed int and compares it to ctx->length before deciding whether to memcpy into ctx->enc_data at line 11. With attacker-controlled large inl, the addition can overflow to a small or negative value, making the guard pass even though inl exceeds the remaining buffer space.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because an integer addition wraps and the wrapped value is used as a size/offset guard for a memory copy, leading to out-of-bounds writes. This is a classic integer-overflow-to-buffer-overflow chain; the root cause is the unchecked arithmetic, not merely the memcpy itself.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the size check uses an addition (ctx->num + inl) that can wrap for large inl, so the boundary test no longer reflects available space. Trigger: caller supplies very large input to EVP_EncodeUpdate. Consequence: the memcpy on line 11 writes beyond ctx->enc_data, causing heap memory corruption/crash. The patch rewrites the check as ctx->length - ctx->num > inl to avoid the overflow.

commit_msg:
net/rds: Fix info leak in rds6_inc_info_copy()

The rds6_inc_info_copy() function has a couple struct members which
are leaking stack information.  The ->tos field should hold actual
information and the ->flags field needs to be zeroed out.

Fixes: 3eb450367d08 ("rds: add type of service(tos) infrastructure")
Fixes: b7ff8b1036f0 ("rds: Extend RDS API for IPv6 support")
Reported-by: 黄ID蝴蝶 <butterflyhuangxx@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Signed-off-by: Ka-Cheong Poon <ka-cheong.poon@oracle.com>
Acked-by: Santosh Shilimkar <santosh.shilimkar@oracle.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tminfo6.tos = inc->i_conn->c_tos;', '\tminfo6.flags = 0;', '']}
description: In the Linux kernel before 5.2.14, rds6_inc_info_copy in net/rds/recv.c allows attackers to obtain sensitive information from kernel stack memory because tos and flags fields are not initialized.

code_evidence: A stack-allocated struct rds6_info_message minfo6 is declared without an initializer; only seq and len are assigned before the flip branch.
The uninitialized tos and flags members are not written anywhere in the function, yet the entire struct is copied out via rds_info_copy using sizeof(minfo6).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function copies a resource (struct fields) that is never initialized before use, matching CWE-909 Missing Initialization of Resource. The leak is the consequence of the missing initialization rather than a separate out-of-bounds or type-confusion weakness.

evidence_lines.code: rds_info_copy(iter, &minfo6, sizeof(minfo6));

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: minfo6 is an uninitialized stack structure and only some members (seq, len, address/port fields) are set. Trigger: any call that reaches rds_info_copy copies the full struct, including the never-initialized tos and flags fields, to the info iterator. Consequence: residual stack contents in those fields are disclosed to the requester, leaking kernel stack memory.

Check upon `num_rsp` is insufficient. A malformed event packet with a
large `num_rsp` number makes hci_extended_inquiry_result_evt() go out
of bounds. Fix it.

This patch fixes the following syzbot bug:

    https://syzkaller.appspot.com/bug?id=4bf11aa05c4ca51ce0df86e500fce486552dc8d2

Reported-by: syzbot+d8489a79b781849b9c46@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Peilin Ye <yepeilin.cs@gmail.com>
Acked-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Marcel Holtmann <marcel@holtmann.org>

description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel before 5.8.1. net/bluetooth/hci_event.c has a slab out-of-bounds read in hci_extended_inquiry_result_evt, aka CID-51c19bf3d5cf.

code_evidence: Line 5 derives the info pointer from skb->data+1 and line 6 reads num_rsp from the single packet byte, but the only guard at lines 9-10 rejects just num_rsp==0 and never checks skb->len against num_rsp.
The loop at line 14 iterates num_rsp times, advancing info, and dereferences info->bdaddr, dev_class, rssi and data (lines 17-35) without validating remaining buffer length.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads fields through info beyond the received skb buffer, which is exactly an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). It is not a write or a type confusion: the flaw is insufficient bounds validation before reading, matching the target weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is the missing length check tying num_rsp to skb->len, so a malformed event advertising a large num_rsp makes the loop advance past the packet buffer. Trigger is an attacker-supplied HCI extended inquiry result event; the consequence is a slab out-of-bounds read of adjacent memory, potentially leaking data or crashing.

commit_msg:
nfc: replace improper check device_is_registered() in netlink related functions

The device_is_registered() in nfc core is used to check whether
nfc device is registered in netlink related functions such as
nfc_fw_download(), nfc_dev_up() and so on. Although device_is_registered()
is protected by device_lock, there is still a race condition between
device_del() and device_is_registered(). The root cause is that
kobject_del() in device_del() is not protected by device_lock.

   (cleanup task)         |     (netlink task)
                          |
nfc_unregister_device     | nfc_fw_download
 device_del               |  device_lock
  ...                     |   if (!device_is_registered)//(1)
  kobject_del//(2)        |   ...
 ...                      |  device_unlock

The device_is_registered() returns the value of state_in_sysfs and
the state_in_sysfs is set to zero in kobject_del(). If we pass check in
position (1), then set zero in position (2). As a result, the check
in position (1) is useless.

This patch uses bool variable instead of device_is_registered() to judge
whether the nfc device is registered, which is well synchronized.

Fixes: 3e256b8f8dfa ("NFC: add nfc subsystem core")
Signed-off-by: Duoming Zhou <duoming@zju.edu.cn>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tdev->shutting_down = false;']}
description: A use-after-free flaw was found in the Linux kernel's NFC core functionality due to a race condition between kobject creation and delete. This vulnerability allows a local attacker with CAP_NET_ADMIN privilege to leak kernel information.

code_evidence: The function registers the rfkill object under device_lock and then calls nfc_genl_device_added(dev) after releasing the lock at line 23.
The added line sets dev->shutting_down = false before unlocking, establishing the state flag that netlink handlers rely on instead of device_is_registered().
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The flaw is a check of resource state followed by use, with the state changing between them due to a race, matching CWE-367. The added shutting_down flag is the synchronized replacement for the racy check.

evidence_lines.code: rc = nfc_genl_device_added(dev);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: registration state used by netlink operations is not synchronized with the device lifecycle; the check of registration (device_is_registered()) can be invalidated by kobject_del() in device_del() running concurrently. Trigger: a netlink task passes the registration check while a cleanup task deletes the device, leaving the check stale. This supports use of freed resources, i.e., use-after-free and possible information leakage.

commit_msg:
list-objects: pass full pathname to callbacks

When we find a blob at "a/b/c", we currently pass this to
our show_object_fn callbacks as two components: "a/b/" and
"c". Callbacks which want the full value then call
path_name(), which concatenates the two. But this is an
inefficient interface; the path is a strbuf, and we could
simply append "c" to it temporarily, then roll back the
length, without creating a new copy.

So we could improve this by teaching the callsites of
path_name() this trick (and there are only 3). But we can
also notice that no callback actually cares about the
broken-down representation, and simply pass each callback
the full path "a/b/c" as a string. The callback code becomes
even simpler, then, as we do not have to worry about freeing
an allocated buffer, nor rolling back our modification to
the strbuf.

This is theoretically less efficient, as some callbacks
would not bother to format the final path component. But in
practice this is not measurable. Since we use the same
strbuf over and over, our work to grow it is amortized, and
we really only pay to memcpy a few bytes.

Signed-off-by: Jeff King <peff@peff.net>
Signed-off-by: Junio C Hamano <gitster@pobox.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['static void show_object(struct object *object, struct strbuf *path,', '\t\t\tconst char *last, void *data)'], 'added_lines': ['static void show_object(struct object *object, const char *name, void *data)']}
description: revision.c in git before 2.7.4 uses an incorrect integer data type, which allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via a (1) long filename or (2) many nested trees, leading to a heap-based buffer overflow.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The show_object function only calls bitmap_set with find_object_pos and mark_as_seen; it performs no buffer indexing, copying, or bounds-sensitive memory operation, so it does not itself demonstrate an out-of-bounds access supporting CWE-119.

commit_msg:
ucount: Remove the atomicity from ucount->count

Always increment/decrement ucount->count under the ucounts_lock.  The
increments are there already and moving the decrements there means the
locking logic of the code is simpler.  This simplification in the
locking logic fixes a race between put_ucounts and get_ucounts that
could result in a use-after-free because the count could go zero then
be found by get_ucounts and then be freed by put_ucounts.

A bug presumably this one was found by a combination of syzkaller and
KASAN.  JongWhan Kim reported the syzkaller failure and Dmitry Vyukov
spotted the race in the code.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: f6b2db1a3e8d ("userns: Make the count of user namespaces per user")
Reported-by: JongHwan Kim <zzoru007@gmail.com>
Reported-by: Dmitry Vyukov <dvyukov@google.com>
Reviewed-by: Andrei Vagin <avagin@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: "Eric W. Biederman" <ebiederm@xmission.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (atomic_dec_and_test(&ucounts->count)) {', '\t\tspin_lock_irqsave(&ucounts_lock, flags);', '\t\tspin_unlock_irqrestore(&ucounts_lock, flags);', '\t\tkfree(ucounts);', '\t}'], 'added_lines': ['\tspin_lock_irqsave(&ucounts_lock, flags);', '\tucounts->count -= 1;', '\tif (!ucounts->count)', '\telse', '\t\tucounts = NULL;', '\tspin_unlock_irqrestore(&ucounts_lock, flags);', '\tkfree(ucounts);']}
description: Race condition in kernel/ucount.c in the Linux kernel through 4.10.2 allows local users to cause a denial of service (use-after-free and system crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact via crafted system calls that leverage certain decrement behavior that causes incorrect interaction between put_ucounts and get_ucounts.

code_evidence: The decrement-and-test of ucounts->count is performed atomically, but the subsequent cleanup (hlist_del_init and kfree) runs only after the atomic operation and outside the ucounts_lock. The lock at line 5 protects only the list removal, not the count decision or the free.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-362 fits because a shared resource (ucounts->count and the ucounts object) is accessed with improper synchronization: the decrement/test and free are not atomic with respect to concurrent get_ucounts. This is a race condition, distinct from a mere locking omission in list handling.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the count reaching zero and the object's removal/free are not performed as one critical section under ucounts_lock. Trigger: a concurrent get_ucounts can observe the zeroed count between the atomic_dec_and_test and the kfree, take a reference, and then put_ucounts frees the object still in use. Supported consequence: use-after-free and possible system crash.

                          |
nfc_unregister_device     | nfc_fw_download
 device_del               |  device_lock
  ...                     |   if (!device_is_registered)//(1)
  kobject_del//(2)        |   ...
 ...                      |  device_unlock

description: A use-after-free flaw was found in the Linux kernel's NFC core functionality due to a race condition between kobject creation and delete. This vulnerability allows a local attacker with CAP_NET_ADMIN privilege to leak kernel information.

code_evidence: After taking device_lock, the function calls device_is_registered(&dev->dev) and branches to -ENODEV on failure; the check result is then used to decide whether to proceed to dev->ops->start_poll(dev, ...). device_is_registered reads state_in_sysfs, which the commit notes is cleared by kobject_del() in device_del() without holding device_lock, so the registered state can change between this check and the subsequent device access.

commit_msg:
When l2cap_recv_frame() is invoked to receive data, and the cid is
L2CAP_CID_A2MP, if the channel does not exist, it will create a channel.
However, after a channel is created, the hold operation of the channel
is not performed. In this case, the value of channel reference counting
is 1. As a result, after hci_error_reset() is triggered, l2cap_conn_del()
invokes the close hook function of A2MP to release the channel. Then
 l2cap_chan_unlock(chan) will trigger UAF issue.

The process is as follows:
Receive data:
l2cap_data_channel()
    a2mp_channel_create()  --->channel ref is 2
    l2cap_chan_put()       --->channel ref is 1

        hci_dev_do_close()
        ...
        l2cap_disconn_cfm()
            l2cap_conn_del()

                l2cap_chan_del()     --->channel ref is 1

commit_msg:
BUG/MAJOR: htx: fix missing header name length check in htx_add_header/trailer

Ori Hollander of JFrog Security reported that htx_add_header() and
htx_add_trailer() were missing a length check on the header name. While
this does not allow to overwrite any memory area, it results in bits of
the header name length to slip into the header value length and may
result in forging certain header names on the input. The sad thing here
is that a FIXME comment was present suggesting to add the required length
checks :-(

The injected headers are visible to the HTTP internals and to the config
rules, so haproxy will generally stay synchronized with the server. But
there is one exception which is the content-length header field, because
it is already deduplicated on the input, but before being indexed. As
such, injecting a content-length header after the deduplication stage
may be abused to present a different, shorter one on the other side and
help build a request smuggling attack, or even maybe a response splitting
attack. CVE-2021-40346 was assigned to this problem.

As a mitigation measure, it is sufficient to verify that no more than
one such header is present in any message, which is normally the case
thanks to the duplicate checks:

   http-request  deny if { req.hdr_cnt(content-length) gt 1 }
   http-response deny if { res.hdr_cnt(content-length) gt 1 }

This must be backported to all HTX-enabled versions, hence as far as 2.0.
In 2.3 and earlier, the functions are in src/htx.c instead.

Many thanks to Ori for his work and his responsible report!
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t/* FIXME: check name.len (< 256B) and value.len (< 1MB) */'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (name.len > 255 || value.len > 1048575)', '\t\treturn NULL;', '']}
description: An integer overflow exists in HAProxy 2.0 through 2.5 in htx_add_header that can be exploited to perform an HTTP request smuggling attack, allowing an attacker to bypass all configured http-request HAProxy ACLs and possibly other ACLs.

code_evidence: Line 5 computes name.len + value.len and passes it as the block size to htx_add_blk without any bound check on either length.
Line 8 packs the lengths into blk->info as (value.len << 8) + name.len, assuming name.len fits in the low 8 bits; an oversized name.len spills into the value-length field.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe length arithmetic in name.len + value.len and (value.len << 8) + name.len is an integer overflow/wraparound that corrupts the encoded block metadata, matching CWE-190. It is not merely a missing length check; the packed-length overflow is the direct cause of the forged header fields.

evidence_lines.code:
blk = htx_add_blk(htx, HTX_BLK_TLR, name.len + value.len);
blk->info += (value.len << 8) + name.len;

ist2bin_lc(htx_get_blk_ptr(htx, blk), name);
memcpy(htx_get_blk_ptr(htx, blk)  + name.len, value.ptr, value.len);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: htx_add_trailer accepts arbitrary ist lengths and combines them arithmetically without validating name.len < 256 or value.len < 1MB. A caller supplying a name longer than 255 bytes causes the name length bits to overflow into the value-length field in blk->info, so the stored header name/value boundaries no longer match the copied bytes. This forged header metadata can present a different (e.g., content-length) header to downstream HTTP processing, enabling request smuggling or response splitting, and the combined size arithmetic may also wrap on allocation.

commit_msg:
x86: limit linear page table use to a single level

That's the only way that they're meant to be used. Without such a
restriction arbitrarily long chains of same-level page tables can be
built, tearing down of which may then cause arbitrarily deep recursion,
causing a stack overflow. To facilitate this restriction, a counter is
being introduced to track both the number of same-level entries in a
page table as well as the number of uses of a page table in another
same-level one (counting into positive and negative direction
respectively, utilizing the fact that both counts can't be non-zero at
the same time).

Note that the added accounting introduces a restriction on the number
of times a page can be used in other same-level page tables - more than
32k of such uses are no longer possible.

Note also that some put_page_and_type[_preemptible]() calls are
replaced with open-coded equivalents.  This seemed preferrable to
adding "parent_table" to the matrix of functions.

Note further that cross-domain same-level page table references are no
longer permitted (they probably never should have been).

This is XSA-240.

Reported-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Signed-off-by: George Dunlap <george.dunlap@citrix.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    switch ( rc = put_page_and_type_preemptible(v->arch.old_guest_table) )'], 'added_lines': ['    switch ( rc = _put_page_type(v->arch.old_guest_table, true,', '                                 v->arch.old_guest_ptpg) )', '    case 0:', '        put_page(v->arch.old_guest_table);']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.9.x allowing x86 PV guest OS users to cause a denial of service (unbounded recursion, stack consumption, and hypervisor crash) or possibly gain privileges via crafted page-table stacking.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The shown function only performs a bounded, single put_page_and_type_preemptible call on one saved page and clears the pointer; it contains no page-table stacking, recursion, or unbounded resource accumulation logic that would directly demonstrate CWE-400.

Release "3.0.6": Fix crashes in Array for "integer overflow #10"

FossilOrigin-Name: 50642d64b8f0a4e62df68e59fcb2ef0923c3dbec8fc8a15d38b1ddbe655c38d6
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    int i = Jsi_ObjGetLength(interp, obj) - 1;'], 'added_lines': ['    int i = jsi_SizeOfArray(interp, obj) - 1;']}
description: Integer overflow vulnerability in function Jsi_ObjSetLength in jsish before 3.0.6, allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code.

code_evidence: Line 11 computes the pop index as the array length minus one using Jsi_ObjGetLength before any bounds validation.
Lines 12-15 only reject negative i; there is no check that length is representable or that the subtraction did not wrap.
Lines 16-20 dereference obj->arr[i] and decrement arrCnt, while line 28 sets the new length to i; an out-of-range or wrapped index reaches these operations.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the index derivation in line 11 performs arithmetic on a length that can overflow/wrap; the subsequent unchecked index use makes the wraparound security-relevant. This is arithmetic wraparound, not merely a missing bounds check (CWE-125) or an off-by-one error.

evidence_lines.code: Jsi_ObjSetLength(interp, obj, i);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The length value is converted/subtracted without validating its range, so an oversized or malformed array length can wrap the index computation. The trigger is a crafted array whose length causes the subtraction to produce an invalid index; the resulting i is then used to index obj->arr and to set the array length, supporting out-of-bounds access or memory corruption rather than only a benign negative-length return.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t    if (dtable[c] & 0x80) {'], 'added_lines': ['\t    if (dtable[(unsigned char)c] & 0x80) {']}
description: An issue was discovered in PHP before 5.6.40, 7.x before 7.1.26, 7.2.x before 7.2.14, and 7.3.x before 7.3.1. xmlrpc_decode() can allow a hostile XMLRPC server to cause PHP to read memory outside of allocated areas in base64_decode_xmlrpc in ext/xmlrpc/libxmlrpc/base64.c.

b[i] = dtable[c] propagates the out-of-bounds table read into decoding output.

This is an out-of-bounds read, not a write or integer overflow; the missing (unsigned char) cast is the direct cause of the invalid index.

commit_msg:
Bugzilla: 1671904

There are multiple code paths where an hrtimer may have been started to
emulate an L1 VMX preemption timer that can result in a call to free_nested
without an intervening L2 exit where the hrtimer is normally
cancelled. Unconditionally cancel in free_nested to cover all cases.

Embargoed until Feb 7th 2019.

Signed-off-by: Peter Shier <pshier@google.com>
Reported-by: Jim Mattson <jmattson@google.com>
Reviewed-by: Jim Mattson <jmattson@google.com>
Reported-by: Felix Wilhelm <fwilhelm@google.com>
Cc: stable@kernel.org
Message-Id: <20181011184646.154065-1-pshier@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\thrtimer_cancel(&vmx->nested.preemption_timer);']}
description: The KVM implementation in the Linux kernel through 4.20.5 has a Use-after-Free.

code_evidence: free_nested returns early when nested VMX is not active, then clears vmxon flags and frees nested resources including cached_vmcs12, cached_shadow_vmcs12 and vmcs02. The preemption_timer hrtimer is not cancelled here, so its callback may still run after these structures are freed.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the freed nested VMX state is referenced by the still-active hrtimer callback. The missing cancellation is the cause; the stale reference after free is the use-after-free, not merely a resource leak.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: free_nested releases nested VMX state without cancelling vmx->nested.preemption_timer, which can remain armed across code paths lacking an L2 exit. Trigger: the hrtimer fires after free_nested frees the nested structures. Consequence: the timer callback accesses freed memory, a use-after-free that can corrupt memory or crash the kernel.

Fixes: [Semmle Security Reports #19438]

Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
(cherry picked from commit 1f00c97bc3475c477f3c468cf2d924d5761d0982)

description: In FFmpeg 3.2 and 4.1, a denial of service in the subtitle decoder allows attackers to hog the CPU via a crafted video file in Matroska format, because ff_htmlmarkup_to_ass in libavcodec/htmlsubtitles.c has a complex format argument to sscanf.

The scan and the resulting buffer/tag processing operate on a pointer derived from the input without any prior bound check that a closing '>' exists within the buffer; sscanf itself scans for the terminator.

commit_msg: https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/issues/525
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  clone_info=CloneImageInfo(image_info);'], 'added_lines': ['  clone_info=(ImageInfo *) NULL;', '    clone_info=CloneImageInfo(image_info);']}
description: The ReadMATImage function in coders/mat.c in ImageMagick before 6.9.9-0 and 7.x before 7.0.6-1 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory leak) via a crafted file.

code_evidence: clone_info is allocated once at line 40 via CloneImageInfo before header validation (line 41-42 can throw), and is only released at line 387 on the END_OF_READING path.

Within the loop, image2 is set to DecompressBlock(image, ..., clone_info, ...) at line 91; when it returns NULL the code continues (line 92), leaving the loop without reaching a cleanup that frees clone_info for that iteration.
The only unconditional destroy is clone_info=DestroyImageInfo(clone_info) at line 387; the per-iteration error/continue paths and thrown exceptions bypass it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function allocates clone_info but fails to release it on early-continue and exception paths, matching CWE-772 (Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime). This is distinct from a double-free or use-after-free; the defect is failure to release the resource, causing resource-consumption DoS.

evidence_lines.code:
END_OF_READING:
clone_info=DestroyImageInfo(clone_info);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: clone_info is created per call but its lifetime is not bounded to each loop iteration; the DecompressBlock failure path (line 92) continues without freeing the resources associated with clone_info, and ThrowReaderException paths also skip the final destroy. A crafted file that repeatedly triggers the DecompressBlock NULL return causes accumulated ImageInfo/resource leakage, leading to memory exhaustion (DoS).

commit_msg:
cifs: Fix smbencrypt() to stop pointing a scatterlist at the stack

smbencrypt() points a scatterlist to the stack, which is breaks if
CONFIG_VMAP_STACK=y.

Fix it by switching to crypto_cipher_encrypt_one().  The new code
should be considerably faster as an added benefit.

This code is nearly identical to some code that Eric Biggers
suggested.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # 4.9 only
Reported-by: Eric Biggers <ebiggers3@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Andy Lutomirski <luto@kernel.org>
Acked-by: Jeff Layton <jlayton@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Steve French <smfrench@gmail.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tint rc;', '\tstruct crypto_skcipher *tfm_des;', '\tstruct scatterlist sgin, sgout;', '\tstruct skcipher_request *req;', '\ttfm_des = crypto_alloc_skcipher("ecb(des)", 0, CRYPTO_ALG_ASYNC);', '\t\trc = PTR_ERR(tfm_des);', '\t\tgoto smbhash_err;', '\treq = skcipher_request_alloc(tfm_des, GFP_KERNEL);', '\tif (!req) {', '\t\trc = -ENOMEM;', '\t\tcifs_dbg(VFS, "could not allocate des crypto API\\n");', '\t\tgoto smbhash_free_skcipher;', '\t}', '\tcrypto_skcipher_setkey(tfm_des, key2, 8);', '', '\tsg_init_one(&sgin, in, 8);', '\tsg_init_one(&sgout, out, 8);', '', '\tskcipher_request_set_callback(req, 0, NULL, NULL);', '\tskcipher_request_set_crypt(req, &sgin, &sgout, 8, NULL);', '', '\trc = crypto_skcipher_encrypt(req);', '\tif (rc)', '\t\tcifs_dbg(VFS, "could not encrypt crypt key rc: %d\\n", rc);', '', '\tskcipher_request_free(req);', '', 'smbhash_free_skcipher:', '\tcrypto_free_skcipher(tfm_des);', 'smbhash_err:', '\treturn rc;'], 'added_lines': ['\tstruct crypto_cipher *tfm_des;', '\ttfm_des = crypto_alloc_cipher("des", 0, 0);', '\t\treturn PTR_ERR(tfm_des);', '\tcrypto_cipher_setkey(tfm_des, key2, 8);', '\tcrypto_cipher_encrypt_one(tfm_des, out, in);', '\tcrypto_free_cipher(tfm_des);', '\treturn 0;']}
description: The smbhash function in fs/cifs/smbencrypt.c in the Linux kernel 4.9.x before 4.9.1 interacts incorrectly with the CONFIG_VMAP_STACK option, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (system crash or memory corruption) or possibly have unspecified other impact by leveraging use of more than one virtual page for a scatterlist.

code_evidence: The function declares scatterlist objects sgin and sgout as local stack variables and initializes them with sg_init_one() over the 8-byte in and out buffers.
skcipher_request_set_crypt() then points the crypto request's source and destination scatterlists at these stack-allocated sg entries, and crypto_skcipher_encrypt() operates through that scatterlist.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe operation is a memory access driven by a scatterlist that does not correctly describe the intended buffer region under VMAP_STACK, i.e. operations outside the intended memory bounds. CWE-119 captures this out-of-bounds memory-buffer operation; the root cause is the stack-pointed scatterlist rather than a simple length miscalculation.

evidence_lines.code:
skcipher_request_set_callback(req, 0, NULL, NULL);
skcipher_request_set_crypt(req, &sgin, &sgout, 8, NULL);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the scatterlist descriptors are placed on the stack rather than in a stable heap or mapped location. description: Out-of-bounds accesses in the functions pi_next_lrcp, pi_next_rlcp, pi_next_rpcl, pi_next_pcrl, pi_next_rpcl, and pi_next_cprl in openmj2/pi.c in OpenJPEG through 2.3.0 allow remote attackers to cause a denial of service (application crash).

description: A vulnerability classified as problematic has been found in FFmpeg 2.0. This affects the function add_yblock of the file libavcodec/snow.h. The manipulation leads to memory corruption. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue.

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: mutually exclusive clipping of the left/top and right/bottom edges, so a block crossing both edges is only clipped on one side. Trigger: a remotely supplied snow bitstream producing src_x<0 with src_x+b_w>w (or analogous vertical case). Consequence: b_w/b_h exceed the plane bounds and the per-pixel stores write out of bounds.

description: An issue was discovered in the libsofia-sip fork in drachtio-server before 0.8.19. It allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (daemon crash) via a crafted UDP message that causes a url_canonize2 heap-based buffer over-read because of an off-by-one error.

description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. In affected versions the implementation of `tf.raw_ops.ResourceScatterDiv` is vulnerable to a division by 0 error. The [implementation](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/8d72537c6abf5a44103b57b9c2e22c14f5f49698/tensorflow/core/kernels/resource_variable_ops.cc#L865) uses a common class for all binary operations but fails to treat the division by 0 case separately. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.5.1, TensorFlow 2.4.3, and TensorFlow 2.3.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: The function reads the divisor tensor as c->input(2) into updates and then, when N > 0, obtains params_flat and dispatches updates (scalar via updates.scalar<T>() at line 34, or the shaped updates_flat at line 51) into ScatterScalarFunctor/ScatterFunctor with the DIV update op. Trigger: a caller invokes ResourceScatterDiv with an updates tensor containing 0. The functor then divides params by 0, causing a floating-point exception or crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
x86/pv: _toggle_guest_pt() may not skip TLB flush for shadow mode guests

For shadow mode guests (e.g. PV ones forced into that mode as L1TF
mitigation, or during migration) update_cr3() -> sh_update_cr3() may
result in a change to the (shadow) root page table (compared to the
previous one when running the same vCPU with the same PCID). This can,
first and foremost, be a result of memory pressure on the shadow memory
pool of the domain. Shadow code legitimately relies on the original
(prior to commit 5c81d260c2 ["xen/x86: use PCID feature"]) behavior of
the subsequent CR3 write to flush the TLB of entries still left from
walks with an earlier, different (shadow) root page table.

Restore the flushing behavior, also for the second CR3 write on the exit
path to guest context when XPTI is active. For the moment accept that
this will introduce more flushes than are strictly necessary - no flush
would be needed when the (shadow) root page table doesn't actually
change, but this information isn't readily (i.e. without introducing a
layering violation) available here.

This is XSA-294.

Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Tested-by: Juergen Gross <jgross@suse.com>
Reviewed-by: Andrew Cooper <andrew.cooper3@citrix.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        struct cpu_info *cpu_info = get_cpu_info();', '', "    /* Don't flush user global mappings from the TLB. Don't tick TLB clock. */", '    write_cr3(v->arch.cr3);'], 'added_lines': ['    struct cpu_info *cpu_info = get_cpu_info();', '    unsigned long cr3;', '    /*', "     * Don't flush user global mappings from the TLB. Don't tick TLB clock.", '     *', '     * In shadow mode, though, update_cr3() may need to be accompanied by a', '     * TLB flush (for just the incoming PCID), as the top level page table may', '     * have changed behind our backs. To be on the safe side, suppress the', '     * no-flush unconditionally in this case. The XPTI CR3 write, if enabled,', '     * will then need to be a flushing one too.', '     */', '    cr3 = v->arch.cr3;', '    if ( shadow_mode_enabled(d) )', '    {', '        cr3 &= ~X86_CR3_NOFLUSH;', '        cpu_info->pv_cr3 &= ~X86_CR3_NOFLUSH;', '    }', '    write_cr3(cr3);']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.11.x allowing x86 PV guest OS users to cause a denial of service because of an incompatibility between Process Context Identifiers (PCID) and shadow-pagetable switching.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function's flaw is a missing TLB flush when writing CR3 in shadow mode (stale shadow root page table entries), an improper-state/flush issue, not improper validation of input data; no input validation logic is present or implicated.

commit_msg:
x509: excessive resource use verifying policy constraints

A security vulnerability has been identified in all supported versions
of OpenSSL related to the verification of X.509 certificate chains
that include policy constraints.  Attackers may be able to exploit this
vulnerability by creating a malicious certificate chain that triggers
exponential use of computational resources, leading to a denial-of-service
(DoS) attack on affected systems.

Fixes CVE-2023-0464

Reviewed-by: Tomas Mraz <tomas@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Shane Lontis <shane.lontis@oracle.com>
(Merged from https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/20569)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if (level_add_node(curr, data, node, tree) == NULL) {'], 'added_lines': ['    if (level_add_node(curr, data, node, tree, 1) == NULL) {']}
description:
A security vulnerability has been identified in all supported versions

of OpenSSL related to the verification of X.509 certificate chains
that include policy constraints.  Attackers may be able to exploit this
vulnerability by creating a malicious certificate chain that triggers
exponential use of computational resources, leading to a denial-of-service
(DoS) attack on affected systems.

Policy processing is disabled by default but can be enabled by passing
the `-policy' argument to the command line utilities or by calling the
`X509_VERIFY_PARAM_set1_policies()' function.

code_evidence: tree_add_unmatched allocates policy data and inserts an unmatched policy node into the policy tree via level_add_node(curr, data, node, tree), but never bounds how many such unmatched nodes can be added; the call returns NULL only on allocation failure, and the function otherwise succeeds and returns 1. The diff adds a flag argument to level_add_node, indicating the node-count limit is enforced in the callee rather than here.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The changed call is part of X.509 certificate/policy validation, so it touches certificate processing, but the defect is unbounded resource use, not incorrect acceptance or rejection of a certificate. CWE-295's improper validation is not directly demonstrated; the supported weakness is resource exhaustion during verification.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: policy-tree construction permits unbounded insertion of unmatched policy nodes during X.509 chain verification. Trigger: a malicious certificate chain with policy constraints processed while policy checking is enabled causes repeated tree_add_unmatched calls, which the fixed callee caps. Consequence: exponential resource consumption leading to denial of service; this is resource exhaustion, not certificate-acceptance bypass.

crypto/evp: harden AEAD ciphers.

Originally a crash in 32-bit build was reported CHACHA20-POLY1305
cipher. The crash is triggered by truncated packet and is result
of excessive hashing to the edge of accessible memory. Since hash
operation is read-only it is not considered to be exploitable
beyond a DoS condition. Other ciphers were hardened.

Thanks to Robert Święcki for report.

CVE-2017-3731

Reviewed-by: Rich Salz <rsalz@openssl.org>

For OpenSSL 1.1.0, the crash can be triggered when using CHACHA20/POLY1305; users should upgrade to 1.1.0d. For Openssl 1.0.2, the crash can be triggered when using RC4-MD5; users who have not disabled that algorithm should update to 1.0.2k.

Trigger: a truncated packet whose length field is smaller than those values. Consequence: len wraps to a large value, which is written back and later used for hashing/processing, causing reads past the intended buffer (out-of-bounds read, DoS/crash).

code_evidence: r_buf_read(src, tmp, tsize) returns a st64 count of bytes read; the guard only rejects r < tsize, so a short read (0 <= r < tsize) returns -1 but a negative error value is also caught. When r < tsize the function aborts before the switch, so no partial buffer is decoded.

DO NOT MERGE mm-video-v4l2: venc: add checks before accessing heap pointers

Heap pointers do not point to user virtual addresses in case
of secure session.
Set them to NULL and add checks to avoid accesing them

Bug: 28815329
Bug: 28920116

description: The secure-session feature in the mm-video-v4l2 venc component in mediaserver in Android 4.x before 4.4.4, 5.0.x before 5.0.2, 5.1.x before 5.1.1, and 6.x before 2016-08-01 mishandles heap pointers, which allows attackers to gain privileges via a crafted application, aka internal bug 28815329.

code_evidence: In the secure-session branch, m_pOutput_pmem[i].buffer is set to SECURE_BUFPTR (line 93) and, when secure_session is true, the else branch (line 113) overwrites it with malloc(sizeof(OMX_U32) + sizeof(native_handle_t*)) (line 114). The subsequent memcpy at lines 120-121 writes sizeof(OMX_U32)+sizeof(native_handle_t*) bytes into that allocation, but the size is only an assumed constant rather than derived from the actual native_handle_t layout; the malloc return is never checked before dereference at lines 115-121.

When secure_session is true, the code takes the heap-pointer path and writes a type word plus a native_handle_t* into a buffer allocated with a hard-coded size, without verifying the allocation succeeded or that the size matches the handle structure actually created by native_handle_create(1,0). If the assumed size is smaller than the real structure or the allocation fails, the memcpy writes beyond the intended buffer boundary.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The supported weakness is an out-of-bounds write to a heap buffer, which is exactly the memory-boundary violation described by CWE-119. The fixed-size allocation combined with unchecked memcpy writes places data outside the buffer's intended boundary, matching CWE-119 rather than a mere NULL-pointer or resource issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the secure-session branch allocates a buffer using a fixed sizeof(OMX_U32)+sizeof(native_handle_t*) expression and then memcpy's a native_handle_t pointer and type into it without checking malloc success or validating the size against the actual handle. Trigger: a crafted application opening a secure session causes this allocation/write path. Consequence: out-of-bounds write into heap memory, corrupting adjacent data and potentially enabling privilege escalation.

commit_msg:
When running concurrent iptables rules replacement with data, the per CPU
sequence count is checked after the assignment of the new information.
The sequence count is used to synchronize with the packet path without the
use of any explicit locking. If there are any packets in the packet path using
the table information, the sequence count is incremented to an odd value and
is incremented to an even after the packet process completion.

The new table value assignment is followed by a write memory barrier so every
CPU should see the latest value. If the packet path has started with the old
table information, the sequence counter will be odd and the iptables
replacement will wait till the sequence count is even prior to freeing the
old table info.

However, this assumes that the new table information assignment and the memory
barrier is actually executed prior to the counter check in the replacement
thread. If CPU decides to execute the assignment later as there is no user of
the table information prior to the sequence check, the packet path in another
CPU may use the old table information. The replacement thread would then free
the table information under it leading to a use after free in the packet
processing context-

Unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at virtual
address 000000000000008e
pc : ip6t_do_table+0x5d0/0x89c
lr : ip6t_do_table+0x5b8/0x89c
ip6t_do_table+0x5d0/0x89c
ip6table_filter_hook+0x24/0x30
nf_hook_slow+0x84/0x120
ip6_input+0x74/0xe0
ip6_rcv_finish+0x7c/0x128
ipv6_rcv+0xac/0xe4
__netif_receive_skb+0x84/0x17c
process_backlog+0x15c/0x1b8
napi_poll+0x88/0x284
net_rx_action+0xbc/0x23c
__do_softirq+0x20c/0x48c

This could be fixed by forcing instruction order after the new table
information assignment or by switching to RCU for the synchronization.

Fixes: 80055dab5de0 ("netfilter: x_tables: make xt_replace_table wait until old rules are not used anymore")
Reported-by: Sean Tranchetti <stranche@codeaurora.org>
Reported-by: kernel test robot <lkp@intel.com>
Suggested-by: Florian Westphal <fw@strlen.de>
Signed-off-by: Subash Abhinov Kasiviswanathan <subashab@codeaurora.org>
Signed-off-by: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tprivate = READ_ONCE(table->private); /* Address dependency. */'], 'added_lines': ['\tprivate = rcu_access_pointer(table->private);']}
description: An issue was discovered in netfilter in the Linux kernel before 5.10. There can be a use-after-free in the packet processing context, because the per-CPU sequence count is mishandled during concurrent iptables rules replacement. This could be exploited with the CAP_NET_ADMIN capability in an unprivileged namespace. NOTE: cc00bca was reverted in 5.12.

code_evidence: xt_write_recseq_begin() marks the packet path as active via the per-CPU sequence count, then the table private data is read with READ_ONCE(table->private) and immediately dereferenced to obtain entries and jumpstack. The replacement thread relies on this sequence ordering to know no packet path holds the old table before freeing it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences table->private after the replacement thread may have freed it, matching CWE-416 (use after free). This is not merely a null-pointer or race-only issue: the freed allocation is reused while the packet path still holds the pointer.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the compiler/CPU may reorder the private pointer load after the sequence-count check because no ordering constraint ties the read to the recseq begin. Trigger: concurrent iptables replacement frees the old table while the packet path still dereferences the stale private pointer at lines 24-25. Consequence: use-after-free read of freed table info in packet processing, leading to crash or memory corruption.

map_dtype_to_tensor(attr->type(), arg);

CVE-2017-13053/BGP: fix VPN route target bounds checks

decode_rt_routing_info() didn't check bounds before fetching 4 octets of
the origin AS field and could over-read the input buffer, put it right.

It also fetched the varying number of octets of the route target field
from 4 octets lower than the correct offset, put it right.

It also used the same temporary buffer explicitly through as_printf()
and implicitly through bgp_vpn_rd_print() so the end result of snprintf()
was not what was originally intended.

This fixes a buffer over-read discovered by Bhargava Shastry,
SecT/TU Berlin.

commit_msg:
x86/pv: Remove unsafe bits from the mod_l?_entry() fastpath

All changes in writeability and cacheability must go through full
re-validation.

Rework the logic as a whitelist, to make it clearer to follow.

This is XSA-182

Reported-by: Jérémie Boutoille <jboutoille@ext.quarkslab.com>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Cooper <andrew.cooper3@citrix.com>
Reviewed-by: Tim Deegan <tim@xen.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        /* Fast path for identical mapping, r/w, presence, and cachability. */', '        if ( !l1e_has_changed(ol1e, nl1e,', '                              PAGE_CACHE_ATTRS | _PAGE_RW | _PAGE_PRESENT) )'], 'added_lines': ['        /* Fast path for sufficiently-similar mappings. */', '        if ( !l1e_has_changed(ol1e, nl1e, ~FASTPATH_FLAG_WHITELIST) )']}
description: The PV pagetable code in arch/x86/mm.c in Xen 4.7.x and earlier allows local 32-bit PV guest OS administrators to gain host OS privileges by leveraging fast-paths for updating pagetable entries.

code_evidence: The function validates a guest-supplied L1 pagetable entry only through l1_disallow_mask(pt_dom) before proceeding to update the entry.

The fast path at lines 32-41 skips get_page_from_l1e re-validation whenever l1e_has_changed reports only differences outside PAGE_CACHE_ATTRS | _PAGE_RW | _PAGE_PRESENT, i.e. it treats those attributes as unchanged.
The full validation path in the switch calls get_page_from_l1e, which returns _PAGE_RW.._PAGE_RW|PAGE_CACHE_ATTRS and flips flags when the requested write/cacheability is not permitted for the page.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-284 fits because the fast path improperly restricts enforcement of the access-control policy governing pagetable write/cache permissions, letting an unauthorized actor (guest admin) obtain host privileges. It is an enforcement failure in the access-control mechanism rather than a memory-safety bug.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the fast-path whitelist omits writeability and cacheability bits, so a guest can change _PAGE_RW or cache attributes on an existing L1 entry without triggering get_page_from_l1e's permission check. Trigger: a local PV guest administrator submits a mod_l1_entry update that alters those bits while keeping the entry otherwise similar. Consequence: the guest gains write access or cacheability the host policy forbids, enabling privilege escalation to the host.

commit_msg:
Make sure the offset doesn't overflow.

It'd only overflow if the value is *so* large that it won't fit in the
packet (given that we have a 2^32-1-byte limit on the packet size), so
use tvb_ensure_bytes_exist() to ensure we have the entire value before
processing the value.

(The real problem is that we don't handle the case where there's a value
multiplicity > 1 for some types; in those cases, we should loop,
processing all the values, which would cause us to eventually throw an
exception when we ran past the end of the packet.  This is just a quick
fix.)
