commit_msg:
read_boot(): Handle excessive FAT size specifications

The variable used for storing the FAT size (in bytes) was an unsigned
int. Since the size in sectors read from the BPB was not sufficiently
checked, this could end up being zero after multiplying it with the
sector size while some offsets still stayed excessive. Ultimately it
would cause segfaults when accessing FAT entries for which no memory
was allocated.

Make it more robust by changing the types used to store FAT size to
off_t and abort if there is no room for data clusters. Additionally
check that FAT size is not specified as zero.

Fixes #25 and fixes #26.

Reported-by: Hanno Böck
Signed-off-by: Andreas Bombe <aeb@debian.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    unsigned fat_length;'], 'added_lines': ['    off_t fat_length;', '', '    if (!fat_length)', '\tdie("FAT size is zero.");', '', '', '    if (data_size < fs->cluster_size)', '\tdie("Filesystem has no space for any data clusters");', '']}
description: The read_boot function in boot.c in dosfstools before 4.0 allows attackers to cause a denial of service (crash) via a crafted filesystem, which triggers a heap-based buffer overflow in the (1) read_fat function or an out-of-bounds heap read in (2) get_fat function.

code_evidence: fat_length is an unsigned int holding a sector count from the BPB; it is used at line 31 to compute fs->root_start and line 38 to derive fs->data_clusters, with no upper bound or zero check before these uses.

Line 78 computes fs->fat_size = fat_length * logical_sector_size in unsigned arithmetic, which can overflow; line 92 then derives total_fat_entries from this possibly wrapped fat_size, and lines 93-95 only compare against that derived value, so an oversized FAT spec passes validation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked size arithmetic allows subsequent FAT entry accesses to operate outside the allocated FAT buffer, directly matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds read/write. The integer overflow is the upstream cause; the memory-boundary violation is the supported weakness here.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the FAT sector count read from the boot sector is trusted without an upper bound, and the size multiplication at line 78 can wrap in unsigned arithmetic, yielding an undersized fat_size. Trigger: a crafted filesystem image with an excessive fat_length. Consequence: total_fat_entries is computed too small, so the bounds check at line 93 does not reject the filesystem; later FAT lookups (read_fat/get_fat) index beyond the allocated FAT buffer, causing heap overflow or out-of-bounds heap read and a crash.

commit_msg:
The current hfsplus_put_super first calls hfs_btree_close on
sbi->ext_tree, then invokes iput on sbi->hidden_dir, resulting in an
use-after-free issue in hfsplus_release_folio.

As shown in hfsplus_fill_super, the error handling code also calls iput
before hfs_btree_close.

To fix this error, we move all iput calls before hfsplus_btree_close.

Note that this patch is tested on Syzbot.

Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/20230226124948.3175736-1-mudongliangabcd@gmail.com
Reported-by: syzbot+57e3e98f7e3b80f64d56@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Tested-by: Dongliang Mu <mudongliangabcd@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Dongliang Mu <mudongliangabcd@gmail.com>
Cc: Bart Van Assche <bvanassche@acm.org>
Cc: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>
Cc: Muchun Song <songmuchun@bytedance.com>
Cc: Roman Gushchin <roman.gushchin@linux.dev>
Cc: "Theodore Ts'o" <tytso@mit.edu>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tiput(sbi->alloc_file);', '\tiput(sbi->hidden_dir);'], 'added_lines': ['\tiput(sbi->alloc_file);', '\tiput(sbi->hidden_dir);']}
description: A use after free flaw was found in hfsplus_put_super in fs/hfsplus/super.c in the Linux Kernel. This flaw could allow a local user to cause a denial of service problem.

code_evidence: The function closes the attribute, catalog and extent btrees via hfs_btree_close on sbi->attr_tree, sbi->cat_tree and sbi->ext_tree, and only afterward calls iput on sbi->alloc_file and sbi->hidden_dir. The btree close path can release the backing memory that the inode teardown (iput) later accesses, so the ordering leaves the iput work referencing freed btree state.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because memory belonging to the btree is freed by hfs_btree_close and subsequently referenced during iput-driven release (hfsplus_release_folio). This is a lifetime/order defect, not merely a double free or null dereference.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is the teardown ordering: btree structures are closed/freed before the related inodes are released. Trigger occurs on unmount (hfsplus_put_super) when iput on the hidden directory/alloc file reaches folio release that still references the already-closed extent tree. Supported consequence is use-after-free, leading to crash/DoS or memory corruption.

commit_msg:
Merge pull request from GHSA-25j7-9gfc-f46x

cpdb-libs uses the fscanf() and scanf() functions to parse command
lines and configuration files, dropping the read string components
into fixed-length buffers, but does not limit the length of the
strings to be read by fscanf() and scanf() causing buffer overflows
when a string is longer than 1023 characters.

As all buffers have a length of 1024 characters we limit the maximum string
length to be read to 1023 by replaceing all occurences of "%s" by "%1023s"
in all calls of the fscanf() and scanf() functions.

Simply done by

perl -p -i -e 's/(scanf\(.*?".*?)%s/\1%1023s/' cpdb/cpdb-frontend.c tools/cpdb-text-frontend.c

and verifying with

grep scanf */*.c
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if (fscanf(file, "%s", obj_path) == 0)'], 'added_lines': ['    if (fscanf(file, "%1023s", obj_path) == 0)']}
description: cpdb-libs provides frontend and backend libraries for the Common Printing Dialog Backends (CPDB) project. In versions 1.0 through 2.0b4, cpdb-libs is vulnerable to buffer overflows via improper use of `scanf(3)`. cpdb-libs uses the `fscanf()` and `scanf()` functions to parse command lines and configuration files, dropping the read string components into fixed-length buffers, but does not limit the length of the strings to be read by `fscanf()` and `scanf()` causing buffer overflows when a string is longer than 1023 characters. A patch for this issue is available at commit f181bd1f14757c2ae0f17cc76dc20421a40f30b7. As all buffers have a length of 1024 characters, the patch limits the maximum string length to be read to 1023 by replacing all occurrences of `%s` with `%1023s` in all calls of the `fscanf()` and `scanf()` functions.

code_evidence: Line 9 declares obj_path as a fixed-size stack buffer of CPDB_BSIZE (1024) characters.
Line 21 calls fscanf with the unbounded "%s" conversion, writing the file's first token into obj_path without any width limit.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The overflow target obj_path is a local stack-allocated array, and the unbounded %s conversion is the direct write primitive, matching CWE-121's stack-based buffer overflow. It is distinguished from the heap variant because the overwritten buffer is a stack local, not heap-allocated memory.

evidence_lines.code: char obj_path[CPDB_BSIZE];
if (fscanf(file, "%s", obj_path) == 0)

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The configuration file is opened and its first whitespace-delimited token is read by fscanf("%s", obj_path) with no field-width bound. If the token exceeds the 1024-byte stack buffer obj_path, fscanf writes past the buffer, corrupting adjacent stack memory. The root cause is the missing length constraint; the trigger is an overlong token in an attacker-influenced backend file, and the supported consequence is stack memory corruption potentially leading to crash or code execution.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    bufSize = nameLen + ROUND_UP(tag->rawNameLength, sizeof(XML_Char));'], 'added_lines': ['    size_t rawNameLen;', '    rawNameLen = ROUND_UP(tag->rawNameLength, sizeof(XML_Char));', '    /* Detect and prevent integer overflow. */', '    if (rawNameLen > (size_t)INT_MAX - nameLen)', '      return XML_FALSE;', '    bufSize = nameLen + (int)rawNameLen;']}
description: In Expat (aka libexpat) before 2.4.5, there is an integer overflow in storeRawNames.

code_evidence: Line 6 computes nameLen as an int from the tag name string length; line 10 adds nameLen to ROUND_UP(tag->rawNameLength, sizeof(XML_Char)) directly into the int bufSize with no overflow check.
bufSize is then used at line 11 as the allocation-size test and at line 12 as the size passed to REALLOC; line 24 memcpy copies tag->rawNameLength bytes into rawNameBuf, which is tag->buf + nameLen.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The direct defect is an unchecked integer addition feeding a size calculation, matching CWE-190 (integer overflow/wraparound). The out-of-bounds heap write is the downstream consequence, not a separate weakness class.

evidence_lines.code: memcpy(rawNameBuf, tag->rawName, tag->rawNameLength);

ColladaParser: check values length

fixes: #4286
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['            if (acc->mOffset + acc->mCount * acc->mStride > acc->mData->mValues.size()) {', '                throw DeadlyImportError("Not enough data for accessor");', '            }', '            if (acc->mOffset + acc->mCount * acc->mStride > acc->mData->mValues.size()) {', '                throw DeadlyImportError("Not enough data for accessor");', '            }']}
description: An issue was discovered with assimp 5.1.4, a use after free occurred in function ColladaParser::ExtractDataObjectFromChannel in file /code/AssetLib/Collada/ColladaParser.cpp.

code_evidence: Resolves an accessor, then when acc->mData is null stores a pointer to the resolved data library entry into acc->mData; no check that mData->mValues has enough elements for the accessor offsets/count/stride.
Same pattern for per-index channels: acc->mData is assigned from ResolveLibraryReference without validating mValues size before later indexing.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The fix adds a bounds check on acc->mOffset + acc->mCount * acc->mStride against mValues.size(), confirming the function reused an accessor data reference without validating that the referenced memory still covers the accessor range. That stale/insufficient reference being dereferenced is the use-after-free condition, matching CWE-416 rather than a pure out-of-bounds read, because the resolved pointer's backing data is no longer valid for the requested range.

A malformed Collada file with an accessor whose range exceeds the data array triggers out-of-bounds reads when vertices are copied, and the stale/insufficient resolved data pointer is used after the library reference lifecycle, supporting the reported use-after-free behavior.

target/loongarch: Clean up tlb when cpu reset

We should make sure that tlb is clean when cpu reset.

Reviewed-by: Richard Henderson <richard.henderson@linaro.org>

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    memset(env->tlb, 0, sizeof(env->tlb));']}
description: softmmu/physmem.c in QEMU through 7.0.0 can perform an uninitialized read on the translate_fail path, leading to an io_readx or io_writex crash. NOTE: a third party states that the Non-virtualization Use Case in the qemu.org reference applies here, i.e., "Bugs affecting the non-virtualization use case are not considered security bugs at this time.

code_evidence: The reset routine rebuilds CSR_DMW entries and sets env->pc but does not clear the TLB; the diff adds a memset of env->tlb to the #ifndef CONFIG_USER_ONLY block after the pc assignment.

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The root cause is that loongarch_cpu_reset leaves env->tlb uninitialized on reset; the trigger is a later TLB lookup on the translate path, which can read stale/uninitialized entries and resolve to an invalid host access, producing an io_readx/io_writex crash. Prevent segfault in `embedding_lookup_sparse.cc`

Previous fixes missed one additional case.

description: Tensorflow is an Open Source Machine Learning Framework. An attacker can craft a TFLite model that would cause an integer overflow in embedding lookup operations. Both `embedding_size` and `lookup_size` are products of values provided by the user. Hence, a malicious user could trigger overflows in the multiplication. In certain scenarios, this can then result in heap OOB read/write. Users are advised to upgrade to a patched version.

code_evidence: embedding_size and lookup_size are size_t products of user-controlled dimensions; MultiplyAndCheckOverflow guards the loops but output_size = lookup_size * embedding_size at line 44 is computed without an overflow check, then used to reallocate output at line 45.

current_output_offset comes from output_bucket * embedding_size (line 71) and example_embedding_offset from idx * embedding_size (line 82); both int multiplications can wrap, and the loop at lines 86-88 indexes output_ptr and value_ptr with those offsets without bounds checks.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The root cause is unchecked integer multiplication of user-provided sizes producing wrapped offsets used for memory access, matching CWE-190. The consequence (OOB access) is downstream; a pure OOB-read/write label would not capture the arithmetic origin.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: User-controlled dense_shape and value dimensions drive size_t products and int offset multiplications. output_offset and example_embedding_offset can overflow to small or negative values, so the loop indexes output_ptr and value_ptr out of bounds, causing heap OOB read/write (the patch adds range checks to prevent this).

commit_msg:
cryp: prevent direct calls to update and final functions

With inconsistent or malformed data it has been possible to call
"update" and "final" crypto functions directly. Using a fuzzer tool [1]
we have seen that this results in asserts, i.e., a crash that
potentially could leak sensitive information.

By setting the state (initialized) in the crypto context (i.e., the
tee_cryp_state) at the end of all syscall_*_init functions and then add
a check of the state at the beginning of all update and final functions,
  we prevent direct entrance to the "update" and "final" functions.

[1] https://github.com/MartijnB/optee_fuzzer

Fixes: OP-TEE-2019-0021

Signed-off-by: Joakim Bech <joakim.bech@linaro.org>
Reported-by: Martijn Bogaard <bogaard@riscure.com>

commit_msg: minor: Fix overflow in Clipsal-CMR113 and Somfy-IOHC reported by aug5t7
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    int offset = bitbuffer_search(bitbuffer, 0, 0, preamble_pattern, 24) + 24;', '    if (offset >= bitbuffer->bits_per_row[0] - 19 * 10)', '    int num_bits = bitbuffer->bits_per_row[0] - offset;', '    bitrow_printf(b, len * 8, "%s: offset %d, num_bits %d, len %d, msg_len %d\\n", __func__, offset, num_bits, len, msg_len);'], 'added_lines': ['    unsigned offset = bitbuffer_search(bitbuffer, 0, 0, preamble_pattern, 24) + 24;', '    if (offset + 19 * 10 >= bitbuffer->bits_per_row[0])', '    unsigned num_bits = bitbuffer->bits_per_row[0] - offset;', '    num_bits = MIN(num_bits, sizeof (b) * 8);', '    bitrow_printf(b, len * 8, "%s: offset %u, num_bits %u, len %d, msg_len %d\\n", __func__, offset, num_bits, len, msg_len);']}
description: rtl_433 21.12 was discovered to contain a stack overflow in the function somfy_iohc_decode(). This vulnerability allows attackers to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) via a crafted file.

code_evidence: b is a fixed 34-byte stack buffer; offset is derived from bitbuffer_search on attacker-controlled bits_per_row, and num_bits = bits_per_row[0] - offset is passed to extract_bytes_uart writing into b with no bound relative to sizeof(b).

msg_len from b[0] drives bitrow_snprint(&b[9], msg_len*8,...) and b[len-10]/b[len-9]/&b[len-8] index using len; neither is constrained to the 34-byte buffer, so crafted input can read/write out of bounds.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes attacker-influenced lengths into a fixed stack buffer without a size constraint, directly matching CWE-787 out-of-bounds write. This is distinct from a pure out-of-bounds read, since extract_bytes_uart writes into b and subsequent snprint/pointer operations operate past the buffer.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function computes num_bits and msg_len/len from the crafted bitbuffer without clamping to the fixed-size stack buffer b[19+15]. Trigger: a crafted row whose preamble offset leaves num_bits larger than the buffer, or a msg_len/len that exceeds it. Consequence: extract_bytes_uart and the subsequent bitrow_snprint/pointer arithmetic write past b, corrupting the stack and causing a crash (DoS) or memory modification.

commit_msg:
Fix shift overflow when parsing an overlarge note value.

	PR binutils/21378
	* readelf.c (print_gnu_build_attribute_name): Check for an
	overlarge name field.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tunsigned int   bytes = pnote->namesz - (name - pnote->namedata);', '\tunsigned long  val = 0;', '\tunsigned int   shift = 0;', '\tchar *         decoded = NULL;', '\t      left -= printf ("0x%lx", val);', '\t      left -= printf ("0x%-.*lx", left, val);'], 'added_lines': ['\tunsigned int        bytes = pnote->namesz - (name - pnote->namedata);', '\tunsigned long long  val = 0;', '\tunsigned int        shift = 0;', '\tchar *              decoded = NULL;', '', '\t/* PR 21378 */', '\tif (bytes > sizeof (val))', '\t  {', '\t    error (_("corrupt name field: namesz of %lu is too large for a numeric value\\n"),', '\t\t   pnote->namesz);', '\t    return FALSE;', '\t  }', '\t      left -= printf ("0x%llx", val);', '\t      left -= printf ("0x%-.*llx", left, val);']}
description: readelf.c in GNU Binutils 2017-04-12 has a "shift exponent too large for type unsigned long" issue, which might allow remote attackers to cause a denial of service (application crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted ELF file.

code_evidence: bytes is derived from attacker-controlled pnote->namesz minus the parsed offset without bounding it to the capacity of val; the loop shifts each name byte by shift and increments shift by 8 per iteration, so a large namesz drives shift past the width of unsigned long (32 bits), producing an out-of-range shift.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function consumes untrusted ELF note metadata (namesz) and processes it without validating its required property (size within the numeric value width), directly matching CWE-20 improper input validation; the shift overflow is the downstream manifestation, not a separate root cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the numeric-name parser trusts the ELF note namesz field and never checks that the remaining byte count fits the destination value before shifting. Trigger: a crafted ELF with an overlarge GNU build-attribute name field. Consequence: shift exponent exceeds the type width, causing undefined behavior and a readelf crash (DoS).

gf_list_insert(ptr->global_access_entries, ae, i);

commit_msg:
hw/nvme: fix CVE-2021-3929

This fixes CVE-2021-3929 "locally" by denying DMA to the iomem of the
device itself. This still allows DMA to MMIO regions of other devices
(e.g. doing P2P DMA to the controller memory buffer of another NVMe
device).

Fixes: CVE-2021-3929
Reported-by: Qiuhao Li <Qiuhao.Li@outlook.com>
Reviewed-by: Keith Busch <kbusch@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Philippe Mathieu-Daudé <f4bug@amsat.org>
Signed-off-by: Klaus Jensen <k.jensen@samsung.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '    if (nvme_addr_is_iomem(n, addr)) {', '        return NVME_DATA_TRAS_ERROR;', '    }']}
description: A DMA reentrancy issue was found in the NVM Express Controller (NVME) emulation in QEMU. This CVE is similar to CVE-2021-3750 and, just like it, when the reentrancy write triggers the reset function nvme_ctrl_reset(), data structs will be freed leading to a use-after-free issue. A malicious guest could use this flaw to crash the QEMU process on the host, resulting in a denial of service condition or, potentially, executing arbitrary code within the context of the QEMU process on the host.

code_evidence: nvme_map_addr only distinguishes CMB (line 8) and PMR (line 10) targets; otherwise it falls through to qemu_sglist_add(&sg->qsg, addr, len) at line 32 for any DMA address. There is no check rejecting an address that lies in the device's own iomem/MMIO region, so a guest-supplied address can map the controller's own registers into the DMA scatter-gather list.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The supported consequence is reuse of freed memory (structs freed by reset while the original path still references them), matching CWE-416. The missing iomem exclusion is the enabling cause, not a distinct weakness such as CWE-119; the reentrancy-triggered free-and-reuse is the core defect.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the mapping routine accepts DMA to the device's own MMIO without an exclusion check. Trigger: a guest programs an NVMe DMA address pointing at the controller's iomem; the resulting write reenters emulation and invokes nvme_ctrl_reset(), which frees data structures still referenced by the in-flight operation. Consequence: use-after-free leading to host QEMU crash or potential code execution.

commit_msg:
avcodec/ac3_parser: Check init_get_bits8() for failure

Fixes: null pointer dereference
Fixes: ffmpeg_crash_6.avi

Found-by: Thuan Pham, Marcel Böhme, Andrew Santosa and Alexandru Razvan Caciulescu with AFLSmart
Reviewed-by: Paul B Mahol <onemda@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>

description: In FFmpeg 4.0.1, a missing check for failure of a call to init_get_bits8() in the avpriv_ac3_parse_header function in libavcodec/ac3_parser.c may trigger a NULL pointer dereference while converting a crafted AVI file to MPEG4, leading to a denial of service.

code_evidence: Line 12 calls init_get_bits8(&gb, buf, size) and discards its return value, so gb is used by ff_ac3_parse_header on line 13 even when initialization failed and gb's internal buffer pointer remains NULL. The error check on lines 14-15 only validates ff_ac3_parse_header's result, not the failed init_get_bits8 call.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked init_get_bits8 failure leads to use of a GetBitContext whose buffer pointer is NULL, and the subsequent parse dereferences it, matching CWE-476's NULL pointer dereference. This is distinct from an integer/bounds issue: the defect is the missing failure check, not malformed bit-length arithmetic.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the return value of init_get_bits8() is ignored, allowing an uninitialized/NULL-backed GetBitContext to reach ff_ac3_parse_header(). Trigger: a crafted AVI input whose size makes init_get_bits8 fail. Consequence: ff_ac3_parse_header dereferences the NULL buffer pointer, crashing the process (DoS).

joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The loop reads buf[j + idx] beyond the intended buffer end, which is precisely an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). It is not a write overflow, since only reads occur; the missing length constraint on size is the direct cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the byte-dump loop trusts op.size/hint->size as the read count and never clamps it to the bytes actually available (len - idx). Trigger: a crafted binary whose disassembled instruction reports a size exceeding the remaining buffer. Consequence: out-of-bounds read of buf, causing an application crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
Command-line client. Do not trust SSL certificates by default, unlss '--trust' option is set.

Signed-off-by: allexzander <blackslayer4@gmail.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    account->setTrustCertificates(options.trustSSL);']}
description: Nextcloud also ships a CLI utility called nextcloudcmd which is sometimes used for automated scripting and headless servers. Versions of nextcloudcmd prior to 3.6.1 would incorrectly trust invalid TLS certificates, which may enable a Man-in-the-middle attack that exposes sensitive data or credentials to a network attacker. This affects the CLI only. It does not affect the standard GUI desktop Nextcloud clients, and it does not affect the Nextcloud server.

code_evidence: options.trustSSL defaults to false at line 13, and the SimpleSslErrorHandler is attached to the account at line 94. In the non-TOKEN_AUTH_ONLY build, line 89-91 only marks credentials SSL-trusted when options.trustSSL is set, but the account's SSL error handling is installed unconditionally at line 94 with no trust flag propagation, so the handler can accept invalid certificates regardless of the default.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-295 covers failure to properly validate a certificate. Here invalid certificates are accepted by default, matching improper certificate validation rather than a mere configuration error.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the CLI accepts TLS certificates without enforcing a trust decision; the default trustSSL=false is not enforced against the account's SSL error handler, which is attached unconditionally. Trigger: connecting to a server presenting an invalid/self-signed certificate. Consequence: the TLS handshake proceeds, enabling a man-in-the-middle to read credentials and synced data.

commit_msg:
In commit 6a53b7593233 ("xfrm: check id proto in validate_tmpl()")
I introduced a check for xfrm protocol, but according to Herbert
IPSEC_PROTO_ANY should only be used as a wildcard for lookup, so
it should be removed from validate_tmpl().

And, IPSEC_PROTO_ANY is expected to only match 3 IPSec-specific
protocols, this is why xfrm_state_flush() could still miss
IPPROTO_ROUTING, which leads that those entries are left in
net->xfrm.state_all before exit net. Fix this by replacing
IPSEC_PROTO_ANY with zero.

This patch also extracts the check from validate_tmpl() to
xfrm_id_proto_valid() and uses it in parse_ipsecrequest().
With this, no other protocols should be added into xfrm.

commit_msg:
Fix #78863: DirectoryIterator class silently truncates after a null byte

Since the constructor of DirectoryIterator and friends is supposed to
accepts paths (i.e. strings without NUL bytes), we must not accept
arbitrary strings.

(cherry picked from commit a5a15965da23c8e97657278fc8dfbf1dfb20c016)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tparsed = zend_parse_parameters(ZEND_NUM_ARGS(), "s|l", &path, &len, &flags);', '\t\tparsed = zend_parse_parameters(ZEND_NUM_ARGS(), "s", &path, &len);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tparsed = zend_parse_parameters(ZEND_NUM_ARGS(), "p|l", &path, &len, &flags);', '\t\tparsed = zend_parse_parameters(ZEND_NUM_ARGS(), "p", &path, &len);']}
description: In PHP versions 7.2.x below 7.2.26, 7.3.x below 7.3.13 and 7.4.0, PHP DirectoryIterator class accepts filenames with embedded \0 byte and treats them as terminating at that byte. This could lead to security vulnerabilities, e.g. in applications checking paths that the code is allowed to access.

code_evidence: Both branches parse the constructor argument with the "s"/"s|l" format specifiers, which accept arbitrary byte strings including embedded NUL bytes, storing them into path with length len.

The parsed path is passed to strstr(path, "glob:") and then to spl_filesystem_dir_open(intern, path); these downstream string consumers interpret path as a NUL-terminated C string, so any embedded \0 silently truncates the value actually used.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is improper neutralization of a special element (the NUL byte) in input that is later interpreted by a downstream string-parsing component, altering how the path is parsed; this matches CWE-74's injection class. A narrower CWE (e.g., CWE-158 NUL byte injection) is a more specific child, but the target class CWE-74 still applies.

evidence_lines.code:
parsed = zend_parse_parameters(ZEND_NUM_ARGS(), "s|l", &path, &len, &flags);
parsed = zend_parse_parameters(ZEND_NUM_ARGS(), "s", &path, &len);

if (SPL_HAS_FLAG(ctor_flags, DIT_CTOR_GLOB) && strstr(path, "glob:spprintf(&path, 0, "glob:spl_filesystem_dir_open(intern, path);
spl_filesystem_dir_open(intern, path);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the constructor accepts a string containing special NUL elements rather than rejecting it. Trigger: a caller supplies a path like "/allowed\0/forbidden" or vice versa; downstream C-string operations stop at the NUL, so the path checked differs from the path opened. Consequence: access-control or path-validation checks can be bypassed, enabling access to unintended directories.

commit_msg:
Release "3.0.6": Fix crashes in Array for "integer overflow #10"

FossilOrigin-Name: 50642d64b8f0a4e62df68e59fcb2ef0923c3dbec8fc8a15d38b1ddbe655c38d6
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    uint n = Jsi_ObjGetLength(interp, obj);', '    assert(n <= obj->arrCnt);'], 'added_lines': ['    uint n = jsi_SizeOfArray(interp, obj);']}
description: Integer overflow vulnerability in function Jsi_ObjSetLength in jsish before 3.0.6, allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code.

code_evidence: Line 7 obtains the array length as a uint and line 8 only asserts (n <= obj->arrCnt), which is not enforced in release builds.
Line 12 decrements n; line 14 then computes n*sizeof(Jsi_Value*) for memmove and line 15 indexes obj->arr[n].
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the decrement at line 12 wraps a uint used directly as a memory-copy size and index, and the only guard on line 8 is a non-enforcing assert. The root cause is the unchecked arithmetic on the length, not a mere out-of-bounds read.

evidence_lines.code:
uint n = Jsi_ObjGetLength(interp, obj);
assert(n <= obj->arrCnt);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The length is read from the array object and used as a uint size without a validated upper bound; the assert on line 8 is removed in release builds. If the length is at the maximum uint value, line 12 wraps n to a small value, so the memmove size on line 14 is computed from a wrapped count and line 15 writes obj->arr[n] at a mismatched index, corrupting memory. The trigger is an array whose length reaches the integer limit before shift.

commit_msg:
mac80211: Fix NULL ptr deref for injected rate info

The commit cb17ed29a7a5 ("mac80211: parse radiotap header when selecting Tx
queue") moved the code to validate the radiotap header from
ieee80211_monitor_start_xmit to ieee80211_parse_tx_radiotap. This made is
possible to share more code with the new Tx queue selection code for
injected frames. But at the same time, it now required the call of
ieee80211_parse_tx_radiotap at the beginning of functions which wanted to
handle the radiotap header. And this broke the rate parser for radiotap
header parser.

The radiotap parser for rates is operating most of the time only on the
data in the actual radiotap header. But for the 802.11a/b/g rates, it must
also know the selected band from the chandef information. But this
information is only written to the ieee80211_tx_info at the end of the
ieee80211_monitor_start_xmit - long after ieee80211_parse_tx_radiotap was
already called. The info->band information was therefore always 0
(NL80211_BAND_2GHZ) when the parser code tried to access it.

For a 5GHz only device, injecting a frame with 802.11a rates would cause a
NULL pointer dereference because local->hw.wiphy->bands[NL80211_BAND_2GHZ]
would most likely have been NULL when the radiotap parser searched for the
correct rate index of the driver.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Reported-by: Ben Greear <greearb@candelatech.com>
Fixes: cb17ed29a7a5 ("mac80211: parse radiotap header when selecting Tx queue")
Signed-off-by: Mathy Vanhoef <Mathy.Vanhoef@kuleuven.be>
[sven@narfation.org: added commit message]
Signed-off-by: Sven Eckelmann <sven@narfation.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20210530133226.40587-1-sven@narfation.org
Signed-off-by: Johannes Berg <johannes.berg@intel.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tstruct ieee80211_supported_band *sband =', '\t\tlocal->hw.wiphy->bands[info->band];', '\t/* check for not even having the fixed radiotap header part */', '\tif (unlikely(skb->len < sizeof(struct ieee80211_radiotap_header)))', '\t\treturn false; /* too short to be possibly valid */', '', '\t/* is it a header version we can trust to find length from? */', '\tif (unlikely(rthdr->it_version))', '\t\treturn false; /* only version 0 is supported */', '', '\t/* does the skb contain enough to deliver on the alleged length? */', '\tif (unlikely(skb->len < ieee80211_get_radiotap_len(skb->data)))', '\t\treturn false; /* skb too short for claimed rt header extent */', '\t\t} else {'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (!ieee80211_validate_radiotap_len(skb))', '\t\treturn false;', '\t\tstruct ieee80211_supported_band *sband =', '\t\t\tlocal->hw.wiphy->bands[info->band];', '', '\t\t} else if (sband) {']}
description: The mac80211 subsystem in the Linux kernel before 5.12.13, when a device supporting only 5 GHz is used, allows attackers to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference in the radiotap parser) by injecting a frame with 802.11a rates.

code_evidence: Line 9-10 eagerly reads local->hw.wiphy->bands[info->band] into sband before any rate handling; info->band is not yet populated at this point in the call flow.
In the plain-rate branch (line 131 else), the loop at line 132 dereferences sband->n_bitrates without a NULL check, so if bands[info->band] was NULL the loop walks a NULL pointer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences a pointer (sband) that is not guaranteed non-NULL on the rate path, matching CWE-476's NULL-pointer dereference. It is not merely an out-of-bounds read; the missing NULL check on the band table entry is the direct flaw.

evidence_lines.code:
struct ieee80211_supported_band *sband =
local->hw.wiphy->bands[info->band];

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the band table lookup for the injected rate occurs before the selected band is written into info, so info->band is 0 (2 GHz). Trigger: a 5 GHz-only device receiving an injected frame with 802.11a rates, where bands[NL80211_BAND_2GHZ] is NULL. Consequence: sband->n_bitrates dereference crashes the kernel (DoS).

commit_msg: Don't process empty input for cherokee_validator_parse_basic and cherokee_validator_parse_digest
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\t/* Guard empty input', '\t */', '\tif (unlikely(str == NULL || str_len == 0))', '\t\tgoto error;']}
description: Cherokee 0.4.27 to 1.2.104 is affected by a denial of service due to a NULL pointer dereferences. A remote unauthenticated attacker can crash the server by sending an HTTP request to protected resources using a malformed Authorization header that is mishandled during a cherokee_buffer_add call within cherokee_validator_parse_basic or cherokee_validator_parse_digest.

code_evidence: The function unconditionally passes the caller-supplied str and str_len into cherokee_buffer_add, then decodes base64, without checking whether str is NULL or str_len is zero.
After decoding, strchr searches auth.buf for ':'. If the input is empty, auth.buf may be NULL or lack a colon, so colon becomes NULL and execution branches to error.
Lines 11-12 use the decoded buffer and colon-derived offsets; the unguarded empty/NULL input path is what the added guard addresses.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits because the mishandled empty input leads to a NULL pointer being used in buffer operations, causing a crash. This is a null-dereference availability flaw, not merely a logic error.

evidence_lines.code:
cherokee_buffer_add (&auth, str, str_len);
cherokee_buffer_decode_base64 (&auth);

cherokee_buffer_add (&validator->user, auth.buf, colon - auth.buf);
cherokee_buffer_add (&validator->passwd, colon+1, auth.len  - ((colon+1) - auth.buf));

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function processes an empty or NULL Authorization value without validating it before buffer add/decode. Trigger: a malformed header yields empty str/str_len, causing the decoded buffer or colon lookup to be NULL. Consequence: the subsequent buffer handling dereferences an invalid pointer, crashing the server (DoS).

commit_msg:
Bug 703902: Fix op stack management in sampled_data_continue()

Replace pop() (which does no checking, and doesn't handle stack extension
blocks) with ref_stack_pop() which does do all that.

We still use pop() in one case (it's faster), but we have to later use
ref_stack_pop() before calling sampled_data_sample() which also accesses the
op stack.

Fixes:
https://bugs.chromium.org/p/oss-fuzz/issues/detail?id=34675
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    pop(num_out);\t\t    /* Move op to base of result values */', '', '            pop(O_STACK_PAD);\t    /* Remove spare stack space */', '            pop(stack_depth_adjust - num_out);', '                pop(stack_depth_adjust);', '                push(O_STACK_PAD - stack_depth_adjust);'], 'added_lines': ['    pop(num_out); /* Move op to base of result values */', '', '    /* From here on, we have to use ref_stack_pop() rather than pop()', '       so that it handles stack extension blocks properly, before calling', '       sampled_data_sample() which also uses the op stack.', '     */', '            ref_stack_pop(&o_stack, O_STACK_PAD);\t    /* Remove spare stack space */', '            ref_stack_pop(&o_stack, stack_depth_adjust - num_out);', '                ref_stack_pop(&o_stack, stack_depth_adjust);', '                ref_stack_push(&o_stack, O_STACK_PAD - stack_depth_adjust);']}
description: Ghostscript GhostPDL 9.50 through 9.54.0 has a heap-based buffer overflow in sampled_data_finish (called from sampled_data_continue and interp).

code_evidence: Line 42 uses pop(num_out) which performs no stack-extension-block handling; the commit replaces it with ref_stack_pop so that subsequent sampled_data_sample() accesses a consistent op stack.

Lines 44-47 and 55-65 adjust the op stack with pop()/push() using stack_depth_adjust values derived from ref_stack_count; when the stack straddles extension blocks these raw operations miscompute the effective stack position, leaving op/osp inconsistent before sampled_data_sample() writes result data.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The supported consequence is an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787): stack mismanagement causes a write past the end of a heap buffer. The flaw is not merely an incorrect stack count but an actual memory write beyond bounds, matching CWE-787 rather than a pure logic/state error.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: raw pop()/push() on the op stack ignore stack extension blocks, so stack_depth_adjust and num_out bookkeeping desynchronizes osp from the actual stack. Trigger: processing sampled data where the operand stack spans extension blocks. Consequence: sampled_data_sample() then writes past the intended buffer, a heap-based out-of-bounds write.

commit_msg:
Track byteSize of HeaderMap internally.

Introduces a cached byte size updated internally in HeaderMap. The value
is stored as an optional, and is cleared whenever a non-const pointer or
reference to a HeaderEntry is accessed. The cached value can be set with
refreshByteSize() which performs an iteration over the HeaderMap to sum
the size of each key and value in the HeaderMap.

Signed-off-by: Asra Ali <asraa@google.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  // Refresh byte sizes of the HeaderMaps before logging.', '  // TODO(asraa): Remove this when entries in HeaderMap can no longer be modified by reference and', '  // HeaderMap holds an accurate internal byte size count.', '  if (request_headers_ != nullptr) {', '    request_headers_->refreshByteSize();', '  }', '  if (response_headers_ != nullptr) {', '    response_headers_->refreshByteSize();', '  }', '  if (response_trailers_ != nullptr) {', '    response_trailers_->refreshByteSize();', '  }']}
description: Upon receiving each incoming request header data, Envoy will iterate over existing request headers to verify that the total size of the headers stays below a maximum limit. The implementation in versions 1.10.0 through 1.11.1 for HTTP/1.x traffic and all versions of Envoy for HTTP/2 traffic had O(n^2) performance characteristics. A remote attacker may craft a request that stays below the maximum request header size but consists of many thousands of small headers to consume CPU and result in a denial-of-service attack.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The destructor only refreshes cached header byte sizes before logging; it contains no header-size accounting, limit check, or per-request iteration loop, so the O(n^2) header-parsing resource-consumption weakness described is not present in this function.

commit_msg:
Patch series "Fix several device private page reference counting issues",
v2

This series aims to fix a number of page reference counting issues in
drivers dealing with device private ZONE_DEVICE pages.  These result in
use-after-free type bugs, either from accessing a struct page which no
longer exists because it has been removed or accessing fields within the
struct page which are no longer valid because the page has been freed.

During normal usage it is unlikely these will cause any problems.  However
without these fixes it is possible to crash the kernel from userspace. 
These crashes can be triggered either by unloading the kernel module or
unbinding the device from the driver prior to a userspace task exiting. 
In modules such as Nouveau it is also possible to trigger some of these
issues by explicitly closing the device file-descriptor prior to the task
exiting and then accessing device private memory.

This involves some minor changes to both PowerPC and AMD GPU code. 
Unfortunately I lack hardware to test either of those so any help there
would be appreciated.  The changes mimic what is done in for both Nouveau
and hmm-tests though so I doubt they will cause problems.


This patch (of 8):

When the CPU tries to access a device private page the migrate_to_ram()
callback associated with the pgmap for the page is called.  However no
reference is taken on the faulting page.  Therefore a concurrent migration
of the device private page can free the page and possibly the underlying
pgmap.  This results in a race which can crash the kernel due to the
migrate_to_ram() function pointer becoming invalid.  It also means drivers
can't reliably read the zone_device_data field because the page may have
been freed with memunmap_pages().

Close the race by getting a reference on the page while holding the ptl to
ensure it has not been freed.  Unfortunately the elevated reference count
will cause the migration required to handle the fault to fail.  To avoid
this failure pass the faulting page into the migrate_vma functions so that
if an elevated reference count is found it can be checked to see if it's
expected or not.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tif (page_mapped(page) || !migrate_vma_check_page(page)) {'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (page_mapped(page) ||', '\t\t    !migrate_vma_check_page(page, migrate->fault_page)) {']}
description: A vulnerability was found in Linux Kernel. It has been classified as problematic. Affected is an unknown function of the file mm/memory.c of the component Driver Handler. The manipulation leads to use after free. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue. The identifier of this vulnerability is VDB-211020.

code_evidence: Line 8 obtains `page` from `migrate_pfn_to_page(migrate->src[i])` without taking a reference; for a device-private page the zone-device branch at 12 is skipped, so no get_page is performed before line 25 derives `folio = page_folio(page)` and lines 26-28 dereference the page/folio via `folio_mapped`, `try_to_migrate`, `page_mapped` and `migrate_vma_check_page(page)` (the pre-patch call without `migrate->fault_page`).

Because no reference is held, a concurrent migration can free the device-private page and its pgmap between lookup and these dereferences. The failure path at 29-36 only re-references non-zone-device pages, and the restore loop at 39-48 later calls `folio_unlock`/`folio_put` on the page, compounding use of possibly-freed memory.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function operates on a page pointer whose lifetime is not pinned, so concurrent freeing makes subsequent dereferences use freed memory—matching CWE-416. The patch's addition of `migrate->fault_page` to `migrate_vma_check_page` confirms the page was previously checked without the reference needed to keep it valid; this is a lifetime/use-after-free issue, not merely a missing bounds or type check.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: `migrate_vma_unmap` dereferences a device-private page obtained from `migrate_pfn_to_page` without first acquiring a page reference under the ptl. Trigger: concurrent migration of the same device-private page frees the page/pgmap while this function is between lookup and the `folio_mapped`/`try_to_migrate`/`migrate_vma_check_page` operations. Consequence: use-after-free of the struct page and pgmap, allowing invalid function-pointer access (crash) or reads of freed `zone_device_data`.

Bug 698908: Resize object use and renumbering lists after repair.

Previously repair might end up increasing xref_len, but the lists

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tint xref_len = pdf_xref_len(ctx, doc);', '\tfor (num = 0; num < xref_len; num++)'], 'added_lines': ['\t/* xref_len may change due to repair, so check it every iteration */', '\tfor (num = 0; num < pdf_xref_len(ctx, doc); num++)']}
description: In Artifex MuPDF 1.12.0, there is a heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in the do_pdf_save_document function in the pdf/pdf-write.c file. Remote attackers could leverage the vulnerability to cause a denial of service via a crafted pdf file.

code_evidence: Line 5 caches xref_len once before the loop, and line 6 bounds the iteration by this stale value. Line 8 indexes the xref entry table with num, and line 10 loads object num. If pdf_load_object or repair logic grows the xref table during iteration, the cached xref_len no longer reflects the actual table size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the stale xref_len causes indexing/loading beyond the intended xref table bounds, an out-of-bounds write/access. It is not merely a logic error: the inconsistent length directly enables memory corruption via the object-loading path.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the loop bound is snapshotted before iteration, while xref_len can change due to repair during pdf_load_object. Trigger: a crafted PDF causing repair to increase the xref length mid-loop. Consequence: subsequent pdf_get_xref_entry/pdf_load_object accesses use an inconsistent length, leading to out-of-bounds access and potential heap buffer overflow/DoS.

commit_msg: Reset memory for RLE decoder (patch provided by scarybeasts)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    (void) ResetMagickMemory(pixels,0,pixel_info_length);']}
description: ImageMagick before 7.0.5-2 and GraphicsMagick before 1.3.24 use uninitialized memory in the RLE decoder, allowing an attacker to leak sensitive information from process memory space, as demonstrated by remote attacks against ImageMagick code in a long-running server process that converts image data on behalf of multiple users. This is caused by a missing initialization step in the ReadRLEImage function in coders/rle.c.

code_evidence: A buffer is allocated for decoded pixels via AcquireVirtualMemory and its base pointer obtained from GetVirtualMemoryBlob; the allocation is not zeroed or otherwise initialized in this version.
The buffer is only partially written when the header flag branch (flags & 0x01 && !(flags & 0x02)) fills it with background_color; otherwise the fill is skipped, leaving the region uninitialized.
ByteDataOp writes pixels only at computed offsets and only when (y < rows) and (x+i < columns); out-of-range positions are skipped, so gaps remain unwritten.
RunDataOp similarly writes a run pixel only for in-range coordinates, leaving other buffer positions untouched.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-908 covers use of a resource that has not been initialized, matching this decoder reading uninitialized heap bytes as pixel data. The patch's ResetMagickMemory(pixels,0,...) confirms the missing initialization. This is not an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787); the offset checks bound writes, but they do not guarantee every buffer position is initialized before use.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the pixel buffer returned by GetVirtualMemoryBlob is used to build the output image without being initialized, and the RLE opcodes (ByteData/RunData) and background-fill branch write only a subset of positions. Trigger: a crafted RLE image whose opcodes skip or leave portions of the pixel buffer unwritten. Consequence: those uninitialized bytes are later copied into pixel channels (e.g., SetPixelRed/Green/Blue/Index and SyncImage), leaking process memory contents into the decoded image.

opj_t1_encode_cblks: fix UBSAN signed integer overflow

Fixes #1053 / CVE-2018-5727

practice.
At least with gcc or clang compilers on x86_64 which generate the same
assembly code with or without that fix.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['                                    tiledp[tileIndex] *= (1 << T1_NMSEDEC_FRACBITS);'], 'added_lines': ['                            /* Do multiplication on unsigned type, even if the', '                             * underlying type is signed, to avoid potential', '                             * int overflow on large value (the output will be', '                             * incorrect in such situation, but whatever...)', '                             * This assumes complement-to-2 signed integer', '                             * representation', '                             * Fixes https://github.com/uclouvain/openjpeg/issues/1053', '                             */', '                            OPJ_UINT32* OPJ_RESTRICT tiledp_u = (OPJ_UINT32*) tiledp;', '                                    tiledp_u[tileIndex] <<= T1_NMSEDEC_FRACBITS;']}
description: In OpenJPEG 2.3.0, there is an integer overflow vulnerability in the opj_t1_encode_cblks function (openjp2/t1.c). Remote attackers could leverage this vulnerability to cause a denial of service via a crafted bmp file.

code_evidence: When qmfbid == 1, the loop multiplies each signed OPJ_INT32 coefficient tiledp[tileIndex] by (1 << T1_NMSEDEC_FRACBITS) (i.e., 8192) in place. For large magnitude coefficients near INT32_MAX this signed multiplication wraps, producing an incorrect value before opj_t1_encode_cblk consumes it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe operation is a signed integer multiplication whose result can exceed the OPJ_INT32 range, matching CWE-190 integer overflow/wraparound. It is not a bounds or pointer issue; the weakness is the unchecked arithmetic itself.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the in-place scaling of signed 32-bit samples by 8192 is performed without a range check or wider intermediate type, so crafted coefficient values overflow. Trigger: a crafted BMP yielding large coefficients with qmfbid == 1. Consequence: incorrect encoded output and undefined signed-overflow behavior that can crash the encoder (DoS).

__skb_pull(skb, hlen);
skb->protocol = eth->h_proto;

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '    g_assert (box_width > 0);']}
description: A SIGFPE is raised in the function box_blur_line of rsvg-filter.c in GNOME librsvg 2.40.17 during an attempted parse of a crafted SVG file, because of incorrect protection against division by zero.

code_evidence: box_width is a caller-supplied gint; the odd/even branching computes output and trail from it, and when box_width is even with even_offset not 1 or -1 the else branch only asserts, leaving output/trail unset, but more critically nothing constrains box_width to be positive before use.
coverage is derived from lead/trail bounds (line 30), and it is used as the divisor in multiple integer divisions (lines 46, 51, 60, 64) without any check that coverage != 0.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-369 is exactly a divide-by-zero: an unvalidated dimension (box_width) leads to a zero divisor in the coverage divisions, producing an availability crash (SIGFPE). This is not a mere integer overflow or out-of-bounds read; the direct consequence is division by zero.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The divisor coverage can evaluate to zero when lead and trail collapse (e.g., lead == len-1 and trail == -1 yields coverage = (len-1) - (-1) = len, but other lead/trail combinations with a zero or negative box_width can produce coverage == 0). A crafted SVG drives box_width to an invalid size, causing the division to raise SIGFPE. The patch's g_assert(box_width > 0) confirms box_width was not validated before the divisions.

commit_msg:
PR22443, Global buffer overflow in _bfd_elf_get_symbol_version_string

Symbols like *ABS* defined in bfd/section.c:global_syms are not
elf_symbol_type.  They can appear on relocs and perhaps other places
in an ELF bfd, so a number of places in nm.c and objdump.c are wrong
to cast an asymbol based on the bfd being ELF.  I think we lose
nothing by excluding all section symbols, not just the global_syms.

	PR 22443
	* nm.c (sort_symbols_by_size): Don't attempt to access
	section symbol internal_elf_sym.
	(print_symbol): Likewise.  Don't call bfd_get_symbol_version_string
	for section symbols.
	* objdump.c (compare_symbols): Don't attempt to access
	section symbol internal_elf_sym.
	(objdump_print_symname): Don't call bfd_get_symbol_version_string
	for section symbols.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      if ((a->flags & BSF_SYNTHETIC) == 0)', '      if ((b->flags & BSF_SYNTHETIC) == 0)'], 'added_lines': ['      if ((a->flags & (BSF_SECTION_SYM | BSF_SYNTHETIC)) == 0)', '      if ((b->flags & (BSF_SECTION_SYM | BSF_SYNTHETIC)) == 0)']}
description: nm.c and objdump.c in GNU Binutils 2.29.1 mishandle certain global symbols, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (_bfd_elf_get_symbol_version_string buffer over-read and application crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted ELF file.

code_evidence: Lines 75-76 gate entry on both symbols' BFD flavour being ELF, then lines 80-81 and 83-84 cast each asymbol to elf_symbol_type and read internal_elf_sym.st_size. The guard only excludes BSF_SYNTHETIC, so section symbols (BSF_SECTION_SYM) that are not synthetic still pass the check and are cast even though they are not elf_symbol_type.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The cast-and-read at lines 81/84 accesses memory beyond the actual asymbol object layout, matching CWE-125 out-of-bounds read. It is not merely a type-confusion logic error because the supported consequence is reading past the intended object boundary.

description: Contiki-NG is an open-source, cross-platform operating system for IoT devices. Because of insufficient validation of IPv6 neighbor discovery options in Contiki-NG, attackers can send neighbor solicitation packets that trigger an out-of-bounds read. When attempting to match EXTENDED COPY CSCD descriptors with corresponding
se_devices, target_xcopy_locate_se_dev_e4() currently iterates over LIO's
global devices list which includes all configured backstores.

This change ensures that only initiator-accessible backstores are
considered during CSCD descriptor lookup, according to the session's
se_node_acl LUN list.

To avoid LUN removal race conditions, device pinning is changed from being
configfs based to instead using the se_node_acl lun_ref.

description: In drivers/target/target_core_xcopy.c in the Linux kernel before 5.10.7, insufficient identifier checking in the LIO SCSI target code can be used by remote attackers to read or write files via directory traversal in an XCOPY request, aka CID-2896c93811e3. For example, an attack can occur over a network if the attacker has access to one iSCSI LUN. The attacker gains control over file access because I/O operations are proxied via an attacker-selected backstore.

code_evidence: The function resolves a caller-supplied dev_wwn against every device returned by target_for_each_device, which walks LIO's global device list including all configured backstores. No check restricts the matched device to those exposed through the requesting session's se_node_acl LUN list, and on a match the matched device pointer is returned directly.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-22 fits because external input (dev_wwn) selects a resource without being constrained to the restricted set of devices the session may access, letting the request escape the intended directory/backstore boundary. This is an improper limitation of an externally supplied identifier to a restricted namespace, not a memory-safety defect.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: identifier lookup is performed over the global backstore list instead of the initiator-accessible LUN set, so an attacker who can reach one LUN can name an arbitrary backstore in an XCOPY CSCD descriptor. Trigger: a remote XCOPY request with a crafted NAA identifier. Consequence: I/O is proxied to an attacker-selected backstore, enabling reads or writes outside the permitted LUN (CVE-2020-28374).

description: A heap-based buffer overflow issue was discovered in UPX in PackTmt::pack() in p_tmt.cpp file. The flow allows an attacker to cause a denial of service (abort) via a crafted file.

code_evidence: wrkmem is allocated as rsize + EXTRA_INFO, then rsize bytes are read into wrkmem + 4, so the usable write region for relocation processing is bounded by the allocation.
The loop iterates ic from 4 to rsize inclusive and writes set_le32(wrkmem + ic, ...) at wrkmem + rsize, i.e. one 4-byte word beyond the read data and near the allocation end.

After optimizeReloc32, wrkmem[relocsize++] and successive set_le32(wrkmem + relocsize, ...) writes append data; relocsize is derived from the relocation count and is not bounded against the mb_wrkmem allocation size before memcpy(ibuf + usize, wrkmem, relocsize).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes to wrkmem past its allocated bounds, which is the out-of-bounds write described by CWE-787. The weakness is the missing capacity check and off-by-one write, not merely reading untrusted input.

evidence_lines.code:
for (unsigned ic = 4; ic <= rsize; ic += 4)
set_le32(wrkmem + ic, get_le32(wrkmem + ic) - 4);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the working buffer is sized from rsize plus a fixed EXTRA_INFO but the relocation rewrite and appended entry-point/relocsize fields can write at or beyond the allocation end, and relocsize is not checked against remaining capacity. Trigger: a crafted TMT file with relocation data driving the loop and optimizeReloc32 output. Consequence: heap out-of-bounds write, corrupting adjacent memory and causing abort/denial of service.

commit_msg:
xen/rwlock: Add missing memory barrier in the unlock path of rwlock

The rwlock unlock paths are using atomic_sub() to release the lock.
However the implementation of atomic_sub() rightfully doesn't contain a
memory barrier. On Arm, this means a processor is allowed to re-order
the memory access with the preceeding access.

In other words, the unlock may be seen by another processor before all
the memory accesses within the "critical" section.

The rwlock paths already contains barrier indirectly, but they are not
very useful without the counterpart in the unlock paths.

The memory barriers are not necessary on x86 because loads/stores are
not re-ordered with lock instructions.

So add arch_lock_release_barrier() in the unlock paths that will only
add memory barrier on Arm.

Take the opportunity to document each lock paths explaining why a
barrier is not necessary.

This is XSA-314.

Signed-off-by: Julien Grall <jgrall@amazon.com>
Acked-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    /*', '     * atomic_cmpxchg() is a full barrier so no need for an', '     * arch_lock_acquire_barrier().', '     */']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.13.x, allowing guest OS users to cause a denial of service or possibly gain privileges because of missing memory barriers in read-write unlock paths. The read-write unlock paths don't contain a memory barrier. On Arm, this means a processor is allowed to re-order the memory access with the preceding ones. In other words, the unlock may be seen by another processor before all the memory accesses within the "critical" section. As a consequence, it may be possible to have a writer executing a critical section at the same time as readers or another writer. In other words, many of the assumptions (e.g., a variable cannot be modified after a check) in the critical sections are not safe anymore. The read-write locks are used in hypercalls (such as grant-table ones), so a malicious guest could exploit the race. For instance, there is a small window where Xen can leak memory if XENMAPSPACE_grant_table is used concurrently. A malicious guest may be able to leak memory, or cause a hypervisor crash resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS). Information leak and privilege escalation cannot be excluded.

code_evidence: The trylock reads the shared lock word with atomic_read into cnts, then conditionally attempts atomic_cmpxchg to acquire the write lock only if the word was zero.

On the failure path the function releases preemption (preempt_enable) and returns 0, leaving the caller to handle a busy lock; on success it returns 1 without any explicit acquire barrier, relying on the full barrier semantics of atomic_cmpxchg.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-362 fits because the underlying defect is improper synchronization of a shared rwlock resource across concurrent processors, where an interfering sequence can violate the exclusivity/atomicity of the critical section. This function itself is the trylock acquire path and its cmpxchg is a full barrier; the missing release barrier is in the unlock paths, so the function is only contextual evidence of the locking protocol rather than the direct defect site.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The lock's shared state is the rwlock word; acquisition depends on the read-then-cmpxchg sequence succeeding only when the word was zero. This trylock path uses a full-barrier cmpxchg, so the acquire side is ordered; the race described in the commit arises in the corresponding unlock paths, which use atomic_sub without a release barrier, letting a processor observe the unlock before its critical-section accesses. The consequence is a concurrent writer/reader entering the critical section, violating exclusivity and potentially causing memory leak or hypervisor crash.

description: opmov in libr/asm/p/asm_x86_nz.c in radare2 before 3.1.0 allows attackers to cause a denial of service (buffer over-read) via crafted x86 assembly data, as demonstrated by rasm2.

code_evidence: SEG_REG_PREFIXES is indexed by op->operands[1].regs[0] from parsed assembly; the only guard checks scale[0] == 0, not the register index, so an out-of-range regs[0] reads past the prefix table.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Reading SEG_REG_PREFIXES at an attacker-influenced index beyond its size is a direct out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). The consequence is a read of adjacent memory, not a write past bounds (CWE-787).
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is a missing bounds check on the segment-register index before indexing the SEG_REG_PREFIXES array. Crafted x86 assembly reaching the segment-register branch triggers an out-of-bounds read, causing a crash (DoS) per the fix's modulo-6 clamp.

description: epan/dissectors/packet-nbap.c in the NBAP dissector in Wireshark 1.12.x before 1.12.9 and 2.0.x before 2.0.1 does not validate conversation data, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference and application crash) via a crafted packet.

code_evidence: find_conversation may return NULL; the condition evaluates conversation == NULL first and short-circuits, so the dereference of conversation_get_proto_data(conversation, proto_fp)->channel is guarded against a NULL conversation. However, conversation_get_proto_data can itself return NULL (no proto_fp data registered), and that NULL is dereferenced via ->channel without any check.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function consumes attacker-controlled packet-derived conversation data without validating that the retrieved proto-data pointer is non-NULL before dereferencing it, matching CWE-20's failure to validate required input properties. The crash is a consequence of that missing validation, not the weakness itself.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the code assumes conversation_get_proto_data always returns a valid umts_fp_conversation_info_t pointer when a conversation exists, and dereferences it via ->channel. Trigger: a crafted packet creates/finds a UDP conversation lacking proto_fp conversation data, making the lookup return NULL. Consequence: NULL pointer dereference and application crash (DoS).

description: xorg-x11-server before 1.19.5 was missing length validation in XINERAMA extension allowing malicious X client to cause X server to crash or possibly execute arbitrary code.

code_evidence: Line 4 casts the untrusted request buffer to xPanoramiXGetScreenSizeReq, but the request-length check REQUEST_SIZE_MATCH is only performed at line 10, after line 8 has already read stuff->screen.

Lines 18-19 then index screenInfo.screens[stuff->screen]; the screen bound check at line 8 depends on the request having been length-validated first, which the patch corrects by moving the size check ahead of the screen access.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function consumes client-controlled request data without first validating its required length/size, matching CWE-20's failure to check input properties (specified length) before safe processing. The fix inserts the missing length validation prior to use, confirming improper input validation as the root cause.

.width = screenInfo.screens[stuff->screen]->width,
.height = screenInfo.screens[stuff->screen]->height,

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the request's declared length is not validated before request fields are dereferenced, so a short/malformed XINERAMA request is read out of bounds. Consequence: out-of-bounds read of stuff->screen and subsequent screen table access, crashing the X server or potentially enabling memory disclosure/code execution.

description: Integer overflow in the php_html_entities function in ext/standard/html.c in PHP before 5.5.36 and 5.6.x before 5.6.22 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service or possibly have unspecified other impact by triggering a large output string from the htmlspecialchars function.

code_evidence: Line 7 computes new_size = TRAVERSE_FOR_ENTITIES_EXPAND_SIZE(oldlen), an expansion of the caller-supplied oldlen. Line 13 guards against wraparound only by comparing oldlen > new_size; when that test fails, line 18 allocates new_size bytes and line 20 sets retlen = oldlen. The guard at line 13 is the sole protection against an oversized oldlen reaching the allocation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is an integer overflow/wraparound in a size calculation (TRAVERSE_FOR_ENTITIES_EXPAND_SIZE) that feeds memory allocation, matching CWE-190's scope of size/offset determination in allocation. The incomplete oldlen > new_size check is the flawed overflow detection, not a separate out-of-bounds weakness; the out-of-bounds write is the consequence of the wrapped size.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the expansion macro in line 7 can wrap size_t when oldlen is near SIZE_MAX, producing a small new_size. The line 13 check catches only cases where the wrapped value is smaller than oldlen; a value that wraps to something still >= oldlen (or the boundary case) bypasses it, so line 18 allocates a buffer too small for the oldlen bytes later processed by traverse_for_entities. Trigger: a very large input length. Consequence: undersized allocation leading to heap overflow/memory corruption and DoS.

commit_msg: Improve the client certificate checking logic. Make sure calling `wolfSSL_CTX_mutual_auth` is also checked.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['static void DoCertFatalAlert(WOLFSSL* ssl, int ret)'], 'added_lines': ['void DoCertFatalAlert(WOLFSSL* ssl, int ret)']}
description: In wolfSSL before 5.2.0, a TLS 1.3 server cannot properly enforce a requirement for mutual authentication. A client can simply omit the certificate_verify message from the handshake, and never present a certificate.

code_evidence: When the certificate check returns NO_PEER_CERT, the code distinguishes TLS 1.3 from earlier versions: in TLS 1.3 it sends certificate_required, otherwise handshake_failure. This is the only path that handles a missing peer certificate.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is that mutual-authentication certificate validation is not properly enforced, allowing a client to skip presenting a certificate. That is improper certificate validation (CWE-295); it is not merely a generic handshake error because the missing validation bypasses authentication.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function only maps an already-detected missing-certificate error (NO_PEER_CERT) to an alert; it does not itself enforce that a peer certificate was validated before the handshake proceeds. If the caller never produces NO_PEER_CERT for an omitted certificate_verify message, the TLS 1.3 server continues without mutual authentication.

security fixes

https://hhvm.com/blog/2021/02/25/security-update.html
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    if (ImageInfo->Thumbnail.size - 2 < pos) return 0;']}
description: xbuf_format_converter, used as part of exif_read_data, was appending a terminating null character to the generated string, but was not using its standard append char function. As a result, if the buffer was full, it would result in an out-of-bounds write. This issue affects HHVM versions prior to 4.56.3, all versions between 4.57.0 and 4.80.1, all versions between 4.81.0 and 4.93.1, and versions 4.94.0, 4.95.0, 4.96.0, 4.97.0, 4.98.0.

code_evidence: At line 16 pos advances by length, then data[pos++] is read at line 19 and again at line 26; the added guard at line 33 checks size-2 < pos only after marker is read, but php_jpg_get16(data+pos) at line 33 reads two bytes at pos. The prior bounds check at line 34 uses size - length which can underflow when length exceeds size, and it is evaluated after the two-byte read, so a full/truncated buffer can make data+pos point past the Thumbnail.data allocation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the unchecked offset into Thumbnail.data permits memory access beyond the intended buffer, matching an out-of-bounds write/read condition. It is not merely a logic error; the missing pos+2 <= size constraint is the direct cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the segment-length read at line 33 occurs before any constraint guarantees two bytes remain at pos; the subsequent check at line 34 compares pos against size-length, which can wrap when length > size. Trigger: a crafted JPEG thumbnail with a marker near the buffer end or a bogus segment length. Consequence: out-of-bounds read/write on Thumbnail.data past the allocated image buffer.

description: Gifsicle v1.9.3 was discovered to contain a heap buffer overflow via the ambiguity_error component at /src/clp.c.

code_evidence: When argcmp returns len < 0, the function stores the option index at ambiguous_values[*ambiguous] only if *ambiguous < MAX_AMBIGUOUS_VALUES, but then increments *ambiguous unconditionally on line 25.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The guarded store followed by an unguarded counter increment allows the ambiguity counter to exceed the array capacity, enabling an out-of-bounds write of ambiguous_values in the caller. This is a direct out-of-bounds write (CWE-787), not merely an integer overflow, because the counter drives memory indexing.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The bounds check on line 23 guards only the write on line 24, while the increment on line 25 is unconditional. Once *ambiguous reaches MAX_AMBIGUOUS_VALUES, further ambiguous matches keep increasing the counter without writing, leaving the counter desynchronized from the array; the caller's later use of the over-counted value can index ambiguous_values out of bounds and write past the heap buffer.

commit_msg:
x86/shadow: restore dropped check in sh_unshadow_for_p2m_change()

As a result of 241702e064604dbb3e0d9b731aa8f45be448243b the
mfn_valid() check in sh_unshadow_for_p2m_change() was lost.  That
allows sh_remove_shadows() to be called with gfns that have no backing
page, causing an ASSERT to trigger in debug builds or dereferencing an
arbitrary pointer partially under guest control in non-debug builds:

RIP:    e008:[<ffff82d0402dcf2c>] sh_remove_shadows+0x19f/0x722
RFLAGS: 0000000000010246   CONTEXT: hypervisor (d0v2)
[...]
Xen call trace:
   [<ffff82d0402dcf2c>] R sh_remove_shadows+0x19f/0x722
   [<ffff82d0402e28f4>] F arch/x86/mm/shadow/hvm.c#sh_unshadow_for_p2m_change+0xab/0x2b7
   [<ffff82d040311931>] F arch/x86/mm/p2m-pt.c#write_p2m_entry+0x19b/0x4d3
   [<ffff82d0403131b2>] F arch/x86/mm/p2m-pt.c#p2m_pt_set_entry+0x67b/0xa8e
   [<ffff82d040302c92>] F p2m_set_entry+0xcc/0x149
   [<ffff82d040305a50>] F unmap_mmio_regions+0x17b/0x2c9
   [<ffff82d040241e5e>] F do_domctl+0x11f3/0x195e
   [<ffff82d0402c7e10>] F hvm_hypercall+0x5b1/0xa2d
   [<ffff82d0402adc72>] F vmx_vmexit_handler+0x130f/0x1cd5
   [<ffff82d040203602>] F vmx_asm_vmexit_handler+0xf2/0x210

****************************************
Panic on CPU 1:
Assertion 'mfn_valid(gmfn)' failed at arch/x86/mm/shadow/common.c:2203
****************************************

Fix this by restoring the mfn_valid() check in
sh_unshadow_for_p2m_change(), unifying it with the rest of the checks
that are done at the start of the function.

This is XSA-430 / CVE-2022-42335

Fixes: 241702e064 ('x86/shadow: slightly consolidate sh_unshadow_for_p2m_change() (part II)')
Signed-off-by: Roger Pau Monné <roger.pau@citrix.com>
Reviewed-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>

+++ func_after

-         (!p2m_is_valid(p2mt) && !p2m_is_grant(p2mt)) )

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['         (!p2m_is_valid(p2mt) && !p2m_is_grant(p2mt)) )'], 'added_lines': ['         (!p2m_is_valid(p2mt) && !p2m_is_grant(p2mt)) ||', '         !mfn_valid(omfn) )']}
description: x86 shadow paging arbitrary pointer dereference In environments where host assisted address translation is necessary but Hardware Assisted Paging (HAP) is unavailable, Xen will run guests in so called shadow mode. Due to too lax a check in one of the hypervisor routines used for shadow page handling it is possible for a guest with a PCI device passed through to cause the hypervisor to access an arbitrary pointer partially under guest control.

code_evidence: omfn is extracted from the old PTE via l1e_get_mfn(old); the guard at lines 11-13 only checks _PAGE_PRESENT and p2m validity, so a present entry whose mfn is not backed by a page passes through.
sh_remove_all_shadows_and_parents(d, omfn) and sh_remove_all_mappings(d, omfn, ...) are then invoked with this unvalidated omfn.
For level 2, when oflags lacks _PAGE_PSE, map_domain_page(omfn) dereferences the unvalidated mfn directly.
Inside the loop, opte[i] is re-read and omfn re-derived from the guest-controlled PTE, then passed to sh_remove_all_shadows_and_parents and sh_remove_all_mappings without an mfn_valid check.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The root cause is use of an unvalidated pointer/MFN that may not reference a valid page, leading to dereference of an invalid address (NULL or arbitrary), matching CWE-476's NULL/invalid pointer dereference. It is distinct from a simple integer or bounds issue because the failure is dereferencing a pointer that was assumed valid.

evidence_lines.code:
sh_remove_all_shadows_and_parents(d, omfn);
if ( sh_remove_all_mappings(d, omfn, _gfn(gfn)) )

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function trusts the MFN encoded in a guest-controlled p2m entry after only checking presence and p2m type; the missing mfn_valid(omfn) constraint lets an invalid/absent backing page reach sh_remove_shadows and map_domain_page. Triggered by a p2m change on a present-but-invalid entry, causing an ASSERT in debug builds or dereference of an arbitrary pointer partially under guest control in non-debug builds.

description: res_query in libresolv in glibc before 2.25 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference and process crash).

code_evidence: Line 28 issues a query with QTYPE T_UNSPEC (the special internal query type) via __libc_res_nsearch, passing host_buffer.buf->buf and the ans2p/nans2p/resplen2 outputs.

On success (n >= 0) lines 33-35 pass the returned answer to gaih_getanswer together with ans2p and resplen2; the T_UNSPEC query can produce a second answer buffer (ans2p) that is NULL, which gaih_getanswer dereferences.

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the caller requests the special T_UNSPEC QTYPE, so __libc_res_nsearch may return answers where the secondary buffer ans2p is NULL while resplen2 is nonzero. Trigger: a remote DNS response to such a query. Consequence: gaih_getanswer dereferences ans2p, causing a NULL pointer dereference and process crash (DoS).
