diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['static unsigned int XBMInteger(Image *image,short int *hex_digits)', '      return(0);', '      return(0);', '  return(value);'], 'added_lines': ['static int XBMInteger(Image *image,short int *hex_digits)', '      return(-1);', '      return(-1);', '  return((int) value);']}
description: In coders/xbm.c in ImageMagick 7.0.6-1 Q16, a DoS in ReadXBMImage() due to lack of an EOF (End of File) check might cause huge CPU consumption. When a crafted XBM file, which claims large rows and columns fields in the header but does not contain sufficient backing data, is provided, the loop over the rows would consume huge CPU resources, since there is no EOF check inside the loop.

code_evidence: The leading whitespace-skip do/while loop reads bytes via ReadBlobByte and exits only on a non-whitespace byte; on EOF it returns 0 (treated as a valid value), so the caller cannot distinguish EOF from a parsed zero.

The hex-digit accumulation do/while loop is bounded only by INT_MAX overflow checks and by hex_digits[c] >= 0; EOF returns 0 rather than signaling failure, and no iteration/EOF counter limits the loop.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-834 fits because the parsing loops are not bounded by an EOF/iteration limit and the EOF-as-zero return removes the constraint that would stop caller iteration, enabling excessive iteration and CPU consumption.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: XBMInteger returns 0 on EOF instead of an error sentinel, so callers cannot detect truncated input and may continue iterating over claimed large row/column dimensions. Trigger: a crafted XBM header with large dimensions but insufficient backing data. Supported consequence: lack of EOF propagation lets the row loop run with excessive CPU consumption (DoS).

Fix the bounds checking for the NFSv3 WRITE procedure to check whether the
length of the opaque data being written is present in the captured data,
not just whether the byte count is present in the captured data.
furthest forward in the packet, not the item before it.  (This also lets

commit_msg:
staging/android/ion : fix a race condition in the ion driver

There is a use-after-free problem in the ion driver.
This is caused by a race condition in the ion_ioctl()
function.

A handle has ref count of 1 and two tasks on different
cpus calls ION_IOC_FREE simultaneously.

cpu 0                                   cpu 1
-------------------------------------------------------
ion_handle_get_by_id()
(ref == 2)
                            ion_handle_get_by_id()
                            (ref == 3)

ion_free()
(ref == 2)

ion_handle_put()
(ref == 1)

                            ion_free()
                            (ref == 0 so ion_handle_destroy() is
                            called
                            and the handle is freed.)

                            ion_handle_put() is called and it
                            decreases the slub's next free pointer

The problem is detected as an unaligned access in the
spin lock functions since it uses load exclusive
 instruction. In some cases it corrupts the slub's
free pointer which causes a mis-aligned access to the
next free pointer.(kmalloc returns a pointer like
ffffc0745b4580aa). And it causes lots of other
hard-to-debug problems.

This symptom is caused since the first member in the
ion_handle structure is the reference count and the
ion driver decrements the reference after it has been
freed.

To fix this problem client->lock mutex is extended
to protect all the codes that uses the handle.

Signed-off-by: Eun Taik Lee <eun.taik.lee@samsung.com>
Reviewed-by: Laura Abbott <labbott@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tbool valid_handle;', '', '\tvalid_handle = ion_handle_validate(client, handle);', '', '\tif (!valid_handle) {', '\t\tWARN(1, "%s: invalid handle passed to free.\\n", __func__);', '\t\tmutex_unlock(&client->lock);', '\t\treturn;', '\t}', '\tion_handle_put(handle);'], 'added_lines': ['\tion_free_nolock(client, handle);']}
description: Race condition in the ion_ioctl function in drivers/staging/android/ion/ion.c in the Linux kernel before 4.6 allows local users to gain privileges or cause a denial of service (use-after-free) by calling ION_IOC_FREE on two CPUs at the same time.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The ion_free function only validates and decrements a handle reference count; it contains no permission, privilege, or access-control logic, so CWE-264 (a category for access-control weaknesses) is not directly supported by this code.

This also disabled the case of mixed x/ymin with tiles, the code
handles these cases inconsistent for the 2 coordinate axis and is
unlikely working correctly.

Fixes crash
Fixes: poc1.exr, poc2.exr

Found-by: Yaoguang Chen of Aliapy unLimit Security Team
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
(cherry picked from commit 01aee8148d4fa439cce678a11f5110656c98de1f)
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    uint32_t data_size, line, col = 0;', '    uint32_t tileX, tileY, tileLevelX, tileLevelY;'], 'added_lines': ['    uint32_t data_size;', '    uint64_t line, col = 0;', '    uint64_t tileX, tileY, tileLevelX, tileLevelY;', '        if (s->xmin || s->ymin) {', '            avpriv_report_missing_feature(s->avctx, "Tiles with xmin/ymin");', '            return AVERROR_PATCHWELCOME;', '        }', '', '', '        if (line < s->ymin || line > s->ymax ||', '            col  < s->xmin || col  > s->xmax)', '            return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;']}
description: Heap-based buffer overflow in the decode_block function in libavcodec/exr.c in FFmpeg before 3.1.3 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (application crash) via vectors involving tile positions.

code_evidence: Tile branch computes line = tile_attr.ySize * tileY and col = tile_attr.xSize * tileX directly from attacker-controlled tile coordinates read at lines 26-27, then derives td->ysize/td->xsize via FFMIN without validating line/col against the image window.

Line 110 forms the output pointer as p->data[0] + line * p->linesize[0] + col * nb_components * 2 and the loop writes td->xsize pixels per row; oversized tileY/tileX push this pointer past the allocated frame buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs writes through a pointer derived from unchecked tile positions, producing an out-of-bounds write on a heap buffer, which matches CWE-119's improper restriction of operations within a memory buffer's bounds. The fix adds line/col range checks confirming the missing boundary constraint is the defect.

evidence_lines.code: ptr = p->data[0] + line * p->linesize[0] + (col * s->desc->nb_components * 2);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: tile coordinates are used to compute the destination offset without bounds checks against ymax/xmax. A crafted EXR with large tileY/tileX makes line/col exceed the frame, so the write loop at lines 111-166 writes outside the picture buffer, causing heap corruption or crash.

commit_msg:
Invalid generator were not removed from list

fluid_list_remove() should receive the beginning of a list, so it can adjust the predecessor of the element to be removed. Otherwise the element would remain in the list, which in this case led to a use-after-free afterwards.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    fluid_list_t *p, *p2, *p3, *dup, **hz = NULL;', '        p2 = ((SFPreset *)(p->data))->zone;', '                    *hz = fluid_list_remove(*hz, p2->data);', '                    delete_zone((SFZone *)fluid_list_get(p2));'], 'added_lines': ['    fluid_list_t *p, *p2, *p3, *dup, **hz = NULL, *start_of_zone_list;', '        start_of_zone_list = p2 = ((SFPreset *)(p->data))->zone;', '                    SFZone * pzone = fluid_list_get(p2);', '                    *hz = fluid_list_remove(start_of_zone_list, pzone);', '                    delete_zone(pzone);']}
description: fluidsynth is a software synthesizer based on the SoundFont 2 specifications. A use after free violation was discovered in fluidsynth, that can be triggered when loading an invalid SoundFont file.

code_evidence: hz is set to &p2, the head of the preset's zone list [17]. When a later zone is found to be an invalid global zone, the code calls fluid_list_remove(*hz, p2->data) [138] and then delete_zone((SFZone *)fluid_list_get(p2)) [139]. Because fluid_list_remove is passed *hz (a pointer advanced by SLADVREM at [129]) rather than the list head, it may fail to unlink p2; the zone is freed anyway. The loop then advances p2 = fluid_list_next(p2) [153], dereferencing the freed node.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function frees a zone via delete_zone while the list still references it, then continues iterating through that list, reusing the freed element. This is directly a use-after-free (CWE-416), not merely a memory leak or double free, since the freed allocation is referenced afterward by p2.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the invalid global zone is freed without being reliably removed from the zone list, because the removal call receives a non-head list pointer. Trigger: an invalid SoundFont whose global zone is not first in the list. Consequence: traversal at [153] follows and dereferences freed memory, a use-after-free that can corrupt memory or crash.

commit_msg:
extractor: Do not allow symlink in parents

Currently, it is still possible that some files are extracted outside of
the destination dir in case of malicious archives. The checks from commit
adb067e6 can be still bypassed in certain cases. See GNOME/file-roller#108
for more details. After some investigation, I am convinced that it would be
best to	simply disallow symlinks in parents. For example, `tar` fails to
extract such files with the `ENOTDIR` error. Let's do the same here.

Fixes: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/gnome-autoar/-/issues/12
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['static gboolean', 'autoar_extractor_check_file_conflict (GFile  *file,', '  /* If there is no file with the given name, there will be no conflict */', '  if (file_type == G_FILE_TYPE_UNKNOWN) {', '    return FALSE;', '  /* It is not problem if the directory already exists */', '  if (file_type == G_FILE_TYPE_DIRECTORY &&', '      extracted_filetype == AE_IFDIR) {', '    return FALSE;', '  return TRUE;'], 'added_lines': ['static GFile *', 'autoar_extractor_check_file_conflict (AutoarExtractor *self,', '                                      GFile  *file,', '  g_autoptr (GFile) parent = NULL;', '', '  /* It is a conflict if the file already exists with an exception for already', '   * existing directories.', '   */', '  if (file_type != G_FILE_TYPE_UNKNOWN &&', '      (file_type != G_FILE_TYPE_DIRECTORY ||', '       extracted_filetype != AE_IFDIR)) {', '    return g_object_ref (file);', '  if ((self->new_prefix && g_file_equal (self->new_prefix, file)) ||', '      (!self->new_prefix && g_file_equal (self->destination_dir, file))) {', '    return NULL;', '  /* Check also parents for conflict to be sure it is directory. */', '  parent = g_file_get_parent (file);', '  return autoar_extractor_check_file_conflict (self, parent, AE_IFDIR);']}
description: autoar-extractor.c in GNOME gnome-autoar before 0.3.1, as used by GNOME Shell, Nautilus, and other software, allows Directory Traversal during extraction because it lacks a check of whether a file's parent is a symlink in certain complex situations. NOTE: this issue exists because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2020-36241.

code_evidence: The function queries the target file's type with G_FILE_QUERY_INFO_NOFOLLOW_SYMLINKS, so a symlink at the final path component is not resolved and its type is not G_FILE_TYPE_DIRECTORY.
Only the final file is examined; when it is a directory matching an extracted directory the function returns FALSE (no conflict) without inspecting any parent component.
Otherwise it returns TRUE, treating the path as a plain conflict, but never verifies whether a parent directory in the path is actually a symlink pointing outside the destination.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The code performs file access based on a path without preventing a component (parent directory) from resolving through a symlink to an unintended location, which is improper link resolution before file access. This is distinct from pure path traversal because the redirection is achieved via a symlink component rather than raw '..' sequences.

evidence_lines.code: return TRUE;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The conflict check inspects only the leaf path and does not resolve or reject symlinked parent directories. A malicious archive can first create a symlink directory and then place a file beneath it; because the parent is not validated, the extracted path follows the link and writes outside the intended destination. Root cause is missing parent-link validation; consequence is directory traversal and out-of-destination file write.

commit_msg:
vt_kdsetmode: extend console locking

As per the long-suffering comment.

Reported-by: Minh Yuan <yuanmingbuaa@gmail.com>
Cc: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
Cc: Jiri Slaby <jirislaby@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t/* FIXME: this needs the console lock extending */', '\tconsole_lock();', '\tconsole_unlock();'], 'added_lines': []}
description: A race problem was seen in the vt_k_ioctl in drivers/tty/vt/vt_ioctl.c in the Linux kernel, which may cause an out of bounds read in vt as the write access to vc_mode is not protected by lock-in vt_ioctl (KDSETMDE). The highest threat from this vulnerability is to data confidentiality.

code_evidence: vt_kdsetmode reads vc->vc_mode at line 15 and writes it at line 17 before acquiring console_lock(), which is only taken at line 20 after the fg_console check and mode update. The lock therefore does not cover the check-then-set of vc_mode, leaving the mode transition unprotected.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the race permits vc_mode to become inconsistent with the console's actual state, and the supported consequence is an out-of-bounds read that leaks memory. The defect here is the missing lock around the mode transition; the out-of-bounds read is its downstream effect, not a separate buffer-handling flaw.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: vc->vc_mode is read and written outside the console lock, so a concurrent KDSETMODE path can change the mode between the check at line 15 and the blank/unblank decision at line 21. Trigger: racing ioctls on the console. Supported consequence: inconsistent vc_mode and console state, which the referenced report links to an out-of-bounds read in vt, affecting confidentiality.

commit_msg: Guard binary expressions from too much recursion.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tSAVEREC();', '\tINCREC();', '\tPOPREC();']}
description: jsparse.c in Artifex MuJS through 1.0.2 does not properly maintain the AST depth for binary expressions, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (excessive recursion) via a crafted file.

code_evidence: The loop repeatedly consumes '*'/'/'/'%' operators and calls unary(J) for each right operand, building a left-associative binary AST via EXP2 and goto loop. No depth counter or recursion bound is checked in this function before recursing into unary(J) and re-entering the loop.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-674 fits because the parser fails to control recursion depth during binary-expression parsing, causing resource exhaustion. This is uncontrolled recursion, not merely a stack-buffer overflow (CWE-121), since the missing constraint is a depth check rather than a bounds check on a fixed buffer.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: multiplicative parsing lacks any recursion-depth accounting, so a crafted input with a long chain of multiplicative operators drives repeated unary(J) recursion without limit. Trigger: a file containing many consecutive operators. Supported consequence: excessive stack consumption leading to denial of service (crash/abort).

commit_msg:
MDEV-29644 a potential bug of null pointer dereference in spider_db_mbase::print_warnings()

The function spider_db_mbase::print_warnings() can potentially result
in a null pointer dereference.

Remove the null pointer dereference by cleaning up the function.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        print_warnings(l_time);'], 'added_lines': ['        fetch_and_print_warnings(l_time);']}
description: MariaDB Server before 10.3.34 thru 10.9.3 is vulnerable to Denial of Service. It is possible for function spider_db_mbase::print_warnings to dereference a null pointer.

code_evidence: When logging is enabled and warning_count > 0, the code calls print_warnings(l_time) — the call the patch replaces with fetch_and_print_warnings.
l_time is produced by localtime_r(&cur_time, &lt), which returns NULL on failure; that return value is stored without any NULL check.
l_time is later dereferenced unconditionally in the fprintf arguments (l_time->tm_year, tm_mon, tm_mday, tm_hour, tm_min, tm_sec).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function stores a potentially NULL pointer from localtime_r and dereferences it without a check, which is exactly CWE-476. This is a missing NULL check on a returned pointer, not a buffer or bounds issue, so CWE-476 is the appropriate base-level label.

evidence_lines.code:
if (spider_param_log_result_errors() >= 3)
print_warnings(l_time);

fprintf(stderr, "%04d%02d%02d %02d:%02d:%02d [WARN SPIDER RESULT] "
"from [%s] %ld to %ld:  "
"affected_rows: %llu  id: %llu  status: %u  warning_count: %u\n",
l_time->tm_year + 1900, l_time->tm_mon + 1, l_time->tm_mday,
l_time->tm_hour, l_time->tm_min, l_time->tm_sec,
conn->tgt_host, (ulong) db_conn->thread_id, (ulong) thd->thread_id,
db_conn->affected_rows, db_conn->insert_id,
db_conn->server_status, db_conn->warning_count);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the result of localtime_r is assigned to l_time and used without validating it against NULL. Trigger: if localtime_r fails (returning NULL), the subsequent fprintf dereferences l_time->tm_year and related fields. Supported consequence: a NULL pointer dereference, causing the server process to crash (denial of service).

commit_msg:
Fix double-free in gdImageWebPtr()

The issue is that gdImageWebpCtx() (which is called by gdImageWebpPtr() and
the other WebP output functions to do the real work) does not return whether
it succeeded or failed, so this is not checked in gdImageWebpPtr() and the
function wrongly assumes everything is okay, which is not, in this case,
because there is a size limitation for WebP, namely that the width and
height must by less than 16383.

We can't change the signature of gdImageWebpCtx() for API compatibility
reasons, so we introduce the static helper _gdImageWebpCtx() which returns
success respective failure, so gdImageWebpPtr() and gdImageWebpPtrEx() can
check the return value. We leave it solely to libwebp for now to report
warnings regarding the failing write.

This issue had been reported by Ibrahim El-Sayed to security@libgd.org.

CVE-2016-6912
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tgdImageWebpCtx(im, out, quality);', '\trv = gdDPExtractData(out, size);'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (_gdImageWebpCtx(im, out, quality)) {', '        rv = NULL;', '    } else {', '        rv = gdDPExtractData(out, size);', '    }']}
description: Double free vulnerability in the gdImageWebPtr function in the GD Graphics Library (aka libgd) before 2.2.4 allows remote attackers to have unspecified impact via large width and height values.

code_evidence: Line 8 calls gdImageWebpCtx() but ignores its return value, so a failed WebP encode is not detected. Line 9 unconditionally invokes gdDPExtractData() on the dynamic context regardless of whether the encode succeeded, and line 10 then frees the same out context. Because the failure path is unchecked, the subsequent extraction and free operate on state that may already have been released.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked encoding failure causes the same dynamic context to be freed again after the failed operation, matching CWE-415's double free of one address. This is distinct from a mere null-pointer dereference because the same context is released twice.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the missing check on gdImageWebpCtx() return value means the function assumes success and proceeds to extract data and free the dynamic context. Trigger: oversized width/height (>=16383) causes WebP encoding to fail. Supported consequence: the unchecked failure path leads to double-free of the context, enabling memory corruption.

commit_msg:
Fix addition overflows in range checks in LoaderTiff::getData

Several checks for extracted values performed no overflow checks on the
addition. They can be tricked into passing, albeit the individual summands are
too large.
=> use Safe::add() which now aborts when an overflow occurs
This fixes #366
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['                    if (offset + size <= static_cast<uint32_t>(io.size()))', '                        enforce(idxBuf + size < size_, kerCorruptedMetadata);', '                        if (size!=0 && offset + size <= static_cast<uint32_t>(io.size()))'], 'added_lines': ['                    if (Safe::add(offset, size) <= static_cast<uint32_t>(io.size()))', '                        enforce(Safe::add(idxBuf, size) < size_, kerCorruptedMetadata);', '                        if (size!=0 && Safe::add(offset, size) <= static_cast<uint32_t>(io.size()))']}
description: Exiv2 0.26 has integer overflows in LoaderTiff::getData() in preview.cpp, leading to an out-of-bounds read in Exiv2::ValueType::setDataArea in value.hpp.

code_evidence: Lines 24-26 read attacker-controlled offset/size from TIFF preview tags and check `offset + size <= io.size()` before `setDataArea(base + offset, size)`; the addition can wrap in uint32_t, so an oversized offset passes the bound check and yields an out-of-range pointer.

Lines 33-37 similarly compute `idxBuf + size < size_` and `offset + size <= io.size()` before `memcpy(&buf.pData_[idxBuf], base + offset, size)`; wraparound lets the check pass while the true sum exceeds the buffer, leading to out-of-bounds read/copy.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs integer additions (offset+size, idxBuf+size) whose wraparound defeats the size validation, exactly the CWE-190 pattern of arithmetic overflow subverting a subsequent memory operation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: bound checks use unchecked 32-bit additions of offset/size values derived from the file, which can wrap to a small value. Trigger: crafted TIFF offset/size fields whose sum overflows. Consequence: checks pass incorrectly, producing out-of-bounds read via setDataArea/memcpy.

commit_msg:
Fixed recursive async function calls.

Previously, PromiseCapability record was stored (function->context)
directly in function object during a function invocation.  This is
not correct, because PromiseCapability record should be linked to
current execution context.  As a result, function->context is
overwritten with consecutive recursive calls which results in
use-after-free.

This closes #451 issue on Github.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    frame->function->context = capability;', '', '    ret = njs_function_lambda_call(vm);'], 'added_lines': ['    ret = njs_function_lambda_call(vm, capability, NULL);']}
description: njs through 0.7.0, used in NGINX, was discovered to contain a heap use-after-free in njs_await_fulfilled.

code_evidence: The function obtains the current native frame and stores the newly created PromiseCapability into the per-function field frame->function->context, then invokes the lambda. Because context is attached to the function object rather than the execution context, a recursive or re-entrant call to the same async function overwrites this field with a newer capability while earlier frames still reference the previous one.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This is CWE-416: a stored pointer to a capability object is reused after that object has been freed due to overwriting across recursive invocations. It is not merely a stale-logic bug, since the stale reference is dereferenced, matching use-after-free rather than a generic resource leak.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the promise capability is linked to the shared function object instead of the active invocation/execution context. Trigger: recursive async calls to the same function overwrite function->context, leaving earlier frames with a stale capability pointer whose lifetime has ended; subsequent use (resolve/reject or await fulfillment) dereferences freed memory, supporting use-after-free consequences such as memory corruption or crash.

commit_msg:
Adding Error Check for f_code Parameters

In MPEG1, the valid range for the forward and backward f_code parameters
is [1, 7]. Adding a check to enforce this. Without the check, the value
could be 0. We read (f_code - 1) bits from the stream and reading a
negative number of bits from the stream is undefined.

Bug: 64550583
Test: monitored temp ALOGD() output
Change-Id: Ia452cd43a28e9d566401f515947164635361782f
(cherry picked from commit 71d734b83d72e8a59f73f1230982da97615d2689)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['        if (ps_dec->u2_forw_f_code < 1 || ps_dec->u2_forw_f_code > 7 ||', '                        ps_dec->u2_back_f_code < 1 || ps_dec->u2_back_f_code > 7)', '        {', '            return IMPEG2D_UNKNOWN_ERROR;', '        }']}
description: An information disclosure vulnerability in the Android media framework (libmpeg2). Product: Android. Versions: 7.0, 7.1.1, 7.1.2, 8.0, 8.1. Android ID: A-64550583.

code_evidence: Lines 17 and 22 read 3-bit f_code fields from the stream into u2_forw_f_code and u2_back_f_code, so the value 0 is representable.
Lines 24-28 copy those fields into au2_f_code when the stream is MPEG1 without validating the [1,7] range before later use.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-200 fits because the missing f_code range check allows a malformed stream to drive an undefined negative-bit read, resulting in exposure of sensitive in-memory data to an unauthorized observer. The root cause is the absent input constraint, not an explicit leak, but the supported impact is confidentiality loss via the undefined read.

evidence_lines.code:
ps_dec->u2_forw_f_code          = impeg2d_bit_stream_get(ps_stream,3);
ps_dec->u2_back_f_code          = impeg2d_bit_stream_get(ps_stream,3);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The f_code parameters extracted from the picture header are stored unchecked for MPEG1 streams. A crafted stream can supply f_code = 0, and downstream motion-vector parsing reads (f_code - 1) bits, i.e. a negative count, producing undefined stream behavior. The supported consequence is an out-of-bounds or undefined read that may expose adjacent decoder memory (information disclosure).

commit_msg:
v2: Protect against integer overflow (Alan Coopersmith)

Reviewed-by: Alan Coopersmith <alan.coopersmith@oracle.com>
Reviewed-by: Jeremy Huddleston Sequoia <jeremyhu@apple.com>
Reviewed-by: Julien Cristau <jcristau@debian.org>
Signed-off-by: Nathan Kidd <nkidd@opentext.com>
Signed-off-by: Julien Cristau <jcristau@debian.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    if (stuff->n > UINT32_MAX / sizeof(CARD32))', '        return BadLength;', '    REQUEST_FIXED_SIZE(xDbeGetVisualInfoReq, stuff->n * sizeof(CARD32));']}
description: xorg-x11-server before 1.19.5 was vulnerable to integer overflow in ProcDbeGetVisualInfo function allowing malicious X client to cause X server to crash or possibly execute arbitrary code.

code_evidence: The request length check REQUEST_AT_LEAST_SIZE only validates the fixed header; stuff->n (client-controlled CARD32) is then used to size the drawable array at line 18 and to index drawables[i] at line 23.
The count of visuals is derived from stuff->n at line 31, and length accumulates pScrVisInfo[i].count * sizeof(xDbeVisInfo) at line 49 in a signed int, which can wrap.
The patch adds a guard that stuff->n > UINT32_MAX / sizeof(CARD32) must be rejected and a REQUEST_FIXED_SIZE check before the request array is read.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The root cause is an unchecked multiplication of a client-controlled count (stuff->n) by an element size, producing an integer overflow/wraparound, matching CWE-190. The fix enforces UINT32_MAX / sizeof(CARD32), confirming the missing arithmetic bound rather than a simple length mismatch.

evidence_lines.code:
length += sizeof(CARD32);
length += pScrVisInfo[i].count * sizeof(xDbeVisInfo);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function trusts the client-supplied stuff->n without first bounding it against the request length or against the size of CARD32. The new guard shows the intended constraint: stuff->n * sizeof(CARD32) must not overflow before REQUEST_FIXED_SIZE computes the needed payload. Without it, the length calculation and subsequent reads can wrap, letting a malicious X client trigger a crash or memory corruption.

commit_msg: fix runtime error: applying zero offset to null pointer
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    const char *ep = s + slen;', '    const char *cp = s;'], 'added_lines': ['        const char *ep = s + slen;', '        const char *cp = s;']}
description: A null pointer dereference issue was found in Libtiff's tif_dir.c file. This issue may allow an attacker to pass a crafted TIFF image file to the tiffcp utility which triggers a runtime error that causes undefined behavior. This will result in an application crash, eventually leading to a denial of service.

code_evidence: Lines 4-5 compute ep = s + slen and cp = s before any check on s, so when s is NULL and slen is zero or nonzero the pointer arithmetic on a null base is performed unconditionally.

The slen > 0 guard at lines 6-7 was moved to enclose the pointer setup and the dereference loop, so the dereference of *cp at line 10 only executes when slen > 0; the null-pointer offset at lines 4-5 still occurs before that guard.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits because the function performs pointer arithmetic on a pointer expected to be valid but NULL (s + slen), yielding undefined behavior and a crash. This is a null-pointer dereference/offset issue rather than an out-of-bounds read, since the defect stems from the null base pointer.

evidence_lines.code:
const char *ep = s + slen;
const char *cp = s;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: pointer arithmetic on the caller-supplied buffer pointer s is performed before validating that s is non-NULL. Trigger: a crafted TIFF whose InkNames field yields a NULL buffer pointer calls countInkNamesString, causing undefined behavior at the s + slen offset. Supported consequence: application crash, i.e., denial of service.

commit_msg:
net: rose: fix UAF bugs caused by timer handler

There are UAF bugs in rose_heartbeat_expiry(), rose_timer_expiry()
and rose_idletimer_expiry(). The root cause is that del_timer()
could not stop the timer handler that is running and the refcount
of sock is not managed properly.

One of the UAF bugs is shown below:

    (thread 1)          |        (thread 2)
                        |  rose_bind
                        |  rose_connect
                        |    rose_start_heartbeat
rose_release            |    (wait a time)
  case ROSE_STATE_0     |
  rose_destroy_socket   |  rose_heartbeat_expiry
    rose_stop_heartbeat |
    sock_put(sk)        |    ...
  sock_put(sk) // FREE  |
                        |    bh_lock_sock(sk) // USE

The sock is deallocated by sock_put() in rose_release() and
then used by bh_lock_sock() in rose_heartbeat_expiry().

Although rose_destroy_socket() calls rose_stop_heartbeat(),
it could not stop the timer that is running.

This patch adds refcount of sock when we use functions
such as rose_start_heartbeat() and so on to start timer,
and decreases the refcount of sock when timer is finished
or deleted by functions such as rose_stop_heartbeat()
and so on. As a result, the UAF bugs could be mitigated.

Signed-off-by: Duoming Zhou <duoming@zju.edu.cn>
Tested-by: Duoming Zhou <duoming@zju.edu.cn>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220629002640.5693-1-duoming@zju.edu.cn
Signed-off-by: Paolo Abeni <pabeni@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tdel_timer(&rose->timer);', '\tadd_timer(&rose->timer);'], 'added_lines': ['\tsk_stop_timer(sk, &rose->timer);', '\tsk_reset_timer(sk, &rose->timer, rose->timer.expires);']}
description: There are use-after-free vulnerabilities caused by timer handler in net/rose/rose_timer.c of linux that allow attackers to crash linux kernel without any privileges.

code_evidence: Line 4 calls del_timer(&rose->timer), which stops a pending timer but does not prevent an already-running rose_timer_expiry handler from executing; it also does not hold a reference on the owning sock.
Line 7 calls add_timer(&rose->timer) without taking a sock reference, so the timer can fire and run rose_timer_expiry after rose_release() has dropped the final reference and freed the sock.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function arms a timer whose handler later accesses a sock that may already be deallocated, directly enabling reuse of freed memory. This is CWE-416 rather than a simple race: the defect is the missing lifetime/refcount constraint that lets the handler touch freed memory.

evidence_lines.code: del_timer(&rose->timer);
add_timer(&rose->timer);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The timer is armed without acquiring a reference to the socket, and del_timer() cannot synchronize with a handler already running. If the socket is released concurrently while the timer fires, rose_timer_expiry dereferences freed sock memory, producing a use-after-free crash.

commit_msg:
Bluetooth: L2CAP: Fix accepting connection request for invalid SPSM

The Bluetooth spec states that the valid range for SPSM is from
0x0001-0x00ff so it is invalid to accept values outside of this range:

  BLUETOOTH CORE SPECIFICATION Version 5.3 | Vol 3, Part A
  page 1059:
  Table 4.15: L2CAP_LE_CREDIT_BASED_CONNECTION_REQ SPSM ranges

CVE: CVE-2022-42896
CC: stable@vger.kernel.org
Reported-by: Tamás Koczka <poprdi@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Luiz Augusto von Dentz <luiz.von.dentz@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Tedd Ho-Jeong An <tedd.an@intel.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\t/* BLUETOOTH CORE SPECIFICATION Version 5.3 | Vol 3, Part A', '\t * page 1059:', '\t *', '\t * Valid range: 0x0001-0x00ff', '\t *', '\t * Table 4.15: L2CAP_LE_CREDIT_BASED_CONNECTION_REQ SPSM ranges', '\t */', '\tif (!psm || __le16_to_cpu(psm) > L2CAP_PSM_LE_DYN_END) {', '\t\tresult = L2CAP_CR_LE_BAD_PSM;', '\t\tgoto response;', '\t}']}
description:
There are use-after-free vulnerabilities in the Linux kernel's net/bluetooth/l2cap_core.c's l2cap_connect and l2cap_le_connect_req functions which may allow code execution and leaking kernel memory (respectively) remotely via Bluetooth. A remote attacker could execute code leaking kernel memory via Bluetooth if within proximity of the victim.

We recommend upgrading past commit   https://www.google.com/url  https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/711f8c3fb3db61897080468586b970c87c61d9e4 https://www.google.com/url

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The shown function only validates SPSM range and channel/SCID parameters; it contains no free or post-free reuse of memory, so CWE-416 is not directly supported by this code.

commit_msg:
packet: in packet_do_bind, test fanout with bind_lock held

Once a socket has po->fanout set, it remains a member of the group
until it is destroyed. The prot_hook must be constant and identical
across sockets in the group.

If fanout_add races with packet_do_bind between the test of po->fanout
and taking the lock, the bind call may make type or dev inconsistent
with that of the fanout group.

Hold po->bind_lock when testing po->fanout to avoid this race.

I had to introduce artificial delay (local_bh_enable) to actually
observe the race.

Fixes: dc99f600698d ("packet: Add fanout support.")
Signed-off-by: Willem de Bruijn <willemb@google.com>
Reviewed-by: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (po->fanout)', '\t\treturn -EINVAL;', ''], 'added_lines': ['', '\tif (po->fanout) {', '\t\tret = -EINVAL;', '\t\tgoto out_unlock;', '\t}']}
description: net/packet/af_packet.c in the Linux kernel before 4.13.6 allows local users to gain privileges via crafted system calls that trigger mishandling of packet_fanout data structures, because of a race condition (involving fanout_add and packet_do_bind) that leads to a use-after-free, a different vulnerability than CVE-2017-6346.

code_evidence: Lines 11-12 test po->fanout and return -EINVAL before any lock is acquired.
Lines 13-15 acquire lock_sock, spin_lock(&po->bind_lock) and rcu_read_lock only after the fanout check, so the check is outside the critical section.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This is a classic time-of-check-to-time-of-use race on a shared resource lacking exclusive access: the concurrent sequence fanout_add modifies po->fanout in the unchecked window. CWE-362 directly describes such improper synchronization; the inconsistency is the supported consequence, not the cause.

evidence_lines.code:
if (po->fanout)
return -EINVAL;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The fanout membership test reads the shared po->fanout field without holding po->bind_lock. A concurrent fanout_add can set po->fanout between the test at line 11 and the locking at lines 13-14, so packet_do_bind proceeds to change type/dev while the socket is already a fanout member, leaving group state inconsistent with the bind.

commit_msg:
Fixed typo while calculating module path length.

The issue was introduced in 77c398f26d7e (not released yet).
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        length = dir->length;'], 'added_lines': ['        length += dir->length;']}
description: Nginx NJS v0.7.3 was discovered to contain a stack overflow in the function njs_default_module_loader at /src/njs/src/njs_module.c. NOTE: multiple third parties dispute this report, e.g., the behavior is only found in unreleased development code that was not part of the 0.7.2, 0.7.3, or 0.7.4 release

code_evidence: length is initialized to info->name.length, but when dir is non-NULL it is overwritten with dir->length instead of accumulated, losing the module-name length.
trail and the optional slash increment only account for the directory portion, so length no longer reflects the total path.
The bound check compares this understated length against NJS_MAX_PATH, allowing a total path larger than the buffer to pass.
The copy writes dir->start, an optional '/', and info->name.start into src[NJS_MAX_PATH + 1] using the unchecked name length, followed by a NUL terminator.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because an incorrect length calculation bypasses the NJS_MAX_PATH guard and lets writes through njs_cpymem (and the NUL store) exceed the fixed src buffer. This is a direct out-of-bounds write, not merely an over-read or integer overflow; the integer miscalculation is the cause, and the buffer overrun is the supported consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: length is assigned dir->length rather than adding it to info->name.length, so the size check at line 20 underestimates the bytes copied at lines 25 and 30. Trigger: a directory path plus a long module name whose combined length exceeds NJS_MAX_PATH while dir->length alone does not. Consequence: njs_cpymem writes past src and the terminator at line 31 also lands out of bounds, corrupting the stack.

commit_msg:
floppy: fix div-by-zero in setup_format_params

This fixes a divide by zero error in the setup_format_params function of
the floppy driver.

Two consecutive ioctls can trigger the bug: The first one should set the
drive geometry with such .sect and .rate values for the F_SECT_PER_TRACK
to become zero.  Next, the floppy format operation should be called.

A floppy disk is not required to be inserted.  An unprivileged user
could trigger the bug if the device is accessible.

The patch checks F_SECT_PER_TRACK for a non-zero value in the
set_geometry function.  The proper check should involve a reasonable
upper limit for the .sect and .rate fields, but it could change the
UAPI.

The patch also checks F_SECT_PER_TRACK in the setup_format_params, and
cancels the formatting operation in case of zero.

The bug was found by syzkaller.

Signed-off-by: Denis Efremov <efremov@ispras.ru>
Tested-by: Willy Tarreau <w@1wt.eu>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
diff_func:
--- func_before
+++ func_after
@@ -6,6 +6,8 @@
 	/* sanity checking for parameters. */
 	if (g->sect <= 0 ||
 	    g->head <= 0 ||
+	    /* check for zero in F_SECT_PER_TRACK */
+	    (unsigned char)((g->sect << 2) >> FD_SIZECODE(g)) == 0 ||
 	    g->track <= 0 || g->track > UDP->tracks >> STRETCH(g) ||
 	    /* check if reserved bits are set */
 	    (g->stretch & ~(FD_STRETCH | FD_SWAPSIDES | FD_SECTBASEMASK)) != 0)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t    /* check for zero in F_SECT_PER_TRACK */', '\t    (unsigned char)((g->sect << 2) >> FD_SIZECODE(g)) == 0 ||']}
description: In the Linux kernel before 5.2.3, drivers/block/floppy.c allows a denial of service by setup_format_params division-by-zero. Two consecutive ioctls can trigger the bug: the first one should set the drive geometry with .sect and .rate values that make F_SECT_PER_TRACK be zero. Next, the floppy format operation should be called. It can be triggered by an unprivileged local user even when a floppy disk has not been inserted. NOTE: QEMU creates the floppy device by default.

code_evidence: The sanity check in set_geometry validates g->sect > 0, g->head > 0, g->track range and stretch bits, but places no constraint tying g->sect and g->rate (via FD_SIZECODE) together. A positive g->sect can still yield a zero F_SECT_PER_TRACK when shifted by FD_SIZECODE(g).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function's missing cross-field constraint permits a zero divisor later consumed by a division, directly matching CWE-369 (divide by zero). This is distinct from a simple input-validation gap because the supported harm is the zero-divisor arithmetic fault.

evidence_lines.code:
if (g->sect <= 0 ||
g->head <= 0 ||
g->track <= 0 || g->track > UDP->tracks >> STRETCH(g) ||
(g->stretch & ~(FD_STRETCH | FD_SWAPSIDES | FD_SECTBASEMASK)) != 0)
return -EINVAL;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: set_geometry accepts .sect and .rate geometry values that make F_SECT_PER_TRACK zero because the validation only checks individual fields, not their combination. Trigger: a first ioctl sets such geometry, then a format ioctl reaches setup_format_params, which divides by F_SECT_PER_TRACK. Supported consequence: divide-by-zero crash, a denial of service reachable by an unprivileged local user.

Fixes: 13ac695e7ea1 ("net:hns: Add support of Hip06 SoC to the Hislicon Network Subsystem")
Signed-off-by: Yunsheng Lin <linyunsheng@huawei.com>
Signed-off-by: lipeng <lipeng321@huawei.com>
Reported-by: Jun He <hjat2005@huawei.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['int hns_nic_net_xmit_hw(struct net_device *ndev,', '\t\t\tstruct sk_buff *skb,', '\t\t\tstruct hns_nic_ring_data *ring_data)'], 'added_lines': ['netdev_tx_t hns_nic_net_xmit_hw(struct net_device *ndev,', '\t\t\t\tstruct sk_buff *skb,', '\t\t\t\tstruct hns_nic_ring_data *ring_data)', '\tnetif_trans_update(ndev);', '\tndev->stats.tx_bytes += skb->len;', '\tndev->stats.tx_packets++;', '']}
description: In drivers/net/ethernet/hisilicon/hns/hns_enet.c in the Linux kernel before 4.13, local users can cause a denial of service (use-after-free and BUG) or possibly have unspecified other impact by leveraging differences in skb handling between hns_nic_net_xmit_hw and hns_nic_net_xmit.

code_evidence: maybe_stop_tx failure paths branch to out_err_tx_ok, where dev_kfree_skb_any(skb) frees the skb and NETDEV_TX_OK is returned.
The -EBUSY path calls netif_stop_subqueue(ndev, skb->queue_mapping) and returns NETDEV_TX_BUSY without freeing, so the caller retains ownership.
The function returns NETDEV_TX_OK after freeing skb on error, so the caller treats the skb as consumed; any subsequent use of that skb by the caller is a use-after-free.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the skb is released inside this function and then referenced afterward through the caller's stale pointer; the defect is a use-after-free, not merely a double free or leak.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: on the -ENOMEM and DMA-map failure paths, hns_nic_net_xmit_hw frees skb via dev_kfree_skb_any yet returns NETDEV_TX_OK, signaling successful transmission. The caller then may access the skb that hns_nic_net_xmit_hw already freed, triggering the reported KASAN use-after-free and possible crash/DoS.

commit_msg: Validate the segments_left field in the SRH.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    } else if(segments_left > path_len) {', '      /* Discard the packet because of a parameter problem. */', '      LOG_ERR("SRH with too many segments left (%u > %u)\\n",', '              segments_left, path_len);', '      return 0;']}
description: Contiki-NG is an open-source, cross-platform operating system for internet of things devices. In versions prior to 4.5, buffer overflow can be triggered by an input packet when using either of Contiki-NG's two RPL implementations in source-routing mode. The problem has been patched in Contiki-NG 4.5. Users can apply the patch for this vulnerability out-of-band as a workaround.

code_evidence: segments_left is read from rh_header->seg_left (line 16) and path_len is computed from header fields (line 21); before the patch, segments_left is used without any bound relative to path_len.

In the else branch, i = path_len - segments_left (line 27) drives addr_ptr = base + RPL_RH_LEN + RPL_SRH_LEN + i*(16-cmpri) (line 28), and memcpy copies 16-cmpr bytes into UIP_IP_BUF->destipaddr and back to addr_ptr (lines 31-32), with addr_ptr potentially pointing outside the header buffer when segments_left > path_len.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-120 fits because the memcpy copies a fixed 16-cmpr byte count to/from an address derived from unvalidated input without checking that the destination lies within the header buffer, i.e., a buffer copy without size/placement validation. It is not merely CWE-125 because the memcpy also writes out of bounds.

evidence_lines.code:
segments_left = rh_header->seg_left;

commit_msg: Fix integer overflow in row allocation. #60.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    int tabs = 0, nonprint = 0, j, idx;'], 'added_lines': ['    unsigned int tabs = 0, nonprint = 0;', '    int j, idx;', '', '    unsigned long long allocsize =', '        (unsigned long long) row->size + tabs*8 + nonprint*9 + 1;', '    if (allocsize > UINT32_MAX) {', '        printf("Some line of the edited file is too long for kilo\\n");', '        exit(1);', '    }']}
description: Buffer Overflow vulnerability in Antirez Kilo before commit 7709a04ae8520c5b04d261616098cebf742f5a23 allows a remote attacker to cause a denial of service via the editorUpdateRow function in kilo.c.

code_evidence: tabs and nonprint are int counters; the allocation size row->size + tabs*8 + nonprint*9 + 1 is computed in int arithmetic, so a row with many tabs can overflow the size expression and malloc a buffer smaller than needed.
The render loop writes a space and then pads with spaces in the while loop, advancing idx for each tab expansion without any bound check against the allocated size.
The terminating NUL is written at row->render[idx] using the same unchecked idx, past the undersized buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes spaces and a NUL beyond the end of an undersized malloc buffer, which is exactly an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). The integer overflow is the enabling cause, but the supported consequence is the out-of-bounds write.

evidence_lines.code:
int tabs = 0, nonprint = 0, j, idx;
row->render = malloc(row->size + tabs*8 + nonprint*9 + 1);
row->render[idx] = '\0';

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the render buffer size is computed with 32-bit int arithmetic that overflows when tabs*8 is large, allocating too few bytes. Trigger: editing a line containing many tab characters. Consequence: the tab-expansion writes and the trailing NUL write past the end of the heap buffer, causing memory corruption or a crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
mime-actions: use file metadata for trusting desktop files

Currently we only trust desktop files that have the executable bit
set, and don't replace the displayed icon or the displayed name until
it's trusted, which prevents for running random programs by a malicious
desktop file.

However, the executable permission is preserved if the desktop file
comes from a compressed file.

To prevent this, add a metadata::trusted metadata to the file once the
user acknowledges the file as trusted. This adds metadata to the file,
which cannot be added unless it has access to the computer.

Also remove the SHEBANG "trusted" content we were putting inside the
desktop file, since that doesn't add more security since it can come
with the file itself.

https://bugzilla.gnome.org/show_bug.cgi?id=777991

description: When using certain mbstring functions to convert multibyte encodings, in PHP versions 7.2.x below 7.2.27, 7.3.x below 7.3.14 and 7.4.x below 7.4.2 it is possible to supply data that will cause function mbfl_filt_conv_big5_wchar to read past the allocated buffer. This may lead to information disclosure or crash.

code_evidence: The CP950 PUA branch computes c2 from c1 and c, then scans cp950_pua_tbl with a loop that breaks only on a matching range; if no entry matches, k equals the table count and the subsequent accesses cp950_pua_tbl[k][2] and cp950_pua_tbl[k][0] read one element past the table end.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function directly reads past the end of cp950_pua_tbl via an unchecked loop index, which matches CWE-125 (Out-of-bounds Read). This is a read overrun rather than a write or integer issue, since the missing constraint is the post-loop index bound before table dereference.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the PUA lookup loop lacks a bounds check after iteration, so when c2 falls outside all cp950_pua_tbl ranges, k indexes past the array. Trigger: attacker-supplied Big5/CP950 byte pairs reaching the PUA path without a matching table entry. Consequence: out-of-bounds read of adjacent memory used to compute w, leading to information disclosure or crash.

commit_msg:
Track byteSize of HeaderMap internally.

Introduces a cached byte size updated internally in HeaderMap. The value
is stored as an optional, and is cleared whenever a non-const pointer or
reference to a HeaderEntry is accessed. The cached value can be set with
refreshByteSize() which performs an iteration over the HeaderMap to sum
the size of each key and value in the HeaderMap.

Signed-off-by: Asra Ali <asraa@google.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  // Prior to logging, refresh the byte size of the HeaderMaps.', '  // TODO(asraa): Remove this when entries in HeaderMap can no longer be modified by reference and', '  // HeaderMap holds an accurate internal byte size count.', '  if (upstream_headers_ != nullptr) {', '    upstream_headers_->refreshByteSize();', '  }', '  if (upstream_trailers_ != nullptr) {', '    upstream_trailers_->refreshByteSize();', '  }']}
description: Upon receiving each incoming request header data, Envoy will iterate over existing request headers to verify that the total size of the headers stays below a maximum limit. The implementation in versions 1.10.0 through 1.11.1 for HTTP/1.x traffic and all versions of Envoy for HTTP/2 traffic had O(n^2) performance characteristics. A remote attacker may craft a request that stays below the maximum request header size but consists of many thousands of small headers to consume CPU and result in a denial-of-service attack.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The destructor only logs upstream headers/trailers and refreshes cached byte sizes; it contains no header-size limit check or iteration over request headers, so it does not support the O(n^2) resource-consumption weakness.

commit_msg:
manager: if falling back to X11 retry autologin

Right now, we get one shot to autologin. If it fails, we fall back to
the greeter.  We should give it another go if the reason for the failure
was wayland fallback to X.

https://bugzilla.gnome.org/show_bug.cgi?id=780520
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        g_object_get (display, "x11-display-number", &display_number, NULL);'], 'added_lines': ['        char       *session_type = NULL;', '        g_object_get (display,', '                      "x11-display-number", &display_number,', '                      "session-type", &session_type,', '                      NULL);', '                        if (status == GDM_DISPLAY_FINISHED || g_strcmp0 (session_type, "x11") == 0) {', '                                manager->priv->ran_once = TRUE;', '                        }']}
description: A flaw was discovered in gdm 3.24.1 where gdm greeter was no longer setting the ran_once boolean during autologin. If autologin was enabled for a victim, an attacker could simply select 'login as another user' to unlock their screen.

code_evidence: Line 16 reads only x11-display-number; the function never reads or initializes the display's session-type, so no session_type value is available to the fallback logic.

The switch handles GDM_DISPLAY_FAILED, UNMANAGED and FINISHED identically: it only quits plymouth and calls maybe_start_pending_initial_login. It never sets manager->priv->ran_once, the flag that records that autologin has been attempted.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-665 fits because the security-relevant state (ran_once) is left uninitialized on the fallback path, and that unset flag controls whether autologin is considered already attempted, enabling an access-control bypass. This is a missing initialization of a state flag rather than a memory-safety or logic-only error.

evidence_lines.code: g_object_get (display, "x11-display-number", &display_number, NULL);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The autologin-attempt flag ran_once is not initialized/set on the failure and finish paths that lead to the greeter. Trigger: autologin fails and the display transitions to FAILED/UNMANAGED/FINISHED; the greeter then appears with ran_once still unset. Consequence: the greeter treats the session as a fresh autologin opportunity, so an attacker selecting 'login as another user' can reach the victim's session without authentication.

commit_msg:
Add stack limit check to proxy operations

Fixes #3785.

JerryScript-DCO-1.0-Signed-off-by: Dániel Bátyai dbatyai@inf.u-szeged.hu
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  ECMA_CHECK_STACK_USAGE ();']}
description: JerryScript 2.2.0 allows attackers to cause a denial of service (stack consumption) via a proxy operation.

code_evidence: Entry only asserts the object is a proxy before extracting handler/target; no stack-depth guard exists in the original body.
When the trap is undefined, the function recurses into ecma_op_object_has_property on the target object, which can re-enter proxy handling.
When a trap exists, it invokes the user-supplied handler via ecma_op_function_call, allowing attacker-controlled recursion through proxy operations.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-400 fits because the function fails to throttle a limited resource—native stack depth—during recursive proxy operations. The patch adds ECMA_CHECK_STACK_USAGE, confirming missing resource control; this is exhaustion of stack resource rather than a memory-safety write.

JERRY_ASSERT (ECMA_OBJECT_IS_PROXY (obj_p));
ecma_proxy_object_t *proxy_obj_p = (ecma_proxy_object_t *) obj_p;

ecma_value_t trap_result = ecma_op_function_call (func_obj_p, handler, args, 2);
ecma_deref_object (func_obj_p);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: proxy 'has' operations recurse into target property lookup or invoke traps without any stack consumption limit. Trigger: a crafted chain of nested proxy objects whose 'has' traps/targets re-enter this function. Consequence: unbounded native stack growth leading to stack exhaustion and denial of service (crash).

commit_msg:
Handle pixel formats with odd shift values

Our fast paths assume that each channel fits in to a separate byte.
That means the shift needs to be a multiple of 8. Start actually
checking this so that a client cannot trip us up and possibly cause
incorrect code exection.

Issue found by Pavel Cheremushkin from Kaspersky Lab.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  if ((redShift & 0x7) != 0)', '    return false;', '  if ((greenShift & 0x7) != 0)', '    return false;', '  if ((blueShift & 0x7) != 0)', '    return false;']}
description: TigerVNC version prior to 1.10.1 is vulnerable to stack buffer overflow, which could be triggered from CMsgReader::readSetCursor. This vulnerability occurs due to insufficient sanitization of PixelFormat. Since remote attacker can choose offset from start of the buffer to start writing his values, exploitation of this vulnerability could potentially result into remote code execution. This attack appear to be exploitable via network connectivity.

code_evidence: is888 validates trueColour, bpp==32, depth==24 and that red/green/blueMax all equal 255, then returns true. It never constrains redShift, greenShift or blueShift, so a PixelFormat with byte-sized maxima but arbitrary shift offsets (e.g. shift values not multiples of 8) is accepted as an 888 fast path.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the missing shift alignment check allows callers to write past the intended cursor buffer. The weakness is the absent constraint enabling an out-of-bounds write, not merely improper input validation (CWE-20), which is the underlying cause rather than the supported consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: is888 accepts pixel formats whose channel shifts are not byte-aligned, so callers assume each channel occupies a separate byte. Trigger: a remote client sends a SetCursor PixelFormat with maximal values 255 but odd shift offsets; the accepted format drives cursor buffer writes at attacker-chosen offsets. Supported consequence: out-of-bounds stack writes, potentially leading to code execution.

commit_msg:
Add integer overflow check to the malloc wrappers

Add a check that the combined size of the buffer to allocate and
alloc_info_t does not exceed the maximum integer value representable
by size_t.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    alloc_info_t *alloc_info = (alloc_info_t *)SUPER_MALLOC(size + sizeof(alloc_info_t));'], 'added_lines': ['    alloc_info_t *alloc_info = NULL;', '    if (size <= SIZE_MAX - sizeof(alloc_info_t)) {', '        alloc_info = (alloc_info_t *)SUPER_MALLOC(size + sizeof(alloc_info_t));', '    }']}
description: ARM mbed-ualloc memory library version 1.3.0 is vulnerable to integer wrap-around in function mbed_krbs, which can lead to arbitrary memory allocation, resulting in unexpected behavior such as a crash or a remote code injection/execution.

code_evidence: Line 9 computes the allocation size as `size + sizeof(alloc_info_t)` without any bound check before passing it to SUPER_MALLOC. Lines 11-13 then write `alloc_info->size` and `alloc_info->signature` and derive the returned pointer from the allocation, so the allocation size directly governs the metadata header and returned buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe operation is an unchecked integer addition used as a memory-allocation size, exactly the size-calculation wraparound described by CWE-190, and the commit adds `size <= SIZE_MAX - sizeof(alloc_info_t)` to prevent it. This is not merely a missing length check (CWE-1284); the arithmetic wraparound is the root cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the sum `size + sizeof(alloc_info_t)` in the allocation expression can wrap when `size` is near SIZE_MAX, since no constraint ensures the sum stays representable. Trigger: a caller supplies a very large size_t. Consequence: SUPER_MALLOC receives a small wrapped size and returns an undersized block, while lines 11-13 write header fields and line 13 returns `alloc_info + 1`, yielding an out-of-bounds allocation whose use can corrupt memory or crash.

commit_msg:
Kafka: Be more strict when dissecting varints.

The Kafka dissector uses the return value of tvb_get_varint to advance
the packet offset in many places. If tvb_get_varint fails it returns 0,
which means our offset isn't guaranteed to advance. Stop dissection
whenever that happens. Fixes #17811.

description: Large loop in the Kafka dissector in Wireshark 3.6.0 allows denial of service via packet injection or crafted capture file

code_evidence: tvb_get_varint is called at line 9; if it fails it returns 0. The guard at line 10 treats len==0 as a bad array length and returns offset unchanged at line 12, so the caller's offset does not advance. Trigger: a crafted packet/capture with a non-advancing or oversized compact-array varint. Consequence: repeated dissection and unbounded iteration, causing CPU exhaustion (denial of service).

commit_msg:
cryp: prevent direct calls to update and final functions

With inconsistent or malformed data it has been possible to call
"update" and "final" crypto functions directly. Using a fuzzer tool [1]
we have seen that this results in asserts, i.e., a crash that
potentially could leak sensitive information.

By setting the state (initialized) in the crypto context (i.e., the
tee_cryp_state) at the end of all syscall_*_init functions and then add
a check of the state at the beginning of all update and final functions,
  we prevent direct entrance to the "update" and "final" functions.

[1] https://github.com/MartijnB/optee_fuzzer

Fixes: OP-TEE-2019-0021

Signed-off-by: Joakim Bech <joakim.bech@linaro.org>
Reported-by: Martijn Bogaard <bogaard@riscure.com>
Acked-by: Jerome Forissier <jerome.forissier@linaro.org>
Reviewed-by: Jens Wiklander <jens.wiklander@linaro.org>

code_evidence: Image descriptor width w and height h are read from the input at lines 46-47, then only bounds-checked via (x+w)>(g->w) and (y+h)>(g->h) at line 48; a zero width passes this check and computes max_x=start_x and max_y=start_y+h*line_size.
g->cur_x/cur_y are initialized to start_x/start_y (lines 55-56) and passed to stbi__process_gif_raster, whose output o is not validated for a zero-width rectangle before returning.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The accepted zero-width descriptor leads directly to writing past the intended buffer boundary, matching CWE-787 (out-of-bounds write). It is not merely an integer overflow; the missing width constraint is the cause and the OOB write is the supported consequence.

evidence_lines.code:
o = stbi__process_gif_raster(s, g);
if (o == NULL) return NULL;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: a zero-width image descriptor is accepted because the descriptor bounds check does not reject w==0, leaving max_x==start_x. The raster decoder then writes pixels based on the malformed rectangle, producing an out-of-bounds write into g->out. Trigger is a crafted GIF with a zero-width image descriptor; consequence is heap buffer overflow.

description: An out of bounds read in the function d2alaw_array() in alaw.c of libsndfile 1.0.28 may lead to a remote DoS attack or information disclosure, related to mishandling of the NAN and INFINITY floating-point values.

code_evidence: Line 7 obtains max via SFC_CALC_SIGNAL_MAX without validating it; if max is NaN/Infinity, the comparison max < 1.0 at line 8 is false, so control falls into the else branch.

Lines 17-19 read frames into data and divide each element by the unvalidated max; for NaN/Infinity max, data[k] becomes non-finite and is then written at line 20. The loop bound readcount*channels relies on readcount from sf_readf_double without checking non-finite values, and the division by a non-finite max can propagate NaN/Infinity into data.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function's unchecked non-finite max and division feed non-finite data values into subsequent array conversions that read past buffer bounds, matching CWE-125 out-of-bounds read. It is not merely a divide-by-zero error; the supported consequence is an out-of-bounds read.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: max from SFC_CALC_SIGNAL_MAX is used as a divisor without checking it is normal/finite. Trigger: input file yields NaN or Infinity signal max. Consequence: non-finite values propagate through data[], and the unvalidated readcount/array handling leads to out-of-bounds reads in downstream array conversion (d2alaw_array), causing DoS or information disclosure.

description: epan/dissectors/packet-wbxml.c in the WBXML dissector in Wireshark 1.12.x before 1.12.12 mishandles offsets, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (integer overflow and infinite loop) via a crafted packet.

code_evidence: tvb_len is the reported length and off advances by token-dependent amounts while the loop only bounds off < tvb_len.
ENT token: tvb_get_guintvar reads an encoded length from off+1 and off += 1+len, so off can overflow or jump past tvb_len.
Literal tag: idx from tvb_get_guintvar plus str_tbl is passed to tvb_strsize/tvb_get_ptr without validating str_tbl+idx against the buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The dissector performs reads on tvb memory at attacker-influenced offsets (str_tbl+idx, off+1) outside the intended buffer boundary, matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds memory operation. The integer wrap is the mechanism enabling the out-of-bounds condition.

evidence_lines.code:
ent = tvb_get_guintvar (tvb, off+1, &len);
off += 1+len;

idx = tvb_get_guintvar (tvb, off+1, &tag_len);
tag_new_literal = (const gchar*)tvb_get_ptr (tvb, str_tbl+idx, str_len);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Untrusted WBXML token lengths and table indices drive 32-bit off/idx arithmetic without bounds validation; crafted values can wrap off below its prior value, keeping the while loop alive indefinitely (infinite loop) while tvb accessors read past the reported buffer. Root cause is unchecked offset arithmetic; consequence is DoS and out-of-bounds reads.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tif (!tmp) {', '\t\t\tr_list_free (ret->data);', '\t\t\tR_FREE (ret);', '\t\t\treturn NULL;', '\t\t}', '\t\tif (!r_list_append (ret->data, tmp)) {'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (!tmp || !r_list_append (ret->data, tmp)) {', '\t\t\t((RList*)ret->data)->free = NULL;']}
description: Use After Free in GitHub repository radareorg/radare2 prior to 5.6.2.

code_evidence: ret->data is created with r_list_newf((RListFree)free_object), so the list owns and frees each appended pyc_object via free_object on list destruction.
On get_object failure, r_list_free(ret->data) destroys the list, invoking free_object on every already-appended element, then R_FREE(ret) releases the container and returns.
On append failure, free_object(tmp) frees the new object, then r_list_free(ret->data) frees all prior elements through the same free callback; free(ret) then releases the struct.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the cleanup logic frees owned objects through the list callback and the container, leaving dangling references that can be reused after the error return. This is specifically reuse-after-free rather than a double free or leak, since the flaw is in later access to the freed memory.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The error paths destroy the list, which invokes its free_object callback on each stored element. Because get_object can return objects that alias or share state with elements already owned by the list, freeing the list can free memory that remains referenced elsewhere; subsequent use of those pointers is a use-after-free. The trigger is a failed get_object or r_list_append during array parsing, and the supported consequence includes memory corruption or a crash.

commit_msg:
HFSC assumes that inner classes have an fsc curve, but it is currently
possible for classes without an fsc curve to become parents. This leads
to bugs including a use-after-free.

Don't allow non-root classes without HFSC_FSC to become parents.

Fixes: 1da177e4c3f4 ("Linux-2.6.12-rc2")
Reported-by: Budimir Markovic <markovicbudimir@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Budimir Markovic <markovicbudimir@gmail.com>
Acked-by: Jamal Hadi Salim <jhs@mojatatu.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20230824084905.422-1-markovicbudimir@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tif (!(parent->cl_flags & HFSC_FSC) && parent != &q->root) {', '\t\tNL_SET_ERR_MSG(extack, "Invalid parent - parent class must have FSC");', '\t\treturn -EINVAL;', '\t}']}
description:
A use-after-free vulnerability in the Linux kernel's net/sched: sch_hfsc (HFSC qdisc traffic control) component can be exploited to achieve local privilege escalation.

If a class with a link-sharing curve (i.e. with the HFSC_FSC flag set) has a parent without a link-sharing curve, then init_vf() will call vttree_insert() on the parent, but vttree_remove() will be skipped in update_vf(). This leaves a dangling pointer that can cause a use-after-free.

We recommend upgrading past commit b3d26c5702c7d6c45456326e56d2ccf3f103e60f.

code_evidence: For a new class, parentid == TC_H_ROOT yields the root class; otherwise the parent is resolved via hfsc_find_class(parentid, sch), and only a NULL result is rejected. There is no check that the resolved parent has HFSC_FSC set, so a non-root class without a link-sharing curve can become a parent.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing parent-flag constraint allows an unbalanced tree insertion that leaves a stale reference, and subsequent operations on that freed tree node constitute a use-after-free (CWE-416). This is a dangling-pointer lifetime issue, not merely a logic or input-validation error.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: A class carrying HFSC_FSC may be attached to a parent lacking HFSC_FSC. When queued data later triggers init_vf(), vttree_insert() runs on the parent, but update_vf() skips vttree_remove() because the parent lacks the flag, leaving a dangling pointer that is used after the node is freed.

description: In nDPI through 3.2, the packet parsing code is vulnerable to a heap-based buffer over-read in ndpi_parse_packet_line_info in lib/ndpi_main.c.

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the copy length is clamped to the destination size without first verifying that a1 is within the payload. Trigger: a crafted packet whose CRLFCRLF terminator sits near the buffer end, making a+4 exceed payload_packet_len. commit_msg:
MBIM: stop pre sizing wmem arrays

In case of malformed packet, this can lead to an insane amount of
memory.
Instead let's use the automatic growth mecanism. This way the malformed
packet is caught by the dissection engine.

Bug: 14056
Change-Id: I7bf5b80a516210b341356f5d495f08d1dba05805
Reviewed-on: https://code.wireshark.org/review/23537
Reviewed-by: Pascal Quantin <pascal.quantin@gmail.com>
Petri-Dish: Pascal Quantin <pascal.quantin@gmail.com>
Tested-by: Petri Dish Buildbot <buildbot-no-reply@wireshark.org>
Reviewed-by: Michael Mann <mmann78@netscape.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        pair_list = wmem_array_sized_new(wmem_packet_scope(), sizeof(struct mbim_pair_list), elem_count);'], 'added_lines': ['        pair_list = wmem_array_new(wmem_packet_scope(), sizeof(struct mbim_pair_list));']}
description: In Wireshark 2.4.0 to 2.4.1 and 2.2.0 to 2.2.9, the MBIM dissector could crash or exhaust system memory. This was addressed in epan/dissectors/packet-mbim.c by changing the memory-allocation approach.

code_evidence: Line 24 reads an attacker-controlled 32-bit elem_count from the packet. Line 26 only checks it is nonzero, and line 27 pre-allocates a wmem array sized to elem_count entries without any upper bound, so a malformed packet declaring a huge count forces a huge allocation. Line 28 likewise computes 8*elem_count for the subtree length from the same unvalidated value.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is uncontrolled consumption of a limited resource (memory) driven by unvalidated input, matching CWE-400. It is not a simple buffer overflow; the allocation size itself is the attack vector, and the fix removes pre-sizing so malformed packets are caught by the dissection engine.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the dissector pre-sizes a wmem array using the packet-supplied elem_count without validating it against the remaining packet data. Trigger: a malformed MBIM packet with an enormous element count. Consequence: excessive memory allocation that can exhaust system memory or crash the dissector, a denial of service.

commit_msg:
Small memory leak fix (CVE-2019-6502 in #1586)

CVE-2019-6502 was assigned to what appears to be a very minor
memory leak that only occurs on an error-case in a CLI tool.
If util_connect_card fails, we still need to release the sc
context previously allocated by sc_context_create else memory
will leak.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\tsc_release_context(ctx);']}
description: sc_context_create in ctx.c in libopensc in OpenSC 0.19.0 has a memory leak, as demonstrated by a call from eidenv.

code_evidence: Line 11 allocates a context through sc_context_create, storing the pointer in ctx. Lines 12-16 handle allocation failure by returning early, which is fine because no context exists yet.

Line 17 calls util_connect_card using the already-allocated ctx. Lines 18-20 handle a connection failure by printing an error and returning 1 without calling sc_release_context(ctx), so the context allocated on line 11 is never freed on this path.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function allocates memory via sc_context_create and omits its release on an error path, matching CWE-401 (missing release of memory after effective lifetime). This is an error-condition leak, not a use-after-free or double-free, so CWE-401 is the fitting label.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the error branch for util_connect_card failure (lines 18-20) returns without releasing the context created at line 11. Trigger: util_connect_card returns nonzero, e.g. when the card cannot be connected. Consequence: the allocated sc_context_t leaks; the later cleanup at lines 40-42 is bypassed by the early return.
