commit_msg:
avcodec/jpeg2000dec: More completely check cdef

Fixes out of array read
Fixes: j2k-poc.bin

Found-by: Lucas Leong <wmliang.tw@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if (s->cdef[0] < 0) {', '        for (x = 0; x < s->ncomponents; x++)', '            s->cdef[x] = x + 1;', '        if ((s->ncomponents & 1) == 0)', '            s->cdef[s->ncomponents-1] = 0;'], 'added_lines': ['    for (x = 0; x < s->ncomponents; x++) {', '        if (s->cdef[x] < 0) {', '            for (x = 0; x < s->ncomponents; x++) {', '                s->cdef[x] = x + 1;', '            }', '            if ((s->ncomponents & 1) == 0)', '                s->cdef[s->ncomponents-1] = 0;', '            break;', '        }']}
description: The jpeg2000_decode_tile function in libavcodec/jpeg2000dec.c in FFmpeg before 2.8.6 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds array read access) via crafted JPEG 2000 data.

code_evidence: The guard checks only s->cdef[0] < 0 before the loop writes s->cdef[x] for every x < s->ncomponents. If cdef[0] is non-negative but a later entry (e.g. cdef[x] for x>0) is negative, the loop still assigns all ncomponents entries, but the condition that should gate this initialization is only evaluated at index 0.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs buffer operations (array indexing of s->cdef) without ensuring all accessed locations lie within the intended initialized/valid range, matching CWE-119 improper restriction of operations within a memory buffer. The consequence is an out-of-bounds read rather than a different weakness class.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the initialization of the cdef array is gated solely on the first element being negative, so a crafted JPEG 2000 stream with a non-negative cdef[0] but negative entries elsewhere bypasses the intended initialization path. The loop then writes s->cdef[x] for all x up to ncomponents, and the subsequent write_frame_* consumers read these cdef values when mapping components, leading to an out-of-bounds array read (DoS) as described.

commit_msg:
9pfs: fix memory leak in v9fs_xattrcreate

The 'fs.xattr.value' field in V9fsFidState object doesn't consider the
situation that this field has been allocated previously. Every time, it
will be allocated directly. This leads to a host memory leak issue if
the client sends another Txattrcreate message with the same fid number
before the fid from the previous time got clunked.

Signed-off-by: Li Qiang <liqiang6-s@360.cn>
Reviewed-by: Greg Kurz <groug@kaod.org>
[groug, updated the changelog to indicate how the leak can occur]
Signed-off-by: Greg Kurz <groug@kaod.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    g_free(xattr_fidp->fs.xattr.value);']}
description: Memory leak in the v9fs_xattrcreate function in hw/9pfs/9p.c in QEMU (aka Quick Emulator) allows local guest OS administrators to cause a denial of service (memory consumption and QEMU process crash) via a large number of Txattrcreate messages with the same fid number.

code_evidence: get_fid returns the existing V9fsFidState for the client-supplied fid and it is reused as xattr_fidp (lines 23-29). Line 30 unconditionally assigns a fresh g_malloc0(size) to xattr_fidp->fs.xattr.value, overwriting any value buffer already held by that fid without freeing it first.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-772 fits because a resource (heap buffer) whose lifetime ends when it is overwritten is never released, matching missing release after effective lifetime; the reallocation-overwrite pattern is the allocation-side counterpart of a use-after-free, not a buffer overflow.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the fid state persists across Txattrcreate calls, but each call reallocates fs.xattr.value with g_malloc0 while discarding the previous pointer. Trigger: a guest repeatedly sends Txattrcreate for the same fid before the fid is clunked, so the old allocation is leaked each time. Supported consequence: unbounded host memory consumption leading to DoS of the QEMU process.

commit_msg:
Avoid infinite recursion in the ALTER TABLE code when a view contains an unused CTE that references, directly or indirectly, the view itself.

FossilOrigin-Name: 1d2e53a39b87e364685e21de137655b6eee725e4c6d27fc90865072d7c5892b5
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  pSelect->selFlags |= SF_View;']}
description: alter.c in SQLite through 3.30.1 allows attackers to trigger infinite recursion via certain types of self-referential views in conjunction with ALTER TABLE statements.

code_evidence: During ALTER TABLE (IN_RENAME_OBJECT), the parsed view SELECT is stored directly in p->pSelect without the EXPRDUP_REDUCE duplication used on the else branch. The added SF_View flag on pSelect in the patched version is what prevents later ALTER TABLE processing from treating the view's SELECT as an ordinary query and recursing back into the view.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect is a missing guard (SF_View) that fails to stop recursive re-entry into the same view's SELECT, matching CWE-674's uncontrolled recursion consuming stack resources. It is not CWE-835 (infinite loop) because the failure is recursive self-reference, not a loop lacking an exit condition.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the view's SELECT is attached to the table while still in rename context, so an unused CTE in that SELECT that references the view (directly or indirectly) can be re-entered during ALTER TABLE processing. Trigger: ALTER TABLE on a self-referential view containing such a CTE. Consequence: unbounded recursion consuming stack/CPU until failure (DoS).

commit_msg:
Unsquashfs: additional write outside destination directory exploit fix

An issue on github (https://github.com/plougher/squashfs-tools/issues/72)
showed how some specially crafted Squashfs filesystems containing
invalid file names (with '/' and '..') can cause Unsquashfs to write
files outside of the destination directory.

Since then it has been shown that specially crafted Squashfs filesystems
that contain a symbolic link pointing outside of the destination directory,
coupled with an identically named file within the same directory, can
cause Unsquashfs to write files outside of the destination directory.

Specifically the symbolic link produces a pathname pointing outside
of the destination directory, which is then followed when writing the
duplicate identically named file within the directory.

This commit fixes this exploit by explictly checking for duplicate
filenames within a directory.  As directories in v2.1, v3.x, and v4.0
filesystems are sorted, this is achieved by checking for consecutively
identical filenames.  Additionally directories are checked to
ensure they are sorted, to avoid attempts to evade the duplicate
check.

Version 1.x and 2.0 filesystems (where the directories were unsorted)
are sorted and then the above duplicate filename check is applied.

Signed-off-by: Phillip Lougher <phillip@squashfs.org.uk>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t/* check directory for duplicate names and sorting */', '\tif(check_directory(dir) == FALSE) {', '\t\tERROR("File system corrupted: directory has duplicate names or is unsorted\\n");', '\t\tgoto corrupted;', '\t}', '']}
description: squashfs_opendir in unsquash-2.c in Squashfs-Tools 4.5 allows Directory Traversal, a different vulnerability than CVE-2021-40153. A squashfs filesystem that has been crafted to include a symbolic link and then contents under the same filename in a filesystem can cause unsquashfs to first create the symbolic link pointing outside the expected directory, and then the subsequent write operation will cause the unsquashfs process to write through the symbolic link elsewhere in the filesystem.

code_evidence: Directory entries are read and their names validated only by check_name (lines 72-75), which rejects '/' and '..' but does not detect a symlink entry and an identically named file entry in the same directory.
Each entry, including its type (dire->type), is stored into a new dir_ent appended to the linked list (lines 79-92) without comparing against prior entries for duplicate names.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is improper link resolution before file access: a crafted symlink entry causes a later same-named file access to resolve through the link to an unintended path. check_name alone does not prevent this link-following behavior, matching CWE-59 rather than mere path traversal.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: squashfs_opendir builds the directory listing without rejecting a symlink and a same-named regular file in one directory, so extraction first creates the symlink pointing outside the destination and then writes the duplicate file through it. The missing duplicate/ordering check (added by the patch) is the trigger; the supported consequence is a write outside the destination directory.

commit_msg:
tipc: fix an infoleak in tipc_nl_compat_link_dump

link_info.str is a char array of size 60. Memory after the NULL
byte is not initialized. Sending the whole object out can cause
a leak.

Signed-off-by: Kangjie Lu <kjlu@gatech.edu>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

commit_msg:
Fix invalid memory accesses while loading .a2m files

Missing checks and wrong calculations in src/a2m.cpp cause
multiple heap-based buffer overflows and out-of-bounds reads
in heap, stack, and static data.

Bugs addressed in this commit:
* Check the number of patterns. Too big values can cause reads
  past the end of the len array.
* Reading a not packed data block with odd length will allocate
  a buffer which is one byte too small and write past the end
  of it (issue #88). Change the allocation/deallocation code
  to fix that in both places.
* Check that data blocks (afer unpacking if applicable) are big
  enough for the expected data before accessing the memory.
* Ensure that the length byte for author, song name, and instrument
  names doesn't exceed the maximum size available.
* Also change the accessor functions for these strings to call
  the proper std::string constructors for char arrays.
* Avoid reads past the end of convfx/newconvfx arrays while
  converting track data.

This commit fixes CVE-2019-14732.

Fixes: https://github.com/adplug/adplug/issues/88

commit_msg:
virtio: properly validate address before accessing config

There are several several issues in the current checking:

- The check was based on the minus of unsigned values which can overflow
- It was done after .{set|get}_config() which can lead crash when config_len
  is zero since vdev->config is NULL

Fix this by:

- Use addition instead minus to do the validation

commit_msg:
Disable sub frame loads more reliably in frame detach.

Previously, guarding against attaching a new frame in frame detach
was done by inspecting LoadEventProgress. There are certain
operations, such as document.open(), that can cause LoadEventProgress
to never advance, causing the guard to get skipped.

BUG=577105

Review URL: https://codereview.chromium.org/1659013003

Cr-Commit-Position: refs/heads/master@{#373581}
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        disabledSubtreeRoots().remove(m_root);'], 'added_lines': ['        if (m_root)', '            disabledSubtreeRoots().remove(m_root);']}
description: The DOM implementation in Google Chrome before 48.0.2564.109 does not properly restrict frame-attach operations from occurring during or after frame-detach operations, which allows remote attackers to bypass the Same Origin Policy via a crafted web site, related to FrameLoader.cpp, HTMLFrameOwnerElement.h, LocalFrame.cpp, and WebLocalFrameImpl.cpp.

code_evidence: The destructor unconditionally calls disabledSubtreeRoots().remove(m_root) with no check that m_root is valid; the patch adds a null guard before removal, indicating m_root may be unset when the disabler is torn down.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-264 covers weaknesses in managing security-feature state; here the subframe-loading restriction's bookkeeping is corrupted, allowing the frame-attach guard to be bypassed. It is not a memory-safety issue, since the observable effect is bypass of the loading restriction rather than a crash.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the SubframeLoadingDisabler destructor removes its root from the global disabled-subtree set without validating m_root, so a disabler created or reset without a root mutates the shared set using an invalid key. Trigger: frame-detach paths (e.g., document.open()) that leave the disabler in this state. Consequence: incorrect state of the subframe-loading guard, letting frame-attach operations proceed during detach and undermining the same-origin restriction.

commit_msg:
ACPICA: Namespace: fix operand cache leak

ACPICA commit a23325b2e583556eae88ed3f764e457786bf4df6

I found some ACPI operand cache leaks in ACPI early abort cases.

Boot log of ACPI operand cache leak is as follows:
>[    0.174332] ACPI: Added _OSI(Module Device)
>[    0.175504] ACPI: Added _OSI(Processor Device)
>[    0.176010] ACPI: Added _OSI(3.0 _SCP Extensions)
>[    0.177032] ACPI: Added _OSI(Processor Aggregator Device)
>[    0.178284] ACPI: SCI (IRQ16705) allocation failed
>[    0.179352] ACPI Exception: AE_NOT_ACQUIRED, Unable to install
System Control Interrupt handler (20160930/evevent-131)
>[    0.180008] ACPI: Unable to start the ACPI Interpreter
>[    0.181125] ACPI Error: Could not remove SCI handler
(20160930/evmisc-281)
>[    0.184068] kmem_cache_destroy Acpi-Operand: Slab cache still has
objects
>[    0.185358] CPU: 0 PID: 1 Comm: swapper/0 Not tainted 4.10.0-rc3 #2
>[    0.186820] Hardware name: innotek gmb_h virtual_box/virtual_box, BIOS
virtual_box 12/01/2006
>[    0.188000] Call Trace:
>[    0.188000]  ? dump_stack+0x5c/0x7d
>[    0.188000]  ? kmem_cache_destroy+0x224/0x230
>[    0.188000]  ? acpi_sleep_proc_init+0x22/0x22
>[    0.188000]  ? acpi_os_delete_cache+0xa/0xd
>[    0.188000]  ? acpi_ut_delete_caches+0x3f/0x7b
>[    0.188000]  ? acpi_terminate+0x5/0xf
>[    0.188000]  ? acpi_init+0x288/0x32e
>[    0.188000]  ? __class_create+0x4c/0x80
>[    0.188000]  ? video_setup+0x7a/0x7a
>[    0.188000]  ? do_one_initcall+0x4e/0x1b0
>[    0.188000]  ? kernel_init_freeable+0x194/0x21a
>[    0.188000]  ? rest_init+0x80/0x80
>[    0.188000]  ? kernel_init+0xa/0x100
>[    0.188000]  ? ret_from_fork+0x25/0x30

When early abort is occurred due to invalid ACPI information, Linux kernel
terminates ACPI by calling acpi_terminate() function. The function calls
acpi_ns_terminate() function to delete namespace data and ACPI operand cache
(acpi_gbl_module_code_list).

But the deletion code in acpi_ns_terminate() function is wrapped in
ACPI_EXEC_APP definition, therefore the code is only executed when the
definition exists. If the define doesn't exist, ACPI operand cache
(acpi_gbl_module_code_list) is leaked, and stack dump is shown in kernel log.

This causes a security threat because the old kernel (<= 4.9) shows memory
locations of kernel functions in stack dump, therefore kernel ASLR can be
neutralized.

To fix ACPI operand leak for enhancing security, I made a patch which
removes the ACPI_EXEC_APP define in acpi_ns_terminate() function for
executing the deletion code unconditionally.

Link: https://github.com/acpica/acpica/commit/a23325b2
Signed-off-by: Seunghun Han <kkamagui@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Lv Zheng <lv.zheng@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Bob Moore <robert.moore@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Rafael J. Wysocki <rafael.j.wysocki@intel.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['#ifdef ACPI_EXEC_APP', '\t{', '\t\tunion acpi_operand_object *prev;', '\t\tunion acpi_operand_object *next;', '\t\t/* Delete any module-level code blocks */', '', '\t\tnext = acpi_gbl_module_code_list;', '\t\twhile (next) {', '\t\t\tprev = next;', '\t\t\tnext = next->method.mutex;', '\t\t\tprev->method.mutex = NULL;\t/* Clear the Mutex (cheated) field */', '\t\t\tacpi_ut_remove_reference(prev);', '\t\t}', '#endif'], 'added_lines': ['\tunion acpi_operand_object *prev;', '\tunion acpi_operand_object *next;', '\t/* Delete any module-level code blocks */', '\tnext = acpi_gbl_module_code_list;', '\twhile (next) {', '\t\tprev = next;', '\t\tnext = next->method.mutex;', '\t\tprev->method.mutex = NULL;\t/* Clear the Mutex (cheated) field */', '\t\tacpi_ut_remove_reference(prev);']}
description: The acpi_ns_terminate() function in drivers/acpi/acpica/nsutils.c in the Linux kernel before 4.12 does not flush the operand cache and causes a kernel stack dump, which allows local users to obtain sensitive information from kernel memory and bypass the KASLR protection mechanism (in the kernel through 4.9) via a crafted ACPI table.

code_evidence: The operand-cache cleanup loop that walks acpi_gbl_module_code_list and calls acpi_ut_remove_reference is enclosed in '#ifdef ACPI_EXEC_APP' ... '#endif'. When that define is absent, the loop is compiled out, so the early-abort path performs no cleanup of the module-code list.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect is failure to handle an exceptional early-abort condition correctly: cleanup is not performed on that path, matching improper handling of exceptional conditions. The conditional omission is the cause; the leak and stack dump are consequences.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the cache-release code is conditionally compiled, so the normal termination/early-abort path skips flushing the operand cache. Trigger: acpi_ns_terminate runs after an early ACPI abort with ACPI_EXEC_APP undefined. Consequence: the operand cache leaks and the subsequent kmem_cache_destroy emits a kernel stack dump exposing kernel addresses (KASLR bypass on older kernels).

commit_msg:
When opening files for write, ensure they aren't symbolic links

Issue #1048 identified that if, for example, a non privileged user
created a symbolic link from /etc/keepalvied.data to /etc/passwd,
writing to /etc/keepalived.data (which could be invoked via DBus)
would cause /etc/passwd to be overwritten.

This commit stops keepalived writing to pathnames where the ultimate
component is a symbolic link, by setting O_NOFOLLOW whenever opening
a file for writing.

This might break some setups, where, for example, /etc/keepalived.data
was a symbolic link to /home/fred/keepalived.data. If this was the case,
instead create a symbolic link from /home/fred/keepalived.data to
/tmp/keepalived.data, so that the file is still accessible via
/home/fred/keepalived.data.

There doesn't appear to be a way around this backward incompatibility,
since even checking if the pathname is a symbolic link prior to opening
for writing would create a race condition.

Signed-off-by: Quentin Armitage <quentin@armitage.org.uk>

description: Stack-based buffer overflow in the ipv6_addr_from_str function in sys/net/network_layer/ipv6/addr/ipv6_addr_from_str.c in RIOT prior to 2017-04-25 allows local attackers, and potentially remote attackers, to cause a denial of service or possibly have unspecified other impact via a malformed IPv6 address.

Two bytes are then written at result->u8[i++] and result->u8[i++], so when i equals the buffer size the writes land one and two bytes past the end of result.
The IPv4 path condition `(i <= sizeof(ipv6_addr_t))` likewise permits i == sizeof(ipv6_addr_t) while ipv4_addr_from_str writes a full ipv4_addr_t at &result->u8[i], overflowing the buffer.

This is an improper restriction of operations within a memory buffer, matching CWE-119; the off-by-one check is the root cause, and the out-of-bounds write is the supported consequence.

result->u8[i++] = (uint8_t)(val >> 8) & 0xff;
result->u8[i++] = (uint8_t) val & 0xff;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is an off-by-one bounds check comparing i alone against the buffer size instead of accounting for the size of the value about to be written. commit_msg:
win: fix unsavory rwlock fallback implementation

Before this patch an uv_mutex_t (backed by a critical section) could be
released by a tread different from the thread that acquired it, which is
not allowed. This is fixed by using a semaphore instead.

Note that the affected code paths were used on Windows XP and Windows
Server 2003 only.

Fixes: https://github.com/libuv/libuv/issues/515
PR-URL: https://github.com/libuv/libuv/pull/516
Reviewed-By: Ben Noordhuis <info@bnoordhuis.nl>
Reviewed-By: Saúl Ibarra Corretgé <saghul@gmail.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  uv_mutex_lock(&rwlock->fallback_.read_mutex_);', '  if (++rwlock->fallback_.num_readers_ == 1)', '    uv_mutex_lock(&rwlock->fallback_.write_mutex_);', '  uv_mutex_unlock(&rwlock->fallback_.read_mutex_);'], 'added_lines': ['  /* Acquire the lock that protects the reader count. */', '  EnterCriticalSection(&rwlock->fallback_.read_lock_.cs);', '  /* Increase the reader count, and lock for write if this is the first', '   * reader.', '   */', '  if (++rwlock->fallback_.num_readers_ == 1) {', '    DWORD r = WaitForSingleObject(rwlock->fallback_.write_lock_.sem, INFINITE);', '    if (r != WAIT_OBJECT_0)', '      uv_fatal_error(GetLastError(), "WaitForSingleObject");', '  }', '  /* Release the lock that protects the reader count. */', '  LeaveCriticalSection(&rwlock->fallback_.read_lock_.cs);']}
description: The uv_rwlock_t fallback implementation for Windows XP and Server 2003 in libuv before 1.7.4 does not properly prevent threads from releasing the locks of other threads, which allows attackers to cause a denial of service (deadlock) or possibly have unspecified other impact by leveraging a race condition.

code_evidence: The reader count is incremented with ++rwlock->fallback_.num_readers_ under read_mutex_, but the write lock is taken with uv_mutex_lock(&rwlock->fallback_.write_mutex_), a Windows critical section. A critical section must be released by the thread that entered it, so if the first reader acquires write_mutex_ and a different thread later performs the matching rdunlock, the release occurs in a non-owning thread.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The shared reader-count/writer-lock protocol lacks proper synchronization that preserves exclusivity across threads, so concurrent rdlock/rdunlock sequences can interfere and corrupt lock ownership. This is a race condition in concurrent access to a shared resource, matching CWE-362; the ownership violation is the mechanism, not a separate CWE.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the write side of the fallback rwlock is a critical-section-backed mutex, which enforces thread ownership, while the reader/writer protocol allows the first reader to acquire it and any last reader to release it. Trigger: two threads where the first reader acquires write_mutex_ and a different thread is the last to unlock; the non-owning release is invalid. Consequence: the lock state becomes inconsistent, leading to deadlock or unspecified behavior (DoS).

commit_msg: Fix wrong boundary checks in inflections parser resulting in stack buffer over-read with corrupt input
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            if (pos < 0 || pos > *decoded_size) {', '                debug_print("Position setting failed (%s)\\n", decoded);', '                return MOBI_DATA_CORRUPT;', '            }', '                if (l < 0 || d + l > decoded + INDX_INFLBUF_SIZEMAX) {', '                if (l < 0 || d + l > decoded + INDX_INFLBUF_SIZEMAX) {'], 'added_lines': ['                if (pos < 0 || l < 0 || d + l > decoded + INDX_INFLBUF_SIZEMAX) {', '                if (pos < 0 || l < 0 || s + l > decoded + INDX_INFLBUF_SIZEMAX) {']}
description: Buffer Over-read in GitHub repository bfabiszewski/libmobi prior to 0.11. This vulnerability is capable of arbitrary code execution.

code_evidence: In the insertion branch, pointers s = decoded + pos and d = decoded + pos + 1 are formed and l = *decoded_size - pos is computed before the check; the guard only tests l < 0 and the upper bound, so a negative pos yields s/d before the buffer and a large l, then memmove(d, s, l) reads before decoded.

In the deletion branch, s = decoded + pos + 1 and d = decoded + pos are formed and l computed; the guard omits a pos < 0 test, so a negative pos makes s before the buffer while l stays positive, and memmove(d, s, l) reads out of bounds.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe memmove reads data before the beginning of the decoded buffer, which is exactly an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). It is not an out-of-bounds write, since the destination stays within bounds; the flaw is the unchecked read source.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the boundary checks in both branches do not reject a negative pos, so pointer arithmetic decoded + pos (or + pos + 1) and the computed length l allow memmove to read outside decoded. Trigger: a corrupt inflection rule that drives pos negative, as the commit message describes. Consequence: stack buffer over-read, leading to crash or disclosure of adjacent memory.

commit_msg:
Fix double-free in gdImageWebPtr()

The issue is that gdImageWebpCtx() (which is called by gdImageWebpPtr() and
the other WebP output functions to do the real work) does not return whether
it succeeded or failed, so this is not checked in gdImageWebpPtr() and the
function wrongly assumes everything is okay, which is not, in this case,
because there is a size limitation for WebP, namely that the width and
height must by less than 16383.

We can't change the signature of gdImageWebpCtx() for API compatibility
reasons, so we introduce the static helper _gdImageWebpCtx() which returns
success respective failure, so gdImageWebpPtr() and gdImageWebpPtrEx() can
check the return value. We leave it solely to libwebp for now to report
warnings regarding the failing write.

This issue had been reported by Ibrahim El-Sayed to security@libgd.org.

CVE-2016-6912
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tgdImageWebpCtx(im, out, -1);', '\trv = gdDPExtractData(out, size);'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (_gdImageWebpCtx(im, out, -1)) {', '\t\trv = NULL;', '\t} else {', '\t\trv = gdDPExtractData(out, size);', '\t}']}
description: Double free vulnerability in the gdImageWebPtr function in the GD Graphics Library (aka libgd) before 2.2.4 allows remote attackers to have unspecified impact via large width and height values.

code_evidence: Line 8 calls gdImageWebpCtx() and ignores its return value; the commit message states this call fails when width/height exceed WebP's 16383 limit. Line 9 unconditionally calls gdDPExtractData() on the failed context, then line 10 frees the dynamic context via out->gd_free(out). Because the failure path still extracts data and frees the context, the same underlying buffer can be released twice.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-415 is double free: two calls release the same memory address. The unchecked failing write followed by unconditional extraction and gd_free(out) produces exactly that pattern; it is not merely a null dereference or use-after-free, since the defect is the duplicate release of the same buffer.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the unchecked failure of gdImageWebpCtx() leaves the dynamic context in a state where gdDPExtractData() and the subsequent out->gd_free(out) both release the same memory. Trigger: an image with width or height >= 16383 passed to gdImageWebpPtr(). Supported consequence: a double free, which can corrupt memory and potentially enable code execution.

description: GPAC version 2.1-DEV-rev505-gb9577e6ad-master was discovered to contain a memory leak via the afrt_box_read function at box_code_adobe.c.

code_evidence: Line 14 allocates tmp_str with gf_malloc(tmp_strsize+1), where tmp_strsize is derived from ptr->size (line 12). The read loop at lines 17-24 may break early on a NUL byte (line 21) without consuming the full allocation, and line 25 inserts the pointer into quality_segment_url_modifiers. In the before version the insert happened after the loop; the patch moves it before the loop so the pointer is tracked even when the loop returns early.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-401 fits because a heap allocation has no tracked owner on error/early-exit paths, so it is never released after its effective lifetime. This is a tracking/release failure, not an out-of-bounds access or double free.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the allocated tmp_str is only linked into the box's list after the read loop completes. When the loop terminates early (NUL byte at line 21) or the function returns GF_ISOM_INVALID_FILE/GF_OUT_OF_MEM, the buffer is never recorded and cannot be freed by box cleanup. Trigger: crafted afrt box data causing an early termination or error return. Consequence: leaked heap memory on repeated parsing, leading to resource exhaustion/DoS.

commit_msg:
scsi: ufs: ufs-mediatek: Fix error checking in ufs_mtk_init_va09_pwr_ctrl()

The function regulator_get() returns an error pointer. Use IS_ERR() to
validate the return value.

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20211222070930.9449-1-linmq006@gmail.com
Fixes: cf137b3ea49a ("scsi: ufs-mediatek: Support VA09 regulator operations")
Signed-off-by: Miaoqian Lin <linmq006@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Martin K. Petersen <martin.petersen@oracle.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (!host->reg_va09)'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (IS_ERR(host->reg_va09))']}
description: In the Linux kernel before 5.16.3, drivers/scsi/ufs/ufs-mediatek.c misinterprets the regulator_get return value (expects it to be NULL in the error case, whereas it is actually an error pointer).

code_evidence: regulator_get() returns an ERR_PTR on failure, but line 5 tests !host->reg_va09, which only detects NULL. An error pointer is non-NULL, so the else branch runs and sets UFS_MTK_CAP_VA09_PWR_CTRL despite the failed lookup.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits only partially: the misclassified error pointer is later used where a valid regulator is expected, and that downstream use can dereference an invalid pointer. The flaw in this function is the missing IS_ERR() check, not a dereference at these lines.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the error-pointer return of regulator_get() is checked as if failure were NULL. Trigger: regulator_get() fails and returns an ERR_PTR. The capability bit is set, so later VA09 power-control paths may use the invalid reg_va09 pointer; this function itself does not dereference it, so the immediate consequence is downstream misuse rather than a direct crash here.

commit_msg:
Fix UAF in comps_objmrtree_unite function

The added field is not used at all in many places and it is probably the
left-over of some copy-paste.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        char added;', '        //pair->added = 0;'], 'added_lines': []}
description: A use-after-free flaw has been discovered in libcomps before version 0.1.10 in the way ObjMRTrees are merged. An attacker, who is able to make an application read a crafted comps XML file, may be able to crash the application or execute malicious code.

code_evidence: The loop pops the head item, reads its data pointer into parent_pair/tmp_subnodes, then frees the list item with free(it) at line 20 while parent_pair still references the same Pair object; parent_pair is later used (e.g., parent_pair->key at line 24) and freed at lines 50-51.

For a child node, pair is appended to tmplist (line 44) when subnodes->first is set, otherwise pair->key and pair are freed (46-47); a node whose subnodes list is non-empty keeps the pair alive, but the traversal/free ordering is what the UAF fix targets.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the code dereferences and frees memory through pointers after the underlying traversal item/pair has been freed, matching use-after-free rather than a simple double free or leak.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the traversal frees list items while retaining and reusing pointers (parent_pair) into the same structures, and pair objects are freed based on a subnodes->first check. Trigger: merging crafted ObjMRTrees whose subnode lists drive the traversal. Consequence: freed memory is dereferenced on later iterations, enabling crash or potentially code execution as described.

commit_msg:
Add str len check in config_sortlist to avoid stack overflow

In ares_set_sortlist, it calls config_sortlist(..., sortstr) to parse
the input str and initialize a sortlist configuration.

However, ares_set_sortlist has not any checks about the validity of the input str.
It is very easy to create an arbitrary length stack overflow with the unchecked
`memcpy(ipbuf, str, q-str);` and `memcpy(ipbufpfx, str, q-str);`
statements in the config_sortlist call, which could potentially cause severe
security impact in practical programs.

This commit add necessary check for `ipbuf` and `ipbufpfx` which avoid the
potential stack overflows.

fixes #496

Signed-off-by: hopper-vul <hopper.vul@gmail.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['      if (q-str >= 16)', '        return ARES_EBADSTR;', '          if (q-str >= 32)', '            return ARES_EBADSTR;']}
description: A flaw was found in the c-ares package. The ares_set_sortlist is missing checks about the validity of the input string, which allows a possible arbitrary length stack overflow. This issue may cause a denial of service or a limited impact on confidentiality and integrity.

code_evidence: ipbuf and ipbufpfx are fixed 16- and 32-byte stack buffers. q advances over the token, then memcpy(ipbuf, str, q-str) copies q-str bytes with no bound check; ipbuf[q-str]='\0' writes at that offset.
For the '/' prefix branch, q advances again and memcpy(ipbufpfx, str, q-str) copies a length that can exceed 32; ipbufpfx[q-str]='\0' is likewise unbounded.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The input specifies a token length that is used directly as a copy quantity, and the code fails to validate that this quantity fits the destination. CWE-1284 covers improper validation of a specified quantity in input; the unchecked length is the root cause of the overflow.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The parser accepts a caller-supplied sort string without validating the length of each IP/prefix token. A long token makes q-str exceed the destination buffer size, so the memcpy and terminating NUL write past the stack buffers, causing a stack overflow (crash/DoS and potential memory corruption).

commit_msg:
Fixed OOB read in ntlm_av_pair_get

CVE-2020-11097 thanks to @antonio-morales for finding this.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\twhile (pAvPair && ntlm_av_pair_get_id(pAvPair) != MsvAvEOL)', '\t\tWLog_INFO(TAG, "\\t%s AvId: %" PRIu16 " AvLen: %" PRIu16 "",', '\t\t          AV_PAIR_STRINGS[ntlm_av_pair_get_id(pAvPair)], ntlm_av_pair_get_id(pAvPair),', '\t\t          ntlm_av_pair_get_len(pAvPair));', '\t\twinpr_HexDump(TAG, WLOG_INFO, ntlm_av_pair_get_value_pointer(pAvPair),', '\t\t              ntlm_av_pair_get_len(pAvPair));'], 'added_lines': ['\tUINT16 pair;', '\twhile (pAvPair && ntlm_av_pair_get_id(pAvPair, cbAvPair, &pair) && (pair != MsvAvEOL))', '\t\tsize_t cbLen = 0;', '\t\tntlm_av_pair_get_len(pAvPair, cbAvPair, &cbLen);', '', '\t\tWLog_INFO(TAG, "\\t%s AvId: %" PRIu16 " AvLen: %" PRIu16 "", get_av_pair_string(pair), pair);', '\t\twinpr_HexDump(TAG, WLOG_INFO, ntlm_av_pair_get_value_pointer(pAvPair), cbLen);']}
description: In FreeRDP before version 2.1.2, an out of bounds read occurs resulting in accessing a memory location that is outside of the boundaries of the static array PRIMARY_DRAWING_ORDER_FIELD_BYTES. This is fixed in version 2.1.2.

code_evidence: The loop condition calls ntlm_av_pair_get_id(pAvPair) without passing the remaining buffer size cbAvPair, so the AV-pair id is read from pAvPair with no bounds check against the buffer end.

The id returned is used directly to index the static AV_PAIR_STRINGS array and to read length/value via ntlm_av_pair_get_len and ntlm_av_pair_get_value_pointer, none validating that the id or length stay within the buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the function reads memory past the end of the supplied AV-pair buffer, matching the fixed OOB read. It is not CWE-787 since no write past bounds occurs; the defect is an unchecked read.

evidence_lines.code: while (pAvPair && ntlm_av_pair_get_id(pAvPair) != MsvAvEOL)

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the loop reads the AV-pair id and length from pAvPair without validating them against the remaining cbAvPair bytes. Trigger: a truncated or malformed AV-pair list where pAvPair points near the buffer end. Consequence: out-of-bounds reads of the AV-pair header, the AV_PAIR_STRINGS lookup, and the dumped value.

commit_msg: fixed #1785 (fuzz)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tif (op->layer_count > GF_ARRAY_LENGTH(op->layers_info))'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (op->layer_count > GF_ARRAY_LENGTH(op->layers_info)) {', '\t\t\tgf_free(op);', '\t\t}']}
description: Memory leak in the gf_isom_oinf_read_entry function in MP4Box in GPAC 1.0.1 allows attackers to read memory via a crafted file.

code_evidence: Line 23 allocates an LHEVC_OperatingPoint with GF_SAFEALLOC(op, ...). Line 24 returns GF_OUT_OF_MEM if allocation fails (no leak there). Line 28 checks op->layer_count against GF_ARRAY_LENGTH(op->layers_info); when the check fails, line 29 returns GF_NON_COMPLIANT_BITSTREAM without freeing op. The allocation is never added to ptr->operating_points (that only happens at line 52), so the only reference to op is lost on this early return.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function allocates memory and returns on an error condition without releasing it, exactly the error-condition cause of CWE-401. It is not a buffer overflow: the range check itself is present and correct; the defect is the missing gf_free(op) before the early return.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the error path on an out-of-range attacker-controlled layer_count abandons the heap object allocated at line 23. Trigger: a crafted file whose 8-bit layer_count exceeds the layers_info array length. Consequence: each such read leaks an LHEVC_OperatingPoint, so repeated parsing of malformed input exhausts memory (resource-consumption DoS).

commit_msg:
libnsgif: Fix null pointer deref on frameless GIF input

A crafted GIF file with no frame data could cause a null pointer
dereference leading to denial of service (crash). Reported by
@JieyongMa via huntr.dev.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '        /* If the GIF has no frame data, frame holders will not be allocated in', '         * gif_initialise() */', '        if (gif->frames == NULL) {', '                return GIF_INSUFFICIENT_DATA;', '        }']}
description: chafa: NULL Pointer Dereference in function gif_internal_decode_frame at libnsgif.c:599 allows attackers to cause a denial of service (crash) via a crafted input file. in GitHub repository hpjansson/chafa prior to 1.10.2. chafa: NULL Pointer Dereference in function gif_internal_decode_frame at libnsgif.c:599 allows attackers to cause a denial of service (crash) via a crafted input file.

code_evidence: The function immediately indexes gif->frames[frame] to test display without first checking that gif->frames is non-NULL.
A second unchecked access reads gif->frames[frame] inside the frame_count_partial bound test.
gif->frames[frame].frame_pointer is dereferenced to compute gif_data, and the same array is used later at the exit label for virgin/opaque handling.
The cleanup block at gif_decode_frame_exit unconditionally reads and writes gif->frames[frame] fields.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is a direct NULL pointer dereference (CWE-476): the code reads through gif->frames without a null check, and the patch adds exactly that guard. This is distinct from an out-of-bounds index, since the pointer itself is NULL rather than the index being invalid.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: gif_internal_decode_frame assumes gif->frames was allocated, but for a crafted GIF with no frame data gif_initialise leaves it NULL. commit_msg:
libceph: harden msgr2.1 frame segment length checks

ceph_frame_desc::fd_lens is an int array.  decode_preamble() thus
effectively casts u32 -> int but the checks for segment lengths are
written as if on unsigned values.  While reading in HELLO or one of the
AUTH frames (before authentication is completed), arithmetic in
head_onwire_len() can get duped by negative ctrl_len and produce
head_len which is less than CEPH_PREAMBLE_LEN but still positive.
This would lead to a buffer overrun in prepare_read_control() as the
preamble gets copied to the newly allocated buffer of size head_len.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: cd1a677cad99 ("libceph, ceph: implement msgr2.1 protocol (crc and secure modes)")
Reported-by: Thelford Williams <thelford@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Ilya Dryomov <idryomov@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Xiubo Li <xiubli@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\tBUG_ON(ctrl_len < 0 || ctrl_len > CEPH_MSG_MAX_CONTROL_LEN);']}
description: An issue was discovered in net/ceph/messenger_v2.c in the Linux kernel before 6.4.5. There is an integer signedness error, leading to a buffer overflow and remote code execution via HELLO or one of the AUTH frames. This occurs because of an untrusted length taken from a TCP packet in ceph_decode_32.

code_evidence: head_onwire_len() derives head_len from the untrusted ctrl_len: in the non-secure path it adds ctrl_len + CEPH_CRC_LEN to CEPH_PREAMBLE_PLAIN_LEN, and in the secure path it computes rem_len = ctrl_len - CEPH_PREAMBLE_INLINE_LEN and adds padded_len(rem_len). No check constrains ctrl_len before these arithmetic operations, and the resulting head_len is returned for use as the allocation size for the preamble copy.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function supplies an unchecked, attacker-influenced size that governs a subsequent buffer copy, matching CWE-120's 'buffer copy without checking size of input.' CWE-131 (size calculation error) is the immediate arithmetic flaw, but the supported consequence is the classic copy overflow, so CWE-120 fits the target.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: ctrl_len is an untrusted int that can be negative, so the length arithmetic produces a small positive head_len even though a larger control segment is later copied. Trigger: a crafted HELLO or AUTH frame received before authentication. Consequence: prepare_read_control() copies the preamble into an undersized buffer, causing a buffer overflow that can modify memory and potentially enable remote code execution.

commit_msg: check error code on call to gf_utf8_wcstombs (#1177)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tif (i >= (u32)ARRAY_LENGTH(szLineConv))', '\t\treturn NULL;']}
description: In GPAC 0.7.1 and earlier, gf_text_get_utf8_line in media_tools/text_import.c in libgpac_static.a allows an out-of-bounds write because a certain -1 return value is mishandled.

code_evidence: sptr is cast from szLine and passed to gf_utf8_wcstombs, which writes converted bytes into the fixed 1024-byte stack buffer szLineConv and returns a count in i. Line 72 then writes szLineConv[i] = 0 without checking i against the buffer size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs a write at an unchecked index derived from external input length, which is an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). The flaw is the missing length constraint before the store, not merely an integer conversion issue; the write past szLineConv is the directly supported weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the return value of gf_utf8_wcstombs is used directly as an index into szLineConv[1024] with no bounds check. Trigger: a UTF-16 input line whose converted UTF-8 form reaches or exceeds 1024 bytes (or the function returns -1, cast to u32), making i out of range. Consequence: the terminating NUL write at szLineConv[i] occurs out of bounds, corrupting stack memory and potentially enabling crash or code execution.

commit_msg:
vhdx: Bounds checking for block_size and logical_sector_size (CVE-2014-0148)

Other variables (e.g. sectors_per_block) are calculated using these
variables, and if not range-checked illegal values could be obtained
causing infinite loops and other potential issues when calculating
BAT entries.

The 1.00 VHDX spec requires BlockSize to be min 1MB, max 256MB.
LogicalSectorSize is required to be either 512 or 4096 bytes.

Reported-by: Kevin Wolf <kwolf@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Jeff Cody <jcody@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Kevin Wolf <kwolf@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Max Reitz <mreitz@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Stefan Hajnoczi <stefanha@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if (s->logical_sector_size == 0 || s->params.block_size == 0) {', '        ret = -EINVAL;', '        goto exit;', '    }', '', '    /* both block_size and sector_size are guaranteed powers of 2 */'], 'added_lines': ['    if (s->params.block_size < VHDX_BLOCK_SIZE_MIN ||', '        s->params.block_size > VHDX_BLOCK_SIZE_MAX) {', '        ret = -EINVAL;', '        goto exit;', '    }', '', '    /* only 2 supported sector sizes */', '    if (s->logical_sector_size != 512 && s->logical_sector_size != 4096) {', '        ret = -EINVAL;', '        goto exit;', '    }', '', '    /* Both block_size and sector_size are guaranteed powers of 2, below.', '       Due to range checks above, s->sectors_per_block can never be < 256 */']}
description: Qemu before 2.0 block driver for Hyper-V VHDX Images is vulnerable to infinite loops and other potential issues when calculating BAT entries, due to missing bounds checks for block_size and logical_sector_size variables. These are used to derive other fields like 'sectors_per_block' etc. A user able to alter the Qemu disk image could ise this flaw to crash the Qemu instance resulting in DoS.

code_evidence: Lines 141-144 only reject zero values for logical_sector_size and block_size, so any nonzero value passes without an upper/lower bound (e.g. block_size far below 1MB or logical_sector_size not 512/4096).
Line 145 computes sectors_per_block = block_size / logical_sector_size from these unvalidated attacker-controlled values.
Lines 146-148 compute chunk_ratio using the same unchecked block_size and logical_sector_size as divisors, so an out-of-range value can yield zero or otherwise degenerate ratios.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing bounds checks produce derived loop bounds that can never be satisfied, matching CWE-835's unreachable exit condition. This is not merely an integer overflow (CWE-190); the supported consequence is non-terminating iteration.

evidence_lines.code: s->sectors_per_block = s->params.block_size / s->logical_sector_size;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The metadata-read values block_size and logical_sector_size are attacker-controlled and only checked for being nonzero, not for range. Derived fields such as sectors_per_block and chunk_ratio can therefore take illegal values (e.g. zero or non-power-of-two), which later BAT-entry calculation loops use as iteration bounds, leading to an unreachable exit condition and CPU/memory exhaustion (DoS). The root cause is the missing range constraint; the infinite loop is the consequence.

commit_msg:
Fix NULL deference when validating FFC public key.

Fixes CVE-2023-0217

When attempting to do a BN_Copy of params->p there was no NULL check.
Since BN_copy does not check for NULL this is a NULL reference.

As an aside BN_cmp() does do a NULL check, so there are other checks
that fail because a NULL is passed. A more general check for NULL params
has been added for both FFC public and private key validation instead.

Reviewed-by: Matt Caswell <matt@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Paul Dale <pauli@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Tomas Mraz <tomas@openssl.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    if (params == NULL || pub_key == NULL || params->p == NULL) {', '        *ret = FFC_ERROR_PASSED_NULL_PARAM;', '        return 0;', '    }', '']}
description:
An invalid pointer dereference on read can be triggered when an
application tries to check a malformed DSA public key by the
EVP_PKEY_public_check() function. This will most likely lead
to an application crash. This function can be called on public
keys supplied from untrusted sources which could allow an attacker
to cause a denial of service attack.

The TLS implementation in OpenSSL does not call this function
but applications might call the function if there are additional
security requirements imposed by standards such as FIPS 140-3.

code_evidence: Line 7 initializes *ret but performs no validation of the params, pub_key or params->p arguments before use. Line 16 passes pub_key directly to BN_cmp, and line 20 passes params->p directly to BN_copy without a NULL check. If params->p is NULL, BN_copy dereferences it; the commit confirms BN_copy does not guard against NULL.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits because the function dereferences a pointer (params->p via BN_copy) that it assumes valid but may be NULL, producing a crash. This is a NULL dereference (availability impact), not a buffer over-read or arithmetic flaw, so the Base-level CWE-476 mapping is appropriate.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function trusts caller-supplied FFC parameters and public key to be non-NULL and dereferences them (params->p at line 20, pub_key at line 16) without validation. Trigger: an application calls EVP_PKEY_public_check() on a malformed/untrusted DSA public key whose params->p is NULL. Consequence: a NULL pointer dereference causes an application crash, enabling denial of service.

commit_msg:
Propagate allocation failure from ogg_sync_buffer.

Instead of segfault, report OP_EFAULT if ogg_sync_buffer returns
a null pointer. This allows more graceful recovery by the caller
in the unlikely event of a fallible ogg_malloc call.

We do check the return value elsewhere in the code, so the new
checks make the code more consistent.

Thanks to https://github.com/xiph/opusfile/issues/36 for reporting.

Signed-off-by: Timothy B. Terriberry <tterribe@xiph.org>
Signed-off-by: Mark Harris <mark.hsj@gmail.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  if(OP_UNLIKELY(buffer==NULL))return OP_EFAULT;']}
description: A null pointer dereference issue was discovered in functions op_get_data and op_open1 in opusfile.c in xiph opusfile 0.9 thru 0.12 allows attackers to cause denial of service or other unspecified impacts.

code_evidence: Line 5 assigns the result of ogg_sync_buffer to buffer without a null check in the pre-patch code. Line 6 immediately passes buffer to the read callback, which dereferences and writes through it, so a NULL return from ogg_sync_buffer flows directly into a pointer dereference.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits because a pointer expected to be valid is NULL and is dereferenced without a check. This is a direct NULL dereference, not a general bounds or integer issue; the added check confirms the missing constraint on buffer.

evidence_lines.code:
buffer=(unsigned char *)ogg_sync_buffer(&_of->oy,_nbytes);
nbytes=(int)(*_of->callbacks.read)(_of->stream,buffer,_nbytes);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the return value of ogg_sync_buffer is assumed non-NULL. Trigger: a failed allocation makes ogg_sync_buffer return NULL. Consequence: the read callback dereferences the NULL buffer, causing a crash (DoS) rather than a graceful OP_EFAULT.

commit_msg: Fixed oob read in irp_write and similar
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t\tnego_process_negotiation_response(nego, s);', '\t\t\t\tnego_process_negotiation_failure(nego, s);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t\tif (!nego_process_negotiation_response(nego, s))', '\t\t\t\t\treturn -1;', '\t\t\t\tif (!nego_process_negotiation_failure(nego, s))', '\t\t\t\t\treturn -1;']}
description: In FreeRDP before 2.1.0, there is an out-of-bound read in irp functions (parallel_process_irp_create, serial_process_irp_create, drive_process_irp_write, printer_process_irp_write, rdpei_recv_pdu, serial_process_irp_write). This has been fixed in 2.1.0.

code_evidence: After reading a length field li, the function only checks li > 6 before calling Stream_Read_UINT8 to read the type byte and dispatching to nego_process_negotiation_response on the stream; the return value is ignored.
The TYPE_RDP_NEG_FAILURE branch similarly calls nego_process_negotiation_failure without validating the return or that the stream holds the required negotiation payload.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is a read past the intended buffer: the missing length/return-value validation permits parsing of insufficient data. This matches CWE-125; it is not an out-of-bounds write because only reads of stream fields occur.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function trusts the transport-provided length li and invokes negotiation parsers on the stream without confirming sufficient remaining bytes or checking parser failure. A truncated or malformed negotiation PDU triggers the parsers to read past the stream buffer, yielding an out-of-bounds read (possible crash or memory disclosure).

commit_msg:
Block Verification Vulnerability Eliminated

Fixed a critical vulnerability allowing to accept a proof-of-work block
containing one or more coin stake transactions in addition to a valid

description: A vulnerability has been found in ghostlander Halcyon and classified as critical. Affected by this vulnerability is the function CBlock::AddToBlockIndex of the file src/main.cpp of the component Block Verification. The manipulation leads to improper access controls. The attack can be launched remotely. Upgrading to version 1.1.1.0-hal is able to address this issue. The identifier of the patch is 0675b25ae9cc10b5fdc8ea3a32c642979762d45e. It is recommended to upgrade the affected component. The identifier VDB-217417 was assigned to this vulnerability.

code_evidence: The proof-of-work branch at [4,5,6,7,8,9] only verifies the PoW hash and block signature; it never inspects vtx[1..] for coinstake transactions, so a PoW block may carry arbitrary coin stakes.

The coinstake restriction loop at [19,20,21,22,23,24,25,26,27] runs only inside the IsProofOfStake() branch, so PoW blocks bypass the 'more than one coinstake' and coinstake-placement checks entirely.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-284 fits because the function fails to enforce an access/validity restriction on which transaction types may appear in a PoW block, letting a peer include privileged coinstake transactions the policy intends to exclude.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the block-verification policy that forbids coinstake transactions in proof-of-work blocks is enforced only under IsProofOfStake(), so the PoW path accepts blocks containing coin stakes. Trigger: a remote peer submits a PoW block whose vtx includes coinbase plus one or more coinstake transactions. Consequence: those coin stakes are accepted with out-of-control output values, bypassing the intended transaction-placement policy.

description: An issue was discovered in libbzip3.a in bzip3 before 1.2.3. There is an xwrite out-of-bounds read.

code_evidence: crc32sum takes buf and size from the caller and iterates while (size--), dereferencing *(buf++) on each iteration; the loop reads size bytes from buf with no validation that buf actually spans size bytes. The function itself never checks the buffer length against size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the function reads memory beyond the intended buffer: the pointer increment in the loop is bounded only by size, not by the actual buffer extent, so an oversized size yields reads past the end. This is an out-of-bounds read, not a write (CWE-787) or a length-arithmetic error alone.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the loop bound is the caller-supplied size, and each iteration unconditionally reads *(buf++) without confirming that buf has at least size valid bytes. Trigger: a caller passing an inconsistent size relative to the allocated/valid buffer (the commit's stated buffer/block inconsistency) causes reads past the end of buf. Consequence: out-of-bounds read of adjacent memory, matching the reported xwrite out-of-bounds read, potentially leaking or crashing on the read data.

description: Integer Overflow vulnerability in mp_grow in libtom libtommath before commit beba892bc0d4e4ded4d667ab1d2a94f4d75109a9, allows attackers to execute arbitrary code and cause a denial of service (DoS).

code_evidence: digs is an int size/limit parameter consumed without any lower-bound check before being passed to mp_init_size and used as the digit count for the temporary mp_int.

t.used is set to digs, and digs bounds the inner loop via MP_MIN(b->used, digs - ix) and the write guard (ix + iy) < digs, so a negative or wrapped digs directly controls allocation size and digit writes.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because a signed int size value is used in calculations (allocation size, digs - ix, ix + iy) that assume it remains a valid positive magnitude; a negative or wrapped value breaks that assumption. This is an integer-overflow/wraparound size flaw, not merely a generic bounds check.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function trusts caller-supplied digs and derives allocation size and loop bounds from it without validating that it is non-negative. Trigger: a caller passing a negative or overflow-wrapped digs reaches mp_init_size and the digit loops. Consequence: undersized allocation combined with loop-bound arithmetic leads to out-of-bounds digit writes and memory corruption, with DoS or arbitrary code execution.

commit_msg:
unix: properly account for FDs passed over unix sockets

It is possible for a process to allocate and accumulate far more FDs than
the process' limit by sending them over a unix socket then closing them
to keep the process' fd count low.

This change addresses this problem by keeping track of the number of FDs
in flight per user and preventing non-privileged processes from having
more FDs in flight than their configured FD limit.

commit_msg:
Commit a23740ec43ba ("bpf: Track contents of read-only maps as scalars") is
checking whether maps are read-only both from BPF program side and user space
side, and then, given their content is constant, reading out their data via
map->ops->map_direct_value_addr() which is then subsequently used as known
scalar value for the register, that is, it is marked as __mark_reg_known()
with the read value at verification time. Before a23740ec43ba, the register
content was marked as an unknown scalar so the verifier could not make any
assumptions about the map content.

The current implementation however is prone to a TOCTOU race, meaning, the
value read as known scalar for the register is not guaranteed to be exactly
the same at a later point when the program is executed, and as such, the
prior made assumptions of the verifier with regards to the program will be
invalid which can cause issues such as OOB access, etc.

While the BPF_F_RDONLY_PROG map flag is always fixed and required to be
specified at map creation time, the map->frozen property is initially set to
false for the map given the map value needs to be populated, e.g. for global
data sections. Once complete, the loader "freezes" the map from user space
such that no subsequent updates/deletes are possible anymore. For the rest
of the lifetime of the map, this freeze one-time trigger cannot be undone
anymore after a successful BPF_MAP_FREEZE cmd return. Meaning, any new BPF_*
cmd calls which would update/delete map entries will be rejected with -EPERM
since map_get_sys_perms() removes the FMODE_CAN_WRITE permission. This also
means that pending update/delete map entries must still complete before this
guarantee is given. This corner case is not an issue for loaders since they
create and prepare such program private map in successive steps.

However, a malicious user is able to trigger this TOCTOU race in two different
ways: i) via userfaultfd, and ii) via batched updates. For i) userfaultfd is
used to expand the competition interval, so that map_update_elem() can modify
the contents of the map after map_freeze() and bpf_prog_load() were executed.
This works, because userfaultfd halts the parallel thread which triggered a
map_update_elem() at the time where we copy key/value from the user buffer and
this already passed the FMODE_CAN_WRITE capability test given at that time the
map was not "frozen". Then, the main thread performs the map_freeze() and
bpf_prog_load(), and once that had completed successfully, the other thread
is woken up to complete the pending map_update_elem() which then changes the
map content. For ii) the idea of the batched update is similar, meaning, when
there are a large number of updates to be processed, it can increase the
competition interval between the two. It is therefore possible in practice to
modify the contents of the map after executing map_freeze() and bpf_prog_load().

One way to fix both i) and ii) at the same time is to expand the use of the
map's map->writecnt. The latter was introduced in fc9702273e2e ("bpf: Add mmap()
support for BPF_MAP_TYPE_ARRAY") and further refined in 1f6cb19be2e2 ("bpf:
Prevent re-mmap()'ing BPF map as writable for initially r/o mapping") with
the rationale to make a writable mmap()'ing of a map mutually exclusive with
read-only freezing. The counter indicates writable mmap() mappings and then
prevents/fails the freeze operation. Its semantics can be expanded beyond
just mmap() by generally indicating ongoing write phases. This would essentially
span any parallel regular and batched flavor of update/delete operation and
then also have map_freeze() fail with -EBUSY. For the check_mem_access() in
the verifier we expand upon the bpf_map_is_rdonly() check ensuring that all
last pending writes have completed via bpf_map_write_active() test. Once the
map->frozen is set and bpf_map_write_active() indicates a map->writecnt of 0
only then we are really guaranteed to use the map's data as known constants.
For map->frozen being set and pending writes in process of still being completed
we fall back to marking that register as unknown scalar so we don't end up
making assumptions about it. With this, both TOCTOU reproducers from i) and
ii) are fixed.

Note that the map->writecnt has been converted into a atomic64 in the fix in
order to avoid a double freeze_mutex mutex_{un,}lock() pair when updating
map->writecnt in the various map update/delete BPF_* cmd flavors. Spanning
the freeze_mutex over entire map update/delete operations in syscall side
would not be possible due to then causing everything to be serialized.
Similarly, something like synchronize_rcu() after setting map->frozen to wait
for update/deletes to complete is not possible either since it would also
have to span the user copy which can sleep. On the libbpf side, this won't
break d66562fba1ce ("libbpf: Add BPF object skeleton support") as the
anonymous mmap()-ed "map initialization image" is remapped as a BPF map-backed
mmap()-ed memory where for .rodata it's non-writable.

Fixes: a23740ec43ba ("bpf: Track contents of read-only maps as scalars")
Reported-by: w1tcher.bupt@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>
Acked-by: Andrii Nakryiko <andrii@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (vma->vm_flags & VM_MAYWRITE) {', '\t\tmutex_lock(&map->freeze_mutex);', '\t\tmap->writecnt--;', '\t\tmutex_unlock(&map->freeze_mutex);', '\t}'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (vma->vm_flags & VM_MAYWRITE)', '\t\tbpf_map_write_active_dec(map);']}
description: A race condition was found in the Linux kernel's ebpf verifier between bpf_map_update_elem and bpf_map_freeze due to a missing lock in kernel/bpf/syscall.c. In this flaw, a local user with a special privilege (cap_sys_admin or cap_bpf) can modify the frozen mapped address space. This flaw affects kernel versions prior to 5.16 rc2.

code_evidence: On mmap close, bpf_map_mmap_close checks vma->vm_flags & VM_MAYWRITE and then decrements map->writecnt under freeze_mutex; this counter tracks in-flight writable operations that must reach zero before a map can be treated as frozen/read-only.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function is part of the mechanism whose state (writecnt/frozen) is checked before the map's data is trusted, while concurrent updates can change it between check and use, matching CWE-367. This is a race/TOCTOU rather than a simple missing-lock bug because the security impact comes from validating a resource then using it after its state changed.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The writecnt bookkeeping is only updated on mmap close; writable update/delete paths that begin while the map is not yet frozen can still be pending when the map is frozen and the verifier reads map contents as known scalars. The check of frozen state and the use of the map data are separated by a window in which writecnt does not yet reflect the pending write, so the verifier's assumptions become invalid, supporting OOB access.

commit_msg: OGRExpatRealloc(): fix double-free when size to allocate is above the default 10MB threshold. Fixes https://bugs.chromium.org/p/oss-fuzz/issues/detail?id=16178. Credit to OSS Fuzz
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    free(ptr);'], 'added_lines': []}
description: GDAL through 3.0.1 has a poolDestroy double free in OGRExpatRealloc in ogr/ogr_expat.cpp when the 10MB threshold is exceeded.

code_evidence: OGRExpatRealloc takes ownership of ptr. When CanAlloc(size) is true it returns realloc(ptr, size), which may free the old block on success or leave it allocated on failure. When CanAlloc(size) is false, line 5 unconditionally calls free(ptr) before returning nullptr. The caller retains no indication that ptr was freed, so the same address can be released again by the caller's cleanup path.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-415 is the direct fit: free(ptr) at line 5 releases an address the caller still owns and may free again. This is not a use-after-free, which would require a dereference of freed memory rather than a second release.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function frees ptr on the over-threshold path without transferring or nulling ownership, while the caller still treats ptr as live. Trigger: a reallocation request with size above the 10MB threshold. Consequence: the caller later frees the same address, producing a double free and possible heap corruption or arbitrary code execution.

disconnects while a WriteValue call is being processed with dbus.

This patch includes the addition of a pending disconnect callback to handle
cleanup better if a disconnect occurs during a write, an acquire write
or read operation using bt_att_register_disconnect with the cb.

+++ func_after
@@ -17,8 +17,8 @@

 	}
 
-	if (send_read(device, attrib, desc->proxy, desc->pending_reads, id,
-					offset, bt_att_get_link_type(att)))
+	if (send_read(att, attrib, desc->proxy, desc->pending_reads, id,
+					offset))
 		return;

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (send_read(device, attrib, desc->proxy, desc->pending_reads, id,', '\t\t\t\t\toffset, bt_att_get_link_type(att)))'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (send_read(att, attrib, desc->proxy, desc->pending_reads, id,', '\t\t\t\t\toffset))']}
description: An issue was discovered in gatt-database.c in BlueZ 5.61. A use-after-free can occur when a client disconnects during D-Bus processing of a WriteValue call.

code_evidence: The callback resolves the device from the bt_att pointer via att_get_device(att) and bails out when it is NULL, otherwise proceeds to send_read using the device object.
send_read is invoked with device and attribute state; if the client disconnects during D-Bus processing of the read, the underlying device/att may be torn down while this callback still runs.
On failure the code calls gatt_db_attribute_read_result using attrib/id, but no disconnect registration guards against the att/device being freed concurrently.

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the callback holds device/att references without a pending-disconnect guard, so a client disconnect during D-Bus read processing can free the underlying objects. Trigger: disconnect racing the read callback. Consequence: use-after-free of freed memory, leading to crash or memory corruption.

In summary, this patch solves those use-after-free by

1. Re-implement the nfc_llcp_find_local(). The current version does not
grab the reference when getting the local from the linked list.  For
example, the llcp_sock_bind() gets the reference like below:

// llcp_sock_bind()

    local = nfc_llcp_find_local(dev); // A
    ..... \
           | raceable
    ..... /
    llcp_sock->local = nfc_llcp_local_get(local); // B

There is an apparent race window that one can  drop the reference
and free the local object fetched in (A) before (B) gets the reference.

2. Some callers of the nfc_llcp_find_local() do not grab the reference
at all. For example, the nfc_genl_llc_{{get/set}_params/sdreq} functions.
We add the nfc_llcp_local_put() for them. Moreover, we add the necessary
error handling function to put the reference.

3. Add the nfc_llcp_remove_local() helper. The local object is removed
from the linked list in local_release() when all reference is gone. This
patch removes it when nfc_llcp_unregister_device() is called.

Therefore, every caller of nfc_llcp_find_local() will get a reference
even when the nfc_llcp_unregister_device() is called. This promises no
use-after-free for the local object is ever possible.

commit_msg:
ring-buffer: Prevent overflow of size in ring_buffer_resize()

If the size passed to ring_buffer_resize() is greater than MAX_LONG - BUF_PAGE_SIZE
then the DIV_ROUND_UP() will return zero.

Here's the details:

  # echo 18014398509481980 > /sys/kernel/debug/tracing/buffer_size_kb

tracing_entries_write() processes this and converts kb to bytes.

 18014398509481980 << 10 = 18446744073709547520

and this is passed to ring_buffer_resize() as unsigned long size.

 size = DIV_ROUND_UP(size, BUF_PAGE_SIZE);

Where DIV_ROUND_UP(a, b) is (a + b - 1)/b

BUF_PAGE_SIZE is 4080 and here

 18446744073709547520 + 4080 - 1 = 18446744073709551599

where 18446744073709551599 is still smaller than 2^64

 2^64 - 18446744073709551599 = 17

But now 18446744073709551599 / 4080 = 4521260802379792

and size = size * 4080 = 18446744073709551360

This is checked to make sure its still greater than 2 * 4080,
which it is.

Then we convert to the number of buffer pages needed.

 nr_page = DIV_ROUND_UP(size, BUF_PAGE_SIZE)

but this time size is 18446744073709551360 and

 2^64 - (18446744073709551360 + 4080 - 1) = -3823

Thus it overflows and the resulting number is less than 4080, which makes

  3823 / 4080 = 0

an nr_pages is set to this. As we already checked against the minimum that
nr_pages may be, this causes the logic to fail as well, and we crash the
kernel.

There's no reason to have the two DIV_ROUND_UP() (that's just result of
historical code changes), clean up the code and fix this bug.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # 3.5+
Fixes: 83f40318dab00 ("ring-buffer: Make removal of ring buffer pages atomic")
Signed-off-by: Steven Rostedt <rostedt@goodmis.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tsize = DIV_ROUND_UP(size, BUF_PAGE_SIZE);', '\tsize *= BUF_PAGE_SIZE;', '\tif (size < BUF_PAGE_SIZE * 2)', '\t\tsize = BUF_PAGE_SIZE * 2;', '\tnr_pages = DIV_ROUND_UP(size, BUF_PAGE_SIZE);'], 'added_lines': ['\tnr_pages = DIV_ROUND_UP(size, BUF_PAGE_SIZE);', '\tif (nr_pages < 2)', '\t\tnr_pages = 2;', '\tsize = nr_pages * BUF_PAGE_SIZE;']}
description: The ring_buffer_resize function in kernel/trace/ring_buffer.c in the profiling subsystem in the Linux kernel before 4.6.1 mishandles certain integer calculations, which allows local users to gain privileges by writing to the /sys/kernel/debug/tracing/buffer_size_kb file.

code_evidence: The caller-supplied unsigned long size is transformed by DIV_ROUND_UP(size, BUF_PAGE_SIZE) and multiplied by BUF_PAGE_SIZE before any bound check. For sizes near ULONG_MAX, the addition a+b-1 inside DIV_ROUND_UP wraps, and the later round-up at line 16 can collapse to zero nr_pages despite the minimum-page check at line 14.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs integer calculations that wrap for large inputs and then uses the wrapped result as a page count, which is CWE-190. It is not a plain bounds check miss; the arithmetic itself produces the incorrect small value.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is unchecked arithmetic on an attacker-controlled size: the round-up and multiply overflow, so nr_pages becomes 0 or a tiny value after the size < 2*BUF_PAGE_SIZE guard passes. This zero nr_pages drives the page-update logic to a bogus state, crashing the kernel; the trigger is a large buffer_size_kb write.

description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. An attacker can trigger a denial of service via a `CHECK` failure by passing an empty image to `tf.raw_ops.DrawBoundingBoxes`. This is because the implementation(https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/ea34a18dc3f5c8d80a40ccca1404f343b5d55f91/tensorflow/core/kernels/image/draw_bounding_box_op.cc#L148-L165) uses `CHECK_*` assertions instead of `OP_REQUIRES` to validate user controlled inputs. Whereas `OP_REQUIRES` allows returning an error condition back to the user, the `CHECK_*` macros result in a crash if the condition is false, similar to `assert`. In this case, `height` is 0 from the `images` input. This results in `max_box_row_clamp` being negative and the assertion being falsified, followed by aborting program execution. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.5.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.4.2, TensorFlow 2.3.3, TensorFlow 2.2.3 and TensorFlow 2.1.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: height and width come from the user-supplied images tensor (lines 17-18); box coordinates are scaled by (height - 1) and (width - 1) (lines 56-62), so an empty image makes these dimensions 0 and the scaled clamps negative.

The function does guard against boxes outside the image (lines 75-81), but the subsequent CHECK_GE(max_box_row_clamp, 0) and CHECK_LT(min_box_row_clamp, height) assertions (lines 83-85) assume the clamp values are valid and abort if not.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The code fails to properly check an unusual but attacker-reachable condition (zero-sized image dimensions) and instead asserts, matching CWE-754's improper check for exceptional conditions leading to a crash. This is not a bounds/overflow flaw but a missing graceful validation of an unexpected input state.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: user-controlled image dimensions are used to compute box clamps, but the code validates them with CHECK_* assertions that abort instead of returning an error. Trigger: an empty image (height or width 0) makes max_box_row_clamp negative, falsifying CHECK_GE at line 84. Consequence: the process aborts, giving a denial of service from a single malformed input.

commit_msg:
vfs: ioctl: prevent double-fetch in dedupe ioctl

This prevents a double-fetch from user space that can lead to to an
undersized allocation and heap overflow.

Fixes: 54dbc1517237 ("vfs: hoist the btrfs deduplication ioctl to the vfs")
Signed-off-by: Scott Bauer <sbauer@plzdonthack.me>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tsame->dest_count = count;']}
description: Race condition in the ioctl_file_dedupe_range function in fs/ioctl.c in the Linux kernel through 4.7 allows local users to cause a denial of service (heap-based buffer overflow) or possibly gain privileges by changing a certain count value, aka a "double fetch" vulnerability.

code_evidence: The function reads dest_count from user memory via get_user into local count, which is then used to size the allocation and memdup_user copy.
size is computed from the local count and passed to memdup_user, which copies the whole user structure including a possibly different dest_count field.
vfs_dedupe_file_range is then called on the copied structure whose dest_count was not synchronized with the count used for allocation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The root cause is a double-fetch race: a shared user-memory value is read non-atomically across two operations without synchronization, letting an interfering thread modify it. This concurrent modification of shared resource state matches CWE-362.

evidence_lines.code:
size = offsetof(struct file_dedupe_range __user, info[count]);
same = memdup_user(argp, size);
ret = vfs_dedupe_file_range(file, same);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The count is fetched once into a local variable for allocation sizing, but the user-supplied structure is re-read by memdup_user, so a concurrent user thread can change dest_count between the two reads. The copied structure can then advertise a larger dest_count than the allocation supports, and vfs_dedupe_file_range trusts that field, producing the undersized-allocation heap overflow.

commit_msg: Fix a crash bug with bogus text (Issue #426)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ["\tif (t->data[strlen((char *)t->data) - 1] == '\\n')"], 'added_lines': ["\tif (t->data[0] && t->data[strlen((char *)t->data) - 1] == '\\n')"]}
description: HTMLDoc v1.9.15 was discovered to contain a heap overflow via (write_header) /htmldoc/htmldoc/html.cxx:273.

code_evidence: In the preformatted branch, t->data is iterated until '\0' and then strlen((char *)t->data) - 1 is used to index t->data[16]. If t->data is an empty string, strlen returns 0, so the index becomes (size_t)-1, an out-of-bounds read before the buffer; the added guard t->data[0] prevents this underflow.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect is an unchecked index that can address before the start of the intended buffer, matching CWE-787's out-of-bounds access scope. The fix adds t->data[0] before the length-based index, confirming the empty-string boundary condition; this is a boundary/indexing error rather than a length-truncation weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the length-1 index is computed without checking that the string is non-empty. Trigger: a preformatted node whose data is an empty string reaches line 16. Consequence: the index underflows to a huge unsigned value, reading before the allocated buffer, which can crash the process (the reported heap-related crash).

description: fs/f2fs/segment.c in the Linux kernel before 4.13 allows local users to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference and panic) by using a noflush_merge option that triggers a NULL value for a flush_cmd_control data structure.

The missing constraint (no '..' rejection) is the cause; the out-of-directory file open is the consequence, not the cause.

Fix out of bounds access
