commit_msg:
tracing/syscalls: Ignore numbers outside NR_syscalls' range

ARM has some private syscalls (for example, set_tls(2)) which lie
outside the range of NR_syscalls.  If any of these are called while
syscall tracing is being performed, out-of-bounds array access will
occur in the ftrace and perf sys_{enter,exit} handlers.

 # trace-cmd record -e raw_syscalls:* true && trace-cmd report
 ...
 true-653   [000]   384.675777: sys_enter:            NR 192 (0, 1000, 3, 4000022, ffffffff, 0)
 true-653   [000]   384.675812: sys_exit:             NR 192 = 1995915264
 true-653   [000]   384.675971: sys_enter:            NR 983045 (76f74480, 76f74000, 76f74b28, 76f74480, 76f76f74, 1)
 true-653   [000]   384.675988: sys_exit:             NR 983045 = 0
 ...

 # trace-cmd record -e syscalls:* true
 [   17.289329] Unable to handle kernel paging request at virtual address aaaaaace
 [   17.289590] pgd = 9e71c000
 [   17.289696] [aaaaaace] *pgd=00000000
 [   17.289985] Internal error: Oops: 5 [#1] PREEMPT SMP ARM
 [   17.290169] Modules linked in:
 [   17.290391] CPU: 0 PID: 704 Comm: true Not tainted 3.18.0-rc2+ #21
 [   17.290585] task: 9f4dab00 ti: 9e710000 task.ti: 9e710000
 [   17.290747] PC is at ftrace_syscall_enter+0x48/0x1f8
 [   17.290866] LR is at syscall_trace_enter+0x124/0x184

Fix this by ignoring out-of-NR_syscalls-bounds syscall numbers.

Commit cd0980fc8add "tracing: Check invalid syscall nr while tracing syscalls"
added the check for less than zero, but it should have also checked
for greater than NR_syscalls.

Link: http://lkml.kernel.org/p/1414620418-29472-1-git-send-email-rabin@rab.in

Fixes: cd0980fc8add "tracing: Check invalid syscall nr while tracing syscalls"
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # 2.6.33+
Signed-off-by: Rabin Vincent <rabin@rab.in>
Signed-off-by: Steven Rostedt <rostedt@goodmis.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (syscall_nr < 0)'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (syscall_nr < 0 || syscall_nr >= NR_syscalls)']}
description: kernel/trace/trace_syscalls.c in the Linux kernel through 3.17.2 does not properly handle private syscall numbers during use of the perf subsystem, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read and OOPS) or bypass the ASLR protection mechanism via a crafted application.

commit_msg:
Reported as

  https://bugs.chromium.org/p/oss-fuzz/issues/detail?id=941
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '    /* in malformed fonts it can happen that a contour was started */', '    /* but no points were added                                    */', '    if ( outline->n_contours && first == outline->n_points )', '    {', '      outline->n_contours--;', '      return;', '    }']}
description: FreeType 2 before 2017-03-26 has an out-of-bounds write caused by a heap-based buffer overflow related to the t1_builder_close_contour function in psaux/psobjs.c.

code_evidence: first is derived from the previous contour's end index (or 0 when there is at most one contour); no check ensures first remains within the point array when a contour was started but no points were added.
The block guarded only by n_contours > 0 compares first with n_points - 1 and otherwise writes outline->contours[n_contours - 1] = n_points - 1, without verifying that first < n_points.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs point/contour array accesses and a write without enforcing that first and n_points stay within the allocated outline buffers, which is an operation outside the intended memory buffer boundary. CWE-119 fits; the more specific heap overflow is a consequence of this missing bound check.

evidence_lines.code:
first = outline->n_contours <= 1
? 0 : outline->contours[outline->n_contours - 2] + 1;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: a malformed font can start a contour without adding points, so first equals n_points (or exceeds the valid range). The code then indexes outline->points + first at line 12 and writes the contour end index at line 27 based on inconsistent point counts, producing an out-of-bounds read/write on the heap.

commit_msg:
x86/spec-ctrl: Mitigate the Zen1 DIV leakage

In the Zen1 microarchitecure, there is one divider in the pipeline which
services uops from both threads.  In the case of #DE, the latched result from
the previous DIV to execute will be forwarded speculatively.

This is an interesting covert channel that allows two threads to communicate
without any system calls.  In also allows userspace to obtain the result of
the most recent DIV instruction executed (even speculatively) in the core,
which can be from a higher privilege context.

Scrub the result from the divider by executing a non-faulting divide.  This
needs performing on the exit-to-guest paths, and ist_exit-to-Xen.

Alternatives in IST context is believed safe now that it's done in NMI
context.

This is XSA-439 / CVE-2023-20588.

Signed-off-by: Andrew Cooper <andrew.cooper3@citrix.com>
Reviewed-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>

commit_msg:
Added a bunch of `assert(b)`'s to address CVE-2018-17073
See https://github.com/wernsey/bitmap/issues/1
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tassert(b);']}
description: wernsey/bitmap before 2018-08-18 allows a NULL pointer dereference via a 4-bit image.

code_evidence: Line 4 dereferences b via b->font without first verifying that b itself is non-NULL.
Line 6 calls b->font->width(b->font), again relying on b being valid before any null check.
Line 21 returns max_len * glyph_width, but the function cannot be reached safely if b is NULL.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits because the code reads a pointer member through a pointer it assumes valid but never checks, and the patch adds assert(b) at function entry to guard exactly this dereference.

evidence_lines.code: if(!b->font || !b->font->width)
glyph_width = b->font->width(b->font);
return max_len * glyph_width;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function dereferences its Bitmap pointer b (b->font on line 4 and b->font->width on line 6) without validating that b is non-NULL. Trigger: a caller passes a NULL Bitmap, as reported for 4-bit images. Consequence: a NULL pointer dereference causing a crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
In __htab_map_lookup_and_delete_batch(), hash buckets are iterated
over to count the number of elements in each bucket (bucket_size).
If bucket_size is large enough, the multiplication to calculate
kvmalloc() size could overflow, resulting in out-of-bounds write
as reported by KASAN:

  [...]
  [  104.986052] BUG: KASAN: vmalloc-out-of-bounds in __htab_map_lookup_and_delete_batch+0x5ce/0xb60
  [  104.986489] Write of size 4194224 at addr ffffc9010503be70 by task crash/112
  [  104.986889]
  [  104.987193] CPU: 0 PID: 112 Comm: crash Not tainted 5.14.0-rc4 #13
  [  104.987552] Hardware name: QEMU Standard PC (i440FX + PIIX, 1996), BIOS 1.13.0-1ubuntu1.1 04/01/2014
  [  104.988104] Call Trace:
  [  104.988410]  dump_stack_lvl+0x34/0x44
  [  104.988706]  print_address_description.constprop.0+0x21/0x140
  [  104.988991]  ? __htab_map_lookup_and_delete_batch+0x5ce/0xb60
  [  104.989327]  ? __htab_map_lookup_and_delete_batch+0x5ce/0xb60
  [  104.989622]  kasan_report.cold+0x7f/0x11b
  [  104.989881]  ? __htab_map_lookup_and_delete_batch+0x5ce/0xb60
  [  104.990239]  kasan_check_range+0x17c/0x1e0
  [  104.990467]  memcpy+0x39/0x60
  [  104.990670]  __htab_map_lookup_and_delete_batch+0x5ce/0xb60
  [  104.990982]  ? __wake_up_common+0x4d/0x230
  [  104.991256]  ? htab_of_map_free+0x130/0x130
  [  104.991541]  bpf_map_do_batch+0x1fb/0x220
  [...]

In hashtable, if the elements' keys have the same jhash() value, the
elements will be put into the same bucket. By putting a lot of elements
into a single bucket, the value of bucket_size can be increased to
trigger the integer overflow.

Triggering the overflow is possible for both callers with CAP_SYS_ADMIN
and callers without CAP_SYS_ADMIN.

It will be trivial for a caller with CAP_SYS_ADMIN to intentionally
reach this overflow by enabling BPF_F_ZERO_SEED. As this flag will set
the random seed passed to jhash() to 0, it will be easy for the caller
to prepare keys which will be hashed into the same value, and thus put
all the elements into the same bucket.

If the caller does not have CAP_SYS_ADMIN, BPF_F_ZERO_SEED cannot be
used. However, it will be still technically possible to trigger the
overflow, by guessing the random seed value passed to jhash() (32bit)
and repeating the attempt to trigger the overflow. In this case,
the probability to trigger the overflow will be low and will take
a very long time.

Fix the integer overflow by calling kvmalloc_array() instead of
kvmalloc() to allocate memory.

Fixes: 057996380a42 ("bpf: Add batch ops to all htab bpf map")
Signed-off-by: Tatsuhiko Yasumatsu <th.yasumatsu@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/bpf/20210806150419.109658-1-th.yasumatsu@gmail.com
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tkeys = kvmalloc(key_size * bucket_size, GFP_USER | __GFP_NOWARN);', '\tvalues = kvmalloc(value_size * bucket_size, GFP_USER | __GFP_NOWARN);'], 'added_lines': ['\tkeys = kvmalloc_array(key_size, bucket_size, GFP_USER | __GFP_NOWARN);', '\tvalues = kvmalloc_array(value_size, bucket_size, GFP_USER | __GFP_NOWARN);']}
description: In kernel/bpf/hashtab.c in the Linux kernel through 5.13.8, there is an integer overflow and out-of-bounds write when many elements are placed in a single bucket. NOTE: exploitation might be impractical without the CAP_SYS_ADMIN capability.

code_evidence: bucket_size starts at 5 and is reallocated via kvmalloc(key_size * bucket_size, ...) and kvmalloc(value_size * bucket_size, ...); the multiplication is performed in 32-bit u32 before the size is passed to the allocator.
When a bucket's element count exceeds bucket_size, bucket_size is set to bucket_cnt and the function jumps back to alloc, so a large bucket_cnt directly feeds the multiplication.
The loop then memcpy's key_size bytes per element and advances dst_key by key_size, dst_val by value_size for each element, writing bucket_cnt entries into the undersized buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The allocation-size multiplication overflows a 32-bit integer before allocation, exactly CWE-190; the out-of-bounds write is the downstream consequence, not a separate weakness. The fix switches to kvmalloc_array, which checks the multiplication, confirming the overflow is the defect.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: key_size * bucket_size and value_size * bucket_size are computed as u32 without overflow checking, so an attacker-influenced bucket_cnt can wrap the product to a small allocation size. Trigger: many colliding keys placed in one hash bucket raise bucket_size. Consequence: the following memcpy loop writes bucket_cnt elements into a small kvmalloc buffer, causing an out-of-bounds write.

commit_msg:
gnttab: correct maptrack table accesses

In order to observe a consistent (limit,pointer-table) pair, the reader
needs to either hold the maptrack lock (in line with documentation) or
both sides need to order their accesses suitably (the writer side
barrier was removed by commit dff515dfea ["gnttab: use per-VCPU
maptrack free lists"], and a read side barrier has never been there).

Make the writer publish a new table page before limit (for bounds
checks to work), and new list head last (for racing maptrack_entry()
invocations to work). At the same time add read barriers to lockless
readers.

Additionally get_maptrack_handle() must not assume ->maptrack_head to
not change behind its back: Another handle may be put (updating only
->maptrack_tail) and then got or stolen (updating ->maptrack_head).

This is part of XSA-218.

Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Reviewed-by: George Dunlap <george.dunlap@citrix.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['        smp_rmb();']}
description: The grant-table feature in Xen through 4.8.x provides false mapping information in certain cases of concurrent unmap calls, which allows backend attackers to obtain sensitive information or gain privileges, aka XSA-218 bug 1.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function only scans maptrack entries for map kind; it contains no free() or deallocation operation, so it cannot demonstrate a double free (CWE-415).

commit_msg:
Avoid a read off-by-one error for UTF16 names in RAR archives.

Reported-By: OSS-Fuzz issue 573
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ["      filename[filename_size++] = '\\0';"], 'added_lines': ['      /*', '       * Do not increment filename_size here as the computations below', '       * add the space for the terminating NUL explicitly.', '       */', "      filename[filename_size] = '\\0';"]}
description: read_header in archive_read_support_format_rar.c in libarchive 3.3.2 suffers from an off-by-one error for UTF-16 names in RAR archives, leading to an out-of-bounds read in archive_read_format_rar_read_header.

code_evidence: The UTF-16 branch sets fn_end = filename_size * 2 and resets filename_size = 0, then writes decoded bytes into filename while the loop condition only bounds filename_size < fn_end.
After the loop, lines 207-208 write two NUL bytes at filename[filename_size++] twice, so the final write can land at index fn_end+1, one past the intended capacity of filename_size*2+2.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The root cause is an incorrect maximum: the termination space is added twice relative to the bound fn_end, yielding a one-byte overrun. This is a classic CWE-193 off-by-one error rather than a generic buffer overflow, since the flaw is the miscalculated boundary.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The buffer is sized filename_size*2+2 to hold the decoded UTF-16 bytes plus a two-byte terminator, but the loop can fill up to fn_end bytes and the post-loop code appends two more bytes starting at that boundary. This off-by-one writes past the allocated buffer, causing a heap out-of-bounds write reachable via a crafted RAR UTF-16 filename.

commit_msg:
mnt: Add a per mount namespace limit on the number of mounts

CAI Qian <caiqian@redhat.com> pointed out that the semantics
of shared subtrees make it possible to create an exponentially
increasing number of mounts in a mount namespace.

    mkdir /tmp/1 /tmp/2
    mount --make-rshared /
    for i in $(seq 1 20) ; do mount --bind /tmp/1 /tmp/2 ; done

Will create create 2^20 or 1048576 mounts, which is a practical problem
as some people have managed to hit this by accident.

As such CVE-2016-6213 was assigned.

Ian Kent <raven@themaw.net> described the situation for autofs users
as follows:

> The number of mounts for direct mount maps is usually not very large because of
> the way they are implemented, large direct mount maps can have performance
> problems. There can be anywhere from a few (likely case a few hundred) to less
> than 10000, plus mounts that have been triggered and not yet expired.
>
> Indirect mounts have one autofs mount at the root plus the number of mounts that
> have been triggered and not yet expired.
>
> The number of autofs indirect map entries can range from a few to the common
> case of several thousand and in rare cases up to between 30000 and 50000. I've
> not heard of people with maps larger than 50000 entries.
>
> The larger the number of map entries the greater the possibility for a large
> number of active mounts so it's not hard to expect cases of a 1000 or somewhat
> more active mounts.

So I am setting the default number of mounts allowed per mount
namespace at 100,000.  This is more than enough for any use case I
know of, but small enough to quickly stop an exponential increase
in mounts.  Which should be perfect to catch misconfigurations and
malfunctioning programs.

For anyone who needs a higher limit this can be changed by writing
to the new /proc/sys/fs/mount-max sysctl.

Tested-by: CAI Qian <caiqian@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: "Eric W. Biederman" <ebiederm@xmission.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\treturn 0;'], 'added_lines': ['\treturn count_mounts(m->mnt_ns, child);']}
description: fs/namespace.c in the Linux kernel before 4.9 does not restrict how many mounts may exist in a mount namespace, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (memory consumption and deadlock) via MS_BIND mount system calls, as demonstrated by a loop that triggers exponential growth in the number of mounts.

code_evidence: propagate_one() calls copy_tree() to allocate a new mount (child) for each propagated mount, links it via mnt_set_mountpoint() and hlist_add_head(), then returns 0 unconditionally. The function performs no check on the number of mounts already in m->mnt_ns before creating another child, so each invocation grows the namespace's mount count without any throttling.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function fails to control allocation/maintenance of a limited resource (mounts per namespace), matching CWE-400's lack of throttling for allocated resources. The fix replaces the unconditional return 0 with count_mounts(), confirming the missing count/limit is the specific defect, not a separate memory-safety issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the mount-propagation path unconditionally allocates and links a new mount without consulting any per-namespace mount limit. Trigger: a local user performs repeated MS_BIND mounts on a shared subtree, causing exponential propagation; each propagate_one() call adds another mount. Supported consequence: unbounded memory consumption and possible deadlock in the mount namespace (DoS).

commit_msg:
crypto: user - fix leaking uninitialized memory to userspace

All bytes of the NETLINK_CRYPTO report structures must be initialized,
since they are copied to userspace.  The change from strncpy() to
strlcpy() broke this.  As a minimal fix, change it back.

Fixes: 4473710df1f8 ("crypto: user - Prepare for CRYPTO_MAX_ALG_NAME expansion")
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org> # v4.12+
Signed-off-by: Eric Biggers <ebiggers@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Herbert Xu <herbert@gondor.apana.org.au>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tstrlcpy(ualg->cru_name, alg->cra_name, sizeof(ualg->cru_name));', '\tstrlcpy(ualg->cru_driver_name, alg->cra_driver_name,', '\tstrlcpy(ualg->cru_module_name, module_name(alg->cra_module),', '\t\tstrlcpy(rl.type, "larval", sizeof(rl.type));'], 'added_lines': ['\tstrncpy(ualg->cru_name, alg->cra_name, sizeof(ualg->cru_name));', '\tstrncpy(ualg->cru_driver_name, alg->cra_driver_name,', '\tstrncpy(ualg->cru_module_name, module_name(alg->cra_module),', '\t\tstrncpy(rl.type, "larval", sizeof(rl.type));']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel before 4.19.3. crypto_report_one() and related functions in crypto/crypto_user.c (the crypto user configuration API) do not fully initialize structures that are copied to userspace, potentially leaking sensitive memory to user programs. NOTE: this is a CVE-2013-2547 regression but with easier exploitability because the attacker does not need a capability (however, the system must have the CONFIG_CRYPTO_USER kconfig option).

code_evidence: Lines 4–8 copy alg->cra_name, alg->cra_driver_name and module_name into the ualg fields using strlcpy with the full field size, which zero-fills the remainder of each destination field. Lines 16–20 declare a local struct crypto_report_larval rl and fill rl.type via strlcpy before nla_put copies the whole struct to the netlink skb; strlcpy guarantees the tail bytes are initialized, whereas a bounded non-zero-filling copy would leave them uninitialized. The ualg structure and rl are subsequently delivered to userspace through the netlink skb.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function builds structures that are explicitly sent to userspace; incomplete initialization means kernel memory contents leak to an unauthorized actor, matching CWE-200's exposure of sensitive information. This is the intended confidentiality failure, not a buffer overflow: the copies are size-bounded and the issue is the missing zero-fill that the strlcpy calls provide.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the report structures are copied to userspace in full, so every byte must be initialized. The strlcpy calls are what ensure trailing bytes of cru_name, cru_driver_name, cru_module_name and rl.type are zeroed; replacing them with a copy that does not pad (as the commit message states was done) leaves uninitialized stack/struct memory. Trigger: a user requests a crypto algorithm report via NETLINK_CRYPTO. Consequence: uninitialized kernel memory is disclosed to the unprivileged userspace caller.

commit_msg:
loop: fix concurrent lo_open/lo_release

范龙飞 reports that KASAN can report a use-after-free in __lock_acquire.
The reason is due to insufficient serialization in lo_release(), which
will continue to use the loop device even after it has decremented the
lo_refcnt to zero.

In the meantime, another process can come in, open the loop device
again as it is being shut down. Confusion ensues.

Reported-by: 范龙飞 <long7573@126.com>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tstruct loop_device *lo = disk->private_data;', '\tint err;', '', '\tif (atomic_dec_return(&lo->lo_refcnt))', '\t\treturn;', '', '\tmutex_lock(&lo->lo_ctl_mutex);', '\tif (lo->lo_flags & LO_FLAGS_AUTOCLEAR) {', '\t\t/*', '\t\t * In autoclear mode, stop the loop thread', '\t\t * and remove configuration after last close.', '\t\t */', '\t\terr = loop_clr_fd(lo);', '\t\tif (!err)', '\t\t\treturn;', '\t} else if (lo->lo_state == Lo_bound) {', '\t\t/*', '\t\t * Otherwise keep thread (if running) and config,', '\t\t * but flush possible ongoing bios in thread.', '\t\t */', '\t\tblk_mq_freeze_queue(lo->lo_queue);', '\t\tblk_mq_unfreeze_queue(lo->lo_queue);', '\t}', '', '\tmutex_unlock(&lo->lo_ctl_mutex);'], 'added_lines': ['\tmutex_lock(&loop_index_mutex);', '\t__lo_release(disk->private_data);', '\tmutex_unlock(&loop_index_mutex);']}
description: In the Linux kernel through 4.14.13, drivers/block/loop.c mishandles lo_release serialization, which allows attackers to cause a denial of service (__lock_acquire use-after-free) or possibly have unspecified other impact.

code_evidence: lo_release decrements lo_refcnt and returns early when other references remain; only the final close proceeds to mutex_lock(&lo->lo_ctl_mutex). The decrement uses atomic_dec_return, but the subsequent check of lo_flags/lo_state and the loop_clr_fd teardown occur under lo_ctl_mutex, not under the lock that serializes device open/registration.

When the last reference is dropped, the code calls loop_clr_fd(lo) if LO_FLAGS_AUTOCLEAR is set and returns without unlocking only on success; a concurrent open can re-acquire the loop device while this teardown uses lo, so the reference count reaching zero is not an exclusive point.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function contains a concurrent sequence needing exclusive access to shared loop-device state, but a timing window lets another code sequence (open) interfere after lo_refcnt hits zero. This is improper synchronization, i.e., CWE-362; the use-after-free is the resulting consequence, not the labeled weakness itself.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the reference-count decrement and subsequent teardown are not serialized against concurrent loop-device open, so lo_refcnt reaching zero does not guarantee exclusive ownership of lo. Trigger: one thread closes the last reference while another opens the same loop device; the teardown path then uses a structure being reconfigured, leading to use-after-free and KASAN __lock_acquire crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
avcodec/apedec: Fix integer overflow

Fixes: out of array access
Fixes: PoC.ape and others

Found-by: Bingchang, Liu@VARAS of IIE
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        if (!nblocks || nblocks > INT_MAX) {', '    av_fast_malloc(&s->decoded_buffer, &s->decoded_size,', '                   2 * FFALIGN(blockstodecode, 8) * sizeof(*s->decoded_buffer));'], 'added_lines': ['    uint64_t decoded_buffer_size;', '        if (!nblocks || nblocks > INT_MAX / 2 / sizeof(*s->decoded_buffer) - 8) {', '    decoded_buffer_size = 2LL * FFALIGN(blockstodecode, 8) * sizeof(*s->decoded_buffer);', '    av_assert0(decoded_buffer_size <= INT_MAX);', '    av_fast_malloc(&s->decoded_buffer, &s->decoded_size, decoded_buffer_size);']}
description: Integer overflow in the ape_decode_frame function in libavcodec/apedec.c in FFmpeg 2.4 through 3.3.2 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-array access and application crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted APE file.

code_evidence: The decoded_buffer allocation size is computed as 2 * FFALIGN(blockstodecode, 8) * sizeof(*s->decoded_buffer) in 32-bit arithmetic; a large blockstodecode can wrap this product, allocating a smaller buffer than the subsequent pointer setup at lines 82-83 and the per-sample writes in the 8/16/24-bit loops expect.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The overflowed allocation leaves the decoded sample buffer too small for the indices derived from blockstodecode, so the decode/packing loops read and write outside the intended buffer, matching CWE-125 out-of-bounds read (with the integer overflow as the enabling cause).
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the buffer-size multiplication in the av_fast_malloc call overflows, so s->decoded_buffer is allocated smaller than 2*FFALIGN(blockstodecode,8) int32 elements. Trigger: a crafted APE file yielding a large blockstodecode. Consequence: s->decoded[1] and the decode loops index beyond the allocation, causing out-of-bounds access and crash.

commit_msg:
ARM: 7735/2: Preserve the user r/w register TPIDRURW on context switch and fork

Since commit 6a1c53124aa1 the user writeable TLS register was zeroed to
prevent it from being used as a covert channel between two tasks.

There are more and more applications coming to Windows RT,
Wine could support them, but mostly they expect to have
the thread environment block (TEB) in TPIDRURW.

This patch preserves that register per thread instead of clearing it.
Unlike the TPIDRURO, which is already switched, the TPIDRURW
can be updated from userspace so needs careful treatment in the case that we
modify TPIDRURW and call fork(). To avoid this we must always read
TPIDRURW in copy_thread.

Signed-off-by: André Hentschel <nerv@dawncrow.de>
Signed-off-by: Will Deacon <will.deacon@arm.com>
Signed-off-by: Jonathan Austin <jonathan.austin@arm.com>
Signed-off-by: Russell King <rmk+kernel@arm.linux.org.uk>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tthread->tp_value = childregs->ARM_r3;'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tthread->tp_value[0] = childregs->ARM_r3;', '\tthread->tp_value[1] = get_tpuser();']}
description: The Linux kernel before 3.11 on ARM platforms, as used in Android before 2016-08-05 on Nexus 5 and 7 (2013) devices, does not properly consider user-space access to the TPIDRURW register, which allows local users to gain privileges via a crafted application, aka Android internal bug 28749743 and Qualcomm internal bug CR561044.

code_evidence: When CLONE_SETTLS is set, the child's TPIDRURW value is taken from childregs->ARM_r3, a user-controlled register copied from current_pt_regs() at line 9; the user-writable TPIDRURW register itself is not preserved across fork.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-264 covers weaknesses in managing permissions and privileges used for access control. Here improper handling of a user-space register that controls per-thread TLS state enables privilege escalation, matching that category.

evidence_lines.code:
if (clone_flags & CLONE_SETTLS)
thread->tp_value = childregs->ARM_r3;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: fork copies the user TLS value from the ARM_r3 argument rather than reading the user-writable TPIDRURW register, so the per-thread value is not faithfully carried over. A local user can supply a crafted TLS value via clone/fork, and the child inherits a stale or zeroed TPIDRURW, which the description states can be leveraged to gain privileges.

commit_msg:
Prevent division by 0

PiperOrigin-RevId: 370995582
Change-Id: I670ffaf52d1ff8823ec31ea5f438f9125b402223
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  TF_LITE_ENSURE(context, rank != 0);']}
description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. The implementation of the `SVDF` TFLite operator is vulnerable to a division by zero error(https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/7f283ff806b2031f407db64c4d3edcda8fb9f9f5/tensorflow/lite/kernels/svdf.cc#L99-L102). An attacker can craft a model such that `params->rank` would be 0. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.5.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.4.2, TensorFlow 2.3.3, TensorFlow 2.2.3 and TensorFlow 2.1.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: Line 17 reads rank from attacker-controlled model parameters (params->rank). Line 20 performs num_filters % rank, and line 21 computes num_filters / rank without first verifying rank is nonzero, so a crafted model with rank == 0 reaches a modulo/division by zero in Prepare.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-369 (Divide By Zero) directly matches: the function divides (and takes modulo) by the unvalidated rank value, which an attacker can set to zero. This is a missing-input-validation divide-by-zero, not an out-of-bounds or integer-overflow issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the rank parameter from builtin_data is used as a divisor (modulo at line 20, division at line 21) without a nonzero check. Trigger: a crafted TFLite SVDF model whose params->rank is 0. Consequence: divide-by-zero during model preparation, crashing the interpreter (DoS).

commit_msg:
media: xirlink_cit: add missing descriptor sanity checks

Make sure to check that we have two alternate settings and at least one
endpoint before accessing the second altsetting structure and
dereferencing the endpoint arrays.

This specifically avoids dereferencing NULL-pointers or corrupting
memory when a device does not have the expected descriptors.

Note that the sanity check in cit_get_packet_size() is not redundant as
the driver is mixing looking up altsettings by index and by number,
which may not coincide.

Fixes: 659fefa0eb17 ("V4L/DVB: gspca_xirlink_cit: Add support for camera with a bcd version of 0.01")
Fixes: 59f8b0bf3c12 ("V4L/DVB: gspca_xirlink_cit: support bandwidth changing for devices with 1 alt setting")
Cc: stable <stable@vger.kernel.org>     # 2.6.37
Cc: Hans de Goede <hdegoede@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Johan Hovold <johan@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Hans Verkuil <hverkuil-cisco@xs4all.nl>
Signed-off-by: Mauro Carvalho Chehab <mchehab+huawei@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\talt = &gspca_dev->dev->actconfig->intf_cache[0]->altsetting[1];'], 'added_lines': ['\tstruct usb_interface_cache *intfc;', '\tintfc = gspca_dev->dev->actconfig->intf_cache[0];', '', '\tif (intfc->num_altsetting < 2)', '\t\treturn -ENODEV;', '', '\talt = &intfc->altsetting[1];', '', '\tif (alt->desc.bNumEndpoints < 1)', '\t\treturn -ENODEV;', '']}
description: In the Linux kernel before 5.6.1, drivers/media/usb/gspca/xirlink_cit.c (aka the Xirlink camera USB driver) mishandles invalid descriptors, aka CID-a246b4d54770.

code_evidence: Line 16 unconditionally dereferences intf_cache[0]->altsetting[1] without verifying that a second alternate setting exists; line 17 then accesses endpoint[0] without checking that the selected altsetting declares at least one endpoint.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked descriptor-derived pointer is dereferenced as if guaranteed valid, matching CWE-476's NULL pointer dereference. The missing bounds checks on descriptor counts are the cause; the dereference of a NULL/invalid pointer is the consequence.

evidence_lines.code:
alt = &gspca_dev->dev->actconfig->intf_cache[0]->altsetting[1];
alt->endpoint[0].desc.wMaxPacketSize = cpu_to_le16(max_packet_size);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the driver assumes the USB device exposes two altsettings and an endpoint, but these are attacker/device-controlled descriptors. A device with fewer altsettings or zero endpoints makes the altsetting[1] or endpoint[0] access invalid, causing a NULL/invalid-pointer dereference and kernel crash (DoS) when sd_isoc_init runs.

commit_msg:
Fix heap OOB read in macho.iterate_chained_fixups ##crash

* Reported by peacock-doris via huntr.dev
* Reproducer 'tests_65305'

mrmacete:
* Return early if segs_count is 0
* Initialize segs_count also for reconstructed fixups

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    tsize_t buffersize,', '                if( *bufferoffset + 2 > buffersize )', '                    return(0);', '                    if( *bufferoffset + datalen + 2 + 6 > buffersize )', '                        return(0);', '                    if( *bufferoffset + 9 >= buffersize )', '                        return(0);', '                    if( *bufferoffset + 11 + 3*(ncomp-1) >= buffersize )', '                        return(0);', '                if( *bufferoffset + datalen + 2 > buffersize )', '                    return(0);', '                    if( *bufferoffset + datalen + 2 > buffersize )', '                        return(0);', '                    if( *bufferoffset + 2 > buffersize )', '                        return(0);', '                if( *bufferoffset + *striplength - i > buffersize )', '                    return(0);']}
description: tif_pixarlog.c in libtiff 4.0.6 has out-of-bounds write vulnerabilities in heap allocated buffers. Reported as MSVR 35094, aka "PixarLog horizontalDifference heap-buffer-overflow."

code_evidence: The function copies 2 bytes into buffer at the caller-controlled *bufferoffset without checking remaining capacity.

A datalen+2 memcpy is performed, then six more bytes are appended via buffer[(*bufferoffset)++]; *bufferoffset is advanced only after the datalen copy, and the appended bytes plus reads at offsets +9 and +11 assume the buffer holds datalen+2+6 bytes.
DHT/DQT copies datalen+2 bytes at *bufferoffset with no bounds check.
SOS copies datalen+2 bytes, or appends 2 marker bytes, then copies *striplength - i remaining bytes, all with no capacity check.
The trailing memcpy writes *striplength - i bytes past *bufferoffset.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The writes at lines 34, 43-74, 79-80, 84-89 and 92-93 go past the end of the intended buffer because no capacity bound is enforced, directly matching CWE-787 (out-of-bounds write). It is not merely an over-read or integer issue; the defect manifests as memory writes beyond the allocated region.

evidence_lines.code:
_TIFFmemcpy(&(buffer[*bufferoffset]), &(strip[i-1]), 2);
*bufferoffset+=2;

_TIFFmemcpy(&(buffer[*bufferoffset]), &(strip[i-1]), datalen+2);
*bufferoffset+=datalen+2;

_TIFFmemcpy(&(buffer[*bufferoffset]), &(strip[i]), *striplength - i);
*bufferoffset+= *striplength - i;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function writes into a caller-supplied heap buffer using attacker-influenced datalen and *striplength values but never compares *bufferoffset against the buffer's size. Trigger: a crafted JPEG strip whose segments or trailing data exceed the allocated output buffer causes _TIFFmemcpy and byte stores to write beyond it. Consequence: heap out-of-bounds write, corrupting adjacent memory (crash or potential code execution).

description: In GPAC 2.1-DEV-rev87-g053aae8-master, function BS_ReadByte() in utils/bitstream.c has a failed assertion, which causes a Denial of Service. This vulnerability was fixed in commit 9ea93a2.

code_evidence: The function reads counts from the bitstream (scalability_mask at line 6, count at line 7, u16 count at line 20, u8 count at line 56) and uses them to bound loops that repeatedly call gf_bs_read_* without checking whether the bitstream is exhausted.
Bounds checks exist only on layer_count and num_layers_dependent_on (lines 28-31, 63-66); nothing validates the stream position after the reads in the loops at lines 8-19, 21-55 and 57-74.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is a reachable assertion: attacker-controlled bitstream data causes an internal assert to fire, terminating the application. This matches CWE-617 (availability impact from an assert) rather than a memory-corruption CWE, since the supported consequence is a crash/exit, not out-of-bounds write.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: bitstream reads in the entry-parsing loops are not guarded by a stream-overflow check, so truncated or malformed input drives gf_bs_read_* past the buffer. The trigger is a crafted oinf box whose declared counts or fixed fields exceed the available data; the read past end reaches the assertion in BS_ReadByte(), aborting the process (DoS). The added gf_bs_is_overflow guards in the patch confirm this reachable assertion path.

description: Sigil before 0.9.16 is vulnerable to a directory traversal, allowing attackers to write arbitrary files via a ../ (dot dot slash) in a ZIP archive entry that is mishandled during extraction.

code_evidence: Archive entry name is read from the ZIP into file_name via unzGetCurrentFileInfo64 [22] and converted to qfile_name [25]. The name is used unchecked to build file_path = m_ExtractedFolderPath + "/" + qfile_name [31], then directories are created [37] and the file is opened for writing [48,49].

joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-22 fits because external archive input constructs a pathname intended to stay under a restricted extraction directory, but "../" elements are not neutralized, allowing resolution outside that directory. joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: attacker-controlled ZIP entry names containing "../" are concatenated onto the extraction root without normalization or containment checks, so the resulting path can resolve outside the target folder. commit_msg:
KGDB and KDB allow read and write access to kernel memory, and thus
should be restricted during lockdown.  An attacker with access to a
serial port (for example, via a hypervisor console, which some cloud
vendors provide over the network) could trigger the debugger so it is
important that the debugger respect the lockdown mode when/if it is
triggered.

Fix this by integrating lockdown into kdb's existing permissions
mechanism.  Unfortunately kgdb does not have any permissions mechanism
(although it certainly could be added later) so, for now, kgdb is simply
and brutally disabled by immediately exiting the gdb stub without taking
any action.

For lockdowns established early in the boot (e.g. the normal case) then
this should be fine but on systems where kgdb has set breakpoints before
the lockdown is enacted than "bad things" will happen.

commit_msg:
app: fix #8120 GIMP 2.10.30 crashed when allocate large memory

GIMP could crash if the information regarding old path properties read
from XCF was incorrect. It did not check if xcf_old_path succeeded and
kept trying to load more paths even if the last one failed to load.

Instead we now stop loading paths as soon as that function fails.
In case we have a failure here we also try to skip to the next property
based on the size of the path property, in hopes that the only problem
was this property.

description: Buffer Overflow vulnerability in OpenImageIO oiio v.2.4.12.0 allows a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code and cause a denial of service via the read_subimage_data function.

code_evidence: The colormap pointer is taken from either the local or global GIF color map, but its palette size is never recorded or checked against pixel values.

Each pixel byte fscanline[wx] is used directly as an index into colormap without any bound check; the loop only validates the destination x coordinate and transparency, then reads colormap[fscanline[wx]] and writes to m_canvas[idx..idx+3].
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 is the target, but the code most directly performs an unchecked out-of-bounds access on colormap via fscanline[wx]; the missing upper-bound constraint on the palette index is the defect the patch adds (colormap_count check). The write to m_canvas is bounded by x/y checks, so the write-out-of-bounds aspect is weaker; the index-driven memory access is the concrete flaw.

if (m_gif_file->Image.ColorMap) {          colormap = m_gif_file->Image.ColorMap->Colors;
} else if (m_gif_file->SColorMap) {          colormap = m_gif_file->SColorMap->Colors;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: fscanline[wx] is an attacker-controlled palette index used to index colormap with no verification that it is below the color map's ColorCount. A crafted GIF supplying an index at or above the palette size triggers an out-of-bounds read of colormap; the subsequent writes to m_canvas at idx are not themselves bounded by the palette value, so the primary supported consequence is an out-of-bounds read of the color table (and potential downstream memory corruption/DoS).

commit_msg:
tools/xenstore: create_node: Don't defer work to undo any changes on failure

XSA-115 extended destroy_node() to update the node accounting for the
connection. The implementation is assuming the connection is the parent
of the node, however all the nodes are allocated using a separate context
(see process_message()). This will result to crash (or corrupt) xenstored
as the pointer is wrongly used.

In case of an error, any changes to the database or update to the
accounting will now be reverted in create_node() by calling directly
destroy_node(). This has the nice advantage to remove the loop to unset
the destructors in case of success.

Take the opportunity to free the nodes right now as they are not
going to be reachable (the function returns NULL) and are just wasting
resources.

This is XSA-414 / CVE-2022-42309.

Fixes: 0bfb2101f243 ("tools/xenstore: fix node accounting after failed node creation")
Signed-off-by: Julien Grall <jgrall@amazon.com>
Reviewed-by: Juergen Gross <jgross@suse.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tstruct node *node, *i;', '\t\t\terrno = ENOSPC;', '\t\t\treturn NULL;', '\t\tif (write_node(conn, i, false))', '\t\t\treturn NULL;', '\t\t/* Account for new node, set destructor for error case. */', '\t\tif (i->parent) {', '\t\t\ttalloc_set_destructor(i, destroy_node);', '\t\t}', '\t/* OK, now remove destructors so they stay around */', '\tfor (i = node; i->parent; i = i->parent)', '\t\ttalloc_set_destructor(i, NULL);'], 'added_lines': ['\tstruct node *node, *i, *j;', '\tint ret;', '\t\t\tret = ENOSPC;', '\t\t\tgoto err;', '\t\tret = write_node(conn, i, false);', '\t\tif (ret)', '\t\t\tgoto err;', '', '\t\t/* Account for new node */', '\t\tif (i->parent)', '', 'err:', '\t/*', '\t * We failed to update TDB for some of the nodes. Undo any work that', '\t * have already been done.', '\t */', '\tfor (j = node; j != i; j = j->parent)', '\t\tdestroy_node(conn, j);', '', "\t/* We don't need to keep the nodes around, so free them. */", '\ti = node;', '\twhile (i) {', '\t\tj = i;', '\t\ti = i->parent;', '\t\ttalloc_free(j);', '\t}', '', '\terrno = ret;', '', '\treturn NULL;']}
description: Xenstore: Guests can crash xenstored Due to a bug in the fix of XSA-115 a malicious guest can cause xenstored to use a wrong pointer during node creation in an error path, resulting in a crash of xenstored or a memory corruption in xenstored causing further damage. Entering the error path can be controlled by the guest e.g. by exceeding the quota value of maximum nodes per domain.

code_evidence: On the success path, each new node with a parent increments accounting via domain_entry_inc and installs destroy_node as its talloc destructor, so destruction later routes through destroy_node(conn, i).
The destructors are then cleared only up to the first node lacking a parent (loop condition i->parent), leaving the top node's destructor in place while returning node to the caller.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The code installs a release routine (destroy_node) for nodes allocated in a different context than the connection it assumes, so destruction operates on an invalid pointer/reference rather than the correct owner. This is incorrect use of the release function, matching CWE-763; it is not merely a mismatched allocator/free pair (CWE-762).

evidence_lines.code:
for (i = node; i->parent; i = i->parent)
talloc_set_destructor(i, NULL);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: destroy_node is registered as the talloc destructor for nodes created under a separate context, but destroy_node assumes the connection is the node's parent and dereferences that wrong pointer. Trigger: a guest forces the error path (e.g. exceeding the per-domain node quota) after some nodes were accounted and tagged. Consequence: xenstored crashes or corrupts memory when the destructor runs against an invalid parent reference.

commit_msg:
patch 9.0.2112: [security]: overflow in shift_line

Problem:  [security]: overflow in shift_line
Solution: allow a max indent of INT_MAX

[security]: overflow in shift_line

When shifting lines in operator pending mode and using a very large
value, we may overflow the size of integer. Fix this by using a long
variable, testing if the result would be larger than INT_MAX and if so,
indent by INT_MAX value.

Special case: We cannot use long here, since on 32bit architectures (or
on Windows?), it typically cannot take larger values than a plain int,
so we have to use long long count, decide whether the resulting
multiplication of the shiftwidth value * amount is larger than INT_MAX
and if so, we will store INT_MAX as possible larges value in the long
long count variable.

Then we can safely cast it back to int when calling the functions to set
the indent (set_indent() or change_indent()). So this should be safe.

Add a test that when using a huge value in operator pending mode for
shifting, we will shift by INT_MAX

closes: #13535

Signed-off-by: Christian Brabandt <cb@256bit.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    int\t\tcount;', '    count = get_indent();\t// get current indent', '\t    count += sw_val * amount;', '\tchange_indent(INDENT_SET, count, FALSE, NUL, call_changed_bytes);', '\t(void)set_indent(count, call_changed_bytes ? SIN_CHANGED : 0);'], 'added_lines': ['    long long\tcount;', '    count = (long long)get_indent();\t// get current indent', '\t{', '\t    if ((long long)sw_val * (long long)amount > INT_MAX - count)', '\t\tcount = INT_MAX;', '\t    else', '\t\tcount += (long long)sw_val * (long long)amount;', '\t}', '\tchange_indent(INDENT_SET, (int)count, FALSE, NUL, call_changed_bytes);', '\t(void)set_indent((int)count, call_changed_bytes ? SIN_CHANGED : 0);']}
description: Vim is an open source command line text editor. In affected versions when shifting lines in operator pending mode and using a very large value, it may be possible to overflow the size of integer. Impact is low, user interaction is required and a crash may not even happen in all situations. This issue has been addressed in commit `6bf131888` which has been included in version 9.0.2112. Users are advised to upgrade. There are no known workarounds for this vulnerability.

code_evidence: Line 7 declares count as a plain int, and line 10 assigns get_indent() to it. On lines 26 and 31 the code computes count -= sw_val * amount and count += sw_val * amount, multiplying two ints and accumulating the result into int count with no overflow check. The resulting count is then passed as the int indent value to change_indent (line 34) and set_indent (line 36).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the function performs an unchecked integer multiplication and accumulation that can wrap when a large shift amount is supplied, and the wrapped value is used as the indent. This is a direct integer overflow, not a separate memory-safety flaw such as a buffer overflow (CWE-120), since no length copy is involved.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the shift amount and shiftwidth are multiplied and added to the current indent in int arithmetic. Trigger: operator-pending shifting with a very large amount, causing the product or the accumulated count to exceed INT_MAX and wrap. Consequence: a corrupted, typically negative or small indent value is passed to set_indent/change_indent, producing incorrect buffer state and possible crash; impact is limited to availability/integrity of the edit session.

The call's result is then used at 75-79.

The root cause is the missing size constraint between buffer capacity and realpath's PATH_MAX expectation; this is a buffer-bounds violation rather than merely an unchecked return value.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the buffer size passed to realpath is not matched to the fixed 1024-byte stack buffer on non-Apple POSIX systems. When realpath resolves a path longer than 1024 bytes, it writes past the stack array's intended boundary, producing an out-of-bounds stack write. Trigger: a long input path reaching the typeImage branch. Consequence: memory corruption potentially leading to code execution or crash.

commit_msg:
Fix invalid memory accesses while loading .a2m files

Missing checks and wrong calculations in src/a2m.cpp cause
multiple heap-based buffer overflows and out-of-bounds reads
in heap, stack, and static data.

Bugs addressed in this commit:
* Check the number of patterns. Too big values can cause reads
  past the end of the len array.
* Reading a not packed data block with odd length will allocate
  a buffer which is one byte too small and write past the end
  of it (issue #88). Change the allocation/deallocation code
  to fix that in both places.
* Check that data blocks (afer unpacking if applicable) are big
  enough for the expected data before accessing the memory.
* Ensure that the length byte for author, song name, and instrument
  names doesn't exceed the maximum size available.
* Also change the accessor functions for these strings to call
  the proper std::string constructors for char arrays.
* Avoid reads past the end of convfx/newconvfx arrays while
  converting track data.

This commit fixes CVE-2019-14732.

Fixes: https://github.com/adplug/adplug/issues/88

description: TensorFlow is an open source platform for machine learning. Prior to versions 2.9.0, 2.8.1, 2.7.2, and 2.6.4, the implementation of `tf.raw_ops.UnsortedSegmentJoin` does not fully validate the input arguments. This results in a `CHECK`-failure which can be used to trigger a denial of service attack. The code assumes `num_segments` is a positive scalar but there is no validation. Since this value is used to allocate the output tensor, a negative value would result in a `CHECK`-failure (assertion failure), as per TFSA-2021-198. joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the extracted num_segments scalar is used without checking its sign. Trigger: an attacker supplies a negative num_segments via the op input. Because the value flows into GetOutputShape and allocate_output, a negative segment count produces an invalid tensor shape, causing a CHECK-failure/assertion crash rather than a clean error.

commit_msg:
The SNDRV_RAWMIDI_IOCTL_PARAMS ioctl may resize the buffers and the
current code is racy.  For example, the sequencer client may write to
buffer while it being resized.

As a simple workaround, let's switch to the resized buffer inside the
stream runtime lock.

Reported-by: syzbot+52f83f0ea8df16932f7f@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Takashi Iwai <tiwai@suse.de>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tchar *newbuf;', '\t\tnewbuf = krealloc(runtime->buffer, params->buffer_size,', '\t\t\t\t  GFP_KERNEL);'], 'added_lines': ['\tchar *newbuf, *oldbuf;', '\t\tnewbuf = kmalloc(params->buffer_size, GFP_KERNEL);', '\t\tspin_lock_irq(&runtime->lock);', '\t\toldbuf = runtime->buffer;', '\t\truntime->appl_ptr = runtime->hw_ptr = 0;', '\t\tspin_unlock_irq(&runtime->lock);', '\t\tkfree(oldbuf);']}
description: It was found that the raw midi kernel driver does not protect against concurrent access which leads to a double realloc (double free) in snd_rawmidi_input_params() and snd_rawmidi_output_status() which are part of snd_rawmidi_ioctl() handler in rawmidi.c file. A malicious local attacker could possibly use this for privilege escalation.

code_evidence: When buffer_size differs, the code calls krealloc(runtime->buffer, ...) to resize the shared runtime buffer without holding runtime->lock. krealloc may free the old buffer and return a new one, but runtime->buffer is only updated at line 18 with no synchronization against concurrent readers/writers of the buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function frees the old buffer via krealloc while another path may retain and use the runtime->buffer pointer, matching CWE-416 (use after free). The unsynchronized realloc is the cause; double free is a related consequence but the primary supported weakness is reuse of freed memory.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: buffer resizing via krealloc is performed outside runtime->lock, so a concurrent stream access (e.g., sequencer writing to the buffer) can still use the old runtime->buffer pointer while krealloc frees it. Trigger: a SNDRV_RAWMIDI_IOCTL_PARAMS call changing buffer_size races with buffer I/O. Consequence: use-after-free/double-free of the resized buffer, enabling crash or possibly privilege escalation.

commit_msg:
can: gs_usb: gs_can_open(): prevent memory leak

In gs_can_open() if usb_submit_urb() fails the allocated urb should be
released.

Fixes: d08e973a77d1 ("can: gs_usb: Added support for the GS_USB CAN devices")
Cc: linux-stable <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Navid Emamdoost <navid.emamdoost@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Marc Kleine-Budde <mkl@pengutronix.de>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t\tusb_free_urb(urb);']}
description: A memory leak in the gs_can_open() function in drivers/net/can/usb/gs_usb.c in the Linux kernel before 5.3.11 allows attackers to cause a denial of service (memory consumption) by triggering usb_submit_urb() failures, aka CID-fb5be6a7b486.

code_evidence: usb_alloc_urb() at line 15 allocates a URB stored in the local variable 'urb'. On the usb_submit_urb() failure path (line 39), the code calls usb_unanchor_urb(urb) at line 45 and then breaks out of the loop at line 46 without ever calling usb_free_urb(urb). The allocation reference is lost when the function returns, so the URB is never released.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function allocates memory (usb_alloc_urb) and fails to release it on an error path, which is exactly CWE-401 (missing release of memory after effective lifetime). This is not a use-after-free or double-free, since the memory is simply never freed; the added usb_free_urb() confirms the omission.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the error branch for a failed usb_submit_urb() unanchors the URB but omits usb_free_urb(), dropping the last reference to the allocation. Trigger: repeatedly causing usb_submit_urb() to fail while opening the CAN channel. Consequence: each failure leaks one URB, leading to memory exhaustion and denial of service.

commit_msg:
Bug 697762: Fix scan converter SEGVs.

The SEGVs are caused by the scan converter allowing less room
in the table than is actually required. This happens due to
the mark_curve subdivision overflowing.

For example, if we have a curve such as:

 0 0x80000000 moveto
 0 0x80000000 0 0x80000000 0 0x80000000 curveto

Then the current subdivision logic does:

 fixed ay = (sy + c1y)>>1

For sy = c1y = 0x80000000 this gives ay = 0, when clearly
the average should be 0x80000000.

An alternative formulation of the splitting code:

 fixed ay = (sy>>1) + (c1y>>1)

gives the required result, at the expense of dropping accuracy at
the low end.

This commit therefore has 2 formulations of the splitting code, one
for 'big' values (values that might overflow), and ones for normal
values (values that won't).

We select between the two pieces of code by comparing the top 2
bits of each value; if they differ, then we use the big variant.

Also, when calculating the size of the table required, we were
incorrectly closing the curve more often than we needed to. This
had no ill effect other than inflating the amount of memory we
needed.

commit_msg:
(uid_t) -1 is still used as placeholder to mean "unset". This is OK, since
there should be no users with such number, see
https://systemd.io/UIDS-GIDS#special-linux-uids.

(uid_t) -1 is used as the default value in class initialization.

When a user or group above INT32_MAX is created, the numeric uid or
gid wraps around to negative when the value is assigned to gint, and
polkit gets confused. Let's accept such gids, except for -1.

A nicer fix would be to change the underlying type to e.g. uint32 to
not have negative values. But this cannot be done without breaking the
API, so likely new functions will have to be added (a
polkit_unix_user_new variant that takes a unsigned, and the same for
_group_new, _set_uid, _get_uid, _set_gid, _get_gid, etc.). This will
require a bigger patch.

Fixes https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/polkit/polkit/issues/74.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  g_return_if_fail (uid >= -1);'], 'added_lines': []}
description: A flaw was found in PolicyKit (aka polkit) 0.115 that allows a user with a uid greater than INT_MAX to successfully execute any systemctl command.

code_evidence: The function validates only the process object at line 5, then applies the constraint 'uid >= -1' at line 6 before storing the caller-supplied gint uid into process->uid at line 7. The patch removes that range check, so any negative gint value (including values that represent unsigned uids above INT32_MAX) is accepted and persisted.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-20 fits because the setter accepts input data (uid) without validating that it satisfies the required non-negative range constraint before processing. The weakness is the missing range validation, not a transformation or encoding issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the setter no longer validates the numeric uid range, allowing negative gint values that wrap from large unsigned uids to be stored. Trigger: a caller passes a uid whose value exceeds INT32_MAX and wraps negative. Consequence: downstream polkit authorization logic mishandles the wrapped uid, permitting privilege/authorization confusion per the commit description.

commit_msg:
CVE-2017-12985/IPv6: Check for print routines returning -1 when running past the end.

rt6_print(), ah_print(), and esp_print() return -1 if they run up
against the end of the packet while dissecting; if that happens, stop
dissecting, don't try to fetch the next header value, because 1) *it*
might be past the end of the packet and 2) we won't be using it in any
case, as we'll be exiting the loop.

Also, change mobility_print() to return -1 if it runs up against the
end of the packet, and stop dissecting if it does so.

This fixes a buffer over-read discovered by Brian 'geeknik' Carpenter.

commit_msg:
x86/insn-eval: Fix use-after-free access to LDT entry

get_desc() computes a pointer into the LDT while holding a lock that
protects the LDT from being freed, but then drops the lock and returns the
(now potentially dangling) pointer to its caller.

Fix it by giving the caller a copy of the LDT entry instead.

Fixes: 670f928ba09b ("x86/insn-eval: Add utility function to get segment descriptor")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tstruct desc_struct *desc;', '\tdesc = get_desc(sel);', '\tif (!desc)', '\tlimit = get_desc_limit(desc);', '\tif (desc->g)'], 'added_lines': ['\tstruct desc_struct desc;', '\tif (!get_desc(&desc, sel))', '\tlimit = get_desc_limit(&desc);', '\tif (desc.g)']}
description: In arch/x86/lib/insn-eval.c in the Linux kernel before 5.1.9, there is a use-after-free for access to an LDT entry because of a race condition between modify_ldt() and a #BR exception for an MPX bounds violation.

code_evidence: get_desc(sel) returns a pointer into the LDT after its internal lock is released; the local desc then dereferences that pointer at get_desc_limit(desc) and desc->g without any lock held, so the entry may be freed or modified concurrently.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function relies on a shared LDT entry outside the lock that protected it, so an interfering code sequence can modify the resource during the sequence; this violates exclusivity/atomicity, matching CWE-362. CWE-416 is the downstream effect, not the root cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: get_desc() returns an LDT pointer whose lifetime is not guaranteed once the LDT lock is dropped. Trigger: concurrent modify_ldt() frees or rewrites the LDT entry between get_desc() and the dereferences. Supported consequence: use-after-free of the LDT entry, giving a race window that can corrupt state or crash.

commit_msg:
Prevent instability and crash due to message flood

This patch adds a rate limiting to selected patches. The underlying rate limiter
used is the Leaky-Bucket algorithm. It allows for a burst of messages, but
limits them after a specified amount of messages within a time frame.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\tRATELIMIT(uSource);']}
description: murmur in Mumble through 1.2.19 before 2018-08-31 mishandles multiple concurrent requests that are persisted in the database, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (daemon hang or crash) via a message flood.

code_evidence: Function entry performs only authentication via MSG_SETUP and takes the cache mutex; no rate or frequency check on the incoming TextMessage is applied before processing.

channel_id_size() and each channel_id(i) are consumed without bounding the number of entries or validating the referenced channel beyond a lookup; the loop can iterate arbitrarily many attacker-supplied IDs.
tree_id_size()/tree_id(i) are likewise iterated without limit, and each tree channel is enqueued for traversal.
The tree traversal while-loop dequeues channels and enqueues all subchannels and users with no depth or size cap, so a large tree_id set can expand into unbounded work and user-set growth.
session_size()/session(i) are iterated without limit and appended to tm.qlSessions while users are inserted, so a message flood of many IDs amplifies per-request work and allocations.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-20 fits because the function receives structured input whose specified quantities (number of IDs, message rate) are not validated before use, enabling resource-exhaustion DoS. It is not merely transformation or filtering; the missing constraint is on input properties.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the handler accepts attacker-controlled repeated fields (channel_id, tree_id, session) and does not validate their quantity or frequency, and the added RATELIMIT macro is the only constraint. Trigger: a remote client sends a flood of text messages or messages with very large repeated-ID lists. Consequence: unbounded loops, tree traversal and set/queue growth consume CPU/memory and can hang or crash the daemon (DoS).

commit_msg:
Add heartbeat extension bounds check.

A missing bounds check in the handling of the TLS heartbeat extension
can be used to reveal up to 64k of memory to a connected client or
server.

Thanks for Neel Mehta of Google Security for discovering this bug and to
Adam Langley <agl@chromium.org> and Bodo Moeller <bmoeller@acm.org> for
preparing the fix (CVE-2014-0160)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t/* Read type and payload length first */', '\thbtype = *p++;', '\tn2s(p, payload);', '\tpl = p;', ''], 'added_lines': ['', '\t/* Read type and payload length first */', '\tif (1 + 2 + 16 > s->s3->rrec.length)', '\t\treturn 0; /* silently discard */', '\thbtype = *p++;', '\tn2s(p, payload);', '\tif (1 + 2 + payload + 16 > s->s3->rrec.length)', '\t\treturn 0; /* silently discard per RFC 6520 sec. 4 */', '\tpl = p;']}
description: The (1) TLS and (2) DTLS implementations in OpenSSL 1.0.1 before 1.0.1g do not properly handle Heartbeat Extension packets, which allows remote attackers to obtain sensitive information from process memory via crafted packets that trigger a buffer over-read, as demonstrated by reading private keys, related to d1_both.c and t1_lib.c, aka the Heartbleed bug.

code_evidence: Line 8 reads the heartbeat type from the record, and line 9 decodes the attacker-supplied 16-bit payload length from the same record without validating it against s->s3->rrec.length. Line 10 sets pl to the payload pointer, and line 23 memcpy(bp, pl, payload) copies that many bytes from the record buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The root cause is a missing length check causing a read beyond the intended buffer, matching CWE-125 (Out-of-bounds Read) whose impact is read memory disclosure. It is not CWE-787 (out-of-bounds write), since memcpy only reads the over-long source and writes within the allocated response buffer.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The payload length is taken directly from the incoming heartbeat packet and never compared to the actual record length. A crafted request with a small record but a large declared payload makes memcpy read past the end of the record buffer; the copied bytes are echoed in the response, leaking adjacent process memory (including keys) to the remote peer.

commit_msg:
x86/PV: writes of %fs and %gs base MSRs require canonical addresses

Commit c42494acb2 ("x86: fix FS/GS base handling when using the
fsgsbase feature") replaced the use of wrmsr_safe() on these paths
without recognizing that wr{f,g}sbase() use just wrmsrl() and that the
WR{F,G}SBASE instructions also raise #GP for non-canonical input.

Similarly arch_set_info_guest() needs to prevent non-canonical
addresses from getting stored into state later to be loaded by context
switch code. For consistency also check stack pointers and LDT base.
DR0..3, otoh, already get properly checked in set_debugreg() (albeit
we discard the error there).

The SHADOW_GS_BASE check isn't strictly necessary, but I think we
better avoid trying the WRMSR if we know it's going to fail.

This is CVE-2016-9385 / XSA-193.

Reported-by: Andrew Cooper <andrew.cooper3@citrix.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Reviewed-by: Andrew Cooper <andrew.cooper3@citrix.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        if ( is_pv_32bit_domain(currd) )', '        if ( is_pv_32bit_domain(currd) )', '        if ( is_pv_32bit_domain(currd) ||'], 'added_lines': ['        if ( is_pv_32bit_domain(currd) || !is_canonical_address(val) )', '        if ( is_pv_32bit_domain(currd) || !is_canonical_address(val) )', '        if ( is_pv_32bit_domain(currd) || !is_canonical_address(val) ||']}
description: The x86 segment base write emulation functionality in Xen 4.4.x through 4.7.x allows local x86 PV guest OS administrators to cause a denial of service (host crash) by leveraging lack of canonical address checks.

code_evidence: For MSR_FS_BASE, the only guard is is_pv_32bit_domain(currd); val is passed directly to wrfsbase(val) and stored into curr->arch.pv_vcpu.fs_base without any canonical-address check.
The MSR_GS_BASE case likewise checks only is_pv_32bit_domain(currd), then calls wrgsbase(val) and stores val into gs_base_kernel.
The MSR_SHADOW_GS_BASE case checks is_pv_32bit_domain(currd) or wrmsr_safe failure, but does not test is_canonical_address(val) before storing val into gs_base_user.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The root cause is missing validation of an externally supplied value's required property (canonical form) before use, matching CWE-20 improper input validation. The consequence is host denial of service via an unchecked guest-controlled MSR value.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: A PV guest administrator controls the MSR write value val. The function accepts non-canonical addresses because it validates only the 32-bit domain flag, not the address form. wrfsbase/wrgsbase raise #GP on non-canonical input, and the value is also persisted into vCPU state for later context-switch loading, causing a host crash (DoS).

This is part of XSA-260 / CVE-2018-8897

description: A statement in the System Programming Guide of the Intel 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer's Manual (SDM) was mishandled in the development of some or all operating-system kernels, resulting in unexpected behavior for #DB exceptions that are deferred by MOV SS or POP SS, as demonstrated by (for example) privilege escalation in Windows, macOS, some Xen configurations, or FreeBSD, or a Linux kernel crash. The MOV to SS and POP SS instructions inhibit interrupts (including NMIs), data breakpoints, and single step trap exceptions until the instruction boundary following the next instruction (SDM Vol. 3A; section 6.8.3). (The inhibited data breakpoints are those on memory accessed by the MOV to SS or POP to SS instruction itself.) Note that debug exceptions are not inhibited by the interrupt enable (EFLAGS.IF) system flag (SDM Vol. 3A; section 2.3). If the instruction following the MOV to SS or POP to SS instruction is an instruction like SYSCALL, SYSENTER, INT 3, etc. that transfers control to the operating system at CPL < 3, the debug exception is delivered after the transfer to CPL < 3 is complete. OS kernels may not expect this order of events and may therefore experience unexpected behavior when it occurs.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function only computes a stack-trace bottom address via a switch on get_stack_page; it contains no concurrent code sequence or shared-resource synchronization, so it does not directly support CWE-362.

commit_msg:
do_last(): fetch directory ->i_mode and ->i_uid before it's too late

may_create_in_sticky() call is done when we already have dropped the
reference to dir.

Fixes: 30aba6656f61e (namei: allow restricted O_CREAT of FIFOs and regular files)
Signed-off-by: Al Viro <viro@zeniv.linux.org.uk>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\terror = may_create_in_sticky(dir,'], 'added_lines': ['\tkuid_t dir_uid = dir->d_inode->i_uid;', '\tumode_t dir_mode = dir->d_inode->i_mode;', '\t\terror = may_create_in_sticky(dir_mode, dir_uid,']}
description: fs/namei.c in the Linux kernel before 5.5 has a may_create_in_sticky use-after-free, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (OOPS) or possibly obtain sensitive information from kernel memory, aka CID-d0cb50185ae9. One attack vector may be an open system call for a UNIX domain socket, if the socket is being moved to a new parent directory and its old parent directory is being removed.

code_evidence: Line 4 captures dir = nd->path.dentry as a pointer to the parent dentry/inode.

Lines 92-100: after complete_walk and audit_inode, when O_CREAT is set, may_create_in_sticky(dir, ...) dereferences the saved dir pointer to read the inode's i_uid and i_mode; the parent dentry/inode reference may already have been dropped by this point.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences a dentry/inode pointer after the reference may have been dropped, which is a use-after-free (CWE-416). The patch confirms this by snapshotting i_uid and i_mode before the reference is lost; this is not merely a missing permission check.

evidence_lines.code: struct dentry *dir = nd->path.dentry;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: do_last() stores the parent dentry pointer in dir at entry and later, in the O_CREAT path after complete_walk, passes dir to may_create_in_sticky(), which reads dir->d_inode->i_uid and i_mode. If the parent directory is moved/removed and its reference dropped during the intervening lookup, these reads access freed inode memory. Trigger: an open(O_CREAT) racing with parent directory removal/rename. Supported consequence: use-after-free leading to OOPS/DoS or kernel memory disclosure.

commit_msg:
Add back in HTTP method override in service control filter (#802)

This is NOT used by ESPv2, but it is needed for CAG temporarily. We can remove once their rollout is complete.

Signed-off-by: Teju Nareddy <nareddyt@google.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  }', '', '  // TODO(b/273531500): Temporary until CAG rollout is complete.', '  if (utils::handleHttpMethodOverride(headers)) {', '    // Update later filters that the HTTP method has changed by clearing the', '    // route cache.', '    ENVOY_LOG(debug, "HTTP method override occurred, recalculating route");', '    decoder_callbacks_->downstreamCallbacks()->clearRouteCache();']}
description:
ESPv2 is a service proxy that provides API management capabilities using Google Service Infrastructure. ESPv2 2.20.0 through 2.42.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability. API clients can craft a malicious `X-HTTP-Method-Override` header value to bypass JWT authentication in specific cases.

ESPv2 allows malicious requests to bypass authentication if both the conditions are true: The requested HTTP method is **not** in the API service definition (OpenAPI spec or gRPC `google.api.http` proto annotations, and the specified `X-HTTP-Method-Override` is a valid HTTP method in the API service definition. ESPv2 will forward the request to your backend without checking the JWT. Attackers can craft requests with a malicious `X-HTTP-Method-Override` value that allows them to bypass specifying JWTs. Restricting API access with API keys works as intended and is not affected by this vulnerability.

Upgrade deployments to release v2.43.0 or higher to receive a patch. This release ensures that JWT authentication occurs, even when the caller specifies `x-http-method-override`. `x-http-method-override` is still supported by v2.43.0+. API clients can continue sending this header to ESPv2.

code_evidence: The function reads the route via decoder_callbacks_->route() at line 18 and returns Continue early when route is nullptr (lines 19-20), before creating the handler and calling handler_->callCheck (lines 22-27), which performs the JWT/service-control authentication check. No method-override handling or route-cache invalidation is present in the shown body.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs an authentication check but skips it under a route-null condition, insufficiently proving the caller's identity claim. This matches CWE-287 (Improper Authentication); the bypass is the authentication failure, not merely an authorization or routing defect.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The authentication check (callCheck) is gated on a non-null route. If the original HTTP method is not in the API definition, route() is null and the filter returns Continue without invoking callCheck, forwarding the request unauthenticated. A crafted X-HTTP-Method-Override value that maps to a defined method is the trigger; the consequence is bypass of JWT authentication.

commit_msg:
Fix use-after-free for repeated fetchrow_arrayref calls when mysql_server_prepare=1

Function dbd_st_fetch() via Renew() can reallocate output buffer for
mysql_stmt_fetch() call. But it does not update pointer to that buffer in
imp_sth->stmt structure initialized by mysql_stmt_bind_result() function.
That leads to use-after-free in any mysql function which access
imp_sth->stmt structure (e.g. mysql_stmt_fetch()).

This patch fix this problem and properly updates pointer in imp_sth->stmt
structure after Renew() call.

Test 40server_prepare_crash.t is extended to check for that use-after-free
crash.

description: There is a vulnerability of type use-after-free affecting DBD::mysql (aka DBD-mysql or the Database Interface (DBI) MySQL driver for Perl) 3.x and 4.x before 4.041 when used with mysql_server_prepare=1.

Lines 121-122 update only the local MYSQL_BIND buffer->buffer/buffer_length, leaving the persistent binding inside imp_sth->stmt (set earlier by mysql_stmt_bind_result) pointing at the old, freed allocation.
Later calls such as mysql_stmt_fetch at line 67 and mysql_stmt_fetch_column at line 133 operate through imp_sth->stmt, whose stale bind[i].buffer now references freed memory.

This is a classic dangling-pointer reuse, not merely a buffer overflow.

if ((rc= mysql_stmt_fetch(imp_sth->stmt)))
if (mysql_stmt_fetch_column(imp_sth->stmt, buffer , i, 0))

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: Renew() reallocates fbh->data but the corresponding bind entry in imp_sth->stmt is not refreshed, so the driver retains a dangling pointer. Trigger: a repeated fetch where a column exceeds the current buffer length, causing reallocation. Consequence: subsequent MySQL calls dereference freed memory, yielding use-after-free (crash or memory corruption).
