commit_msg:
In theory, IO scheduler belongs to request queue, and the request pool
of sched tags belongs to the request queue too.

However, the current tags allocation interfaces are re-used for both
driver tags and sched tags, and driver tags is definitely host wide,
and doesn't belong to any request queue, same with its request pool.
So we need tagset instance for freeing request of sched tags.

Meantime, blk_mq_free_tag_set() often follows blk_cleanup_queue() in case
of non-BLK_MQ_F_TAG_SHARED, this way requires that request pool of sched
tags to be freed before calling blk_mq_free_tag_set().

Commit 47cdee29ef9d94e ("block: move blk_exit_queue into __blk_release_queue")
moves blk_exit_queue into __blk_release_queue for simplying the fast
path in generic_make_request(), then causes oops during freeing requests
of sched tags in __blk_release_queue().

Fix the above issue by move freeing request pool of sched tags into
blk_cleanup_queue(), this way is safe becasue queue has been frozen and no any
in-queue requests at that time. Freeing sched tags has to be kept in queue's
release handler becasue there might be un-completed dispatch activity
which might refer to sched tags.

Cc: Bart Van Assche <bvanassche@acm.org>
Cc: Christoph Hellwig <hch@lst.de>
Fixes: 47cdee29ef9d94e485eb08f962c74943023a5271 ("block: move blk_exit_queue into __blk_release_queue")
Tested-by: Yi Zhang <yi.zhang@redhat.com>
Reported-by: kernel test robot <rong.a.chen@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Ming Lei <ming.lei@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tstruct blk_mq_tag_set *set = q->tag_set;', '\tqueue_for_each_hw_ctx(q, hctx, i)', '\t\tblk_mq_sched_free_tags(set, hctx, i);'], 'added_lines': ['\tqueue_for_each_hw_ctx(q, hctx, i) {', '\t\tif (hctx->sched_tags) {', '\t\t\tblk_mq_free_rq_map(hctx->sched_tags);', '\t\t\thctx->sched_tags = NULL;', '\t\t}', '\t}']}
description: The block subsystem in the Linux kernel before 5.2 has a use-after-free that can lead to arbitrary code execution in the kernel context and privilege escalation, aka CID-c3e2219216c9. This is related to blk_mq_free_rqs and blk_cleanup_queue.

code_evidence: The function derives a tag_set from q->tag_set and then calls blk_mq_sched_free_tags(set, hctx, i) for each hardware context, freeing sched tags through the queue's tag set rather than the sched-tag request pool.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the teardown path references and frees sched-tag request structures whose backing tag set may already be freed, so the original pointer is used after free. This is a use-after-free rather than a mere double free or leak.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: sched-tag request-pool freeing is tied to the queue's tag_set, which is host-wide and may be freed by blk_mq_free_tag_set() before the queue release handler runs. Trigger: blk_cleanup_queue() followed by blk_mq_free_tag_set() then __blk_release_queue() invokes this teardown and frees sched-tag requests after their backing tag set/pool was already released. Supported consequence: use-after-free of the freed request pool, leading to kernel oops and potential arbitrary code execution.

commit_msg:
avcodec/alsdec: check predictor order against block length

Fixes out of array access
Fixes: abd3c041acbcb816be113455d138166b-asan_heap-oob_b11634_3707_cov_1707137151_als_05_2ch48k16b.mp4
Found-by: Mateusz "j00ru" Jurczyk and Gynvael Coldwind
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michaelni@gmx.at>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [''], 'added_lines': ['        if (*bd->opt_order > bd->block_length) {', '            *bd->opt_order = bd->block_length;', '            av_log(avctx, AV_LOG_ERROR, "Predictor order too large.\\n");', '            return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;', '        }']}
description: A vulnerability classified as critical has been found in FFmpeg 2.0. Affected is the function read_var_block_data. The manipulation leads to memory corruption. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue.

code_evidence: opt_order_length is derived from block_length, and get_bits reads a predictor order into *bd->opt_order; the only bound checked is sconf->max_order, not bd->block_length. Later loops (e.g. k < opt_order) and raw_samples usage rely on opt_order being consistent with the block size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing constraint on opt_order relative to block_length lets attacker-controlled values drive writes past buffer ends, matching CWE-787 (writes beyond intended buffer). It is not merely an out-of-bounds read, since the order governs write/index loops.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the parsed predictor order is validated against max_order but never against the actual block length, so a crafted bitstream can yield an order larger than the block. Trigger: remote input sets adapt_order and a large opt_order. Consequence: subsequent coefficient/sample loops and array indexing exceed intended buffer bounds, causing out-of-bounds writes/memory corruption.

description: In ImageMagick 7.0.8-43 Q16, there is a heap-based buffer over-read in the function WritePNGImage of coders/png.c, related to Magick_png_write_raw_profile and LocaleNCompare.

commit_msg:
proto/detect: workaround dns misdetected as dcerpc

The DCERPC UDP detection would misfire on DNS with transaction
ID 0x0400. This would happen as the protocol detection engine
gives preference to pattern based detection over probing parsers for
performance reasons.

This hack/workaround fixes this specific case by still running the
probing parser if DCERPC has been detected on UDP. The probing
parser result will take precedence.

Bug #2736.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            goto end;'], 'added_lines': ['    AppProto pm_alproto = ALPROTO_UNKNOWN;', '', '            /* HACK: if detected protocol is dcerpc/udp, we run PP as well', '             * to avoid misdetecting DNS as DCERPC. */', '            if (!(ipproto == IPPROTO_UDP && alproto == ALPROTO_DCERPC))', '                goto end;', '', '            pm_alproto = alproto;', '', '            /* fall through */', '    if (alproto == ALPROTO_UNKNOWN)', '        alproto = pm_alproto;', '']}
description: Open Information Security Foundation Suricata prior to version 4.1.2 is affected by: Denial of Service - DNS detection bypass. The impact is: An attacker can evade a signature detection with a specialy formed network packet. The component is: app-layer-detect-proto.c, decode.c, decode-teredo.c and decode-ipv6.c (https://github.com/OISF/suricata/pull/3590/commits/11f3659f64a4e42e90cb3c09fcef66894205aefe, https://github.com/OISF/suricata/pull/3590/commits/8357ef3f8ffc7d99ef6571350724160de356158b). The attack vector is: An attacker can trigger the vulnerability by sending a specifically crafted network request. The fixed version is: 4.1.2.

code_evidence: When pattern matching returns matches (pm_matches > 0), the function immediately assigns pm_results[0] to alproto and jumps to end, skipping the probing-parser stage entirely.
The end label returns alproto without any cross-check against the probing parser result, so a pattern match is trusted unconditionally.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function fails to validate its classification decision against the available probing-parser evidence, accepting an insufficiently validated protocol identification; this matches CWE-20's improper validation of input-derived properties. The consequence (detection bypass) is a downstream effect, not the weakness itself.

evidence_lines.code:
end:
SCReturnUInt(alproto);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the detection routine accepts a pattern-based protocol match without validating it against the probing parser. Trigger: a DNS packet whose transaction ID bytes (0x0400) coincidentally match DCERPC UDP patterns is classified as DCERPC and short-circuits the DNS probe. Consequence: the packet is attributed to the wrong protocol, enabling signature-detection bypass.

commit_msg:
tmpfiles: refuse to chown()/chmod() files which are hardlinked, unless protected_hardlinks sysctl is on

Let's add some extra safety.

Fixes: #7736
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '        if (hardlink_vulnerable(&st)) {', '                log_error("Refusing to set permissions on hardlinked file %s while the fs.protected_hardlinks sysctl is turned off.", path);', '                return -EPERM;', '        }']}
description: systemd-tmpfiles in systemd before 237 attempts to support ownership/permission changes on hardlinked files even if the fs.protected_hardlinks sysctl is turned off, which allows local users to bypass intended access restrictions via vectors involving a hard link to a file for which the user lacks write access, as demonstrated by changing the ownership of the /etc/passwd file.

code_evidence: The file is opened with O_NOFOLLOW and then stat'ed via fstatat on the fd, but the code never checks whether the resulting inode has additional hard links (st_nlink > 1) before applying permission/ownership changes.
Subsequent chmod() and chown() operate on /proc/self/fd/<fd>, which resolves to the same inode; if that inode is hardlinked elsewhere, the change affects the linked target too.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The code accesses and modifies a file without preventing the path from resolving to an unintended hardlinked resource, matching CWE-59 link resolution before file access. Unlike a symlink (blocked by O_NOFOLLOW), the hardlink vector is unguarded, so the target CWE fits directly.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function resolves and modifies a file without verifying that the inode is not hardlinked to an attacker-chosen victim. Trigger: a local user creates a hard link to a file they cannot write (e.g., /etc/passwd) and a tmpfiles rule targets the attacker-controlled path. Consequence: chmod/chown are applied to the linked victim, bypassing access restrictions and enabling privilege escalation.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['', '\tif (likely(walk.nbytes == nbytes))', '\t{', '\t\tsalsa20_encrypt_bytes(ctx, walk.dst.virt.addr,', '\t\t\t\t      walk.src.virt.addr, nbytes);', '\t\treturn blkcipher_walk_done(desc, &walk, 0);', '\t}'], 'added_lines': []}
description: The Salsa20 encryption algorithm in the Linux kernel before 4.14.8 does not correctly handle zero-length inputs, allowing a local attacker able to use the AF_ALG-based skcipher interface (CONFIG_CRYPTO_USER_API_SKCIPHER) to cause a denial of service (uninitialized-memory free and kernel crash) or have unspecified other impact by executing a crafted sequence of system calls that use the blkcipher_walk API. Both the generic implementation (crypto/salsa20_generic.c) and x86 implementation (arch/x86/crypto/salsa20_glue.c) of Salsa20 were vulnerable.

code_evidence: After blkcipher_walk_virt_block() at line 10, the code checks walk.nbytes == nbytes at line 12 and, if so, calls salsa20_encrypt_bytes() and returns blkcipher_walk_done(desc, &walk, 0) at line 16 without verifying that nbytes is nonzero.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function fails to validate the zero-length input condition before routing it into blkcipher_walk_done(), which requires a nonzero byte count; this missing input constraint is the root cause, matching CWE-20. The crash is the consequence, not the weakness itself.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: When nbytes is 0, blkcipher_walk_virt_block() leaves walk.nbytes at 0, so the equality check at line 12 succeeds and line 16 invokes blkcipher_walk_done() with zero processed bytes. The walk buffer/page were never initialized in this case, so the callee frees uninitialized memory, causing a kernel crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
evtchn: address races with evtchn_reset()

Neither d->evtchn_port_ops nor max_evtchns(d) may be used in an entirely
lock-less manner, as both may change by a racing evtchn_reset(). In the
common case, at least one of the domain's event lock or the per-channel
lock needs to be held. In the specific case of the inter-domain sending
by evtchn_send() and notify_via_xen_event_channel() holding the other
side's per-channel lock is sufficient, as the channel can't change state
without both per-channel locks held. Without such a channel changing
state, evtchn_reset() can't complete successfully.

Lock-free accesses continue to be permitted for the shim (calling some
otherwise internal event channel functions), as this happens while the
domain is in effectively single-threaded mode. Special care also needs
taking for the shim's marking of in-use ports as ECS_RESERVED (allowing
use of such ports in the shim case is okay because switching into and
hence also out of FIFO mode is impossihble there).

As a side effect, certain operations on Xen bound event channels which
were mistakenly permitted so far (e.g. unmask or poll) will be refused
now.

This is part of XSA-343.

Reported-by: Julien Grall <jgrall@amazon.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Acked-by: Julien Grall <jgrall@amazon.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        if ( evtchn_from_port(d, port)->state != ECS_FREE ||', '             evtchn_port_is_busy(d, port) )'], 'added_lines': ['        const struct evtchn *chn = evtchn_from_port(d, port);', '', '        if ( chn->state != ECS_FREE || evtchn_is_busy(d, chn) )']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.14.x. There are evtchn_reset() race conditions. Uses of EVTCHNOP_reset (potentially by a guest on itself) or XEN_DOMCTL_soft_reset (by itself covered by XSA-77) can lead to the violation of various internal assumptions. This may lead to out of bounds memory accesses or triggering of bug checks. In particular, x86 PV guests may be able to elevate their privilege to that of the host. Host and guest crashes are also possible, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS). Information leaks cannot be ruled out. All Xen versions from 4.5 onwards are vulnerable. Xen versions 4.4 and earlier are not vulnerable.

code_evidence: The function checks port bounds against d->max_evtchn_port and max_evtchns(d), then re-reads port validity and channel state (chn->state, evtchn_is_busy) without holding the domain event lock or per-channel lock, so a concurrent evtchn_reset() can change these fields between checks.

After the free/busy check, the function allocates a bucket and writes d->valid_evtchns and d->active_evtchns; these shared counters are only updated with write_atomic, not serialized against a racing reset that may also modify or shrink the channel state.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This is a concurrent sequence requiring exclusive access to shared event-channel state, but a timing window lets evtchn_reset() interfere, matching CWE-362's exclusivity/atomicity violation. It is not merely a missing bounds check; the bounds are checked but can be invalidated concurrently by the reset.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the port allocation sequence reads and updates shared event-channel state (max_evtchns(d), chn->state, valid_evtchns/active_evtchns) without the domain event lock required to exclude a concurrent evtchn_reset(). Trigger: a guest invokes EVTCHNOP_reset (or soft reset) racing with port allocation, letting the reset change state mid-sequence. Consequence: violated internal assumptions leading to out-of-bounds accesses, bug checks, DoS, and potential privilege escalation.

commit_msg:
receive: fix buffer leak when receiving invalid packets

For fastd versions before v20, this was just a memory leak (which could
still be used for DoS, as it's remotely triggerable). With the new
buffer management of fastd v20, this will trigger an assertion failure
instead as soon as the buffer pool is empty.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\tbreak;', '', '\tdefault:', '\t\tfastd_buffer_free(buffer);', '\t\tpr_debug("received packet with invalid type from unknown address %I", remote_addr);']}
description: receive.c in fastd before v21 allows denial of service (assertion failure) when receiving packets with an invalid type code.

code_evidence: Line 4 reads the packet type from buffer->data; the switch at line 5 only handles PACKET_DATA and PACKET_HANDSHAKE. For PACKET_HANDSHAKE (line 13), the buffer is passed to fastd_handshake_handle (line 14) and the switch ends at line 15 without a break or default. Any other type code falls through with no cleanup, leaving the buffer allocated, which depletes the buffer pool.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The commit message states the leaked buffer causes an assertion failure once the buffer pool is empty, matching CWE-617: an attacker-reachable assertion terminates the application. The code's missing default/cleanup is the leak causing that assertion, a denial-of-service, rather than merely a memory-safety corruption.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the switch lacks a default branch, so a remotely supplied invalid packet type bypasses all cleanup and leaks the buffer. The trigger is an attacker-sent packet with an unrecognized type code; the supported consequence is exhaustion of the buffer pool, which in this version leads to an assertion failure and process exit (remote DoS).

commit_msg:
ieee802154: ca8210: prevent memory leak

In ca8210_probe the allocated pdata needs to be assigned to
spi_device->dev.platform_data before calling ca8210_get_platform_data.
Othrwise when ca8210_get_platform_data fails pdata cannot be released.

Signed-off-by: Navid Emamdoost <navid.emamdoost@gmail.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20190917224713.26371-1-navid.emamdoost@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Stefan Schmidt <stefan@datenfreihafen.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tpriv->spi->dev.platform_data = pdata;'], 'added_lines': ['\tpriv->spi->dev.platform_data = pdata;']}
description: A memory leak in the ca8210_probe() function in drivers/net/ieee802154/ca8210.c in the Linux kernel before 5.3.8 allows attackers to cause a denial of service (memory consumption) by triggering ca8210_get_platform_data() failures, aka CID-6402939ec86e.

code_evidence: pdata is allocated with kmalloc and only checked for NULL; on failure the code jumps to error without freeing it.
ca8210_get_platform_data is called with pdata before pdata is stored anywhere reachable; if it returns nonzero the error path is taken.
Only after the get_platform_data success check does the code assign pdata to priv->spi->dev.platform_data, making it discoverable by ca8210_remove.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-401 fits because the allocated pdata is not released after its effective lifetime when the error path is triggered; the missing assignment before the failing call means the pointer is lost to cleanup. This is a memory leak, not a use-after-free or double-free, since no freed memory is subsequently accessed.

evidence_lines.code: priv->spi->dev.platform_data = pdata;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The freshly kmalloc'd pdata is not published to priv->spi->dev.platform_data until after ca8210_get_platform_data succeeds. When that call fails, the error label calls ca8210_remove, which cannot locate or free the still-unreferenced allocation, leaking the buffer on each probe failure and enabling memory-consumption DoS.

commit_msg:
Bug 706898: pcl - deal with corrupt numGlyphs in a TTF

A corrupt TrueType font can end up with a numGlyphs of 0, which we stored in an
unsigned value. Checking the validity of a GID we subtract 1 from numGlyphs,
having undesireable effects with an unsigned value.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        uint numGlyphs;', '        numGlyphs = u16(postp + 32);', '        if (glyph > numGlyphs - 1) {'], 'added_lines': ['        int numGlyphs;', '        numGlyphs = (int)u16(postp + 32);', '        if ((int)glyph > numGlyphs - 1) {']}
description: An integer overflow flaw was found in pcl/pl/plfont.c:418 in pl_glyph_name in ghostscript. This issue may allow a local attacker to cause a denial of service via transforming a crafted PCL file to PDF format.

code_evidence: numGlyphs is read from the corrupt post table as an unsigned value via u16(postp + 32), then the bounds check computes numGlyphs - 1. With numGlyphs == 0 this subtraction wraps to UINT_MAX, so the guard glyph > numGlyphs - 1 never rejects an out-of-range GID.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect is an unsigned integer wraparound (0 - 1 producing UINT_MAX) that defeats a bounds check, matching CWE-190. It is not merely an out-of-bounds read; the wraparound is the root cause enabling the subsequent unsafe access.

evidence_lines.code:
numGlyphs = u16(postp + 32);
if (glyph > numGlyphs - 1) {

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: an unsigned subtraction in the range check wraps when the font-supplied numGlyphs is 0. Trigger: a crafted TrueType font with numGlyphs 0 reaches pl_glyph_name with a glyph index that should be rejected. The failed check lets execution proceed to read the glyph name index and pascal strings at attacker-influenced offsets, supporting out-of-bounds access and denial of service.

commit_msg:
PS interpreter - check the Implementation of a Pattern before use

Bug #700141 "Type confusion in setpattern"

As the bug thread says, we were not checking that the Implementation
of a pattern dictionary was a structure type, leading to a crash when
we tried to treat it as one.

Here we make the st_pattern1_instance and st_pattern2_instance
structures public definitions and in zsetcolor we check the object
stored under the Implementation key in the supplied dictionary to see if
its a t_struct or t_astruct type, and if it is that its a
st_pattern1_instance or st_pattern2_instance structure.

If either check fails we throw a typecheck error.

We need to make the st_pattern1_instance and st_pattern2_instance
definitions public as they are defined in the graphics library and we
need to check in the interpreter.

commit_msg:
s390/mm: four page table levels vs. fork

The fork of a process with four page table levels is broken since
git commit 6252d702c5311ce9 "[S390] dynamic page tables."

All new mm contexts are created with three page table levels and
an asce limit of 4TB. If the parent has four levels dup_mmap will
add vmas to the new context which are outside of the asce limit.
The subsequent call to copy_page_range will walk the three level
page table structure of the new process with non-zero pgd and pud
indexes. This leads to memory clobbers as the pgd_index *and* the
pud_index is added to the mm->pgd pointer without a pgd_deref
in between.

The init_new_context() function is selecting the number of page
table levels for a new context. The function is used by mm_init()
which in turn is called by dup_mm() and mm_alloc(). These two are
used by fork() and exec(). The init_new_context() function can
distinguish the two cases by looking at mm->context.asce_limit,
for fork() the mm struct has been copied and the number of page
table levels may not change. For exec() the mm_alloc() function
set the new mm structure to zero, in this case a three-level page
table is created as the temporary stack space is located at
STACK_TOP_MAX = 4TB.

This fixes CVE-2016-2143.

Reported-by: Marcin Kościelnicki <koriakin@0x04.net>
Reviewed-by: Heiko Carstens <heiko.carstens@de.ibm.com>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Martin Schwidefsky <schwidefsky@de.ibm.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (oldmm->context.asce_limit < mm->context.asce_limit)', '\t\tcrst_table_downgrade(mm, oldmm->context.asce_limit);'], 'added_lines': []}
description: The fork implementation in the Linux kernel before 4.5 on s390 platforms mishandles the case of four page-table levels, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (system crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted application, related to arch/s390/include/asm/mmu_context.h and arch/s390/include/asm/pgalloc.h.

code_evidence: arch_dup_mmap compares oldmm->context.asce_limit with mm->context.asce_limit and, when the old limit is smaller, calls crst_table_downgrade(mm, oldmm->context.asce_limit). This trusts the copied mm context's asce_limit as the basis for the page-table level decision without validating that the child context's page-table level matches the parent's.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function accepts the mm context's asce_limit/page-table-level metadata without validating that it is consistent with the parent's level before processing, matching CWE-20's improper validation of data properties required for safe processing. The consequence is a kernel memory clobber/DoS rather than a separate index or bounds weakness.

evidence_lines.code:
if (oldmm->context.asce_limit < mm->context.asce_limit)
crst_table_downgrade(mm, oldmm->context.asce_limit);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The root cause is that the fork path derives the new context's page-table level from an unvalidated asce_limit rather than from the parent's actual page-table level. When the parent has four levels and the child was created with a three-level context and a 4TB limit, the downgrade logic does not reconcile the mismatch, so copy_page_range walks a three-level structure using non-zero pgd and pud indexes, causing memory clobbers and a system crash.

Allow only up to 64 buffers on input/output port (since the
allocation bitmap is only 64-wide).
Add safety checks to free only as many buffers were allocated.

Fixes: Heap Overflow and Possible Local Privilege Escalation in
MediaServer (libOmxVenc problem)
Bug: 27532497

description: The mm-video-v4l2 venc component in mediaserver in Android 4.x before 4.4.4, 5.0.x before 5.0.2, 5.1.x before 5.1.1, and 6.x before 2016-06-01 mishandles a buffer count, which allows attackers to gain privileges via a crafted application, as demonstrated by obtaining Signature or SignatureOrSystem access, aka internal bug 27532497.

code_evidence: The output-free loop iterates i from 0 up to m_sOutPortDef.nBufferCountActual and unconditionally calls free_output_buffer(&m_out_mem_ptr[i]) for every index, without checking whether buffer i was actually allocated (no bitmap check).
The input-free loop does the same: it iterates to m_sInPortDef.nBufferCountActual and calls free_input_buffer(&m_inp_mem_ptr[i]) for each index regardless of allocation state.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The loops perform memory operations (free_output_buffer/free_input_buffer on m_out_mem_ptr[i]/m_inp_mem_ptr[i]) at indices outside the allocated buffer range because the count is not validated against allocation, which is precisely an out-of-bounds memory buffer operation described by CWE-119.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The buffer count m_sOutPortDef.nBufferCountActual / m_sInPortDef.nBufferCountActual drives the loop bound and is not constrained to the allocated buffer array (allocation bitmap is 64-wide). An attacker-controlled buffer count larger than the number of allocated entries makes the loops index m_out_mem_ptr / m_inp_mem_ptr past their intended bounds, causing out-of-bounds access and freeing of unallocated entries.

description: The IEEE 802.11 dissector in Wireshark 1.12.x before 1.12.11 and 2.0.x before 2.0.3 does not properly restrict element lists, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (deep recursion and application crash) via a crafted packet, related to epan/dissectors/packet-capwap.c and epan/dissectors/packet-ieee80211.c.

code_evidence: The subelement loop reads attacker-controlled id (line 22) and len (line 26) from the packet, bounds the subelement length (line 30), and dispatches on id via switch (line 35).

For TFS_REQ_SUBELEM_TFS, the inner loop (line 39) calls add_tagged_field with no restriction on which element IDs may be recursed into, then advances offset by len (line 51) while the outer condition remains offset + 1 < end.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-20 fits because the function accepts packet-derived element IDs and lengths without validating that the IDs are among the safe, expected set before passing them into recursive processing. The fix adds an explicit allowed-id list, confirming the defect is improper input validation of element identity rather than a length/offset error.

evidence_lines.code:
offset += len;
}

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function validates length bounds but never constrains the set of subelement IDs that trigger recursive parsing. A crafted packet can nest TFS subelements that repeatedly invoke add_tagged_field, causing deep recursion and a crash (DoS). The missing constraint on the element list is the cause; the recursion/crash is the consequence.

commit_msg: Fix sscanf-related security issues
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t\tif(sscanf(line, "a=rtpmap:%d %s", &pt, name) == 2) {'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t\tif(sscanf(line, "a=rtpmap:%d %99s", &pt, name) == 2) {']}
description: An issue was discovered in janus-gateway (aka Janus WebRTC Server) through 0.10.0. janus_streaming_rtsp_parse_sdp in plugins/janus_streaming.c has a Buffer Overflow via a crafted RTSP server.

code_evidence: Line 18 declares a fixed 100-byte buffer `name`. Line 19 uses `sscanf(line, "a=rtpmap:%d %s", &pt, name)`, where `%s` copies an unbounded token from the attacker-controlled RTSP SDP line into `name` with no width limit, so a codec name longer than 99 characters writes past the buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-120 fits because input is copied to a fixed output buffer without checking input size. This is a write-past-buffer copy, not an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125), and the patch confirms the fix by adding the `%99s` width limit.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is the unbounded `%s` conversion writing into a fixed-size stack buffer. Trigger is a crafted RTSP SDP line containing `a=rtpmap:<pt> <long codec string>`; the copy overruns `name`, corrupting adjacent stack memory and potentially enabling code execution or crash.

commit_msg:
x86/hvm/ioreq: fix page referencing

The code does not take a page reference in hvm_alloc_ioreq_mfn(), only a
type reference. This can lead to a situation where a malicious domain with
XSM_DM_PRIV can engineer a sequence as follows:

- create IOREQ server: no pages as yet.
- acquire resource: page allocated, total 0.
- decrease reservation: -1 ref, total -1.

This will cause Xen to hit a BUG_ON() in free_domheap_pages().

This patch fixes the issue by changing the call to get_page_type() in
hvm_alloc_ioreq_mfn() to a call to get_page_and_type(). This change
in turn requires an extra put_page() in hvm_free_ioreq_mfn() in the case
that _PGC_allocated is still set (i.e. a decrease reservation has not
occurred) to avoid the page being leaked.

This is part of XSA-276.

Reported-by: Julien Grall <julien.grall@arm.com>
Signed-off-by: Paul Durrant <paul.durrant@citrix.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if ( !iorp->page )', '    put_page_and_type(iorp->page);', '    iorp->page = NULL;'], 'added_lines': ['    struct page_info *page = iorp->page;', '    if ( !page )', '', '    iorp->page = NULL;', '    /*', '     * Check whether we need to clear the allocation reference before', '     * dropping the explicit references taken by get_page_and_type().', '     */', '    if ( test_and_clear_bit(_PGC_allocated, &page->count_info) )', '        put_page(page);', '', '    put_page_and_type(page);']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen 4.11 allowing HVM guest OS users to cause a denial of service (host OS crash) or possibly gain host OS privileges because x86 IOREQ server resource accounting (for external emulators) was mishandled.

code_evidence: The function frees the ioreq page only after an early return when iorp->page is NULL; otherwise it calls put_page_and_type() and clears iorp->page.

The original code takes only a type reference via get_page_type() in the allocation path, so freeing via put_page_and_type() without first dropping the allocation reference (put_page when _PGC_allocated is set) leaves the page refcount inconsistent.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The supported consequence is a reachable BUG_ON() assertion in the hypervisor triggered by attacker-controlled resource accounting, matching CWE-617 (Reachable Assertion). This is a denial-of-service via an assertion, not a generic memory leak or use-after-free.

evidence_lines.code:
if ( !iorp->page )
return;

put_page_and_type(iorp->page);
iorp->page = NULL;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the free path drops the type reference but not the allocation reference when _PGC_allocated remains set, so a malicious domain with XSM_DM_PRIV can drive the page refcount to -1 after a decrease reservation. The trigger is the create/acquire/decrease sequence; the consequence is free_domheap_pages() hitting a BUG_ON(), crashing the host.

description: xbuf_format_converter, used as part of exif_read_data, was appending a terminating null character to the generated string, but was not using its standard append char function. As a result, if the buffer was full, it would result in an out-of-bounds write. This issue affects HHVM versions prior to 4.56.3, all versions between 4.57.0 and 4.80.1, all versions between 4.81.0 and 4.93.1, and versions 4.94.0, 4.95.0, 4.96.0, 4.97.0, 4.98.0.

code_evidence: Lines 21-23 compute cmp_len by first taking s1_len - offset, then enlarging it to s2_len if smaller (line 22), then capping at length (line 23). Because the buffer for s1 holds only s1_len - offset bytes, cmp_len can exceed that available length whenever s2_len > s1_len - offset and length is large.
Lines 26 and 28 pass cmp_len to bstrcasecmp/string_ncmp with s1 + offset as the first buffer; the comparison then reads/writes up to cmp_len bytes from a buffer bounded by s1_len - offset.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the faulty length calculation lets string comparison write past the end of the intended s1 buffer; the fix replaces the max-style computation with std::min bounds. This is a bounds/write issue rather than merely incorrect comparison semantics.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The length used for comparison is derived incorrectly: line 22 replaces the available s1 remainder with the larger s2_len instead of taking the minimum. When the main string's remaining tail is shorter than str and length permits, the comparison functions operate with a cmp_len larger than the s1 buffer remainder, causing an out-of-bounds access past the end of main_str's buffer.

commit_msg:
bpf: fix incorrect tracking of register size truncation

Properly handle register truncation to a smaller size.

The old code first mirrors the clearing of the high 32 bits in the bitwise
tristate representation, which is correct. But then, it computes the new
arithmetic bounds as the intersection between the old arithmetic bounds and
the bounds resulting from the bitwise tristate representation. Therefore,
when coerce_reg_to_32() is called on a number with bounds
[0xffff'fff8, 0x1'0000'0007], the verifier computes
[0xffff'fff8, 0xffff'ffff] as bounds of the truncated number.
This is incorrect: The truncated number could also be in the range [0, 7],
and no meaningful arithmetic bounds can be computed in that case apart from
the obvious [0, 0xffff'ffff].

Starting with v4.14, this is exploitable by unprivileged users as long as
the unprivileged_bpf_disabled sysctl isn't set.

Debian assigned CVE-2017-16996 for this issue.

v2:
 - flip the mask during arithmetic bounds calculation (Ben Hutchings)
v3:
 - add CVE number (Ben Hutchings)

Fixes: b03c9f9fdc37 ("bpf/verifier: track signed and unsigned min/max values")
Signed-off-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Acked-by: Edward Cree <ecree@solarflare.com>
Signed-off-by: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tregs[value_regno].var_off =', '\t\t\ttnum_cast(regs[value_regno].var_off, size);', '\t\t__update_reg_bounds(&regs[value_regno]);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tcoerce_reg_to_size(&regs[value_regno], size);']}
description: kernel/bpf/verifier.c in the Linux kernel through 4.14.8 allows local users to cause a denial of service (memory corruption) or possibly have unspecified other impact by leveraging register truncation mishandling.

code_evidence: When a sub-register (b/h/w) read succeeds on a scalar destination, lines 101-103 rewrite var_off via tnum_cast and then call __update_reg_bounds, which intersects the old arithmetic bounds with the bitwise-derived bounds. This is the pre-fix truncation handling replaced by coerce_reg_to_size in the patch.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The incorrect truncation tracking lets the verifier approve memory operations beyond the buffer's intended boundary, matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds read/write within a memory buffer. The underlying verifier bounds-tracking flaw is the root cause; CWE-119 captures the resultant out-of-bounds memory operation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: after truncating var_off to a smaller size, the verifier intersects the stale 64-bit min/max range with the truncated tristate range, producing bounds inconsistent with the actual truncated value. A crafted BPF program with a register bounded like [0xfffffff8, 0x100000007] yields a truncated range that omits [0,7], so subsequent bounds checks accept out-of-bounds accesses. Consequence: verifier-approved memory access outside the intended buffer (memory corruption/DoS).

commit_msg:
Fix null pointer dereference in echo-message

The bug was introduced while fixing #1705. If a client did not enable
echo-message, and doesn't have a network, it crashes.

Thanks to LunarBNC for reporting this
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            (pClient != this && (m_pNetwork->IsChan(Message.GetParam(0)) ||'], 'added_lines': ['            (pClient != this && ((m_pNetwork && m_pNetwork->IsChan(Message.GetParam(0))) ||']}
description: ZNC 1.8.0 up to 1.8.1-rc1 allows authenticated users to trigger an application crash (with a NULL pointer dereference) if echo-message is not enabled and there is no network.

code_evidence: The loop condition is evaluated for every client. When pClient->HasEchoMessage() is false, the right operand of || is evaluated, and the expression dereferences m_pNetwork via m_pNetwork->IsChan(...) without checking that m_pNetwork is non-NULL. The dereference is reached only when pClient != this, and the short-circuit || means the network pointer is not touched when echo-message is enabled.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences m_pNetwork without a NULL check, exactly matching CWE-476 (NULL Pointer Dereference). This is not a generic input-validation issue; the defect is the unchecked pointer dereference reachable through the short-circuit condition.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the condition assumes m_pNetwork is always valid. Trigger: an authenticated client with echo-message disabled and no network causes HasEchoMessage() to be false, so m_pNetwork->IsChan() is invoked on a NULL pointer, crashing the process. The supported consequence is a NULL pointer dereference leading to denial of service (application crash).

commit_msg: Fix arbitrary heap exposure problem
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        state->array_nl = strdup(RSTRING_PTR(array_nl));'], 'added_lines': ['        state->array_nl = fstrndup(RSTRING_PTR(array_nl), len);']}
description: Ruby through 2.2.7, 2.3.x through 2.3.4, and 2.4.x through 2.4.1 can expose arbitrary memory during a JSON.generate call. The issues lies in using strdup in ext/json/ext/generator/generator.c, which will stop after encountering a '\0' byte, returning a pointer to a string of length zero, which is not the length stored in space_len.

code_evidence: Line 6 records the string's true byte length in len via RSTRING_LEN, and line 15 stores that same len as array_nl_len. Line 14, however, copies the buffer with strdup, which stops at the first NUL byte and may allocate a shorter buffer than len. The length and the allocated buffer can therefore disagree whenever the Ruby string contains an embedded NUL.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The mismatch between the stored length and the actual buffer size causes subsequent operations to read outside the allocated buffer, directly matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds memory access within a buffer's intended boundary. The specific defect is an incorrect length computation from NUL-terminated copying, but the supported consequence is the out-of-bounds read.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: strdup truncates the copy at an embedded NUL, but array_nl_len is set to the original, larger len. Trigger: a JSON.generate call using an array_nl string containing a NUL byte. Consequence: later code trusting array_nl_len reads past the end of the shorter strdup allocation, exposing adjacent heap memory (out-of-bounds read).

commit_msg:
Regression on Mov File Seek

Until unforeseen issues are solved (with some mp4, fail to complete muxing see issue #780).
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    ', '    '], 'added_lines': ['    /*', '    */']}
description: A memory leak in tsMuxer version git-2539d07 allows attackers to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) via a crafted MP4 file.

code_evidence: The loop repeatedly calls m_bufferedReader->seek(m_readerID, m_fileBlockSize) and only advances m_processedBytes and skipLeft; no buffer or resource returned by seek is released or reset within the loop. The loop is entered whenever skipLeft exceeds 4LL*m_fileBlockSize, so large crafted skip sizes drive many iterations.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-401 fits because allocated resources are not sufficiently tracked and released after use, producing availability impact. The loop's repeated seek without release is the missing-release behavior, not merely an out-of-bounds or integer issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: an unbounded seek loop consumes resources per iteration without releasing them, while tracking only byte counters. Trigger: a crafted MP4 producing a very large skip size. Consequence: resource consumption/instability leading to DoS, matching the reported memory leak.

commit_msg:
thumbnailer: fix incomplete TIOCSTI filtering

Fixes #112

See also: https://github.com/flatpak/flatpak/issues/2782
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    {SCMP_SYS (ioctl), &SCMP_A1(SCMP_CMP_EQ, (int)TIOCSTI)},'], 'added_lines': ['    {SCMP_SYS (ioctl), &SCMP_A1(SCMP_CMP_MASKED_EQ, 0xFFFFFFFFu, (int)TIOCSTI)},']}
description: An issue was discovered in GNOME gnome-desktop 3.26, 3.28, and 3.30 prior to 3.30.2.2, and 3.32 prior to 3.32.1.1. A compromised thumbnailer may escape the bubblewrap sandbox used to confine thumbnailers by using the TIOCSTI ioctl to push characters into the input buffer of the thumbnailer's controlling terminal, allowing an attacker to escape the sandbox if the thumbnailer has a controlling terminal. This is due to improper filtering of the TIOCSTI ioctl on 64-bit systems, similar to CVE-2019-10063.

code_evidence: The ioctl blacklist entry compares argument 1 with SCMP_CMP_EQ against (int)TIOCSTI. This exact-equality check fails to match the full 64-bit ioctl request value on 64-bit systems, so a crafted request that differs in its upper bits can bypass the filter and reach the TIOCSTI path.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function builds a security filter that fails to correctly validate the ioctl request argument before allowing it, which is an input-validation flaw matching CWE-20. The missing constraint on the input value directly enables bypass of the intended restriction.

evidence_lines.code: {SCMP_SYS (ioctl), &SCMP_A1(SCMP_CMP_EQ, (int)TIOCSTI)},

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the seccomp rule validates the ioctl request with an exact comparison that does not account for the full-width request encoding, leaving the TIOCSTI operation insufficiently constrained. Trigger: a sandboxed thumbnailer issues an ioctl whose request value is not equal to the compared constant but still resolves to TIOCSTI. Consequence: characters can be injected into the controlling terminal, enabling sandbox escape.

commit_msg:
lagarith: reallocate rgb_planes when needed

Fixes invalid writes on pixel format changes.

Found-by: Mateusz "j00ru" Jurczyk and Gynvael Coldwind
CC:libav-stable@libav.org
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            l->rgb_stride = FFALIGN(avctx->width, 16);', '            l->rgb_planes = av_malloc(l->rgb_stride * avctx->height * planes + 1);', '            if (!l->rgb_planes) {', '                av_log(avctx, AV_LOG_ERROR, "cannot allocate temporary buffer\\n");', '                return AVERROR(ENOMEM);', '            }'], 'added_lines': ['        l->rgb_stride = FFALIGN(avctx->width, 16);', '        av_fast_malloc(&l->rgb_planes, &l->rgb_planes_allocated,', '                       l->rgb_stride * avctx->height * planes + 1);', '            av_log(avctx, AV_LOG_ERROR, "cannot allocate temporary buffer\\n");', '            return AVERROR(ENOMEM);']}
description: A vulnerability was found in FFmpeg 2.0. It has been rated as critical. Affected by this issue is the function lag_decode_frame. The manipulation leads to memory corruption. The attack may be launched remotely. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue.

code_evidence: The temporary buffer rgb_planes is allocated only once, guarded by if (!l->rgb_planes), using a size derived from avctx->width, avctx->height and the local planes value (3 or 4).
srcs[i] pointers are computed from the existing rgb_planes buffer and the current l->rgb_stride and avctx->height, without reallocating when dimensions or planes change.
lag_decode_arith_plane writes into srcs[i] using avctx->width/height and -l->rgb_stride, so if the buffer was sized for a smaller/earlier frame these writes exceed it.
The reconstruction loops read srcs[i][i] and write dst, using the same stale stride/plane layout, propagating the undersized-buffer assumption.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes decoded plane data into a buffer whose size no longer matches the current frame dimensions/plane count, producing writes past the end of the intended buffer. This is an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787), not merely a read overflow or integer issue.

evidence_lines.code:
for (i = 0; i < planes; i++)
srcs[i] = l->rgb_planes + (i + 1) * l->rgb_stride * avctx->height - l->rgb_stride;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: rgb_planes is allocated only on first use and never resized, while later frames can change width, height or planes (RGB24 vs RGBA). Trigger: a stream whose first ARITH frame is small/3-plane followed by a larger or 4-plane frame. Consequence: lag_decode_arith_plane and the reconstruction loops write past the allocated temporary buffer, corrupting memory.

avcodec/dxtory: fix src size checks

Fixes integer overflow
Fixes out of array read
Fixes: d104661bb59b202df7671fb19a00ca6c-asan_heap-oob_d6429d_5066_cov_1729501105_dxtory_mic.avi
Found-by: Mateusz "j00ru" Jurczyk and Gynvael Coldwind

description: A vulnerability was found in FFmpeg 2.0. It has been classified as problematic. Affected is an unknown function of the file libavcodec/dxtroy.c. The manipulation leads to integer coercion error. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue.

code_evidence: Line 7 computes avctx->width * avctx->height * 3 as an int expression, then compares it to src_size in the size guard; lines 8-10 reject only when this (possibly overflowed) product exceeds src_size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The guard relies on an arithmetic result whose type cannot represent the true value, so the numeric conversion/overflow produces an unexpected value used in a sensitive size check - Incorrect Conversion between Numeric Types. This is not merely an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125); the read is the consequence of the flawed numeric computation.

Trigger: a crafted packet declaring sufficiently large width/height. Consequence: the guard passes, and the loops at lines 17-21 read three bytes per pixel from src, causing an out-of-bounds read.

commit_msg:
vfs: make AIO use the proper rw_verify_area() area helpers

We had for some reason overlooked the AIO interface, and it didn't use
the proper rw_verify_area() helper function that checks (for example)
mandatory locking on the file, and that the size of the access doesn't
cause us to overflow the provided offset limits etc.

Instead, AIO did just the security_file_permission() thing (that
rw_verify_area() also does) directly.

This fixes it to do all the proper helper functions, which not only
means that now mandatory file locking works with AIO too, we can
actually remove lines of code.

Reported-by: Manish Honap <manish_honap_vit@yahoo.co.in>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tret = rw_verify_area(type, kiocb->ki_filp, &kiocb->ki_pos, ret);', '\tif (ret < 0)', '\t\tgoto out;', '']}
description: Integer overflow in fs/aio.c in the Linux kernel before 3.4.1 allows local users to cause a denial of service or possibly have unspecified other impact via a large AIO iovec.

code_evidence: The function passes user-controlled kiocb->ki_nbytes as the iovcnt argument to rw_copy_check_uvector() and only checks ret < 0; in the vulnerable version no rw_verify_area() bounds/offset check was performed before trusting the resulting length.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the flaw is an integer overflow/wraparound of the AIO iovec length when validating the access size against offset limits; the missing rw_verify_area() call is the constraint whose absence permits the overflow. It is not merely a permission check, since the added helper enforces the size arithmetic that prevents wraparound.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: A large AIO iovec length from userspace is used as the segment count for rw_copy_check_uvector(); without the rw_verify_area() size/offset validation the length can overflow offset limits, yielding an undersized or negative computed size. The trigger is a local user submitting an oversized AIO iovec; the supported consequence is denial of service and possible further impact from the corrupted length.

description: The HTTP/2 protocol allows a denial of service (server resource consumption) because request cancellation can reset many streams quickly, as exploited in the wild in August through October 2023.

code_evidence: For every valid RST_STREAM frame, the function looks up the stream and unconditionally resets it via h2o_http2_stream_reset when found; there is no per-connection limit or throttling of how many streams a peer may reset.

Trigger: a peer cancels many streams quickly, each producing a reset. return (gif_read_image(fp, img, cmap, buf[8] & GIF_INTERLACE, transparent));

description: A HTTP response header injection vulnerability in Swoole v4.5.2 allows attackers to execute arbitrary code via supplying a crafted URL.

code_evidence: The CRLF rejection at [27,28,29] is gated on !url_encode, so a value containing \r\n bypasses the check whenever url_encode is true.
When url_encode is true, [36,37,38,39,40,41,42,43] percent-encodes the value before building the cookie, neutralizing CR/LF.
When url_encode is false, [44,45,46,47,48] interpolates the raw value into the Cookie header via snprintf without any CRLF filtering, since the guard at [27,28,29] was skipped.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Unneutralized CR/LF special elements from caller-supplied value are concatenated into a Cookie header consumed by a downstream HTTP parser, matching CWE-74 injection into a structured record. The encoding branch shows neutralization is possible but omitted on the raw path; a more specific CRLF-injection child would be narrower, but the target class fits the demonstrated flaw.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the CRLF filter is bypassed for the non-encoding path because the condition requires !url_encode, yet that same path copies the raw value into the header. Trigger: a caller invokes the cookie setter with url_encode false and a value containing \r\n. Supported consequence: injected CRLF sequences reach the downstream HTTP header parser, enabling response splitting/header injection.

commit_msg:
sched/fair: Fix low cpu usage with high throttling by removing expiration of cpu-local slices

It has been observed, that highly-threaded, non-cpu-bound applications
running under cpu.cfs_quota_us constraints can hit a high percentage of
periods throttled while simultaneously not consuming the allocated
amount of quota. This use case is typical of user-interactive non-cpu
bound applications, such as those running in kubernetes or mesos when
run on multiple cpu cores.

This has been root caused to cpu-local run queue being allocated per cpu
bandwidth slices, and then not fully using that slice within the period.
At which point the slice and quota expires. This expiration of unused
slice results in applications not being able to utilize the quota for
which they are allocated.

The non-expiration of per-cpu slices was recently fixed by
'commit 512ac999d275 ("sched/fair: Fix bandwidth timer clock drift
condition")'. Prior to that it appears that this had been broken since
at least 'commit 51f2176d74ac ("sched/fair: Fix unlocked reads of some
cfs_b->quota/period")' which was introduced in v3.16-rc1 in 2014. That
added the following conditional which resulted in slices never being
expired.

if (cfs_rq->runtime_expires != cfs_b->runtime_expires) {
	/* extend local deadline, drift is bounded above by 2 ticks */
	cfs_rq->runtime_expires += TICK_NSEC;

Because this was broken for nearly 5 years, and has recently been fixed
and is now being noticed by many users running kubernetes
(https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/67577) it is my opinion
that the mechanisms around expiring runtime should be removed
altogether.

This allows quota already allocated to per-cpu run-queues to live longer
than the period boundary. This allows threads on runqueues that do not
use much CPU to continue to use their remaining slice over a longer
period of time than cpu.cfs_period_us. However, this helps prevent the
above condition of hitting throttling while also not fully utilizing
your cpu quota.

This theoretically allows a machine to use slightly more than its
allotted quota in some periods. This overflow would be bounded by the
remaining quota left on each per-cpu runqueueu. This is typically no
more than min_cfs_rq_runtime=1ms per cpu. For CPU bound tasks this will
change nothing, as they should theoretically fully utilize all of their
quota in each period. For user-interactive tasks as described above this
provides a much better user/application experience as their cpu
utilization will more closely match the amount they requested when they
hit throttling. This means that cpu limits no longer strictly apply per
period for non-cpu bound applications, but that they are still accurate
over longer timeframes.

This greatly improves performance of high-thread-count, non-cpu bound
applications with low cfs_quota_us allocation on high-core-count
machines. In the case of an artificial testcase (10ms/100ms of quota on
80 CPU machine), this commit resulted in almost 30x performance
improvement, while still maintaining correct cpu quota restrictions.
That testcase is available at https://github.com/indeedeng/fibtest.

Fixes: 512ac999d275 ("sched/fair: Fix bandwidth timer clock drift condition")

description: kernel/sched/fair.c in the Linux kernel before 5.3.9, when cpu.cfs_quota_us is used (e.g., with Kubernetes), allows attackers to cause a denial of service against non-cpu-bound applications by generating a workload that triggers unwanted slice expiration, aka CID-de53fd7aedb1. (In other words, although this slice expiration would typically be seen with benign workloads, it is possible that an attacker could calculate how many stray requests are required to force an entire Kubernetes cluster into a low-performance state caused by slice expiration, and ensure that a DDoS attack sent that number of stray requests. An attack does not affect the stability of the kernel; it only causes mismanagement of application execution.)

code_evidence: Line 16-17: when quota is finite and cfs_b->runtime exceeds slice, runtime is set to the full cfs_b->runtime, so an entire period's quota is pulled into one slack-timer distribution.

Line 18 captures cfs_b->runtime_expires; line 24 passes it to distribute_cfs_runtime, and lines 26-27 only subtract consumed runtime when expires still matches, tying slice accounting to per-period expiration.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-400 fits because the function fails to properly maintain and consume the limited CFS bandwidth quota resource: allocated slices expire without being used, causing the quota to be effectively wasted and applications throttled. The weakness is uncontrolled/mismanaged resource accounting, not a memory-safety flaw.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: distribution of cpu-local bandwidth slices is gated on expiration of cfs_b->runtime_expires, so when the expiry check (line 26) fails or the period boundary passes, the remaining runtime is not consumed and the per-CPU slice expires unused. Trigger: a high-thread-count, non-CPU-bound workload under a finite quota (line 16). Consequence: throttling occurs while allocated quota is unused, degrading application performance (availability DoS).

commit_msg:
x86/fpu/xsaves: Fix improper uses of __ex_table

Commit:

  f31a9f7c7169 ("x86/xsaves: Use xsaves/xrstors to save and restore xsave area")

introduced alternative instructions for XSAVES/XRSTORS and commit:

  adb9d526e982 ("x86/xsaves: Add xsaves and xrstors support for booting time")

added support for the XSAVES/XRSTORS instructions at boot time.

Unfortunately both failed to properly protect them against faulting:

The 'xstate_fault' macro will use the closest label named '1'
backward and that ends up in the .altinstr_replacement section
rather than in .text. This means that the kernel will never find
in the __ex_table the .text address where this instruction might
fault, leading to serious problems if userspace manages to
trigger the fault.

Signed-off-by: Quentin Casasnovas <quentin.casasnovas@oracle.com>
Signed-off-by: Jamie Iles <jamie.iles@oracle.com>
[ Improved the changelog, fixed some whitespace noise. ]
Acked-by: Borislav Petkov <bp@alien8.de>
Acked-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Cc: Allan Xavier <mr.a.xavier@gmail.com>
Cc: H. Peter Anvin <hpa@zytor.com>
Cc: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
Fixes: adb9d526e982 ("x86/xsaves: Add xsaves and xrstors support for booting time")
Fixes: f31a9f7c7169 ("x86/xsaves: Use xsaves/xrstors to save and restore xsave area")
Signed-off-by: Ingo Molnar <mingo@kernel.org>

commit_msg:
avcodec/mpeg4videodec: Remove use of FF_PROFILE_MPEG4_SIMPLE_STUDIO as indicator of studio profile

The profile field is changed by code inside and outside the decoder,
its not a reliable indicator of the internal codec state.
Maintaining it consistency with studio_profile is messy.
Its easier to just avoid it and use only studio_profile

Fixes: assertion failure
Fixes: ffmpeg_crash_9.avi

Found-by: Thuan Pham, Marcel Böhme, Andrew Santosa and Alexandru Razvan Caciulescu with AFLSmart
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        av_assert1(avctx->profile == FF_PROFILE_MPEG4_SIMPLE_STUDIO);'], 'added_lines': ['    MpegEncContext *s = avctx->priv_data;', '        av_assert1(s->studio_profile);']}
description: In libavcodec in FFmpeg 4.0.1, improper maintenance of the consistency between the context profile field and studio_profile in libavcodec may trigger an assertion failure while converting a crafted AVI file to MPEG4, leading to a denial of service, related to error_resilience.c, h263dec.c, and mpeg4videodec.c.

code_evidence: h263_get_format reads avctx->bits_per_raw_sample and, when it exceeds 8, executes av_assert1(avctx->profile == FF_PROFILE_MPEG4_SIMPLE_STUDIO) before returning avctx->pix_fmt. The assertion depends on the externally mutable profile field rather than the decoder's internal studio_profile state, so a crafted input can leave bits_per_raw_sample > 8 while profile differs from the expected value.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function contains a reachable av_assert1 whose failure condition is attacker-influenced through input parsing, causing process exit. This matches CWE-617 (Reachable Assertion), a DoS via attacker-triggerable assert, rather than a memory-safety weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the assertion checks a context field (profile) that can be changed outside the decoder and is not kept consistent with internal codec state. Trigger: a crafted AVI/MPEG4 input drives the decoder into a state where bits_per_raw_sample > 8 but profile != FF_PROFILE_MPEG4_SIMPLE_STUDIO, making the assertion fail. Supported consequence: assertion failure aborts the process, a denial of service.

commit_msg:
_bfd_clear_contents bounds checking

This PR shows a fuzzed binary triggering a segfault via a bad
relocation in .debug_line.  It turns out that unlike normal
relocations applied to a section, the linker applies those with
symbols from discarded sections via _bfd_clear_contents without
checking that the relocation is within the section bounds.  The same
thing now happens when reading debug sections since commit
a4cd947aca23, the PR23425 fix.

	PR 23770
	PR 23425
	* reloc.c (_bfd_clear_contents): Replace "location" param with
	"buf" and "off".  Bounds check "off".  Return status.
	* cofflink.c (_bfd_coff_generic_relocate_section): Update
	_bfd_clear_contents call.
	* elf-bfd.h (RELOC_AGAINST_DISCARDED_SECTION): Likewise.
	* elf32-arc.c (elf_arc_relocate_section): Likewise.
	* elf32-i386.c (elf_i386_relocate_section): Likewise.
	* elf32-metag.c (metag_final_link_relocate): Likewise.
	* elf32-nds32.c (nds32_elf_get_relocated_section_contents): Likewise.
	* elf32-ppc.c (ppc_elf_relocate_section): Likewise.
	* elf32-visium.c (visium_elf_relocate_section): Likewise.
	* elf64-ppc.c (ppc64_elf_relocate_section): Likewise.
	* elf64-x86-64.c *(elf_x86_64_relocate_section): Likewise.
	* libbfd-in.h (_bfd_clear_contents): Update prototype.
	* libbfd.h: Regenerate.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['void', '\t\t     bfd_byte *location)'], 'added_lines': ['bfd_reloc_status_type', '\t\t     bfd_byte *buf,', '\t\t     bfd_vma off)', '  bfd_byte *location;', '', '  if (!bfd_reloc_offset_in_range (howto, input_bfd, input_section, off))', '    return bfd_reloc_outofrange;', '  location = buf + off;', '  return bfd_reloc_ok;']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Binary File Descriptor (BFD) library (aka libbfd), as distributed in GNU Binutils 2.31. An invalid memory address dereference was discovered in read_reloc in reloc.c. The vulnerability causes a segmentation fault and application crash, which leads to denial of service, as demonstrated by objdump, because of missing _bfd_clear_contents bounds checking.

code_evidence: _bfd_clear_contents receives a raw bfd_byte *location from the caller with no size or offset information, so the function cannot verify the pointer refers to a valid buffer region. Line 8 passes location directly to read_reloc, and line 14 passes it to write_reloc, both of which dereference memory at that address.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs read and write operations through a location pointer that is never validated to lie within the input section's buffer, which is exactly an out-of-bounds memory access (CWE-119). The later patch adds bfd_reloc_offset_in_range and returns bfd_reloc_outofrange, confirming the missing boundary constraint was the defect.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the relocation target address is dereferenced without any bounds check against the input section. Trigger: a crafted relocation (e.g., in .debug_line) whose offset falls outside the section, passed in by the caller. Consequence: read_reloc/write_reloc access memory outside the intended buffer, causing an invalid memory dereference and a segfault (denial of service); the write path could also corrupt adjacent memory.

Solution:   Get the line again after getvvcol().
