commit_msg:
xen/rwlock: Add missing memory barrier in the unlock path of rwlock

The rwlock unlock paths are using atomic_sub() to release the lock.
However the implementation of atomic_sub() rightfully doesn't contain a
memory barrier. On Arm, this means a processor is allowed to re-order
the memory access with the preceeding access.

In other words, the unlock may be seen by another processor before all
the memory accesses within the "critical" section.

The rwlock paths already contains barrier indirectly, but they are not
very useful without the counterpart in the unlock paths.

The memory barriers are not necessary on x86 because loads/stores are
not re-ordered with lock instructions.

So add arch_lock_release_barrier() in the unlock paths that will only
add memory barrier on Arm.

Take the opportunity to document each lock paths explaining why a
barrier is not necessary.

This is XSA-314.

Signed-off-by: Julien Grall <jgrall@amazon.com>
Acked-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
diff_func:
--- func_before
+++ func_after
@@ -1,9 +1,18 @@
 static inline void _write_lock(rwlock_t *lock)
 {
-    /* Optimize for the unfair lock case where the fair flag is 0. */
     preempt_disable();
+    /*
+     * Optimize for the unfair lock case where the fair flag is 0.
+     *
+     * atomic_cmpxchg() is a full barrier so no need for an
+     * arch_lock_acquire_barrier().
+     */
     if ( atomic_cmpxchg(&lock->cnts, 0, _write_lock_val()) == 0 )
         return;
 
     queue_write_lock_slowpath(lock);
+    /*
+     * queue_write_lock_slowpath() is using spinlock and therefore is a
+     * full barrier. So no need for an arch_lock_acquire_barrier().
+     */
 }
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    /* Optimize for the unfair lock case where the fair flag is 0. */'], 'added_lines': ['    /*', '     * Optimize for the unfair lock case where the fair flag is 0.', '     *', '     * atomic_cmpxchg() is a full barrier so no need for an', '     * arch_lock_acquire_barrier().', '     */', '    /*', '     * queue_write_lock_slowpath() is using spinlock and therefore is a', '     * full barrier. So no need for an arch_lock_acquire_barrier().', '     */']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.13.x, allowing guest OS users to cause a denial of service or possibly gain privileges because of missing memory barriers in read-write unlock paths. The read-write unlock paths don't contain a memory barrier. On Arm, this means a processor is allowed to re-order the memory access with the preceding ones. In other words, the unlock may be seen by another processor before all the memory accesses within the "critical" section. As a consequence, it may be possible to have a writer executing a critical section at the same time as readers or another writer. In other words, many of the assumptions (e.g., a variable cannot be modified after a check) in the critical sections are not safe anymore. The read-write locks are used in hypercalls (such as grant-table ones), so a malicious guest could exploit the race. For instance, there is a small window where Xen can leak memory if XENMAPSPACE_grant_table is used concurrently. A malicious guest may be able to leak memory, or cause a hypervisor crash resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS). Information leak and privilege escalation cannot be excluded.

code_evidence: _write_lock() disables preemption, then attempts atomic_cmpxchg(&lock->cnts, 0, _write_lock_val()) to acquire exclusive write ownership of cnts; on failure it falls back to queue_write_lock_slowpath(). The function is the acquisition side of a read-write lock whose release path (per the commit) used atomic_sub() without a memory barrier, so the shared cnts field can be observed as released before the critical-section accesses complete.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-362 fits because the rwlock critical section requires temporary exclusive access to shared resource cnts, but the missing barrier permits an interfering concurrent sequence to access that resource while a critical section is still in progress, violating exclusivity. The lock-acquisition code here is the counterpart of the flawed unlock, so the race is code-grounded rather than speculative.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the lock release lacks a release barrier on Arm, allowing stores inside the critical section to be reordered after the unlock. Trigger: a guest invokes hypercalls using rwlock-protected data concurrently on multiple CPUs. Consequence: another writer or reader observes stale/inconsistent state, violating exclusivity and atomicity of the critical section, enabling memory leak, hypervisor crash, or privilege escalation.

commit_msg:
SECURITY: CVE-2016-8740

mod_http2: properly crafted, endless HTTP/2 CONTINUATION frames could be used to exhaust all server's memory.

Reported by: Naveen Tiwari <naveen.tiwari@asu.edu> and CDF/SEFCOM at Arizona State University



git-svn-id: https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/httpd/httpd/trunk@1772576 13f79535-47bb-0310-9956-ffa450edef68
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        ap_log_cerror(APLOG_MARK, APLOG_ERR, 0, session->c,', '    if (status != APR_SUCCESS && !h2_stream_is_ready(stream)) {'], 'added_lines': ['        ap_log_cerror(APLOG_MARK, APLOG_DEBUG, 0, session->c,', '    if (status == APR_ECONNRESET) {', '        ap_log_cerror(APLOG_MARK, APLOG_TRACE1, status, session->c,', '                      "h2-stream(%ld-%d): on_header, reset stream",', '                      session->id, stream->id);', '        nghttp2_submit_rst_stream(ngh2, NGHTTP2_FLAG_NONE, stream->id,', '                                  NGHTTP2_INTERNAL_ERROR);', '    }', '    else if (status != APR_SUCCESS && !h2_stream_is_ready(stream)) {']}
description: The mod_http2 module in the Apache HTTP Server 2.4.17 through 2.4.23, when the Protocols configuration includes h2 or h2c, does not restrict request-header length, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory consumption) via crafted CONTINUATION frames in an HTTP/2 request.

code_evidence: on_header_cb passes the frame-supplied name/namelen and value/valuelen directly to h2_stream_add_header and only reacts to the returned status; it imposes no check on header name length, value length, or accumulated header size before or after adding the header. The only rejection path is the generic status/readiness test, which does not bound total header data.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function receives attacker-controlled header name/value data and metadata (lengths) but performs no validation of the required length property, matching CWE-20 improper input validation. The memory exhaustion is the downstream impact; the missing length constraint at input handling is the validation failure.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the callback accepts arbitrary CONTINUATION-frame header fields without enforcing any request-header length limit, so repeated frames accumulate unbounded header data in the stream. Trigger: a remote peer sends crafted, endless CONTINUATION frames. Supported consequence: memory exhaustion leading to denial of service, as stated in the CVE (CWE-770/CWE-400).

commit_msg:
Use spinlocks to deal with workers introducing a wrapper
asus_schedule_work(), and several spinlock checks.
Otherwise, asus_kbd_backlight_set() may schedule led->work after the
structure has been freed, causing a use-after-free.

Fixes: af22a610bc38 ("HID: asus: support backlight on USB keyboards")
Signed-off-by: Pietro Borrello <borrello@diag.uniroma1.it>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20230125-hid-unregister-leds-v4-5-7860c5763c38@diag.uniroma1.it
Signed-off-by: Benjamin Tissoires <benjamin.tissoires@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['', '\tif (led->removed)', '\t\treturn;'], 'added_lines': []}
description: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel. A use-after-free may be triggered in asus_kbd_backlight_set when plugging/disconnecting in a malicious USB device, which advertises itself as an Asus device. Similarly to the previous known CVE-2023-25012, but in asus devices, the work_struct may be scheduled by the LED controller while the device is disconnecting, triggering a use-after-free on the struct asus_kbd_leds *led structure. A malicious USB device may exploit the issue to cause memory corruption with controlled data.

code_evidence: Line 3 recovers the containing asus_kbd_leds struct from the queued work; lines 7-8 only check led->removed before dereferencing led. Line 9 then takes led->lock and lines 10-12 read led->brightness and pass led->hdev, all through the same pointer without any lifetime guarantee.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function accesses memory through a pointer whose object may already be freed, which is exactly CWE-416. It is not merely a race on a field value: the missing lifetime constraint permits reads of led->brightness and led->hdev after release.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The work callback dereferences the led structure that was obtained from the work item, but nothing in this function pins that allocation. If the device is disconnected and the structure freed while the work is pending, the check at line 7 and the subsequent lock/dereference at lines 9-12 operate on freed memory; the consequence is a use-after-free, potentially with attacker-influenced data written via asus_kbd_set_report.

commit_msg:
prevent buffer overrun in NGIFLIB_NO_FILE mode

fixes #18
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tgif->input.bytes = buffer;'], 'added_lines': ['\tgif->input.buffer.bytes = buffer;', '\tgif->input.buffer.count = (unsigned long)filesize;']}
description: ngiflib 0.4 has a heap overflow in GetByte() at ngiflib.c:70 in NGIFLIB_NO_FILE mode, GetByte() reads memory buffer without checking the boundary.

code_evidence: The function allocates a heap buffer sized to filesize via malloc(filesize) and reads the file into it with fread(buffer,1,filesize,fgif). It then stores only the raw pointer in gif->input.bytes without recording the buffer length, so the memory-backed decoder has no boundary information. The companion GetByte() in ngiflib.c reads through this pointer without a limit check.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect is a missing length bound on a heap buffer used by the decoder, enabling access past the allocation. CWE-787 covers out-of-bounds memory access caused by absent bounds; here the observable impact is an out-of-bounds read, but the underlying root cause (unbounded buffer access) is the same missing-constraint pattern fixed by adding the count field.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the in-memory input is exposed as a bare pointer with no associated length, so downstream GetByte() cannot enforce the allocation boundary. Trigger: a crafted GIF whose parsing consumes bytes beyond the malloc(filesize) region. Consequence: an out-of-bounds read from the heap buffer (the issue-18 heap overflow), potentially leading to disclosure or crash; the patch adds input.buffer.count to bound reads.

commit_msg:
The ptrace PEEKUSR/POKEUSR (aka PEEKUSER/POKEUSER) API allows a process
to read/write registers of another process.

To get/set a register, the API takes an index into an imaginary address
space called the "USER area", where the registers of the process are
laid out in some fashion.

The kernel then maps that index to a particular register in its own data
structures and gets/sets the value.

The API only allows a single machine-word to be read/written at a time.
So 4 bytes on 32-bit kernels and 8 bytes on 64-bit kernels.

The way floating point registers (FPRs) are addressed is somewhat
complicated, because double precision float values are 64-bit even on
32-bit CPUs. That means on 32-bit kernels each FPR occupies two
word-sized locations in the USER area. On 64-bit kernels each FPR
occupies one word-sized location in the USER area.

Internally the kernel stores the FPRs in an array of u64s, or if VSX is
enabled, an array of pairs of u64s where one half of each pair stores
the FPR. Which half of the pair stores the FPR depends on the kernel's
endianness.

To handle the different layouts of the FPRs depending on VSX/no-VSX and
big/little endian, the TS_FPR() macro was introduced.

Unfortunately the TS_FPR() macro does not take into account the fact
that the addressing of each FPR differs between 32-bit and 64-bit
kernels. It just takes the index into the "USER area" passed from
userspace and indexes into the fp_state.fpr array.

On 32-bit there are 64 indexes that address FPRs, but only 32 entries in
the fp_state.fpr array, meaning the user can read/write 256 bytes past
the end of the array. Because the fp_state sits in the middle of the
thread_struct there are various fields than can be overwritten,
including some pointers. As such it may be exploitable.

It has also been observed to cause systems to hang or otherwise
misbehave when using gdbserver, and is probably the root cause of this
report which could not be easily reproduced:
  https://lore.kernel.org/linuxppc-dev/dc38afe9-6b78-f3f5-666b-986939e40fc6@keymile.com/

Rather than trying to make the TS_FPR() macro even more complicated to
fix the bug, or add more macros, instead add a special-case for 32-bit
kernels. This is more obvious and hopefully avoids a similar bug
happening again in future.

Note that because 32-bit kernels never have VSX enabled the code doesn't
need to consider TS_FPRWIDTH/OFFSET at all. Add a BUILD_BUG_ON() to
ensure that 32-bit && VSX is never enabled.

Fixes: 87fec0514f61 ("powerpc: PTRACE_PEEKUSR/PTRACE_POKEUSER of FPR registers in little endian builds")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # v3.13+
Reported-by: Ariel Miculas <ariel.miculas@belden.com>
Tested-by: Christophe Leroy <christophe.leroy@csgroup.eu>
Signed-off-by: Michael Ellerman <mpe@ellerman.id.au>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220609133245.573565-1-mpe@ellerman.id.au
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (fpidx < (PT_FPSCR - PT_FPR0))', '\t\tmemcpy(&child->thread.TS_FPR(fpidx), &data, sizeof(long));', '\telse'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (fpidx < (PT_FPSCR - PT_FPR0)) {', '\t\tif (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_PPC32))', '\t\t\t// On 32-bit the index we are passed refers to 32-bit words', '\t\t\t((u32 *)child->thread.fp_state.fpr)[fpidx] = data;', '\t\telse', '\t\t\tmemcpy(&child->thread.TS_FPR(fpidx), &data, sizeof(long));', '\t} else']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel through 5.18.3 on powerpc 32-bit platforms. There is a buffer overflow in ptrace PEEKUSER and POKEUSER (aka PEEKUSR and POKEUSR) when accessing floating point registers.

code_evidence: fpidx is derived from the user-controlled index minus PT_FPR0, so it is an attacker-chosen offset into the FPR area.
The check only bounds fpidx below PT_FPSCR - PT_FPR0; the subsequent memcpy writes sizeof(long) bytes to &child->thread.TS_FPR(fpidx), where TS_FPR indexes fp_state.fpr by fpidx.
On 32-bit kernels each FPR occupies two word-sized USER-area slots, so valid user indices can exceed the number of fpr array entries, letting TS_FPR(fpidx) address past the array.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs a copy into a fixed fp_state.fpr array without verifying that fpidx stays within the array bounds, so the input-derived size/offset allows writing past the destination. This is a buffer copy without an adequate size check, matching CWE-120; an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) is not the supported consequence here.

evidence_lines.code: unsigned int fpidx = index - PT_FPR0;

if (fpidx < (PT_FPSCR - PT_FPR0))
memcpy(&child->thread.TS_FPR(fpidx), &data, sizeof(long));

else
child->thread.fp_state.fpscr = data;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the index-to-register mapping ignores the 32-bit USER-area layout, so fpidx can exceed the fp_state.fpr array while still passing the check. Trigger: a ptrace POKEUSR call with a large FPR index on a 32-bit kernel. Consequence: memcpy writes past fp_state.fpr into adjacent thread_struct fields, corrupting memory (potentially pointers) and causing crashes or possible code execution.

commit_msg: Always enable hostname verification
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  const auto remote_hostname = *client_options_.remote_hostname_;', '', '  bool verify_hostname = false;', '    verify_hostname = true;', '    verify_hostname = true;', '    verify_hostname = true;', '                             remote_hostname.c_str());', '  if (verify_hostname) {', '    ssl_sock_->set_verify_callback(', '        boost::asio::ssl::rfc2818_verification(remote_hostname));', '  }'], 'added_lines': ['                             client_options_.remote_hostname_->c_str());', '  ssl_sock_->set_verify_callback(boost::asio::ssl::rfc2818_verification(', '      *client_options_.remote_hostname_));']}
description: Incorrect validation of the TLS SNI hostname in osquery versions after 2.9.0 and before 4.2.0 could allow an attacker to MITM osquery traffic in the absence of a configured root chain of trust.

code_evidence: The function reads remote_hostname and initializes verify_hostname to false; hostname verification is only enabled when always_verify_peer_ is set, otherwise verify mode is verify_none.
Setting server_certificate_ enables peer verification and sets verify_hostname true, but this flag governs whether rfc2818_verification is installed.
Likewise verify_path_ enables verify_peer and sets verify_hostname true; neither branch independently enforces hostname matching unless the flag is set.

The SNI name is set unconditionally, but the rfc2818_verification callback is installed only inside if (verify_hostname); otherwise the TLS session completes without checking the certificate's hostname.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-295 covers failure to validate or incorrect validation of a certificate. Here the server certificate's identity (hostname) is not validated in the default path because the verification callback is skipped, directly matching improper certificate validation rather than a generic trust-store issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: hostname verification is conditional on verify_hostname, which stays false unless a peer-verification option or trust store is configured. Trigger: a client connecting with default options (verify_none) performs the handshake without installing the rfc2818_verification callback. Consequence: a MITM presenting any certificate is accepted, since neither chain nor hostname is checked, enabling traffic interception.

description: In radare2 2.4.0, there is a heap-based buffer over-read in the dalvik_op function of anal_dalvik.c. Remote attackers could leverage this vulnerability to cause a denial of service via a crafted dex file.

code_evidence: For case 0x29 (goto/16), the code immediately reads data[2] and data[3] to compute op->jump without verifying that len covers those bytes.
For case 0x2a (goto/32), it reads data[2] through data[5] to build the 32-bit offset, again with no length check.
For the conditional-jump group (0x32–0x3d), op->jump reads data[2] and data[3] guarded only by len>3, which still permits a read of data[2] when len is 2.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Reading data[2..5] beyond the supplied len is an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). It is not a write or an integer overflow; the weakness is the missing bounds check before buffer access.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The root cause is that the instruction decoder indexes the data buffer for opcode operands without first constraining the operand count against len. A crafted/truncated dex instruction with a short buffer triggers reads past the end of the allocated buffer, causing a heap-based over-read whose supported consequence is a crash/denial of service.

commit_msg:
qxl: check release info object

When releasing spice resources in release_resource() routine,
if release info object 'ext.info' is null, it leads to null
pointer dereference. Add check to avoid it.

Reported-by: Bugs SysSec <bugs-syssec@rub.de>
Signed-off-by: Prasad J Pandit <pjp@fedoraproject.org>
Message-id: 20190425063534.32747-1-ppandit@redhat.com
Signed-off-by: Gerd Hoffmann <kraxel@redhat.com>
(cherry picked from commit d52680fc932efb8a2f334cc6993e705ed1e31e99)
Signed-off-by: Michael Roth <mdroth@linux.vnet.ibm.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    if (!ext.info) {', '        return;', '    }']}
description: interface_release_resource in hw/display/qxl.c in QEMU 3.1.x through 4.0.0 has a NULL pointer dereference.

code_evidence: Line 7 branches on ext.group_id; line 8 dereferences ext.info->id without verifying ext.info is non-NULL, so the host-group path can fault on a NULL pointer.
In the ring path, lines 20-22 dereference ext.info->id and ext.info->next without a NULL check on ext.info.
Lines 27-32 likewise dereference ext.info->id and store ext.info in qxl->last_release, propagating a NULL pointer if ext.info is NULL.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits: the root cause is an unchecked pointer expected to be valid, and the supported consequence is a NULL pointer dereference crash. This is distinct from a general invalid-pointer or use-after-free issue, since the specific flaw is the missing NULL check on ext.info before dereference.

evidence_lines.code:
if (ext.group_id == MEMSLOT_GROUP_HOST) {
QXLCommandExt *cmdext = (void *)(intptr_t)(ext.info->id);

qxl->last_release->next = ext.info->id;
qxl->last_release = ext.info;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function assumes ext.info is valid and dereferences it on multiple paths (lines 8, 21-22, 27-30) and stores it (line 32). If a caller passes an ext with NULL info, the dereference causes a NULL pointer dereference, crashing the guest/host QXL resource release path (availability DoS).

commit_msg:
libsepol/cil: Destroy classperms list when resetting classpermission

Nicolas Iooss reports:
  A few months ago, OSS-Fuzz found a crash in the CIL compiler, which
  got reported as
  https://bugs.chromium.org/p/oss-fuzz/issues/detail?id=28648 (the title
  is misleading, or is caused by another issue that conflicts with the
  one I report in this message). Here is a minimized CIL policy which
  reproduces the issue:

  (class CLASS (PERM))
  (classorder (CLASS))
  (sid SID)
  (sidorder (SID))
  (user USER)
  (role ROLE)
  (type TYPE)
  (category CAT)
  (categoryorder (CAT))
  (sensitivity SENS)
  (sensitivityorder (SENS))
  (sensitivitycategory SENS (CAT))
  (allow TYPE self (CLASS (PERM)))
  (roletype ROLE TYPE)
  (userrole USER ROLE)
  (userlevel USER (SENS))
  (userrange USER ((SENS)(SENS (CAT))))
  (sidcontext SID (USER ROLE TYPE ((SENS)(SENS))))

  (classpermission CLAPERM)

  (optional OPT
      (roletype nonexistingrole nonexistingtype)
      (classpermissionset CLAPERM (CLASS (PERM)))
  )

  The CIL policy fuzzer (which mimics secilc built with clang Address
  Sanitizer) reports:

  ==36541==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free on address
  0x603000004f98 at pc 0x56445134c842 bp 0x7ffe2a256590 sp
  0x7ffe2a256588
  READ of size 8 at 0x603000004f98 thread T0
      #0 0x56445134c841 in __cil_verify_classperms
  /selinux/libsepol/src/../cil/src/cil_verify.c:1620:8
      #1 0x56445134a43e in __cil_verify_classpermission
  /selinux/libsepol/src/../cil/src/cil_verify.c:1650:9
      #2 0x56445134a43e in __cil_pre_verify_helper
  /selinux/libsepol/src/../cil/src/cil_verify.c:1715:8
      #3 0x5644513225ac in cil_tree_walk_core
  /selinux/libsepol/src/../cil/src/cil_tree.c:272:9
      #4 0x564451322ab1 in cil_tree_walk
  /selinux/libsepol/src/../cil/src/cil_tree.c:316:7
      #5 0x5644513226af in cil_tree_walk_core
  /selinux/libsepol/src/../cil/src/cil_tree.c:284:9
      #6 0x564451322ab1 in cil_tree_walk
  /selinux/libsepol/src/../cil/src/cil_tree.c:316:7
      #7 0x5644512b88fd in cil_pre_verify
  /selinux/libsepol/src/../cil/src/cil_post.c:2510:7
      #8 0x5644512b88fd in cil_post_process
  /selinux/libsepol/src/../cil/src/cil_post.c:2524:7
      #9 0x5644511856ff in cil_compile
  /selinux/libsepol/src/../cil/src/cil.c:564:7

The classperms list of a classpermission rule is created and filled
in when classpermissionset rules are processed, so it doesn't own any
part of the list and shouldn't retain any of it when it is reset.

Destroy the classperms list (without destroying the data in it)  when
resetting a classpermission rule.

Reported-by: Nicolas Iooss <nicolas.iooss@m4x.org>
Signed-off-by: James Carter <jwcart2@gmail.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tcil_reset_classperms_list(cp->classperms);'], 'added_lines': ['\tcil_list_destroy(&cp->classperms, CIL_FALSE);']}
description: The CIL compiler in SELinux 3.2 has a use-after-free in __cil_verify_classperms (called from __cil_verify_classpermission and __cil_pre_verify_helper).

code_evidence: The reset function returns early only when cp is NULL, so a non-NULL classpermission is always reset.

For a non-NULL cp, the code calls cil_reset_classperms_list(cp->classperms) on the classperms list. This treats the list as owned data and resets/frees its contents, but the commit states the list is created and filled by classpermissionset rules and is not owned here.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the reset path frees list data that remains referenced elsewhere, and subsequent verification dereferences it. This is a use-after-free rather than a simple memory leak or double free, since the supported consequence is reading memory after release.

evidence_lines.code: cil_reset_classperms_list(cp->classperms);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: cil_reset_classpermission resets the classperms list contents that the classpermission does not own, so elements referenced by other structures are freed. Trigger: an optional/classpermissionset construct causes the classpermission to be reset while its classperms list is still referenced. Consequence: later verification in __cil_verify_classperms reads freed memory, producing a use-after-free crash.

commit_msg:
x86/PV: check GDT/LDT limits during emulation

Accesses beyond the LDT limit originating from emulation would trigger
the ASSERT() in pv_map_ldt_shadow_page(). On production builds such
accesses would cause an attempt to promote the touched page (offset from
the present LDT base address) to a segment descriptor one. If this
happens to succeed, guest user mode would be able to elevate its
privileges to that of the guest kernel. This is particularly easy when
there's no LDT at all, in which case the LDT base stored internally to
Xen is simply zero.

Also adjust the ASSERT() that was triggering: It was off by one to
begin with, and for production builds we also better use
ASSERT_UNREACHABLE() instead with suitable recovery code afterwards.

This is XSA-298.

Reported-by: Andrew Cooper <andrew.cooper3@citrix.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Reviewed-by: Andrew Cooper <andrew.cooper3@citrix.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['     * Hardware limit checking should guarantee this property.  NB. This is', '    ASSERT((offset >> 3) <= curr->arch.pv.ldt_ents);'], 'added_lines': ['     * Prior limit checking should guarantee this property.  NB. This is', '    if ( unlikely((offset >> 3) >= curr->arch.pv.ldt_ents) )', '    {', '        ASSERT_UNREACHABLE();', '        return false;', '    }']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.12.x allowing 32-bit PV guest OS users to gain guest OS privileges by installing and using descriptors. There is missing descriptor table limit checking in x86 PV emulation. When emulating certain PV guest operations, descriptor table accesses are performed by the emulating code. Such accesses should respect the guest specified limits, unless otherwise guaranteed to fail in such a case. Without this, emulation of 32-bit guest user mode calls through call gates would allow guest user mode to install and then use descriptors of their choice, as long as the guest kernel did not itself install an LDT. (Most OSes don't install any LDT by default). 32-bit PV guest user mode can elevate its privileges to that of the guest kernel. Xen versions from at least 3.2 onwards are affected. Only 32-bit PV guest user mode can leverage this vulnerability. HVM, PVH, as well as 64-bit PV guests cannot leverage this vulnerability. Arm systems are unaffected.

code_evidence: The LDT base plus the caller-supplied offset is computed as the linear address used for the shadow LDT mapping, but the only guard on the offset is ASSERT((offset >> 3) <= curr->arch.pv.ldt_ents), which is compiled out in production builds.

The offset is then used to index pv_ldt_ptes(curr)[offset >> PAGE_SHIFT] and the resulting PTE is overwritten with guest-controlled gl1e (with _PAGE_RW added), so an unchecked offset writes into the shadow LDT page table.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing limit check lets a lower-privileged PV guest user actor obtain and exercise descriptor privileges reserved for the guest kernel, which is improper privilege management/assignment (CWE-269). The assertion-only check is the access-control mistake enabling the unintended sphere of control.

evidence_lines.code:
unsigned long linear = curr->arch.pv.ldt_base + offset;
ASSERT((offset >> 3) <= curr->arch.pv.ldt_ents);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the descriptor-table limit is enforced only by a debug-only assertion, so production builds accept offsets beyond ldt_ents (or any offset when no LDT exists and ldt_base is zero). Trigger: 32-bit PV guest user mode emulates a call gate through the LDT. Consequence: the out-of-range offset promotes an arbitrary guest page to a segment-descriptor page, letting user mode install and use descriptors and elevate to guest-kernel privileges.

commit_msg:
patch 8.2.5072: using uninitialized value and freed memory in spell command

Problem:    Using uninitialized value and freed memory in spell command.
Solution:   Initialize "attr".  Check for empty line early.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    hlf_T\tattr;', '\t// possible.', '\t    if (*skipwhite(line) == NUL)'], 'added_lines': ['    hlf_T\tattr = 0;', '\tint empty_line;', '', '\t// possible.  Note: this ml_get_buf() may make "line" invalid, check', '\t// for empty line first.', '\tempty_line = *skipwhite(line) == NUL;', '\t    if (empty_line)']}
description: Use After Free in GitHub repository vim/vim prior to 8.2.

code_evidence: Line 31 fetches the current line pointer; line 50 may refresh it via ml_get_buf after check_need_cap, and lines 52-55 copy line and concatenate the next line, which can reallocate the buffer and invalidate the earlier line pointer.
Later, lines 154-160 dereference line via skipwhite(line) to decide capcol after the inner loop, but line may already have been invalidated by the ml_get_buf/STRCPY/spell_cat_line calls.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the function uses a pointer to buffer memory after later operations may have freed or invalidated it; the fix captures the empty-line test in empty_line before the invalidating calls, confirming the stale-pointer use.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the code retains and later dereferences the line pointer obtained from ml_get_buf after intervening buffer operations (line 50 refresh, lines 52-55 copy/concatenate) can free or reallocate that storage. Trigger: spell_move_to processes a line, reaches the backward/forward branch, and evaluates skipwhite(line). Consequence: reading freed/reallocated memory, causing the reported use-after-free and possible crash or corrupted behavior.

commit_msg:
Fixed OOB read in update_recv_secondary_order

CVE-2020-4032 thanks to @antonio-morales for finding this.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tdiff = start - end;', '\t\tStream_Seek(s, diff);'], 'added_lines': ['\tdiff = end - start;', '\t\tif (!Stream_SafeSeek(s, diff))', '\t\t\treturn FALSE;']}
description: In FreeRDP before version 2.1.2, there is an integer casting vulnerability in update_recv_secondary_order. All clients with +glyph-cache /relax-order-checks are affected. This is fixed in version 2.1.2.

code_evidence: At line 132 the code compares size_t start and end; if start > end it logs end - start and returns FALSE. Otherwise line 138 computes diff = start - end, but since this branch implies start <= end, the unsigned size_t subtraction yields a wrapped (underflowed) huge value rather than a small positive shortfall. Line 139 then tests diff > 0, which is always true after wrapping, and line 143 calls Stream_Seek(s, diff) with the wrapped magnitude.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect is an incorrect numeric conversion between the signed conceptual shortfall and the unsigned size_t result, producing an unexpected wrapped value later used in a sensitive seek operation. This matches CWE-681's incorrect conversion between numeric types; it is distinct from a plain integer overflow because the value is silently reinterpreted through unsigned subtraction, not merely exceeding a bound.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: an unsigned size_t subtraction start - end is performed in the branch where start <= end, so the intended 'bytes short' value is produced as a huge wrapped number instead of a small positive difference. Trigger: any secondary order where end exceeds start, reachable with +glyph-cache/relax-order-checks. The wrapped diff drives Stream_Seek to an out-of-bounds position, enabling an out-of-bounds read.

commit_msg:
BGP: Validate length of Path Attribute records.

Bug 13741 showed a case where the BGP dissector's failure to validate the
length of the Path Attribute record allowed a pathological BGP UPDATE packet to
generate more than one million items in the protocol tree by repeatedly
dissecting certain segments of the packet.

It's easy enough to detect when the Path Attribute length cannot be valid, so
let's do so.  When the condition arises, let's raise an Expert Info error in
the same style and format as used elsewhere in the same routine, and abandon
dissection of the Path Attributes list.

With this check in place, an incorrect length computation is revealed at a
callsite.  This would only have prevented a small (less than 5 bytes) Path
Attribute from being dissected if it was at the very end of the Path Attributes
list, but the bounds checking added in this change makes this problem much more
apparent, so we fix the length computation while we're here.

Testing Done: Built wireshark on Linux amd64.  Using bgp.pcap from the Sample
   Captures page on the wiki, verified that the dissection of the UPDATE
   packets were unaltered by this fix.  Using the capture attached to bug 13741
   (clusterfuzz-testcase-minimized-6689222578667520.pcap), verified that the
   packet no longer triggers the "too many items" exception, instead we see
   an Expert Info for each oversized Path Attribute length, and eventually an
   exception for "length of contained item exceeds length of containing item".
   30,000 iterations of fuzz test with bgp.pcap as input, and many iterations
   of randpkt-test too.  Crafted a packet with a 3-byte ATOMIC_AGGREGATE Path
   Attribute at the end of the Path Attributes list; Before this change, an
   exception is raised during dissection, but after this change it is dissected
   correctly.

Bug: 13741
Change-Id: I80f506b114a61e5b060d93b59bed6b94fb188b3e
Reviewed-on: https://code.wireshark.org/review/27466
Reviewed-by: Peter Wu <peter@lekensteyn.nl>
Petri-Dish: Peter Wu <peter@lekensteyn.nl>
Tested-by: Petri Dish Buildbot
Reviewed-by: Anders Broman <a.broman58@gmail.com>
(cherry picked from commit 6e88943d0eabc8c8bc11334ba4213ec64129575c)
Reviewed-on: https://code.wireshark.org/review/28403
Reviewed-by: Guy Harris <guy@alum.mit.edu>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['        if (aoff + tlen > path_attr_len - i) {', '            proto_tree_add_expert_format(subtree2, pinfo, &ei_bgp_length_invalid, tvb, o + i + aoff, tlen,', '                                         "Path attribute length is invalid: %u byte%s", tlen,', '                                         plurality(tlen, "", "s"));', '            return;', '        }']}
description: In Wireshark 2.6.0 to 2.6.1, 2.4.0 to 2.4.7, and 2.2.0 to 2.2.15, the BGP protocol dissector could go into a large loop. This was addressed in epan/dissectors/packet-bgp.c by validating Path Attribute lengths.

code_evidence: The loop at line 41 iterates while i < path_attr_len, reading bgpa_flags and bgpa_type at o+i and o+i+1 and computing aoff/tlen from the attribute header without verifying that the declared attribute length fits within the remaining Path Attributes region.

Lines 66-77 immediately build tree items spanning tlen+aoff bytes and add the attribute subtree; later case branches index the tvb using o+i+aoff and tlen, so an oversized tlen drives repeated dissection and tree growth.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-834 fits because the weakness is a loop whose iteration count is not sufficiently bounded by validated input lengths, enabling resource exhaustion. It is not merely an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125); the supported impact emphasized here is excessive iteration leading to DoS.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the per-attribute length (tlen/alen) is trusted without a bounds check against path_attr_len - i, so a crafted BGP UPDATE can declare lengths that cause the loop body to repeatedly add items and dissect segments. Trigger: a malformed Path Attribute record in an attacker-supplied packet. Consequence: excessive resource consumption (CPU/memory) and possible crash, i.e., the large-loop DoS described in the commit.

commit_msg:
Strict KEX 対応 (CVE-2023-48795)

とりあえず Strict KEX のネゴシエーションとシーケンス番号のリセットに対応。
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tpvar->server_strict_kex = FALSE;']}
description: The SSH transport protocol with certain OpenSSH extensions, found in OpenSSH before 9.6 and other products, allows remote attackers to bypass integrity checks such that some packets are omitted (from the extension negotiation message), and a client and server may consequently end up with a connection for which some security features have been downgraded or disabled, aka a Terrapin attack. This occurs because the SSH Binary Packet Protocol (BPP), implemented by these extensions, mishandles the handshake phase and mishandles use of sequence numbers. For example, there is an effective attack against SSH's use of ChaCha20-Poly1305 (and CBC with Encrypt-then-MAC). The bypass occurs in chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com and (if CBC is used) the -etm@openssh.com MAC algorithms. This also affects Maverick Synergy Java SSH API before 3.1.0-SNAPSHOT, Dropbear through 2022.83, Ssh before 5.1.1 in Erlang/OTP, PuTTY before 0.80, AsyncSSH before 2.14.2, golang.org/x/crypto before 0.17.0, libssh before 0.10.6, libssh2 through 1.11.0, Thorn Tech SFTP Gateway before 3.4.6, Tera Term before 5.1, Paramiko before 3.4.0, jsch before 0.2.15, SFTPGo before 2.5.6, Netgate pfSense Plus through 23.09.1, Netgate pfSense CE through 2.7.2, HPN-SSH through 18.2.0, ProFTPD before 1.3.8b (and before 1.3.9rc2), ORYX CycloneSSH before 2.3.4, NetSarang XShell 7 before Build 0144, CrushFTP before 10.6.0, ConnectBot SSH library before 2.2.22, Apache MINA sshd through 2.11.0, sshj through 0.37.0, TinySSH through 20230101, trilead-ssh2 6401, LANCOM LCOS and LANconfig, FileZilla before 3.66.4, Nova before 11.8, PKIX-SSH before 14.4, SecureCRT before 9.4.3, Transmit5 before 5.10.4, Win32-OpenSSH before 9.5.0.0p1-Beta, WinSCP before 6.2.2, Bitvise SSH Server before 9.32, Bitvise SSH Client before 9.33, KiTTY through 0.76.1.13, the net-ssh gem 7.2.0 for Ruby, the mscdex ssh2 module before 1.15.0 for Node.js, the thrussh library before 0.35.1 for Rust, and the Russh crate before 0.40.2 for Rust.

description: ImageMagick 7.0.8-34 has a "use of uninitialized value" vulnerability in the ReadPANGOImage function in coders/pango.c.

code_evidence: SetImageExtent allocates the image pixel cache with image->columns and image->rows; if it fails the code destroys the list and returns.

After layout rendering, SetImageBackgroundColor is called before the loop reads pixels. The loop reads four bytes per pixel from the cairo buffer and composites them over the image via CompositePixelOver.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-665 fits because the image resource (background/pixel state) is initialized late or conditionally, so subsequent access reads an unexpected/uninitialized state. This is improper initialization rather than an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125), since the buffer is allocated but its contents are not guaranteed initialized before use.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The cairo surface is created over the virtual-memory buffer and cleared, but the image background is initialized only after rendering. If the earlier background initialization is skipped (e.g., zero columns/rows path) or the surface content is not fully written by pango_cairo_show_layout, the loop consumes pixel data whose alpha/color state was not properly initialized by SetImageBackgroundColor, leading to use of uninitialized values in CompositePixelOver.

description: In function lys_node_free() in libyang <= v1.0.225, it asserts that the value of node->module can't be NULL. But in some cases, node->module can be null, which triggers a reachable assertion (CWE-617).

code_evidence: read_yin_common() is called with retval before the node is fully attached; on failure it jumps to error.
lys_node_addchild() failure also jumps to error.

The error label calls lys_node_free(retval, NULL, 0) on the partially initialized uses node. Because the node->module is not set in these early-failure paths, lys_node_free's assertion on node->module fires.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function's error path invokes a free routine that asserts on a NULL module, so an attacker-influenced parse failure reaches an assert and terminates the process, matching CWE-617.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the error cleanup path frees a partially initialized node whose module is unset, reaching an assertion inside lys_node_free. Trigger: a malformed/parsed 'uses' statement causing read_yin_common or lys_node_addchild to fail before module assignment. Consequence: reachable assertion and process abort (DoS).

description: Out-of-bounds read in GitHub repository radareorg/radare2 prior to 5.6.8. This vulnerability allows attackers to read sensitive information from outside the allocated buffer boundary.

commit_msg: Json library: fix a number of potential buffer overflows
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    /* TODO check max depth */'], 'added_lines': ['    if(js_ctx->depth >= JSONTREE_MAX_DEPTH - 1) {', '      /* Too deep: return 0 */', '      return 0;', '    }']}
description: Contiki-NG before 4.2 has a stack-based buffer overflow in the push function in os/lib/json/jsonparse.c that allows an out-of-bounds write of an '{' or '[' character.

code_evidence: Before the fix, js_ctx->depth is incremented unconditionally and then used to index the fixed-size arrays js_ctx->index[] and js_ctx->values[] without any bound check. The removed 'TODO check max depth' comment confirms no depth constraint existed, so nesting through JSON_TYPE_OBJECT/JSON_TYPE_ARRAY repeatedly advances depth past the array capacity.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe operation is a write past the end of the intended js_ctx->values/js_ctx->index buffers due to an unchecked depth, matching CWE-787 Out-of-bounds Write. An out-of-bounds read or missing recursion limit alone would be CWE-125/674, but here the indexed arrays are written, so CWE-787 fits.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: missing bound check on js_ctx->depth before indexing js_ctx->index and js_ctx->values. Trigger: a deeply nested object/array structure causes repeated recursion into the OBJECT/ARRAY case, incrementing depth each time. Consequence: writes to js_ctx->index[js_ctx->depth] and js_ctx->values[js_ctx->depth] go past the fixed array bounds, an out-of-bounds stack write.

description: In Wireshark 2.4.0 to 2.4.4 and 2.2.0 to 2.2.12, epan/dissectors/packet-wccp.c had a large loop that was addressed by ensuring that a calculated length was monotonically increasing.

code_evidence: The loop count n_routers is read directly from the packet (tvb_get_ntohl) with no upper bound, then used as the termination condition of the for loop at line 17. Offset advances only by EAT(12) per iteration, and the loop body's guard at line 18 only checks the remaining length against 12, returning a computed value when exhausted rather than limiting iterations.
The second call at line 26/27 also feeds a packet-derived length into the same consumption path.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-834 fits because the for loop at line 17 iterates up to a packet-supplied n_routers without sufficient limiting, matching excessive iteration driven by attacker input; the resource-consumption impact aligns with the entry's availability scope.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: an attacker-controlled router count (n_routers) drives the loop without a maximum bound, while the per-iteration offset advance is small (EAT(12)). Trigger: a crafted WCCP packet declaring a very large n_routers with a sufficiently long body. Consequence: excessive iteration consuming CPU, and the commit's fix (CHECK_LENGTH_ADVANCE_OFFSET) confirms the offset was not guaranteed to advance, enabling a large/effectively unbounded loop.

commit_msg:
Fix integer overflow in num_images

Includes the fix for CVE-2021-29338
Credit to @kaniini based on #1346
Fixes #1338

description: Integer Overflow in OpenJPEG v2.4.0 allows remote attackers to crash the application, causing a Denial of Service (DoS). This occurs when the attacker uses the command line option "-ImgDir" on a directory that contains 1048576 files.

code_evidence: num_images is obtained from get_num_images(img_fol.imgdirpath) as an OPJ_INT32 and used as the element count for allocation of filename_buf via malloc((size_t)num_images * OPJ_PATH_LEN) at lines 29-30, and for filename via malloc((size_t)num_images * sizeof(char*)) at line 35. No bound is checked on num_images before these multiplications.
The loop at lines 40-42 indexes filename[it_image] and computes filename_buf + it_image * OPJ_PATH_LEN, assuming the allocation size matches num_images entries.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect is an integer overflow/wraparound in a size computation that feeds memory allocation, matching CWE-190. It is not merely a missing length check (CWE-1284) because the arithmetic itself wraps before the allocation, and the wrapped size is what causes the out-of-bounds access.

evidence_lines.code:
for (it_image = 0; it_image < num_images; it_image++) {
dirptr->filename[it_image] = dirptr->filename_buf + it_image * OPJ_PATH_LEN;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The size calculation (size_t)num_images * OPJ_PATH_LEN can wrap when num_images is large (e.g., 1048576 files with a large OPJ_PATH_LEN), yielding a small allocation. The subsequent loop then writes num_images pointers/offsets beyond the allocated buffer, causing heap corruption and a crash (DoS). The root cause is the unchecked multiplication used as an allocation size; the trigger is a directory with many files passed via -ImgDir.

commit_msg:
mime-actions: use file metadata for trusting desktop files

Currently we only trust desktop files that have the executable bit
set, and don't replace the displayed icon or the displayed name until
it's trusted, which prevents for running random programs by a malicious
desktop file.

However, the executable permission is preserved if the desktop file
comes from a compressed file.

To prevent this, add a metadata::trusted metadata to the file once the
user acknowledges the file as trusted. This adds metadata to the file,
which cannot be added unless it has access to the computer.

Also remove the SHEBANG "trusted" content we were putting inside the
desktop file, since that doesn't add more security since it can come
with the file itself.

https://bugzilla.gnome.org/show_bug.cgi?id=777991

Not sure why the general monitor doesn't fire in this", '             * case when setting the metadata', '             */', '            nautilus_file_invalidate_all_attributes (parameters->file);', '']}
description: GNOME Nautilus before 3.23.90 allows attackers to spoof a file type by using the .desktop file extension, as demonstrated by an attack in which a .desktop file's Name field ends in .pdf but this file's Exec field launches a malicious "sh -c" command. In other words, Nautilus provides no UI indication that a file actually has the potentially unsafe .desktop extension; instead, the UI only shows the .pdf extension. One (slightly) mitigating factor is that an attack requires the .desktop file to have execute permission. The solution is to ask the user to confirm that the file is supposed to be treated as a .desktop file, and then remember the user's answer in the metadata::trusted field.

code_evidence: The RESPONSE_RUN branch immediately launches the untrusted desktop file via nautilus_launch_desktop_file using only its URI, with no check of the .desktop extension, Name field, or Exec content before execution.

The RESPONSE_MARK_TRUSTED branch marks the file trusted and returns without re-validating that the file is a genuine desktop launcher; the trust decision relies on the user's dialog response rather than inspecting the file's actual type/content.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-20 fits because the function processes the desktop file (a structured input with Name/Exec metadata) without validating that its declared type and contents match a safe launcher, allowing spoofed metadata to drive execution. This is a missing-validation root cause, not mere encoding or filtering.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the callback acts on a user dialog response without validating the desktop file's actual content or extension, so a file whose displayed name ends in .pdf but whose Exec runs a malicious command is launched. Trigger: user accepts the untrusted-launcher prompt. Supported consequence: unauthorized code execution as the user.

description: In GIMP 2.8.22, there is a stack-based buffer over-read in xcf_load_stream in app/xcf/xcf.c when there is no '\0' character after the version string.

code_evidence: id is a fixed 14-byte stack buffer [11]; xcf_read_int8 fills exactly 14 bytes [32] without guaranteeing a terminator. The version branch [41] calls atoi(id + 10) [43], which scans until a NUL byte; if the 14 bytes contain no '\0' after position 10, atoi reads past the end of id.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits: the code reads memory beyond the intended 'id' buffer via atoi on a non-terminated string. Contrast CWE-126 (over-read past the end is not the issue) and CWE-119 (broader); the specific weakness is an out-of-bounds read.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the version string is assumed NUL-terminated, but the 14-byte read may fill the whole buffer. Trigger: a crafted XCF header whose version field lacks a '\0'. Consequence: atoi reads past the stack buffer (out-of-bounds read), causing disclosure/crash potential, as the commit message notes.

commit_msg:
Fix for null pointer dereference in jmem_heap_free_block

Fixes #2435.

JerryScript-DCO-1.0-Signed-off-by: Daniel Balla dballa@inf.u-szeged.hu
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [''], 'added_lines': ['', '  if (len == 0)', '  {', '    return ecma_op_create_typedarray_with_type_and_length (obj_p, 0);', '  }']}
description: JerryScript version Tested on commit f86d7459d195c8ba58479d1861b0cc726c8b3793. Analysing history it seems that the issue has been present since commit 64a340ffeb8809b2b66bbe32fd443a8b79fdd860 contains a CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference vulnerability in Triggering undefined behavior at jerry-core/ecma/builtin-objects/typedarray/ecma-builtin-typedarray-prototype.c:598 (passing NULL to memcpy as 2nd argument) results in null pointer dereference (segfault) at jerry-core/jmem/jmem-heap.c:463 that can result in Crash due to segmentation fault. This attack appear to be exploitable via The victim must execute specially crafted javascript code. This vulnerability appears to have been fixed in after commit 87897849f6879df10e8ad68a41bf8cf507edf710.

code_evidence: len is obtained from the typedarray (line 15) and used to size the local array via len * element_size (line 21); when len is 0 this macro allocates a zero-length/NULL buffer.

pass_value_p starts at pass_value_list_p; with len 0 the loop is skipped, pass_num becomes 0 (line 42), a new zero-length typedarray is created (line 43), and memcpy (lines 48-50) copies 0 bytes from the possibly-NULL source buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences a buffer pointer it assumes is valid, but which is NULL for zero length, matching CWE-476's null pointer dereference. The added len==0 early return confirms the missing guard; this is not a general buffer overflow (CWE-787) since the copy size is zero.

uint32_t len = ecma_typedarray_get_length (obj_p);
JMEM_DEFINE_LOCAL_ARRAY (pass_value_list_p, len * element_size, lit_utf8_byte_t);

uint32_t pass_num = (uint32_t) ((pass_value_p - pass_value_list_p) >> shift);
(size_t) (pass_value_p - pass_value_list_p));

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: a zero-length input typedarray produces a NULL/zero-size local buffer, yet the code still passes it to memcpy. Trigger: calling TypedArray.prototype.filter on an empty typedarray. The unsupported consequence is a NULL pointer dereference (segfault) rather than a defined empty result.

commit_msg: Added received buffer size checks.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            if( MAX( 0, ( int16_t )( ( int16_t ) size - ( int16_t ) LORA_MAC_FRMPAYLOAD_OVERHEAD ) ) > ( int16_t )phyParam.Value )'], 'added_lines': ['            // Check if the received frame size is valid', '            if( size < LORAMAC_JOIN_ACCEPT_FRAME_MIN_SIZE )', '            {', '                MacCtx.McpsIndication.Status = LORAMAC_EVENT_INFO_STATUS_ERROR;', '                PrepareRxDoneAbort( );', '                return;', '            }', '            if( ( MAX( 0, ( int16_t )( ( int16_t ) size - ( int16_t ) LORAMAC_FRAME_PAYLOAD_OVERHEAD_SIZE ) ) > ( int16_t )phyParam.Value ) ||', '                ( size < LORAMAC_FRAME_PAYLOAD_MIN_SIZE ) )']}
description: In LoRaMac-node before 4.4.4, a reception buffer overflow can happen due to the received buffer size not being checked. This has been fixed in 4.4.4.

code_evidence: size is taken directly from the received radio frame (RxDoneParams.Size) and used to populate macMsgJoinAccept.BufSize before the join-accept is parsed; the CFList size is computed as size - 17, which underflows when size < 17, and the join-accept path lacks the minimum-size check added by the patch.

For data frames, macMsgData.BufSize is set to the untrusted size and FRMPayloadSize is fixed to LORAMAC_PHY_MAXPAYLOAD, so the parser works from an attacker-controlled length without a lower-bound validation.
In the proprietary branch, memcpy1 copies size - pktHeaderLen bytes from the received payload into the fixed MacCtx.RxPayload buffer with no check that the length fits the destination.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The proprietary branch copies attacker-controlled received data into MacCtx.RxPayload without verifying the input size against the destination capacity, matching CWE-120's buffer copy without input-size checking. This is a write-side overflow, not merely an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125).
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the received frame length is trusted and used to size copies/parses without a minimum or capacity check. Trigger: a short or oversized received frame reaches the join-accept, data, or proprietary paths. Consequence: size underflow and out-of-bounds copies into fixed buffers, corrupting memory.

description: In freeradius, when an EAP-SIM supplicant sends an unknown SIM option, the server will try to look that option up in the internal dictionaries. This lookup will fail, but the SIM code will not check for that failure. Instead, it will dereference a NULL pointer, and cause the server to crash.

code_evidence: fr_pair_afrom_num returns a VALUE_PAIR pointer derived from the attacker-controlled eapsim_attribute; the code stores it in newvp and immediately writes newvp->vp_length, newvp->vp_octets and calls memcpy/fr_pair_add without checking whether the lookup succeeded (no NULL test before line 45).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits because the weakness is an unchecked NULL return that is then dereferenced. This is distinct from an out-of-bounds read: the missing constraint is a NULL check, not a length bound.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the return value of fr_pair_afrom_num is assumed non-NULL. Trigger: an EAP-SIM supplicant sends an unknown SIM option, so the dictionary lookup fails and returns NULL. Consequence: the write at line 45 dereferences NULL, crashing the server (DoS).

commit_msg:
netfilter: nf_nat_snmp_basic: add missing length checks in ASN.1 cbs

The generic ASN.1 decoder infrastructure doesn't guarantee that callbacks
will get as much data as they expect; callbacks have to check the `datalen`
parameter before looking at `data`. Make sure that snmp_version() and
snmp_helper() don't read/write beyond the end of the packet data.

(Also move the assignment to `pdata` down below the check to make it clear
that it isn't necessarily a pointer we can use before the `datalen` check.)

Fixes: cc2d58634e0f ("netfilter: nf_nat_snmp_basic: use asn1 decoder library")
Signed-off-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tif (datalen != 1)', '\t\treturn -EINVAL;']}
description: In the Linux kernel before 4.20.12, net/ipv4/netfilter/nf_nat_snmp_basic_main.c in the SNMP NAT module has insufficient ASN.1 length checks (aka an array index error), making out-of-bounds read and write operations possible, leading to an OOPS or local privilege escalation. This affects snmp_version and snmp_helper.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The shown function only performs an out-of-bounds read (dereferencing data without checking datalen); no write past the buffer is present, so the function does not support CWE-787 Out-of-bounds Write.

We will allocate a screen area of width*height*bpp bytes, however this
calculation can easily overflow if too high width or height are given
inside the stream. Nonetheless we would just assume that enough memory
was allocated, try to fill it and overwrite as much memory as wanted.

Also allocate the screen area filled with zeroes to ensure that we start
with full-black and not any random (or not so random) data.

https://scarybeastsecurity.blogspot.gr/2016/11/0day-poc-risky-design-decisions-in.html

Ideally we should just remove this plugin in favour of the one in
gst-libav, which generally seems to be of better code quality.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  dec->imagedata = g_malloc (dec->format.width * dec->format.height *'], 'added_lines': ['  dec->imagedata = g_malloc0 (dec->format.width * dec->format.height *']}
description: Integer overflow in the vmnc decoder in the gstreamer allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (crash) via large width and height values, which triggers a buffer overflow.

code_evidence: Lines 36-37 store attacker-controlled rectangle width and height into dec->format.width and dec->format.height with no range validation.
Lines 83-84 compute the allocation size as width * height * bytes_per_pixel in g_malloc without any overflow check, so the multiplication is performed in a fixed-width integer type.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the allocation-size multiplication can wrap to a small value, and that result is used as a memory-allocation size, which is the classic integer-overflow-to-buffer-overflow pattern. The missing constraint is the overflow check on the product, not a separate out-of-bounds write defect.

evidence_lines.code:
dec->format.width = rect->width;
dec->format.height = rect->height;

dec->imagedata = g_malloc (dec->format.width * dec->format.height *
dec->format.bytes_per_pixel);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the size expression width*height*bytes_per_pixel is computed without checking whether the product exceeds the integer range. Trigger: a WMVi rectangle supplying large width/height values (from the stream) causes wraparound to a small allocation size. The decoder then treats imagedata as large enough and writes pixel data, producing a heap buffer overflow with crash/memory-corruption consequences.

commit_msg:
Add missing returns

Fixes possible invalid read of two bytes.

Reported by Behzad Najjarpour Jabbari, Secunia Research.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if (unlikely (!c->may_dispatch (this, &u.sub_format))) TRACE_RETURN (c->default_return_value ());'], 'added_lines': ['    if (unlikely (!c->may_dispatch (this, &u.sub_format))) return TRACE_RETURN (c->default_return_value ());']}
description: HarfBuzz before 1.0.4 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (invalid read of two bytes and application crash) because of GPOS and GSUB table mishandling, related to hb-ot-layout-gpos-table.hh, hb-ot-layout-gsub-table.hh, and hb-ot-layout-gsubgpos-private.hh.

code_evidence: Line 4 evaluates the may_dispatch guard and calls TRACE_RETURN(c->default_return_value()) without a return statement, so execution falls through to the switch even when dispatch is disallowed. The switch then reads/uses u.single, u.pair, etc. based on lookup_type.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect is an improper return that permits reads of table data after the dispatch guard fails, directly enabling an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). It is not merely a logic error, because the supported consequence is reading memory beyond the intended buffer.

evidence_lines.code:
if (unlikely (!c->may_dispatch (this, &u.sub_format))) TRACE_RETURN (c->default_return_value ());
switch (lookup_type) {

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the missing return after the failed may_dispatch check lets control flow continue into switch cases that access union members (u.single.dispatch, etc.) for a lookup that should have been rejected. Trigger: a lookup_type/sub_format combination that fails may_dispatch. Consequence: downstream dispatch reads GPOS/GSUB data past the intended buffer, the invalid two-byte read and crash described in the commit.

description: PJSIP is a free and open source multimedia communication library written in the C language implementing standard based protocols such as SIP, SDP, RTP, STUN, TURN, and ICE. In various parts of PJSIP, when error/failure occurs, it is found that the function returns without releasing the currently held locks. This could result in a system deadlock, which cause a denial of service for the users. No release has yet been made which contains the linked fix commit. All versions up to an including 2.11.1 are affected. Users may need to manually apply the patch.

code_evidence: Line 6 acquires vid_conf->mutex; the normal exit at line 33 unlocks it.
In the AUTO_STOP_CLOCK branch, if pjmedia_clock_stop fails, lines 29-30 log and return status directly, bypassing the unlock at line 33 while the mutex is still held.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-667 covers improper lock acquisition/release; returning without releasing a held mutex is a direct instance. The added unlock line confirms the missing release on this failure path, distinguishing it from simple race conditions (CWE-362).

evidence_lines.code: pj_mutex_unlock(vid_conf->mutex);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is an early error-path return that skips pj_mutex_unlock, leaving vid_conf->mutex held. Trigger is a failed clock stop when the last connection is removed; the supported consequence is a permanently locked mutex, causing deadlock/denial of service for subsequent operations on the video conference.

commit_msg:
avformat/hls: Fix DoS due to infinite loop

Fixes: loop.m3u

The default max iteration count of 1000 is arbitrary and ideas for a better solution are welcome

Found-by: Xiaohei and Wangchu from Alibaba Security Team

Previous version reviewed-by: Steven Liu <lingjiujianke@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
(cherry picked from commit 7ec414892ddcad88313848494b6fc5f437c9ca4a)
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    int reload_count = 0;', '        reload_count++;', '        if (reload_count > c->max_reload)', '            return AVERROR_EOF;']}
description: In FFmpeg 2.4 and 3.3.3, the read_data function in libavformat/hls.c does not restrict reload attempts for an insufficient list, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (infinite loop).

code_evidence: At the reload label (line 27), the code re-parses the playlist when the reload interval has elapsed (lines 28-36). If the current sequence number has reached the end of the playlist and the playlist is not finished, the code sleeps until the interval passes and then jumps back to reload (lines 43-51). The only exits are when v->finished is set (line 44-45) or an interrupt is raised (line 47-48); a playlist that never becomes finished and never provides new segments loops indefinitely.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-835 fits because the goto reload cycle's exit condition (finished or interrupt) is unreachable for an insufficient, never-finishing playlist, producing an infinite loop. It is not merely an unbounded resource use; the loop lacks any reachable terminating condition without external interruption.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the reload/goto-reload cycle has no bound on the number of reload attempts for a playlist that stays insufficient (cur_seq_no beyond available segments while finished remains false). Trigger: a crafted playlist that parses successfully but never supplies new segments. Consequence: the function spins in the reload loop, consuming CPU and hanging the demuxer (DoS).

commit_msg:
x86/insn-eval: Fix use-after-free access to LDT entry

get_desc() computes a pointer into the LDT while holding a lock that
protects the LDT from being freed, but then drops the lock and returns the
(now potentially dangling) pointer to its caller.

Fix it by giving the caller a copy of the LDT entry instead.

Fixes: 670f928ba09b ("x86/insn-eval: Add utility function to get segment descriptor")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['static struct desc_struct *get_desc(unsigned short sel)', '\t\tstruct desc_struct *desc = NULL;', '\t\tif (ldt && sel < ldt->nr_entries)', '\t\t\tdesc = &ldt->entries[sel];', '\t\treturn desc;', '\t\treturn NULL;', '\treturn (struct desc_struct *)(gdt_desc.address + desc_base);'], 'added_lines': ['static bool get_desc(struct desc_struct *out, unsigned short sel)', '\t\tbool success = false;', '\t\tif (ldt && sel < ldt->nr_entries) {', '\t\t\t*out = ldt->entries[sel];', '\t\t\tsuccess = true;', '\t\t}', '\t\treturn success;', '\t\treturn false;', '\t*out = *(struct desc_struct *)(gdt_desc.address + desc_base);', '\treturn true;']}
description: In arch/x86/lib/insn-eval.c in the Linux kernel before 5.1.9, there is a use-after-free for access to an LDT entry because of a race condition between modify_ldt() and a #BR exception for an MPX bounds violation.

code_evidence: get_desc() takes context.lock, obtains ldt from current->active_mm->context.ldt, and computes desc = &ldt->entries[sel] while holding the lock. It then unlocks at line 14 and returns the raw pointer at line 15, so the caller dereferences an LDT entry after the mutex protecting the LDT has been released.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The mutex correctly protects the LDT only during lookup, but the shared resource (LDT entries) is accessed after the lock is dropped, so an interfering modify_ldt() sequence can free it concurrently. This is improper synchronization over a shared resource with a timing window, matching CWE-362; the use-after-free is the downstream consequence, not the primary weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function returns a pointer into the LDT rather than a copy of the entry, ending the critical section before the data is consumed. Trigger: a concurrent modify_ldt() frees or replaces the LDT after mutex_unlock but before the caller reads the descriptor, leaving a dangling pointer. Consequence: use-after-free read of freed LDT memory, corrupting descriptor interpretation for the #BR/MPX path.

commit_msg:
virtio-serial: fix ANY_LAYOUT

Don't assume a specific layout for control messages.
Required by virtio 1.

Signed-off-by: Michael S. Tsirkin <mst@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Amit Shah <amit.shah@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Jason Wang <jasowang@redhat.com>

description: Buffer overflow in the send_control_msg function in hw/char/virtio-serial-bus.c in QEMU before 2.4.0 allows guest users to cause a denial of service (QEMU process crash) via a crafted virtio control message.

code_evidence: virtqueue_pop fills elem with guest-controlled scatter-gather entries (in_sg, in_num); the code then copies len bytes into elem.in_sg[0].iov_base with memcpy, ignoring elem.in_sg[0].iov_len and the remaining in_sg entries.

The patch replaces the single-descriptor memcpy with iov_from_buf and notes the missing too-short-buffer detection, confirming the unchecked copy rather than an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125).
