Trigger: a guest supplies a control message and a short output descriptor chain, so len exceeds the writable iov space. Consequence: memcpy writes past the descriptor buffer, corrupting host memory and crashing the QEMU process (DoS).

commit_msg:
Set file metadata via fd-based ops for everything but symlinks

Regular file ops are fd-based already, for the rest we need to open them
manually. Files with temporary suffix must never be followed, for
directories (and pre-existing FA_TOUCHed files) use the rpm symlink
"root or target owner allowed" rule wrt following.

This mostly fixes CVE-2021-35938, but as we're not yet using dirfd-based
operatiosn for everything there are corner cases left undone. And then
there's the plugin API which needs updating for all this.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t    if (!rc && fd == -1 && !S_ISLNK(fp->sb.st_mode)) {', '\t\t/* Only follow safe symlinks, and never on temporary files */', '\t\tfd = fsmOpenat(di.dirfd, fp->fpath,', '\t\t\t\tfp->suffix ? AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW : 0);', '\t\tif (fd < 0)', '\t\t    rc = RPMERR_OPEN_FAILED;', '\t    }', '']}
description: A symbolic link issue was found in rpm. It occurs when rpm sets the desired permissions and credentials after installing a file. A local unprivileged user could use this flaw to exchange the original file with a symbolic link to a security-critical file and escalate their privileges on the system. The highest threat from this vulnerability is to data confidentiality and integrity as well as system availability.

code_evidence: fd starts at -1 and is only populated for regular files via fsmMkfile; for non-regular types fd stays -1. When fp->suffix is set, fsmVerify is skipped and rc is forced to RPMERR_ENOENT, so the temporary path is created fresh.
For symlink entries, fsmSymlink creates the link at fp->fpath; the pre-existing path is not opened with a no-follow constraint here.
setmeta calls fsmSetmeta with fd, which for non-regular files (or failed opens) is -1, so metadata is applied by path via di.dirfd and fp->fpath.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-59 fits because the function accesses a file by name (fp->fpath) and fails to prevent that name from resolving through a symlink to an unintended resource during metadata application. This is link resolution before file access, not merely a TOCTOU race.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: metadata (ownership/mode) is applied through a path-based operation because fd remains -1 for non-regular file types, without consistently resolving the path with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW. An attacker who swaps the target path for a symlink to a security-critical file between creation/verification and setmeta can cause the privileged install to chmod/chown the linked target, enabling privilege escalation.

commit_msg:
CVE-2018-10756: Fix heap-use-after-free in tr_variantWalk

In libtransmission/variant.c, function tr_variantWalk, when the variant
stack is reallocated, a pointer to the previously allocated memory
region is kept. This address is later accessed (heap use-after-free)
while walking back down the stack, causing the application to crash.
The application can be any application which uses libtransmission, such
as transmission-daemon, transmission-gtk, transmission-show, etc.

Reported-by: Tom Richards <tom@tomrichards.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if (node->v == &node->sorted)', '        tr_free(node->sorted.val.l.vals);'], 'added_lines': ['    TR_ASSERT(node != NULL);', '', '    if (node->sorted != NULL)', '        tr_free(node->sorted->val.l.vals);', '        tr_free(node->sorted);']}
description: Use-after-free in libtransmission/variant.c in Transmission before 3.00 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (crash) or possibly execute arbitrary code via a crafted torrent file.

code_evidence: nodeDestruct checks whether node->v equals &node->sorted (i.e., the sorted field is the active variant) and then frees node->sorted.val.l.vals. The destructor frees the inner vals array but leaves node->sorted.val.l.vals pointing at the released memory; no pointer is nulled or removed afterward.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the function frees memory and retains a reference to it without invalidating or clearing that reference, permitting later reuse. This is a direct dangling-pointer condition, not a double free or missing bounds check.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The freed vals array remains reachable through the still-live sorted variant pointer in the node. If nodeDestruct or later traversal/destruction logic reads or frees node->sorted.val.l.vals again, the stale pointer is dereferenced after the allocation has been released, yielding a heap use-after-free (crash or memory corruption).

commit_msg:
Fix null pointer dereference in getName/getString

Whenever getString or getName are called with an act such that act->p.String
is a NULL pointer, a NULL pointer dereference might happen
(strlen(act->p.string) is called).

In this commit we add checks at the beginning of the PUSH_STRING block so
that a warning is displayed and an empty string is returned in this case.

This patch fixes #121.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tt=malloc(strlen(act->p.String)+3); ', '\t\t/*', '\t\tstrcpy(t,"\\"");', '\t\tstrcat(t,act->p.String);', '\t\tstrcat(t,"\\"");', '\t\t*/', '\t\tstrcpy(t,act->p.String);', '\t\tif(strlen(t)) /* Not a zero length string */', '\t\telse', '\t\t\treturn "this";'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (!act->p.String) /* Not a NULL string */', '\t\t{', '\t\t        SWF_warn("WARNING: Call to getName with NULL string.\\n");', '\t\t        break;', '\t\t}', '\t\telse if (strlen(act->p.String)) /* Not a zero length string */', '\t\t{', '\t\t        t=malloc(strlen(act->p.String)+3);', '\t\t        strcpyext(t,act->p.String);', '\t\t        return t;', '\t\t}', '\t\telse', '\t\t{', '\t\t        char *return_string = "this";', '\t                t=malloc(strlen(return_string)+1); /* string length + \\0 */', '\t                strcpyext(t,return_string);', '\t\t}']}
description: The pushdup function in util/decompile.c in libming through 0.4.8 does not recognize the need for ActionPushDuplicate to perform a deep copy when a String is at the top of the stack, making the library vulnerable to a util/decompile.c getName NULL pointer dereference, which may allow attackers to cause a denial of service via a crafted SWF file.

code_evidence: In the PUSH_STRING case, act->p.String is passed to strlen at line 8 and to strcpy at line 9 without any NULL check; a NULL action string causes both calls to dereference NULL.
The function then falls through to the switch epilogue at line 13, where t = malloc(sizeof(char)) is allocated but never freed, so the early return path also leaks the string buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits because the code dereferences a pointer (act->p.String) expected to be valid but which can be NULL, yielding a crash/DoS. This is distinct from a buffer overflow (CWE-787), since the flaw is the unchecked NULL rather than a size mismatch.

evidence_lines.code: return "this";

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the PUSH_STRING branch assumes act->p.String is always non-NULL and immediately calls strlen/strcpy on it. Trigger: a crafted SWF action whose push parameter has a NULL String pointer reaches getName, causing a NULL pointer dereference and crash (DoS). The missing NULL guard is the cause; the crash is the supported consequence.

commit_msg:
northd, controller: Add CoPP for SVC monitor

The SVC monitor was exposed without any limitation.
Add CoPP for the SVC monitor flow, which adds a way
for CMSs to limit the traffic that this flow accepts.

Signed-off-by: Ales Musil <amusil@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        ovn_lflow_add(lflows, od, S_SWITCH_IN_L2_LKUP, 110,', '                      "eth.dst == $svc_monitor_mac && (tcp || icmp || icmp6)",', '                      "handle_svc_check(inport);");'], 'added_lines': ['        ovn_lflow_metered(lflows, od, S_SWITCH_IN_L2_LKUP, 110, "eth.dst == "', '                          "$svc_monitor_mac && (tcp || icmp || icmp6)",', '                          "handle_svc_check(inport);",', '                          copp_meter_get(COPP_SVC_MONITOR, od->nbs->copp,', '                                         meter_groups));']}
description: A flaw was found in Open Virtual Network where the service monitor MAC does not properly rate limit. This issue could allow an attacker to cause a denial of service, including on deployments with CoPP enabled and properly configured.

code_evidence: Inside the od->nbs branch, the function installs the SVC monitor L2 lookup flow at priority 110 using ovn_lflow_add, matching eth.dst == $svc_monitor_mac with tcp/icmp/icmp6 and invoking handle_svc_check(inport). No meter or CoPP argument is supplied; unlike the later IGMP/MLD flows (lines 15-22) which use ovn_lflow_metered with copp_meter_get, this flow is added unmetered.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-770 covers allocating a reusable resource without intended limits on size or number. Here the switch pipeline accepts unlimited service-monitor packets because the flow lacks a meter, directly matching the missing-throttling omission; the contrast with the metered IGMP flows on lines 15-22 confirms the intended control was simply not applied.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the service-monitor flow is installed without any rate-limiting meter, so every packet matching the service monitor MAC is forwarded to handle_svc_check without a throttle. Trigger: a remote sender floods traffic to the service monitor MAC; the missing CoPP binding means the configured meter is never applied. Supported consequence: unbounded packet processing consumes CPU/other resources, enabling denial of service even when CoPP is configured.

commit_msg: Fixed bug #71323 - Output of stream_get_meta_data can be falsified by its input
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t'], 'added_lines': ['']}
description: In PHP before 5.5.32, 5.6.x before 5.6.18, and 7.x before 7.0.3, all of the return values of stream_get_meta_data can be controlled if the input can be controlled (e.g., during file uploads). For example, a "$uri = stream_get_meta_data(fopen($file, "r"))['uri']" call mishandles the case where $file is data:text/plain;uri=eviluri, -- in other words, metadata can be set by an attacker.

code_evidence: In the PHP_STREAM_OPTION_META_DATA_API case, the function checks only that ts->meta is non-null, then copies the entire metadata hash into the caller-supplied zval array with zend_hash_copy; no key or value is inspected or constrained before being returned as stream metadata.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is missing validation of incoming input-derived metadata before it is accepted and returned, matching CWE-20's improper input validation of metadata properties. It is not a transformation/filtering flaw; the code simply fails to check the data's required properties.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: metadata accumulated in ts->meta is exposed wholesale without validating which keys (e.g. uri) or values are legitimate. Trigger: attacker-controlled input such as a data:text/plain;uri=eviluri stream populates ts->meta, and a later stream_get_meta_data call reaches this case. Consequence: attacker-chosen metadata is returned to the application, enabling falsification of trusted stream properties.

Fixes #52

commit_msg:
kvm: fix excessive pages un-pinning in kvm_iommu_map error path.

The third parameter of kvm_unpin_pages() when called from
kvm_iommu_map_pages() is wrong, it should be the number of pages to un-pin
and not the page size.

This error was facilitated with an inconsistent API: kvm_pin_pages() takes
a size, but kvn_unpin_pages() takes a number of pages, so fix the problem
by matching the two.

This was introduced by commit 350b8bd ("kvm: iommu: fix the third parameter
of kvm_iommu_put_pages (CVE-2014-3601)"), which fixes the lack of
un-pinning for pages intended to be un-pinned (i.e. memory leak) but
unfortunately potentially aggravated the number of pages we un-pin that
should have stayed pinned. As far as I understand though, the same
practical mitigations apply.

This issue was found during review of Red Hat 6.6 patches to prepare
Ksplice rebootless updates.

Thanks to Vegard for his time on a late Friday evening to help me in
understanding this code.

Fixes: 350b8bd ("kvm: iommu: fix the third parameter of... (CVE-2014-3601)")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Quentin Casasnovas <quentin.casasnovas@oracle.com>
Signed-off-by: Vegard Nossum <vegard.nossum@oracle.com>
Signed-off-by: Jamie Iles <jamie.iles@oracle.com>
Reviewed-by: Sasha Levin <sasha.levin@oracle.com>
Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t   unsigned long size)', '\tend_gfn = gfn + (size >> PAGE_SHIFT);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t   unsigned long npages)', '\tend_gfn = gfn + npages;']}
description: The kvm_iommu_map_pages function in virt/kvm/iommu.c in the Linux kernel through 3.17.2 miscalculates the number of pages during the handling of a mapping failure, which allows guest OS users to cause a denial of service (host OS page unpinning) or possibly have unspecified other impact by leveraging guest OS privileges.  NOTE: this vulnerability exists because of an incorrect fix for CVE-2014-3601.

code_evidence: Line 7 computes end_gfn by shifting the size argument right by PAGE_SHIFT, treating the parameter as a byte size. The loop at lines 11-12 pins pages from gfn+1 up to end_gfn. Because the caller passes a page count, this shift under-scales the iteration bound and causes the wrong number of pages to be pinned/unpinned relative to the requested range.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-119 fits because the flawed bound computation causes operations over an unintended range of memory pages, i.e., outside the intended buffer boundary. The unit-confusion arithmetic is the cause; the out-of-intended-range page operation is the supported weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: a unit mismatch between the function's size-based computation and the caller's page-count argument, so the loop bound is calculated from a misinterpreted value. Trigger: a mapping failure path invoking this pinning helper with a page count. Consequence: page pinning/unpinning operates on a range inconsistent with the intended buffer, leading to host page unpinning and resource/availability impact.

commit_msg:
crypto: user - fix leaking uninitialized memory to userspace

All bytes of the NETLINK_CRYPTO report structures must be initialized,
since they are copied to userspace.  The change from strncpy() to
strlcpy() broke this.  As a minimal fix, change it back.

Fixes: 4473710df1f8 ("crypto: user - Prepare for CRYPTO_MAX_ALG_NAME expansion")
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org> # v4.12+
Signed-off-by: Eric Biggers <ebiggers@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Herbert Xu <herbert@gondor.apana.org.au>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tstrlcpy(rcipher.type, "cipher", sizeof(rcipher.type));'], 'added_lines': ['\tstrncpy(rcipher.type, "cipher", sizeof(rcipher.type));']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel before 4.19.3. crypto_report_one() and related functions in crypto/crypto_user.c (the crypto user configuration API) do not fully initialize structures that are copied to userspace, potentially leaking sensitive memory to user programs. NOTE: this is a CVE-2013-2547 regression but with easier exploitability because the attacker does not need a capability (however, the system must have the CONFIG_CRYPTO_USER kconfig option).

code_evidence: strlcpy copies the literal "cipher" into rcipher.type and zero-pads the rest of the fixed-size field, so the entire type array is initialized.
The whole rcipher structure, including all of its bytes, is passed to nla_put with sizeof(struct crypto_report_cipher) and then delivered to userspace via the netlink skb.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-200 fits only if the copied structure can expose uninitialized kernel memory to an unprivileged userspace reader. Here strlcpy initializes the entire type buffer before the full-structure copy, so this function does not itself support the exposure; the leak came from the strncpy variant that the patch restores in the before-state, not this after-state code.

evidence_lines.code: strlcpy(rcipher.type, "cipher", sizeof(rcipher.type));

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function builds a stack structure and copies it in full to a netlink message for userspace. With strlcpy, the type array is fully zero-filled, so no uninitialized stack bytes are included; the padding and remaining fields are set or covered. The prior strncpy version left the tail of type uninitialized, causing a kernel stack memory leak, but that unsafe variant is not present in this function.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tsprintf (buf, "\\\\%03o", (unsigned int) c);'], 'added_lines': ['\tsprintf (buf, "\\\\%03o", (unsigned int) c & 0xff);']}
description: ihex.c in GNU Binutils before 2.26 contains a stack buffer overflow when printing bad bytes in Intel Hex objects.

code_evidence: A fixed 40-byte stack buffer buf is declared, then sprintf writes an octal escape for any non-printable c.
The format "\\%03o" with (unsigned int) c allows values above 0xff when c is a signed char widened to a negative int, producing more digits than the 3-digit field and overflowing buf.
The printable branch is bounded, but the non-printable branch has no width cap; the resulting buf is then passed to the error handler.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The sprintf writes beyond buf's intended boundary, directly matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds write. CWE-120 (unbounded sprintf) is a more specific child, but the supplied target is the buffer-bounds class CWE-119.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: sprintf into a 40-byte stack buffer with a value not masked to 8 bits, so sign-extended negative c yields long octal output. Trigger: a corrupt S-record containing a non-printable byte (e.g., \200-\376) reaches srec_bad_byte. Consequence: stack buffer overflow and memory corruption when reporting the bad byte.

commit_msg:
avformat/vividas: improve extradata packing checks in track_header()

Fixes: out of array accesses
Fixes: 26622/clusterfuzz-testcase-minimized-ffmpeg_dem_VIVIDAS_fuzzer-6581200338288640

Found-by: continuous fuzzing process https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz/tree/master/projects/ffmpeg
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            int xd_size = 0;', '                xd_size += len;', '            ret = ff_alloc_extradata(st->codecpar, 64 + xd_size + xd_size / 255);', '                if (delta > data_len[j]) {', '                    return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;', '                }'], 'added_lines': ['            int xd_size = 1;', '                xd_size += len + 1 + len/255;', '            ret = ff_alloc_extradata(st->codecpar, xd_size);', '                av_assert0(delta <= xd_size - offset);', '                av_assert0(data_len[j] <= xd_size - offset);']}
description: track_header in libavformat/vividas.c in FFmpeg 4.3.1 has an out-of-bounds write because of incorrect extradata packing.

code_evidence: xd_size starts at 0 and offset starts at 1; data_len[256] holds per-entry lengths read from the input.
Each len from ffio_read_varlen is bounds-checked only against INT_MAX/2 - xd_size, then accumulated as xd_size += len without accounting for the xiph lacing bytes.
ff_alloc_extradata allocates 64 + xd_size + xd_size/255, but the lacing expansion can exceed xd_size/255, so the buffer is undersized for the packed layout.
av_xiphlacing writes lacing bytes at p[offset]; delta is checked only against data_len[j], not against remaining allocation, and offset advances by delta.
The copy loop writes data_len[j] bytes at p[offset] and advances offset, with no check that offset + data_len[j] stays within extradata_size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function computes an allocation smaller than the data it later writes and lacks a remaining-space check before writing at p[offset], so writes can exceed the intended buffer. This is a direct out-of-bounds write (CWE-787); an integer-overflow label would not fit because the defect is a size-computation mismatch rather than wraparound.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The allocation size is computed from raw data lengths plus a heuristic xd_size/255 allowance, but the actual packed size includes one lacing byte per entry plus len/255 expansion bytes, which can exceed that allowance. When crafted track data makes the accumulated offset pass the allocated extradata buffer, av_xiphlacing and avio_read write past the heap buffer, causing an out-of-bounds write and heap corruption/crash.

commit_msg: fixed #1774 (fuzz)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (!nb_pack) nb_pack = 1;', '\t\tif (stbl->SampleSize->sampleCount+nb_pack > stbl->SampleSize->alloc_size)'], 'added_lines': ['\tCHECK_PACK(GF_ISOM_INVALID_FILE)', '', '\t\tif (stbl->SampleSize->sampleCount+nb_pack > stbl->SampleSize->alloc_size) {', '\t\t}']}
description: Buffer overflow in the stbl_AppendSize function in MP4Box in GPAC 1.0.1 allows attackers to cause a denial of service or execute arbitrary code via a crafted file.

code_evidence: On lines 14-19 the table is grown to alloc_size using sampleCount+nb_pack, but the write loop at line 28-31 writes nb_pack entries starting at sizes[sampleCount+i] without re-checking that sampleCount+nb_pack stays within alloc_size after the equality fast path.
nb_pack is attacker-controlled from the crafted file; the guard only covers the reallocation branch, so the subsequent copy of size values can index past the allocated sizes array.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function copies nb_pack u32 size values into the sizes buffer without verifying that the destination holds them, i.e., a buffer copy without checking input size, matching CWE-120. It is not merely an integer overflow (CWE-190) because the supported consequence is an out-of-bounds write during the copy loop.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: nb_pack is trusted without an upper-bound constraint, and the growth check on line 14/17 is bypassed when the equality path at lines 10-13 or a stale alloc_size is used. Trigger: a crafted file supplies a large nb_pack, causing the loop on lines 28-30 to write past the sizes buffer. Consequence: heap memory corruption, leading to crash (DoS) or potential arbitrary code execution.

commit_msg:
avcodec/mpeg4videodec: Check for bitstream end in read_quant_matrix_ext()

Fixes: out of array read
Fixes: asff-crash-0e53d0dc491dfdd507530b66562812fbd4c36678

Found-by: Paul Ch <paulcher@icloud.com>
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['static void read_quant_matrix_ext(MpegEncContext *s, GetBitContext *gb)'], 'added_lines': ['static int read_quant_matrix_ext(MpegEncContext *s, GetBitContext *gb)', '        if (get_bits_left(gb) < 64*8)', '            return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;', '        if (get_bits_left(gb) < 64*8)', '            return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;', '        if (get_bits_left(gb) < 64*8)', '            return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;', '        if (get_bits_left(gb) < 64*8)', '            return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;', '    return 0;']}
description: FFmpeg before commit 5aba5b89d0b1d73164d3b81764828bb8b20ff32a contains an out of array read vulnerability in ASF_F format demuxer that can result in heap memory reading. This attack appear to be exploitable via specially crafted ASF file that has to provided as input. This vulnerability appears to have been fixed in 5aba5b89d0b1d73164d3b81764828bb8b20ff32a and later.

code_evidence: When the intra_quantiser_matrix flag bit is set, the loop unconditionally calls get_bits(gb, 8) 64 times without checking get_bits_left(gb), then indexes idct_permutation/ff_zigzag_direct and writes s->intra_matrix[j] and s->chroma_intra_matrix[j].
The chroma_intra_quantiser_matrix branch likewise reads 64 bytes via get_bits without any remaining-bit count check before indexing and writing the matrix.
The chroma_non_intra_quantiser_matrix branch reads 64 bytes via get_bits(gb, 8) with no bounds check on the bitstream.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the missing length check lets get_bits read beyond the end of the input buffer, matching the commit's 'out of array read' fix. It is a read overrun, not a write, so CWE-787 would not apply.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function consumes 64*8 bits per enabled matrix without verifying get_bits_left(gb). Trigger: a crafted bitstream sets these flag bits near the end of the buffer. The bit reader then advances past the available data, causing an out-of-bounds read of the bitstream buffer (the fixed version adds get_bits_left checks and returns AVERROR_INVALIDDATA).

commit_msg: MC: check that image bit-depth matches SPS bit depth (#343)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '  if (sps->BitDepth_Y != img->get_bit_depth(0) ||', '      sps->BitDepth_C != img->get_bit_depth(1)) {', '    img->integrity = INTEGRITY_DECODING_ERRORS;', '    ctx->add_warning(DE265_WARNING_BIT_DEPTH_OF_CURRENT_IMAGE_DOES_NOT_MATCH_SPS, false);', '    return;', '  }']}
description: Libde265 v1.0.8 was discovered to contain a stack-buffer-overflow vulnerability via put_qpel_fallback<unsigned short> in fallback-motion.cc. This vulnerability allows attackers to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) via a crafted video file.

code_evidence: Fixed-size stack buffers predSamplesL[2][MAX_CU_SIZE*MAX_CU_SIZE] and predSamplesC[2][2][...] are sized for a bounded range of samples; bit_depth_L/bit_depth_C come from sps and drive the motion-compensation and prediction-write routines.
mc_luma/mc_chroma write into these fixed stack arrays using nCS/nPbW/nPbH and the sps bit depth; the buffer dimensions are not validated against the actual image bit depth here.

put_unweighted_pred/put_weighted_pred copy predSamples into pixels[0..2] using stride and bit_depth_L/bit_depth_C, so a bit-depth mismatch between SPS and image plane changes element size and write extent.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe operation is a write past the end of a fixed stack buffer in the prediction paths, matching CWE-787 (out-of-bounds Write). The missing bit-depth consistency check is the enabling condition, not a separate weakness; the supported consequence is memory corruption/DoS rather than merely an incorrect value.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function trusts sps->BitDepth_Y/C to select 8- vs 16-bit processing and buffer sizing, without checking that the decoded image plane's actual bit depth matches. A crafted stream whose SPS bit depth disagrees with the image causes mc/put routines to write 16-bit samples into an 8-bit-sized buffer (or vice versa), overflowing the fixed stack arrays; consequence is stack-buffer-overflow leading to DoS/crash.

commit_msg:
Fix for bug #76582

The brigade seems to end up in a messed up state if something fails
in shutdown, so we clean it up.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\tapr_brigade_cleanup(brigade);']}
description: The Apache2 component in PHP before 5.6.38, 7.0.x before 7.0.32, 7.1.x before 7.1.22, and 7.2.x before 7.2.10 allows XSS via the body of a "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" request, because the bucket brigade is mishandled in the php_handler function in sapi/apache2handler/sapi_apache2.c.

code_evidence: After script execution, when there is no parent request, the handler builds an EOS bucket and passes the brigade to ap_pass_brigade without first clearing any buckets already present in the shared brigade (ctx->brigade, reused at line 80).

The patch inserts apr_brigade_cleanup(brigade) before creating the EOS bucket; the original code only cleans up after passing, so stale/unprocessed request body buckets (e.g. chunked Transfer-Encoding data) can be flushed into the response.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect causes user-controllable request content to be placed into served output without neutralization, matching CWE-79's improper neutralization between attacker input and victim. It is not merely an information-disclosure bug because the injected body executes as page markup.

evidence_lines.code: apr_brigade_cleanup(brigade);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the request bucket brigade is reused across the handler path and is not purged before the response EOS bucket is appended and passed to the output filters. Trigger: a request whose body buckets remain in the brigade (chunked body) reaches this flush path. Consequence: attacker-controlled request body data is emitted in the served response, enabling script injection in a victim's browser context.

Sonivox: add SafetyNet log.

Bug: 26366256
Change-Id: Ief72e01b7cc6d87a015105af847a99d3d9b03cb0

description: Sonivox in mediaserver in Android 4.x before 4.4.4, 5.0.x before 5.0.2, 5.1.x before 5.1.1, and 6.x before 2016-04-01 does not check for a negative number of samples, which allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code or cause a denial of service (memory corruption) via a crafted media file, related to arm-wt-22k/lib_src/eas_wtengine.c and arm-wt-22k/lib_src/eas_wtsynth.c, aka internal bug 26366256.

code_evidence: Lines 11-12 compute numSamples from loopEnd, phaseAccum and phaseFrac as a signed EAS_I32; line 14 divides it by phaseIncrement and stores the result in pWTIntFrame->numSamples. Lines 18-21 detect a negative numSamples and clamp it to 0, but only after the value has already been assigned to the frame.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function's arithmetic produces a negative sample count that is propagated into frame processing, supporting out-of-bounds memory operations (CWE-119). A signedness/integer-conversion issue (CWE-190/195) is the arithmetic origin, but the supported weakness in this function is the resulting improper bounds restriction on the buffer operation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The sample count derived from phase arithmetic can become negative because the unsigned phase values are cast to signed EAS_I32; the function stores this value in pWTIntFrame->numSamples before validating it. The clamp at lines 18-21 runs only after assignment, so a negative count can still reach downstream frame processing, where it is used to drive buffer indexing and leads to out-of-bounds memory access.

Fix #196 and #199: Out of bound reads security issues

Check args before calling memmove() and memset() in remap_struct()
function to avoid out of bound reads which would possibly lead to
unknown code execution and/or sadf command crash.

Signed-off-by: Sebastien GODARD <sysstat@users.noreply.github.com>

description: An issue was discovered in sysstat 12.1.1. The remap_struct function in sa_common.c has an out-of-bounds read during a memmove call, as demonstrated by sadf.

code_evidence: rec_hdr_tmp is a fixed-size stack buffer (MAX_RECORD_HEADER_SIZE) passed to read_record_hdr; before the fix no size argument constrained how many bytes the callee could copy into it.
handle_curr_act_stats receives rec_hdr_tmp with only endian/arch flags; the callee was not told the buffer size, so it could read/copy beyond the buffer.
The second handle_curr_act_stats call in the multi-output branch likewise passes rec_hdr_tmp without a length, repeating the unconstrained access.
read_record_hdr is again invoked on rec_hdr_tmp with no size limit, so a malformed record header can drive reads past the buffer end.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The patch adds sizeof(rec_hdr_tmp) to these calls precisely to prevent reads beyond the intended rec_hdr_tmp buffer during memmove/memset, which is the defining behavior of CWE-125. It is not CWE-787 because the observed/patched flaw is reading past the buffer rather than writing past it.

evidence_lines.code:
handle_curr_act_stats(ifd, fpos, &curr, &cnt, &eosaf, rows,
act[p]->id, &reset, file_actlst,
from_file, &file_magic, rec_hdr_tmp,
endian_mismatch, arch_64);

handle_curr_act_stats(ifd, fpos, &curr, &cnt, &eosaf,
rows, act[p]->id, &reset, file_actlst,
from_file, &file_magic, rec_hdr_tmp,
endian_mismatch, arch_64);

eosaf = read_record_hdr(ifd, rec_hdr_tmp, &record_hdr[curr],
&file_hdr, arch_64, endian_mismatch, UEOF_STOP);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the fixed-size rec_hdr_tmp buffer is handed to read_record_hdr and handle_curr_act_stats without conveying its size, so those callees' memmove/memset operations can use an attacker-influenced length. Trigger: a crafted sa file with an oversized record header. Consequence: out-of-bounds read of stack memory, potentially leaking data or crashing sadf.

commit_msg: Use the correct rights.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        if (IsRightsAuthorized(ModulePolicyDomain,AllPolicyRights,'], 'added_lines': ['  PolicyRights', '    rights;', '', '  rights=ReadPolicyRights|WritePolicyRights;', '        if (IsRightsAuthorized(ModulePolicyDomain,rights,']}
description: ImageMagick is free software delivered as a ready-to-run binary distribution or as source code that you may use, copy, modify, and distribute in both open and proprietary applications. In affected versions and in certain cases, Postscript files could be read and written when specifically excluded by a `module` policy in `policy.xml`. ex. <policy domain="module" rights="none" pattern="PS" />. The issue has been resolved in ImageMagick 7.1.0-7 and in 6.9.12-22. Fortunately, in the wild, few users utilize the `module` policy and instead use the `coder` policy that is also our workaround recommendation: <policy domain="coder" rights="none" pattern="{PS,EPI,EPS,EPSF,EPSI}" />.

code_evidence: The authorization check calls IsRightsAuthorized with AllPolicyRights, which covers every policy right rather than the specific read/write operation being performed.
A module whose policy grants only a subset of rights still passes the check because AllPolicyRights is supplied, so its register_module is invoked and the module is marked registered.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The module resource is exposed to actors outside the policy-defined control sphere because the rights check uses an over-broad rights mask. This is the access-control mistake enabling unintended access, matching CWE-668's exposure of a resource to the wrong sphere.

evidence_lines.code:
(void) (MagickModules[i].register_module)();
MagickModules[i].registered=MagickTrue;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the module gate requests AllPolicyRights instead of the rights the registration actually needs, so a module policy restricting rights (e.g. rights="none" for PS) is not enforced. Trigger: a policy.xml module entry denying read/write rights for a module. Consequence: the excluded module is registered and its coder remains usable, exposing Postscript read/write capability outside the intended control sphere.

commit_msg:
mwifiex: Fix three heap overflow at parsing element in cfg80211_ap_settings

mwifiex_update_vs_ie(),mwifiex_set_uap_rates() and
mwifiex_set_wmm_params() call memcpy() without checking
the destination size.Since the source is given from
user-space, this may trigger a heap buffer overflow.

Fix them by putting the length check before performing memcpy().

This fix addresses CVE-2019-14814,CVE-2019-14815,CVE-2019-14816.

Signed-off-by: Wen Huang <huangwenabc@gmail.com>
Acked-by: Ganapathi Bhat <gbhat@marvell.comg>
Signed-off-by: Kalle Valo <kvalo@codeaurora.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (rate_ie)'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (rate_ie->len > MWIFIEX_SUPPORTED_RATES)', '\t\t\treturn;', '\tif (rate_ie) {', '\t\tif (rate_ie->len > MWIFIEX_SUPPORTED_RATES - rate_len)', '\t\t\treturn;', '\t}']}
description: A vulnerability was found in Linux Kernel, where a Heap Overflow was found in mwifiex_set_wmm_params() function of Marvell Wifi Driver.

code_evidence: cfg80211_find_ie locates the supported-rates IE in the beacon head; its length field rate_ie->len is copied into bss_cfg->rates with no bound check against the destination array size.

The extended supported-rates IE from beacon.tail is copied to bss_cfg->rates + rate_len using its own attacker-influenced length, with no check that rate_len + rate_ie->len stays within bss_cfg->rates.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This is a heap-based buffer overflow (CWE-122): an unbounded copy into a heap-allocated destination. It is not merely an out-of-bounds read, since the overflow writes past the heap buffer; the missing length check is the root cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The element lengths parsed from user-supplied cfg80211_ap_settings are used directly as memcpy sizes into the fixed bss_cfg->rates buffer (a heap-allocated structure), without validating them against the buffer capacity. An oversized or repeated rates IE therefore overflows the heap allocation, allowing adjacent heap memory to be overwritten (potential code execution or crash).

commit_msg:
Merge pull request from GHSA-cv8x-p47p-99wr

* - Avoid SSL socket parent/listener getting destroyed during handshake by increasing parent's reference count.
- Add missing SSL socket close when the newly accepted SSL socket is discarded in SIP TLS transport.

* - Fix silly mistake: accepted active socket created without group lock in SSL socket.
- Replace assertion with normal validation check of SSL socket instance in OpenSSL verification callback (verify_cb()) to avoid crash, e.g: if somehow race condition with SSL socket destroy happens or OpenSSL application data index somehow gets corrupted.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    pj_ssl_sock_t *ssock;', '    SSL *ossl_ssl;', '    pj_assert(ossl_ssl);', '    pj_assert(ssock);'], 'added_lines': ['    pj_ssl_sock_t *ssock = NULL;', '    SSL *ossl_ssl = NULL;', '    if (!ossl_ssl) {', '\tPJ_LOG(1,(THIS_FILE,', '\t\t  "SSL verification callback failed to get SSL instance"));', '\tgoto on_return;', '    }', '    if (!ssock) {', '\t/* SSL socket may have been destroyed */', '\tPJ_LOG(1,(THIS_FILE,', '\t\t  "SSL verification callback failed to get SSL socket "', '\t\t  "instance (sslsock_idx=%d).", sslsock_idx));', '\tgoto on_return;', '    }', 'on_return:']}
description: PJSIP is a free and open source multimedia communication library written in C language implementing standard based protocols such as SIP, SDP, RTP, STUN, TURN, and ICE. In PJSIP before version 2.11.1, there are a couple of issues found in the SSL socket. First, a race condition between callback and destroy, due to the accepted socket having no group lock. Second, the SSL socket parent/listener may get destroyed during handshake. Both issues were reported to happen intermittently in heavy load TLS connections. They cause a crash, resulting in a denial of service. These are fixed in version 2.11.1.

code_evidence: verify_cb retrieves the SSL instance from the X509_STORE_CTX and then the pj_ssl_sock_t via SSL_get_ex_data, relying only on pj_assert to validate both pointers before use.

The retrieved ssock is dereferenced to update verify_status and read param.verify_peer without any lock or lifetime guarantee; the commit context states the accepted SSL socket had no group lock, so a concurrent destroy can invalidate ssock between retrieval and dereference.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This is CWE-362: verify_cb accesses the shared ssock resource concurrently with socket destruction without exclusive access or synchronization, and the race is the root cause of the crash. A use-after-free is the consequence, not the primary weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The callback assumes the SSL socket remains alive after SSL_get_ex_data returns it, but another thread can destroy the socket concurrently because no group lock protects the accepted socket. The assertion does not prevent the race; the use-after-free causes a crash, a denial of service.

description: In radare2 2.0.1, libr/bin/dwarf.c allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (invalid read and application crash) via a crafted ELF file, related to r_bin_dwarf_parse_comp_unit in dwarf.c and sdb_set_internal in shlr/sdb/src/sdb.c.

code_evidence: Entry guard only checks obuf_len < 0, which is never true for a signed int, so obuf_len == 0 passes and buf == buf_end is accepted; reads then occur with no remaining bytes.
DW_FORM_string dereferences *buf and calls strlen on the NUL-terminated pointer without verifying a terminator lies before buf_end.
DW_FORM_block reads a ULEB128 length via r_uleb128 bounded by buf_end - buf, but then loops block.length times using READ(buf, ut8) with no check that length bytes remain.
DW_FORM_block1 reads a ut8 length and then reads that many bytes into the allocated buffer without confirming the length fits within the remaining input.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe operations are reads of memory beyond the intended input buffer, matching CWE-125. It is not a write overflow: the loops write into calloc'd blocks; the defect is unbounded source reads.

description: An incomplete string comparison in the numpy.core component in NumPy before 1.22.0 allows attackers to trigger slightly incorrect copying by constructing specific string objects. NOTE: the vendor states that this reported code behavior is "completely harmless."

code_evidence: The deprecated-type check iterates dep_tps and calls strncmp(type, dep_tp, strlen(dep_tp)) == 0, comparing only the leading strlen(dep_tp) bytes of type against each entry. type is the user-supplied typestr pointer (possibly advanced past an endian prefix), and only a prefix match is required, so longer strings beginning with 'Bytes','Str','Uint', or 'Datetime64' also match. The comparison does not verify that the full type string length equals the deprecated token length.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-697 fits because the security-relevant determination of whether a typestr is a deprecated Numeric-style code uses an incorrect comparison: it checks only a prefix rather than requiring full-length equality. A related CWE-1023-style partial-string comparison is the concrete form, but the target CWE-697 correctly captures the incorrect comparison.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: prefix-only strncmp with strlen(dep_tp) never checks that the matched token spans the entire type string. Trigger: a user-supplied typestr such as 'BytesX' or 'Strfoo' that shares the deprecated prefix. Consequence: the deprecation branch fires for non-deprecated strings, and the code then falls through to _convert_from_any using the dict item, enabling the described slightly incorrect copying behavior.

commit_msg: Fixed a unicode properrty matching issue in JIT
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if (*cc == PT_CLIST)'], 'added_lines': ['    if (*cc == PT_CLIST && *cc == XCL_PROP)']}
description: An out-of-bounds read vulnerability was discovered in the PCRE2 library in the compile_xclass_matchingpath() function of the pcre2_jit_compile.c file. This involves a unicode property matching issue in JIT-compiled regular expressions. The issue occurs because the character was not fully read in case-less matching within JIT.

code_evidence: After asserting *cc is XCL_PROP/XCL_NOTPROP, cc++ moves past the property marker, so *cc is the property type; when *cc==PT_CLIST the code computes other_cases = PRIV(ucd_caseless_sets) + cc[1] and walks it until NOTACHAR. The guard at line 56 only checks PT_CLIST and does not verify the preceding marker is XCL_PROP, so an XCL_NOTPROP entry also enters this branch.
Later, the same PT_CLIST handling dereferences other_cases[0..2] and iterates while *other_cases != NOTACHAR, relying on the caseless-set table layout.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the flaw is a missing validity constraint on the property kind that lets code index and read past the intended ucd_caseless_sets buffer. This is an out-of-bounds read, not a write or an injection issue; the incorrect condition permits reads beyond the buffer.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the branch that treats cc[1] as an index into ucd_caseless_sets is entered for both XCL_PROP and XCL_NOTPROP because the check tests only PT_CLIST. When a negated property (XCL_NOTPROP) with PT_CLIST is compiled, cc[1] is not a valid caseless-set offset, so the subsequent walk/dereferences read outside the intended table bounds. The trigger is a JIT-compiled character class containing a negated PT_CLIST property; the supported consequence is an out-of-bounds read of the caseless-set table.

description: Akashi is an open source server implementation of the Attorney Online video game based on the Ace Attorney universe. Affected versions of Akashi are subject to a denial of service attack. An attacker can use a specially crafted evidence packet to make an illegal modification, causing a server crash. This can be used to mount a denial-of-service exploit. Users are advised to upgrade. There is no known workaround for this issue.

commit_msg:
scsi: target: Fix XCOPY NAA identifier lookup

When attempting to match EXTENDED COPY CSCD descriptors with corresponding
se_devices, target_xcopy_locate_se_dev_e4() currently iterates over LIO's
global devices list which includes all configured backstores.

This change ensures that only initiator-accessible backstores are
considered during CSCD descriptor lookup, according to the session's
se_node_acl LUN list.

To avoid LUN removal race conditions, device pinning is changed from being
configfs based to instead using the se_node_acl lun_ref.

Reference: CVE-2020-28374
Fixes: cbf031f425fd ("target: Add support for EXTENDED_COPY copy offload emulation")
Reviewed-by: Lee Duncan <lduncan@suse.com>
Signed-off-by: David Disseldorp <ddiss@suse.de>

commit_msg:
mnt: Add a per mount namespace limit on the number of mounts

CAI Qian <caiqian@redhat.com> pointed out that the semantics
of shared subtrees make it possible to create an exponentially
increasing number of mounts in a mount namespace.

    mkdir /tmp/1 /tmp/2
    mount --make-rshared /
    for i in $(seq 1 20) ; do mount --bind /tmp/1 /tmp/2 ; done

Will create create 2^20 or 1048576 mounts, which is a practical problem
as some people have managed to hit this by accident.

As such CVE-2016-6213 was assigned.

Ian Kent <raven@themaw.net> described the situation for autofs users
as follows:

> The number of mounts for direct mount maps is usually not very large because of
> the way they are implemented, large direct mount maps can have performance
> problems. There can be anywhere from a few (likely case a few hundred) to less
> than 10000, plus mounts that have been triggered and not yet expired.
>
> Indirect mounts have one autofs mount at the root plus the number of mounts that
> have been triggered and not yet expired.
>
> The number of autofs indirect map entries can range from a few to the common
> case of several thousand and in rare cases up to between 30000 and 50000. I've
> not heard of people with maps larger than 50000 entries.
>
> The larger the number of map entries the greater the possibility for a large
> number of active mounts so it's not hard to expect cases of a 1000 or somewhat
> more active mounts.

So I am setting the default number of mounts allowed per mount
namespace at 100,000.  This is more than enough for any use case I
know of, but small enough to quickly stop an exponential increase
in mounts.  Which should be perfect to catch misconfigurations and
malfunctioning programs.

For anyone who needs a higher limit this can be changed by writing
to the new /proc/sys/fs/mount-max sysctl.

Tested-by: CAI Qian <caiqian@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: "Eric W. Biederman" <ebiederm@xmission.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tnew_ns->mounts = 0;', '\tnew_ns->pending_mounts = 0;']}
description: fs/namespace.c in the Linux kernel before 4.9 does not restrict how many mounts may exist in a mount namespace, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (memory consumption and deadlock) via MS_BIND mount system calls, as demonstrated by a loop that triggers exponential growth in the number of mounts.

code_evidence: inc_mnt_namespaces(user_ns) enforces a namespace-count limit and returns NULL on failure, so the function already checks one resource before allocating.

kmalloc(sizeof(struct mnt_namespace), GFP_KERNEL) allocates the namespace; on failure it frees the ucount reference and returns -ENOMEM, but no per-namespace bound on the number of mounts is established here.
The added initialization sets new_ns->mounts = 0, introducing the per-namespace mount counter whose limit is enforced elsewhere; this allocator does not itself throttle mount growth.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-400 fits because the weakness is failure to properly control allocation of a limited resource (mounts per namespace), enabling resource-consumption DoS. It is not CWE-401, since no reference is lost; the issue is lack of throttling of resource quantity.

evidence_lines.code: new_ns->ucounts = ucounts;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the mount namespace tracks a count of mounts but this allocation path only bounds the number of namespaces, not the mounts within one namespace. A local user can repeatedly issue MS_BIND mounts (e.g., under shared subtrees) so the count grows without an effective ceiling, exhausting memory and causing denial of service. The counter initialization here supports the limit mechanism but is not itself the unsafe operation.

commit_msg:
xen: Make coherent PV IOMMU discipline

In order for a PV domain to set up DMA from a passed-through device to
one of its pages, the page must be mapped in the IOMMU.  On the other
hand, before a PV page may be used as a "special" page type (such as a
pagetable or descriptor table), it _must not_ be writable in the IOMMU
(otherwise a malicious guest could DMA arbitrary page tables into the
memory, bypassing Xen's safety checks); and Xen's current rule is to
have such pages not in the IOMMU at all.

At the moment, in order to accomplish this, the code borrows HVM
domain's "physmap" concept: When a page is assigned to a guest,
guess_physmap_add_entry() is called, which for PV guests, will create
a writable IOMMU mapping; and when a page is removed,
guest_physmap_remove_entry() is called, which will remove the mapping.

Additionally, when a page gains the PGT_writable page type, the page
will be added into the IOMMU; and when the page changes away from a
PGT_writable type, the page will be removed from the IOMMU.

Unfortunately, borrowing the "physmap" concept from HVM domains is
problematic.  HVM domains have a lock on their p2m tables, ensuring
synchronization between modifications to the p2m; and all hypercall
parameters must first be translated through the p2m before being used.

Trying to mix this locked-and-gated approach with PV's lock-free
approach leads to several races and inconsistencies:

* A race between a page being assigned and it being put into the
  physmap; for example:
  - P1: call populate_physmap() { A = allocate_domheap_pages() }
  - P2: Guess page A's mfn, and call decrease_reservation(A).  A is owned by the domain,
        and so Xen will clear the PGC_allocated bit and free the page
  - P1: finishes populate_physmap() { guest_physmap_add_entry() }

  Now the domain has a writable IOMMU mapping to a page it no longer owns.

* Pages start out as type PGT_none, but with a writable IOMMU mapping.
  If a guest uses a page as a page table without ever having created a
  writable mapping, the IOMMU mapping will not be removed; the guest
  will have a writable IOMMU mapping to a page it is currently using
  as a page table.

* A newly-allocated page can be DMA'd into with no special actions on
  the part of the guest; However, if a page is promoted to a
  non-writable type, the page must be mapped with a writable type before
  DMA'ing to it again, or the transaction will fail.

To fix this, do away with the "PV physmap" concept entirely, and
replace it with the following IOMMU discipline for PV guests:
 - (type == PGT_writable) <=> in iommu (even if type_count == 0)
 - Upon a final put_page(), check to see if type is PGT_writable; if so,
   iommu_unmap.

In order to achieve that:

- Remove PV IOMMU related code from guest_physmap_*

- Repurpose cleanup_page_cacheattr() into a general
  cleanup_page_mappings() function, which will both fix up Xen
  mappings for pages with special cache attributes, and also check for
  a PGT_writable type and remove pages if appropriate.

- For compatibility with current guests, grab-and-release a
  PGT_writable_page type for PV guests in guest_physmap_add_entry().
  This will cause most "normal" guest pages to start out life with
  PGT_writable_page type (and thus an IOMMU mapping), but no type
  count (so that they can be used as special cases at will).

Also, note that there is one exception to to the "PGT_writable => in
iommu" rule: xenheap pages shared with guests may be given a
PGT_writable type with one type reference.  This reference prevents
the type from changing, which in turn prevents page from gaining an
IOMMU mapping in get_page_type().  It's not clear whether this was
intentional or not, but it's not something to change in a security
update.

This is XSA-288.

Reported-by: Paul Durrant <paul.durrant@citrix.com>
Signed-off-by: George Dunlap <george.dunlap@citrix.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>

commit_msg:
firewire: net: guard against rx buffer overflows

The IP-over-1394 driver firewire-net lacked input validation when
handling incoming fragmented datagrams.  A maliciously formed fragment
with a respectively large datagram_offset would cause a memcpy past the
datagram buffer.

So, drop any packets carrying a fragment with offset + length larger
than datagram_size.

In addition, ensure that
  - GASP header, unfragmented encapsulation header, or fragment
    encapsulation header actually exists before we access it,
  - the encapsulated datagram or fragment is of nonzero size.

Reported-by: Eyal Itkin <eyal.itkin@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Eyal Itkin <eyal.itkin@gmail.com>
Fixes: CVE 2016-8633
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Stefan Richter <stefanr@s5r6.in-berlin.de>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\tif (len <= RFC2374_UNFRAG_HDR_SIZE)', '\t\treturn 0;', '', '', '\tif (len <= RFC2374_FRAG_HDR_SIZE)', '\t\treturn 0;', '', '', '\tif (fg_off + len > dg_size)', '\t\treturn 0;']}
description: drivers/firewire/net.c in the Linux kernel before 4.8.7, in certain unusual hardware configurations, allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via crafted fragmented packets.

code_evidence: The function reads buf[0] as the header word and, for unfragmented packets, advances buf and subtracts RFC2374_UNFRAG_HDR_SIZE from len without first checking that len is large enough to contain that header; the subsequent memcpy at line 29 copies len bytes from buf into a newly allocated skb.

For fragmented packets it reads buf[1], advances buf by two words, and subtracts RFC2374_FRAG_HDR_SIZE from len, again without verifying the length; fg_off from the header and the remaining len are then passed to fwnet_pd_new/fwnet_pd_update.

Existing-datagram handling validates overlap (fwnet_frag_overlap) and datagram_size but never checks that fg_off + len stays within dg_size before fwnet_pd_update copies the fragment into the datagram buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-119 fits because the function performs buffer operations (memcpy of len bytes, fragment updates at fg_off) on memory whose bounds are not properly restricted by input validation, resulting in out-of-bounds access. The missing length/offset checks are the specific cause; the out-of-bounds memory operation is the class-level weakness described by CWE-119.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the receive path trusts attacker-controlled length/offset header fields without confirming the header fits in len or that a fragment's offset plus length stays within the declared datagram_size. Trigger: a crafted fragmented (or undersized) IP-over-1394 datagram with a large datagram_offset or a len shorter than the header. Consequence: memcpy operations read/write outside the intended buffer, yielding out-of-bounds memory access that can corrupt memory or crash the kernel.

commit_msg:
Don't allow too many consecutive warning alerts

Certain warning alerts are ignored if they are received. This can mean that
no progress will be made if one peer continually sends those warning alerts.
Implement a count so that we abort the connection if we receive too many.

Issue reported by Shi Lei.

Reviewed-by: Rich Salz <rsalz@openssl.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '    /*', "     * Reset the count of consecutive warning alerts if we've got a non-empty", "     * record that isn't an alert.", '     */', '    if (SSL3_RECORD_get_type(rr) != SSL3_RT_ALERT', '            && SSL3_RECORD_get_length(rr) != 0)', '        s->rlayer.alert_count = 0;', '', '            s->rlayer.alert_count++;', '            if (s->rlayer.alert_count == MAX_WARN_ALERT_COUNT) {', '                al = SSL_AD_UNEXPECTED_MESSAGE;', '                SSLerr(SSL_F_DTLS1_READ_BYTES, SSL_R_TOO_MANY_WARN_ALERTS);', '                goto f_err;', '            }', '']}
description: A denial of service flaw was found in OpenSSL 0.9.8, 1.0.1, 1.0.2 through 1.0.2h, and 1.1.0 in the way the TLS/SSL protocol defined processing of ALERT packets during a connection handshake. A remote attacker could use this flaw to make a TLS/SSL server consume an excessive amount of CPU and fail to accept connections from other clients.

code_evidence: When a warning-level alert arrives, the function stores alert_descr in s->s3->warn_alert and then, for non-close-notify warnings, reaches line 292's goto start without any limit on how many such alerts are accepted.
Fatal alerts are handled separately by shutting down, but warning alerts other than close_notify fall through to the restart at line 292, so an attacker can keep sending them.
The loop restarts at line 293, re-entering record processing with no count or throttle of consecutive warning alerts, allowing repeated CPU-consuming iterations.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function fails to throttle a resource-consuming operation (repeated alert processing), matching CWE-400's lack of throttling for resource consumption. The DoS is the impact; the underlying mistake is the missing limit on consecutive warning alerts.

evidence_lines.code:
goto start;
}

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the read loop accepts an unbounded number of warning alerts because no counter limits consecutive warnings. Trigger: a remote peer continuously sends warning-level alerts that are not close_notify, causing the goto start path to re-read records indefinitely. Consequence: the server consumes excessive CPU and fails to serve other clients (denial of service).

[  421.739719] iwlwifi 0000:01:00.0: iwl_sta_ucode_activate Added STA id 148 addr 00:00:00:00:00:00 to uCode

commit_msg:
Don't follow symlinks on file creation (CVE-2017-7501)

Open newly created files with O_EXCL to prevent symlink tricks.
When reopening hardlinks for writing the actual content, use append
mode instead. This is compatible with the write-only permissions but
is not destructive in case we got redirected to somebody elses file,
verify the target before actually writing anything.

As these are files with the temporary suffix, errors mean a local
user with sufficient privileges to break the installation of the package
anyway is trying to goof us on purpose, don't bother trying to mend it
(we couldn't fix the hardlink case anyhow) but just bail out.

Based on a patch by Florian Festi.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t    rc = expandRegular(fi, fn, psm, nodigest, 0);'], 'added_lines': ['\t    rc = expandRegular(fi, fn, psm, 0, nodigest, 0);']}
description: It was found that versions of rpm before 4.13.0.2 use temporary files with predictable names when installing an RPM. An attacker with ability to write in a directory where files will be installed could create symbolic links to an arbitrary location and modify content, and possibly permissions to arbitrary files, which could be used for denial of service or possibly privilege escalation.

code_evidence: The temporary suffix (tid) is appended to the destination path via fsmFsPath to form fpath, which is then used for file creation/verification without any check that the resulting path is not a pre-existing symlink.

For regular files, fsmMkfile is invoked on fpath when it appears missing; the newly created temporary file path is derived from a predictable name, allowing a pre-planted symlink to redirect creation.

For hardlinked content, expandRegular is called on fn (the first hardlink's path) to write the archive content, again operating on a path that was resolved earlier without re-validating that it is not a symlink.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function accesses files by pathname (fpath, fn) and does not prevent that name from resolving through a symlink to an unintended resource before creation/write, which is exactly CWE-59 link following. This is distinct from, e.g., predictable-name issues alone, because the security-relevant flaw is the unverified link resolution before file access.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function builds temporary/hardlink paths from predictable names and then creates or writes to them without O_EXCL-style exclusion or symlink verification. Trigger: an attacker with write access to the target directory pre-creates a symlink at the predictable temporary path. Consequence: file content/permissions can be redirected to an arbitrary target, enabling modification of unintended files (integrity/DoS, possibly escalation).

commit_msg:
We call skb_cow_data, which is good anyway to ensure we can actually
modify the skb as such (another error from prior). Now that we have the
number of fragments required, we can safely allocate exactly that amount
of memory.

Fixes: c09440f7dcb3 ("macsec: introduce IEEE 802.1AE driver")
Signed-off-by: Jason A. Donenfeld <Jason@zx2c4.com>
Acked-by: Sabrina Dubroca <sd@queasysnail.net>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\treq = macsec_alloc_req(rx_sa->key.tfm, &iv, &sg);', '\tsg_init_table(sg, MAX_SKB_FRAGS + 1);'], 'added_lines': ['\tstruct sk_buff *trailer;', '\tret = skb_cow_data(skb, 0, &trailer);', '\tif (unlikely(ret < 0)) {', '\t\tkfree_skb(skb);', '\t\treturn ERR_PTR(ret);', '\t}', '\treq = macsec_alloc_req(rx_sa->key.tfm, &iv, &sg, ret);', '\tsg_init_table(sg, ret);']}
description: Heap-based buffer overflow in drivers/net/macsec.c in the MACsec module in the Linux kernel through 4.10.12 allows attackers to cause a denial of service or possibly have unspecified other impact by leveraging the use of a MAX_SKB_FRAGS+1 size in conjunction with the NETIF_F_FRAGLIST feature, leading to an error in the skb_to_sgvec function.

code_evidence: The pre-patch allocation request macsec_alloc_req(tfm,&iv,&sg) provides no fragment count, so the scatterlist sg has no size tied to the actual skb layout.

sg_init_table(sg, MAX_SKB_FRAGS + 1) then fixes the scatterlist capacity at a constant, and skb_to_sgvec(skb, sg, 0, skb->len) walks the skb to fill it, with no check that the skb's real fragment count stays within that assumed capacity.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-119 fits because the code performs a write into the scatterlist memory region outside its intended boundary, caused by the mismatch between the fixed capacity and the actual fragment count. The patch fixes it by deriving the count from skb_cow_data and passing that count to both allocation and sg_init_table, which is a bounds-restriction fix rather than a separate weakness.

evidence_lines.code: req = macsec_alloc_req(rx_sa->key.tfm, &iv, &sg);

sg_init_table(sg, MAX_SKB_FRAGS + 1);
skb_to_sgvec(skb, sg, 0, skb->len);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the scatterlist size is a hard-coded constant rather than the actual number of fragments needed for this skb. Trigger: an incoming skb whose frag layout (fraglist/NETIF_F_FRAGLIST) requires more entries than the assumed MAX_SKB_FRAGS+1. skb_to_sgvec then writes scatterlist entries past the allocated buffer, producing a heap-based out-of-bounds write (CWE-119) that can crash or corrupt kernel memory.

commit_msg:

When attempting to match EXTENDED COPY CSCD descriptors with corresponding
se_devices, target_xcopy_locate_se_dev_e4() currently iterates over LIO's
global devices list which includes all configured backstores.

This change ensures that only initiator-accessible backstores are
considered during CSCD descriptor lookup, according to the session's
se_node_acl LUN list.

To avoid LUN removal race conditions, device pinning is changed from being
configfs based to instead using the se_node_acl lun_ref.

Fixed CVE-2018-8784

Thanks to Eyal Itkin from Check Point Software Technologies.

description: FreeRDP prior to version 2.0.0-rc4 contains a Heap-Based Buffer Overflow in function zgfx_decompress_segment() that results in a memory corruption and probably even a remote code execution.

code_evidence: Segment size is derived from untrusted input; cbSegment = segmentSize - 1 and the check only rejects segmentSize < 1, so the uncompressed path writes cbSegment bytes into zgfx->OutputBuffer via CopyMemory without bounding cbSegment against the buffer size.
In the token loop, the literal byte token writes zgfx->OutputBuffer[zgfx->OutputCount++] with no check that OutputCount is within the buffer.

For a match token, count is decoded from the bitstream and passed to zgfx_history_buffer_ring_read/write targeting &(zgfx->OutputBuffer[zgfx->OutputCount]) with count bytes, then OutputCount += count, with no bounds check.
For the literal-copy token, count is read via zgfx_GetBits(15) and CopyMemory writes count bytes to &(zgfx->OutputBuffer[zgfx->OutputCount]) with no bound.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes attacker-controlled lengths (cbSegment, count) and incrementing indices into zgfx->OutputBuffer without size validation, directly matching CWE-787 out-of-bounds write. This is a write-past-end buffer overflow rather than an out-of-bounds read.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: no upper-bound check on cbSegment, count, or OutputCount before writing into the fixed-size zgfx->OutputBuffer. Trigger: a crafted compressed segment (large segmentSize, large match count, or literal-copy count) drives writes past the buffer end; consequence is heap memory corruption potentially leading to remote code execution.

commit_msg:
gryphon: Create pkt_info if it doesn't exist

Try to retrieve the per packet info data first, and create it if
it doesn't exist, rather than assuming it is there on the second
pass. Prevents segfaults in cases with strange TCP sequence issues
(that still show up as bugs in the TCP dissector.) Fix #17737.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if (!pinfo->fd->visited) {', '    } else {', '        pkt_info = (gryphon_pkt_info_t*)p_get_proto_data(wmem_file_scope(), pinfo, proto_gryphon, (guint32)tvb_raw_offset(tvb));'], 'added_lines': ['    pkt_info = (gryphon_pkt_info_t*)p_get_proto_data(wmem_file_scope(), pinfo, proto_gryphon, (guint32)tvb_raw_offset(tvb));', '', '    if (!pkt_info) {']}
description: Crash in the Gryphon dissector in Wireshark 3.4.0 to 3.4.10 allows denial of service via packet injection or crafted capture file

code_evidence: Before the fix, pkt_info is only fetched from proto data in the visited branch; on a non-visited pass where the second-pass condition does not match, pkt_info can remain uninitialized/NULL.
pkt_info->cmd_context is written under !visited without a NULL check on pkt_info.
pkt_info->rsp_frame_num is dereferenced unconditionally, so a NULL pkt_info causes a crash.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits: the function retrieves a pointer that may be NULL and dereferences it without a check, directly yielding a NULL pointer dereference and crash. This is a missing validity check, not a buffer over-read.

evidence_lines.code: if (pkt_info->rsp_frame_num > 0) {

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The code assumes per-packet proto data exists on the second pass and dereferences pkt_info without verifying retrieval succeeded. A crafted capture or strange TCP sequence causes p_get_proto_data to return NULL, and the subsequent pkt_info->rsp_frame_num access dereferences NULL, crashing the dissector (DoS).

net: vmxnet3: fix possible use-after-free bugs in vmxnet3_rq_alloc_rx_buf()

In vmxnet3_rq_alloc_rx_buf(), when dma_map_single() fails, rbi->skb is
freed immediately. Similarly, in another branch, when dma_map_page() fails,
rbi->page is also freed. In the two cases, vmxnet3_rq_alloc_rx_buf()
returns an error to its callers vmxnet3_rq_init() -> vmxnet3_rq_init_all()
-> vmxnet3_activate_dev(). Then vmxnet3_activate_dev() calls
vmxnet3_rq_cleanup_all() in error handling code, and rbi->skb or rbi->page
are freed again in vmxnet3_rq_cleanup_all(), causing use-after-free bugs.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t\t\trbi->skb = NULL;', '\t\t\t\t\trbi->page = NULL;']}
description: A use-after-free flaw was found in vmxnet3_rq_alloc_rx_buf in drivers/net/vmxnet3/vmxnet3_drv.c in VMware's vmxnet3 ethernet NIC driver in the Linux Kernel. This issue could allow a local attacker to crash the system due to a double-free while cleaning up vmxnet3_rq_cleanup_all, which could also lead to a kernel information leak problem.

code_evidence: On dma_mapping_error for the SKB path, dev_kfree_skb_any(rbi->skb) frees the skb but leaves rbi->skb pointing at freed memory; the loop breaks and the function returns an error count to its caller.
Similarly, when dma_map_page fails, put_page(rbi->page) releases the page but rbi->page is not cleared before the break and error return.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The freed skb/page remains referenced through rbi and is subsequently accessed/freed again during cleanup, which is reuse of memory after free, matching CWE-416. It is not merely a NULL-pointer or leak issue: the stale pointer is dereferenced by later code.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the error paths free rbi->skb/rbi->page without nulling the pointers. Trigger: a DMA mapping failure returns an error up through vmxnet3_rq_init to vmxnet3_activate_dev, whose error handling calls vmxnet3_rq_cleanup_all; that cleanup sees the non-NULL stale pointer and frees it again, producing a double-free/use-after-free (KASAN consume_skb report).

description: GPAC v2.3-DEV-rev449-g5948e4f70-master was discovered to contain a heap-use-after-free via the gf_bs_align function at bitstream.c. This vulnerability allows attackers to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) via supplying a crafted file.

code_evidence: At line 101-102 a new bitstream uncomp_bs is created over uncomp_data and bs is reassigned to point to uncomp_bs, losing the original caller bitstream reference.
At lines 193-195 the compressed-stream teardown frees uncomp_data and deletes uncomp_bs, but bs still aliases the now-freed uncomp_bs.
Line 220 records GF_ISOM_BOX_COMPRESSED on newBox while bs remains dangling, so subsequent gf_bs operations in callers use freed memory.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the stale bs pointer is used after the underlying GF_BitStream was freed via gf_bs_del. The root cause is the missing restoration of the original bitstream, not a simple out-of-bounds read.

bs = uncomp_bs;
newBox->internal_flags = GF_ISOM_BOX_COMPRESSED;
