commit_msg:
usbip_host updates device status without holding lock from stub probe,
disconnect and rebind code paths. When multiple requests to import a
device are received, these unprotected code paths step all over each
other and drive fails with NULL-ptr deref and use-after-free errors.

The driver uses a table lock to protect the busid array for adding and
deleting busids to the table. However, the probe, disconnect and rebind
paths get the busid table entry and update the status without holding
the busid table lock. Add a new finer grain lock to protect the busid
entry. This new lock will be held to search and update the busid entry
fields from get_busid_idx(), add_match_busid() and del_match_busid().

match_busid_show() does the same to access the busid entry fields.

get_busid_priv() changed to return the pointer to the busid entry holding
the busid lock. stub_probe(), stub_disconnect() and stub_device_rebind()
call put_busid_priv() to release the busid lock before returning. This
changes fixes the unprotected code paths eliminating the race conditions
in updating the busid entries.

Reported-by: Jakub Jirasek
Signed-off-by: Shuah Khan (Samsung OSG) <shuah@kernel.org>
Cc: stable <stable@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t/* now run rebind */'], 'added_lines': ['\t/* now run rebind - no need to hold locks. driver files are removed */']}
description: In the Linux Kernel before version 4.16.11, 4.14.43, 4.9.102, and 4.4.133, multiple race condition errors when handling probe, disconnect, and rebind operations can be exploited to trigger a use-after-free condition or a NULL pointer dereference by sending multiple USB over IP packets.

code_evidence: The first loop reads busid_table[i].name and shutdown_busid and writes busid_priv->status while holding busid_table_lock, then releases the lock at line 14.

The second loop re-reads the same table entries and calls do_rebind(busid_table[i].name, busid_priv) without holding any busid-entry lock, so the entry fields can change concurrently between the two loops and during do_rebind.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This is a concurrent sequence accessing shared busid_table entries with improper synchronization, matching CWE-362: a timing window lets another code sequence modify the shared resource. The lock is absent for the do_rebind phase, violating exclusivity/atomicity rather than a distinct memory-safety root cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The status update and rebind are split into two separately locked/unlocked phases: the status is set under busid_table_lock, but do_rebind runs after unlock with only the table lock, which does not protect per-entry fields. A concurrent probe, disconnect, or import path can modify or free the busid entry between the check and use, producing a NULL-pointer dereference or use-after-free.

commit_msg:
netfilter: ipv6: nf_defrag: drop mangled skb on ream error

Dmitry Vyukov reported GPF in network stack that Andrey traced down to
negative nh offset in nf_ct_frag6_queue().

Problem is that all network headers before fragment header are pulled.
Normal ipv6 reassembly will drop the skb when errors occur further down
the line.

netfilter doesn't do this, and instead passed the original fragment
along.  That was also fine back when netfilter ipv6 defrag worked with
cloned fragments, as the original, pristine fragment was passed on.

So we either have to undo the pull op, or discard such fragments.
Since they're malformed after all (e.g. overlapping fragment) it seems
preferrable to just drop them.

Same for temporary errors -- it doesn't make sense to accept (and
perhaps forward!) only some fragments of same datagram.

Fixes: 029f7f3b8701cc7ac ("netfilter: ipv6: nf_defrag: avoid/free clone operations")
Reported-by: Dmitry Vyukov <dvyukov@google.com>
Debugged-by: Andrey Konovalov <andreyknvl@google.com>
Diagnosed-by: Eric Dumazet <Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Florian Westphal <fw@strlen.de>
Acked-by: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\treturn -EINVAL;', '\t\treturn -EINVAL;'], 'added_lines': ['\t\treturn 0;', '\t\treturn 0;']}
description: The netfilter subsystem in the Linux kernel before 4.9 mishandles IPv6 reassembly, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (integer overflow, out-of-bounds write, and GPF) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted application that makes socket, connect, and writev system calls, related to net/ipv6/netfilter/nf_conntrack_reasm.c and net/ipv6/netfilter/nf_defrag_ipv6_hooks.c.

code_evidence: On a zero payload_len, the function logs and returns -EINVAL instead of accepting the malformed packet.
When find_prev_fhdr fails to locate a valid fragment header, it also returns -EINVAL rather than continuing.
pskb_may_pull is checked for fhoff + sizeof(*fhdr); only after this does it set the transport header and cast to frag_hdr.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The supported consequence is an out-of-bounds write: the mangled skb carries an invalid header offset into downstream reassembly, where memory is written past the intended buffer. This matches CWE-787; it is not merely an integer overflow, which is the upstream trigger rather than the memory-safety outcome.

evidence_lines.code:
if (find_prev_fhdr(skb, &prevhdr, &nhoff, &fhoff) < 0)
return -EINVAL;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The pre-patch error paths in the fragment-gather routine returned -EINVAL and the caller passed the original skb onward after network headers had been pulled. A crafted IPv6 fragment with a zero payload length or malformed header chain triggers these early returns, leaving a mangled skb that is later processed with a negative header offset, enabling an out-of-bounds write.

commit_msg:
tmx: allocate space to store ending 0 for branch value

- reported by Alfred Farrugia and Sandro Gauci
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tdsize += svbranch.len;'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tdsize += svbranch.len + 1;']}
description: A Buffer Overflow issue was discovered in Kamailio before 4.4.7, 5.0.x before 5.0.6, and 5.1.x before 5.1.2. A specially crafted REGISTER message with a malformed branch or From tag triggers an off-by-one heap-based buffer overflow in the tmx_check_pretran function in modules/tmx/tmx_pretran.c.

code_evidence: dsize is computed from callid, cseqnum, cseqmet and From tag lengths plus 4, then adds svbranch.len when a Via branch exists, but omits the terminating NUL that will later be written for the branch string.
The buffer is allocated with shm_malloc(dsize) and dbuf.len set to dsize; the size check only reallocates when dsize exceeds the current buffer length.

At copy time the branch is placed at cseqmet.s + cseqmet.len + 1, memcpy copies svbranch.len bytes, then line 114 writes a NUL at vbranch.s[vbranch.len], one byte past the allocated region when dsize is exactly consumed.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function allocates a buffer sized without the trailing NUL and then writes that NUL one byte beyond the buffer, which is a write past the end of an intended buffer, matching CWE-787. This is distinct from a read overrun or integer overflow because the size arithmetic itself is not wrapped; the missing terminator causes the out-of-bounds store.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the size accounting forgets the NUL terminator for the Via branch, while the write path still stores it. Trigger: a REGISTER request carrying a Via branch value whose total dsize fits the allocation exactly. Consequence: a one-byte heap out-of-bounds write past the shared-memory buffer, corrupting adjacent heap metadata or data.

commit_msg: fixed #1900
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (pps_id > 255)'], 'added_lines': ['\tif ((pps_id<0) || (pps_id > 255))']}
description: A buffer overflow vulnerability exists in Gpac through 1.0.1 via a malformed MP4 file in the svc_parse_slice function in av_parsers.c, which allows attackers to cause a denial of service, even code execution and escalation of privileges.

A malformed file yielding a negative Exp-Golomb value passes the check and dereferences avc->pps out of bounds; the subsequent write via si->pps->id corrupts memory, supporting crash or code execution as described.

commit_msg:
Input: sunkbd - avoid use-after-free in teardown paths

We need to make sure we cancel the reinit work before we tear down the
driver structures.

Reported-by: Bodong Zhao <nopitydays@gmail.com>
Tested-by: Bodong Zhao <nopitydays@gmail.com>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Dmitry Torokhov <dmitry.torokhov@gmail.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tschedule_work(&sunkbd->tq);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (sunkbd->enabled)', '\t\t\tschedule_work(&sunkbd->tq);']}
description: A vulnerability was found in the Linux Kernel where the function sunkbd_reinit having been scheduled by sunkbd_interrupt before sunkbd being freed. Though the dangling pointer is set to NULL in sunkbd_disconnect, there is still an alias in sunkbd_reinit causing Use After Free.

code_evidence: Line 4 retrieves the sunkbd driver data pointer from the serio device without any lifetime/validity check. On receiving SUNKBD_RET_RESET (line 16), the interrupt handler unconditionally calls schedule_work(&sunkbd->tq) at line 17, queuing sunkbd_reinit to run later against the sunkbd structure, then sets reset to -1 (line 18).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the function queues work whose callback later accesses a freed sunkbd object; the fix gates scheduling on sunkbd->enabled, confirming the lifetime defect. This is use-after-free, not merely a race or null dereference, since the referenced memory is released before reuse.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the interrupt path schedules deferred work referencing sunkbd without verifying that the device is still enabled/live. Trigger: a SUNKBD_RET_RESET byte arriving during teardown, after sunkbd has been freed. The queued sunkbd_reinit then dereferences freed memory, causing use-after-free (crash or memory corruption).

The function `ProcessRadioRxDone` implicitly expects incoming radio frames to have at least a payload of one byte or more. An empty payload leads to a 1-byte out-of-bounds read of user controlled content when the payload buffer is reused. This allows an attacker to craft a FRAME_TYPE_PROPRIETARY frame with size -1 which results in an 65280-byte out-of-bounds memcopy likely with partially controlled attacker data. Corrupting a large part if the data section is likely to cause a DoS. If the large out-of-bounds write does not immediately crash the attacker may gain control over the execution due to now controlling large parts of the data section. Users are advised to upgrade either by updating their package or by manually applying the patch commit `e851b079`.

code_evidence: Line 10-11 bind payload to RxDoneParams.Payload and size to RxDoneParams.Size, both attacker-influenced from the received radio frame. Line 65 reads payload[0] via pktHeaderLen++ without first confirming size > 0.

In the FRAME_TYPE_PROPRIETARY branch, line 375 copies size - pktHeaderLen bytes into MacCtx.RxPayload. With size == 0 and pktHeaderLen == 1, the length expression underflows to 65535; line 379 stores the same underflowed value as BufferSize.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect is an off-by-one boundary error: the code treats a zero-length buffer as if it held one header byte, producing an incorrect length that is one less than the true size and underflows. This matches CWE-193's incorrect minimum/boundary value. The consequence is an out-of-bounds write, but the root cause is the off-by-one length assumption, not a generic buffer overflow.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function assumes an incoming frame has at least one header byte but never validates size before reading payload[0] and incrementing pktHeaderLen. A zero-length frame causes pktHeaderLen to exceed size, so size - pktHeaderLen wraps to 65535, driving an out-of-bounds memcpy1 write of attacker-influenced data into MacCtx.RxPayload, enabling memory corruption and DoS.

commit_msg:
packet: fix races in fanout_add()

Multiple threads can call fanout_add() at the same time.

We need to grab fanout_mutex earlier to avoid races that could
lead to one thread freeing po->rollover that was set by another thread.

Do the same in fanout_release(), for peace of mind, and to help us
finding lockdep issues earlier.

Fixes: dc99f600698d ("packet: Add fanout support.")
Fixes: 0648ab70afe6 ("packet: rollover prepare: per-socket state")
Signed-off-by: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Cc: Willem de Bruijn <willemb@google.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (!f)', '\t\treturn;', '\tmutex_lock(&fanout_mutex);', '\tpo->fanout = NULL;', '\tif (atomic_dec_and_test(&f->sk_ref)) {', '\t\tlist_del(&f->list);', '\t\tdev_remove_pack(&f->prot_hook);', '\t\tfanout_release_data(f);', '\t\tkfree(f);', '', '\tif (po->rollover)', '\t\tkfree_rcu(po->rollover, rcu);'], 'added_lines': ['\tmutex_lock(&fanout_mutex);', '\tif (f) {', '\t\tpo->fanout = NULL;', '\t\tif (atomic_dec_and_test(&f->sk_ref)) {', '\t\t\tlist_del(&f->list);', '\t\t\tdev_remove_pack(&f->prot_hook);', '\t\t\tfanout_release_data(f);', '\t\t\tkfree(f);', '\t\t}', '\t\tif (po->rollover)', '\t\t\tkfree_rcu(po->rollover, rcu);']}
description: Race condition in net/packet/af_packet.c in the Linux kernel before 4.9.13 allows local users to cause a denial of service (use-after-free) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a multithreaded application that makes PACKET_FANOUT setsockopt system calls.

code_evidence: Lines 5-8 read po->fanout into f and early-return before taking fanout_mutex, so the NULL check and the unlock-protected read of po->fanout are not synchronized with concurrent fanout_add().

Lines 9-15 set po->fanout to NULL and free f only under fanout_mutex, but the initial f was captured outside the lock; another thread may have replaced or freed the fanout state between line 5 and line 8.
Lines 17-18 free po->rollover outside fanout_mutex, allowing a concurrent fanout_add() to install a rollover that is then freed or to free it twice.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This is a concurrent execution flaw where a shared resource (packet socket fanout/rollover state) is accessed without proper exclusive synchronization, matching CWE-362. The unsynchronized read/free window directly violates atomicity, rather than being a simple memory-safety bug.

evidence_lines.code:
if (po->rollover)
kfree_rcu(po->rollover, rcu);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The root cause is that po->fanout and po->rollover are read and manipulated without holding fanout_mutex across the whole sequence: f is loaded at line 5 before locking, and rollover is freed at line 18 after unlocking. Concurrent PACKET_FANOUT setsockopt calls from multiple threads can interleave, so one thread frees state that another has just installed, causing a use-after-free or double free and a denial of service.

patch 8.2.3611: crash when using CTRL-W f without finding a file name

Problem:    Crash when using CTRL-W f without finding a file name.

description: vim is vulnerable to Heap-based Buffer Overflow

code_evidence: In the characterwise branch, *pp is set to a line position and *lenp is computed as a column difference plus one ([22,23],[27,28]); when the selection is empty or the cursor starts at NUL, *lenp can be zero. Line [31] then indexes *pp + (*lenp - 1), i.e. one byte before *pp, and passes that pointer to mb_ptr2len, which reads beyond the intended selection into heap line storage.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe index reads outside a heap-allocated line buffer, matching CWE-122's heap-based out-of-bounds memory access. The missing zero-length constraint is the direct cause, distinguishing it from an integer overflow that merely produces a bad length elsewhere.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the length is not checked for zero before the multibyte correction indexes at *lenp - 1. Trigger: a characterwise visual selection whose computed length is zero (e.g. CTRL-W f with no file name). The out-of-bounds read from heap-allocated line memory supports a crash/DoS; the patch adds the zero-length guard and the *lenp > 0 condition.

commit_msg:
Ignore certain messages in plugin broker process if they are not sent by the
browser.

BUG=610600
CQ_INCLUDE_TRYBOTS=tryserver.chromium.linux:linux_site_isolation

Review-Url: https://codereview.chromium.org/2069853002
Cr-Commit-Position: refs/heads/master@{#400495}
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  base::ProcessId process_id = (process_handle == base::kNullProcessHandle) ?', '      0 : base::GetProcId(process_handle);'], 'added_lines': ['  base::ProcessId process_id = base::kNullProcessId;', '  if (process_handle != base::kNullProcessHandle) {', '    // This channel is not used by the browser itself.', '    process_id = base::GetProcId(process_handle);', '    CHECK_NE(base::kNullProcessId, process_id);', '  }']}
description: The PPAPI implementation in Google Chrome before 52.0.2743.82 does not validate the origin of IPC messages to the plugin broker process that should have come from the browser process, which allows remote attackers to bypass a sandbox protection mechanism via an unexpected message type, related to broker_process_dispatcher.cc, ppapi_plugin_process_host.cc, ppapi_thread.cc, and render_frame_message_filter.cc.

code_evidence: RequestPluginChannel obtains channel information from the client via GetPpapiChannelInfo, yielding process_handle and renderer_child_id without verifying the origin or authenticity of the requesting party.

The process_handle is converted to a process_id using a null-handle ternary that maps a null handle to 0; the resulting process_id (and the unvalidated renderer_child_id) is embedded directly into PpapiMsg_CreateChannel and sent.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-20 fits because the code accepts client-supplied channel metadata and forwards it without checking the required property (browser origin/authenticity) before use. The fix adds a null-process-id constraint, confirming missing input validation; this is improper validation rather than mere message filtering.

PpapiMsg_CreateChannel* msg = new PpapiMsg_CreateChannel(
process_id, renderer_child_id, client->OffTheRecord());

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function builds and dispatches PpapiMsg_CreateChannel using process_handle/renderer_child_id derived from the client without validating that the message actually originated from the browser process. Trigger: a non-browser sender (e.g., a compromised renderer) supplies channel info via GetPpapiChannelInfo. Consequence: an unexpected message type reaches the plugin broker, bypassing the sandbox protection that should restrict broker IPC to the browser.

commit_msg:
Jan Kara's analysis of the syzbot report (edited):

  The reproducer opens a directory on FUSE filesystem, it then attaches
  dnotify mark to the open directory.  After that a fuse_do_getattr() call
  finds that attributes returned by the server are inconsistent, and calls
  make_bad_inode() which, among other things does:

          inode->i_mode = S_IFREG;

  This then confuses dnotify which doesn't tear down its structures
  properly and eventually crashes.

Avoid calling make_bad_inode() on a live inode: switch to a private flag on
the fuse inode.  Also add the test to ops which the bad_inode_ops would
have caught.

This bug goes back to the initial merge of fuse in 2.6.14...

Reported-by: syzbot+f427adf9324b92652ccc@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Signed-off-by: Miklos Szeredi <mszeredi@redhat.com>
Tested-by: Jan Kara <jack@suse.cz>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\tif (fuse_is_bad(inode))', '\t\treturn -EIO;']}
description: An issue was discovered in the FUSE filesystem implementation in the Linux kernel before 5.10.6, aka CID-5d069dbe8aaf. fuse_do_getattr() calls make_bad_inode() in inappropriate situations, causing a system crash. NOTE: the original fix for this vulnerability was incomplete, and its incompleteness is tracked as CVE-2021-28950.

code_evidence: fuse_setattr derives fc and file from the inode and only checks fuse_allow_current_process; there is no test for a bad/aborted inode before proceeding.
When ATTR_KILL_SUID/SGID is set and the connection lacks handle_killpriv, the code calls fuse_do_getattr and then reads inode->i_mode to adjust suid/sgid bits.
The final fuse_do_setattr is invoked and only on success are ACLs and the dentry cache cleaned up; no cleanup occurs on the bad-inode path.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-459 fits because the weakness is failure to tear down/clean up supporting resources (dnotify state) after the inode becomes unusable; the setattr path lacks the fuse_is_bad check that would stop work on a bad inode. This is incomplete cleanup, not merely a type confusion.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: setattr operations proceed on an inode that fuse_do_getattr may have marked bad via make_bad_inode, without a bad-inode guard. Trigger: a FUSE server returns inconsistent attributes so make_bad_inode rewrites i_mode to S_IFREG while dnotify structures remain attached. The subsequent setattr path and mode handling operate on the corrupted inode, leaving supporting dnotify state uncleaned and leading to a crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
gvariant: Don’t allow child elements to overlap with each other

If different elements of a variable sized array can overlap with each
other then we can cause a `GVariant` to normalise to a much larger type.

This commit changes the behaviour of `GVariant` with non-normal form data. If
an invalid frame offset is found all subsequent elements are given their
default value.

When retrieving an element at index `n` we scan the frame offsets up to index
`n` and if they are not in order we return an element with the default value
for that type.  This guarantees that elements don't overlap with each
other.  We remember the offset we've scanned up to so we don't need to
repeat this work on subsequent accesses.  We skip these checks for trusted
data.

Unfortunately this makes random access of untrusted data O(n) — at least
on first access.  It doesn't affect the algorithmic complexity of accessing
elements in order, such as when using the `GVariantIter` interface.  Also:
the cost of validation will be amortised as the `GVariant` instance is
continued to be used.

I've implemented this with 4 different functions, 1 for each element size,
rather than looping calling `gvs_read_unaligned_le` in the hope that the
compiler will find it easy to optimise and should produce fairly tight
code.

Fixes: #2121

commit_msg:
Prevent KDC unset status assertion failures

Assign status values if S4U2Self padata fails to decode, if an
S4U2Proxy request uses invalid KDC options, or if an S4U2Proxy request
uses an evidence ticket which does not match the canonicalized request
server principal name.  Reported by Samuel Cabrero.

If a status value is not assigned during KDC processing, default to
"UNKNOWN_REASON" rather than failing an assertion.  This change will
prevent future denial of service bugs due to similar mistakes, and
will allow us to omit assigning status values for unlikely errors such
as small memory allocation failures.

CVE-2017-11368:

In MIT krb5 1.7 and later, an authenticated attacker can cause an
assertion failure in krb5kdc by sending an invalid S4U2Self or
S4U2Proxy request.

  CVSSv3 Vector: AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H/E:H/RL:O/RC:C

description: In MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.7 and later, an authenticated attacker can cause a KDC assertion failure by sending invalid S4U2Self or S4U2Proxy requests.

code_evidence: On invalid S4U2Proxy KDC options, the function returns KRB5KDC_ERR_BADOPTION without assigning *status.
When the evidence ticket's server principal mismatches the canonicalized server principal, it returns KRB5KDC_ERR_SERVER_NOMATCH without assigning *status.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing *status assignment reaches a caller assertion on attacker-controlled request fields, matching CWE-617 (reachable assertion leading to exit/DoS). This is an availability impact from an assert, not a memory-safety or authentication-bypass weakness.

evidence_lines.code:
if (request->kdc_options & (NON_TGT_OPTION | KDC_OPT_ENC_TKT_IN_SKEY)) {
return KRB5KDC_ERR_BADOPTION;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: two error paths return without setting the caller-supplied *status out-parameter, so callers that assert a status was assigned fail. Trigger: an authenticated attacker sends an S4U2Proxy request with disallowed KDC options or an evidence ticket whose server principal does not match the canonicalized request server principal. Consequence: the KDC assertion terminates the krb5kdc process, causing denial of service.

commit_msg:
netmon: Initialize struct netmonrec_comment on alloc

This avoids an illegal pointer to free() on error.

Bug: 14397
Change-Id: Id6e535141c7a3ee7b3d1822875b571e2199a5387
Reviewed-on: https://code.wireshark.org/review/25660
Reviewed-by: Stig Bjørlykke <stig@bjorlykke.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\tcomment_rec = g_new(struct netmonrec_comment, 1);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\tcomment_rec = g_new0(struct netmonrec_comment, 1);']}
description: The netmonrec_comment_destroy function in wiretap/netmon.c in Wireshark through 2.4.4 performs a free operation on an uninitialized memory address, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (application crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact.

code_evidence: At line 193 the comment record is allocated with g_new, which does not zero the struct. Lines 194-196 set only numFramePerComment, frameOffset and titleLength; title is assigned at 197, but description remains uninitialized. The record is inserted into the hash table at 198 with netmonrec_comment_destroy as value destroyer.
If the title read at 199 fails, lines 200-201 destroy the hash table, invoking the destroy function on the partially initialized record; the uninitialized description pointer is then freed.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-763 fits because a memory resource is released via an invalid pointer (uninitialized description) during cleanup, not merely a mismatched allocator. The fix uses g_new0 to zero the struct so the cleanup free is valid.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: g_new leaves description uninitialized before the record is registered with a destroy callback. Trigger: a truncated/short read of the comment title causes error-path hash-table destruction. Consequence: free() of an invalid pointer, causing a crash/DoS.

commit_msg:
Prevent division by 0 in TFLite

PiperOrigin-RevId: 370800311
Change-Id: I21ccdbd31c30118acc67df8751807ee2e0b12f91
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  TF_LITE_ENSURE(context, block_size > 0);']}
description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. The implementation of the `DepthToSpace` TFLite operator is vulnerable to a division by zero error(https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/0d45ea1ca641b21b73bcf9c00e0179cda284e7e7/tensorflow/lite/kernels/depth_to_space.cc#L63-L69). An attacker can craft a model such that `params->block_size` is 0. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.5.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.4.2, TensorFlow 2.3.3, TensorFlow 2.2.3 and TensorFlow 2.1.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: Line 18 reads block_size from model-supplied builtin_data without validating it. Line 24 divides input_channels by block_size twice, and lines 25-28 divide output dimensions by block_size and multiply output_channels by block_size, all before any check that block_size is nonzero.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs integer division using an unvalidated, attacker-controllable divisor, so a zero value leads directly to divide-by-zero. CWE-369 captures this exact division-by-zero flaw; the missing validation is the root cause, and the crash is its consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: params->block_size is taken from the crafted model and used as a divisor without a nonzero constraint. Trigger: a model setting block_size to 0, which makes the divisions in the Prepare path evaluate a zero divisor, causing a crash (DoS) during interpreter preparation.

commit_msg:
KEYS: Remove key_type::match in favour of overriding default by match_preparse

A previous patch added a ->match_preparse() method to the key type.  This is
allowed to override the function called by the iteration algorithm.
Therefore, we can just set a default that simply checks for an exact match of
the key description with the original criterion data and allow match_preparse
to override it as needed.

The key_type::match op is then redundant and can be removed, as can the
user_match() function.

Signed-off-by: David Howells <dhowells@redhat.com>
Acked-by: Vivek Goyal <vgoyal@redhat.com>
diff_func:
--- func_before
+++ func_after
@@ -5,7 +5,7 @@
 		.index_key.type		= &key_type_request_key_auth,
 		.index_key.description	= description,
 		.cred			= current_cred(),
-		.match_data.cmp		= user_match,
+		.match_data.cmp		= key_default_cmp,
 		.match_data.raw_data	= description,
 		.match_data.lookup_type	= KEYRING_SEARCH_LOOKUP_DIRECT,
 	};
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t.match_data.cmp\t\t= user_match,'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t.match_data.cmp\t\t= key_default_cmp,']}
description: The KEYS subsystem in the Linux kernel before 3.18 allows local users to gain privileges or cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference and system crash) via vectors involving a NULL value for a certain match field, related to the keyring_search_iterator function in keyring.c.

code_evidence: The search context is initialized with .match_data.cmp = user_match and lookup_type KEYRING_SEARCH_LOOKUP_DIRECT, but no NULL check is performed on the cmp field before the context is used.
The context is passed to search_process_keyrings, which drives the keyring_search_iterator path that invokes the match comparison function.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is a NULL pointer dereference: an expected-valid function pointer in match_data is used without validation in the keyring search iteration. Related missing-check issues differ, but the supported consequence here is a NULL dereference crash.

evidence_lines.code: authkey_ref = search_process_keyrings(&ctx);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the search context supplies a comparison callback (user_match) without guaranteeing it is non-NULL when the iterator dereferences it. Trigger: a caller reaches search_process_keyrings with this context and the iteration path invokes the match field; if the field is NULL, the iterator dereferences it, causing a crash or DoS.

commit_msg:
In sctp_sendmesg(), when walking the list of endpoint associations, the
association can be dropped from the list, making the list corrupt.
Properly handle this by using list_for_each_entry_safe()

Fixes: 4910280503f3 ("sctp: add support for snd flag SCTP_SENDALL process in sendmsg")
Reported-by: Secunia Research <vuln@secunia.com>
Tested-by: Secunia Research <vuln@secunia.com>
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
Acked-by: Marcelo Ricardo Leitner <marcelo.leitner@gmail.com>
Acked-by: Neil Horman <nhorman@tuxdriver.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tstruct sctp_association *asoc;', '\t\tlist_for_each_entry(asoc, &ep->asocs, asocs) {'], 'added_lines': ['\tstruct sctp_association *asoc, *tmp;', '\t\tlist_for_each_entry_safe(asoc, tmp, &ep->asocs, asocs) {']}
description: In the Linux Kernel before versions 4.20.8 and 4.19.21 a use-after-free error in the "sctp_sendmsg()" function (net/sctp/socket.c) when handling SCTP_SENDALL flag can be exploited to corrupt memory.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function's flaw is an unsafe list iteration that can use a freed association after list mutation (use-after-free), not an out-of-bounds write past a buffer; no buffer write with an out-of-range index/pointer is present.

commit_msg:
Remove unnecessary padding code

Bug: 213170822

Remove the code that CursorWindow::writeToParcel() uses to ensure slot
data is 4-byte aligned.  Because mAllocOffset and mSlotsOffset are
already 4-byte aligned, the alignment step here is unnecessary.

CursorWindow::spaceInUse() returns the total space used.  The tests
verify that the total space used is always a multiple of 4 bytes.

Test: atest
 * libandroidfw_tests
(cherry picked from https://googleplex-android-review.googlesource.com/q/commit:5d4afa0986cbc440f458b4b8db05fd176ef3e6d2)
(cherry picked from https://googleplex-android-review.googlesource.com/q/commit:5b0232d7e1c2087839d9bc029943c8780b2484ab)
Merged-In: I720699093d5c5a584283e5b76851938f449ffa21
Change-Id: I720699093d5c5a584283e5b76851938f449ffa21
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        uint32_t slotsSize = mSize - mSlotsOffset;'], 'added_lines': ['        uint32_t slotsSize = sizeOfSlots();']}
description: In writeToParcel of CursorWindow.cpp, there is a possible information disclosure due to uninitialized data. This could lead to local information disclosure with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

code_evidence: slotsSize is computed as mSize - mSlotsOffset and used to place the slot block at newSlotsOffset in the freshly mmap'd region; only mAllocOffset bytes from the old allocation and slotsSize bytes of slots are copied into newData. The new mapping is created by ashmem_create_region/mmap and is not zero-filled or otherwise initialized by this function.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function copies selected ranges into a new resource and then installs it as mData without initializing the remainder, directly matching CWE-908's use of an uninitialized resource with a read-memory consequence. CWE-457 concerns uninitialized variables rather than an uninitialized allocated region.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The new ashmem region backing newData is not initialized before the two memcpy calls; any gap between mAllocOffset and newSlotsOffset (or over-counted slotsSize) remains uninitialized. Subsequent reads from that window, e.g. when writeToParcel serializes the region, can expose stale/uninitialized memory content.

commit_msg:
avcodec/webp: Always set pix_fmt

Fixes: out of array access
Fixes: 1434/clusterfuzz-testcase-minimized-6314998085189632
Fixes: 1435/clusterfuzz-testcase-minimized-6483783723253760

Found-by: continuous fuzzing process https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz/tree/master/targets/ffmpeg
Reviewed-by: "Ronald S. Bultje" <rsbultje@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        if (s->has_alpha)', '            avctx->pix_fmt = AV_PIX_FMT_YUVA420P;'], 'added_lines': ['    avctx->pix_fmt = s->has_alpha ? AV_PIX_FMT_YUVA420P : AV_PIX_FMT_YUV420P;']}
description: libavcodec/webp.c in FFmpeg before 2.8.12, 3.0.x before 3.0.8, 3.1.x before 3.1.8, 3.2.x before 3.2.5, and 3.3.x before 3.3.1 does not ensure that pix_fmt is set, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (heap-based buffer overflow and application crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted file, related to the vp8_decode_mb_row_no_filter and pred8x8_128_dc_8_c functions.

code_evidence: pix_fmt is assigned only inside the one-time initialization block, and only when has_alpha is true; when has_alpha is false no pix_fmt is chosen here, so the decoder may proceed with an unset/incorrect pixel format before ff_vp8_decode_frame and the alpha path consume it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The description and commit explicitly report an out-of-array access (heap buffer overflow) resulting from the missing pix_fmt constraint, which is an operation outside the intended memory buffer, matching CWE-119.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the pixel format is not guaranteed to be set on every decode call, because the assignment is conditional and coupled to the single initialization. Trigger: a crafted lossy WebP without alpha reaches vp8_lossy_decode_frame with a stale/unset pix_fmt. Consequence: downstream VP8 decode and pred8x8_128_dc_8_c operate with mismatched format assumptions, causing an out-of-bounds heap access and crash.

commit_msg:
Fixed a BMP decoding bug (buffer underrun)

Fixes issue #8
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tif(rctx->infoheader_size<12) goto done;']}
description: The iwbmp_read_info_header function in imagew-bmp.c in libimageworsener.a in ImageWorsener 1.3.0 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference) via a crafted file.

code_evidence: The 32-bit little-endian infoheader_size is read from the file into rctx->infoheader_size at line 7 and copied to n at line 8. n is only capped to sizeof(buf) at line 9, so a size of 0 through 3 is not rejected. Line 10 then passes n-4 to iwbmp_read; when n<4 this size_t subtraction wraps to a huge value, so the read into &buf[4] can exceed or underflow the 124-byte stack buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The described defect is a missing size validation leading to a buffer underrun, not a NULL pointer dereference; the function contains no pointer that is dereferenced while NULL. CWE-476 does not fit the code-level root cause, so the target label is not supported by this function.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: absence of a lower-bound check on the attacker-controlled infoheader_size before the n-4 length computation. Trigger: a crafted BMP whose infoheader_size is below 4. Consequence: size_t underflow produces an oversized length passed to iwbmp_read, enabling buffer corruption or a crash; the patch adds an infoheader_size<12 guard.

commit_msg:
scsi/lsi53c895a: fix use-after-free in lsi_do_msgout (CVE-2022-0216)

Set current_req->req to NULL to prevent reusing a free'd buffer in case of
repeated SCSI cancel requests. Thanks to Thomas Huth for suggesting the patch.

Fixes: CVE-2022-0216
Resolves: https://gitlab.com/qemu-project/qemu/-/issues/972
Signed-off-by: Mauro Matteo Cascella <mcascell@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Thomas Huth <thuth@redhat.com>
Message-Id: <20220705200543.2366809-1-mcascell@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            if (current_req) {'], 'added_lines': ['            if (current_req && current_req->req) {', '                current_req->req = NULL;']}
description: A use-after-free vulnerability was found in the LSI53C895A SCSI Host Bus Adapter emulation of QEMU. The flaw occurs while processing repeated messages to cancel the current SCSI request via the lsi_do_msgout function. This flaw allows a malicious privileged user within the guest to crash the QEMU process on the host, resulting in a denial of service.

code_evidence: In the ABORT TAG (0x0d) case, the code checks only that current_req is non-NULL before calling scsi_req_cancel(current_req->req). It does not check or clear current_req->req after cancellation, so the pointer to the freed SCSI request remains in the lsi_request structure.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect is reuse of a pointer to memory already freed by scsi_req_cancel, which matches CWE-416 (Use After Free). It is not merely a NULL-check omission; the missing constraint is invalidating/clearing the freed pointer, so the stale reference is dereferenced on a subsequent abort.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: after scsi_req_cancel frees the underlying request, current_req->req is left dangling. Trigger: a malicious guest repeatedly issues ABORT TAG messages, causing the same stale request pointer to be passed to scsi_req_cancel again. Consequence: use-after-free of the freed SCSI request, leading to a host QEMU crash/denial of service (and potential memory corruption).

description:
A heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the Linux Kernel ipvlan network driver can be exploited to achieve local privilege escalation.

The out-of-bounds write is caused by missing skb->cb  initialization in the ipvlan network driver. The vulnerability is reachable if CONFIG_IPVLAN is enabled.


We recommend upgrading past commit 90cbed5247439a966b645b34eb0a2e037836ea8e.

code_evidence: After routing succeeds, skb_dst_set(skb, dst) is called and the skb is immediately passed to ip6_local_out(net, skb->sk, skb) at line 24. The function never clears IP6CB(skb) before handing the skb to the IPv6 output path, so control-block state left by an earlier qdisc enqueue (which reuses skb->cb) persists into the output stack.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The stale, uninitialized control-block state drives a memcpy that writes beyond the intended buffer, matching CWE-787's out-of-bounds write. The patch confirms the fix is a memset of IP6CB(skb) before ip6_local_out; the defect is missing initialization leading to an OOB write, not merely an information leak.

evidence_lines.code:
skb_dst_set(skb, dst);
err = ip6_local_out(net, skb->sk, skb);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the ipvlan IPv6 outbound path reuses an skb whose skb->cb region was overwritten by a qdisc (e.g., fq time_to_send) but does not reset the IPv6 control block. Trigger: a locally generated packet is routed out through ipvlan with a qdisc, then passed to ip6_local_out, whose consumers (e.g., option echo) interpret the stale cb fields as valid offsets/lengths. Supported consequence: an out-of-bounds memcpy write past the control block, i.e., stack/heap memory corruption.

Line 225 repeats the unchecked *(p4++) dereference at the end of each loop iteration.

opcode = *(p4++) & 0xff;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is the absence of a NULL/range check on the pointer returned by r_buf_get_at before it is dereferenced. commit_msg:
Should not call `initialize_copy` for `TT_ICLASS`; fix #4027

Since `TT_ICLASS` is a internal object that should never be revealed
to Ruby world.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    case MRB_TT_ICLASS:', '      copy_class(mrb, dest, obj);', '      return;']}
description: The init_copy function in kernel.c in mruby 1.4.1 makes initialize_copy calls for TT_ICLASS objects, which allows attackers to cause a denial of service (mrb_hash_keys uninitialized pointer and application crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact.

code_evidence: The switch dispatches on mrb_type(obj); MRB_TT_CLASS/MODULE perform class-specific copy (copy_class, iv copy, classname removal) and break, while all other types including MRB_TT_ICLASS fall through the default branch with no copy performed.

After the switch, line 24 unconditionally calls initialize_copy on dest with obj, so for TT_ICLASS dest was never populated by copy_class and the Ruby-level initialize_copy runs against an uninitialized internal object.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The consequence is access/use of an uninitialized pointer arising from missing initialization of the copied ICLASS object before initialize_copy. This matches CWE-824 rather than a mere logic error, since the uninitialized internal object state is dereferenced, causing a crash.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: TT_ICLASS objects reach init_copy but the switch has no case for them, so no class/instance-variable state is copied to dest before initialize_copy is invoked. Trigger: copying an internal ICLASS object (e.g. via mrb_hash_keys). The uninitialized internal state is then exposed to Ruby code, leading to an uninitialized pointer use and application crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
crypto: fix af_alg_make_sg() conversion to iov_iter

Commit 1d10eb2f156f ("crypto: switch af_alg_make_sg() to iov_iter")
broke af_alg_make_sg() and skcipher_recvmsg() in the process of moving
them to the iov_iter interfaces.  The 'npages' calculation in the formar
calculated the number of *bytes* in the pages, and in the latter case
the conversion didn't re-read the value of 'ctx->used' after waiting for
it to become non-zero.

This reverts to the original code for both these cases.

Cc: Al Viro <viro@zeniv.linux.org.uk>
Cc: David Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tused = ctx->used;', '\t\tif (!used) {', '\t\tused = min_t(unsigned long, used, iov_iter_count(&msg->msg_iter));'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (!ctx->used) {', '\t\tused = min_t(unsigned long, ctx->used, iov_iter_count(&msg->msg_iter));']}
description: A flaw was found in the subsequent get_user_pages_fast in the Linux kernel’s interface for symmetric key cipher algorithms in the skcipher_recvmsg of crypto/algif_skcipher.c function. This flaw allows a local user to crash the system.

code_evidence: The function snapshots ctx->used into local 'used' at line 21, tests it at line 22, and if zero waits for data at line 23 while holding the socket lock. After the wait returns, line 27 reuses the stale local 'used' rather than re-reading ctx->used, so the value consumed by af_alg_make_sg at line 28 reflects the pre-wait state.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The shared ctx->used is accessed non-atomically across a blocking wait, allowing an interfering code sequence to modify it between the check and use; this check-then-use window on shared state is exactly the race condition described by CWE-362. The stale-value consequence (crash) matches its availability impact, rather than a separate bounds or integer weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the local 'used' is read before skcipher_wait_for_data and not refreshed after waiting, so the subsequent min_t/af_alg_make_sg operate on a value that may be stale relative to the shared ctx->used updated by a concurrent producer. Trigger: another thread deposits data (changing ctx->used) during the wait window. Supported consequence: a mismatched page count/length reaching get_user_pages_fast, leading to a crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
Fix heap-buffer-overflows when accessing pool

Constants are usually retrieved from the constant pool without verifying
that the pool actually contains them, which may lead to various heap
buffer overflow issues.

In this patch we add a counter keeping track of how many elements the pool
contains, and checks making sure that whenever the pool is accessed, the
constant in present in the pool (constant position < pool counter).

Also, do not return "" when a pointer is excepted (it should be legal to free
this return value).

This patch fixes #112 (CVE-2018-7875), fixes #120 (CVE-2018-7871),
fixes #117 (CVE-2018-7870), fixes #114 (CVE-2018-7872), fixes #122,
fixes #113 (CVE-2018-7868), fixes #123.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (act->p.Constant8 > poolcounter)', '\t\t{', '\t\t        SWF_warn("WARNING: retrieving constants not present in the pool.\\n");', '\t\t        break;', '\t\t}', '\t\tif (act->p.Constant16 > poolcounter)', '\t\t{', '\t\t        SWF_warn("WARNING: retrieving constants not present in the pool.\\n");', '\t\t        break;', '\t\t}', '', '\tt = malloc(sizeof(char));', '\tstrcpyext(t,"");', '', '\treturn t;']}
description: There is a heap-based buffer over-read in the getName function of util/decompile.c in libming 0.4.8 for CONSTANT8 data. A Crafted input will lead to a denial of service attack.

code_evidence: In the PUSH_CONSTANT case, act->p.Constant8 indexes pool directly in the strlen and strcpy calls with no check that the index is within the pool's bounds.
The PUSH_CONSTANT16 case similarly indexes pool[act->p.Constant16] for strlen and strcpy without any bounds validation of the 16-bit constant index.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-119 fits because the function performs buffer operations (strlen/strcpy) on memory selected by an unchecked index, reading outside the intended buffer boundary. The patch in the diff adds the missing poolcounter check, confirming the out-of-bounds access is the fixed weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The attacker-controlled constant index from the SWF action selects a pool slot, but the code reads pool[index] before any bounds check. An out-of-range index causes the strlen/strcpy to read a pointer from beyond the pool array, producing a heap-based out-of-bounds read (and possible crash/DoS). The root cause is the missing index constraint; the consequence is an out-of-bounds memory read.

DIRECT mode to prevent concurrent access to extent tree with
ocfs2_dio_end_io_write(), which may cause BUGON in the following
situation:

description: In the Linux kernel before 4.15, fs/ocfs2/aops.c omits use of a semaphore and consequently has a race condition for access to the extent tree during read operations in DIRECT mode, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (BUG) by modifying a certain e_cpos field.

code_evidence: For READ operations the function selects ocfs2_get_block as the get_block callback, while writes select ocfs2_dio_get_block; the read path then proceeds through __blockdev_direct_IO without acquiring ip_alloc_sem. The write end_io path (ocfs2_dio_end_io_write) separately takes ip_alloc_sem and mutates the extent tree, so the two callbacks access the shared extent records under different synchronization.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function assigns the read callback that lacks the locking used by the concurrent writer, creating a timing window where the shared extent tree is modified during lookup. This improper synchronization of a shared resource across concurrent sequences is exactly CWE-362; it is a race rather than a missing bounds check because the failure arises from interleaving, not malformed input.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the read-side get_block callback traverses the extent tree without holding ip_alloc_sem, which the concurrent DIO write end_io path takes while splitting/modifying extent records. Trigger: a local user reads file A in DIRECT mode concurrently with completion of a write to the same file. Supported consequence: the reader observes an e_cpos modified mid-lookup and hits BUG_ON(v_cluster < e_cpos), a kernel crash/DoS.

commit_msg:
The VT_DISALLOCATE ioctl can free a virtual console while tty_release()
is still running, causing a use-after-free in con_shutdown().  This
occurs because VT_DISALLOCATE considers a virtual console's
'struct vc_data' to be unused as soon as the corresponding tty's
refcount hits 0.  But actually it may be still being closed.

Fix this by making vc_data be reference-counted via the embedded
'struct tty_port'.  A newly allocated virtual console has refcount 1.
Opening it for the first time increments the refcount to 2.  Closing it
for the last time decrements the refcount (in tty_operations::cleanup()
so that it happens late enough), as does VT_DISALLOCATE.

Reproducer:
	#include <fcntl.h>
	#include <linux/vt.h>
	#include <sys/ioctl.h>
	#include <unistd.h>

	int main()
	{
		if (fork()) {
			for (;;)
				close(open("/dev/tty5", O_RDWR));
		} else {
			int fd = open("/dev/tty10", O_RDWR);

			for (;;)
				ioctl(fd, VT_DISALLOCATE, 5);
		}
	}

description: A race condition in the Linux kernel before 5.6.2 between the VT_DISALLOCATE ioctl and closing/opening of ttys could lead to a use-after-free.

code_evidence: vc_allocate() kzallocs a struct vc_data and publishes it by storing it into the global shared array vc_cons[currcons].d at line 13 before tty_port_init() initializes the embedded reference-counted port at line 14. The object becomes visible to concurrent VT_DISALLOCATE/tty_release paths before its port (refcount/ops) is initialized, so another sequence can free or use it while this sequence is still setting it up.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect is improper synchronization over a shared resource: a timing window between publishing vc_cons[currcons].d and initializing vc->port lets an interfering concurrent sequence access the object. This matches CWE-362's concurrent shared-resource access without proper exclusivity, distinct from a simple null-dereference or missing bounds check.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the new vc_data is linked into the globally shared vc_cons[] before its vc->port is initialized, so concurrent close/disallocate code can observe and act on a partially initialized object, violating exclusivity/atomicity of the allocation sequence. Trigger: racing VT_DISALLOCATE against tty open/close. Supported consequence: use-after-free and crash in con_shutdown().

commit_msg:
board: factor out tiny_dispatch

And add stronger checks on what tiny_msg's are allowed to be decoded.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        uint8_t buf[64];', '        memcpy(buf, msg, sizeof(buf));', '', '        uint16_t msgId = buf[4] | ((uint16_t)buf[3]) << 8;', '        uint32_t msgSize = buf[8]        |', '                ((uint32_t)buf[7]) <<  8 |', '                ((uint32_t)buf[6]) << 16 |', '                ((uint32_t)buf[5]) << 24;', '', '        if (msgSize > 64 - 9) {', '            (*msg_failure)(FailureType_Failure_UnexpectedMessage, "Malformed tiny packet");', '            return;', '        }', '', '        // Determine callback handler and message map type.', '        const MessagesMap_t *entry = message_map_entry(NORMAL_MSG, msgId, IN_MSG);', '        if (!entry) {', '            (*msg_failure)(FailureType_Failure_UnexpectedMessage, "Unknown message");', '            return;', '        }', '', '        tiny_dispatch(entry, buf + 9, msgSize);'], 'added_lines': ['        msg_read_tiny(msg, len);']}
description: Insufficient checks in the USB packet handling of the ShapeShift KeepKey hardware wallet before firmware 6.2.2 allow out-of-bounds writes in the .bss segment via crafted messages. The vulnerability could allow code execution or other forms of impact. It can be triggered by unauthenticated attackers and the interface is reachable via WebUSB.

code_evidence: A fixed 64-byte stack buffer buf is declared and filled with memcpy(buf, msg, sizeof(buf)), copying exactly 64 bytes regardless of the caller-supplied len.
msgSize is decoded from attacker-controlled payload bytes buf[5..8] as a 32-bit big-endian value.
The only bound check rejects msgSize > 64 - 9 (55), but msgSize is a uint32_t compared against an int expression; msgSize is not validated against the actual received len.
tiny_dispatch(entry, buf + 9, msgSize) passes the decoded size with a pointer into buf, so the destination write length is attacker-controlled.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because an attacker-controlled size derived from packet bytes flows into a dispatch operation whose destination capacity is not constrained by the true input length, enabling writes beyond the intended buffer. This is an out-of-bounds write rather than a mere read, since the unchecked size governs the handler's write length.

evidence_lines.code:
uint8_t buf[64];
memcpy(buf, msg, sizeof(buf));

uint32_t msgSize = buf[8]        |
((uint32_t)buf[7]) <<  8 |
((uint32_t)buf[6]) << 16 |
((uint32_t)buf[5]) << 24;
tiny_dispatch(entry, buf + 9, msgSize);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the length field is trusted without cross-checking it against the real input len, and memcpy always reads 64 bytes. A crafted tiny packet can declare a msgSize that passes the 55-byte check but exceeds the data actually present; the dispatch handler then writes/reads based on this unchecked size, producing out-of-bounds memory access. Consequence is memory corruption in .bss, potentially leading to code execution.

commit_msg:
adb: fix buffer overflow while processing message payload

Fix a heap buffer overflow (write) when the message header length is
smaller than the actual message payload length. Add expert info to
detect this since it can also occur when the header is wrongly matched
with a data fragment (this dissector issue is not fixed here).

description: In Wireshark 2.4.0 to 2.4.5 and 2.2.0 to 2.2.13, the ADB dissector could crash with a heap-based buffer overflow. This was addressed in epan/dissectors/packet-adb.c by checking for a length inconsistency.

code_evidence: When reassembling, the code copies tvb_captured_length_remaining(tvb, offset) bytes into command_data->reassemble_data at offset reassemble_data_length without bounding the copy by the remaining allocated space (data_length - reassemble_data_length). If the header's data_length is smaller than the actual payload, the copy writes past the end of the heap buffer, then increments reassemble_data_length by the full copied amount.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe tvb_memcpy writes beyond the intended reassembly buffer, which is precisely an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). The fix adds a chunklen bound against data_length - reassemble_data_length, confirming the missing constraint was the write bound.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the memcpy length is the captured remaining bytes rather than the space left in the reassembly buffer. Trigger: a message header whose data_length is smaller than the payload actually delivered (malicious app or mismatched fragment). Consequence: heap out-of-bounds write, corrupting adjacent memory and potentially crashing the dissector.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['   BigInt i(msg, msg_len, q.bits());', '   while(i >= q)', '      i -= q;', '   const BigInt k = generate_rfc6979_nonce(m_x, q, i, m_rfc6979_hash);', '   BigInt s = inverse_mod(k, q);', '   s = m_mod_q.multiply(s, mul_add(m_x, r, i));'], 'added_lines': ['   BigInt m(msg, msg_len, q.bits());', '   while(m >= q)', '      m -= q;', '   const BigInt k = generate_rfc6979_nonce(m_x, q, m, m_rfc6979_hash);', '   const BigInt k_inv = inverse_mod(k, q);', '', '   /*', '   * Blind the input message and compute x*r+m as (x*r*b + m*b)/b', '   */', '   m_b = m_mod_q.square(m_b);', '   m_b_inv = m_mod_q.square(m_b_inv);', '', '   m = m_mod_q.multiply(m_b, m);', '   const BigInt xr = m_mod_q.multiply(m_mod_q.multiply(m_x, m_b), r);', '', '   const BigInt s = m_mod_q.multiply(m_b_inv, m_mod_q.multiply(k_inv, xr + m));']}
description: Botan 2.5.0 through 2.6.0 before 2.7.0 allows a memory-cache side-channel attack on ECDSA signatures, aka the Return Of the Hidden Number Problem or ROHNP, related to dsa/dsa.cpp, ec_group/ec_group.cpp, and ecdsa/ecdsa.cpp. To discover an ECDSA key, the attacker needs access to either the local machine or a different virtual machine on the same physical host.

code_evidence: The message is reduced into i and the nonce k is derived (via RFC6979 or RNG) before the signature arithmetic.

The signature computation inverse_mod(k,q), power_g_p(k) and mul_add(m_x,r,i) operates directly on the secret key m_x and nonce k without blinding, so the timing/cache behavior of these BigInt operations depends on secret values.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function leaks sensitive key material through an observable side channel to an unauthorized actor, matching CWE-200 (exposure of sensitive information). The fix adds multiplicative blinding (m_b/m_b_inv) precisely to hide secret-dependent operation patterns.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: secret-dependent modular arithmetic (inverse_mod, power_g_p, mul_add) on the private key and nonce is performed without blinding. Trigger: an attacker co-resident on the same host observes memory-cache/timing side channels during signing. Consequence: the secret nonce and key can be recovered, exposing sensitive private-key information.

description: A buffer overflow vulnerability in tiff12_print_page() in devices/gdevtfnx.c of Artifex Software GhostScript v9.50 allows a remote attacker to cause a denial of service via a crafted PDF file. This is fixed in v9.51.

code_evidence: Buffer data is allocated with exactly size bytes (size = gdev_prn_raster) and zeroed to size; no slack for the 6-byte reads performed later.
The loop advances src by 6 while x < size, so the final iteration reads src[5] even when size is not a multiple of 6, accessing bytes past the allocated buffer.
gdev_prn_copy_scan_lines fills data with size bytes; the subsequent 6-byte-group unpacking reads beyond that region.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 covers writing past buffer bounds; here the analogous out-of-bounds access past the allocated buffer at src[5] is the memory-safety violation fixed by enlarging the allocation, matching the target weakness class of buffer overrun.

evidence_lines.code: code = gdev_prn_copy_scan_lines(pdev, y, data, size);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the allocation and loop bound assume size is a multiple of 6, but the loop reads a full 6-byte group whenever x < size. Trigger: a crafted PDF producing a raster size not divisible by 6 causes src[5] to be read past the end of data. Supported consequence: out-of-bounds read leading to crash/DoS (the patch adds 5 bytes to avoid it).

description: Istio 1.4.x before 1.4.9 and Istio 1.5.x before 1.5.4 contain the following vulnerability when telemetry v2 is enabled: by sending a specially crafted packet, an attacker could trigger a Null Pointer Exception resulting in a Denial of Service. This could be sent to the ingress gateway or a sidecar, triggering a null pointer exception which results in a denial of service. This also affects servicemesh-proxy where a null pointer exception flaw was found in servicemesh-proxy. When running Telemetry v2 (not on by default in version 1.4.x), an attacker could send a specially crafted packet to the ingress gateway or proxy sidecar, triggering a denial of service.

code_evidence: Line 2 invokes onCreate(root_context_id_), which creates the VM context; only after this call does the code proceed to use the wasm_ VM object. Line 3 checks wasm_->onNewConnection_ and line 6 dispatches wasm_->onNewConnection_(this, id_), both dereferencing the wasm_ pointer and invoking into the VM. The patch adds in_vm_context_created_ = true after onCreate so that downstream code does not call into the VM before the context exists.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The supported consequence is dereferencing an uninitialized/NULL VM pointer during a network callback, matching CWE-476's NULL pointer dereference with availability impact. It is not merely a missing-initialization bug (CWE-457) because the observable failure is a NULL dereference crash.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: VM callbacks (onNewConnection_ and related network entry points) were reachable before the VM context was created, so the wasm_/VM state was not initialized. A crafted packet triggering a network connection reaches this callback while the VM context is absent, causing a NULL pointer dereference and process crash (DoS). The fix sets the in_vm_context_created_ flag in onNetworkNewConnection so later calls are guarded.

commit_msg:
Graphics library - prevent buffer overrun in (T)BCP encoding

Bug #706494 "Buffer Overflow in s_xBCPE_process"

As described in detail in the bug report, if the write buffer is filled
to one byte less than full, and we then try to write an escaped
character, we overrun the buffer because we don't check before
writing two bytes to it.

This just checks if we have two bytes before starting to write an
escaped character and exits if we don't (replacing the consumed byte
of the input).

Up for further discussion; why do we even permit a BCP encoding filter
anyway ? I think we should remove this, at least when SAFER is true.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['            /* Make sure we have space to store two characters in the write buffer,', "             * if we don't then exit without consuming the input character, we'll process", '             * that on the next time round.', '             */', '            if (pw->limit - q < 2) {', '                p--;', '                break;', '            }']}
description: In Artifex Ghostscript through 10.01.0, there is a buffer overflow leading to potential corruption of data internal to the PostScript interpreter, in base/sbcp.c. This affects BCPEncode, BCPDecode, TBCPEncode, and TBCPDecode. If the write buffer is filled to one byte less than full, and one then tries to write an escaped character, two bytes are written.

code_evidence: Line 10 sizes the loop bound end using min(rcount, wcount), so the loop assumes at most one output byte per input byte. Inside the escaped-character branch at line 13, lines 18 and 19 write CtrlA then the escaped byte, i.e. two output bytes, and line 21 only decrements end after those writes. When wcount is 1, the writes at 18-19 advance q past pw->limit before any space check, and line 23 adds the third write.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes past the end of the intended output buffer (pw->limit), directly matching CWE-787 Out-of-bounds Write. This is a write-side boundary error, not a read overrun (CWE-125) or a simple integer issue; the missing capacity check before the two-byte escape write is the root cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The loop bound is computed for one-byte-per-input output, but the escape path writes two bytes (CtrlA plus the escaped character) without verifying remaining write capacity. When the write buffer has only one free byte, the second write at line 19 exceeds pw->limit, corrupting adjacent memory; the fix adds a pw->limit - q < 2 check before writing.

commit_msg:
evtchn: evtchn_reset() shouldn't succeed with still-open ports

While the function closes all ports, it does so without holding any
lock, and hence racing requests may be issued causing new ports to get
opened. This would have been problematic in particular if such a newly
opened port had a port number above the new implementation limit (i.e.
when switching from FIFO to 2-level) after the reset, as prior to
"evtchn: relax port_is_valid()" this could have led to e.g.
evtchn_close()'s "BUG_ON(!port_is_valid(d2, port2))" to trigger.

Introduce a counter of active ports and check that it's (still) no
larger then the number of Xen internally used ones after obtaining the
necessary lock in evtchn_reset().

As to the access model of the new {active,xen}_evtchns fields - while
all writes get done using write_atomic(), reads ought to use
read_atomic() only when outside of a suitably locked region.

Note that as of now evtchn_bind_virq() and evtchn_bind_ipi() don't have
a need to call check_free_port().

This is part of XSA-343.

Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Reviewed-by: Stefano Stabellini <sstabellini@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Julien Grall <jgrall@amazon.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    write_atomic(&d->active_evtchns, d->active_evtchns + 1);', '']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.14.x. There are evtchn_reset() race conditions. Uses of EVTCHNOP_reset (potentially by a guest on itself) or XEN_DOMCTL_soft_reset (by itself covered by XSA-77) can lead to the violation of various internal assumptions. This may lead to out of bounds memory accesses or triggering of bug checks. In particular, x86 PV guests may be able to elevate their privilege to that of the host. Host and guest crashes are also possible, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS). Information leaks cannot be ruled out. All Xen versions from 4.5 onwards are vulnerable. Xen versions 4.4 and earlier are not vulnerable.

code_evidence: The port-validity and busy checks at [3] and [5] and the eventual success return at [29] are not performed under any lock; the function only updates the shared valid_evtchns counter at [27] with write_atomic, which makes the increment atomic but does not serialize the check-then-act sequence against concurrent callers.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-362 fits because a shared resource (the event-channel port table and counters) is accessed through a non-atomic check-then-act sequence with no exclusive synchronization, allowing an interfering code sequence to modify it concurrently. The atomic write only protects the counter increment, not the surrounding critical section.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: evtchn_allocate_port validates and allocates a port without holding the domain event-channel lock, so concurrent callers can pass the checks and allocate ports simultaneously. Trigger: a racing EVTCHNOP_reset or bind request interleaves between the checks and the bucket allocation. Consequence: the active-port accounting and reset assumptions are violated, enabling out-of-bounds accesses or bug checks and possible privilege escalation.

commit_msg:
There is a race between the assignment of `table->data` and write value
to the pointer of `table->data` in the __do_proc_doulongvec_minmax() on
the other thread.

  CPU0:                                 CPU1:
                                        proc_sys_write
  hugetlb_sysctl_handler                  proc_sys_call_handler
  hugetlb_sysctl_handler_common             hugetlb_sysctl_handler
    table->data = &tmp;                       hugetlb_sysctl_handler_common
                                                table->data = &tmp;
      proc_doulongvec_minmax
        do_proc_doulongvec_minmax           sysctl_head_finish
          __do_proc_doulongvec_minmax         unuse_table
            i = table->data;
            *i = val;  // corrupt CPU1's stack

Fix this by duplicating the `table`, and only update the duplicate of
it.  And introduce a helper of proc_hugetlb_doulongvec_minmax() to
simplify the code.

The following oops was seen:

    #PF: supervisor instruction fetch in kernel mode

description: A race condition between hugetlb sysctl handlers in mm/hugetlb.c in the Linux kernel before 5.8.8 could be used by local attackers to corrupt memory, cause a NULL pointer dereference, or possibly have unspecified other impact, aka CID-17743798d812.

code_evidence: The handler writes the address of the stack-local tmp into the shared ctl_table via table->data = &tmp and sets maxlen, then calls proc_doulongvec_minmax, which reads table->data and dereferences it to store the sysctl value.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This is a concurrent use of a shared resource (the ctl_table) with improper synchronization: the check/assignment/use sequence on table->data is neither exclusive nor atomic against an interfering handler invocation, matching CWE-362. The consequence is stack corruption or a crash, not a simple missing bounds check.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Concurrent invocations of hugetlb sysctl handlers share the same ctl_table. Each call mutates table->data to point at its own stack-local tmp without synchronization, so one thread can overwrite table->data while another is inside proc_doulongvec_minmax; the later read of table->data then dereferences a pointer into another thread's stack (or a stale/NULL value), causing memory corruption or a NULL pointer dereference crash.

commit_msg:
copy: CVE-2022-0485: Fail nbdcopy if NBD read or write fails

nbdcopy has a nasty bug when performing multi-threaded copies using
asynchronous nbd calls - it was blindly treating the completion of an
asynchronous command as successful, rather than checking the *error
parameter.  This can result in the silent creation of a corrupted
image in two different ways: when a read fails, we blindly wrote
garbage to the destination; when a write fails, we did not flag that
the destination was not written.

Since nbdcopy already calls exit() on a synchronous read or write
failure to a file, doing the same for an asynchronous op to an NBD
server is the simplest solution.  A nicer solution, but more invasive
to code and thus not done here, might be to allow up to N retries of
the transaction (in case the read or write failure was transient), or
even having a mode where as much data is copied as possible (portions
of the copy that failed would be logged on stderr, and nbdcopy would
still fail with a non-zero exit status, but this would copy more than
just stopping at the first error, as can be done with rsync or
ddrescue).

Note that since we rely on auto-retiring and do NOT call
nbd_aio_command_completed, our completion callbacks must always return
1 (if they do not exit() first), even when acting on *error, so as not
leave the command allocated until nbd_close.  As such, there is no
sane way to return an error to a manual caller of the callback, and
therefore we can drop dead code that calls perror() and exit() if the
callback "failed".  It is also worth documenting the contract on when
we must manually call the callback during the asynch_zero callback, so
that we do not leak or double-free the command; thankfully, all the
existing code paths were correct.

The added testsuite script demonstrates several scenarios, some of
which fail without the rest of this patch in place, and others which
showcase ways in which sparse images can bypass errors.

Once backports are complete, a followup patch on the main branch will
edit docs/libnbd-security.pod with the mailing list announcement of
the stable branch commit ids and release versions that incorporate
this fix.

Reported-by: Nir Soffer <nsoffer@redhat.com>
Fixes: bc896eec4d ("copy: Implement multi-conn, multiple threads, multiple requests in flight.", v1.5.6)
Fixes: https://bugzilla.redhat.com/2046194
Message-Id: <20220203202558.203013-6-eblake@redhat.com>
Acked-by: Richard W.M. Jones <rjones@redhat.com>
Acked-by: Nir Soffer <nsoffer@redhat.com>
[eblake: fix error message per Nir, tweak requires lines in unit test per Rich]
Reviewed-by: Laszlo Ersek <lersek@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  if (cb.callback (cb.user_data, &dummy) == -1) {', '    perror (rw->name);', '    exit (EXIT_FAILURE);', '  }'], 'added_lines': ['  cb.callback (cb.user_data, &dummy);']}
description: A flaw was found in the copying tool `nbdcopy` of libnbd. When performing multi-threaded copies using asynchronous nbd calls, nbdcopy was blindly treating the completion of an asynchronous command as successful, rather than checking the *error parameter. This could result in the silent creation of a corrupted destination image.

code_evidence: The callback `cb.callback(cb.user_data, &dummy)` is invoked and its return value is compared with -1; on failure the code calls `perror(rw->name)` and `exit(EXIT_FAILURE)`. The completion callback's status is therefore not ignored here: a failed asynchronous operation aborts instead of being treated as success.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-252 (Unchecked Return Value) fits because the callback's return/error indication is not verified, so the failure state is not detected and the copy proceeds. This is distinct from a mere error-message omission; the weakness is the unchecked failure signal driving incorrect program state.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is the missing check of the NBD completion callback's error status: the callback return is assumed to indicate success, so a failed read/write is not detected. Trigger is an asynchronous NBD read or write that fails; the supported consequence is continued processing as if data was copied, producing a silently corrupted destination image.
